context.description: SGLang is a high-performance serving framework for large language models and multimodal models.

latestRelease.title: v0.5.17
latestRelease.notes:
# Highlights

*582 PRs from 194 contributors.*

**Kimi K3 day-0 support**: A 2.8T-parameter multimodal LatentMoE (896 experts, top-16, routed in a 3584-dim latent space) with a 1M-token context, 69 KDA linear-attention layers interleaved with 24 MLA layers, and a MoonViT3d vision tower, shipping as a native MXFP4 checkpoint. SGLang serves it from day 0 with DCP, DSpark speculative decoding, chunked-prefill PP with TP decode, KDA-aware prefix caching, HiCache L2 over DCP, LoRA on the quantized weights, and reasoning, tool-call and OpenAI-compatible serving, verified on NVIDIA GB300 and AMD MI35x ([#32541](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/32541), [#32828](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/32828), [#32890](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/32890), [#33025](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/33025), [#33112](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/33112), [blog](https://www.lmsys.org/blog/2026-07-27-kimi-k3-day0-support), [cookbook](https://docs.sglang.io/cookbook/autoregressive/Moonshotai/Kimi-K3), [roadmap](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/32607)).

**MiniMax-H3 day-0 support**: MiniMax's video generation model that produces a video and a synchronized stereo audio track in one request, served natively on SGLang-Diffusion across all three public task profiles: text-to-video-and-audio (`t2va`), first/last-frame conditioning (`fl2va`), and image/video/audio reference conditioning (`ref2va`, which also covers video-to-video). Verified on B200 (TP2 + Ulysses4), H100 (TP2 + Ulysses2), AMD MI300X and MI355X (Ulysses1/2/4/8), and 2x RTX 5090 with layerwise offload ([#33275](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/33275), [cookbook](https://docs.sglang.io/cookbook/diffusion/MiniMax/MiniMax-H3)).

**Other new models added**: [EmbeddingGemma](https://docs.sglang.io/cookbook/autoregressive/Google/EmbeddingGemma) and [LFM2.5](https://docs.sglang.io/cookbook/autoregressive/LiquidAI/LFM2.5) embedding models, nvidia/MiniMax-M3-NVFP4, plus cookbook recipes for Poolside's [Laguna-S-2.1](https://docs.sglang.io/cookbook/autoregressive/Poolside/Laguna-S-2.1) family and [Inkling-Small](https://docs.sglang.io/cookbook/autoregressive/ThinkingMachines/Inkling-Small).

**Initial support for the Rust frontend**: Migrates the front half of the server, everything from network ingress up to the point a tokenized request is handed to the GPU scheduler, from Python to a multi-threaded Rust implementation ([#29799](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/29799)).

**DCP communication backends and q-replicate (Helix)**: The DeepSeek-MLA decode context-parallel path gains pluggable comm backends. `a2a` exchanges packed attention output plus fp32 LSE in a single NCCL collective per layer, with fp8 KV carried as uint8 byte transport; `fi_a2a` delegates the cross-rank exchange to the FlashInfer MNNVL kernel on GB200. `--dcp-replicate-q-proj` projects full-head Q locally and skips the per-layer Q head-dim all-gather. Select with `--dcp-comm-backend {ag_rs, a2a, fi_a2a}` ([#21637](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/21637)).

**DWDP for MoE prefill**: A new prefill parallelism strategy that prefetches peer expert weights over NVLink P2P and computes all experts locally, removing EP all-to-all token dispatch. On 4x B200 with gpt-oss-120b, prefill-only, DWDP4 reaches **1.92x over DEP4** at MNT 32K / ISL 32K, and **506K vs 329K tok/s (1.54x)** at saturation (CONC=128, ISL=8K). Enable with `--dwdp-size`; the authors mark it early-development ([#29778](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/29778)).

**Session-reference-aware Unified Radix Cache**: For agentic and RL-rollout workloads, requests can carry a stable `session_id` so eviction knows which prefixes an active session still references, instead of evicting purely by cache policy. Release the references with `/close_session`. Opt in with `--enable-session-radix-cache` ([#29173](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/29173)).

**SM90 FP8 MegaMoE for DeepSeek-V4**: Adds the DeepGEMM MegaMoE A2A path on SM90 for DeepSeek-V4-Flash/Pro FP8, including the pre-dispatch JIT kernel and FP8 expert weight preparation. Guarded behind `SGLANG_OPT_USE_DEEPGEMM_MEGA_MOE=1` ([#29016](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/29016)).

**Faster large-MoE model loading**: Oversized or non-contiguous CPU weight views were driving pathological H2D transfers, with DeepSeek-V4-Pro TP8 spending 27 to 32 minutes in H2D on some ranks. Copying those views into contiguous storage before H2D cuts full model loading from about **35 minutes to 6m20s (5.6x)**, and GPT-OSS-20B BF16 from **545s to 70s (7.8x)**, with Qwen3.5-397B measured at 1.93x to 2.3x. Opt in with `SGLANG_MOE_COPY_WEIGHT_VIEWS_BEFORE_H2D`, off by default ([#32315](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/32315)).

**Lower DeepSeek-V4 memory on AMD**: Removing unnecessary expert padding drops MI355X FP4 MoE model weights from **159.07 GB to 112.36 GB**, and bringing the HIP compress-state pool into the memory_saver KV_CACHE region lets colocated RL reclaim it, cutting the measured training-phase footprint from about **143 GiB to 87 GiB per GPU** ([#31450](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/31450), [#31747](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/31747)).

**Faster engine recovery**: Large-model restarts cost 3 to 6+ minutes today, about 6.5 minutes for Qwen3-235B FP8 on 4 GPUs, because weights reload from storage and CUDA graphs recapture. A weight-cache daemon holds weights per GPU so a restarting engine can recover from cache instead ([#27139](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/27139)).

**Lower host overhead in hybrid-linear MTP decode**: Under spec-v2 overlap scheduling each decode step runs draft, verify and extend CUDA graphs, and the eager seams between them become GPU idle time at low concurrency. This trims that host work so the host stays off the critical path ([#32219](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/32219)).

**Dependencies**: flashinfer 0.6.15.post1 ([#31927](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/31927)), sgl-deep-gemm 0.1.5.post1 ([#32345](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/32345), [#33143](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/33143)), helion 1.4 ([#32562](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/32562)), mooncake 0.3.12.post1 ([#32302](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/32302)), dynamo-tokenizers 1.7.0 ([#32981](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/32981)). PyTorch stays at 2.11.0 and the CUDA base image at 13.0.1.

*Full release notes by category below; breaking changes and known issues are at the end.*

* [Fix][AMD] Qwen3.5 MoE: disable global-slot shared-expert fusion under per-rank EP backends (MoRI + dp-attention init crash): [#31793](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/31793)

* [AMD] Fix JIT compile failure in sgl_kernel/warp.cuh: [#33195](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/33195)

## NPU / Ascend

* [NPU] Optimize DeepSeek-V4 performance: [#31931](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/31931)
* :sparkles: [llm][npu][quant] Add W8A8 MXFP8 quantization for Qwen3 MoE on Ascend NPU: [#30768](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/30768)
* [NPU] adapt dflash v2 on npu: [#31739](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/31739)
* [NPU] Adapt MiMo-V2.5-W8A8: [#29131](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/29131)

* [NPU] ascend fuseep use moe ep group: [#32040](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/32040)

* [NPU] [FIX] Fix performance degradation of Qwen3.5-397B-A17B: [#32130](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/32130)

* [Intel GPU] Add XPU Platform support: [#31949](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/31949)
* [XPU] Enable breakable prefill CUDA graph on XPU: [#30273](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/30273)

* [CPU] refactor rope kernels: [#31897](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/31897)

* [Bugfix] Fix CUDA import on non-CUDA platforms: [#31919](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/31919)

## Dependencies

* Bump FlashInfer to 0.6.15.post1: [#31927](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/31927) ⭐
* Bump sgl-deep-gemm to 0.1.5: [#32345](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/32345)
* Replace Kimi K3 DeepGEMM patch with 0.1.5.post1: [#33143](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/33143)
* Bump helion version to 1.4: [#32562](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/32562)
* chore: bump mooncake version to 0.3.12.post1: [#32302](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/32302)
* bump dynamo-tokenizers to 1.7.0: [#32981](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/32981)
* [AMD] ROCm AITER pin reverted to 9127c94, then updated to d9e5ef7: [#32879](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/32879), [#32939](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/32939)
* Fix PyPI release: drop the git-only sgl-eval dep from packaged metadata: [#32354](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/32354)

## Breaking Changes & Upgrade Notes

* **`helion` jumps 0.2.6 to 1.4**, a major-version move for anyone depending on helion-backed kernels: [#32562](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/32562)
* **`sglang.jit_kernel` is retired into `sglang.kernels`**, completing RFC [#29630](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/29630). Imports from the old module path must move: [#32072](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/32072), [#31666](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/31666), [#32015](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/32015), [#32045](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/32045)
* **Breakable prefill CUDA graph is now on by default for DP attention**: [#31682](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/31682)
* **CuteDSL BF16 GEMM on SM100 is on by default** when the heuristic allows it: [#30567](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/30567)
* **sgl-kernel AOT `bmm_fp8` is deleted in favor of `flashinfer.bmm_fp8`; the AOT router GEMM and fused A GEMM are also removed**: [#31202](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/31202), [#30280](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/30280)
* **The FP8 per-tensor GEMM backend on SM120 switches to cuBLAS**: [#31961](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/31961)
* **Unfetchable or unparseable multimodal inputs now return HTTP 400 instead of 500**, and text-only models reject media input outright: [#31417](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/31417), [#32914](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/32914)
* **Diffusion request-level quality is restricted to two validated tiers**, lossless (default) and high: [#33453](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/33453)
* **`ServerArgs` is being made read-only** behind namespace config bags. Code that mutated `ServerArgs` at runtime must route through the new accessors: [#31809](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/31809), [#31811](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/31811), [#33334](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/33334), [#33338](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/33338)

## Known Issues

* **The FlashInfer rmsnorm + quant fusion for SM90/SM100/SM120 was landed and reverted** this cycle ([#32994](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/32994), [#33455](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/33455)). It is not in this release.
* **Breakable CUDA graph is disabled for NemotronH** pending a fix: [#33130](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/33130)
* **`test_update_weights_from_disk` is skipped on ROCm** pending a reload fix ([#31924](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/31924)): [#31925](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/31925)
* **The SM120 DeepGEMM release-pipeline test is temporarily skipped**: [#32193](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/32193)

**Full Changelog**: [`v0.5.16...v0.5.17`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/compare/v0.5.16...v0.5.17)

signals.title: [Feature] Improve Unit Test Coverage
signals.text: ## Motivation SGLang's test suite has **600+ test files**, but most are E2E tests that launch a full server. While these cover many code paths, core modules like `managers/`, `mem_cache/`, `entrypoints/`, `sampling/`, `parser/`, `function_call/`, and `utils/` still need better unit test coverage (tests that run without launching a server). **Why this matters:** - E2E tests launch a server and load model weights, taking minutes. Unit tests run in seconds with mocked dependencies. - When an E2E test fails, the root cause could be anywhere. Unit tests pinpoint the exact broken function. ## What's Already Done - **Unit test directory** [`test/registered/unit/`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/tree/main/test/registered/unit) with READMEs ([`test/registered/README.md`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/test/registered/README.md), [`test/registered/unit/README.md`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/test/registered/unit/README.md)) documenting conventions - **32 unit tests migrated** across 12 subdirectories - **Coverage tooling** configured ([`.coveragerc`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.coveragerc), `pytest-cov`) - **CI coverage reporting** in [`ci-coverage-overview.yml`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/workflows/ci-coverage-overview.yml) (daily + manual trigger) — [example run](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/24032286387/attempts/1#summary-70083527423) - **Contribution guide** updated with [unit test section](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/docs/developer_guide/contribution_guide.md#run-and-add-unit-tests) ## Directory Structure ``` test/registered/unit/ # mirrors python/sglang/srt/ ├── mem_cache/ (6 files) ├── function_call/ (5 files) ├── utils/ (4 files) ├── parser/ (3 files) ├── managers/ (3 files) ├── entrypoints/ (2 files) ├── layers/ (2 files) ├── observability/ (2 files) ├── model_loader/ (2 files) ├── server_args/ (1 file) ├── model_executor/ (1 file) ├── batch_invariant_ops/ (1 file) └── ... (new subdirs added as tests are written) ``` **Principle:** Source file at `srt/mem_cache/radix_cache.py` → test at `unit/mem_cache/test_radix_cache.py`. ## Open Tasks Below are some suggested starting points. Comment on this issue to claim one. You can check the latest UT coverage report run ([example](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/24032286387/attempts/1#summary-70083527423)) or run coverage locally to find your own opportunities — modules with low coverage under core directories (`managers/`, `sampling/`, `parser/`, etc.) are good candidates: ```bash pytest test/registered/unit/ --cov --cov-config=.coveragerc --cov-report=term-missing -v ``` ### Easy (good first issue) - `srt/parser/` — conversation templates, reasoning parsers, code completion parser - `srt/sampling/` — parameter validation, normalization, logit processor serialization - `srt/entrypoints/openai/` — encoding/decoding, tool call formatting - `srt/function_call/` — extend existing detector tests, add new detector coverage ### Medium - `srt/utils/` — common util helpers - `srt/multimodal/` — media utils, processor base logic - `srt/constrained/` — grammar dispatch logic - `srt/managers/` — template manager, tokenizer utils, batch metadata helpers ## How to Contribute 1. **Pick a task** from above (or find your own via coverage), comment to claim it 2. **Look at existing examples:** - `test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_evict_policy.py` — pure logic, zero deps - `test/registered/unit/managers/test_prefill_adder.py` — mock factories for scheduler tests - `test/registered/unit/parser/test_reasoning_parser.py` — streaming parser tests 3. **Follow the conventions** in [`test/registered/unit/README.md`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/tree/main/test/registered/unit/README.md) and the [contribution guide](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/docs/developer_guide/contribution_guide.md#run-and-add-unit-tests) 4. **Run locally:** ```bash pytest test/registered/unit/ -v pytest test/registered/unit/ --cov --cov-config=.coveragerc -v # with coverage ``` 5. **Submit a PR** titled `[Test] Add unit tests for <module_name>`, referencing this issue ### PR Quality Bar **Note:** AI-assisted code is acceptable, but you are responsible for the quality — **understand every line you submit.** We will reject PRs that look auto-generated without understanding — e.g., tests that only check trivial cases, assert on mock return values, or don't actually exercise the real code logic. Read the source code first, then write tests that would catch real bugs. ### PR Requirements - [ ] Test is in `test/registered/unit/<module>/` (mirroring `srt/`) - [ ] Does NOT launch a server or load real model weights - [ ] Includes edge cases, not just happy paths - [ ] Use `CustomTestCase` instead of `unittest.TestCase`. - [ ] Registered with `register_cpu_ci()` or `register_cuda_ci()` - [ ] **Locally tested and passing.** Paste both the command and its output in your PR description: ```bash # command pytest test/registered/unit/<your_module>/test_xxx.py -v # output (copy-paste the full result) ```

signals.title: CI Maintenance Mode
signals.text: This post introduces a maintenance mode for our CI infrastructure. When the CI is unhealthy (due to too many flaky tests or unstable machines), we will open this issue, and the project will enter CI Maintenance mode. While maintenance mode is active, normal PRs' CI runs will be paused. Instead, we will allocate all resources to PRs that attempt to fix the CI. Once the CI is healthy and `pr-test.yml` is all green, we will close this issue to declare the end of maintenance mode. Typically, we will enter the maintenance mode when the scheduled pr-test on main is broken for some consecutive runs https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/workflows/pr-test.yml?query=event%3Aschedule Rebase required past #33384 (build the Rust extension modules once per run): without it every CUDA job recompiles the `rust/` cargo workspace during its editable install, and jobs sharing a host serialize on uv's editable sdist lock until the queue's tail hits its timeout. MIN_BASE_SHA: aa3f7667993038f6cd273d114497a458f0d7a671

signals.title: [RFC] Sglang non-GPU process rust migration
signals.text: ### Checklist - [x] If this is not a feature request but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed. - [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed. **PR** - https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/29799 Refer Roadmap https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/22949 Release Roadmap https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/1Y71GY3DOzZwuAp2ytehW0rJ4uzOx276PMtgTORgD49c/edit?slide=id.g3e59bc0132c_0_0#slide=id.g3e59bc0132c_0_0 ### Motivation **Status**: Draft **Author**: @rainj-me **Created**: Apr 20 2026 **Version**: 0.1 # Rust Server Migration Plan **Status:** Draft · **Last updated:** 2026-06-18 · **Owner:** Rain Jiang Migration of the SGLang request front-half (everything from network ingress up to the point a tokenized request is handed to the GPU scheduler) from Python to a multi-threaded Rust implementation. --- ## 1. Goals & scope **Goal.** Replace the Python tokenizer/detokenizer managers and HTTP server with a single-process, thread-per-core Rust implementation that owns the request lifecycle up to scheduler submission. **In scope:** HTTP(S)/gRPC/WS/h2/h3 server, request FSM, tokenizer & detokenizer managers, multimodal encoder dispatch, control API (abort/flush/weight update etc.), large tensor zero-copy handoff to the scheduler, cross-dp-group dispatch. **Out of scope (this plan):** model kernels, attention backends, KV-cache internals, quantization. The Rust server keeps the existing Python scheduler and GPU worker framework; it does not reimplement them. **Non-goals:** behavioral changes to the public API. The Rust server must be a drop-in for the Python one — same endpoints, same request/response schemas, same streaming semantics — so it can ship behind a flag and be A/B'd against Python. --- ## 2. Architecture summary The design this phase implement (decided separately; recorded here for context): - **Two FSMs, one process.** An **ingress FSM** (per request, multi-threaded, thread-per-core) carrying a request from `Received` through validation and optional encode/tokenize to `Queued`; and an **egress FSM** handling streaming (`Streaming` self-loop → `Finalizing` → `Completed`). They are the two halves of one request's lifecycle, owned by the same core and meeting at the ring-buffer / scheduler boundary — no shared locks. - **Six thread groups:** (1) **api-server** on an async runtime — accepts connections, terminates protocols; (2) **tokenizer-manager** running the ingress/egress request FSMs, CPU-core-bound; (3) **encoder** (core-bound); (4) **tokenizer** (core-bound); (5) **detokenizer** (core-bound); and (6) the python **scheduler** group within main thread. Groups talk only via channels — no shared locks across group boundaries. - **Channels:** bounded **MPSC** TokenizerManager→Scheduler (`try_send` = backpressure), per-core **SPSC** returns; userspace rings carry the payload, no ZMQ involved. Crossing the Rust→Python boundary, request objects are serialized with **msgpack** so only immutable bytes transfer — keeping the GIL out of the hot path. Tensor data bypasses msgpack entirely and is shared through **pinned memory**, handed across as a handle rather than copied or serialized. - **Zero-copy:** for encoded multimodal data, Python pre-allocates the pinned buffer pool at startup and Rust writes into slots by index during the encode/tokenize phase. Channels move slot handles (plus small msgpack metadata), never tensor bytes; lifetime is the pool's slot-reuse policy — a slot returns to the free list only after both Python's read and any GPU DMA complete, not Rust's `Drop`. - **Cross-rank:** For DP attention, the first rank of each DP group runs the Rust server *without* the api-server; a single api-server then fans **control** messages to every DP group (duplicated, since control must reach all), while **generation** requests are **round-robined** across DP groups for load balancing. - **Streaming:** a single `Streaming` macro state self-loops per chunk; non-streaming is just a stream whose frames are accumulated and emitted in `Finalizing`. See the request-FSM and topology diagrams in the Appendix for detail. --- ## 3. Phase 1 — Rust server (tok/detok manager + HTTP server) **Target: 2026-07-17** Phase 1 delivers the Rust front-half running in front of the **existing Python scheduler + GPU worker**, inside one process via multi-threaded Rust ⇄ Python. ### 3.1 Work breakdown | | Item | Status | Depends on | Notes | | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | | 1 | Rust frontend \+ scheduler PoC | ✅ Done | — | PR [\#23360](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/23360) \[Closed\] | | 2 | Architecture design | ✅ Done | — | Pending final approval | | 3 | Pickle → msgpack migration | ✅ Done | — | PR [\#28688](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/28688) \[Merged\] Followup issue [\#29465](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/29465) | | 4 | Single-process framework: multi-threaded Rust \+ Python scheduler/GPU worker | ✅ Done | 3 | | | 5 | Tokenizer & detokenizer manager | ✅ Done | 4 | | | 6 | HTTP server: /generate \+ streaming | ✅ Done | 4, 5 | | | 7 | Encoder support | 🟡 WIP | 4, 5 | Work with dynamo team check whether this can export to dynamo crate. | | 8 | PD disaggregation | ✅Done | 4 | Large. Prefill/decode split — see risk note. | | 9 | DP attention \+ cross-node DP controller | ✅ Done | 4 | Large, cross-node. See risk note. | | 10 | Metrics / logging | 🟡 WIP | 4 | Logging Done, Metrics WIP | | 11 | Port existing HTTP APIs other than the listed APIs below | ⏳ Pending | 6 | Full endpoint parity for drop-in replacement. | | 12 | Unified multi-protocol lib (server \+ gateway) | ⏳ Pending | 6 | Shared http(s)/h2/h3/gRPC/WS layer reused by sglang-gateway. | | 13 | Code Refactor | 🟡 WIP | | | | 14 | AuthZ support | | | | | 15 | Parallel Sampling | | | | | 16 | Benchmark\_serving perf optimization | 🟡 WIP | | | | 17 | Embedding request | | | | | 18 | offline Engine API support | | | | | 19 | Other flags in the TokenizedGenerateReqInput | | | | | 20 | cache\_tokens | | | | | 21 | custom\_logit\_processor | | | | | 22 | preferred\_sampling\_params | | | | | 23 | Standalone API-Server for DP Attn | 🟡 WIP | | | | 24 | Anthorpic API support | | | | | 25 | SageMaker API support | | | | | 26 | Vertex AI API support | | | | | 27 | Ollama compatible API support | | | | | 28 | Weight update APIs | | | | | 29 | HiCache APIs | | | | ### 3.2 Sequencing & critical path Items are **not** independent. The dependency spine is: ``` #3 pickle→msgpack ──► #4 single-process framework ──► #5 tok/detok ──► #6 /generate+stream ──► #11 API parity └─► #10 metrics (parallel) └─► #7 encoder (parallel, after #5) ``` **Critical path to a usable July 17 milestone:** 3 → 4 → 5 → 6, with 10 landing in parallel and 11 close behind. That subset is what makes the Rust server a working, A/B-testable drop-in for text LLM traffic. **Recommend deferring out of the July 17 milestone** (track as Phase 1.5 / stretch): items **8 (PD disaggregation)** and **9 (DP attention + cross-node DP controller)**. Both are large, both can land after the core path is proven, and bundling them into the July date puts the whole milestone at risk. Item **12 (unified protocol lib)** is valuable but is a refactor that can follow once #6 stabilizes the protocol surface. > **Date reality check.** July 17 is ~4 weeks out and #4 (the foundation) is still > pending-start. The 3→4→5→6+7 path is achievable in that window if #4 starts > immediately and 8/9/12 are explicitly descoped. Carrying all 12 to July 17 is not > realistic; pick the milestone definition deliberately. ### 3.3 Phase 1 exit criteria - Rust server handles `/generate` (streaming + non-streaming) at parity with Python. - Tok/detok managers run in-process; detok is incremental and order-correct. - Encoder path works for at least one multimodal input type. - Metrics + logs at parity; runs behind a flag, A/B-able against Python. - Endpoint parity sufficient to route production text traffic. --- ## 4. Cross-cutting concerns **Rollout / fallback.** Every phase ships behind a flag with the Python path as the live fallback. Migrate by traffic slice (shadow → small % → ramp), not big-bang. keep the Python path runnable as the live fallback until the Rust path reaches parity. **Testing.** Differential testing against Python (same inputs → same tokens/frames) is the primary correctness gate. Add: FSM property tests (every state has a terminal exit; post-terminal events are no-ops/idempotent); streaming order + UTF-8-boundary tests for detok. **Observability.** Metrics/logging (P1 #10) should land *with* the core path, not after — debugging the channel/FSM/threading layers without it is painful. Per-state request counts, queue depths (ring-buffer occupancy = backpressure signal), per-core load, and control-op latencies. **Kernel / environment.** io_uring features used (`MSG_RING` 5.18+, `SEND_ZC` 6.0+, `DEFER_TASKRUN` 6.1+) set a minimum kernel; some hardened/container environments disable io_uring — keep an epoll+eventfd fallback behind the same loop abstraction. --- ## 5. Top risks | Risk | Impact | Mitigation | | ------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | July 17 scope (all 12 items) | Milestone slips / quality suffers | Descope 8/9/12; define milestone as 3→4→5→6+10. | | #4 framework is the foundation and hasn't started | Blocks 5–7; whole phase waits | Start immediately; treat as the single highest-priority item. | | Rust↔Python boundary in the single-process step | Perf cliffs, GIL contention | Keep the boundary narrow (handles, not data); measure early. | | Detok ordering / UTF-8 under streaming | Corrupt user-visible output | Shard by `hash(req_id)`; stateful decode offsets; boundary tests. | | Slow-client backpressure on egress | GPU stalls / memory growth | Bounded egress buffers; treat persistent slow consumer as disconnect. | --- ## 6. Milestones | Date | Milestone | | ---------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | ~Now | #1 PR #23360, #3 merged (PR #28688); #4 started. | | 2026-07-17 | **Phase 1 core:** Rust server with `/generate` + streaming + encoder + metrics, A/B-able vs Python (items 3–7, 10, 11). | | Phase 1.5 | PD disaggregation (#8), DP attention + cross-node controller (#9), unified protocol lib (#12). | ## 7. Appendix 1. [Initial plan](https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/1Y71GY3DOzZwuAp2ytehW0rJ4uzOx276PMtgTORgD49c/edit?slide=id.g3e59bc0132c_0_0#slide=id.g3e59bc0132c_0_0) 2. [Architecture Design](https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/1_DJ_Fjq_tgMTmzWcmm5uacCi9RJGW_lwZGeXiecc6XY/edit?slide=id.g3eebae54d8d_0_0#slide=id.g3eebae54d8d_0_0)

signals.title: [RFC][Refactor] `mem_cache` pool / allocator restructure
signals.text: > **Roadmap v2.** Rewritten against `sglang/main` @ 2026-08-20; the original body is > in this issue's edit history. Hardware backends (`hardware_backend/npu/`, > `hardware_backend/mlx/`) are **out of scope** and are not covered by any item or > guard below. --- ## 1. TL;DR Reorganize `mem_cache/` from "a few catch-all files plus cross-feature pollution" into per-family one-module-per-family packages: - `allocator.py` → `allocator/` package — **done**, keep it closed - `memory_pool_host.py` → `pool_host/` package — **in progress**, 3 items left - `memory_pool.py` + 6 sibling files → `pool/` package — **not started**, and it is the only part of `mem_cache/` still actively getting worse - Untangle DSv4 ↔ HiSparse class misplacement - Naming rule: **remove role affixes that don't differentiate** - Add `mem_cache/README.md` (type × scope) index - Land a CI guard so the layout cannot regress once a target directory exists --- ## 2. Why v2: what changed since the RFC was opened The RFC was opened 2026-05-15. Three months of data: | File | 2026-05-15 | 2026-08-20 | Δ | |---|---|---|---| | `memory_pool.py` | 2257 lines / 11 classes | **5042 lines / 17 classes** | **+123%** | | `memory_pool_host.py` | 2105 lines / 8 classes | **1517 lines / 6 classes** | −28% | The layer that got a target directory shrank. The layer that did not got 2.8k lines and 6 new classes dumped into it: `PageMajorMHATokenToKVPool`, `MHATokenToKVPoolMXFP8`, `MHATokenToKOnlyPool`, `MiniMaxSparseKVPool`, `DSATokenToKVPool`, plus `KVWriteLoc` / `KvBufferDesc`. Two consequences drive v2: 1. **`pool/` moves from last to first.** It is the only remaining catch-all and the only one still growing. 2. **A directory alone is not a rule.** #29678 (2026-07-01) added `multi_ended_allocator.py` (2559 lines, 3 allocator classes) at top level *two months after* `allocator/` existed. Section 8 adds the guard. Additional drift the original body does not reflect: - `unified_cache_components/` was moved to `unified_cache/components/` in 60d6914f1 (2026-07-28), but the `_component` suffix was kept. The naming rule was silently dropped; the tree in the old §3.2 is contradicted by a landed PR. - `NSATokenToKVPool` → `DSATokenToKVPool`; `NSAIndexerPoolHost` → `DSAIndexerPoolHost`. All `nsa` names in the old tree are stale. - `allocator/mamba.py` holds `MambaSlotAllocator`, not `MambaTokenToKVPoolAllocator`. - `allocator/swa.py` gained `PureSWATokenToKVPoolAllocator` — filed correctly, which is the evidence that the rule works once the directory exists. - New, entirely uncovered by the old roadmap: `unified_memory_pool.py` (1691), `multi_ended_allocator.py` (2559), `kv_cache_configurator.py` (2190), `mamba_checkpoint_pool.py`, `index_key_cache.py`, `dsa_cache_layer_split.py`, `mamba_slot_fused.py`, `kv_vmm_backing.py`, `layout/`, `buffer_mode/`, `allocation.py`, `allocation_sizing.py`, `embedding_store.py`. --- ## 3. Rules for every PR under this issue 1. Title must carry the `[mem_cache][N/N]` prefix and state whether it is a **Mechanical Move**. 2. Mechanical Moves must satisfy the `mechanical-refactor-verify` skill. 3. Preserve git blame as far as possible; `git blame -C -C` is the accepted fallback. 4. **No compatibility shims.** Each move updates all importers in the same PR. This is the established precedent — `allocator.py` was deleted outright, not left as a re-export. `memory_pool.py` currently has 98 importers; they get updated, not forwarded. 5. Every PR must shrink the guard allowlist (§8) by exactly the classes it moved. 6. Adequate test coverage, and detailed review — no exceptions for "trivial" moves. --- ## 4. Naming rules 1. **Drop role affixes that do not differentiate.** If every file in a directory shares the role the directory already names, the affix carries no information: `pool_host/mha.py`, not `pool_host/mha_pool_host.py`. Keep `_backend` / `_controller` style only where same-directory siblings have *different* roles. 2. **A family is a module, and a module may be a file or a package.** One file per family is the default; a family over ~1500 lines becomes a package (`pool/deepseek_v4/` already does this, and `pool/mha/` must — see §5). 3. `Allocator` is overloaded and the two meanings must not be merged: - **slot allocator** — a `BaseTokenToKVPoolAllocator` subclass, answers "which slots are free". These belong in `allocator/`. - **host tensor allocator** — `HostTensorAllocator` and its subclasses (`ShmHostTensorAllocator`, `MooncakeHostTensorAllocator`, `UMBPHostTensorAllocator`), answers "give me pinned host memory". These stay in `pool_host/common.py` and `storage/`, and are **not** in scope for `allocator/`. --- ## 5. Target tree ``` mem_cache/ ├── README.md # (type × scope) index │ ├── allocator/ # slot indexing — CLOSED except for the two items in §6.1 │ ├── __init__.py │ ├── base.py # BaseTokenToKVPoolAllocator (abc only) │ ├── token.py # TokenToKVPoolAllocator (page_size=1) │ ├── paged.py # PagedTokenToKVPoolAllocator │ ├── mamba.py # MambaSlotAllocator │ ├── swa.py # SWATokenToKVPoolAllocator │ │ # PureSWATokenToKVPoolAllocator │ ├── hisparse.py # HiSparseTokenToKVPoolAllocator │ │ # DeepSeekV4HiSparseTokenToKVPoolAllocator │ └── multi_ended.py # MultiEndedAllocator │ # UnifiedMambaTokenToKVPoolAllocator │ # UnifiedSWATokenToKVPoolAllocator │ ├── pool/ # device physical storage │ ├── __init__.py │ ├── base.py # KVCache + BaseSWAKVPool + KVWriteLoc + KvBufferDesc │ ├── req_to_token.py # ReqToTokenPool + HybridReqToTokenPool │ ├── mha/ # 6 classes / ~1900 lines → package │ │ ├── __init__.py │ │ ├── base.py # MHATokenToKVPool │ │ ├── noop.py # NoOpMHATokenToKVPool │ │ ├── fp4.py # MHATokenToKVPoolFP4 │ │ ├── mxfp8.py # MHATokenToKVPoolMXFP8 │ │ ├── page_major.py # PageMajorMHATokenToKVPool │ │ └── k_only.py # MHATokenToKOnlyPool │ ├── mla.py # MLATokenToKVPool + MLATokenToKVPoolFP4 │ ├── dsa.py # DSATokenToKVPool + HiSparseDSATokenToKVPool │ │ # + LayerSplitDSATokenToKVPool │ │ # + IndexKeyCache + LayerSplitIndexKeyCache │ ├── mamba.py # MambaPool + MambaCheckpointPool + Int8CheckpointStore │ ├── hybrid.py # HybridLinearKVPool │ ├── swa.py # SWAKVPool │ ├── hisparse.py # HiSparseC4DevicePool │ ├── minimax.py # MiniMaxSparseKVPool │ ├── unified/ # shared-arena variants (see §9 D1) │ │ ├── __init__.py │ │ ├── arena.py # UnifiedKVPool + SubPoolSpec + MHA/MLA/Mamba specs │ │ ├── mha.py # UnifiedMHATokenToKVPool │ │ ├── mla.py # UnifiedMLATokenToKVPool │ │ ├── mamba.py # UnifiedMambaPool + UnifiedMambaSlotAllocator │ │ ├── swa.py # UnifiedSWAKVPool │ │ └── hybrid.py # UnifiedHybridReqToTokenPool + UnifiedHybridLinearKVPool │ └── deepseek_v4/ │ ├── __init__.py │ ├── composite.py # DeepSeekV4TokenToKVPool + DeepSeekV4UnifiedKVPool │ ├── single.py # DeepSeekV4SingleKVPool │ ├── indexer.py # DeepSeekV4IndexerPool │ └── compress_state.py # KVAndScore + CompressStatePool │ ├── pool_host/ # host-side mirrors for supported device pools │ ├── __init__.py │ ├── base.py # HostKVCache (abc) + synchronized decorator │ ├── common.py # HostTensorAllocator + ShmHostTensorAllocator + helpers │ ├── mha.py # MHATokenToKVPoolHost + MHATokenToKOnlyPoolHost │ │ # + AsymmetricMHATokenToKVPoolHost │ ├── mla.py # MLATokenToKVPoolHost │ ├── dsa.py # DSAIndexerPoolHost │ ├── mamba.py # MambaPoolHost │ ├── hisparse.py # HiSparseHostPoolMixin │ ├── group.py # PoolEntry + HostPoolGroup + LogicalHostPool │ └── deepseek_v4.py # DeepSeekV4PagedHostPool + DeepSeekV4StateHostPool │ ├── hybrid_cache/ # multi-pool orchestrator │ ├── controller.py # HybridCacheController │ └── pool_assembler.py # HybridPoolAssembler │ ├── unified_cache/components/ │ ├── __init__.py │ ├── base.py # TreeComponent (abc) + shared enums │ ├── full.py # FullComponent │ ├── mamba.py # MambaComponent │ └── swa.py # SWAComponent │ ├── allocation.py # scheduler-facing allocation policy (unchanged) ├── layout/ # cross-cutting memory layout helpers (unchanged) ├── buffer_mode/, storage/, sparsity/ # (unchanged) └── ... tree-layer files # (unchanged, #20415 territory) ``` Deleted when their last class moves out: `memory_pool.py`, `memory_pool_host.py`, `deepseek_v4_memory_pool.py`, `deepseek_v4_compress_state.py`, `swa_memory_pool.py`, `base_swa_memory_pool.py`, `hisparse_memory_pool.py`, `unified_memory_pool.py`, `multi_ended_allocator.py`, `mamba_checkpoint_pool.py`, `dsa_cache_layer_split.py`, `index_key_cache.py`. --- ## 6. Roadmap ### 6.1 `mem_cache/allocator/` — nearly done - [x] [Mechanical Move] split `allocator.py` into `allocator/` subpackage — #26675 - [x] [Mechanical Move] `SWATokenToKVPoolAllocator` — #26676 - [x] [Mechanical Move] HiSparse allocators — #26678 - [x] [Modify] Mamba allocator — #27256 - [ ] [Mechanical Move] `MultiEndedAllocator` → `allocator/multi_ended.py` (2559 lines / 3 classes — split into 3 PRs: `MultiEndedAllocator`, `UnifiedMambaTokenToKVPoolAllocator`, `UnifiedSWATokenToKVPoolAllocator`) - [ ] [Guard] land §8 with `allocator/` at zero allowlist entries ### 6.2 `mem_cache/pool_host/` — 3 items left - [x] [Mechanical Move] base subpackage (`__init__` + `base` + `hisparse` + `common`) — #27273 - [x] [Mechanical Move] `MHATokenToKVPoolHost` — #30249 - [x] [Mechanical Move] `MLATokenToKVPoolHost` — #30616 - [x] [Mechanical Move] `MambaPoolHost` — #31180 - [ ] [Mechanical Move] `DSAIndexerPoolHost` → `pool_host/dsa.py` — #35306 *(in review)* - [ ] [Mechanical Move] `DeepSeekV4PagedHostPool` + `DeepSeekV4StateHostPool` → `pool_host/deepseek_v4.py` - [ ] [Mechanical Move] `PoolEntry` + `HostPoolGroup` + `LogicalHostPool` → `pool_host/group.py`, delete `memory_pool_host.py` - [ ] [Guard] extend §8 to `pool_host/` at zero allowlist entries ### 6.3 `mem_cache/pool/` — **promoted to top priority, not started** Order matters: `base.py` first so every later PR has a target for its base class, then leaves before composites. - [x] [Mechanical Move] create `pool/` + `base.py` — `KVCache`, `BaseSWAKVPool` (from `base_swa_memory_pool.py`), `KVWriteLoc`, `KvBufferDesc`, `unwrap_write_loc` — #35647. The `_set_kv_buffer_*` helpers stay put: the moved region references none of them, so moving them would only widen the diff. - [ ] [Mechanical Move] `ReqToTokenPool` + `HybridReqToTokenPool` → `pool/req_to_token.py` - [ ] [Mechanical Move] `pool/mha/` package — one PR for `base.py` (`MHATokenToKVPool`, 1112 lines), then one PR per variant group: `noop` + `k_only`, `fp4` + `mxfp8`, `page_major` - [ ] [Mechanical Move] `MLATokenToKVPool` + `MLATokenToKVPoolFP4` → `pool/mla.py` - [ ] [Mechanical Move] `DSATokenToKVPool` + `HiSparseDSATokenToKVPool` → `pool/dsa.py`, delete `hisparse_memory_pool.py` - [ ] [Mechanical Move] `IndexKeyCache` → `pool/dsa.py`, delete `index_key_cache.py` *(same module as its sole owner `DSATokenToKVPool`, which removes the `TYPE_CHECKING` import cycle between the two)* - [ ] [Mechanical Move] `LayerSplitDSATokenToKVPool` + `LayerSplitIndexKeyCache` → `pool/dsa.py`, delete `dsa_cache_layer_split.py` - [ ] [Mechanical Move] `MambaPool` → `pool/mamba.py`; fold in `MambaCheckpointPool` + `Int8CheckpointStore`, delete `mamba_checkpoint_pool.py` - [ ] [Mechanical Move] `SWAKVPool` → `pool/swa.py`, delete `swa_memory_pool.py` - [ ] [Modify] `HybridLinearKVPool` → `pool/hybrid.py` (rename to `HybridKVPool` — the only non-mechanical item here, needs its own discussion) - [ ] [Mechanical Move] `MiniMaxSparseKVPool` → `pool/minimax.py` - [ ] [Mechanical Move] `HiSparseC4DevicePool` → `pool/hisparse.py` *(untangles the DSv4 ↔ HiSparse misplacement in `deepseek_v4_memory_pool.py`)* - [ ] [Mechanical Move] `pool/deepseek_v4/` — `single.py`, `indexer.py`, `composite.py`, `compress_state.py`; delete `deepseek_v4_memory_pool.py` and `deepseek_v4_compress_state.py` - [ ] [Mechanical Move] `pool/unified/` (see §9 D1); delete `unified_memory_pool.py` - [ ] Delete `memory_pool.py` - [ ] [Guard] extend §8 to `pool/` at zero allowlist entries ### 6.4 Naming cleanups - [ ] [Mechanical Move] `hybrid_cache/hybrid_cache_controller.py` → `controller.py` - [ ] [Mechanical Move] `hybrid_cache/hybrid_pool_assembler.py` → `pool_assembler.py` - [x] [Mechanical Move] `unified_cache/components/{full,mamba,swa}_component.py` → `{full,mamba,swa}.py`; `tree_component.py` → `base.py` — #35644 *(this was missed by #32484, which moved the directory but kept the suffixes)* ### 6.5 Documentation and guard - [x] `mem_cache/README.md` — layer map, placement-by-base-class, §4 naming rules, §7 dependency invariants — #35643. Deliberately coarse: a per-class inventory would need updating by every remaining move, and it already has a rot-proof home in §8's shrink-only pins. - [x] `test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_mem_cache_layout_ratchet.py` (§8) — R1 (allocator + pool_host), R2, R3, R4 — #35638 (draft, stacked on #35306) - [x] `.claude/skills/mem-cache-layout/SKILL.md` + trigger line in `.claude/rules/modify-component-must-read.md` - [ ] enable R1 for the `pool` role once `mem_cache/pool/` exists (first item of §6.3) --- ## 7. Layering and dependency invariants ``` scheduler / model_runner / attention backend │ ▼ ┌──────────────────────────────────────────┐ │ allocation.py │ per-batch allocation policy └──────────────────────────────────────────┘ │ ▼ ┌──────────────────────────────────────────┐ │ hybrid_cache/ │ multi-pool router └──────────────────────────────────────────┘ │ ▼ ┌──────────────────────────────────────────┐ │ allocator/ │ "give me N slots" └──────────────────────────────────────────┘ │ holds a reference to ↓ ▼ ┌────────────────────────┐ ┌──────────────────────────┐ │ pool/ (device, L1) │ ─ hicache ►│ pool_host/ (host, L2) │ └────────────────────────┘ offload └──────────────────────────┘ │ ▼ ┌──────────────────────────┐ │ storage/ (L3) │ └──────────────────────────┘ construction layer (cuts across all of the above, not a tier): kv_cache_configurator.py, kv_cache_builder.py, cache_init_params.py, allocation_sizing.py, kv_cache_dtype.py, kv_vmm_backing.py, hybrid_cache/pool_assembler.py ``` | Module | Cares about | In → Out | |---|---|---| | `allocation.py` | per-batch allocation policy | `batch` → `out_cache_loc` | | `hybrid_cache/` | per-layer routing across pools | `layer_id` → pool | | `allocator/` | which slots are free | `need_size` → `indices` | | `pool/` | physical KV / SSM state layout | `(layer_id, indices) ↔ tensor` | | `pool_host/` | host mirror + H2D/D2H | `device_indices ↔ host_indices` | **Dependency invariants** (machine-checkable, enforced by §8): - `pool/` must not import `allocator/`, `hybrid_cache/`, or `allocation.py`. - `pool_host/` must not import `allocator/` or `hybrid_cache/`. - `allocator/` may import `pool/` (it holds the pool it allocates into); the reverse is forbidden. - Nothing under `pool/`, `pool_host/`, or `allocator/` may import the construction layer. Construction depends on them, never the other way round. The original RFC declared per-layer responsibilities but no dependency direction. Without an enforced direction, the split only relocates files — the layers stop being layers the first time a pool reaches back up into an allocator. --- ## 8. Guard: `test_mem_cache_layout_ratchet.py` A directory is not a rule (see §2). The guard is a ratchet test in `test/registered/unit/mem_cache/`, modelled on the existing `test/registered/unit/test_module_state_ratchet.py` and registered into `base-a-test-cpu`. Four pins, each shrink-only, each covering one way the layout regressed after the restructure was agreed. ### R1 — a class lives where its base class says **Role is decided by base class, never by class name** — `HostTensorAllocator` is named `Allocator` but hands out pinned host memory, not KV slots (§4.3). Because inheritance crosses modules, the test builds a class graph over `mem_cache/` and takes its transitive closure. Class names do collide (three modules define `TreeNode`), so ancestry is unioned across same-named definitions: over-approximating turns a collision into a review conversation, where dropping all but one definition would turn it into a silent miss. | Transitive base | Required home | |---|---| | `BaseTokenToKVPoolAllocator` | `mem_cache/allocator/` | | `HostKVCache` | `mem_cache/pool_host/` | | `KVCache`, `BaseSWAKVPool`, `ReqToTokenPool`, `MambaPool` | `mem_cache/pool/` *(deferred)* | `_LEGACY_HOMES` pins the five classes still misfiled today (3 allocators in `multi_ended_allocator.py`, 2 host pools in `memory_pool_host.py`). **The pool role is enforced only once `mem_cache/pool/` exists.** An error telling someone to file a class into a package nobody has created is a trap, not a rule. R3 covers the device pools in the meantime; when the first `pool/` PR lands, `pool` joins the enforced roles and its 29 classes move from R3's pin into `_LEGACY_HOMES`. ### R2 — no new top-level modules `_TOP_LEVEL_MODULES` freezes the 40 `mem_cache/*.py` files that exist today. A new top-level module must go into a package, or grow the pin in the same PR — which forces the "why is this not in a package?" conversation into review instead of leaving it to be noticed three months later. ### R3 — modules slated for deletion only shrink R1 and R2 both miss the most damaging case: a class appended to a module that already exists. That is exactly how `memory_pool.py` gained `PageMajorMHATokenToKVPool`, `MHATokenToKVPoolMXFP8`, `MHATokenToKOnlyPool`, `MiniMaxSparseKVPool` and `DSATokenToKVPool` after the split was agreed. `_SHRINKING_MODULES` pins the class list of every module §5 marks for deletion. It needs no target package to exist, so it is what stands in for the pool role until R1 takes over. ### R4 — layers don't import upwards Asserts the §7 dependency invariants over the import graph. It passes on `main` today, so it locks in a property the code already has rather than demanding new work. ### Mechanics - Pins hold today's state, so the test is green on landing and never blocks unrelated work. - A violation that is not pinned → fail, with an error naming the correct target file and linking this roadmap. - **Every pin also fails when it rots**: a class that has moved, a module that is gone, a file that no longer exists. This makes every move PR shrink a pin (Rule 5 in §3) and turns the pins into the migration's progress ledger. - Scope is `python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/` only. `hardware_backend/` is explicitly excluded — its NPU/MLX pools and allocators are a separate device axis and are not governed by this issue. Each of the six failure paths (four violations, two rot cases) was verified to fire by injecting the violation into a scratch copy of the tree; a guard nobody has seen go red is not a guard. A skill (`.claude/skills/mem-cache-layout/SKILL.md`) covers the same rules for coding agents, but is *not* the guard: human PRs never read `.claude/skills/`. The ratchet blocks; the skill only teaches. --- ## 9. Resolved design decisions **D1 — `Unified*` shared-arena classes stay cohesive.** `unified_memory_pool.py` and `multi_ended_allocator.py` (both from #29678) are `Unified*` variants of every family, but they are coupled to a shared `UnifiedKVPool` arena rather than to their own families. Folding each into its family file would spread one concern across six files. They keep their cohesion in `pool/unified/` and `allocator/multi_ended.py`, as §5 shows. `pool/unified/` is the one place where the one-module-per-family rule (§4.2) is deliberately overridden by a one-module-per-arena split. **D2 — the construction layer is a follow-up issue, not part of this one.** `kv_cache_configurator.py` (2190) + `kv_cache_builder.py` + `cache_init_params.py` + `allocation_sizing.py` + `kv_cache_dtype.py` + `kv_vmm_backing.py` + `hybrid_cache/pool_assembler.py` (1960) is ~5.5k lines with no home in the tier diagram. §7 recognizes it as a cross-cutting layer; §5 deliberately leaves the files where they are. `mem_cache/build/` gets planned as its own issue **after §6.3 lands** — moving construction and storage in the same window would churn the same importers twice and make every Mechanical Move proof harder to review. **D3 — `IndexKeyCache` goes into `pool/dsa.py`, with no new base class.** Its only two importers are `DSATokenToKVPool` and `LayerSplitIndexKeyCache`, both of which land in `pool/dsa.py`; it holds a `self.pool` back-reference and reads ten pool attributes, so today the two sides only avoid an import cycle via `TYPE_CHECKING` and a string annotation. Same module removes the cycle. Its whole API (`move`, `get_buffer`, `store_quantized`, `cpu_copy`, `load_cpu_copy`, `state_buf_infos`) is the storage contract, and `DSATokenToKVPool` forwards to it one line at a time — it is simply DSA's second device buffer. It is **not** given a `KVCache` base just so the guard can classify it: inventing an abstraction to satisfy a linter is the wrong direction. Rule 2 of §8 covers it instead, by pinning the top-level module list.

signals.title: Bug: `repetition_penalty` parameter is ignored due to missing `BatchedRepetitionPenalizer`
signals.text: ## Summary The `repetition_penalty` sampling parameter is accepted by the API but completely ignored during inference. This occurs because `BatchedRepetitionPenalizer` is not implemented or registered in SGLang's `penaltylib` orchestrator, causing the penalty to never be applied to logits. ## What Happens (User-facing symptoms) **Scenario A - Repetition loops in generation:** When setting `repetition_penalty > 1.0` (e.g., `1.15`) via the API, the model occasionally gets stuck in a repetition loop where it generates the same content indefinitely. The penalty has zero effect on the output distribution. **Scenario B - Silent parameter drop:** Users configure `repetition_penalty` expecting standard HuggingFace-style behavior (multiplicative logit adjustment), but the generation behaves identically to `repetition_penalty=1.0`. No warning or error is raised. ## Reproduction Steps This issue is sporadic and cannot be reliably reproduced, but it occurs frequently enough to be a concern. The following setup has been observed to trigger it: 1. Start an SGLang server with DFlash speculative decoding: ```bash python -m sglang.launch_server --model-path <your-model> --speculative-algo dflash --port 30000 ``` 2. Send a completion request with `repetition_penalty > 1.0`: ```bash curl http://localhost:30000/v1/completions -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"model": "<your-model>", "prompt": "Hello, ", "repetition_penalty": 1.15}' ``` 3. Observe that the output sometimes contains repeated tokens/phrases identical to a request with `repetition_penalty: 1.0`. ## Observed Behavior (Logs) The following logs show a request stuck in a repetition loop with 100% accept rate and continuously increasing token count: ``` [2026-06-14 15:28:57] Decode batch, #running-req: 1, #full token: 47360, accept len: 8.00, accept rate: 1.00, gen throughput (token/s): 290.40, #queue-req: 0 [2026-06-14 15:28:58] Decode batch, #running-req: 1, #full token: 47680, accept len: 8.00, accept rate: 1.00, gen throughput (token/s): 290.22, #queue-req: 0 [2026-06-14 15:28:59] Decode batch, #running-req: 1, #full token: 48000, accept len: 8.00, accept rate: 1.00, gen throughput (token/s): 290.38, #queue-req: 0 [2026-06-14 15:29:00] Decode batch, #running-req: 1, #full token: 48320, accept len: 8.00, accept rate: 1.00, gen throughput (token/s): 289.19, #queue-req: 0 [2026-06-14 15:29:01] Decode batch, #running-req: 1, #full token: 48640, accept len: 8.00, accept rate: 1.00, gen throughput (token/s): 289.10, #queue-req: 0 [2026-06-14 15:29:02] Decode batch, #running-req: 1, #full token: 48960, accept len: 8.00, accept rate: 1.00, gen throughput (token/s): 288.85, #queue-req: 0 [2026-06-14 15:29:03] Decode batch, #running-req: 1, #full token: 49280, accept len: 8.00, accept rate: 1.00, gen throughput (token/s): 289.00, #queue-req: 0 [2026-06-14 15:29:05] Decode batch, #running-req: 1, #full token: 49600, accept len: 8.00, accept rate: 1.00, gen throughput (token/s): 260.42, #queue-req: 0 [2026-06-14 15:29:06] Decode batch, #running-req: 1, #full token: 49920, accept len: 8.00, accept rate: 1.00, gen throughput (token/s): 287.98, #queue-req: 0 [2026-06-14 15:29:07] Decode batch, #running-req: 1, #full token: 50240, accept len: 8.00, accept rate: 1.00, gen throughput (token/s): 287.31, #queue-req: 0 ``` Key observations: - `accept rate: 1.00` (100%) - draft model predictions are fully accepted - `#full token` continuously increases (47360 to 50240+) - `#running-req: 1` - request never terminates - `gen throughput` remains stable (~290 token/s) - Model is stuck in a repetition loop despite `repetition_penalty` being set ## Root Cause Analysis 1. In `sglang/srt/sampling/sampling_batch_info.py`, the `SamplingBatchInfo` class initializes the penalty orchestrator: ```python penalizer_orchestrator = penaltylib.BatchedPenalizerOrchestrator( vocab_size=vocab_size, batch=batch, penalizers={ penaltylib.BatchedFrequencyPenalizer, penaltylib.BatchedMinNewTokensPenalizer, penaltylib.BatchedPresencePenalizer, }, ) ``` 2. `BatchedRepetitionPenalizer` is **missing** from the `penalizers` set. 3. The `SamplingParams` class accepts and validates `repetition_penalty`, but since no penalizer implements it, the value is never read or applied during the `_apply_penalties()` phase. 4. This is a gap in SGLang's sampling pipeline compared to HuggingFace/vLLM, which fully support `repetition_penalty`. ## Impact - Users cannot control repetition behavior via the standard `repetition_penalty` parameter. - Models prone to looping (especially under high temperature or long context) cannot be stabilized. - Breaks compatibility with HuggingFace `generation_config` and other frameworks that rely on this parameter. - Particularly problematic with speculative decoding (DFlash/Eagle) where repetition loops can cause infinite generation. ## Proposed Fix 1. Implement `BatchedRepetitionPenalizer` in `sglang/srt/sampling/penaltylib/repetition_penalty.py` following the HuggingFace formula: - If `logit > 0`: `logit /= repetition_penalty` - If `logit < 0`: `logit *= repetition_penalty` - If `logit == 0`: unchanged 2. Register it in `penaltylib/__init__.py`. 3. Add `penaltylib.BatchedRepetitionPenalizer` to the `penalizers` set in `SamplingBatchInfo.__init__`. 4. Add unit tests to verify logit modification matches HF behavior. ## Environment - **Model:** Qwen3.6-27B (FP8) - **Speculative Decoding:** DFlash (with Mamba hybrid layers) - **GPU:** RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell (96GB) - **Python Version:** 3.11 - **SGLang Version:** Both main branch and release versions tested - **Relevant Files:** - `sglang/srt/sampling/sampling_batch_info.py` - `sglang/srt/sampling/penaltylib/__init__.py` - `sglang/srt/sampling/sampling_params.py`

signals.title: [RFC][NPU][DLLM] Add fused tracker and coreset kernels for LLaDA2 JointThreshold
signals.text: # [RFC][NPU][DLLM] Fused tracker and coreset kernels for LLaDA2 JointThreshold ## Summary Two NPU-only fused kernels for the LLaDA2.1-mini dLLM JointThreshold decode path on Ascend, replacing per-layer small-op swarms in MoE expert tracking and coreset keep-mask selection with single kernels, behind a runtime flag with a pure-Torch fallback. On GSM8K (n=50) they deliver **+5.14% output throughput at identical accuracy (92.0%)**. This RFC proposes kernel placement and the kernel → release → integration upstream sequence. ## Motivation In the JointThreshold decode loop, two operations run per MoE layer per denoising forward: 1. the history-gate tracker max + EMA update, and 2. the per-call coreset keep-mask selection (softmax-sum score → group-balanced top-q). On NPU these are dispatch-bound: each is a handful of small kernels whose host launch cost dominates their compute, so the device idles between launches. Fusing each path into one kernel removes those launches from the decode critical path without changing the selection semantics. ## Proposed kernels 1. **`moe_gate_max_update`** — fuses the per-expert running-max update and the EMA update into one NPU kernel (replaces a `torch.maximum(...)` + `mul_`/`add_` pair per layer). 2. **`moe_shortlist_mask`** — computes the per-call coreset selection (bf16-rounded softmax-sum score; exact top-q-per-group with lowest-index tie-break, matching `torch.topk(q)`), writes the keep-set, and masks dropped experts, in one HBM round-trip (replaces ~6–10 small vector ops per layer). Both are NPU-only and shape-specialized to the current LLaDA2 MoE (E=256, 8 groups). The Python integration uses them only when enabled; otherwise the existing Torch path runs unchanged. ## Upstream sequence (kernel / release / integration) Kernel source and the SGLang Python caller land as separate PRs because the kernel package is released separately: 1. **[sgl-kernel-npu] Kernel source PR** — add the two ops + bindings + a correctness test. 2. **[sgl-kernel-npu] Release** — a maintainer ships a release containing the new ops. 3. **[sglang] Python integration PR** — env-gated NPU-only call sites with Torch fallback, depending on the sgl-kernel-npu release that contains the ops. Target repos: kernels → `github.com/sgl-project/sgl-kernel-npu`; Python → `github.com/sgl-project/sglang`. ## Guarded-fallback design (integration PR) The integration is NPU-only and guarded; CUDA/default execution is structurally untouched because the kernels are NPU-only. The call site checks: `device.type == "npu"`, fp32 dtype + contiguity, op availability (`hasattr(torch.ops.npu, "moe_gate_max_update")` / `"moe_shortlist_mask"`), and the runtime flag — otherwise it runs the existing Torch path. The model still loads and serves when the kernels are not present; the Torch path simply runs. ## Evidence GSM8K (n=50), Ascend 910B3, LLaDA2.1-mini, SGLang dLLM JointThreshold. Control runs the identical recipe and runtime-flag stack with the two new kernels off (`TRACKER_MAX_UPD_KERNEL=0`, `PERCALL_KEEP_KERNEL=0`). | Run | Accuracy | Output TPS | Elapsed | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | | Control (kernels off) | 46/50 = 92.0% | 355.107 | 42.68 s | | + tracker-max-update + coreset-keep kernels | 46/50 = 92.0% | 373.346 | 40.60 s | Δ = **+18.24 tok/s (+5.14%)** at identical accuracy. Next: extend to n ≥ 100 and add a per-op fallback equivalence test. Excluded from this RFC: cbout, maxfold, tracker sum-update, and deferred-flush variants. They were tested locally but were not reproducible release candidates. ## Environment | Component | Version | | --- | --- | | NPU | Ascend 910B3 | | CANN | 9.0.0 (V100R001C10SPC001B250) | | torch / torch_npu | 2.10.0 / 2.10.0 | | dtype / attention / max-running-requests | bfloat16 / ascend / 1 | ## Open questions 1. Should these kernels live under the existing `sgl-kernel-npu` layout, or a dLLM-specific submodule? 2. What is the release/version mechanism for sgl-kernel-npu — how should the integration PR pin the release that contains these ops? ## Reviewers / references NPU backend: @ping1jing2 @iforgetmyname @whybeyoung · DLLM: @ClawSeven @btw616 Style references: #27127 (guarded NPU-only fallback), #21094 (before/after dLLM throughput evidence), #18485 (how-to-run + benchmark evidence), #27144 (concise NPU dLLM PR with GSM8K evidence).

signals.title: Speculative EAGLE verify: greedy/HIP branch missing TP broadcast -> rank divergence -> collective deadlock on ROCm
signals.text: ## Summary On ROCm with TP>1 and speculative decoding (EAGLE/NEXTN), the EAGLE verify step can desynchronize TP ranks, producing different per-request accept counts across ranks → divergent running-batch composition → a subsequent collective (all-reduce) with mismatched shapes → **permanent TP deadlock** (all GPUs at 100% compute, 0% memory traffic; FastAPI still answers `/health` but `/v1/chat/completions` hangs). This is the same failure *class* as #27221 / #27164 (TP rank-divergence into a collective), but a **different trigger**: not abort-on-timeout, but the speculative **verify** path. ## Root cause In `python/sglang/srt/speculative/eagle_utils.py` (main @ `f42ec350b431`), the verify branch: ```python if sampling_info.is_all_greedy or _is_npu or _is_hip: # ROCm ALWAYS enters here target_predict = torch.argmax(next_token_logits, dim=-1) predict, accept_index, num_correct_drafts = verify_tree_greedy_func(...) # <-- NO cross-rank broadcast else: ... tree_speculative_sampling_target_only(...) # the sampling branch DOES broadcast: if tp_group.world_size > 1: tp_group.broadcast(predict, src=0) tp_group.broadcast(accept_index, src=0) tp_group.broadcast(num_correct_drafts, src=0) ``` Because `_is_hip` forces the greedy branch on ROCm, the verify result (`predict`, `accept_index`, `num_correct_drafts`) is computed **locally per rank from `torch.argmax(next_token_logits)`** and is **never broadcast**. `next_token_logits` depends on the preceding all-reduce; when that all-reduce is **not bitwise-deterministic across ranks** (e.g. AMD aiter custom all-reduce, which is used on the speculative path even when the main path is on NCCL), ranks can pick different argmax on near-ties → different accept counts → divergent batch composition → deadlock on the next forward's collective. The sampling branch already added a broadcast for exactly this reason ("different GPUs may produce slightly different ... causing different sampled tokens. Broadcast from rank 0 to ensure consistency."). The greedy branch needs the same. ## Proposed fix Add the identical broadcast to the greedy branch after `verify_tree_greedy_func`: ```python if sampling_info.is_all_greedy or _is_npu or _is_hip: target_predict = torch.argmax(next_token_logits, dim=-1) predict, accept_index, num_correct_drafts = verify_tree_greedy_func(...) tp_group = get_attention_tp_group() if is_dp_attention_enabled() else get_tp_group() if tp_group.world_size > 1: tp_group.broadcast(predict, src=0) tp_group.broadcast(accept_index, src=0) tp_group.broadcast(num_correct_drafts, src=0) ``` This guarantees rank-consistent accept results regardless of all-reduce determinism. Happy to open a PR. ## Environment - SGLang `lmsysorg/sglang:v0.5.13.post1-rocm700-mi30x`; bug also present on `main` @ `f42ec350b431`. - ROCm 7.0, 8x AMD MI300X (gfx942), TP=8, single node. - Model: GLM-5.2-FP8 (`GlmMoeDsaForCausalLM`, DSA+MLA+MoE), `--speculative-algorithm NEXTN --speculative-num-steps 3 --speculative-num-draft-tokens 4`, `--kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3`. - Startup logs: main forward `All-reduce call path: NCCL (custom AR disabled)`, but speculative path `Using AiterCustomAllreduce (AMD default)`. ## Reproduction Concurrent, transition-heavy load (long decodes kept alive + long prefills joining + short request churn + streaming client-aborts + a few invalid payloads) wedges the server in ~5 min, even at low concurrency (1-2 running requests) — it is a batch-composition *transition* trigger, not raw overload. When wedged, all 8 TP scheduler processes are stuck at the same `run_batch` forward frame (py-spy), with GPUs at 100% use / 0% memory activity. ## Confirmed workaround `--disable-custom-all-reduce` (forces deterministic NCCL all-reduce, so all ranks compute the same argmax). A/B on identical hardware/load: baseline wedges in ~5 min; with `--disable-custom-all-reduce` the same load ran 28 min with zero wedges. Setting `SYNC_TOKEN_IDS_ACROSS_TP=1` is a related backstop for the main-sampler path (`sampler.py`), though it does not cover the spec-verify accept counts.

signals.text: ### Checklist - [x] I searched related issues but found no solution. - [x] The bug persists in the latest version. - [x] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback. - [x] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed. - [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed. ### Describe the bug gemma4 run video faile when use sdpa as mm_attention_backend ` File "sglang/python/sglang/srt/models/gemma4_vision.py", line 238, in forward output = self.qkv_backend.forward( ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^ File "sglang/python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/vision.py", line 281, in forward assert bsz == 1, "flatten_batch is True, bsz must be 1" ^^^^^^^^ AssertionError: flatten_batch is True, bsz must be 1 ` ### Reproduction ### server ```bash python -m sglang.launch_server \ --mm-attention-backend sdpa \ --model-path google/gemma-4-E2B-it/ \ --context-length 32768 --host 0.0.0.0 --port 20001 ``` ### clint ```python from openai import OpenAI client = OpenAI( api_key="token-abc123", base_url="http://localhost:20001/v1", timeout=3600 ) chat_completion_from_base64 = client.chat.completions.create( messages=[ { "role": "user", "content": [ {"type": "text", "text": "What is depicted in the image or video?"}, { "type": "video_url", "video_url": {"url": "https://qianwen-res.oss-cn-beijing.aliyuncs.com/Qwen2-VL/space_woaudio.mp4"}, # 程图片 base64 }, ], } ], model="google/gemma-4-E2B-it/", max_completion_tokens=640, temperature=0, ) result = chat_completion_from_base64.choices[0].message.content print(result) ``` ### Environment Python 3.12.13 torch 2.11.0+cpu sglang-cpu 0.5.12 sglang-kernel-cpu 0.4.3 torchvision 0.26.0+cpu ### fix ``` diff --- a/python/sglang/srt/models/gemma4_vision.py +++ b/python/sglang/srt/models/gemma4_vision.py @@ -173,7 +173,9 @@ class Gemma4VisionAttention(nn.Module): num_heads=self.num_heads_per_partition, num_kv_heads=self.num_kv_heads_per_partition, dropout=0.0, - flatten_batch=True, + flatten_batch=False if backend == "sdpa" else True, softmax_in_single_precision=False, softmax_scale=1.0, ) ``` ### Related resources Gemma4 run cpu fail: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/28427 Related Gemma 4 roadmap: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/26596

signals.title: [Bug] GLM-5.2-FP8 DSA fails to load: GlmMoeDsaConfig attribute_map overwrites qk_rope_head_dim + PPMissingLayer missing embedding_dim
signals.text: ### Checklist - [x] I searched related issues but found no solution. - [x] The bug persists in the latest version. - [x] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed. - [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed. ### Describe the bug When deploying **GLM-5.2-FP8 DSA** (GlmMoeDsaForCausalLM) with SGLang, two bugs prevent the model from loading: 1. **Transformers `GlmMoeDsaConfig.attribute_map` overwrites `qk_rope_head_dim`** — causes weight shape mismatch on ALL configurations (even PP1 TP=8) 2. **`PPMissingLayer` lacks `embedding_dim` attribute** — crashes on PP > 1 when the non-first stage tries to check `self.embed_tokens.embedding_dim` ### Environment - **SGLang version**: 0.5.12.post2.dev680 - **Model**: GLM-5.2-FP8 (GlmMoeDsaForCausalLM, 78 layers, 256 routed experts, FP8 block-quantized) - **Hardware**: 8× AMD MI355X (ROCm 7.2.4) - **Container image**: rocm/private:rocm7.2.4-93-torch2.9.1-aiter-g46e6c92-sgl-gc062201-20260603 - **Python**: 3.10 ### Bug 1: GlmMoeDsaConfig attribute_map overwrites qk_rope_head_dim #### Reproduction ```bash python3 -m sglang.launch_server \ --model-path /data/models/GLM-5.2-FP8 \ --tp-size 8 \ --pp-size 1 \ --trust-remote-code \ --host 0.0.0.0 --port 30000 ``` #### Error ``` AssertionError: param.shape=torch.Size([2752, 6144]) param.dtype=torch.bfloat16 loaded_weight.shape=torch.Size([2624, 6144]) loaded_weight.dtype=torch.bfloat16 ``` Also for FP8 weight scales: ``` param.shape=torch.Size([22, 48]) loaded_weight.shape=torch.Size([21, 48]) ``` #### Root cause Transformers' `GlmMoeDsaConfig` class in `transformers/models/glm_moe_dsa/configuration_glm_moe_dsa.py` has: ```python attribute_map = { "num_local_experts": "n_routed_experts", "head_dim": "qk_rope_head_dim", # BUG! } ``` The model's `config.json` contains both `head_dim: 192` and `qk_rope_head_dim: 64`. The `attribute_map` causes `head_dim` (192) to **overwrite** `qk_rope_head_dim` (64) during config initialization. This makes SGLang compute the fused QKV projection size incorrectly: - **Wrong**: `q_lora_rank + kv_lora_rank + qk_rope_head_dim = 2048 + 512 + 192 = 2752` - **Correct**: `q_lora_rank + kv_lora_rank + qk_rope_head_dim = 2048 + 512 + 64 = 2624` FP8 scale mismatch is downstream: `ceil(2752/128)=22` vs `ceil(2624/128)=21`. #### Verification ```python from transformers import AutoConfig config = AutoConfig.from_pretrained("/data/models/GLM-5.2-FP8", trust_remote_code=True) print(f"qk_rope_head_dim = {config.qk_rope_head_dim}") # Prints 192 (WRONG, should be 64) print(f"head_dim = {config.head_dim}") # Prints 192 ``` #### Suggested fix Remove the `"head_dim": "qk_rope_head_dim"` mapping from `GlmMoeDsaConfig.attribute_map`. SGLang's `model_config.py` already sets `head_dim` for MLA architectures, so this mapping is unnecessary and harmful. ```python # In transformers/models/glm_moe_dsa/configuration_glm_moe_dsa.py attribute_map = { "num_local_experts": "n_routed_experts", # "head_dim": "qk_rope_head_dim", # Removed: causes head_dim(192) to overwrite qk_rope_head_dim(64) } ``` **Note**: This bug affects ALL frameworks using transformers' `GlmMoeDsaConfig` (vLLM, SGLang, etc.), not just SGLang. ### Bug 2: PPMissingLayer lacks embedding_dim attribute #### Reproduction ```bash python3 -m sglang.launch_server \ --model-path /data/models/GLM-5.2-FP8 \ --tp-size 4 \ --pp-size 2 \ --trust-remote-code \ --host 0.0.0.0 --port 30000 ``` #### Error ``` AttributeError: 'PPMissingLayer' object has no attribute 'embedding_dim' ``` #### Root cause In `sglang/srt/models/deepseek_v2.py` around line 2290, the code checks for aiter gfx95 optimization: ```python if ... and self.embed_tokens.embedding_dim == 7168: ``` When `pp_size > 1`, the non-first pipeline stage has `self.embed_tokens` set to a `PPMissingLayer` placeholder, which doesn't have an `embedding_dim` attribute. #### Suggested fix Use `getattr` with a default value for safe attribute access: ```python # Line ~2290 if ... and getattr(self.embed_tokens, 'embedding_dim', 0) == 7168: # Line ~2322 (function call argument) getattr(self.embed_tokens, 'embedding_dim', config.hidden_size) ``` ### Test results after fixes Both bugs were fixed with runtime patches and the following tests passed: **PP1+TP8 (single node, 8 GPUs):** | Test | Result | |------|--------| | Basic chat | ✅ | | Tool calling | ✅ Correct `get_weather({"city": "Beijing"})` | | Streaming | ✅ | | Streaming + tool calling | ✅ | **PP2+TP4 (single node, 8 GPUs, 4 per PP stage):** | Test | Result | |------|--------| | Basic chat | ✅ | | Tool calling | ✅ Correct `get_weather({"city": "Beijing"})` | | Streaming | ✅ | | Streaming + tool calling | ✅ | ### Launch command ```bash SGLANG_PP_LAYER_PARTITION="39,39" python3 -m sglang.launch_server \ --model-path /data/models/GLM-5.2-FP8 \ --tp-size 4 --pp-size 2 \ --trust-remote-code \ --host 0.0.0.0 --port 30000 \ --tool-call-parser glm47 --reasoning-parser glm45 \ --mem-fraction-static 0.85 \ --watchdog-timeout 3600 ```
