signals.title: [Roadmap]Fast Engine Recovery: Weight Cache Daemon
signals.text: # [Roadmap] Fast Engine Recovery: Weight Cache Daemon @liusy58 @QiuMike @alexnails Phase 1 landed in #27139 — a per-rank daemon holds post-quantized weights and serves them over CUDA IPC; weight load drops from ~306–327s to <1s on Qwen3-235B FP8 ([blog](https://github.com/QiuMike/lm-sys.github.io/blob/sglang_fast_recovery/blog/2026-07-28-sglang-fast-recovery.md)). This issue tracks the next steps. Contributions and feedback are welcome. Related: #27052 (Fast Recovery framework), #27310 (GPU Memory Service / VMM) Goals: <10s cold restart and <1s warm standby switch; broaden model & quant coverage; make the cache outlive the daemon; make resident weights usable beyond the one GPU they sit on. Where Phase 1 stands: TP + PP, single-node and multi-node launch (each node spawns its share of ranks and joins one dist group), zero-copy IPC per GPU, unquantized + block-wise FP8. Not yet: cross-node daemon coordination / failover, DP & EP shard keying, spec-decoding draft models, weight update / sleep-wake, cache surviving daemon death. ## Model & quantization coverage - [ ] parity harness — disk-load vs daemon-load `state_dict` diff (names / shape / dtype / stride / byte hash) + short GSM8K gate; required evidence for every new allowlist entry - [ ] carry post-processing metadata in the manifest (final shape/stride, layout tag, whitelisted module attrs) instead of reproducing `process_weights_after_loading` on a meta-init model — this is what blocks most quant methods today - [ ] quant methods: per-tensor fp8 / w8a8 int8 / mxfp8 / nvfp4 / compressed-tensors / awq / gptq-marlin #32398 - [ ] archs: MoE (DeepSeek V3/V4, Ling, Kimi K3) / hybrid linear attention / multimodal (vision tower + projector) / LoRA base weights - [ ] MTP & EAGLE draft models (per-rank draft daemon), removing the `--speculative-algorithm` rejection in `server_args.py` #32744 - [ ] generic post-map rebuild hook to replace the hardcoded `_rebuild_stale_views`; make tied storages, param→buffer flips and non-persistent buffers explicit in the manifest - [ ] publish the support matrix in docs; unsupported combinations keep hard-erroring (no silent wrong numerics) ## Transport: CUDA VMM shareable handles (#27310 §4.2) - [ ] `vmm_fd` backend (skeleton already in `weight_cache/transport.py`): `cuMemCreate` + FD handles over `SCM_RIGHTS`, VA reservation on import, `torch_ipc` stays the fallback, `--weight-cache-transport {auto,torch_ipc,vmm_fd}` #33279 ## Weight update without reload - [ ] epoch handoff on stable VAs: readers unmap → writer commits → readers remap at the same VAs, so captured CUDA graphs stay valid - [ ] daemon as the weight delivery agent for trainer pushes (NCCL/RDMA); un-gate the `update_weights_*` rejections in `weight_updater.py` - [ ] colocated RL: engine itself takes the writer role, same protocol, no daemon in the loop ## Multi-instance & cross-GPU sharing - [ ] key the cache by physical GPU UUID + config fingerprint (plus optional `--weight-cache-namespace`) under a configurable runtime dir. Today the socket is `/tmp/sglang_weight_cache_rank{global_rank}.sock`, so 2× tp=4 on one 8-GPU node collide and rank 0 of the second instance attaches to the GPU 0 daemon - [ ] discovery: replace static socket paths with a lightweight registry (file-based dir, optionally etcd) so an engine rank selects a daemon by `CacheConfig` match rather than by process rank, and locates daemons across nodes without a manual `--weight-cache-socket` - [ ] `--weight-cache-peer-copy` — when no daemon holds the shard on the local GPU, `cudaMemcpyPeerAsync` it from a peer-GPU daemon (NVLink-domain check, chunked on a low-priority stream, bandwidth cap so a serving neighbour is not disturbed). 1× memory per instance, sub-second over NVLink vs ~300s from disk - [ ] preference order local zero-copy > peer copy > disk, reported per rank - [ ] fleet fill: a daemon fills itself from a peer daemon instead of disk (P2P on-node, NCCL/RDMA cross-node), so a fleet cold start pays one disk read per shard group — the real bottleneck for 1T+ models on shared FS; align with the checkpoint-engine broadcast path - [ ] out of scope for now: resharding across TP/EP topologies (tp=4 daemon → tp=8 engine) ## Multi-node, DP & EP - [ ] primary–secondary daemon coordination for multi-node TP (e.g. TP=16 = 2 nodes × 8 GPUs): primary orchestrates daemon startup, cross-node NCCL process-group formation and readiness signalling; secondaries load their local shards in parallel and serve IPC handles to engines on their own node. Basic multi-node launch already works via `--nnodes/--node-rank/--dist-init-method`; what is missing is the cluster state machine - [ ] cross-node daemon lifecycle: primary tracks which secondaries are alive, triggers coordinated restarts, signals engines on a dead secondary's node to fall back to disk; promote a secondary when the primary dies - [ ] DP support: every DP rank on a GPU maps the same daemon's handles, so a model is read from disk and quantized exactly once per GPU regardless of DP degree (today each DP rank disk-loads independently). This is about supporting SGLang's DP deployment model, not cross-GPU sharing - [ ] EP support: expert shards differ per EP rank, so cache and key them by `ep_rank`; handle partial expert loading when a rank owns a subset of experts - [ ] `CacheConfig`: add `ep_rank`, `dp_rank` and `node_rank` for correct shard identification under EP and multi-node (`dp_size`/`ep_size` are already there) ## Ops & reliability - [ ] `daemon status` command + Prometheus metrics (resident bytes, attached clients, load time, hit / mismatch / fallback), and an engine endpoint reporting how each rank got its weights - [ ] runtime dir with owner-only permissions + `SO_PEERCRED` check before handing out handles (no world-writable `/tmp` sockets) - [ ] `protocol_version` in the handshake with a documented skew policy (the env stamp already covers torch / arch skew) - [ ] `--weight-cache-max-bytes`, refcount-aware eviction, admission check against `gpu_memory_utilization` - [ ] systemd unit + k8s DaemonSet recipes; document container requirements for cross-container IPC - [ ] CI: CPU unit tests, 1-GPU daemon→client restart e2e with accuracy, 2-GPU TP e2e, nightly multi-node, restart-latency regression gate - [ ] docs page: three modes, support matrix, ops runbook, failure semantics - [ ] reclaim on daemon restart (Phase 6): the daemon holds no heavy logic and is robust by construction, but if it exits for an external reason its clients still hold the GPU memory alive through IPC refcounts — a restarted daemon should re-adopt that memory from a live client's references instead of reloading from disk ## Rest of the startup path - [ ] Phase 2 — CUDA graph serialization: persist captured graphs to shared memory or disk and replay instead of recapturing; needs pool-offset translation for address relocation, which is why it depends on the stable VAs above. ~34.9s (~9% of startup) → <3s - [ ] Phase 3 — kernel warmup: persist DeepGEMM JIT-compiled kernels across restarts, parallelize warmup across batch sizes. ~23.1s → <2s - [ ] Phase 4 — server & distributed init: lazy tokenizer init, config caching, NCCL session reuse. ~22s → <5s - [ ] KV cache alloc + warmup ~3.9s → <1.5s (KV reuse, skip warmup requests on restart) - [ ] standby orchestration: health / promotion, request draining and KV handoff, scheduler-level pause/resume for priority co-serving ## Open questions - [ ] manifest schema + versioning: SGLang-owned, stored by the memory owner as an opaque blob — what compatibility window across SGLang versions? - [ ] backend selection UX: server arg, TMS-side registration, or both? - [ ] peer copy: automatic whenever a peer daemon exists, or always explicit opt-in? default bandwidth cap next to a serving instance? ## KV Restore?

signals.title: [Bug] Cancelling the tail request in a chunked-prefill batch still leaks one visible token and leaves negative scheduler output ids
signals.text: ### Checklist - [x] I searched related issues but found no solution. - [ ] The bug persists in the latest version. - [x] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback. - [x] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed. - [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed. ### Describe the bug In a frontend-legal three-request chunked-prefill workload, cancelling the tail request does not stop it cleanly. On the verified setup: - all caller `input_ids` stay in range - the third request is cancelled after the shared batch has already entered the chunked-prefill path - the cancelled request still emits one visible token before finishing with `abort` - later scheduler steps still contain negative `output_ids` such as `[-1, -2, -3]` So this is not a direct invalid-token crash. It looks like overlap / chunked-prefill delayed-output bookkeeping is not fully cleaned up after cancel, and the stale placeholder state remains visible in later scheduler records. ### Reproduction Assume `MODEL_PATH` points to a local copy of `meta-llama/Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct`. Assume the attached reproducer script is placed in the current working directory. Run the local reproducer: ```bash python run_issue30294_chunked_prefill_cancel_poc.py \ --model-path "$MODEL_PATH" \ --gpu 0 \ --mem-fraction-static 0.3 \ --variant a \ --stagger-ms 35 \ --cancel-delay-ms 120 \ --repeat 3 ``` The action sequence is: 1. submit `pressure_a` 2. sleep `35 ms` 3. submit `pressure_b` 4. sleep `35 ms` 5. submit `pressure_c` 6. sleep `120 ms` 7. cancel `pressure_c` 8. wait for the remaining requests to finish Observed result on the verified run: - the cancelled request still emits one visible token before `finish_reason.type="abort"` - `negative_schedule_output_id_steps` is large and stable - the first negative scheduler state appears in `schedule_batch_post_run` - `min_negative_schedule_output_id` reaches a large negative value instead of being cleaned up immediately This reproduced stably in the verified local run. [run_issue30294_chunked_prefill_cancel_poc.py](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/30854993/run_issue30294_chunked_prefill_cancel_poc.py) [summary.json](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/30854992/summary.json) ### Environment Repro model: `meta-llama/Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct` `python -m sglang.check_env`: ```text Python: 3.10.20 (main, Jun 11 2026, 15:17:37) [GCC 14.3.0] CUDA available: True GPU 0,1: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4090 GPU 0,1 Compute Capability: 8.9 CUDA_HOME: /usr/local/cuda NVCC: Cuda compilation tools, release 12.9, V12.9.41 CUDA Driver Version: 575.51.03 PyTorch: 2.9.1+cu129 sglang: 0.5.9 sgl_kernel: 0.3.21 flashinfer_python: 0.6.3 flashinfer_cubin: 0.6.3 flashinfer_jit_cache: Module Not Found triton: 3.5.1 transformers: 4.57.1 torchao: 0.9.0 numpy: 2.2.6 aiohttp: 3.14.1 fastapi: 0.139.0 hf_transfer: 0.1.9 huggingface_hub: 0.36.2 interegular: 0.3.3 modelscope: 1.38.1 orjson: 3.11.9 outlines: 0.1.11 packaging: 26.0 psutil: 7.2.2 pydantic: 2.13.4 python-multipart: 0.0.32 pyzmq: 27.1.0 uvicorn: 0.51.0 uvloop: 0.22.1 vllm: Module Not Found xgrammar: 0.1.27 openai: 2.6.1 tiktoken: 0.13.0 anthropic: 0.116.0 litellm: Module Not Found decord2: 3.4.0 NVIDIA Topology: GPU0 GPU1 CPU Affinity NUMA Affinity GPU NUMA ID GPU0 X NODE 96-191,288-383 1 N/A GPU1 NODE X 96-191,288-383 1 N/A Legend: X = Self SYS = Connection traversing PCIe as well as the SMP interconnect between NUMA nodes (e.g., QPI/UPI) NODE = Connection traversing PCIe as well as the interconnect between PCIe Host Bridges within a NUMA node PHB = Connection traversing PCIe as well as a PCIe Host Bridge (typically the CPU) PXB = Connection traversing multiple PCIe bridges (without traversing the PCIe Host Bridge) PIX = Connection traversing at most a single PCIe bridge NV# = Connection traversing a bonded set of # NVLinks ulimit soft: 1000000

signals.title: [NPU][Tracking] Ascend A5 MXFP8/MXFP4 Capability and Model Coverage
signals.text: ## Background The community-wide Quantization 2026 H2 Roadmap (#31783) already covers the common quantization framework, weight lifecycle, capability validation, and related infrastructure. The Ascend cross-generation adaptation architecture is defined separately in #35709: > **Standalone kernel/provider differences belong to `sgl-kernel-npu`; runtime-visible dtype/layout/metadata differences belong to SGLang `DeviceOperator`.** Therefore, this issue does not introduce another quantization or device-abstraction framework. It focuses on: > **Ascend A5 MXFP8/MXFP4 model/operator coverage and applying the cross-generation adaptation model from #35709 to MXFP-specific differences.** --- ## 1. Scope This issue mainly tracks the following A5 MXFP schemes: | Scheme | Target | | ---------- | ----------- | | MXFP8 W8A8 | Dense / MoE | | MXFP4 W4A8 | Dense / MoE | | MXFP4 W4A4 | Dense / MoE | Primary model coverage: * Qwen3 Dense / MoE * Qwen3.5 Dense / MoE * Future models should preferably reuse existing Scheme / Kernel implementations instead of introducing model-specific MXFP paths. --- ## 2. A5 MXFP Capability Matrix | Model / Layer | MXFP8 W8A8 | MXFP4 W4A8 | MXFP4 W4A4 | | ----------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------ | | **Qwen3 Dense** | ✅ Merged [#22352](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/22352) | ✅ Merged [#23650](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/23650) | ✅ Merged [#23795](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/23795) | | **Qwen3 MoE** | ✅ Merged [#30768](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/30768) | ✅ Merged [#30318](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/30318) | ✅ Merged [#30319](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/30319) | | **Qwen3.5 Dense** | 🚧 Validation [#32150](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/32150) / Offline fix [#32266](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/32266) | 🚧 Validation [#32150](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/32150) | 🚧 Validation [#32150](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/32150) | | **Qwen3.5 MoE** | 🚧 Online supported / Offline WIP [#30768](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/30768) [#32266](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/32266) | 🚧 WIP [#32601](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/32601) | 🚧 WIP [#32602](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/32602) | The Qwen3.5 dense validation PR remains open, while the offline W8A8 fix and MoE W4A8/W4A4 work are still draft/WIP. Suggested status labels: * Production * Experimental * WIP * Planned * Unsupported A merged implementation does not automatically imply production readiness. Final status should consider correctness, accuracy, performance, representative TP/EP scenarios, CI coverage, and known limitations. ### Supporting PRs | Area | PR | | --------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | MXFP8 Dense online/offline kernel reuse | [#28505](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/28505) | | ModelSlim MXFP4 packed-weight loading | [#32013](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/32013) | | Qwen3.5 A5 GemmaRMSNorm support | [#32745](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/32745) | | Portable GemmaRMSNorm API | [sgl-kernel-npu #638](https://github.com/sgl-project/sgl-kernel-npu/pull/638) | | Generic target-provider staging | [sgl-kernel-npu #734](https://github.com/sgl-project/sgl-kernel-npu/pull/734) | | Cross-generation adaptation RFC | [#35709](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/35709) | --- ## 3. MXFP Integration with Cross-Generation Device Adaptation The common quantization architecture continues to follow #31783: ```text Config → Method → Scheme → Kernel ``` #35709 defines an orthogonal device-adaptation boundary. It does **not** add another mandatory layer to every quantization path. For MXFP, generation-specific differences should be classified as follows: ```text MXFP generation difference │ ▼ Can it be hidden behind a stable standalone operator contract? │ ┌────┴────┐ │ Yes │ No ▼ ▼ sgl-kernel-npu Runtime-visible dtype/layout/ Stable Operator metadata/state difference? │ ▼ SGLang DeviceOperator ``` ### 3.1 Kernel-local differences Differences that are local to one operator should preferably be hidden by `sgl-kernel-npu`, including: * provider differences across Ascend targets; * operator-local scale/layout normalization; * local reshape/cast/preprocessing; * equivalent operator implementations with the same logical I/O contract. `sgl-kernel-npu #638` provides the first reference implementation, while #734 generalizes it into target-specific provider staging: ```text Stable Operator API │ ┌────┴─────┐ ▼ ▼ Ascend910 Ascend950 provider provider ``` The build system selects the provider; SGLang does not perform runtime provider dispatch. ### 3.2 Runtime-visible differences If an MXFP representation is visible across multiple runtime components, it should follow SGLang `DeviceOperator` from #35709. Examples may include: * scale/layout shared across multiple MoE stages; * generation-specific metadata consumed by multiple operators; * tensor representation that affects runtime buffer preparation; * operator contracts that cannot be normalized inside one standalone kernel. In these cases: ```text Quant Scheme │ ▼ SGLang DeviceOperator runtime contract │ ▼ Stable Operator API │ ▼ sgl-kernel-npu ``` `DeviceOperator` remains optional and should only appear where a runtime-visible generation contract actually exists. ### 3.3 Quantization policy remains in the quantization layer The following decisions remain in Config / Method / Scheme rather than `DeviceOperator`: * whether MXFP8/MXFP4 is enabled; * W8A8 / W4A8 / W4A4 scheme selection; * online vs offline quantization; * supported layer/model validation. `DeviceOperator` adapts **how** an already-selected quantization feature runs on the current generation; it does not decide **whether** to enable that feature. --- ## 4. H2 Work Items ### P0 — Capability Closure * [ ] Complete validation of major Qwen3 MXFP Dense / MoE paths * [ ] Complete Qwen3.5 Dense / MoE MXFP coverage * [ ] Validate major Online / ModelSlim paths * [ ] Resolve packed-weight, scale, and layout compatibility issues * [ ] Add necessary accuracy, performance, and CI coverage ### P0 — Cross-Generation Adaptation Following #35709: * [ ] Classify existing A2/A3/A5 MXFP differences by ownership * [ ] Move standalone provider/operator differences behind stable `sgl-kernel-npu` APIs * [ ] Reuse the target-provider mechanism from `sgl-kernel-npu #734` where applicable * [ ] Move only runtime-visible dtype/layout/metadata differences into SGLang `DeviceOperator` * [ ] Avoid new generation branches in Model / QuantMethod / QuantScheme code ### P1 — Follow-up Based on actual requirements and profiling results: * MXFP Attention * MXFP / INT8 Communication * Additional model coverage --- ## 5. Out of Scope This issue does not redesign: * Common Quant Framework / Weight Lifecycle → #31783 * Ascend cross-generation adaptation architecture → #35709 * Global Capability Registry → #31774 * INT8 / FP8 / FP4 KV Cache → corresponding roadmaps/issues * Unified Communication Quantization → #31783 * Future formats such as HiF4 * A new `AscendQuantOps` framework * A second quantization-specific `DeviceOperator` --- ## Success Criteria 1. Close the major A5 MXFP8/MXFP4 Dense and MoE capability gaps. 2. Allow Qwen3.5 and future models to primarily reuse existing Scheme / Kernel implementations. 3. Avoid further propagation of A2/A3/A5 differences into Model / QuantMethod / QuantScheme code. 4. Follow #35709 for all cross-generation ownership decisions. 5. Prefer `sgl-kernel-npu` stable operators for kernel-local differences. 6. Use SGLang `DeviceOperator` only for runtime-visible representation/contract differences. 7. Keep this issue as the source of truth for A5 MXFP model/format capability coverage. --- ## Related * #31783 — Quantization 2026 H2 Roadmap * **#35709 — Ascend Cross-Generation Device Adaptation** * #31774 — Capability / Compatibility Validation * #29762 — Ascend A5 MoE MXFP * #24695 — Ascend INT8 KV Cache * #29641 — Ascend FP8 KV Cache * #29913 — FP4 KV Roadmap * #20520 — Ascend TP Communication Compression * [sgl-kernel-npu #638](https://github.com/sgl-project/sgl-kernel-npu/pull/638) — Portable GemmaRMSNorm API * **[sgl-kernel-npu #734](https://github.com/sgl-project/sgl-kernel-npu/pull/734) — Generic target-specific provider staging**

signals.title: [Bug] [XPU] Qwen3.5 GDN + speculative decode: causal_conv1d_update_xpu() got an unexpected keyword argument 'intermediate_conv_window'
signals.text: ### Checklist - [x] I searched related issues but found no solution. - [x] The bug persists in the latest version. - [ ] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback. - [ ] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed. - [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed. ### Describe the bug On --device xpu, any speculative-decoding run on a hybrid GDN/linear-attention model (Qwen3.5) crashes in the target-verify path during the server's own warmup generation, before any user request. gdn_backend.py:43-48 binds the XPU kernel as-is: elif is_xpu(): from sgl_kernel import causal_conv1d_fn_xpu, causal_conv1d_update_xpu causal_conv1d_update = causal_conv1d_update_xpu but the is_target_verify branch at gdn_backend.py:539 calls it with five spec-only kwargs that the XPU op schema does not have — intermediate_conv_window, intermediate_state_indices, retrieve_next_token, retrieve_next_sibling, retrieve_parent_token. The XPU signature stops at conv_state_indices / pad_slot_id. File "python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/linear/gdn_backend.py", line 539, in forward_extend mixed_qkv_processed = causal_conv1d_update( TypeError: causal_conv1d_update_xpu() got an unexpected keyword argument 'intermediate_conv_window' The scheduler dies, and the client then reports a downstream ConnectionError (secondary noise). Non-spec decode on the same model/backend is unaffected — only TARGET_VERIFY takes this branch. The NPU and CPU bindings a few lines below (gdn_backend.py:49-60) are wired the same way and look exposed to the identical gap; unverified. Issue is induce #31250 fix. ### Reproduction With simple below steps able to reproduce issue ``` python -m sglang.benchmark.one_batch_server \ --model-path Qwen/Qwen3.5-9B --trust-remote-code \ --device xpu --tp-size 4 \ --mem-fraction-static 0.8 --disable-radix-cache --chunked-prefill-size -1 \ --max-total-tokens 8192 --max-prefill-tokens 4096 --max-running-requests 1 \ --batch-size 1 --input-len 512 --output-len 8 \ --speculative-algorithm NEXTN TypeError: causal_conv1d_update_xpu() got an unexpected keyword argument 'intermediate_conv_window' ``` Note : #34712 is required to reproduce the above error using shell command. ### Environment Intel Environment - sglang : 0.5.18.dev364+g667e18d99 torch : 2.12.0+xpu | cuda: None | hip: None | xpu: 20250302 python : 3.12.13 | Linux-6.14.0-37-generic-x86_64-with-glibc2.41 device : 8 x Intel(R) Arc(TM) Pro B60 Graphics driver : 1.14.36300+8 | mem GB: 22.7

signals.title: [Feature] Bit-exact correctness coverage for Unified Radix Cache
signals.text: ## Motivation Cache correctness is difficult to verify from model output alone. A corrupted KV block or recurrent-state checkpoint can still produce fluent text, and the resulting numerical drift can remain far below the tolerance used by accuracy and KL tests. These failures have shipped because the existing signals are approximate. Bit-exact logprob consistency turns one of these approximate signals into a correctness oracle. `kl_test_utils` evaluates the same token through prefill and decode. If both paths are batch-invariant and compute the same function, they must produce identical logprobs. Once that baseline is established, the contract for every cache-reuse path becomes: > **Any nonzero KL is a KV/state reuse bug.** This is stronger than threshold-based testing. It does not ask whether the error is large enough to matter to a benchmark. It asks whether restoring cached state is exactly equivalent to recomputing it. Bugs that previously sat below a model-specific noise floor become unambiguous regressions. Examples: - Incorrect reused state: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/34043, https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/34184, https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/29792 ## Foundation Bit-exactness depends on the model and execution path. Deterministic inference can remove batch-dependent kernel and communication behavior, but it cannot make two mathematically different algorithms identical. For example, Qwen3-Next uses different GDN kernels for prefill and decode, and retains a nonzero numerical floor. Inkling provides the combination needed for continuous gating. Its prefill and decode paths compute the same function, so under deterministic inference its prefill-versus-decode KL is exactly `0`. A shrunken checkpoint runs on one GPU. The model also contains `FULL`, `SWA`, and `MAMBA` cache components, so one test process exercises full KV, sliding-window, and recurrent-state reuse together. The resulting foundation has four layers: 1. deterministic execution makes repeated computation batch-invariant; 2. logprob consistency establishes an exact prefill/decode baseline; 3. cache tests apply that baseline to each state restoration path; 4. revert-then-red validation proves that each regression guard can detect the defect it claims to cover. Supporting work: - Inkling deterministic execution: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/33417, https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/34159 - Workflow tools: [KL consistency test skill](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/tree/main/.claude/skills/kl-consistency-test), https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/34169 - Real-weight consistency coverage: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/34168, https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/34356 - Per-commit guards: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/34607 - Calibration and follow-up validation: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/34405, https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/34653 ## Roadmap The remaining work is coverage, not a new testing method. Every feature that can save, move, or restore model state introduces a distinct correctness boundary and needs its own exact-KL test class. - [x] Base cache path - [x] Mamba `extra_buffer` - [x] Mamba `extra_buffer_lazy` - [x] HiCache multi-turn - [x] Speculative decoding - [x] MTP https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/35161 - [x] DSpark / DFlash @alphabetc1 - Support return_logprob https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/35058 - https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/35293 - [ ] Unified memory

signals.title: [Bug] NIXL/UCX prefill segfault (nixlUcxSharedThread -> cuEventQuery) is not fixed — reproduces on v0.5.17 / CUDA 13.0 / B200; #23489 and #23499 were closed without a root cause
signals.text: ## Summary The NIXL/UCX prefill segfault reported in #23489 and #23499 is **not fixed**. Both issues were closed without a root cause — #23489 same-day as "Resolved via rebase", #23499 with no linked PR or commit — and #23499 already has an unanswered 2026-07-07 comment from someone hitting it again on a different GPU/CUDA/SGLang combination. We reproduce it today on **v0.5.17 / CUDA 13.0 / B200 x86**, and we have traced it to a missing CUDA context in NIXL's UCX progress thread. Filing separately here because SGLang's `num_threads = 8` choice for prefill is what exposes every NIXL PD user to it, while decode's `0` makes decode immune. Upstream issue: https://github.com/ai-dynamo/nixl/issues/2102 ## Reproduction Production 8×B200 host, both roles co-located: - prefill: TP4/DP4 on GPUs 0-3, decode: TP4/DP4 on GPUs 4-7 - `--disaggregation-transfer-backend nixl`, `--moe-a2a-backend megamoe`, `--kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3` - `nixl` / `nixl-cu13` 1.3.2, `UCX_TLS=cuda_copy,cuda_ipc,tcp`, `UCX_MEMTYPE_CACHE=n` - image `lmsysorg/sglang:v0.5.17-cu130` **9 prefill crashes in 43 hours** of steady traffic, ~one every 4.8h, evenly spread across the clock — not tied to load, deploys, or any request shape. The decode role, on the same host with the same image, UCX env and traffic, has **never** crashed. ## Stack — identical every time ``` Fatal Python error: Segmentation fault File "<unknown>", line 0, in cuEventQuery File "<unknown>", line 0, in uct_cuda_base_iface_event_fd_arm File "<unknown>", line 0, in ucp_worker_arm File "<unknown>", line 0, in nixlUcxWorker::arm() const File "<unknown>", line 0, in nixlUcxSharedThread::run() File "<unknown>", line 0, in __clone ``` ## A debugging note that cost us time `faulthandler` dumps **every** thread, and the Python main-thread frame is different on every crash — we saw `deepseek_v4_backend.init_compression_metadata`, `mem_cache/allocator/swa.free_swa`, `forward_batch_info.init_new`, `scheduler_components/dp_attn.all_gather`, and `utils/common.broadcast_pyobj` across nine dumps of the same bug. All of those are innocent bystanders. Only the C++ frames matter, and they never change. Likewise the `Scheduler hit an exception: ... RuntimeError: [gloo] ... Connection reset by peer` tracebacks that follow are the surviving DP ranks reacting to a dead peer, not the fault. #23499's original report made the same observation. Anyone triaging a report like this should grep the dump for `nixlUcxSharedThread`, not for the scheduler frames. ## Root cause `nixlUcxSharedThread::run()` (nixl `src/plugins/ucx/ucx_backend.cpp:339`) calls `worker->arm()` without ever establishing a CUDA context on that thread. `arm()` reaches UCX's `cuda_copy` transport, which calls `cuEventQuery` and segfaults. NIXL's UCX plugin contains **no** CUDA context management at all — a repo-wide grep for `vramApplyCtx|pthrCudaCtx|cuCtxSetCurrent` hits only `src/plugins/libfabric/`, which received exactly this fix in ai-dynamo/nixl#1157. ## Why prefill only `python/sglang/srt/disaggregation/nixl/conn.py`: ```python num_threads = 8 if disaggregation_mode == DisaggregationMode.PREFILL else 0 ``` and in nixl `ucx_backend.cpp:763`, the shared progress thread is only constructed when the UCX backend receives `num_threads > 0`. So prefill gets `nixlUcxSharedThread` and decode does not, which matches our 9-vs-0 crash split exactly. ## Workaround (confirmed at the source level, running it now) ```bash export SGLANG_DISAGGREGATION_NIXL_BACKEND_PARAMS='{"num_threads":"0"}' ``` The `setdefault` in `conn.py` means an explicit value wins, and `num_threads=0` makes NIXL skip `nixlUcxThreadPoolEngine` entirely, so the crashing thread never exists. ## Asks 1. **Reopen #23499.** It was closed without a fix and its 2026-07-07 follow-up is still unanswered. 2. **Document `SGLANG_DISAGGREGATION_NIXL_BACKEND_PARAMS`** in `docs/advanced_features/pd_disaggregation.md`. It was added in #24169 but the PD docs only mention `SGLANG_DISAGGREGATION_NIXL_BACKEND`, so the only workaround for this crash is currently undiscoverable without reading `environ.py`. 3. **Reconsider the hardcoded `num_threads = 8` for prefill**, or at minimum make it a documented, overridable knob with a note about this failure mode, until the NIXL fix lands.

signals.title: [Bug] PrefillDelayer can enter a persistent mixed-state feedback loop and collapse prefill progress under DP Attention + chunked prefill
signals.text: ### Checklist - [x] I searched related issues / PRs and did not find one matching this exact failure mode. - [x] The issue is reproducible across repeated runs with the same server/client configuration. - [x] Requests complete successfully; this is primarily a scheduler / performance-stability issue rather than a model-correctness failure. - [x] I compared the behavior against `PrefillDelayer` disabled and inspected the relevant scheduler / delayer source code. - [x] I collected per-DP-rank scheduler metrics and prefill-progress counters. --- ## Summary Under a long-prefill workload with: - DeepSeek-V4-Pro - TP=8 - DP=8 - DP Attention enabled - chunked prefill enabled - PrefillDelayer enabled - one 8-GPU node an identical server configuration and deterministic workload can enter two qualitatively different runtime regimes: ### Healthy synchronized state - Input throughput: ~94.6–94.8k tok/s - DP ranks progress through prefill nearly in lockstep - `PrefillDelayer` converges to sustained `all / no_wait` - average running requests is ~8.5 ### Pathological LOW state - Input throughput: ~62–79k tok/s - within the first ~5 s of the formal workload, DP-rank prefill progress diverges by an integer number of effective prefill chunks - the first observed spread is typically exactly **16384 tokens**, i.e. one effective per-rank chunk - `PrefillDelayer` remains dominated by `mixed / delay` - average running requests collapses to ~0.15 - residual / under-filled prefill batches increase sharply This is not explained by persistent per-rank request-count imbalance. In one representative LOW run, the first 30 s admitted exactly the same number of sequences on all 8 DP ranks, yet rank-level prefill progress had already diverged by one full chunk within 5 s. Disabling `PrefillDelayer` does **not** recover the healthy state. Instead, the system enters a third regime with lower but more continuous concurrency: - throughput: ~48–68k tok/s - avg running requests: ~4.7–5.9 - residual batches: ~11–14% Therefore the LOW state with PrefillDelayer enabled is not equivalent to "PrefillDelayer disabled". It appears to be a distinct scheduler regime in which the delayer participates in suppressing prefill progress. The exact upstream trigger is still being localized. I am opening this issue because the observed `mixed/delay` feedback loop appears different from the already-known `all/slot_condition` starvation fixed in #29898. --- ## Environment ```text SGLang version : 0.5.14 commit : 49e384ce9d304648e9959666ecb8ce8cd98d0deb git log -1 : 49e384c [Cherry-pick to release/v0.5.14] Revert Gemma4 modelopt fp4 MoE backend change (#28347) (#29246) git describe : v0.5.14 remote : https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang.git local patches : no tracked-file modifications ``` The earlier scheduler-debug instrumentation was fully reverted before the measurements described here. The remaining untracked files were only local backup files / an empty accidental file; tracked scheduler source matched the clean release tree. Hardware / topology: ```text 1 node 8 × NVIDIA B30Z TP = 8 DP = 8 DP Attention = enabled MoE A2A backend = MegaMoE ``` Relevant server configuration: ```bash --tp 8 --dp 8 --enable-dp-attention --enable-prefill-delayer --chunked-prefill-size 131072 ``` With DP Attention, the effective per-rank prefill chunk is: ```text 131072 / 8 = 16384 tokens ``` Relevant MegaMoE cap: ```bash SGLANG_OPT_DEEPGEMM_MEGA_MOE_NUM_MAX_TOKENS_PER_RANK=16512 ``` Workload: ```text input length : 60000 output length : 1 max concurrency : 16 num prompts : 160 ignore_eos : true seed : 1 ``` The 60k prompt is therefore processed approximately as: ```text 16384 + 16384 + 16384 + remainder ``` The client workload is burst-style; no request-rate throttling or intentional staggering is used in the baseline. --- ## Reproduction behavior Representative post-reboot runs: | Run | Input TPS | Median TTFT | avg running | avg queue | residual batches | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | good | 94,634 | 9.66 s | 8.13 | 0.16 | 11.96% | | LOW | 72,923 | 12.38 s | 0.17 | 0.84 | 27.17% | | LOW | 62,379 | 13.81 s | 0.12 | 0.85 | 29.03% | | good | 94,690 | 9.65 s | 8.37 | 0.17 | 9.52% | | mid | 82,688 | 9.68 s | 5.90 | 0.29 | 12.81% | | LOW | 78,571 | 10.45 s | 0.24 | 0.84 | 28.41% | The healthy-state throughput is extremely stable (~94.6k tok/s, sub-percent variation), while LOW runs have a qualitatively different scheduler signature rather than ordinary run-to-run noise. A host reboot did not eliminate the problem. --- ## Observation 1: LOW starts as a rank-level prefill-progress divergence Using the per-rank counter: ```text sglang:realtime_tokens_total{dp_rank="...", mode="prefill_compute"} ``` I computed: ```text progress_spread(t) = max_i(prefill_tokens_i(t)) - min_i(prefill_tokens_i(t)) ``` Results: | Run | TPS | spread@5s | spread@10s | spread@15s | spread@20s | spread@30s | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | good | 94,634 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | | good | 94,690 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | | mid | 82,688 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | | LOW | 72,923 | 16k | 22k | 27k | 11k | 16k | | LOW | 62,379 | 16k | 16k | 60k | 60k | 60k | | LOW | 78,571 | 16k | 22k | 27k | 0 | 0 | The important feature is that the first LOW-state divergence is quantized at approximately: ```text 16384 tokens ``` which is exactly one effective prefill chunk. `realtime_tokens_total` is incremented from `report_prefill_stats()` after a prefill batch result is processed, so this metric represents completed/reported prefill progress. It does **not** by itself prove whether the original cause was scheduler suppression or slower GPU execution. ### Metric-cadence validation I separately validated the observable cadence of `realtime_tokens_total` using 0.2 s scrapes during a smaller N32/C16 run with the same 16k effective chunk. Across all ranks: ```text jump interval p50 = 1.397 s jump interval p95 = 1.535 s min interval = 0.401 s ``` Jump-size distribution: ```text 16384 ×112 (one full chunk) 11264 ×8 (tail chunks) 256 ×3 (small startup fragments) 32768 ×0 (no two-chunk merge observed) ``` Thus the progress-spread observation is not an artifact of multiple 16k completions being collapsed into one scrape sample in this validation run. --- ## Observation 2: persistent request-count imbalance is not required for LOW I counted per-rank `#new-seq` admissions during the first 30 s of the formal workload. | Run | r0 | r1 | r2 | r3 | r4 | r5 | r6 | r7 | range | CV | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | good | 26 | 26 | 26 | 26 | 26 | 27 | 26 | 26 | 1 | 1.4% | | good | 26 | 25 | 25 | 25 | 25 | 25 | 25 | 26 | 1 | 1.8% | | mid | 27 | 26 | 26 | 26 | 26 | 26 | 26 | 26 | 1 | 1.4% | | LOW | 18 | 18 | 18 | 18 | 18 | 18 | 18 | 18 | **0** | **0.0%** | | LOW | 18 | 18 | 18 | 18 | 17 | 17 | 18 | 18 | 1 | 2.6% | | LOW | 14 | 15 | 10 | 14 | 10 | 14 | 13 | 14 | 5 | 14.8% | The strongest case is the 72.9k TPS LOW run: ```text 18 18 18 18 18 18 18 18 ``` All eight ranks admitted exactly the same number of sequences during the first 30 s, yet prefill progress had already diverged by one 16k chunk at 5 s. Therefore persistent per-rank request-count imbalance is not a necessary condition for entering the LOW state. Sub-second request-arrival / dispatch timing skew is **not** ruled out by this measurement. Also, `#new-seq` is scheduler admission into a prefill batch, not a direct counter of the initial DataParallelController request dispatch. --- ## Observation 3: PrefillDelayer state strongly separates healthy and LOW runs From: ```text sglang:prefill_delayer_outcomes_total ``` healthy runs eventually converge to sustained: ```text input_estimation="all" output_reason="no_wait" ``` while LOW runs remain dominated by: ```text input_estimation="mixed" output_reason="delay" ``` In healthy runs, after an initial transient, `mixed/delay` can disappear for long intervals and all 8 ranks repeatedly observe an immediately releasable state. In LOW runs, `mixed/delay` remains persistent and the scheduler never establishes the same synchronized regime. I use: ```text all_no_wait / (all_no_wait + mixed_delay) ``` only as a diagnostic state index, not as a literal request-release probability, because `mixed/delay` may be counted repeatedly across multiple scheduler passes during one waiting episode. The observed behavior is best described as synchronization / phase-locking-like behavior; I am not claiming a formal oscillator model. --- ## Observation 4: LOW is not equivalent to disabling PrefillDelayer I ran a separate six-run experiment with the same 16k effective chunk but with PrefillDelayer disabled. | Run | Input TPS | avg running | residual batches | median TTFT | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:| | 1 | 67,658 | 5.65 | 11.78% | 12.62 s | | 2 | 48,536 | 4.73 | 12.01% | 15.11 s | | 3 | 53,299 | 5.26 | 11.18% | 15.43 s | | 4 | 64,174 | 5.36 | 12.24% | 13.29 s | | 5 | 55,500 | 4.69 | 14.04% | 15.70 s | | 6 | 64,715 | 5.90 | 12.02% | 13.10 s | Mean throughput: ```text 58,980 tok/s CV = 12.88% ``` The important mechanism difference is: ```text PrefillDelayer ON, healthy : avg running ≈ 8.5 PrefillDelayer ON, deep LOW: avg running ≈ 0.15 PrefillDelayer OFF : avg running ≈ 4.7–5.9 ``` Thus the ON-LOW state is not simply the delayer becoming ineffective and behaving like OFF. The delayer-enabled LOW regime suppresses running concurrency far more aggressively than the OFF regime. This OFF experiment was not interleaved with the ON runs, so I do **not** use it to estimate relative state-entry probabilities. I also do not claim six samples prove a statistically unimodal OFF distribution. The robust observation is the mechanism-signature difference above. --- ## Observation 5: staggered arrivals make the failure worse As a diagnostic experiment, I changed the formal client traffic from a burst to: ```text 2 requests/s, fixed interval ``` while keeping concurrency=16. This was intentionally stopped after the direction was clearly harmful. Representative results: ```text burst: 94,630 tok/s ramp : 53,449 tok/s burst: 64,016 tok/s ramp : LOW again ``` The ramp sends approximately one new request every 0.5 s. With DP=8 this naturally exposes only a subset of ranks to new work at a time, increasing the probability that the delayer observes a `mixed` state. This is not presented as a production benchmark because the arrival process itself changed. It is included because the behavior is consistent with the delayer being highly sensitive to cross-rank arrival phase. Related newer work such as #35191 independently discusses trickle arrivals and persistent fragmented prefills, although that PR operates on a newer optional queue-trigger path that is not enabled in this configuration. --- ## Local source comparison against later upstream fixes I compared this exact `v0.5.14` tree against several later PrefillDelayer / scheduler fixes. ### 1. #29898 — missing locally The local `PrefillDelayer` has a bounded delay in the `mixed` branch: ```python prev_delayed_count = prev_state.delayed_count if prev_state else 0 if prev_delayed_count < self._max_delay_passes - 1: ... output_reason="delay" else: ... output_reason="wait_timeout" ``` but its `all` branch can still delay indefinitely when `slot_condition` or `queue_condition` remains true: ```python if slot_condition or queue_condition: ... next_state = next_state.bump_delayed_count() return _NegotiateOutput( output_allow=False, output_reason="delay", ... ) ``` with no equivalent `max_delay_passes` bound. This confirms that the local tree predates #29898. However, I do **not** claim #29898 is the direct cause here: in the collected workload, `all/delay` was not observed; the pathological state is dominated by `mixed/delay`. Its relevance is that upstream has independently confirmed that PrefillDelayer feedback can cause prefill starvation and running-batch collapse. --- ### 2. #31835 — current reproduction hits the older negotiation placement The local `schedule_policy.py` contains two paths: ```text add_one_req_ignore_eos() -> negotiation after budget/admission checks add_one_req() -> negotiation at the beginning of the function ``` The dispatch condition is: ```python if req.sampling_params.ignore_eos and getattr(self.tree_cache, "disable", True): return self.add_one_req_ignore_eos(req) ``` This reproduction has: ```text ignore_eos = true radix cache enabled -> tree_cache.disable = false ``` so the condition is false and the workload falls through to `add_one_req()`. In the local tree, `add_one_req()` begins with: ```python if (self.prefill_delayer_single_pass is not None) and ( not self.prefill_delayer_single_pass.negotiate_should_allow_prefill( local_prefillable=True, running_batch=self.running_batch.batch_size(), max_prefill_bs=self.max_prefill_bs, max_running_requests=self.max_running_requests, waiting_queue_len=self.waiting_queue_len, ) ): return AddReqResult.OTHER ``` before later request / chunk / admission checks. Therefore, on the actual reproduction path, `local_prefillable=True` is sampled before all subsequent admission checks. The alternate `add_one_req_ignore_eos()` path samples after budget checks, so the two paths have different semantics. This is directly relevant to interpretation of `all/mixed`: `local_prefillable` is a scheduler-side estimate whose meaning depends on where it is sampled, not a direct GPU-readiness signal. That said, I do **not** currently think this semantic issue alone explains the LOW state. In the failing workload, KV/SWA pressure is very low (observed full-pool usage ~0.55%, SWA usage ~2.74%), so most post-negotiation admission checks are unlikely to fail. The placement issue is therefore real in this path but not yet demonstrated to be the active trigger. --- ### 3. #30295 — key chunked-request double-count shape is still present The local scheduler already contains an early guard: ```python if ( self.get_num_allocatable_reqs(running_bs) <= 0 and self.chunked_req is None ... ): ``` but the later waiting-queue loop still contains: ```python if len(adder.can_run_list) >= self.get_num_allocatable_reqs(running_bs): self.running_batch.batch_is_full = True ``` while `add_chunked_req(...)` adds the in-flight chunked request to `self.can_run_list`, and `get_num_allocatable_reqs()` uses: ```python min( pp_max_micro_batch_size - running_bs, req_to_token_pool.available_size(), ) ``` where the in-flight request's slot is already reflected in `available_size()`. This preserves the shape of the later double-count fixed by #30295. I do not think this alone explains the reported collapse: #30295 causes a stable one-slot loss, whereas the LOW state here collapses avg running from approximately 8.5 to approximately 0.15. It may still be an adjacent bug or amplification factor. --- ### 4. #24768 — present locally, but current configuration uses CPU/Gloo negotiation The local tree contains the NCCL/device-group option for PrefillDelayer synchronization. With the current settings: ```text disable_overlap_schedule = false SGLANG_NCCL_ALL_GATHER_IN_OVERLAP_SCHEDULER_SYNC_BATCH = false ``` PrefillDelayer uses the CPU/Gloo negotiation path. Enabling the NCCL synchronization path in this MegaMoE configuration was not stable in my environment and led to an NVLink/barrier timeout, so it is not currently usable as a workaround. If the failure is ultimately localized to scheduler/readiness coordination, this cross-DP negotiation path is one area I plan to investigate further. --- ### 5. #35191 — not directly active, but relevant to the dynamics This newer work describes a separate PrefillDelayer problem where trickle arrivals can keep the observed batching target small and sustain fragmented prefills. The optional queue-trigger feature involved there is not enabled in this workload (`queue_min_ratio` unset), so this is not a direct code-path match. It is nevertheless consistent with the observation here that staggered arrivals strongly destabilize synchronized prefill behavior. --- ## Current interpretation The strongest evidence currently supports this descriptive sequence: ```text formal workload begins ↓ DP ranks initially receive approximately balanced request counts ↓ within the first few seconds, per-rank prefill progress diverges by an integer prefill-chunk amount ↓ PrefillDelayer repeatedly observes mixed states ↓ mixed/delay persists ↓ under-filled / residual batches increase ↓ running concurrency collapses ↓ LOW throughput state becomes self-sustaining ``` One causal distinction is still unresolved: ### Hypothesis B — execution-duration divergence One or more ranks receive comparable forward work but their GPU forward takes longer: ```text same/similar forward opportunity ↓ one rank completes later ↓ prefill progress diverges ↓ Delayer subsequently observes mixed ``` ### Hypothesis C — scheduler/readiness suppression The scheduler / delayer gives some ranks fewer forward opportunities: ```text scheduler readiness / negotiation diverges ↓ Delayer suppresses some prefill admissions ↓ those ranks do less forward work ↓ prefill progress diverges ``` I am instrumenting: ```text sglang:realtime_tokens_total{dp_rank,mode="prefill_compute"} ``` together with: ```text sglang:forward_execution_seconds_total{dp_rank,category} ``` using `SGLANG_ENABLE_METRICS_DEVICE_TIMER=1`. The DeviceTimer implementation uses CUDA events plus non-blocking `end_event.query()` rather than `synchronize()`, but I am first validating that enabling the timer itself does not perturb this timing-sensitive synchronization state. The intended discriminator is **not** event timestamp ordering, because Delayer negotiation necessarily precedes forward completion in the source code. Instead, the discriminator is the per-rank relationship between: ```text Δprefill_progress and Δcompleted_forward_execution_time ``` over a short window after the first rank-level progress divergence. Roughly: ```text ΔP lower and ΔF proportionally lower → rank likely completed less forward work → supports scheduler/readiness-side cause ΔP lower but ΔF similar or higher → rank spent comparable/more GPU time for less progress → supports execution-duration-side cause ``` This follow-up work is ongoing and is not required for the observations reported above. --- ## Why I think this deserves a separate issue I could not find an upstream issue matching all of these properties together: ```text DP Attention + PrefillDelayer + chunked long-prefill workload + same deterministic configuration + healthy ~94.8k state vs persistent LOW state + LOW dominated by mixed/delay + avg running collapsing near zero + rank progress diverging by exactly one effective prefill chunk + request-count admission remaining balanced in at least one LOW reproduction ``` #29898 is the closest known failure family, but it is specifically an `all / slot_condition` liveness bug. The behavior reported here appears to be a different `mixed`-branch feedback failure mode. --- ## Questions for maintainers 1. Is a persistent `mixed/delay` loop with very low `num_running_reqs` an expected / known failure mode of PrefillDelayer? 2. Are there known cases where the cross-DP `local_prefillable` negotiation can remain phase-shifted even when request counts are balanced across DP ranks? 3. Is there a known interaction between chunked prefill, an in-flight `chunked_req`, `can_run_list`, `batch_is_full`, and PrefillDelayer state that can create a self-reinforcing mixed state? 4. Would you expect #29898 / #31835 / #30295 to materially change this workload even though the observed state is primarily `mixed/delay` rather than `all/delay`? 5. Is there a recommended way to trace the first divergence between per-rank PrefillDelayer negotiation, prefill admission, and model-forward execution without materially perturbing scheduler timing? --- ## Additional data available I retained: - per-run server logs - per-rank Prefill batch logs - `#new-seq` / `#new-token` traces - 0.2 s Prometheus cadence captures - per-rank `realtime_tokens_total` - PrefillDelayer outcome counters - queue/running-request counters - host/GPU telemetry - good-state and LOW-state profiling artifacts I can provide a reduced reproduction package or additional per-rank timelines if useful.

signals.title: [Bug] Qwen3.6/Qwen3.8 multimodal mRoPE positions are passed to a 1D fused QK RMSNorm+RoPE CUDA kernel
signals.text: ### Checklist - [x] I searched related issues but found no solution. - [x] The bug persists in the latest version. - [x] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback. - [x] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed. - [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed. ### Describe the bug ## Summary On NVIDIA CUDA, the Qwen3.5-family full-attention implementation unconditionally selects `fused_qk_gemma_rmsnorm_rope_gate` when `attn_output_gate=True`. The fused kernel accepts only one-dimensional token positions (`positions: [T]`) and loads one scalar with: ```python pos = tl.load(positions_ptr + token).to(tl.int64) ``` However, Qwen3.6-27B and Qwen3.8-27B are multimodal Qwen3.5-family checkpoints. Their image/video prefill path supplies contiguous mRoPE positions with shape `(3, T)`, representing temporal, height, and width positions. Passing contiguous `(3, T)` positions to the current kernel makes it read only the first (temporal) row. Height and width positions are not applied to their assigned rotary dimensions. This silently changes Q/K for visual tokens and can degrade image understanding and GUI coordinate grounding. The same defect is present in SGLang v0.5.16, v0.5.17, and current `main`. ## Affected checkpoints | Checkpoint | Immutable revision | Architecture/config | Affected by this bug | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `Qwen/Qwen3.6-27B` | [`6a9e13bd6fc8f0983b9b99948120bc37f49c13e9`](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3.6-27B/blob/6a9e13bd6fc8f0983b9b99948120bc37f49c13e9/config.json) | Multimodal `Qwen3_5ForConditionalGeneration`, interleaved mRoPE | Yes | | `Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B` | [`1d4bf0f2ff6012fd82039f2fa52739d0dd7c60c0`](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B/blob/1d4bf0f2ff6012fd82039f2fa52739d0dd7c60c0/config.json) | Multimodal `Qwen3_5ForConditionalGeneration`, interleaved mRoPE | Yes | | `Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B-FP8` | [`017b9c7af6b5689d5dd426a76e0bc077eb5ca20a`](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B-FP8/blob/017b9c7af6b5689d5dd426a76e0bc077eb5ca20a/config.json) | Same multimodal architecture and mRoPE config | Yes | | `Qwen/Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B` | [`207bd685a7e3696cfaff12ded7c6a7ea0f88c996`](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B/blob/207bd685a7e3696cfaff12ded7c6a7ea0f88c996/config.json) | Text-only `Qwen3_5MoeForCausalLM`, no `mrope_section` | No, not this specific bug | The affected 27B configs contain: ```json { "architectures": ["Qwen3_5ForConditionalGeneration"], "language_model_only": false, "text_config": { "attn_output_gate": true, "head_dim": 256, "partial_rotary_factor": 0.25, "rope_parameters": { "mrope_interleaved": true, "mrope_section": [11, 11, 10], "rope_theta": 10000000, "rope_type": "default" } } } ``` SGLang registers `Qwen3_5ForConditionalGeneration` through the same `qwen3_5.py` implementation that contains the fused CUDA dispatch: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/63d783bbe0955237ec41f9ddabf7235ddf04673c/python/sglang/srt/models/qwen3_5.py#L2354-L2366 ## SGLang versions reviewed | Version | Commit | | --- | --- | | v0.5.11 reference path | [`612785ffdcaf35552f1ed433a981d596ca9fe900`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/commit/612785ffdcaf35552f1ed433a981d596ca9fe900) | | v0.5.16 | [`fdebc938f7f4d16fe6b9f55dcd9a767cf0899ea1`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/commit/fdebc938f7f4d16fe6b9f55dcd9a767cf0899ea1) | | v0.5.17 | [`29481685462732237d80d86076d6563e1f658102`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/commit/29481685462732237d80d86076d6563e1f658102) | | latest `main` reviewed on 2026-08-18 | [`63d783bbe0955237ec41f9ddabf7235ddf04673c`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/commit/63d783bbe0955237ec41f9ddabf7235ddf04673c) | The kernel file has the same Git blob ID in v0.5.16, v0.5.17, and the reviewed `main`: ```text 56d442098c02fa289414fecf0958638dd7906d5b ``` ## Source-level reproduction ### 1. The multimodal processor constructs three-axis positions `QwenVLImageProcessor.compute_mrope_positions()` calls `MRotaryEmbedding.get_rope_index()`: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/63d783bbe0955237ec41f9ddabf7235ddf04673c/python/sglang/srt/multimodal/processors/qwen_vl.py#L451-L471 `ForwardBatch` documents the result as `[3, total_seq_len]` and concatenates it along dimension 1 before moving it to the model device: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/63d783bbe0955237ec41f9ddabf7235ddf04673c/python/sglang/srt/model_executor/forward_batch_info.py#L1128-L1132 https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/63d783bbe0955237ec41f9ddabf7235ddf04673c/python/sglang/srt/model_executor/forward_batch_info.py#L1212-L1253 For image/video tokens, the temporal, height, and width rows are different. For ordinary text prefill/decode they are normally equal, which is why text-only accuracy tests may not expose the bug. ### 2. The VLM passes `(3, T)` positions into the language model The Qwen3-VL wrapper replaces normal positions with `forward_batch.mrope_positions` and asserts `(3, seq_len)` for multimodal prefill: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/63d783bbe0955237ec41f9ddabf7235ddf04673c/python/sglang/srt/models/qwen3_vl.py#L1423-L1453 ### 3. CUDA dispatch has no shape or mRoPE guard Current `main` uses the fused path whenever CUDA and the attention output gate are enabled: ```python if _is_cuda and self.attn_output_gate: q, k, v, gate = self.forward_prepare_cuda_fused( positions=positions, hidden_states=hidden_states, ) ``` https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/63d783bbe0955237ec41f9ddabf7235ddf04673c/python/sglang/srt/models/qwen3_5.py#L1147-L1163 There is no check for `positions.ndim`, `MRotaryEmbedding`, `mrope_section`, or `mrope_interleaved`. ### 4. The selected kernel is strictly one-dimensional The wrapper documents `positions: [T]`, and the Triton kernel loads only `positions_ptr + token`: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/63d783bbe0955237ec41f9ddabf7235ddf04673c/python/sglang/kernels/ops/attention/fused_qk_rmsnorm_rope_gate.py#L107-L114 https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/63d783bbe0955237ec41f9ddabf7235ddf04673c/python/sglang/kernels/ops/attention/fused_qk_rmsnorm_rope_gate.py#L131-L153 The kernel receives no positions row stride, mRoPE section sizes, or interleaving metadata. For a contiguous `(3, T)` tensor, `positions_ptr + token` addresses only row 0. ## Minimal runtime assertion On an NVIDIA CUDA machine, add this temporary assertion at the beginning of `forward_prepare_cuda_fused`: ```diff def forward_prepare_cuda_fused(self, positions, hidden_states): + assert positions.ndim == 1, ( + f"1D fused RoPE received shape={tuple(positions.shape)}, " + f"stride={positions.stride()}, rotary={type(self.rotary_emb).__name__}" + ) ``` Then launch either multimodal checkpoint and send one image request: ```bash python -m sglang.launch_server \ --model-path Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B \ --host 0.0.0.0 \ --port 30000 ``` Expected result with current code: image prefill reaches the assertion with a shape equivalent to `(3, T)`. Removing the assertion silently feeds that tensor to the one-dimensional kernel. The same assertion can be reproduced with `Qwen/Qwen3.6-27B`. ## Why existing validation missed it The fused CUDA path was introduced by PR #28320: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/28320 That PR changed two production files and did not add a fused-vs-native tensor correctness test. Its reported accuracy validation used a text Qwen3.5 checkpoint and AIME26. Text positions have equal T/H/W rows, so reading only the first row is accidentally equivalent for that control case. ## Expected behavior For two-dimensional mRoPE positions, Q/K must use the configured temporal, height, and width positions according to `mrope_section` and `mrope_interleaved`, matching `MRotaryEmbedding`. The one-dimensional fused kernel must not be called with a two-dimensional tensor unless it is explicitly extended to implement the same mRoPE semantics. ## Actual behavior On NVIDIA CUDA with `attn_output_gate=True`, `(3, T)` positions are passed to a `[T]` kernel. Only temporal positions are read, so H/W rotary dimensions are incorrect during image/video prefill. ## Suggested minimal correctness fix Use the fused path only for its documented one-dimensional input contract: ```diff -if _is_cuda and self.attn_output_gate: +if _is_cuda and self.attn_output_gate and positions.ndim == 1: q, k, v, gate = self.forward_prepare_cuda_fused(...) else: q, k, v, gate = self.forward_prepare_native(...) ``` Also fail fast in the fused wrapper: ```python if positions.ndim != 1: raise ValueError( f"fused_qk_gemma_rmsnorm_rope_gate only supports [T] positions, " f"got {tuple(positions.shape)}" ) ``` This is a conservative fix. In the current mRoPE scheduler, Qwen3.6/Qwen3.8 text and decode positions may also be represented as `(3, T)` with equal rows, so this guard can reduce fusion coverage for those models. Correctness should take priority; a follow-up optimization can safely pass `positions[0]` in paths where equal rows are guaranteed without performing a synchronizing GPU comparison. The complete performance fix is to extend the fused kernel to accept `(3, T)` positions plus the row stride, `mrope_section`, and interleaving mode. ## Tests requested Please add a CUDA fused-vs-native test using identical Q/K, norm weights, and RoPE cache: | Case | Positions | Expected result | | --- | --- | --- | | Text control | `[T]` | Fused and native close within dtype tolerance | | Equal-axis control | `(3, T)`, all rows equal | Either safely reduce to row 0 or use the native path | | Real mRoPE | `(3, T)`, T/H/W differ | Must bypass the 1D kernel or match `MRotaryEmbedding` numerically | An end-to-end image grounding regression test would also be useful, but the tensor-level contract test should be sufficient to prevent this silent correctness bug from recurring. ## Scope and current evidence The source-level shape/semantic mismatch is deterministic and independently reproducible. It confirms a correctness defect in the CUDA path and confirms that Qwen3.8-27B shares the affected configuration and implementation path. I do not include a controlled end-to-end CUDA grounding A/B in this report yet. Therefore, this issue does not claim that this kernel explains every observed visual benchmark regression; it claims the narrower, directly provable bug that genuine three-axis mRoPE positions are silently processed as one-dimensional positions. ### Reproduction ``` python -m sglang.launch_server \ --model-path Qwen/Qwen3.6-27B \ --port 8000 \ --tp-size 8 \ --mem-fraction-static 0.8 \ --reasoning-parser qwen3 ``` ### Environment I use the 0.5.16+cu129 docker. ``` Python: 3.12.3 (main, Jun 19 2026, 12:46:00) [GCC 13.3.0] CUDA available: True GPU 0,1,2,3,4,5,6,7: NVIDIA H100 80GB HBM3 GPU 0,1,2,3,4,5,6,7 Compute Capability: 9.0 CUDA_HOME: /usr/local/cuda NVCC: Cuda compilation tools, release 12.9, V12.9.86 CUDA Driver Version: 535.129.03 PyTorch: 2.11.0+cu129 sglang: 0.5.16 sglang-kernel: 0.4.5+cu129 flashinfer_python: 0.6.14 flashinfer_cubin: 0.6.14 flashinfer_jit_cache: 0.6.14+cu129 triton: 3.6.0 transformers: 5.12.1 torchao: 0.17.0+cu129 numpy: 2.4.4 aiohttp: 3.14.3 signals.title: [Bug] deepseekv32/deepseekv4 tool-call parsers drop calls when the streamed output has two chunks
signals.text:
### Checklist - [x] I searched related issues but found no solution. - [x] The bug persists in the latest version. - [x] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback. - [x] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed. - [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed. ### Describe the bug Use the `deepseekv32` or `deepseekv4` parser with streaming on. ``` deepseekv32 non-streaming: 3 calls {0: search {}, 1: run_query {}, 2: get_weather {"city": -7}} deepseekv32 2-chunk stream: 1 call {2: ['', '{"city": -7}']} # 2 calls and the names are gone deepseekv4 non-streaming: 2 calls {0: get_weather {"city": 42}, 1: get_weather {"city": -7}} deepseekv4 2-chunk stream: 1 call {1: ['', '{"city": -7}']} # 1 call and the name are gone ``` The non-streaming `detect_and_parse` on the same text is correct. Thus streaming clients and non-streaming clients get different tool calls. **Expected:** each division of the same text must give the calls that `detect_and_parse` gives. ### Reproduction
reproduce_deepseek_dsml_two_chunk.py ```python #!/usr/bin/env python3 """deepseekv32 / deepseekv4 detectors: splitting the model output into just TWO streaming chunks makes earlier tool calls disappear from the stream. The split point is inside the number "-7" ("-" | "7") — a perfectly normal token boundary — so any real streamed generation can hit it. pip install "sglang[all]==0.5.17" (CPU is enough) python reproduce_deepseek_dsml_two_chunk.py # exit 1 = bug present """ import json import warnings warnings.filterwarnings("ignore") from sglang.srt.entrypoints.openai.protocol import Function, Tool from sglang.srt.function_call.function_call_parser import FunctionCallParser def tool(name): return Tool(type="function", function=Function( name=name, parameters={"type": "object", "properties": {}})) TOOLS = [tool("get_weather"), tool("search"), tool("run_query")] CASES = { # three calls; the last one has an argument whose value "-7" straddles # the chunk boundary "deepseekv32": ( '<｜DSML｜function_calls>' '<｜DSML｜invoke name="search">' '<｜DSML｜invoke name="run_query">' '<｜DSML｜invoke name="get_weather">' '<｜DSML｜parameter name="city" string="false">-7' '', 189, ), # two calls; same "-7" straddle in the second one "deepseekv4": ( '<｜DSML｜tool_calls>' '<｜DSML｜invoke name="get_weather">' '<｜DSML｜parameter name="city" string="false">42' '' '<｜DSML｜invoke name="get_weather">' '<｜DSML｜parameter name="city" string="false">-7' '', 208, ), } def stream(name, chunks): d = FunctionCallParser.ToolCallParserEnum[name]() calls = {} for chunk in list(chunks) + ["", ""]: # trailing flushes, as serving does r = d.parse_streaming_increment(chunk, TOOLS) for c in r.calls: e = calls.setdefault(c.tool_index, ["", ""]) if c.name: e[0] = c.name if c.parameters: e[1] += c.parameters return calls bad = 0 for name, (text, cut) in CASES.items(): d = FunctionCallParser.ToolCallParserEnum[name]() final = {i: [c.name, c.parameters] for i, c in enumerate(d.detect_and_parse(text, TOOLS).calls)} streamed = stream(name, [text[:cut], text[cut:]]) print(f"{name}: split {text[cut-2:cut]!r} | {text[cut:cut+2]!r}") print(f" non-streaming: {len(final)} calls {final}") print(f" 2-chunk stream: {len(streamed)} calls {streamed}") same = len(streamed) == len(final) and all( streamed.get(i, ["", ""])[0] == final[i][0] and json.loads(streamed.get(i, ["", "null"])[1] or "null") == json.loads(final[i][1] or "null") for i in final) if not same: bad += 1 print(" BUG: streaming lost tool calls vs non-streaming\n") raise SystemExit(1 if bad else 0) ```

signals.title: [RFC] Integrating Ascend MemCache as an HiCache L3 Backend
signals.text: ## 1. Summary This RFC proposes an Ascend MemCache-backed L3 storage backend for SGLang HiCache. SGLang preserves its existing hierarchy: L1 resides in NPU HBM, L2 resides in local host DRAM, and L3 is a distributed memory pool provided by MemCache. Radix Cache and HiCache Controller continue to own prefix matching, page lifetime, and tier migration. MemCache owns object metadata, cross-process addressing, and host/device data transfer. The backend implements the existing `HiCacheStorage` interface and uses `batch_exists`, `batch_get`, and `batch_set` for batched page lookup, read, and write. Its data plane uses MemFabric transport protocols and reuses pages already allocated in the HiCache host KV pool, avoiding serialization of KV tensors into Python bytes. We have validated the initial MHA/MLA path on Ascend NPU and evaluated Qwen3-32B-W8A8 for accuracy and performance. The same architecture will be extended to the cache layouts required by DeepSeek V4, hybrid Qwen3.x models, GLM-5.x, and Kimi K3. --- ## 2. Motivation Long-context and high-concurrency inference produce large KV caches. NPU HBM provides the lowest latency but limited capacity. L2 expands capacity with local host DRAM, but remains local to one instance. Once a page is evicted from L2, or when a request with the same prefix is routed to another instance, the service must recompute the prefix. This cost is particularly visible with long system prompts, multi-turn conversations, shared document prefixes, and multi-replica or Prefill/Decode deployments. Repeated prefill directly increases TTFT and consumes compute capacity that could otherwise process new tokens. HiCache already defines L1, L2, and L3 semantics, but Ascend requires an L3 backend that understands NPU/host memory, supports batched object operations, and uses Ascend transfer primitives. Ascend MemCache, built on MemFabric, provides a distributed memory pool, MetaService, object APIs, and data paths such as `device_sdma` and `host_shm`, making it suitable for HiCache L3. The integration changes only where cache pages are stored and how they are restored. It does not change the attention algorithm, Radix Cache matching, or model computation. If restored cache values are identical, it introduces no additional numerical approximation. --- ## 3. Goals - Provide an Ascend HiCache L3 backend enabled by `--hicache-storage-backend ascend_memcache`. - Reuse `HiCacheStorage` and HiCache Controller instead of creating a MemCache-specific prefix cache or scheduler. - Use batched lookup and transfer to reduce per-page RPC, Python scheduling, and unnecessary copies. - Support MHA/MLA layouts used by the current Ascend host KV pool, including `page_first_kv_split`. - Isolate TP-rank objects correctly and define a clear key extension path for DCP, PP, and cross-instance sharing. - Treat temporary MemCache or MetaService unavailability as an L3 miss so L1/L2 and normal inference continue. - Define verifiable tests for real L3 hits, accuracy, and performance. --- ## 4. Non-Goals - Replacing Mooncake, file, HF3FS, or other existing HiCache L3 backends. - Changing prefix matching or eviction semantics in Radix Cache and Unified Radix Cache. - Claiming automatic compatibility with every model architecture. A model is supported only after all required cache states can be exported and restored correctly. --- ## 5. Design ### 5.1. Architecture Overview ```text ┌──────────────────────────────── SGLang Worker ────────────────────────────────┐ │ │ │ Radix / Unified Radix Cache │ │ │ │ │ HiCache Controller │ │ │ │ │ ┌───────┴────────┐ │ │ │ │ │ │ L1 NPU HBM L2 Host KV Pool │ │ │ │ │ AscendMemcacheStore │ └───────────────────────┼───────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ │ object metadata + memory descriptors ▼ ┌───────────────────────┐ │ MemCache MetaService │ └───────────┬───────────┘ │ ┌───────────▼───────────┐ │ MemFabric Data Plane │ │ host_shm/device_sdma │ └───────────┬───────────┘ ▼ Distributed L3 Pool ``` HiCache Controller decides when to back up L2 pages to L3 and when to prefetch L3 pages for a matching prefix. `AscendMemcacheStore` translates these operations into MemCache object operations. MetaService manages object placement and node information, while MemFabric moves the data. Each TP rank creates an independent MemCache client and processes its local cache shard. Ranks share prefix semantics, but keys contain rank and parallel-configuration information so different shards cannot overwrite each other. ### 5.2. Memory Registration and Buffer Metadata HiCache L2 pages reside in the host KV pool. For memory directly accessible by the selected MemFabric protocol, `AscendMemcacheStore` submits page addresses, lengths, and buffer metadata without serializing data into Python bytes. `page_first_direct` locates a logical page in one contiguous buffer. With `page_first_kv_split`, K/V or MLA data for one logical page may live in multiple physical buffers. The backend registers every relevant buffer and describes each page with correct offsets and lengths. Registration lifetime covers asynchronous `batch_set` and `batch_get`; a page cannot be released or reused before I/O completes. Zero-copy is valid only for registered address ranges understood by MemFabric. If an address type, alignment, or object size violates protocol constraints, the backend must not pass the invalid pointer to a native API. Unsupported combinations return a clear error during initialization or initial layout validation. ### 5.3. Storage Interface `AscendMemcacheStore` implements the following HiCache L3 operations: ```text batch_exists(keys) -> test whether cache pages exist batch_set(keys, pages) -> write L2 pages into L3 batch_get(keys, pages) -> restore L3 pages into target L2 buffers ``` Control messages carry keys, object information, and memory descriptors. KV tensors travel through the MemFabric data plane. Batched operations inspect and restore multiple consecutive pages without a per-page call bottleneck. `batch_set` runs asynchronously in the HiCache backup worker. Pages remain pinned until transfer completes. `batch_get` runs in the prefetch path, and HiCache exposes tokens as hits only after complete pages have been restored successfully. ### 5.4. Cache Key and Parallelism L3 keys must distinguish models, cache formats, and parallel shards. The current key covers at least a model identifier, page or prefix hash, TP rank, and page ordinal. To prevent incompatible services from sharing objects, the schema should additionally include cache-layout version, dtype, quantization mode, TP size, DCP size/rank, and PP rank. Process-local information such as virtual addresses and PIDs cannot be part of persistent keys. Two instances may share L3 objects only when model weights, cache layout, and parallel sharding match. Until DCP-aware keys are implemented, combining L3 with `dcp_size > 1` should fail explicitly rather than silently collide. ### 5.5. Write and Restore Flow The write flow is: 1. Radix Cache identifies complete cacheable pages. 2. HiCache Controller pins the pages and enqueues backup work. 3. `AscendMemcacheStore` builds keys and memory descriptors and invokes `batch_set`. 4. MemCache stores the objects and updates metadata. 5. Page pins are released after I/O; write failure does not invalidate existing L1/L2 data. The restore flow is: 1. Radix Cache completes local L1/L2 prefix matching. 2. HiCache invokes `batch_exists` for remaining candidate pages and finds the longest continuous L3 prefix. 3. HiCache reserves destination L2 pages and invokes `batch_get`. 4. Fully restored pages return to NPU HBM through the existing L2-to-L1 path. 5. The scheduler skips only successfully restored prefix tokens; failed pages are recomputed. ### 5.6. Configuration and Deployment The backend uses existing HiCache arguments: ```bash python3 -m sglang.launch_server \ --model-path /path/to/model \ --device npu \ --attention-backend ascend \ --enable-hierarchical-cache \ --hicache-storage-backend ascend_memcache \ --hicache-ratio 2.0 \ --hicache-storage-prefetch-policy timeout \ --hicache-storage-backend-extra-config \ '{"meta_service_url":"tcp://127.0.0.1:5000", "config_store_url":"tcp://127.0.0.1:6000", "protocol":"device_sdma", "prefetch_threshold":128, "dram_size":"50GB"}' ``` MetaService starts before SGLang workers connect. The protocol is selected according to memory placement and topology, not performance expectations alone. For example, `device_sdma` requires device mappings and target memory compatible with MemFabric. A configuration-file environment variable and trace/debug controls support deployment and diagnosis. --- ## 6. Evaluation We evaluate Qwen3-32B-W8A8 with TP2 and `page_first_kv_split` on Ascend NPU. ### 6.1. Accuracy The accuracy experiment uses 200 GSM8K samples: | Configuration | Accuracy | Invalid rate | Total time | Output throughput | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | | HiCache disabled | 0.835 | 0.000 | 606.545 s | 98.032 token/s | | MemCache L3 enabled | 0.825 | 0.000 | 582.603 s | 101.762 token/s | Both runs have an invalid rate of zero, and we observe no systematic output error caused by L3 data movement. The dataset-score difference requires more samples and token-by-token equality tests; one GSM8K run alone does not establish complete equivalence. ### 6.2. Prefix-Reuse Performance The performance experiment uses an average input length of approximately 3.5K tokens and a fixed output length of 100 tokens: | Configuration | Average E2EL | Average TTFT | Average TPOT | Average per-request output rate | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | | HiCache disabled | 18011.7 ms | 6120.7 ms | 120.1 ms | 5.734 token/s | | MemCache L3 enabled | 12826.0 ms | 3601.4 ms | 93.2 ms | 8.179 token/s | | Change | -28.8% | -41.2% | -22.4% | +42.6% | For requests reusing a sufficiently long cached prefix, restore can cost less than recomputing prefill. Actual gains depend on a real L3 hit, hit length, transfer bandwidth, concurrency, and background-backup overhead. --- ## 7. Future Work ### 7.1. Model Support We will extend support to the following model families: - **DeepSeek V4 family:** support its MLA/DSA cache layouts, including L3 persistence and restore of sparse-attention metadata and speculative-decoding auxiliary states. - **Qwen3.x family:** cover regular MHA/GQA models and hybrid models containing Mamba/SSM or linear-attention states. - **GLM-5.x family:** support MLA/DSA, `page_first_kv_split`, and auxiliary states produced by NEXTN and other speculative-decoding methods. - **Kimi K3:** add L3 write and restore for the cache states required by its actual attention and cache layout in SGLang. Each model family must pass baseline-output validation, a real L3 hit after L1/L2 eviction, and token-by-token greedy-decoding equality. A model is marked supported only when every cache state required for inference can be stored and restored correctly. ### 7.2. PP and DCP Parallelism Support The current cache key and page management primarily target TP. Future work will support Pipeline Parallelism (PP) and Decode Context Parallelism (DCP). PP support will add the pipeline rank or equivalent layer-ownership information to L3 keys. Each stage will write and restore only its locally owned cache layers, and objects belonging to the same prefix but different PP stages will remain isolated. DCP support will add `dcp_size` and `dcp_rank` to keys and persist pages by DCP shard. Lookup and restore must preserve shard consistency. Until this support is complete, combining L3 with `dcp_size > 1` should fail explicitly at startup to prevent different DCP ranks from reading or writing the same object. PP and DCP qualification will cover each strategy independently and in combination with TP. Tests will verify consistent L3 hit-page counts across ranks, correct restored cache content, and model output equal to the HiCache-disabled baseline.
