signals.title: [Feature] [RFC] Same-GPU model replicas with managed CUDA MPS and a shared KV pool
signals.text: ## Summary This issue proposes an experimental SGLang mode for running multiple homogeneous replicas of a small or medium language model on one NVIDIA GPU. The initial target is two replicas of `Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B`. The mode combines: 1. native data-parallel request routing; 2. optional SGLang-managed CUDA Multi-Process Service (MPS); 3. one daemon-owned CUDA allocation for model weights, when weight-cache mode is enabled; and 4. one global HBM KV pool shared by every colocated scheduler. `DataParallelController` is the authority for shared KV metadata. A minimal CUDA helper process owns the physical KV slab and exports CUDA-IPC handles. Schedulers map the slab and write only pages leased to them. This is an RFC and performance hypothesis, not a claim that MPS always improves throughput. ## Motivation Small models can leave GPU execution resources underutilized because serving also contains CPU tokenization, scheduling, serialization, launch gaps, and small or irregular batches. Multiple scheduler processes may fill some of those gaps under CUDA MPS. Today, however, colocating independent replicas duplicates the resources that matter most: - model weights; - KV pools; - prefix-cache contents; - CUDA graphs and workspaces; and - unused capacity stranded inside each process-local allocator. MPS alone only multiplexes execution. It does not combine CUDA allocations, allocator state, or prefix metadata. A prefix computed by replica 0 is still a miss on replica 1. For a memory-constrained GPU, process-local KV pools also create a packing problem. One replica can retract or reject work while another replica has free pages that it cannot lend. ## Potential benefits The proposal is intended to test the following benefits. ### 1. Eliminate duplicate prefix KV across replicas Identical prefixes would resolve to the same physical KV pages regardless of which DP rank receives the next request. System prompts, shared document contexts, few-shot examples, and repeated conversation prefixes would consume one set of pages instead of one copy per replica. ### 2. Pool capacity globally All schedulers allocate from one global page budget. Bursty traffic can use currently free pages without pre-partitioning HBM equally between replicas. This should reduce stranded capacity and avoid cases where one rank retracts requests while another rank's private pool is idle. ### 3. Increase effective context or concurrency on GPUs The approximate private-replica memory shape is: ```text replicas * weights + replicas * KV reservation + replicas * graph/workspace memory ``` With shared immutable weights and a shared KV pool, it becomes: ```text one weight allocation + one global KV reservation + replicas * graph/workspace memory + shared-control metadata ``` This does not remove per-process graph and activation overhead, but it can leave substantially more of VRAM available for useful KV. ### 4. Preserve prefix locality without sticky routing Round-robin or load-aware routing would no longer destroy prefix reuse merely because related requests reach different ranks. Sticky routing may still be valuable for active sessions and CPU locality, but it would not be required to reuse published KV pages. ### 5. Improve utilization for underfilled workloads CUDA MPS may overlap otherwise-idle execution from multiple small-model schedulers. This is most plausible for CPU-gapped, bursty, prefill-heavy, or small-batch workloads. ### 6. Reduce retraction and improve burst absorption A global allocator can admit a request using any free page in the pool. Compared with fixed per-rank pools, this can reduce decode retraction caused by temporary imbalance. ### 7. Keep one endpoint and native request ownership The existing DP controller remains the frontend. A request is dispatched once and stays with one scheduler through prefill, decode, streaming, abort, and completion. Operators do not need to run and route between separate HTTP servers. ### 8. Create a foundation for broader replica packing If the ownership and recovery protocol proves reliable, later work could support larger Qwen models, more replicas, multiple GPUs with per-GPU pools, and cache-aware admission policies. ## Why these benefits are hypotheses There are meaningful costs: - allocator and radix-directory RPCs enter the scheduling path; - multiple decode processes can contend for the same SMs and memory bandwidth; - per-process CUDA graphs and activations remain duplicated; - global metadata can become a controller bottleneck; - cross-process synchronization adds latency; and - long concurrent decodes may worsen inter-token latency even if aggregate throughput improves. The feature should not be promoted based only on reduced HBM. It needs measured throughput, TTFT, ITL, tail latency, hit rate, and failure behavior. ## Current SGLang behavior The checked-in implementation currently has these boundaries: - `DataParallelController.launch_dp_schedulers()` advances each replica by `tp_size * pp_size * gpu_id_step`. - `ServerArgs.check_server_args()` requires `gpu_id_step >= 1`. - `build_kv_cache()` constructs a request pool, token-to-KV allocator, device KV pool, and radix tree inside each scheduler process. - `PagedTokenToKVPoolAllocator` owns a process-local free-page tensor. - `RadixCache` owns process-local tree nodes, lock references, LRU state, and physical KV indices. - CUDA MPS is not started, stopped, or verified by SGLang. - Existing CUDA-IPC weight-cache support can map one immutable daemon-owned model allocation into multiple engine processes. - Existing multimodal CUDA-IPC transport demonstrates pooled allocation, process mapping, generations, and stream-ordered ready/ack words, but it is a transport pool rather than a serving KV allocator. Therefore, making a tensor visible through CUDA IPC is not the main missing piece. The missing subsystem is authoritative cross-process allocation, publication, reference counting, eviction, synchronization, and recovery. ## Proposed user experience The initial experimental command would be: ```bash python -m sglang.launch_server \ --model-path Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B \ --same-gpu-replicas 2 \ --enable-shared-kv-pool \ --shared-kv-max-total-tokens 4096 \ --cuda-mps-mode managed \ --max-running-requests 8 ``` Proposed arguments ( Just a suggestion) : | Argument | Meaning | |---|---| | `--enable-shared-kv-pool` | Enable the experimental controller-owned shared allocator and prefix directory. | | `--shared-kv-max-total-tokens` | Global capacity across all colocated replicas, after page alignment. | | `--cuda-mps-mode off` | Do not use or manage MPS; ordinary CUDA time-slicing remains valid. | | `--cuda-mps-mode external` | Require and verify an operator-managed MPS daemon. | | `--cuda-mps-mode managed` | Start a private MPS daemon before any SGLang CUDA process and stop only that daemon at shutdown. | `--max-total-tokens` retains its existing per-scheduler meaning when shared KV is disabled. Shared mode uses a separate global argument to avoid silently changing an existing option's semantics. ## Initial support boundary The first draft PR intentionally supports only: - NVIDIA CUDA on native Linux; - one physical GPU; - `Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B`; - two homogeneous native-DP replicas; - TP1 and PP1; - standard dense Qwen3 MHA/GQA KV layout; - page size 1; - one tokenizer/model configuration; - greedy and ordinary sampling generation; - streaming and non-streaming requests; and - optional existing CUDA-IPC shared weights. It does not support: - heterogeneous models or revisions; - more than one GPU; - tensor or pipeline parallelism; - DP attention; - speculative decoding; - sliding-window attention; - Mamba or other recurrent state caches; - multimodal models; - HiCache or LMCache integration; - disaggregation; - elastic scaling; - online weight mutation; - memory release/resume; or - controller recovery without restarting the endpoint. Unsupported combinations must fail before a CUDA process launches. ##MPS test plan 1. one Qwen3-0.6B replica; 2. two same-GPU replicas with private KV and no MPS; 3. two replicas with private KV and managed MPS; 4. two replicas with shared KV and managed MPS; ## Acceptance criteria The experiment is successful when: 1. both schedulers map one physical KV allocation; 2. page ownership prevents concurrent writes; 3. rank 1 reuses a prefix written by rank 0 without recomputation; 4. active decode uses globally allocated pages; 5. no stale generation can be read after page reuse; 6. global eviction never frees reserved or referenced pages; 7. scheduler death reclaims only unsafe/uncommitted state; 8. controller, memory-server, and MPS failures stop the endpoint safely; 9. single-replica output parity holds; 10. the 12 GB host completes sustained concurrent generation without corruption or OOM; and 11. measured results identify whether HBM savings and MPS concurrency justify the controller-RPC overhead. ## Requested maintainer feedback 1. Is `DataParallelController` the right authority for global KV metadata, or should the CUDA memory server own metadata too? 2. Should managed MPS be part of SGLang, or should the first version support only external verification? 3. Is a separate `--shared-kv-max-total-tokens` clearer than changing `--max-total-tokens` semantics? 4. Is page-size-1 Qwen3-0.6B narrow enough for an initial experimental draft? 5. Should the first mergeable version be reduced to immutable published prefixes while retaining the full mutable-pool work in a follow-up?

Otherwise, it will be closed. - [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed. ### Describe the bug ## [Bug] Gemma-4-31B-it TP=8 hangs in the vision path on AMD/ROCm When running Gemma-4-31B-it with TP=8 and hybrid SWA enabled on AMD/ROCm, all TP ranks initialize and load the model successfully, but the server never becomes healthy. ### Observed behavior - TP0–TP7 complete distributed initialization. - Model weights and KV cache are loaded successfully. - `/model_info` returns HTTP 200. - `/health` continuously returns HTTP 503. - After several minutes, scheduler watchdog timeouts occur. The watchdog stack traces show multiple TP ranks blocked in: ```text rocr::core::BusyWaitSignal::WaitRelaxed resolve_precomputed_max_seqlen (vision.py:237) get_image_feature (gemma4_mm.py:443) general_mm_embed_routine (mm_utils.py:1260) run_scheduler_process (scheduler.py:4639) ``` TP0 also shows: ```text set_full_to_swa_mapping (allocator/swa.py:345) ``` The server eventually receives SIGQUIT and is killed. ### Configuration - Model: Gemma-4-31B-it - TP/PP/EP: 8/1/1 - AMD GPU server with 8 GPUs An earlier run with only `HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0` failed with `invalid device ordinal`. After exposing all eight GPUs, that error disappeared, but the TP=8 run still hung in the vision/SWA execution path and failed readiness. ### Expected behavior The server should complete startup and `/health` should return HTTP 200. ### Questions 1. Is TP=8 supported for Gemma 4 hybrid models on AMD/ROCm? 2. Is the hang in `gemma4_mm.py` / `vision.py` a known issue? 3. Could hybrid SWA allocation or TP=8 synchronization cause this ROCr wait? 4. signals.title: [Feature] Support Custom OTLP Trace Service Name
signals.text: ### Checklist - [x] If this is not a feature request but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed. - [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed. ### Motivation ## Summary Currently, SGLang hardcodes the OpenTelemetry trace service name as `"sglang"` in all components. This makes it difficult to distinguish between multiple SGLang instances in distributed tracing systems (Jaeger, Tempo, etc.) when running multiple servers for different purposes (staging, production, different models, etc.). Request: Add support for customizing the OTLP trace service name via CLI parameter and/or environment variable. ## Current Behavior When `--enable-trace` is set, all traces report with `service.name = "sglang"`: ```bash python -m sglang.launch_server \ --model-path Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B-FP8 \ --enable-trace \ --otlp-traces-endpoint localhost:4317 ``` **Result in OTLP collector:** - All spans show `service.name: "sglang"` - Cannot distinguish between multiple SGLang instances - Environment variable `OTEL_SERVICE_NAME` is ignored ### Related resources ## Proposed Changes ### 1. Add CLI parameter in `server_args.py` ```python otlp_service_name: A[ str, "Service name for OTLP traces (displayed as 'service.name' in trace backends). Defaults to 'sglang'.", NS("observability"), ] = "sglang" ``` ### 2. Update all `process_tracing_init` calls Replace `"sglang"` with `server_args.otlp_service_name` in: - `http_server.py` - `scheduler.py` - `engine.py` - `encode_server.py` - `data_parallel_controller.py` ### 3. (Optional) Support `OTEL_SERVICE_NAME` fallback In `trace.py`, only set `SERVICE_NAME` if `server_name` is provided: ```python attributes = {} if server_name: attributes[SERVICE_NAME] = server_name # If not provided, OTEL_SERVICE_NAME env var will be used by OpenTelemetry SDK resource = Resource.create(attributes=attributes) ``` Or read the env var explicitly: ```python import os service_name = server_name or os.getenv("OTEL_SERVICE_NAME", "sglang") resource = Resource.create(attributes={SERVICE_NAME: service_name}) ```

signals.title: [Bug] Anthropic endpoint: tool_reference parts in tool_result break chat templates without deferred-reference support (HTTP 500)
signals.text: ## Describe the bug The Anthropic-compatible endpoint (`/v1/messages`) converts `tool_reference` blocks found inside `tool_result` content into structured parts `{"type": "tool_reference", "name": ...}` (deferred tool loading, #22702). That part type is only understood by chat templates that implement deferred-reference expansion (GLM family). For any other model, the template hits the unknown item type and the whole request fails with HTTP 500: ``` jinja2.exceptions.TemplateError: Unexpected item type in content. ... [ts] Anthropic error response api_error (exception=ValueError): Internal server error ``` With Claude Code this is especially disruptive: once a session uses deferred tool loading (ToolSearch) and a `tool_reference` block enters the conversation history, **every subsequent request in that session fails** — the history carries the block forward, so retries cannot recover and only clearing/compacting the context fixes it. We observed ~26 consecutive 500s on a single session until it was abandoned. ## Reproduction Server: SGLang 0.5.17 (same code on `main`), any model whose chat template does not handle `tool_reference` (reproduced with the stock Qwen3.8-27B template): ```bash curl -s http://127.0.0.1:30000/v1/messages \ -H 'content-type: application/json' -H 'x-api-key: dummy' -d '{ "model": "qwen3.8-27b", "max_tokens": 16, "stream": false, "tools": [{"name": "DemoTool", "description": "demo", "input_schema": {"type": "object", "properties": {}}}], "messages": [ {"role": "user", "content": "list the deferred tools"}, {"role": "assistant", "content": [ {"type": "tool_use", "id": "toolu_1", "name": "ToolSearch", "input": {"query": "select:Foo"}} ]}, {"role": "user", "content": [ {"type": "tool_result", "tool_use_id": "toolu_1", "content": [ {"type": "text", "text": "Found 1 tool:"}, {"type": "tool_reference", "tool_name": "DemoTool"} ]} ]}, {"role": "user", "content": "now use it"} ] }' ``` Actual: `HTTP 500 {"type":"error","error":{"type":"api_error","message":"Internal server error"}}` with `TemplateError: Unexpected item type in content` in the server log. Same request with the `tool_reference` item removed: `HTTP 200`. (A `thinking` block in assistant history does not trigger this; the minimal trigger is the `tool_reference` item in a `tool_result` content list.) ## Root cause `python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/anthropic/serving.py`, `_convert_to_chat_completion_request` → `_convert_tool_result_content`: ```python elif item_type == "tool_reference": ref_name = item.get("tool_name") or item.get("name") if ref_name: tool_content_parts.append( {"type": "tool_reference", "name": ref_name} ) ``` The structured part is emitted unconditionally. Templates without deferred-reference expansion (e.g. Qwen's `render_content` macro, which only accepts `text`/`image`/`video` items) raise `TemplateError`, which is surfaced as a 500. Suggested fix: detect whether the loaded chat template handles `tool_reference` (e.g. substring check on the template source, mirroring how the unit tests fake `tokenizer_manager.tokenizer.chat_template`) and, when it does not, degrade the reference to a text part such as `[tool reference: <name>]` so history echoes keep working for all models while GLM behavior is preserved. A PR implementing this is coming. ## Environment ``` Python: 3.12.12 | packaged by conda-forge CUDA available: True GPU: 8x NVIDIA H100 80GB HBM3 (CC 9.0), Driver 580.95.05, CUDA 12.9 PyTorch: 2.11.0+cu130 sglang: 0.5.17 sglang-kernel: 0.4.5 flashinfer_python: 0.6.15.post1 triton: 3.6.0 transformers: 5.12.1 numpy: 2.3.5 fastapi: 0.141.1 pydantic: 2.14.0b1 anthropic: 0.125.0 ``` Full `python3 -m sglang.check_env` output: ``` Python: 3.12.12 | packaged by conda-forge | (main, Oct 22 2025, 23:25:55) [GCC 14.3.0] CUDA available: True GPU 0,1,2,3,4,5,6,7: NVIDIA H100 80GB HBM3 GPU signals.title: [Bug] `sharded_state` cannot save and load an MLA model
signals.text: ### Checklist - [x] I searched related issues but found no solution. - [x] The bug persists in the latest version. - [x] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback. - [ ] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed. - [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed. ### Describe the bug This issue is the same as the closed #25332 for which pr #25373 exists but did not get much attention. Saving a `sharded_state` checkpoint of a DeepSeek-V2-style (MLA) model **after any forward has run** writes the `kv_b_proj` weight under `self_attn.attn_mha.kv_b_proj.weight` and never under `self_attn.kv_b_proj.weight`. A freshly constructed model has no such key, so loading that checkpoint back with `load_format="sharded_state"` dies during model init: ``` File "python/sglang/srt/model_loader/loader.py", line 1796, in load_model param_data = state_dict[key].data ~~~~~~~~~~^^^^^ KeyError: 'model.layers.22.self_attn.attn_mha.kv_b_proj.weight' ``` ### Reproduction Reproduced on a single GPU with `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V2-Lite`, TP=1, PP=1. ### Repro ```python """ usage: python3 mla_sharded_state_repro.py save /path/to/DeepSeek-V2-Lite /path/to/out [--skip-forward] python3 mla_sharded_state_repro.py load /path/to/out """ import os import shutil import sys from sglang import Engine def main(): if sys.argv[1] == "save": model_path, out_dir = sys.argv[2], sys.argv[3] os.makedirs(out_dir, exist_ok=True) llm = Engine( model_path=model_path, trust_remote_code=True, attention_backend="triton", disable_cuda_graph=True, ) if "--skip-forward" not in sys.argv: llm.generate("hi", {"max_new_tokens": 1}) llm.save_sharded_model(path=out_dir, pattern=None, max_size=5 * 1024**3) llm.shutdown() for name in os.listdir(model_path): if os.path.splitext(name)[1] not in (".bin", ".pt", ".safetensors"): shutil.copy(f"{model_path}/{name}", f"{out_dir}/{name}") else: # load llm = Engine( model_path=sys.argv[2], load_format="sharded_state", trust_remote_code=True, attention_backend="triton", ) print(llm.generate("hi", {"max_new_tokens": 1})) llm.shutdown() print("=== loaded fine ===") if __name__ == "__main__": main() ``` Run: ``` python3 signals.title: [RFC][NPU] Ascend Cross-Generation Device Adaptation
signals.text: ## Summary As Ascend A5 support is being added to SGLang, generation differences are no longer limited to kernel availability. They increasingly affect operator providers, signatures, tensor dtypes/layouts, KV representations, and quantization metadata. If these differences continue to be handled directly in Attention, MoE, Quantization, Model, and Memory components: ```python if is_a5(): ... else: ... ``` generation-specific logic will keep leaking into feature code. This RFC proposes a two-layer adaptation model: ```text Model / Attention / MoE / Quant / Memory │ ▼ SGLang DeviceOperator runtime-visible device contract │ ▼ sgl-kernel-npu Stable Operator │ ▼ target-specific provider Ascend910 / Ascend950 │ ▼ torch_npu / ACLNN / AscendC / Triton ``` The core rule is: > Hardware differences that can be fully hidden behind a stable standalone operator contract should be handled in `sgl-kernel-npu`. Differences that change SGLang runtime-visible dtype, layout, metadata, or cross-operator state should be handled by SGLang `DeviceOperator`. --- ## Motivation Current A5 support already exposes two fundamentally different kinds of generation differences. ### Kernel-local differences For example, Gemma RMSNorm uses different implementations across generations: ```text A2/A3: torch_npu.npu_gemma_rms_norm A5: torch_npu.npu_rms_norm(input, 1 + weight) ``` However, both can expose the same semantic API: ```python npu_gemma_rms_norm(input, weight, eps) ``` `sgl-kernel-npu`[#638](https://github.com/sgl-project/sgl-kernel-npu/pull/638) demonstrates this model: provider selection happens while building a target-specific wheel, while SGLang only consumes a stable operator API and does not select providers at runtime. ### Runtime-visible differences Other generation differences cannot be hidden inside a standalone operator. For example, an A5 KV/attention path may change: ```text INT8 KV -> FP8 KV scale format -> different metadata representation KV layout -> packed representation attention API -> different operator contract ``` These differences affect Memory Pool, Attention, and possibly other runtime components before a kernel is invoked. Therefore, we need an explicit ownership boundary between kernel implementation differences and runtime device contract differences. --- ## Goals This RFC aims to: * reduce scattered Ascend generation checks in SGLang; * keep kernel/provider differences inside `sgl-kernel-npu` whenever possible; * centralize runtime-visible generation contracts in SGLang `DeviceOperator`; * preserve existing ownership of Attention, MoE, Memory, and Quantization components; * provide a consistent extension model for future Ascend generations; * avoid introducing a large device abstraction that wraps every NPU operator. --- ## Ownership Model The default decision rule is: ```text Generation difference │ ▼ Can it be hidden behind one stable standalone operator API? │ ┌────┴────┐ │ Yes │ No ▼ ▼ sgl-kernel Does runtime require different -npu dtype/layout/metadata/state? │ ┌────┴────┐ │ Yes │ No ▼ ▼ SGLang Feature / DeviceOp capability ``` Typical ownership: | Difference | Owner | | ------------------------------------------------------------ | ----------------------- | | torch_npu / ACLNN / AscendC / Triton provider difference | `sgl-kernel-npu` | | Same semantic operator with different kernel implementations | `sgl-kernel-npu` | | Operator-local reshape/cast | `sgl-kernel-npu` | | Runtime KV dtype/layout | SGLang `DeviceOperator` | | Runtime metadata contract | SGLang `DeviceOperator` | | Representation shared across multiple operators | SGLang `DeviceOperator` | | Enable MXFP4 / FP8 KV | Feature / Config | | KV allocation and lifetime | Memory Pool | | DSA/MLA or TP/EP policy | Feature | An operator signature difference alone does **not** require SGLang `DeviceOperator`. If the difference can be cleanly normalized behind a stable standalone API, it should remain in `sgl-kernel-npu`. --- ## sgl-kernel-npu: Stable Operator + Target Provider We do not propose another large abstraction such as: ```python class BaseDeviceOps: ... class A5DeviceOps(BaseDeviceOps): ... ``` inside `sgl-kernel-npu`. Instead, the kernel layer follows: > **Stable Operator Contract + Target-specific Provider** For example: ```text npu_gemma_rms_norm() │ ┌────────┴────────┐ ▼ ▼ Ascend910 provider Ascend950 provider native ACLNN ``` SGLang only depends on: ```python npu_gemma_rms_norm(...) ``` and does not need to know which provider is used. A stable operator should remain standalone: ```text Tensor / scalar / attributes │ ▼ Stable Operator │ ▼ Tensor / outputs ``` It should not depend on SGLang runtime objects such as: ```text ForwardBatch MemoryPool Scheduler ModelRunner AttentionBackend ``` --- ## Target-specific Provider Staging `sgl-kernel-npu` [#734](https://github.com/sgl-project/sgl-kernel-npu/pull/734) generalizes the Gemma-specific mechanism introduced in[#638](https://github.com/sgl-project/sgl-kernel-npu/pull/638) into generic target-provider staging. Its core principle is: > **The build system knows targets, but does not know operators.** Providers are organized by target and stable module path: ```text target_providers/ ├── Ascend910/ │ └── norm/ │ └── gemma_rmsnorm.py │ └── Ascend950/ └── norm/ └── gemma_rmsnorm.py ``` During wheel build: ```text target_providers/Ascend950/norm/gemma_rmsnorm.py │ ▼ sgl_kernel_npu/ norm/ gemma_rmsnorm.py ``` The installed public API therefore remains: ```python sgl_kernel_npu.norm.gemma_rmsnorm ``` regardless of the target implementation. ### Directory as Registry There is intentionally no global operator registry such as: ```python PROVIDERS = { "norm.gemma_rmsnorm": ..., "quant.dynamic_mx": ..., } ``` Instead, the directory layout itself acts as the registration mechanism. Adding another portable operator only requires matching module paths: ```text target_providers/ ├── Ascend910/ │ └── quant/dynamic_mx.py └── Ascend950/ └── quant/dynamic_mx.py ``` The generic build framework does not need to know whether the module implements Gemma RMSNorm, MXFP, MoE, or Attention. [#734](https://github.com/sgl-project/sgl-kernel-npu/pull/734) reduces provider staging to: ```text validate target ↓ scan provider tree ↓ stage provider modules ``` No operator-specific build logic is required. --- ## Build-time, Not Runtime Dispatch Provider selection should happen while building the target-specific wheel: ```text Concrete SoC │ ▼ normalize provider target │ ├── Ascend910 └── Ascend950 │ ▼ stage provider tree │ ▼ target-specific wheel ``` The runtime does not contain: ```python if is_a5(): ... ``` or: ```python provider = registry[current_device] ``` There is also no silent runtime fallback. Unknown targets, missing provider directories, and conflicts with common modules should fail during the build. This keeps provider compatibility out of the inference hot path and makes target mismatches explicit. --- ## Provider Contract A target-specific provider is appropriate when all of the following are true: ```text same semantic operation + different target implementation + same logical input/output contract ``` For example: ```text Ascend910: npu_gemma_rms_norm(input, weight, eps) Ascend950: npu_rms_norm(input, 1 + weight, eps) ``` Both expose: ```python npu_gemma_rms_norm(input, weight, eps) -> (output, rstd) ``` [#734](https://github.com/sgl-project/sgl-kernel-npu/pull/734) also enforces that target provider trees expose the same module set, keeping target differences at the implementation layer rather than the public API layer. --- ## SGLang DeviceOperator When generation differences cross the standalone operator boundary, they should be handled in SGLang. For example: ```text A3: INT8 KV FP16 scale legacy sparse-attention contract A5: FP8 packed KV different scale metadata different sparse-attention contract ``` In this case, the Memory Pool must allocate a different representation before the kernel executes. A kernel provider alone cannot hide the difference. The proposed responsibility is: ```text SGLang DeviceOperator │ ├── runtime dtype contract ├── layout contract ├── metadata contract └── semantic operator adaptation │ ▼ sgl-kernel-npu stable ops ``` `DeviceOperator` should **not** own: ```text kernel provider selection feature enable/disable KV lifetime algorithm selection ``` In short: > `DeviceOperator` defines how an already-selected feature runs on the current device generation. It does not decide whether the feature should be enabled. --- ## Representative Cases ### Gemma RMSNorm ```text different implementation same standalone semantic contract ``` → `sgl-kernel-npu` target provider [#638](https://github.com/sgl-project/sgl-kernel-npu/pull/638) + [#734](https://github.com/sgl-project/sgl-kernel-npu/pull/734)provide the reference implementation. ### MXFP scale layout If normalization is operator-local: ```text kernel output ↓ local reshape / normalization ↓ stable public representation ``` → `sgl-kernel-npu` If the representation is stored and consumed across multiple runtime components: ```text producer ↓ runtime state ↓ multiple consumers ``` → SGLang `DeviceOperator` ### KV / Sparse Attention If generation differences affect: ```text KV dtype physical KV layout scale metadata memory allocation contract ``` → SGLang `DeviceOperator` The concrete standalone kernels used by that path remain in: ```text sgl-kernel-npu ``` --- ## Rollout The two repositories can evolve independently under the same ownership model. ### sgl-kernel-npu ```text #638(https://github.com/sgl-project/sgl-kernel-npu/pull/638) Gemma stable operator ↓ #734(https://github.com/sgl-project/sgl-kernel-npu/pull/734) generic target-provider staging ↓ additional portable operators ``` After [#734](https://github.com/sgl-project/sgl-kernel-npu/pull/734), adding a new cross-generation operator only requires: 1. confirm that it has the same semantic and logical I/O contract; 2. add the same module path under the required `target_providers/<target>/` directories; 3. add contract tests. No generic build-system changes should be required. ### SGLang Introduce a minimal `DeviceOperator` and migrate only existing runtime-visible differences, such as: ```text KV representation Sparse Attention contract Indexer dtype/layout cross-operator quantization metadata ``` This RFC does not propose wrapping every NPU operator. --- ## Acceptance Criteria The intended long-term rules are: 1. SGLang feature code does not directly select kernel providers. 2. Standalone generation differences are handled in `sgl-kernel-npu` whenever possible. 3. `sgl-kernel-npu` exposes stable semantic/module contracts. 4. Target-specific providers are selected during wheel build. 5. The build framework knows targets, not individual operators. 6. Provider dispatch is kept out of the inference hot path. 7. SGLang `DeviceOperator` only handles runtime-visible device contracts. 8. Feature, Memory, and Scheduler ownership remains unchanged. 9. Neither repository introduces a God Object covering all NPU operators. --- ## Open Questions 1. Do we agree on the following default ownership rule? ```text standalone kernel/provider difference → sgl-kernel-npu runtime-visible representation/contract difference → SGLang DeviceOperator ``` 2. Which existing runtime-visible A5 difference should be the first minimal SGLang `DeviceOperator` migration to validate the abstraction? --- ## References * [sgl-kernel-npu #638 — Add portable Gemma RMSNorm API](https://github.com/sgl-project/sgl-kernel-npu/pull/638) * [sgl-kernel-npu #734 — Generalize target-specific operator provider staging](https://github.com/sgl-project/sgl-kernel-npu/pull/734) * [SGLang #32745 — Fix Qwen3.5 GemmaRMSNorm on Ascend 950](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/32745) * [SGLang #33030 — Add Ascend 950 backend paths for DeepSeek-V4](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/33030) * vLLM-Ascend `device_op.py` — prior art for runtime device adaptation

signals.title: [Bug] 0.5.17: generation degenerates into token loops on Qwen3.5-arch model (works on 0.5.6.dev, with/without DFLASH)
signals.text: ### Bug report **Model**: orcarouter/Qwen3.8-27B-Uncensored-NVFP4 (arch `Qwen3_5ForConditionalGeneration`, NVFP4 quantized) + z-lab/Qwen3.8-27B-DFlash2 draft, single 80GB GPU. **Version broken**: 0.5.17 (PyPI wheel). **Version working**: 0.5.6.post3.dev9196+ga4ffb996d (git @a4ffb996d). Same model, same flags, same venv. **Symptom**: after upgrading to 0.5.17, generation degenerates into single-token repetition loops (e.g. `What What What What …` in content, or `"Let's verify." "Let's verify." …` inside reasoning_content), and never exits thinking / never reaches tool calls. `finish_reason: length`, empty content. **Isolation already done** (all still reproduce on 0.5.17): 1. With DFLASH (8 draft tokens) → loops 2. Without DFLASH (no spec) → loops 3. Without `--reasoning-parser qwen3` → loops (no reasoning_content now, content loops) 4. Plain chat request, no tools → loops 5. Same requests on 0.5.6.dev9196, identical flags → clean output, tool call returned normally **Repro** (plain chat, no tools): ```bash python -m sglang.launch_server \ --model-path <main-model> --served-model-name qwen3.8-27b \ --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 --attention-backend flashinfer \ --reasoning-parser qwen3 --max-running-requests 8 \ --mem-fraction-static 0.90 --max-total-tokens 1500000 curl -s localhost:8000/v1/chat/completions -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{ "model":"qwen3.8-27b","max_tokens":160,"temperature":0.6, "messages":[{"role":"user","content":"What is the capital of France? Answer in one short sentence."}]}' ``` Expected: clean answer. Actual (0.5.17): `content: "The user asks for the answer one short sentence.The question asks What What What What What What What What …"`, `finish_reason: length`. Looks like a generation-level regression in 0.5.17 for this Qwen3.5-based arch (sampling/logits/pipe), independent of speculative decoding. Happy to provide full logs or bisect help.

signals.title: [Bug] DeepSeek-V4 leaks raw DSML when tool_choice="none"
signals.text: ### Checklist - [x] I searched related issues but found no solution. - [x] The bug persists in the latest version. - [x] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback. - [x] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed. - [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed. ### Describe the bug DeepSeek-V4 leaks its raw DSML tool-call markup into `message.content` when a Chat Completions request contains a non-empty `tools` array and sets `tool_choice: "none"`. The response is HTTP 200 with `finish_reason: "stop"` and no structured `tool_calls`, but `message.content` contains output such as: ```text <｜DSML｜tool_calls> <｜DSML｜invoke name="Bash"> <｜DSML｜parameter name="command" string="true">pwd</｜DSML｜parameter> </｜DSML｜invoke> </｜DSML｜tool_calls> ``` This reproduced 7/7 times across streaming and non-streaming requests, with and without `reasoning_effort`. The official DeepSeek API does not reproduce the leak. With an equivalent user prompt and the same tool schema, `tool_choice: "none"` used 94 prompt tokens and returned no DSML or tool call. The `auto` request used 359 prompt tokens and returned a structured tool call. The `none` response's reasoning also explicitly stated that no tool was available. This indicates that the official implementation removes the tool definition from the model input when tools are disabled. The causal path in SGLang is: 1. `serving_chat.py` correctly skips the tool constraint and output parser when `request.tool_choice == "none"`. 2. The DSV4 encoding path still unconditionally copies `request.tools` into the first system message: ```python if request.tools: messages[0]["tools"] = [tool.model_dump() for tool in request.tools] ``` 3. `encoding_dsv4.py` renders those tools into `TOOLS_TEMPLATE`, which instructs the model to emit DSML. 4. Because output parsing is disabled for `none`, generated DSML is returned as normal content. The deployed source files match the official `v0.5.17` tag byte-for-byte. The same unconditional DSV4 tool injection remains on current `origin/main` at `a4ffb996db3e823708a53637f851e2677d4455a8`. Related issue #30925 reported a similar symptom for GLM, but it was closed after the reporter could not reproduce it on v0.5.15. This report is specific to the DSV4 encoder and is deterministic on v0.5.17. Expected behavior: `tool_choice: "none"` must not expose the tool schema or native tool-call instructions to the model. The response must contain neither structured tool calls nor raw DSML markup. ### Reproduction Model: `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash` Start SGLang: ```bash python3 -m sglang.launch_server \ --model-path deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash \ --served-model-name DeepSeek-V4-Flash \ --tp-size 2 \ --tool-call-parser deepseekv4 \ --reasoning-parser deepseek-v4 \ --port 30000 ``` Send the minimal non-streaming request: ```bash curl -sS http://127.0.0.1:30000/v1/chat/completions \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d '{ "model": "DeepSeek-V4-Flash", "messages": [ {"role": "user", "content": "Call Bash to run pwd. Return no prose."} ], "tools": [{ "type": "function", "function": { "name": "Bash", "description": "Run a command", "parameters": { "type": "object", "properties": { "command": {"type": "string"} }, "required": ["command"] } } }], "tool_choice": "none", "temperature": 0, "max_tokens": 384 }' | jq '.choices[0]' ``` Observed response shape: ```json { "message": { "role": "assistant", "content": "<｜DSML｜tool_calls>...<｜DSML｜invoke name=\"Bash\">...", "tool_calls": null }, "finish_reason": "stop" } ``` A minimal fix is to avoid attaching `request.tools` to DSV4 messages when `request.tool_choice == "none"`. A regression test should assert that the encoded DSV4 prompt does not contain `## Tools`, the tool name, or `<｜DSML｜tool_calls>` for this request shape. ### Environment Output of `python3 -m sglang.check_env` from the reproducing server: ```text Python: 3.12.3 (main, Jun 19 2026, 12:46:00) [GCC 13.3.0] CUDA available: True GPU 0,1: NVIDIA B300 SXM6 AC GPU 0,1 Compute Capability: 10.3 signals.title: [Bug] A global --attention-backend kills the server when a non-DiT component does not declare it (MiniMax-H3 audio_vae)
signals.text: ### Checklist - [x] I searched related issues but found no solution. - [x] The bug persists in the latest version. - [x] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback. - [x] Please use English. ### Describe the bug Passing a global `--attention-backend` that the *DiT* supports takes the whole server down if any **non-DiT** component's attention layer does not declare that backend — even when the layer declares a `default_attention_backend` for exactly this case. With MiniMax-H3 and `--attention-backend sage_attn`: ``` ValueError: Attention backend 'sage_attn' is not supported by this attention layer; supported backends: ['fa', 'torch_sdpa'] ... Failed to load customized audio_vae ... Rank 0 scheduler is dead ``` The audio VAE's attention layer is constructed with both a supported set and a default: `python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/models/vaes/minimax_h3_audio_vae/audio_vae.py:60-70` ```python supported_attention_backends={AttentionBackendEnum.FA, AttentionBackendEnum.TORCH_SDPA}, default_attention_backend=AttentionBackendEnum.TORCH_SDPA, ``` `get_attn_backend()` does have a fallback path, but it is gated on the selection not being explicit (`selector.py:188-201`): ```python selection_is_explicit = isinstance(server_args, ServerArgs) and server_args.is_arg_explicitly_set("attention_backend") ... elif not selection_is_explicit: allowed_fallback_reason = "platform default fallback" ``` A `--attention-backend` on the command line is explicit, so `allowed_fallback_reason` stays `None`, `candidate_backends` holds only the requested backend, and `selector.py:233-241` turns it into the hard `ValueError` above. Not honouring an explicit request silently is reasonable; the problem is that a *global* flag is treated as an explicit request **for every component**, including ones that cannot possibly satisfy it and that ship a declared default for that situation. Practical consequence: any global sparse/fp8 attention backend requires the operator to know the full component list up front and repeat it, and getting it wrong is a dead server rather than a warning. On MiniMax-H3 all three non-DiT components (`text_encoder`, `audio_vae`, `video_vae`) have to be exempted, and the set has grown between nightlies, so a config that worked on an earlier image fails on a later one with an error that points at the VAE rather than at the flag. ### Reproduction ```bash sglang serve --model-path <MiniMax-H3> --model-variant fl2va \ --num-gpus 1 --attention-backend sage_attn ``` Startup fails as above. Works with the components enumerated: ```bash --attention-backend sage_attn \ --component-attention-backends text_encoder=torch_sdpa,audio_vae=torch_sdpa,video_vae=torch_sdpa ``` ### Environment One RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition (sm_120), CUDA 13, `lmsysorg/sglang` nightly. The code path is unchanged on current `main` (read at `a49560ce50`), so this is not specific to that GPU or image — any global backend a non-DiT component doesn't declare reproduces it. ### Suggested direction Any of these would work; the first is the smallest: 1. Treat `--attention-backend` as explicit only for components that declare support, and fall back to the layer's `default_attention_backend` elsewhere with a `logger.warning` naming the component. This keeps "don't silently downgrade what the user asked for" for the DiT, where the request is meaningful. 2. Keep failing closed, but make the message actionable: name the component being loaded and print the `--component-attention-backends component=torch_sdpa` line that fixes it. Happy to send a PR for either once maintainers pick one.

signals.title: [Feature] Support Prometheus name[] filtering for multiprocess metrics
signals.text: ### Checklist - [x] If this is not a feature request but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed. - [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed. ### Motivation Upper-layer schedulers and resource managers, such as llm-d and AIBrix, rely on the `/metrics` endpoint to retrieve selected serving resource-utilization metrics for placement, routing, and scaling decisions. The default HTTP exposition implementationprovided by `prometheus_client` supports repeated `name[]` parameters so these consumers can request only the samples they need. SGLang currently does not preserve this capability in multiprocess mode. Filtered requests can omit the `MultiProcessCollector` and return no SGLang samples, forcing consumers to fall back to the full metrics payload and filter it client-side. With frequent scheduler polling or many SGLang instances, serializing, transferring, parsing, and discarding unrelated samples wastesnetwork bandwidth and CPU resources on both sides. SGLang exposes Prometheus metrics through `prometheus_client.make_asgi_app` when `--enable-metrics` is enabled. The upstream ASGI app supports restricting a scrape to specific sample names with repeated `name[]` query parameters: ```bash curl -G http://localhost:30000/metrics \ --data-urlencode 'name[]=sglang:num_running_reqs' \ --data-urlencode 'name[]=sglang:prompt_tokens_total' ``` This filtering does not work correctly with SGLang's multiprocess registry today. `MultiProcessCollector` discovers metric names only during collection, so the default `CollectorRegistry.restricted_registry()` path can omit it. As a result, a filteredrequest may return no SGLang samples even though an unfiltered `/metrics` request returns them. Supporting name-based filtering is useful for targeted diagnostics and monitoring clients that only need a small subset of metrics. It also reduces response size and downstream parsing overhead without changing the existing unfiltered endpoint. Proposed changes: 1. Raise the minimum `prometheus-client` version from `0.20.0` to `0.25.0` across all SGLang package variants. 2. Create the multiprocess registry with `CollectorRegistry(support_collectors_without_names=True)`. 3. Continue using the upstream `make_asgi_app`, which already parses repeated `name[]` parameters and applies `restricted_registry()`. 4. Add end-to-end coverage that requests multiple metric names and verifies that only the requested samples are returned. Expected behavior: ```text GET /metrics?name[]=sglang:num_running_reqs&name[]=sglang:prompt_tokens_total ``` returns those two sample names and excludes unrelated metrics. Requests without `name[]` remain unchanged and return the complete metrics payload. ### Related resources - `prometheus-client` v0.25.0 release: https://github.com/prometheus/client_python/releases/tag/v0.25.0 - Upstream multiprocess restricted-registry support: https://github.com/prometheus/client_python/pull/1150

signals.title: Support sampling masks without finite top-k
signals.text: ## Context #27408 introduced sampling-mask responses with finite `top_k` as the bound on reconstruction and returned metadata. #33593 admitted top-p-only mask requests and exposed the feature through the OpenAI chat extension. However, `top_p < 1` does not bound realized support: depending on the distribution, a mask can still approach the full vocabulary. #35205 restores the finite-`top_k` requirement while this general case is designed. #34037 contains an initial implementation exploring faithful support capture, fixed transport capacity, and explicit bounded output. ## Goal Support `return_sampling_mask` without finite `top_k` while preserving the requested sampling distribution, bounding serving work and transport, and giving clients an unambiguous response contract. ## Requirements - Define support from the post-filter distribution used to sample the token, including backend cutoff-tie semantics. - Restrict support computation and transfer to requests that opt in. - Bound transport independently of `top_k`, `top_p`, and `min_p`. - Never silently present partial support as exact. - Define exact overflow behavior and, if bounded output is supported, expose truncation explicitly per token. - Keep the selected-token logprob normalized over the complete sampling distribution rather than a truncated response. - Preserve the contract through batching, TP/CP, pipeline parallelism, streaming, sessions, and prefill/decode disaggregation. - Add correctness coverage across supported sampling backends and measure feature-on and feature-off overhead.

signals.title: [Bug] Target-only speculative sampler can accept a zero-probability draft at RNG boundary
signals.text: ### Checklist - [x] I searched related issues but found no solution. - [x] The affected condition and callers are still present on upstream `main`. - [x] This report includes minimal GPU reproductions and environment information. - [x] This is a bug report rather than a general question. - [x] This issue is written in English. ### Describe the bug `tree_speculative_sampling_target_only` can accept a draft token whose target probability is exactly zero when its verification coin is also exactly zero. This was originally observed during non-greedy DFlash decoding. The native sampler currently accepts when: ```cpp coin <= prob_acc / threshold_acc ``` DFlash creates unseeded verification coins with `torch.rand(..., dtype=torch.float32)`, whose range includes zero. A draft model may legitimately propose a token removed by the target model's top-k/top-p filtering. For that token, `target_prob_single == 0` and `prob_acc == 0`. If the RNG returns zero, the inclusive comparison evaluates `0 <= 0` and accepts the impossible draft. This violates the target distribution: a token with zero target probability must never be accepted. It can also make the emitted token inconsistent with sampling metadata derived from the positive-probability target support. The bug is not confined to DFlash. Non-greedy EAGLE verification calls the same target-only sampler when rejection sampling is disabled, and `_verify_coins` also produces half-open `[0, 1)` coins. The EAGLE-level reproducer below reaches the same invalid result through `eagle_sample`. NEXTN/MTP reuses this EAGLE verification path, so it has the same boundary condition. I have reproduced the complete DFlash and EAGLE verification paths synthetically; I have not observed this as an end-to-end MTP model failure. The exact boundary does not apply to greedy verification or to configurations using the separate rejection-sampling kernel. The affected code is still present on upstream `main` at `f825d729363136a2d4a4b330fa694d0b37a878fa`: - `python/sglang/kernels/aot/csrc/speculative/speculative_sampling.cuh` - `python/sglang/srt/speculative/dflash_utils.py` - `python/sglang/srt/speculative/eagle_utils.py` - `python/sglang/srt/speculative/eagle_worker_common.py` The target-only sampler and all of its RNG producers should have one consistent boundary contract. In particular, a zero-probability candidate must be rejected for every valid RNG output. ### DFlash reproduction This synthetic reproducer requires one CUDA GPU and an SGLang build with DFlash sampling verification. It does not load a model. ```python from types import SimpleNamespace from unittest import mock import torch from sglang.srt.speculative.dflash_utils import ( build_dflash_verify_target_probs, compute_dflash_sampling_correct_drafts_and_bonus, ) device = "cuda" # Token 2 is the DFlash proposal. The target distribution keeps only token 1, # so token 2 has exactly zero target probability after top-k filtering. candidates = torch.tensor([[0, 2]], dtype=torch.int64, device=device) logits = torch.full((2, 4), -1000.0, device=device) logits[:, 1] = 1000.0 sampling_info = SimpleNamespace( temperatures=torch.ones((1, 1), device=device), top_ks=torch.ones(1, dtype=torch.int32, device=device), top_ps=torch.ones(1, device=device), need_top_k_sampling=True, need_top_p_sampling=False, ) target_probs = build_dflash_verify_target_probs( next_token_logits=logits, sampling_info=sampling_info, draft_token_num=2, bs=1, max_top_k=1, uniform_top_k_value=1, ) assert target_probs[0, 0, 2].item() == 0.0 # Force the rare boundary value produced by the ordinary torch.rand path. with mock.patch( "sglang.srt.speculative.dflash_utils.torch.rand", return_value=torch.zeros((1, 2), dtype=torch.float32, device=device), ): accepted, bonus = compute_dflash_sampling_correct_drafts_and_bonus( candidates=candidates, next_token_logits=logits, sampling_info=sampling_info, max_top_k=1, uniform_top_k_value=1, threshold_single=1.0, threshold_acc=1.0, uniform_samples_for_final_sampling=torch.full( (1,), 0.5, dtype=torch.float32, device=device ), ) print("target probability:", target_probs[0, 0, 2].item()) print("accepted drafts:", accepted.item()) print("bonus token:", bonus.item()) # Fails on the affected implementation: accepted.item() is 1. assert accepted.item() == 0, "zero-probability draft was accepted" ``` Observed result: ```text target probability: 0.0 accepted drafts: 1 AssertionError: zero-probability draft was accepted ``` Expected result: ```text target probability: 0.0 accepted drafts: 0 ``` ### EAGLE / MTP verification-path reproduction This probe enters through `eagle_sample`, rather than calling the native sampler directly. It forces the same valid zero coin and captures the target probability passed by EAGLE to the native kernel. MTP reuses this verification function. <details> <summary>Standalone EAGLE probe</summary> ```python from contextlib import nullcontext from types import SimpleNamespace from unittest import mock import sgl_kernel import torch from sglang.srt.model_executor.forward_batch_info import ForwardMode from sglang.srt.speculative.eagle_utils import eagle_sample device = "cuda" candidates = torch.tensor([[0, 2]], dtype=torch.int64, device=device) logits = torch.full((2, 4), -1000.0, device=device) logits[:, 1] = 1000.0 sampling_info = SimpleNamespace( temperatures=torch.ones((1, 1), device=device), top_ks=torch.ones(1, dtype=torch.int32, device=device), top_ps=torch.ones(1, device=device), need_top_k_sampling=True, need_top_p_sampling=False, is_all_greedy=False, sampling_seed=None, acc_additive_penalties=None, acc_scaling_penalties=None, logit_bias=None, ) batch = SimpleNamespace( device=device, forward_mode=ForwardMode.DECODE, seq_lens=torch.ones(1, dtype=torch.int32, device=device), sampling_info=sampling_info, ) verify_input = SimpleNamespace( draft_token=candidates.flatten(), draft_token_num=2, max_tree_depth=2, tree_topk=1, retrieve_index=torch.tensor([[0, 1]], dtype=torch.int64, device=device), retrieve_next_token=torch.tensor([[1, -1]], dtype=torch.int64, device=device), retrieve_next_sibling=torch.tensor( [[-1, -1]], dtype=torch.int64, device=device ), draft_probs=None, ) spec = SimpleNamespace( speculative_use_rejection_sampling=False, speculative_accept_threshold_single=1.0, speculative_accept_threshold_acc=1.0, ) observed = {} native_sampler = sgl_kernel.tree_speculative_sampling_target_only def capture_sampler(**kwargs): observed["target_probability"] = kwargs["target_probs"][0, 0, 2].item() return native_sampler(**kwargs) with ( mock.patch("sglang.srt.speculative.eagle_utils.get_spec", return_value=spec), mock.patch( "sglang.srt.speculative.eagle_utils.borrow_graph_pool", return_value=nullcontext(), ), mock.patch( "sglang.srt.speculative.eagle_utils._verify_coins", return_value=( torch.zeros((1, 2), dtype=torch.float32, device=device), torch.full((1,), 0.5, dtype=torch.float32, device=device), ), ), mock.patch.object( sgl_kernel, "tree_speculative_sampling_target_only", side_effect=capture_sampler, ), mock.patch( "sglang.srt.layers.dp_attention.is_dp_attention_enabled", return_value=False, ), mock.patch( "sglang.srt.distributed.get_tp_group", return_value=SimpleNamespace(world_size=1), ), ): _, accepted_with_bonus, _ = eagle_sample( verify_input, batch, SimpleNamespace(next_token_logits=logits), ) accepted_drafts = accepted_with_bonus.item() - 1 print("target probability:", observed["target_probability"]) print("accepted drafts:", accepted_drafts) assert observed["target_probability"] == 0.0 assert accepted_drafts == 0, "EAGLE accepted a zero-probability draft" ``` </details> Observed result: ```text target probability: 0.0 accepted drafts: 1 AssertionError: EAGLE accepted a zero-probability draft ``` ### Environment - SGLang: the issue is present in upstream `main` at `f825d729363136a2d4a4b330fa694d0b37a878fa` - Both synthetic reproductions were validated on an NVIDIA B300 CUDA GPU against the SGLang v0.5.17 runtime - Python 3.12 - The reproducers exercise only synthetic tensors and the installed `sgl_kernel`; no model checkpoint is required

Otherwise, it will be closed. - [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed. ### Describe the bug ### Summary On the latest release, SGLang v0.5.17 (commit `29481685462732237d80d86076d6563e1f658102`), we observe a large accuracy discrepancy for fine-grained visual grounding with two Qwen3-VL-family checkpoints: `Tencent/UI-Mate-27B` and `Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B`. We replayed the same captured prompt contents and image bytes through SGLang, Hugging Face Transformers, and vLLM under greedy decoding (`temperature=0.0`, `top_p=1.0`). Only the engine changed. Transformers and vLLM agree closely, while SGLang produces systematically incorrect click coordinates. | Model | Engine | Dtype | Half-row hits | Median absolute y error / row pitch | |---|---|---:|---:|---:| | UI-Mate-27B | SGLang 0.5.17 | BF16 | 0/20 | 0.9748 | | UI-Mate-27B | Transformers | BF16 | 20/20 | 0.0636 | | UI-Mate-27B | vLLM (official-style TP2) | BF16 | 20/20 | 0.0649 | | Qwen3.8-27B | SGLang 0.5.17 | BF16 | 1/20 | 4.5964 | | Qwen3.8-27B | Transformers | BF16 | 20/20 | 0.0481 | | Qwen3.8-27B | vLLM | BF16 | 20/20 | 0.0559 | The criterion is whether the first click falls within half of one rendered row pitch. All arms use the same 20 fixed first-step inputs. This is intentionally a narrow fine-grained grounding test; we are not claiming that all Qwen3-VL tasks fail in SGLang. ### Evidence localizing the discrepancy For an aligned Qwen3.8 seed: - `input_ids` are identical between the Transformers replay and SGLang (same shape and hash). - `image_grid_thw` is identical: `[[1, 62, 100]]`. - The processor output shape is identical: `pixel_values=[6200, 1536]`, float32. - The default SGLang GPU processor differs slightly from the CPU processor (max absolute pixel delta `2/255`, mean absolute delta `1.56e-6`). Disabling the fast image processor remains 1/20, so this small preprocessing delta is not sufficient to explain the failure. - Text token embeddings before multimodal replacement are exactly equal elementwise in our probe. - Immediately after the vision merge, image-token relative L2 difference is approximately `0.0401`. - After the first GDN layer and the first full-attention layer, the relative L2 difference remains approximately `0.036`. This suggests the discrepancy is already present in the vision output and is then propagated by the language model. With an exact Transformers-generated prefix forced into both engines, both choose the same first action token and, after a prefix ending in `"y":`, the same leading coordinate digit with probability effectively 1. This argues against an action parser problem or a fixed coordinate-output-head bias. ### Controlled SGLang ablations (Qwen3.8 BF16, same 20 inputs) | Change from baseline | Half-row hits | Median error / row pitch | |---|---:|---:| | Baseline | 1/20 | 4.5964 | | Disable fast image processor | 1/20 | 4.5068 | | Disable prefill CUDA graph | 1/20 | 4.5516 | | Multimodal attention FA3 -> SDPA | 1/20 | 3.5061 | | Enable precise embedding interpolation | 1/20 | 4.5964 | | Compatibility-adapted v0.5.6.post2 `qwen3_vl.py` vision path | 0/20 | 4.5964 | ### Related issue This may be related to #19513, which reported incorrect Qwen3-VL vision output in older SGLang releases. However, we do not assume the same root cause: unlike that report, a compatibility-adapted v0.5.6.post2 vision-file rollback did **not** recover accuracy on our current v0.5.17 / Transformers 5.12 stack. We would appreciate guidance on the best supported way to compare the vision-encoder output against the Transformers reference, or on any known correctness flags/patches for this model family. ### Reproduction ### Minimal replay (Qwen3.8-27B, seed 8001) The attachment `qwen_seed8001_greedy_payload.json.txt` is a self-contained OpenAI chat-completions payload. It contains the exact prompt and the screenshot as a data URL. Compared with the captured benchmark request, only three fields were normalized: model ID → `Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B`, `temperature` → `0.0`, and `top_p` → `1.0`. The message contents and image bytes are unchanged. Start SGLang: ```bash python3 -m sglang.launch_server \ --model-path Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B \ --host 0.0.0.0 --port 30000 \ --tp-size 1 \ --dtype bfloat16 \ --trust-remote-code \ --context-length 131072 \ --chunked-prefill-size 4096 \ --reasoning-parser qwen3 ``` Download the attachment and replay it: ```python import json import requests payload = json.load(open("qwen_seed8001_greedy_payload.json.txt")) response = requests.post( "http://127.0.0.1:30000/v1/chat/completions", json=payload, timeout=600, ) response.raise_for_status() message = response.json()["choices"][0]["message"] print(message.get("reasoning_content")) print(message.get("content")) ``` Oracle row center for this screenshot: `y=277.1328125` in the declared 1000x1000 output space. Half-row acceptance interval: `[260.39453125, 293.87109375]`. Observed final actions under greedy decoding: ```text SGLang 0.5.17 BF16: {"type":"click","x":150,"y":125,"button":"left"} Transformers BF16: {"type":"click","x":150,"y":276,"button":"left"} vLLM BF16: {"type":"click","x":144,"y":275,"button":"left"} ``` Prompt-token counts are identical for this Qwen replay (2639). The same 20-input discrepancy was independently reproduced with UI-Mate-27B using its official-style vLLM TP2 serving configuration. SHA-256 of the proposed attachment: `d74eb21f628f4f9d172b916c2ec31e54162a954f15cc2f4bd0226ca3517287c2`. [qwen_seed8001_greedy_payload.json.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/31285951/qwen_seed8001_greedy_payload.json.txt) ### Environment ```text Python: 3.12.3 (main, Jun 19 2026, 12:46:00) [GCC 13.3.0] CUDA available: True GPU 0,1,2,3: NVIDIA H200 NVL GPU 0,1,2,3 Compute Capability: 9.0 CUDA_HOME: /usr/local/cuda NVCC: Cuda compilation tools, release 12.9, V12.9.86 CUDA Driver Version: 580.105.08 PyTorch: 2.11.0+cu129 sglang: 0.5.17 sglang-kernel: 0.4.5+cu129 flashinfer_python: 0.6.15.post1 flashinfer_cubin: 0.6.15.post1 flashinfer_jit_cache: 0.6.15.post1+cu129 triton: 3.6.0 transformers: 5.12.1 torchao: 0.17.0+cu129 numpy: 2.4.4 aiohttp: 3.14.3 fastapi: 0.141.1 huggingface_hub: 1.27.0 interegular: 0.3.3 modelscope: 1.39.1 orjson: 3.11.9 outlines: 0.1.11 packaging: 26.3 psutil: 7.2.2 pydantic: 2.13.4 python-multipart: 0.0.32 pyzmq: 27.1.0 uvicorn: 0.52.1 uvloop: 0.22.1 vllm: Module Not Found xgrammar: 0.2.1 openai: 2.6.1 tiktoken: 0.13.0 anthropic: 0.121.0 litellm: Module Not Found torchcodec: 0.11.1+cu129 NVIDIA topology: GPU0 GPU1 GPU2 GPU3 NIC0 NIC1 CPU_Affinity NUMA GPU0 X NV6 NV6 NV6 SYS SYS 0-31,64-95 0 GPU1 NV6 X NV6 NV6 SYS SYS 0-31,64-95 0 GPU2 NV6 NV6 X NV6 SYS SYS 32-63,96-127 1 GPU3 NV6 NV6 NV6 X SYS SYS 32-63,96-127 1 ulimit soft: 131072 ``` SGLang source commit: `29481685462732237d80d86076d6563e1f658102` Container image: `sglang-0.5.17-cu129.sif` Primary SGLang launch settings: BF16, TP1 for Qwen3.8; BF16, TP2 for UI-Mate; FA3 default attention backend; chunked prefill size 4096. Exact Qwen command is included in Reproduction.

signals.title: Qwen3.8-27B NVFP4 on RTX 5090: cookbook mem-fraction OOMs at decode-graph capture (~5GB) and torch.compile + decode graph is a 6x regression
signals.text: ## Describe the bug The Qwen3.8-27B cookbook recipe for **RTX 5090 (32GB) + NVFP4 + no-spec + low-latency tier** (`hw=rtx5090&variant=default&quant=nvfp4&nodes=single&spec=none&tier=low-latency&ssmDtype=float32`) has two issues we measured on real hardware: 1. **The recommended `--mem-fraction-static` values cannot boot on an RTX 5090**: the no-spec recipe enables a *full* target decode CUDA graph capture that consumes **~5 GB of VRAM during capture** (see log below). At the recommended mem-fraction (0.90–0.94) the server enters an OOM crash-restart loop during graph capture. We had to drop to `--mem-fraction-static 0.80` **and** add `--cuda-graph-backend-prefill disabled` to boot at all. 2. **`--enable-torch-compile` combined with a captured decode CUDA graph is a ~6x performance regression** on this model/GPU: 9.8–10.2 tok/s vs 59.4 tok/s with the graph alone. The graph apparently bakes in unoptimized kernels when torch.compile is active. ## Environment - GPU: 1x RTX 5090 32GB (SM120), driver 595.80, CUDA 13.2 - SGLang: 0.5.17 (pip) + the DFlash2 overlay files from the Qwen3.8-27B cookbook (runs fine otherwise) - Model: `RadixArk/Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4` (quantized checkpoint, `kv_cache_quant_algo: FP8` honored via `--kv-cache-dtype auto`) - Container instance (compshare), pure-text serving with `--language-only` - Benchmark: single-stream chat completion, 1024 output tokens, streaming, Chinese technical prompt ## Reproduction Recipe A (as emitted by the cookbook panel for rtx5090/nvfp4/spec=none/low-latency/float32): ```bash python -m sglang.launch_server \ --model-path RadixArk/Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4 \ --attention-backend flashinfer \ --chunked-prefill-size 2048 \ --mamba-ssm-dtype float32 \ --mamba-radix-cache-strategy extra_buffer_lazy \ --mem-fraction-static 0.94 \ # also tried 0.90, 0.85, 0.88 --max-running-requests 4 \ --reasoning-parser qwen3 --tool-call-parser qwen3_coder ``` Result at 0.94 / 0.90 / 0.85 — crash loop during capture: ``` Capture target decode CUDA graph begin. backend=full, num_tokens_per_req=1, bs=[1], avail mem=1.41 GB Exception: Capture cuda graph failed: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 96.00 MiB. GPU 0 has a total capacity of 31.36 GiB of which 39.81 MiB is free. ``` Only at 0.80 + `--cuda-graph-backend-prefill disabled` does capture succeed — and it reveals the real budget: ``` Capture target decode CUDA graph begin. backend=full, num_tokens_per_req=1, bs=[1], avail mem=5.72 GB Capture target decode CUDA graph end. elapsed=215.75 s, mem usage=4.95 GB, avail mem=0.77 GB. ``` **The decode graph itself permanently consumes 4.95 GB.** With NVFP4 weights ~16.5 GB + a ~1 GB CUDA-IPC multimodal feature pool (see finding 3), there is simply no room for the cookbook's mem-fraction on 32 GB. Side finding: `SGLANG_MM_FEATURE_CACHE_MB` defaults to 1024 MiB and is reserved on the base GPU even for **text-only** serving (we use `--language-only`). Setting `SGLANG_MM_FEATURE_CACHE_MB=16` frees ~1 GB. Might be worth defaulting low when the served path is text-only. ## Measured matrix (same GPU, same checkpoint, same benchmark) | # | Spec | torch.compile | Decode graph | mem-frac | tok/s (single stream) | |---|------|---------------|--------------|----------|------------------------| | 1 | none | no | yes | 0.80 | **59.4** | | 2 | none | yes | yes | 0.80 | 10.2 | | 3 | none | yes | yes | 0.80 (bf16 ssm) | 9.8 | | 4 | DFLASH2 (DFlash2 draft, bf16 ssm, `--speculative-num-draft-tokens 8`) | yes | no (verify graph only) | 0.92 | **86–98 steady, 142–151 peak** | Notably, the DFlash2 configuration cannot capture the full decode graph either (VRAM), but it doesn't need to: with only the target-verify + draft-verify graphs plus torch.compile it is **1.5–2.5x faster than the best bootable no-spec recipe** (86–98 vs 59.4 tok/s) and ~9x faster than the torch.compile+graph combination. ## Expected behavior - The RTX 5090 cells of the cookbook should either (a) carry a mem-fraction that actually boots with the decode graph budget included (0.80 or lower + prefill graph disabled), or (b) note that the decode graph costs ~5 GB so users can make an informed trade-off. - The interaction between `--enable-torch-compile` and decode CUDA graph capture looks like a real bug worth investigating (graph should capture *post-compile* kernels), or at minimum the cookbook should warn not to combine them on this model. - Consider lowering the default multimodal IPC feature pool for text-only serving. Happy to provide full logs, the exact launch scripts, or to re-run any cell with instrumentation if that helps.

signals.title: [MoonEP] Kimi-K3 production integration roadmap
signals.text: ## Goal Track the work required to take MoonEP support for Kimi-K3 from the merged BF16 correctness PoC to a reproducible, tested, and performance-validated production integration. This is the dedicated MoonEP roadmap under the broader Kimi-K3 roadmap in #32607. ## Current status (2026-08-21) - The BF16 integration seam and correctness PoC were merged into the `moonep` branch in #33249. - #34874 is the production-path candidate for MXFP4 experts in symmetric memory using the DeepGEMM runner. It reports end-to-end Kimi-K3 validation on 4x GB200 with TP16/EP16, but is currently open and needs to be rebased onto the merged `moonep` branch. - The compatible generalized MoonEP prefetch/local-first API is being developed in MoonshotAI/MoonEP#32. - The original fork-side PoC map is wirybeaver/sglang#7. ## Completed: BF16 PoC and integration seam - [x] Research the SGLang DeepEP seam and MoonEP dispatch/plan/prefetch/combine contract. - [x] Add `moonep` as a distinct MoE A2A backend. - [x] Add MoonEP dispatch and combine data contracts. - [x] Add the process-wide static MoonEP buffer facade and sizing knobs. - [x] Define the initial static token-capacity policy. - [x] Add the correctness-first contiguous BF16 expert layout. - [x] Add the BF16 `cu_seqlens` segment runner. - [x] Wire eager dispatch -> prefetch -> compute -> combine. - [x] Add the distributed BF16 validation harness. - [x] Validate the synthetic BF16 path on 8x H100 SXM: all eight ranks passed with zero numerical error. - [x] Merge the BF16 PoC into upstream `moonep` via #33249. The merged work intentionally remains a PoC: eager-only, BF16-only, memory-heavy global expert storage, and a correctness-first Python expert loop. ## Milestone 0: Land the MXFP4/DeepGEMM production-path candidate - [ ] Land and version the MoonEP API needed by the SGLang integration. - [ ] Merge or supersede MoonshotAI/MoonEP#32. - [ ] Pin/document an exact compatible MoonEP revision or wheel. - [ ] Rebase #34874 onto the latest `upstream/moonep`. - [ ] Resolve conflicts so the PR contains only its MXFP4/DeepGEMM/symmetric-memory delta. - [ ] Run pre-commit and fix lint. - [ ] Trigger and pass the required SGLang CPU/GPU CI suites. ## Milestone 1: Make the supported runtime contract safe and explicit - [ ] Remove the silent rank-0 fallback from MoonEP rank resolution. - [ ] Prevent padded routes from distorting MoonEP planner expert statistics. - [ ] Explicitly reject unsupported expert-bias configurations. - [ ] Define the TBO/SBO contract. - Near-term option: fail fast or disable overlap for MoonEP. - Long-term option: give every in-flight sub-batch explicit buffer/plan ownership. - [ ] Keep CUDA graph disabled unless capture/replay is validated; do not expose an unverified opt-in as supported behavior. - [ ] Replace broad DeepEP-family capability assumptions with explicit MoonEP capability checks where necessary. ## Milestone 2: Add automated coverage for the production path - [ ] Test symmetric-pool alignment, sizing, lifecycle, and global-expert-to-row mapping across EP ranks. - [ ] Test MXFP4 checkpoint loading and post-load weight/scale residency in symmetric memory. - [ ] Test remote-prefetch source and destination slot remapping. - [ ] Test MoonEP-to-DeepGEMM pre/post-permute logic, including `m_indices`. - [ ] Test route-weight application, empty groups, padded groups, and capacity boundaries. - [ ] Test prefill/decode capacity selection and rank-uniform buffer selection. - [ ] Add a real SGLang integration test that instantiates the actual Kimi-K3 `FusedMoE`/MXFP4 path without import stubs. - [ ] Retain the synthetic BF16 harness as a separately identified component test. ## Milestone 3: Reproducible Kimi-K3 acceptance validation - [ ] Re-run end-to-end Kimi-K3 validation on the rebased, pinned stack. - [ ] Record exact SGLang, MoonEP, and DeepGEMM revisions. - [ ] Record the complete launch command, container/wheel versions, topology, GPU count, and TP/EP configuration. - [ ] Validate prefill and decode over small and large batches. - [ ] Validate token-capacity overflow and unsupported-configuration failure behavior. - [ ] Measure resident and peak memory for the symmetric expert pool. - [ ] Run long-duration/stability validation. - [ ] Validate correctness with an agreed evaluation suite and thresholds. ## Milestone 4: Demonstrate the performance value - [ ] Define acceptance thresholds before benchmarking. - [ ] Compare MoonEP with DeepEP under identical Kimi-K3 MXFP4 settings. - [ ] Measure TTFT, inter-token latency, throughput, and memory. - [ ] Cover decode/small-batch and larger-batch operating points relevant to #32607. - [ ] Break down dispatch, planning, prefetch, expert GEMM, and combine time. - [ ] Tune and document token capacity, padding, prefetch slots, and communication SM count. - [ ] Profile representative bottlenecks where profiler permissions and hardware permit. ## Milestone 5: Package and document the supported configuration - [ ] Provide a reproducible MoonEP wheel/container installation path. - [ ] Add hardware and topology prerequisite checks with actionable errors. - [ ] Add a Kimi-K3 MoonEP launch recipe. - [ ] Document supported dtype, quantization, EP topology, CUDA graph, overlap, PP, and disaggregation combinations. - [ ] Add troubleshooting guidance for capacity, VMM/fabric, multicast, and dependency-version failures. - [ ] Update #32607 when the agreed completion boundary is met. ## Follow-up capabilities These should not block the first narrowly defined Kimi-K3 production configuration unless the acceptance contract explicitly requires them. - [ ] Asynchronous dispatch/prefetch/combine event chaining and stream overlap. - [ ] CUDA graph capture/replay. - [ ] TBO/SBO support with explicit multi-in-flight ownership. - [ ] Fused shared experts. - [ ] Sharded symmetric storage for the BF16 diagnostic path, or removal of the memory-heavy BF16 production path. - [ ] Pipeline parallelism. - [ ] PD disaggregation and speculative-decoding combinations. - [ ] Additional models, quantization formats, and hardware generations. ## Decisions still required Child decision issues should settle these before this roadmap is converted into implementation tickets: 1. Is the first completion boundary Kimi-K3 MXFP4 on GB200/GB300 only, or a generic MoonEP backend contract? 2. What exact topology and GPU matrix is required for acceptance? 3. What DeepEP-relative performance threshold is required to call the integration successful? 4. Should TBO/SBO and CUDA graph be explicitly unsupported for v1, or required before completion? 5. Who owns and publishes the compatible MoonEP dependency artifact? 6. Which follow-up capabilities belong in this roadmap versus separate roadmaps? ## Completion criteria The primary roadmap is complete when: - the compatible MoonEP dependency and SGLang integration are merged and reproducibly installable; - the MXFP4 symmetric-memory + DeepGEMM path passes focused tests and SGLang CI; - the supported configuration fails early for unsupported combinations; - Kimi-K3 acceptance validation is reproducible from recorded revisions and commands; and - MoonEP's benefit relative to DeepEP is measured against a pre-agreed threshold, or the result is documented and the roadmap scope is explicitly revised.

signals.title: diffusion(tests): Add per-test sampling overrides
signals.text: ## Summary Enabled per-test sampling overrides for diffusion video runs so we can exercise resolution/steps/FPS controls via the `/videos` API without changing global defaults. Allows for some tests to be run with lower resolution/steps/FPS, to increase speed. Aligns with the TODO points described in #12987 (Reducing ```num_inference_steps``` to shorten testing time, Lower the video/image resolution to reduce testing time.) ## Modifications - Added optional override fields (`num_inference_steps`, `height`, `width`, `guidance_scale`) to `DiffusionSamplingParams`. - Added a helper to build `extra_body` for `/videos` calls and wired it through all video generation paths so `steps/height/width/num_frames/fps/guidance_scale` are sent alongside `size` (including reference URL / input-reference flows). - Added an env override that let you opt into lower steps/res for faster runs without changing the baseline configs; the alternative would be to hardcode reductions into the test cases or add separate fast cases, wasn't sure if this is what was what we were looking for, lmk if it is though. ## Checklist - [ ] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [ ] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). - [ ] Work with maintainers to merge your PR.
