signals.title: refactor(server_args): use set_defaults for config file merging
signals.text: Replace argv-reconstruction approach with `parser.set_defaults()` for merging YAML/JSON config values. This provides cleaner code, better type handling, and comprehensive validation. ## Motivation Fix #16256 Previously, the server argument parsing logic handled configuration files by manually reconstructing a list of command-line arguments (e.g., converting config values back to strings and appending them to sys.argv). This approach had several drawbacks: - **Complexity & Fragility**: Manually reconstructing argv strings is error-prone, especially when dealing with different data types (booleans, lists) and edge cases. - **Redundancy**: The old approach manually converted config values to CLI argument strings (handling booleans, lists, type-to-string conversion), then had argparse re-parse them. This duplicated logic that `parser.set_defaults()` handles natively without string conversion. - **Maintenance**: It makes the codebase harder to read and maintain. ## Modifications ### Core Changes | Before | After | |--------|-------| | Manually reconstructed CLI arguments from config | Use `parser.set_defaults(**config)` directly | | Type validation by argparse (after string conversion) | Explicit type validation in ConfigArgumentMerger (no string round-trip) | | Boolean handling required manual `--flag` construction | Direct boolean value support with strict validation | | Only YAML support | YAML and JSON support | | Silent failures for invalid options | Explicit errors for invalid choices, types, and rejected options | ### Key Implementation Details 1. **ConfigArgumentMerger class** (server_args_config_parser.py) - parse_config(): Parses config file and returns validated dict - remove_config_from_argv(): Removes `--config` from argv for argparse - _parse_config_file(): Supports both YAML and JSON formats - _convert_value(): Smart type conversion with special handling for: - `None` values (YAML null) - pass through - Already matched types - skip redundant conversion - `json.loads`/`json_list_type` - skip for pre-parsed dict/list - nullable_str - convert numeric values to string first 2. **Validation Features** - **Rejected options**: `config`, `help`, `h`, and custom actions (e.g., `DeprecatedAction`, `LoRAPathAction`) cannot be specified in config files - **Choices validation**: Validates both single values and nargs lists - **store_true validation**: Rejects non-boolean values (int, string) - **Unknown options**: Logs warning and ignores 3. **Dynamic Required Argument Handling** When a required argument is provided in the config file, we dynamically set `action.required = False`: ```python for action in parser._actions: if action.dest in config_values and action.required: action.required = False ``` Why this is needed: - parser.set_defaults() only sets default values, it doesn't affect the required flag - Without this, argparse would still raise "required argument missing" error even when the value is in config - This allows config file to satisfy required arguments without CLI specification 4. **Argument Precedence** CLI Args > Config File > Default Values ### Files Changed | File | Change | |------|--------| | python/sglang/srt/server_args.py | Added config merging logic in `prepare_server_args()` | | python/sglang/srt/server_args_config_parser.py | Refactored ConfigArgumentMerger class with enhanced validation| | test/manual/test_config_integration.py | Updated test suite with comprehensive coverage | ## Tests Added comprehensive test suite in test/manual/test_config_integration.py ### Test Coverage | Test Class | Coverage | |------------|----------| | TestConfigArgumentMerger | Basic parsing, key normalization, choices validation | | TestPrepareServerArgs | End-to-end config loading, JSON support, CLI override | | TestErrorHandling | File not found, multiple configs, unsupported extension, rejected options | | TestTypeValidation | store_true, type conversion, null passthrough, dict/JSON skip | | TestEdgeCases | Empty config, .yml extension, unknown options, non-dict root, nullable_str | ### Practical scenario validation ```bash root@localhost:/workspace/sglang/python# cat /workspace/config.yaml enable-metrics: true disable_cuda_graph: true host: 127.0.0.1 port: 3009 model-path: /root/.cache/Qwen3-4B-GGUF/Qwen3-4B-Q8_0.gguf device: npu attention-backend: ascend tokenizer_mode: auto log-requests-target: ["/workspace/mock1","/workspace/mock2"] log-requests: true mem-fraction-static: 0.8 quantization_param_path: null zzzzzzzzz: 11111111111111 root@localhost:/workspace/sglang/python# python3 -m sglang.launch_server --config /workspace/config.yaml [2026-01-16 02:43:45] WARNING server_args_config_parser.py:54: Unknown config option 'zzzzzzzzz' will be ignored. Check if the option name is correct. /workspace/sglang/python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/awq.py:76: UserWarning: Only CUDA, HIP and XPU support AWQ currently. warnings.warn(f"Only CUDA, HIP and XPU support AWQ currently.") signals.title: Enhance Kimi K2.5 support with improved reasoning parser and function call detector
signals.text: ## Motivation Kimi K2.5 models exhibit special behaviors that required dedicated handling: - Reasoning Mode Issue: When deciding to invoke a tool while in reasoning mode (`<think>...</think>`), the model may output tool call markers directly without first outputting the `</think>` closing tag. - UUID Format Support: Support UUID-style call IDs (e.g., `call_6b0e7c24f0c44f0d996b59e5`). This ensures compatibility for scenarios that mix models (e.g., using Model A in the first round and Model Kimi-K2.5 in the second round). - Streaming Robustness: The original streaming parser had issues with special token leakage and incomplete state management. Related Issues: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/18086 ## Modifications ### Reasoning Parser 1. New KimiK2Detector Class (inherits from Qwen3Detector) Force exit reasoning mode, return content before marker as reasoning_text, content from marker onwards as normal_text ### Function Call Detector 1. UUID Format Support Extended regex patterns to support both standard and UUID formats 3. Function Name Inference New `_infer_function_name_from_args()` method for UUID format 4. Robust State Management Added proper state tracking and reset methods 5. Special Token Leakage Prevention Comprehensive token filtering to prevent special tokens from leaking to normal_text 6. Improved Streaming State Machine Refactored `parse_streaming_increment()` with clearer state transitions 7. signals.title: [Scheduler] Add early finish check for overlap mode to prevent redundant decode
signals.text: ## Motivation Based on [#18165](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/18165), we find redundant decode in overlap mode, not only for requests with attribute max_tokens=1, but all requests due to overlap mechanism, which would not check results after forward immediately. Problem: In event_loop_overlap scheduling mode, when a request reaches its max_tokens limit, it cannot terminate early before the next batch starts. This causes redundant decode iterations because: 1. Batch N completes forward pass 2. Batch N+1 is prepared and started before batch N's results are processed 3. Requests that reached max_tokens in batch N are incorrectly included in batch N+1, wasting GPU compute ## Modifications Add environment variable SGLANG_ENABLE_OVERLAP_EARLY_FINISH_CHECK (default: false) to enable early termination check in get_next_batch_to_run(). When enabled: - Checks current output_ids length against max_new_tokens before batch preparation - Marks requests with to_finish flag if they've reached the limit - Filters them out to prevent inclusion in the next batch ## Accuracy Tests <!-- If this pull request affects model outputs (e.g., changes to the kernel or model forward code), provide accuracy test results. --> ## Benchmarking and Profiling <!-- If this pull request impacts inference speed, provide benchmarking and profiling results. --> ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review Process 1. signals.title: feat: Add proportion-based scheduler for router selection
signals.text: <!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. --> ## Motivation In real-world production environments, LLM inference workloads are rarely uniform. They typically consist of a mix of requests with varying prompt lengths. Sgl-router offers two highly effective yet specialized router, each with distinct performance characteristics: * Regular router: It can achieve very high QPS for chat-like workloads. * PD router: The prefill and decode stages are handled by separate, specialized workers. This architecture is exceptionally efficient for long-prompt requests. This hybrid scheduling approach delivers significant performance and efficiency gains, primarily by: * Maximizing QPS: By routing short-prompt requests to regular router and long-prompt requests to PD router, the system prevents either workload type from creating a bottleneck. This specialization allows each part of the cluster to operate at its peak efficiency, dramatically increasing the total QPS the system can handle for mixed workloads. * Reducing TTFT and Preventing Head-of-Line Blocking: Long-prompt requests are a primary cause of high latency, not just for themselves, but for all other requests due to head-of-line blocking in a standard worker queue. * Isolate Heavyweight Tasks: We prevent long prefill computations from blocking the processing of short, interactive queries. * Accelerate Long Prompts: We leverage the PD cluster's specialized design to reduce the TTFT for these complex requests. ## Modifications ### Proportion Scheduler #### Crossover Point Adjustment Goal: Find a single crossover point T_c (a token count) that splits the total token load of recent requests proportionally between Regular and PD worker pools, based on their respective capacities. Algorithm Steps (runs every adjust_interval) 1. Calculate Ideal Share: Determine the ideal load share S_ideal for the Regular pool using the current worker counts and weights. * S_ideal = (N_reg * W_reg) / ( (N_reg * W_reg) + N_pd ) * N_reg: Number of active Regular workers. * N_pd: Number of active PD workers. * W_reg: The configured regular_worker_weight. 2. Analyze Recent Load: Collect all token counts T_i from the current request history queue. Calculate the total load in this window, L_total = Σ T_i. 3. Determine Crossover T_c: * Sort the collected token counts in ascending order to get T_sorted. * Linearly scan T_sorted, accumulating load: L_accum += T_i. * When the running sum L_accum first meets or exceeds the target proportional load (L_accum / L_total ≥ S_ideal), set T_c to the current token count T_i and stop. Complexity: O(M log M) due to sorting the M requests in the time window. #### Routing Scheduler (per request) 1. Load-Imbalance Guard: First, check if the normalized load on one router type significantly exceeds the other (beyond configured balance_abs_threshold and balance_rel_threshold). If so, immediately route the request to the less-loaded pool, bypassing the crossover logic. 2. Crossover Logic: If the system is balanced, compare the incoming request's token count T with the current crossover point T_c. * If T ≤ T_c, route to the Regular pool. * If T > T_c, route to the PD pool. Complexity: O(1). ### Modify Bucket Policy The existing BucketPolicy was designed exclusively for Prefill/Decode (PD) disaggregated deployments. This PR extends its functionality to support Regular (non-disaggregated) workers, enabling bucket-based routing in a wider range of deployment scenarios. Step | Description -- | -- 1.1 Worker Detection | A new step is added during the server's initialization phase to detect if the default routing policy is bucket. 1.2 Grouping | If the bucket policy is active, the system now retrieves all active Regular workers from the WorkerRegistry. These workers are then grouped by their model_id. 1.3 Initialization | For each model group, the BucketPolicy now calls a new method, init_regular_worker_urls. This method initializes or updates the corresponding model's bucket with the URLs of the Regular workers, just as it previously did for Prefill workers. 2. Unified Bucket Logic The internal logic of the Bucket struct (including threshold adjustment and worker selection) is reused for both Regular and PD worker pools. The key change is in the initialization path: the policy can now be populated with worker URLs from either Prefill workers (in a PD setup) or Regular workers (in a regular setup). 3. Routing Decision (Impact) When a request arrives and the bucket policy is active for a Regular router, it now correctly locates the appropriate bucket for the request's model. It then uses the established bucket thresholds to select a Regular worker from that bucket's pool, applying the same load-balancing and imbalance-guarding logic that was previously only available for Prefill workers. ## Benchmarking and Profiling ### Test Command: 1. regular & pd worker ``` python -m sglang.launch_server \ --model-path /workspace/model \ --served-model-name Qwen3 \ --tp 1 \ --trust-remote-code \ --host 0.0.0.0 \ --port 9001 \ --mem-fraction-static 0.70 \ --attention-backend fa3 \ --page-size 64 \ --max-running-requests 48 \ --cuda-graph-max-bs 16 \ --chunked-prefill-size 2048 \ --disable-radix-cache \ --dtype auto \ --kv-cache-dtype auto \ --context-length 32768 \ --log-level info \ --disable-cuda-graph \ --enable-metrics python -m sglang.launch_server \ --model-path /workspace/model \ --served-model-name Qwen3/32B \ --tp 1 \ --trust-remote-code \ --disaggregation-mode prefill \ --disaggregation-bootstrap-port 30001 \ --host 0.0.0.0 \ --port 9002 \ --mem-fraction-static 0.70 \ --attention-backend fa3 \ --page-size 64 \ --max-running-requests 48 \ --cuda-graph-max-bs 48 \ --chunked-prefill-size 2048 \ --disable-radix-cache \ --dtype auto \ --kv-cache-dtype auto \ --context-length 32768 \ --log-level debug \ --enable-cache-report \ --enable-metrics python -m sglang.launch_server \ --model-path /workspace/model \ --served-model-name Qwen3/32B \ --trust-remote-code \ --disaggregation-mode decode \ --host 0.0.0.0 \ --port 9003 \ --mem-fraction-static 0.70 \ --tp 1 \ --max-running-requests 48 \ --chunked-prefill-size 2048 \ --attention-backend fa3 \ --page-size 64 \ --cuda-graph-max-bs 48 \ --disable-radix-cache \ --dtype auto \ --kv-cache-dtype auto \ --context-length 32768 \ --log-level debug \ --enable-cache-report \ --enable-metrics ``` 2. 2p4d(pd-disaggregation) ``` python3 -m sglang_router.launch_router \ --pd-disaggregation \ --prefill http://33.181.225.19:9001 30001 \ --prefill http://33.181.225.19:9002 30002 \ --decode http://33.184.122.82:9001 \ --decode http://33.184.122.82:9002 \ --decode http://33.184.122.82:9003 \ --decode http://33.184.122.82:9004 \ --policy random ``` 3. 1r2p3d(enable-igw) ``` python3 -m sglang_router.launch_router \ --enable-igw \ --scheduler-strategy proportion \ --scheduler-balance-abs-threshold 2000 \ --scheduler-balance-rel-threshold 1.0001 \ --scheduler-regular-worker-weight 0.4 \ --scheduler-adjust-interval-secs 1 \ --scheduler-adjust-window-sec 5 \ --policy bucket \ --balance-rel-threshold 1.0001 \ --balance-abs-threshold 3200 \ --bucket-adjust-interval-secs 1 ``` 3. benchmark ``` export HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 python3 -m sglang.bench_serving \ --backend sglang-oai \ --base-url "http://127.0.0.1:30000" \ --model "Qwen3/32B" \ --tokenizer "/workspace/Qwen3-32B" \ --max-concurrency 150 \ --request-rate inf \ --dataset-name random-ids \ --random-input-len 4096 \ --random-output-len 1536 \ --num-prompts 500 \ --random-range-ratio 0.1 \ --output-file "test_dynamoic.json" ``` ### conclusion To better evaluate the performance of the PDR hybrid strategy, I conducted two sets of experiments using 12 H20 GPUs. The control group had a PD ratio of 2:4, which is the best PD separation ratio given a constant total number of GPUs. The experimental group had a PDR ratio of 2:3:1, which is also the best configuration. Here we set a service level SLO, with P50 TTFT at 3000ms and TTOT P99 at 100ms. Then we continuously increase the concurrency to obtain the maximum performance of the two sets of experiments. Metric Category | Metric | Scenario A (150 Concurrency) | Scenario B (180 Concurrency) | Change -- | -- | -- | -- | -- QPS & Throughput | Request Throughput (QPS) | 3.43 req/s | 3.70 req/s | +7.87% | Output Token Throughput | 2869.49 tok/s | 3098.12 tok/s | +7.97% | Total Token Throughput | 10646.16 tok/s | 11497.41 tok/s | +7.80% Time to First Token | Mean TTFT | 6536.12 ms | 6021.32 ms | -7.88% | Median (P50) TTFT | 2723.44 ms | 2221.30 ms | -18.44% | P99 TTFT (Tail Latency) | 30204.30 ms | 28186.24 ms | -6.68% 1. Throughput and QPS: Request Throughput (QPS) saw a substantial 7.87% increase, rising from 3.43 to 3.70 req/s. Output Token Throughput grew by 7.97%, from 2869 tok/s to 3098.12 tok/s. This indicates a clear enhancement in the system's overall processing capacity and efficiency. 2. Time to First Token (TTFT): The user-perceived initial response time improved, with Mean TTFT decreasing by 7.88%. Median TTFT decreasing by 18.44% and P99 TTFT decreasing by 6.68%, optimize overall long-tail latency. In summary, the changes successfully boosted the system's throughput while simultaneously improving the average and tail-end latencies for Time to First Token, showcasing a more robust and higher-capacity serving performance. ## Checklist - [ ] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [ ] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review Process 1. signals.title: fix: avoid shutdown hang on warmup thread
signals.text: <!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. --> ## Motivation When `uvicorn` fails to bind (e.g., the port is already in use), the HTTP server process hangs for around 120 seconds before exiting. The reason is: 1. The warmup thread keeps polling `/model_info` and may run for up to 120s. 2. In the FastAPI lifespan handler, the `finally` block calls `warmup_thread.join()`, which blocks indefinitely while waiting for the thread. 3. After `uvicorn.run()` returns, Python’s internal `threading._shutdown()` also waits for non-daemon threads, causing another blocking point. As a result, the process appears stuck instead of exiting promptly. ## Modifications - Set `daemon=True` when creating the warmup thread so interpreter shutdown does not wait for it. - Change the explicit join in lifespan to use a timeout: `warmup_thread.join(timeout=5.0)` This prevents indefinite blocking during shutdown and allows the process to exit quickly if startup fails. ## Notes - `grpc_server.py` already contains similar explicit cleanup logic. - This change only affects shutdown behavior when the server fails to start. - Normal warmup and serving flow are unchanged. ## Checklist - [ ] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [ ] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review Process 1. ## Motivation Addresses #18935 Added Prometheus metrics to diffusion serving This adds Prometheus `/metrics` support for SGLang-Diffusion serving. It reports metrics through a small observer layer ```mermaid flowchart TD SCHED["Scheduler"] STAGE["StageProfiler"] WORKER["GPUWorker
(LoRA status updates)"] SCHED --> OBS["DiffusionObserver"] STAGE --> OBS WORKER --> OBS OBS --> NOOP["NoopDiffusionObserver"] OBS --> POBS["PrometheusDiffusionObserver"] POBS --> COLLECTOR["DiffusionMetricsCollector"] COLLECTOR --> REG["prometheus_client multiprocess registry"] HTTP["/metrics endpoint"] --> REG ``` Runtime code reports events to `DiffusionObserver`; `PrometheusDiffusionObserver` records them as Prometheus metrics, and the no-op observer is used when metrics are disabled. ## Metrics Added - `sglang:diffusion_num_queue_reqs` - `sglang:diffusion_num_running_reqs` - `sglang:diffusion_requests_total` - `sglang:diffusion_request_latency_seconds` - `sglang:diffusion_queue_time_seconds` - `sglang:diffusion_generation_batch_size` - `sglang:diffusion_stage_latency_seconds` (which will populate with labels like `InputValidationStage`, `TextEncodingStage`, `DenoisingStep` etc.) - `sglang:diffusion_lora_loaded_adapters` - `sglang:diffusion_lora_active_modules` - `sglang:diffusion_lora_active_adapters` - `sglang:diffusion_lora_module_active` Dynamic batches are counted per original client request after the merged output is split, not per merged GPU forward. ## Validation 1x H100 with `black-forest-labs/FLUX.2-klein-4B`. Command: ```bash PYTHONPATH=python python -m sglang.multimodal_gen.runtime.launch_server \ --model-path black-forest-labs/FLUX.2-klein-4B \ --host 0.0.0.0 \ --port 30000 \ --enable-metrics \ --batching-max-size 4 \ --batching-delay-ms 250 \ --enable-batching-metrics ``` ### Non-Merged Request I sent one image request. The scheduler dispatched it alone: ```text Dynamic batch dispatch: size=1/4, user_max=4, queue_wait=250.00ms, stop_reason=delay Completed batch processing. Generated 1 outputs in 3.80 seconds ``` metrics after the single request: ```text sglang:diffusion_queue_time_seconds_count{is_warmup="false"} 1.0 sglang:diffusion_generation_batch_size_count{stop_reason="delay"} 1.0 sglang:diffusion_request_latency_seconds_count{is_warmup="false",status="success"} 1.0 sglang:diffusion_requests_total{is_warmup="false",status="success"} 1.0 ``` ### Merged Dynamic Batch I sent four compatible concurrent image requests. The scheduler merged them into one dynamic batch: ```text Dynamic batch dispatch: size=4/4, user_max=4, queue_wait=2.17ms, stop_reason=config_cap:4 Processed dynamic batch of 4/4 request(s) with max_delay=250.00ms ``` all four client requests returned HTTP 200 with one output each. Metrics after the concurrent run: ```text sglang:diffusion_queue_time_seconds_count{is_warmup="false"} 5.0 sglang:diffusion_generation_batch_size_count{stop_reason="delay"} 1.0 sglang:diffusion_generation_batch_size_count{stop_reason="config_cap"} 1.0 sglang:diffusion_request_latency_seconds_count{is_warmup="false",status="success"} 5.0 sglang:diffusion_requests_total{is_warmup="false",status="success"} 5.0 ``` ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): :x: [Run #26116423223](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/26116423223) Latest PR Test (Extra): :warning: **Not enabled** -- add `run-ci-extra` label to opt in.

signals.title: [Perf] O(1) expert weight matching in DeepSeek weight loader
signals.text: ## Motivation Large MoE models like GLM-5 with 256 routed experts generate hundreds of thousands of weight tensors. The original weight loading code used an O(N*M) algorithm (linear scan of 771+ mapping entries for each tensor), causing weight loading to take 25-40+ minutes on Blackwell GPUs. ## Modifications Replaced the O(N*M) linear scan with an O(1) dict lookup: 1. Pre-build a dict mapping projection names → (param_name, shard_id) from expert_params_mapping 2. Use regex to extract expert_id and projection name from weight names 3. Perform single dict lookup instead of scanning all 771 entries per tensor 4. Added comprehensive unit tests validating against real HuggingFace model weight maps ## Benchmarking and Profiling Measured on nvidia/DeepSeek-R1-NVFP4 (256 experts, 180,364 weight tensors): | Metric | Before | After | Speedup | |--------|--------|-------|---------| | **Total matching time** | 6.67s | 0.13s | **50x** | | **Per-tensor latency** | 36.9 μs | 0.7 μs | **50x** | | **String comparisons** | ~179M | 0 | — | ## Accuracy Tests All 10 unit tests pass, verifying bit-for-bit identical matching results on all three test models (DeepSeek-V3.2, DeepSeek-V3, DeepSeek-R1-NVFP4). No changes to model behavior—pure optimization. ## Checklist - [x] Code follows SGLang style guidelines - [x] Unit tests added and passing (3 correctness tests + 7 threshold tests) - [x] Performance benchmarked against real model weight maps

signals.title: feat(disagg): KV return — reverse RDMA transfer from decode to prefill
signals.text: ## Summary Adds **KV return**: when a disaggregated decode worker finishes generating tokens, it transfers the generated KV cache back to the originating prefill worker via NIXL RDMA and inserts it into the prefill's RadixCache. This enables multi-turn cache hits without re-computing prefill for prior conversation turns. **Key design choices:** - **On-demand page allocation**: Decode requests destination pages from prefill via ZMQ round-trip (no pre-reserved pools). Prefill can decline under memory pressure. - **Async post-and-poll**: `_try_kv_return()` posts the alloc request non-blocking; `_poll_kv_return_replies()` handles alloc replies and RDMA completions from the scheduler event loop. Decode scheduler never blocks on KV return. - **Page-aligned insertion**: Returned KV is truncated to `floor(N/page_size) * page_size` tokens to match RadixCache page boundaries. ## Changes **9 commits, 1,744 lines across 13 files:** | File | Purpose | |------|---------| | `server_args.py` | `--enable-kv-return` flag | | `disaggregation/nixl/conn.py` | NIXL reverse RDMA transport, ZMQ metadata/alloc channels, prefill-side insertion receiver | | `managers/scheduler.py` | `_process_kv_return_alloc_requests()`, `_process_kv_return_insertions()`, memory accounting, poll integration | | `managers/scheduler_output_processor_mixin.py` | `_try_kv_return()` (async post), `_poll_kv_return_replies()` (non-blocking poll), `_start_kv_return_rdma()` (RDMA helper), `PendingKvReturn` state machine | | `managers/scheduler_runtime_checker_mixin.py` | Idle-path poll + alloc processing, queue size accounting for pending KV returns | | `disaggregation/decode.py` | Decode-side integration hook | | `disaggregation/fake/conn.py` | Stub for non-NIXL backends | | `test_kv_return_insertion_unit.py` | 261-line CPU-only unit test (insertion, dedup, memory accounting) | | `test_kv_return_2worker.sh` | Single-GPU integration test | | `test_kv_return_multiturn.sh` | 3-request multi-turn flow (cold → cache hit → partial prefix) | ## Bugs Found & Fixed | ID | Bug | Discovery | Fix | Commit | |----|-----|-----------|-----|--------| | B1 | `_process_kv_return_alloc_requests()` missing from scheduler idle path → 0% cache hits | Same-GPU test | Added to dict from earlier implementation | Code review | Removed | `5e17e661` | | B2 | Alloc serialization under 5x concurrent — sync ZMQ round-trip caused 52.8ms blocking | Cross-node test | Refactored to async post-and-poll (`PendingKvReturn` state machine) | `5f09b75c` | | R2 | Duplicated RDMA-start logic in 2 code paths | Code review (C2) | Extracted `_start_kv_return_rdma()` helper | `0a4aacff` | | Failures | Key Result | |------|----------|-----------|----------|------------| | 10x concurrent burst | 10 | 10 | 0 | ~2.14s batched, 4 pages/req | | Photosynthesis (3 turns) | 3 | 3 | 0 | 67% → 9% → 50% cache hits | | Neural networks (3 turns) | 3 | 3 | 0 | 0% → 9% → 51% cache hits | | Climate (4 turns) | 4 | 4 | 0 | 0% → 10% → 51% → 66% cache hits | | **Subtotal** | **22** | **22** | **0** | Progressive multi-turn caching confirmed | ### Sustained Load (bench_serving, Qwen3-8B, 2x H100-PCIe) `bench_serving --dataset-name random --num-prompts 500 --random-input-len 256 --random-output-len 128 --request-rate 4 --max-concurrency 16` | Metric | Value | |--------|-------| | **Successful requests** | 500/500 (100%) | | **Duration** | 118.4s | | **Request throughput** | 4.22 req/s | | **Total throughput** | 842 tok/s | | **Mean E2E latency** | 1088ms | | **P99 E2E latency** | 2603ms | | **Mean TTFT** | 255ms | | **Median TPOT** | 12.5ms | | **P99 ITL** | 72.3ms | | **KV return attempts** | 497 | | **KV return RDMA succeeded** | 445 | | **KV return declined (pool full)** | 0 | | **NIXL RDMA failures** | **0** | | **Crashes / deadlocks** | 0 | | **Page leaks** | 0 | **Bug fix (838135b)**: Earlier runs showed permanent `NIXL_ERR_NOT_FOUND` failures. Root cause was a page-index bug in the reverse RDMA path — source KV indices were not divided by `page_size`, causing RDMA source addresses to be `page_size`× too large and exceeding the registered memory region. The forward path (prefill→decode) correctly used `kv_to_page_indices()` but the reverse path (decode→prefill) did not. Fixed in `838135b`. ### Memory Pressure (60K token pool) Prefill deployed with `--mem-fraction-static 0.30` → 60,048 token pool (3,753 pages). 200 requests at 4 req/s with 256-token prompts and 512-token outputs: | Outcome | Count | |---------|-------| | Allocs granted | 412 | | Allocs declined (pool full) | 33 | | NIXL RDMA failures | **0** | | Requests completed | **500/500 (100%)** | When the pool reaches `avail=0`, the prefill declines subsequent alloc requests with empty replies. Decode detects the empty reply, logs `"prefill declined alloc"`, calls `release_kv_cache()`, and skips RDMA — no crash, no data corruption, no impact to user requests. KV return declines are entirely transparent to end users. ### Aggregate | Metric | Value | |--------|-------| | **Total KV returns** | **445+** | | **RDMA failures** | **0** | | **Page leaks** | **0** | | **Models tested** | Qwen3-0.6B, Qwen3-8B | | **Concurrency tested** | 1x, 5x, 10x, 20x | | **Multi-turn sessions** | 7 (3-4 turns each, two model sizes) | | **Sustained load** | 500 requests at 4 req/s, 0 RDMA failures, 445 KV returns | | **Memory pressure** | 500 requests against 60K-token pool, 33 graceful declines, 0 RDMA failures | ### Multi-Turn Cache Hit Pattern Each conversation shows progressive cache accumulation: ``` Turn 1: 0% hit (cold start) Turn 2: ~9-10% hit (only original prompt prefix matches) Turn 3: ~50% hit (Turn 1+2 KV now in cache) Turn 4: ~66% hit (Turn 1+2+3 KV accumulated) ``` Cache alignment: `floor(N/page_size) * page_size` — e.g., 128 generated tokens with page_size=16 → 8 pages returned. ## Configuration ```bash # Prefill worker python3 -m sglang.launch_server \ --disaggregation-mode prefill \ --disaggregation-transfer-backend nixl \ --enable-kv-return \ --page-size 16 # Decode worker python3 -m sglang.launch_server \ --disaggregation-mode decode \ --disaggregation-transfer-backend nixl \ --enable-kv-return \ --page-size 16 ``` `--enable-kv-return` is opt-in and has no effect when disaggregation is not enabled. ## Test plan - [x] Unit tests: `test_kv_return_insertion_unit.py` (CPU-only, page alignment, dedup, memory accounting) - [x] Same-GPU integration: `test_kv_return_2worker.sh` (single H100, basic P↔D transfer) - [x] Multi-turn integration: `test_kv_return_multiturn.sh` (3-request flow: cold → cache hit → partial prefix) - [x] Cross-node RDMA: 2x H100-PCIe, Qwen3-0.6B (5x/10x/20x concurrent, multi-turn chain) - [x] 8B model: 2x H100-PCIe, Qwen3-8B (10x concurrent, 3 multi-turn sessions with 3-4 turns) - [x] Async KV return (C2): scheduler non-blocking under concurrent load - [x] Sustained load: `bench_serving` 500 requests at 4 req/s — 100% success, 0 RDMA failures, 445 KV returns succeeded - [x] Memory pressure: `--mem-fraction-static 0.30` (60K pool) — 500 requests, 33 graceful declines under pressure, 0 RDMA failures

signals.title: [DLLM] [BUG] Fix topk kernel bug for lower arch
signals.text: ## Motivation FlashInfer's `fused_topk_deepseek` only supports compute capability 89, 90, 100, 103, 120, 121, and does not support lower archs like sm_86. Running MoE models (LLaDA2.0) on sm_86 GPUs raises `BackendSupportedError`. This PR adds a capability check and falls back to `moe_fused_gate` or `biased_grouped_topk_impl` on unsupported architectures. ## Modifications - **topk.py**: Add `get_device_capability()` check before using `fused_topk_deepseek`; when capability is not in `[89, 90, 100, 103, 120, 121]`, use the existing fallback path instead. ## Testing - **test_llada2_mini**: Add `test_for_lower_arch`, mocking sm_86 to verify the fallback path. - Manually verified on RTX 3090 with TP 8: LLaDA2.0 server starts and runs without `BackendSupportedError`. ## Checklist - [x] Format code - [x] Add unit tests - [ ] Update documentation (N/A) - [ ] Benchmark (N/A – correctness-only fix) - [x] Follow SGLang code style

signals.text: <!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. --> ## Motivation <!-- Describe the purpose and goals of this pull request. --> 1. Fuse the element-wise operations at the end of block i (`MulAdd`) and the beginning of block i+1 (`LayerNormScaleShift`) into a single `ScaleResidualLayerNormScaleShift` kernel to reduce kernel launches and improve efficiency. 2. Store null_gate, null_shift, and null_scale as attributes instead of recreating them in each block during the forward pass, reducing repeated tensor allocations and runtime overhead. 3. Modified block inputs and outputs to propagate residual, ff_output, and c_gate_msa between blocks, improving data flow. ## Modifications <!-- Detail the changes made in this pull request. --> ## Accuracy Tests <!-- If this pull request affects model outputs (e.g., changes to the kernel or model forward code), provide accuracy test results. --> ## Wan2.2 benchmark: Test input image: ![ikun](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5ea81548-b369-404a-81da-a149cde3a67c) ### command ```bash CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES="0,1,2,3,4,5,6,7" sglang generate \ --model-path "Wan-AI/Wan2.2-I2V-A14B-Diffusers" \ --attention-backend fa \ --trust-remote-code \ --num-gpus 8 \ --ulysses-degree 8 \ --use-fsdp-inference false \ --dit-cpu-offload false \ --dit-layerwise-offload false \ --text-encoder-cpu-offload false \ --image-encoder-cpu-offload false \ --vae-cpu-offload false \ --pin-cpu-memory false \ --backend sglang \ --num-frames 81 \ --fps 16 \ --height 720 \ --width 1280 \ --num-inference-steps 40 \ --prompt "一位名叫蔡徐坤的中国男明星站在室外篮球场中央，夕阳的金色光线洒在球场上。他手持篮球，深情而自信地凝望镜头。镜头缓慢推进，他开始运球，在球场上做出流畅的篮球动作。随着节奏感强烈的音乐，他一边打篮球一边跳舞，将篮球动作与舞蹈动作自然结合。他的身材修长而结实，动作充满节奏感和魅力，舞步干净利落，充满舞台表现力。篮球在地面弹跳，他转身、运球、投篮，同时加入优雅又富有力量感的舞蹈动作。整体氛围充满运动活力与男性魅力，画面具有电影质感，慢动作镜头、动态跟拍、光影细节丰富，4K，high detail，cinematic lighting。" \ --image-path "ikun.jpeg" \ --warmup \ --save-output ``` ### log: - main: ```text [02-27 07:26:49] Running pipeline stages: ['input_validation_stage', 'text_encoding_stage', 'image_v_a_e_encoding_stage', 'latent_preparation_stage', 'timestep_preparation_stage', 'denoising_stage', 'decoding_stage'] [02-27 07:26:49] [InputValidationStage] started... signals.title: [Quantization] Fix per-tensor FP8 MoE parameter identity for EPLB hot-reload
signals.text: ## Motivation When using per-tensor FP8 quantized MoE models (e.g., `RedHatAI/DeepSeek-Coder-V2-Lite-Instruct-FP8`) with Elastic EP Load Balancing (EPLB), the failover weight hot-reload crashes with: ``` AttributeError: 'Parameter' object has no attribute 'weight_loader' ``` followed by (after working around the above): ``` RuntimeError: mat1 and mat2 shapes cannot be multiplied (2x2048 and 1536x2048) ``` This was also mentioned in https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/18191. **Issue 1 — Parameter identity loss in per-tensor FP8 MoE** `Fp8MoEMethod.process_weights_after_loading()` creates new `Parameter` objects via `torch.nn.Parameter(...)` for `w13_input_scale`, `w2_input_scale`, and `w13_weight_scale`. This destroys custom attributes (`weight_loader`, `quant_method`) that `deepseek_weight_loader.py` relies on during EPLB hot-reload. The block-quant path was already fixed in #17449 via `_copy_or_rebind()`, but the per-tensor path was never updated. **Issue 2 — Double `process_weights_after_loading` on partial reload** `update_weights_from_disk()` calls `load_weights_and_postprocess()`, which runs `process_weights_after_loading()` on **all** quantized modules unconditionally — even when only expert weights were reloaded. For FP8 linear attention layers (e.g., `q_proj`), this means the weight gets transposed twice (once during initial load, once during reload), corrupting the shape from `[K, N]` back to `[N, K]`. ## Modifications ### `python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/fp8.py` **Dynamic-quant path** (non-checkpoint FP8): - Use `.data =` for weight rebinding and `.data[expert].fill_()` for scale updates instead of `Parameter` replacement. **Checkpoint-FP8 path — `input_scale` merging:** - Replace `torch.nn.Parameter(max_val)` with `layer.w13_input_scale.data.fill_(max_val)` to preserve the original `Parameter` object in-place. **Checkpoint-FP8 path — `w13_weight_scale` merging:** - Instead of replacing the `[E, 2]` Parameter with a new `[E]` one, fill both columns with the same per-expert max in-place. The `[E, 2]` shape is preserved so `weight_loader` can still index `param.data[expert_id][shard_idx]` during reload. **`apply()` — DeepGEMM path:** - Add `ndim == 2` guard to collapse `w13_weight_scale` from `[E, 2]` to `[E]` via `[:, 0]` before expanding to block shape. ### `python/sglang/srt/model_executor/model_runner.py` **Partial reload isolation:** - When `weight_name_filter` is set (EPLB expert rebalancing), split `load_weights` and `process_weights_after_loading` into two steps, only calling the latter on modules whose names match the filter. This prevents double-processing of attention layers and other non-expert modules. ## Accuracy Tests Validated with `test_mooncake_ep_small.py` (use DeepSeek-Coder-V2-Lite-Instruct-FP8): 7/7 tests passed. ![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7ed0ab46-5794-4cd1-a930-32e93a7ef841) ## Benchmarking and Profiling <!-- If this pull request impacts inference speed, provide benchmarking and profiling results. --> ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [ ] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review Process 1. signals.title: [Feature] Implement image number limitation for image processors
signals.text: ## Motivation Fixes #8540 Currently, there is no default limitation on the number of images during multimodal data processing. The only existing check (`_validate_mm_limits` in TokenizerManager) only runs if the admin explicitly sets `--limit-mm-data-per-request`, which defaults to `None`. Without this, a user could send an excessive number of images, each consuming ~1GB GPU memory via the fast image processor, potentially causing OOM. This PR adds a per-processor default image limit as a safety net. ## Modifications **`python/sglang/srt/multimodal/processors/base_processor.py`:** - Added `IMAGE_NUM_LIMITATION = 5` class constant to `BaseMultimodalProcessor` - Added `_get_image_limit()` helper method that returns the effective limit (CLI override takes priority over processor default) - Added image count validation in `load_mm_data()` before any images are downloaded **`python/sglang/srt/multimodal/processors/internvl.py`:** - Added `IMAGE_NUM_LIMITATION = 12` override (InternVL supports more images) **`test/unit/test_image_num_limitation.py`:** - Unit tests covering: default limit, subclass override, CLI override priority, within-limit pass-through, exceeds-limit rejection ## Priority Order `--limit-mm-data-per-request` CLI flag > processor `IMAGE_NUM_LIMITATION` constant > no protection ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). - [ ] Work with maintainers to merge your PR. signals.title: [EPLB] Add topology-aware expert placement algorithm
signals.text: ## Summary Implements a topology-aware Expert Parallel Load Balancing (EPLB) algorithm that reduces cross-node RDMA traffic by **25.2%** while maintaining comparable decode performance for DeepSeek-R1 inference, fix #19487 ## Problem The default DeepSeek hierarchical EPLB algorithm places redundant experts without considering network topology, resulting in high cross-node traffic during expert dispatch. In multi-node deployments with Expert Parallelism (EP) spanning across nodes, this causes: - Increased RDMA communication overhead - Higher latency for expert token routing - Suboptimal network bandwidth utilization ## Solution The topology-aware EPLB algorithm: 1. **Prioritizes node locality** - Places redundant experts on the same node as their primary experts 2. **Minimizes cross-node dispatches** - Reduces inter-node communication while maintaining load balance 3. **Greedy allocation strategy** - Optimizes expert placement based on network topology ## Benchmark Results **Configuration:** - Model: DeepSeek-R1-0528 (256 experts + 64 redundant) - Hardware: 8xH20, Decode: EP=16 across 2 nodes (DP=16) - Workload: 200 prompts, max concurrency 200 ### Cross-Node Traffic Reduction | Algorithm | Cross-Node Ratio | Improvement | |-----------|------------------|-------------| | DeepSeek r64 | 0.5038 | baseline | | Topology-Aware r64 | 0.3770 | **-25.2%** | ### Decode Performance | Metric | DeepSeek r64 | Topology-Aware r64 | Change | |--------|--------------|-------------------|--------| | Mean ITL (ms) | 49.84 | 49.29 | -1.1% | | Mean TPOT (ms) | 36.72 | 36.15 | -1.6% | | Output Throughput (tok/s) | 4154 | 4223 | +1.7% | ## Key Findings | Metric | Result | |--------|--------| | Cross-Node Traffic | **-25.2%** reduction (0.50 → 0.38) | | Output Throughput | **+1.7%** improvement | | ITL/TPOT | Comparable or slightly better | ## Recommendation Use **Topology-Aware EPLB with 64 redundant experts** for: - Significant reduction in cross-node RDMA traffic - Slight improvement in decode throughput - Better network efficiency in multi-node deployments This is especially beneficial for: - Multi-node inference clusters with RDMA networking - High-concurrency production workloads - Cost-sensitive deployments where network bandwidth is a constraint ## Usage The benchmark results use **static dispatch** with a pre-generated expert location file. ### Step 1: Generate Expert Location File ```bash python eplb/generate_expert_location.py \ --algorithm topology_aware \ --output expert-location-topology-aware-r64.json \ --num-logical-experts 256 \ --num-redundant-experts 64 \ --num-gpus 16 \ --num-nodes 2 \ --num-groups 128 ``` ### Step 2: Deploy with Static Dispatch ```bash python -m sglang.launch_server \ --model-path /models/DeepSeek-R1-0528/ \ --tp 16 --dp 16 \ --ep-num-redundant-experts 64 \ --init-expert-location expert-location-topology-aware-r64.json \ --ep-dispatch-algorithm static ``` ### Step 3: Monitor Cross-Node Traffic (Optional) ```bash python -m sglang.launch_server \ --model-path /models/DeepSeek-R1-0528/ \ --tp 16 --dp 16 \ --ep-num-redundant-experts 64 \ --init-expert-location expert-location-topology-aware-r64.json \ --ep-dispatch-algorithm static \ --expert-distribution-recorder-mode per_pass \ --enable-expert-distribution-metrics ``` ### Monitoring Logs Example When `--enable-expert-distribution-metrics` is enabled, cross-node traffic is logged per forward pass: ``` [Expert Balancedness] forward_pass_id=100 balancedness=0.603 avg10=0.590 avg100=0.585 avg1000=0.548 cross_node_ratio=0.377 tokens=92800 [Expert Balancedness] forward_pass_id=101 balancedness=0.595 avg10=0.591 avg100=0.584 avg1000=0.549 cross_node_ratio=0.381 tokens=92800 [Expert Balancedness] forward_pass_id=102 balancedness=0.603 avg10=0.592 avg100=0.585 avg1000=0.550 cross_node_ratio=0.373 tokens=92800 ``` - **balancedness**: Expert utilization rate (higher = better load balance) - **cross_node_ratio**: Fraction of expert accesses crossing node boundaries (lower = less RDMA traffic) - **tokens**: Total tokens processed in this forward pass ## Testing - [x] Benchmarked with 200 prompts on 4-node cluster - [x] Verified 25.2% cross-node traffic reduction - [x] Confirmed decode performance parity - [x] Generated step-by-step visualization

signals.title: Fix conv_states dtype mismatch when using --dtype half with Mamba models
signals.text: ## Motivation Fix https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/19773 I reproduce this bug using ``` # For simplicity I use 9B model python -m sglang.launch_server --model-path Qwen/Qwen3.5-9B --dtype half # And send a request curl -s http://localhost:30000/v1/completions \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"model": "default", "prompt": "Write a long story about", "max_tokens": 256}' ``` ``` RuntimeError: Expected conv_states_.scalar_type() == input_type to be true, but got false. ``` **Root cause:** The Mamba `conv_states` cache is allocated using the dtype from [`mamba2_state_dtype()`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/python/sglang/srt/configs/mamba_utils.py#L68), which defaults to `bfloat16` (hardcoded via [`SGLANG_MAMBA_CONV_DTYPE`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/python/sglang/srt/environ.py#L443) env var default). When the user passes `--dtype half`, model activations are `float16`, but conv_states remain `bfloat16`. The `causal_conv1d` kernel rejects this mismatch. The existing workaround in [`test_generation_models.py`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/test/registered/models/test_generation_models.py#L151-L152) explicitly sets `SGLANG_MAMBA_CONV_DTYPE` to match the inference dtype, confirming this is a known gap. ## Modifications **[`python/sglang/srt/configs/model_config.py`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/python/sglang/srt/configs/model_config.py#L200)** - After `_get_and_verify_dtype()` resolves the final dtype, sync it back to `hf_text_config.torch_dtype` so downstream consumers can read the actual running dtype. **[`python/sglang/srt/configs/mamba_utils.py`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/python/sglang/srt/configs/mamba_utils.py#L68)** - In `mamba2_state_dtype()`, use `envs.SGLANG_MAMBA_CONV_DTYPE.is_set()` to distinguish between a user-explicit env var and the default. - When the user has **not** explicitly set the env var, read `config.torch_dtype` (now reflecting the resolved `--dtype` value) instead of hardcoding `bfloat16`. - When the user **has** explicitly set the env var, honor it as before. - Fall back to `bfloat16` if neither source provides a valid dtype. ## Result Before modification [2026-03-03 13:52:30] Mamba2 state dtype: conv_dtype=torch.bfloat16, ssm_dtype=torch.float32 and it crash like in the issue After modification [2026-03-03 13:51:03] Mamba2 state dtype: conv_dtype=torch.float16, ssm_dtype=torch.float32 And it can work properly ## Accuracy Tests No changes to model forward code or kernels — this only affects the dtype used for conv_states cache allocation, ensuring it matches the model's actual running dtype. Existing Mamba model tests (which explicitly set `SGLANG_MAMBA_CONV_DTYPE`) are unaffected since `is_set()` returns `True` for those. ## Benchmarking and Profiling No impact on inference speed — this change only affects cache allocation dtype selection at startup. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review Process 1. signals.title: fix: avoid aliased tensor in fused add+norm for EXAONE4 post-LN in forward_split_prefill
signals.text: ## Summary - EXAONE4 uses **post-LN** architecture where each decoder layer returns `hidden_states` and `residual` pointing to the **same tensor object** (`residual = hidden_states`) - The `forward_split_prefill` path called `self.model.norm(hidden_states, residual)` with two args, passing both aliased tensors to `fused_add_rmsnorm` - This is inconsistent with the regular `forward` path (line 386) which correctly calls `self.norm(hidden_states)` with a single argument - Fix: match the regular forward path's single-arg norm call ## Root cause In EXAONE4's post-LN decoder layer, the final lines are: ```python hidden_states = self.post_feedforward_layernorm(hidden_states) hidden_states = hidden_states + residual residual = hidden_states # same object return hidden_states, residual ``` When `forward_split_prefill` passes both to `fused_add_rmsnorm`, it computes `residual += hidden_states` in-place on aliased memory. ## Test plan - Run EXAONE4 inference with chunked prefill / pipeline parallelism - Compare logits between `forward` and `forward_split_prefill` paths

signals.title: [fix] Parameter 'enable_thinking' not working for nemotron_3 reasoning parser
signals.text: ## Motivation When using Nemotron 3 models (e.g., NVIDIA-Nemotron-3-Super-120B-FP8) with `enable_thinking=False`, the model response is incorrectly placed in `reasoning_content` instead of `content`, leaving `content` empty. This happens because `template_manager.force_reasoning` (detected from the raw chat template) overrides the user's explicit `enable_thinking=False` setting via an OR condition, causing the reasoning parser to treat all output as reasoning text. ## Modifications - Remove `template_manager.force_reasoning` from the `is_force_reasoning` computation in both non-stream and stream response handlers (`serving_chat.py`) - Rely solely on `_get_reasoning_from_request(request)` which already correctly handles per-model logic (including `enable_thinking` for nemotron_3, qwen3, glm45, interns1) ### Testing - [1] Test with `enable_thinking=True` - reasoning enabled - [2] Test with `enable_thinking=False` - reasoning disabled - [3] Test with no `enable_thinking` parameter - reasoning enabled (default) - [4] Test with `chat_template_kwargs=None` - reasoning enabled (default)

signals.title: Enable num_splits > 1 for FA3 deterministic inference
signals.text: ## Summary SGLang's deterministic inference mode currently forces `num_splits=1` for FA3, which limits prefill throughput. With the `batch_invariant` scheduling fix in flash-attention (sgl-project/sgl-flash-attn#43), we can safely use `num_splits > 1` while maintaining bit-exact determinism. This PR sets `num_splits=4` for FA3 deterministic mode, improving prefill throughput by up to **2.1x** on prefill-bound workloads. ## Benchmark Results (Qwen3-8B, H200, `--attention-backend fa3 --decode-attention-backend flashinfer --enable-deterministic-inference`) | Workload | num_splits=1 | num_splits=4 | Speedup | |----------|-------------|-------------|---------| | **Short prefill** (512 in, 128 out) | | | | | Total throughput (tok/s) | 8,614 | 18,101 | **2.10x** | | Mean TTFT (ms) | 482 | 1,432 | 0.34x | | Mean E2E (ms) | 8,970 | 3,986 | **2.25x** | | Mean ITL (ms) | 131 | 40 | **3.3x** | | P99 ITL (ms) | 5,875 | 704 | **8.3x** | | **Medium prefill** (2048 in, 256 out) | | | | | Total throughput (tok/s) | 18,533 | 23,371 | **1.26x** | | Mean TTFT (ms) | 2,628 | 2,688 | 0.98x | | Mean E2E (ms) | 10,409 | 8,073 | **1.29x** | | Mean ITL (ms) | 62 | 34 | **1.8x** | | P99 ITL (ms) | 4,397 | 2,068 | **2.1x** | | **Long prefill** (4096 in, 512 out) | | | | | Total throughput (tok/s) | 16,601 | 18,073 | **1.09x** | | Mean TTFT (ms) | 2,850 | 1,887 | **1.51x** | | Mean E2E (ms) | 9,233 | 8,910 | **1.04x** | > **TTFT vs ITL tradeoff on short prefill:** With `num_splits=1` at `request-rate=inf`, prefills run serially — early requests get fast TTFT (482ms) but cause massive decode stalls (P99 ITL 5.9s). With `num_splits=4`, prefills complete faster in aggregate, so decode runs smoothly (P99 ITL 704ms, 8x better), but individual TTFT is higher because more prefills are batched concurrently. E2E latency and throughput are the meaningful comparisons. At realistic request rates this TTFT difference disappears. ## Changes - **`flashattention_backend.py`**: Set `num_splits=4` for FA3 deterministic mode, pass `batch_invariant=True` - **`flash_attention.py`**, **`flash_attention_v3.py`**: Thread `batch_invariant` param through FA3 call chain - **sgl-kernel**: Add `batch_invariant` to fwd op schema, Python wrapper, C++ header - **sgl-kernel/tests**: Add `test_flash_attn_deterministic_num_splits` (128 test cases, all passing) ## Deterministic validation All three sglang deterministic test modes pass with `num_splits=4`: - `test_deterministic --test-mode single` (15 trials, batch 1-15): **PASS** (1 unique output) - `test_deterministic --test-mode prefix` (4 prefix lengths, logprobs): **PASS** (all identical) - `test_deterministic --test-mode radix_cache`: **PASS** (cached == uncached) ## Reproduce benchmark results **1. Launch server (num_splits=4, this PR):** ```bash python3 -m sglang.launch_server \ --model Qwen/Qwen3-8B \ --trust-remote-code \ --attention-backend fa3 \ --decode-attention-backend flashinfer \ --enable-deterministic-inference \ --cuda-graph-max-bs 32 \ --port 30000 ``` **2. Run benchmarks (in a separate terminal):** ```bash # Short prefill (512 input, 128 output) python3 -m sglang.bench_serving \ --backend sglang --port 30000 \ --dataset-name random \ --random-input-len 512 --random-output-len 128 \ --num-prompts 300 --request-rate inf # Medium prefill (2048 input, 256 output) python3 -m sglang.bench_serving \ --backend sglang --port 30000 \ --dataset-name random \ --random-input-len 2048 --random-output-len 256 \ --num-prompts 200 --request-rate inf # Long prefill (4096 input, 512 output) python3 -m sglang.bench_serving \ --backend sglang --port 30000 \ --dataset-name random \ --random-input-len 4096 --random-output-len 512 \ --num-prompts 100 --request-rate inf ``` **3. For num_splits=1 baseline**, temporarily change `flashattention_backend.py` line 210 from `self.num_splits = 4` to `self.num_splits = 1`, restart server, and re-run the same benchmarks. ## Reproduce deterministic tests ```bash python3 -m sglang.launch_server \ --model Qwen/Qwen3-8B \ --trust-remote-code \ --attention-backend fa3 \ --decode-attention-backend flashinfer \ --enable-deterministic-inference \ --cuda-graph-max-bs 32 \ --port 30000 # In a separate terminal: python3 -m sglang.test.test_deterministic \ --host 0.0.0.0 --port 30000 --test-mode single --n-start 10 --n-trials 15 python3 -m sglang.test.test_deterministic \ --host 0.0.0.0 --port 30000 --test-mode prefix --n-start 10 --n-trials 10 --return-logprob python3 -m sglang.test.test_deterministic \ --host 0.0.0.0 --port 30000 --test-mode radix_cache ``` ## Dependencies Requires: sgl-project/sgl-flash-attn#43 (`batch_invariant` flag) ## Test plan - [x] 128/128 kernel-level batch invariance tests pass (sgl-kernel) - [x] All 3 sglang deterministic test modes pass - [ ] CI passes <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #28138299519](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/28138299519)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #28138299333](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/28138299333)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [ROCm]Add RDNA4 GPU Support for sgl-kernel
signals.text: ## Motivation Based on the existed sgl-kernel codes, added the AMD Radeon GPU support for sgl-kernel ## Modifications - RDNA4 architecture support (setup_rocm.py): Extended the build system to recognize and compile for RDNA4 (gfx1200/1201) targets in addition to the existing CDNA3/4 (gfx942, gfx950). Introduced SGL_IS_RDNA, SGL_IS_RDNA3, SGL_IS_RDNA4 compile-time macros propagated to both hipcc and cxx compilation units. - Quick allreduce gated to CDNA only (common_extension_rocm.cc, sgl_kernel_ops.h, allreduce.py): The quick_all_reduce (qr_*) family relies on CDNA-specific MUBUF instructions that are unavailable on RDNA. These are now conditionally compiled (#ifndef SGL_IS_RDNA) and skipped at runtime on RDNA devices, preventing link errors and undefined symbol crashes. - WARP_SIZE fix for ROCm host code (utils.h): Host-side code previously always resolved WARP_SIZE to 64 via the !__HIP_DEVICE_COMPILE__ branch, causing incorrect grid/block math in MoE topk launchers on RDNA (which uses warp size 32). A new SGL_ROCM_WARP_SIZE macro (64 for CDNA, 32 for RDNA) is injected at build time and takes priority, making both host and device code agree on the logical warp width. - FP8 handling for RDNA3: RDNA3 has no hardware FP8 support; the build now skips -DENABLE_FP8 for those targets instead of raising a compile error. ## Accuracy Tests This PR didn't change the kernel codes directly, so doesn't run the accuracy test used sgl-kernel unit test to verify the PR on RDNA4 GPU. python3 -m pytest test_moe_align.py test_moe_topk_softmax.py test_apply_token_bitmask_inplace.py test_activation.py test_topk.py test_moe_topk_sigmoid.py test_torch_defaults_reset.py speculative/test_eagle_utils.py ## Speed Tests and Profiling ## Checklist - [* ] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [* ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [ ] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. signals.title: Multinode cuda
signals.text: <!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. --> ## Motivation Multi-node serves of `Qwen3NextForCausalLM`, `Qwen3_5MoeForConditionalGeneration`, and `Qwen3_5ForConditionalGeneration` deadlock under any concurrent (`#running-req > 1`) decode load. The first decode batch logs and returns, then the scheduler stops emitting Decode batch lines and HTTP requests stop returning. Both ranks go quiescent — no exception, no NCCL warning. The pattern is independent of attention backend (`trtllm_mha` and `triton` both deadlock), of `--mamba-scheduler-strategy` (`extra_buffer` and `no_buffer` both deadlock), and of `--disable-overlap-schedule` (eliminates the `bs=1` repro but does not survive batched decode). Root cause: the captured decode CUDA graph records the inter-rank TP all-reduce. Replaying that captured graph under multi-node batched decode does not complete on both ranks, so the scheduler blocks indefinitely waiting for the post-decode `next_token_ids` copy. Disabling CUDA graph or forcing `--cuda-graph-max-bs 1` masks the bug but is ~5× slower at decode. Repro on stock main (2 × 4 × GB200, `Qwen/Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B-Instruct`): - Sequential `/v1/completions` requests succeed. - 32 concurrent requests via `python -m sglang.bench_serving` or any small stress: server stops responding within ~2 s and never recovers. ## Modifications - **`python/sglang/srt/server_args.py`** - Add `enable_cuda_graph_collective_break: bool = False` and a hidden `--enable-cuda-graph-collective-break` CLI flag. - In `_handle_model_specific_adjustments`, auto-enable the flag for `Qwen3NextForCausalLM` / `Qwen3_5MoeForConditionalGeneration` / `Qwen3_5ForConditionalGeneration` when `nnodes > 1 and not disable_cuda_graph`. - **`python/sglang/srt/distributed/communication_op.py`** - Wrap `tensor_model_parallel_all_reduce` with `eager_on_graph(True)`. When the new flag triggers `BreakableCUDAGraphCapture`, the TP all-reduce executes eagerly between captured graph segments instead of being baked into the captured graph; outside that capture context the wrapper is a no-op (one extra ContextVar read at capture time, zero overhead at replay). - **`python/sglang/srt/model_executor/cuda_graph_runner.py`** - In `_capture_graph` and `_create_device_graph`, OR the new flag with the existing `SGLANG_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDA_GRAPH` env var so the breakable capture/replay path is selected when the flag is on. The change is opt-in for non-targeted models (manual flag only) and a strict no-op for single-node and for any model that doesn't enter `BreakableCUDAGraphCapture`. ## Accuracy Tests This PR does not change kernels, model code, or sampling; it only relocates the TP all-reduce from inside the captured graph to between captured graph segments. Output tokens at the same prompt and `temperature=0` are identical across runs in the bench tables below (matching first-token outputs across all batch sizes). ## Speed Tests and Profiling 2 × 4 × GB200, `Qwen/Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B-Instruct`, `--tp 8 --nnodes 2`. Run-once-bench server: ``` python -m sglang.bench_one_batch_server \ --base-url http://127.0.0.1:30000 \ --model-path /root/Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B-Instruct \ --batch-size 1 4 8 16 32 64 \ --input-len 128 --output-len 256 --show-report ``` Compared against the only stable workaround on stock main (`--disable-cuda-graph`): | bs | this PR — out tput (tok/s) | this PR — ITL (ms) | `--disable-cuda-graph` — out tput | `--disable-cuda-graph` — ITL | speedup | |----:|---------------------------:|-------------------:|----------------------------------:|-----------------------------:|--------:| | 1 | 67.0 | 14.9 | 11.5 | 86.9 | **5.8×** | | 4 | 267.6 | 15.0 | 46.0 | 87.0 | **5.8×** | | 8 | 532.1 | 15.0 | 91.1 | 87.8 | **5.8×** | | 16 | 1038.9 | 15.4 | 187.5 | 85.3 | **5.5×** | | 32 | 1935.1 | 16.5 | 353.4 | 90.6 | **5.5×** | | 64 | 3088.8 | 20.7 | 705.2 | 90.8 | **4.4×** | Sustained-load sanity (32 concurrent workers, 60 s+), one row per auto-enabled architecture: | arch | model | duration | requests completed | errors | longest stall | |---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:| | `Qwen3_5MoeForConditionalGeneration` | `Qwen3.5-397B-A17B` (`--ep 8 --moe-runner-backend triton`) | 120 s | **1232** | 0 | 0 s | | `Qwen3NextForCausalLM` | `Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B-Instruct` | 60 s | **1440** | 0 | 0 s | | `Qwen3_5ForConditionalGeneration` | `Qwen3.5-27B` | 60 s | **864** | 0 | 2 s | Stock main on the same configs deadlocks within ~2 s (request counter flatlines and never recovers; both ranks quiescent). Single-node sanity (same fix-installed binary, `--tp 4`, no `--nnodes`/`--node-rank` so the auto-enable gate is closed and stock CUDA graph runs): | arch | model | duration | requests completed | errors | longest stall | |---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:| | `Qwen3_5ForConditionalGeneration` | `Qwen3.5-27B` | 60 s | **2464** | 0 | 0 s | | `Qwen3NextForCausalLM` | `Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B-Instruct` | 60 s | **3040** | 0 | 0 s | So the deadlock is multi-node specific and the fix's `nnodes > 1` gate keeps single-node entirely on the upstream code path. Microbench on the off-path wrap (`eager_on_graph(True)` with no `BreakableCUDAGraphCapture` active): +0 ns/replay, +121 ns/eager-call on GB200. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

signals.title: [LoRA][MoE] Fix EP correctness: NVFP4 cutlass_moe_params sizing + Triton OOB pointer clamp
signals.text: ## Motivation Two unrelated EP-correctness issues in the LoRA / NVFP4 stack, both reliably hit on multi-rank EP deployments and both root-causes for the same class of failure (CUDA "illegal memory access" or null TMA descriptor on the first forward). ### Bug 1 — `ModelOptNvFp4FusedMoEMethod.cutlass_moe_params` sized by global `num_experts` The FlashInfer-CUTLASS NVFP4 path constructs `CutlassMoEParams` with `num_experts=layer.num_experts` (the global expert count). Under EP, the per-rank `w13_weight` / `w2_weight` tensors are sized by `num_local_experts`, but the FP4 grouped-GEMM kernel iterates `expert_offsets.size(0)` and indexes the weight tensors by `expert_id`. With `num_experts=384`, `ep_size=8`, `num_local_experts=48`, the kernel walks past the loaded weight tensors and produces a null TMA descriptor → first forward crashes with `CUDA error: an illegal memory access was encountered`. When `ep_size=1`, `num_local_experts == num_experts`, so the change is a no-op for non-EP runs. ### Bug 2 — Existing LoRA Triton kernels build OOB pointers in masked lanes The four kernels `sgemm_lora_a`, `sgemm_lora_b`, `qkv_lora_b`, `gate_up_lora_b` compute their `x_ptrs` / `w_ptrs` via raw arithmetic over `s_offset`, `n_offset`, `k_offset`, then mask the load: ```python x_ptrs = x + (s_physical[:, None] * x_stride_0 + k_offset[None, :] * x_stride_1) ... x_tile = tl.load(x_ptrs, mask=(s_offset[:, None] < seg_len) & ...) ``` When a tile straddles the segment boundary (`s_offset >= seg_len`) or `n_offset` exceeds the rank-truncated `N`, `x_ptrs` / `w_ptrs` are computed with out-of-bounds offsets even though the load mask ultimately drops the values. On some Triton / cuBLAS / driver combos the pointer expression is materialised before the mask is applied, tripping CUDA "illegal memory access". In practice this surfaces with wider LoRA target sets (e.g. `q_b_proj`, `kv_b_proj`, `fused_qkv_a_proj_with_mqa` for MLA models) where the rank-truncated `N` does not align with `BLOCK_N`. ## Modifications ### `python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/modelopt_quant.py` In `ModelOptNvFp4FusedMoEMethod.process_weights_after_loading`, size `cutlass_moe_params` by `layer.num_local_experts` (per-rank) instead of `layer.num_experts` (global). Two-line fix: ```diff - or existing_params.num_experts != layer.num_experts + or existing_params.num_experts != layer.num_local_experts ... - num_experts=layer.num_experts, # global num experts + num_experts=layer.num_local_experts, ``` ### `python/sglang/srt/lora/triton_ops/{sgemm_lora_a,sgemm_lora_b,qkv_lora_b,gate_up_lora_b}.py` Same pattern in all four kernels: 1. Pass total row count `S` as a kernel arg (used as the row-axis clamp). 2. Replace pointer-walk-then-mask with: clamp masked-out lane indices into the valid range first, then load with the mask. The mask still controls correctness; the clamp only ensures the *unmasked* pointer expression itself is in-bounds. ```python # Before: x_ptrs = x + (s_physical[:, None] * x_stride_0 + k_offset[None, :] * x_stride_1) ... x_tile = tl.load(x_ptrs, mask=(s_offset[:, None] < seg_len) & (k_offset[None, :] < K - k * BLOCK_K), other=0.0) # After: row_mask = s_offset < seg_len safe_row = tl.minimum(s_physical, S - 1) safe_n = tl.minimum(n_offset, N - 1) ... cur_k = k * BLOCK_K + k_offset k_mask = cur_k < K safe_k = tl.minimum(cur_k, K - 1) x_tile = tl.load( x + safe_row[:, None] * x_stride_0 + safe_k[None, :] * x_stride_1, mask=row_mask[:, None] & k_mask[None, :], other=0.0, ) ``` Per-iteration K advancement also moves from `x_ptrs += BLOCK_K * x_stride_1` to recomputing `cur_k = k * BLOCK_K + k_offset` inside the loop, so the load expression is built fresh from clamped indices each step. The patch is **semantically a no-op** — the load mask already prevented the OOB *value* from contributing; the clamp only prevents the OOB *pointer* from being computed. ## Accuracy Tests ### Triton kernels — bit-identical to `main` 12 case combinations (3 shapes × 4 kernels), exercised on a single B200 (per pod). For each shape we ran the kernel on `main`, saved the output, applied the patch, re-ran, and compared: ``` sgemm_lora_a (32, 32): max_abs_diff=0 rel=0 OK sgemm_lora_a (23, 24): max_abs_diff=0 rel=0 OK sgemm_lora_a (31, 32): max_abs_diff=0 rel=0 OK (K=513 straddles 2 BLOCK_K iters) sgemm_lora_b (32, 256): max_abs_diff=0 rel=0 OK sgemm_lora_b (31, 257): max_abs_diff=0 rel=0 OK (N=257 straddles BLOCK_N=256) sgemm_lora_b (27, 513): max_abs_diff=0 rel=0 OK qkv_lora_b (32, 128): max_abs_diff=0 rel=0 OK qkv_lora_b (31, 131): max_abs_diff=0 rel=0 OK (n_q=65, n_kv=33 straddle BLOCK_OUT=64) qkv_lora_b (27, 259): max_abs_diff=0 rel=0 OK gate_up_lora_b (32, 128): max_abs_diff=0 rel=0 OK gate_up_lora_b (31, 514): max_abs_diff=0 rel=0 OK (output_dim=257 straddles BLOCK_OUT=64) gate_up_lora_b (27, 1026):max_abs_diff=0 rel=0 OK ALL OK ``` Same 12 cases reproduced on a second host with the same byte-for-byte equivalence. The clamp does not change results on any covered shape. ### `modelopt_quant.py` — logical / structural check Constructed `CutlassMoEParams` with both `(num_experts=384, num_local_experts=384)` (the no-EP case) and `(num_experts=384, num_local_experts=48)` (`ep_size=8`): | ep_size | params.num_experts | tensor sizes (e.g. `expert_offsets`, `problem_sizes1/2`, `a_ptrs`, …) | |---:|---:|---| | 1 | 384 | sized 384 — unchanged from pre-patch (`num_local_experts == num_experts`) | | 8 | 48 | sized 48 — matches per-rank `w13_weight` / `w2_weight` | | 16| 24 | sized 24 — matches per-rank `w13_weight` / `w2_weight` | The `ep_size=1` row demonstrates this is a no-op for non-EP deploys (the common case). End-to-end EP launch was previously validated by the original author at TP=16 / EP=16 on Kimi-K2.5-NVFP4 with the `flashinfer_cutlass` MoE backend; on `main` (without this patch) the same launch crashes at the first forward with the null-TMA-descriptor failure described above. ## Speed Tests and Profiling No expected impact: - The clamp adds two `tl.minimum` operations per kernel invocation — trivially cheap relative to the GEMM body. Per-iteration `cur_k = k * BLOCK_K + k_offset` replaces an in-place `x_ptrs += BLOCK_K * x_stride_1` and is no more expensive. - The `cutlass_moe_params` change is at weight-load time only; no hot-path cost. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

signals.title: [PD] Abort prefill KV transfer before page reuse
signals.text: ## Root cause In PD mode, decode could abort a request and release its KV pages while prefill-side Mooncake transfers were still in flight. Because prefill had no abort barrier with decode page release, a stale transfer could still land after decode-side reuse and corrupt the new request KV contents. ## Test plan - run PD-separated prefill/decode serving with Mooncake transfer - force decode-side request timeout / abort on a long-context request - verify prefill ranks receive abort fanout and return ABORT_ACK - verify prefill request fails fast instead of hanging after decode abort - verify decode releases KV pages only after abort ACKs are received - stress with delayed Mooncake transfer to validate the in-flight write drain path
