signals.title: [AMD] Add dense-FP8 for MXFP4 checkpoints with fused silu, mul, activation quant
signals.text: <!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. --> ## Motivation Quark MXFP4 checkpoints leave a handful of large dense projections unquantized in bf16 — most notably the Qwen3.5 `shared_expert.down_proj`. On the AMD ROCm/aiter path these leftover bf16 GEMMs are comparatively heavy, and the cost shows up most in prefill-bound regimes where the dense projection is on the critical path. Today there is no way to promote just these excluded layers without re-quantizing the whole checkpoint. This PR adds an opt-in `--enable-dense-fp8` path that promotes only the eligible large bf16 dense layers (which the checkpoint left unquantized) to **online w8a8 FP8**, and fuses the preceding `SiluAndMul` + per-token activation quantization into a single aiter kernel. Instead of running `SiluAndMul`, then a separate activation quant, then the GEMM, the fused kernel emits a pre-quantized `(fp8, scale)` tuple that feeds straight into `down_proj`. The path is numerically a dynamic per-token FP8 quant of an otherwise bf16 layer, is ROCm/aiter-only, and is fully opt-in, so default behavior is unchanged. ## Modifications - **`server_args.py`**: Add the `--enable-dense-fp8` server arg (AMD/aiter, default **off**). Requires `SGLANG_USE_AITER` and `SGLANG_USE_AITER_FP8_PER_TOKEN`. - **`quark/quark.py`**: Give `QuarkConfig` a model-registered dense-FP8 policy. `register_dense_fp8_modules(include, exclude, min_output_size)` lets a model declare which excluded (bf16) layers may be promoted — quark itself owns no module names or thresholds. In `get_quant_method`, a layer that would normally fall back to `UnquantizedLinearMethod` is instead routed to an online dynamic `Fp8LinearMethod` (`Fp8Config(is_checkpoint_fp8_serialized=False, activation_scheme="dynamic")`) when `--enable-dense-fp8` is set and the layer matches the policy (include substring, not excluded, output size ≥ min). - **`models/qwen3_5.py`**: Register the Qwen3.5 policy — include only `.shared_expert.down_proj`, exclude tiny/routing/embedding layers (`conv1d`, `shared_expert_gate`, `mlp.gate`, `in_proj_*`, `lm_head`, `embed`), and require `N ≥ 2048`. Aiter-only, so the tuned policy lives with the model. - **`models/qwen2_moe.py`**: In the MoE block forward, when `down_proj` is running as online w8a8 FP8 per-token on aiter, fuse `SiluAndMul` + per-token quant into a single `aiter.silu_and_mul_quant` call that produces the `(fp8, scale)` tuple consumed directly by `down_proj`, skipping a separate activation + quant pass. Gated on `use_aiter_fp8_per_token`; default off. - **`layers/quantization/fp8.py`**: Teach `Fp8LinearMethod.apply` to accept a pre-quantized `(fp8, scale)` tuple input (from the fused kernel) and route it to the aiter PTPC helper `apply_fp8_ptpc_linear`, since `apply_fp8_linear` has no tuple path. Weight is transposed `(K, N) → (N, K)` to match the helper's expectation. ## Usage Opt-in via `--enable-dense-fp8`. It is AMD/aiter-only and requires aiter FP8 per-token, so set the two aiter env flags. The same command applies to both Qwen3.5 checkpoints (add `--kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3` for the MXFP4-AttnFP8 checkpoint): ```bash SGLANG_USE_AITER=1 SGLANG_USE_AITER_FP8_PER_TOKEN=1 \ python3 -m sglang.launch_server \ --model-path /path/to/Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-MXFP4 \ --trust-remote-code \ --tensor-parallel-size 2 \ --attention-backend aiter \ --enable-dense-fp8 ``` The `SiluAndMul`+per-token-quant fusion is on by default whenever `--enable-dense-fp8` is active on the aiter per-token path; it can be disabled for debugging with `SGLANG_DISABLE_DENSE_FP8_SILU_FUSE=1` (not recommended — fusion is neutral-to-faster and saves the bf16 intermediate round-trip). ## Accuracy Tests The same `--enable-dense-fp8` config (online PTPC FP8 + fused `SiluAndMul`+quant) is applied to **both** Qwen3.5-397B-A17B checkpoints, TP=2, aiter backend. GSM8K 5-shot, 1319 questions. **MXFP4-AttnFP8** (fp8_e4m3 KV cache): | config | accuracy (flexible / strict) | |------------------------------------------|------------------------------| | `dense_off` (baseline, down_proj bf16) | 0.9363 / 0.9409 | | `dense_on` (this PR, down_proj FP8) | 0.9393 / 0.9454 | **Plain MXFP4** (3-seed mean ± per-seed stderr ≈ 0.007): | config | flexible (3 seeds) | strict (3 seeds) | |------------------------------------------|-------------------------------|-------------------------------| | `dense_off` (baseline, down_proj bf16) | 0.9340 / 0.9356 / 0.9295 | 0.9401 / 0.9409 / 0.9371 | | `dense_on` (this PR, down_proj FP8) | 0.9340 / 0.9257 / 0.9325 | 0.9401 / 0.9409 / 0.9416 | Accuracy is unchanged within noise on both checkpoints — the per-seed spread (±0.007) exceeds the dense_off↔dense_on difference, so promoting `down_proj` to FP8 is accuracy-neutral. ## Speed Tests and Profiling TP=2, `--attention-backend aiter`, `--page-size 16`, `--chunked-prefill-size 8192`, `--mem-fraction-static 0.8`, allreduce-fusion on, tuned bf16 GEMM present. A = `dense_off` (baseline), B = `dense_on` (this PR); all other knobs identical. **Throughput below is total token throughput (input+output) across the TP=2 group**, i.e. `tok/s = (tok/s/gpu) × 2`. TPOT is the median per-output-token latency. ### MXFP4-AttnFP8 (`--kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3`) **ISL/OSL = 1024/1024** (decode-bound): | concurrency | total tok/s OFF→ON | Δ throughput | median TPOT OFF→ON (ms) | Δ TPOT | |-------------|--------------------|--------------|-------------------------|--------| | 4 | 776 → 774 | −0.3% | 9.96 → 9.97 | +0.1% | | 8 | 1362 → 1372 | +0.7% | 11.39 → 11.31 | −0.7% | | 16 | 2238 → 2240 | +0.1% | 14.10 → 14.09 | −0.1% | | 32 | 3124* → 3140 | +0.5% | 20.06* → 20.00 | −0.3% | | 64 | 4378 → 4360 | −0.4% | 28.97 → 29.11 | +0.5% | \* The captured `dense_off` cc=32 point was a noisy outlier; a repeat baseline run is used here. At 1k/1k the dense projection is too compute-light to move the needle — results are **at parity (no regression)** on both throughput and TPOT. **ISL/OSL = 8192/1024** (prefill-heavy): | concurrency | total tok/s OFF→ON | Δ throughput | median TPOT OFF→ON (ms) | Δ TPOT | |-------------|--------------------|--------------|-------------------------|--------| | 4 | 3170 → 3182 | +0.4% | 10.76 → 10.68 | −0.7% | | 8 | 5216 → 5338 | +2.3% | 13.05 → 12.74 | −2.4% | | 16 | 7874 → 8008 | +1.7% | 17.46 → 17.14 | −1.8% | | 32 | 10260 → 10462 | +2.0% | 27.07 → 26.34 | −2.7% | | 64 | 12840 → 13120 | +2.2% | 44.06 → 42.88 | −2.7% | In the prefill-heavy 8k/1k regime — where the bf16 `down_proj` GEMM actually matters — the fused FP8-dense path gives a **consistent ~2% total-throughput gain** and a **~2–3% lower TPOT** at every concurrency. Net: neutral at 1k/1k, a clear win for prefill-bound workloads, with no TPOT regression anywhere. ### Plain MXFP4 Node-pinned (single NUMA node, fixed GPU pair) to suppress host/neighbor contention. **ISL/OSL = 8192/1024** (prefill-heavy): | concurrency | total tok/s OFF→ON | Δ throughput | median TPOT OFF→ON (ms) | Δ TPOT | |-------------|--------------------|--------------|-------------------------|--------| | 4 | 3258 → 3348 | +2.8% | 10.22 → 10.18 | −0.4% | | 8 | 5140 → 5174 | +0.7% | 13.25 → 13.15 | −0.8% | | 16 | 7798 → 7804 | +0.1% | 17.62 → 17.58 | −0.2% | | 32 | 10184 → 10198 | +0.1% | 27.06 → 27.01 | −0.2% | | 64 | 12878 → 12884 | +0.05% | 43.68 → 43.64 | −0.1% | **ISL/OSL = 1024/1024** (decode-bound) — mean of 3 warm sweeps per arm, with a flat `dense_off` control measured in the same window (control spread ≤0.6%, confirming an uncontended measurement): | concurrency | total tok/s OFF→ON | Δ throughput | median TPOT OFF→ON (ms) | Δ TPOT | |-------------|--------------------|--------------|-------------------------|--------| | 4 | 819 → 819 | 0.0% | 9.43 → 9.42 | −0.1% | | 8 | 1331 → 1341 | +0.8% | 11.68 → 11.58 | −0.9% | | 16 | 2203 → 2199 | −0.2% | 14.30 → 14.32 | +0.1% | | 32 | 3089 → 3091 | +0.1% | 20.28 → 20.34 | +0.3% | | 64 | 4352 → 4323 | −0.7% | 29.08 → 29.32 | +0.8% | On the plain MXFP4 checkpoint the dense-FP8 path is **at parity (no regression)** on this host — both throughput and TPOT are unchanged within run-to-run noise across all concurrencies, verified at **8k/1k** and **1k/1k** (the latter across 3 warm sweeps against a flat control). The PTPC+fusion config is therefore **safe to enable uniformly on both checkpoints**: a clear prefill-bound win on MXFP4-AttnFP8, and neutral on plain MXFP4. ## Checklist - [ ] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [ ] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process). 2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers. 3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so. - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci` 4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:no_entry_sign: [Run #32274360852](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32274360852)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32274359653](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32274359653)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32274360208](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32274360208)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: feat: make mm_inputs msgpack-native
signals.text: <!-- codex-pr-description:start --> Multimodal preprocessing produces `MultimodalProcessorOutput`, but SGLang wrapped the complete `mm_inputs` field in `PickleWrapper` before msgpack IPC. This change sends the structure and unsupported leaf values through msgpack directly, which removes duplicate serialization and reduces scheduler IPC latency. Part of #29465. ### How This Was Implemented - Made `MultimodalProcessorOutput` and `MultimodalDataItem` mutable `msgspec.Struct` types, while routing undeclared processor fields through `model_specific_data` so dataclass-era dynamic assignments still survive IPC. - Added stable msgpack Ext codecs only for unsupported leaves. Tensor and array payloads use a small length-prefixed metadata header followed by raw bytes; existing SHM/CUDA IPC transports remain descriptors rather than being flattened into raw data. - Kept heterogeneous model-specific values behind one named `MultimodalDataValue = object` boundary instead of scattering `Any`; the encoder and regression tests define the supported leaves, including NumPy scalar normalization. - Stored EVS-only fields in `model_specific_data`. Because `mm_items` decodes as the base item type, relying on Python subclasses would silently discard subtype-only fields on the wire. - Made nested CUDA IPC fallback state use the same Ext codecs and explicitly reconstruct `tuple`, `torch.Size`, dtype, and device metadata. Updated the multimodal pool's `check_drv` import after main consolidated the CUDA VMM helpers. - Added a golden tensor Ext fixture plus regressions for offsets, weakrefs, oversized hashes, dynamic fields, malformed/unknown Ext values, CUDA fallback state, device preservation, and `transformers_auto` token-type tensors. <details> <summary>Request flow before and after</summary> ```mermaid flowchart LR subgraph Before A[Preprocessed MM output] --> B[Pickle entire mm_inputs] B --> C[Msgpack request] C --> D[Scheduler] D --> E[Unpickle mm_inputs] end subgraph After F[Preprocessed MM output] --> G[Msgpack Struct fields] G --> H[Ext leaves: tensor / ndarray / SHM / CUDA IPC] H --> I[Scheduler receives typed output] end ``` - The changed boundary starts after model-specific image/video preprocessing has produced `MultimodalProcessorOutput` and ends when the scheduler receives the tokenized request. - Request APIs, processor selection, feature extraction, and model execution are unchanged. - Native msgpack values remain native. Ext is used only at unsupported leaves, allowing the outer request and multimodal containers to avoid pickle. - Raw CUDA tensors still require expected device-to-host and host-to-device copies. Normal multimodal paths generally place features on CPU or carry SHM/CUDA IPC descriptors before scheduler materialization. - Generic tuples in open model-specific data follow msgpack semantics and decode as lists. Typed offset pairs and transport-proxy state explicitly reconstruct tuples and `torch.Size` where exact runtime types are required. </details> <details> <summary>Industry prior art</summary> MessagePack reserves application-defined [extension types](https://msgpack.org/index.html) for values outside its native scalar, list, map, string, and byte types. The common tensor-serving pattern is to keep control metadata in the main message, inline only small payloads, and use auxiliary buffers or IPC handles for large CPU/CUDA allocations. - [vLLM's v1 serializer](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/72f639927f6caf3495d69dec63b9d4a87ed782ef/vllm/v1/serial_utils.py#L136-L173) is the closest precedent: it uses `msgspec`, MessagePack Ext code `3` for small tensor/ndarray raw views, native `(dtype, shape, data)` metadata, auxiliary frames for larger buffers, and an optional out-of-band tensor provider. - [vLLM tensor IPC](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/72f639927f6caf3495d69dec63b9d4a87ed782ef/vllm/v1/engine/tensor_ipc.py#L30-L105) sends the actual CPU/CUDA tensor through `torch.multiprocessing.Queue` and leaves a lightweight `{sender_id, message_id, tensor_id}` handle in the msgpack request. - [Dask Distributed](https://distributed.dask.org/en/latest/protocol.html) uses msgpack headers plus separate frames for large or complex data. [Ray](https://docs.ray.io/en/latest/ray-core/objects/serialization.html) similarly separates object metadata from NumPy buffers stored in its shared-memory object store. - [NVIDIA Triton](https://docs.nvidia.com/deeplearning/triton-inference-server/user-guide/docs/protocol/extension_shared_memory.html) registers a serialized CUDA IPC handle with device ID and byte size; inference requests reference the registered region, offset, and size. [Apache Arrow](https://arrow.apache.org/docs/cpp/api/cuda.html) also exposes CUDA IPC handles as serializable opaque buffers. - CUDA IPC correctness is primarily a transport-lifetime concern, not a MessagePack concern: [PyTorch requires](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/multiprocessing.html#sharing-cuda-tensors) the producer to retain the original allocation while consumers hold references. This PR follows the same control-envelope/data-plane split for SGLang's existing SHM and CUDA IPC proxies. Raw tensor Ext remains a copying fallback; thresholded auxiliary frames would only be warranted if future profiling shows that fallback is still material. </details> ### Validation - `test/registered/unit/managers/test_io_struct.py`: `45 passed`. - `test/registered/unit/managers/test_msgpack_ipc_roundtrip.py`: `7 passed`. - `test/registered/unit/managers --ignore=test/registered/unit/managers/test_hisparse_unit.py`: `253 passed, 567 subtests passed`. - `test/registered/unit/managers/test_hisparse_unit.py` on an isolated port: `9 passed, 2 skipped`. - `test/registered/unit/multimodal/test_cuda_ipc_transport.py`: `2 passed in 8.048s`. - `test/registered/vlm/test_token_id_retokenize_e2e.py`: `1 passed in 63.361s` with Qwen2.5-VL-3B and default CUDA IPC. - Full semantic VLM E2E through `/v1/chat/completions`: Qwen2.5-VL-3B identified red and blue image payloads correctly before and after stress with default CUDA IPC. - The changed IPC tests pass with torch's global default device forced to CUDA. - Full-repository Ruff and targeted pre-commit pass, including isort, Black, codespell, and CI registry checks. ### Profiling Methodology - Compared detached `origin/main` (`91cf159696`) with the implementation (`b8e0d3df76`) in separate worktrees and checkout-local virtual environments. - Timed the exact changed operation around an already-preprocessed output: wrap configured pickle fields, msgpack encode/decode the tokenized request, then unwrap configured pickle fields. - Reversed A/B order between medium and large cases to reduce ordering bias, and attached `py-spy --native` only after warmup. - Collected root `nsys profile` CPU/GIL/OSRT and CUDA traces because the host's `perf_event_paranoid=4` prevented non-root CPU IP sampling. - The VLM A/B used separate checkout-local environments and an A/B then B/A run order. Each launch ran three 64-request rounds at concurrency 16. - Both VLM checkouts used CPU transport because the base commit's stale VMM import prevents a default CUDA IPC run. ### Benchmark Results Local artifacts: `/ephemeral/sglang-profile/results/2026-06-29-b8e0d3df/`. | Case | Payload | Baseline p50 | Current p50 | Speedup | Baseline p95 | Current p95 | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | medium | 4 x `[1,3,336,336]`, 5.44 MB wire | 11.420 ms | 1.296 ms | 8.81x | 11.729 ms | 1.372 ms | | large | 8 x `[1,3,448,448]`, 19.3 MB wire | 38.553 ms | 4.946 ms | 7.79x | 42.097 ms | 7.257 ms | - Baseline flamegraph: wrapping/unwrapping pickle accounted for 74.9% of samples, with torch pickle restore visible beneath it. - Current flamegraph: the pickle stack disappears; msgspec encode/decode becomes the hot path. - Root `nsys` medium trace: GIL wait fell from about 32.4% to 10.6%. - CUDA small smoke: p50 improved from 946.5 us to 377.9 us (2.50x). - Review profiling found recursive encoding took 8.19 ms for one 8 MiB NumPy buffer; the final length-prefixed metadata/raw-buffer Ext path takes 0.630 ms (13.0x faster). #### CUDA IPC VLM stress One Qwen2.5-VL-3B server processed red and blue image requests through `/v1/chat/completions`. Each request had to identify its image color correctly. | Success | Errors | Throughput | p50 | p95 | Post-stress output | |---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---| | 64/64 | 0 | 81.789 req/s | 0.179 s | 0.246 s | Red and blue both matched | - GPU memory was 34,557 MiB before stress, 34,721 MiB at peak, and 34,721 MiB after stress. Server shutdown returned both GPUs to 0 MiB. #### CPU transport VLM A/B Each Qwen2.5-VL-3B request contained a red or blue image and had to return the correct color. Both variants passed 384/384 stress requests and all pre/post checks. | Variant | Aggregate throughput | Median round p50 | Median round p95 | Throughput range | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:| | Base `a58fa0388e` | 61.141 req/s | 0.256 s | 0.282 s | 58.242-64.812 req/s | | PR `1ef79cf0de` | 60.898 req/s (-0.4%) | 0.261 s (+2.0%) | 0.299 s (+6.2%) | 57.567-65.728 req/s | The ranges overlap, so this load shows no measurable end-to-end throughput gain. The benefit remains visible at the scheduler IPC boundary. <!-- codex-pr-description:end --> <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #32419697668](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32419697668)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #32419697439](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32419697439)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #32419697584](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32419697584)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [SM120] DeepSeek-V4: DeepGEMM paged-MQA indexer +FP4 MoE+ page-split
signals.text: **Motivation:** a 4x RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell (SM120) box can hold DeepSeek-V4-Flash, but on current main the only configuration that starts there is the slow torch fallback — this PR makes the DeepGEMM and FlashInfer paths work on SM120, cutting decode latency up to 3.4x. It routes the sparse-MLA indexer to DeepGEMM's paged-MQA-logits kernel, enables batched sparse-MLA prefill through FlashInfer, and unblocks the DeepGEMM FP4 MoE backend. ## Split out of this PR Following @Fridge003's review, the changes here that were not SM120 enablement now have their own PRs: - #35116 — allocate the page-split buffer outside inference mode (correctness fix) - #35118 — fuse the hc-prenorm combine into a Triton kernel (arch-independent) **This PR now depends on #35116**: without it the page-split buffer is allocated under inference mode during autotune and CUDA graph capture cannot write to it. Will rebase once it lands. The E2E tables below were measured with #35118 still in this tree. Measured separately on the same box with only that kernel toggled (ISL 8K, BS1, TP4, deep_gemm MoE), it accounts for **3.2% of the TPOT gain** (12.81 -> 12.40 ms, two repeats each, run-to-run spread 0.01 ms) and roughly 2% of TTFT. Discount the tables by that much, or land #35118 first to reproduce them as written. ## What is in it 1. **Sparse-MLA indexer on DeepGEMM** — route the indexer to DeepGEMM's paged-MQA-logits kernel instead of the eager-torch fallback that scales with batch x context and dominates decode. Opt in with `SGLANG_FP8_PAGED_MQA_LOGITS_TORCH=0 SGLANG_OPT_USE_TILELANG_INDEXER=0`. 2. **Batched sparse-MLA prefill** — prefill (q_len > 64) goes through FlashInfer's `_sparse_mla_sm120_paged_attention`; indexer metadata is chunked at M=4096 (the DeepGEMM row cap is SKU-dependent) and built once per batch instead of per layer. 3. **Page-split dirty mask** — `_split_kv_pages_to_64` re-laid out the whole SWA KV pool (~105 MB/layer) every decode step; now only the pages this step's top-k references are split (CUDA-graph safe, bit-identical). 4. **DeepGEMM FP4 MoE on SM120** — probe the block-scale entry point (DeepGEMM#324) instead of hard-disabling DeepGEMM at `sm==120`, plus the contiguous grouped-GEMM prefill path, the UE8M0 pow2-scale quant fix, and the swiglu-clamp fallback for TP>=2 shapes. 5. **SM120 kernel fixes** — u64 page-split copy, sparse-prefill head pad removal, TileLang `mhc_pre` compile fix, and the paged-MQA metadata kernel now sizes its shared-memory request from the device budget instead of a fixed 128 KB. Non-SM120 architectures are unchanged: every behavioural change is either gated on `is_sm120_supported()` or is a fix that only engages where the previous code was wrong (the UE8M0 pow2-scale quant and the shared-memory cap). ## E2E benefit "main" is marlin MoE + the torch paged-MQA fallback, because that is the only SM120 path on `14bd315d` that starts: the default (`flashinfer_mxfp4` + TileLang indexer) dies in the TileLang JIT for `sm_120a` (TileLang ships nvcc 13.3, `lmsysorg/sglang:dev-cu13` has CUDA 13.0 headers), and `--moe-runner-backend deep_gemm` raises `AttributeError: module 'sglang.srt.layers.deep_gemm_wrapper' has no attribute 'get_mn_major_tma_aligned_tensor'` (SM120 disables `ENABLE_JIT_DEEPGEMM` while the runner stays selectable). Both sides then run identical server args, only the tree differs: TP4, marlin MoE, CUTLASS FP8, chunked prefill 8192, `--disable-radix-cache`, and no speculative decoding except where the tables say otherwise. 4x RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell (SM120, 96 GB, PCIe), DeepSeek-V4-Flash, OSL 256, `--warmup-requests 0` so every measured request is a real prefill. TTFT is a median. **Single request (BS=1)** — 3 sequential requests, median. TTFT: | ISL | main | this PR | | |---|---|---|---| | 8K | 1124 ms | 899 ms | −20% | | 32K | 4540 ms | 3585 ms | −21% | | 128K | 20107 ms | 15481 ms | −23% | TPOT, without and with MTP-2 (EAGLE, 2 steps / 3 draft tokens) on both sides: | ISL | main | this PR | | main + MTP-2 | this PR + MTP-2 | | |---|---|---|---|---|---|---| | 8K | 36.1 ms | 10.5 ms | **3.4x** | 13.6 ms | 6.0 ms | 2.3x | | 32K | 35.8 ms | 10.7 ms | **3.3x** | 12.6 ms | 5.7 ms | 2.2x | | 128K | 36.1 ms | 11.9 ms | **3.0x** | 13.4 ms | 6.8 ms | 2.0x | Accepted length is within 0.2 of each other on the two sides at every context length, so the MTP gain comes from the decode path itself, not from better speculation. **Concurrent (ISL 8K)** — `--num-prompts BS --max-concurrency BS`: | BS | TTFT main | TTFT this PR | | TPOT main | TPOT this PR | | output tok/s main | output tok/s this PR | |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---| | 4 | 3574 ms | 2826 ms | −21% | 42.9 ms | 16.8 ms | 2.6x | 71 | 147 | | 8 | 5660 ms | 4530 ms | −20% | 51.9 ms | 24.3 ms | 2.1x | 108 | 191 | | 16 | 10482 ms | 8365 ms | −20% | 71.6 ms | 40.9 ms | 1.8x | 143 | 219 | TTFT holds at −20% across batch sizes; the decode multiple decays with batch (3.4x at BS1, 1.8x at BS16) because what this PR removes is per-step fixed cost, which amortises as the batch grows. Speculative decoding amortises it the same way. GSM8K (50 questions) is 0.980 on main and 0.960 on this PR at 8K — one question apart. All tables are without prefill context parallelism, which is upstream code this PR does not touch. <details> <summary>Recipes</summary> Common to both: `--fp8-gemm-backend cutlass --chunked-prefill-size 8192 --max-prefill-tokens 8192 --swa-full-tokens-ratio 0.15 --cuda-graph-max-bs 32`, plus `SGLANG_SM120_FLASHMLA_BACKEND=flashinfer SGLANG_FP8_PAGED_MQA_LOGITS_TORCH=0 SGLANG_OPT_USE_TILELANG_INDEXER=0`. **Prefill-optimised** — `--moe-runner-backend deep_gemm --mem-fraction-static 0.85`, `SGLANG_OPT_FIX_MEGA_MOE_MEMORY=1 SGLANG_OPT_DEEPGEMM_HC_PRENORM=1`. **Decode-optimised** — `--moe-runner-backend marlin --mem-fraction-static 0.90 --speculative-algorithm EAGLE --speculative-eagle-topk 1 --speculative-num-steps 2 --speculative-num-draft-tokens 3`, `SGLANG_OPT_USE_TILELANG_MHC_PRE=1`. </details> ## Dependencies - FlashInfer 0.6.15.post1 (SM120 sparse-MLA kernels) and sglang-kernel 0.4.5 — both are what `lmsysorg/sglang:dev-cu13` currently ships. - DeepGEMM at or after deepseek-ai/DeepGEMM#324 for the FP4 MoE backend. The `fp8_paged_mqa_logits` indexer path additionally needs DeepGEMM's attention host-gates to accept SM120 (a 3-line arch gate, not yet upstream in sgl-project/DeepGEMM); without it, keep the TileLang indexer default. ## Tests `test/registered/kernels/ops/attention/test_silu_and_mul_contig_post_quant.py` (9 cases, registered for CI) covers the fused swiglu-clamp + silu_mul + fp8-quant kernel against a reference. GSM8K numbers are from `sglang.test.few_shot_gsm8k`. Reviewed and validated with @ormandj (conflict resolution) and @moxcat (inference-mode buffer fix, now #35116) on 2x and 4x RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell. Re-validated after the split on 4x RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell, FlashInfer 0.6.15.post1 (the pinned version), this tree plus #35116: GSM8K-50 1.000 with `--moe-runner-backend deep_gemm`, 0.960 with MTP-2; ISL 8K BS1 TTFT 116/88 ms, TPOT 12.8/7.3 ms. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32351543120](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32351543120)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32351542983](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32351542983)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32351543356](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32351543356)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [XPU] Support INT4 dense linear (AWQ/GPTQ) for XPU
signals.text: <!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. --> ## Motivation As per the title. Add INT4 dense linear support for AWQ/GPTQ quantized models on Intel XPU, enabling INT4 inference on this backend. ## Modifications - New `python/sglang/srt/hardware_backend/xpu/quantization/: int4pack_utils.py, awq_kernels.py, gptq_kernels.py` — INT4 checkpoint conversion and native XPU packed-MM helpers. - Wire up scheme routing in `awq/awq.py, awq/schemes/awq_linear.py, gptq/gptq.py, gptq/schemes/gptq_linear.py, and layers/quantization/__init__.py` to dispatch dense INT4 linear to the XPU kernels. - Add unit tests: `test/registered/xpu/test_xpu_int4_dense.py`. ## Accuracy Tests Model: `hugging-quants/Meta-Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct-AWQ-INT4` / `hugging-quants/Meta-Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct-GPTQ-INT4` GSM8K: AWQ `~0.78`; GPTQ `~0.785`. ## Limitations GPTQ + TP>1 is only rejected when a row-parallel shard actually splits a quantization group — i.e. when `act_order` (`desc_act=true`) has permuted `g_idx` so the local channels no longer sort into whole `group_size` blocks. signals.title: [AMD]DSV4 Fix KV pool sizing for the unified_kv backend
signals.text: ## Motivation The DSV4 `unified_kv` backend has a different physical KV layout than the fp8 path, but `DSV4PoolConfigurator` sized both identically. Under `unified_kv` this over-allocates memory (and can OOM), because: - KV is stored in **bf16 over the full latent** (`attn_head_dim * 2` bytes), not the fp8(nope) + bf16(rope) + scale 584-byte cell. - SWA and the c4/c128 compress-states are **fixed per-request rings** (`num_req_slots * ring_size`), independent of `full_token`, so they must be fixed biases rather than per-token terms. ## Modifications All changes are gated on the same `is_unified_kv_triton()` / `_unified_kv` switch the pool itself uses, so sizing and allocation cannot drift apart. **No behavior change on the non-unified (fp8) path.** ### Pool sizing (`pool_configurator.py`) - Use bf16 full-latent bytes for the per-token coeff on the unified path (`_get_bytes_per_full_token`). - Exclude SWA from the per-token coeff and account for it as a fixed bias (`_fixed_swa_bytes`), inflated for the speculative draft worker the same way as the coeff. - Move the **c4 compress-state (attn + indexer)** off the per-token coeff and size it as a request-scoped fixed bias (`_fixed_c4_state_bytes` / `_unified_c4_state_pool_size`), finalized once `max_running_requests` is known — mirroring the c128 state pool. Subtract it from the token budget and log `c4_state_fixed`. - Factor the `max_running_requests`-per-worker resolution into a shared helper (`_resolve_max_running_requests_per_worker`) reused by the c128 state, SWA ring, and c4 state fixed-byte terms. - Log the SWA ring and c4-state fixed biases alongside the existing c128 fixed bias. ### Memory pool (`deepseek_v4_memory_pool.py`) - Clamp `c4_state_pool_size` up to `num_req_slots * c4_ring_size` as a safety net (mirrors the c128 clamp). ### SWA idle accounting on the unified ring - `model_runner`: reconcile `swa_max_total_num_tokens` down to the allocator ring capacity (`swa_available_size`) so the idle pool-leak invariant matches the fixed per-request SWA ring (gated on unified_kv; no real buffer is resized). - `invariant_checker`: skip the SWA token-pool leak invariant on the unified ring — its `available` is non-binding and cached radix prefixes report a spurious `swa_evictable`, so `available + evictable + protected == total` does not hold; ring slots are still covered by the `req_to_token` leak check. - `pool_stats_observer`: zero `swa_evictable` on the unified ring so `swa_num_used` / `swa_token_usage` stay coherent (cached prefixes hold no ring slot). ### Review-fix follow-ups - Detect unified-KV via the canonical `get_kvcache()._unified_kv` (the previous `getattr(alloc, "_unified", ...)` was always `False` on the wrapped allocators — thanks @amd-danli103). Applied consistently in `invariant_checker`, `pool_stats_observer`, and `schedule_batch`. - Unwrap `logical_attn_allocator` in the `_check_kv_page_invariants` sub-allocator probe so the DSV4-HiSparse wrapper reaches its inner full/swa allocators. - `schedule_policy`: align the `add_one_req` SWA admission gate (`>=` -> `>`) with `add_one_req_ignore_eos` so an exact-fit request is admitted. ## Accuracy / Validation Validated on **DeepSeek-V4-Pro, `unified_kv` + EAGLE MTP (speculative), TP8 / DP8, ROCm**. <details> <summary>Server launch command</summary> ```bash export SGLANG_DEFAULT_THINKING=1 export SGLANG_DSV4_REASONING_EFFORT=max export SGLANG_OPT_DEEPGEMM_HC_PRENORM=false export SGLANG_USE_AITER=1 export SGLANG_USE_ROCM700A=1 export SGLANG_OPT_USE_FUSED_COMPRESS=true export SGLANG_HACK_FLASHMLA_BACKEND=unified_kv_triton export SGLANG_OPT_FP8_WO_A_GEMM=false export SGLANG_OPT_USE_JIT_INDEXER_METADATA=false export SGLANG_OPT_USE_TOPK_V2=false export SGLANG_OPT_USE_AITER_INDEXER=true export SGLANG_OPT_USE_TILELANG_INDEXER=false export SGLANG_OPT_USE_TILELANG_MHC_PRE=false export SGLANG_OPT_USE_TILELANG_MHC_POST=false export SGLANG_FP8_PAGED_MQA_LOGITS_TORCH=1 export SGLANG_OPT_USE_FUSED_COMPRESS_TRITON=true export SGLANG_OPT_USE_MULTI_STREAM_OVERLAP=false export SGLANG_ROCM_USE_MULTI_STREAM=false export AITER_BF16_FP8_MOE_BOUND=0 export SGLANG_OPT_FP4_MOE_K_ALIGN=128 export SGLANG_DSV4_INDEXER_K_CACHE_PRESHUFFLE=1 export SGLANG_EAGER_INPUT_NO_COPY=false export SGLANG_DP_USE_GATHERV=1 python3 -m sglang.launch_server \ --model-path /models/DeepSeek-V4-Pro \ --trust-remote-code \ --swa-full-tokens-ratio 0.10 \ --tp 8 \ --dp 8 \ --enable-dp-attention \ --enable-cache-report \ --attention-backend dsv4 \ --max-running-request 2048 \ --page-size 256 \ --chunked-prefill-size 32768 \ --mem-fraction-static 0.9 \ --port 30001 \ --disable-shared-experts-fusion \ --tool-call-parser deepseekv4 \ --reasoning-parser deepseek-v4 \ --speculative-algorithm EAGLE \ --speculative-num-steps 3 \ --speculative-num-draft-tokens 4 \ --speculative-eagle-topk 1 \ --enable-prefill-delayer ``` </details> <details> <summary>Client / bench_serving command</summary> ```bash NUM_PROMPT=2048 INPUT_LEN=50 python3 -m sglang.bench_serving \ --dataset-name random \ --random-range-ratio 1 \ --num-prompt ${NUM_PROMPT} \ --max-concurrency ${NUM_PROMPT} \ --random-input $((INPUT_LEN * 1024)) \ --random-output 1024 \ --port 30001 ``` </details> ### Pool sizing (startup) `unified=True`, `bytes_per_full_token=9064` (spec-inflated), `c128_state_fixed=7.83 GB`, `swa_ring_fixed=1.99 GB`, `c4_state_fixed=1.21 GB` — matches the bf16 layout + request-scoped fixed rings. Non-unified (fp8) path logs/sizes are unchanged. | full_token | before | after | | --- | --- | --- | | capacity | 8, 898, 560 | 12,047,104 | ### Stress (`bench_serving`, random) 1800 prompts × 51200-token input, 500-token output, concurrency 1800 (92.16M input tokens). - **1800 / 1800 requests completed, 0 crashes / 0 pool-leak errors** across the full run. - Peak `full token usage` 0.96 (previously the saturation zone that tripped idle/leak asserts). - Peak concurrent requests 1800. - MTP accept length 3.07; total token throughput 44,415 tok/s. ### Throughput (8k in / 1k out, concurrency 1024) | config | Total token throughput (tok/s) | Mean TTFT (ms) | Mean TPOT (ms) | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | before | 4523.21 | 89981.16 | 130.75 | | apply PR | 4559.63 | 90483.00 | 129.75 | ### GSM8K (5-shot,) **accuracy 0.950, invalid 0.000** — confirms the sizing / SWA-accounting changes do not affect correctness. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:no_entry_sign: [Run #32342868416](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32342868416)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32342868309](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32342868309)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32342868355](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32342868355)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [Feature] Add MiniCPM-SALA support
signals.text: <!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. --> ## Motivation Add native serving support for MiniCPM-SALA checkpoints, which interleave MiniCPM sparse softmax-attention layers with constant-decay Lightning linear-attention layers. The implementation integrates the model with SGLang's existing attention, linear-attention, CUDA graph, and memory-pool infrastructure. It also replaces the serving-time dependency on the original out-of-tree block-table extension with SGLang JIT kernels. ## Modifications - Add `MiniCPMHybridConfig` and register both `MiniCPMForCausalLM` and `MiniCPMSALAForCausalLM`. - Normalize mixer aliases and repeat mixer patterns to the configured layer count. - Parse both flattened and legacy nested sparse-attention configuration. - Describe Lightning state using the existing `Mamba2CacheParams` and linear-attention model registry. - Extend the MiniCPM model with SALA mixer support. - Add Lightning QKV projection, optional Q/K normalization, RoPE, output normalization and gating, configurable attention scaling, and checkpoint-compatible weight loading. - Reuse the in-tree Lightning backend and `seg_la` kernels instead of introducing a model-specific linear-attention backend or external dependency. - Generalize the shared Lightning backend to read the linear KV-head count, layerwise decay mode, and per-layer attention scale from the model config. - Add `minicpm_flashattn` and `minicpm_flashinfer` sparse-attention backends. - Compose with `FlashAttentionBackend` for dense metadata and CUDA graph state. - Keep FlashInfer support as a composed decode path rather than duplicating its wrapper management. - Select FA4 automatically on supported Blackwell GPUs. - Support dense/sparse prefill and decode, CUDA graph capture/replay, K1/K2 key compression, sparse top-k selection, and optional fused TileLang kernels. - Add JIT-compiled CUDA block-table kernels. - Use v2 for prefill and v3 for the optimized decode layout, with automatic v2 fallback for unsupported v3 shapes. - Cache compiled modules by top-k, head-group count, and block size. - Attach the MiniCPM compressed cache to the existing `ReqToTokenPool`. - Reserve and account for K1/K2 capacity without introducing a model-specific pool subclass. - Route extend/decode allocation, rollback, request release, streaming-session cleanup, allocator reset, and pool statistics through generic no-op auxiliary-cache hooks. - Add MiniCPM model overrides and developer controls. - Default sparse SALA models to `minicpm_flashattn`, or `minicpm_flashinfer` on supported Blackwell GPUs. - Disable radix caching only for configs that actually contain sparse or Lightning layers. - Reject unsupported sparse-attention PD disaggregation early. - Add `SGLANG_MINICPM_FUSE_TOPK`, `SGLANG_MINICPM_SPLIT_STAGE1`, `SGLANG_MINICPM_DENSE_AS_SPARSE`, and `SGLANG_MINICPM_FORCE_DENSE` environment switches. - Add CPU and CUDA coverage for configuration defaults, model overrides, Lightning dispatch, compressed-cache lifecycle, sparse metadata, block-table kernels, and compression kernels. ## Accuracy Tests The following CPU regression suite passes on the final rebased branch: ```text 112 passed, 8 subtests passed ``` It covers: - signals.title: [Refactor] New EPD
signals.text: ## Motivation The EPD encoder had grown into a single 4464-line `python/sglang/srt/disaggregation/encode_server.py` that owned the FastAPI application, the DP launcher, the request scheduler, CPU preprocessing, the GPU forward, and both transfer backends at the same time. That coupling caused three concrete problems: **1. Duplicated orchestration.** HTTP non-DP and DP workers each maintained their own copy of encode scheduling, batch/direct branching, backend detection, metadata publication, embedding staging, send scheduling, error handling, resource release and metrics updates. On top of that: - single-request and batch encode had two separate implementations; - Mooncake, ZMQ-to-scheduler and ZMQ-to-tokenizer each carried near-identical send logic; - `send` and `release` were tightly coupled, and embedding cleanup was scattered across the normal, error and timeout branches. **2. Unsafe resource lifetimes.** Because `send` implicitly released embeddings and cleanup lived in several places, concurrent encode / send / release had no ordering guarantee: a release racing an in-flight forward could tear down state that a pending send still needed, and a failed encode could leave a `send` waiting forever. **3. No layer to build on.** There was no protocol-neutral home for scheduling, so gRPC could not reuse the HTTP backend topology, and neither the CPU preprocessing nor the HTTP layer could be replaced by a Rust implementation. This PR restructures the encoder into a package with explicit layers and unifies everything after `receive` into a single pipeline, while keeping the external HTTP/gRPC surface unchanged. ## Modifications ## 2. One inference lifecycle for every path Everything after `receive` now follows a single chain, identically for HTTP non-DP and for DP workers: ``` receive (protocol-specific entry point) → execute_encode_pipeline → MMEncoder.encode / batch_encode → acquire encode ref → preprocess → publish metadata → model forward → stage embedding → release encode ref → delivery.send → release_request ``` - `encode()` becomes a batch-of-one call into `batch_encode()`, so there is no second encode implementation. `EncoderScheduler` only decides *whether* requests coalesce into a batch. - `execute_encode_pipeline()` owns metrics and tracing, direct-vs-batched dispatch, metadata publication, the `MMEncoder` call, final metadata sync, the ZMQ synchronous send or the Mooncake metadata response, and resource release on the normal, error and timeout paths. - `ReqState` holds the whole per-request lifecycle: `embedding_data`, `embedding_ready`, `active_encodes`, `active_sends`, `release_requested`, `preserve_metadata_on_release`, `lifecycle_condition`, driven by `_acquire_encode_ref()` / `_release_encode_ref()`. The resulting guarantees: - a release issued during encode cannot delete request state early; - a release waits until `active_sends == 0`; - once a release is requested, new sends are rejected; - a shared embedding is freed only after all destinations have finished; - a failed encode still stages the error, so a waiting `send` can never block forever. - `EncoderDelivery` isolates the backend differences. The previous `ZmqSchedulerDelivery` and `ZmqTokenizerDelivery` collapse into one `ZmqDelivery` parameterized by `cleanup_receive_state`; `self.transfer_backend` / `self.use_mooncake` are cached on `MMEncoder` instead of re-reading `server_args.encoder_transfer_backend` all over the code. - `embedding_to_send.pop()`, `discard_embedding()`, handler-`finally` cleanup, the Mooncake callback cleanup and the ZMQ rendezvous cleanup all collapse into `release_request()`. - Mooncake marks an embedding ready **only after the CUDA stream is synchronized**, so an RDMA read can no longer observe a GPU buffer whose write has not landed. Global-cache embeddings keep their existing per-send registration semantics. ### 3. Metadata is published right after preprocess Every backend publishes embedding shape, dtype and size as soon as preprocessing completes — before the forward runs. At that point `ReqState.embedding_data` holds a metadata placeholder; the real embedding is staged and validated afterwards, which is what sets `embedding_ready`. For Mooncake non-DP this lets the receiver call `/scheduler_receive_meta_data`, then allocate and register its landing buffer **in parallel with the encoder forward**; the RDMA transfer itself still waits for `embedding_ready`. ZMQ publishes the same metadata today, but has no early consumer yet. ### 4. Preprocessing metadata consolidated `EncoderPreprocessResult` returns `mm_inputs`, `grid_thw` and `token_counts` together. Grid normalization and patch/token counting move out of `MMEncoder` into `EncoderPreprocessor`, so `process_mm_items` parses the grid exactly once and the direct, cache, Mooncake and batch paths reuse the same result. `slice_embedding` and `_encode_missing` no longer recompute token counts from the grid. ### 5. Receiver: one embedding pool for both backends - `EmbeddingPool` absorbs `MooncakeEmbeddingPool` and gains `try_stage` / `release_on_gc`. When `SGLANG_EMBEDDING_POOL_SIZE_MB` is set explicitly, `zmq_to_scheduler` also keeps received embeddings resident in the GPU pool: zero-copy per-modality views, slot lifetime bound to `mm_inputs` garbage collection, and a `PENDING` retry when the pool is full. **Default behaviour is unchanged** — the 4096 MB default still applies to Mooncake only. - RDMA buffer release becomes an ownership transfer to the receiving thread, which removes an up-to-1800 s `join` block on the scheduler main thread. - `WaitingMMRequestBase` (ABC) unifies `recv_embedding`; the backend differences shrink to three abstract methods — `send_encode_request`, `_extract_embedding_from_buffer`, `_prepare_embedding_buffer`. Seven separate failure paths merge into `_fail_and_release`, and the classes are renamed off "Image" into the `Zmq` / `Grpc` / `RDMA` families. - Dead code on the `zmq_to_tokenizer` path is removed. ## EPD performance results ### Common workload - 4 random 1080p JPEG images per request - Random input length 1024, output length 64 - Temperature 0, request rate `inf` - Radix cache and MM global cache disabled - Paired values below are `main/new_epd` ## Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct ### Test setup - One 8×H20 node - Encoder TP1 on GPU 0–1; Language TP1 on GPU 2 - Encoder/Language memory fraction: 0.60 - `single`: client concurrency 1, scheduler max batch 1, 8 requests per round - `batch`: client concurrency 4, scheduler max batch 4, 16 requests per round - Each case used 2 warmup requests followed by 3 measured rounds - Results are the median of the 3 rounds - `zmq_to_scheduler` used a 4096 MB embedding pool ### Results | Encoder DP | Path | Backend | Throughput (req/s) | Median TTFT (ms) | Median TPOT (ms) | |---:|---|---|---:|---:|---:| | 1 | single | Tokenizer | 0.288/0.294 | 3058/2976 | 6.774/6.783 | | 1 | single | Scheduler | 0.293/0.362 | 2990/2331 | 6.786/6.775 | | 1 | single | Mooncake | 0.368/0.403 | 2280/2047 | 6.783/6.778 | | 1 | batch | Tokenizer | 0.447/0.448 | 7095/7076 | 19.498/19.452 | | 1 | batch | Scheduler | 0.436/0.519 | 7476/5945 | 19.439/18.077 | | 1 | batch | Mooncake | 0.525/0.566 | 5860/5352 | 19.421/19.429 | | 2 | single | Tokenizer | 0.282/0.297 | 3122/2934 | 6.780/6.776 | | 2 | single | Scheduler* | 0.334/0.362 | 2556/2343 | 6.777/6.776 | | 2 | single | Mooncake | 0.366/0.402 | 2299/2058 | 6.784/6.779 | | 2 | batch | Tokenizer | 0.488/0.487 | 6369/6367 | 28.541/28.516 | | 2 | batch | Scheduler* | 0.478/0.582 | 6708/5121 | 26.301/27.547 | | 2 | batch | Mooncake | 0.591/0.636 | 4975/4574 | 28.569/26.525 | \* For DP2 Scheduler, main used two independent TP1/DP1 Encoders, while new_epd used one internal TP1/DP2 Encoder. ## Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-FP8 ### Test setup - Two 8×H20 nodes - Language TP8 and Encoder deployed on separate nodes - Encoder/Language memory fraction: 0.70 - `DP4`: one TP1/DP4 Encoder process and one Encoder URL - `4×DP1`: four independent TP1/DP1 Encoders and four Encoder URLs - Concurrency 1: 16 warmup and 16 measured requests - Concurrency 8/32: 32 warmup and 64 measured requests - Results below use the second measured round - Scheduler embedding pool: 4096 MB ### Configurations | Client concurrency / scheduler max batch | Encoder layout | Encoder URLs | |---|---|---:| | 1/1 | DP1 | 1 | | 8/8 | DP4 | 1 | | 8/8 | 4×DP1 | 4 | | 32/8 | DP4 | 1 | | 32/8 | 4×DP1 | 4 | | 32/32 | 4×DP1 | 4 | ### Results | Concurrency / max batch | Layout | Backend | Throughput (req/s) | Median TTFT (ms) | Median TPOT (ms) | |---|---|---|---:|---:|---:| | 1/1 | DP1 | Tokenizer | 0.555/0.532 | 1438/1444 | 5.227/5.521 | | 1/1 | DP1 | Scheduler | 0.536/0.554 | 1470/1388 | 5.287/5.357 | | 1/1 | DP1 | Mooncake | 0.579/0.634 | 1315/1216 | 5.550/5.468 | | 8/8 | DP4 | Tokenizer | 1.487/1.495 | 4179/4183 | 18.838/18.889 | | 8/8 | DP4 | Scheduler | —/1.543 | —/3864 | —/19.014 | | 8/8 | DP4 | Mooncake | —/1.761 | —/3339 | —/19.010 | | 8/8 | 4×DP1 | Tokenizer | 1.568/1.651 | 3398/2815 | 18.652/33.909 | | 8/8 | 4×DP1 | Scheduler | 1.358/1.464 | 4323/4158 | 19.737/19.054 | | 8/8 | 4×DP1 | Mooncake | 1.865/1.910 | 2965/2718 | 20.067/18.725 | | 32/8 | DP4 | Tokenizer | 1.605/1.687 | 12621/11471 | 85.097/97.416 | | 32/8 | DP4 | Scheduler | —/1.585 | —/13857 | —/96.598 | | 32/8 | DP4 | Mooncake | —/2.246 | —/7814 | —/95.164 | | 32/8 | 4×DP1 | Tokenizer | 1.683/1.603 | 11529/12062 | 112.268/122.776 | | 32/8 | 4×DP1 | Scheduler | 1.341/1.389 | 16667/13518 | 108.282/108.752 | | 32/8 | 4×DP1 | Mooncake | 2.126/2.310 | 8433/7584 | 109.113/95.207 | | 32/32 | 4×DP1 | Tokenizer | 1.625/1.656 | 12093/11577 | 96.304/93.734 | | 32/32 | 4×DP1 | Scheduler | 1.551/1.607 | 12602/13285 | 115.445/96.704 | | 32/32 | 4×DP1 | Mooncake | 2.101/2.112 | 8615/8826 | 100.019/69.134 | `—` denotes an unsupported main DP4 combination. ### Known limitations in `main` - `main` does not support the `zmq_to_scheduler` path with Encoder DP enabled. - On the Mooncake path, enabling Encoder DP while running the Language service with TP greater than 1 causes request routing and embedding-lifecycle errors. signals.text: ## Motivation Integrates TRT-LLM attention kernel for DSv4 style attention (CSA, HCA). ## Modifications ## Accuracy Tests ``` SGLANG_DSV4_ATTN_DECODE_BACKEND=flashmla/trtllm_gen \ python -m sglang.launch_server --model-path deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro \ --trust-remote-code --tp 8 --moe-runner-backend flashinfer_mxfp4 \ --chunked-prefill-size 4096 --disable-flashinfer-autotune \ --mem-fraction-static 0.88 --max-running-requests 32 ``` ### GSM8K Accuracy GSM8K V4-Pro flashmla: 0.965 GSM8K V4-Pro trtllm_gen: 0.985 ### GPQA (add --chat-template to above server command) ``` python3 -m sglang.test.run_eval --port 21000 --eval-name gpqa \ --num-examples 198 --max-tokens 120000 --repeat 8 \ --thinking-mode deepseek-v3 ``` FlashMLA: Repeat: 8, mean: 0.885 Scores: ['0.889', '0.879', '0.889', '0.879', '0.869', '0.899', '0.904', '0.874'] TRTLLM: Repeat: 8, mean: 0.907 Scores: ['0.919', '0.904', '0.894', '0.904', '0.909', '0.919', '0.904', '0.904'] ## Speed Tests and Profiling ### Unit Kernel Benchmarking (ran with private benchmarking repo): ``` # prefill (varlen), long contexts python benchmark.py --backends flashmla_dsv4,trtllm_gen_dsv4 --model deepseek-v4 \ --hw b200 --dtype fp8 --mode prefill --tp 1 \ --batch-sizes 1,2 --seq-lens 4096,16384,65536 --graph # decode, low/mid concurrency x long contexts python benchmark.py --backends flashmla_dsv4,trtllm_gen_dsv4 --model deepseek-v4 \ --hw b200 --dtype fp8 --mode decode --tp 1 \ --batch-sizes 1,4,16,64 --seq-lens 1024,4096,16384,65536,131072 --graph # decode, high concurrency python benchmark.py --backends flashmla_dsv4,trtllm_gen_dsv4 --model deepseek-v4 \ --hw b200 --dtype fp8 --mode decode --tp 1 \ --batch-sizes 128,256,512,1024 --seq-lens 256,1024,4096,16384 --graph ``` Prefill: ~1.2x faster Decode: ~1.45x faster The performance for TP > 1 scales better on trtllm-gen, since it seems the flashmla variant requires padding the head_dim to 64 or 128. signals.title: [Benchmark] Add optional steady-state window for serving metrics
signals.text: ## Motivation In prefill-decode (PD) disaggregated deployments, the benchmark includes ramp-up and drain phases: - Decode workers have not reached their sustained concurrency during ramp-up. - Requests gradually leave decode workers during drain. - Full-run throughput therefore does not accurately represent steady-state PD performance. This PR adds a dedicated steady-state benchmark mode for measuring sustained throughput in PD-disaggregated serving, without changing the shared `serving.py` implementation or affecting existing benchmarks. ## Changes - Add a standalone steady-state metrics module. - Add a dedicated entry point: `sglang.benchmark.steady_state_serving`. - Select the longest continuous interval whose request concurrency remains above a configured ratio of peak concurrency. - Exclude low-concurrency ramp-up and drain periods from steady-state metrics. - Report: - steady-state duration - minimum and peak concurrency - completed requests - input token throughput - output token throughput - retokenized output throughput - average concurrency - peak output throughput - Support writing steady-state results to a separate JSONL file. - Keep the regular full-run serving benchmark results unchanged. - Keep `python/sglang/benchmark/serving.py` identical to the base branch. ## Metric Definition The concurrency threshold is calculated as: ```text ceil(peak_concurrency * steady_state_concurrency_ratio) ``` The longest continuous interval above this threshold is selected as the steady-state window. Output throughput uses the available TTFT and ITL timestamps to estimate how many output tokens fall inside the window. Input tokens do not have per-token prefill timestamps. Input throughput therefore uses an arrival-based definition: prompt tokens from successful requests started within [window_start, window_end) ÷ steady_state duration For workloads where aligned input requests are unavailable, such as the current multi-turn path, input throughput is reported as N/A. ## Usage python -m sglang.benchmark.steady_state_serving \ --steady-state-concurrency-ratio 0.8 \ --backend sglang \ --base-url http://: \ --dataset-name random \ --num-prompts 1000 Optionally save the steady-state result separately: --steady-state-output-file steady_state_results.jsonl

signals.title: [AMD][DSV4] unified_kv: SWA per-request ring runtime accounting
signals.text: ## Motivation Follow-up to #30315 (pool **sizing** for `unified_kv`), complementary to #29168 (unified-KV **HiSparse device pool**). This PR adds the **runtime accounting** so the scheduler and allocator treat the unified SWA pool as a **fixed per-request ring** instead of a linearly-consumed token pool. On the unified path SWA/compress state is addressed by `state_slot (== req_pool_idx)` inside the DSV4 kernels; the paged SWA indices / `full_to_swa_index_mapping` are never consumed. Accounting SWA as a linear token pool therefore over-throttles admission and decode retract, even though the real bound is concurrency (`num_req_slots`). > Stacked on #30315 — the first commits belong to that PR; review only the last commit (`SWA per-request ring runtime accounting`). Will rebase onto `main` once #30315 merges. The unified HiSparse C4 device pool is **not** in this PR (that is #29168); this PR only forwards `swa_ring_cost_tokens` through the DSV4-HiSparse wrapper. ## Modifications All changes are gated on `get_kvcache()._unified_kv`; the non-unified (fp8) path is unchanged. - **`swa.py`** — account SWA as a fixed per-request ring slot (`swa_ring_cost_tokens`) bounded by `num_req_slots` (via `req_to_token_pool`), not linear token consumption. `available_size` / `swa_available_size` / `new_pages_available` / `alloc_extend` / `alloc_decode` take the unified branch and skip the vestigial paged SWA allocator + mapping. - **`schedule_policy.py`** — `rem_swa_tokens` / `_swa_budget_for_req` use the ring-based `swa_available_size` and charge exactly one fixed ring slot per request; skip the linear SWA clamp and the double-charge on chunked continuations. - **`schedule_batch.py`** — unified-KV `check_decode_mem` diagnostic (`[SWA-BOTTLENECK]`, throttled). - **`hisparse.py`** — forward `swa_ring_cost_tokens` through the DSV4-HiSparse wrapper (device pool itself is #29168). - **`model_runner_kv_cache_mixin.py`** — wire `req_to_token_pool` into the SWA allocator. ## Validation Validated on **DeepSeek-V4-Pro, `unified_kv`, TP8 / DP8, ROCm** (with #29168 for `--enable-hisparse`). Server reaches ready and unified ring accounting engages: ``` [SWA-BOOKKEEPING] unified ring accounting enabled: num_slots=129, swa_ring_size=128, ring_cost_tokens=256, unified_swa_pages=16512 | legacy paged size_swa=... (bypassed) Unified-KV: reconciling swa_max_total_num_tokens ... -> ... (fixed per-request SWA ring capacity) ``` <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:no_entry_sign: [Run #32342868725](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32342868725)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32342868372](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32342868372)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #32342868681](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32342868681)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [PP&Spec] enable speculative decoding (eagle_worker_v2) under PP
signals.text: Roadmap: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/11857 PP+Dspark is supported base on this PR, the link is https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/32281 ## Motivation `server_args.py` previously asserted that `pp_size > 1` and a speculative algorithm could not be enabled together. This PR removes that restriction and enables EAGLE speculative decoding to run under pipeline parallelism, tested on GLM52 and Deepseek-V4-Flash. ## Modifications The draft worker is created only on the last PP rank; every rank runs its own target forward and verify, the draft tree is carried across stages and rebuilt locally per rank, and the accepted-token KV bookkeeping is moved out of the verify epilogue into a per-rank post-processing step. 1. Draft worker created only on the last PP rank. Non-last ranks have no draft worker, draft KV pool, or draft `lm_head`; they forward target layers and relay hidden states / proxy tensors downstream. All draft-accessing paths are null-guarded. 2. Target hidden capture (`capture_hidden = FULL`) enabled only on the last rank; upstream ranks capture nothing and pass the hidden/proxy along. 3. The draft tree produced on the last rank (draft/bonus/parent indices, accept info) is serialized as plain lists, added to the existing PP tensor dict, and reconstructed on every other pp rank into a verify input matching that rank's own KV layout and attention buffers, so each rank builds its tree mask / positions locally. 4. Sampling / acceptance / grammar run only on the last rank; non-last ranks skip that epilogue and execute only the target-layer forward for the verified tokens. 5. Accept-token write-back and sequence-length update are moved into the scheduler's `batch_result_processor`, which runs on every PP rank; the old single-point finalize path is skipped under PP. 6. The scheduler takes a dedicated non-overlap path that threads `pp_proxy_tensors` through generation and triggers the per-rank cache update afterwards. Other changes: - MTP/nextn model layer: the context-parallel split is applied to the spec hidden states under PP + MTP. On GLM-5.2 (chunked-prefill-size 8192) this lowers per-step `draft_extend_for_prefill` time on the last PP rank from 27 ms to 20 ms (The data is profiled on 2 8*H20 nodes). - Weight loading: the nextn draft's `embed_tokens` is loaded on the last rank directly rather than recycled from the target; non-last ranks keep skipping it. `lm_head` / `embed` access is split into separate hooks so the PP draft shares only `lm_head`. - CUDA graph compatibility: the static `pp_proxy_tensors` buffers are sized by max token count (not batch size); the decode graph runner copies the proxy tensors into the graph buffer before replay. Limitations asserted: PP + spec disables `mixed-chunk` prefill and `speculative_adaptive`; only EAGLE algorithm are permitted under PP for now. ## Accuracy Tests Setup: DeepSeek-V4-Flash-FP8, single 8*H20 node; GSM8K accuracy (200 examples, 5-shot, temperature=0) | Configuration | GSM8K Accuracy (%) | |---|---| | PP2-TP4 (no spec) | 98.50 | | PP2-TP4 + MTP314 (this PR) | 98.50 | | TP8 + MTP314 | 98.50 | ## Speed Tests Setup: DeepSeek-V4-Flash-FP8, single 8*H20 node; EAGLE draft with `speculative-num-steps=3`, `speculative-eagle-topk=1`, `speculative-num-draft-tokens=4`. Three configs sweep the input length (16k / 32k / 64k): **TTFT (ms)** | Configuration | 16k | 32k | 64k | |---|---|---|---| | PP2-TP4 (no spec) | 653.59 | 1142.21 | 2197.28 | | PP2-TP4 + MTP314 | 658.30 | 1135.22 | 2124.52 | | TP8 + MTP314 | 534.70 | 1080.04 | 2212.80 | **TPOT (ms)** | Configuration | 16k | 32k | 64k | |---|---|---|---| | PP2-TP4 | 11.67 | 11.71 | 11.68 | | PP2-TP4 + MTP314 (this PR) | 5.42 | 5.53 | 5.65 | | TP8 + MTP314 | 4.19 | 4.26 | 4.45 | ## Checklist - [ ] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to the [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to the [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [ ] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process). 2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers. 3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so. - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci` 4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32382552977](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32382552977)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32382552472](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32382552472)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32382552886](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32382552886)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [dLLM] Decouple prefill chunk size from decode block size
signals.text: ## Motivation This PR addresses the long-prefill optimization proposed in #24644 and #24645. Previously, dLLM prefill and decode shared the same `block_size` (typically 32). As a result, a long prompt could advance by only one decode block per scheduler round, causing excessive scheduling overhead and underutilizing the GPU. This PR decouples the maximum prefill chunk size from the fixed decode block size: - decode still processes exactly one `block_size` block per request; - pure prefill can process multiple aligned blocks in one scheduler round; - the non-aligned prompt tail is handled together with masks by the following decode block. ### Execution-mode separation Pure-prefill requests intentionally use the regular `ForwardMode.EXTEND`, while decode requests continue to use `ForwardMode.DLLM_EXTEND`. Pure prefill has a dynamic extend length and commits only real prompt KV; decode must preserve the fixed `block_size` dLLM semantics and its dedicated CUDA Graph path. **This separation is a key correctness point for review.** The scheduler must determine the final request phase before it constructs the phase-aware `PrefillAdder` and selects the forward mode. A stale or prematurely selected prefill phase could incorrectly send a decode request through regular `EXTEND` instead of `DLLM_EXTEND`. ### Phase-selection correctness problems addressed This PR also fixes two ordering issues exposed by multi-block prefill: 1. `determine_dllm_phase()` previously ran with stale `prefix_indices`. Prefix-cache matching could update the matched prefix without reclassifying the request, so a prompt-tail-plus-mask block could remain incorrectly classified as pure prefill. Phase determination now runs after cache matching has finalized `prefix_indices`. 2. `get_new_batch_dllm()` previously selected `is_prefill`, created the adder, and selected the forward mode before incoming requests were fully prepared. Even if `process_dllm_incoming_reqs()` later changed a request to decode, the current round had already been configured as prefill. All managed dLLM requests are now collected and prepared before phase selection, so the adder and forward mode are constructed from the final cache-matched phases. Related to #24644, #24645. ## Modifications ### Configurable multi-block prefill - Add an optional `prefill_block_size` field to `--dllm-algorithm-config`. - Add `--dllm-prefill-block-size` as a command-line override for the YAML `prefill_block_size` value. - Default `prefill_block_size` to `block_size` to preserve the existing behavior. - Require `prefill_block_size >= block_size` and divisibility by `block_size`. - Require users to explicitly pass `--attention-backend flashinfer` when `prefill_block_size > block_size`, because multi-block dLLM prefill currently depends on FlashInfer's custom attention-mask support. - Reject unsupported attention backend combinations at startup instead of silently using incorrect attention semantics. The existing single-block behavior (`prefill_block_size == block_size`) is unaffected by this requirement. Example: ```yaml block_size: 32 prefill_block_size: 1024 threshold: 0.95 ``` The YAML value can be overridden without editing the configuration file: ```bash python -m sglang.launch_server ... \ --dllm-prefill-block-size 1024 \ --attention-backend flashinfer ``` ### Phase-aware dLLM scheduling - Separate pure-prefill scheduling from fixed-size decode scheduling. - Fetch incoming requests and prepare all managed dLLM requests before selecting the round phase. - Re-run phase determination after prefix-cache matching updates `prefix_indices`, preventing stale-prefix phase classification. - Use phase-aware scheduler budgets: - prefill: `max_running_requests * prefill_block_size`; - decode: `max_running_requests * block_size`. - Perform prefix-cache matching before determining the dLLM phase. - Construct the phase-aware adder and select `EXTEND` versus `DLLM_EXTEND` only after the final request phases are known. - Preserve the incoming request lifecycle until admission by `PrefillAdder`. - Prefer staging requests over incoming requests within the same phase. - Prevent unadmitted requests from advancing `dllm_block_offset`. - Align pure-prefill frontiers to `block_size`. For example, with `block_size=32` and a 300-token prompt, pure prefill advances to token 288. The remaining 12 prompt tokens and 20 masks are processed by the next 32-token decode block. ### Block-wise prefill attention Multi-block dLLM prefill uses the following visibility rule, where `B` is the dLLM block size: ```text visible(q, k) = floor(k / B) <= floor(q / B) ``` The custom-mask implementation in this PR is an interim solution until FlashInfer's native [Block Extend Attention support](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/2722) is merged, released, and available in SGLang's supported FlashInfer version. Once that native operator is available, this path can use its block-expanding mask semantics directly and avoid constructing and passing an additional attention mask. Migrating to the native operator is therefore the intended follow-up rather than keeping the explicit custom-mask path permanently. This provides: - bidirectional attention within the same dLLM block; - visibility into all preceding blocks; - isolation from future blocks. Masked and unmasked ragged prefill use separate persistent FlashInfer wrappers. The custom-mask wrapper is pinned to FA2, preventing an unmasked FA3 plan from being incorrectly reused for a later masked request on SM90. Unsupported combinations such as multi-block custom masks with sliding-window dispatch or multi-item scoring fail explicitly. ### Breakable prefill CUDA Graph - Run pure dLLM prefill through `ForwardMode.EXTEND`. - Allow reuse of Breakable prefill CUDA Graphs when: - CUDA and FlashInfer are used; - the prefill graph backend is Breakable; - the token count exactly matches a captured bucket; - no unsupported input mode is active. - Fall back to eager execution when these conditions are not satisfied. - Propagate dLLM prefill metadata through graph replay so the same block-wise mask is reconstructed. Exact bucket matching is required because upward padding would change dLLM bidirectional attention and KV-write semantics. ### Tests and documentation - Add scheduler/configuration tests for: - phase-aware budgets; - aligned and non-aligned prompt boundaries; - incoming request lifecycle and prefix-cache phase detection; - fixed decode blocks; - request admission and offset updates; - FlashInfer backend validation; - Breakable CUDA Graph capability checks. - Add FlashInfer attention tests for: - block-mask construction; - heterogeneous batches; - single-block fast path; - non-aligned prefixes; - masked/unmasked wrapper isolation; - ragged output against a dense reference; - prefix cascade output and LSE parity; - future-block isolation; - paged fallback parity. - Document the new server argument and scheduling/attention design. ## Accuracy Tests Validation environment: | Item | Value | | ------------------------ | --------------------------- | | GPU | 2x NVIDIA H200 143 GB | | Model | `inclusionAI/LLaDA2.0-mini` | | PyTorch | `2.11.0+cu128` | | FlashInfer | `0.6.12` | | dLLM block size | 32 | | Multi-block prefill size | 1024 | ### GSM8K quality GSM8K was evaluated with 200 examples, `temperature=0`, TP=1, and radix cache disabled. | Configuration | Score | | -------------------------- | ----- | | Main baseline | 0.895 | | Current single-block eager | 0.895 | | Multi-block eager | 0.915 | | Multi-block Breakable | 0.910 | Acceptance results: ```text multi_eager - main = +0.020 multi_eager - single_block = +0.020 multi_breakable - multi_eager = -0.005 ``` Both the multi-block eager and Breakable configurations pass the configured absolute and relative quality thresholds. Single-block and multi-block execution are not expected to be token-identical for longer prompts because changing the prefill chunk boundaries also changes kernel shapes, KV submission boundaries, and floating-point accumulation. This difference was also observed after forcing both paths to FA2. The end-to-end GSM8K quality evaluation shows no accuracy regression. ## Speed Tests and Profiling ### GSM8K latency (H200, TP=1, 200 examples) | Configuration | Latency (s) | Output throughput (tok/s) | | --- | ---: | ---: | | Main baseline | 65.8 | 381.0 | | Current single-block eager | 121.6 | 205.2 | | Multi-block eager | 58.6 | 435.0 | | Multi-block Breakable | 47.1 | 540.7 | Compared with the existing single-block eager configuration: - multi-block eager improves output throughput from `205.2` to `435.0 tok/s` (`2.12x`); - multi-block Breakable improves output throughput to `540.7 tok/s` (`2.63x`); - multi-block Breakable reduces evaluation latency from `121.6s` to `47.1s`. Compared with multi-block eager, Breakable prefill graph replay improves output throughput by approximately `1.24x`. ### Prefill serving matrix (H200, TP=1, exact Breakable buckets) Full matrix under `benchmark_results/pr_prefill_perf_matrix_20260720/`: - configs: `main` (`block_size=32`) + current-branch `prefill_block_size ∈ {32,128,512,1024,2048,4096}` - input lengths: `128, 256, 512, 1024, 4096, 8192, 16384` - `num_prompts=16`, `output_len=64`, `max_concurrency=1`, fixed seeds (`seed = 2000 + input_len`) Input token throughput (tok/s): | input | main | pbs32 | pbs128 | pbs512 | pbs1024 | pbs2048 | pbs4096 | | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | | 128 | 528 | 416 | 451 | 438 | 441 | 441 | 442 | | 256 | 917 | 774 | 897 | 846 | 850 | 847 | 849 | | 512 | 1832 | 1545 | 1967 | 1968 | 1982 | 1989 | 1977 | | 1024 | 2563 | 2251 | 2975 | 3245 | 3250 | 3268 | 3299 | | 4096 | 4784 | 4251 | 8561 | 10759 | 12420 | 12810 | 12320 | | 8192 | 5517 | 4543 | 11845 | 18841 | 23248 | 25174 | 25671 | | 16384 | 5193 | 3757 | 13103 | 22751 | 27713 | 30709 | 29577 | vs `main` input-throughput delta at long context: | input | pbs1024 | pbs2048 | pbs4096 | | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | | 4k | +160% | +168% | +158% | | 8k | +321% | +356% | +365% | | 16k | +434% | +491% | +470% | Mean TTFT (ms) at 16k: `main 2996` → `pbs1024 410` / `pbs2048 351` / `pbs4096 365`. Notes: - Current-branch `pbs32` is slightly slower than `main` (expected overhead of the new phase-aware path with the same chunk size). - Gains grow with prompt length; sweet spot on this setup is about `prefill_block_size=2048` for 8k–16k. - Prefill CUDA-graph miss count was `0` across completed sweeps; no OOM on H200 with `mem-fraction-static` 0.75–0.85. ## Checklist - [ ] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [ ] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1.
