signals.title: feat(load-reporter): add push-based engine load reporting
signals.text:
## Motivation Load-aware routing needs one authoritative view of scheduler load across data-parallel ranks. Polling every Worker from every Router adds fan-out, creates inconsistent views, and churns connections. This PR adds the Worker-side reporter: a push channel built on the scheduler's existing snapshot publication. One shared pull per fire is broadcast to every registered Router over long-lived bidirectional gRPC streams. Router-side ingestion, discovery, retries, and the Prefill throughput extension are intentionally split into follow-up PRs so each layer can be reviewed independently. > The push channel controls *delivery*, not *snapshot age*. End-to-end > freshness stays bounded by the scheduler's snapshot publication interval; > see [Freshness](#freshness). ## Modifications ### Architecture ```mermaid flowchart LR Scheduler["Scheduler
published per-DP-rank load snapshots"] Source["Per-mode snapshot source
manager get_loads / Router SHM reader"] Fire["Single fire loop
one pull per fire + rank-set validation"] Builder["LoadReport builder
HEALTHY / STALE / UNREACHABLE"] Service["Worker gRPC service
--load-reporter-port"] Router["Routers dial in
drive Monitor streams"] Scheduler --> Source --> Fire --> Builder --> Service --> Router ``` ### Protocol and configuration - The Worker hosts `sglang.router.loadmonitor.v1.LoadMonitorService.Monitor(stream RouterFrame) returns (stream WorkerFrame)` on a fixed, opt-in `--load-reporter-port`; each external Router dials in and drives its own stream (`register` → ack → bounded first fire → periodic reports). Stable field numbers and enum values are preserved. - `RouterFrame` = `register | update_config | keep_alive | stop`, with `register` required first; `WorkerFrame` = `registered | report | error`. Re-registering the same `router_id` replaces its old session; different `router_id`s coexist. - Package `grpcio` and `protobuf` through the optional `load-reporter` extra across all supported Python wheel variants. - Reporting stays opt-in so normal SGLang installations gain no mandatory runtime dependencies. ### Reporter runtime — one timer, one pull, broadcast - A single fire-loop task owns the only timer; sessions are passive bookkeeping (deadline, lease, capacity-1 queue) and own no task or timer. - Each fire performs exactly one bounded snapshot pull (`get_loads()`, 1 s budget). The same budget covers one retry when the expected DP-rank set changes mid-pull. - One report per pull, validated and built from that attempt only: `HEALTHY`, `STALE`, or `UNREACHABLE` (empty ranks + `last_error`). There is no persistent store and no cross-report merge, so a slow or stale rank is never replaced with historical data. - The fire broadcasts the same report to every session whose deadline fired; sessions registered before the next fire share its pull for their initial report. - Each session has a capacity-1 latest-wins queue, lease TTL with keep-alive renewal, mid-stream config updates, registration-anchored deadlines, and idempotent shutdown. - Pull, transport, and shutdown failures never propagate into the inference request path. ### Freshness End-to-end snapshot freshness is bounded by the scheduler's snapshot publication path (`load_snapshot_publish_interval`), not by the gRPC delivery cadence. The report interval controls how often a report is sent, not how old the snapshot inside it is — a poll at the same cadence observes data of the same age. What the push stream adds over polling is delivery, not freshness: a negotiated per-Router cadence, connection reuse, one-pull multi-Router fan-out, leases, and bounded backpressure. ### Tokenizer integration - Single-tokenizer HTTP and native gRPC start one reporter runtime in the FastAPI lifespan (native gRPC reuses the same process and listener). - Multi-tokenizer mode: `MultiTokenizerRouter` is the sole runtime owner; HTTP workers open no streams, and elastic scale changes update the expected DP-rank set (observed by the next fire). - Standalone SMG gRPC starts the reporter at request-manager readiness; older servicers without the readiness hook fail loudly when the reporter is enabled. - The embedded offline Engine API does not own the reporter; cleanup runs in the HTTP-server lifespan, the SMG gRPC-server finally path, and `MultiTokenizerRouter.close()`. ### Tests and documentation - Unit/integration coverage (CPU, real in-process `grpc.aio`): proto contract, fire loop (shared pull deadlines, broadcast to due sessions, per-session lease gating, rank-set-change retry sharing one budget, registration-anchored cadence, stale/error reports, re-registration, shutdown), snapshot validation and report-builder contracts, snapshot sources, service handshake and error frames, composition-root lifecycle, and standalone SMG wiring. - Negative invariants: request dispatch/completion/abort never trigger a pull; topology updates never pull immediately. - Registered GPU E2E tests with a real `grpc.aio` fake Router cover single-owner, multi-owner, and standalone SMG reporting. - Documentation covers the wire contract, serving-mode matrix, fire-loop schedule, freshness model, network/deployment assumptions, and shutdown behavior. ### Design advantages - **Zero request-path coupling:** dispatch, completion, and abort have no edge into the reporting graph; there is no per-request overhead. - **Efficient fan-out:** one pull per fire shared by all due sessions, persistent bidi streams, no Router-side polling fan-out or connection churn. - **Topology-safe:** reports preserve per-DP-rank detail; rank-set changes are validated and retried within the same fire budget. - **Resilient:** per-attempt status semantics, session replacement, leases, latest-wins backpressure, and bounded shutdown prevent stale tasks from accumulating. - **Extensible:** a stable protocol and a single validation entry point provide a clean foundation for the separately reviewed Router monitor and future metrics. ## Accuracy Tests N/A for model accuracy. This PR does not change model forward code, kernels, sampling, or generated outputs. Functional validation: - Registered CPU tests cover the protocol contract, fire-loop scheduling/broadcast, snapshot validation, report builder, service behavior, lifecycle, and standalone SMG wiring. - Registered GPU E2E tests drive a real `grpc.aio` fake Router against single-owner, multi-owner, and standalone SMG modes. - Generated protobuf/gRPC bindings import successfully and expose the expected `sglang.router.loadmonitor.v1` service. ## Speed Tests and Profiling N/A for inference throughput benchmarking. This is an opt-in control-plane feature and does not modify model execution. The reporter adds no request-path overhead: there are no hooks on the dispatch/completion paths, and sampling/network I/O runs in the single background fire task. No inference-speed improvement is claimed. Reporter cadence and freshness are exercised functionally by the registered tests; no new micro-benchmarks are claimed in this revision. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process). 2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers. 3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so. - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci`. 4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR. --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): :x: [Run #32371571988](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32371571988) Latest PR Test (Extra): :x: [Run #32371571891](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32371571891) Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): :hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #32371571967](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32371571967)

signals.title: [AMD] DeepSeek-V4: add aiter fused mHC post+pre with cross-layer boundary dispatch
signals.text: ## Summary Add a HIP/aiter fused `mhc_post` + next-layer `mhc_pre` path for DeepSeek-V4 on gfx95, dispatched across the attention/MoE boundary alongside the existing TileLang and Triton fused paths. On MI355X (gfx950) this is a **+0.8%–1.8% output-throughput win across concurrency 4–64 with accuracy preserved**. ## What changed - **`python/sglang/srt/models/deepseek_common/amd/deepseek_v4_fused_mhc.py`** - `try_aiter_fused_mhc_post_pre()`: wraps `aiter.ops.mhc.mhc_fused_post_pre`. The aiter kernel self-gates fused-vs-unfused per arch/token-count, so no token threshold is duplicated here; import/runtime failures fall back and warn once. - `try_mhc_fused_post_pre_boundary()`: aiter → Triton dispatch. The two kernels expect opposite fn orientations (Triton transposed, aiter native). - `is_cross_layer_mhc_fusion_enabled()` / `_is_production_mhc_enabled()`: enable cross-layer fusion when either the TileLang path or the aiter gfx95 path is available. `_is_fused_mhc_post_pre_enabled()` is consolidated here (previously duplicated in `deepseek_v4.py`). - **`python/sglang/srt/models/deepseek_v4.py`**: route the attn-side, FFN-side, and `op_mhc_post_attn_pre_mlp` boundaries through `_apply_mhc_post_pre_boundary()`, falling back to the unfused `hc_post` + `hc_pre` sequence when no fused kernel fires. In the operation/batch-overlap path (DP attention) `state` is a `_StateDict` (attribute access, no `__getitem__`), so read it via `state.<field>`. - **`test/registered/unit/models/test_deepseek_v4_amd_fused_mhc.py`**: gating/dispatch unit tests plus a gfx95-gated numerical test asserting `next_residual` (bit-exact) and `layer_input`/`post_mix` (bf16 tolerance) vs the unfused reference. ## Validation Model: `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro`. Hardware: MI355X (gfx950), TP4. Image: `rocm/sgl-dev:v0.5.15.post1-rocm720-mi35x-20260724`. Baseline = image tree; Patched = image tree + this patch (only 2 model files differ). Env: `SGLANG_USE_AITER=1 AITER_BF16_FP8_MOE_BOUND=0 SGLANG_HACK_FLASHMLA_BACKEND=unified_kv_triton`. ### Unit test ``` $ python3 -m pytest test/registered/unit/models/test_deepseek_v4_amd_fused_mhc.py -q 8 passed ``` ### Accuracy (GSM8K, 1319 questions × 3 runs) | run | baseline | patched | |----:|:--------:|:-------:| | 1 | 0.942 | 0.947 | | 2 | 0.943 | 0.943 | | 3 | 0.937 | 0.944 | | **avg** | **0.941** | **0.945** | Invalid = 0.000 for all runs. Accuracy preserved (within run-to-run noise). ### Performance (ISL=8192, OSL=1024, output token throughput) | concurrency | baseline (tok/s) | patched (tok/s) | Δ | baseline TPOT (ms) | patched TPOT (ms) | |------------:|:----------------:|:---------------:|:-----:|:---:|:---:| | 4 | 216.38 | 219.66 | **+1.5%** | 17.507 | 17.242 | | 8 | 367.65 | 372.98 | **+1.4%** | 20.715 | 20.423 | | 16 | 568.64 | 579.04 | **+1.8%** | 26.460 | 25.960 | | 32 | 792.79 | 800.70 | **+1.0%** | 38.165 | 37.808 | | 64 | 1033.97 | 1042.04 | **+0.8%** | 58.854 | 58.412 | ### Commands used ```bash # Accuracy python3 benchmark/gsm8k/bench_sglang.py --num-questions 2000 --parallel 1200 # Performance (per concurrency C in 4 8 16 32 64) python3 benchmark_serving.py --model deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro --backend sglang \ --dataset-name random --random-input-len 8192 --random-output-len 1024 \ --random-range-ratio 0.8 --num-prompts $((C*10)) --max-concurrency C --ignore-eos ``` ## Test plan / Checklist - [x] New unit test `test_deepseek_v4_amd_fused_mhc.py` passes (8 passed; gfx95 numerical). - [x] GSM8K accuracy preserved vs baseline (0.945 vs 0.941, invalid 0.000). - [x] Output throughput improves +0.8%–1.8% at concurrency 4–64 (TP4, 8k/1k), TPOT reduced. - [x] Falls back to unfused hc_post + hc_pre when no fused kernel fires (non-gfx95 / import failure). <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:no_entry_sign: [Run #32326688204](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32326688204)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32326688046](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32326688046)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32326688151](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32326688151)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [HCU] Add Qwen3.5 and GLM-5 support
signals.text: <!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. --> ## Motivation <!-- Describe the purpose and goals of this pull request. --> ## Motivation This PR adds initial HCU support to SGLang for `gfx928`, `gfx936`, and `gfx938`, enabling Qwen3.5 and GLM-5 model serving on HCU. The changes address HCU-specific kernel compilation, unsupported runtime fast paths, EAGLE CUDA Graph buffer allocation, and GLM-5 inference accuracy. All platform-specific behavior is isolated behind `is_hcu()` or `USE_HCU` to preserve the existing CUDA and ROCm paths. This PR contains the following commits: - `[HCU] Adapt Qwen3.5-27B` - `[HCU] Fix EAGLE CUDA Graph custom mask buffer allocation` - `[HCU] Fix GLM-5 inference accuracy` - `[HCU] Unify MoE align kernel implementation` ## Modifications ### HCU platform detection and runtime fallbacks - Add `is_hcu()` detection for `gfx928`, `gfx936`, and `gfx938`. - Disable the unsupported multimem symmetric-memory all-gather path on HCU. - Disable the unavailable vLLM RMSNorm fast path on HCU. - Reject Quark W4A4 MXFP4 explicitly on HCU because its required AITER kernels are unavailable. - Keep these fallbacks HCU-only without changing the existing CUDA and ROCm behavior. ### sgl-kernel build support - Add and refine `setup_hcu.py`. - Support `gfx928`, `gfx936`, and `gfx938`. - Add `HCU_TARGET` for explicitly selecting the compilation target. - Use HCU-specific names for target detection and configuration. - Compile with `USE_HCU` and the HCU FP8 configuration. - Reuse the common `csrc/moe/moe_align_kernel.cu`. - Select the HCU Blelloch scan through `USE_HCU`. - Preserve the original CUDA warp scan and ROCm Blelloch scan paths. - Remove the duplicated `moe_align_kernel_hcu.cu`. ### EAGLE CUDA Graph support - Increase the HCU CUDA Graph custom-mask buffer capacity for EAGLE verification. - Account for the per-request draft-token square in addition to the context mask. - Keep the additional allocation isolated to HCU. ### GLM-5 inference accuracy - Bypass the unavailable Hadamard transform on HCU while keeping query and key tensors in the same unrotated space. - Preserve the existing CUDA and standard ROCm indexer paths. - Prevent the routed scaling factor from being applied twice when the HCU Triton MoE runner already applies it. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32437222023](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32437222023)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32437221867](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32437221867)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32437222146](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32437222146)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [RFC] Rust Tree Core Full Component
signals.text: ## Motivation UnifiedTreeCoreInterface support in Rust (focus on FULL component-only in this PR for early review feedbacks) ## Motivation The Unified Radix Cache was split so the tree state machine lives behind `UnifiedTreeCoreInterface`, selected by `SGLANG_UNIFIED_RADIX_TREE_CORE_BACKEND` (default `python`). This PR adds a Rust implementation of that interface as an in-tree backend registered under `rust`, covering the Full attention component. The tree core does the per-request radix walks, lock bookkeeping, and eviction scans on the scheduler's critical path; moving it to Rust takes that work off the GIL and smooths tail latency, while cache orchestration (pools, controller, action application) stays in Python. **Review guide**: the PR is two commits. The first seeds the three main Rust files with their python counterparts commented out; the second replaces them with the Rust implementation, so its diff reads as the python-to-rust translation side by side. Files without a direct python counterpart arrive as new files in the second commit. ## Modifications ### `rust/mem-cache/` — the tree core crate **Tree state machine** - `src/unified_tree_core.rs` — match/insert walks (resumable inserts with action barriers), lock APIs, device/host eviction walks, tombstone-chain deletion, HiCache backup/load-back/prefetch specs, and the sanity checker. - `src/node.rs` — the tree node: per-(component × tier) value slots and child edges keyed `(namespace, page key)`, mirroring `RadixKey.child_key`. - `src/node_arena.rs` — node storage: freelist-recycled slots behind monotonic never-recycled `NodeId` handles, with a single root serving every namespace. - `src/value.rs` — the `NodeId`/`NodeIdx_` handle types and per-slot value state. **Keys and hashing** - `src/key.rs` — the child-key trait over unigram (`Vec<i64>`) and bigram/EAGLE (`(i64, i64)`) page keys. - `src/hash.rs` — per-page SHA-256 hash chains, bit-identical to the python/native hasher. **Eviction machinery** - `src/unified_lru_list.rs` — intrusive per-slot LRU lists with lock-aware walkers. - `src/evictable_node_set.rs` — O(1) evictable-leaf sets (swap-remove vector plus a slot lookup table). - `src/eviction_strategy.rs` — LRU/FIFO/FILO priority keys for the eviction heap. **Components** - `src/components/mod.rs` — the `TreeComponent` trait the per-attention components implement, plus shared dispatch helpers. - `src/components/full.rs` — the Full attention component: lock walks, eviction, and transfer commits. Only the `[Full]` set is enabled; SWA and Mamba follow later. - `src/component_type.rs` — the `ComponentType` boundary enum (`FULL`/`SWA`/`MAMBA` values shared with python). **Boundary** - `src/python_bindings.rs` — the PyO3 binding exposing unigram and bigram tree cores; component sets other than `[Full]` are rejected with a clear error. - `src/events.rs` — KV cache events (`BlockStored`/`BlockRemoved`/`AllBlocksCleared`) for cache-aware routing. - `src/error.rs` — typed tree-core errors. **Crate scaffolding** - `Cargo.toml` / `README.md` / `src/lib.rs` — standalone crate (links libtorch via `tch`; PyO3 behind a default feature, so `cargo test` runs `--no-default-features`), docs, and module wiring. - `src/tests/` — the unit suite mirroring `src/` one file per module (566 tests, including a randomized multi-namespace op-sequence fuzz with per-step sanity checks). ### `python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/rust_tree_core/` — the backend package - `__init__.py` — registers the `rust` backend factory; the extension import stays inside the factory so unselected installs pay nothing. - `adapter.py` — `RustUnifiedTreeCore`, satisfying `UnifiedTreeCoreInterface` over the binding (tagged-tuple action/transfer marshaling at the boundary). - `extension.py` — build-and-load shim: compiles the crate with cargo on first use, deriving libtorch and the Python headers from the running interpreter's torch install, and rpaths torch/lib into the cdylib. ### Wiring and tests - `python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/unified_cache/tree_core_registry.py` — `SGLANG_UNIFIED_RADIX_TREE_CORE_BACKEND=rust` lazy-registers the in-tree backend on first lookup (no import-order dependence). - `test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_rust_tree_core.py` — end-to-end smoke through the compiled extension: registry resolution, insert/match round trip, lock accounting, and namespace isolation; module-skips when cargo is absent. ## Verification - `cargo test --no-default-features`: 566 passed. - Smoke suite: 4 passed end-to-end, including the first-use cargo build path. ## Perf Measurement & Accuracy TBD ## Review and Merge Process 1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process). 2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers. 3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so. - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci` 4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:no_entry_sign: [Run #32414095165](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32414095165)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32414095034](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32414095034)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #32414095095](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32414095095)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: :bug: [NPU] Fix Qwen3.5 GemmaRMSNorm on Ascend 950
signals.text: ## Motivation Qwen3.5 uses Gemma RMSNorm. Ascend 950 has no registered kernel for `torch_npu.npu_gemma_rms_norm`, so the previous direct NPU path prevents Qwen3.5 from loading and serving on Ascend 950. This PR is the SGLang half of the paired fix with sgl-project/sgl-kernel-npu#638. `sgl-kernel-npu` owns build-time SoC dispatch and exposes stable APIs; SGLang does not detect the SoC or choose providers. ## Modifications - keep `KernelBackend.SGL_KERNEL_NPU` as the only Gemma RMSNorm backend on Ascend - remove Gemma `TORCH_NPU` registration and the duplicated native forward path - import `npu_gemma_rms_norm` from `norm.gemma_rmsnorm` for the ordinary path and preserve the existing `norm.add_rmsnorm_bias.add_gemma_rms_norm` residual API - keep SoC/provider probing out of SGLang; preserve the legacy `srt` import fallback to `torch_npu.npu_gemma_rms_norm` for pre-provider 910 wheels, while an explicitly selected `SGL_KERNEL_NPU` backend does not silently fall back when its stable API is unavailable - report an actionable package/version error if the stable API is unavailable - preserve the established ordinary and residual call signatures in `GemmaRMSNorm` and `Gemma3RMSNorm` - preserve the explicit pure-Torch debugging switch ## Paired architecture ```text SGLang GemmaRMSNorm -> ordinary: sgl-kernel-npu npu_gemma_rms_norm -> 910 wheel (A2/A3): native Gemma ACLNN -> 950 wheel: standard RMSNorm ACLNN with 1 + weight -> residual: sgl-kernel-npu add_gemma_rms_norm -> all target wheels: add RMSNorm ACLNN with 1 + weight ``` For Ascend support, this PR requires a target-specific package built from sgl-project/sgl-kernel-npu#638. Provider selection occurs only while building that wheel; `910` is the unified logical target for both A2 and A3. ## Accuracy Tests - registry/mock coverage verifies that Ascend Gemma operations register only `SGL_KERNEL_NPU`, preserve the generic `out=` contract, and fail clearly on missing/incompatible packages - delegation tests cover the established `npu_gemma_rms_norm(...)->(output, rstd)` and `add_gemma_rms_norm(...)->(norm_output, residual_sum)` contracts for `GemmaRMSNorm` and `Gemma3RMSNorm` - `py_compile`, Black, isort, and `git diff --check` passed on Windows - Ascend 950PR_958b ordinary-path correctness: 13 cases passed - Ascend 950PR_958b residual-add correctness: 32/32 FP16/BF16 cases passed; residual sums matched exactly and normalized outputs passed `atol=2e-2, rtol=2e-2` ## Speed Tests and Profiling Both provider comparisons used Ascend 950PR_958b, 50 warmups, 200 synchronized p50 iterations, FP16/BF16, rows `1/16/128/512`, and hidden sizes `256/2048/4096/5120`. - ordinary Triton geometric speedup versus `npu_rms_norm(input, 1 + weight)`: **-20.25%**; worst regression **82.34%** - residual-add geometric `Triton / ACLNN` p50 latency ratio: **1.7765x** - residual-add ACLNN p50 latency reduction relative to Triton: **43.7%** - both Triton performance gates: **FAIL** Therefore, sgl-kernel-npu #638 uses target-specific ACLNN providers for the ordinary Gemma RMSNorm path: native `npu_gemma_rms_norm(input, weight, eps)` on the 910 target (A2/A3), and standard `npu_rms_norm(input, 1 + weight, eps)` on the 950 target. The residual-add path uses `npu_add_rms_norm(..., 1 + weight, eps)` on all supported Ascend targets. SGLang contains no shape- or SoC-based runtime dispatch. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32344726325](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32344726325)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32344726140](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32344726140)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32344726192](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32344726192)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [AMD] Enable gfx1250 Support
signals.text: ## Motivation AMD gfx1250 is a new GPU architecture that differs substantially from the existing gfx95x and gfx942 targets SGLang already supports. Several components require gfx1250-specific paths due to architectural differences: - **No MFMA/WMMA FP4 scale instructions** (`V_WMMA_SCALE_F32_32X16X128_F4`): the existing CK/ASM `fused_moe` and fp4 dense GEMM paths produce garbage or crash. - **Triton `tl.dot(fp8, fp8)` miscompiles** for contraction dim ≥ 128 on gfx1250 (verified correct at K=64, broken at K≥128), requiring bf16 upcasting in the MLA attention Triton kernels. - **`llvm.amdgcn.raw.buffer.*` buffer instructions are absent** on RDNA4 (gfx12): the `quick_all_reduce` kernel would fail to compile. - **aiter CK-backed kernels (rope, QK RMSNorm, etc.) do not build** against the gfx1250 ROCm 7.15 image's composable_kernel. - **TileLang CK-backed buffer addressing does not compile** on gfx1250, blocking the Sinkhorn/MHC path. - **`num_stages > 1` Triton pipelines miscompile** on gfx1250, causing NaN in block-FP8 matmuls. - **ROCm SDK is pip-installed** (not at `/opt/rocm`) on this new image, requiring build and runtime path fixups for AITER, TileLang, MORI, and SGLang itself. This PR brings up gfx1250 support for DSv4, DSR1, and GPT-OSS-120B models with MXFP4/FP8 quantization. ## Modifications ### Infrastructure & Docker (`docker/rocm.Dockerfile`, `scripts/ci/amd/amd_ci_install_dependency.sh`, `python/pyproject_other.toml`) - Added a new `gfx1250-rocm7_15` Docker build stage starting from `ubuntu:24.04` with pip-installed ROCm 7.15 SDK, PyTorch 2.11, and Triton 3.7. Includes path and symlink workarounds for a pip-based (non-`/opt/rocm`) ROCm SDK. - Added `GPU_ARCH_LIST_ARG` build-arg and made `PYTORCH_ROCM_ARCH` configurable; per-arch `TRITON_COMMIT_DEFAULT` env vars. - Added gfx1250-specific AITER build path (`ENABLE_CK=0`, pip `--no-build-isolation`) and MORI build path using `CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH` for the ROCm SDK. - Added gfx1250-aware TileLang `ROCM_PATH` override during CMake build. - Updated Triton rebuild logic to preserve the installed version string (workaround for ROCm 7.15 / [rocm-systems#7643](https://github.com/ROCm/rocm-systems/issues/7643)). - Renamed `SETUPTOOLS_SCM_PRETEND_VERSION` → `SGLANG_VERSION` to avoid leaking SGLang's nightly version into AITER's version. - Added `compressed-tensors==0.16.0` pin to `runtime_common` (supports torch ≥ 2.10) and dropped the old per-`srt_hip` `==0.15.0` pin. - CI install script: ROCm-version-aware AITER rebuild (`pip --no-build-isolation` for ROCm ≥ 7.15), MORI `CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH` fix, and MORI commit extraction validation. ### Core utility (`python/sglang/srt/utils/common.py`) - Added `is_gfx1250_supported()` (cached) to detect AMD RDNA4 by `gcnArchName`. - Extended `mxfp_supported()` to include `"gfx1250"`. ### sgl-kernel (`sgl-kernel/setup_rocm.py`, `sgl-kernel/csrc/allreduce/quick_all_reduce_base.h`) - Added `gfx1250` to the allowed arch list in `setup_rocm.py`; gfx1250 shares the `E4M3` FP8 type and the 128KB dynamic smem budget with gfx950. - Guarded `llvm.amdgcn.raw.buffer.load/store.v4i32` declarations behind `#if !defined(__gfx1250__)`, providing stub no-ops for RDNA4 where those intrinsics don't exist. ### Attention kernels (`python/sglang/kernels/ops/attention/`) - **`decode_attention.py`**: Do not downcast `q` to `fp8` before the QK dot; instead upcast K to `q`'s dtype (`bf16`) for the dot product, avoiding the gfx1250 fp8 dot bug at K≥128. Also keep softmax weights `p` in fp32 for the P·V accumulation (recovers GSM8K accuracy ~0.82 → ~0.92 on gfx1250 R1). - **`extend_attention.py`**: Same fp8 upcast fix and fp32 P·V fix for the prefill extend/unified kernels. - **`dsv4/unified_kv_kernels/paged_decode.py`**: On gfx1250, dispatch DSv4 sparse decode attention to `aiter.ops.triton.attention.pa_decode_sparse.pa_decode_sparse` (the triton path) instead of the custom Triton implementation. - **`dsv4/unified_kv_kernels/paged_prefill.py`**: Disable the OPUS (gfx950 ASM) prefill path on gfx1250. ### MoE gate JIT kernel (`python/sglang/kernels/jit/csrc/moe/moe_fused_gate.cuh`) - Widened `__shfl_down_sync` mask from `0xFFFFFFFF` to a 64-bit `0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFULL` on gfx1250 (which requires a 64-bit sync mask), while staying 32-bit on all other arches. ### Layernorm (`python/sglang/kernels/ops/layernorm/mhc.py`, `python/sglang/srt/layers/layernorm.py`) - On gfx1250, use aiter's Triton RMSNorm and `rmsnorm2d_fwd_with_add` instead of the CK-backed aiter equivalents (which do not build). - Added pure-torch (`_hc_split_sinkhorn_torch`) and Triton (`_hc_split_sinkhorn_triton`) implementations of the Sinkhorn MHC kernel, dispatched on gfx1250 since TileLang's CK-backed addressing does not compile there. ### Quantization – FP8 (`python/sglang/kernels/ops/quantization/fp8_kernel.py`, `python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/fp8.py`, `python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/fp8_utils.py`) - **`fp8_kernel.py`**: Added `_w8a8_block_fp8_matmul_gfx1250`, a gfx1250-specific block-FP8 matmul that: (1) upcasts fp8 operands to bf16 before `tl.dot`, (2) uses only `num_stages=1` (no SW pipelining), and (3) avoids modulo-wrap index tricks that miscompile on gfx1250. Selected automatically when `_is_gfx1250` is set. - **`fp8_utils.py`**: Force `_use_aiter = False` on gfx1250 (CK/MFMA-dependent aiter quant/GEMM kernels cannot run), directing gfx1250 to the pure-Triton block-FP8 path. Extended `triton_w8a8_block_fp8_linear` to accept pre-quantized `(input, input_scale)` from gfx1250's fused quant ops (skipping re-quantization). - **`fp8.py`**: On gfx1250, use `moe_shuffle_scale` (n32k4 layout) instead of the gfx950 `shuffle_scale` (e8m0 layout) for FP8 MoE weight scales. Respect the `AITER_FORCE_A8W4` flag to select the triton a8w4 kernel shuffle layout. ### Quantization – MXFP4 Quark schemes (`python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/quark/schemes/`) - **`quark_w4a4_mxfp4.py`**: On gfx1250 with `AITER_FORCE_A8W4=1`, dequantize FP4 weights to bf16 at load time (since no dense fp4 GEMM is available) and run a plain bf16 linear forward. Includes a pure-Python MXFP4 e2m1 → bf16 dequantization LUT. - **`quark_w4a4_mxfp4_moe.py`**: On gfx1250, use `moe_shuffle_scale` (n32k4 layout) for W4A4 MoE weight scales (instead of `e8m0_shuffle`). Shuffle weights with the (16,16) aiter layout when `AITER_FORCE_A8W4` is set. - **`quark_w4a8_mxfp4_moe.py`**: Added a dedicated gfx1250 W4A8 MoE path (`_use_gfx1250_w4a8`): bypasses the aiter CK/ASM fused_moe entirely; uses aiter's triton `moe_gemm_a8w4` kernel with a contraction-major, gate/up-interleaved, unshuffled weight layout. Weight preparation (`_process_weights_gfx1250`) and forward (`aiter_w4a8_gfx1250_forward` in new file `aiter_mxfp4_w4a8_moe.py`) are implemented separately from the gfx950 path. ### New file: `python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/fused_moe_triton/aiter_mxfp4_w4a8_moe.py` - Implements MXFP4 W4A8 GPT-OSS MoE forward for gfx1250 via `moe_gemm_a8w4`: routing, manual activation gather (in-kernel TDM gather disabled on gfx1250), static-FP8 downcast, two-GEMM (gate_up + down) execution with fused SwiGLU, and scatter back to token order. ### RoPE (`python/sglang/srt/layers/rotary_embedding/factory.py`) - Fall back from aiter's CK rope kernels to SGLang's native rope on gfx1250 (aiter rope does not build on this arch). ### Communicator / fused quant (`python/sglang/srt/layers/communicator.py`) - On gfx1250, use `fused_rms_fp8_group_quant` (triton, group_size=hidden_size = per-token) instead of aiter's CK `rmsnorm_quant` / `add_rmsnorm_quant` kernels. ### Sampler (`python/sglang/srt/layers/sampler.py`) - Disable aiter's greedy sample kernel on gfx1250 (not supported), falling back to `torch.argmax`. ### Capture mode (`python/sglang/srt/model_executor/runner_utils/capture_mode.py`) - Disable `torch.compile` during CUDA graph capture on gfx1250 (compilation + capture together triggers issues on this arch). ### MLA attention (`python/sglang/srt/models/deepseek_common/attention_forward_methods/forward_mla.py`, new `triton_qk_rmsnorm.py`) - On gfx1250 (`AITER_FORCE_A8W4=1`), substitute the aiter `fused_qk_rmsnorm` (CK-backed, doesn't build) with a self-contained Triton RMSNorm or pure-torch fallback from the new `triton_qk_rmsnorm.py`. - Fixed the RoPE skip condition to check membership in `FORWARD_ABSORB_CORE_ATTENTION_BACKENDS` (not a string equality check), preventing an incorrect empty-K bug on non-aiter backends. ### DSv4 decoder layer (`python/sglang/srt/models/deepseek_v4.py`, `deepseek_common/utils.py`, `amd/deepseek_v4_fused_mhc.py`) - Extended all `_is_gfx95_supported` guards that gate MXFP4 fused quant, MQA q/k-norm, post-attention layernorm fused rmsnorm, and the fused MHC post/pre path to also include `_is_gfx1250_supported`. - On gfx1250, the fused MHC path is enabled by `SGLANG_OPT_FUSE_MHC_POST_PRE` alone (no TileLang dependency), and the aiter Triton `try_fused_hc_post_pre` is used at all token batch sizes (no M-threshold cap, since there is no TileLang fallback). - gfx1250 does not skip the post-layernorm step after the Triton MHC kernel (since `norm_fused=False` for the aiter path). ### C4 attention indexer (`python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/dsv4/indexer.py`) - Added `_use_torch_fn` guard so the `SGLANG_FP8_PAGED_MQA_LOGITS_TORCH` env var correctly prevents the 1D c4sl unsqueeze on gfx1250. ### Server args (`python/sglang/srt/server_args.py`) - Track `_mem_fraction_static_set_by_user`: when the user explicitly sets `--mem-fraction-static`, skip the automatic 0.85 scaling for `aiter` backend with long contexts (instead, emit a warning so the user knows what is happening). ## Accuracy Tests Passed E2E accuracy tests of DSv4, DSR1, and GPT-OSS-120B. GPT-OSS-120B > AITER_FORCE_A8W4=1 ENABLE_CK=0 SGLANG_USE_AITER=1 SGLANG_USE_AITER_MOE_GU_ITLV=1 SGLANG_USE_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN=1 python3 -m sglang.launch_server --model-path /dockerx/model/gpt-oss-120b-w-mxfp4-a-fp8/ --trust-remote-code --tp 1 --prefill-attention-backend triton --decode-attention-backend aiter --max-running-requests 1024 --mem-fraction-static 0.9 --disable-radix-cache --page-size 64 DSR1 > ENABLE_CK=0 SGLANG_USE_AITER=1 AITER_FORCE_A8W4=1 AITER_GROUPED_FORCE_SPLIT_K1=1 SGLANG_MOE_SHUFFLE_GFX1250=1 ROCM_QUICK_REDUCE_QUANTIZATION=NONE SGLANG_AITER_FP8_PREFILL_ATTN=0 SGLANG_AITER_MLA_PERSIST=0 SGLANG_INT4_WEIGHT=0 SGLANG_MOE_PADDING=1 SGLANG_SET_CPU_AFFINITY=1 SGLANG_ROCM_FUSED_DECODE_MLA=0 SGLANG_USE_ROCM700A=1 AITER_GROUPED_CONTIGUOUS_TOKEN_THRESHOLD=16 python3 -m sglang.launch_server --model-path /dockerx/model/DeepSeek-R1-0528-MXFP4 --tensor-parallel-size 1 --trust-remote-code --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000 --mem-fraction-static 0.90 --chunked-prefill-size 16384 --attention-backend triton --max-running-requests 128 --kv-cache-dtype auto --page-size 64 DSv4-Flash > SGLANG_DEFAULT_THINKING=1 AITER_GROUPED_CONTIGUOUS_TOKEN_THRESHOLD=16 SGLANG_DSV4_REASONING_EFFORT=max SGLANG_USE_ROCM700A=0 SGLANG_HACK_FLASHMLA_BACKEND=unified_kv_triton AITER_BF16_FP8_MOE_BOUND=0 AITER_FORCE_A8W4=1 SGLANG_USE_AITER_MOE_GU_ITLV=0 SGLANG_OPT_FUSE_MHC_POST_PRE=0 ENABLE_CK=0 SGLANG_USE_AITER=1 AITER_GROUPED_FORCE_SPLIT_K1=1 python3 -m sglang.launch_server --model-path /dockerx/model/DeepSeek-V4-Flash --trust-remote-code --tp 1 --attention-backend dsv4 --page-size 256 --mem-fraction-static 0.60 --swa-full-tokens-ratio 0.15 --disable-shared-experts-fusion --tool-call-parser deepseekv4 --reasoning-parser deepseek-v4 --chunked-prefill-size 8192 --cuda-graph-max-bs 256 --max-running-requests 256 --disable-radix-cache --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 ## signals.title: [AMD] [sgl-kernel] Bypass caches for peer traffic in ROCm custom all-reduce
signals.text: <!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. --> ## Motivation Bypass caches for peer traffic in ROCm custom all-reduce ## Modifications The custom all-reduce reads every peer's buffer over xGMI and writes results peers consume once, so caching that traffic in L2 only pollutes the cache with single-use data. Route the packed 128-bit peer loads and result stores through cache-bypassing accessors modeled on RCCL's op128.h load128/store128. The bypass path is enabled via ROCM_HAVE_GLOBAL_DWORDX4_BUILTINS, derived from __has_builtin(__builtin_amdgcn_global_load_b128) && __has_builtin(__builtin_amdgcn_global_store_b128): when present, the b128 builtins with a system syncscope lower to global_{load,store}_dwordx4 with the sc0/sc1 cache-bypass bits set; otherwise it falls back to nontemporal (SLC) 64-bit accesses. All paths are guarded by USE_ROCM so CUDA builds are unchanged. ## Accuracy Tests Verified on gfx950 (MI35x): ISA confirms sc0/sc1 on the reduce kernel, and correctness passes for TP=2/4/8 (bitwise deterministic). ## Speed Tests and Profiling Deterministic all-reduce benchmark (TP=8, hidden=16384, bf16, 10 trials, deterministic-kernel latency in ms), baseline (ce1f2c6f4a) vs this change: batch tensor baseline bypass delta 1 32 KB 0.094 0.043 -54% 2 64 KB 0.034 0.029 -15% 4 128 KB 0.035 0.030 -14% 8 256 KB 0.038 0.032 -16% 16 512 KB 0.045 0.037 -18% 32 1 MB 0.059 0.046 -22% 64 2 MB 0.086 0.064 -26% 128 4 MB 0.146 0.100 -32% 256 8 MB 0.256 0.172 -33% 384 12 MB 0.365 0.250 -32% 512 16 MB 2.804 2.763 -1% 768 24 MB 3.054 2.940 -4% 1024 32 MB 3.276 3.052 -7% Within the custom-AR operating range (<=~8 MB) bypass consistently cuts latency ~14-33%, growing with size as L2 pollution matters more. Beyond that the 1-stage kernel is out of its intended regime (per-rank O(N) reads); bypass still never regresses. All sizes remain bitwise deterministic on both builds. ## Checklist - [ ] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [ ] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. signals.title: [CPU] Fix NUMA/core binding for DP ranks
signals.text: <!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. --> ## Motivation <!-- Describe the purpose and goals of this pull request. --> Before this PR, `ModelRunner.init_threads_binding` picked the NUMA node / core group for a worker using `tp_rank`. Under DP, DP rank 0 and DP rank 1 both resolve to tp_rank=0 and get bound to the same NUMA node/cores instead of being spread across the machine. This PR fixes this incorrect binding. ## Modifications <!-- Detail the changes made in this pull request. --> 1. `init_threads_binding` now takes `numa_index` (the worker's global device id) and `world_size = dp_size * tp_size * pp_size`, instead of `tp_rank` and `tp_size`, so every rank across every DP replica maps to a distinct NUMA node / core group. Removed the `world_size == len(threads_bind_list)` equality assert for the explicit `SGLANG_CPU_OMP_THREADS_BIND` path, replacing it with only the per-rank bounds check. This permits the router-mode case (local `world_size=1`, multi-group bind string) while still catching a bind list that's too short. 2. `test/registered/cpu/test_subblock_sparse_attention.py`, added in https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/34680, fails in Xeon CPU CI with `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'imageio'`: importing it pulls in `sglang.multimodal_gen`, which needs `diffusers/imageio/addict` from the diffusion extra. Install `.[diffusion]` instead of `.` in `docker/xeon.Dockerfile` — the extra is already declared in `python/pyproject_cpu.toml`. signals.title: [AMD][gfx95] Fill the chunked-prefill compute budget exactly
signals.text: ## Summary * A prefill batch never reaches `chunked_prefill_size`. Two page roundings leak tokens out of it: `_update_prefill_budget` charges the **page-ceiled** extend length against the compute budgets (`rem_chunk_tokens` / `rem_input_tokens`, counted in forward-pass tokens), and `add_one_req` floors the last request's truncation back down to a page. With `page_size=64` and `chunked_prefill_size=16384`, the forward runs 16289–16368 tokens instead of 16384. * **On gfx95, landing 16 tokens short of 16384 doubles the cost of one kernel.** The MLA absorb bmm's `EVEN_MN` heuristic is a compile-time `constexpr` keyed on `M % BLOCK_SIZE_M == 0`, so a misaligned M selects a **different compiled binary** — 3819 instructions against 1562 for identical MFMA work. Measured on that kernel alone: **311.2 us at M=16368 vs 155.8 us at M=16384.** * **Fix:** a `compute_charge` argument to `_update_prefill_budget` moves the compute budgets in raw tokens while the KV budgets stay counted in pages and page-ceiled; the last request of a batch takes the remainder verbatim. Both compute budgets have to switch together — they are usually configured to the same value, so leaving either ceiled makes it hit zero first and stop admission with the slack unspent. Neither floor is a correctness requirement: `alloc_extend` handles a partial leading/trailing page, DSA builds its page tables per token, and `add_chunked_req` already commits non-page-aligned chunks. The ledger says the batch spent all 16384 tokens; the forward ran 16328 (`page_size=64`, arbitrary 8100-token prompts): | req | admitted | runs | charged | budget left | | --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | | 1 | whole | 8100 | 8128 | 8256 | | 2 | whole | 8100 | 8128 | 128 | | 3 | chunked | 128 | 128 | 0 | | | | **16328** | **16384** | | Only requests admitted whole leak: the one that gets chunked has already been floored to a page, so its charge and its run agree. ## Changes All in `managers/schedule_policy.py` except the last: * `_update_prefill_budget`: new `compute_charge` argument. When passed, the compute budgets (`rem_chunk_tokens` / `rem_input_tokens` / `rem_dllm_tokens`) and the `log_input_tokens` metrics take the raw token count; the KV reservations stay page-ceiled. * `add_one_req`: the "fits whole" test now uses the **raw** length, and a new truncation branch takes `chunk_tokens_limit` verbatim, still honouring `truncation_align_size`. * Gate: `_use_exact_chunk_fill()`, exposed as `PrefillAdder.exact_chunk_fill`. `add_chunked_req` / `add_req_state` / `add_one_req` pass `compute_charge` only when it is on. * `environ.py`: register `SGLANG_EXACT_CHUNK_FILL` (`EnvBool`, default on). ## Scope gfx95 (MI355X) chunked prefill, gated on `SGLANG_EXACT_CHUNK_FILL` **and** gfx95 — CUDA and other AMD parts keep upstream behaviour on every path. The dLLM path is excluded. ## Test plan **Baseline** — `rocm/sgl-dev:v0.5.15.post1-rocm720-mi35x-20260714` plus six AMD PRs (#30519, #30575, #30715, #30808, #31323, #31324). **This PR** — that baseline plus this PR plus ROCm/aiter#4453. **Kernel level** (same config): | | before | after | | --- | ---: | ---: | | trace token annotation | `toks=16350` | `toks=16384` | | dense GEMM total | 163.5 ms | 136.6 ms | | EXTEND wall | 695.4 ms | 671.6 ms | **End to end-Overview** (GLM-5.2-MXFP4, MI355X TP4, in8192 / out1024): | Concurrency | Mean TTFT base | this PR | Δ | Median TPOT base | this PR | Δ | | ----------- | -------------- | ------- | - | ---------------- | ------- | - | | 4 | 512.25 | 484.58 | **−5.4%** | 13.04 | 13.00 | −0.3% | | 8 | 727.92 | 681.18 | **−6.4%** | 16.41 | 16.23 | −1.1% | | 16 | 999.91 | 930.41 | **−7.0%** | 21.91 | 21.61 | **−1.4%** | | 32 | 1558.20 | 1442.90 | **−7.4%** | 31.00 | 30.37 | **−2.0%** | | 64 | 2742.82 | 2481.36 | **−9.5%** | 49.83 | 48.39 | **−2.9%** | Mean TTFT improves monotonically with concurrency, which is what a shorter prefill should look like: the saving is per prefill forward, so the deeper the queue, the more of them a request waits behind. **End to end-Prefill kernel attribution** — one prefill forward at in8192 / concurrency 64: | Category| baseline (ms) | this PR (ms) | Δ | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | | dense/linear GEMM | 173.15 | 107.18 | **−65.97** | | sparse-MLA attn | 177.39 | 179.49 | +2.10 | | all-reduce/comm | 134.31 | 134.79 | +0.48 | | MoE moe1 + moe2 + routing | 143.81 | 144.59 | +0.78 | | DSA indexer + topk | 24.91 | 25.15 | +0.24 | | rmsnorm/quant/act | 26.09 | 25.83 | −0.26 | | Σ kernel | 709.34 | 646.71 | −62.62 | Only dense/linear GEMM got improved with expectation. Other categories kernels shift within noise. **Accuracy:** GSM8K 0.933 → 0.927, single scoring pass each — within what one pass resolves. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:no_entry_sign: [Run #32347096502](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32347096502)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32347096073](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32347096073)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #32347096390](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32347096390)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [PD] Fix reasoning token accounting for the handoff token
signals.text: ## Motivation Fixes #32897. In PD disaggregation, the prefill worker samples the first output token and the decode worker commits it to the request. The colocated prefill path updates reasoning-token accounting at the same point, but the PD handoff path previously only appended the token to `output_ids`. This undercounts reasoning usage by one for a normal handoff. If the handoff token is the think-end token, it can also leave the accounting state in the reasoning phase and count later answer tokens incorrectly. ## Modifications - Update reasoning-token accounting when decode commits a newly sampled PD handoff token. - Skip the update when true-retraction rebootstrap replays an already emitted boundary token, because its accounting state is retained and must not be counted twice. ## Accuracy Tests This change does not alter model outputs, sampling, or KV transfer behavior. It only updates usage metadata for the handoff token. Live PD validation passed: with the change applied, reasoning-token usage was correct for a response stopped by `max_tokens` during the reasoning phase. Validation performed: - `black --check python/sglang/srt/disaggregation/decode.py` - `ruff check --no-cache python/sglang/srt/disaggregation/decode.py` - Python syntax compilation of `decode.py` - `git diff --check` The existing decode-queue CPU test file could not be collected locally because Triton is unavailable in the CPU-only environment. No new test file is included in this minimal patch. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Not applicable. The change adds one scalar accounting check once per PD request handoff and does not affect the model-forward or per-token decode path. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). signals.title: [Bugfix] Fix Llama 4 FA3 local attention with paged KV cache
signals.text: [by Codex] ## Motivation Llama 4 Scout with FlashAttention 3 crashes during warmup on H100 when the KV cache uses pages larger than one token. The same workload succeeds with `--page-size 1`. This is a long-standing paged-local-attention bug rather than a new 0.5.7 regression: the explicit page-size-16 reproducer fails on 0.5.6.post2, 0.5.7, and current `main`. Related to #7936. ## Reproduction Environment: - 8x NVIDIA H100 80GB HBM3 - Llama 4 Scout 17B-16E Instruct - Tensor parallel size 8 - FlashAttention 3 - Dummy weights Run: ```bash export CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1 python -m sglang.bench_one_batch \ --model-path <path-to-Llama-4-Scout-17B-16E-Instruct> \ --disable-radix-cache \ --context-length 2048 \ --attention-backend fa3 \ --load-format dummy \ --batch-size 128 \ --tp-size 8 \ --input-len 1000 \ --output-len 1000 \ --page-size 16 ``` ### Before The run reaches warmup, then all TP ranks fail in the FA3 forward launch: ```text Warmup ... CUDA error (.../hopper/flash_fwd_launch_template.h:209): an illegal memory access was encountered ``` Changing only `--page-size 16` to `--page-size 1` completes warmup and the benchmark. ## Root cause There are two related issues in eager local-attention metadata construction: 1. `_maybe_init_local_attn_metadata` passes the token-granular `metadata.page_table` to `make_local_attention_virtual_batches`. The helper and FlashAttention consume page IDs. At page size 16, physical token locations are therefore interpreted as physical page IDs and can address beyond the allocated KV cache. 2. The shared helper normally reduces the requested attention chunk to a page-aligned value based on the current sequence length. For this 1,000-token prompt, that turns Llama 4's model-defined 8,192-token boundary into 992 and creates a spurious final 8-token virtual batch. Page size 1 masks both problems because token and page indices are identical, and the chunk reduction does not leave a page-sized remainder. ## Changes - Convert eager FlashAttention token locations to a page-granular block table before creating local virtual batches: ```python page_table = page_table[:, :: self.page_size] // self.page_size ``` - Let FlashAttention local-metadata construction explicitly preserve the model-defined attention chunk in eager execution, CUDA graph capture, and CUDA graph replay. - Keep the shared helper's existing chunk-normalization behavior as the default for callers that do not opt in. - Add regression coverage for token-to-page conversion, Llama 4's 8,192-token boundary, and the unchanged default helper behavior. ## Why other attention backends are unaffected - The token-to-page conversion is inside `FlashAttentionBackend`'s local-attention metadata path. Other backend classes build their own metadata and do not execute this code. - `make_local_attention_virtual_batches` is shared with the XPU backend, so the new `preserve_attn_chunk_size` option defaults to `False`. XPU does not pass the option and therefore retains the previous normalization and output layout. A regression test covers this default path. - The new option is enabled only at the three `FlashAttentionBackend` call sites. No attention kernel, global KV-cache layout, or metadata builder for Triton, FlashInfer, TensorRT-LLM, or other backends is changed. - Within FlashAttention, models without local attention return before this metadata path, and page size 1 skips the token-to-page conversion. ## After The exact page-size-16 command above completes both warmup and the full 1,000-token decode benchmark: ```text Warmup ... Prefill. latency: 3.44482 s, throughput: 37157.24 token/s Decode. median latency: 0.01917 s, median throughput: 6675.84 token/s Total. latency: 4.091 s, throughput: 32285.56 token/s Benchmark ... Prefill. latency: 1.79242 s, throughput: 71411.78 token/s Decode. median latency: 0.01957 s, median throughput: 6539.82 token/s Total. latency: 21.433 s, throughput: 11943.97 token/s ``` ## Validation - Reproduced the FA3 illegal memory access on: - SGLang 0.5.6.post2, page size 16 - SGLang 0.5.7, page size 16 - Current `main`, page size 16 - Verified the page-size-1 control passes. - Verified patched current source passes with page size 16 and output lengths 128 and 1,000. - Focused regression tests passed on the original fix; the review follow-up's opt-in and compatibility paths passed isolated validation against the actual helper source. - Full repository validation after the review follow-up: ```bash BLACK_NUM_WORKERS=1 SKIP=no-commit-to-branch \ pre-commit run --all-files --show-diff-on-failure ``` All hooks passed. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #31579432381](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31579432381)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #32217618644](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32217618644)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [AMD] perf: fuse Kimi-K2.5 MLA projection, RoPE, and KV-cache write
signals.text: <!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. --> ## Motivation During Kimi-K2.5 MXFP4 graph decode on ROCm gfx95, the absorbed MLA key projection, rotary embedding, and KV-cache write are launched separately on the latency-critical path even though they share operands. Fusing these operations reduces decode launch overhead and improves long-context serving performance. ## Modifications - Fuse the absorbed MXFP4 `w_kc` projection, RoPE, and KV-cache write into one AITER grid using `fused_fp4_bmm_rope_cat_and_cache_mla`. - Add `SGLANG_ROCM_FUSE_MLA_PROJECTION_ROPE_CACHE`, enabled by default. - Restrict the fast path to ROCm gfx95/AITER graph decode with MXFP4 `w_kc`. - Validate the fused kernel's shape requirements before dispatch: - `kv_lora_rank` must be a power of two. - `qk_rope_head_dim` must be a power of two and at least 2. - `qk_nope_head_dim` must be a power of two between 32 and 256. - Retain the existing split path for unsupported configurations, including DSA, DCP, optimized LoRA execution, and active `kv_b_proj` LoRAs. - Carry the fusion decision from `forward_absorb_prepare` to `forward_absorb_core` through `RocmMlaProjectionFusionPlan`. - Add CPU unit coverage for backend, graph-decode, and kernel-shape gating. - Document the new environment variable. ## Accuracy Tests Hardware and model: - 4× AMD Instinct MI355X (`gfx950`) - Model: `Kimi-K2.5-MXFP4` - TP=4 - AITER prefill and decode attention - AITER MoE and all-reduce fusion - FP8 E4M3 KV cache - Full GSM8K test set: 1,319 questions, 8-shot, maximum 512 new tokens - Project accuracy threshold: 0.92 | Configuration | Accuracy | Invalid responses | Status | | --- | ---: | ---: | --- | | Fusion disabled | 0.925 | 0.000 | PASS | | Fusion enabled | 0.930 | 0.000 | PASS | The fused path preserved accuracy and remained above the existing 0.92 threshold. Focused unit tests: ```text 2 passed, 5 subtests passed ``` The tests cover the AITER graph-decode gate and reject unsupported non-power-of-two or out-of-range shapes. ## Speed Tests and Profiling The A/B benchmark follows the Kimi-K2.5 ROCm recipe. Configuration: - 4× AMD Instinct MI355X (`gfx950`) - Kimi-K2.5 MXFP4, TP=4 - AITER prefill/decode attention and MoE - AITER all-reduce fusion - FP8 E4M3 KV cache, page size 16 - Breakable prefill graph and full decode graph - Maximum concurrency: 4 - ISL: 8,192 - OSL: 1,024 - 20 measured requests after warmup - Identical seed and generated workload for both arms - The only A/B feature change was `SGLANG_ROCM_FUSE_MLA_PROJECTION_ROPE_CACHE=0/1` | Metric | Fusion disabled | Fusion enabled | Change | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | | Output throughput | 428.77 tok/s | 433.33 tok/s | +1.06% | | Total token throughput | 3,861.04 tok/s | 3,902.11 tok/s | +1.06% | | Median TPOT | 8.81 ms | 8.68 ms | -1.48% | | Median end-to-end latency | 8,455.36 ms | 8,328.59 ms | -1.50% | | Median TTFT | 246.43 ms | 247.99 ms | +0.63% | The fusion improves decode-sensitive throughput, TPOT, and end-to-end latency for the 8k/1k workload. The small TTFT variation is expected because this optimization targets graph decode rather than prefill. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. signals.text: Migrates the Qwen3.6 cookbook page to the **config-driven Deployment/Playground engine** (as for DeepSeek-V4 / Qwen3.5) and adds **measured speed benchmarks**. The legacy `qwen36-deployment.jsx` generator is removed. ## Config — `configs/qwen/qwen3.6.jsx` (44 cells) `h100/h200/b200/b300` × `{35B-A3B (MoE), 27B (Dense)}` × `{bf16, fp8, +nvfp4 on Blackwell}` × `{low-latency, high-throughput}`, plus **Xeon `balanced`** (27B/35B-A3B × bf16/fp8). low-latency = MTP/EAGLE + mamba radix-cache v2; high-throughput = MTP off; Xeon = spec unsupported → single `balanced` recipe (`--device cpu`, tp 3/6). signals.title: [MLX] Upgrade to Torch 2.13/MLX 0.32+ and redesign the Torch-MLX tensor bridge
signals.text: ## Motivation MLX 0.32 can import Torch MPS allocations directly, while Torch 2.13 changes the runtime and DLPack edge cases that the Apple Silicon integration must support. The existing bridge stages MPS tensors through CPU memory, obscures borrowed-versus-owned lifetimes, and pays payload-sized copies. Separately, diffusion's `SGLANG_USE_MLX` norm override is not selected by normal MPS `CustomOp` dispatch; forcing those norms through Torch-MLX crossings is slower end to end. This PR upgrades the `srt_mps` runtime, fails fast on unsupported Torch/MLX pairs, separates owned copies from scoped zero-copy borrows, and removes the unreachable diffusion-only MLX fallback. It does not replace the existing SRT MLX runner; the stacked [yeahdongcn/sglang#7](https://github.com/yeahdongcn/sglang/pull/7) consumes these bridge primitives while redesigning that backend. ## Modifications - Update `srt_mps` in `python/pyproject_other.toml` to Torch 2.13.0, MLX >= 0.32.0, TorchVision 0.28.0, TorchAudio 2.11.0, and TorchCodec 0.15.0. The versions stay directly in `srt_mps`, matching the existing extra layout; `all_mps` inherits them through `srt_mps`. MLX keeps a 0.32.0 minimum but has no upper bound; startup accepts newer stable MLX releases. TorchAudio 2.11 remains intentional and was validated with the tested Torch 2.13 MPS stack. CPU and standalone `diffusion_mps` dependency lists are unchanged. - Move the SRT MLX version/device validation to the earliest model-independent `ServerArgs` bootstrap. With `SGLANG_USE_MLX=1`, SGLang requires stable Torch 2.13.x and stable MLX >= 0.32.0. Older MLX, Torch outside 2.13.x, and rc/dev builds fail before model path resolution/downloads and before the dummy-model short circuit. With the flag unset, importing SGLang still does not import MLX. - Redesign `tensor_bridge.py` around explicit ownership and batching: - `torch_to_mlx` creates and materializes MLX-owned storage when the result must outlive its Torch source. - `MlxTensorView` and `borrow_torch_tensors` provide persistent and batched zero-copy MPS borrows while retaining every Torch storage owner. - `mlx_call` and `mlx_call_multi` validate the target before work, fence Torch producers once, keep all borrowed inputs alive through lazy evaluation, evaluate ordinary multi-output results at one shared `mx.eval` boundary, batch the additional materialization boundary required by negative-stride outputs, and export them through DLPack. - `mlx_to_torch` uses evaluated DLPack views for MPS and explicit CPU views. Positive-stride layouts, including CPU float64, remain zero-copy. Negative-stride MLX views are materialized because Torch 2.13's DLPack importer otherwise aborts the process instead of raising a Python exception; unsupported CPU dtypes fail instead of silently narrowing. This PR intentionally owns these shared Torch-MLX bridge primitives. The stacked MPS redesign in [yeahdongcn/sglang#7](https://github.com/yeahdongcn/sglang/pull/7) consumes them for Torch-owned model weights and provider outputs, while its provider-specific invalidation callbacks and phase timing stay in that PR. - Remove `mps_fallback.py`, route diffusion MPS kernels to native Torch fallbacks, and use `F.layer_norm`/`F.rms_norm` instead of the old manual decomposition. The shared fallback remains compatible with both the default Torch 2.11 and CPU-backend Torch 2.12 stacks. RMSNorm preserves the optional-bias and input-dtype contracts even with fp32 parameters. The removed rotary and scale/shift entries were already aliases to Torch implementations; only the norm entries had MLX-specific implementations. - Remove diffusion's `SGLANG_USE_MLX` runtime handling and clarify in the existing documentation that the variable applies only to SRT serving. SRT keeps its existing `SGLANG_USE_MLX=1` opt-in. - Add Torch 2.13-compatible Triton import-stub symbols used by Inductor on MPS. - Rebase the branch onto upstream `main` at `978244d67148`; update VAE and Transformer component loaders to the upstream unified residency API so MPS layerwise offload remains valid after the upstream loader refactor. The diffusion MLX norm path is intentionally dropped after tracing and measurement. `CustomOp.dispatch_forward()` routes MPS to `forward_native`, so the legacy MLX override is unreachable in the normal production graph. Sana instrumentation confirmed zero legacy entrypoint calls, and forcing all 58 norms per DiT forward through MLX was slower end to end. Isolated large fp32 LayerNorm microbenchmarks sometimes favored MLX by a few percent, but the result was not robust across the common fp16/bf16 cases and did not justify repeated framework crossings. A future fully MLX-resident diffusion path can be evaluated separately. ## Accuracy Tests - `PATH="$PWD/sglang-metal/bin:$PATH" SGLANG_USE_MLX=1 HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 ./sglang-metal/bin/python test/run_suite.py --hw mlx --suite stage-a-unit-test-mlx` - **21/21 registered test files passed locally** on Apple M1 at PR head `c1f34a81d1`, including bridge, startup runtime gate, Triton-stub, and diffusion fallback coverage. - The focused bridge/runtime/diffusion-loader bundle passed **121 tests plus 36 subtests** after the rebase. - All four new test files are registered in `stage-a-unit-test-mlx`. `test_diffusion_torch_fallback.py` is additionally registered in `base-a-test-cpu`, `base-b-test-cpu`, and `base-b-test-cpu-arm64`. - The same six fallback UTs passed **6/6** in isolated Torch 2.11.0 and 2.12.0 CPU environments, including fp16/bf16 inputs with fp32 parameters. - Runtime tests verify Torch 2.12/2.14, MLX 0.31, and Torch/MLX rc/dev builds are rejected, while stable Torch 2.13 patch releases and stable MLX releases from 0.32.0 onward (including future minor versions) are accepted. Incompatible versions abort `ServerArgs` creation even for `model_path="dummy"`; missing MLX, unavailable PyTorch MPS, and unavailable MLX Metal each produce actionable startup errors. The disabled path constructs `ServerArgs` without importing MLX. - Bridge ownership checks cover owned/scoped/persistent lifetimes, source mutation and deletion, single-fence batched borrows, shared-eval multi-output calls, bfloat16/non-contiguous views, CPU float64 and unsupported dtypes, autograd detachment, invalid-target fail-fast behavior, and negative-stride materialization in an abort-safe subprocess. - SRT serving smoke with local `Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B`: both `SGLANG_USE_MLX=1` and the no-env Torch-MPS path returned **200** from `/health` and `/generate`. For prompt `The capital of France is` with greedy 8-token decoding, both paths returned identical output token IDs `[12095, 13, 576, 6722, 315, 9625, 374, 1083]` and text `Paris. The capital of France is also`. - Sana 600M, prompt `A small red cube on a plain white background`, seed 42, 256x256, 4 steps: native Torch output and the hypothetical all-MLX norm output remained visually consistent (PSNR 41.95 dB; max pixel delta 50). The final `mlx_call` image was byte-identical to the earlier explicit- keepalive MLX image. The ordinary Sana path recorded 58 Torch norm calls per DiT forward and zero legacy norm-fallback entrypoint calls. After the rebase, a native Torch-MPS Sana smoke with the same 256x256/4-step configuration produced a valid RGB PNG in 24.87s with 6.33GB peak memory. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Environment: Apple M1, macOS 26.5.2, Torch 2.13.0, MLX 0.32.0. All timings include the required producer/consumer synchronization. The operation table reports end-to-end norm-call timings, including bridge/export and synchronization, rather than raw kernel-only timings. It is one representative median-after-warmup run; an independent rerun preserved the common-Sana ordering but flipped whether large-fp32 MLX was slightly ahead or behind. | Case | Torch native | MLX owned copy | MLX scoped borrow | |---|---:|---:|---:| | Sana RMSNorm `(1,300,1152)` fp32 | 230 us | 676 us | 259 us | | Sana LayerNorm `(1,256,1152)` bf16 | 254 us | 913 us | 324 us | | Flux LayerNorm `(1,4096,3072)` fp32 | 2508 us | 4763 us | 2441 us | Bridge A/B directly calls the final `mlx_call(lambda a: a, tensor)` API against the pre-change CPU-staging implementation at the branch merge base (Apple M1, Torch 2.13.0, MLX 0.32.0). The table reports the range of per-batch p50 values across three independent batches; each batch used 5 warmups and 20 measured samples with producer/consumer synchronization: | Logical tensor | dtype / payload | Old CPU-staging p50 range | Final `mlx_call` p50 range | Minimum paired speedup | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:| | `(4096,4096)` | fp32 / 64 MiB | 32.134-57.424 ms | 0.0410-0.0871 ms | 368.8x | | `(4096,4096)` | bf16 / 32 MiB | 10.301-34.715 ms | 0.0293-0.0418 ms | 351.2x | | `(4096,8192)` | bf16 / 64 MiB | 16.896-22.184 ms | 0.0407-0.0617 ms | 273.7x | The old MPS round-trip staged payload through CPU/NumPy in both directions. The final `mlx_call` path aliases the Metal allocation through DLPack, removing the payload-sized copies; the synchronized wrapper/barrier cost was 29-87 us across these repeats. The same-shape bf16 case is 32 MiB because each element uses two bytes; the final row adds a true 64 MiB bf16 payload. This zero-copy result applies to the scoped-borrow API, not to an MLX array that must own its storage after the call. For that ownership contract, the 64 MiB fp32 materialized copy is about 4.08 ms versus about 60 us for a scoped borrow. This is why the API separates owned and borrowed semantics instead of exposing an unchecked `copy=False` default. Final-API Sana 4-step E2E forced-MLX experiment using `mlx_call` for all 58 norms per DiT forward (clean paired repeat): | Metric | Torch native | MLX scoped borrow | MLX penalty | |---|---:|---:|---:| | Denoising step median | 720.18 ms | 1170.40 ms | +62.5% | | DiT forward median | 375.06 ms | 581.92 ms | +55.2% | | Steady DiT median (drop first 2) | 353.42 ms | 581.92 ms | +64.7% | A second same-configuration measurement had higher Torch variance and a smaller penalty (+20.6% step, +21.9% DiT), but MLX was slower in both runs. ## Checklist - [x] Formatted with repository pre-commit hooks. - [x] Added and ran registered unit tests. - [x] Registered the shared diffusion fallback in CPU CI. - [x] Updated Apple Metal and diffusion documentation. - [x] Included accuracy and speed evidence above. - [x] CPU dependency pins remain unchanged. ## Review and Merge Process This is a draft for review of the ownership contract and the diffusion path decision. Please review the Torch/MLX lifetime semantics first; CI should run the MLX, CPU, JIT-kernel, and multimodal-generation change paths before promotion. In particular, the draft-gated MLX, Xeon CPU, and ARM64 CPU jobs must complete before this PR is marked ready. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #32438848514](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32438848514)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32438848397](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32438848397)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #32438848438](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32438848438)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->
