signals.title: Improve M3 performance on MI350
signals.text: <!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. --> ## Motivation Improve M3 performance on MI350. <!-- Describe the purpose and goals of this pull request. --> ## Modifications MI350X (gfx950) decode/prefill optimizations for MiniMax-M3 and M3-VL. Measured on TP8 / MXFP8 / 80k context: **1144 -> ~2035 tok/s decode** (13.98 -> 15.72 ms/step at the higher batch), GSM8K unchanged (88.55% before and after at the same budget; 95.3-95.7% at a 2048-token budget). ### MXFP8 / dense GEMM - AITER FlyDSL MXFP8 MoE support: pre-shuffled gate/up weights, E8M0 scales, OAI-SwiGLU activation handling, and fused shared-expert execution. - `--fp8-gemm-backend bf16`: dequantize MXFP8 weights once at load and run BF16 hipBLASLt linear. - `SGLANG_FORCE_MXFP8_BLOCK_CONVERT_DENSE=1`: convert *dense* weights to block-FP8 `[128,128]` at load while MoE stays on the native per-1x32 MX path (the block-scale MoE kernel does not support SwiGLU-OAI). ~+35% prefill. - `SGLANG_OPT_MXFP8_DENSE_PTPC_DECODE_M` (default 128): rowwise-FP8 (ptpc) dense fast path for skinny-M decode, falling back to the block-FP8 GEMM above it. The old cap of 8 silently disabled both this path and the quant fusions below at bs16; raising it was +14.2%. - Allows `--moe-runner-backend aiter` for MXFP8 on gfx950, and errors early if `SGLANG_USE_AITER=1` is not set. ### Fusions - Per-token FP8 quantization fused into the Gemma fused-add-RMSNorm Triton kernel, so the ptpc decode GEMM consumes `(fp8, scale)` directly. Uses an explicitly rounded `1/448` reciprocal (Triton `/` lowers to a fast reciprocal on ROCm, which cost 1 ULP vs AITER). - MoE all-reduce fused into the next layer's norm + qkv quant (`forward_with_allreduce_fusion_quant_per_token`), opt-in per model via `enable_fused_ar_quant_per_token` so it cannot fire for unrelated AITER GemmaRMSNorm models. - Shared-expert append folded into the Triton fused MoE gate (`nfse` handling fixed - the previous path double-appended the shared expert and dropped a routed one). - Shared-expert compute overlapped onto an alternate stream when the routed path forces fusion off. - Small-batch MoE sorting + MXFP8 quant kernel (`moe_sorting_small`), replacing a two-kernel path at decode shapes. ### Router GEMV - New Triton split-K router GEMV (`kernels/ops/gemm/router_gemv.py`) with in-kernel split-K fixup (no separate zero-init launch), per-M-bucket configs (BK 512, BN by batch), and the gate weight read once per decode batch. ~+2.8% then +5.5% on top. ### Sparse attention (ATOM port) - Gluon-based paged sparse prefill (`minimax_sparse_ops/atom_prefill.py`), default on via `SGLANG_OPT_USE_ATOM_PREFILL`, with Triton fallback for unsupported shapes and a scratch-size cap that falls back rather than OOMs. - Score-only index kernel at every page size: the per-page slot addressing is now a `PER_PAGE_SLOTS` constexpr chosen from `block_size_k // page_size`, instead of gating the whole (~1.6x) kernel behind `page_size >= 16`. - Index top-k shared across every N sparse layers, `SGLANG_MINIMAX_M3_INDEX_TOPK_FREQ` (default 2, ROCm only, never under two-batch overlap) - it changes which KV blocks skip layers attend, so it is an accuracy knob. - Decode top-k written straight into the reuse buffer; per-forward caches keyed on the owning `ForwardBatch` so they are TBO-safe. - JIT radix top-k unblocked under CUDA graphs (`kMaxNumBlocks` 4096 -> 16384). ### Dense decode attention - ROCm decode-attention KV tile 32 -> 64 tokens and a software-pipelined KV loop (`num_stages` 2) for `Lk <= 128`: 690 -> 285 us/launch, ~+7% e2e. - Decode `kv_indices` build parallelized across sequence spans. - Skips redundant sparse KV-cache writes when fusion already populated the cache, and top-k id sanitization when EP is off. ### Defaults and memory accounting - On ROCm gfx950, `--prefill-attention-backend` defaults to `aiter` (ck-tile fmha) while decode stays on Triton. Decode on the AITER backend costs ~3 points on AIME25, so it is not defaulted. - Replaced the blanket `mem_fraction_static *= 0.85` for the AITER backend at `context_len > 8192` with an exact charge: the paged-decode split workspace is fp32 and linear in context length (~4 GiB at 128k) and is allocated after the KV pool, so `KVCacheConfigurator` now re-solves the budget once with the measured size (`aiter_attn_workspace_bytes`) subtracted. The old flat haircut over-reserved ~28 GB. - MiniMax-M3-VL gets the same ROCm shared-expert support; EP/DeepEP guards preserved. ### Launch recipes ### Higher-accuracy dense path Keeps dense weights on the native MXFP8 path with the original per-1×32 scales. ``` SGLANG_USE_AITER=1 \ sglang serve \ --trust-remote-code \ --model-path /persistent/models/MiniMax-M3-MXFP8 \ --reasoning-parser auto \ --tool-call-parser auto \ --tp 8 \ --quantization mxfp8 \ --moe-runner-backend aiter \ --fp8-gemm-backend bf16 \ --enable-aiter-allreduce-fusion \ --attention-backend triton \ --prefill-attention-backend aiter \ --dtype bfloat16 \ --chunked-prefill-size 32768 \ --mem-fraction-static 0.80 \ --host 0.0.0.0 \ --port 30000 ``` ### Fast decode path Converts dense weights to block-FP8 at load and selects the automatic block-FP8/PTPC dispatch. MoE remains on native MXFP8. ``` SGLANG_USE_AITER=1 \ SGLANG_FORCE_MXFP8_BLOCK_CONVERT_DENSE=1 \ sglang serve \ --trust-remote-code \ --model-path /persistent/models/MiniMax-M3-MXFP8 \ --reasoning-parser auto \ --tool-call-parser auto \ --tp 8 \ --quantization mxfp8 \ --moe-runner-backend aiter \ --fp8-gemm-backend auto \ --enable-aiter-allreduce-fusion \ --attention-backend triton \ --prefill-attention-backend aiter \ --dtype bfloat16 \ --chunked-prefill-size 32768 \ --mem-fraction-static 0.80 \ --host 0.0.0.0 \ --port 30000 ``` ## Accuracy Tests baseline ``` == gsm8k == 1319 examples (single-shot) | 227.1s | 1485 tok/s | 337K tokens * score = 88.55% stop_rate = 89.61% truncated_rate = 10.39% [warn: hitting max_tokens] error_rate = 0.00% ``` this pr ``` == gsm8k == 1319 examples (single-shot) | 119.9s | 2862 tok/s | 343K tokens * score = 88.55% stop_rate = 89.69% truncated_rate = 10.31% [warn: hitting max_tokens] error_rate = 0.00% ``` <!-- If this pull request affects model outputs (e.g., changes to the kernel or model forward code), provide accuracy test results. --> ## Speed Tests and Profiling MI350X, TP8, MXFP8 MiniMax-M3. ### Dense-path configurations (bs1 / il8192) | Configuration | Decode | Prefill | | |---|---:|---:|---| | Native MXFP8 dense, `--fp8-gemm-backend bf16` (higher-accuracy dense) | 131 tok/s | 22.1k tok/s | reference | | Dense block-convert only (`SGLANG_FORCE_MXFP8_BLOCK_CONVERT_DENSE=1`) | 92.5 tok/s | 29.9k tok/s | **+35% prefill, -30% decode** — the CK a8w8 blockscale kernel is a prefill kernel, ~2.5x worse than bf16 hipBLASLt at M=1 | | Block-convert + PTPC decode fast path + the rest of this PR (fast decode) | 169 tok/s | ~46k tok/s | **+29% decode, +2.1x prefill** vs the first row | The two rows the launch recipes above expose are rows 1 and 3; row 2 is why the skinny-M PTPC path exists at all. ### Concurrency sweep (TP8) | CC | baseline tok/s/user | baseline tok/s/GPU | high accuracy tok/s/user | high accuracy tok/s/GPU | |---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | 1 | 49.8 | 6.2 | 131.1 | 16.4 | | 2 | 48.9 | 12.2 | 126.0 | 31.5 | | 4 | 47.9 | 23.9 | 120.5 | 60.3 | | 8 | 46.5 | 46.5 | 112.4 | 112.5 | | 16 | 42.0 | 83.9 | 92.9 | 186.1 | | 32 | 36.8 | 147.3 | 73.9 | 296.0 | | 64 | 30.9 | 247.3 | 57.1 | 457.3 | | 128 | - | - | 41.7 | 667.0 | | 256 | - | - | 29.0 | 929.9 | ### Long-context decode (bs16-32 / il80000) 1144 -> 2035 tok/s (13.98 -> 15.72 ms/step at bs32) across the MXFP8 decode-M cap (+14.2%), the router GEMV M-keyed configs (+5.5%), the fmoe atomic reduce pick (+4.3%), the dense decode-attention tile+pipelining (+3.6% and +7.2%), and the ATOM sparse port. ## Checklist - [ ] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [ ] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process). 2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers. 3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so. - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci` 4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32190927680](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32190927680)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32190927496](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32190927496)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #32190927737](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32190927737)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [Sampling] Add explicit bounded sampling-mask mode
signals.text: ## Why #27408 added SGLang's native sampling-mask response, but reconstructed support after sampling and used finite `top_k` as its safety bound. #33593, now merged in `main`, made top-p-only requests valid and exposed sampling masks through the OpenAI chat extension. The remaining contract must therefore be general: top-p/min-p support is data-dependent, and SGLang's threshold primitives retain every token tied at the cutoff, so even finite top-k does not bound realized support. This PR makes the response describe the distribution that actually sampled the token, then bounds only its transport. This is a general serving contract, not an RL-only path. ## Contract For the post-filter weights `w` used to sample token `y`, let `S = {i | w[i] > 0}` and `C = --sampling-mask-max-tokens`: - sampling itself is unchanged; - if `|S| <= C`, the returned token IDs are the complete support `S`; - exact mode is the default, so `|S| > C` aborts before `y` is committed; - `sampling_mask_mode="bounded"` opts into at most `C` IDs and reports `output_token_sampling_mask_truncated=true`; - bounded mode keeps the highest-weight prefix and retains `y` by replacing its final entry when necessary; - the selected-token logprob is always `log(w[y] / sum(w))` over the full realized support, never over the truncated return; - missing or internally inconsistent producer output is an internal error, not truncation. The cap changes metadata only. It never changes the sampling distribution. ## Design - Capture the producer's representation. PyTorch reuses its filtered weights and token permutation; FlashInfer uses SGLang's existing top-k/top-p renormalization primitives and min-p predicate; deterministic logprob sampling and greedy sampling use their native representations. - Keep internal results tensor-backed. `SamplingMaskOutput` is a dataclass following the existing result-holder `map_device_tensors`/async-D2H path; `_SamplingMaskCapture` is a sampler-private `NamedTuple`. - Maintain opted-in device row indices in `SamplingBatchInfo`, including filter/merge, so mixed batches restrict dense work and transfer to requested rows. - Emit factual `OK`, `TRUNCATED`, or `INVALID` status in the sampler, reach TP/CP consensus through the existing process groups, and apply exact/bounded policy in the scheduler. - Propagate the per-token truncation bit through streaming, multi-tokenizer output, sessions, PP, and PD disaggregation. PD reuses its existing 64-byte padded metadata row; the first two slots carry returned length and truncation. - Reuse the OpenAI chat sampling-mask path merged in #33593 and forward its `sampling_mask_mode` into the existing native request field. - Abort exact overflow before committing the sampled token and release every request-owned KV slot, including overlap-allocated slots without a committed token ID. ## Internal API changes - Private `Sampler._sample_from_probs` now returns sampled IDs plus optional producer capture data. - `top_k_top_p_min_p_sampling_from_probs_torch` keeps its existing token-only behavior by default; a keyword-only opt-in returns already-computed filtered data for capture. - Private `_attach_*` helpers became `_build_*` because they now return a tensor holder. The post-hoc `_compute_sampling_mask_from_probs` reconstruction was removed because it was not the producer's source of truth. - Request fields are placed so existing positional constructors and the tokenized Rust wire layout do not shift. - The PD field changed from `output_token_sampling_mask_len` to `output_token_sampling_mask_metadata` because the same padded row now carries length and truncation. No layout class, one-use global size constant, or additional RDMA buffer is introduced. - Existing PP `get_logprob_*` helper names remain unchanged; only their logits-output payload is widened. - Existing optional backend KV-release hooks are used at the release site; no new base-worker lifecycle interface is added. No public sampling function is removed or renamed. ## Performance - Feature-off requests add Python flag/tuple plumbing only: no new tensor operation, dense allocation, D2H copy, PP tensor, or TP/CP collective. - Opted-in rows require dense `O(R * V)` support work because current sampling primitives produce dense weights. Packing transfers `4 * R * C + 12 * R` bytes. A fixed cap avoids a GPU-to-CPU synchronization to discover a data-dependent width; finite top-k is not a valid bound because cutoff ties are retained. - On one H200 at `V=128256`, `C=4096`, measured opt-in operator overhead was approximately 0.28-0.72 ms across FlashInfer joint, min-p, and PyTorch paths. - Dense temporary storage scaled with opted-in rows: approximately 1.7 MB at `R=1`, 54 MB at `R=32`, and 107 MB at `R=64`. Bounded D2H payload p50 was approximately 53-55 us from `R=1` through `R=64` (16 KB to 1.05 MB). - Same-node TP2/4/8 status consensus measured approximately 20-42 us across 1-1024 rows. ## Validation - 295 focused tests passed, 2 skipped, with 75 subtests on one H200 using `lmsysorg/sglang:nightly-dev-cu13-20260817-d91c3682` and the rebased PR source. - Seven end-to-end H200 serving contracts passed on the rebased tree: finite support/logprob consistency, exact overflow abort, bounded truncation signal, top-p-only policy, OpenAI chat bounded-mode propagation, invalid-mode rejection, and deterministic sampling preservation. - A 4,927-check H200 operator matrix passed against independent support and selected-logprob oracles, including uniform cutoff ties and min-p input isolation. - One-node H200 TP2/4/8 collective probes passed. - Repository-native `pre-commit run --all-files` passed on current `main`, including registered-test validation, lint-checker tests, Rust formatting, and workspace clippy. `git diff --check` passed. The existing CUDA/AMD end-to-end sampling-mask test remains registered in its current CI suites. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32076643369](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32076643369)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32076642814](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32076642814)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [Fix] Account resident weight memory in KV sizing
signals.text: ## Motivation The IPC weight-cache daemon keeps model weights resident before the engine starts, so `ModelRunner` samples its pre-load free-memory baseline after those weights have already reduced free memory. Without correcting that baseline, KV sizing reserves headroom from only the remaining free memory and can over-allocate the KV cache. The correction must be rank-local before the distributed `MIN`: adding preloaded weight memory after ranks have already reduced their baselines is incorrect when rank footprints differ. Target KV sizing also happens after draft loading, so target, multi-runner, and future speculative draft weights must be aggregated before sizing. ## Modifications - Add a generic rank-local `BaseModelLoader.preloaded_weights_bytes` contract, defaulting to zero, and validate loader-provided values before use. - Aggregate preloaded bytes across target, multi-runner, and speculative draft workers. The current built-in IPC weight cache plus speculative decoding combination remains explicitly rejected because draft-model daemon support is not implemented yet, but the accounting path is ready for it. - Immediately before target KV-pool allocation, compute `MIN(local pre-load baseline + local preloaded weight bytes)` and update `pre_model_load_memory`, so initial sizing and post-capture resizing use the same corrected value. - Measure the daemon's process-local PyTorch allocator growth during model loading and return it through the IPC protocol as `preloaded_weights_bytes`. ## Accuracy Tests Ran a real persistent-daemon restart A/B with `Qwen/Qwen2.5-32B-Instruct` in BF16 at TP=1 on an 80 GB GPU. The standalone daemon retained 63,004 MiB of GPU memory while two independent engine clients were started sequentially against the same daemon. | Result | Without this fix | With this fix | |---|---:|---:| | Client pre-load available memory | 17.23 GB | 17.23 GB | | Reported preloaded weights | Not available | 65,546,485,760 bytes (61.045 GiB) | | KV cache tokens | 63,434 | 38,430 | | K + V allocation | 15.48 GB | 9.38 GB | | Memory before decode graph capture | 0.88 GB | 4.37 GB | | First client start | CUDA OOM during graph capture | Healthy; inference succeeded | | Second client start | Same CUDA OOM | Healthy; inference succeeded | Without the correction, both starts selected the same oversized KV cache and failed during decode CUDA graph capture while the daemon remained alive. With the correction, both starts completed graph capture, reached health, and served a completion against the same persistent daemon. This validates the final implementation and reproduces the accounting defect as a deterministic startup failure with a model whose resident weights occupy more than half of GPU memory. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Not benchmarked. The steady-state inference path is unchanged. Startup adds two process-local allocator reads and one existing-world-group reduction before KV-pool allocation. ## Validation - Large-model persistent-daemon restart A/B passed as described above - Python syntax checks passed for all changed production files - Ruff error checks passed for all changed production files - Full Ruff checks passed for the central accounting and IPC modules - Diff whitespace checks passed ## Checklist - [x] Format code according to the repository hooks. - [x] Validate the exact final implementation with a persistent GPU daemon and two engine starts. - [ ] Update documentation — not applicable; no user-facing option or workflow changed. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32431288185](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32431288185)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32431288040](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32431288040)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32431288139](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32431288139)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: perf(unified-memory): batch lazy-compaction mapping lookup
signals.text: ## Motivation Unified-memory lazy compaction reads `physical_to_virtual[src].item()` for every relocated survivor. Each scalar read synchronizes the GPU and CPU, making compaction a major bottleneck under memory pressure. Batching these lookups improved unified-memory throughput by 20.4% to 128.2% across Qwen3.5-0.8B, 4B, and 9B in eviction-heavy benchmarks. ## Modifications - Gather all survivor virtual IDs with one indexed tensor operation per move batch. - Keep the invalid-mapping assertion with one check per batch. - Add a regression test that rejects per-row mapping reads and verifies the virtual/physical mappings and relocated cache data. ## Accuracy Tests | Test | Result | |---|---:| | Complete allocator test file | **66 passed** | | Eviction/replay parity | **80/80 exact matches** | | Test-only diff applied to upstream base | **1 failed** (expected) | | New regression test with this patch | **1 passed** | The parity test compared output IDs, logprob token IDs, and logprob values between upstream unified memory and this patch after eviction. Maximum logprob difference was 0.0. <details> <summary>Test commands</summary> ```bash PYTHONPATH=python:test python -m pytest -q \ test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_multi_ended_allocator.py \ -k lazy_flush_gathers_survivor_mappings_as_one_batch PYTHONPATH=python:test python -m pytest -q \ test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_multi_ended_allocator.py ``` To reproduce the failure, apply only the test-file diff to the upstream base. The regression test fails at the per-row mapping lookup; it passes after the production-file diff is applied. </details> ## Speed Tests and Profiling ### Environment - GPU: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5090, 32,607 MiB; driver 610.62 - Models: `Qwen/Qwen3.5-0.8B`, `Qwen/Qwen3.5-4B`, and `Qwen/Qwen3.5-9B`, bfloat16 The three variants differ only as follows: | Configuration | Source revision | Server option | |---|---|---| | Static memory | `52afe87a08c6` (upstream base) | `--enable-unified-memory` disabled | | Unified memory (upstream) | `52afe87a08c6` | `--enable-unified-memory` | | Unified memory + batched mapping (this PR) | this PR | `--enable-unified-memory` | Each run used 80 prefix groups, four measured rounds, 1,024 input tokens, four output tokens, concurrency 16, and two priming passes. A fresh server was used for every variant and repetition. Results are medians of three runs. <details> <summary>Reproduction commands and workload</summary> ### Server Create isolated source trees for the exact revisions: ```bash git fetch upstream main git worktree add ../sglang-upstream-base \ 52afe87a08c6aa049c52f9507b4f0ca26cecb562 git fetch https://github.com/seokwoosong/sglang.git \ perf/unified-compaction-batch-mapping git worktree add ../sglang-unified-batched-mapping \ 66535cef39775b13a589668fc1429d57e8f8ff03 ``` Use `../sglang-upstream-base` for Static memory and Unified memory (upstream). Use `../sglang-unified-batched-mapping` for Unified memory + batched mapping (this PR). Start a fresh server for every variant, memory fraction, and repetition. ```bash PYTHONPATH=<SOURCE_TREE>/python python -m sglang.launch_server \ --model-path <MODEL> \ --host 127.0.0.1 --port 30000 --tp 1 --dtype bfloat16 \ --page-size 1 \ --attention-backend triton \ --linear-attn-backend triton \ --mamba-backend triton \ --mamba-radix-cache-strategy extra_buffer \ --max-total-tokens 60000 \ --max-running-requests 16 \ --chunked-prefill-size 4096 \ --context-length 65536 \ --cuda-graph-backend-decode disabled \ --cuda-graph-backend-prefill disabled \ --enable-metrics \ --mem-fraction-static <MEMORY_FRACTION> \ [--enable-unified-memory] ``` Stop the server after each run so that every measurement starts from a fresh allocator and radix cache. Use these model-specific memory fractions: | Model | Memory fractions | |---|---| | `Qwen/Qwen3.5-0.8B` | 0.30, 0.15 | | `Qwen/Qwen3.5-4B` | 0.55, 0.40 | | `Qwen/Qwen3.5-9B` | 0.85, 0.75 | Each pair above leaves a valid cache pool and still causes L1 eviction. ### Workload reproduction The workload is deterministic and uses token IDs directly through `/generate`: 1. Initialize `random.Random(42)`. 2. Create 80 groups. Each group has a 972-token shared prefix (`int(1024 * 0.95)`) consisting of token `1000 + group_id`, followed by 971 values from `rng.randrange(2000, 200000)`. 3. Prime the radix cache twice. In each pass, submit every prefix sequentially with `temperature=0`, `max_new_tokens=1`, and `ignore_eos=true`. 4. Build four measured rounds. In each round, visit groups in reverse order (`79` through `0`) and append 52 new values from `rng.randrange(2000, 200000)` to the group's prefix. This produces 320 measured requests of exactly 1,024 input tokens each. 5. Submit all measured requests through the streaming `/generate` endpoint, limiting in-flight requests with `asyncio.Semaphore(16)`. Use `temperature=0`, `max_new_tokens=4`, and `ignore_eos=true`. 6. Measure wall-clock time immediately around the 320-request `asyncio.gather()`. Compute total token throughput as `sum(prompt_tokens + completion_tokens) / measured_seconds` using the token counts returned by the server. 7. Read `/metrics` immediately before and after the measured phase. Reject the run if a request failed or if `sglang:evicted_tokens_total` did not increase. Run three repetitions at each memory fraction. Rotate server order to reduce thermal and order bias: - repetition 1: Static memory, Unified memory (upstream), Unified memory + batched mapping - repetition 2: Unified memory (upstream), Unified memory + batched mapping, Static memory - repetition 3: Unified memory + batched mapping, Static memory, Unified memory (upstream) Report the median of the three runs. Across the three models, the matrix contains 54 clean runs and 17,280 measured requests in total. </details> ### Results | Model | GPU memory fraction | Static memory | Unified memory (upstream) | This PR | Improvement | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | Qwen3.5-0.8B | 0.30 | 88,366 tok/s | 50,938 tok/s | 97,612 tok/s | +91.6% | | Qwen3.5-0.8B | 0.15 | 82,397 tok/s | 31,320 tok/s | 71,467 tok/s | +128.2% | | Qwen3.5-4B | 0.55 | 19,253 tok/s | 13,501 tok/s | 18,404 tok/s | +36.3% | | Qwen3.5-4B | 0.40 | 17,390 tok/s | 12,311 tok/s | 16,961 tok/s | +37.8% | | Qwen3.5-9B | 0.85 | 10,650 tok/s | 8,612 tok/s | 10,372 tok/s | +20.4% | | Qwen3.5-9B | 0.75 | 10,155 tok/s | 8,276 tok/s | 10,226 tok/s | +23.6% | All 54 runs and 17,280 measured requests passed. L1 eviction occurred in every run. Upstream unified memory and this PR evicted exactly the same number of tokens in every repetition for five of the six rows; 0.8B/0.30 is an end-to-end comparison with scheduling-dependent eviction. The maximum throughput range across the three repetitions of any 4B or 9B variant was 1.04%. ### Profiler At 0.8B/0.15, both traces contained the same 51 `_flush` calls and 18 move-batch commits: | Metric inside `_flush` | Upstream | This PR | Change | |---|---:|---:|---:| | `aten::item` calls | 32,646 | 18 | -99.9% | | `_flush` CPU duration | 1,060.4 ms | 68.0 ms | -93.6% | The remaining 18 scalar reads are the intentional invalid-mapping check, once per committed move batch. <details> <summary>Profiler reproduction</summary> Use memory fraction 0.15 and the same priming procedure, but run one measured round (80 requests). Immediately before the measured phase, start the built-in profiler: ```bash curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:30000/start_profile \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d '{ "output_dir": "/tmp/sglang-compaction-profile", "num_steps": 64, "activities": ["CPU", "GPU"], "with_stack": false, "record_shapes": false }' ``` Count `aten::item` events whose timestamps and thread IDs fall inside a `MultiEndedAlloc._flush` event, and sum the durations of those `_flush` events. </details> ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). No user-facing documentation change is required. - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #31776840250](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31776840250)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #31776840055](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31776840055)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [Fix] Overlap spec-v2 lifetime: pin the draft-extend ForwardBatch, record_stream the mixed-gather indices
signals.text: ## Motivation Two cross-stream tensor-lifetime violations in the overlap scheduler (torch.Tensor.record_stream contract: a tensor allocated on stream A and consumed on stream B must stay alive until B finishes, or be record_stream'd; wait_stream orders execution but does not protect deallocation). Reachability is allocator-config-dependent, measured on B200-class hardware with the production stream ordering: default native allocator latent (0/40 corruptions: free-list eventing happens to order the reuse write after pending readers) expandable_segments:True corrupts 19/20 backend:cudaMallocAsync corrupts 19/20 Seam 1 (opt-in SGLANG_ENABLE_OVERLAP_PLAN_STREAM=1): prepare_for_draft_extend runs inside the plan stream; its ForwardBatch owns plan-stream allocations that are NOT ScheduleBatch attributes (init_new's positions / extend_start_loc). When _draft_extend_for_decode returns, the ForwardBatch's only reference dies while forward-stream kernels still read those tensors. Fix (both the single-layer and multi-layer workers): append the draft-extend ForwardBatch to GenerationBatchResult.extra_keep_alive_refs beside verify_forward_batch, gated on the plan stream being active (the hazard exists only there; the default path keeps its prior no-retention behavior) -- the scheduler ring slot is the designed extension point ("a list (not tuple) so that workers can register additional refs") and already retains it for the 2-iteration window. Seam 2 (non-spec overlap + mixed chunked prefill): mix_with_running aliases the running batch's req_pool_indices into mix_running_indices. last_batch / the 2-slot record ring usually keep the running batch alive, but that ages out: intervening non-mixed prefills advance last_batch and overwrite both ring slots; a later mix leaves the staging field as the LAST owner, and resolve_forward_inputs clears it right after enqueueing the forward-stream gather. Fix: record_stream the indices on the gathering stream (CPU-device guarded). Corrections to the previous revision of this PR, from review (thanks): - The earlier seam-1 claim (verify input_ids / out_cache_loc unprotected) was wrong: production covers those via record_stream_each after eagle_prepare_for_verify plus the verify_forward_batch keepalive. The broad exit-time vars(batch) capture in the scheduler is removed: it covered only the batch-reachable subset and missed ForwardBatch-only tensors; the keepalive covers all of them, present and future. - The silent corruption that motivated this PR family came from the relay staging fence (#34077), not these seams; these are latent-by-accident on the default allocator and observable under the supported alternative allocator configs above. ## Modifications - `srt/speculative/eagle_worker_v2.py` and `srt/speculative/multi_layer_eagle_worker_v2.py`: append the draft-extend `ForwardBatch` to `GenerationBatchResult.extra_keep_alive_refs` beside `verify_forward_batch`, gated on the plan stream being active (the hazard exists only there; the default path keeps its prior no-retention behavior). - `srt/managers/overlap_utils.py`: `record_stream` the mixed-gather indices on the gathering stream (CPU-device guarded). - `test/registered/unit/managers/test_spec_v2_overlap_lifetime.py`: rewritten suite preserving the production ownership graph (see Test below). ## Test Tests (test_spec_v2_overlap_lifetime.py, rewritten to preserve the production ownership graph): the seam-1 arms drive the REAL prepare_for_draft_extend -> ForwardBatch.init_new -> compute_position chain under a real plan stream with production ordering (wait_stream) and natural reference death (function scope; scheduler ring mirrored verbatim); the seam-2 arms walk the real aging-out sequence (real mix alias, real 2-slot ring, real resolve_forward_inputs) and prove last-owner death with a weakref. Only kernel latency (torch.cuda._sleep) and next-round allocation pressure are compressed for determinism. Corruption arms run in a subprocess pinned to PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True so red/green is deterministic regardless of the CI host's allocator default. Red/green on the base commit (test file alone on pristine 2b4381956): test_gather_survives_aging_out FAILS -- the recycled indices fire a device-side IndexKernel out-of-bounds assert (the loud variant; in-range recycled values corrupt silently); the seam-1 ring/keepalive pair shows CORRUPTED vs CLEAN on the same real producer chain. With the fix: 6/6 pass. ## Speed Tests and Profiling No kernel or scheduling change. Cost per overlap iteration under the opt-in plan stream: one list append into the existing ring slot (freed on the same 2-iteration cadence). The default path adds nothing. `record_stream` on mixed prefill+decode batches is O(1) host-side. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32068311405](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32068311405)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32068310608](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32068310608)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [Diffusion] Enable vectorized JointThreshold decoding on CUDA
signals.text: ## Motivation JointThreshold decoding already has a batched tensor implementation, but CUDA defaults to the per-row Python path. At higher concurrency, that path serializes argmax, confidence, edit, and completion work across requests and repeatedly synchronizes the host with the device. This PR enables the existing vectorized JointThreshold path by default on CUDA. The change targets JointThreshold specifically: LowConfidence is already vectorized, and DiffusionGemma uses the separate Gemma4Renoise sampler. ## Modifications - Default `vectorized_decoding` to true on CUDA, matching the existing NPU policy. - Preserve `vectorized_decoding: false` as a compatibility/debug escape hatch. - Document the default and its applicability to `LLaDA2MoeModelLM`, `SDARForCausalLM`, and `SDARMoeForCausalLM`. ## Accuracy Tests SGLang already has a registered CUDA E2E test for this exact path: `test/registered/dllm/test_dllm_fdfo_joint_threshold.py`. It launches `inclusionAI/LLaDA2.1-mini` with JointThreshold and requires byte-identical outputs between FDFO and synchronous execution. Since this PR changes the CUDA default, both arms exercise the vectorized implementation. I also ran an external real-model E2E A/B matrix by launching two SGLang HTTP servers with `sglang.launch_server` and driving them with `sglang.benchmark.serving`. All 3,968/3,968 measured LLaDA2.1-mini requests completed with the requested output token count and no request errors. This validates the real serving path and output completion, not downstream task accuracy. No locally available SDAR checkpoint was available, so this PR does not claim real-model SDAR coverage. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Configuration: - H200, TP1, BF16, FDFO; - FlashInfer attention; - radix cache disabled; - maximum 128 running requests; - 8,192-token context; - exact token-ID inputs; - baseline and vectorized arms used identical server and benchmark settings; - each result below contains 32, 64, 128, 256, or 512 requests at concurrency 1, 8, 32, 64, or 128 respectively. **Metric definitions:** request throughput is the achieved end-to-end client throughput (`completed requests / benchmark duration`). TPOT is time per output token excluding the first token: `(request E2E latency - TTFT) / (output tokens - 1)`. The latency columns below are TPOT, not full end-to-end request latency. ### Decode-heavy: 512 input / 2,048 output tokens | Concurrency | E2E request throughput | Delta | Mean TPOT | Delta | p95 TPOT | Delta | |---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | 1 | 0.172 -> 0.168 req/s | -2.7% | 2.72 -> 2.79 ms | +2.8% | 5.07 -> 5.20 ms | +2.5% | | 8 | 0.532 -> 0.685 req/s | +28.7% | 6.89 -> 5.03 ms | -27.0% | 12.87 -> 10.66 ms | -17.2% | | 32 | 0.774 -> 1.079 req/s | +39.4% | 17.60 -> 12.40 ms | -29.6% | 31.66 -> 22.11 ms | -30.2% | | 64 | 1.001 -> 1.493 req/s | +49.2% | 27.67 -> 18.32 ms | -33.8% | 54.96 -> 37.30 ms | -32.1% | | 128 | 1.158 -> 1.842 req/s | +59.0% | 48.08 -> 29.78 ms | -38.1% | 100.22 -> 64.81 ms | -35.3% | ### Long-prefill: 4,096 input / 1,536 output tokens | Concurrency | E2E request throughput | Delta | Mean TPOT | Delta | p95 TPOT | Delta | |---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | 1 | 0.269 -> 0.258 req/s | -4.0% | 1.84 -> 1.91 ms | +3.7% | 5.06 -> 5.20 ms | +2.8% | | 8 | 0.641 -> 0.674 req/s | +5.2% | 6.61 -> 6.44 ms | -2.6% | 25.42 -> 24.67 ms | -3.0% | | 32 | 0.878 -> 0.924 req/s | +5.2% | 20.29 -> 19.36 ms | -4.6% | 70.97 -> 62.97 ms | -11.3% | | 64 | 0.984 -> 1.119 req/s | +13.8% | 36.76 -> 32.41 ms | -11.9% | 138.68 -> 122.23 ms | -11.9% | | 128 | 1.173 -> 1.308 req/s | +11.5% | 61.80 -> 56.39 ms | -8.8% | 237.48 -> 219.20 ms | -7.7% | A GPU-swapped control reproduced the concurrency-64 gains: - decode-heavy: +49.0% request throughput and -33.4% mean TPOT; - long-prefill: +12.5% request throughput and -10.2% mean TPOT. The batch-1 regression is an intentional tradeoff for one consistent CUDA execution path; the benefit grows with batch size because it removes per-request Python work and host synchronization. Benchmark runtime used PyTorch `2.11.0+cu130` and FlashInfer `0.6.14`. Current SGLang pins FlashInfer `0.6.15.post1`. ## Checklist - [x] Format code according to the pre-commit configuration. - [x] Add unit tests. - [x] Update documentation. - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results. - [x] Follow the SGLang code style guidance. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #31730664744](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31730664744)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #31730664268](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31730664268)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [AMD] [Spec] Enable stochastic tree verification on ROCm
signals.text: ## Motivation ROCm EAGLE verification currently routes every HIP request through greedy `argmax`, even when `temperature`, `top_p`, or `top_k` request stochastic sampling. ROCm also lacks the CUDA target-only tree-sampling kernel and its top-k/top-p renormalization operators. While validating a portable tree verifier with GLM-5.2-FP8, EAGLE top-k > 1 exposed a second blocker: DSA’s page-64 index cache received physical token-slot IDs but indexed them as page rows: ```python index_k[tgt_loc_flat] = index_k[src_loc_flat] ``` On MI355X this failed during draft cache preparation, before target verification: ```text HSA_STATUS_ERROR_EXCEPTION: An HSAIL operation resulted in a hardware exception (0x1016) torch.AcceleratorError: HIP error: unspecified launch failure ``` Both the stochastic verifier and page-aware DSA relocation are required for a complete ROCm top-k > 1 tree path. ## Modifications ### Target-only tree verification - `python/sglang/kernels/ops/speculative/tree_sampling.py` - Add the Triton target-only stochastic tree verifier and residual bonus-token sampling. - `python/sglang/kernels/ops/speculative/__init__.py` - Register the Triton tree-sampling operator for CUDA and HIP. - `python/sglang/srt/speculative/eagle_utils.py` - Route non-greedy HIP EAGLE requests to the Triton tree verifier; preserve chain rejection sampling and greedy dispatch. - `python/sglang/srt/speculative/dflash_utils.py` - Enable the same target-only Triton verifier for DFLASH on HIP. - `python/sglang/srt/speculative/spec_utils.py` - Advertise tree-kernel availability on HIP. ### Portable probability renormalization - `python/sglang/kernels/ops/sampling/renorm.py` - Add exact threshold-based top-k/top-p pivots, tie handling, and full-sort overflow fallback. - `python/sglang/kernels/ops/sampling/renorm_triton.py` - Fuse pivot application, masked reduction, and normalization for HIP. - `python/sglang/kernels/ops/sampling/__init__.py` - Select CUDA AOT, HIP Triton, or portable Torch implementations through the kernel registry. - `python/sglang/srt/layers/sampler.py` - Reuse the portable top-p semantics in the Torch sampler path. ### Page-aware DSA tree relocation - `python/sglang/kernels/ops/attention/dsa/index_buf_accessor.py` - Add overlap-safe gather/scatter kernels that move each token’s 128-byte FP8 index key and 4-byte FP32 scale by `(page, offset)`. - Preserve AITer’s 16x16 preshuffled K layout and CUDA’s row-major layout. - `python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/index_key_cache.py` - Replace token-slot-as-page-row indexing with logical K/scale relocation. - `python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/dsa_cache_layer_split.py` - Remove the duplicated broken override so layer-sharded caches inherit the corrected implementation. ### Tests - `test/registered/kernels/ops/speculative/test_tree_speculative_sampling_triton.py` - `test/registered/kernels/ops/speculative/test_spec_verify_distribution.py` - `test/registered/kernels/ops/attention/test_dsa_index_cache_move.py` ## Accuracy Tests ### MI355X unit tests on final PR commit ```text TestTreeSpeculativeSamplingTriton.test_matches_torch_oracle TestTreeSpeculativeSamplingTriton.test_seeded_inputs_are_repeatable TestTreeSpeculativeSamplingTriton.test_dflash_sampling_integration_matches_oracle signals.title: [Scheduler] Fix final chunked-prefill abort commit race
signals.text: ## Motivation Fixes #34149. Related prior report: #34112. While testing chunked-prefill cancellation on latest `main`, we independently reproduced the same user-visible symptom reported in #34112: a cancelled request can expose one token and then finish with `abort`. The #34112 attachment used SGLang v0.5.9. Its negative batch-level output IDs were old FutureMap relay handles and are not the failure criterion or target of this PR. Current `main` no longer uses that `ScheduleBatch.output_ids` representation. Our deterministic current-main reproduction isolates a final-prefill overlap race. An abort can arrive after the final chunked-prefill `EXTEND` is launched but before its delayed result is committed. At that point `scheduler.chunked_req` is already clear, `Req.output_ids` is empty, and the result is pending in `result_queue`. ## Root cause There were two commit boundaries to protect: 1. `abort_request()` records `req.to_finish = FINISH_ABORT()`, but the prefill result processor previously appended the sampled token and token-derived metadata before `update_finish_state()` consumed the pending finish. 2. In the CUDA/HIP overlap loop, scheduling the next batch happens before processing the delayed final-prefill result. Without an admission guard, the pending-finish prefill request can enter optimistic decode, increment `decode_batch_idx` / the KV committed watermark, and perform an optimistic decode step and its associated allocation before the result is dropped (which may reserve multiple slots or pages under speculative decoding). Filtering only in the output streamer is too late: request output, reasoning state, logprobs, hidden states, sampling metadata, grammar state, and KV accounting may already be mutated. ## Modifications - When a delayed result is actually pending, exclude pending-finish prefill requests from the prefill-to-decode merge before optimistic decode preparation. - Keep decode requests in mixed batches on their existing partial-output path. - In the final-prefill result processor, promote the pending finish with `new_accepted_len=0` and reuse normal finished-request cleanup. - Do not commit the dropped token's output ID, reasoning state, hidden state, customized info, sampling mask, returned logprob values, or grammar state. - Still advance packed hidden-state and logprob cursors so later live requests in the same batch read their own slices. - Preserve synchronous, MLX, and PP scheduling semantics by applying the merge guard only while `result_queue` contains a delayed result. - Leave PD-prefill transfer lifecycle unchanged; it uses a separate scheduler/result path. ## Regression coverage The scripted test deterministically waits for this window: - the request has passed through chunked prefill; - the final `EXTEND` is launched; - `scheduler.chunked_req is None`; - no middle chunks remain in flight; - `Req.output_ids` is empty; - the final result is pending. It then aborts and verifies: - finish reason is `FINISH_ABORT`; - no token is appended; - no optimistic decode step occurs; - the request-pool row and KV object are released; - reclaimable KV capacity returns to its baseline after the scheduler drains. Additional CPU tests cover both sides of the scheduler gate (pending queue vs. already-processed result), mixed prefill/decode membership, and a two-request packed-logprob case where the aborted segment advances the cursor without attaching metadata to the aborted request. ## Accuracy Tests Cancellation control flow only; normal token generation is unchanged. Validated on top of `main` commit `7605529bdf98ded2815e48c7054b1bc4533256c9`: ```text PYTHONPATH=python .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q \ test/registered/unit/managers/test_scheduler_chunked_req_gate.py \ test/registered/unit/managers/test_batch_result_processor_hidden_states.py \ test/registered/unit/managers/test_batch_result_processor_spec_grammar.py 11 passed, 2 subtests passed ``` ```text SGLANG_USE_MLX=1 PYTHONPATH=python .venv/bin/python \ test/registered/scripted_runtime/test_scripted_runtime_core.py \ TestScriptedRuntimeCore.test_abort_at_last_chunk_does_not_append_output Ran 1 test in 129.234s OK ``` Also passed: - direct CI-style execution of the two modified CPU test files; - Python compile checks for all touched files; - registered-test and package-registration repository checks; - Black 26.1.0, Ruff 0.15.1, isort 7.0.0, codespell 2.4.1, and `git diff --check`. The packed-logprob test was mutation-checked: it fails both if the aborted request attaches returned logprobs and if its packed cursor contribution is skipped. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Not applicable. The new checks are scheduler control-flow predicates; the result-drop branch runs only for a request that is already finishing. ## Topology notes The race is not caused by TP, DP, or PP. TP/DP use the same per-request result state. PP and MLX process their pending result before the relevant `last_batch` is reused, so the queue-gated admission change is a no-op there while the result-drop protection remains valid. PD-prefill is intentionally out of scope because it has a separate transfer and result lifecycle. The registered end-to-end regression is TP=1 / DP=1 / PP=1. Multi-rank topology behavior was source-reviewed but not claimed as a multi-GPU runtime validation. ## Checklist - [x] Rebased onto current `main`. - [x] Added deterministic registered regression coverage. - [x] Added focused scheduler and packed-metadata unit coverage. - [x] Ran relevant unit and scripted-runtime tests. - [x] Ran formatting, compile, and test-registration checks. - [x] Documentation and performance benchmarks are not applicable to this abort-only correctness fix. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32135933113](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32135933113)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32135932799](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32135932799)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [Kimi K3] Rework skipped-think fix as opt-in force_nonempty_content with streaming coverage
signals.text: Stacked on top of #33995. Keeps @yhyang201's original commit `d11868d7d9` in history and supersedes it with a rework. ## Problem K3 sometimes closes its think channel before producing any answer (EOS inside think), so responses come back with `reasoning_content` but empty `content`. #33995 fixed the non-stream path by treating marker-less output as content, which has two leaks: - **Truncated reasoning becomes content**: a `max_tokens` cut also produces zero think markers, so truncated thinking gets misclassified as the answer. - **Streaming stays broken**: the branch only exists in `detect_and_parse`; `parse_streaming_increment` starts in `force_reasoning=True` and streams the raw payload as `reasoning_text`, so `stream=True` still returns `content=""`. ## What this PR does Reworks the fix as an opt-in, K3-native `force_nonempty_content`: - `KimiK3Detector.__init__` accepts `force_nonempty_content` so the existing `chat_template_kwargs` plumbing in `ReasoningParser` works (previously `TypeError`). - `detect_and_parse` reclassifies only on positive evidence: `RESPONSE_CLOSE` or `MESSAGE_CLOSE` present and zero think markers (full or partial). Bare marker-free text (truncated reasoning) stays reasoning. - Streaming **never holds chunks back**. A hold-back would starve SSE during long thinking runs (no delta until the channel decision) and trip client idle timeouts (observed: ~300 s client-side `terminated` while the server is still decoding). Instead, undecided prethink text streams as `reasoning_content` in real time, and `finish()` re-emits the cleaned payload as `content` once the response/message close proves skipped-think — mirroring the base class's `finish()` re-emit of accumulated reasoning. - The `finish()` re-emit is gated on `_in_reasoning`, i.e. it only fires when no channel decision ever happened mid-stream. Without the gate, answers that already streamed as `content` (`RESPONSE_OPEN` expressible, or `force_reasoning=False`) would be emitted a second time. - Under `stream_reasoning=False`, reasoning buffered past a mid-stream cut (e.g. `max_tokens`) still flushes: the non-fnc path delegates to the base `finish()`, and the fnc path flushes the buffer as `reasoning_text` itself, because the base implementation would reclassify it as `content` under fnc — the leak this flag exists to prevent. Clients therefore see: live `reasoning_content` while the model thinks → final `content` delta carrying the actual answer for skipped-think runs; long thinking runs stream uninterrupted end to end. No behavior change for `force_nonempty_content=False`; all existing K3 parser tests unchanged. ## Tests - `test_fnc_non_stream_skipped_think_vs_truncated_reasoning` — non-stream skipped-think vs truncated reasoning under `force_nonempty_content=True`. - `test_fnc_streaming_skipped_think_answer` — real-time reasoning deltas + finish() content re-emit, across chunk sizes 1/5/13. - `test_fnc_streaming_truncated_reasoning_stays_reasoning` — no close evidence → stays reasoning. - `test_fnc_streaming_long_think_streams_without_close` — 20k chars of marker-free thinking streams every chunk live; no hold-back. - `test_fnc_streaming_response_open_not_reemitted` / `test_fnc_streaming_force_reasoning_off_not_reemitted` — answer streams exactly once; the finish() re-emit never duplicates it. - `test_stream_reasoning_off_truncation_flushes_reasoning` — truncated reasoning flushes as reasoning, fnc on and off. - `test_fnc_stream_reasoning_off_skipped_think_reemits_content` — skipped-think re-emit still works when nothing streamed live. The duplication and flush-regression tests fail on the pre-gate code (verified by stashing the fix); everything passes after it. ``` $ pytest test/registered/unit/parser/test_kimik3_reasoning_parser.py test/registered/unit/parser/test_reasoning_parser.py 138 passed ``` <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:no_entry_sign: [Run #32400319883](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32400319883)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32400319481](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32400319481)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #32400319720](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32400319720)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [AMD] Perf Kimi-K3 fuse ROCm KDA decode boundary
signals.text: Defer the `f_b` projection into the gfx950 FlyDSL kernel so decode fuses convolution, recurrent state update, and gated RMSNorm while preserving the existing fail-closed fallback. ## Summary - Vendor the Kimi-K3 KDA-only FlyDSL wrapper and gfx950 decode kernels in SGLang. - Prefer the local implementation through the source selector while retaining the AITER module as a fail-closed fallback. - Remove the dependency on the unreleased `aiter.ops.flydsl.kimi_k3_kda_decode` module; stock pinned AITER supplies only FlyDSL tensor/vector/JIT shims. - Automatically select the validated cooperative `f_a`, wave-specialized front, fused norm reduction, BF16 `fdot2`, WPE3 schedule only for exact C2. - Keep every other batch on the original kernel schedule. ## Modifications - Add a trimmed KDA-only vendored FlyDSL package and source selector. - Route the existing HIP fused KDA adapter through the SGLang module first. - Make the exact-C2 winner an internal batch specialization with no per-knob environment configuration. - Add focused recurrent/graph tests and an allocation-free graph benchmark. ## Runtime gate and fallback The fused ROCm KDA boundary is opt-in: ```bash export SGLANG_K3_KDA_FUSED_BACKEND=aiter ``` This flag controls the entire PR path, not only the C2 tuning. During model initialization, Kimi-K3 prepares the deferred `f_b` weights and fused decode arguments only when the value is exactly `aiter` and the gfx950 FlyDSL implementation is available. During decode, `covered()` revalidates runtime shapes, dtypes, strides, state indices, and output buffers before dispatch. Behavior by configuration: - Flag unset or any value other than `aiter`: preserve the existing unfused KDA path. - Flag set to `aiter`, supported gfx950 inputs: use the fused `f_b + convolution + recurrence + gated RMSNorm` boundary. - Flag set but unsupported runtime inputs: fail closed to the existing KDA implementation. - Exact C2: automatically select the validated WPE3/cooperative/front-specialized/fused-reduction/`fdot2` schedule. - C1 and C4+: use the original fused-kernel build options; the C2 specialization does not apply. `SGLANG_K3_FLYDSL_SOURCE` defaults to `auto`, which prefers the vendored SGLang kernel and falls back to the AITER module if needed. `SGLANG_K3_AITER_KDA_GROUP64` is a separate, optional input-preparation optimization and is not required by this PR. ## Accuracy Tests - GSM8K 1319: `0.950` - Invalid responses: `0.001` ## Speed Tests and Profiling Automatic-profile micro A/B on the integration branch: ```text batch baseline us auto-profile us delta 1 12.2758 12.3008 +0.20% 2 12.7725 11.9959 -6.08% 4 12.8509 12.8770 +0.20% 8 13.4043 13.3785 -0.19% 16 14.0342 14.0324 -0.01% ``` Non-C2 changes are within the measurement noise floor; only C2 changes build options. Prior production-like results: - 69-layer graph: `9.20 -> 8.38 us/layer` (`-8.9%`). - Matched C2 endpoint: `+0.19%` throughput, `-0.20%` TPOT. ## Validation - [x] KDA FlyDSL focused tests on PR branch: 15 passed - [x] KDA FlyDSL focused tests on integration branch: 15 passed - [x] C1/C2/C4/C8/C16 graph micro A/B - [x] GSM8K 1319 - [x] Fail-closed non-C2 fallback ## Checklist - [ ] Run repository pre-commit hooks - [x] Add focused unit tests - [x] Provide accuracy and speed results - [x] Preserve fail-closed fallback <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:no_entry_sign: [Run #32343549943](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32343549943)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32343549985](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32343549985)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32343550227](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32343550227)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [AMD] Port CP V2 to the DeepSeek-V4 HIP backend
signals.text: ## Motivation #33532 added the CP-v2 strategy for DeepSeek-V4 but wired it into the CUDA backend only. `deepseek_v4_backend_hip_radix.py` was not touched, so on ROCm the model/runner splits tokens for CP-v2 while the HIP attention backend still builds metadata for the un-split layout. Nothing gates CP-v2 by platform — `SGLANG_ENABLE_CP_V2` (`environ.py:319`) and `is_cp_v2_active` (`layers/cp/utils.py:139-155`) have no `is_hip` branch — so enabling it on ROCm today produces wrong metadata rather than a clear error. This ports the contract rather than gating the feature off. ## Modifications The contract, mirroring `deepseek_v4_backend.py`: CP-v2 pads the causal metadata rows for per-rank partitioning (`P` rows) while cache-write locations stay one-per-logical-token (`N` rows). The reindex must therefore anchor its global-field post-condition to `N`, not to the padded metadata length. - **`apply_cp_reindex` gains `num_tokens`** (default `None` → `pre_global_len`), keeping the existing CP-v1 model-hook calls at `models/deepseek_v4.py:2698` and `models/deepseek_v4_nextn.py:272` byte-compatible. - **`init_compression_metadata` gains `num_tokens`.** Its `raw_out_loc` / `seq_lens_casual` shape-equality assert would otherwise fail on the very first CP-v2 prefill, since under CP-v2 those two legitimately differ. - **`make_core_attn_metadata` and `init_forward_metadata_prefill` thread `num_tokens` / `forward_batch`** so `cp_v2_active` and `padded_num_tokens = sum(per_rank_actual_token)` can be computed, matching `deepseek_v4_backend.py:746-774`. - **HIP-only:** `UnifiedKvMetadata` mirrors `c4/c128_out_loc` with a page offset. Those are write addresses too, so they are checked to stay global. They are nested under `.unified` and so cannot join `_CP_GLOBAL_FIELDS`, which `getattr`s off `self`. **No kernel work was required.** The shared Triton metadata kernel already implements the `num_write_tokens < bs` masking CP-v2 relies on (`kernels/ops/attention/dsv4/metadata_kernel.py:106-126`), and HIP's flashmla scheduler metadata is a no-op (`_create_flashmla_metadata` returns `None` under `is_hip()`). `dspark_block_size` is deliberately **not** added to `make_core_attn_metadata`: HIP has no `get_dspark_swa_page_indices`, and it is unrelated to CP-v2. ## Accuracy Tests 8×MI355X, DeepSeek-V4-Flash-DSpark, TP8, single node, GSM8K 200 questions. Only `SGLANG_ENABLE_CP_V2` differs between the CP arms: | arm | Accuracy | Invalid | | --- | --- | --- | | no CP (baseline) | 0.950 | 0.000 | | CP8, CP-v1 (reference) | 0.955 | 0.000 | | **CP8, CP-v2 (this PR)** | **0.950** | **0.000** | All within noise for n=200 (1σ ≈ 0.015). `ATTN_CP0`–`ATTN_CP7` confirmed active in the server log, and no `apply_cp_reindex` / `init_compression_metadata` assertion fired. Server config: ``` --tp-size 8 --attention-backend dsv4 --page-size 256 --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 --enable-prefill-cp --cp-strategy interleave --attention-context-parallel-size 8 --mem-fraction-static 0.4 --disable-radix-cache --disable-shared-experts-fusion SGLANG_HACK_FLASHMLA_BACKEND=unified_kv_triton SGLANG_ENABLE_CP_V2=1 ``` `unified_kv_triton` is pinned deliberately. The default `tilelang` HIP path has a **pre-existing, separate** CP bug: `fused_qk_norm_rope_swa_store` writes the rank-local KV shard at the global `swa_out_cache_loc` (`models/deepseek_v4.py:1114-1142`) and nothing re-stores the gathered KV, so CP on HIP is only correct under `unified_kv` today. Validating this port on a known-broken substrate would prove nothing. That bug is out of scope here; happy to file it separately. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Provide accuracy benchmark results. - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). cc @kkHuang-amd @HaiShaw @1am9trash <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32339382800](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32339382800)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32339382543](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32339382543)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32339382881](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32339382881)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [RL, Spec] DFlash: top-p mask capture
signals.text: ## Relationship to existing work https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/27408 introduced the machinery needed to return masks from nucleus sampling via `/generate`. https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/33593 expands that functionality with top-p only masks and laces it through `/v1/chat/completions` via `return_meta_info=true`. https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/34037 bounds the effects of such requests on concurrent requests. As of #33459, the DFlash SpecV2 path is capable of returning logprobs. This PR extends this line of work to allow for top-p masking when DFlash SpecV2 is enabled. ## Motivation Top-p sampling masks are useful in RL to reduce trainer-inference mismatch. Speculative decoding can [accelerate RL training](https://www.lmsys.org/blog/2025-11-19-miles/#speculative-decoding-with-online-draft-model-training) and reduce rollout generation bottleneck. Top-p sampling masks are useful for reduce training-inference mismatch, which is often necessary for stable async RL. ## Modifications - Enable return_sampling_mask for DFlash speculative decoding. - Return one sampling support and selected-token logprob for every accepted output token. - Preserve support after top-k/top-p/min-p filtering and renormalization. - Align metadata with DFlash accepted-token lengths and finished/EOS truncation. - Support mixed batches and greedy decoding; greedy masks are singleton token sets. - Reject requests whose realized support exceeds --sampling-mask-max-tokens. - Require exact DFlash acceptance thresholds (1.0) when masks are requested. - Defer Python-list materialization until result processing, keeping outputs tensor-backed and using asynchronous device-to-host copying. ## Accuracy Tests Targeted final implementation: - 4/4 DFlash sampling-mask unit tests passed in Modal: - tensor-backed deferred materialization; - filtered target probabilities and selected-token logprobs; - greedy singleton masks; - whole-request rejection on support overflow. - Added registered DFlash server coverage asserting: - seven generated tokens produce seven masks and seven logprobs; - every sampled token belongs to its corresponding support. - Full Qwen3.6 NVFP4+DFlash B200 run: - 98,304 measured output tokens; - 49,152 requested masks returned, with no missing masks; - maximum observed top-p support was 5,306; a repeat reached 7,476; - completed without generation or mask-alignment errors. This feature only returns metadata and is not intended to change sampling decisions, so no downstream task-accuracy benchmark was run. ## Speed Tests and Profiling One B200 with: - nvidia/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-NVFP4; - modal-labs/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-DFlash; - DFlash block size 8, FA4 draft attention; - 32 concurrent requests, 512 generated tokens each; - warmup followed by six alternating mask/no-mask rounds. Results: - Without masks: 4,163.78 tok/s median - With masks: 4,160.45 tok/s median - Ratio: 0.9992, or approximately −0.08% The difference was within run-to-run noise. A complete repeat also showed no slowdown. ## Checklist - [ ] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [ ] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. signals.title: [AMD][DCP] Skip unused QuickAllReduce allocation for DCP groups
signals.text: ## Motivation On ROCm, `GroupCoordinator` currently initializes QuickAllReduce whenever custom all-reduce is enabled. That is useful for TP, but current DCP communication paths do not dispatch to QuickAllReduce: - `ag_rs`: all-gather plus reduce-scatter for MLA, or an FP32 all-reduce for MHA. - `a2a` / `fi_a2a`: all-to-all. In a Kimi-K3 TP8/DCP8 profile on MI350X, constructing the DCP QuickAllReduce communicator reserved 4.002 GiB per GPU. Across 1,152 recorded rank-0 DCP collective dispatches, QuickAllReduce was selected zero times. TP QuickAllReduce remains useful and must stay enabled. Related to #29736. ## Modifications - Add an optional `use_quick_allreduce` control to `GroupCoordinator` and `init_model_parallel_group`. - Preserve the existing behavior by default: the new option inherits `use_custom_allreduce` when unspecified. - Disable QuickAllReduce only for the DCP group. - Keep the AITER custom-all-reduce and PyNccl setup unchanged. - Add a unit test that verifies DCP opts out while TP retains the default behavior. ## Accuracy Tests This does not change model math or the collective selected by current DCP paths. The targeted construction test passes: ``` 1 passed, 5 deselected ``` ## Speed Tests and Profiling This PR targets static memory rather than latency. Measured DCP communicator initialization on MI350X: | Component | Reserved per GPU | | --- | ---: | | PyNccl | 1.883 GiB | | AITER custom all-reduce | 3.002 GiB | | QuickAllReduce | 4.002 GiB | QuickAllReduce had zero selections in the recorded DCP dispatches, so this change reclaims the 4.002 GiB DCP allocation without removing TP QuickAllReduce. ## Checklist - [x] Ran pre-commit on the changed files. - [x] Added a focused unit test. - [x] No documentation change is required; the default API behavior is preserved. - [x] No model kernel or output math is changed. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #31354533291](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31354533291)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #31354533157](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31354533157)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:heavy_minus_sign: **No AMD PR run found for this commit**.<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [BugFix] Fix symmetric memory allocation during CUDA graph capture
signals.text: ## Motivation With symmetric memory, speculative decoding, TP > 1, and CUDA graph capture enabled together, collective buffers could be captured at different NCCL registration windows across ranks. This violates the `NCCL_WIN_COLL_SYMMETRIC` contract and can silently produce incorrect model outputs without a CUDA or NCCL error. The divergence came from using the eager NCCL memory pool during graph capture. Rank-local JIT and warmup history changed that pool's free-list state before multiple speculative-decoding graphs were captured. ## Modifications - Keep the existing eager NCCL memory pool and add a dedicated pool for symmetric-memory CUDA graph allocations. - Before retaining each breakable or full CUDA graph, run the same shape once in a disposable capture. Defer NCCL registration during that capture, then register any newly created segments outside capture. - Recapture the retained graph from the same pool so its collective buffers reuse registered graph-pool blocks with rank-consistent window/offset pairs. - Preserve the existing eager and `tc_piecewise` behavior. - Add a 2-GPU regression that creates rank-divergent eager-pool state and captures and replays three successive graphs. Priming is intentionally done per retained graph. Later shapes can be the first to require another symmetric-memory segment, so a session-wide one-time prime does not establish the invariant for every graph. ## Reproduction The minimal regression requires two CUDA GPUs and recreates rank-divergent eager-pool state without loading a model: ```bash python3 test/registered/cuda_graph/test_pynccl_symmetric_memory_pool.py ``` The model-level reproduction used Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-FP8 with 1P1D, TP4 on prefill and decode, PP1 prefill, NEXTN with 3 speculative steps / top-k 1 / 4 draft tokens, breakable prefill CUDA graphs, full decode CUDA graphs, and symmetric memory enabled. After starting the server, run the accuracy evaluation with: ```bash python3 -m sglang.test.run_eval --base-url http://<router-host>:<port> --model qwen35-397b --eval-name gsm8k --num-examples 200 --num-shots 8 --max-tokens 16384 --num-threads 16 --temperature 0 ``` Run the serving benchmark once for each of the following three arms while keeping every other server setting unchanged: parent commit with symmetric memory enabled, this PR with symmetric memory disabled, and this PR with symmetric memory enabled. ```bash for concurrency in 16 64 256; do python3 -m sglang.benchmark.serving --backend sglang --base-url http://<router-host>:<port> --model qwen35-397b --tokenizer <tokenizer-path> --dataset-name random --num-prompts $((concurrency * 5)) --random-input-len 8192 --random-output-len 64 --random-range-ratio 1.0 --request-rate inf --max-concurrency "$concurrency" --warmup-requests $((concurrency * 2)) --output-file "result_c${concurrency}.jsonl"; done ``` ## Accuracy Tests GSM8K used 200 questions, 8-shot prompts, temperature 0, and reports accuracy as a score in `[0, 1]`. | Configuration | GSM8K score | Accuracy | | --- | ---: | ---: | | Before fix, symmetric memory enabled | 0.940 | 94.0% | | After fix, symmetric memory enabled | 0.990 / 0.990 / 0.990 | 99.0% / 99.0% / 99.0% | | After fix, symmetric memory disabled control | 0.990 | 99.0% | The before-fix result reproduces the previously observed approximately `0.95` accuracy. The fix restores the expected `0.99` accuracy without disabling symmetric memory, speculative decoding, or CUDA graphs. The 2-GPU/TP2 regression fails during capture on the parent implementation. The fixed implementation captures and replays three successive graphs and verifies rank-consistent offsets and outputs. An instrumented model-level capture recorded 94,328 symmetric-memory allocations across target prefill/verify and draft extend/decode with zero cross-rank window/offset mismatches. The GPU results above were collected on the same core implementation before a final non-functional cleanup that removed unused state and test compatibility scaffolding. The exact public commit passes targeted pre-commit hooks, `py_compile`, `git diff --check`, and `git show --check`; public CI on the exact commit is pending. ## Speed Tests and Profiling The metric is `total_token_throughput` in `tokens/s`. All three arms were run in the same batch with random fixed-length ISL 8192 / OSL 64, request rate `inf`, and three repetitions per concurrency. | Concurrency | Before fix, symm ON (tokens/s) | After fix, symm OFF (tokens/s) | After fix, symm ON (tokens/s) | | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | | 16 | 52,229.25 / 51,756.62 / 52,104.05 (mean 52,029.97) | 50,252.12 / 49,789.34 / 50,190.87 (mean 50,077.44) | 52,033.24 / 52,304.27 / 52,258.73 (mean 52,198.75) | | 64 | 53,474.89 / 53,194.81 / 53,184.14 (mean 53,284.61) | 50,592.58 / 50,734.43 / 50,860.22 (mean 50,729.08) | 53,276.41 / 53,006.39 / 53,212.94 (mean 53,165.25) | | 256 | 52,544.23 / 52,435.58 / 52,499.45 (mean 52,493.09) | 50,290.20 / 49,808.08 / 50,323.21 (mean 50,140.50) | 52,340.47 / 52,666.02 / 52,603.16 (mean 52,536.55) | | Concurrency | After fix symm ON / before fix symm ON | After fix symm ON / after fix symm OFF | | ---: | ---: | ---: | | 16 | 1.0032 | 1.0424 | | 64 | 0.9978 | 1.0480 | | 256 | 1.0008 | 1.0478 | The fix preserves the before-fix symmetric-memory throughput and retains its approximately 4-5% advantage over disabling symmetric memory. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). (N/A: no user-facing API or configuration change.) - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1.
