signals.title: [Perf] Fuse prefill norm/act quantization for NVFP4 W4A4 hybrid models (Qwen3.5 family)
signals.text: > Rebased onto `main` after #34859 merged: the SiLU+FP4-quant base fusion landed with the model support, so this PR's net diff contains the three remaining changes (attention-layer SiLU coverage, post-LN+FP4-quant, and gated-norm+FP8-quant). ## Motivation For Qwen3.5-family hybrid (GDN + attention) models served with a mixed ModelOpt NVFP4(W4A4)+FP8 checkpoint, prefill spends a measurable share of GPU time in standalone norm / activation / quantization glue kernels: every projection input is normalized, written to HBM in bf16, then re-read and quantized by a separate kernel. Kernel-level tracing against vLLM 0.27.1 on the same model showed the GEMM/attention/GDN families at parity while SGLang lost time in this glue (vLLM fuses norm+quant and act+quant via torch.compile). This PR removes the extra round-trips with three targeted fusions (all bit-equivalent up to FP4/FP8 rounding ties, each with a kill switch): 1. **SiLU+mul + NVFP4 quant** for dense MLPs: replaces `act_and_mul` + the standalone per-block FP4 quantize with FlashInfer's `silu_and_mul_scaled_nvfp4_experts_quantize` (single-group form), handing `down_proj` a prequantized `(fp4, swizzled_scale)` tuple through the existing `_accepts_prequantized_fp4` path. Enabled for both GDN-layer and attention-layer MLPs. 2. **Post-attention GemmaRMSNorm + NVFP4 quant**: FlashInfer `add_rmsnorm_fp4quant` fuses the residual-add, the norm, and the `gate_up` input quant into one kernel. Gemma's `(1 + w)` scaling is folded into a precomputed weight; the swizzled block-scale is exposed as the 2D `(m_padded, K/16)` view so the cuDNN mm_fp4 backend's shape validation also passes. 3. **GDN gated RMSNorm + static-FP8 quant**: adds an fp8-store epilogue to the `fla` `layernorm_gated` Triton kernel (skips the bf16 intermediate write entirely) and teaches `ModelOptFp8LinearMethod` to accept a prequantized `(fp8, scale)` tuple for `out_proj` (explicit opt-in attribute, mirroring the fp4 path). Kill switches: `SGLANG_DISABLE_SILU_FP4_QUANT_FUSION=1`, `SGLANG_DISABLE_POST_LN_FP4_QUANT_FUSION=1`, `SGLANG_DISABLE_GATED_NORM_FP8_QUANT_FUSION=1`. The fusions auto-enable only when the touched projections use the matching ModelOpt linear method (NVFP4 W4A4 for 1-2, per-tensor static FP8 for 3), so other checkpoints and quant modes keep their current control flow. ## Benchmark Re-benchmarked on 2026-08-20 against the current PR base and head. Both lanes ran back-to-back on the same otherwise-idle physical GPU with the same container, model snapshot, server flags, prompt seed, and client command. ### Environment and revisions | Item | Value | |---|---| | GPU | NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition (SM120), physical GPU 2 | | Driver | 580.159.03 | | Container | `lmsysorg/sglang:qwen38` | | PyTorch / CUDA | `2.13.0+cu130` / CUDA 13.0 | | FlashInfer | 0.6.18 | | Model | `RadixArk/Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4` | | Model snapshot | `554ebba9b5f1b79dc11246341960360e6ef05ef4` | | main/base | `a4ffb996db3e823708a53637f851e2677d4455a8` | | PR head | `a3facf77a9bf07464d87299d21dede0837df8e9d` | | merge base | `a4ffb996db3e823708a53637f851e2677d4455a8` | Because the merge base equals the tested main revision, this comparison isolates the PR's net diff. ### Commands The commands below were run inside the existing `sglang_bbuf` container. For the main lane, `SGLANG_TREE=/work/pr34934-rebench-main`; for the PR lane, `SGLANG_TREE=/work/pr34934-rebench-head`. Server: ```bash SGLANG_TREE=/work/pr34934-rebench-head CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=2 \ PYTHONPATH="${SGLANG_TREE}/python" \ python -m sglang.launch_server \ --model-path RadixArk/Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4 \ --host 0.0.0.0 \ --port 31002 \ --tp-size 1 \ --chunked-prefill-size 8192 \ --max-prefill-tokens 8192 \ --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 \ --mamba-ssm-dtype bfloat16 \ --disable-radix-cache ``` Benchmark client: ```bash SGLANG_TREE=/work/pr34934-rebench-head LANE=pr ROUND=1 CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES= \ PYTHONPATH="${SGLANG_TREE}/python" \ python -m sglang.bench_serving \ --backend sglang \ --host 127.0.0.1 \ --port 31002 \ --dataset-name random \ --model RadixArk/Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4 \ --random-input-len 8192 \ --random-output-len 1024 \ --random-range-ratio 1 \ --num-prompts 5 \ --request-rate inf \ --max-concurrency 1 \ --seed 1234 \ --warmup-requests 1 \ --disable-tqdm \ --output-details \ --output-file "/work/pr34934-rebench-artifacts/${LANE}-round-${ROUND}.jsonl" ``` For each revision, one complete five-request run was discarded as a pre-run, then the recorded command was run three times (five requests per round, 15 measured requests per revision). Every invocation also ran the client's one built-in warmup request. GPU 2 had 0 MiB allocated before the first server was started and after the final server was stopped. ### Per-round results | Revision | Round | Mean TTFT (ms) | Median TTFT (ms) | Output tok/s | Median ITL (ms) | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | main | 1 | 655.48 | 642.42 | 64.66 | 14.94 | | main | 2 | 655.66 | 649.62 | 64.22 | 14.96 | | main | 3 | 653.87 | 638.01 | 64.41 | 14.96 | | PR | 1 | 638.52 | 626.78 | 64.32 | 14.95 | | PR | 2 | 640.99 | 627.77 | 64.42 | 14.95 | | PR | 3 | 640.33 | 628.54 | 64.53 | 14.95 | ### Aggregate result TTFT aggregates all 15 per-request observations. Output throughput is total generated tokens divided by total benchmark duration across the three recorded rounds. | Metric | main | main + this PR | Delta | |---|---:|---:|---:| | Mean TTFT | 655.00 ms | **639.95 ms** | **-15.06 ms (-2.30%)** | | Median TTFT | 642.42 ms | **627.77 ms** | **-14.65 ms (-2.28%)** | | Output throughput | 64.43 tok/s | 64.42 tok/s | -0.02% | | Median ITL | 14.957 ms | 14.949 ms | -0.008 ms | For the paired TTFT observations, the mean gain was 15.06 ms and the approximate 95% confidence interval was 10.79-19.32 ms. The current result supports a stable ~2.3% prefill TTFT improvement; decode throughput and ITL are unchanged within run-to-run noise. Startup logs confirmed that the optimized paths were active for the expected layers: - post-LN + FP4 quant: 64 layers - SiLU + FP4 quant: 64 layers - gated RMSNorm + FP8 quant: 48 GDN layers Both server logs were checked for traceback, CUDA error, OOM, and exception signatures; none were found. ### Correctness validation Correctness was not rerun as part of the 2026-08-20 performance pass. The earlier full GSM8K validation (1319 examples) reported: | Configuration | Score | |---|---:| | fusions off | 0.9635 | | fusions on | 0.9658 | The fused kernels were also previously checked for identical residual propagation relative to `fused_add_rmsnorm`. ### Data provenance The performance tables above come from the current PR head and its exact merge base, using three saved `bench_serving --output-details` JSONL results per lane. They replace the older 5-request/FlashInfer-0.6.17 table, which was measured against an earlier base and was not reproducible as a current-main/current-PR comparison. The previous H200 FP8-dynamic table was removed because these W4A4-specific fusions are inactive for that checkpoint and therefore it did not measure this PR's performance effect. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Code Formatting with Pre-Commit](https://docs.sglang.ai/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-formatting-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests as outlined in the [Running Unit Tests](https://docs.sglang.ai/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#running-unit-tests). - [x] Update documentation / docstrings / example tutorials as needed, according to [Writing Documentation](https://docs.sglang.ai/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#writing-documentation). - [x] Provide throughput / latency benchmark results and accuracy evaluation results as needed, according to [Benchmark and Profiling](https://docs.sglang.ai/developer_guide/benchmark_and_profiling.html) and [Accuracy Results](https://docs.sglang.ai/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#accuracy-results). - [x] For reviewers: If you haven't made any contributions to this PR and are only assisting with merging the main branch, please remove yourself as a co-author when merging. - [x] Please feel free to join our Slack channel at https://slack.sglang.ai to discuss your PR. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32368351888](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32368351888)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32368351907](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32368351907)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32368351823](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32368351823)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [NPU]Ensure tensors allocated by empty_like are contiguous
signals.text: ## Motivation `torch.empty_like(q)` inherits the memory format of `q` by default. signals.title: [NPU] [FIX] Fix non-contiguous parameter issue in FIA operator
signals.text: <!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. --> ## Motivation <!-- Describe the purpose and goals of this pull request. --> The `npu_fused_infer_attention_score` operator receives non-contiguous inputs. signals.title: perf: overlap Qwen shared expert with DeepEP routed experts
signals.text: ## Motivation For Qwen MoE models using CUDA and DeepEP, the shared expert currently runs on the default stream before the routed-expert path. This serializes two independent computations and leaves an available alternate stream unused. This PR adds an opt-in path that overlaps the Qwen shared expert with routed-expert/DeepEP execution. ## Modifications - Add `SGLANG_QWEN_DEEPEP_SHARED_OVERLAP` (default: `false`). - When enabled on CUDA, enqueue the shared expert on `alt_stream`, execute the routed-expert path on the current stream, and wait on an event immediately before accumulating the shared output. - When breakable CUDA graph is active, skip this optimization and retain the existing serial shared-expert path; cross-segment overlap across the eager DeepEP break is out of scope. - Document the new environment variable. ## Accuracy Tests The accuracy evidence below was collected on predecessor `38f714d28e1fa01ae5b1ce38ce576373b8293722`, based on upstream main `0c072235f44fce4b89e594c2d3348e4f48e774b8`, with a clean source tree. Current head `76815b3766deb3a3c9aceef1cb346093f691d976` differs only by making breakable CUDA graph use the pre-existing serial fallback instead of an alternate-stream path with an immediate wait; the non-breakable overlap implementation measured below is unchanged. Configuration: `nvidia/Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-NVFP4`, 8x GB300, FP4 weights, FP8 KV cache, TP8/DP8/EP8, NEXTN draft length 6, DeepEP low-latency mode, 200 GSM8K examples, 5 shots, temperature 0.6, top-p 0.95, and top-k 20. The run used natural NEXTN acceptance. | Metric | Result | Gate | |---|---:|---:| | GSM8K score | **0.990** (200/200) | >= 0.95 | | Request-weighted mean accepted length | **4.6102** (1,379 decode-log rows; request weight 11,625) | > 3.3 | | Evaluation latency | 95.646 s | -- | | Evaluation output throughput | 5,621.1 token/s | -- | All eight ranks completed target verify CUDA graph capture, followed by draft decode and draft extend graph capture. The job completed successfully with exit code 0. Breakable CUDA graph is now intentionally excluded from this optimization, and no performance gain is claimed for that fallback. ## Speed Tests and Profiling The performance A/B exercised the same overlap mechanism on the benchmark stack before this upstream-main port. The upstream-main commit listed in the accuracy section was validated separately through CUDA graph capture and GSM8K. The end-to-end A/B comparison used the same configuration and differed only in the job name and `SGLANG_QWEN_DEEPEP_SHARED_OVERLAP=true`. Configuration: `nvidia/Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-NVFP4`, 24x GB300 disaggregated serving (four TP4/DP4/EP4 prefill replicas and one TP8/DP8/EP8 decode replica), FP4 weights, FP8 KV cache, NEXTN draft length 6, concurrency 896, fixed accepted length 4.8, and a 3,600-second AgentX replay. | AIPerf metric | Disabled | Enabled | Delta | |---|---:|---:|---:| | Total token throughput | 2,649,331.82 token/s | 2,705,912.48 token/s | **+2.14%** | | Output token throughput | 25,466.20 token/s | 26,000.99 token/s | **+2.10%** | | Request throughput | 27.980 request/s | 28.516 request/s | **+1.91%** | | Mean inter-token latency | 18.220 ms | 17.623 ms | **-3.28%** | | Theoretical prefix-cache hit | 95.433% | 95.452% | +0.020 pp | These are end-to-end AIPerf results without profiler instrumentation. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). signals.title: [Diffusion] Align MiniMax H3 request RNG with reference
signals.text: ## Summary - use one request-local CPU generator for MiniMax H3 noise - preserve the reference draw order: visual conditions, target video tensor, then target audio rows - precompute condition noise before denoising instead of re-seeding per modality or condition - keep the existing H3-only scope so other diffusion consistency trajectories are unchanged ## Why The previous implementation independently re-seeded video, audio, and condition streams. For T2VA this made the target audio latent diverge immediately; because H3 jointly attends over video and audio rows, video output also drifted. The new contract follows the official Diffusers MiniMax H3 implementation from huggingface/diffusers#14355. ## Validation - focused MiniMax H3 numerical contract: 5 passed on H100 devbox - pre-commit: passed on the exact remote checkout - standard 2-GPU H100 E2E: 1 passed in 176.29s (47.50s generation, 22.5 GiB peak GPU memory) - official GT workflow: [run 31890047128](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31890047128) succeeded - ci-data GT commit: [81ca8f18](https://github.com/sgl-project/ci-data-diffusion/commit/81ca8f18d485df4e4bac9a5a40c5b4666f0fa57f) - NVIDIA PR CI: [run 31890556920](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31890556920) succeeded The GT follow-up is intentionally limited to the affected MiniMax H3 H100 T2VA frames. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32387986025](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32387986025)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32387985835](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32387985835)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32387986295](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32387986295)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [MoE] Add FlashInfer SM90 MXFP4 W4A8 CUTLASS MoE
signals.text: ## Motivation SGLang currently supports FlashInfer's SM90 MXFP4 W4A16 CUTLASS MoE path, which was introduced in SGLang #24816 on top of FlashInfer [#3084](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/3084). FlashInfer [#3738](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/3738) adds a different Hopper path that dynamically quantizes activations to FP8 and runs MXFP4-weight x FP8-activation MoE GEMMs using Humming-style pre-MMA E8M0 scale fusion. This PR wires that path into SGLang as an explicit opt-in: ```bash --moe-runner-backend flashinfer_mxfp4 \ --flashinfer-mxfp4-moe-precision fp8 ``` The existing `default` and `bf16` behavior is unchanged. Related work: - SGLang https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/24816 - FlashInfer https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/3738 ### FlashInfer version requirement This integration intentionally targets the corrected API from FlashInfer #4431, where the FC1 and FC2 residual scales are FP32 tensors in local-expert order with shape `[num_local_experts]`. FlashInfer reuses its internal expert permutation to map those scales to routed rows, including global-to-local expert mapping under EP. The original #3738 ABI briefly shipped before being reverted from FlashInfer 0.6.17 by #4411. It required downstream runtimes to construct routed-row residual tensors during every forward. SGLang does not support that older ABI. The new option therefore requires both: - `flashinfer-python >= 0.6.18` - `preprocess_moe_weights_for_sm90_mixed_gemm_humming` SGLang currently pins FlashInfer 0.6.17. This PR does not change that global pin. With 0.6.17, selecting `fp8` fails immediately with an actionable error, while all existing FlashInfer paths remain compatible. The dependency, cubin, and JIT-cache pins should be upgraded together in a follow-up change. GPU validation for this PR used FlashInfer 0.6.18 built from commit `8044d94bf9acc5369857baf88d28906bb32bf264`, which contains the corrected API from FlashInfer #4431. ## Modifications ### Runtime selection and compatibility - Add `fp8` to `--flashinfer-mxfp4-moe-precision`. - Select the new path only for `flashinfer_mxfp4` on SM90. - Keep W4A16 as the default SM90 behavior. - Reject the SM90-specific `fp8` option on SM100 and SM120 to avoid confusing it with their existing MXFP8 activation paths. - Require the corrected FlashInfer 0.6.18+ API instead of accepting the older routed-row residual ABI. - Pass `use_wfp4afp8_humming=True` only when the new path is selected. The keyword is omitted completely for FlashInfer 0.6.17 compatibility. ### Weight preprocessing - Use `preprocess_moe_weights_for_sm90_mixed_gemm_humming` for both FC1 and FC2 during post-load processing. - Store the folded interleaved weight scales produced by FlashInfer. - Store `residual * 64` as one FP32 value per local expert for FC1 and FC2. - Preserve GPT-OSS gate/up layout conversion and its existing padding rules. - Fill synthetic E8M0 scale padding from an existing scale in the same expert, preventing padding from changing that expert's min/max exponent range. - Support both the GPT-OSS MXFP4 quantization path and the DeepSeek-V4 MXFP4 expert path. ### Kernel invocation Construct the five Humming quant-scale slots expected by the corrected FlashInfer API: 1. FC1 folded weight block scales 2. FC1 per-local-expert residual scale, including the fixed `2^6` compensation 3. Reserved scalar FC2 activation scale 4. FC2 folded weight block scales 5. FC2 per-local-expert residual scale, including the fixed `2^6` compensation The existing TP/EP topology is forwarded to FlashInfer so it can map global expert IDs to the corresponding local residual scale. ### Tests and benchmark - Extend the registered SM90 MXFP4 test suite with: - GPT-OSS preprocessing checks against the FlashInfer helper - five-scale kernel invocation and direct FlashInfer comparison - aligned and non-aligned hidden/intermediate dimensions - padding invariance for per-expert residual scales - EP rank with global expert IDs - DeepSeek-V4 preprocessing - fail-fast behavior on FlashInfer versions before 0.6.18 - Extend the manual SM90 benchmark to compare: - SGLang Marlin W4A16 - FlashInfer CUTLASS W4A16 - FlashInfer CUTLASS W4A8 - Update the server-argument documentation. ## Accuracy Tests The registered SM90 MXFP4 suite passed: ```bash python -m pytest \ test/registered/unit/layers/quantization/test_mxfp4_sm90_cutlass.py -v ``` ```text 18 passed, 1 skipped ``` The DeepSeek-V4 MXFP4 checkpoint was launched with: ```bash python -m sglang.launch_server \ --model-path /home/models/DeepSeek-V4-Flash \ --trust-remote-code \ --tp 4 \ --moe-runner-backend flashinfer_mxfp4 \ --flashinfer-mxfp4-moe-precision fp8 \ --enforce-disable-flashinfer-allreduce-fusion \ --host 0.0.0.0 \ --port 30000 ``` DeepSeek-V4 accuracy was evaluated using the same 200-example GSM8K setup as SGLang #24816. Both runs used the same TP=4 configuration, dataset, sampling parameters, and server options; only `--flashinfer-mxfp4-moe-precision` changed between `bf16` and `fp8`. ```bash PYTHONPATH=/sgl-workspace/sglang_dev/python \ python -m sglang.test.run_eval \ --port 30000 \ --eval-name gsm8k \ --num-examples 200 \ --api chat \ --max-tokens 1024 \ --num-threads 32 \ --temperature 0 \ --gsm8k-data-path /tmp/gsm8k-test.jsonl ``` | MoE precision | GSM8K score | Total latency | Output throughput | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | | W4A16 (`bf16`) | 0.985 | 37.301 s | 611.809 token/s | | W4A8 (`fp8`) | 0.985 | 32.952 s | 683.574 token/s | W4A8 preserved the W4A16 GSM8K score while reducing evaluation latency by 11.7% and increasing output throughput by 11.7%. The score also matches the 0.985 W4A16 result reported in SGLang #24816. ## Speed Tests and Profiling The downstream benchmark uses the GPT-OSS-like shape from SGLang #24816: hidden size 4096, intermediate size 2048, 256 experts, and top-k 6. Each FlashInfer path was fully autotuned, followed by 5 warmup iterations and 30 timed iterations. The remaining token shapes were run in parallel with one independent shape per H20 GPU; each W4A16/W4A8 pair ran on the same GPU. The benchmark can be reproduced with FlashInfer 0.6.18+: ```bash PYTHONPATH=python:/path/to/flashinfer \ FLASHINFER_DISABLE_VERSION_CHECK=1 \ python test/manual/layers/moe/bench_mxfp4_sm90_kernels.py ``` Results on NVIDIA H20-3e: | Tokens | CUTLASS W4A16 median (min) | CUTLASS W4A8 median (min) | Speedup | | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | | 4 | 0.275 ms (0.272 ms) | 0.164 ms (0.162 ms) | 1.68x | | 16 | 0.842 ms (0.840 ms) | 0.463 ms (0.460 ms) | 1.82x | | 64 | 1.894 ms (1.892 ms) | 1.037 ms (1.019 ms) | 1.83x | | 256 | 2.410 ms (2.403 ms) | 1.478 ms (1.383 ms) | 1.63x | | 1024 | 3.912 ms (3.906 ms) | 2.093 ms (1.999 ms) | 1.87x | | 2048 | 6.973 ms (6.954 ms) | 3.394 ms (3.384 ms) | 2.05x | | 4096 | 13.013 ms (12.971 ms) | 6.295 ms (6.210 ms) | 2.07x | | 8192 | 25.624 ms (25.546 ms) | 12.308 ms (12.293 ms) | 2.08x | FlashInfer CUTLASS W4A8 was faster at every measured token count, with speedups ranging from 1.63x to 2.08x. The gain reaches approximately 2.0x for token counts of 2048 and above. The GSM8K latency and throughput numbers above provide an end-to-end serving sanity check, but the kernel benchmark is the more controlled performance comparison because generated output lengths are not fixed. ## Scope and Limitations - The implementation is SM90-only. - It is opt-in and does not change the default W4A16 path. - A coordinated FlashInfer 0.6.18 dependency update is required before production enablement. ## Checklist - [x] Format the code with pre-commit. - [x] Add unit tests according to the repository test conventions. - [x] Update server-argument documentation. - [x] Run the registered tests on an SM90 GPU with FlashInfer 0.6.18. - [x] Add a DeepSeek-V4 end-to-end smoke-test result. - [ ] Upgrade the FlashInfer Python, cubin, and JIT-cache pins together in a coordinated follow-up change. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32393619327](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32393619327)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32393619734](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32393619734)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #32393619293](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32393619293)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [AMD] DSv4: fuse the qk-norm-rope pair on the MTP target-verify path
signals.text: ## Summary On the DeepSeek-V4 unified-KV path, the fused qk-norm-rope kernel is wired to decode only. MTP **target-verify** falls back to running the same work as two separate launches per layer — `sglang::fused_q_norm_rope` for q and `sglang::fused_norm_rope` for kv — which is 122 launches per verify step across the 61 target layers. This PR routes target-verify through the same fused kernel, **with the cache store left off**. The store half deliberately does not move. Decode is a 1-source consumer: the ring holds everything, so writing it before attention is required. Target-verify is **2-source** — attention reads history from the ring and takes the current chunk as `k`/`v` so the draft tokens stay causally masked against one another. Writing the current chunk into the ring ahead of attention makes those tokens indistinguishable from history, and every draft position then attends to all of them regardless of order. Fusing the store as well drops GSM8K from 0.950 to 0.027 while looking like a ~7% throughput win, because it skips exactly the work correctness depends on. Only the norm+RoPE half is sound, and that is what this PR fuses. ## Modifications - **`python/sglang/srt/models/deepseek_v4.py`** (`MQALayer._forward_prepare`) - `do_fused_store` now also admits `is_target_verify()` when the new gate is on. The kernel is token-indexed (`q`, `kv` and `positions` are all length M), so a verify batch carrying several draft tokens per request is a shape it already handles. - On that path the kernel is called with `swa_cache`/`swa_loc` left as `None`, so it performs q-norm+RoPE and kv-norm+RoPE and stores nothing. `get_unified_swa_loc` is not called at all — it exists solely to address a store this path no longer performs. - `kv` is returned instead of being set to `None`, so the caller's existing contract drives the rest unchanged: `attn_k = kv` gives attention the real current-chunk source, and `save_kv_cache = kv is not None` makes the backend write the ring after attention, exactly as the unfused path did. - `kv` is materialised with `.contiguous()` first: it is a strided slice of `qkv_a`, and the ring store requires a contiguous buffer. The unfused path pays the identical copy inside `_compute_kv_bf16`, so this is parity, not added overhead. - **`python/sglang/srt/environ.py`** — new `SGLANG_OPT_FUSED_QK_NORM_ROPE_VERIFY` (default on). Set to 0 to fall back to the unfused chain on the verify path. Decode, prefill and the non-unified paths are untouched. ### Kernel-level evidence Per target-verify forward, from graphs-off traces segmented by the 61 `DeepseekV4DecoderLayer` frames (TP8, 8k/1k, conc 16, rank 0). `fused_q_norm_rope` and `fused_norm_rope` both go to zero and one `_fused_qk_norm_rope_store_kernel` replaces them; no other kernel is added. | layer type | launches/fwd (base → patched) | GPU us/fwd excl. collective | |---|---|---| | CSA (30 layers) | 1920.0 → 1800.0 | 15779 → 15488 (−1.8%) | | HCA (31 layers) | 1526.8 → 1410.5 | 12385 → 12014 (−3.0%) | "excl. collective" is the number to read: `cross_device_reduce` blocks until the slowest rank arrives, so its duration tracks inter-rank skew rather than work this change moves. ## Accuracy Model `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro`, MI355X (gfx950), TP8. GSM8K, full 1319 questions, 5-shot, greedy. | run | accuracy | invalid | |---|---|---| | baseline (gate 0) | 0.950 | 0.000 | | patched (gate 1) | 0.949 | 0.000 | | patched (gate 1, repeat) | 0.945 | 0.000 | Note this is measured **without** `SGLANG_SIMULATE_ACC_LEN`. The throughput harness pins acceptance to the golden AL, which fabricates which draft tokens are accepted — fine for speed, but it would bypass the accept/reject path this change touches. Acceptance here is whatever the draft model earns. ```bash export SGLANG_HACK_FLASHMLA_BACKEND=unified_kv_triton export SGLANG_ENABLE_UNIFIED_RADIX_TREE=1 export SGLANG_OPT_UNIFIED_CACHE_FREE_OUT_OF_WINDOW_SLOTS=1 export AITER_BF16_FP8_MOE_BOUND=0 export SGLANG_DEFAULT_THINKING=1 SGLANG_DSV4_REASONING_EFFORT=high # flip this between 0 (baseline) and 1 (patched) export SGLANG_OPT_FUSED_QK_NORM_ROPE_VERIFY=1 python3 -m sglang.launch_server \ --model-path deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro \ --served-model-name deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro \ --host 0.0.0.0 --port 31710 --trust-remote-code \ --tensor-parallel-size 8 \ --attention-backend dsv4 \ --page-size 256 --swa-full-tokens-ratio 0.10 \ --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 \ --disable-shared-experts-fusion \ --tool-call-parser deepseekv4 --reasoning-parser deepseek-v4 \ --chunked-prefill-size 8192 --mem-fraction-static 0.85 \ --max-running-requests 32 --cuda-graph-max-bs 32 \ --speculative-algorithm EAGLE --speculative-num-steps 3 \ --speculative-eagle-topk 1 --speculative-num-draft-tokens 4 python3 benchmark/gsm8k/bench_sglang.py \ --backend srt --host http://127.0.0.1 --port 31710 \ --num-questions 1319 --num-shots 5 \ --max-new-tokens 1024 --temperature 0.0 --parallel 32 ``` ## Performance Same model and hardware. 8k input / 1k output, TP8, steady state (10 waves through a `--max-concurrency` gate). Each cell is the mean of 2 repeats run in `off, on, on, off` order per concurrency, so a monotonic drift over the block shifts both arms equally instead of being credited to the patch. Repeated all-gates-off runs on this node put the noise floor at 0.25% (1σ). | concurrency | output tok/s (base → patched) | uplift | mean TPOT ms | accept len | |---|---|---|---|---| | 4 | 332.43 → 341.07 | **+2.60%** | 11.37 → 11.06 | 2.499 → 2.498 | | 8 | 543.73 → 555.57 | **+2.18%** | 13.75 → 13.46 | 2.499 → 2.469 | | 16 | 839.00 → 857.32 | **+2.18%** | 17.98 → 17.57 | 2.499 → 2.507 | | 32 | 1167.14 → 1186.66 | **+1.67%** | 25.79 → 25.34 | 2.482 → 2.508 | Acceptance length is flat across arms, so the uplift is kernel time and not a shift in speculation behaviour. ```bash # same server launch as above, with SGLANG_OPT_FUSED_QK_NORM_ROPE_VERIFY # flipped 0/1 between arms, plus the throughput harness env: export SGLANG_SIMULATE_ACC_LEN=2.49 export SGLANG_SIMULATE_ACC_METHOD=match-expected export SGLANG_SIMULATE_ACC_TOKEN_MODE=real-draft-token # CONC in {4, 8, 16, 32}; --max-running-requests/--cuda-graph-max-bs = 2*CONC # capped at 32 on both arms (this image cannot capture a decode graph at bs 48). signals.title: fix(unified-cache): allow multiple concurrent load-back pins per node
signals.text: ## Motivation Under heavy device-eviction↔load-back cycling (small-VRAM GPUs with `--enable-hierarchical-cache`, hybrid GDN/mamba models), the scheduler crashes with: ``` AssertionError: node 2498 pinned by load-back 2563, new anchor 2498 ``` at `UnifiedTreeCore.commit_load_back` (`unified_tree_core.py`). Hit repeatedly serving `nvidia/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-NVFP4` + EAGLE + hicache ratio-12 on RTX 5090 (32GB) under a production-trace replay; 96GB GPUs never trip it (no deep evicted chains → no overlap). ## Root cause `UnifiedTreeNode.load_back_pending_id` is single-valued, but two live load-backs can legitimately pin the same node: 1. Request A load-backs anchored at a **descendant**; its Full-KV chain covers the evicted **ancestor** and pins it (`load_back_pending_id = A`). 2. Before A's ack, request B anchors **at that ancestor** to restore its **independently-evicted mamba state** (`mamba_component.build_hicache_transfers` pins `[node.id]`). 3. The single pin slot can't represent both live pins → assertion (`new anchor` == the node itself, matching the production message shape exactly). The overlap is semantically safe: both in-flight DMAs only **read** the shared host slots, and their writes target disjoint destinations (Full-KV pool vs mamba pool). Only the bookkeeping cannot represent it. ## Modifications - `load_back_pending_id: Optional[int]` → `load_back_pending_ids: set[int]`. - `commit_load_back` adds the anchor id (idempotent for a node sitting in both the Full and an aux transfer list of one anchor). - `finish_load_back` discards its anchor id along the root path; duplicate tracking updates once the last pin drains. - Reclaim guards (`_is_settled_full_host_duplicate`, `_can_reclaim_full_host_duplicate`) and the sanity check test set-emptiness; split inheritance copies the set. ## Test / repro `test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_unified_loadback_multipin.py` — a deterministic CPU repro built on the existing `UnifiedRadixCacheSuite` fixtures (FULL+MAMBA): backup → full evict → load-back anchored at the leaf (ack withheld) → load-back anchored at the pinned ancestor. - **Unpatched**: fails in 0.3s with the exact production assertion. - **Patched**: passes; pins drain to empty after both acks; `sanity_check` clean. - Full inherited FULL+MAMBA suite under the new class: 107 tests green. - Serving-level: the patched server sustains 400-span production-trace replays at hicache ratio-12 on RTX 5090 with zero assertions (previously crashed mid-run). ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Code Formatting with Pre-Commit](https://docs.sglang.ai/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-formatting-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests as outlined in the [Running Unit Tests](https://docs.sglang.ai/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#running-unit-tests). - [x] Update documentation / docstrings as needed. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #31902335393](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31902335393)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #31902335225](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31902335225)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: fix(npu): split packed MTP HiCache transfers by pool
signals.text: > [!IMPORTANT] > For standalone Ascend HiCache validation, this PR branch bundles the complete > commit history of #32500 through `#32500@9acc6b733`. Users can fork this branch > and run it directly without fetching another PR. For upstream review and > merge, #32500 should still land first; GitHub will then remove the shared > commits from this PR's diff. #34560 is already merged into `main`. End-to-end > Qwen3.6 validation also uses the checkpoint semantic fix in #35086, but that > PR is not included in this branch. Recommended merge order: #32500, #35086, > then this PR. ## Motivation After #34560, the HiCache host K/V layer dimension includes both the target model layers and the NEXTN/MTP draft layers. #32500 adds the Ascend fused `transfer_kv_dim_exchange` path for `page_first_direct`, but that path invokes the operator once with the target device pool and the full packed host buffer. On Ascend, the target and draft K/V layers are separate device pools. A single invocation therefore pairs a target-only device buffer with a `target + draft` host-layer range, so the draft K/V layers are not transferred through the matching device pool. CUDA does not have this mismatch. Its existing path packs target and draft per-layer pointers into one pointer array, and the per-layer transfer kernels map each host layer to the corresponding device pointer. The Ascend fused operator accepts one contiguous device pool per invocation, so each pool must be transferred separately. ## Minimal reproduction Apply #32500 on top of a revision that contains #34560, then launch Qwen3.6-27B on Ascend with the following relevant options: ```text --tp-size 2 --attention-backend ascend --device npu --page-size 128 --enable-hierarchical-cache --hicache-write-policy write_through --hicache-storage-backend mooncake --hicache-storage-prefetch-policy wait_complete --speculative-algorithm NEXTN --speculative-num-steps 3 --speculative-eagle-topk 1 --speculative-num-draft-tokens 4 ``` 1. Generate from a 3000-token prompt to populate HiCache. 2. For L2, generate a separate 6000-token filler to evict the original prefix from L1, then replay the original prompt. 3. For L3, wait for write-through completion, call `/flush_cache`, then replay the original prompt. 4. Request `return_cached_tokens_details` and inspect the target/draft transfer at the first `kernel_ascend` H2D or D2H operation. Without this change, the fused operation receives the full packed host layer range with only the target device pool. The draft pool is not transferred by a matching invocation. ## Changes - Skip CUDA-style packed device pointer arrays for the Ascend MTP path. - Iterate over the target pool and every draft pool on Ascend. - Slice the packed host K/V buffer to the layer range that belongs to each device pool. - Invoke `transfer_kv_dim_exchange` once per pool for both H2D and D2H. - Add focused tests for Ascend initialization and target/draft host-layer slicing. - Bundle all #32500 commits through `9acc6b733` so this fork branch is directly runnable for Ascend HiCache validation. Focused validation: - latest `upstream/main`: `2 passed` - exact branch head with `#32500@9acc6b733`: `3 passed, 17 deselected` - complete stacked focused tests with #35086: `8 passed` - pre-commit on both changed files: passed ## L2/L3 replay validation Validation stack: latest `main` with #34560, `#32500@9acc6b733`, #35086, and this fix. Model: Qwen3.6-27B BF16, TP2, Ascend NPU, NEXTN enabled, 4 prompts with 3000 input tokens and 512 output tokens. | Replay tier | Isolated cache details | Result | | --- | --- | --- | | Host L2 | `host=2944, device=0, storage=0` for 4/4 prompts | passed | | Mooncake L3 | `storage=2944, device=0, host=0` for 4/4 prompts | passed | The L2 and L3 replay output IDs were identical for all four prompts: ```text sha256=a0349ca2a8cdf023da0ef7b86370fbc25eac55ba5d8a656665a845c4a1d969d9 ``` Their speculative statistics were also identical: - weighted accept rate: `62.8169%` - weighted accept length: `2.8845` - correct/proposed drafts: `1338/2130` Cold generation and cache replay were not token-identical. The first mismatch positions were `[217, 322, 293, 58]` for both L2 and L3. Since the L2 and L3 replays match each other exactly, Mooncake L3 does not introduce an additional divergence. #35086 fixes the packed Mamba checkpoint index; the remaining cold/replay divergence is the separate cold-prefill persistence-boundary issue described in #33515. ## Accuracy validation Ran the repository's `benchmark/gsm8k/bench_sglang.py` against the same NEXTN + Mooncake service using the first 200 examples from the official GSM8K test set: ```text num_questions=200 num_shots=5 parallel=4 temperature=0 max_new_tokens=512 chat_template_kwargs={"enable_thinking": false} ``` Result on the complete stack: `194/200` correct (`97.0%` accuracy), `0%` invalid responses, no request failures, and `218.519 s` latency. The earlier incomplete-stack result was `195/200`; only prompt 182 changed correctness, from the correct answer `23` to `24`. This run includes #35086 but does not include #33515's cold-prefill alignment change. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: **Missing `run-ci` label** -- add it to run CI tests.<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: **Blocked** -- `run-ci` is required first.<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:heavy_minus_sign: **No AMD PR run found for this commit**.<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: fix(mamba): separate state and checkpoint chunk sizes
signals.text: > [!IMPORTANT] > This PR contains only the Mamba checkpoint semantic fix. It does not include > #32500 or #35013. Merge this after #32500; #34560 is already merged into > `main`. The end-to-end validation stack also included #35013 for packed MTP > HiCache transfers. ## Motivation Mamba radix caching currently uses `mamba_cache_chunk_size` for two different concepts: - the page-aligned granularity at which checkpoints can be stored in the radix cache; and - the physical chunk size used by the kernel to pack the intermediate state tensor `h`. These values are not always equal on Ascend. Qwen3.6 GDN uses 64-token kernel state chunks with `page_size=128`, so L1 checkpoints remain on a 128-token grid while `h` is packed every 64 tokens. Indexing `h` with the L1 grid restores the wrong recurrent state. The incorrect state is selected before tier transfer, so L2 and L3 can both replay the same wrong checkpoint; this is not a Mooncake transport issue. CUDA does not use this new semantic. The shared backend and non-NPU scheduler path continue to use the existing `mamba_cache_chunk_size`, preserving their current behavior. This is the minimal checkpoint-semantics part of #33515, adapted to the latest `main`. It intentionally does not include that PR's cold-prefill boundary change. ## Minimal reproduction Use Qwen3.6 GDN on Ascend with: ```text kernel state chunk = 64 L1 page/checkpoint grid = 128 extend length = 3008 checkpoint depth = 2944 ``` The scheduler uses a synthetic tracked length of 2945 to select the interior state at checkpoint 2944. The packed state index must therefore be: ```text 2944 / 64 = h[46] ``` The previous code instead used the L1 checkpoint grid and selected: ```text 2944 / 128 = h[23] ``` The NPU backend comment records this concrete L1 failure, and the regression test covers the per-request packed offset with expected `h_src=[46, 93]` for a two-request batch. ## Modifications - Add `npu_mamba_state_chunk_size` for the Ascend kernel's packed intermediate states. - Override the state chunk only in `AscendMambaAttnBackendBase`. - Use the new state chunk in scheduler tracking only when running on NPU. - Keep `mamba_cache_chunk_size` and the checkpoint grid unchanged for radix placement, branching, convolution tracking, and all non-NPU backends. - Preserve the latest `mamba_checkpoint_grid`/DCP checkpoint-depth behavior. - Add focused regression tests for the 64-token state / 128-token L1 case and for unchanged shared-backend behavior. ## L1 divergence comparison The A/B test used commits that differ only by this PR's patch. The before commit was the validation stack parent `c2f86df61`; the after commit `14f0e87f3` has the same stable patch-id as this PR head. Both runs used Qwen3.6-27B BF16, TP2, Ascend NPU, NEXTN, 4 prompts with 3000 input tokens and 512 output tokens, and reused exactly 2944 L1 device tokens for every prompt. ```text before PR after PR first mismatch [65, 88, 101, 23] [217, 322, 293, 58] weighted accept rate 60.4396% 62.8169% weighted accept length 2.8132 2.8845 ``` The cold baseline was identical in both runs: weighted accept rate `63.4988%` and weighted accept length `2.9050`. The later first mismatches and improved NEXTN statistics show that the wrong `h` index is fixed. Replay is still not token-identical to cold generation; that remaining divergence is the separate cold-prefill boundary issue intentionally left out of this PR. ## L2/L3 replay verification The end-to-end validation stack was latest `main` with #34560, `#32500@9acc6b733`, #35013, and this PR. Model and request settings matched the L1 test above. - PR-focused tests on the standalone PR head: `6 passed`. - Focused scheduler, state-index, and stacked NPU host-pool tests: `8 passed`. - Host L2: `host=2944, device=0, storage=0` for 4/4 prompts. - Mooncake L3: `storage=2944, device=0, host=0` for 4/4 prompts. - L2 and L3 replay output IDs were identical for all four prompts: `sha256=a0349ca2a8cdf023da0ef7b86370fbc25eac55ba5d8a656665a845c4a1d969d9`. - L2 and L3 speculative statistics were identical: weighted accept rate `62.8169%`, weighted accept length `2.8845`, and correct/proposed drafts `1338/2130`. L2 and L3 had the same first mismatch positions as the fixed L1 run: `[217, 322, 293, 58]`. Mooncake therefore adds no additional divergence. ## Accuracy verification Ran the repository's `benchmark/gsm8k/bench_sglang.py` against the same full NEXTN + Mooncake validation stack using the first 200 examples from the official GSM8K test set: ```text num_questions=200 num_shots=5 parallel=4 temperature=0 max_new_tokens=512 chat_template_kwargs={"enable_thinking": false} ``` Result: `194/200` correct (`97.0%` accuracy), `0%` invalid responses, no request failures, and `218.519 s` latency. The previous incomplete-stack result was `195/200`; only prompt 182 changed correctness, from the correct answer `23` to `24`. ## Speed tests and profiling This change adds no kernel launch or state copy. It only gives the Ascend state index calculation its own chunk semantic. The 200-example accuracy run took `218.519 s`; this is not a controlled performance comparison. ## Checklist - [x] Format code with pre-commit. - [x] Add focused unit tests, including unchanged non-NPU semantics. - [x] Compare L1 replay before and after the exact PR patch. - [x] Complete Qwen3.6 L2/L3 replay validation on the stated stacked setup. - [x] Complete the 200-example GSM8K accuracy rerun on the stated stacked setup. - [x] Release NPU resources after validation. - [x] Documentation is not required for this internal correctness fix. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #32013403511](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32013403511)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #32013403405](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32013403405)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [sglang-miles] Extract Anthropic conversion into standalone utils
signals.text: ## Summary Expose SGLang's Anthropic/OpenAI conversion for reuse by external frontends. ## Motivation External OpenAI-compatible frontends that must interpret Anthropic Messages exactly as this server does (e.g. [Miles PR #2358](https://github.com/radixark/miles/pull/2358)) previously had to vendor `protocol.py`/`serving.py` and maintain a derived codec, plus a sync ledger to keep the copies honest. This gives the server and external callers one conversion implementation, maintained here. ## Usage An external handler validates `AnthropicMessagesRequest`, then wraps its own OpenAI path with the shared converters: ```python from sglang.srt.entrypoints.anthropic.serving import ( convert_response, convert_to_chat_completion_request, ) chat_request = convert_to_chat_completion_request( anthropic_request, merge_inline_system=merge_inline_system, ) chat_response = await openai_backend(chat_request) anthropic_response = convert_response(chat_response) ``` The result uses the same conversion as SGLang's `/v1/messages`; endpoint validation, routing, and transport remain caller-owned. ## Design Notes - **Mental model:** An external `/v1/messages` handler parses `AnthropicMessagesRequest`; passes its deployment's `merge_inline_system` choice plus optional reasoning callbacks into `convert_to_chat_completion_request`; runs the resulting `ChatCompletionRequest` through its OpenAI-compatible backend; then converts the completed response with `convert_response` or `to_anthropic_fake_sse_events`. SGLang owns format conversion; the caller owns endpoint policy, session state, and transport. - **Runtime boundary:** `convert_to_chat_completion_request` receives request data plus explicit inline-system policy and optional reasoning hooks; `convert_response` is data-only. `AnthropicServing` invokes both while supplying hooks from `OpenAIServingChat`, preserving server routing plus live streaming. - **Utility boundary:** `utils.py` contains Anthropic error-envelope mapping plus eager fake-SSE construction from a completed OpenAI response. Raw-body parsing, feature policy, routing, and state remain caller-owned; no fake serving instance, `AnthropicRequestContext`, or `allow_*` matrix is exposed. - **Streaming boundary:** Eager fake SSE materializes one delta per block after completion; SGLang's token-by-token streaming path is unchanged. ## Verification - `PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 PYTHONPATH=python python -m pytest -p no:cacheprovider -q test/registered/unit/entrypoints/anthropic/test_utils.py test/registered/unit/entrypoints/anthropic/test_serving.py`: `84 passed, 55 subtests passed`; covers request/response goldens, existing serving behavior, error mapping, fake SSE, and import hygiene. - Miles `tests/fast/router/test_session_anthropic.py` plus `tests/fast/utils/test_utils/test_mock_sglang_server.py`: `58 passed, 1 skipped`; verifies the paired session/TITO integration. - `pre-commit run --files python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/anthropic/utils.py test/registered/unit/entrypoints/anthropic/test_utils.py`: passed. ## Review Focus - `convert_to_chat_completion_request` / `AnthropicServing`: reasoning-callback injection and preservation of server conversion behavior. - `utils.py`: error mapping, message scrubbing, and the eager fake-SSE boundary. - Cross-repo ABI with Miles #2358: `merge_inline_system`, request/response types, and completed-response streaming. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32354150517](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32354150517)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32354150309](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32354150309)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:heavy_minus_sign: **No AMD PR run found for this commit**.<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [Mac] Keep SGLang compile decorators eager with the Triton stub
signals.text: ## Problem On Apple Silicon, SGLang installs its lightweight Triton import stub because a real Triton runtime is unavailable. The stub is sufficient to define/import Triton kernels, but import-time `torch.compile` decorators still initialize TorchInductor and inspect Triton runtime types before the decorated function is ever called. As a result, importing common SRT modules fails during module initialization. This happens before model selection, so even a small dense CPU model is blocked by compile decorators in common MoE, sampling, embedding, and speculative modules. ## Reproduction before this PR Run on Apple Silicon with the PyTorch CPU engine enabled and MLX disabled: ```bash SGLANG_USE_CPU_ENGINE=1 SGLANG_USE_MLX=0 python - <<'PY' from sglang.srt.layers.moe.moe_runner.deep_gemm import ( _cast_to_e8m0_with_rounding_up, ) print(_cast_to_e8m0_with_rounding_up) PY ``` Before this change, the import enters `torch.compile`, initializes TorchInductor against the Triton stub, and fails with an error such as: ```text TypeError: unsupported operand type(s) for |: 'module' and 'type' ``` Other common call sites fail similarly while inspecting missing members such as `triton.language.core.view`. ## Solution - Mark the SGLang Triton stub explicitly. - Add an SGLang-local compile wrapper that forwards the original arguments to `torch.compile`. - When and only when the installed Triton module is the SGLang stub, force `disable=True` so the decorated callable stays eager. - Migrate the 12 import-time compile call sites that are reached by the common HTTP/model-registry import chain. The wrapper does not replace the process-wide `torch.compile` function. Real Triton platforms preserve the existing compile arguments and behavior. The 12 call sites were checked individually: restoring any one of them to raw `torch.compile` reproduces the import-time failure. ## Behavior after this PR The reproduction above imports successfully, and `torch.compile` remains the original process-global function: ```text deep_gemm import: OK global torch.compile unchanged: True ``` This PR intentionally addresses the compile/import boundary only. macOS CPU topology and optional `sgl_kernel` CPU AOT handling are separate follow-up changes. ## Validation ```bash pytest -q test/registered/unit/compilation/test_torch_compile_stub.py ``` Result: ```text 2 passed ``` Also verified: - real-Triton arguments are passed through unchanged; - the stub overrides an explicit `disable=False` only for SGLang call sites; - the global `torch.compile` function object is unchanged; - each migrated call site fails the common import when individually restored to raw `torch.compile`. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32094681555](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32094681555)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32094681381](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32094681381)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [DSA] Route the ragged prefill top-k to the v2 kernel
signals.text: > Generated by Claude. **Stacked on #35041.** GitHub cannot use that PR's branch as a base here (its head lives in the fork, and a cross-fork PR's base must be a branch of the base repo), so this targets `main` and carries #35041's commit underneath. **Review only the second commit** (`[DSA] Route the ragged prefill top-k to the v2 kernel`); the diff collapses to it once #35041 merges and this is rebased. ## Motivation The extend-shaped `RAGGED` transform is the last DSA top-k path still served by the legacy sgl-kernel kernel (`topk_transform_prefill_ragged_kernel`), even though it is the cheapest one to serve. The DeepGEMM contiguous-KV indexer emits columns that are already absolute positions in the batch's flattened KV, so unlike the paged path there is no page table to gather through -- the entire transform is a per-row add. That is exactly v2's raw-index mode (added in #35041) plus a bias. ## What this does - **`TopKProblem` gains a `bias` field (default 0)** that `emit` adds to every selected index. Every pre-existing construction site omits it, so the compiler constant-folds the add away — see the SASS check below. - **`topk_ragged_kernel`** selects inside `[row_starts[b], row_starts[b] + seq_lens[b])` and emits `position + out_offsets[b]`. One block per row, and **no cluster path**: the cluster split exists to spread one very long row across blocks, which only pays off for the few-row decode shapes; prefill has thousands of rows. - **Unaligned window starts.** The window start is an arbitrary token offset, so the read base is rounded down to a 4-float boundary and the ≤ 3 columns that pulls in are masked to `-FLT_MAX` in place. They are a preceding request's columns *of the same row* — real finite scores that would otherwise win the selection. The row belongs to this block alone and the score buffer is dead after the top-k, so the write races with nothing. It lands after the PDL wait (the indexer rounds its own KV base down to 4 as well and would otherwise overwrite the mask) and is published by the `__syncthreads()` that every `forward()` already runs before it reads any score. - Rows with `seq_len <= topk` keep a trivial path that never reads the scores, so alignment never arises there. It cannot reuse `trivial_transform`, whose `-1` padding would pick up the bias. - `dsa_topk_backend` routes the RAGGED branch to it; prefill-CP (`batch_idx_list is not None`) stays on the legacy kernel, since its `topk_indices_offset` is built from `cu_seqlens_q` rather than the KV bases. ## The existing kernels are untouched Built the JIT module before and after and diffed the SASS per function (`cuobjdump -sass`, 12 kernels / 56648 instructions): | kernel | result | |---|---| | `topk_main_kernel` × {level 0..3} × {INDICES, PAGE_TABLE} | byte-identical | | `topk_small_batch_kernel` × {INDICES, PAGE_TABLE} | byte-identical | | `topk_plan` | byte-identical | | `topk_persistent_cluster_kernel` | same instruction count (2808); `+1 IMAD.MOV.U32 / -1 NOP` | `cuobjdump -res-usage` is identical field for field on all 12 (`REG:32 STACK LOCAL:0 SHARED CONSTANT`). The new kernel itself is `REG:32 STACK:0 SHARED:20224 LOCAL:0`, no spill. To keep it that way, the ragged bias must be set through its own construction path — assigning a runtime bias in `TopKPagedParams::problem()` would put a real `IADD` in every mode's `emit`. ## Tests `test/registered/kernels/ops/attention/test_topk_v2.py`: **278 passed** (234 existing + 44 new). The new cases cover every `row_start % 4` residue against each template band (trivial / Register2 / Register4 / Streaming), mixed lengths in one launch, the selection boundaries (`seq == k`, `k+1`, 8192/8193, 16385), long context, `row_starts=None`, and an offset distinct from `row_starts`. Everything outside a window is filled with a score that beats every in-window value, so a leak shows up as a wrong selection; each case also asserts that nothing outside the masked head was written. Also checked, unchanged from the base branch: `test_dsa_indexer.py` (same pass/fail set) and `test/registered/attention/unittests/dsa/test_dsa.py` (3 pre-existing `impl='trtllm'` hardware-gate failures, per `KNOWN_FAILURES.md §B`). And the v2 output matches the legacy kernel exactly when driven through `DSATopKBackend`, across aligned/unaligned starts and both the trivial and radix paths. ## Benchmark `bench_topk.py` gains a ragged benchmark alongside the paged one (this also un-shadows `benchmark_paged`, which a duplicate function name had replaced with a body-less stub). B200, k=2048, µs: | seq_len | batch | jit_v1 | **jit_v2** | flashinfer | torch | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | 4096 | 1 | 4.10 | **4.03** | 6.37 | 34.27 | | 4096 | 128 | 7.35 | **4.34** | 7.07 | 45.34 | | 4096 | 1024 | 24.61 | **16.52** | 28.20 | 147.51 | | 65536 | 1 | 37.52 | 20.35 | **13.15** | 71.30 | | 65536 | 128 | 39.40 | **21.52** | 37.48 | 157.22 | | 65536 | 1024 | 175.84 | **103.70** | 195.88 | 923.18 | 1.3–1.8× over the legacy kernel, except the single-row 64K shape where the cluster split flashinfer/the paged path use still wins — not a prefill shape (prefill's row count is the extend-token count). <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:no_entry_sign: [Run #32349896322](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32349896322)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #32364175881](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32364175881)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #32349896357](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32349896357)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [Kernel] 2shot_lamport custom all-reduce for the 1–8 MB band
signals.text: ## Motivation Inspired by *Every Microsecond Matters: Achieving Near Speed-of-Light Latency in GPU Collectives* ([arXiv:2607.16100](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.16100)), which argues that the memory barriers conventional all-reduce kernels use to signal data readiness are a first-order cost at small message sizes, and replaces them with synchronization carried by the data itself. This PR brings the "Two-shot (Sentinel)" algorithm to `CustomAllReduceV2`. ## Main Changes **`AllReducePullImpl::forward_2shot_lamport`** (`custom_all_reduce.cuh`) — a 2-shot all-reduce whose all-gather is a lamport handshake instead of a barrier: **A dedicated gather plane**, double buffered, added to the symmetric slab and carried on `CommunicatorObj` as `gather_workspaces` / `gather_bytes`. **Dispatch config** — `Heuristic` gains a `lamport` `Range`, defaulting to disabled. `_pick_algo` tries `lamport` **before** `1shot_push`. Resulting dispatch at world 4: ``` graph before after 16B .. 2.25MB 1shot_push 16B .. 1.125MB 1shot_push 2.25MB .. 16MB 2shot_pull 1.125MB .. 8MB 2shot_lamport <- new 8MB .. 16MB 2shot_pull eager before after 16B .. 3MB 1shot_push 16B .. 2MB 1shot_push 3MB .. 16MB 2shot_pull 2MB .. 8MB 2shot_lamport <- new 8MB .. 16MB 2shot_pull ``` ## Accuracy Tests ``` $ python test/registered/kernels/ops/communication/test_custom_all_reduce.py --num-gpu 2,4 242 passed (world 2) 242 passed (world 4) ``` ## Benchmark Run with `bench_custom_all_reduce.py` on GB200, both `jit-graph` and `jit-eager` are affected: ``` python test/registered/kernels/benchmark/communication/bench_custom_all_reduce.py --num-gpu 4 ``` | message | graph before | graph after | **Δ** | eager signals.title: fix(kernel) Fix Helion small-token prefill bug
signals.text: ## Motivation Fix shape handling in the wrapper for Helion KDA for short prefill requests. Also clearly reject non power of 2 head dim in decode. ## Modifications The Helion KDA backend had three issues. - For short prefill, the prefill Q/K/V may contain only the active tokens while gate and beta remain padded to a CUDA-graph bucket. Deriving the token count from the padded gate tensor caused invalid reshapes for short prompts. - Edge case: If the first prefill request had `T=1`, PyTorch could specialize size-one dimensions in the generated Helion trace. This issue only occurs if the first prefill is `T = 1`, `T > 1` is fine. - Decode used padded `hl.arange` lanes without masks when the key or value dimension was not a power of two. We made the following changes. - Validate that gate and beta cover every Q token, then trim their padded rows at the public Helion prefill boundary. This keeps direct callers consistent with the Triton `chunk_kda` contract. - Route only `T=1` prefill through Triton, preventing a size-one trace from poisoning later Helion shapes. The normal `T>1` Helion path is unchanged. - Reject non power of two head dim for decode (both kimi linear and kimi k3 have head dim = 128 so they're fine). ## Accuracy Tests A standalone sweep compared the public Helion and Triton prefill wrappers, including output, intermediate chunk states, and the mutated final state. Gate and beta padding was filled with large values so the comparison could not pass if either backend consumed padded rows. This not only confirms that Helion works now on short seqs, but that the accuracy is preserved. - input lengths `1, 3, 7, 15, 17, 31, 51, 63, 65, 127, 255, 513, 1023, 2047, 2049, 3001, 8191, 16385`; - fixed and two-sequence packed-varlen layouts; - `H=32`, `H=16`, and `H=12`; - FP32 and BF16 state. All **216/216 cases passed** with `atol=0.02, rtol=0.02`. | Compared value | Maximum absolute difference | |---|---:| | Output | 9.77e-4 | | Intermediate state | 7.81e-3 | | Final state | 4.02e-3 | ## Speed Tests and Profiling The change does not affect performance. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. signals.title: Fix graceful shutdown: drain survives group-delivered stop signals
signals.text: ## Motivation The tokenizer manager's graceful-drain path (`gracefully_exit` → `/health` 503 → wait for in-flight requests → `ShutdownReq` → kill) is bypassed when stop signals reach the **whole process group** rather than only the main process: - Scheduler and detokenizer subprocesses receive SIGINT and can exit through the default handler during a forward pass, severing in-flight streaming responses before the drain completes. - In the main process, SIGINT reaches uvicorn's default handler and begins shutting down the HTTP server instead of entering SGLang's drain path. Group delivery occurs with terminal Ctrl-C and with entrypoints or supervisors that forward signals to a process group, such as `tini -g`, `kill -- -PID` wrappers, or `killpg`-based supervisors. In our Modal canaries, SIGINT and SIGTERM both reached the SGLang process group within the same second, with their order varying between stops. Plain Kubernetes and `docker stop` normally send SIGTERM to the main process only. Those setups do not expose workers to group delivery, but this change still gives SIGINT the same drain behavior as SIGTERM and adds explicit escalation and timeout semantics. This was traced in production after a healthy container received a stop signal and returned 502s for its in-flight requests, including a 14-minute stream. With this patch, a canary on the same platform completed a rolling redeploy: workers survived the observed SIGINT/SIGTERM delivery, the drain armed, and the in-flight stream completed before shutdown with zero requests remaining. ## Modifications 1. **Worker subprocesses ignore SIGINT and SIGTERM.** `ignore_external_stop_signals()` is installed at worker process startup in `run_scheduler_process`, `run_detokenizer_process`, `run_multi_detokenizer_router_process`, and `run_data_parallel_controller_process`, and as the initializer for the multimodal preprocessing `ProcessPoolExecutor`. Worker lifecycle remains owned by the shutdown coordinator: drain, then `ShutdownReq`, then cleanup through `kill_process_tree`. 2. **SIGINT uses the graceful-drain handler.** The tokenizer manager handles SIGINT through the same path as SIGTERM, so Ctrl-C or group-delivered SIGINT drains instead of invoking uvicorn's default shutdown behavior. 3. **Distinct signals join the active drain; repetition escalates.** During a drain, the first occurrence of another signal kind is treated as part of the same stop event. Repeating an already-seen signal kind is treated as an explicit escalation and force-exits, abandoning in-flight requests. Deduplication is identity-based rather than time-window-based so closely delivered distinct signals are not mistaken for escalation. 4. **`SGLANG_GRACEFUL_SHUTDOWN_TIMEOUT` bounds the drain when configured.** The new float-valued environment variable is registered in `sglang/srt/environ.py`. Unset or `<= 0` preserves the existing unbounded wait, leaving the orchestrator's SIGKILL as the backstop. An invalid value logs a warning and falls back to no timeout. SIGQUIT crash cleanup and SIGKILL behavior are unchanged. ## Tests `test/registered/core/test_graceful_drain_signals.py` is registered in CPU CI (`base-a-test-cpu`) and covers: - workers ignoring group-delivered stop signals through a real process group (`killpg` with SIGTERM and SIGINT); - the first stop signal arming the drain, a distinct signal joining it, and a repeated signal forcing exit; - parsing valid `SGLANG_GRACEFUL_SHUTDOWN_TIMEOUT` values and tolerating invalid values. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32086531607](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32086531607)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32086531508](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32086531508)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [Scheduler] Release all request-owned KV on no-insert cleanup
signals.text: ## Why `RadixCache.cache_finished_req(..., is_insert=False)` discards a request without inserting its KV into the radix cache. The old implementation derived the release range from committed token IDs rather than from `kv_len_to_handle`. Under overlap scheduling, a forward pass can commit a KV slot before its sampled output token is accepted, leaving the token-ID list one element shorter and leaking the final request-owned slot. ## Ownership contract - `[0, cache_protected_len)` is cache-owned and must be preserved. - `[cache_protected_len, kv_len_to_handle)` is request-owned committed KV and must be released on no-insert cleanup. - Overallocated KV after `kv_len_to_handle` is released by `release_kv_cache`. ## Change - Release the request-owned committed range directly from the request-to-token mapping with the existing `free_segment` allocator primitive. - Release the request's radix-node lock as before. - Leave the normal cache-insertion path unchanged. - Extend the existing matched-prefix failure test to cover a committed KV slot with no corresponding output token. ## Validation - Focused registered unit test: 6 passed on one H200 using `lmsysorg/sglang:nightly-dev-cu13-20260817-d91c3682`. - Repository pre-commit checks passed for both changed files, including the registered-test validator. - `git diff --check` passed. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32076641901](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32076641901)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32076641658](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32076641658)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [Fix] Transformers-fallback (GPT-NeoX) + KV pool config (DeepSeek-VL2)
signals.text: ## Summary Three small fixes surfaced by consecutive downstream accuracy runs. All three are one-liners (plus comments); the first two live in the Transformers-fallback layer, the third in `ModelConfig`. ### 1. `hf_to_sglang_mapper` — map `gpt_neox.` and `embed_out.` `GPTNeoXForCausalLM` has no native SGLang impl → falls back to `TransformersForCausalLM`. The fallback calls `AutoModel.from_config(config)`, which returns the bare `GPTNeoXModel` backbone (`embed_in`, `layers`, `final_layer_norm`) as `self.model`; `self.lm_head` is materialized separately by `CausalMixin`. Pythia / NeoX checkpoints were saved from `GPTNeoXForCausalLM.state_dict()`, so keys carry a `gpt_neox.` wrapper prefix for the backbone and a top-level `embed_out.` for the LM head. The base mapper has no rule for either, so the catch-all `""` → `"model."` fires and produces `model.gpt_neox.embed_in.weight` — which the loader can't find (`ValueError: No module or parameter named 'model.gpt_neox' ...`). **Fix:** add two prefix rules alongside the existing `"transformer.": "model."` (GPT-2 analogue): - `"gpt_neox.": "model."` — strip the wrapper prefix so backbone keys land under `self.model.*`. - `"embed_out.": "lm_head."` — route the LM head to SGLang's `self.lm_head` slot. ### 2. `skip_substrs` — skip GPT-NeoX-style `.attention.bias` causal-mask buffer Older GPT-NeoX checkpoints include a persistent causal-mask buffer named `gpt_neox.layers.N.attention.bias`. Newer transformers versions register the same buffer with `persistent=False`, so it is absent from the constructed model's tree. `self.skip_substrs` already skips GPT-2-style `.attn.bias` / `.attn.masked_bias` (attention module named `attn`), but not GPT-NeoX-style `.attention.bias` (attention module named `attention`). Result: `ValueError: No module or parameter named 'model.layers.0.attention.bias' ...`. **Fix:** add `.attention.bias` to the skip list. The already-present `.masked_bias` catches the fill-value counterpart regardless of attention module name. ### 3. `ModelConfig.v_head_dim` — treat `0` as unset (fixes DeepSeek-VL2 non-MLA V-cache) `deepseek-ai/deepseek-vl2-tiny`'s `language_config` sets `use_mla=False` **and** `v_head_dim=0` — the `0` is an MLA-disabled sentinel from the checkpoint's DeepseekV2-flavored config, not a real head dimension. `ModelConfig.__init__` currently substitutes `head_dim` for `v_head_dim` only when the attribute is `None`, so a `getattr` that returns `0` slips through into `self.v_head_dim`. `pool_configurator.py` then reads `model_config.v_head_dim` directly in the non-MLA branch, and per-slot V-buffers get allocated with last dim = 0. The first extend prefill fails: ``` File ".../mem_cache/memory_pool.py", line 192, in _set_kv_buffer_impl v_cache[indices] = v RuntimeError: shape mismatch: value tensor of shape [432, 10, 128] cannot be broadcast to indexing result of shape [432, 10, 0] ``` DeepSeek-VL2 explicitly selects the standard (non-MLA) `DeepseekForCausalLM` language model when `use_mla=False` (`sglang/srt/models/deepseek_vl2.py`), which produces real V with the usual `num_kv_heads * head_dim` layout — the attention layer is correct; the pool is what's mis-sized. **Fix:** swap the guard to `if not self.v_head_dim:` so both `None` and `0` fall back to `self.head_dim`. MLA architectures are unaffected — their architecture-specific `elif` branches later in the same block overwrite `self.v_head_dim` with the real value from the text config. ## Test plan - [x] `pre-commit run --files <changed>` — passes locally for all three files. - [x] `EleutherAI/pythia-12b` (TP=2, triton) — reproduces the missing-mapper failure on `main`; loads through with fix 1. - [x] `EleutherAI/gpt-neox-20b` (TP=2, triton) — with fix 1 applied, reproduces the missing-skip failure on `main`; loads through with fix 2, warmup succeeds, first `POST /generate` returns 200. - [x] `deepseek-ai/deepseek-vl2-tiny` (TP=1, triton, `--disable-radix-cache`, mem-fraction 0.55) — reproduces the `_set_kv_buffer_impl` shape-mismatch on `main`; with fix 3, KV cache allocates `K size = V size = 3.38 GB` (previously `V size = 0.00 GB`), text `POST /generate` returns 200 with valid tokens. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:no_entry_sign: [Run #32404965067](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32404965067)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32404964663](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32404964663)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #32404964731](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32404964731)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->
