signals.title: [Model Loader] Harden startup weight-load overlap and expand model coverage
signals.text: ## Summary This is the hardening and coverage follow-up to #32017. It keeps startup weight-load overlap opt-in, makes admission/fallback deterministic, and extends the path to hybrid, MoE/EP, and one narrowly validated FP8 model profile. - Replace implicit support checks with a structured admission plan and deterministic rejection report. - Add `--startup-weight-load-mode=auto`: admitted configurations use overlap; rejected configurations preserve serial startup. - Check resolved checkpoint capabilities before capture-safe mutation, so `auto` can fall back for PT or secondary weights without allocating the model twice. - Freeze graph-visible parameter, buffer, and explicitly registered derived-tensor storage across the real-weight commit, then reject stale capture sentinels or storage rebinding. - After graph capture, cooperatively cancel and drain checkpoint prefetch before the real commit. If the bounded drain times out, continue with the conservative commit-reader policy while the cancelled daemon worker exits, without waiting a second time. - Preserve serial post-load semantics for optional parameters that intentionally skip dummy-weight validation. - Report complete overlap phase timings and assign `ModelRunner.weight_load_time` only after the real commit. - Add exact profiles for Qwen hybrid/MoE models and GLM-5.2 FP8. The default remains `serial`. Explicit `overlap` fails during preflight with actionable reasons when unsupported; `auto` logs the same reasons and follows the serial path. ## Supported profiles | Profile | Admitted configuration | | --- | --- | | Native dense | Native `LlamaForCausalLM`, `Qwen2ForCausalLM`, or `Qwen3ForCausalLM`; FP16/BF16; TP1/TP2 | | Qwen3.5-family hybrid VLM | Native `Qwen3_5ForConditionalGeneration` (including Qwen3.6 dense checkpoints); BF16; TP2/TP4; Triton linear attention; breakable or disabled prefill CUDA graphs | | Qwen3.5 MoE hybrid VLM | Native `Qwen3_5MoeForConditionalGeneration`; BF16; TP2+EP2; Triton MoE and linear attention; standard EP path; breakable or disabled prefill CUDA graphs | | Qwen3 MoE EP | Native `Qwen3MoeForCausalLM`; BF16; TP2+EP2; Triton MoE runner; standard EP path (`moe_a2a_backend=none`) | | GLM-5.2 FP8 | Native `GlmMoeDsaForCausalLM` with the GLM-5.2 fingerprint; serialized dynamic E4M3 FP8 with 128x128 blocks; BF16 execution/KV cache; Hopper SM90; TP8/TP16 with EP1; DSA with FA3 prefill/decode; Triton FP8 GEMM and MoE; prefill graphs disabled; shared-expert fusion off | The GLM profile is keyed to the native GLM-5.2 IndexShare fingerprint (default `cli_factor`, no custom `index_topk_pattern`, `index_topk_freq=4`, and `index_skip_topk_offset=3`), not merely the architecture name. Other quantized/repacked-weight paths, speculative decoding, LoRA/offload, and parallel/backend combinations outside the rows above remain rejected. `auto` sends them through serial startup. ## Design details `StartupWeightLoadAdmission` separates side-effect-free config preflight from native model-class resolution. Cheap rules run first; implementation resolution/import only happens for a viable candidate. Checkpoint format and secondary weights are checked after source resolution but before sentinel initialization, which gives `auto` a final safe serial-fallback boundary. `ModelStorageManifest` records tensor identity, pointer, shape, stride, dtype, device, and storage offset after dummy post-load preparation. Finalization proves that real loading refreshed the same graph-visible storage. Models can enumerate derived tensors through a per-module hook without a recursive attribute scan; the GLM/DeepSeek path uses this for MLA-derived weights and scales. Checkpoint staging remains best-effort. After graph capture, the manager cooperatively stops and joins the worker before starting normal multithreaded commit. If the bounded stop times out, the handle remains active and the loader preserves its conservative concurrency policy. Worker failure, intentional cancellation, and full-file completion remain distinguishable, and no filesystem/path-specific policy is used. Real-weight commit failures after capture-safe preparation are terminal startup failures. `auto` intentionally does not retry serial loading after model mutation or graph capture. ## H100 validation ### Controlled Qwen3.6 startup benchmark `Qwen/Qwen3.6-27B@6a9e13bd6fc8f0983b9b99948120bc37f49c13e9`, BF16, TP2, FA3, Triton GDN/linear attention, prefill CUDA graph disabled, decode FullCG, local NVMe. Three interleaved trials per mode were run after separate JIT warmup. Before every trial, checkpoint pages were evicted with `POSIX_FADV_DONTNEED` and verified with `mincore` to have zero resident bytes. | Metric (median) | Serial | Overlap | Change | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | | Process ready | 50.193 s | 46.122 s | **-8.11% / 1.088x** | | Scheduler startup | 30.03 s | 26.30 s | -12.4% | | `load_weight` | 11.66 s | 7.50 s | -35.7% | Every overlap trial exercised the active handoff rather than an already-complete prefetch: capture ended with only 8-9 of 15 shards fully staged, the worker stopped in about 3.8 s, and multithreaded commit then resumed. There were no fallback, timeout, manifest, or sentinel errors. The server requested decode graph BS 256, but the hybrid Mamba-state capacity resolved the maximum running/captured BS to 39. The actual capture shapes were `[1, 2, 4, 8, 12, 16, 24, 32, 39]`; this resolved limit was identical in both modes. Across all six startups, two fixed prompts produced bit-identical text, token IDs, input/output logprobs, and top-logprobs. The timing is an end-to-end `serial` versus `overlap` mode comparison; coordinated checkpoint staging and its handoff are part of the overlap path, not a claim about graph capture in isolation. ### Coverage and correctness probes - `zai-org/GLM-5.2-FP8@ba978f7d347eaf65d22f1a86833408afdb953541`, BF16, TP16 on H100, DSA+FA3, Triton FP8/MoE, BF16 KV: `serial`, `overlap`, and `auto` passed storage validation and produced matching token IDs/logprobs. - `Qwen/Qwen3.5-35B-A3B`, BF16, TP2+EP2, FA3, Triton MoE/linear attention: text, image, batched, and prefix-branching requests matched across `serial`, `overlap`, and `auto`. - `Qwen/Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct-2507`, BF16, TP2+EP2, FA3, Triton MoE: multi-route batched and prefix-branching requests matched exactly across startup modes. These additional probes establish model/topology correctness coverage; the controlled Qwen3.6 experiment above is the performance result. ## Tests - Final focused startup/prefetch suite on the GPU development image: `84 passed, 98 subtests passed`. - Unit coverage includes deterministic admission/rejection, `auto` fallback boundaries, timing ownership, storage/sentinel validation, derived-tensor refresh, optional single/both-scale post-load behavior, prefetch EOF/cancel/crash races, bounded drain/timeout, and loader dispatch after handoff. - The registered one-GPU parity test compares both `overlap` and `auto` with default serial startup. - `black --check`, `isort --check-only`, `ruff check --select F401,F821,UP037`, `codespell`, `py_compile`, and `git diff --check` pass on the changed files. ## Follow-up This PR intentionally leaves `serial` as the default. Follow-up work can add separately validated DeepSeek V4 Flash and Kimi Linear/K3 profiles; define a two-phase, capture-stable contract for quantization methods that repack or replace weight storage; broaden backend/topology and storage evidence; isolate graph overlap with a serial-plus-coordinated-prefetch benchmark arm; and then consider making automatic overlap selection the default. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32357825842](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32357825842)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32357825733](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32357825733)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32357825862](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32357825862)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [Bug][Spec] fix startup crash and reduce CUDA graph memory usage for speculative adaptive
signals.text: ## Motivation Three separate problems show up when `--speculative-adaptive` is enabled: 1. **Startup crash.** `ModelRunner.max_decode_logits_rows()` sizes the shared logits buffer from the *static* `decode_num_tokens_per_req()`, but adaptive speculative decoding replays runners built for larger draft-token widths. The buffer is too small and the server fails to start. (mentioned in #30549) 2. **IMA on the first replay.** `DecodeCudaGraphRunner.capture_one_shape` looked up `on_after_cuda_graph_warmup` on `self.model_runner.attn_backend` instead of on the backend this capture actually ran against (`attn_backend` from `capture_prepare`). For the runner the `ModelRunner` owns these are the same object, but adaptive speculative decoding builds extra runners bound to their own freshly created backend while `model_runner.attn_backend` still points at the active one. Hooking the wrong backend leaves this capture's warmup-upgraded metadata (raw→full, FlashMLA scheduler meta) frozen into the graph, which produces an illegal memory access on the first replay. 3. **Redundant CUDA graph memory.** Each capture pass opened `graph_capture()` without a stream, so every pass captured on a fresh stream. The caching allocator partitions the graph pool's segments **by stream**, so each pass re-reserved the pool's MoE / DeepEP scratch instead of reusing what an earlier pass left inactive. With adaptive speculative decoding that is one pass per candidate step × three runners — tens of GB of segments that all read back `inactive`. ## Modifications 1. `max_decode_logits_rows()` now derives `num_tokens_per_req` from `max_speculative_num_draft_tokens`, so the shared logits buffer is sized for the widest adaptive graph. (Same fix as #30554.) 2. `decode_cuda_graph_runner.py:1226-1237` — resolve `post_warmup_hook` from the capture-local `attn_backend` rather than `model_runner.attn_backend`, with a comment recording why. 3. Added `get_or_create_global_graph_capture_stream()` in `runner_utils/pool.py` (a named stream lease in the `Resources` tier, alongside the existing process-wide graph memory pool) and used it as the `graph_capture(stream=...)` argument in both `DecodeCudaGraphRunner.capture` and `PrefillCudaGraphRunner.capture`. All capture passes therefore share one stream and reserve that scratch exactly once. Captures are strictly serial (`Scheduler.init_all_cuda_graphs` runs target and draft workers in turn; the adaptive controller builds one runtime state at a time), so a single shared stream is safe. Also added a CPU unit test `test/registered/unit/model_executor/test_graph_capture_resources.py` covering both the pool and the new capture-stream lease. ## Accuracy Tests Server launched following the cookbook: ```bash sglang serve \ --trust-remote-code \ --model-path deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash \ --tp 4 \ --moe-runner-backend flashinfer_mxfp4 \ --speculative-algorithm EAGLE \ --speculative-num-steps 3 \ --speculative-eagle-topk 1 \ --speculative-num-draft-tokens 4 \ --speculative-adaptive \ --disable-flashinfer-autotune \ --swa-full-tokens-ratio 0.1 \ --host 0.0.0.0 \ --port 30000 ``` Evaluated on the three datasets shown in the cookbook: | | GPQA Diamond | AIME25 | GSM8k | | -------- | ------------ | ------ | ----- | | cookbook | 88.1 | 95 | 96.13 | | before | 88.13 | 98.33 | 96.89 | | after | 88.04 | 97.29 | 96.97 | ## Speed Tests and Profiling No throughput change is expected; the win is memory. With the launch command above and the default adaptive speculative decoding parameters, CUDA graph memory drops from **14.4 GB → 10.13 GB**. With my own serving config and adaptive speculative decoding parameters, it drops from **44.3 GB → 16 GB**, which frees the corresponding capacity for the KV cache. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. signals.title: [AMD] Perf Kimi-K3 low concurrency optimizations
signals.text: ## Summary - Vendor selected Kimi-K3 gfx950 FlyDSL kernels in SGLang with a fail-closed source selector. - Add MLA output-gate, KDA group64/B2, 12-head AITER MLA decode-side padding, and optional latent-tail integrations. - Use one cooperative preactivated MoE producer for exact M2/M4 while larger batches retain the existing fallback. - Add the Kimi-K3 M16384 GEMM tuning profile. - Use the AITER revision already pinned by SGLang; no AITER update is required. ## Runtime configuration Base Kimi-K3 AITER configuration: ```bash export SGLANG_USE_AITER=1 export SGLANG_AITER_K3_OPT=1 export AITER_FLYDSL_FORCE=1 export AITER_SITUV2_A8W4=1 export AITER_SITUV2_A4W4=0 export SGLANG_K3_FLYDSL_SOURCE=sglang ``` Enable the PR features: ```bash # MLA output-gate fusion export SGLANG_K3_AITER_MLA_GATE=1 # KDA input projection; B2_FUSIONS adds its exact-M2 specialization export SGLANG_K3_AITER_KDA_GROUP64=1 export SGLANG_K3_AITER_B2_FUSIONS=1 # Unified exact-M2/M4 cooperative MoE preroute export SGLANG_K3_AITER_MOE_PREROUTE_FP8=1 export SGLANG_K3_PREROUTE_PREACTIVATED_SHARED=1 # M=16384 GEMM tuning rows export SGLANG_K3_AITER_M16384_PROFILE=1 ``` The latent-tail profile is independent and remains off by default because it reduces token capacity. Enable it only when explicitly evaluating that trade-off: ```bash export SGLANG_K3_AITER_LATENT_TAIL_FP8=1 ``` The 12-head padding path has no feature flag. It is selected automatically for the covered Kimi-K3 shape when using AITER MLA decode, for example: ```bash sglang serve \ --model-path /path/to/Kimi-K3 \ --tp-size 8 \ --attention-backend aiter \ --decode-attention-backend aiter ``` All integrations are shape/architecture guarded and fail closed to the existing implementation when the runtime contract is not covered. ## Performance - Unified M2 cooperative preroute: `+1.08%` throughput, `-1.11%` TPOT over the prior M2 design. - Unified M4 cooperative preroute: `+3.08%` throughput, `-3.33%` TPOT over the matched M4 baseline. - M16384 profile: approximately `+0.7%` throughput at C8/C16/C32 and `-2.34%` C32 TTFT. ## Accuracy - GSM8K 1319: `0.953` - Invalid responses: `0.001` ## Test plan - [x] Selected FlyDSL tests against pinned AITER `d9e5ef7`: 35 passed - [x] C2 8192/256 smoke: 8/8 requests succeeded - [x] C4 8192/256 smoke: 8/8 requests succeeded - [x] GSM8K 50: 1.000 - [x] GSM8K 1319: 0.953 - [x] Forbidden listed-PR path audit and `git diff --check` The current container installs a newer FlyDSL than the old AITER pin expects for full-model MoE startup. The vendored focused kernels were tested directly against the exact pin; full-model smoke used the current compatible AITER checkout. Made with [Cursor](https://cursor.com) <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:no_entry_sign: [Run #32324067708](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32324067708)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32324067621](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32324067621)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32324067909](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32324067909)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.text: ## Motivation Roadmap item under #34899 — bit-exact correctness coverage for the unified radix cache, speculative-decoding row (DSpark / DFlash). `TestUnifiedHybridMTPBitExact` in `test_unified_radix_cache_kl_hybrid_bitexact.py` was added to cover the spec side of the sconv/mamba checkpoint save. It cannot reach it: `_is_mamba_track_enabled()` is a method of `PrefillCudaGraphRunner`, and EAGLE targets disable the prefill CUDA graph outright (`cuda_graph_setup.py`, #28386), so the runner is never constructed. Measured — reverting #34043 leaves that class green: ``` TestUnifiedHybridMTPBitExact, #34043 reverted → 2 passed, avg_kl_div=0.0 log: "Disable prefill CUDA graph for EAGLE target on tc_piecewise (#28386)" ``` DSPARK and DFlash are not `is_eagle()`, keep the prefill graph, and are the algorithms #34043 actually fixed (that PR measured a DFlash SWEBench subset going 55% → 35% from zeroed sconv state). ## Modifications `TestInklingSmallNvfp4Deterministic` now runs with DSPARK driving decode, and is renamed `TestInklingSmallNvfp4DsparkDeterministic`. The helpers, the 1e-9 floor, the `extra_buffer` / SWA / mamba-ratio / `KL_MAX_NEW_TOKENS` setup and the dedicated server are all unchanged. Three knobs move: `--mem-fraction-static` 0.85 → 0.80 for this class only (see below), the file's `est_time` 1700 → 2000 for the draft load and graph capture, and `min_cache_hit_ratio` 0.99 → 0.90 on the decode case (see *Why the hit-ratio bar moves*). This replaces rather than adds: the DSPARK config exercises the same NVFP4 weights and the same `flashinfer_trtllm` fp4 GEMM/MoE path, so the FP4-regression coverage the class was written for is retained, and the non-spec cache-restore logic is covered on the shrunken checkpoint in `test_unified_radix_cache_kl_hybrid_bitexact.py`. A second no-spec arm here would cost another server launch on a `4-gpu-b200` slot for coverage that is not unique. The trade that buys: a reading here is no longer self-attributing. Inkling-Small is a 256-expert MoE where dropping `--enable-deterministic-inference` alone reads 5.0e-02 — the same order as the bug signal below — so a red case needs a manual re-run without the speculative flags to separate a state-reuse bug from batch variance. That is written into the class docstring. ## Accuracy Tests Revert-then-red against #34043. First measured on the **bf16** `Inkling-Small` checkpoint at tp=4 on GB300 (same server args plus `--speculative-algorithm DSPARK`, minus the fp4 flags): | | fix in place | #34043 reverted | |---|---|---| | `..._logprobs_match` | 0.0 | 0.0 | | **`..._prefill_cache_hit`** | 0.0 | **8.05e-02** | | `..._decode_cache_hit` | 0.0 | 0.0 | | no-spec arm (all three) | 0.0 | 0.0 | Eight orders of magnitude above the floor, and the failure lands where the mechanism predicts — the corruption reaches a request that *restores* a prefix, so the flush-both comparison and the decode-side reuse stay clean. The no-spec arm staying green under the same revert is what identified the reading as speculative-state-specific. Sanity of that run: `speculative_algorithm='DSPARK'`, accept len 1.7–3.5, `cuda graph: True`, and `cuda_graph_config.prefill.backend` resolves to `full`, so the class reaches the line #34043 changed. Probe sensitivity with `--enable-deterministic-inference` dropped: 5.0e-02 / 4.3e-02 / 5.9e-03. Since re-measured on this file's own config — NVFP4 `Inkling-Small` at tp=4 on 4x GB300 (SM100, same `modelopt_fp4` / `flashinfer_trtllm` path the class already used; there is precedent for that pairing in `test/registered/gb300/test_glm52_nvfp4.py`): | | fix in place | #34043 reverted | |---|---|---| | `..._logprobs_match` | 0.0 | 0.0 | | **`..._prefill_cache_hit`** | 0.0 | **1.10e-01** | | **`..._decode_cache_hit`** | 0.0 | **`Too few decode cache hits: 31/32`** | ``` fix in place : 3 passed (650.79s) #34043 revert: 2 failed, 1 passed ``` So both open questions are closed: the bf16 DSPARK draft does pair with the `modelopt_fp4` target, and the exact-0 baseline holds on NVFP4. The signal is stronger here than on bf16 — the revert also drops one prompt out of the decode-cache reuse. Note that at the 0.90 bar this PR ships, that second symptom no longer trips the assertion; the 1.10e-01 on `prefill_cache_hit` is what detects the revert. Whole file on 4x GB300: 5 passed in 1093 s. **`--mem-fraction-static` is 0.80 for this class, not the 0.85 the others use.** The first CI run OOMed mid-test on B200: the draft weights and the speculative CUDA graphs (`974.89 MiB allocated in private pools`) left `avail mem=0.40 GB` at 0.85 on a 178 GB card. The GB300 verification could not have caught this — 284 GB per GPU is 60% more headroom. At 0.80 the KV pool still reports ~6.2M tokens against the ~130k this file uses, so the slack costs nothing. ## Why the hit-ratio bar moves The class inherited `min_cache_hit_ratio=0.99` from the non-speculative version, where every prompt reuses its decode region unconditionally. Under DSPARK it fails on B200 for roughly one prompt in 32 (`Too few decode cache hits: 31/32`), reproducibly, and passes 32/32 on GB300. That is not a test artifact. The last verify step commits a whole accepted chunk, so a request overshoots `max_new_tokens` by up to `chain_len - 1` — measured 0–7 for DSPARK `block_size=7`. Those tokens are in the KV pool and in the radix insert but truncated from the `output_ids` the client receives, so a follow-up turn diverges from the cached sequence at `prompt + returned`. With `extra_buffer`, the insert carries exactly one mamba checkpoint, at `floor(committed / interval) * interval`. When that lands past the divergence point the matched prefix has no checkpoint at all and the whole decode region is unreusable: ``` prompt=3964 committed=1029 insert_len=4992 reachable=4988 -> miss, 10/10 reps Decode cache miss for prompt 1 | cached=3840 prompt_len=3964 ``` `3840 == floor(3964 / 128) * 128` — the second turn matched a page-aligned prefix of the prompt and none of the 1024 generated tokens. The two misses seen in earlier CI runs on this PR fit the same arithmetic (2302 → 3328 > 3326; 3071 → 4096 > 4095). Without speculation `committed == returned`, the gap is empty, and 260 sampled requests showed no deficit. So it is a reuse-efficiency defect in the product, not a correctness one — KL over the prompts that do hit reads exactly 0 in every run measured, including the ones that miss. Loosening the bar keeps the exactness check running; the bar goes back to 0.99 when the insert stops storing tokens the client never received. Filed separately rather than fixed here, so this PR stays test-only. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Test-only. On 4x GB300 the class runs 650.79 s and the whole file 1093 s; spec roughly doubles this class against the no-spec arm it replaces (360 s → 685 s on the bf16 checkpoint at the same tp). `est_time` 2000 is an estimate for B200 pending a real CI number, which `scripts/ci/update_est_time.py` will correct. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32355177021](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32355177021)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32355176714](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32355176714)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32355176809](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32355176809)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [XPU][model]: Intel XPU support for encoder embeddings (bge/NomicBERT/ModernBERT) + InternVL3_5
signals.text: Intel XPU support for four embedding / vision models, combined for review: `BAAI/bge-base-en-v1.5`, `nomic-ai/nomic-embed-text-v1.5`, `ibm-granite/granite-embedding-english-r2`, and `OpenGVLab/InternVL3_5-30B-A3B`. ## Motivation - **bge-base-en-v1.5** (`BertModel`) loads on XPU but returns wrong embeddings — SciFact 0, cosine vs HF 0.26-0.47. Two XPU-specific bugs in shared code affect every BERT/RoBERTa encoder on `intel_xpu`. - **nomic-embed-text-v1.5** (`NomicBertModel`) had no SGLang model, so the Transformers fallback raised `NotImplementedError: get_input_embeddings ...`. - **granite-embedding-english-r2** (`ModernBertModel`) fell back and crashed in the forward pass (`RuntimeError` in `set_kv_buffer`) — a bidirectional encoder routed through the paged decoder KV cache. - **InternVL3_5-30B-A3B** crashed at load (`AttributeError: 'InternVLChatConfig' object has no attribute 'num_experts'`) and, once loading, hung/crashed the vision encoder under concurrent multimodal at tp>1 (Level Zero USM-memcpy deadlock on a per-block device->host `.item()`; DEVICE_LOST batching ViT tiles). ## Modifications Encoder embeddings: - `layers/attention/xpu_backend.py`: honor `AttentionType.ENCODER_ONLY` / `DECODER_BIDIRECTIONAL` (was `causal = not is_cross_attention`). - `managers/{scheduler,tokenizer_manager,utils}.py`: preserve the trailing separator token when truncating over-length embedding inputs (gated on `not is_generation`). - `models/nomic_bert.py` (new): `NomicBertModel` — RoPE, SwiGLU, post-norm; SDPA. - `models/modernbert.py` (new): `ModernBertModel` — RoPE, local/global attn, GeGLU; SDPA. InternVL: - `models/internvl.py`: read `num_experts` from `config.llm_config`; pass the host-side `max_seqlen` into `prepare_vision_attention_metadata`; chunk the ViT forward to `SGLANG_VIT_MAX_TILES` tiles on XPU. - `layers/attention/vision.py`: `VisionIntelXPUAttention` uses the metadata's host `max_seqlen` instead of re-deriving it from GPU `cu_seqlens` per block. - `environ.py`: add `SGLANG_VIT_MAX_TILES` (default 12). All XPU paths are guarded by `is_xpu()`; the encoder truncation change is embedding-only; decoder generation is unchanged. ## Accuracy Test Intel XPU (Arc Pro B60), vs the HuggingFace reference. Encoder — MTEB SciFact NDCG@10 (300 queries / 5183 corpus), tp-1: | Model | cosine vs HF | SciFact NDCG@10 | HF ref | |---|---|---|---| | bge-base-en-v1.5 | 0.99997 | 0.6981 | 0.7387 | | nomic-embed-text-v1.5 | 1.00000 | 0.6803 | (prefix-sensitive) | | granite-r2 (ModernBERT) | 1.000000 fp32 / >=0.9999 bf16 | 0.6720 | 0.6815 | InternVL3_5-30B-A3B — tp-4 (61.7 GB bf16, ~14.43 GB/rank): loads with 0 skipped params, MoE initialized, multimodal smoke (red image -> "Red"); P1 lmms-eval: **mathvision_testmini 38.2, mmmu_val 27.4**. All four load with 0 skipped params. ## Speed Test and Profiling No change to existing code paths. Encoder fixes flip a boolean / run once per over-length request; the two new encoders are small SDPA models (no KV cache). InternVL removes a per-block device->host sync on XPU and bounds the ViT forward; non-XPU paths are unchanged. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32368977663](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32368977663)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32368977011](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32368977011)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #32368977328](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32368977328)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [Kimi-K3] Fix "wrong grids" crash in DP-sharded vision preprocessing
signals.text: ## Motivation Regression introduced by #34404 On Kimi-K3 with cpu transport and DP-sharded vision, one batch with ≥2 images of different resolutions crashes the server with `ValueError: Kimi-K3 deferred GPU preprocessing produced wrong grids`. Root cause: the deferred path reads `grid_thws_host` with shard-local positions instead of global image positions. ## Modifications - `python/sglang/srt/models/kimi_k3.py`: index `grid_thws_host` by global image position at both deferred reads, mapping shard-local positions back via `image_indices`. - `test/registered/unit/models/test_kimi_k3_vision.py`: `test_kimi_k3_preprocesses_only_dp_owner_images` now uses distinct per-image grids (identical ones mask the bug); signals.text: ## Motivation Part of the `pool_host` phase of the mem_cache refactor (issue #25371), continuing from PR #31180 ([8/N]). That PR relocated `MambaPoolHost` into `pool_host/mamba.py`, leaving the remaining concrete pools in `memory_pool_host.py`. This PR relocates the DSA indexer host pool — `DSAIndexerPoolHost` — into its own `pool_host/dsa.py` module, following the same mechanical pattern. ## Modifications Mechanical relocation with a **byte-for-byte identical** implementation body: | Symbol | From | To | |--------|------|-----| | `DSAIndexerPoolHost` | `memory_pool_host.py` | `pool_host/dsa.py` | - The DSA-specific imports move with the class, including `DSATokenToKVPool` and the type-only `MLATokenToKVPoolHost` dependency. The new module imports its shared host-pool base symbols and transfer helpers directly. - `memory_pool_host.py` needs no back-import: none of the surviving classes reference `DSAIndexerPoolHost`. Its diff is therefore deletion-only. - Consistent with the preceding `pool_host` moves, no re-export shim or backward-compatibility layer is added. - The new module keeps the same platform-gated `sgl_kernel` imports and runtime platform flags used by the original implementation. ### Caller-site impact Three import sites are redirected from `memory_pool_host` to `pool_host.dsa`: - **Runtime (1):** `hybrid_cache/hybrid_pool_assembler.py`. - **Tests (2):** `test_dsa_pool_host_unit.py` and `test_hicache_staged_write_back_dispatch.py`. The staged write-back test also patches transfer helpers in the new owning module so that it continues to exercise the same dispatch paths after the move. ## Mechanical move — verification This is a verified mechanical move: - Extracting `DSAIndexerPoolHost` from the merge base's `memory_pool_host.py` and comparing it with the class in `pool_host/dsa.py` produces an empty diff: **PASS**. - After removing the relocated class and its DSA-only imports, the surviving implementation in `memory_pool_host.py` is unchanged. - All remaining Python references to `DSAIndexerPoolHost` import it from `pool_host.dsa`; no stale import from `memory_pool_host` remains. - `git diff --check` on the PR diff: **PASS**. ## Accuracy Tests This PR only relocates code and does not change model outputs or host-cache behavior. - Python compilation for the new module and all touched caller/test files: **PASS**. - GitHub lint check: **PASS**. - The affected registered suites remain assigned to the standard CI matrix: - `test_hicache_staged_write_back_dispatch.py`: `base-a-test-cpu`. - `test_dsa_pool_host_unit.py`: CUDA `base-b` / `1-gpu-small` and AMD `stage-b-test-1-gpu-small-amd`. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Not applicable — no runtime or kernel behavior changes. ## Checklist - [x] Format and whitespace checks pass (`lint`, `git diff --check`). - [x] Adjust affected unit tests and patch targets for the new module path. - [x] Follow SGLang code style. - [x] Verify the moved implementation body is byte-for-byte identical. - [x] Documentation is not applicable for this internal module relocation. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #32437333918](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32437333918)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #32437333699](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32437333699)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #32437333852](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32437333852)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [AMD] Perf Kimi-K3 fuse MLA Q and cache preparation
signals.text: ## Summary - Fuse Kimi-K3 identity-RoPE Q materialization, Q concat, and latent KV-cache write through AITER's per-head MLA cache operator. - Support BF16-Q/BF16-KV, FP8-Q/FP8-KV, and BF16-Q/FP8-KV mixed output for Triton decode. - Dispatch only on gfx950 decode/idle batches with contiguous covered inputs; DCP and unsupported contracts fail closed to the existing split/cat/cache path. ## Runtime configuration ```bash export SGLANG_K3_AITER_MLA_Q_CACHE_FUSION=1 ``` Validated FP8-KV configuration: ```bash sglang serve \ --model-path /path/to/Kimi-K3 \ --tp-size 8 \ --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 \ --attention-backend triton \ --prefill-attention-backend triton \ --decode-attention-backend triton ``` BF16 KV is also covered. The larger measured gain is with BF16-Q + FP8-KV. ## AITER dependency This SGLang integration requires AITER #4342 / commit `770790cd` or newer `fused_qk_rope_concat_and_cache_mla` semantics, including the `compute_all_q_rope` behavior used for correct batch-64 execution. The AITER revision currently pinned by main (`d9e5ef7`) is insufficient: its old schema rejects the new argument, and a 14-argument compatibility call produces incorrect token-64 output. This PR intentionally documents rather than changes the AITER pin. ## Accuracy Tests - Focused operator tests: `9 passed` - GSM8K 1319: `0.955` - Invalid responses: `0.001` ## Speed Tests and Profiling Historical matched results for the same integration: - BF16 KV: C32 `+0.63%`, C64 `+0.53%` - FP8 KV: C32 `+3.26%`, C64 `+3.57%` - FP8-KV median TPOT: approximately `-4%` ## Test plan - [x] BF16/BF16, FP8/FP8, and BF16-Q/FP8-KV operator tests at token counts 1 and 64 - [x] Negative slot handling - [x] CUDA Graph replay with changed inputs - [x] Narrow support/fallback predicates - [x] Full GSM8K 1319 with Triton prefill/decode and FP8 KV - [ ] Re-run after the target branch updates its AITER pin AITER prefill was not used in the full-model test because 12-head AITER attention-backend enablement is maintained separately; this fusion acts on the decode path. signals.title: Support deepseek v4 and kimi k3 on ssd
signals.text: # [Feature] Add SSD-backed Expert Pack inference for DeepSeek-V4-Flash and Kimi-K3 ## Summary This PR adds an opt-in SSD-backed inference path for **DeepSeek-V4-Flash** and **Kimi-K3**. It allows these MoE models to run when their complete weights are larger than GPU VRAM and host RAM combined. Routed expert weights are stored on SSD and loaded only when selected by the router. The implementation uses: - an expert-major **Expert Pack** layout for efficient random access; - direct I/O into aligned pinned host buffers; - asynchronous host-to-device transfers; and - a byte-budgeted LFU/LRU GPU cache for frequently used experts. The runtime does not prune, merge, skip, replace, or re-quantize experts, and does not reduce Expert Top-K. The default `auto`, `safetensors`, and `gguf` loading paths remain unchanged; SSD execution is enabled only through the explicit `expert_pack` path. ## Usage Install this branch from source before running the examples: ```bash python3 -m pip install -e "python" ``` ### DeepSeek-V4-Flash Download the tested FP4/FP8 GGUF from [`frob/deepseek-v4-flash`](https://ollama.com/frob/deepseek-v4-flash). The benchmark used the immutable model blob with SHA-256 `947ac34c08c0e5c5752ac76398f934b3b6b4075cfe915ba43dd5ac754900a4cd`. ```bash python3 examples/runtime/deepseek_v4/benchmark_deepseek_5090.py \ --gguf /path/to/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-FP4-FP8-native.gguf \ --prompt "Explain why the sky appears blue." \ --max-new-tokens 200 ``` ### Kimi-K3 Download all 38 Q2_K GGUF shards from [`Blackfrost-AI/KIMI-K3-Q2_K-GGUF-ABLITERATED`](https://huggingface.co/Blackfrost-AI/KIMI-K3-Q2_K-GGUF-ABLITERATED). Also place the tokenizer/config files from [`moonshotai/Kimi-K3`](https://huggingface.co/moonshotai/Kimi-K3) in a sibling directory named `kimi-k3-tokenizer`. ```bash hf download Blackfrost-AI/KIMI-K3-Q2_K-GGUF-ABLITERATED \ --include "KIMI-K3-MXP4-DERISKED-Q2_K-*.gguf" \ --local-dir /path/to/kimi-k3 ``` ```bash python3 examples/runtime/kimi_k3/benchmark_kimi_k3_5090.py \ --gguf /path/to/kimi-k3/KIMI-K3-MXP4-DERISKED-Q2_K-00001-of-00038.gguf \ --prompt "Explain why the sky appears blue." \ --max-new-tokens 200 ``` The first shard is only the entrypoint. The launcher automatically discovers and uses all 38 shards in the same directory. Both launchers derive the remaining paths automatically. If the Expert Pack is missing, it is built on the first launch and reused afterward. | Model | First Expert Pack build | Approximate first-run readiness | | --- | ---: | ---: | | DeepSeek-V4-Flash | Estimated **5-10 minutes** on the benchmark NVMe SSD | **8-15 minutes** | | Kimi-K3 | **29 minutes 42 seconds measured** | **35-45 minutes** | The 38 Kimi-K3 source shards and generated Expert Pack occupy approximately 1.814 TiB in total, so a 4 TB SSD is recommended for practical headroom. ## Correctness - DeepSeek-V4-Flash produced semantically equivalent answers to Ollama across travel planning, science, history, programming, and mathematics prompts. - Kimi-K3 matched the 200-token SGLang reference output exactly. All 92 routed layers executed Top-16 experts with `fallback_count=0` and `io_errors=0`. ## Performance The target platform is one RTX 5090 with 32 GB VRAM, 32 GB host RAM, and NVMe SSD storage. The retained measurements were collected on RTX 5090 hosts; host RAM and SSD capacity differed between the two model runs. ### DeepSeek-V4-Flash vs Ollama Five prompts were measured with 200 generated tokens per prompt. | Metric | SGLang | Ollama | Result | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | | Prefill | 3.265 token/s | 1.457 token/s | **2.24x faster** | | Decode | 2.020 token/s | 1.354 token/s | **1.49x faster** | ### Kimi-K3 vs llama.cpp The SGLang run used a 91-token prompt and generated 200 tokens. | Metric | SGLang | llama.cpp | Result | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | | Prefill | 0.66412 token/s | 0.11289 token/s | **5.88x faster** | | Decode | 0.44830 token/s | 0.1810 token/s | **2.48x faster** | The llama.cpp decode baseline came from an earlier 50-token run, so the 2.48x decode figure is indicative rather than a strict equal-length comparison. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: **Missing `run-ci` label** -- add it to run CI tests.<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: **Blocked** -- `run-ci` is required first.<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:heavy_minus_sign: **No AMD PR run found for this commit**.<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [AMD] Add ROCm 7.14 (gfx942 / gfx950) release
signals.text: ## Motivation ROCm 7.14 is published only as pip wheels and docker images — `repo.radeon.com` has no apt repo for it — so its stack has to be assembled from AMD's ROCm pip channels on top of `ubuntu:24.04`. That places the SDK in `site-packages` instead of `/opt/rocm`, which the existing stages of `docker/rocm.Dockerfile` assume throughout. This PR adds gfx942 and gfx950 ROCm 7.14 stages built that way, plus the adjustments the pip-SDK layout forces on the existing build and CI steps. The index is `https://repo.amd.com/rocm/whl-multi-arch/`, AMD's release channel. Deliberately not the nightly or devrelease channels: those get pruned. An earlier revision of this PR pinned a 7.15 nightly (`7.15.0a20260712`) because 7.15 never had a stable release — the line ran from `7.15.0a20260626` to `7.15.0a20260728` and was then renumbered 10.0 — which would have left this Dockerfile unbuildable, and the image unreproducible, once that nightly aged out of the index. 7.14 is a released SDK, so the pin is stable. torch is 2.11, the same as the `rocm724` flavors already on `main`, so the 7.14 stages reuse the existing `*_rocm724` extras for the `compressed-tensors` 0.16.0 pin rather than adding a third hand-synced copy of the same dependency list. `python/pyproject_other.toml` is unchanged by this PR. The `rocm7_15` / gfx1250 stage and its workflow are untouched. ## Modifications ### `docker/rocm.Dockerfile` - Added a shared `rocm714-base` stage: `ubuntu:24.04` + Python 3.12 in a venv + the ROCm 7.14 pip stack — `rocm-sdk-{core,libraries,devel,device-gfx942,device-gfx950}==7.14.0`, `torch`/`torchaudio` `2.11.0+rocm7.14.0`, `torchvision 0.26.0+rocm7.14.0`, `triton 3.7.1+git0263a6a6.rocm7.14.0`. - Added two thin per-arch stages, `gfx942-rocm714` and `gfx950-rocm714`, which set build flags and `PIP_CONSTRAINT`. Both arches' torch device wheels go into the shared base; `GPU_ARCH_LIST` still narrows what AITER and sgl-kernel actually compile for. - `BASE_IMAGE_942_ROCM714` / `BASE_IMAGE_950_ROCM714` default to the `rocm714-base` stage rather than a published image. Naming them keeps these stages shaped like every other stage in this file, which matters because `scripts/ci/amd/amd_ci_install_dependency.sh` locates a stage's `AITER_COMMIT_DEFAULT` by grepping for `FROM $BASE_IMAGE_<arch><suffix> AS <arch><suffix>`. They can also be pointed at a prebuilt image to skip building the base. - Single `--index-url`; the release index mirrors the PyPI packages torch pulls in, so no `--extra-index-url` and no `--pre` are needed. - torch and torchvision device wheels are named as separate specs rather than combined device extras. Several device extras in one spec (`torch[device-gfx942,device-gfx950]`) silently installs only the first, and the missing arch then fails at runtime with `hipErrorInvalidImage`. - Python 3.12 (the Ubuntu 24.04 default) rather than 3.13/3.14: `st_attn==0.0.7`, `vsa==0.0.4`, `petit_kernel==0.0.2` and `wave-lang==3.8.2` publish wheels only up to cp313 and no sdist, so on 3.14 pip has no candidate at all for `srt_hip`. - Path fixups for the non-`/opt/rocm` SDK: `ROCM_HOME` / `ROCM_PATH` / `CPATH` / `LIBRARY_PATH` / `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` point at the site-packages `_rocm_sdk_devel` tree; a `/opt/rocm` symlink because AITER shells out to `/opt/rocm/llvm/bin/amdgpu-arch` to pick `DEFAULT_GPU_ARCH` and the rest of this Dockerfile refers to `/opt/rocm`; and a `/usr/lib64/libc.so` symlink because the SDK's `hsakmtTargets.cmake` hardcodes that path from its own build host. - libdrm: skipped for `*rocm714*`. The pip SDK's `libdrm_amdgpu.so` links the device-ID table in rather than reading `share/libdrm/amdgpu.ids` — the `.so` carries the MI300X / MI325X / MI355X names and never opens that file — so the apt step the 7.2.4 flavor needs is unnecessary here. - amdsmi: installed for `*rocm714*` (same branch as the 7.2 flavors), since the pip SDK does not pre-install it. - `PIP_CONSTRAINT`: the 7.14 stages define and populate it the same way the `rocm724` stages do, so resolving AITER and SGLang dependencies cannot swap the image's ROCm torch for a PyPI CUDA build. - MORI: point the build at the SDK's vendored `lib/rocm_sysdeps` tree via `CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH` / `CPATH` / `LIBRARY_PATH` plus an `ldconfig` entry, for NUMA (`hsakmt-config.cmake` calls `find_dependency(NUMA)`) and libdrm (`rocm_smi.h` includes `<libdrm/drm.h>`, `mori_application` links `-ldrm`/`-ldrm_amdgpu`). Guarded on the directory existing, so the apt-based ROCm images keep their current behaviour. - nixl: the existing `libabsl-dev` removal is extended to `*-rocm714`, which is on the same Ubuntu 24.04 base as `rocm724` and hits the same meson/abseil conflict. - The SGLang install and the post-install validation step both treat `rocm714` like `rocm724`. ### `scripts/ci/amd/amd_ci_install_dependency.sh` - Recognise `-rocm714` in the image `GPU_ARCH` stamp and map it to `_ROCM714` / `-rocm714` so the AITER pin lookup finds the right Dockerfile stage. - Select the `dev_hip_rocm724` extras for `-rocm714` as well, matching what the Dockerfile does at build time. Without this a 7.14 image would get `compressed-tensors` 0.15.0, which requires `torch<2.11`, and the resolve would fail. - Apply the same `rocm_sysdeps` handling to the in-image MORI rebuild, kept scoped to that build instead of exported image-wide because `rocm_sysdeps/include` also carries `zlib.h` / `expat.h` / `elf.h`, which would shadow the system headers for every other component. ### `.github/workflows/release-docker-amd-rocm714-nightly.yml` - New workflow, following this repo's one-file-per-ROCm-version convention (`rocm700` / `rocm720` / `rocm7_15`), with a `gfx942-rocm714` / `gfx950-rocm714` matrix and `rocm714-mi30x` / `rocm714-mi35x` tags. The `rocm7_15` workflow is not modified. - The schedule is commented out for now; the workflow is dispatch-only until the gfx950 leg has had a green run. ## Accuracy Tests All of the following was run on an MI300X host (gfx942). **1. Image build.** `GPU_ARCH=gfx942-rocm714` builds end to end, all 34 steps, 45.8 GB image. The in-image validation step reports: ``` Validated ROCm stack: {'torch': '2.11.0+rocm7.14.0', 'torchaudio': '2.11.0+rocm7.14.0', 'torchvision': '0.26.0+rocm7.14.0', 'triton': '3.7.1'} HIP 7.14.60850 ``` with `pip check` clean and no `nvidia-*-cu*` packages pulled in. **2. In-image smoke test on real hardware.** 8 devices visible, `get_device_name(0)` is `AMD Instinct MI300X` (correct marketing name with no `amdgpu.ids` file present, confirming the ids table is linked into the SDK's libdrm), `gcnArchName` is `gfx942:sramecc+:xnack-`, a bf16 matmul on device returns finite values, and `triton`, `torchvision`, `torchaudio`, `aiter`, `mori`, `tilelang`, `nixl`, `amdsmi`, `sglang` and `compressed_tensors` (0.16.0, i.e. the right extras were selected) all import. **3. CI dependency install.** `scripts/ci/amd/amd_ci_install_dependency.sh` exits 0 against a `ci_sglang` container started from the image. The parts this PR touches behave as intended: ``` [CI-IMAGE] Image GPU_ARCH=gfx942-rocm714 Image torch 2.11.0+rocm7.14.0, HIP 7.14.60850; installing python extras: [dev_hip_rocm724,tracing] [CI-AITER-CHECK] Using FROM $BASE_IMAGE_942_ROCM714 AS gfx942-rocm714 from Dockerfile... [CI-AITER-CHECK] Dockerfile expects AITER_COMMIT=d9e5ef7ce08ee7045d583aed768cff41aa9210fe [CI-AITER-CHECK] AITER version inside CI image: v0.1.20.dev12+gd9e5ef7ce [MORI] Reinstalling MORI 12d1bc32d0c93dcd5062e74f4e0f772e36e1aac4 (MORI_GPU_ARCHS=gfx942) [MORI] Done. ``` **4. CI test suite.** `run_suite.py --hw amd --suite stage-a-test-1-gpu-small-amd` reports **8/8 passed**, exit code 0: | Test | Result | Elapsed | | --- | --- | --- | | `attention/test_wave_attention_kernels.py` | pass | 73s | | `quant/test_fused_rms_fp8_group_quant.py` | pass | 20s | | `quant/test_awq_dequant.py` | pass | 22s | | `amd/test_fp8_per_channel_detection.py` | pass | 14s | | `core/test_basic_sanity.py` | pass | 396s | | `core/test_basic_sanity_eagle3.py` | pass | 220s | | `unit/mem_cache/test_umbp_store.py` | pass | 14s | | `unit/models/test_vit_pos_embed_interpolate.py` | pass | 16s | `test_umbp_store.py` passing is the relevant check for the MORI changes above: it exercises `mori.umbp`, which needs the gRPC symbols the rebuilt MORI must carry. **Both arches build.** `gfx950-rocm714` had never been built when the local verification above was done; it has since built successfully on CI, first try, in the same run as gfx942. See the upstream validation note below. What is still unverified for gfx950 is *runtime* behaviour — the only host available here is MI300X, so nothing has executed on MI355X hardware yet. **Upstream CI validation.** The workflow added here cannot be `workflow_dispatch`-ed until it exists on the default branch, so it is being exercised from a throwaway branch, `bingxche/rocm714-ci-test`, which carries this PR head plus a branch-scoped `push` trigger. That branch also redirects the images to a scratch repository (`bingxche/sgl-test`) so nothing unvalidated lands in `rocm/sgl-dev` or `lmsysorg/sglang-rocm`. Neither the trigger nor the scratch registry is part of this PR. [Run #32380153563](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32380153563) built and pushed both arches successfully: | Image | Size | | --- | --- | | `bingxche/sgl-test:v0.5.17-rocm714-mi30x-20260820` | 16.3 GB | | `bingxche/sgl-test:v0.5.17-rocm714-mi35x-20260820` | 16.5 GB | **Follow-up, not in this PR.** Wiring the AMD test workflows to pick a 7.14 image automatically needs two small changes elsewhere: `find_latest_image` in `scripts/ci/amd/amd_ci_start_container.sh` hardcodes `rocm/sgl-dev`, so the repository has to become configurable before images in any other namespace can be discovered; and `rocm714` needs to be an accepted `rocm_version` in `pr-test-amd-rocm720.yml` (plus a fallback entry in the same script). The arch selection itself already works by convention: the script maps the runner hostname to `mi30x` / `mi35x` and looks for `v<version>-<rocm_version>-<arch>-<date>`, which is exactly the tag shape the workflow here produces. **Note on reproducing the local build above:** `arrayref` 0.3.5-0.3.9 were briefly yanked on crates.io on 2026-08-20, which broke `blake3`'s `arrayref = "^0.3.5"` and with it the `sgl-model-gateway` step for every ROCm image build on `main`, not just this branch. They have since been un-yanked. The local verification above was done during that window with a `[patch.crates-io]` pointing `arrayref` at the authentic 0.3.9 artifact from `static.crates.io`; that patch was never part of this PR and nothing in the diff depends on it. ## Speed Tests and Profiling <!-- If this pull request impacts inference speed, provide benchmarking and profiling results. --> ## Checklist - [ ] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [ ] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process). 2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers. 3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so. - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci` 4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR.

signals.title: fix(openai): avoid duplicate routed expert in response when `return_meta_info = True`
signals.text: ## Summary Avoid duplicate routed-expert payloads in non-streaming chat completion responses. ## Symptom & Reproduction - **Symptom:** The base64 `routed_experts` payload appeared in both `choices[*].meta_info` and response-level `sglext` when both return flags were enabled. - **Reproduction:** Build and serialize a non-streaming `/v1/chat/completions` response with both flags enabled. - **Expected:** Each choice contains its routed experts once in `meta_info`. - **Observed before the fix:** `sglext.routed_experts` repeated the first choice's routed experts. ## Root Cause 1. `_build_chat_response` projected first-choice `routed_experts` into `SglExt`. 2. `choice_meta_info` serialized the same routed payload for every choice. ## Fix When `return_meta_info` is enabled, omit only response-level `sglext.routed_experts` and keep each choice's `meta_info` authoritative for routed experts. Independently requested `cached_tokens_details` and `spec_tokens_details` remain in `sglext`; `return_meta_info=false`, streaming chat, and `/v1/completions` behavior remain unchanged. ## Verification - `env PYTHONPATH=/tmp/sglang-dedupe-chat-meta-sglext/python python3 -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider test/registered/unit/entrypoints/openai/test_serving_chat.py test/registered/unit/entrypoints/openai/test_serving_completions.py`: 130 passed and 55 subtests passed. - `ruff check --ignore E402 python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/openai/serving_chat.py test/registered/unit/entrypoints/openai/test_serving_chat.py`: passed. - `ruff format --check python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/openai/serving_chat.py test/registered/unit/entrypoints/openai/test_serving_chat.py`: both files already formatted. - `git merge-tree --write-tree 1f87d8f512e09a6fe230da1e6d4ab228f6bbb91c 584a0880b29cbb5fa0db5a67e08ec8b8c8e0ffaf`: merged cleanly against `main@1f87d8f512e09a6fe230da1e6d4ab228f6bbb91c`. ## Review Focus - `_build_chat_response`: dual-flag requests must omit only response-level routed experts. - `SglExt`: cache/spec projections and their `n > 1` ordering must remain intact. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:no_entry_sign: [Run #32402094935](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32402094935)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32402094501](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32402094501)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:no_entry_sign: [Run #32402094636](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32402094636)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [diffusion] Warmup-calibrated auto residency promotion in performance-mode auto
signals.text: ## Motivation Under `--performance-mode auto`, component placement is decided **before load** from static per-model thresholds (`keep_resident_min_available_gb`). On GPUs with ample free VRAM this leaves components needlessly offloaded — e.g. a layerwise-offloaded text encoder on an 80–140 GB card pays a full H2D reload every request for VRAM nobody else uses — and fixing it by hand requires per-model, per-GPU flag tuning. This PR makes `auto` mode **calibrate residency from the server warmup it already runs**: measure real memory behavior, then promote implicitly offloaded components to GPU-resident when the default workload provably fits, before the server turns ready. Frozen after `/health`; no changes after startup. ## Modifications **Measurement** - Server warmup forwards record `peak_reserved` + a pre-forward baseline on **every rank** (previously output-rank only). - Video warmup (which caps frames to bound startup) adds one extra small-frame **calibration forward**; a two-point affine fit in workload units (`batch × W × H × frames`) separates constant (weights/buffers) from linear (activation) memory and extrapolates the default-workload peak with a 1.2× margin on the linear part only. Image warmup already runs the default shape, so it is a direct measurement, no extrapolation. - The loader now records real weight/buffer sizes alongside the GPU-load delta (`memory_usages` is ≈0 for exactly the offloaded components residency decisions are about). **Decision + promotion (between last warmup req and ready)** - All ranks all-gather `{estimated peak, budget, candidates}` and compute one deterministic plan: candidates are implicitly offloaded, known-size, native CUDA components only; ranked by per-request H2D savings (layerwise DiT counts default denoise steps); promoted greedily while `estimated_peak + promoted_bytes + reserve ≤ budget`, with `reserve = max(10 % budget, 4 GiB)` and `budget = free + torch-reserved` (min across ranks; excludes other processes on shared GPUs). - Promotion reuses existing primitives: component-offload → resident via `require_component_resident`, layerwise via `disable_offload()`; the strategy cache is invalidated explicitly. - A **re-warm forward** after promotion re-establishes compile/kernel caches and proves the promoted layout actually serves; any failure rolls every rank back to the original strategy (only a rollback failure aborts startup). - Excluded paths: explicit placement / `manual` mode, FSDP, diffusers backend, quantized DiT (ModelOpt FP8/NVFP4, SVDQuant), Cache-DiT, breakable CUDA graph, realtime/disagg, `batching_max_size > 1`, any warmup failure. Kill switch: `SGLANG_DIFFUSION_DISABLE_AUTO_RESIDENCY=1`. **Fixes and unification along the way** - Warmup frame caps now run the pipeline's `adjust_num_frames`: LongLive2's server warmup was silently a no-op (17 capped frames → 5 latent frames, not divisible by `num_frames_per_block=8`, error swallowed by fail-open). - The post-request residency hint (`get_can_stay_resident_components`) now shares the promotion's candidate collection and H2D ranking — it previously read the ≈0 `memory_usages`, making the recommendation meaningless, and could recommend FSDP/custom-strategy components. - Logs narrate the adjustment: decision summary (`target/measured/estimated_peak/reserve/budget/promoted`), per-component `mode -> resident` with the **equivalent `--component-residency` flags** users can pin, and the kill switch. ``` Server warmup complete; adjusting component residency for the default workload (--performance-mode auto). Auto residency: target=1024x1024x1f steps=9, measured=[1024x1024x1f=17.4GiB], estimated_peak=17.4 GiB, reserve=13.3 GiB, budget=133.5 GiB, promoted=[text_encoder(layerwise-offload, 6.8 GiB)] Auto residency: adjusted text_encoder: layerwise-offload -> resident. Equivalent server args: --component-residency text_encoder=resident. ... ``` The optimization target is the model-default workload (default resolution/frames, batch 1). Larger or batched workloads should pin residency explicitly; the reserve bounds the blast radius. Static model deployment configs remain as the fallback when calibration is skipped. No numerics change for non-promoted paths; promoted components run identical code at a different placement. ## Test - `test/unit/test_auto_residency.py`: estimation (same-shape, single-point, two-point fit, negative-slope fallback, covering measurement), plan (skip propagation, reserve, cumulative fit, ranking), multi-rank worst-casing, promotion/rollback on stub modules, eligibility gates, LongLive2 frame alignment, applied-changes log, hint/promotion ranking consistency. - H200, Z-Image-Turbo serve: text encoder (layerwise, 6.8 GiB) promoted; warmup 9.15 s, decision <1 s, post-promotion re-warm 0.15 s; `/health` stays 503 until after promotion. - 2×H100, Wan2.1-T2V-14B: VAE promoted; text encoder correctly refused (estimated 65.6 GiB + 6.5 GiB TE > 70.2 GiB budget). Single-GPU 14B correctly refuses all promotions (72.6 vs 72.8 GiB). - Steady-state E2E improved on promoted image cases; no OOM observed in any validated case, including the refusal boundaries. ## Post-submission hardening (adversarial review pass) A 10-angle review over the diff surfaced and fixed, in `harden auto residency against review findings`: - **Measurement**: per-forward `empty_cache` + peak reset (allocator-pool carryover flattened the calibration slope → under-estimate → post-ready OOM); calibration forward moved after the main warmup so one-time allocations can only steepen the slope (safe direction); only `is_warmup` requests are measured (compile prewarm ran a different layout); failed warmups are recorded on every exit path; **`--enable-torch-compile` is excluded** — its warmup deliberately runs a stripped memory layout (layerwise DiT + evicted aux components) whose peaks are not serving peaks; unknown default workloads skip instead of trusting the capped peak. - **Distributed/rollback**: everything before the first all-gather is fenced into a skip report (a raise there parked peer ranks in the collective); error gathers filter on `is not None` with never-empty error strings; a failed in-apply rollback now surfaces as `rollback_failed` (aborts startup) instead of masquerading as rolled back; `disable_offload` re-arms hooks when `load_all_layers` fails; mechanism/mode mismatches from the `offload_during_compile` window are excluded and guarded; `_required_resident_components` tracks an owner feature so rollback cannot release loader hard-requirements. - **Startup contract**: apply-RPC failures honor the warmup fail-open contract; the post-rollback restore warmup keeps `--warmup-resolutions`' fail-closed contract; the calibration request shares `auto_residency_skip_reason` (the kill switch and excluded configs no longer pay for a measurement they never consume); warmup records are consumed exactly once (one-shot handler); re-warm passes no longer double-advance the warmup progress bar. - The warmup/target frame contract (cap → `adjust_num_frames` → `num_gpus` latent alignment) is now one shared helper extracted from `SamplingParams._adjust_visual_fields`, used by real requests, warmup requests, and the workload resolver. Known accepted conservatisms (documented in code): the budget check double-counts bytes of a component already partially on GPU at the measured peak (safe direction), and the reserve stays at `max(10 %, 4 GiB)`. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #32410205639](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32410205639)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32410205044](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32410205044)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #32410205559](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32410205559)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [VLM] Default to two multimodal preprocessing workers
signals.text: Stacked on #35342 (which routes every processor through the worker pool's call site). Review that one first; this PR is the one line that actually turns the pool on. ## Motivation Preprocessing an image costs real CPU time on the tokenizer's event loop, so with a single worker a model's request throughput is capped at `1 / preprocess_time` no matter how much GPU is idle. That cap is why PaddleOCR-VL saturated at 6.7 req/s on an H200 with GPU headroom to spare — and only four processors in tree had opted out of it. ## The benefit generalizes, because the mechanism does Image preprocessing is numpy / torch / PIL underneath, so it releases the GIL. Wall-clock speedup of 4 threads over 1 on the same work, 1080p input, `torch.set_num_threads(1)` so intraop parallelism cannot be mistaken for thread scaling: | image processor | 1 thread | 4 threads | speedup | `deepcopy` | |---|---|---|---|---| | Qwen2VL (fast / slow) | 24.3 / 24.1 ms | 7.1 / 7.0 ms | 3.41x / 3.45x | ok | | Idefics3 | 46.1 ms | 12.7 ms | 3.64x | ok | | Pixtral | 19.0 ms | 5.2 ms | 3.64x | ok | | Llama4 | 27.0 ms | 7.7 ms | 3.52x | ok | | GLM4V | 31.8 ms | 9.0 ms | 3.51x | ok | | PaddleOCR-VL | 28.4 ms | 8.7 ms | 3.27x | ok | | CLIP | 9.1 ms | 2.8 ms | 3.28x | ok | | Gemma3 | 5.7 ms | 1.9 ms | 2.94x | ok | | SigLIP | 5.5 ms | 2.1 ms | 2.69x | ok | | *pure-Python control* | *81.0 ms* | *80.5 ms* | *1.01x* | — | The control validates the probe. `copy.deepcopy` succeeded on all nine, and the executor already falls back to synchronous processing with a warning if cloning ever fails. ## Two workers, and not more Past two, spreading request arrivals fragments the GPU prefill batches faster than the extra overlap pays for itself — the tradeoff `qwen_vl`'s processor already documents. Swept at 32-way concurrency on an H200: | workload | 1 worker | 2 workers | 4 workers | |---|---|---|---| | PaddleOCR-VL 1080p pages, 128-token outputs | 6.72 | **9.55** | 8.92 req/s | | PaddleOCR-VL 360p pages, 512-token outputs | 22.38 | **25.20** | 25.06 req/s | | Qwen2.5-VL 360p images, 512-token outputs | 12.54 | **12.60** | 12.25 req/s | The middle row is the shape that was supposed to break this: light preprocessing, where overlap has little to win, and long outputs, where batch fragmentation has the most to cost. Two workers gained 13% there instead of regressing. Four workers is where the documented regression actually appears (bottom row, −2.3%). Greedy output is unaffected: two workers against one is byte-identical across five page geometries × two task prompts on PaddleOCR-VL. ## Limitation reviewers should weigh All of this is **Hopper**. The regression `qwen_vl` documents was observed on Blackwell, and no B200 was available to me (GB300 is arm64). A Blackwell check on the light-preprocessing / long-output shape would be worth having before this rides a release — that is the one measurement that could still overturn the default. ## Checklist - [x] Format the code and run lint locally - [x] Add a test pinning the default (`test_default_worker_count_stays_at_the_measured_optimum`), so raising it requires a fresh sweep - [x] Benchmark on real hardware, including the shape most likely to regress - [x] Verify greedy output is unchanged 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:no_entry_sign: [Run #32224837223](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32224837223)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32224837024](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32224837024)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32224837269](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32224837269)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [Fix]: exclude SM120 from attn-res TMA dispatch
signals.text: # [Kimi-K3] Exclude SM120 from the attention-residual TMA path ## Summary The Kimi-K3 attention-residual dispatcher previously enabled the TMA fast path for every CUDA architecture with a compute-capability major version greater than or equal to 10. This incorrectly selected the SM100-oriented TMA kernel on SM120 GPUs such as the NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5090, where the required `tcgen05`/TMEM path is not supported. This PR changes the capability gate to: ```python major >= 10 and major != 12 ``` SM12x devices now use the existing Triton fallback. The fast path remains available on SM10x, SM11x, and later non-SM12x architectures. ## Scope This is a standalone Kimi-K3 attention-residual dispatch fix. ## Validation - Verified that the modified Python module passes `py_compile`. - Verified that the PR changes only `python/sglang/srt/layers/attn_residual.py`. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:no_entry_sign: [Run #32322724028](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32322724028)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32322723630](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32322723630)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #32322723882](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32322723882)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->
signals.author: beyondHJM

signals.title: [diffusion] feat: load GGUF transformer checkpoints (MiniMax-H3)
signals.text: ## Motivation MiniMax-H3's transformer is 61.7 GiB in BF16, and the FL2VA partition is 135 GiB in total. Layerwise offload already lets the model run on a consumer GPU, so the remaining barriers are the checkpoint download, host memory, and bytes streamed per layer. This adds a pre-quantized GGUF transformer path. The validated Q4_K_M DiT is 17.5 GiB instead of 61.7 GiB. It complements online `kitchen_int8`: GGUF avoids first downloading and pinning the complete BF16 DiT, while `kitchen_int8` remains the faster compute-oriented path. ## Interface `--model-path` continues to provide the pipeline components and `--transformer-weights-path` selects the GGUF DiT. The loader accepts a local file, `owner/repo/path/file.gguf`, or `owner/repo:QUANT_TYPE` when that suffix matches exactly one file. Repositories containing multiple variants require the full file path. ```bash sglang serve \ --model-path MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3 \ --model-variant fl2va \ --transformer-weights-path \ leejet/MiniMax-H3-GGUF/minimax_h3_fl2va-Q4_K_M.gguf \ --attention-backend fa \ --performance-mode memory \ --layerwise-offload-components dit,text_encoder \ --dit-offload-prefetch-size 1 \ --dit-layerwise-resident-layers 0 \ --enable-torch-compile false \ --port 30010 ``` `--quantization gguf` is intentionally rejected: quantization is encoded in the checkpoint and the file path is the selector. ## Implementation - Reuses SRT's GGUF file detection, Hub resolver, quantization type sets, and CUDA dequantization helper. Diffusion no longer carries duplicate download resolution, GGML support tables, or dequantization shape logic. - Keeps a small diffusion-specific header reader because model construction needs each tensor's exact logical and packed shape before parameters exist. Packed tensors stay mmap-backed until the generic loader copies their TP shard, which avoids cloning the complete 17.5 GiB checkpoint during load. - Uses dequantization followed by native GEMM for DiT linears. SRT's fused MMVQ/MMQ path is optimized for low-token LLM inference and regresses normal diffusion sequence lengths. - Supports block-aligned tensor parallel row/column/merged linear slicing. Incompatible TP degrees fail during model construction. - Supports both the original MiniMax-H3 timestep MLP and pruned community checkpoints containing an unquantized `adaln_t_table` curve. - Fails before download for conflicting or unsupported configurations: non-CUDA, FSDP for the GGUF component, LoRA, another `--quantization`, SVDQuant, and the separate MiniMax-H3 AdaLN cache/online paths. - Keeps `quality=high` fail-closed when replacement transformer weights are supplied. F32/F16/BF16 tensors use the ordinary linear path. Quantized tensors must be 2D `.weight` matrices and have valid GGML block alignment; malformed, corrupt, opposite-endian, or unsupported files fail at load. ## Validation ### Automated - Changed-files pre-commit: passed. - Focused remote NVIDIA suite: **163 passed, 2 subtests passed**. - Coverage includes header corruption/endianness/BF16 handling, Hub resolution and ambiguity, type selection, CPU-offload loading, pre-download guards, quality admission, pruned curve interpolation, and TP row/column/merged slicing. ### Kernel selection On H200 with the real H3 Q4_K QKV matrix `(21504, 5376)`, fused MMVQ is useful only at one or two tokens. At 256 and 2048 tokens, SRT MMQ took 2.60 ms and 20.61 ms versus 0.37 ms and 0.91 ms for dequantize + GEMM. The final diffusion adapter therefore keeps the native-GEMM path. ### End to end 1x H200, FL2VA Q4_K_M, layerwise-offloaded DiT/text encoder, fixed seed, 1344x768, 107 frames, 2 inference steps: | Revision | Warmup | Generation | Peak GPU | Output | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- | | Original PR dense-dequant path | 12.67 s | 10.11 s | 17,174 MB | H.264 + AAC | | Refactored SRT-reuse path | 12.64 s | 10.13 s | 17,174 MB | H.264 + AAC | The two MP4 files are byte-identical (same SHA-256; PSNR infinite, SSIM 1.0). The refactored loader constructed the 17.49 GiB DiT in about 1 second versus about 19 seconds in the original PR run because packed values are no longer cloned wholesale during iteration. The pruned `unsloth/MiniMax-H3-GGUF` FL2VA Q4_K checkpoint also completed server warmup and a real 1344x768, 107-frame video + AAC request on H200; its loaded DiT size was 10.72 GiB. The original RTX 5090 measurements remain valid: 39.0 s denoise and 26.3 GiB peak with `dit,text_encoder` offload; adding VAE offload lowered peak to 19.6 GiB and increased VAE decode from 9.5 s to 57.2 s. Not yet validated end to end: `ref2va`, quantization types other than the listed Q4 variants, and multi-GPU GGUF. TP packed slicing is unit-tested, but a requested 2x H100 validation box remained in infrastructure provisioning and is not reported as a successful run. ## Checklist - [x] Format code with pre-commit. - [x] Add unit tests. - [x] Update CLI, quantization, compatibility, and MiniMax-H3 documentation. - [x] Run real checkpoint and end-to-end NVIDIA validation. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32256244219](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32256244219)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #32256243954](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32256243954)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->
