signals.title: [Kernel] Add H200 Nemotron MoE configs and cache selection
signals.text: > [!NOTE] > **Draft: default-H200 CUDA-graph A/B/A is serving-positive.** The earlier > inconclusive A/B/A accidentally capped decode graphs at batch 16, forcing the > parallel-64 workload onto the eager path. With SGLang's default H200 graph > configuration, tuned v2 improves median GSM8K latency by 6.12% and median > output-token throughput by 3.15% against the average of stable bracketing > baselines, with zero invalid outputs. ## Summary Add NVIDIA H200 Triton 3.6 fused-MoE configs for `nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Lightning-30B-A3B-BF16`: - TP1: `E=128,N=1856`, with 26 measured serving token counts from M=1 to 8192 - TP2 per rank: `E=128,N=928` Both shapes previously used the generic fallback config. The change also caches nearest-config selection by shape and token count so a dense JSON table does not rescan every key for all 23 MoE layers on every forward step. ## Forced-Triton real-model validation Tested official revision `d468880b6ad3c6e0d21377ce7242adaea4cc884d` with SGLang v0.5.17 (`29481685462732237d80d86076d6563e1f658102`), Torch 2.11.0, Triton 3.6.0, and `--moe-runner-backend triton` on one H200. Each comparison used ten 200-question GSM8K runs, five shots, parallelism 64, and zero-temperature sampling. | TP1 candidate | Median latency | Median output throughput | Quality | |---|---:|---:|---:| | Original up only vs baseline | +0.79% | -1.70% | up to 0.5% invalid in three runs | | Original up + tuned down vs baseline | +5.78% | -4.68% | zero invalid | | Decode-aware up + down vs fresh baseline | -2.23% | -1.69% | zero invalid | | Decode-aware up only vs fresh baseline | -0.22% | -1.68% | zero invalid | | Alignment-aware up only vs reverse-order baseline | +3.95% | -2.86% | zero invalid | | Full-path v1 vs baseline | +4.86% | -2.91% | 0.5% invalid in one run | | Corrected dense full-path v2 vs baseline | +10.04% | -6.64% | zero invalid; 3-run rejection screen | | Dense full-path v2 + config-selection cache vs fresh baseline | -4.50% | +5.30% | zero invalid; initial non-bracketed 3-run screen | | Dense v2 + cache, graph capped at 16 | +6.94% | -2.37% | inconclusive: parallel-64 ran eager and baselines drifted | | Dense v2 + cache, default H200 graphs | **-6.12%** | **+3.15%** | zero invalid; fresh A/B/A acceptance | The decode-aware searches added M=1,4,16,32,64,128 entries, used 100 real routed-expert tensors covering all 128 experts, and matched up/down `BLOCK_SIZE_M`. A conservative follow-up fixed decode `BLOCK_SIZE_M=16` to reduce expert padding and route-alignment overhead. Neither approach produced a serving-positive table. A reverse-order baseline recovered its original performance, ruling out simple node drift. The first full-path search included route alignment, padding, both projections, `relu2`, and combine, but its synthetic benchmark modeled the non-gated Nemotron up projection at twice its real width. The corrected search used the exact serving shapes (`w1=[128,1856,2688]`, `w2=[128,2688,1856]`), added the previously omitted baseline dimensions, and tuned 26 observed serving token sizes from M=1 through M=8192. It evaluated 6,674 valid candidates, produced exact output matches at every size, and measured isolated reductions from 1.48% to 35.77%. Its three-run serving screen nevertheless regressed median latency by 10.04% and normalized output throughput by 6.64%. An actual SGLang trace exposed the missing cost and the limited end-to-end headroom. Across the complete 12-step trace, v2 reduced total `fused_moe_kernel` GPU time by 17.77%, but that number includes non-steady work. In steady decode, fused-MoE time fell only from 7.867 ms to 7.468 ms (-5.08%). Fused MoE was 62.8% of steady GPU-active time, so Amdahl's law predicts about a 3.19% reduction in GPU-active time; the trace measured 3.10%. Meanwhile, uncached CPU decode-step time increased by 0.66%. `try_get_optimal_moe_config` CPU time increased from 2.64 ms to 13.99 ms because each of the 23 MoE layers scanned all 26 keys for both projections. Caching the nearest config removes that repeated Python work: | Controlled 64-request test | Baseline median | v2 median | v2 delta | |---|---:|---:|---:| | Before lookup cache | 1,784.8 tok/s | 1,757.2 tok/s | -1.54% | | With lookup cache | 1,816.3 tok/s | 1,817.8 tok/s | +0.08% | The initial cache-aware three-run GSM8K screen measured: - Median latency: 17.186 s baseline, 16.413 s v2 (**-4.50%**) - Median output throughput: 1,074.6 tok/s baseline, 1,131.6 tok/s v2 (**+5.30%**) - Mean output throughput: **+2.46%** - Invalid outputs: **0%** An initial fresh A/B/A on a new two-H200 iDev appeared inconclusive: | Phase | Median latency | Median output throughput | Invalid | |---|---:|---:|---:| | Baseline A | 16.657 s | 1,097.7 tok/s | up to 0.5% in one run | | Tuned v2 + cache | 17.101 s | 1,098.3 tok/s | 0% | | Baseline A2 | 15.326 s | 1,152.3 tok/s | 0% | The post baseline was 7.99% faster in median latency and 4.97% higher in median throughput than the pre baseline, confirming substantial run-order drift. Tuned was effectively tied with baseline A on throughput (+0.06%) and 2.67% slower on latency. The arithmetic comparison against the average of the two baselines is +6.94% latency and -2.37% throughput, but that is not a valid causal estimate when the baseline itself moves this much. One tuned run also stalled at 26.025 seconds and 717.4 tokens/s; excluding that outlier, the other two tuned runs still show no meaningful throughput gain over baseline A. That experiment had `--cuda-graph-max-bs-decode 16` hard-coded while serving 64 concurrent requests, so its high-concurrency decode path ran eagerly. Removing the manual cap resolves the H200 TP1 default to max batch 256, clamped by this model's request pool to 241. SGLang captured `[1,2,4,8,12,16,24,...,240,241]`; all measured decode batches used CUDA graphs. Capture consumed 0.61 GB and left 19.64 GB available. The corrected default-graph A/B/A measured: | Phase | Median latency | Median output throughput | Invalid | |---|---:|---:|---:| | Baseline A | 11.318 s | 1,648.9 tok/s | 0% | | Tuned v2 + cache | 10.602 s | 1,703.4 tok/s | 0% | | Baseline A2 | 11.269 s | 1,653.8 tok/s | 0% | Relative to the average of the two bracketing baselines, tuned v2 reduced median latency by 6.12% and increased median output throughput by 3.15%. Baseline A2 differed from baseline A by only -0.43% latency and +0.30% throughput, so the prior order-drift problem did not recur. Fixed 128-token decode sweeps show where the table helps: | Client concurrency | Tuned vs bracket-average baseline | |---:|---:| | 64 | -0.55% throughput | | 128 | -0.19% throughput | | 256 | **+17.64% throughput** | The 256-client run used the server's maximum 241 active requests with 15 queued. This agrees with the isolated full-path result: the dense table is roughly neutral at fixed 64/128-request decode but substantially faster near the M=192–256 configurations, while the variable-length GSM8K workload gains 3.15% overall. The model is not corrupted: all 14 user-NFS weight shards and the tokenizer, config, index, generation config, and chat template are byte-identical to the canonical ELR publication at `/shared/public/elr-models/nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Lightning-30B-A3B-BF16/ce38b6ab8b252b4b8ee7165b4605e93191cafd73`. **Decision:** retain the corrected 26-point table and bounded nearest-config cache in the draft PR. Under SGLang's actual default H200 decode-graph path, the combined change provides a stable end-to-end GSM8K gain and a large high-batch fixed-decode gain. Keep the PR in draft for reviewer assessment of the config-cache runtime change and the model-specific table. ## Environment - GPU: NVIDIA H200 - GPUs available: 2 - Torch: `2.11.0+cu130` - CUDA runtime: 13.0 - Triton: 3.6.0 - SGLang tuning commit: `c2c1c4d3ebc42402264002f6ec57f90fee58c30c` - Token counts: 256, 512, 1024 - Validation repetitions: 3 baseline and 3 tuned per shape ## Results | TP | Tokens | Baseline (us) | Tuned (us) | Speedup | Latency reduction | |---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | 1 | 256 | 1435.44 | 930.48 | 1.543x | 35.18% | | 1 | 512 | 1550.47 | 967.20 | 1.603x | 37.62% | | 1 | 1024 | 1694.77 | 1023.66 | 1.656x | 39.60% | | 2 | 256 | 734.74 | 493.07 | 1.490x | 32.89% | | 2 | 512 | 780.75 | 529.32 | 1.475x | 32.20% | | 2 | 1024 | 845.91 | 548.78 | 1.541x | 35.13% | The TP2 per-rank config was also run concurrently on both H200s. Both ranks selected the same configs; their measured means were within 0.6% to 1.0%. ## Reproduction commands The upstream tuner imports Ray only for scheduling. Ray was not available in the test environment, so the same worker was executed directly by `tuning_fused_moe_triton_no_ray.py`, one process per GPU. ```bash ROOT=/shared/user/vjhaveri/sglang-h200-tuning VENV=/shared/user/qwen35-9ms-sla/venvs/sglang-v0.5.16-cu130 MODEL=/shared/user/vjhaveri/sglang-h200-model-configs/nemotron35-lightning RESULTS=/shared/user/vjhaveri/sglang-h200-tuning-results export PATH="$VENV/bin:$PATH" export PYTHONPATH="$ROOT/python:$ROOT/benchmark/kernels/fused_moe_triton" export CPATH="/shared/user/qwen35-9ms-sla/system-deps/python3-devel/root/usr/include/python3.12${CPATH:+:$CPATH}" ``` Full TP1 and TP2 searches: ```bash mkdir -p "$RESULTS/nemotron-tp1" "$RESULTS/nemotron-tp2" ( cd "$RESULTS/nemotron-tp1" CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 \ TRITON_CACHE_DIR="$RESULTS/cache-nemotron-tp1/triton" \ TORCHINDUCTOR_CACHE_DIR="$RESULTS/cache-nemotron-tp1/torch" \ "$VENV/bin/python" /shared/user/vjhaveri/tuning_fused_moe_triton_no_ray.py \ --model "$MODEL" \ --tp-size 1 \ --batch-sizes 256 512 1024 \ --tune \ 2>&1 | tee tune.log ) & ( cd "$RESULTS/nemotron-tp2" CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=1 \ TRITON_CACHE_DIR="$RESULTS/cache-nemotron-tp2/triton" \ TORCHINDUCTOR_CACHE_DIR="$RESULTS/cache-nemotron-tp2/torch" \ "$VENV/bin/python" /shared/user/vjhaveri/tuning_fused_moe_triton_no_ray.py \ --model "$MODEL" \ --tp-size 2 \ --batch-sizes 256 512 1024 \ --tune \ 2>&1 | tee tune.log ) & wait ``` Baseline and tuned validation, repeated three times for each TP size: ```bash for repeat in 1 2 3; do CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 "$VENV/bin/python" \ /shared/user/vjhaveri/tuning_fused_moe_triton_no_ray.py \ --model "$MODEL" --tp-size 1 --batch-sizes 256 512 1024 \ 2>&1 | tee "$RESULTS/nemotron-tp1/baseline-repeat-$repeat.log" CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=1 "$VENV/bin/python" \ /shared/user/vjhaveri/tuning_fused_moe_triton_no_ray.py \ --model "$MODEL" --tp-size 2 --batch-sizes 256 512 1024 \ 2>&1 | tee "$RESULTS/nemotron-tp2/baseline-repeat-$repeat.log" done CONFIG_DIR="$ROOT/python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/moe_runner/triton_utils/configs/triton_3_6_0" cp "$RESULTS/nemotron-tp1/E=128,N=1856,device_name=NVIDIA_H200.json" "$CONFIG_DIR/" cp "$RESULTS/nemotron-tp2/E=128,N=928,device_name=NVIDIA_H200.json" "$CONFIG_DIR/" for repeat in 1 2 3; do CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 "$VENV/bin/python" \ /shared/user/vjhaveri/tuning_fused_moe_triton_no_ray.py \ --model "$MODEL" --tp-size 1 --batch-sizes 256 512 1024 \ 2>&1 | tee "$RESULTS/nemotron-tp1/tuned-repeat-$repeat.log" CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=1 "$VENV/bin/python" \ /shared/user/vjhaveri/tuning_fused_moe_triton_no_ray.py \ --model "$MODEL" --tp-size 2 --batch-sizes 256 512 1024 \ 2>&1 | tee "$RESULTS/nemotron-tp2/tuned-repeat-$repeat.log" done ``` Concurrent dual-H200 TP2 per-rank validation: ```bash for gpu in 0 1; do ( CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES="$gpu" "$VENV/bin/python" \ /shared/user/vjhaveri/tuning_fused_moe_triton_no_ray.py \ --model "$MODEL" --tp-size 2 --batch-sizes 256 512 1024 \ >"$RESULTS/nemotron-tp2-dual-rank-gpu$gpu.log" 2>&1 ) & done wait ``` Patch checks: ```bash git diff --check git apply --check --reverse \ /shared/user/vjhaveri/sglang-h200-tuning-results/nemotron35-lightning-h200-configs.patch ```

signals.title: [Test] Tighten the DCP HiCache KL threshold to 0.005
signals.text: ## Motivation `test_unified_radix_cache_kl_dcp.py` (Kimi Linear + DCP4 + HiCache L2 + UnifiedRadixCache) has gated at `kl_threshold = 0.01` since it landed in #33112. Every other fp8 hybrid cache-hit KL case in the same directory gates at 0.005: | case | threshold | | --- | --- | | `test_unified_radix_cache_kl_mamba.py` | 0.005 | | `test_unified_radix_cache_kl_cp.py` | 0.005 | | `test_unified_radix_cache_hicache_pp_kl.py` | 0.005 | | `test_unified_radix_cache_kl_dsv4.py` | 0.005 | | `test_unified_radix_cache_kl_dcp.py` | **0.01** | A looser threshold tolerates float noise and small state bugs alike, and the thing this case exists to catch — a missing DCP logical→physical translation handing back another rank's KV on a cache hit — is exactly what slack hides. This PR tries the house value so the DCP translation path is held to the same bar as the non-DCP ones. This is an experiment: the point is to find out whether the DCP path actually holds at 0.005 in CI. If it flakes, the measured headroom tells us either to keep 0.01 with a comment recording why (the way the mamba case documents its own 0.003 → 0.005 bump) or that there is real divergence worth chasing. ## Modifications One line: `kl_threshold` 0.01 → 0.005 in `test/registered/radix_cache/unified_radix_tree/test_unified_radix_cache_kl_dcp.py`. No source changes. ## Accuracy Tests No model-output changes. The case is registered as `stage="extra-b"`, `runner_config="4-gpu-b200"`, so it needs the extra CI stage to actually exercise the new threshold. ## Speed Tests and Profiling N/A — test threshold only. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32416857232](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32416857232)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32416856827](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32416856827)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32416857265](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32416857265)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [AMD][CI] Add the Qwen3.8 MXFP4 MI35x nightly
signals.text: ## Motivation [Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B-FP8) shipped with [day-0 SGLang support](https://www.lmsys.org/blog/2026-08-12-qwen3-8-day0-support/) and a [day-0 AMD recipe](https://www.amd.com/en/developer/resources/technical-articles/2026/day-0-support-for-qwen-3-8-on-amd-instinct-gpus.html), but the AMD nightly has no coverage for it. It reuses the Qwen3.5 architecture (`Qwen3_5MoeForCausalLM`), so it runs with no model-code changes — which is exactly why nothing guards it: a change to the shared hybrid path or the AITER MXFP4 MoE kernels can silently degrade it on ROCm. FP8 is ~2.4 TB against 8 x 288 GB per MI355X node, so there is no single-node FP8 recipe; single-node means FP4. The job serves [`amd/Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B-Quark-MXFP4`](https://huggingface.co/amd/Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B-Quark-MXFP4), AMD's Quark quantization of the FP8 checkpoint. Only routed experts are quantized, so AMD measures the same 97.49 GSM8K as the FP8 baseline — this job gates the FP8 checkpoint's quality in the shape that fits one node. ## Modifications **`test/registered/amd/accuracy/mi35x/test_qwen38_mxfp4_eval_mi35x.py`** (new) — two phases in the `nightly-amd-8-gpu-mi35x-qwen38-mxfp4` suite: `test_a_gsm8k_accuracy` (TP8 GSM8K, gated at 0.93) and `test_b_serving_perf` (batch 1/8/16/64 at 1024 in / 1024 out). Both launch from one `SERVER_ARGS` reproducing the AMD model card recipe, so the throughput numbers describe exactly the configuration the accuracy gate covers. Perf is skipped unless accuracy passed. Two flags are load-bearing rather than defaults: `--page-size 1` (on HIP the default becomes 64 when the container sets `SGLANG_AITER_KV_CACHE_LAYOUT=vectorized_5d`) and `--attention-backend aiter` (no arg override picks a backend for this architecture on ROCm). The server runs with no `--reasoning-parser` so a `<think>` block still scores under the last-number extractor. **`.github/workflows/nightly-test-amd-rocm720.yml`** — new `nightly-8-gpu-mi35x-qwen38-mxfp4-rocm720` job on `linux-mi35x-gpu-8`. ROCm 7.2 only: MXFP4 needs gfx95x. Also removes the two Qwen3-235B jobs from this nightly; `Qwen3MoeForCausalLM` is gated per-commit by `test/registered/quant/test_quark_mxfp4.py` (gsm8k >= 0.89, on both ROCm lanes) and runs nightly at 30B-A3B scale, so this frees two 8-GPU jobs per night. No file under `test/` is touched by that removal, and `nightly-test-amd.yml` (ROCm 7.0) is left alone since that lane is being retired. **`test/run_suite.py`** — register the new suite. **`scripts/ci/amd/check_hf_cache_space.sh`** (new) — run [#32196787596](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32196787596) died 40 minutes into the download on ENOSPC, and free space was never reported anywhere in its log. This records it before the download, says whether the checkpoint is already cached, and clears stale artifacts via the existing `scripts/ci/utils/cleanup_hf_cache.py`. It deletes no other checkpoints: `/sgl-data` is a 15 TB volume shared by the whole AMD fleet at 100% used, and an eviction attempt removed 48 of them while free space went from 298 MB to 227 MB. Never fails the job. **`scripts/ci/utils/amd_cache_audit.py`** (new) — joins `register_amd_ci` tests to the checkpoints they name and the jobs that dispatch them, counting the per-commit `pr-test-amd*.yml` workflows and not just nightly. 289 of 429 AMD registrations are per-commit only and run on runners sharing the same PVC, so a nightly-only join badly overstates what is reclaimable. `--runner` scopes to a cluster by the dispatching job's `runs-on` label; suite -> models extraction is reused from `list_stage_models.py`. ## Accuracy Tests **[Run #32313140175](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32313140175) — green. GSM8K 0.973** against the 0.930 gate and AMD's published 0.9749. Both phases ran, neither skipped. The gate sits ~5% below AMD's number, the same relative tolerance the sibling Qwen3.5 MI35x evals allow (`rtol: 0.05`). Caveat: the checkpoint was already cached on that runner, so the run exercised load-and-serve but not a cold download. A confirmation run on the current head is in flight at [#32424018092](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32424018092); it is the first to exercise the cache-check step, which the green run predates. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Published to the job summary rather than asserted, so it reports regressions without becoming a flaky gate. Measured on 8x MI355X, TP8, 1024 in / 1024 out: | batch size | latency (s) | input tput (tok/s) | output tput (tok/s) | ITL (ms) | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | 1 | 14.83 | 6961.62 | 69.73 | 14.34 | | 8 | 18.48 | 20833.04 | 452.87 | 17.67 | | 16 | 21.94 | 21758.80 | 773.39 | 20.69 | | 64 | 37.74 | 21993.04 | 1885.58 | 33.94 | Overridable via `NIGHTLY_BATCH_SIZES` / `NIGHTLY_INPUT_LENS` / `NIGHTLY_OUTPUT_LENS`. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). — the Qwen3.8 cookbook page already documents this recipe. - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process). 2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers. 3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so. 4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32426781948](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32426781948)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32426781690](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32426781690)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #32426781946](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32426781946)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [AMD] Add a probe that verifies torch.profiler captures HIP-graph kernels
signals.text: ## Motivation AMD/Silo report that on every `lmsysorg/sglang*` ROCm 7.2 image (v0.5.12 through v0.5.17, `*-rocm720-*`), `torch.profiler` traces contain no GPU kernels for work launched through hipGraph, and they have been swapping `libamdhip64.so.7.2.70200` / `libroctracer64.so.4.1.70200` for the 7.2.4 versions to work around it. The cause is upstream and already fixed: - ROCTracer can fail to report kernel operations: [ROCm/ROCm#6102](https://github.com/ROCm/ROCm/issues/6102), closed with "Resolved in ROCm 7.2.2". - ROCm 7.2.0's HIP runtime also has a wrong doorbell index in `dispatchGenericAqlPacketBatch` (the graph batch-dispatch path) plus an InterceptQueue ring-buffer heap corruption, both fixed in 7.2.1 ([pytorch/pytorch#177873](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/pull/177873)). That matches the `CUDAGraph::replay` deadlock inside `libamdhip64.so.7.2.70200` seen in our own CI (#34452) — the same bug class surfacing as a hang instead of a gap. - The 7.2.4 bases carry the fixed libraries: `rocm/pytorch:rocm7.2.4_*` ships `libamdhip64.so.7.2.70204` and `libroctracer64.so.4.1.70204` (`hip-runtime-amd` 7.2.26015.70200 -> 7.2.53211.70204, `roctracer` 4.1.70200 -> 4.1.70204). #30984 has since landed the `rocm724` flavors, so images with the fixed ROCm are being published — and the measurement in [this comment](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/35390#issuecomment-5350686772) shows why that is not the end of it: the torch wheel vendors its own HIP and roctracer under `torch/lib` and `libtorch_hip.so` carries `RPATH $ORIGIN`, so a 7.2.4 image still profiles through 7.2.0 libraries unless they are preloaded, and `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` cannot override an `RPATH`. Reading the ROCm version in the image tells you nothing about what `torch.profiler` is using. What is missing is a way to tell those states apart, for these images and for any future base or torch bump. Nothing in CI can currently tell a working profiler from a broken one: `test/registered/profiling/test_start_profile.py` only asserts that the trace directory is non-empty, so an image whose traces contain no GPU kernels passes it, and since #34452 the profiling suite runs without CUDA graphs on ROCm, so it never exercises the replay path at all. ## Modifications ### `scripts/ci/amd/check_hip_graph_profiling.py` Captures a graph, replays it under `torch.profiler`, and counts the device events that reach the exported trace against the number of dispatches it asked for. Counting matters: the reported loss is partial (448 of 512 kernels on 7.2.0), and a 4-node graph is traced correctly there, so both a "non-empty trace" threshold and a small graph would call the broken runtime healthy. The default workload is therefore 64 nodes replayed 8 times, and any shortfall fails with the count. An eager control run separates "this runtime cannot trace graph replay" from "this runtime cannot trace anything", and each phase runs in its own process under a timeout because ROCm 7.2.0 can wedge inside `hipGraphLaunch` rather than merely lose events. It also reports the **paths** of the HIP and tracing libraries torch mapped, not their sonames, flags any that did not come from the ROCm install, and prints the `LD_PRELOAD` that switches them — otherwise this failure reads as an unfixable image rather than a load-order problem. `--print-ld-preload` exposes that value for callers that must set it before the process starts. It also warns when the device reports no marketing name, the symptom of an image without libdrm-amdgpu. It depends on nothing but torch and the HIP runtime, so it qualifies any image or base image: A rocm724 image as shipped, which is the case the comment measured: ``` torch 2.11.0+rocm7.2 (hip 7.2.41134), rocm 7.2.4 device: 'AMD Instinct MI355X' (gfx950) hip/tracing libs: /opt/venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages/torch/lib/libamdhip64.so, .../libroctracer64.so eager launch: 512/512 kernel events, 9000 us device time, 12000 trace events graph replay: 448/512 kernel events, 7800 us device time, 12000 trace events note: torch is using its own HIP/roctracer, not the ROCm install's: .../torch/lib/libamdhip64.so, .../torch/lib/libroctracer64.so export LD_PRELOAD="/opt/rocm/lib/libamdhip64.so.7.2.70204:/opt/rocm/lib/libroctracer64.so.4.1.70204..." must be set before the process starts; LD_LIBRARY_PATH cannot override the RPATH the wheel's libtorch_hip.so carries VERDICT: FAIL -- eager launches are traced in full but 64 of 512 graph-replay kernels never reached the trace. ... ``` With that preload it reaches `512/512` and `VERDICT: PASS`. Not registered in the AMD suites here: on a rocm720 image it is expected to fail and, per #34452, can take the process down with it. #35398 runs it against the published rocm724 images instead. ### `test/registered/unit/ci/test_hip_graph_profiling_probe.py` The probe's value is that a red run says *which* failure happened: nothing traceable at all, a wedged `hipGraphLaunch`, or kernels lost under graph replay. A GPU job can only ever exercise whichever case its image is in, so the mapping is driven on CPU with canned phase results instead — every verdict, the exit codes, the ROCm/ROCm#6102 citation appearing only for the untraced-graph case, the marketing-name warning, and the trace parser, where counting a host-only trace as device work would turn the whole check into a false pass. Registered as `base-a-test-cpu`, 9 tests, no GPU. ### `docs/docs/developer_guide/benchmark_and_profiling.mdx` Document the gap, how to check an image, that the `rocm724` tags install the fix but need the `LD_PRELOAD` to actually use it, and the `--disable-cuda-graph` fallback where preloading is not an option, with the caveat that decode numbers collected that way exclude the replay path. ## Accuracy Tests No model or kernel code changes. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Not applicable to the change itself; it measures whether profiling works rather than changing performance. ## Test plan Verified locally without a GPU: - The new unit test passes (16 tests): every verdict path and exit code, the partial-loss shortfall, vendored-runtime detection, the preload value (real files, not the symlinks), and the trace parser. - Trace parsing additionally checked against a real `export_chrome_trace` output, including a capitalized `Kernel` category. - The timeout path's process-group kill verified against a wedged child. - On a host with no GPU the probe reports `environment: unusable -- no GPU visible to torch` and exits 1. - `scripts/lint/check_registered_tests.py`, `check_no_bare_pytest_main.py`, black, isort and codespell all pass. Needs a GPU host — the decisive measurement, and it needs no SGLang build: ```bash GPU="--device=/dev/kfd --device=/dev/dri --group-add video --security-opt seccomp=unconfined" # ROCm 7.2.0 runtime: expected FAIL (reproduces the report) docker run --rm $GPU -v "$PWD:/w" -w /w \ rocm/pytorch:rocm7.2_ubuntu22.04_py3.10_pytorch_release_2.9.1 \ python3 scripts/ci/amd/check_hip_graph_profiling.py # ROCm 7.2.4 runtime: expected PASS docker run --rm $GPU -v "$PWD:/w" -w /w \ rocm/pytorch:rocm7.2.4_ubuntu22.04_py3.10_pytorch_release_2.9.1 \ python3 scripts/ci/amd/check_hip_graph_profiling.py ``` Same torch 2.9.1, same probe, only the ROCm patch level differs. Then run it in a published `*-rocm724-*` image (expected PASS) and a `*-rocm720-*` image (expected FAIL). ## Measured on hardware Run against today's published image (`rocm/sgl-dev:v0.5.17-rocm724-mi35x-20260820`) on an MI355X, via a dispatch of the nightly workflow with this branch's probe and #35398's job ([run](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32337394284)): | run | mapped HIP/roctracer | eager | graph replay | verdict | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | image default | `torch/lib/libamdhip64.so`, `torch/lib/libroctracer64.so` | 512/512 | **448/512** | FAIL | | `LD_PRELOAD` of the image's 7.2.4 | `/opt/rocm-7.2.4/lib/…70204` | 512/512 | **512/512** | PASS | That reproduces the numbers in [the review comment](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/35390#issuecomment-5350686772) exactly, on the artifact users pull. Also confirmed there: `torch.cuda.get_device_name(0)` is `'AMD Instinct MI355X'` (libdrm is fine), torch reports `hip 7.2.26015` — the 7.2.0 build — inside a ROCm 7.2.4 image, and `--print-ld-preload` resolved to the same value by hand-checking `/opt/rocm/lib`. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). <!-- The probe is the test; registering it in the AMD suites requires images on a ROCm 7.2.2 or newer runtime. --> - [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). <!-- N/A --> - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process). 2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers. 3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so. 4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:no_entry_sign: [Run #32421463756](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32421463756)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32422816691](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32422816691)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #32421463820](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32421463820)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [AMD] Verify the nightly ROCm 7.2.4 images trace HIP-graph kernels
signals.text: ## Motivation #30984 landed the `rocm724` flavors and the nightly now publishes them to `rocm/sgl-dev` and `lmsysorg/sglang-rocm`. Those flavors exist because ROCm 7.2.0 drops kernel-dispatch events for work submitted through `hipGraphLaunch` ([ROCm/ROCm#6102](https://github.com/ROCm/ROCm/issues/6102), fixed in 7.2.2), which is what AMD/Silo hit when profiling SGLang decoding on every `*-rocm720-*` image. Nothing verifies that the published images actually restore it. A trace with no GPU kernels in it still looks like a successful profile, `test/registered/profiling/test_start_profile.py` only asserts the trace directory is non-empty, and since #34452 the profiling suite runs without CUDA graphs on ROCm, so CI never exercises the replay path at all. A future base bump could quietly take the fix away again. ## Modifications One job in `release-docker-amd-rocm720-nightly.yml`. After publish, each `rocm724` flavor is probed on the GPU it targets — gfx942 on MI300X, gfx950 on MI355X — because the behaviour lives in the HIP runtime rather than in SGLang, so it is worth confirming per device generation. The job pulls the tag the publish job recorded in its artifact, starts the standard CI container against it, and runs `scripts/ci/amd/check_hip_graph_profiling.py` inside the image. No dependency install: the point is to exercise the image's own torch and HIP runtime, which is what was just published. Gating details: - **Per leg, not per workflow.** A `rocm720` leg failing in publish must not stop the `rocm724` images from being checked, so the job does not require all of publish to succeed. A `rocm724` leg that never published has no artifact and fails at the download — the same behaviour the mirror job below documents. - **`rocm720` legs are excluded**, since they are expected to fail; a dispatch selecting a single `rocm720` arch skips the job. - **`job_select` is respected**, so a `publish`-only dispatch does not run it. - **`job_select=verify_profiling` + `probe_image`** qualifies an already-published tag without a rebuild; pair it with `gpu_arch` to choose the GPU. That is the quickest way to answer the question for one image, and it is how this should be run first. - The container is removed at the end, since these runners are shared with the AMD test suites and it would otherwise hold VRAM until something else reclaims it. This verifies after publish rather than gating it, so the daily images are not held behind a GPU runner queue. A red leg means the day's `rocm724` image traces nothing under graph replay and should not be recommended for profiling. Turning it into a real gate means splitting the publish job's `rocm/sgl-dev` and `lmsysorg` pushes, which is worth doing separately if you want that. ## Accuracy Tests No model or kernel code changes; this adds a verification job to a release workflow. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Not applicable. The job measures whether profiling works on the published image. ## Test plan - `actionlint` reports nothing on the new job; the only findings in the file are the pre-existing self-hosted runner labels and `docker/login-action@v2` in the publish and mirror jobs. - Job names pass `scripts/lint/check_workflow_job_names.py`. - The job's gating was simulated across the combinations that matter — schedule, `all`/`all`, `publish`-only, a `rocm720` arch, a single `rocm724` arch, `verify_profiling` with a skipped publish, and publish `failure` vs `cancelled` — confirming it runs exactly the intended legs in each. - The probe itself is unit-tested in #35390 (trace parsing, every verdict path) and validated for timeout handling and no-GPU behaviour. `workflow_dispatch` only offers a workflow that exists on the default branch, so this cannot be exercised until it merges. Once it has, the fastest check is one already-published image on one GPU: ```bash gh workflow run release-docker-amd-rocm720-nightly.yml --ref main \ -f job_select=verify_profiling \ -f probe_image=rocm/sgl-dev:v0.5.17-rocm724-mi35x-20260820 \ -f gpu_arch=gfx950-rocm724 ``` Expected `VERDICT: PASS`, against the same probe failing on a `*-rocm720-*` tag. A full `gh workflow run ... --ref main` then covers build plus both GPUs. ## Notes for reviewers - Depends on #35390, which adds the probe script this job runs. Merge that first. - This PR previously proposed its own `rocm724` stages, nightly workflow, release-matrix entry, and torch Triton-pin patch. #30984 landed all four, so only the verification remains. ## Measured on hardware Dispatched against a branch carrying this job plus #35390's probe, targeting today's published image ([run](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32337394284), 4.5 minutes end to end on `linux-mi35x-gpu-1`): - `publish` and `push_local_registry` skipped, one `verify_profiling (gfx950-rocm724)` leg, artifact download skipped because `probe_image` was set — the gating behaved as intended. - Image default: `graph replay: 448/512` → step outcome `failure`, job still green (`continue-on-error`), and the summary records it as `**Image default** (failure)`. - signals.title: [GDN] Route Qwen TP4 decode and verify rows through Cake
signals.text: ## Summary - lazily load the optional public FlashInfer Cake GDN decode package on SM100/SM103 - fail closed on unsupported dtype, layout, shape, stride, state-pool, or graph-capture combinations - preserve caller-stream and CUDA graph semantics with preallocated workspace/state and cached FP32 dt bias - route the actual Qwen3-Next TP4 BF16 decode and verify rows through the promoted tile16 full-warp kernels ## Qualification - rebased onto current SGLang main b814a7e812fb9367d994af307085bd30de329f96 - B200/SM100, job 3752127 on umbriel-b200-037: 9 tests passed and 26 subtests passed, including actual TP4 eager and CUDA Graph paths - GB300/SM103, job 510532 on nvl72d093-T03: 9 tests passed and 26 subtests passed, including the same paths - exact route IDs: cake.gdn_decode.indexed_bf16_t1.tile16_fullwarp and cake.gdn_decode.indexed_bf16_verify_t4.tile16_fullwarp - exact TP4 shapes: B=4,T=1,H=4,HV=8 and B=2/3/5/8,T=4,H=4,HV=8; adjacent B=4,T=4 and every unmeasured layout fail closed - same-environment cold-L2 CUPTI kernel A/B versus live FlashInfer 8044d94bf9: - B200 T1 0.003296 vs 0.003472 ms (1.053x), T4 0.006400 vs 0.006944 ms (1.085x), geometric mean 1.069x - GB300 T1 0.003040 vs 0.003296 ms (1.084x), T4 0.006304 vs 0.006736 ms (1.069x), geometric mean 1.076x - correctness uses fixed BF16 atol=rtol=1e-2; dual-arch public ABI/stream/graph and sanitizer gates pass - exact Qwen3-Next 80B FP8 TP4/MTP model replay, four GB300s, job 3137824: 4/4 tests pass; cache-hit KL 0.0007701/0.0017106 versus the fixed 0.0035 ceiling; all four TP ranks record the Cake T4 route during CUDA Graph capture - attributed serving ABBA, four GB300s, job 3137849: all eight measured 128-request rounds complete; four-round median output/total throughput 1.000280x, mean/median TPOT 1.003214x/1.005037x, and mean TTFT 0.987693x versus FlashInfer (the ~1.25% TTFT regression is retained explicitly) Current-head real-model evidence is recorded below. Review and merge are intentionally deferred in this evidence-only phase. ## Current-head decision evidence This replay uses FlashInfer #4581 head `4215a24cb` and supersedes the earlier `45b60f98` jobs/comment. Review and merge are intentionally deferred. ### Environment and attribution - real Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B-Instruct-FP8 weights, revision `c5f5f263bdd5cc134092897864e8905d8fe7b928` - four NVIDIA GB300 CC 10.3 GPUs on healthy replacement nodes; SGLang `ee8378ad4`, Torch `2.13.0a0+nv26.07`, CUDA 13.3 - `sglang-kernel 0.4.6.post1+cu130`, `sgl-deep-gemm 0.1.5.post3`, `apache-tvm-ffi 0.1.11` - source-matched FlashInfer JIT in both arms; the released image AOT package is removed equally. Candidate phases route all four TP ranks through Cake; baseline phases route none ### Accuracy and model behavior Both arm orders run the full 1,319-row GSM8K file with five fixed exemplars, so 1,314 answers are scored, plus decode/prefill cache-hit KL and prefix-cache branching: | Job / order | FlashInfer | Cake | Paired delta | FlashInfer KL | Cake KL | |---|---:|---:|---:|---|---| | `516222`, baseline → Cake | 1256/1314 (0.955860) | 1248/1314 (0.949772) | -8 / -0.608828 pp | 0.00136385 / 0.00157485 | 0.00134804 / 0.00159145 | | `516345`, Cake → baseline | 1249/1314 (0.950533) | 1248/1314 (0.949772) | -1 / -0.076104 pp | 0.00078810 / 0.00255420 | 0.00073162 / 0.00252816 | All four tests pass in every arm, all scores exceed the fixed `0.93` gate, and every KL value is below `0.0035`. Cake's exact score reproduces across node and order, but exact no-drop is false. The baseline itself varies by seven answers, so the first paired eight-answer delta cannot be assigned wholly to Cake. ### Uninstrumented E2E A/B Job `516223` uses baseline/Cake/Cake/baseline order, counterbalanced workload order, eight rounds per arm/workload, and 20,000 deterministic round-bootstrap resamples. Every request completes. | Workload | Metric | FlashInfer | Cake | Speedup (95% CI) | Decision | |---|---|---:|---:|---:|---| | 128 prompts, 512 in / 256 out, c=8 | output throughput | 1231.754012 tok/s | 1237.596662 tok/s | 1.004743x [0.998292, 1.020776] | indistinguishable | | | mean E2E latency | 839.608126 ms | 832.389779 ms | 1.008672x [0.999705, 1.020929] | indistinguishable | | | mean TPOT | 6.216159 ms | 6.113625 ms | 1.016771x [1.001588, 1.026764] | speedup | | 64 prompts, 128 in / 1024 out, c=8 | output throughput | 1403.321505 tok/s | 1412.172752 tok/s | 1.006307x [0.994657, 1.042125] | indistinguishable | | | mean E2E latency | 2834.498442 ms | 2840.753832 ms | 0.997798x [0.986704, 1.034864] | indistinguishable | | | mean TPOT | 5.561249 ms | 5.532944 ms | 1.005116x [0.993362, 1.016897] | indistinguishable | Dynamic B2/B3/B5 coverage removes the former statistically resolved decode-heavy throughput regression. Balanced mean TPOT has a resolved gain, and both aggregate-throughput point estimates are positive, but both throughput confidence intervals cross 1.0. Therefore this head passes the fixed model correctness gates but does not establish exact GSM8K no-drop or a general statistically resolved E2E throughput speedup. ## Dependencies - FlashInfer: https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/4581 Supersedes #35328 because repository rules prohibit force-pushing its protected head branch after rebase. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32381879935](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32381879935)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32381879713](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32381879713)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32381880059](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32381880059)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [Fix] Land the decode mamba checkpoint depth on the tree page under DCP
signals.text: ## Motivation A donated mamba checkpoint is only reusable at a depth the radix tree can name. `cache_finished_req` / `cache_unfinished_req` floor the insert key with `page_aligned(tree_page)`, so a checkpoint taken off that grid is attached to the *preceding* node while its state already covers tokens past it — a later request matching that node resumes the linear-attention recurrence mid-stream and then re-consumes those tokens. Silent, no assert, wrong output. #34808 fixed this for the **extend** path with `mamba_checkpoint_grid(tree_page)`, and scoped itself explicitly: > Only the prefill donation depth changes here. Decode tracking keeps its own `--mamba-track-interval` grid. That decode grid does not land on the tree page. `--mamba-track-interval` has one guard, `assert mamba_track_interval % view.page_size == 0` (`server_args.py`), against the **configured** page — and is never resolved anywhere (`grep` over `arg_groups/` and `configs/` is empty). Under DCP the tree allocates on `page_size * dcp_size` (`kv_cache_builder.py`: `page_size=... else token_to_kv_pool_allocator.page_size`), so that guard stops implying the invariant. The insert-time guard that would have caught this was deferred to #34760 and #34780 — **both closed, never merged** — and there is no mamba depth check on the insert in `main` today, so the misalignment stays silent. **Break condition:** `mamba_track_interval % (page_size * dcp_size) != 0`. | page | dcp | tree page | interval | | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | 64 | 4 | 256 | 256 | ok | | 64 | 8 | **512** | 256 | **broken** | | 128 | 4 | 512 | 256 | broken | | 256 | 2 | 512 | 256 | broken | Two shipped recipes are on the broken row today, both in `test_kimi_k3_b300.py`: `TestKimiK3B300Balanced` (`--tp-size 8 --dcp-size 8 --enable-hierarchical-cache`) and `TestKimiK3B300MegaMoE` (`--dcp-size 8` + DSPARK — spec is only rejected under DCP *with* HiCache, so the mamba grid is live there too). Kimi-K3 DCP forces `cutedsl_mla`, which pins `page_size` to 64, and `KimiK3Config.text_config` is a `KimiLinearConfig` so the tree carries a `MAMBA` component. The tree pages at 512 while decode checkpoints every 256, so every odd multiple of 256 names a depth no node carries. Every other DCP hybrid config in tree is page 64 × dcp 4, where `64 * 4 == 256` — the default interval — and the two grids line up by coincidence. That is also why the DCP HiCache KL case (#35380) cannot catch this. ## Modifications `mamba_track_grid(tree_page)` beside `mamba_checkpoint_grid` — the same `lcm`, carrying the requested interval as well: ```python def mamba_track_grid(tree_page: int) -> int: return math.lcm( mamba_checkpoint_grid(tree_page), get_exec().mamba.mamba_track_interval ) ``` Read where a checkpoint depth is picked: `schedule_batch.prepare_for_decode`, the three `batch_result_processor` boundary sites, and the spec verify/prepare paths in `spec_utils`, `dspark_worker_v2`, `dflash_worker_v2`. Pure derivation — nothing is mutated, and `server_args.mamba_track_interval` keeps the value the operator typed. The tree page is a process constant, so each site only needs a live handle to the tree. `prepare_for_decode` and the spec paths take it off the batch, as the extend path already does. The batch-result processor takes it off **its own** `tree_cache`: the batch it is handed is the result-queue `copy()`, whose field list is scoped to what `process_batch_result` needs and does not carry one. Going through `mamba_checkpoint_grid` rather than just rounding onto the page keeps the decode depth chunk-aligned too, which the extend path relies on: a decode-donated depth becomes the prefix of a later extend, and `_force_track_h` asserts `i % mamba_cache_chunk_size == 0` there. Two readers stay on the raw arg because they are flush/write cadence rather than checkpoint depth: `hybrid_linear_attn_backend`'s ReplaySSM force-flush mask and Inkling's `sconv` (which holds only a `ForwardBatch`). `lcm` makes the derived grid a multiple of the raw interval, so every snapshot step is still a flush step and the flush mask's invariant survives. Note the comment at `hybrid_linear_attn_backend.py:403` says the two "fire on the same steps"; after this change they fire on nested sets of steps. `test_batch_result_processor_mamba_boundary.py` is a pre-existing test (#33477) whose hand-built `ScheduleBatch` and processor double now need a `tree_cache`, since `prepare_for_decode` did not read one before this change. Same edit #34808 made to its own double. Page and chunk are set to the interval already under test, so the derived grid stays 4 and every existing boundary expectation is unchanged. ## Accuracy Tests **Not yet measured — this is why the PR is a draft.** #34808 shipped a cold-vs-warm teacher-forced logprob comparison on a live Kimi-Linear dcp8 server for the prefill half; the decode half deserves the same evidence, and this PR currently argues from page alignment alone. An 8×B300 run on the `TestKimiK3B300Balanced` recipe, before and after, is the next step. What is verified statically: - **Cache reuse is unchanged.** The insert floors the donated depth to the tree page, so the node it lands on is `floor(min(N, floor(N/grid)·grid) / 512) · 512` — which collapses to the same `512q` under both grids (checked for every request length in [0, 4096): zero differ). Same number of cached checkpoints, same node depths, same KV prefix. What changes is *which state* is attached: previously a state that had already consumed 256 more tokens than the node it hung on. Snapshot writes into the ping-pong buffer halve on the affected recipes — less decode work, not fewer cache entries. - **Grid unchanged everywhere else:** page 64 × dcp 4, page 32 × dcp 4 (tree 128), and every non-DCP config. New CPU unit case in `test_mamba_checkpoint_depth.py`, beside #34808's extend cases since it is the same invariant from the other end. ## Speed Tests and Profiling N/A. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32304189342](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32304189342)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #32304189109](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32304189109)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32304189359](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32304189359)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [Diffusion] Support MiniMax-H3 pruned safetensors checkpoints
signals.text: ## Summary - Build on the generic diffusion GGUF support merged in #35370; this PR no longer carries a duplicate GGUF loader or GGUF tests. - Auto-detect MiniMax-H3 AdaLN-pruned BF16 and Comfy `pruned_fp8_scaled` transformer checkpoints. - Reuse the native static-FP8 linear path where possible and preserve Comfy's `full_precision_matrix_mult` semantics for layers that require dequantized computation. - Reject unsupported `pruned_int8_convrot` checkpoints before model construction instead of failing later with misleading missing-weight errors. ## Loading and compatibility - `--transformer-weights-path` accepts a local file, a direct Hugging Face file URL, or an `owner/repo/path/file.safetensors` reference. - FL2VA and Ref2VA checkpoint/model-variant mismatches are rejected explicitly. - TP, Ulysses/Ring sequence parallelism, and component offload remain available. Pruned BF16 supports FSDP; Comfy mixed-FP8 checkpoints reject FSDP because their per-layer quantization metadata cannot be represented by the current FSDP loading path. - Self-described Comfy FP8 checkpoints reject a conflicting explicit `--quantization` setting. - `quality=high` continues to require the audited official BF16 transformer rather than a replacement DiT. ## Documentation - Document pruned BF16 and scaled-FP8 loading commands, compatibility, and unsupported ConvRot checkpoints in the MiniMax-H3 cookbook. - Update the diffusion quantization matrix to distinguish generic GGUF support from the Comfy scaled-FP8 format added here. ## Verification - Inspected the published Comfy FP8 safetensors metadata: 200 per-layer format markers, including 50 `full_precision_matrix_mult` layers, with scalar weight/input scales matching the implemented dispatch. - Added focused unit coverage for checkpoint inspection and validation, Hub file resolution, per-layer FP8 dispatch, full-precision dequantized linear numerics, quantization conflicts, and TP-aware MiniMax-H3 QKV loading. - `pre-commit run --all-files` passed before the final focused change; all hooks also pass on the final changed files. - Focused tests on the exact final commit in the remote CUDA environment: `56 passed, 16 subtests passed`. - Real H100 end-to-end validation loaded the published 20,958,205,608-byte Comfy FP8 checkpoint, instantiated the 19.61 GB pruned DiT, and completed text encoding, denoising, video/audio decode, and muxing. The 2-step 1344x768 request produced 107 video frames plus stereo audio in 48.43 seconds with 21,236 MB peak VRAM. `ffprobe` reported H.264 video and 32 kHz two-channel AAC in the 4.458-second output. - The shared H100 host killed additional worker processes during NCCL initialization before model loading, so multi-GPU end-to-end validation is left to CI. The TP-specific FP8 grouped-QKV copy path is covered directly for TP1/2/4 in the focused tests. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #32356124150](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32356124150)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32356123910](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32356123910)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #32356124116](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32356124116)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [AMD] Fix gfx950 Triton compiler crash on fp8 KV-cache attention
signals.text: ## Motivation `test/registered/attention/test_verify_shared_kv.py::test_qwen3_5_fp8_kv_cache` has never passed on `stage-b-1-gpu-small-amd-mi35x` since it was added (#34517); it fails inside the Triton AMD backend, not in sglang code ([latest instance](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32166850277/job/95808413702)): ``` python3: llvm/ADT/SmallVector.h:292: Assertion `idx < size()' failed. extend_attention.py:305:0: error: Failures have been detected while processing an MLIR pass pipeline extend_attention.py:305:0: note: Pipeline failed while executing [`ConvertTritonAMDGPUToLLVM` ...] RuntimeError: PassManager::run failed ``` Only the fp8 variant fails; the bf16 variants of the same test pass. The crash is not test-specific — it is in the shared prefill kernel, so a model served on MI35x with `--kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3` **through the Triton attention backend** hits it, in decode as well as prefill. (Backends that do not route through these kernels, and the two ROCm Triton kernels that cannot take an fp8 pool at all, are out of scope; see Modifications.) **Scope: the ROCm 7.0 image only — 7.2 was never affected.** The dividing line is the Triton wheel, not ROCm. On the pre-fix ROCm 7.2 MI35x lane ([job 95705686213](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32135460766/job/95705686213), Aug 18, before any commit here) `test_verify_shared_kv.py` reported `"passed": true` with no `PassManager::run failed` or `idx < size()` in the log; that lane's only red was the unrelated `test_quark_mxfp4.py` near-miss. The 7.0 log carries aiter's `require triton>=3.6.0, found 3.4.0`, while 7.2 emits no such warning, so its Triton clears 3.6.0 (`docker/rocm.Dockerfile` installs aiter's pin over the base ROCm Torch `triton==3.5.1` when `BUILD_TRITON=1`). ### Root cause Every Triton attention kernel that reads a KV pool casts the wide operand *down* to the pool dtype before the dot (`tl.dot(q.to(k.dtype), k)`, `tl.dot(p.to(v.dtype), v)`), so an fp8 pool also feeds the fp8 matrix core. On gfx950 `AccelerateAMDMatmul` promotes an fp8 x fp8 `tl.dot` to the scaled `V_MFMA_*_F8F6F4` family, which is **16x16x128** under the `matrix_instr_nonkdim=16` launch hint all of these kernels pass. A dot whose reduction is narrower than 128 does not tile that instruction: `AMDMfmaEncodingAttr::getRepForOperand` clamps the resulting zero K-repetitions up to one, and `ScaledDotOpMFMAConversionHelper` then reads `kBase = 32` elements per lane from a register range that only holds `K / 4`. That is the out-of-bounds `SmallVector` access. `P @ V` reduces `BLOCK_N`, which is 64 (extend, verify) or 32 (decode, split-KV verify) — never 128 — so the fp8 path never compiles on gfx950. `Q @ Kpe` reduces `BLOCK_DPE` (32/64) and `Q @ K` reduces `BLOCK_DMODEL`, which is also below 128 at head_dim <= 64. Triton rejects the intrinsic instead of miscompiling it as of [triton-lang/triton#8278](https://github.com/triton-lang/triton/pull/8278), which dropped the `enforcedNonKDim == 0 &&` escape hatch that had let an explicit `matrix_instr_nonkdim` skip Triton's own "K is not a multiple of the intrinsic's kDim" check. That fix missed 3.5 and landed in 3.6: | Triton branch | guard in `chooseMfmaInstruction` | narrow fp8 dot | |---|---|---| | `release/3.4.x`, `release/3.5.x` | `enforcedNonKDim == 0 && inputKSize % kDim != 0` | promoted, then aborts | | `release/3.6.x` and later | `if (inputKSize % kDim != 0)` | rejected, falls back to non-scaled fp8 MFMA | So anything on 3.4 or 3.5 with `matrix_instr_nonkdim` set — which is every kernel here — crashes, and the ROCm 7.0 image ships 3.4.0. This is why the patch is deliberately independent of the Triton version rather than gated on a version check: 7.0 needs it today, and on 7.2 every flag resolves to the same fallback a fixed Triton picks anyway, at identical throughput. An image bump makes the workaround redundant rather than wrong. ## Modifications - New `python/sglang/kernels/ops/attention/fp8_dot_support.py` with `dot_in_kv_dtype(kv_dtype, reduction_width)`: `True` for every non-fp8 pool and every arch other than gfx950, and on gfx950 only for reduction widths that tile the scaled MFMA instruction. - Each dot that casts an operand down to the tile it reads gets its own constexpr verdict (`QK_DOT_IN_KV_DTYPE`, `QK_PE_DOT_IN_KV_DTYPE`, `PV_DOT_IN_KV_DTYPE`, `PV_EXTEND_DOT_IN_V_DTYPE`). When it is `False` the KV tile is upcast to the query dtype instead of the query tile being cast down. This covers `_fwd_kernel` and `_fwd_kernel_unified` (extend), `_fwd_grouped_kernel_stage1` (decode), `_verify_mla_prefix_stage1`, and `_verify_prefix_stage1` — including `_fwd_kernel`'s extend-stage `P @ V`, whose V is the caller's current-chunk tensor rather than the pool. Every flag is `True` on non-gfx950 hardware and for bf16/fp16 pools, so those paths generate the same code as before. `matrix_instr_nonkdim`, tile sizes, warp counts, and the `#mma` layout are all untouched. **Non-AMD impact: none, verified rather than argued.** `is_gfx95_supported()` returns `False` for every non-HIP build without touching the device, so `dot_in_kv_dtype` short-circuits to `True` on NVIDIA and the guards select the pre-existing expression. To confirm that costs nothing, I compiled the original kernel body and the guarded one (flags `True`) for five targets with Triton 3.4.0 and diffed the emitted TTGIR and LLIR modulo debug locations: **identical on sm90 (bf16 and fp8), sm100 (fp8), gfx942 (fp8) and gfx950 (bf16)**. That check is what caught the one real difference — writing the guard as `tl.dot(p.to(v.dtype), v)` reorders the P cast against the `acc * re_scale` multiply, which on Hopper with an fp8 pool moved the async `warp_group_dot` relative to the accumulator scaling. Keeping `p = p.to(v.dtype)` as its own statement inside the guard restores exact equivalence, which is why it is written that way. NVIDIA fp8 KV keeps casting down to fp8 and keeps its fp8 tensor-core path. The residual cost off gfx950 is one extra Triton compile (the new constexpr parameters change the cache key) and three or four integer / `frozenset` comparisons per launch. Two other ROCm Triton kernels dot against a tile that could in principle be fp8, and deliberately get no verdict: - `prefill_attention.py` never reads a KV pool, its `Q @ K` is uncast (so its operands already share a dtype), and its gfx950 `BLOCK_N` is 128 — which tiles the scaled instruction even if `P @ V` ran in fp8. - `rocm_mla_decode_rope.py` does read the pool, but its `Q @ K` is uncast too, so a bf16 query against an fp8 pool fails Triton's frontend with `Unsupported rhs dtype fp8e4nv` well before the AMD backend. That is a separate pre-existing gap in that kernel, not this crash, and a per-dot verdict would not make it work. The verify combine kernels compute their draft-draft block with `tl.sum(q[:, None, :] * ke[None, :, :], 2)`, not `tl.dot`, so no matrix-core promotion applies there. **On unit tests:** I wrote and then dropped a CPU test for the predicate. Asserting `dot_in_kv_dtype(fp8, 64) is False` against a body of `width % 128 == 0` only restates the expression, and the one assertion with real coupling — that the gfx950 head_dim-256 config yields a `BLOCK_N` the guard rejects — would fail if someone legitimately retuned `BLOCK_N` to 128, which is the documented fallback here. Pinning that would block an improvement rather than catch a bug. The failure mode worth guarding is "a new narrow fp8 dot appears on gfx950", and what catches that is compiling the real kernel on real gfx950, i.e. the MI35x lane. Alternatives considered and rejected: dropping or raising `matrix_instr_nonkdim` for the fp8 path (Triton's own guard then rejects the intrinsic, but the 16x16 tile becomes 32x32, which changes `warpsPerTile` for the chain-dot tail from `[8, 1]` to `[4, 2]` and inserts a layout conversion between the two dots), and forcing `BLOCK_N = 128` (fixes only head_dim 256 and re-tunes the bf16 path with it). ## Accuracy Tests `stage-b-test-1-gpu-small-amd-mi35x` now passes on MI35x hardware. [Run 32217006660](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32217006660) is a targeted dispatch of just that stage against this PR's head (ROCm 7.0, since that lane is schedule-only and a PR event never runs it): **9/9 passed**, `test_verify_shared_kv.py` reports `"passed": true` with `test_qwen3_5_fp8_kv_cache` executing, and the log contains no `PassManager::run failed` or `idx < size()`. ([Run 32212523645](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32212523645) is the same result on the first commit.) The change only affects gfx950 with an fp8 KV pool, where nothing compiled before, so there is no prior behaviour to regress. Within that path `P` reaches the dot as bf16 rather than quantized to e4m3, which is strictly more accurate; `extend_attention_fwd` and `verify_shared_kv_fwd` widen the same dots, so `test_qwen3_5_fp8_kv_cache`'s parity check compares like with like. ## Speed Tests and Profiling No throughput measurement yet — the run above establishes correctness, not perf. The reasoning for expecting no loss: the wide `Q @ K` dot keeps `tt.dot_scaled` (verified in the emitted TTGIR below), and for the narrow dots CDNA4's non-scaled `V_MFMA_F32_16X16X32_FP8_FP8` — what a Triton carrying #8278 would fall back to — reduces the same 32 elements per instruction as `V_MFMA_F32_16X16X32_BF16`, so bf16 operands run at the same rate. The extra cost is the fp8 -> bf16 converts on the V tile and a larger LDS footprint for it (80 KB total at head_dim 256 versus 128 KB for a bf16 pool, so still well inside the 160 KB budget). ## Verification Triton 3.4.0's AMD backend compiles for `hip:gfx950` without a GPU, so the fix was checked by driving the ttir/ttgir/llir stages directly on the same tile shape and launch hints as `extend_attention` at head_dim 256 (`BLOCK_M=128`, `num_warps=8`, `matrix_instr_nonkdim=16`): | KV dtype | `PV_DOT_IN_KV_DTYPE` | `BLOCK_N` | Result | |---|---|---|---| | fp8_e4m3 | True (today) | 64 | **`RuntimeError: PassManager::run failed`** | | fp8_e4m3 | False (this PR) | 64 | compiles | | fp8_e4m3 | True | 32 | **`Assertion 'idx < size()' failed`** | | fp8_e4m3 | False | 32 | compiles | | fp8_e4m3 | True | 128 | compiles (128 tiles the instruction) | | bf16 | True | 64 | compiles (unchanged path) | The fixed variant's TTGIR keeps the fp8 fast path where it is legal and drops to bf16 only for `P @ V`, both under the same `#mma` layout as before: ``` %50 = tt.dot_scaled %28, %49, %cst_2 lhs = e4m3 rhs = e4m3 : tensor<128x256xf8E4M3FN, dot_op<{opIdx = 0, parent = #mma, kWidth = 16}>> * tensor<256x64xf8E4M3FN, ...> %77 = tt.dot %76, %75, %73 : tensor<128x64xbf16, dot_op<{opIdx = 0, parent = #mma, kWidth = 4}>> * tensor<64x256xbf16, dot_op<{opIdx = 1, parent = #mma, kWidth = 4}>> ``` The K3 MLA tile (`BLOCK_DMODEL=512`, `BLOCK_DPE=64`, `BLOCK_N=64`), where two of the three dots widen, behaves the same way: crashes today, compiles with the per-dot verdicts. Narrowing `BLOCK_DMODEL` to 64 crashes the `Q @ K` dot too, which is why the verdict is computed per dot rather than assuming `Q @ K` is always wide enough. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). The regression test is the existing `test_verify_shared_kv.py::test_qwen3_5_fp8_kv_cache` on `stage-b-test-1-gpu-small-amd-mi35x`, which this PR turns green; no new test file is added (see below). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

signals.title: [CPU] Fix wrongly causal-masked bidirectional attention
signals.text: <!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. --> ## Motivation <!-- Describe the purpose and goals of this pull request. --> On the Intel AMX CPU attention backend, `extend_attention_cpu` always masked the extend stage of attention as causal. This is correct for decoder-style self-attention, but wrong for bidirectional, encoder-only self-attention (e.g. BERT-family rerankers/embedders like bge-reranker). On this backend such models silently got causally-masked attention scores, producing incorrect outputs. When running `BAAI/bge-reranker-base` on CPU: For the below request: ``` { "model": "BAAI/bge-reranker-base", "query": "what is panda?", "documents": [ "hi", "The giant panda (Ailuropoda melanoleuca), sometimes called a panda bear or simply panda, is a bear species endemic to China." ], "return_documents": true } ``` Before this fix: `"hi"` and `"The giant panda ..."` both get the same score: 2.611328125, which is not reasonble. After this fix: Scores diverge correctly, matching what a real cross-encoder should produce: `"The giant panda ..."`: score is 6.1875 `"hi"`: score is -8.15625 ## Modifications <!-- Detail the changes made in this pull request. --> - `python/sglang/kernels/aot/csrc/cpu/extend.cpp`: add an `is_causal` parameter (default `true`) to `extend_attention_cpu`. The stage-2 loop now iterates over the full extend range and only applies the causal mask when `is_causal` is set, instead of unconditionally limiting keys to `[0, m + BLOCK_M)` and masking `n + n_size - 1 > m`. - `python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/intel_amx_backend.py`: compute `is_causal = not (layer.is_cross_attention or layer.attn_type == AttentionType.ENCODER_ONLY)` and pass it into `extend_attention_fwd`, mirroring the existing pattern in `triton_backend.py`: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/ee1f2e8dfdbb264727134aeac4b8dec155ec6efe/python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/triton_backend.py#L1360-L1368. ## Accuracy Tests <!-- If this pull request affects model outputs (e.g., changes to the kernel or model forward code), provide accuracy test results. --> ```sh python test/registered/cpu/test_extend.py -k test_extend_attention_bidirectional ``` ## Checklist - [ ] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [ ] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. signals.title: Auto-detect aiter decode attention backend for MLA models on ROCm
signals.text: > **Draft migration of #22638 to the correct Miles dependency branch.** Changing the old PR's base from `main` to `sglang-miles` caused GitHub to auto-close it because its historical `amdpilot-org/sglang` source repository is outside the current fork network and could not be reopened. This draft preserves the same two commits on the normal `Arist12/sglang` fork. ## Motivation On MI355X, the AITER MLA decode backend materially reduced GLM-5.1 FP8 decode latency compared with the then-default backend. Automatically selecting it when the user has not chosen either attention backend could remove a manual tuning step for supported ROCm MLA models. ## Current blockers - `sglang-miles` moved DeepSeek-family defaults into `python/sglang/srt/arg_groups/overrides.py`; mechanically resolving the old `server_args.py` hunk would restore code in the wrong layer. - The original condition does not establish whether DSA models such as GLM-5.x should receive a raw `decode_attention_backend="aiter"` override after the newer `attention_backend="dsa"` resolution. - `importlib.util.find_spec("aiter")` proves only that the package exists, not that the installed build, GPU, model shape, and decode mode are supported. - The branch has no regression tests for default selection, explicit user overrides, or unavailable/unsupported AITER. - The 42.6% result was measured on one MI355X GLM configuration and must not be generalized to every listed model or ROCm GPU without evidence. ## Required refresh before marking ready - [x] Target `sglang-miles`, which is the branch Miles images consume. - [ ] Re-implement the default in `_deepseek_family_overrides` or the appropriate current resolution pass. - [ ] Add focused tests for default selection, both user override flags, missing AITER, DSA/non-DSA behavior, and unsupported capability. - [ ] Rerun the GLM-5.1 MI355X benchmark against current `sglang-miles` and record exact commands. - [ ] Smoke-test at least one additional supported MLA architecture or narrow the documented model scope. - [ ] Run current lint and AMD CI. This PR intentionally remains draft and conflicting until the behavior is redesigned and independently validated. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #24352912710](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/24352912710)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: **Blocked** -- `run-ci` is required first.<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [Feature] Support PP in full prefill CUDA graphs
signals.text: ## Motivation Full prefill CUDA graphs currently cannot replay pipeline-parallel stages. The runner has no graph-stable storage for pipeline inputs, does not pass those inputs to non-first stages, and rejects pipeline proxy outputs. ## Modifications - Add token-major pipeline proxy buffers for full-prefill graph capture and replay. - Register pipeline inputs with the prefill graph buffer registry so live inputs are copied and padded safely. - Preserve global attention-layer indexing on partitioned pipeline stages. - Pass graph-stable pipeline inputs to non-first stages and trim pipeline outputs to the live token count. - Add unit coverage for layer alignment, buffer allocation, registry filling, and output trimming. - Add a dedicated two-GPU FullCG test under `test/registered/cuda_graph/full_prefill/` while retaining the existing generic PP canary test. - Replay a 47-token PP prompt through the 64-token prefill bucket with the normal FullCG decode path enabled, and assert that the request actually uses the prefill graph. ## Accuracy Tests No numerical kernels or model math are changed. The two-GPU end-to-end test passes with KV canary checks enabled and observes `cuda graph: True` for the 47-token prefill batch. - 46 focused CPU tests passed. - Two-GPU mock-model FullCG prefill and decode test passed on GB300. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Not applicable. This enables a previously unsupported configuration without changing the non-PP or eager execution paths. ## Checklist - [x] Format code with the repository pre-commit configuration. - [x] Add unit and end-to-end tests. - [x] No documentation update is required for this runner capability. - [x] No benchmark is required because no existing execution path is modified. - [x] Follow the SGLang code style guidance. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:no_entry_sign: [Run #32416467775](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32416467775)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32416467627](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32416467627)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #32416467679](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32416467679)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [Fix] Harden FlashAttention CUDA graph metadata bounds
signals.text: ## Motivation Full-prefill CUDA graph buckets are sized by aggregate batch tokens, which can exceed the maximum context length of any single request. The FlashAttention sliding-window write-location buffer is currently allocated from max_context_len, so a valid aggregate-token bucket can exceed its capacity. Separately, idle graph batches may expose an empty CPU sequence-length tensor, for which max() is invalid. ## Modifications - Size the full-prefill sliding-window write-location buffer from the captured token capacity. - Validate replay token counts before copying into the graph-stable buffer. - Use the static context bound when CPU sequence lengths are absent or empty. - Add CPU regression tests for aggregate-token capacity, replay overflow detection, and empty idle batches. ## Accuracy Tests No attention math is changed. The tests validate metadata sizing and fallback behavior. - 2 focused unit tests passed. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Not applicable. These changes affect metadata allocation and boundary checks, not attention kernels. ## Checklist - [x] Format code with the repository pre-commit configuration. - [x] Add unit tests. - [x] No documentation update is required. - [x] No speed benchmark is required for this metadata correctness fix. - [x] Follow the SGLang code style guidance. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:no_entry_sign: [Run #32416500122](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32416500122)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #32416499661](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32416499661)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #32416499821](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32416499821)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->
