signals.title: [Quant] Load compressed-tensors kv_cache_scheme scales
signals.text: ## Motivation compressed-tensors checkpoints that declare a `kv_cache_scheme` ship calibrated per-tensor attention `k_scale` / `v_scale` tensors, but they are silently dropped at load (`Parameter model.layers.N.k_scale not found in params_dict`), so `--kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3` runs the cache unscaled. Three gaps compound: - `CompressedTensorsConfig.from_config` never forwarded `kv_cache_scheme`, leaving it `None` even when declared. - `get_quant_method` had no `RadixAttention` branch, so the `k_scale` / `v_scale` parameters were never created (ModelOpt has `ModelOptFp8KVCacheMethod` for this; the compressed-tensors equivalent was missing). - The qwen3_5 weight mapper only knew the ModelOpt-style `.k_proj.k_scale` serialization; compressed-tensors stores the scales on the attention module (`.self_attn.k_scale`). ## Modifications - Forward `kv_cache_scheme` in `from_config`. - New `CompressedTensorsKVCacheMethod(BaseKVCacheMethod)`, returned for `RadixAttention` when a `kv_cache_scheme` is declared. It accepts only what `BaseKVCacheMethod` can represent — static, symmetric, per-tensor FP8. A declared-but-unsupported scheme is skipped with a warning instead of failing the boot: such checkpoints serve correctly with an unquantized-scale KV cache, so refusing to load them would regress working deployments. - A `kv_cache_quant_algo` property on the config: `configure_kv_cache_dtype` duck-types this field to resolve `--kv-cache-dtype auto`, so a declared supported scheme gets the fp8 pool its scales calibrate (ModelOpt parity). Without this, an auto-resolved bf16 pool would store unscaled entries while the attention backends apply the loaded scales on read. - Two `orig_to_new_substr` entries in `QWEN3_5_KV_SCALE_MAPPER` for the attention-level scale names, and the mapper applied in the Qwen3.5 MTP loader for symmetry. - Unit test: `test/registered/unit/layers/quantization/test_compressed_tensors_kv_cache.py` (CPU, `base-a-test-cpu`). - The pre-existing `kv_cache_scheme` remap in `apply_weight_name_mapper` (dead until this PR forwarded the scheme) is removed: the scheme holds schema fields, never module names, and `apply_dict` drops keys that match a mapper deletion rule. Checkpoints without a `kv_cache_scheme` are unaffected (`get_quant_method` returns `None` for `RadixAttention` as before), and unloaded scales keep the existing default-to-1.0 behavior in `BaseKVCacheMethod.process_weights_after_loading`. ## Accuracy Tests RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell, Qwen3.8-27B mixed-precision compressed-tensors checkpoint with a declared FP8 `kv_cache_scheme`, `--kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3`, `sglang.test.few_shot_gsm8k --num-questions 200`: - Before: 32 `k_scale`/`v_scale` drop warnings at load; GSM8K 0.960 (cache unscaled — accuracy-benign on this checkpoint because the calibrated scales are near 1, but incorrect). - After: zero drop warnings; GSM8K 0.965, invalid 0.000. Parity within the script's documented variance — this is a correctness fix for the calibration path, not an accuracy rescue. - With `--kv-cache-dtype` left as `auto`: the pool now auto-resolves to `float8_e4m3fn` (previously bf16, ignoring the checkpoint's declared KV calibration); zero drop warnings; GSM8K 0.940 / 0.960 across two runs — statistically identical to the explicit-fp8 lane, as expected since both resolve to the same pool and scales. Note: an MTP draft loaded from the same checkpoint carries the same config, so the draft worker's pool auto-resolves to fp8 as well (its scales default to 1.0; write/read stay symmetric). A standalone bf16 draft export without a `quantization_config` keeps a bf16 pool. Known limit: an explicit bf16 `--kv-cache-dtype` override on a checkpoint with declared scales attaches scales to an unquantized pool — the same pre-existing exposure ModelOpt has today; a shared fix belongs in `BaseKVCacheMethod`. ## Speed Tests and Profiling No runtime impact: scale resolution happens once at init; the scales feed the existing fp8 KV cache path. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. signals.title: [AMD][Spec] Pack AITER target-verify GQA for Qwen3.5
signals.text: ## Motivation AITER `target_verify` `.expand()`s the single TP-local KV head to `tp_q_head_num`. `unified_attention` then computes `num_queries_per_kv = 1` (it runs as MHA). On gfx950 that also inflates the 2D program count until the wrapper drops off the 3D split-KV kernel onto the 2D kernel at high batch (Qwen3.5 TP2, 16 Q heads, 1 KV head). That is the MTP concurrency-64 stall: throughput goes flat while TPOT roughly doubles. `forward_decode` already passes the true KV-head count into the same kernel. This PR makes verify match decode. The `.expand()` is stride-0, so the values are the same KV; `num_queries_per_kv` is tiling, not a different attention formula. <details> <summary> Why #34517 is not the root cause of MTP perf drop</summary> [#34517](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/34517) is the Triton grouped-head / shared-KV verify kernel (`verify_shared_kv_fwd`). It is selected only in `triton_backend.py` (`gfx95`, `topk=1`, Qwen3.5, one TP-local KV head). It does not touch `aiter_backend.py`. In InferenceX, Qwen3.5 MTP on MI355X pins `--attention-backend aiter`. On that path, topk=1 verify already goes through AITER `unified_attention`, so #34517 is never dispatched. A kernel that does not run cannot make MTP slower, and it also cannot fix the AITER `.expand()` stall. The drop people are looking at is the AITER layout: concurrency 32 to 64 goes flat because verify is doing fake MHA. Same unofficial run [32241233599](https://inferencex.semianalysis.com/inference?unofficialRun=32241233599) (stock AITER, expand still on): | | concurrency 64 tok/s/GPU | |---|---:| | Dashboard MTP (AITER, KV expand on) | 5,728 | | Same run, speculative decoding **off** | **7,456** | | Local, same flags, KV expand on | 6,149 | | Local, same flags, this PR (no expand) | 8,101 | MTP slower than no-spec on the same run means the stall is spec verify, not #34517. Local expand matches the dashboard shape (leftover ~5–9% is 20260816 vs 20260818 image). Turning off the expand recovers C64. Time correlation with #34517 (merged 2026-08-15, dashboard image 20260818) is not causation. </details> ## Modifications - Delete the `target_verify` `.expand()` of K/V. Pass the true TP-local KV-head count so `unified_attention` runs as GQA (`num_queries_per_kv = tp_q_head_num`). - No new env var. Opt-out of unified verify remains `SGLANG_AITER_UNIFIED_VERIFY=0`. - Do not import or call Triton's `verify_shared_kv_fwd` from `AiterAttnBackend`. - Draft-extend routing is out of scope (that is [#30105](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/30105)). ## Kernel evidence (MI355X, Qwen3.5 TP2 verify shape, Lq=4, page=16, HIP graph) `unified_attention` only. **Baseline** is current AITER `target_verify` (KV expanded to the Q-head count). **This PR** keeps the true KV-head count so the kernel runs as GQA. B/A < 1 means this PR is faster. | KV | prefix | bs | Baseline ms | This PR ms | B/A | kernels | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---| | bf16 | 8k | 4 | 0.064 | 0.056 | 0.87 | both 3D | | bf16 | 8k | 64 | 1.271 | 0.326 | **0.26** | 2D → 3D split-KV | | fp8 | 8k | 64 | 0.497 | 0.236 | 0.47 | 2D → 3D split-KV | | bf16 | 32k | 64 | 5.555 | 1.246 | 0.22 | 2D → 3D split-KV | ## E2E serving (MI355X, Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-MXFP4, TP2, 8k input / 1k output) Both servers used the same model, GPUs, image, client, and serving flags. The only difference is whether AITER `target_verify` expands the TP-local KV head. **What the two columns mean** - **Baseline** — current upstream AITER `target_verify`. The single TP-local KV head is `.expand()`'d to `tp_q_head_num`, so `unified_attention` sees `num_queries_per_kv = 1` (MHA). - **This PR** — that `.expand()` is removed. `unified_attention` sees `num_queries_per_kv = tp_q_head_num` (GQA; Q heads share one KV load). Same layout as `forward_decode`. **Serving configuration (identical on both servers)** - Hardware: 2× AMD MI355X, `--tensor-parallel-size 2` - Model: `Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-MXFP4` - Image: `rocm/sgl-dev:v0.5.17-rocm720-mi35x-20260816` - Client: InferenceX `benchmark_serving.py --use-chat-template`, 8192 input tokens / 1024 output tokens - Attention: `--attention-backend aiter`, with `SGLANG_USE_AITER=1`, `SGLANG_USE_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN=1`, `AITER_FLYDSL_FORCE=1` - Speculative decoding: `--speculative-algorithm EAGLE --speculative-num-steps 3 --speculative-eagle-topk 1 --speculative-num-draft-tokens 4` - `--page-size 16` - `--context-length 9236` (`8192 + 1024 + 20`) - `--kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3` - `--cuda-graph-max-bs-decode` set to that point's concurrency - `--chunked-prefill-size 32768` and `--max-prefill-tokens 32768` - `--scheduler-recv-interval 1`, `--stream-interval 1`, `--tokenizer-worker-num 6` - `--mem-fraction-static 0.68` Throughput is **total tokens/s per GPU** (`total_token_throughput / TP`), the same unit as the InferenceX dashboard. Δ% = (this PR − baseline) / baseline. Concurrency is the in-flight request count (`--max-running-requests`). | Concurrency | Baseline tok/s/GPU | This PR tok/s/GPU | Δ tput | Baseline TPOT ms | This PR TPOT ms | Δ TPOT | Baseline TTFT ms | This PR TTFT ms | |---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | 4 | 2596 | 2753 | +6.0% | 6.36 | 6.17 | −3.0% | 337 | 336 | | 8 | 3716 | 3885 | +4.5% | 9.16 | 8.76 | −4.3% | 347 | 347 | | 16 | 4893 | 5205 | +6.4% | 14.03 | 13.25 | −5.5% | 356 | 352 | | 32 | 6137 | 6689 | +9.0% | 22.76 | 20.72 | −9.0% | 387 | 370 | | **64** | **6149** | **8101** | **+31.8%** | **46.48** | **35.09** | **−24.5%** | 479 | 503 | | 128 | 9083 | 9637 | +6.1% | 63.10 | 59.39 | −5.9% | 663 | 693 | | 256 | 10187 | 10849 | +6.5% | 112.52 | 105.98 | −5.8% | 1007 | 968 | From concurrency 32 to 64 the baseline stalls: throughput goes 6137 → 6149 tok/s/GPU while median TPOT roughly doubles (22.8 → 46.5 ms). This PR keeps climbing (6689 → 8101) because TPOT only goes 20.7 → 35.1 ms. This is a decode/verify win; median TTFT at concurrency 64 is slightly higher (479 → 503 ms). Three repeats of this PR at concurrency 64: 8101 / 8114 / 8182 tok/s/GPU (range ~1%). ## Relation to #30105 [#30105](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/30105) drops the same `.expand()` **and** reroutes draft_extend. This PR is the verify-only deletion so decode and verify share one KV layout. Draft-extend stays on #30105. ## Tests - Kernel A/B and E2E serving A/B on MI355X as above. - `test_verify_mask.py`: AITER `target_verify` must not expand KV to the Q-head axis and must not call `verify_shared_kv_fwd`. ## Checklist - [x] Format code according to the contribution guide. - [x] Provide accuracy and performance measurements (kernel A/B and E2E serving A/B). - [x] Keep the change scoped to the AITER verify layout (`aiter_backend.py` plus a regression lock in an existing unit test). - [x] No new env var or helper module. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:no_entry_sign: [Run #32337317653](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32337317653)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32337317468](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32337317468)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32337317670](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32337317670)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: Warm PaddleOCR-VL with a page-sized image, not a 32x32 one
signals.text: ### The gap `_get_vlm_warmup_image_base64` already treats warmup image size as something worth choosing per model: Kimi K2.5 gets 512x512 to compile MoonViT position interpolation, Kimi K3 gets 448x448 to match its native patch grid, and the docstring says why — *"This keeps one-time vision setup work out of the first external image request."* PaddleOCR-VL falls through to the 32x32 minimum. Measured against what it actually serves: | warmup image | ViT patches | image tokens | |---|---|---| | current minimum, 32x32 | **4** | 1 | | Kimi K3, 448x448 | 1024 | 256 | | Kimi K2.5, 512x512 | 1296 | 324 | | **a real page** (checkpoint default budget) | **~5184** | ~1296 | Three orders of magnitude below the serving shape, so nothing shape-dependent in the packed vision path is warm when the first page arrives. ### The symptom While measuring this model against vLLM I ran four independent server instances × three rounds. Within every instance the first round came out low and the next two recovered, and the model's run-to-run spread was 4.7% against vLLM's 1.6% on the same host and workload. That pattern is a warmup tail, not noise. Being straight about what is and isn't measured here: the coverage gap in the table is measured, and the variance is measured. The first-request improvement is not — I no longer have the H200 that produced those numbers. So this is proposed on the mechanism plus the precedent already in this function, and I'm happy to attach a before/after TTFT once a box frees up if a reviewer wants that before merging. ### Implementation notes - The image is generated (stdlib `zlib` + `struct`, ~15 lines) instead of checked in as a third kilobyte-long base64 literal, so the next model to need one costs a single call. - Verified by executing the real function over every branch: PaddleOCR-VL (by architecture and by `model_type`) gets a decodable 1008x1008 truecolor PNG, and **Kimi K2.5, Kimi K3 and the default path return byte-identical bytes to before**. No other model's startup cost moves. - Truecolor rather than grayscale, since image processors assume three channels. - Tests cover the size for the new branch, the token arithmetic behind the choice, and the generated PNG's chunk structure and CRCs. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32225952459](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32225952459)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32225952326](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32225952326)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [Fix] Pass Anthropic thinking history as reasoning_content for custom chat encoders
signals.text: ## Motivation Run Kimi-K3 with `--reasoning-parser kimi_k3 --tool-call-parser kimi_k3` and talk to it on `/v1/messages` with `thinking` on. Any agentic client sends assistant `thinking` blocks back in history — the Messages API requires it for tool-use turns — and a few turns in, raw XTML channel markers show up in visible assistant text: ``` turn 3 [text] '<|open|>think<|sep|<|sep|>Something is very strange. […]' turn 4 [text] '<|open|>think<|sep|' ``` Turns 1-2 are fine, then every turn after that is corrupted — it never recovers. Drop the `thinking` blocks from the replayed history and it never happens at all, so the problem is how prior reasoning gets fed back, not the reasoning parser. **Root cause.** K3 ships no Jinja chat template, so SGLang renders it through the checkpoint's own XTML encoder. That encoder frames the `think` / `response` / `tools` channels itself and wants prior reasoning in an assistant `reasoning_content` field. The Anthropic adapter never used it — instead it wrapped prior thinking in the reasoning detector's markers and spliced that into assistant **content**. Here is what the two forms actually render to, straight from the K3 tokenizer: ``` # before — think channel empty, reasoning nested inside the response channel <|open|>think<|sep|><|close|>think<|sep|><|open|>response<|sep|><|open|>think<|sep|>PRIOR <|close|>think<|sep|>Here is my answer.<|close|>response<|sep|> # after <|open|>think<|sep|>PRIOR<|close|>think<|sep|><|open|>response<|sep|>Here is my answer.<|close|>response<|sep|> ``` Every replayed turn taught the model the same lesson: think channel empty, think block sitting inside the response channel. Two turns of that and it starts writing `<|open|>think<|sep|>` as ordinary response text. None of this is K3-specific. All four Python chat encoders that bypass `apply_chat_template` frame their own reasoning channel and read `reasoning_content`, so the splice was wrong for every one of them. ## Modifications - **`entrypoints/openai/chat_encoding.py`** — adds `spec_owns_reasoning_history(spec)`, right under `resolve_chat_encoding_spec` so the contract sits with the specs it describes. It covers the whole custom-encoder family (`spec is not None`) rather than listing specs, so whoever adds the fifth one gets the safe default for free. An encoder that ignores the field drops history — what the splice path already does for models with no reasoning detector — instead of leaking. - **`entrypoints/openai/serving_chat.py`** — `supports_native_reasoning_history()`, a one-line delegate. - **`entrypoints/anthropic/serving.py`** — `_convert_assistant_thinking_blocks` now returns `(reasoning_content, text)`. Custom encoders get the history in the field, everyone else keeps the splice untouched. `redacted_thinking` still raises before the branch, and the best-effort drop for detector-less models survives. Nothing needed a schema change: `ChatCompletionMessageGenericParam` already declared `reasoning_content`, and messages are dumped without `exclude_none`, so it flows straight through. `wrap_reasoning_history` has exactly one production caller, so that is the whole mechanism. `dsv4`/`dsv32` also land on their official multi-turn contract now instead of bypassing it. Jinja-path models stay on the splice on purpose — their markers (`<think>`, `[THINK]`, `◁think▷`) really do live in the content stream, so it reproduces what the model emitted anyway. ## Test Plan ### Live server Same deployment before and after — `moonshotai/Kimi-K3` on 2x4 GB300, TP8, DSPARK spec-decode — same scripts, `temperature=0`: | run | main | with the fix | | --- | --- | --- | | 12-turn tool loop, streaming `/v1/messages` | leaks turns 3-12, all ten of them | clean, and the loop converges at turn 9 | | 8-turn tool loop, non-streaming | leaks turns 3-8 | clean | | 6 concurrent sessions x 5 turns | all six leak, every one first at turn 3 | none leak | | thinking dropped from replayed history | clean | clean | | `thinking: {"type": "disabled"}` | clean | clean | | reasoning passed as `reasoning_content` on `/v1/chat/completions` | clean | clean | | thinking-only history turn, and a turn with two thinking blocks | clean | clean | | `redacted_thinking` history | 400 | 400 | On main the onset is turn 3 every single time, and it never recovers — the `thinking` block stops appearing at all from there on and the markers move into `text`. That is also why the loop never converges: each turn re-reads its own corrupted history and re-diagnoses the same phantom problem. With the fix, `thinking` comes back on essentially every turn and the model finishes the task. Asked what it had just been thinking, the model quoted the injected reasoning back — the history really does land in the think channel rather than being quietly dropped. Prompt rendering was also diffed against the real K3 tokenizer for a thinking + text + tool_use turn. ### Unit tests `anthropic/test_serving.py` — 61/61. Two new cases: history reaches a channel-framing encoder as `reasoning_content` and never through the wrap path, and a thinking-only turn keeps its reasoning across the empty-content placeholder branch. Both go red against pre-fix code, and the existing wrap-path test still covers the default encoder. `openai/test_serving_chat.py` — 111/111. Two more: the real `OpenAIServingChat` predicate across all four specs plus `None`, and a guard that parses the literals `resolve_chat_encoding_spec` can return and checks them against the tuple the capability test iterates. Add an encoder without classifying it and CI fails. Mutation-checked, so it is not passing vacuously. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #32435140730](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32435140730)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32435140644](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32435140644)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #32435140704](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32435140704)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. --> ## Motivation A `/v1/responses` request against a **multimodal Kimi-K3** deployment fails immediately: ```json {"error":{"message":"texts cannot be empty and tokenizer must be initialized","type":"invalid_request_error","param":null,"code":400}} ``` The equivalent /v1/chat/completions request with the same messages and tools works, so the bug is specific to the /v1/responses path for multimodal Kimi-K3. ## Why The kimi_k3 custom encoder produces a usable prompt_ids (via apply_chat_template(tokenize=True, ...)) but leaves prompt == "" — the only prompt = decode(prompt_ids) assignment lives in the prompt_ids is None branch, which kimi_k3 never enters. OpenAIServingResponses._make_request forwarded that empty prompt as text on the multimodal branch, producing GenerateReqInput(text=""). In TokenizerManager.generate_request, input_ids is None and input_text is empty, so control reaches _tokenize_texts(""), which raises the error above. serving_chat._convert_to_internal_request already special-cases this (elif is_multimodal and self.chat_encoding_spec == "kimi_k3": prompt_kwargs = {"input_ids": ...}); the responses path was missing the same guard. A text-only Kimi-K3 deployment (is_multimodal == False) takes the else branch and uses prompt_ids, so it is unaffected — which is why the bug only surfaces for multimodal Kimi-K3. signals.title: [DSV4] unified_kv: isolate C4 compress state per request
signals.text: ## Motivation On the `unified_kv` path the DSV4 **C4 compress state** is addressed through the full→SWA mapping: ``` state_loc = (swa_loc // swa_page_size) * c4_ring_size + swa_loc % c4_ring_size ``` `swa_loc` is derived from `req_to_token`, so **two requests sharing a radix prefix resolve the same prefix positions to the same SWA slot, and therefore to the same C4 state row**. The C4 overlap state is per-request — it carries that request's running compress window — so this aliases one request's state onto another's. The same hazard exists within a single request across a slot reuse: a freshly allocated `req_pool_idx` inherits whatever the previous occupant left in its ring rows. C128 already avoids this by addressing state request-scoped. This PR gives C4 the same contract: ``` state_loc = req_pool_idx * c4_ring_size + position % c4_ring_size ``` a pure function of `(req slot, logical position)`, which cannot alias across requests. > **Stacked on #30315 and #31040.** The first 8 files in this diff belong to those two PRs; this PR's own change is the last 12 files (`+332/-43`, commit `fix(dsv4): isolate unified C4 compress state per request`). It has to be stacked: it rewrites `_unified_c4_state_pool_size`, which #30315 introduces. Will rebase onto `main` once those merge. > > To review this PR alone: > ``` > git diff yuttian1/dsv4-unified-kv-swa-ring...yuttian1/dsv4-unified-c4-per-request-ring > ``` ## Modifications Everything is gated on `compress_ratio == 4 and token_to_kv_pool._unified_kv`. **C128 and the non-unified (full→SWA) C4 path are untouched.** **Sizing and lifecycle** - **`pool_configurator.py`** — `_unified_c4_state_pool_size` becomes exactly `num_req_slots * c4_ring_size`, replacing the page-derived upper bound that the old addressing needed. - **`deepseek_v4_memory_pool.py`** — new `clear_c4_req_states(req_pool_indices)`, which resets the ring rows of the given slots (kv half → `0`, score half → `-inf`). Also documents why C4 needs no MTP-reject cleanup. - **`allocation.py`, `disaggregation/decode.py`** — call `clear_c4_req_states` for **newly allocated slots only**. A chunked continuation reuses its slot and must keep the state its previous chunk captured, so `newly_allocated` is captured *before* `alloc`. **Addressing** - **`compressor.py`, `compressor_v2.py`** — compute `use_req_ring` and thread it into the plan kwargs. - **`compress_hip.py`** — four `self.ratio == 128` guards in `CompressorHip.compress_extend_paged` / `compress_decode_paged` become `ratio == 128 or (ratio == 4 and _unified_kv)`, taking the existing `translate_from_req_position_to_state_loc` branch. - **`kernels/jit/csrc/deepseek_v4/c_plan.cuh`** — `compute_c128_loc` → `compute_req_ring_loc`, now also taken under `use_req_ring` (with `RuntimeCheck(!use_req_ring || compress_ratio == 4)`). Under `use_req_ring` the ring row is `position % ring_size`, so the extra "tail of the SWA page" write the overlap path emitted for full→SWA addressing is dropped. - **`kernels/ops/attention/dsv4/attn.py`, `compress.py`** — plumb `use_req_ring` through the Triton kernel and the plan entry points (XPU signatures unchanged). ## Accuracy Tests This is a correctness fix, not a numerics change: the compressed state values are identical, only the row they live in changes. Two tests pin the new address contract. **New — `test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_dsv4_c4_state_lifecycle.py`** (CPU, `base-a-test-cpu`): - pool size is the exact request-ring product; - `clear_c4_req_states` resets only the selected rings and leaves C128 alone; - `alloc_req_slots` clears new slots but **not** reused ones. **Extended — `test/registered/kernels/ops/attention/test_c4_v2.py`**: new `test_unified_request_ring_plans_ignore_full_to_state` runs the real prefill and decode plan kernels with a deliberately degenerate `full_to_state`, and asserts the emitted read pages / write locs are exactly `req_pool_idx * ring_size + position % ring_size`, and that two requests never land on the same row. Both run green on ROCm (MI355X): ``` test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_dsv4_c4_state_lifecycle.py 3 passed test/registered/kernels/ops/attention/test_c4_v2.py 35 passed ``` Plus the neighbouring suites, unchanged: ``` test_dsv4_compress_write_pad.py, test_pool_configurator.py, test_hisparse_pool_configurator.py, test_prefill_adder.py -> 66 passed, 22 subtests passed ``` No end-to-end serving accuracy run is attached yet — the `unified_kv` path needs DeepSeek-V4-Pro on ROCm, which upstream CI cannot reach. Happy to attach one if a reviewer wants it. ## Speed Tests and Profiling No expected throughput impact: the same number of state rows is written, and `_unified_c4_state_pool_size` gets *smaller* (exact product instead of a page-derived upper bound), so the C4 pool allocation shrinks slightly. ## Notes for reviewers This is the upstream port of an internal fix. Four hunks from the internal version are **intentionally omitted** because they depend on a SWA-HiCache offload line that is not upstream (`_swa_offload_page_stride`, `_restore_state_windows`, `capture_c4_state_windows_unified`): the `swa_component.py` and `deepseek_v4_backend_hip_radix.py` changes, and the two HiCache capture helpers in `compress_hip.py`. When that line lands, the HiCache-side C4 restore will need a follow-up to use the same request-scoped address contract. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32342868830](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32342868830)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32342868495](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32342868495)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32342868737](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32342868737)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [AMD] Improve K3 dspark draft attn kernel perf
signals.text: ## Motivation With DSpark on Kimi-K3, every step runs 5 draft attn layers (qwen-style, non-causal). Draft attn dominates their cost. In a trace study, the 5 draft layers took 2.368 ms, of which the 5 attn kernels alone accounted for 1.244 ms (>50%). The reason is that this falls back to `extend_attention_fwd`. This generic extend kernel is a poor fit for a shared-KV shape. > Note that draft attn is a common path. `--attention-backend` only selects the target-verify kernel. `aiter` is not among the draft worker's supported backends, so on ROCm the draft always falls back to `triton`. Both `--attention-backend triton` and `aiter` therefore reach the kernel this PR changes. ## Modifications Route DSpark draft attn to `verify_shared_kv`, and extend that kernel to cover the two cases it previously rejected. - **Non-causal situation**: The prefix loop never applies a causal mask, so only modify the stage-2 kernel. - **`h_kv > 1`**: Both stages add a KV-head offset (`head // kv_group_num * stride_h`). A `HAS_KV_HEADS` constexpr keeps the single-KV-head (MLA/MQA) path free of that arithmetic, so the existing Kimi-K3 target-verify path compiles exactly as before. Also adds a tuning entry for `head_dim=64` (`BLOCK_N=256`, 4 warps) and `is_dspark_draft()` in `model_config.py` for the gate. ## Accuracy Tests GSM8k, 1319: ``` 100%|███████████| 1319/1319 [02:00<00:00, 10.98it/s] Accuracy: 0.955 Invalid: 0.001 Latency: 120.085 s Output throughput: 1108.066 token/s ``` ## Speed Tests and Profiling Tested with docker image `rocm/sgl-dev:v0.5.17-rocm720-mi35x-20260818`. Since draft attn is a common code path and this change is independent of other work, the numbers are measured directly on `main`, with no other non-merged PRs applied. Perf (isl=8k/16k/32k, cc=4, 32): - On cc=4, ITL improves by 4-12% and TTT by 2-6%. - On cc=32, ITL improves by 1-5% and TTT by 1-2%. The gain grows with input length, from 8k to 32k, in both cases. May be larger with aiter backend, because aiter accelerates target-verify attn, so draft attn takes a larger share of each step. | isl/osl | Concurrency | TP | TTT (tok/s) | Median TPOT (ms) | Median ITL (ms) | acc len | TTT speedup | ITL speedup | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | 8k/1k | 4 | 8 | 4994.24 | 5.57 | 4.42 | 4.71 | 1.02x | 1.04x | | | 32 | 8 | 10026.19 | 23.88 | 10.12 | 5.54 | 1.01x | 1.01x | | 16k/1k | 4 | 8 | 7207.37 | 7.53 | 4.65 | 5.60 | 1.04x | 1.07x | | | 32 | 8 | 11215.29 | 39.36 | 11.70 | 5.90 | 1.01x | 1.02x | | 32k/1k | 4 | 8 | 8924.78 | 10.76 | 5.15 | 5.92 | 1.06x | 1.12x | | | 32 | 8 | 11170.47 | 72.99 | 16.30 | 5.98 | 1.02x | 1.05x | Server script: ``` #!/bin/bash export SGLANG_USE_AITER=1 export SGLANG_AITER_K3_OPT=1 export AITER_FLYDSL_FORCE=1 export AITER_SITUV2_A8W4=1 export SGLANG_K3_FLYDSL_AR_NORM=1 sglang serve \ --model-path /models/Kimi-K3 \ --trust-remote-code \ --model-loader-extra-config '{"enable_multithread_load": true}' \ --tp 8 \ --attention-backend triton \ --dtype bfloat16 \ --mem-fraction-static 0.85 \ --cuda-graph-max-bs-decode 128 \ --host 127.0.0.1 \ --port 8000 \ --reasoning-parser kimi_k3 \ --tool-call-parser kimi_k3 \ --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 \ --mamba-full-memory-ratio 1.64 \ --mamba-ssm-dtype bfloat16 \ --enable-int8-mamba-checkpoint \ --mamba-track-interval 1024 \ --chunked-prefill-size 32768 \ --max-prefill-tokens 32768 \ --disable-radix-cache \ --speculative-draft-model-path /models/Kimi-K3-DSpark \ --speculative-algorithm DSPARK ``` ## Checklist - signals.title: fix(cache): retain shared SWA slots until final free
signals.text: ## Problem Different full-cache indices can reference the same physical sliding-window-attention slot. Freeing one mapping previously returned that slot to the allocator even while another mapping still referenced it, allowing the live slot to be reallocated and later freed again. This PR targets `sglang-miles`; [Miles #2666](https://github.com/radixark/miles/pull/2666) exercises the affected path. ## Change Track a reference count for each physical SWA slot whenever full-to-SWA mappings are written, replaced, or cleared. `free_swa` now clears the requested mappings and returns token slots, or whole pages, only when their remaining counts are zero. Reset counts on allocator clear while preserving PureSWA's direct identity mapping.

signals.title: fix(moe): support Llama4 NVFP4 router input weights on SM120
signals.text: ## Motivation Fixes https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/34192. Llama 4 constructs its MoE layers with `apply_router_weight_on_input=True`. For ModelOpt NVFP4 on SM120/SM121, SGLang selects the FlashInfer CUTLASS MoE runner, which previously rejected this configuration during server warmup. For top-1 routing, the required semantics can be implemented exactly by multiplying each token's hidden states by its router weight before activation quantization and passing unit final scales to CUTLASS. This follows the existing pattern in the AITER MoE runner. The fix remains intentionally restricted to top-1 routing. With top-k greater than one, each selected expert would require a differently scaled copy of the input. ## Modifications - Add top-1 router-weight pre-scaling to the common FlashInfer CUTLASS MoE execution path. - Replace the kernel's output-side router scaling with float32 unit `token_final_scales` when pre-scaling is active. - Normalize all `token_final_scales` passed through this CUTLASS path to float32, as required by the binding. - Remove the ModelOpt NVFP4 and FlashInfer CUTLASS assertions that rejected `apply_router_weight_on_input=True`. - Preserve explicit rejection for: - top-k greater than one; - activations already quantized before dispatch, including the FlashInfer CUTLASS FP4 all-gather path. - Add focused CPU unit tests covering: - top-1 activation pre-scaling; - float32 unit final scales; - preservation of expert IDs; - top-k greater than one rejection; - pre-quantized dispatch rejection. The normal `apply_router_weight_on_input=False` path is unchanged apart from enforcing the CUTLASS binding's float32 scale requirement. ## Accuracy Tests Added: ```text test/registered/unit/layers/moe/test_flashinfer_cutlass_router_weight.py ``` The tests compare the transformed hidden states and final scales against the expected top-1 formulation and verify that unsupported configurations fail explicitly. Local validation: ```text python -m py_compile \ python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/moe_runner/flashinfer_cutlass.py \ python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/modelopt_quant.py \ test/registered/unit/layers/moe/test_flashinfer_cutlass_router_weight.py ``` Result: passed. All commit-time pre-commit checks passed, including Python AST validation, isort, Ruff, Black, codespell, and registered-test validation. The focused pytest test could not be executed in the local development environment because PyTorch is not installed. No real-checkpoint accuracy test was run for this checkout. The equivalent patch and its SM120/SM121 validation evidence are documented in #34192. That validation used dummy weights for end-to-end liveness, so it is not claimed as a model-accuracy result. ## Speed Tests and Profiling No speed test or profiling was run for this checkout. The equivalent patch validation documented in #34192 completed both SM120 scenarios without errors and did not show a decode throughput regression. Those results used dummy weights and a separate validated build, so they are included only as prior evidence, not as performance results for this commit. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). signals.title: Add Spark3 Model
signals.text: ## Summary This PR adds native support for the Spark 3 model architecture in SGLang. The implementation introduces the Spark 3 configuration and causal language model, including sliding-window and full attention, head-wise attention output gating, tensor parallelism, pipeline parallelism, and checkpoint weight loading. ## Changes | File | Purpose | | --- | --- | | `python/sglang/srt/configs/spark3.py` | Adds `Spark3Config`, including model dimensions, attention layout, sliding-window configuration, layer types, RoPE parameters, and tied word embeddings. | | `python/sglang/srt/models/spark3.py` | Implements `Spark3ForCausalLM`, including grouped-query attention, interleaved sliding/full attention, head-wise output gating, gated MLP, parallelism support, split prefill, and checkpoint weight loading. | | `python/sglang/srt/configs/__init__.py` | Exports `Spark3Config` through the SGLang configuration package. | | `python/sglang/srt/utils/hf_transformers/common.py` | Registers `Spark3Config` in SGLang's Hugging Face configuration registry. | ## Key Technical Details 1. Efficient Architecture：The models adopt an efficiency-oriented architecture with Sliding Window Attention (SWA) and other structural optimizations, improving the balance between model quality, memory usage, and inference efficiency. 2. Native 1M Context：Both the 1.7B and 4B models natively support up to 1 million tokens of context, enabling long-document understanding, repository-level coding, and long-horizon agent tasks. 3. Strong Coding & Agent Capabilities：The models deliver leading coding and agent performance among models of comparable size, with strong capabilities in code generation, tool use, multi-step execution, and long-context reasoning. 4. Faster Inference：Through model architecture and inference-stack optimizations, the models achieve higher inference efficiency and throughput than many comparable-size models, especially in long-context scenarios. 5. Strong K–12 and Gaokao Performance：The models achieve leading K–12 question-answering performance at comparable parameter scales, with particularly strong results on challenging Chinese Gaokao-style tasks. 6. Advanced Post-Training：The release applies a comprehensive post-training recipe based on Scaled Reinforcement Learning and MOPD, improving reasoning, coding, instruction following, agentic capabilities, and alignment. 7. Controllable Thinking Budget：The models support configurable reasoning levels — none, low, medium, and high — allowing applications to dynamically trade off reasoning quality, latency, and inference cost. 8. 200+ Languages：Multilingual coverage has been expanded to more than 200 languages, supporting broad cross-lingual understanding, generation, translation, and localized applications. ## Performance We run MMLU-Pro on our internal OAI-server compatible benchmarking suite and the scores match the declared performance. Running on 1xH200 SXM5 ```bash ============ Serving Benchmark Result ============ Backend: sglang Traffic request rate: inf Max request concurrency: not set Successful requests: 500 Benchmark duration (s): 4.48 Total input tokens: 756489 Total input text tokens: 756489 Total generated tokens: 64000 Total generated tokens (retokenized): 63997 Request throughput (req/s): 111.52 Input token throughput (tok/s): 168733.90 Output token throughput (tok/s): 14275.12 Peak output token throughput (tok/s): 27064.00 Peak concurrent requests: 500 Total token throughput (tok/s): 183009.02 Concurrency: 463.05 ----------------End‑to‑End Latency---------------- Mean E2E Latency (ms): 4152.05 Median E2E Latency (ms): 4387.30 P90 E2E Latency (ms): 4391.62 P95 E2E Latency (ms): 4392.38 P99 E2E Latency (ms): 4393.38 ----------------Time to First Token---------------- Mean TTFT (ms): 2348.20 Median TTFT (ms): 2377.59 P90 TTFT (ms): 2386.19 P95 TTFT (ms): 2387.18 P99 TTFT (ms): 2388.39 -----Time per Output Token (excl. 1st token)----- Mean TPOT (ms): 14.20 Median TPOT (ms): 15.81 P90 TPOT (ms): 15.85 P95 TPOT (ms): 15.86 P99 TPOT (ms): 15.87 ----------------Inter‑Token Latency---------------- Mean ITL (ms): 14.20 Median ITL (ms): 12.72 P90 ITL (ms): 16.52 P95 ITL (ms): 17.51 P99 ITL (ms): 29.32 Max ITL (ms): 307.79 ================================================== ``` <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32324473737](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32324473737)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32324473553](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32324473553)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32324473617](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32324473617)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.text: ## Summary - add one fail-closed admission boundary for native auxiliary component loaders that only materialize plain state dicts - reject detected top-level, nested text-config, and compressed-tensors quantization metadata before model construction or large weight reads - apply the boundary to connectors/duration heads, bridges, diffusion decoders, sound tokenizers, spatial upsamplers, and vocoders - keep the local PE model on its Transformers `from_pretrained` path, where compatible quantization formats remain model-specific - use one documentation contract across the overview, CLI, compatibility matrix, and quantization guide ## Motivation #35184 makes independent component repository routing generic and safely routes supported quantized VAEs. signals.title: [diffusion] fix: stop reserving NCCL device buffers for single-rank groups
signals.text: ## Motivation On a single GPU, ~5 GiB of VRAM is gone before a single weight is loaded. On a 12 GiB consumer card that is 44% of the device, and it makes VAE decode fail at any resolution. The cause is that a single-GPU run still builds every parallel group — DP, CFG, TP, SP, PP, VAE_DECODE, DIT, VAE, ulysses, ring — each with one rank, and each got an NCCL-backed process group. NCCL sizes its per-channel device buffers when the communicator is created, so every one of those groups reserved ~390 MiB (the first, the world group, ~470 MiB). None of that memory can ever be used. Every collective in `GroupCoordinator` returns early on `world_size == 1` ("Bypass the function if we are using only 1 GPU"), and the device communicator is only constructed when `world_size > 1`. `pynccl` already skips communicator creation for single-rank groups; the underlying `torch.distributed.new_group` did not. Measured on an RTX 3060 12 GiB with a bare `torch.distributed` repro: | | device memory | |---|---| | CUDA context only | 114 MiB | | + world group | 584 MiB | | each additional `new_group([0])` | **+388 MiB** | `NCCL_MAX_NCHANNELS=1` drops the per-group cost to 10 MiB, which confirms these are per-channel buffers for channels a one-rank communicator can never use. ## Modifications Add `new_device_group()` in `group_coordinator.py`, which gives single-rank groups the gloo backend and leaves multi-rank groups on the requested backend. Route the nine device-group creation sites through it: `GroupCoordinator.__init__`, the`PipelineGroupCoordinator` single-rank branch and its `skip_device_group`, `_DIT` and `_VAE` in `parallel_state.py`, and the four ulysses/ring groups in `parallel_groups.py`. The two-rank `device_group_0_1` / `device_group_1_0` pipeline pair is left alone; it is only reached when the group has exactly two ranks. One consumer needed a matching guard. cache-dit averages its residual-difference statistics across the TP x SP slice using the DIT group, and that all-reduce had no world-size check, so on a single GPU it would now stage device tensors through the host on every cached block of every step. Averaging over one rank returns the input, so the patched `similarity` returns the local value instead of running the collective. Every other consumer of these groups already short-circuits: collectives in `GroupCoordinator` return early on `world_size == 1`, the device communicator is built only above 1, the ulysses/ring groups are reached only under `sp_size > 1` in `attention/layer.py` and behind `world_size <= 1` early returns in `usp.py`, and the VAE group has no consumer outside its getter. ## Accuracy Tests Bit-exact. RTX 3060 12 GiB, `Wan-AI/Wan2.1-T2V-1.3B-Diffusers`, layerwise offload of dit/text_encoder/vae, 320x576, 9 frames, 8 steps, seed 1234. | | free VRAM after load | peak VRAM | VAE decode | output SHA-256 | |---|---|---|---|---| | before | 6.51 GiB | 11552 MiB | **OOM** | no output produced | | `NCCL_MAX_NCHANNELS=1` control | 11.31 GiB | 6886 MiB | ok | `78a2a963…` | | this PR | 11.06 GiB | 6830 MiB | ok | `78a2a963…` | Two-GPU regression on the same box, `--num-gpus 2`: patched and unpatched produce the same output, SHA-256 `361bb915…`, so the multi-rank path is unaffected. New unit test `test_single_rank_device_group.py` covers backend selection for single-rank and multi-rank groups (3 tests, 5 subtests). Existing `test_cache_dit_integration.py` passes with the guard (12 tests together). CI note: `multimodal-gen-test-1-npu-a3` is red here, but every diffusion testcase on that runner is red on unrelated branches too (see #35511, where `ernie_image_t2i_1npu`, `flux_image_t2i_npu`, `flux_2_klein_4b_t2i_1npu`, `z_image_t2i_1npu` and `wan2_1_t2v_1.3b_1_npu` all fail and the job ends with `Executing the custom container implementation failed`). The NPU lane cannot vet this change right now. ## Speed Tests and Profiling No change to per-step time — 1.10 s/step before, 1.06 s/step after, within the run-to-run noise band measured across this configuration. The groups involved never carried traffic. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #32291208968](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32291208968)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32291208893](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32291208893)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [Fix] Preserve deterministic DSpark target-verify parity
signals.text: ## Motivation Addresses #35150. With deterministic inference, ordinary Qwen3.8 decode and linear DSpark `TARGET_VERIFY` differed in two numerically relevant places: - decode rounds the GDN beta value through the activation dtype, while target verify kept it in FP32; - decode uses `decode_attention_fwd`, while target verify used `extend_attention_fwd_unified`. Either difference can perturb the persistent GDN state over repeated reject/commit rounds. A routing-only negative control still diverged from the clean packed-decode Base output at token 13 with all 95 drafts rejected, so attention routing alone is insufficient. ## Modifications - Round target-verify beta through its source activation dtype before accumulating in FP32. - Represent an unmasked linear verify block as independent decode streams with KV lengths `prefix_len + 1, ..., prefix_len + verify_len`. - Route only the deterministic CUDA DSpark target-worker path through the existing Triton decode kernel, in eager execution and CUDA Graph replay. - Preserve the existing path for non-deterministic inference, draft workers, masked/tree or ragged verification, MLA, DCP, sliding-window attention, unified memory, encoder-decoder models, and non-CUDA platforms. ## Validation Status Validation uses one NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5090 with CUDA 13.0, `RadixArk/Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4` and `RadixArk/Qwen3.8-27B-DSpark`, TP=1, Triton attention, deterministic inference, FP32 SSM state, gamma=1, and the exact 96-token reproduction from #35150. - Clean production Base packed-decode oracle: 96 tokens, SHA256 `3ca7a432820875b0dc7c1f2d2e644664e8b864947592a0e876d00400848b6e72`. - Routing-only negative control: 0/95 drafts accepted and first divergence from the clean Base output at token 13. - The combined beta and attention changes match a sequential/unpacked decode diagnostic, but fail against the clean production packed-decode Base oracle: 0/95 drafts accepted, first divergence at output token 6 (`Base=279`, `DSpark=781`), DSpark SHA256 `5fc99930b4c8f106a1267003582448c2f9bfe1f17c4db52839924cfc8e830fa1`. - This PR remains Draft while the remaining packed GDN decode difference is localized; the current commit does not yet fix #35150. - Focused GQA probe: target-verify attention is bitwise equal to sequential decode (`unequal=0`, `max_abs=0`); eager and CUDA Graph `kv_indptr`, KV indices, and split metadata are identical. - `py_compile`, Black 26.1.0, Ruff, and `git diff --check` pass. ## Speed Tests and Profiling No speed claim. The new path is selected only for explicit deterministic inference, where decode parity is the goal. Default non-deterministic serving is unchanged. ## Related Work - The beta-rounding hunk is also present in #34734 by @qq1060; credit to that PR for identifying this alignment. That broader feature PR adds ragged and checkpoint support but does not route deterministic verification through decode and explicitly leaves greedy equivalence unresolved. signals.title: Fix: omit null id/name in streaming tool call deltas
signals.text: ## Problem Streaming `tool_calls` continuation chunks currently emit explicit nulls: ```json // first chunk — OK {"tool_calls":[{"id":"call_abc","index":0,"type":"function","function":{"name":"get_weather","arguments":""}}]} // continuation chunks — id/name serialized as null {"tool_calls":[{"id":null,"index":0,"type":"function","function":{"name":null,"arguments":"{"city":"}}]} ``` `ToolCall`/`FunctionResponse` are built with `id=None`/`name=None` for argument-delta chunks (see `_process_tool_call_stream` and `_check_for_unstreamed_tool_args` in `serving_chat.py`), and `model_dump_json()` serializes `None` as JSON `null`. ## Why this is wrong The de-facto OpenAI streaming contract is that `id`/`function.name`/`type` appear **only in the first delta** of a tool call; continuation chunks carry just `index` and `function.arguments`: - OpenAI's own wire format omits these fields in continuation chunks (developers observe the fields are absent, not null: https://community.openai.com/t/streaming-with-tools-missing-tool-id-name/997791). The `null` values shown in parts of the docs are SDK object reprs, not wire JSON. - vLLM, the other major OpenAI-compatible server, omits unset delta fields via `model_dump_json(exclude_unset=True)` (https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/vllm/entrypoints/openai/chat_completion/serving.py). - The OpenAI streaming reference marks `id`/`function.name` as optional (https://developers.openai.com/api/reference/resources/chat/subresources/completions/streaming-events), and the established convention is omission. ## Why it breaks clients Delta mergers that treat `null` as an explicit value (e.g. `x !== undefined`, the common OpenAI-SDK-style merge) overwrite the `id`/`function.name` streamed in the first chunk with `null`. The accumulated tool call then has an empty name, failing with errors like `unknown tool ""`. This was observed in production against a DeepSeek-V4 sglang deployment (`tool_call_parser=deepseekv4`), but the bug is in the generic OpenAI adapter and affects every `--tool-call-parser`. The same failure mode was reported against vLLM backends emitting nulls (https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/26412). Similar behavior is observed in https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/master/packages/llm/llm-deepseek/src/translate.ts#L160 ## Fix Add `model_serializer(mode="wrap")` to `ToolCall` and `FunctionResponse` that drops `None` `id`/`name`/`arguments` from the serialized output. This matches the existing `DeltaMessage` serializer pattern in the same file. Non-streaming responses are unaffected: `id`/`name`/`arguments` are always present there. ## Clarification Fix implemented by codex and reviewed by human ## Tests Added unit tests in `test/registered/unit/entrypoints/openai/test_protocol.py`: - continuation chunk: `id`/`name` omitted, `index`/`arguments` preserved - first chunk: `id`/`name`/`arguments` kept <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32350299604](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32350299604)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32350299398](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32350299398)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32350300881](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32350300881)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [EAGLE] Prune draft-extend logits to selected rows
signals.text: ## Motivation During EAGLE draft extension under CUDA graph execution, the model computes full-vocabulary logits for every draft row even though the speculative worker only consumes selected per-request rows. The unnecessary LM-head rows increase graph time and temporary memory usage on the decode critical path. ## Modifications - Select the rows consumed by the speculative verifier before applying the LM head during draft-extend CUDA graph execution. - Keep the full six-row draft forward unchanged so hidden-state and speculative-state evolution remain identical. - Preserve the eager path and existing output contract while sizing the graph logits buffer for the selected rows. ## Accuracy Tests | Natural-acceptance metric | Baseline | Candidate | | --- | ---: | ---: | | Completed requests | 112 / 112 | 112 / 112 | | Output length | 860 | 860 | | Mean acceptance length | 3.684250 | 3.652805 | | Acceptance rate | 0.536375 | 0.530488 | | CUDA graph enabled | Yes | Yes | | Queue / retractions / errors | 0 / 0 / 0 | 0 / 0 / 0 | ## Speed Tests and Profiling - Setup: Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-NVFP4 on one node with 4 GB300 GPUs, TP4/DP4/EP4 with DP attention, FP8 KV cache, TRTLLM-MHA, FlashInfer CuTeDSL MoE plus FlashInfer A2A for target and draft, NEXTN with 5 speculative steps and 6 draft tokens, online-NVFP4 draft weights, ReplaySSM circular history, Mamba `extra_buffer`, and CUDA graph tiers through batch 32. - Workload: one frozen 88,786-token input repeated as a 112-request cohort, 112 warmup requests with OSL 64, 112 measurement requests with exact OSL 860, temperature 0, fixed AL 4.8, and no request replenishment during the measured pure-generation interval. - Measurement gate: all four ranks must simultaneously report achieved batch 28, CUDA graph enabled, queue depth 0, and no completion/drain row inside the selected interval. | Serving metric | Baseline | Candidate | Delta | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | | Stable rank intervals | 17 / 17 / 17 / 17 | 17 / 17 / 17 / 16 | — | | Mean context tokens/rank | 103,367.5 | 102,725.7 | -0.6209% | | Target-step host time | 29.688688 ms | 28.996720 ms | -0.691968 ms / -2.3307% | | Fixed-AL4.8 output tokens/s/GPU | 4,526.977 | 4,635.007 | +2.3864% | - To remove the small context difference, an independent exact-context match paired 40 windows at the same mean context of 102,342.4 tokens/rank and measured 4,542.499 to 4,653.987 output tokens/s/GPU (+2.4543%). - The final zero-resident-context drain row is excluded from both arms. | Nsight metric for draft-extend graph `10658` | Baseline | Candidate | Delta | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | | Graph time/GPU-step | 1.113471 ms | 0.974980 ms | -0.138491 ms / -12.44% | | Selected-row projection | 0.371574 ms | 0.296726 ms | -0.074848 ms | | Large output copy | 0.098430 ms | 0.017771 ms | -0.080659 ms | | Graph capture memory | 0.15 GB | 0.07 GB | -0.08 GB / -53.3% | - The Nsight capture contains 40 actual-B28 steps on every rank with CUDA graph enabled and queue depth 0. - Draft-decode graph `10637` still performs four full-vocabulary projections per target step by design; this optimization only owns draft-extend graph `10658`. - `Output tokens/s/GPU` is an engine-side pure-generation metric derived from the fixed-B28 target-step window, not a service-level AIPerf total-throughput metric. - As a cross-engine diagnostic only, applying the measured within-SGL gain to the fixed-work authority gives 4,608.074 output tokens/s/GPU versus TRT-LLM at 4,791.788, or 96.166% with a 3.834% remaining gap; this does not replace a direct final integration comparison. ## Checklist - signals.title: [Bugfix] Fix full prefill CUDA graph padding and EAGLE capture
signals.text: ## Motivation Full prefill CUDA graphs replay fixed token buckets that may be larger than the live batch. Models that mask padded hidden states need the live `num_token_non_padded` boundary even when attention tensors are not gathered. Without it, padded rows can propagate through the captured graph. EAGLE target prefill also consumes the full target hidden-state sequence. FullCG previously captured the configured return-hidden-state mode, which could be insufficient and force target prefill back to eager execution. ## Modifications - Register and populate `num_token_non_padded` for FullCG, including non-gathered execution. - Capture `FULL` hidden states for EAGLE target prefill under FullCG while retaining `LAST` for breakable draft workers. - Keep the EAGLE eager fallback specific to `tc_piecewise`, whose fixed capture ceiling can remain below `FULL`. - Add focused regression tests for the non-gathered token boundary and FullCG EAGLE admission. ## Accuracy Tests No model math or kernels are changed. - 42 focused unit tests passed, including 2 parameterized subtests. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Not applicable. The changes update CUDA graph metadata and capture mode; they do not add work to attention or model kernels. ## Checklist - [x] Format code with the repository pre-commit configuration. - [x] Add focused regression tests. - [x] No documentation update is required. - [x] No speed benchmark is required for this graph-correctness fix. - [x] Follow the SGLang code style guidance. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:no_entry_sign: [Run #32325612785](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32325612785)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32325612649](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32325612649)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32325612768](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32325612768)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [model-gateway] Add opt-in `fips` feature using the AWS-LC FIPS module
signals.text: ## Motivation Some deployments (government and other regulated environments) require all cryptography to come from a FIPS 140-3 validated module. This PR adds an opt-in `fips` cargo feature to sgl-model-gateway so those users can build a compliant gateway. Default builds are not affected. ## Modifications Behind the new `fips` feature (off by default): - rustls uses the AWS-LC FIPS provider instead of ring for all TLS (HTTPS server and the reqwest/kube outbound clients; tonic is built without TLS features and does no TLS itself). - JWT verification uses the jsonwebtoken AWS-LC backend. - The wasm module SHA-256 hash uses AWS-LC. - `aws-lc-fips-sys` uses a normal caret requirement (`0.14`) so builds pick up the latest AWS-LC FIPS release (currently 0.14.1, bundling AWS-LC FIPS 4.1.0). AWS-LC FIPS is a CMVP-validated module lineage (see [certificate #5314](https://csrc.nist.gov/projects/cryptographic-module-validation-program/certificate/5314) for the 3.x static module). The exact module version in any given build can be read from the binary with `strings <binary> | grep "AWS-LC FIPS"`. Deployments that need a version literally listed on an issued certificate can pin, for example `=0.13.11` (AWS-LC FIPS 3.1.0, the exact version on #5314). - At startup the gateway asserts the installed rustls provider is FIPS and that the AWS-LC JWT provider was installed. If not, it fails to start. - The Python and Go bindings expose the same `fips` feature. Changes that apply to all builds: - New `src/crypto.rs` with `ensure_crypto_provider_installed()`, which replaces the two previous ad-hoc `ring::default_provider().install_default()` call sites, and a `Sha256Hasher` wrapper used for wasm module hashing. Default builds keep ring and RustCrypto sha2. - `jsonwebtoken` upgraded 9.3 to 10.4 and `smg-auth` 1.0.0 to 1.2.2. jsonwebtoken 9 was hardwired to ring; version 10 has pluggable backends. Default builds use its `rust_crypto` backend. Not changed: blake3/xxhash (used for cache-aware routing and consistent hashing, not security relevant) and the openssl dependency (test cert generation and the optional `vendored-openssl` feature only). Build note: `--features fips` (and therefore `--all-features`, used by `make lint` and the rust CI lint job) needs cmake and Go to compile AWS-LC. The CI lint job passes since GitHub runners include both. <details> <summary>FIPS verification evidence</summary> - The fips binary embeds the AWS-LC FIPS module version string (checked with `strings`, currently `AWS-LC FIPS 4.1.0`); the default binary does not. - The fips binary starts cleanly and serves `/liveness` and `/health`. - TLS handshake against the fips build negotiates TLS 1.3 `TLS_AES_256_GCM_SHA384`. Forcing `TLS_CHACHA20_POLY1305_SHA256` (not FIPS approved) fails against the fips build and succeeds against the default build, showing the provider swap is active. - Known residual: ring and the jsonwebtoken RustCrypto backend remain linked (cargo features are additive) but are never selected at runtime, which the startup assertions enforce. smg-auth internally uses RustCrypto sha2 for API key fingerprinting; that code only runs when control plane API keys are configured. </details> ## Accuracy Tests N/A, no model or inference code touched. ## Speed Tests and Profiling N/A, default builds keep the same crypto stack. The fips path only affects opt-in builds. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). (`cargo test --test security_tests` passes 48/48 with and without `--features fips`, covering JWT auth, API keys, and mTLS. `cargo clippy --all-targets` is clean in both modes.) - [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). (N/A, no model or inference code touched.) - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process). 2. signals.title: [MUSA] Harden CI dependencies and diffusion warmup
signals.text: ## Summary Harden the SGLang MUSA CI Python environment and restore steady-state timing for the Wan diffusion smoke. ## Changes - Isolate each GitHub Actions MUSA job with a task-local `PYTHONUSERBASE`, while retaining pip's shared wheel cache so independent jobs do not repeatedly cold-download the same artifacts. - Install and verify the MUSA Triton and `torchada` wheels by version, SHA256, MUSA metadata, and `mtgpu` backend. - Install vendor wheels without dependency resolution, then generate constraints from the installed MUSA stack. Fail closed on mismatched Torch/Torch-MUSA lines, an unexpected Triton target, missing MUSA runtime/device, or an incompatible `compressed-tensors` version. - Add unit coverage for stack constraint generation and validation, and make all `scripts/ci/musa/**` changes select the relevant MUSA CI lanes. - Extend MUSA dependency-install timeouts from 15 to 30 minutes to accommodate cold cache/bootstrap jobs. - Remove the stale per-token FP8 AOT test command from the PR and nightly MUSA workflows. The upstream test was removed during the CUDA JIT migration; MUSA production continues to use its AOT path, so this PR does not substitute a CUDA-only registered test. - For the MUSA Wan 2.1 1-GPU benchmark, use request-based warmup. The first parsed request is `832x480x24f`, while the generic server warmup is capped at 17 frames; warming the exact request shape keeps first-shape initialization out of measured denoising metrics. ## Root cause The original MUSA CI failure was not a generally slow Wan model. Every fresh server paid a large first `Denoise Step 0` cost because the synthetic server warmup used 17 frames and the benchmark request used 24 frames. Steps 1–49 remained near the normal steady-state latency. In parallel, reused runner user-sites allowed public dependency resolution to replace the MUSA Triton stack with generic Torch/Triton packages. The Wan change is benchmark warmup hygiene: it does not claim to eliminate cold-start wall time for a first production request. ## Validation - `python3 -m unittest scripts/ci/musa/test_musa_python_stack.py` — 5 passed. - `bash -n scripts/ci/musa/musa_install_dependency.sh` and ShellCheck passed. - Targeted/full pre-commit checks passed for the changed files. - [Exact squashed-head MUSA run](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32361329056) passed all MUSA jobs after rerunning network-only checkout/clone failures: Qwen-Image, Wan 2.1, 2-GPU diffusion, `sgl-kernel`, multimodal layer tests, and the MUSA finish gate. - On that exact head, the Wan request warmup was logged as `832x480x24f, 1/50 steps`; the measured request then passed 50 denoising steps with step 0 `184.75 ms`, average `356.25 ms`, median `354.41 ms`, and `1 passed`. - Qwen-Image may log a non-fatal synthetic-warmup compiler/`.mubin` warning; its real request completed successfully, so that warning is intentionally out of scope here. ## Scope This PR is limited to MUSA CI dependency isolation/validation, stale MUSA workflow cleanup, and the Wan benchmark warmup mismatch. It does not change the global diffusion warmup policy or attempt to fix the non-blocking Qwen-Image compiler warning. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #32361329332](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32361329332)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32361329006](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32361329006)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #32361329046](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32361329046)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: Bound DSpark rejection sampling workspace
signals.text: ## Motivation DSpark's non-greedy verification path materializes full-vocabulary probability tensors for rejection sampling: - draft probabilities: [B, gamma_rows, V] - target probabilities: [B, verify_num_draft_tokens, V] - probability dtype: FP32 The simultaneous workspace therefore scales as: B x (gamma_rows + verify_num_draft_tokens) x V x 4 bytes For Qwen3-8B (V=151,936) and DSpark block7, this workspace becomes the dominant peak-memory allocation at large batches. In local RTX PRO 6000 pressure tests, the original path did not complete reliably at B=3072 and B=4096 and reported CUDA illegal memory access. This PR bounds the probability workspace by splitting verification at request boundaries. This is related to [vLLM #48630](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/48630), which bounds rejection-sampling workspace for large batches. This PR targets SGLang DSpark specifically, reuses the existing rejection sampler, and does not change the acceptance rule. ## Design ### Request-boundary chunked verification The batch is divided into request-aligned chunks. Each chunk independently constructs draft probabilities and invokes the existing rejection sampler. A request is never split across chunks, so its candidate tokens, target logits, sampling metadata, and cutoff lengths remain aligned. The original full-batch path is retained when the estimated workspace fits the available memory. Chunking is therefore only used when the configured budget or current memory pressure requires it. ### Workspace-aware planner The planner estimates the simultaneous FP32 draft/target probability workspace and selects a safe chunk size from: - the configured workspace target; - current CUDA free memory; - reusable bytes held by the CUDA caching allocator; - a configurable memory headroom. The planner also supports a fixed chunk size for deterministic tests. With the default workspace budget of zero, the existing full-batch behavior remains unchanged. ### Sampling and performance preservation Chunking must not change rejection-sampling randomness or add unnecessary tensor copies. The implementation therefore: - generates the complete batch of random uniforms once and slices the corresponding ranges for each chunk; - reuses sliced sampling metadata and output buffers; - threads optional random samples through the existing DSpark acceptance path; - keeps the existing accept/reject kernels and only changes the batch dimension passed to them. This avoids regenerating random streams per chunk and limits additional Python scheduling, tensor allocation, and result concatenation overhead. ## Reproduction The PR-specific unit and parity tests can be run with: ~~~bash python -m pytest -q test/registered/spec/dspark/test_dspark_chunked_rejection_sampling.py ~~~ For the service experiment, set the model paths and start two separate server instances. The first command is the unchanged full-batch baseline; the second enables the 4 GiB workspace planner. ~~~bash export MODEL_PATH=/path/to/Qwen3-8B export DRAFT_PATH=/path/to/dspark_qwen3_8b_block7 # Baseline SGLANG_DSPARK_RS_MAX_WORKSPACE_BYTES=0 \ python -m sglang.launch_server \ --model-path ${MODEL_PATH} \ --speculative-algorithm DSPARK \ --speculative-draft-model-path ${DRAFT_PATH} \ --speculative-dspark-block-size 7 \ --host 0.0.0.0 --port 30000 # Chunked planner SGLANG_DSPARK_RS_MAX_WORKSPACE_BYTES=4294967296 \ SGLANG_DSPARK_RS_DYNAMIC_MEMORY=1 \ SGLANG_DSPARK_RS_MEMORY_HEADROOM_BYTES=536870912 \ python -m sglang.launch_server \ --model-path ${MODEL_PATH} \ --speculative-algorithm DSPARK \ --speculative-draft-model-path ${DRAFT_PATH} \ --speculative-dspark-block-size 7 \ --host 0.0.0.0 --port 30000 ~~~ After each server is ready, run the same workload command and sweep --max-concurrency: ~~~bash python -m sglang.benchmark.serving --backend sglang --host 127.0.0.1 --port 30000 --model ${MODEL_PATH} --dataset-name random --num-prompts 1000 --random-input-len 1024 --random-output-len 1024 --max-concurrency 1024 --output-file result.json ~~~ ## Correctness The chunked path continues to use the existing target distribution, draft distribution, and rejection-sampling kernels. Under the same random inputs, local parity tests verify: - acceptance length; - bonus token; - trim length; - sampled output; - mixed full-batch/chunked execution behavior. Unsupported configurations retain the existing path rather than silently changing sampling semantics. ## Local validation Environment: Qwen3-8B + DSpark block7, SGLang main, RTX PRO 6000. ### Memory and throughput The following results come from three independent service runs with a 4 GiB workspace target. Throughput is shown relative to the unchanged full-batch baseline. | Metric | Original full-batch path | Chunked planner | Result | |---|---:|---:|---:| | GPU memory high-water mark | 73.0 GiB | 58.3 GiB | -20.1% | | B=128 throughput | 100% | 98.92% | -1.08% | | B=256 throughput | 100% | 101.15% | +1.15% | | B=512 throughput | 100% | 92.29% | -7.71% | | B=1024 throughput | 100% | 97.22% | -2.78% | | Batch | Original full-batch path | Chunked planner | Result | |---:|---|---|---| | B=3072 | CUDA illegal memory access | HTTP 200 | completes | | B=4096 | CUDA illegal memory access | HTTP 200 | completes | ### Accuracy and sampling parity On a 100-question GSM8K regression: | Check | Original full-batch path | Chunked planner | Result | |---|---:|---:|---| | GSM8K accuracy | 90/100 | 90/100 | unchanged | | Parse success | 100/100 | 100/100 | unchanged | | Final answers | identical reference | identical reference | identical | | Complete output text | identical reference | identical reference | identical | | Output SHA256 | identical reference | identical reference | identical | Fixed-random-input parity tests also matched acceptance length, bonus token, trim length, and sampled output. The local GPU unit and parity suite passed 5 tests with 22 subtests. ## Configuration used for experiments The current prototype exposes environment controls for experimentation: - SGLANG_DSPARK_RS_MAX_WORKSPACE_BYTES - SGLANG_DSPARK_RS_DYNAMIC_MEMORY - SGLANG_DSPARK_RS_MEMORY_HEADROOM_BYTES - SGLANG_DSPARK_RS_CHUNK_SIZE - SGLANG_DSPARK_RS_FULL_BATCH_MAX The public configuration surface and naming should be aligned with SGLang conventions after review. ## Scope and follow-up This PR targets DSpark's rejection-sampling verification path. It does not change the rejection rule or introduce a new sampler. Follow-up work can add framework-level configuration, broader logprob/grammar coverage, and larger standardized benchmark matrices after the core design is reviewed. ## Review focus Please review: 1. whether the workspace estimate covers the allocations that should be bounded; 2. whether allocator-reusable memory should be included in the planner; 3. whether random-uniform and output-buffer reuse preserve existing sampling semantics; 4. the preferred public configuration and test placement. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32335684428](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32335684428)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32335684260](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32335684260)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32335684445](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32335684445)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->
