signals.title: [diffusion] fix: keep large vocab tables in host memory under layerwise offload
signals.text: ## Motivation Layerwise offload streams a component's layers and then moves everything left over to the device, on the reasonable assumption that the remainder is small — norms, a patch embed, a time embed. For a text encoder it is not: umT5-XXL's token table is `256384 x 4096` in fp32, so **3.91 GiB stays resident**, which on a 12 GiB card is a third of the device. That residency buys almost nothing. A vocab table is read by **gather, not GEMM** — one row per token — so Wan's 512-token prompt touches 8 MiB of those 3.91 GiB, and it does so once per request rather than once per denoising step: | | | |---|---| | resident | 3.91 GiB | | read per request | 512 x 4096 x 4 B = 8 MiB | | utilisation | 0.2% | Streaming it layer by layer would be worse still (3.91 GiB moved to read 8 MiB), so the table belongs in host memory with the lookup running there and only the result crossing PCIe. This is what made `--performance-mode auto` unusable on a 12 GiB card: warmup at the model's default workload had no headroom left and failed at every probe size. ## Modifications Before the post-streaming `.to(device)`, swap tables above 256 MiB for placeholders; restore them afterwards and hook the module so its input goes to the host and its output comes back. Both call sites are covered — `LayerwiseOffloadManager._initialize` and the multi-group path in `configure_layerwise_offload`. Sharded tables are left alone: they are already divided by the world size, and their output feeds an all-reduce that expects a device tensor. ## Accuracy Tests Bit-exact. RTX 3060 12 GiB, `Wan-AI/Wan2.1-T2V-1.3B-Diffusers`, layerwise offload of dit/text_encoder/vae, 320x576, 9 frames, 8 steps, seed 1234 — **three runs each way, six runs, one SHA-256** (`78a2a963...`). New `test_host_resident_vocab_table.py` covers selection (large table picked, small table, plain weight matrix and sharded table left alone), the detach/restore round trip, and that the hooked gather matches a plain lookup — 7 tests. The existing layerwise/offload/residency suites pass unchanged (136 tests together). ## Speed Tests and Profiling Same runs, mean of three: | | before | after | |---|---|---| | peak VRAM | 8540 MiB | **4447 MiB** (-4.0 GiB, -48%) | | `TextEncodingStage` | 3374.9 ms | 3384.4 ms (+0.28%) | | total request | 13838.5 ms | 13815.8 ms | The encode-stage cost is the CPU gather plus an 8 MiB host-to-device copy, once per request. It does not separate from noise: the per-run ranges overlap (patched 3377–3389 vs baseline 3369–3382), and the total request is lower after the change. Peak VRAM is also markedly steadier (4420–4500 vs 8000–9180). ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #32339068564](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32339068564)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32339068469](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32339068469)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #32339068556](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32339068556)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [NPU] Adapt DFlash2 speculative decoding to Ascend NPUs
signals.text: ## Motivation DFlash2 (#35371) landed on main as the successor to DFlash: a block-diffusion drafter with local grouped convolutions and a candidate selector, currently CUDA-only. First-generation DFlash drafts already run on Ascend NPUs (#23122, #31739), but the DFlash2 checkpoints cannot serve on NPU yet, and I found no existing issue/PR tracking this. This PR adapts the DFlash2 verify path so it can serve on Ascend NPUs (and any Triton-free environment), while keeping the CUDA path byte-for-byte identical. ## Changes - **Triton import guards** (`triton_compat.py`, new): kernel modules in `kernels/ops/speculative/` imported triton unconditionally, which broke module import on Triton-free Ascend images. The new compat shim degrades `@triton.jit` to a stub that raises only on *launch*, so non-CUDA devices can import the DFlash/DSpark modules and dispatch to torch fallbacks. This is generic: any environment without triton benefits, CUDA is untouched. - **Torch chain speculative-sampling fallback** (`chain_speculative_sampling_torch` in `reject_sampling.py`): buffer-for- buffer mirror of `speculative_sampling_classic_kernel` (same `coin * q < p` accept rule, same residual `max(p - q, 0)` final sampling, NaN draft entries treated as 0, same `predicts`/`accept_index`/`accept_token_num` layouts). Used by DSpark on NPU and covered by unit tests on CPU. - **Device dispatch** (`dspark_accept.py`): `_accept_sampling_core` now routes through `inputs_on_cuda(candidates)` — triton kernel on CUDA (unchanged), torch fallback elsewhere (NPU/CPU). Also routed the `@triton.jit` helper kernels in this module through the compat shim. - **NPU verify fix** (`dflash_worker_v2.py`): `skip_attn_backend_init` is now `None if _is_npu else True`. The CUDA `prepare_for_verify` pre-plans (load_batch / init_forward_metadata); the NPU branch deliberately leaves planning to the forward path, so marking metadata ready here crashed the NPU graph runner (`raw_num_token` never initialized). - **NPU greedy verify alignment** (`dflash_worker_v2.py`): on NPU, skip the selector full-vocab sampling verify (`_selector_sampling_accept` and the chain-sampling branch) and take the argmax greedy verify instead, matching what EAGLE/first-gen DFLASH already do unconditionally on NPU. The full-vocab path scatters a dense [bs, gamma, vocab] buffer whose cost does not shrink with the verify window; on the 200K-vocab Qwen3.8 it dominates the step. CUDA behavior unchanged. - **Docs**: Qwen3.8-27B cookbook — DFlash2 drafter recipe and NPU support status. ## Tests - New unit tests (`test/registered/unit/spec/test_chain_speculative_sampling.py`, registered in `base-a-test-cpu`): analytic accept/reject/bonus cases, NaN handling, batch independence, statistical losslessness (20k samples, TV < 0.02), triton-compat helpers, and a CUDA parity check that runs the torch and triton kernels on identical buffers (`@skipIf` no CUDA). - Verified end-to-end on Ascend 910C (target `Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B`, draft `z-lab/Qwen3.8-27B-DFlash2`, tp=2): server starts, DFlash2 selector draft loads, both NPU graph captures succeed (incl. the in-graph sampler RNG), and requests pass, before and after the greedy-verify change. ## Plan status - [x] P0: pure-torch chain speculative-sampling verify + device dispatch + CPU unit tests against the Triton reference - [x] P0.5: guard the triton imports so Triton-free environments import the DFlash modules - [x] P1: validate NPU (aclgraph) capture of the DFlash2 selector draft sampler (done on 910C; `SGLANG_DFLASH_EAGER_DRAFT_SAMPLER=1` remains the escape hatch) - [x] P1: e2e greedy + sampling correctness on Ascend (server starts, requests pass) - [x] P2: performance investigation — moved to a follow-up PR. Profiling (phase timing + torch-profiler traces, gated by the new `SGLANG_DFLASH_DEBUG_TIMING` flag) showed the original suspects (vocab-wide `torch.topk` in the selector, dense chain sampling) are not the bottleneck: the selector top-k costs ~0.04 ms/step and DFLASH matches NEXTN kernel-for-kernel. The decode step is bounded by a shared TP2 per-layer allreduce floor (~43 collectives/step) of the target model verify. Optimization directions (accept-length tuning, verify-prep host-path reduction) will be pursued separately. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: **Missing `run-ci` label** -- add it to run CI tests.<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: **Blocked** -- `run-ci` is required first.<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:heavy_minus_sign: **No AMD PR run found for this commit**.<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [Feature] Add DeepEPv2 (ElasticBuffer) MoE A2A backend
signals.text: > Reland of #29525, which was reverted in #35568. > > The revert was caused by one line in the new e2e test: it registered itself to > `runner_config="deepep-8-gpu-h200"`, a runner config that does not exist. > `run_suite.py` validates every registered test's suite before collecting any > of them, so that single bad name aborted unrelated lanes as well -- the ARM CPU > and NPU suites both failed with `Tests registered to invalid suites`. It is > fixed here in a separate commit on top of a clean revert-of-the-revert, so the > restored change can be diffed against the original merge. Running the tests as > single files never goes through `run_suite.py`, which is why local runs stayed > green; `python3 test/run_suite.py --hw cpu --suite base-b-test-cpu-arm64` > reproduces it in one command and now passes. ## Motivation DeepEP v2's `ElasticBuffer` is an NCCL-symmetric-memory all-to-all engine with a fixed per-rank capacity. Fixed capacity means static communication shapes, which makes the MoE decode path CUDA-graph capturable under any topology — including multi-node, where legacy `low_latency` is not available as a graphable path. This PR adds it as a standalone backend `deepep_v2` alongside `deepep`; only expert-parallel dispatch/combine is replaced. Validated on Hopper (H20, H200) and Blackwell (B200 `sm_100`, B300 `sm_103`). ## Modifications - **`layers/moe/token_dispatcher/deepep_v2.py`** (new): the dispatcher. `--deepep-v2-mode direct|hybrid` selects the ElasticBuffer topology — **not** the legacy `normal/low_latency` split. Layout is chosen per batch by inference phase, not by comm mode: decode uses the expanded layout + masked GEMM (static shapes, graph-capturable, available under `hybrid` too), extend/prefill uses the contiguous layout. Single-shot `dispatch()/combine()` with a strict handle lifecycle; the guards run before the DeepEP import check so the module imports cleanly without DeepEP installed. - **`kernels/ops/moe/ep_moe_kernels.py`**: masked-slab repack kernels. A fixed per-expert worker pool keeps the grid static (graph-safe); top-k weights are folded in-kernel; the scale copy takes the source pack-dim stride, which is what makes Blackwell's packed-UE8M0 (column-major) layout correct alongside Hopper's row-major fp32. - **`layers/moe/moe_runner/deep_gemm.py`**: the FP8 adapter (masked decode / contiguous prefill, consuming DeepEP's 128-aligned psum directly as group offsets). `deep_gemm` is the only supported runner: deepep_v2 dispatches FP8 activations plus scales, and no other a2a backend targets a different runner family either. `--moe-runner-backend` is checked at startup, but the runner is chosen per layer by the quant method and several hard-select Triton regardless, so `MoeRunner` rejects the mismatch too — otherwise such a model would reach the permute registry and die on a bare assert after the weights are loaded. - **`layers/moe/ep_moe/layer.py`**: `get_moe_impl_class` resolves `deepep_v2` to `DeepEPMoE` like every other a2a backend — this is what makes the UE8M0 load-time weight requant apply on Blackwell. - **`server_args.py`, `arg_groups/overrides.py`**: the new flags; `ep_size` and `disable_shared_experts_fusion` are declared through the a2a passes, and the runner is validated against `resolved_view(...)` so a model declaration that restores an unsupported runner fails fast. Boot-time capacity check for the chunked-prefill budget. TBO/SBO and enforced shared-expert fusion are rejected at startup. - **`state_capturer/routed_experts.py`**: classify deepep_v2 as a scattered-a2a backend; otherwise `dp_rank > 0` reads unwritten buffer rows under `--enable-return-routed-experts`. - **No CI/Docker changes**: `sgl-deep-ep==0.1.1` already provides `ElasticBuffer`, so CI can exercise this backend as-is; it stays inert for every other configuration, fails fast when DeepEP is missing, and its unit tests need only Triton. - **Tests**: `test_deepep_v2_masked_slab.py` covers the masked-slab repack round-trip -- bf16/fp8, empty experts, the `max_m` boundary, overflow fail-fast, a production packed-UE8M0 scale, and CUDA-graph capture/replay -- and needs only Triton. `test_routed_experts_scattered_a2a.py` pins the capturer's backend classification. `test_routed_experts_dp_readback.py` is the only multi-GPU one: it runs DP>1 with dummy weights over a single 24-expert layer, because `dp_rank 0` sits at buffer offset 0 and looks correct even when the classification is wrong, so nothing below DP>1 can catch that regression; it also covers legacy `deepep` on the same path. Happy to drop or move any of these if they are not worth the coverage. ## Usage DeepEP v2 needs NCCL symmetric memory, which SGLang turns off by default (`NCCL_CUMEM_ENABLE` is set to `int(enable_symm_mem)` when the variable is unset), so an otherwise correct launch fails with `nccl.cu:104: Communicator does not support symmetric memory!`. Pass `NCCL_CUMEM_ENABLE=1` (used for every benchmark here) or `--enable-symm-mem`, which also works but additionally enables NVLS and a 4 GB symmetric-memory prealloc. `SGLANG_DEEPEP_V2_NUM_MAX_DISPATCH_TOKENS_PER_RANK` is the fixed per-rank buffer capacity. It must cover the per-rank chunk (`--chunked-prefill-size / dp_size` under DP attention), and that chunk must be a multiple of `page_size` — with `page_size=256, dp_size=8` the smallest usable pair is capacity 256 with `--chunked-prefill-size 2048`. Smaller capacity is better for decode; prefill servers size it to their chunk budget and add `--disable-cuda-graph`. No extra install step: the pinned `sgl-deep-ep==0.1.1` ships `ElasticBuffer` (`deep_ep 2.1.0`), so this backend runs on a stock environment. Re-validated on H20 x8 against that wheel with no source build and no code change -- `direct` GSM8K 0.970 / MMLU 0.890, `hybrid` 0.970 / 0.886, three-question gate passing in both modes. Earlier development used a DeepEP source build at `d4f41e4`; the packaged API is a superset of what the dispatcher calls. Multi-node: add `--deepep-v2-mode hybrid --enable-dp-lm-head --nnodes 2 --node-rank {0,1}`. Blackwell with a BF16 `wo_a` checkpoint: `SGLANG_OPT_FP8_WO_A_GEMM=0`. ## Accuracy Tests DeepSeek-V4-Flash-FP8, `--tp 8 --dp 8 --ep 8 --enable-dp-attention`, `deep_gemm`, kv fp8. | | deepep_v2 `direct` | deepep_v2 `hybrid` | deepep | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | H20 x8 — MMLU (500) | 0.888 | 0.890 | 0.888 | | H20 x8 — GSM8K (100) | 0.980 | 0.980 | 0.970 | | B200 x8 — MMLU (500) | 0.886 | 0.884 | — | | B200 x8 — GSM8K (100) | 0.950 | 0.970 | — | MMLU at 500 examples has a ~1.4pp standard error at this accuracy, which is wider than every gap in the table; repeat runs of one configuration spanned 0.884-0.896. These numbers show the absence of a systematic shift against the same-node `deepep` baseline, not a ranking. The three-question gate passes on every configuration above. Unit tests (CI, no DeepEP required): masked-slab repack including a production packed-UE8M0 scale and CUDA-graph capture/replay, handle-lifecycle guards, server-args resolution, capturer classification, plus a DP>1 routed-experts readback e2e. The three-question gate also passes on the multi-node configuration below. Earlier validation on the same dispatch path: needle retrieval across chunk boundaries and 8-way concurrent requests 24/24; prefill/decode disaggregation functional. ## Speed Tests | | deepep_v2 | deepep | delta | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | H20 x8 decode | 4,339 tok/s | 4,379 | -0.9% | | H20 x8 prefill | 22,353 in_tok/s | 21,651 | +3.2% | | B200 x8 decode | 8,429 tok/s | 8,675 | -2.8% | | B200 x8 prefill | 32,447 in_tok/s | 31,533 | +2.9% | Each backend pair was measured back-to-back on the same node, on torch 2.13 / sglang-kernel 0.4.6.post1, with the prefill cells interleaved so drift cannot bias one side. H20 prefill averages 4 samples per cell (sd 95 and 72), B200 prefill 2 per cell (sd 132 and 57); decode is one cell per side. Decode reproduces well across nodes -- deepep_v2 measured 8,385 / 8,403 / 8,429 tok/s on three different B200 nodes -- but the `deepep` side moved more, so the decode delta has landed between -0.9% and -2.8% across runs; read it as "a low single-digit percentage behind" rather than a precise figure. Prefill has been consistently ahead by roughly 3%. Multi-node (2x H20x8, TP16/EP16/DP16, `hybrid`, same protocol): **4,610 tok/s** decode with the masked-GEMM + CUDA-graph path over RDMA — a graphable cross-node decode path legacy `low_latency` does not provide — and **20,688 in_tok/s** prefill (two samples: 20,322 / 21,054). There is no same-fabric deepep baseline for this pair: DeepEP's NVSHMEM data plane does not complete across nodes on this RoCE setup, reproduced with DeepEP's own `test_internode.py` outside SGLang. Reproduction (5 rounds per boot, mean of the last 3; prefill flushes the radix cache before each round): ```bash # common: NCCL_CUMEM_ENABLE=1, SGLANG_DEEPEP_V2_NUM_SMS=20, capacity 1024 # deepep_v2: --moe-a2a-backend deepep_v2 --deepep-v2-mode direct # deepep : --moe-a2a-backend deepep --deepep-mode low_latency|normal --deepep-dispatcher-output-dtype fp8 # (with SGLANG_DEEPEP_NUM_MAX_DISPATCH_TOKENS_PER_RANK=1024) NCCL_CUMEM_ENABLE=1 SGLANG_DEEPEP_V2_NUM_SMS=20 \ SGLANG_DEEPEP_V2_NUM_MAX_DISPATCH_TOKENS_PER_RANK=1024 \ python3 -m sglang.launch_server --model-path $MODEL --trust-remote-code \ --tp-size 8 --dp-size 8 --ep-size 8 --enable-dp-attention --context-length 4096 \ --chunked-prefill-size 8192 --moe-runner-backend deep_gemm --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 \ --host 127.0.0.1 --port 30000 $BACKEND_FLAGS \ --mem-fraction-static 0.70 --cuda-graph-max-bs 128 # decode # --mem-fraction-static 0.80 --disable-cuda-graph --disable-piecewise-cuda-graph # prefill # decode python3 -m sglang.bench_serving --backend sglang --port 30000 --dataset-name random \ --num-prompts 128 --random-input-len 1 --random-output-len 1024 --random-range-ratio 1 --max-concurrency 128 # prefill (curl -s localhost:30000/flush_cache before each round) python3 -m sglang.bench_serving --backend sglang --port 30000 --dataset-name random \ --num-prompts 64 --random-input-len 1024 --random-output-len 1 --random-range-ratio 1 --max-concurrency 16 ``` ## Checklist - [x] Format code with pre-commit. - [x] Add unit tests. - [ ] Update documentation (separate follow-up PR). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmarks (above). - [x] Code style. ### Notes for reviewers - Prerequisites: none beyond the current pins -- `sgl-deep-ep==0.1.1` provides `ElasticBuffer`. NCCL symmetric memory must be on (see Usage). - Follow-ups: TBO/SBO comm-compute overlap (a PoC showed the naive two-phase split cannot overlap because `ElasticBuffer.dispatch` is host-blocking; it needs a `return_recv_hook`-style split in DeepEP), adapters for other MoE runners, documentation. signals.title: [Feature] Support partial-page prefix reuse in RadixCache
signals.text: ## Motivation SGLang's paged RadixCache keeps radix-tree ownership page aligned. Before this change, when the logical longest common prefix ended inside a page, only the page-aligned portion was reused and up to `page_size - 1` already-computed tokens were sent through model forward again. This issue is negligible at `page_size=1`, but becomes increasingly relevant with larger physical page sizes such as 16, 32, and 64. With larger practical page sizes such as 16, 32, and 64, treating the physical page boundary as the only logical reuse boundary can discard a meaningful amount of already-computed work. At those sizes, treating the physical page boundary as the only logical reuse boundary can discard a meaningful amount of already-computed work. If the divergence position is uniformly distributed within a page, the average missed reuse is `(page_size - 1) / 2`: 7.5, 15.5, and 31.5 tokens for page sizes 16, 32, and 64 respectively. The page boundary should therefore remain the radix tree's physical ownership boundary, but it is no longer always the best logical prefix-reuse boundary. This PR experimentally reuses those partial-page KV entries without changing the page-aligned radix-tree structure or ownership model. The matched KV entries are copied into a new request-private physical page, allowing the allocator to continue writing into the remainder of that page. The feature is disabled by default and initially targets the ordinary CUDA FULL-attention Python RadixCache path. ## Modifications 1. Optimize `RadixKey.match()` when the first page is already known to match. - Add the `first_page_matched` hint. - Start the galloping search at `page_size` with a `page_size` step instead of rechecking tokens from zero. - Use the hint only at call sites where radix child selection has already proved that the first page matches. - Preserve the existing page-aligned return behavior. 2. Add experimental partial-page prefix reuse behind `--enable-partial-prefix-reuse` (default: disabled). - Add an opt-in `return_exact=True` mode to `RadixKey.match()` while keeping its default return value page aligned. - Keep every legacy tree/split caller on the default page-aligned result; only the experimental partial-reuse path requests the exact LCP. - Preserve both the exact token-level LCP and its page-aligned boundary. - Keep tree splitting, ownership, insertion, eviction, and accounting page aligned. - When enabled, discover partial matches either within a legacy-reachable child or, after a child-key miss, by scanning direct children. - Allocate a new request-private physical page and copy the matched KV slots using the existing all-layer `move_kv_cache()` implementation. - Extend `req.prefix_indices` to the exact match length so the matched tokens are removed from EXTEND/model-forward work. - Continue normal paged allocation in the unused portion of the private destination page. - Protect the source radix node with `lock_ref` until the GPU copy and its dependent forward work are safely ordered before source-page reuse. - Clean up private pages and locks on allocation failure, request rejection, unfinished caching, and normal request completion. 3. Restrict the initial implementation to supported configurations. - CUDA - ordinary Python RadixCache - FULL attention - `PagedTokenToKVPoolAllocator` - unquantized NHD `MHATokenToKVPool` - pipeline parallel size 1 - non-EAGLE requests Unsupported configurations fail with an explicit error when the experimental feature is enabled. 4. Add focused unit tests and a reproducible serving benchmark for page sizes 16, 32, and 64. ## Accuracy Tests Relevant cache unit suite: ```bash pytest -q \ test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_radix_cache_unit.py \ test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_hiradix_cache_unit.py \ test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_mamba_unittest.py \ test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_swa_unittest.py ``` Result: ```text 78 passed 87 subtests passed ``` The tests cover exact LCP calculation, page-aligned tree splitting and accounting, source-page lifetime, private-page allocation and KV copying, continuation within the copied page, `req_to_token` mappings, scheduler EXTEND lengths, allocation failure, eviction, request completion, and `page_size=1`. End-to-end deterministic generation parity was also tested with Qwen3-32B BF16, TP=2, generating 32 output tokens: | Page size | Partial tokens | Baseline cached | Reuse cached | Exact output parity | |---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | 16 | 8 | 1024 | 1032 | 5/5 | | 32 | 16 | 1024 | 1040 | 5/5 | | 64 | 32 | 1024 | 1056 | 5/5 | Overall: 15/15 generated outputs were exactly equal, with no request errors. A separate upstream-versus-current, feature-disabled A/B/B/A comparison produced 160/160 identical generated outputs. ## Speed Tests and Profiling All serving measurements used 2 x NVIDIA A100 80 GB, TP=2, ordinary CUDA FULL-attention Python RadixCache, and unquantized NHD paged KV. Baseline and reuse runs used the same checkout; only `--enable-partial-prefix-reuse` changed. Cache construction and exact-shape warmups were excluded. ### TL;DR - On SGLang's `generated-shared-prefix` workload, the representative Qwen3-32B page 64 / C=16 / Uniform result improves throughput by 2.08%, **mean TTFT by 8.71%, median TTFT by 15.38%**, and mean E2E by 2.04%. Controlled experiments show larger gains as the cost and amount of avoided model work increase. - Across the complete official-workload matrix, throughput improves by 0.24%-2.08% and **mean TTFT by 0.51%-10.01%**; P90/P99 remain mixed. - Controlled experiments on Qwen3-8B and Qwen3-32B show substantial gains when partial-page recomputation constitutes a meaningful fraction of EXTEND work. At half-page reuse on Qwen3-32B, throughput improves by 12.0%, 26.5%, and 34.5% for page sizes 16, 32, and 64 respectively at C=16. These output-length-1 experiments isolate the cost/benefit of partial-page reuse and should not be interpreted as production-traffic gains. - The controlled results support the hypothesis that the optimization becomes more valuable as the amount and cost of avoided model work increase: larger page sizes provide more reusable partial tokens, larger models save more absolute TTFT, and higher concurrency compounds the removed EXTEND work. For Qwen3-32B at half-page R, throughput gain grows from 2.3%/4.7%/10.2% at C=1 to 12.0%/26.5%/34.5% at C=16 for page sizes 16/32/64. - With the feature disabled, upstream-master A/B/B/A testing showed no measurable performance regression on code changs within observed run-to-run variance. ### 1. SGLang `generated-shared-prefix` workload This uses SGLang's existing `sglang.benchmark.serving` path and `generated-shared-prefix` dataset without injecting partial matches: - Qwen3-32B BF16, TP=2 - 64 groups x 16 prompts = 1024 requests - requested system/question/output lengths: 2048 / 128 / 256 - uniform and Zipf (`alpha=1.2`) group popularity - official warmup and cache flush behavior Each metric cell reports `reuse disabled -> reuse enabled (relative improvement)`. Throughput is in requests/second and latency is in milliseconds. Positive percentages favor partial-page reuse; negative percentages are regressions. | Page | C | Distribution | Throughput, req/s | Mean TTFT, ms | Median TTFT, ms | P90 TTFT, ms | P99 TTFT, ms | Mean E2E, ms | |---:|---:|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | 16 | 16 | Uniform | 1.3618 -> 1.3651 (+0.24%) | 2464.98 -> 2452.30 (+0.51%) | 1521.98 -> 1493.90 (+1.85%) | 6524.62 -> 6515.02 (+0.15%) | 14927.03 -> 15002.09 (-0.50%) | 11742.33 -> 11714.58 (+0.24%) | | 16 | 16 | Zipf | 1.3632 -> 1.3673 (+0.30%) | 2593.92 -> 2564.83 (+1.12%) | 1655.91 -> 1891.26 (-14.21%) | 5010.27 -> 4850.01 (+3.20%) | 12339.15 -> 12470.60 (-1.07%) | 11730.73 -> 11695.36 (+0.30%) | | 32 | 16 | Uniform | 1.3444 -> 1.3650 (+1.54%) | 2605.67 -> 2452.81 (+5.87%) | 1595.34 -> 1497.16 (+6.15%) | 6764.00 -> 6501.80 (+3.88%) | 16116.10 -> 15968.84 (+0.91%) | 11894.96 -> 11714.52 (+1.52%) | | 32 | 16 | Zipf | 1.3565 -> 1.3712 (+1.08%) | 2638.40 -> 2545.48 (+3.52%) | 1860.77 -> 1907.94 (-2.53%) | 4885.87 -> 4904.34 (-0.38%) | 12512.70 -> 12264.54 (+1.98%) | 11788.46 -> 11662.04 (+1.07%) | | 64 | 8 | Uniform | 0.8767 -> 0.8878 (+1.27%) | 1411.44 -> 1270.16 (+10.01%) | 938.25 -> 761.34 (+18.86%) | 3327.26 -> 3306.45 (+0.63%) | 9697.80 -> 9764.46 (-0.69%) | 9122.19 -> 9007.33 (+1.26%) | | 64 | 16 | Uniform | 1.3410 -> 1.3689 (+2.08%) | 2655.54 -> 2424.26 (+8.71%) | 1792.84 -> 1517.10 (+15.38%) | 6760.16 -> 6676.21 (+1.24%) | 14123.07 -> 14652.62 (-3.75%) | 11925.26 -> 11681.62 (+2.04%) | | 64 | 8 | Zipf | 0.8784 -> 0.8893 (+1.24%) | 1399.78 -> 1260.38 (+9.96%) | 949.34 -> 768.61 (+19.04%) | 2541.69 -> 2566.58 (-0.98%) | 6551.88 -> 6573.17 (-0.33%) | 9103.76 -> 8992.50 (+1.22%) | | 64 | 16 | Zipf | 1.3468 -> 1.3598 (+0.97%) | 2726.34 -> 2606.81 (+4.38%) | 2140.50 -> 1956.04 (+8.62%) | 4958.26 -> 5008.23 (-1.01%) | 12379.58 -> 12962.30 (-4.71%) | 11873.79 -> 11760.36 (+0.96%) | The official workload confirms positive mean TTFT, mean E2E, and throughput results in every measured configuration. On the uniform C=16 workload, disabled mean TTFT increases from 2464.98 ms at page 16 to 2655.54 ms at page 64 because coarse page alignment loses more cached tokens. With partial-page reuse enabled, mean TTFT instead changes from 2452.30 ms at page 16 to 2424.26 ms at page 64, recovering that degradation. This shows that larger pages create more recoverable partial-prefix work; it does not imply that increasing page size universally improves absolute performance. The run generates approximately 2.34M input tokens and 262K output tokens, so the long decode phase dilutes prefill savings in end-to-end throughput. The page-32 uniform result was repeated with launch order reversed. signals.title: [Feature] Coordinate FullCG prefill across DP-attention ranks
signals.text: ## Motivation DP-attention ranks share communication collectives during prefill, so they must agree on both CUDA-graph admission and the captured shape. The existing coordinated admission vote and shared-shape padding only covered BreakableCG, causing otherwise eligible FullCG prefills to fall back to eager execution. ## Modifications - Extend the all-rank prefill CUDA-graph admission vote and shared `MAX_LEN` padding contract to FullCG. - Use the runner's local replay checks during schedule-time admission, including bounded cached-prefix capture capacity and replacement embeddings. - Keep schedule-time and replay-time cached-prefix eligibility in one helper. - Run the existing DP-attention KL E2E coverage against both BreakableCG and FullCG, and assert that lone-rank and cached-prefix requests actually replay a prefill graph. ## Accuracy Tests - BreakableCG DP-attention E2E: 48 cached-prefix samples, prefill KL = 0 and decode KL = 0; both replay assertions passed. - FullCG DP-attention E2E: 48 cached-prefix samples, prefill KL = 0 and decode KL = 0; both replay assertions passed. - Existing prefill CUDA-graph runner unit suite: 5 passed. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Not applicable. This change does not modify graph execution or kernels; it allows eligible FullCG prefills to use the existing captured path under DP attention. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). signals.title: [diffusion] feat: plan pinned host memory against the cgroup cap not the machine
signals.text: ## Motivation Offloaded weights are held in pinned host memory. That is what lets the copy stream run ahead of compute, and it is also the one tier of host memory the kernel can do nothing with: it cannot swap it and it cannot drop it. How much that buys back depends on the host, and it is worth stating the limit up front. Retreating from pinned to pageable only makes pages reclaimable where swap exists. On a swapless host -- the rented 4x4090 box used below reports `Swap: 0B`, and container runtimes commonly disable it -- anonymous pageable pages have nowhere to go either, so the cgroup accounting and the OOM-kill exposure are unchanged. What the budget buys there is narrower: the process stops attempting pins it cannot afford, and the cap becomes visible. Only file-backed pages are reclaimable without swap, and putting the host copy behind a mapping is a separate change. Nothing in the runtime looked at how much host memory was left before committing it. `pin_cpu_memory` is a single global boolean, every layerwise buffer is allocated with it, and grepping `runtime/managers` and `runtime/loader` for `psutil` returns nothing. On Wan2.1-1.3B that is 21.16 GB of text encoder pinned for the life of the server; H3's components are considerably larger. Reading psutil would not have been enough on its own. `virtual_memory()` comes from /proc/meminfo, which is host-wide and blind to a container's limit: | source | value | |---|---| | `psutil.virtual_memory().total` | 2015.7 GiB | | cgroup v1 `memory.limit_in_bytes` | **1117.2 GiB** | Measured on a rented 4x RTX 4090 box. A 900 GiB over-report, in exactly the direction that gets a container killed. Serving runs in containers, so the cap has to be read directly. ## Modifications New `host_memory_budget.py`: - `cgroup_memory_limit_bytes()` reads the cap and current usage from cgroup v2 (`memory.max`) or v1 (`memory.limit_in_bytes`), handling v2's `max` keyword and v1's near-2^63 sentinel for "unlimited". - `host_memory_available_bytes()` returns the smaller of what the kernel reports free and what the cgroup still allows. - `HostPinBudget` hands out pin allowances until the headroom runs out, keeping a reserve of `max(5%, 2 GiB)` so the process can still allocate activations and staging buffers. `configure_layerwise_offload_modules` builds one budget per configuration pass and offers it in descending order of `pin_benefit_bytes` -- weight bytes times uses per request, where a layerwise DiT's uses are the model's default step count and everything else is one. A component that no longer fits is allocated pageable host memory instead. Ranking on the product rather than on "is it the DiT" matters: for a few-step model a 1 GB DiT stepped four times moves 4 GB per request while a 20 GB text encoder used once moves 20 GB, so a DiT-first rule would hand the budget to the component that needs it less. Both directions are covered by tests. Priority comes from the ordering, not from an exemption. The cap binds even for the hot components, because granting past it does not produce a smaller footprint -- it moves the failure into the pinned allocation itself, or into swapping. Nothing changes on a host with room: the budget only denies when the bytes genuinely do not fit. ## Accuracy Tests Output-neutral; this decides where weights are held, not what is computed. 15 new unit tests in `test_host_memory_budget.py` cover the v2 path, the v1 path, an absent cgroup, both "unlimited" spellings, the cap-versus-free minimum in both directions, the reserve and its floor, hot-first exhaustion, and storage dedup in the size estimate. ## Speed Tests and Profiling The point of the hot-first ordering is that the fallback lands where it costs least. Measured on one RTX 4090, `Wan-AI/Wan2.1-T2V-1.3B-Diffusers`, 320x576x9f, 8 steps, three interleaved pairs, comparing minima (contention only ever adds time): | stage | all pinned | text encoder pageable | | |---|---|---|---| | text encoding | 3.0708 s | 6.1794 s | **2.01x** | | denoising | 7.4064 s | 7.2750 s | no effect | | decoding | 1.6815 s | 1.5445 s | no effect | The two clean pageable samples were 6.1794 s and 6.2630 s, 1.3% apart. A third read 11.3205 s with its denoise and decode elevated too, which is contention from another tenant on the box rather than a property of the path. Denoising is untouched, which is what the mechanism predicts: the text encoder runs once, before the loop, so its pinning cannot reach it. End to end the run goes from about 12.2 s to 15.0 s, so the fallback costs roughly 23% when it fires. Two raw measurements on the same box explain that 2.01x, since it is larger than the bandwidth gap alone: | host memory | H2D bandwidth (2 GiB) | |---|---| | anonymous pinned | 13.09 GB/s | | anonymous pageable | 8.84 GB/s | | file-backed mmap | ~2.8 GB/s | Pinned is only 1.48x the pageable bandwidth. The rest of the stage cost is the loss of overlap: with a pageable source `copy_(non_blocking=True)` is silently synchronous, and the call blocks for the whole transfer (0.3 ms to return for pinned against 253.8 ms for pageable, on an identical 2 GiB copy). Layerwise offload exists to overlap those copies with compute, so losing the asynchrony compounds the slower bytes. That is a real cost, not a free safety net, and the docstring and the log line say so. It is still the right trade against exhausting host memory -- slower is not dead -- which is why it only fires when the weights do not fit. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Notes No automatic eviction, deliberately. The pinned buffers are allocated once in `_initialize()` and never grow, so admission control at startup captures essentially all of the benefit; eviction would only respond to pressure from outside the process, and unpinning our own buffers to relieve a neighbour costs a request that happens to be in flight. If dynamic response is ever wanted, the safe form is to unpin rather than free: the data stays, only the copies get slower, and nothing is re-read from disk. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #32344307920](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32344307920)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32344307630](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32344307630)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #32344307972](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32344307972)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [mem_cache] docs: add a layer map and placement rules
signals.text: ## Motivation Part of #25371. `mem_cache/` has 40 top-level modules plus 10 subpackages and no index. Answering "is this class an allocator or a pool?" or "may `pool_host/` import `allocator/`?" currently means reading the RFC or grepping. ## Modifications Adds `python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/README.md`: - **Layers** -- the stack from `allocation.py` down through `allocator/`, `pool/`, `pool_host/`, `storage/`, with each layer's in/out contract. Names prefix-cache trees and the construction layer (`kv_cache_configurator.py`, `kv_cache_builder.py`, `cache_init_params.py`, `allocation_sizing.py`, `kv_cache_dtype.py`, `kv_vmm_backing.py`, `hybrid_cache/hybrid_pool_assembler.py`) as sitting outside that stack rather than in it. - **Where does my class go?** -- home by base class, not by name, plus the `Allocator`-means-two-things distinction (`BaseTokenToKVPoolAllocator` hands out KV slots and lives in `allocator/`; `HostTensorAllocator` hands out pinned host memory and does not). - **Conventions** -- the naming rule, family-as-package, and the dependency-direction invariants. Documentation only; no code changes. **Deliberately coarse.** An earlier draft carried a per-family x per-layer matrix naming the module that holds each class today. That inventory would need updating by every one of the ~20 remaining moves under #25371, and it already has a home that cannot rot: the shrink-only pins in the layout ratchet (#35638), which fail the build when a pinned class moves. Duplicating it here would just give the same fact a second home to drift from. The README documents the rules, which are stable; for "where does class X live today", `git grep` is the answer, and the README says so. ## Accuracy Test Not applicable -- documentation only. ## Benchmark and Profiling Results Not applicable -- documentation only. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Code Formatting with Pre-Commit](https://docs.sglang.ai/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-formatting-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests as outlined in the [Running Unit Tests](https://docs.sglang.ai/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#running-unit-tests-adding-to-ci). - [x] Update documentation / docstrings / example tutorials as needed, according to [Writing Documentation](https://docs.sglang.ai/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#writing-documentation-running-docs-ci). - [x] Provide throughput / latency benchmark results and accuracy evaluation results as needed, according to [Benchmark and Profiling](https://docs.sglang.ai/developer_guide/benchmark_and_profiling.html). - [x] For reviewers: If you haven't made any contributions to this PR and are only assisting with merging the main branch, please remove yourself as a co-author when merging the PR. - [x] Please feel free to join our Slack channel at https://slack.sglang.ai to discuss your PR. --- Independent of the other in-flight #25371 PRs, and order-independent with respect to them: the README names no module that a pending move deletes or relocates. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:no_entry_sign: [Run #32346100617](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32346100617)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:no_entry_sign: [Run #32346100533](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32346100533)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32346100646](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32346100646)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [mem_cache][10/N] refactor: drop the redundant _component suffix in unified_cache/components
signals.text: ## Motivation Part of #25371. **Mechanical Move.** #32484 moved `unified_cache_components/` to `unified_cache/components/` but kept the `_component` suffix on every file, so the directory now reads `unified_cache/components/full_component.py` -- the role is stated twice, once by the directory and again by every file inside it. The RFC's naming rule is to drop affixes that do not differentiate (compare `models/qwen.py`, not `models/qwen_model.py`); this finishes the move that was started. `tree_component.py` is also misnamed: it is not "a tree component" but the `TreeComponent` ABC plus the shared enums and helpers every component imports. `base.py` matches how `allocator/base.py` and `pool_host/base.py` already name that role. ## Modifications ``` tree_component.py -> base.py TreeComponent ABC, ComponentType, ComponentData, ... full_component.py -> full.py FullComponent mamba_component.py -> mamba.py MambaComponent swa_component.py -> swa.py SWAComponent ``` `git mv` for all four, then the import path updated at every call site. No symbol was renamed, no re-export shim added. Diff surface is exactly: 19 import-path lines, 3 filename string literals in `test_session_unified_radix_cache.py` (which asserts on file contents by name), 5 lines in `unified_cache/components/README.md`, and isort reordering where `base` now sorts ahead of its siblings. Nothing else. ## Accuracy Test Mechanical move, so the bar is byte-level equality rather than accuracy: - `base.py` is **byte-identical** to `tree_component.py`. - `full.py` / `mamba.py` / `swa.py` differ from their originals in **exactly one line** each -- the `tree_component` -> `base` import. Verified on an H200 devbox (`PYTHONPATH` shadowing the image's copy): ``` PR branch: 1117 passed, 1070 skipped, 52 subtests passed pristine main baseline: 1117 passed, 1070 skipped, 52 subtests passed ``` Identical command over `test_unified_radix_cache_unittest.py`, `test_tree_core_registry.py`, `test_mamba_path_state_cap.py`, `test_mamba_donated_alloc_ratio.py`, `test_session_unified_radix_cache.py` against both trees on the same box -- zero delta, so the 1070 skips are pre-existing and none were introduced here. Package and per-module imports were also smoke-tested. ## Benchmark and Profiling Results Not applicable -- no runtime behavior changes. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Code Formatting with Pre-Commit](https://docs.sglang.ai/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-formatting-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests as outlined in the [Running Unit Tests](https://docs.sglang.ai/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#running-unit-tests-adding-to-ci). - [x] Update documentation / docstrings / example tutorials as needed, according to [Writing Documentation](https://docs.sglang.ai/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#writing-documentation-running-docs-ci). - [x] Provide throughput / latency benchmark results and accuracy evaluation results as needed, according to [Benchmark and Profiling](https://docs.sglang.ai/developer_guide/benchmark_and_profiling.html). - [x] For reviewers: If you haven't made any contributions to this PR and are only assisting with merging the main branch, please remove yourself as a co-author when merging the PR. - [x] Please feel free to join our Slack channel at https://slack.sglang.ai to discuss your PR. --- Independent of the other in-flight #25371 PRs -- touches no file that #35306 or #35638 touch. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:no_entry_sign: [Run #32334915486](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32334915486)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:no_entry_sign: [Run #32338867047](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32338867047)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32334915318](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32334915318)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [Scheduler] Stop waiting-queue scan after chunk budget exhaustion
signals.text: ## Motivation Fixes #35642. A resumed chunked request can consume the remaining chunk budget for the current scheduling pass. The scheduler nevertheless continues scanning the waiting queue, so requests can perform prefix-cache matching and host-cache load-back before `add_one_req()` rejects them because no chunk tokens remain. ## Modifications - Check the existing `PrefillAdder.budget_state()` after resuming `chunked_req`. - Skip waiting-queue admission for the current scheduling pass when the updated state is `AddReqResult.OTHER`, while keeping the resumed chunk in the batch. - Avoid Mamba slot preallocation when the waiting queue is skipped. ## Accuracy Tests This change does not modify model computation or output values. - `python -m py_compile python/sglang/srt/managers/scheduler.py` - Focused Ruff undefined-name checks pass. - No new unit test is included; the change is limited to reusing the existing scheduler budget-state check. ## Speed Tests and Profiling No benchmark was run. The change removes cache matching and possible host-cache load-back work for waiting requests that cannot be admitted after the resumed chunk exhausts the chunk budget. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. signals.title: fix: detect cross-node multimodal transport by nnodes
signals.text: <!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. --> ## Motivation `determine_tensor_transport_mode()` currently treats a non-empty `dist_init_addr` as evidence that the deployment spans multiple nodes. However, `dist_init_addr` is a process-group rendezvous endpoint rather than a topology signal. Single-node multi-GPU TP deployments may also set it to bootstrap the TP process group. This false positive selects the `"default"` transport on a single node, causing `wrap_shm_features()` to become a no-op. Large multimodal pixel tensors are then pickled and broadcast through Gloo for every request. In an affected five-image document workload, this resulted in 2.2–6.5 GB transfers and 18–33 seconds spent in `recv_requests`. `nnodes` directly represents whether the deployment is multi-node and is therefore the appropriate source of truth. ## Modifications - Determine cross-node topology using `server_args.nnodes > 1` instead of `server_args.dist_init_addr`. - Move `determine_tensor_transport_mode()` into `managers/mm_utils.py` as the shared implementation. - Update the tokenizer manager, disaggregated encoder receiver, and native Rust multimodal path to use the shared helper. - Remove the duplicated implementations and the reverse lazy import from `mm_utils` to `tokenizer_manager`. - Add regression tests covering: - single-node TP with a configured rendezvous address, which must retain the local `"cuda_ipc"`/shared-memory path; - multi-node topology without relying on the rendezvous-address heuristic, which must use `"default"` transport. ## Accuracy Tests Not applicable. This change only affects multimodal tensor transport selection and does not modify model computation or outputs. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Before this fix, the affected five-image document workload observed 2.2–6.5 GB of pickled/Gloo-broadcast data and 18–33 seconds per `recv_requests` call. This change restores the existing shared-memory transport path for single-node multi-GPU TP deployments. No standalone post-change benchmark was run in the local development environment. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [x] Documentation is not required because this is an internal transport-selection fix with no user-facing API change. - [x] This change has no model accuracy impact. - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process). 2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers. 3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so. - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci` 4. signals.title: [mem_cache][11/N] refactor: extract KVCache and BaseSWAKVPool into pool/base.py
signals.text: ## Motivation Part of #25371. **Mechanical Move.** First PR of the `mem_cache/pool/` layer. `pool/` is the last of the three layer packages and the only one still getting worse. Since the restructure was agreed, `memory_pool.py` went from 2257 to 5042 lines and from 11 to 17 classes, because there was nowhere else for a device pool to go. This creates the package and moves the base layer into it, so every later family move has a target. ## Modifications New `mem_cache/pool/base.py`, holding only what every device pool derives from: | Symbol | From | |---|---| | `KVWriteLoc`, `unwrap_write_loc` | `memory_pool.py` | | `KvBufferDesc` | `memory_pool.py` | | `KVCache` (ABC) | `memory_pool.py` | | `BaseSWAKVPool` (ABC) | `base_swa_memory_pool.py` (deleted) | | `GB` | `memory_pool.py` | `base_swa_memory_pool.py` is deleted: it was a 29-line file holding one cross-family ABC, sitting under the SWA feature's name while `SWAKVPool`, `DeepSeekV4TokenToKVPool` and the disagg paths all depend on it. It belongs next to `KVCache`. No re-export shim: all 44 call sites are updated in this PR, matching how `allocator.py` was deleted outright rather than left forwarding. `RadixAttention` moves under `TYPE_CHECKING` in the new module. It is only ever an annotation (`layer: RadixAttention`), and the file has `from __future__ import annotations`; keeping it at runtime made `pool/base.py` -> `layers.radix_attention` -> ... -> `forward_context` -> `pool/base.py` a genuine import cycle, because `pool/base.py` is imported far earlier in the chain than `memory_pool.py` was. This mirrors how `LayerDoneCounter` was already handled. Two now-unused imports (`abc`, `KVWriteLoc`) drop out of `memory_pool.py`. Both remaining `KVWriteLoc` mentions there are in comments. ## Accuracy Test Mechanical move, so the bar is byte-level equality: - The `KVWriteLoc` / `unwrap_write_loc` / `KvBufferDesc` / `KVCache` block is **byte-identical** to the original `memory_pool.py` region. - The `BaseSWAKVPool` class body is **byte-identical** to `base_swa_memory_pool.py`. - Only the new module's import header is hand-written. signals.title: [docs] Add DFlash2 speculative cells to the Qwen3.8-27B cookbook
signals.text: ## Motivation #35496 (quantized target `lm_head` in the DFlash2 selector) is merged, so the NVFP4 checkpoint can run DFlash2. This adds a DFLASH2 option to the Qwen3.8-27B cookbook's Speculative Decoding row, on every platform with a cell. Validation is graded: NVFP4 measured end-to-end on RTX PRO 6000 / RTX 5090, the RTX PRO 6000 BF16/FP8 cells validated to boot and serve, and the remaining platforms (H200, DGX Spark, GB300) offered with a **Final Verification In Progress** badge while the DFLASH2 pick is selected. ## Modifications - `qwen3.8-27b.jsx`: DFLASH2 Deploy-panel overlay option (draft `incoai/Qwen3.8-27B-DFlash2`, `--speculative-num-draft-tokens 8`) and the matching Playground card entry. On the RTX 5090 the option re-pins `--mem-fraction-static` (0.90 bf16 / 0.945 fp32), and for fp32 also re-pins `--mamba-full-memory-ratio 10` in place of the calculator's balanced value — the L=9216 ratio leaves the fp32 state pool one slot short at every serviceable mem-fraction. - `Qwen3.8-27B.mdx`: DFlash2 bullet in Configuration Tips (including the 5090 fp32 caveats), DFLASH added to the ratio accordion's `D` term, validation Note updated. - `_deployment.jsx`: `verificationStatus` may now be a function of the selection (overlay picks included), so a cell can report "Final Verification In Progress" for one speculative option while staying Verified for the rest. Backward compatible — string/boolean forms unchanged. ## Accuracy Tests N/A (docs only). Serving correctness of the quantized-head path was validated in #35496 (GSM8K 95.5% spec vs 98.0% base, 200q). ## Speed Tests and Profiling All 8 cells validated at ISL 8192 / OSL 1024, concurrency 1 (bench_serving random, 1 warmup + 4 prompts, exact-shape checks, real acceptance): | Card | Tier | SSM dtype | mem-frac | ratio | TPOT | tok/s/user | accept | |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---| | RTX PRO 6000 | Low-Latency | float32 | 0.85 | 6.63 | 7.56 ms | 132.3 | 3.41 | | RTX PRO 6000 | Low-Latency | bfloat16 | 0.85 | 3.38 | 7.64 ms | 130.9 | 3.09 | | RTX PRO 6000 | High-Throughput | float32 | 0.85 | 6.12 | 7.58 ms | 131.9 | 3.41 | | RTX PRO 6000 | High-Throughput | bfloat16 | 0.85 | 3.12 | 7.84 ms | 127.6 | 3.20 | | RTX 5090 | Low-Latency | bfloat16 | 0.90 | 3.38 | 6.11 ms | 143 | 3.30 | | RTX 5090 | High-Throughput | bfloat16 | 0.90 | 3.12 | 6.12 ms | 143 | 3.30 | | RTX 5090 | Low-Latency | float32 | 0.945 | 10 | 8.30 ms | 120.3 | 3.09 | | RTX 5090 | High-Throughput | float32 | 0.945 | 10 | 8.32 ms | 120.1 | 3.09 | 5090 fp32 boundaries, all measured: mf 0.94 → state pool one slot short; mf 0.95 → runtime OOM on the first request; balanced ratios 6.63/6.12 → `max_mamba_cache_size` below the required slots at every mem-fraction. Low-Latency fp32's KV pool is a single-request envelope (9,454 tokens), documented in the Tips bullet. signals.title: Add FlashBoot load format integration
signals.text: ## Motivation Current model loading and cloning paths operate primarily at tensor granularity. The Hugging Face auto loading path loads and copies tensors individually. For large MoE models such as DSV4 Pro, the large number of expert tensors introduces substantial per-tensor overhead and makes large, contiguous I/O difficult. Existing clone implementations have a similar limitation: many small tensor transfers cannot fully utilize NVLink or RDMA bandwidth. NCCL-based cloning also incurs significant communicator setup overhead. In our DSV4 Pro experiments on GB300, NCCL communicator initialization takes more than 10 seconds, while the actual clone transfer takes only about 0.3 seconds. FlashBoot instead treats each rank-local checkpoint as a contiguous storage arena. It copies checkpoint data in large file-level blocks and rebinds model parameters to tensor views within the loaded arena. The same arena can then be cloned as large contiguous ranges over NVLink or RDMA, avoiding per-tensor loading and transfer overhead while making better use of the available link bandwidth. ## Summary - add `flashload` and `flashclone` load formats - dispatch FlashBoot loading to the external `flashboot` package from https://github.com/scitix/flashboot-release - add optional sharded-state export hooks and documentation - add `docker/Dockerfile_flashboot` for images that include FlashBoot, without changing the default `docker/Dockerfile` ## Validation - `python -m py_compile python/sglang/srt/configs/load_config.py python/sglang/srt/server_args.py python/sglang/srt/model_loader/loader.py python/sglang/srt/model_executor/model_runner.py` - `python -m json.tool docs/docs.json` - parsed `python/pyproject.toml` with `tomllib` - installed FlashBoot from `git+https://github.com/scitix/flashboot-release.git` in a local CUDA 13 / H100 environment with `FLASHBOOT_CUDA_ARCH=9.0 FB_BUILD_RDMA=auto` - imported `flashboot._C` after importing `torch` and verified the RDMA `Endpoint` binding exists - verified `get_model_loader` dispatches both `flashload` and `flashclone` to the external FlashBoot loader - checked that `docker/Dockerfile` does not contain FlashBoot install logic The PR intentionally does not vendor the FlashBoot implementation.

signals.title: Fix EnvField.override() leaking the env var when the with body raises
signals.text: <!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. --> ## Motivation <!-- Describe the purpose and goals of this pull request. --> Problem EnvField.override() is a @contextmanager that temporarily sets an env var and restores it on exit. The restore logic sits after yield with no try/finally: When the with body raises, contextlib.contextmanager throws the exception into the generator at the yield point. Because there is no try/finally, the code after yield is skipped, so the env var is never restored and permanently leaks into os.environ for the rest of the process. Impact Any code that does with envs.X.override(...): <raises> permanently contaminates the process environment. This is a real, general bug — it was surfaced by the NPU soft-watchdog test where scenario 4 intentionally fails the launch inside an override(350) block; the leaked SGLANG_TEST_STUCK_DETOKENIZER=350 was then inherited by every later server subprocess, causing cross-scenario contamination and a multi-minute slowdown. ## Modifications <!-- Detail the changes made in this pull request. --> Wrap the post-yield restore in try/finally so it runs on both the normal and the exception path: self.set(value) try: yield finally: if backup_present: os.environ[self.name] = backup_value else: os.environ.pop(self.name, None) self._set_to_none = backup_set_to_none The normal path is byte-for-byte equivalent; only the exception path changes (now it restores instead of leaking). Test Add test_override_restores_on_exception to test/registered/unit/test_environ.py, covering both cases: - the var existed before the override → restored to its previous value after an exception; - the var did not exist before → removed after an exception. This regression test fails against the old code and passes with the fix. ## Accuracy Tests <!-- If this pull request affects model outputs (e.g., changes to the kernel or model forward code), provide accuracy test results. --> ## Speed Tests and Profiling <!-- If this pull request impacts inference speed, provide benchmarking and profiling results. --> ## Checklist - [ ] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [ ] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. signals.title: fix: resolve CPU device compatibility issues
signals.text: ## Motivation This PR fixes two runtime failures in the LTX-2.3 two-stage serving path and one dtype failure in the LTX-2.3 vocoder path. First, LoRA offload management previously used backend-specific cache APIs that were not portable across all device backends in this call site. Second, LTX-2.3 two-stage original mode can build a stage-2 LoRA switch spec that applies both: - user-provided LoRA - built-in distilled LoRA to the same transformer target. Dynamic LoRA supports only one adapter per target, so this could trigger: ValueError: Dynamic LoRA currently supports only one adapter per target Additionally, the LTX-2.3 vocoder BWE path could hit: Input type (float) and bias type (c10::BFloat16) should be the same when input was forced to float32 but module weights/bias were bf16. ## Modifications 1. fix: portable cache-management calls in LoRA offload path - Update cache clear logic in lora_pipeline.py - Replace backend-specific torch device-module calls with platform abstraction: - `current_platform.synchronize()` - `current_platform.empty_cache()` - This keeps behavior consistent across backends and avoids unsupported direct backend API assumptions in this path. 2. fix: Dynamic LoRA one-adapter-per-target conflict in stage2 original mode - Update two-stage LoRA merge decision flow in `ltx_2_pipeline.py` - Keep original default behavior: prefer dynamic LoRA in original mode to avoid request-time merge/unmerge on a single DiT - Add narrow fallback: when stage2 needs both user LoRA and distilled LoRA on the same transformer target, force `merge_weights=true` - Refactor this fallback into `_should_merge_lora_for_phase`, with a new optional parameter `distilled_lora_strength` that has a default value, so existing callers remain compatible without explicit argument passing. 3. fix: vocoder dtype mismatch in BWE path - Update dtype handling in `ltx_2_vocoder.py` - Align vocoder input dtype to `vocoder.conv_pre` weight dtype - Align bwe_generator input dtype to `bwe_generator.conv_pre` weight dtype - Preserve output cast-back behavior ## Accuracy Tests - Verified LTX-2.3 two-stage generation runs successfully in original mode. - The previous Dynamic LoRA multi-adapter stage2 failure is no longer reproducible. - Verified vocoder decode path no longer reproduces the float vs bf16 conv dtype mismatch. - Static checks on modified files report no new errors. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32439571589](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32439571589)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32439571453](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32439571453)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #32439571562](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32439571562)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [AMD] [GLM5] Fuse the DSA indexer Q/K rope + quant + K-cache write in…
signals.text: ## Motivation The DSA indexer Q/K fusion (#27705) is CUDA-only. On ROCm the indexer still runs the unfused path every layer, every step: rope on q and k, LayerNorm on k, an fp8 quant of each, the head-gate scale, and the index-K cache write. On GLM-5.2 decode that work is launch-bound, not arithmetic-bound. aiter ships `indexer_qk_rope_quant_and_cache`, which does all of it in one launch. This wires it up by extending the existing fusion switch to ROCm rather than adding a second one -- the fused `wk_weights_proj` GEMM, the no-Hadamard invariant, the weight loader and the graph split-op plumbing are already platform-agnostic. No kernel changes; the kernel is already in the aiter that ships in the ROCm image. ## Modifications - Extend `use_dsa_indexer_fusion` to ROCm, gated on probing aiter for the kernel at import (aiter is pinned per image; an older one imports fine and would only fail at the first forward, so it falls back with a warning). - Add `_aiter_fused_qk_prepare_and_store`, the single-kernel Q/K path. It returns the same `(q_fp8, weights)` contract as the CUDA path, including the `num_tokens` slicing the graph split-op relies on, so the call site is unchanged. - Build `k_norm` in fp32 whenever fusion is on. The kernel requires fp32 norm params, exactly as the CUDA kernels already do. bf16 stays for the unfused ROCm path, where matching `x.dtype` is what selects aiter's CK layernorm over the native upcast. - Read cos/sin off aiter's rope module, which keeps them apart as `[max_position, 1, 1, rope_dim/2]` rather than in one `cos_sin_cache`. - Give `_fused_k_prepare_and_store` a ROCm branch. Its CUDA fallback is a JIT kernel, and the k-only decode fast path (#31324) reaches it whenever fusion is on. - Gate the JIT fused-store branch on `_is_cuda` so non-CUDA stops paying for a compile attempt that can only fail. Two adjacent fixes, easy to split out if preferred: - `lora_manager` imports `_use_dsa_indexer_fusion`, which #30111 deleted when it moved the flag into `Indexer.__init__`. The indexer-LoRA guard therefore raises `ImportError` instead of its intended error, on CUDA today. Restored as `dsa_indexer_fusion_supported()`. - The ROCm branch of `_store_index_k_cache` read `forward_batch.out_cache_loc`, ignoring the sliced `out_cache_loc` its caller passes under the graph split-op contract. ## Accuracy GLM-5.2-FP8, TP8, 8x MI355X (gfx950). ``` python3 -m sglang.test.run_eval --port 30000 --eval-name gsm8k \ --num-examples 500 --num-threads 128 ``` | | baseline | fused | |---|---|---| | gsm8k (500 examples) | 0.948 | 0.962 | `score:std` puts sigma at ~0.0099 for n=500, so +1.4pp is ~1.4 sigma -- read as no regression, not as a win. GPQA was not run. The two K-cache writers stay live at once, since the k-only decode path keeps writing unfused, and they are **not** byte-identical: the unfused path rounds to bf16 before quantizing while the fused kernel goes fp32 -> fp8 in one step, so a value near an fp8 midpoint can land on either neighbour. Measured over 41x128 elements: ue8m0 scales identical, 15/5248 elements differ, each by exactly one fp8 code, and the fused result is the closer of the two to an fp32 reference. `test_dsa_indexer_qk_fuse_rocm.py` pins that bound. ## Benchmark ``` python3 -m sglang.benchmark.serving --backend sglang-oai --port 30000 \ --dataset-name random --random-input-len 16384 --random-output-len 512 \ --random-range-ratio 1 --max-concurrency 1 --num-prompts 8 ``` BS=1 at 16K context, where `kv_len > index_topk` so the full indexer runs and decode is launch-bound. Two runs per side, both stable to two decimals: | | baseline | fused | | |---|---|---|---| | output tok/s | 70.74 / 70.76 | 75.32 / 75.33 | **+6.5%** | | mean TPOT | 12.50 ms | 11.65 ms | **-6.8%** | | mean TTFT | 850 ms | 841 ms | -1.0% | TTFT is flat because prefill runs the same indexer but is compute-bound; the whole gain lands in decode, which is the signature a launch-count fix should have. At `--random-input-len 8192 --random-output-len 1024 --max-concurrency 64`, 1253.36 -> 1277.21 output tok/s (+1.9%). Launch cost amortizes across a large batch, so that point reads as "no throughput regression" rather than as the fusion's contribution. A short-context BS=1 point is not a measurement of this change: with `index_topk=2048`, a 32-token prompt never exceeds `kv_len` 2048, so every decode step takes the k-only dense path and never calls the fused kernel. ## Profile Torch profiler, GPU activities, decode at 16K context. GLM-5.2 has 78 layers but only 21 run a full indexer (`indexer_types`: 21 `full`, 57 `shared`). Normalising by `_fused_qk_rope_cat_and_cache_mla_kernel`, which fires once per layer per step, the baseline capture covers 2 decode steps and the fused capture 11. Per full-indexer layer per decode step: | kernel | baseline | fused | |---|---|---| | `kn_entry_2c_sbhd_cached_indirect_inplace` (rope q+k) | 1 | 0 | | `Layernorm2dFwd` | 1 | 0 | | `act_quant_kernel__kernel` | 1 | 0 | | `indexer_k_quant_and_cache_kernel` | 1 | 0 | | `indexer_qk_rope_quant_and_cache_kernel` | 0 | 1 | 84 launches per decode step (21 layers x 4) become 21. ## Checklist - `test/registered/kernels/ops/attention/test_dsa_indexer_qk_fuse_rocm.py`, 6 cases, all passing on MI355X: K-cache agreement with the unfused writer in both paged layouts, the one-fp8-step numeric bound, q/head-gate agreement against rope + `act_quant` + `_scale_head_gates`, strided-vs-contiguous byte equality, and the cos/sin 2-D view tracking a replaced rope cache. - Registered under the `jit-kernel-unit-test-amd` suite. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32343456049](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32343456049)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32343455960](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32343455960)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32343455936](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32343455936)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: fix: pass anthropic effort xhigh through instead of collapsing to max
signals.text: <!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. --> ## Motivation The Anthropic-compatible endpoint (`/v1/messages`) rewrites `output_config.effort="xhigh"` to `reasoning_effort="max"` before forwarding the request to the OpenAI pipeline. This collapse was introduced in #25876, when the OpenAI `ReasoningEffortTier` Literal did not include `xhigh`. Since #31681 added `xhigh` to the Literal, the collapse is stale and actively breaks models whose chat templates only accept `xhigh`/`medium`/`low` (e.g. Qwen3.8): an Anthropic request with `effort="xhigh"` fails with: ``` Unexpected reasoning effort max. Supported types are xhigh (default), medium, and low. ``` The OpenAI entrypoint has been passing `xhigh` through untouched for months, so models that support `xhigh` already receive it there; the Anthropic layer is the only path that mangles it. ## Modifications - `python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/anthropic/serving.py`: pass `oc.effort` through as-is instead of collapsing `xhigh` → `max`; update the stale comment. - `python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/anthropic/protocol.py`: update the `AnthropicOutputConfig` docstring that still described the collapse. - `test/registered/unit/entrypoints/anthropic/test_serving.py`: update `test_request_output_config_effort_maps_to_reasoning_effort` to expect `("xhigh", "xhigh")` passthrough. Models whose vocabularies do not include `xhigh` (e.g. Kimi K3, dsv4) already reject it identically on the OpenAI entrypoint, so this only aligns the Anthropic entrypoint with existing OpenAI behavior. ## Accuracy Tests Not applicable — no model forward/kernel changes. signals.title: [diffusion] feat: warn on an unverified short edge instead of rejecting it for minimax-h3
signals.text: ## Motivation `target.short_edge` had to be exactly 768 or the request was refused, in two places — the HTTP gate in `request_validation.py` and the shape policy in `resolved_plan.py`. Nothing in the shape math needs that. `minimax_h3_resolve_spatial_shape` scales the requested short edge by the aspect ratio, clamps to a fixed `768x1344` pixel budget, and rounds both axes to the 32px canvas grid, so any positive value resolves to a valid canvas. A larger short edge is pulled back by the area cap; a smaller one simply produces a smaller canvas. The model runs there too. The MiniMax model card says the short side *"is set to 768 pixels by default"*, and users report generating at 352p and 416p — with **better** prompt adherence than 768p ([discussions/65](https://huggingface.co/MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3/discussions/65)). 768 is what MiniMax publishes recipes and reference outputs for (all 18 scripts in the model repo use it), but it is a default, not a limit. That distinction matters most on a small card, where the short edge is the only knob with real leverage over both memory and time. ## Modifications Accept any positive integer for `target.short_edge`. Warn once per distinct value via a shared `warn_unverified_short_edge()` in `constants.py` — requests repeat, the caveat should not — naming 768 as the only size MiniMax publishes recipes and reference outputs for, and saying plainly that quality and prompt adherence elsewhere are not covered by any MiniMax or SGLang measurement. Non-integer, zero and negative values are still rejected. ## Accuracy Tests No change at 768: the resolver returns the same canvas and does not warn. Existing `test_minimax_h3_admission.py` and `test_video_api_profiling.py` pass unchanged — no test asserted the rejection, they only used 768 as a value. New `test_minimax_h3_short_edge.py` (11 cases): 352/384/416/512/768 all resolve to a 32px-aligned canvas within the pixel budget with the short edge on the requested grid point; halving the short edge quarters the canvas; an oversized short edge falls back to `size_mode="area"` and stays under the cap; zero, negative and fractional values raise; 768 does not warn; a non-768 value warns exactly once across repeated calls. 28 tests pass together with the existing H3 suites. ## Speed Tests and Profiling 2x RTX 4090 24 GB, TP2, `--performance-mode memory`, layerwise offload of dit/text_encoder/vae, `t2va`, 4 steps, 4 s, 16:9: | `short_edge` | denoise | |---|---| | 768 | 57.69 s | | 384 | **11.69 s** (4.9x) | ## Checklist -
