signals.title: [diffusion] feat: add weight source reader
signals.text: ## Motivation Reading a checkpoint was a boolean. `safetensors_weights_iterator` took `use_runai_model_streamer: bool | None`, branched on it inline, and carried one rule hardcoded around it: ```python if key_filter is not None: # streamer filters after materializing all tensors, so it cannot skip # a checkpoint partition at load time use_runai_model_streamer = False ``` That comment is describing a property of the Run:ai streamer, but it lives at the call site, so every future caller has to rediscover it. And the two paths differ in more than speed: `safe_open` maps the file, so the CPU tensors it yields are views into the checkpoint, while the streamer copies into anonymous memory. Nothing named that difference, which makes it invisible to anyone reasoning about host memory. ## Modifications Move both readers into `runtime/loader/weight_readers/` behind a protocol that states what separates them: ``` weight_readers/ ├── __init__.py select_weight_reader() -- the whole decision ├── base.py WeightReader protocol ├── runai_streamer.py RunaiStreamerReader └── safetensors_mmap.py SafetensorsMmapReader ``` Two capabilities: - `supports_key_filter` -- can it skip keys while reading? The streamer cannot, so the rule that used to sit at the call site now sits on the reader that owns it. - `retains_file_mapping` -- are the yielded tensors views into the checkpoint file? `select_weight_reader()` honours an explicit request, falls back when a reader is not installed, and passes over one that cannot filter when the caller needs filtering. The old boolean still works and maps onto a reader name, so no call site changes behaviour. `safetensors_mmap.py` is named for the mapping rather than for `safe_open`, because the mapping is the reason the file exists. ## Accuracy Tests Behaviour-preserving refactor; no numerics touched. Full `test/unit` suite goes from 1720 to 1730 passed, the ten new ones being reader-selection tests, with the same four pre-existing failures (`realtime/`, `sana_wm/`) that fail with this change reverted -- checked by reverting it and re-running those four. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Not applicable: the same reader runs, chosen the same way, for every existing caller. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Notes `retains_file_mapping` is the property a follow-up needs. File-backed pages are droppable under memory pressure without swap; anonymous pages are not, and on a swapless host -- which container runtimes commonly are -- that is the difference between the kernel having something to reclaim and having nothing. Measured on one RTX 4090, host-to-device bandwidth for a 2 GiB transfer: 13.09 GB/s from pinned anonymous memory, 8.84 GB/s from pageable anonymous, and 8.5 GB/s from a cache-resident file mapping. Giving up the consolidated per-layer buffer costs nothing measurable -- 66 per-tensor copies matching a real DiT layer's size distribution move 542 MiB at 13.41 GB/s against 13.39 GB/s for one consolidated copy -- so a mapped host copy is a viable source. This PR only names the property; it does not change which reader anything uses. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #32347298556](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32347298556)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32347298271](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32347298271)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #32347298505](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32347298505)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [NPU] Support DSpark compact verify graph and folded verify epilogue
signals.text: ## Motivation DSpark on the Ascend DSV4 backend currently falls back to a uniform verify window or eager-side post-processing for parts of speculative decoding. This leaves two sources of avoidable overhead: 1. the target model verifies the full draft window even when the SPS policy selects a shorter per-request verify length; 2. accept/finalize and hidden/KV commit remain outside the target verify graph. This PR enables the compact DSpark path on NPU, adds token-tiered graph replay for ragged target verify, and folds the eligible verify epilogue into the graph. ## Modifications ### 1. DSpark compact verify on NPU - Build packed/ragged verify windows from per-request verify lengths selected by the DSpark planner. - Add NPU-safe compact row mapping, verify-ID gathering, cache-location handling, and compact-to-strided scatter. - Construct DSV4 SWA, sparse-attention, C4/C128 compressor, position, state, and page-table metadata from the live compact layout. - Preserve eager fallback when the selected attention backend does not support ragged verify graphs. ### 2. Compact target-verify graph - Advertise ragged verify graph support for the DSV4 Ascend backend. - Select target-verify graphs by compact token tier while retaining fixed graph-owned buffers. - Refresh query indptr, sequence lengths, cache/page tables, compressor locations/state, and sparse indices before replay. - Add an NPU-local bucketed-layout cache so the Ascend and DSV4 metadata consumers reuse the same derived layout. - Use the safe last-location Triton path for DSV4 NPU allocation metadata. ### 3. Verify epilogue graph - Add a DSV4 NPU-specific target-verify tail hook that uses the committed/live prefix lengths from DSV4 metadata. - Fold greedy accept/finalize and eligible hidden/KV commit into the compact target-verify graph. - Keep sampling, grammar-constrained decoding, logits adjustments, and other ineligible cases on the existing eager epilogue path. - Keep the adaptation NPU/DSV4-specific so the existing CUDA behavior remains unchanged. ## Accuracy Tests - GPQA-Diamond accuracy: **0.91** with DSpark on Ascend NPU. - The compact path preserves the target-model verification result; it changes the number of draft tokens verified and where graph-safe post-processing executes. ## Speed Tests and Profiling No standalone performance number is included in this PR. The expected gain comes from reducing target-verify tokens according to the SPS-selected compact lengths and removing eligible verify epilogue launches from the host path. ## Validation - Python syntax compilation passed for all Python files changed by this PR. - Added scheduler coverage for exact eager token counts when the backend does not support ragged verify graphs. ## Checklist - [ ] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy). - [ ] Provide speed benchmark results according to [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32349793068](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32349793068)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32349792784](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32349792784)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32349793014](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32349793014)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [diffusion] docs+skill: which components to stream under layerwise offload
signals.text: ## Motivation The performance skill documented layerwise offload as a DiT knob and never mentioned `--layerwise-offload-components` at all, so the component list reads like a memory switch to turn all the way up. On MiniMax-H3 that costs 35 seconds a request. The rule the measurements support is not "offload the big things". Layerwise offload pays one H2D of a component's weights **per use of that component**, so what matters is how many times per request it runs: - the DiT runs once per denoising step — the transfer amortizes over every step and hides behind attention/FFN - the VAE runs **once** — one pass, nothing to overlap, so streaming it pays the whole weight transfer for a single use - a vocab table is a gather — it belongs in host memory, not in the stream ## Modifications Three subsections in Section 1 of `sglang-diffusion-performance`, plus the single-card H3 recipe they produced. 1. **Choosing what goes in `--layerwise-offload-components`** — the per-use rule, and the measurement behind it. 2. **Prefetch depth has a knee** — `--dit-offload-prefetch-size` is not monotonic; sweep it instead of trusting the default. 3. **When the transfer knobs do nothing** — the check to run first, and the counter-example where the whole exercise returns noise. ## Accuracy Tests Documentation only. Every number is from a measured run; the losslessness note (a residency sweep on Wan2.1-1.3B produced one SHA-256 across all settings) is from the runs behind #35538. ## Speed Tests and Profiling MiniMax-H3, 1x RTX 4090 24 GB, 672x384, 4 steps, `t2va`: | `--layerwise-offload-components` | denoise | decode | peak | |---|---|---|---| | `dit,text_encoder,vae` | 15.51 s | 39.85 s | 16.4 GB | | `dit,text_encoder` | 17.33 s | **5.32 s** | 22.2 GB | Prefetch, VAE resident: | prefetch | denoise | decode | peak | |---|---|---|---| | 1 (default) | 17.33 s | 5.32 s | 22.2 GB | | **2** | **15.29 s** | **4.89 s** | 22.1 GB | | 3 | 15.79 s | 5.25 s | 21.5 GB | | 4 | 16.73 s | 5.17 s | 23.5 GB | Together: 76 s -> 29 s a request on one 24 GB card. The counter-example, Wan2.1-1.3B on a 12 GB RTX 3060, `--dit-layerwise-resident-layers` 0/5/10/20: 1.10 / 1.04 / 1.05 / 1.06 s per step — flat, non-monotonic, noise. 65 MB a layer means a step moves 2.64 GB, 132 ms of a 1.04 s step. H3 is 1.36 GB a layer, 21x, and moves 66 GB a step. Same flags, opposite conclusion — hence the check. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #32353098583](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32353098583)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32353098364](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32353098364)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #32353098860](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32353098860)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [diffusion] keep the checkpoint mapping as the host store when pinning is off
signals.text: ## Motivation With `--pin-cpu-memory false`, layerwise offload copies every weight out of the checkpoint mapping into anonymous host memory. That copy buys nothing. It moves the same bytes at the same speed, and it costs the kernel its ability to reclaim those pages. Host memory is three tiers, ordered by what the kernel can do with them: | tier | reclaimable with swap | reclaimable without swap | |---|---|---| | file-backed (mmap) | yes, dropped | **yes, dropped** | | anonymous pageable | yes, swapped out | **no** | | anonymous pinned | no | no | The middle row is the one this PR is about. Container runtimes commonly run without swap -- the rented 4x4090 box used for the measurements below reports `Swap: 0B` -- and their anonymous pageable memory is exactly as unreclaimable as pinned. Copying a mapping into it converts memory the kernel could have dropped into memory it cannot. ## Modifications When pinning is off and a weight's bytes are already in a file mapping, keep the mapping as the host store instead of allocating and copying. Three facts make this safe, each checked rather than assumed: - `safe_open(...).get_tensor(name)` returns a view into the checkpoint. Verified by looking the storage pointer up in `/proc/self/maps`: it lands inside the file-backed mapping of the blob. - Those views outlive the `safe_open` context that produced them, including a host-to-device copy issued after the context closed. - Writes to them succeed and do not reach the file -- safetensors maps copy-on-write. So the two write-back paths (`update_weights`, the GPU-to-host writeback) need no special case; a written page silently becomes anonymous and only that page loses its reclaimability. With pinning on, the copy still earns its cost: pinning is what lets the copy stream run ahead of compute, and a mapping cannot be pinned and stay reclaimable at once. Two supporting changes: `preserve_strides` / `_strided_cpu_weights` become `standalone_host_store` / `_standalone_cpu_weights`. The flag never meant "preserve strides" -- it meant "this weight has its own host tensor rather than a slice of the flat buffer", and a kept mapping is the second reason for that. Mechanical rename, six sites. `ProcessMappings` in `loader/utils.py` replaces the closure `component_residency_bytes` had inlined, and reports pinned memory as *not* file-backed. CUDA's host allocator sits behind a mapping that carries a pathname, so the address-range check on its own calls pinned memory file-backed, which is the opposite of true. A test pins that ordering. ## Accuracy Tests Output-neutral: this decides where a weight's host copy lives, not what is computed. Full `test/unit` suite goes from 1730 to 1734 passed -- the new ones covering a mapped weight being kept, a pinned one still being copied, and the prefault reporting the bytes it faulted -- with the same four pre-existing failures (`realtime/`, `sana_wm/`) that fail with this change reverted. One bug the new tests caught during development: storing the source tensor directly handed back the placeholder, because `weight.data` is rebound on the next line and the stored reference was the same object. It stores a detached alias now. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Nothing is given up by storing weights per tensor instead of consolidating them into one flat buffer per layer. Measured on one RTX 4090, using a real DiT layer's size distribution (66 tensors, 542.3 MiB, of which 46 are under 64 KiB and carry 0.02% of the bytes), each configuration in its own process so allocator state cannot leak between them: | host layout | copies | H2D | |---|---|---| | one consolidated buffer | 1 | 13.39 GB/s | | one tensor each | 66 | 13.41 GB/s | | big tensors alone, small ones merged | 18 | 13.45 GB/s | Within 0.5%. For reference, the same box moves 2 GiB at 13.09 GB/s from pinned anonymous memory, 8.84 GB/s from pageable anonymous, and about 8.5 GB/s from a cache-resident file mapping -- so a mapping is a slower source than pinned, which is why this only applies where pinning was already off. ## Warmup A mapped page is read from disk on first touch, so the first request after startup would pay for every page it needs. Initialization now touches one byte per page of every kept mapping, which is enough to fault the whole page in. Measured over 512 MiB on the same box: | | prefault | H2D that follows | |---|---|---| | cold, nothing done | 0 ms | 2.63 GB/s | | `MADV_WILLNEED` | 3.7 ms | 2.62 GB/s | | **touch one byte per page** | 171.8 ms | **12.38 GB/s** | Two things worth noting. `MADV_WILLNEED` bought nothing -- it returns in milliseconds and the readahead has not happened by the time the copy starts, so an advisory is the wrong tool when the data is wanted immediately. And a fully resident mapping copies at 12.38 GB/s against 13.39 for pinned, so once faulted in the mapping is within 8% of pinned rather than the 1.6x a partially-warm one suggests. This is best-effort by construction: the pages are reclaimable, which is the reason the mapping was kept, so under pressure the kernel may drop them again and the next copy pays the fault. That is the trade being made, and the docstring says so. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Notes Scoped to `--pin-cpu-memory false` deliberately, so the condition is one a user can already reach and the change needs nothing else to be useful. A follow-up can let the host pin budget in #35641 drive it, so a component that cannot afford pins keeps its mapping rather than falling back to an anonymous copy. Not addressed here: the default loader path is the Run:ai streamer (`SGLANG_USE_RUNAI_MODEL_STREAMER=True`), which copies into anonymous memory, so a mapping only exists on the `safe_open` route. #35668 names that difference as a reader capability; wiring the choice to it comes next. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #32350796436](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32350796436)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32350795915](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32350795915)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #32350796076](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32350796076)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.text: ## Summary - refresh the checked-in SGLang Diffusion skills for recently added LongCat-Image, SANA-Video, LingBot Video MoE, Cosmos3 Edge/distilled, and LTX-2.5 paths - make the denoise benchmark helper eager by default, with `--torch-compile` as an explicit labeled comparator, while keeping nightly presets aligned with the CI comparison config - add task-owned Hugging Face/ModelScope cache isolation, handled-interruption cleanup, zero-residual accounting, and a JSONL cleanup ledger - add dependency-light unit coverage for recent presets, eager/compile behavior, nightly drift, cleanup safety, errors, and interruptions Background survey: https://github.com/BBuf/how-to-optim-algorithm-in-cuda/issues/21 ## Why The existing skill still assumed compile was the default fast path and did not cover several model families added recently. That makes eager-kernel opportunity discovery harder and makes repeated model-backed profiling risky on hosts with limited disk. The helper now treats eager as the ground truth, keeps compile as a separate control, and can guarantee that a newly created per-model download cache is removed after success, failure, or a handled interruption. SGLang JIT caches are deliberately not redirected or deleted. ## Validation - `uvx ruff format ...` - `uvx ruff check ...` - `python3 python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/unit/test_diffusion_benchmark_skill.py` (6 tests) - nightly preset alignment against `scripts/ci/utils/diffusion/comparison_configs.json` - `quick_validate.py` for the add-model, benchmark/profile, and performance skills - `git diff --check` No model weights were downloaded and no GPU was used for this documentation/helper PR. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #32353044878](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32353044878)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32367322127](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32367322127)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32353044883](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32353044883)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.text: ## Motivation Deep radix-cache walks repeatedly sliced `RadixKey`, copying progressively smaller token arrays along the matched path. ## Modifications - Add logical offsets to `RadixKey.match` and `child_key`. - Keep one request key and advance caller-local cursors in Radix, HiRadix, Mamba, SWA, and Unified trees. - Add suffix-equivalence tests and a deep-tree serving benchmark. ## Accuracy Tests - CUDA 12.9 / L40S cache suite: `1148 passed, 1070 skipped, 126 subtests passed`. - Offset matching is checked against sliced-suffix matching across page sizes, bigram keys, limits, partial matches, and empty keys. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Qwen3.5-9B on one L40S; 131,072-token prompt, 131,008 cached tokens, 128-node path, output length 0. Values are averages of two 200-request serving runs. | Server latency | `main` | This PR | Change | |---|---:|---:|---:| | Median | 56.981 ms | 51.661 ms | -9.3% | | P90 | 57.580 ms | 52.829 ms | -8.3% | Benchmark: `python benchmark/scheduler/bench_radix_tree_e2e.py --total-tokens 131072 --depth 128 --branch-tokens 128 --warmup-requests 20 --num-requests 200 --measurement-output-len 0` AI assistance: used to assist validation. ## Checklist - [x] Code formatted with pre-commit. - [x] Unit tests added and run. - [x] Documentation not needed for this internal optimization. - [x] GPU serving benchmark results provided. - [x] SGLang code style followed. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32354435808](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32354435808)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32354435498](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32354435498)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32354435769](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32354435769)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [Fix] Honor `--config=path.yaml` when merging the YAML config
signals.text: ## Problem `--config path.yaml` and `--config=path.yaml` are both accepted by argparse, but only the first one actually works. The YAML merge in `prepare_server_args` is gated on the exact token `"--config"`: ```python if "--config" in argv: ... argv = config_merger.merge_config_with_args(argv) ``` `"--config=path.yaml"` is not that token, so the gate is skipped and `parse_args` receives the raw argv: the file path is stored in `--config` but **every setting inside the file is silently dropped** — no warning, no error. A config-driven deployment quietly runs with defaults for everything that was supposed to come from the YAML. Repro (on current main): ```python from sglang.srt.server_args import prepare_server_args # config.yaml contains: mem-fraction-static: 0.42 # max-running-requests: 128 a = prepare_server_args(["--model-path", "dummy", "--config", "config.yaml"]) b = prepare_server_args(["--model-path", "dummy", "--config=config.yaml"]) print(a.mem_fraction_static, b.mem_fraction_static) # 0.42 None ``` ## Fix Normalize the equals form to the space form in `prepare_server_args` before the gate (`_normalize_config_flag`), so the existing exact-token matching in `server_args_config_parser.py` sees a uniform spelling. Only the `--config=` prefix is split; nothing else in argv is rewritten and the space-form path is byte-identical to before. ## Test `test_config_equals_form_is_merged` in `test/registered/unit/server_args/test_server_args.py` (next to the existing config-merge tests): both spellings must resolve the YAML settings identically. Verified the case fails on main and passes with the fix. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:warning: [Run #32434713762](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32434713762)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:warning: [Run #32434713626](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32434713626)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:warning: [Run #32434713858](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32434713858)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [Fix] Forward an explicit CXX to nvcc via -ccbin in JIT builds
signals.text: ## Problem The JIT build resolves the host compiler from `CXX` (`toolchain.host_compiler_path()`) and uses it for the `.cpp` translation units and the link step — but never tells nvcc. nvcc ignores `CXX` entirely: it takes `-ccbin` or falls back to `gcc` from `PATH`. So on a machine whose default gcc is newer than the CUDA toolkit's nvcc supports, every JIT kernel build fails: ``` host_config.h:132: #error -- unsupported GNU version! gcc versions later than 12 are not supported! ``` even when the user explicitly set `CXX=/usr/bin/g++-12` to fix exactly that. Repro on such a machine (CUDA 12.x nvcc + default gcc 13): ```python import os os.environ["CXX"] = "/usr/bin/g++-12" from sglang.kernels.jit.utils.compile import toolchain print(toolchain.host_compiler_path()) # /usr/bin/g++-12 (.cpp units + link) print(toolchain.base_cuda_flags()) # ['-Xcompiler', '-fPIC'] <- no -ccbin ``` The generated `build.ninja` compiles `.cpp` with `$cxx` (g++-12) while the `compile_cuda` rule lets nvcc pick `gcc` (13) for all host code inside `.cu` units. ## Fix `base_cuda_flags()` appends `-ccbin $CXX` when `CXX` is set explicitly (resolved through the `@cache_once`-cached `explicit_host_compiler()`, so both call sites see one value). When `CXX` is unset the flags are unchanged — nvcc's own default (`gcc` from PATH) is preserved, since forwarding the `"c++"` fallback would silently change the default host compiler. The HIP branch is untouched (hipcc takes no `-ccbin`). The build key follows automatically: it is taken over the generated `build.ninja` text (which now embeds the flag) and `_environment_fingerprint` already fingerprints `host_compiler_path()`, so a changed `CXX` re-keys the build instead of reusing stale binaries. Verified end to end on an RTX 3080 / CUDA 12.0 / default gcc 13 machine: with the JIT cache cleared, `CXX=/usr/bin/gcc-12 python3 -m sglang.launch_server ...` now compiles all JIT kernels and serves traffic. Before the fix the same command failed every `.cu` build with the error above, and the only workaround was to also set `NVCC_CCBIN` — a variable this code path never reads. Per review, no unit test is attached: the behavior depends on a compiler the CI machine is not guaranteed to have, so the change ships without a test. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:warning: [Run #32434634900](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32434634900)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:warning: [Run #32434634637](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32434634637)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:warning: [Run #32434634736](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32434634736)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [diffusion] MiniMax-H3 Spectrum skip-step + fused RMSNorm/AdaLN
signals.text: ## Summary Wires training-free Spectrum skip-step into MiniMax-H3 and fuses RMSNorm + indexed AdaLN. On one 24GB GPU, 50-step BF16+FA (**1008.6 s**) drops to **285.3 s (3.53×)** with exact attention, up to **219.0 s (4.61×)** with Sage→Sol hybrid + Spectrum. 1344×768 · 107 frames · 50 NFE · same process: warmup (seed 0) → timed (seed 42), timed only. PSNR is per-frame vs the **same-tree** INT8+FA video (Spectrum off). | Config | timed e2e | vs BF16+FA | PSNR mean / min | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | | BF16 + FlashAttention (baseline) | 1008.6 s | 1.00× | — | | `kitchen_int8` + FA (Spectrum off) | 718.5 s | 1.40× | — | | **`kitchen_int8` + FA + Spectrum `11/5/1.0`** — recommend | **285.3 s** | **3.53×** | **27.37 / 25.28** | | `kitchen_int8` + FA + Spectrum `15/5/0` | 387.4 s | 2.60× | 30.82 / 28.69 | | `kitchen_int8` + `sage_attn` + Spectrum `15/5/0` | 245.3 s | 4.11× | 23.56 / 21.01 | | `kitchen_int8` + Sage→Sol hybrid + Spectrum `15/5/0.5` | **219.0 s** | **4.61×** | 20.57 / 17.75 | | *(external reference)* ComfyUI INT8 workflow | 752.6 s | 1.34× |- | ComfyUI is a 24GB yardstick only. Same-INT8 gap is 752.6 vs 718.5 s (**1.05×**). ## Motivation [#34581](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/34581) already moved the 24GB path onto `kitchen_int8` + FlashAttention (~14 s/step). H3's default is **50 steps**, so the remaining cost is running the 50-layer stack every step (~12 min). Cache-DiT (`quality="high"`) is the in-tree skip-compute for multi-GPU H3, but it cannot combine with `--dit-layerwise-offload`, so a 24GB card that must stream the DiT cannot use it. On the audited 4×H200 recipe it is also only 1.40× and still walks the first blocks. Spectrum ([arxiv:2603.01623](https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.01623)) is already wired for FLUX.1 / Wan / HunyuanVideo / SD3: it forecasts DiT features and **skips the whole stack**, and it works with layerwise offload. H3 could not use it because the packed sequence is not a uniform video stream. ## Modifications ### 1. Spectrum on MiniMax-H3 Opt-in via `--enable-spectrum`. Off path does not enter the mixin — bit-exact vs today's H3. - Forecast only the packed **target** suffix: contiguous target audio immediately before `infer_out_pos` video. Earlier reference-audio rows are dropped (Wan2GP `hidden[audio_start:]`). - Comfy blends: **audio hold** (0), **video lerp 0.5**. - History on CPU, default `history_size` 100 → **8** (24GB). - `layer_names = ["blocks", "token_refiner.blocks"]` so a skip is the 50-layer stack, not a Cache-DiT wrap. Works with DiT layerwise offload. - Fail-closed with `quality="high"` / `enable_cache_dit`, and with sequence-parallel `sp_ws > 1`. Generic Spectrum defaults (`warmup=5, window=2, flex=0.75`) are the 20 NFE row. H3's model default is 50 steps; **`warmup=5` is a quality cliff there**. The recommended 50-step schedule is `11 / 5 / 1.0` (all frames >25 dB vs FA). Sage / Sol + Spectrum is faster but the PSNR ceiling is the attention backend (~23.6 dB vs FA at 50 NFE). If the bar is "looks like FA", keep `fa`. ### 2. Fused RMSNorm + indexed AdaLN `fused_indexed_rmsnorm_scale_shift` writes `RMSNorm(x) * (1+scale[idx]) + shift[idx]` without materializing the normalized tensor. Gate: BF16, not `torch.compile`; otherwise the existing eager modulate. Lossless (1 ULP; `mean|Δ|≈2e-8`). Exclusive 20 NFE INT8+FA: 290.8 → **289.7 s** (−1.06 s, ~0.3%). Same kernel every step, so ~−2.3 s at 50 NFE. On whenever the Triton path matches; no flag. ## Accuracy Tests Same prompt and seed (42). First pair is 50 NFE, exact attention; the Spectrum row is the recommend schedule. Second pair is 20 NFE library defaults. **`kitchen_int8` + FA, 50 NFE — 718.5 s** **`kitchen_int8` + FA + Spectrum `11/5/1.0`, 50 NFE — 285.3 s (27.4 dB)** **`kitchen_int8` + FA + Spectrum `5/2/0.75`, 20 NFE — 189.5 s (25.6 dB)** ## Example Exact-attention recommend (**3.53×** vs BF16) — INT8 Linear, FlashAttention, Spectrum `11/5/1.0`: ```bash pip install comfy-kitchen # required only for --quantization kitchen_int8 sglang generate \ --model-path MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3 \ --model-variant fl2va \ --quantization kitchen_int8 \ --attention-backend fa \ --enable-spectrum \ --spectrum-warmup-steps 11 \ --spectrum-window-size 5 \ --spectrum-flex-window 1.0 \ --performance-mode memory \ --layerwise-offload-components dit,text_encoder \ --dit-offload-prefetch-size 1 \ --dit-layerwise-resident-layers 0 \ --enable-torch-compile false \ --prompt "A cat walking on a sunny beach, gentle waves." \ --save-output ``` Speed ceiling (**4.61×** vs BF16) — same offload, Sage→Sol hybrid on the DiT and Spectrum `15/5/0.5`. Approximate attention; PSNR 20.6 / 17.8 dB vs FA. ```bash sglang generate \ --model-path MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3 \ --model-variant fl2va \ --quantization kitchen_int8 \ --attention-backend sol_attn \ --attention-backend-config dense_backend=sage_attn,dense_steps=10 \ --component-attention-backends text_encoder=torch_sdpa,transformer=sol_attn \ --enable-spectrum \ --spectrum-warmup-steps 15 \ --spectrum-window-size 5 \ --spectrum-flex-window 0.5 \ --performance-mode memory \ --layerwise-offload-components dit,text_encoder \ --dit-offload-prefetch-size 1 \ --dit-layerwise-resident-layers 0 \ --enable-torch-compile false \ --prompt "A cat walking on a sunny beach, gentle waves." \ --save-output ``` `--layerwise-offload-components` omits `vae` (same as #34581). Omit `--enable-spectrum` and the three `--spectrum-*` flags for the 718 s INT8+FA path. At 20 NFE, `--enable-spectrum` alone is enough (library defaults). Drop `--quantization` for BF16. ## Benchmarking and Profiling RTX 4090 D 24GB · CUDA 13.0 · 1344×768 / 107 frames / euler · `torch.compile` and Cache-DiT **disabled** · load → warmup (seed 0) → timed (seed 42), **timed pass only**. Cross-framework PSNR vs Comfy (~16 dB) is TE NVFP4 vs BF16 — not a quality column. The `kitchen_int8` SwiGLU fuse (`int8_linear(input_act=swiglu)`) is **not** on in these numbers. Released `comfy-kitchen==0.2.26` leaves `silu*up` in fp32 and rewrites INT8 rows (50 NFE vs unfused: **22.0 / 19.8 dB** — a different sample). [comfy-kitchen#124](https://github.com/Comfy-Org/comfy-kitchen/pull/124) rounds to the storage dtype first; fc2 is then bit-exact and the fuse is about **−4.4 s / 20 NFE** (~−10 s at 50). Leave it off until that lands. Results are in the table at the top. Text encoding and VAE decode are unchanged; Spectrum only skips selected DiT stacks. ## Checklist - [ ] Format code with pre-commit hooks - [ ] Unit tests: `test_minimax_h3_spectrum.py` - [ ] Default (`--enable-spectrum` omitted) unchanged - [ ] Cookbook + `spectrum.mdx` list MiniMax-H3 and the 50-step schedule - [ ] Benchmark and PSNR vs same-tree FA included above <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32355274217](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32355274217)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32355273961](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32355273961)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32355274147](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32355274147)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [AMD][CI] Name the ROCm Image That Actually Ran in AMD Job Names
signals.text: Follow-up to #35602 and #35603. After #35602 the ROCm 7.2 PR gate pulls the **7.2.4** image, but every job in it is still named `...-rocm720`. After #35603 a single nightly run covers both images, and since no nightly job declares a `name:`, GitHub auto-appends the matrix value and prints `nightly-test-1-gpu-unit-rocm720 (rocm724)` — one name carrying both version numbers. This stops the name stem from hardcoding a ROCm version. The stem becomes just the job's own name, and the ROCm flavor is shown after it. ## Naming The flavor moves out of the stem into the paren coordinates, ahead of the runner and shard: | before | after | | --- | --- | | `stage-c-test-large-8-gpu-amd-rocm720 (linux-mi300-8gpu-sglang, 3)` | `stage-c-test-large-8-gpu-amd (rocm724, linux-mi300-8gpu-sglang, 3)` | | `stage-c-test-large-8-gpu-amd (linux-mi300-8gpu-sglang, 3)` | `stage-c-test-large-8-gpu-amd (rocm700, linux-mi300-8gpu-sglang, 3)` | | `nightly-test-1-gpu-unit-rocm720 (rocm724)` | `nightly-test-1-gpu-unit (rocm724)` | Three things this buys: - **The flavor is printed unconditionally.** `pr-test-amd-extra.yml` suppressed the suffix for whatever was currently the default, so #35602 silently changed what the bare name `extra-a-test-1-gpu-small-amd` referred to — 7.2.0 before, 7.2.4 after — with no visible diff in the Actions UI. - **The stem stops moving when the pinned image is bumped.** A future 7.2.5 renames nothing. - **The stem is now exactly the `run_suite.py` suite name**, which is what you pass to reproduce a failure locally. The paren value is the ROCm lane the run is configured for, i.e. `inputs.rocm_version` (or the ROCm 7.0 lane's fixed default). It is not a claim about the image digest: `amd_ci_image` / `AMD_CI_IMAGE` still takes priority inside `amd_ci_start_container.sh`, so a dispatch that pins a custom image will show its configured lane rather than that image. That escape hatch is deliberately out of scope here. **Job ids are unchanged.** `needs:` lists, the `target_stage_select` options and the `job_filter` conditions all key off ids, so they are untouched. ## The two consumers that match on display names Neither of these reads job ids, so both have to follow the rename. **`wait-for-jobs`** gates stage B on stage A and stage C on stage B by polling `job.name` with `name === prefix || name.startsWith(prefix + ' ')`. Its four prefixes in the 7.2 gate carried the `-rocm720` suffix and would have matched nothing, spinning stage A for its full 240-minute budget and stage B for 480 after that. They now use the bare stems, which match on the trailing space and still exclude the `-nondeterministic` and `-mi35x` variants (next character is a dash). The 7.0 gate already used bare stems and was unaffected. **`amd-ci-job-monitor.yml`** builds its report targets from job ids and hands them to `query_job_status.py`, which prefix-matches them against display names: - The 7.2 lanes strip the `-rocm720` id suffix to recover the stem. - The nightly asks for each flavor by full name. A stem-only prefix matches both `(rocm724)` and `(rocm720)` — `_job_name_matches_filter` accepts a following space — so it would merge the two images into a single row and show a 7.2.4-only regression as a ~50% flake rate on a row labelled `rocm720`. - The extra call and the two stage waits drop out of the 7.2 gate list: they run on `ubuntu-latest`, so the self-hosted-only snapshot never had data for them. ## Verification Rendered every job name in all four workflows, expanding each `strategy.matrix` the way GitHub does, then replayed both consumers against those names — the monitor filters through the real `_job_name_matches_filter`, and every `wait-for-jobs` prefix through the action's own rule, asserting each resolves to exactly its declared `expected_count`. | workflow | names | monitor filters | wait prefixes | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `pr-test-amd-rocm720.yml` | 45 | 19 | 4 | | `nightly-test-amd-rocm720.yml` | 94 | 94 | 0 | | `pr-test-amd.yml` | 46 | 20 | 4 | | `nightly-test-amd.yml` | 43 | 43 | 0 | Every name is unique, every monitor filter resolves to exactly one job, every job is covered, and every wait prefix hits its expected count. The uniqueness assertion caught a draft in which the explicit `name:` added to the mi35x jobs dropped their `matrix.runner` / `matrix.part` and collapsed three shards onto one name. Per-job history in `query_job_status.py` splits at this commit, since the names change. Nothing gates on the old strings: `GET /repos/sgl-project/sglang/rules/branches/main` returns only `deletion`, `non_fast_forward`, `pull_request` and `required_linear_history`, with no `required_status_checks`. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests <!-- N/A: CI configuration change --> - [ ] Update documentation <!-- N/A --> - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:no_entry_sign: [Run #32388017995](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32388017995)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:no_entry_sign: [Run #32388017547](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32388017547)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:no_entry_sign: [Run #32388018196](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32388018196)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [Unified Cache][Draft POC]: Add optional external-cache linker mode to Unified Radix Cache
signals.text: ## Motivation Unified Radix Cache manages heterogeneous model states, including full-attention KV, SWA KV, and model-specific sidecars. On GB platforms, **deployments may need to aggregate larger memory regions into a shared Global Memory pool**. This requires an efficient way for Unified Radix Cache to access remote memory directly without overhead on the inference critical path. This PR adds an optional external-cache linker mode. It allows the tree to access a Global Memory pool through backends such as Mooncake or UMBP .. while retaining ownership of allocation, insertion, component consistency, and cache-node lifetime. The existing hierarchical cache path remains unchanged. The linker is an opt-in alternative for deployments that need a larger shared memory pool while preserving inference performance. ## Modifications This PR is currently at the proof-of-concept stage and will be split into several smaller, focused PRs: - [ ] Introduce the external linker interface and common linker wrapper - [ ] Integrate external linker support into `UnifiedRadixCache` - [ ] Add direct linker implementations for Mooncake、UMBP - [ ] Expand correctness, compatibility, and performance testing - [ ] Support prefetch - [ ] Support other implementations ## Speed Tests and Profiling The optional Mooncake linker was benchmarked against the existing L3 Mooncake path on 8 * H200 GPUs. Lower TTFT is better. A positive percentage means that the linker is faster. DSV4: ## Accuracy Tests TODO: Add accuracy result for dsv4 / qwen3.8/glm5.2 + gsm8k/mmlu and swe-bench Co-Author With @huangtingwei9988 --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): :x: [Run #32356744626](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32356744626) Latest PR Test (Extra): :x: [Run #32356744437](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32356744437) Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): :x: [Run #32356744511](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32356744511)

signals.title: [diffusion] feat: let every layerwise component be configurable
signals.text: ## Motivation `--layerwise-offload-components` accepts any component, but the three knobs that shape *how* a component streams are named and gated for the DiT. `configure_layerwise_offload` substituted `0.0` for anything outside the DiT group: ```python prefetch_value = server_args.dit_offload_prefetch_size if dit_tuning_enabled else 0.0 resident_value = server_args.dit_layerwise_resident_layers if dit_tuning_enabled else 0.0 ``` so a text encoder or VAE in the layerwise list was pinned at prefetch 1, resident 0, `leading`, with no way to change it. The gate's stated reason was that auxiliary layers "run once per component use and get no reuse benefit from DiT residency". That reads residency as a cache warmed by reuse, and it is not one. `compute_streamed_layers` documents itself as "which layer indices are **streamed rather than held on the GPU**", and the existing `--dit-layerwise-resident-layers` help says resident layers "are transferred once (not re-streamed every step)". They are a static partition: loaded at configure time, removed from the transfer of **every** pass, including a component's first and only one. A component used once per request still gains — it earns the VRAM back once per request instead of once per denoising step. That is a difference in **return**, which argues for a conservative default, not for removing the knob. And prefetch never fit the argument at all: it overlaps a layer's transfer with the previous layer's compute, entirely within a single pass. The measurement that started this: taking H3's 10.4 GB video VAE out of the layerwise list cut decode 39.85 s → 5.32 s on one RTX 4090. "Out of the list" is `resident = all` — the same axis the gate declares useless for a once-per-request component. ## Modifications Three per-component options, using the `component=value` map this repository already uses for `--component-attention-backends` (JSON also accepted): ``` --layerwise-prefetch-size text_encoder=2,vae=2 --layerwise-resident-layers text_encoder=4 --layerwise-residency-policy text_encoder=strided ``` `ServerArgs.layerwise_tuning_for(component_name, dit_group=...)` resolves the triple: a per-component entry wins; without one, the DiT group keeps the `--dit-*` scalars and auxiliaries keep today's `(0.0, 0.0, leading)`. `configure_layerwise_offload` takes the component name and calls it instead of branching on `dit_tuning_enabled`. The `--dit-*` flags keep their meaning as the group default — the defect was that auxiliaries could not be tuned, not that a DiT-shaped default exists. ## Accuracy Tests `test_layerwise_offload.py`: **48 passed**, 44 of them pre-existing — behaviour is unchanged unless a caller sets one of the new options. Four new cases cover the default split, a per-component entry winning without leaking to other components, an unknown policy raising, and both the `a=1,b=2` and JSON spellings. ## Speed Tests and Profiling End-to-end on one RTX 4090, MiniMax-H3 t2va, 672x384, 4 steps, with `--layerwise-prefetch-size text_encoder=2`: | | baseline | text_encoder=2 | |---|---|---| | TextEncodingStage | 3.526 s | 3.516 s | | peak | 22231 MiB | **24006 MiB** | The option is accepted and reaches the component — peak memory moves by 1.8 GB, which is its staging buffers. Text encoding does **not** get faster, and 24006 of 24564 MiB is 98% of the card. That is the honest result, and it is the argument for exposing the knob rather than choosing a value on the user's behalf: the tradeoff is real in both directions and depends on the model, the component and the card. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #32370141859](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32370141859)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32370141679](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32370141679)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #32370141827](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32370141827)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: Skip empty linear-attention state buffers in PD transfer
signals.text: ## Motivation PD disaggregation cannot transfer state for Inkling: every request fails with `Failed to send kv chunk`, and once one send fails the session is blacklisted, so every later request reports `remote mooncake session ... is not alive`. The blacklisting hides the first error. With mooncake logging turned up the real order shows: ``` E transfer_engine_impl.cpp:777] Transfer Engine does not support zero length memory region E rdma_transport.cpp:656] Memory region not registered by any active device(s): 0x7960b8040000 ``` Registration comes first, and it fails on an empty buffer. `MambaPool._iter_transfer_state_tensors` walks the state fields and skips the ones that are `None` or explicitly non-transferable, but a field can also be present and empty: a ShortConv layer has no recurrent temporal state, so its `temporal` shape is declared degenerate and the pool allocates a zero-byte tensor per layer. Those get advertised as transferable state, the engine rejects a zero-length region, and the failed batch registration leaves the real buffers unregistered too, so the transfer then fails on a live buffer with a message that points somewhere else. Measured on Inkling-Small, per role: the mamba component reports 42 empty entries out of 294, one per layer and all from `temporal`, while `conv` reports 0 out of 252 and the attention and aux buffers report none. A model whose linear layers do carry temporal state never hits this. The skip goes in the iterator rather than in a transfer backend: five call sites build parallel per-tensor lists from it (pointers, lengths, item lengths, sliceable dims, field names), so filtering there keeps them aligned with each other, and both the mooncake and NIXL registration paths get it. Prefill and decode run the same code, so they skip the same entries and stay in step. Not a regression: the degenerate `temporal` shape has been there since the initial Inkling support (#31681), the pre-refactor version of this code advertised `temporal` the same way, and the mooncake version is unchanged. ## Accuracy Single-node PD, one prefill and one decode role, TP=2 each, mooncake transfer over IB, hierarchical cache on the prefill role. Before this change no request completes at all. `sgl-eval` aime26, thinking on, `max_tokens=131072`: ``` score = 0.9667 error_rate = 0.00% stop_rate = 1.00 truncated_rate = 0.00% total_completion_tokens = 768226 ``` Long generations are the load-bearing part here: ~25k completion tokens per problem means the decode role advances the convolution state for tens of thousands of steps off what was transferred, so a lossy or misaligned transfer would not survive it. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:no_entry_sign: [Run #32370515187](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32370515187)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #32370515110](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32370515110)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #32370515225](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32370515225)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [Fix][Profiler] Count target verify as decode stage
signals.text: ## Motivation Partially addresses #34943 and complements #35115, which handles asynchronous trace export. During speculative decoding, scheduler batches use `ForwardMode.TARGET_VERIFY`. That mode is intentionally extend-shaped and therefore satisfies `is_prefill()`, so the legacy by-stage profiler counted verify iterations as prefill and never advanced or completed its decode-stage window. The unfinished profile could then stop during a later request. ## Modifications - Treat both `DECODE` and `TARGET_VERIFY` as decode-stage work in the legacy by-stage profiler. - Give that lifecycle classification precedence over the extend-shaped `is_prefill()` classification. - Add a CPU regression test covering the `EXTEND -> TARGET_VERIFY -> TARGET_VERIFY` transition and its stage start/stop calls. ## Accuracy Tests No model computation or output values are changed. - `pytest -q test/registered/unit/managers/scheduler_components/test_profiler_manager.py` (`1 passed`) - Black, isort, and focused Ruff checks pass for both changed files. - `python scripts/lint/check_registered_tests.py` ## Speed Tests and Profiling No benchmark was run. The change only affects profiler stage bookkeeping when legacy `profile_by_stage` is enabled; normal inference scheduling is unchanged. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. signals.title: fix(anthropic): degrade tool_reference to text when template lacks support
signals.text: ## Motivation Fixes #35692. The Anthropic endpoint converts `tool_reference` blocks in `tool_result` content into structured `{"type": "tool_reference", "name": ...}` parts. That part type is only rendered by chat templates that implement deferred-reference expansion (GLM family). For any other model, the template raises on the unknown item type and the request 500s with `Unexpected item type in content`. With Claude Code the failure is sticky: once a reference enters the conversation history, every request in that session fails until the context is cleared. ## Modifications - `AnthropicServing._template_supports_tool_reference()`: detect support by checking whether the chat template source mentions `tool_reference` (a template that expands references must name the item type). Reuses the existing `_chat_template()` accessor and handles dict-valued multi-templates. - `_convert_tool_result_content`: when the template does not support the structured part, emit `[tool reference: <name>]` as a plain text part so history echoes keep working. GLM behavior is unchanged. ## Tests - The three existing `tool_reference` unit tests now pass the GLM reference template through the serving fake, pinning the structured-part path. - Added `test_tool_reference_degrades_to_text_without_template_support` and `test_reference_only_tool_result_degrades_to_text_without_template_support`. - Full test file passes locally: 61/61. Live repro from the issue (500 before, 200 after) uses the stock Qwen3.8-27B template with one `tool_reference` item inside a `tool_result`. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32362870707](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32362870707)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32362870553](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32362870553)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32362870655](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32362870655)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: fix: keep speculative overshoot out of the radix cache key
signals.text: ## Motivation A speculative verify step commits a whole accepted chunk, so a request's `output_ids` can run past the point where it actually stopped — measured 0–7 tokens for DSPARK `block_size=7` at `max_new_tokens=1024`. The client is served `output_ids_through_stop`; the radix cache is keyed on raw `output_ids`: ```python # mem_cache/unified_radix_cache.py, cache_finished_req token_ids = (req.origin_input_ids + req.output_ids)[:kv_len_to_handle] ``` So the tree stores a suffix no continuation can reproduce. A follow-up turn is built from what the client received and therefore diverges from the cached sequence at `prompt + returned`. On a full-KV model that is wasted pages. On a hybrid model it costs the whole decode region. Under `--mamba-radix-cache-strategy extra_buffer` the insert carries exactly one mamba checkpoint, at `floor(committed / interval) * interval`, and `MambaComponent.create_match_validator` is a hard gate — a node without a mamba value cannot extend the mamba boundary. When the checkpoint lands past the divergence point, the matched prefix has no checkpoint at all and reuse falls back to the prefill-time insert: ``` prompt=3964 committed=1029 insert_len=4992 reachable=4988 Decode cache miss for prompt 1 | cached=3840 prompt_len=3964 ``` `3840 == floor(3964 / 128) * 128` — the second turn matched a page-aligned prefix of the prompt and none of the 1024 generated tokens. Predicate: `floor((prompt + committed) / interval) * interval > prompt + returned`. Over a measured 4x B200 sample of 36 first-turn prompts it fires exactly once, on the one prompt that missed, 10/10 reps. The window is at most `chain_len - 1` positions out of `interval`, so it reads as intermittent — roughly one prompt in 32 — but it is deterministic given the prompt. Without speculation `committed == returned` and the gap is empty. ## Modifications `Req.effective_kv_committed_len()` is the single point where the finish-time KV length is decided: `release_kv_cache` hands it to every cache implementation as `kv_len_to_handle`, and everything past it is released as overallocated. Capping it at what the client received keeps the overshoot out of the key and frees it in the same step, for all eight cache implementations at once rather than patching each `(origin_input_ids + output_ids)` site. The method already had precedent for this shape: `strip_thinking_cache` caps at the prompt for the same reason (#22373), "so thinking + answer fall into the overallocated range and are reclaimed by release_kv_cache". `StreamingSession.try_cache_finished_req` is stronger precedent still — the session path already calls `_trim_overshoot(req, finished_len)` and sets `slot.kv_committed_len = min(len(origin_input_ids) + finished_len, ...)`. The overshoot was already understood to be untrustworthy for reuse there; the plain `release_kv_cache` path never learned it. One companion change: `_release_overallocated_kv_indices` asserts a non-speculative request has nothing overallocated, and a stop landing before the last committed token now legitimately breaks that, so the assert learns about it the same way it already knows about `strip_thinking_cache`. No leak. The tail moves from "inserted" to "freed", and `ceil_align(start_p, page_size)` still lands on the page `cache_finished_req` just released, so the two frees meet without a gap and without double-freeing. ## Accuracy Test `test/registered/unit/managers/test_spec_overshoot_cache_len.py`, CPU, 4 cases — length overshoot, EOS landing mid-chunk, an exact stop, and an unfinished request. The last two are the guard against over-capping. ``` 4 passed ``` Reverted against the fix, the two overshoot cases go red and the two no-overshoot cases stay green: ``` 2 failed, 2 passed ``` ### End to end, 4x B200 Two arms of the same tree, differing only in this method, same server config, same prompts, same seed. Prompts constructed so `(prompt + max_new_tokens) % 128 == 127`, which is where the predicate can fire, plus a `% 128 == 0` control group that it can never reach: | prompt | before | after | |---|---|---| | 2431 (`%128 == 127`) | `cached=2304` **MISS** | `cached=3328` **HIT** | | 7 other `%128 == 127` | HIT | HIT | | 8 control `%128 == 0` | HIT | HIT | `2304 == floor(2431 / 128) * 128` is the prefill-time insert — the second turn reused none of the 1024 generated tokens. `3328 == floor((2431 + 1024) / 128) * 128` is exactly the length the cap produces, so the fix does not merely stop the miss, it lands the reuse where the arithmetic says it should. Deterministic: identical across both reps of both arms. The control group is byte-identical between arms, so nothing is over-capped. Model `thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small-NVFP4` + draft `RadixArk/Inkling-Small-DSpark`, `--tp 4 --speculative-algorithm DSPARK --mamba-radix-cache-strategy extra_buffer --mamba-track-interval 128 --page-size 128 --enable-deterministic-inference`, `SGLANG_ENABLE_UNIFIED_RADIX_TREE=1`. #35293 loosened `min_cache_hit_ratio` from 0.99 to 0.90 on the DSPARK class precisely because of this, so this PR puts it back to 0.99 — that class is then the e2e regression guard for this fix on `4-gpu-b200`, at every prompt rather than 90% of them. ### CI, 4x B200 `/rerun-test` on this branch's head, with the bar back at every prompt: ``` [CI Test Method] TestInklingSmallNvfp4DsparkDeterministic.test_input_output_logprobs_match avg_kl_div=0.0 [CI Test Method] TestInklingSmallNvfp4DsparkDeterministic.test_input_output_logprobs_match_decode_cache_hit avg_kl_div=0.0 [CI Test Method] TestInklingSmallNvfp4DsparkDeterministic.test_input_output_logprobs_match_prefill_cache_hit avg_kl_div=0.0 Ran 5 tests in 875.658s All 1 test(s) passed in 893s ``` No `Decode cache miss` lines and no `Too few decode cache hits` — the assertion that read 31/32 twice on this runner now passes at 32/32, and all three KL cases stay at exactly 0. ## Benchmark and Profiling Results Not applicable — one `min()` on the request-finish path, once per request. ## Checklist - signals.title: [docker] cu13 build fails with ResolutionImpossible installing runai-model-streamer: torch pins nvidia-nccl-cu13==2.29.7   but constraints.txt carries SGL_NCCL_VERSION (2.30.7)
signals.text: ## Motivation On the cu13 (CUDA_VERSION=13.0.3) build path with BUILD_TYPE=all (default), the framework stage aborts at the "Install essential Python packages" step: ERROR: Cannot install torch==2.13.0+cu130 because these package versions have conflicting dependencies. The conflict is caused by: torch 2.13.0+cu130 depends on nvidia-nccl-cu13==2.29.7 The user requested (constraint) nvidia-nccl-cu13==2.30.7 ERROR: ResolutionImpossible Root cause is a mismatch between torch's nccl pin and the Dockerfile's nccl override: 1. runai-model-streamer[s3,gcs,azure] (installed at the framework stage, Dockerfile ~line 538) depends on torch<3.0.0,>=2.0.0 (https://pypi.org/project/runai-model-streamer/). Pulling runai therefore makes pip resolve the runai → torch → nvidia-nccl-cu13 chain. 2. torch-2.13.0+cu130 pins nccl exactly: Requires-Dist: nvidia-nccl-cu13==2.29.7 (verified directly from the wheel's METADATA). 3. In the torch_deps stage the Dockerfile overrides nccl with --no-deps --force-reinstall (only for cu13): && if [ "${CUDA_VERSION%%.*}" = "13" ]; then \ python3 -m pip install --force-reinstall --no-deps \ "nvidia-nccl-cu13==${SGL_NCCL_VERSION}"; \ # default 2.30.7 fi and then freezes it into constraints.txt: && pip freeze | grep -v "^sglang==" > /sgl-workspace/constraints.txt so constraints.txt carries nvidia-nccl-cu13==2.30.7. 4. The framework-stage install runs under -c /sgl-workspace/constraints.txt. pip's resolver back-traces torch's transitive nvidia-nccl-cu13==2.29.7 and finds it unsatisfiable alongside the constraint ==2.30.7 → ResolutionImpossible. So whenever SGL_NCCL_VERSION (default 2.30.7) differs from torch's own pin (2.29.7 for torch 2.13.0+cu130), the cu13 image build fails. The cu12 path is unaffected (the nccl override only runs for cu13). ## Modifications Keep nccl out of the constraint solve for the affected install, then restore the override afterwards (commit 854a2e96). 1. Expose SGL_NCCL_VERSION in the framework stage so the restore step can reference it (the ARG was previously only visible in base/torch_deps): ``` ARG MSCCLPP_VERSION ARG SGL_NCCL_VERSION ``` 2. In the "Install essential Python packages" RUN, drop the nccl line from constraints.txt before the constrained install, so pip can pick a nccl consistent with torch's pin: ``` RUN --mount=type=cache,target=/root/.cache/pip \ sed -i '/^nvidia-nccl-cu13==/d' /sgl-workspace/constraints.txt \ && python3 -m pip install -c /sgl-workspace/constraints.txt \ datamodel_code_generator \ ... \ "runai-model-streamer[s3,gcs,azure]>=0.15.7" \ && python3 -m pip install --no-deps --force-reinstall "nvidia-nccl-cu13==${SGL_NCCL_VERSION}" ``` + sed removes only the nvidia-nccl-cu13== line, so the rest of constraints.txt still pins torch/transformers/etc. as intended. + With the nccl constraint gone, pip install -c succeeds; pip will satisfy torch by (down)loading nccl 2.29.7. + The trailing --no-deps --force-reinstall nvidia-nccl-cu13==${SGL_NCCL_VERSION} puts nccl back to the intended override (2.30.7), matching the pre-fix end state. ## Accuracy Tests <!-- If this pull request affects model outputs (e.g., changes to the kernel or model forward code), provide accuracy test results. --> ## Speed Tests and Profiling <!-- If this pull request impacts inference speed, provide benchmarking and profiling results. --> ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [ ] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. signals.title: [Bug] Seeded sampling changes token when a batchmate enables top-k/top-p
signals.text: ## Motivation `--enable-deterministic-inference` forces the pytorch sampling backend. Seeded Gumbel noise is hashed as `murmur_hash32(seed, position, column_index)`. The simple path (`sampling_from_probs_torch`) hashes **token ids**. The top-k/top-p/min-p path sorted first and hashed **rank**, then gathered back to token ids. `need_top_k/top_p/min_p` is a batch-level `any()`, so one filtering request (including greedy `temperature=0` → `top_k=1`) switched every row onto the rank-space path. Same `(seed, distribution, position)` could therefore sample a different token depending on who else was in the batch. Homogeneous batch-size tests do not catch this; mixed sampling params do. The MLX backend already enforces vocab-id noise (`test_seeded_row_unaffected_by_batchmate_filtering`). This ports that contract to the CUDA pytorch path and the Ascend sort fallback. Does not touch the `min_p` + seed assert; that is #33699. ## Modifications - After top-k/top-p/min-p masking, scatter weights back to vocab order, then call `multinomial_with_seed`. The argmax is already a token id. - Same helper on the Ascend sort fallback. The `npu_top_k_top_p` branch was already in vocab order. - Unseeded `torch.multinomial` is unchanged. - Tests in `test/registered/sampling/test_deterministic_vocab_id_noise.py`: - unfiltered row matches the simple path when a batchmate has `top_k=2` - `top_k == vocab_size` (no-op mask) matches the simple path - top-k zeros stay unreachable under Gumbel-max **Compatibility:** seeded + top-k/top-p outputs will change versus previous versions (rank-space → vocab-id-space). Mixed-batch results now match the solo simple path. Replay of old seeded+filter rollouts will not bit-match. ## Accuracy Tests Unit tests only (Triton `murmur_hash32`, no server): ```bash python3 test/registered/sampling/test_deterministic_vocab_id_noise.py python3 test/registered/sampling/test_deterministic_gumbel_u1.py ``` Pre-fix the first two cases failed (6 != 23, 8 != 12). Post-fix all three pass; existing gumbel u=1 tests still pass. No model-forward change for greedy-only or unseeded sampling. ## Speed Tests and Profiling No speed benchmark. The extra work is a [B, vocab] scatter after a full-vocab sort that this path already does. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). Docs/bench left unchecked: the documented seed contract does not need a wording change; this is not a throughput-sensitive kernel. ## Review and Merge Process cc sampling / deterministic-inference: @Fridge003 - Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process). - Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers. - Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so. - Common commands include /tag-and-rerun-ci, /tag-run-ci-label, /rerun-failed-ci - After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32365219565](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32365219565)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32365219295](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32365219295)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32365219450](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32365219450)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: fix(multimodal): keep LLaVA image fetch off the CPU-preprocess timeout budget (flaky test_mixed_batch)
signals.text: ## Summary Fixes the flaky `test/registered/vlm/test_vision_openai_server_a.py::TestLlavaServer::test_mixed_batch` (and removes a real robustness gap that affects all LLaVA‑family models in production). `LlavaImageProcessor._process_single_image` ran the **entire** image pipeline — network fetch **+** decode **+** CPU preprocessing — inside a single `cpu_executor` (ProcessPool) task, wrapped in: ```python timeout = int(os.environ.get("REQUEST_TIMEOUT", "10")) return await asyncio.wait_for(fut, timeout=timeout) ``` So the **network fetch was inside the CPU‑preprocessing timeout budget**. When the image host is transiently slow (e.g. `raw.githubusercontent.com` under CI network contention), the fetch pushes the task past the budget → `asyncio.TimeoutError` → **HTTP 500**. Two things make it worse: 1. **A `ProcessPoolExecutor` future can't be cancelled once it's running.** On timeout `wait_for` abandons the asyncio wrapper, but the worker keeps grinding the slow fetch. With a small pool and a burst of requests (`test_mixed_batch` fires 12 via a 4‑thread client), stuck workers saturate the pool and **cascade 500s** across otherwise‑fast requests — defeating both the OpenAI client's auto‑retries and the CI test‑level `retry()`. 2. Only LLaVA‑family models hit this: every other VLM uses the base `load_mm_data` path, which already separates cancellable io loading from CPU work. That's why this one test is the flaky one. ## Fix Split the two phases, matching `BaseMultimodalProcessor`'s existing io/cpu design: - **fetch + decode** in the shared **io thread pool** (`self.io_executor`), with a couple of retries for transient network blips; - **CPU‑only preprocessing** in the ProcessPool, so `asyncio.wait_for` now bounds **CPU work only**, never the network. No new config is required; `SGLANG_MM_LOAD_MAX_RETRIES` (default `2`) tunes the load retries. ## Evidence — flake probability before/after Controlled fault injection on 1×H200 with `lmms-lab/llava-onevision-qwen2-0.5b-ov`. Each image fetch is made "slow enough to cross the budget" with probability **p = 0.12** (`REQUEST_TIMEOUT=3`, `SGLANG_CPU_WORKERS=4`), reproducing transient network slowness at exactly the point the real code fetches the image. Images served locally (`file://`) so there is **zero real‑network variance** — the only variable between runs is the fix. The exact `test_mixed_batch` body (`image_ids=[0,1,2]*4`, 4‑thread pool) is run **100×** per condition, OpenAI client auto‑retries disabled to expose the raw server‑side rate. | Metric | Before fix | After fix | |---|---|---| | Per‑request server 500 rate | **7.95 %** (159/2001) | **0 %** (0/1200) | | Single‑attempt `test_mixed_batch` failure | **67 %** (67/100) | **0 %** (0/100) | | CI‑equivalent failure (`retry(max_retry=1)`) | **42 %** (42/100) | **0 %** (0/100) | | Server `TimeoutError` / 500 log lines | many | **0** | ## Test plan - ✅ Before/after fault‑injection measurement above. - ✅ Real upstream test with the fix, real image URLs, default timeout, no injection: `pytest test/registered/vlm/test_vision_openai_server_a.py -k TestLlavaServer` → **6 passed** (incl. `test_mixed_batch`, `test_image_prefix_cache_reuse`). 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32392839376](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32392839376)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32392839254](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32392839254)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32392839258](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32392839258)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->
