signals.title: [diffusion] let offloaded weights stay on the checkpoint mapping
signals.text: ## Motivation Layerwise offload copies every layer into host memory at startup, so host memory has to be at least as large as the component. MiniMax-H3's DiT is 61.73 GiB, which rules out a 12 GiB + 32 GiB budget outright -- not by a slow margin, but at initialization. Most of those bytes are already in host memory once, as a mapping. Measured on one H3 load: ``` PRE-OFFLOAD text_encoder: host pageable: 48.09 GB PRE-OFFLOAD transformer: host mmap: 50.53 GB, host pageable: 11.20 GB ``` 50.53 GiB of the DiT's 61.73 GiB reach the offload manager as views into the checkpoint: the loader builds the model on meta and `_can_assign_cpu_tensor_without_copy` hands the parameter the loaded tensor rather than copying into it. That holds because H3 stores the DiT in BF16 and runs it in BF16 -- checked against the safetensors headers, 61.66 GiB of the 61.73 GiB is BF16. Copying them a second time is what does not fit. ## Modifications A third host store sits beside the consolidated and stride-preserving ones, holding weights that are still views into the file. The page cache then decides what stays resident. The choice is not free. Pinning is what lets the copy stream run ahead of compute -- 1.03 s against 1.90 s per step on a measured Wan2.1 run -- and a mapping cannot be pinned, so those copies run on the compute stream instead. It is taken only when the copies do not fit, so nothing changes on a host with room. Three places had to agree that a mapping is the checkpoint, not a buffer: - `sync_layer_to_cpu` skips mapped weights. Inference does not mutate them, and writing would copy-on-write the mapping into the anonymous memory this exists to avoid. - `prefetch_layer` copies straight from the mapping, and no longer treats the consolidated store as the gate for whether a layer has weights at all. - `iter_cpu_weights` yields them, so checksums still see every weight. `MappedRegions` answers "is this tensor in a file mapping", built once because reading /proc/self/maps per tensor would be quadratic over H3's weight count. It replaces the closure #35618 had inlined for the same question. The encoder needed the same thing and mostly already had it. `_mps_zero_copy_weight_loading` let compatible CPU safetensors stay mapped instead of being copied, and the H3 encoder already honoured it -- it was gated on `current_platform.is_mps()`, on the reasoning that unified memory makes the copy pointless. "The copy does not fit" is the stronger form of that same argument and is not platform-specific, so the gate becomes "MPS, or the copies would not fit", measured from the checkpoint's on-disk size because the decision is made before a weight is read. Both callers now ask one predicate, `host_copies_would_not_fit` in host_memory_budget.py, which already owns the question of what this process may commit. The DiT path and the encoder path had each grown their own copy of the 4 GiB reserve and the comparison. Renamed with the gate, since both are now read on non-MPS paths: `_mps_zero_copy_weight_loading` -> `_keep_checkpoint_mapping`, `mps_zero_copy_unsafe` -> `checkpoint_mapping_unsafe`. `mps_layerwise_cpu_staging` keeps its name -- it is still set only under `is_mps()`. ## Accuracy Tests Which memory holds a weight; the weights themselves are untouched. Four new unit tests cover a file-backed weight staying mapped, an affordable one still being copied, the writeback leaving a mapping alone, and checksums still seeing mapped weights. Full `test/unit` suite: 1846 passed, with the same four pre-existing failures (`realtime/`, `sana_wm/`) that fail with this change reverted. Verified end to end on H3 `fl2va`, single GPU, host memory reported as 32 GiB: ``` Layerwise offload: leaving 49.36 GiB of weights on the checkpoint mapping -- copying them into host memory needs more than the 32.00 GiB available [m32] READY after 125s text_encoder (vram: 1.40 GB, host pinned: 0.77 GB, host mmap: 1.45 GB) transformer (vram: 2.09 GB, host pinned: 12.20 GB) video_vae (vram: 0.95 GB, host pinned: 9.00 GB) ``` The DiT's share of host memory goes from 61.73 GiB to 12.20 GiB and the encoder's from 46.18 GiB to 2.22 GiB. Load-time peak is 5176 MiB of VRAM and 23.42 GB of host memory, against the 12 GiB + 32 GiB the model is being asked to fit; before this the load failed outright. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Not measured on H3 yet, and the PR does not claim a speed result. What is known: a page-cache-resident mapping copies at 12.38 GB/s against 13.39 for pinned on one RTX 4090, so the bandwidth gap is small; what is given up is the overlap, which on Wan2.1 was worth 1.03 s against 1.90 s per step. On a host where the copies fit, this path is not taken and nothing changes. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## What this does not do This is a load-time result. It gets H3 into the budget at initialization; it does not claim a runtime one, and runtime activations are measured separately. Nothing here changes a host that has room -- both gates are "the copies do not fit", so a serving box takes the pinned path exactly as before. Building the encoder on meta was tried first and does not work: custom weight loaders such as `VocabParallelEmbedding`'s write into `param.data` slices, which a meta parameter has none of. Reusing the flag the MPS path already had avoids that entirely. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #32437583407](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32437583407)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32437583392](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32437583392)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #32437583361](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32437583361)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [diffusion] fix: fix loading a block-FP8 quantized MiniMax-H3 DiT
signals.text: Quantizing the MiniMax-H3 DiT with SGLang's own per_block_cast_to_fp8 yields a standard block-FP8 checkpoint that loads without error and then generates broken output: H3 stores qkv grouped per head, so the DiT already permutes those rows into [q_all, k_all, v_all] as it loads, but the accompanying weight_scale_inv tensor was passed through untouched, leaving every 128x128 tile scaling rows it no longer covered. Apply the same reorder to the scale, counting its rows in blocks rather than channels; head_dim and the block are both 128 so each head's q/k/v occupies whole scale rows, a block size that straddles heads cannot be fixed by a row permutation and now raises, and checkpoints with no weight_scale_inv parameter return at the first guard. ## Motivation A block-FP8 MiniMax-H3 DiT loads **without any error** and then generates a blank frame. Nothing in the log says anything is wrong: dtypes match, shapes match, `Detected fp8 checkpoint` is printed, the server reaches ready and serves requests at normal speed. Only the output is gone. H3 checkpoints store qkv grouped per attention head — `[h0_q, h0_k, h0_v, h1_q, ...]` — while `QKVParallelLinear` expects `[q_all, k_all, v_all]`. The DiT has always handled this: `_install_qkv_weight_loader` permutes those rows at load time. A block-FP8 checkpoint carries a second tensor alongside the weight, one scale per 128x128 tile, and that tensor reached the generic loader untouched. Once the weight rows moved, every tile was still scaling the rows it covered *before* the permutation. This is not specific to any one quantizer. The scale is produced in checkpoint layout — which is correct, a checkpoint should keep the released layout — and applying the reorder is the runtime's job, so any standard block-FP8 H3 checkpoint hits this. `per_block_cast_to_fp8` is SGLang's own quantization helper, so the bug reproduces with SGLang alone: ```python from sglang.srt.layers.quantization.fp8_utils import per_block_cast_to_fp8 # blocks.0.attn.qkv_proj.weight of MiniMax-H3: [21504, 5376] bf16, 56 heads x 128 q, s = per_block_cast_to_fp8(weight.cuda()) # q [21504, 5376] fp8_e4m3 # s [168, 42] fp32 (168 = 56 heads x 3, so one scale row per head's q / k / v) ``` ## Modifications `MiniMaxH3Attention._install_qkv_block_scale_loader` installs the existing qkv reorder on `weight_scale_inv`, counting its rows in blocks rather than channels, and is called from `_install_qkv_weight_loader` so it inherits that path's gating. - `head_dim` and the block size are both 128, so each head's q/k/v occupies whole scale rows and the row permutation is exact. - A `weight_block_size` that straddles heads cannot be repaired by a row permutation and now raises instead of silently corrupting the model. - Checkpoints with no `weight_scale_inv` parameter — BF16, online fp8, per-tensor fp8 — return at the first guard, so nothing else changes. - The GGUF path is unaffected: it already stores qkv as `[q_all, k_all, v_all]` and is gated out of the reorder entirely. Files:`python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/models/dits/minimax_h3.py`, `python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/unit/test_minimax_h3_dit_contract.py`. ## Accuracy Tests **End to end.** Served on 2x RTX 5090, TP=2, layerwise offload for dit and text_encoder, same prompt / seed 42 / 10 steps / 4s / 768p. | | output | frame contrast | frame-to-frame motion | encoded size | |---|---|---|---|---| | BF16 (reference) | normal | 62.5 | 13.6 | 1.7 MB | | block-FP8, **with** this fix | normal | 67.5 | 15.9 | 1.9 MB | | block-FP8, **without** this fix | blank | **4.0** | **0.7** | **0.5 MB** | Without the fix the frame carries no content at all: spatial contrast collapses 16x and inter-frame motion 19x. With the fix, block-FP8 tracks the BF16 reference at PSNR-Y 16.5 dB / SSIM-Y 0.68; the residual difference is sampling-trajectory divergence from fp8 rounding rather than corruption — the two videos show the same scene, subject and action with a mild composition drift. **Unit tests.** New cases in `test_minimax_h3_dit_contract.py` cover the reorder itself, the straddling-block guard, and the untouched non-block-quantized path. The H3 and quantization suites under `python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/unit/` pass. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Same configuration as above. This PR does not change any compute path — it only fixes what the loader writes into the scale parameter — so the speed difference is simply block-FP8 versus BF16 weights under layerwise offload: | | time | |---|---| | BF16 | 104.7s | | block-FP8 with this fix | **70.4s** (1.49x) | ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). — no user-facing surface changes; block-FP8 checkpoints were already meant to load. - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): :x: [Run #32366132991](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32366132991) Latest PR Test (Extra): :x: [Run #32366132837](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32366132837) Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): :x: [Run #32366132994](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32366132994)

signals.title: [Feature] Support for same GPU native DP replicas with optional CUDA MPS
signals.text: ## Motivation Phase 1 for <https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/35648>. But It will work great for one shot models that don't need to save KV cache, like prefill embedding only models. This change adds `--same-gpu-replicas N` for running `N` native SGLang data-parallel replicas on one physical GPU through one public server endpoint. For example: ```bash --same-gpu-replicas 2 ``` resolves to: ```bash --dp-size 2 --gpu-id-step 0 ``` CUDA MPS is optional and remains externally managed. SGLang runs with normal CUDA scheduling when MPS is unavailable and logs a CUDA startup warning when `nvidia-cuda-mps-control` is not installed. ## Modifications - Add `--same-gpu-replicas N` for guarded same-GPU native DP. - Validate the supported topology: TP=1, PP=1, single node, no DP attention, disaggregation, elastic scaling, or Ray, and explicit `--max-total-tokens`. - Launch same-GPU replicas sequentially to reduce startup memory contention. - Keep one public SGLang endpoint; the native DP controller routes requests across private scheduler/model replicas. - Log whether the NVIDIA MPS control utility is available when same-GPU replicas run on CUDA. - Add unit coverage for flag resolution, the legacy alias, conflicts, and topology validation. - Tested using custom `bench_same_gpu_mps.py` for endpoint throughput and latency benchmarking. ## Accuracy tests N/A. This change modifies replica placement and request routing; it does not change model-forward or kernel numerics. ## Speed tests and profiling Hardware: RTX 4070 Ti 12 GB Model: `Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B` Workload: 100 requests, concurrency 6, four warmup requests, and 128 output tokens per request. CUDA MPS was unavailable in this WSL environment, so these results compare normal CUDA scheduling with one versus two same-GPU replicas. | Configuration | Completion throughput | p50 latency | p90 latency | p99 latency | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:| | 1 replica | 279.7 tok/s | 2.093 s | 3.949 s | 4.157 s | | 2 same-GPU replicas | 538.9 tok/s | 1.176 s | 1.228 s | 4.930 s | Two same-GPU replicas improved aggregate completion throughput by **92.7%** and reduced p50 latency by **43.8%**. The p99 result should be validated with repeated runs. ### CUDA MPS validation CUDA MPS is optional and must be started outside SGLang. ```bash export CUDA_MPS_PIPE_DIRECTORY=/tmp/sglang-mps-pipe export CUDA_MPS_LOG_DIRECTORY=/tmp/sglang-mps-log mkdir -p "$CUDA_MPS_PIPE_DIRECTORY" "$CUDA_MPS_LOG_DIRECTORY" nvidia-cuda-mps-control -d ``` Launch SGLang with two same-GPU replicas: ```bash python -m sglang.launch_server \ --model-path Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B \ --same-gpu-replicas 2 \ --mem-fraction-static 0.35 \ --max-total-tokens 1024 \ --max-running-requests 4 \ --disable-cuda-graph ``` Verify that both scheduler processes attached to the MPS server: ```bash MPS_SERVER_PID=$( printf 'get_server_list\n' | nvidia-cuda-mps-control | awk 'NF {print $1; exit}' ) printf 'get_client_list %s\n' "$MPS_SERVER_PID" | nvidia-cuda-mps-control ps -eo pid,ppid,args | grep '[s]glang::scheduler' ``` The two scheduler PIDs must appear in the MPS client list. ## Checklist - [x] Add unit tests. - [x] Add a manual benchmark utility. - [ ] Run NVIDIA CUDA MPS attachment and benchmark validation on native Linux. - [ ] Run formatting and full relevant CI. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32378164132](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32378164132)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32378164193](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32378164193)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32378164100](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32378164100)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [diffusion] read the cgroup this process is actually in
signals.text: ## Motivation `cgroup_memory_limit_bytes` reads `/sys/fs/cgroup/memory.max` (and the v1 equivalent) at fixed paths -- the mount root. For a process sitting directly in that cgroup, which is the ordinary container case, that is its limit. For a process held below it, it is not. A systemd scope with `MemoryMax`, a container started with `--cgroup-parent`, or anything nesting a tighter cgroup underneath all report the parent's much larger number. Pinned host memory is then planned against memory the process cannot have -- the exact over-commit this module exists to prevent -- and the failure lands as an OOM kill rather than as a graceful fallback to pageable memory. ## Modifications Resolve the process's own cgroup from `/proc/self/cgroup` and take the tightest cap in the chain up to the mount root. Finding that directory needs one wrinkle. The path `/proc` reports is relative to the host's cgroup root, while the mount seen inside a container is already the container's own cgroup, so the two do not concatenate. Measured in the container this was developed in: ``` /proc/self/cgroup 11:memory:/docker/8e1010720ccd5899a86b648e769a5b6d25505ab4195d3abc95ed9c1b489acf37 mount /sys/fs/cgroup/memory <- already that cgroup join /sys/fs/cgroup/memory/docker/8e10... <- names nothing ``` Trying progressively shorter suffixes finds the deepest directory that exists, which is the leaf whichever way the container was set up: the mount itself when nothing nests, `<mount>/h3` when `/proc` says `/docker/<id>/h3`. ## Accuracy Tests Which limit is read; no weights or numerics involved. Four new unit tests cover a tighter nested cap winning, a looser one losing to the root, a container path that resolves to nothing falling back to the mount, and a trailing suffix resolving under it. `test_host_memory_budget.py` and `test_layerwise_offload.py`: 72 passed. Verified against the same container the measurement above came from -- `/proc`'s path still resolves to the mount root, and the reported cap is unchanged: ``` host memory available: 730.5 GiB (cgroup cap 1117.2 GiB, in use 386.7 GiB) ``` ## Speed Tests and Profiling Not applicable -- this runs once at startup and reads a handful of small files. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #32373018109](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32373018109)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32373073558](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32373073558)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32373018075](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32373018075)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: perf: cut device syncs and redundant launches from decode scheduling
signals.text: On a PD-disaggregated decode node there is a ~4ms GPU bubble between two forwards. nsys shows the scheduler thread blocked in cudaStreamSynchronize, 8-12ms each. All of those syncs sit on schedule_stream, and _apply_war_barrier fences that stream behind the in-flight forward, so anything that needs a value back on the host waits out a whole forward; the remaining host work (MLP-sync all_gather plus launch prep) then lands in the window before the next forward. Each sync point is removed in turn: 1. Preallocation (DecodePreallocQueue.pop_preallocated) - torch.tensor([...], device=...) becomes a pinned staging buffer plus a non_blocking copy. A pageable H2D goes through memcpy_and_sync in aten, i.e. cudaMemcpyAsync + cudaStreamSynchronize; the pinned copy is still ordered before the allocator kernel that reads it, so semantics are unchanged. Shared helper: pinned_int64_pair() in allocator/base.py. - Same three blocking H2D in SWATokenToKVPoolAllocator.alloc_extend_swa_tail (swa_seq_lens / swa_last_loc / mapping[...] = 0); the last one now writes a cached device scalar. - The page/state indices sent to the prefill node were read back with .cpu() at admission time. They are now registered as device tensors and read back by flush_pending_metadata() after the next forward has been launched, on a separate stream (gated on an event, pinned async D2H, record_stream). The writes stay on schedule_stream so WAR ordering is unchanged. 2. KV release on request completion free() dedups page ids with torch.unique, and free_swa() additionally reads the mapping back (unique plus a > 0 mask) to discover which pages carry SWA state. Both shapes are data-dependent, hence the sync. The caller can name the range instead: - PagedTokenToKVPoolAllocator.free_page_reps(): release by one representative token per page. - SWATokenToKVPoolAllocator.free_full_segment() / free_swa_segment() / free_swa_page_reps(): the mapping preserves a token's offset within its page (both pools advance on the same seq_lens), so one token every page_size positions from a page-aligned start hits each SWA page exactly once. - SWAChunkCache.cache_finished_req releases the two pools separately: the full pool from cache_protected_len, the SWA pool only from swa_evicted_seqlen, since window eviction already released what came before. _release_overallocated_kv_indices and the window eviction in free_swa_out_of_window_slots go through the same segment API. Composite allocators keep falling back to free(): radix cache nodes are not guaranteed to still be SWA-mapped, so the positional derivation does not hold for them. The aliased-pool allocator (PureSWATokenToKVPoolAllocator, where full_attn_allocator IS swa_attn_allocator) also falls back, otherwise the split release would free the same slots twice. 3. Batched window eviction (maybe_evict_swa) Calling the release per request put O(batch_size) calls on the scheduler thread right before the launch, ~90us each. The whole batch's out-of-window ranges are now gathered in one indexed read. That single call is then made sync-free by gathering one token per page (step=page_size) and releasing through free_swa_page_reps(), so eviction costs one op and no sync. 4. NVTX NVTX ranges for the scheduler's hot regions, and real NVTX step spans for ModelRunner.forward and the multi-layer draft-extend replay path (previously only torch record_function, invisible in nsys). 5. C128 state reset on admission (clear_c128_req_state) With the syncs gone, this region was still bimodal: 0.05ms without an admission, 5-8ms with one. The cost had become launch count -- one fill_ plus one zero_ per C128 pool, ~40 launches per admitted request, and a kernel launch on this ARM host is ~17us. The written constants are fixed, so the first call bakes a template and every later call issues a single _foreach_copy_ over contiguous slices: 40 kernels collapse to 1. The template is built with the same ops as the old path, so the bytes written are bitwise identical even where -inf saturates in the pool dtype. Both C128 layouts are covered; mismatched pool shape/dtype/ring_size falls back to the per-pool loop. Measured on a 4-rank decode node (per-rank per-iteration means): - cudaStreamSynchronize in pop_preallocated: 263 calls / 2518ms -> 0 - prebuilt batch assembly: 1.16 -> 0.22 ms/iter, p90 6.68 -> 1.64ms - get_next_batch_to_run: 10.74 -> 8.31 ms/iter - iteration rate: 35.1 -> 39.3 iter/s per rank (+13%) - clear_c128_req_state microbenchmark: 40 -> 1 kernels, 0.721 -> 0.078 ms - batched sync-free eviction removed 901 syncs / 2761ms per 14.2s window, 85% of the time spent in the eviction region Page conservation for the positional release was validated with SGLANG_DEBUG_MEMORY_POOL=1 over ~10k decode steps (its assertions are host-visible syncs, so that flag must not be mixed into a perf run), plus equivalence tests against the unique-based path for the strided gather and for free_swa_page_reps. The batched out-of-window free in maybe_evict_swa originates from an internal patch by a teammate; a Co-authored-by trailer will be added before merge. <!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. signals.title: [Runtime] Don't override CUDA_MODULE_LOADING
signals.text: ## Motivation `_set_envs_and_config()` currently assigns `CUDA_MODULE_LOADING=AUTO` before spawning scheduler processes. This silently replaces an explicit `DEFAULT`, `EAGER`, or `LAZY` deployment choice, even though SGLang has no corresponding CLI option that would justify overriding this CUDA control plane. This matters when a deployment intentionally uses eager loading to move first-use module initialization out of the request path, accepting additional startup time and memory for more predictable request latency. Today that setting is lost before the model-loading scheduler processes are spawned. ## NVIDIA CUDA contract The NVIDIA CUDA Programming Guide documents [`CUDA_MODULE_LOADING`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cuda-programming-guide/05-appendices/environment-variables.html#cuda-module-loading) with these possible values: > `DEFAULT`: Default behavior, equivalent to `LAZY`. > `LAZY`: The loading of specific kernels is delayed until a CUDA function handle ... is extracted. > `EAGER`: Fully loads CUDA modules and kernels at program initialization. `AUTO` is not a documented value. NVIDIA's [Lazy Loading guide](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cuda-programming-guide/04-special-topics/lazy-loading.html) also states: > As of CUDA 12.3 lazy loading is enabled by default on all platforms, but can be controlled via the `CUDA_MODULE_LOADING` environment variable. and: > Lazy loading can be disabled by setting the `CUDA_MODULE_LOADING` environment variable to `EAGER`. ## Change Stop assigning `CUDA_MODULE_LOADING` in `_set_envs_and_config()`. - Explicit CUDA values now reach spawned scheduler processes unchanged. - When the variable is absent, supported CUDA versions retain their native default lazy-loading behavior. - This PR does not add an SGLang CLI flag or change `CUDA_DEVICE_MAX_CONNECTIONS`. ## Validation - `pre-commit run --files python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/engine.py` - `git diff --check` <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32383857645](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32383857645)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32383857195](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32383857195)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32383857473](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32383857473)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: Add NIXL as a backend for weight transfer
signals.text: Adds NIXL as a passive weight-transfer target backend alongside the existing Mooncake path, so an external training engine (Miles) can RDMA-write updated weights directly into SGLang's GPU memory. The transfer-engine metadata that SGLang publishes is extended to support both backends. Using NIXL yields a 1.5x-5x reduction in weight refit time, depending on model and configuration. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32377150149](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32377150149)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32377150174](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32377150174)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:heavy_minus_sign: **No AMD PR run found for this commit**.<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: feat(grpc): expose KV event discovery metadata
signals.text: ## Motivation Dynamo's native SGLang sidecar needs a validated description of SGLang's ZMQ KV-event publisher to subscribe each registered data-parallel rank for event-driven KV routing. SGLang already exposes this structured `kv_events` descriptor through HTTP `/server_info`, but native gRPC `GetServerInfo` currently returns only the raw `ServerArgs` fields. Consumers would otherwise need to duplicate SGLang's endpoint validation and DCP-aware block-size calculation. ## Modifications - Add the existing `ServerArgs.describe_kv_events_publisher()` result to native gRPC `GetServerInfo.json_info` under `kv_events`. - Preserve all existing flat server-information fields. - Keep the protobuf contract unchanged; this is an additive field inside the existing JSON payload. - Keep the high-volume KV-event stream on SGLang's existing ZMQ publisher rather than proxying it through request/response gRPC. ## Accuracy Tests Not applicable. This change does not affect model execution or generated outputs. Validation: - `python3 test/registered/unit/entrypoints/test_grpc_bridge.py` — 3 passed. - `python3 scripts/lint/check_registered_tests.py` — passed. - Two-H100 using this source branch and the Dynamo consumer PR: - Two native gRPC sidecars discovered independent SGLang KV-event publishers. - Dynamo connected both event streams and initialized event-driven KV routing. - An initial 242-token request reported `overlap_blocks=0`. - The identical repeated request selected the same worker with `overlap_blocks=15`. - Both requests completed successfully. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Not applicable. The descriptor is computed only when `GetServerInfo` is called and is not on the inference path. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). signals.title: fix: manually register kv_b_proj to attn_mha so mla models can round-…
signals.text: ## Motivation address #35702. MLA models now cannot be saved then loaded with `ShardedModelLoader`. The error we get is : ``` File "python/sglang/srt/model_loader/loader.py", line 1796, in load_model param_data = state_dict[key].data ~~~~~~~~~~^^^^^ KeyError: 'model.layers.22.self_attn.attn_mha.kv_b_proj.weight' ``` and the reason is: 1. `DeepseekV2AttentionMLA.__init__` sets `self.attn_mha.kv_b_proj = None` and `forward_prepare` fills it in on first use. Assigning an `nn.Module` goes through `nn.Module.__setattr__`, which **registers `kv_b_proj` as a submodule of `attn_mha`** — so after one forward the same weight appears in `model.state_dict()` under two names sharing one storage. 2. `ShardedStateLoader.save_model` dumps `_filter_subtensors(model.state_dict())`, which dedups tensors sharing storage and keeps the lexicographically smaller key. `...attn_mha.kv_b_proj.weight` sorts before `...kv_b_proj.weight`, so the canonical name is dropped from the checkpoint. 3. On load, `load_model` iterates the checkpoint's keys and indexes a **fresh** model's state dict, which has never forwarded and therefore has no `attn_mha.kv_b_proj` — `KeyError`. ## Modifications We mannually register `kv_b_proj` as attribute of `self.attn_mha` without making it a module. This means, it will not be present in `model.state_dict()` and will not cause the eviction of our beloved `self.kv_b_proj`. ## Accuracy Tests Using DeepSeek-V2-Lite on GH200 node. ``` python3 -m sglang.launch_server --model-path '${model}' \ --trust-remote-code --attention-backend triton \ --host 127.0.0.1 --port ${PORT} python3 -m sglang.test.run_eval --host 127.0.0.1 --port ${PORT} \ --eval-name gsm8k --api completion --num-examples 200 ``` results: ``` Total latency: 21.807 s Score: 0.320 Output throughput: 1987.862 token/s [METRIC] gsm8k_score=0.32 labels={"model": "/iopsstor/scratch/cscs/yboughizane/.cache/huggingface/hub/models--deepseek-ai--DeepSeek-V2-Lite/snapshots/604d5664dddd88a0433dbae533b7fe9472482de0", "eval": "gsm8k"} [METRIC] gsm8k_latency=21.806841063982574 labels={"model": "/iopsstor/scratch/cscs/yboughizane/.cache/huggingface/hub/models--deepseek-ai--DeepSeek-V2-Lite/snapshots/604d5664dddd88a0433dbae533b7fe9472482de0", "eval": "gsm8k"} ``` ## Speed Tests and Profiling Not applicable, this PR does not involve performance-related changes. ## Validation The repro script from #35702 does not fail anymore. ## Checklist - signals.author: Todobe

signals.title: [Scheduler][PD][Perf] Add deficit-aware minimum-transfer victim selection for decode retraction
signals.text: ## Summary This PR adds an opt-in `backup-cost` decode retraction policy that uses deficit-aware minimum-transfer victim selection. It computes the current KV/token shortfall and chooses a low transfer-cost victim set estimated to be sufficient to fill that deficit, while preserving priority-tier boundaries and deterministic ordering. The existing `length` policy remains the default. The optimization target is the PD decode retraction critical path: reducing synchronous backup/restore bytes and scheduler stall. It does not claim improved general end-to-end throughput or a benefit for every workload. ## Rebase and validation - The reported performance evidence uses the pre-rebase baseline `OLD_BASE=b03ac355e795b3a86b26b8732c47c0965fd71bbc`. - This branch was rebased onto the frozen `REBASE_BASE=04444ee352a6a1f5666bf422a09841650c46194a`. - The two audited upstream commits changed only the Inkling-Small NVFP4 deterministic test and diffusion benchmark/skill files. They did not touch decode retraction, token-deficit calculation, victim ordering, backup/restore, KV accounting, the four files in this patch, or the experiment configuration. - `git range-diff` reports the old and rebased patches as equivalent; their stable patch-id and full patch SHA-256 are identical. - Post-rebase validation: 44 focused/related CPU tests passed, including direct victim-selection and scheduler retraction-loop coverage; `git diff --check`, `py_compile`, isort check, Ruff `F401/F821/UP037`, Black check, registered-test lint, and a `backup-cost` CLI parsing smoke all passed. - Correctness: **PASS** for the recorded GPU A/B scope and the post-rebase targeted validation above. - **The full performance matrix was not rerun after the rebase.** The performance numbers below are pre-rebase measurements and are not presented as measurements from the rebased head. ## Recorded performance evidence - Model: `/mnt/si0260014qra/default/models/Qwen/Qwen3-8B` - Topology: Prefill TP2 on GPUs 0-1 + Decode TP2 on GPUs 2-3 - Hardware: 4x A100-80GB - Real retraction events: 22 | Metric | Change | | --- | ---: | | Backup bytes | -74.43% | | Restore bytes | -74.43% | | Retraction scheduler stall | -72.94% | | p99 ITL | -0.74% | | Throughput | -0.0061% (essentially unchanged) | The throughput result is effectively flat and is not claimed as a throughput improvement. The narrow claim is reduced data movement and stall during real PD decode retraction events for heterogeneous batches. ## Scope and safety The policy uses a page-aligned logical target-KV footprint as a transfer-cost proxy and still invokes the existing real memory check after every release, so an optimistic relief estimate causes additional victims to be released rather than bypassing the safety path. Shared-prefix physical byte accuracy and universal end-to-end performance gains are not claimed. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32379275794](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32379275794)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32379275146](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32379275146)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32379275435](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32379275435)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->
signals.author: chengcuiping

signals.title: Support mxfp8 KV cache in PD transfer
signals.text: ## Motivation MXFP8 KV refused PD disaggregation outright: `get_contiguous_buf_infos` raised `KV transfer / disaggregation is unsupported for MXFP8 KV cache (scale buffers are not exposed)`. This exposes them, so a hybrid attention + linear-attention model serves PD with `--kv-cache-dtype mxfp8`. The scales do not go on the KV lists. Four call sites derive geometry from their length -- `len(kv_data_ptrs) // layer_num` in `setup_state_kv_args`, `len(kv_item_lens) // 2` in the staging handler, the layer range in `prefill.py`, and per-token bytes in `common/conn.py` -- so appending buffers there would silently skew all of them. They ride the multi-component state channel instead, which already carries KV-adjacent buffers for `SWA_RING`, `C128_STATE` and `MINIMAX_INDEX_K`. Two components rather than one, because a SWA pool nests two MXFP8 pools and their scales need different index payloads: the full-attention scales follow the whole sequence, the sliding-window scales follow the window through `translate_loc_from_full_to_swa`. One component cannot carry both. `item_lens` splits on the layout: the interleaved buffer (the `page_size == 128` path) puts pages on the leading axis so one row is one page, while the flat buffer is per slot and a page spans `page_size` rows. Removing the refusal surfaced a second gap: this pool overrides `_create_buffers` wholesale, and the base class only builds `_kv_buffer_descs` at the end of the method it replaced, so the inherited accessor hit an `AttributeError`. The descriptors are now built there too. `set_kv_buffer_prefix_valid` still refuses -- its callers are the DSpark and DFlash speculative paths, which PD does not reach. A hybrid model also needs #35689, now on main: without it the empty mamba temporal buffer fails the batch registration before any of this runs. ## Accuracy Single-node PD, one prefill and one decode role, TP=2 each, mooncake over IB, hierarchical cache on the prefill role, `--kv-cache-dtype mxfp8`. `sgl-eval` aime26, thinking on, `max_tokens=131072`: ``` score = 0.9333 error_rate = 0.00% stop_rate = 0.9667 truncated_rate = 0.0333 total_completion_tokens = 822323 ``` One of the two misses is `finish_reason=length` with no answer extracted, so 28/29 of the samples that finished are correct -- level with the 0.9667 the same setup reads on bf16 KV, where nothing truncated. MXFP8 spends about 7% more completion tokens (822k against 768k), which is what pushes one problem into the cap. A prompt whose prefix is well past the sliding window answers correctly and repeatably. Pointing the window component at the whole-sequence payload instead degenerates it to empty or truncated completions, which is what confirms the window scales are read rather than incidentally correct. The flat layout has no hardware coverage here -- fa4 pins `page_size` to 128, so only the interleaved branch runs -- and is covered by the unit test. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #32437324281](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32437324281)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #32437324240](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32437324240)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #32437324245](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32437324245)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [AMD] Fix Qwen3.5 MTP dropping fused shared-expert weights
signals.text: ## Motivation Since #33889, Qwen3.5 MXFP4 with MTP speculative decoding on MI355X lost about 12% throughput. The cause is that the MTP draft model is loaded without its shared-expert weights. **What fusion does to the weight layout.** When a Qwen3.5 MoE layer fuses its shared expert, it deliberately does not build a separate `shared_expert` module — the shared expert becomes one more routed expert, living in slot `num_experts`. Any loader for such a layer therefore has to route `mlp.shared_expert.*` into that slot. `qwen3_5.py` does exactly that; `qwen3_5_mtp.py` never learned to. **Why the target model is unaffected.** In this checkpoint the target's routed experts are MXFP4 while its shared expert stays bf16. Fusing them would push a higher-precision tensor through the quantized routed-expert path, so `can_fuse_shared_expert()` refuses. The target therefore always takes the unfused path, keeps its `shared_expert` module, and loads normally — the gap in the MTP loader is invisible from here. **Why the draft model is affected, and only recently.** The MTP module is excluded from quantization in full: all 1536 `mtp.*` routed-expert tensors and its shared expert alike. The draft is thus uniformly bf16, nothing is mixed-precision, and fusing it is perfectly valid — the gate correctly says yes. It simply never had the chance before. Until #33889, the target's Quark config installed a single process-wide `disable_shared_experts_fusion` override, which switched fusion off for every runner, draft included. #33889 made that decision per-runner, so the draft started fusing for the first time and immediately ran into the loader gap. **Why nobody noticed.** With fusion on there is no `shared_expert` module to load into, and the expert mapping only covers slots `0 .. num_experts-1`, so each `mlp.shared_expert.{gate,up,down}_proj.weight` matches nothing and ends at `logger.warning_once("Parameter ... not found in params_dict, skip loading")` — three tensors per TP rank, one suppressed log line, no error. The draft then runs with an uninitialized shared expert. Since a speculative draft cannot corrupt verified output, accuracy is unaffected; the damage appears only as a fall in accept rate, from 0.65 to 0.51, and hence in throughput. This PR teaches the MTP loader to place those weights into the fused slot, so the draft that #33889 legitimately enabled actually receives them. ## Modifications `python/sglang/srt/models/qwen3_5_mtp.py`, mirroring `qwen3_5.py`: - Size the expert mapping as `num_experts + num_fused_shared_experts` so slot `num_experts` has an entry. The fusion count is read from the constructed modules, because `num_fused_shared_experts` is set on `Qwen3_5MoeForConditionalGeneration` and the MTP wraps a `Qwen3_5ForCausalLM`, which does not carry it. - Rewrite `mlp.shared_expert.` to `mlp.experts.{num_experts}.` before the mapping loops. Both are keyed on the model's actual fusion state rather than on a platform check. When nothing fuses, `num_fused_shared_experts` is `0`, the mapping size is unchanged and the rewrite never fires, so this is a no-op for every non-fusing configuration. Not covered: the fused-checkpoint variant (a single `experts.gate_up_proj` tensor). `qwen3_5.py` handles that with a dedicated branch that chunks the tensor into `w1`/`w3`; the MTP loader's `load_fused_expert_weights` indexes per expert id and cannot serve a single shared-expert tensor. Adding that path untested seemed worse than leaving it, since no checkpoint on hand exercises it. ## Accuracy Tests No accuracy change is expected: only the draft model changes, and a speculative draft cannot alter verified output. The visible effect is the accept rate. Measured over ~100 decode-batch samples per point. | conc | accept_len before | after | accept_rate before | after | |---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | 4 | 2.5278 | 2.9533 | 0.5097 | 0.6509 | | 8 | 2.5507 | 2.9374 | 0.5168 | 0.6457 | | 16 | 2.5144 | 2.9508 | 0.5054 | 0.6501 | Skipped weights during load go from 3 per TP rank to 0. ## Speed Tests and Profiling ### Summary at conc=4 | Config | Total Throughput | Median E2E (ms) | Median TTFT (ms) | Median TPOT (ms) | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:| | `eda0ddc260d4` (last good) | 5365.74 | 5992.71 | 326.84 | 6.25 | | `b61a06921e` (#33889) | 4716.15 | 6662.60 | 322.72 | 7.05 | | `b61a06921e` + PR #35719 | 5429.77 | 5912.64 | 326.93 | 6.11 | The third row was obtained by switching shared-expert fusion off on `b61a06921e`, which removes the unloaded-shared-expert condition from the draft; this PR removes the same condition by loading the fused weights instead of dropping them. ### Full sweep MI355X, `amd/Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-MXFP4`, TP=2, EAGLE MTP (3 steps / topk 1 / 4 draft tokens), page-size 16, `fp8_e4m3` KV, `--attention-backend aiter`, ISL=8192 / OSL=1024, `num_prompts = 10 x conc`, server relaunched per concurrency with `--max-running-requests = conc`. Server flags follow `benchmarks/single_node/fixed_seq_len/qwen3.5_fp4_mi355x_mtp.sh`. Before and after were run back to back on the same GPU pair, both at `7f8f030000`. | conc | Total Throughput before | after | Delta | Median E2E (ms) before | after | Median TTFT (ms) before | after | Median TPOT (ms) before | after | |---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | 4 | 4746.11 | 5417.31 | **+14.14%** | 6726.7 | 5969.1 | 333.3 | 336.7 | 7.07 | 6.22 | | 8 | 6835.64 | 7626.54 | **+11.57%** | 9243.7 | 8370.3 | 336.4 | 335.9 | 9.67 | 8.82 | | 16 | 9011.82 | 10141.08 | **+12.53%** | 13997.8 | 12840.5 | 346.1 | 361.6 | 14.86 | 13.48 | The gain is decode-side, as expected from an accept-rate change: TTFT is flat, TPOT improves by 9–12%. This restores the configuration to its previously published InferenceX level. The last sweep on image `lmsysorg/sglang-rocm:v0.5.16-rocm720-mi35x-20260730` recorded 582.84 / 852.30 / 1130.14 output tok/s at conc 4 / 8 / 16; with this patch the same setup measures 602.47 / 857.12 / 1123.38. Bisecting `accept len` over the 759 commits between that image's sglang and `63d783bbe0` lands on #33889, with a clean split (2.84–2.92 before, 2.50–2.57 after, no intermediate values). ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:no_entry_sign: [Run #32389114863](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32389114863)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32389114508](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32389114508)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32389114842](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32389114842)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [Bugfix] Accept Anthropic x-api-key authentication
signals.text: ## Motivation SGLang exposes an Anthropic-compatible `/v1/messages` endpoint, but servers launched with `--api-key` only authenticate `Authorization: Bearer` credentials. The Anthropic SDK sends its API key in the `x-api-key` header, so otherwise valid SDK requests are rejected with HTTP 401. This is not a duplicate of an existing open PR. I searched the SGLang PRs and issues for `x-api-key`, Anthropic SDK authentication, and API-key middleware changes; the related open work concerns worker/router authentication rather than inbound Anthropic client authentication. ## Modifications - Accept `x-api-key` as an alternative transport for the configured API key. - Keep constant-time token comparison and the existing auth-level rules. - Preserve Bearer authentication and allow either header to satisfy the expected token. - Add unit coverage for valid and invalid Anthropic keys, malformed Bearer fallback, and admin-key isolation. - Document `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` for Claude Code deployments protected by `--api-key`. ## Test Results ```text ruff check python/sglang/srt/utils/auth.py test/registered/unit/utils/test_auth.py All checks passed! ruff format --check python/sglang/srt/utils/auth.py test/registered/unit/utils/test_auth.py 2 files already formatted python3 -m py_compile python/sglang/srt/utils/auth.py passed git diff origin/main..HEAD --check passed ``` I also loaded `auth.py` directly and exercised valid `x-api-key`, invalid `x-api-key`, and existing Bearer authentication paths successfully. The registered SGLang unit-test module could not be collected on this macOS machine because importing the package requires `triton`, which is unavailable here. CI should run the added cases in `base-a-test-cpu`. ## Accuracy Tests Not applicable. This changes HTTP authentication only and does not affect model outputs. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Not applicable. Authentication still performs constant-time comparisons over the same configured token; the additional header check is negligible. ## Checklist - [x] Format code according to the project style. - [x] Add unit tests. - [x] Update documentation. - [x] Accuracy and speed benchmarks are not applicable. - [x] Follow the SGLang code style guidance. AI assistance was used to analyze the compatibility gap, prepare the patch, and draft this PR. I reviewed the changed lines and test results. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32381998319](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32381998319)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32381998067](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32381998067)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32381998359](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32381998359)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [BugFix][DP] Prevent health checks from perturbing user request routing
signals.text: ## Motivation Generation health checks (`HEALTH_CHECK_*`) are intentionally skipped by the scheduler while normal inference is already making progress. Under DP serving, however, the request passes through `DataParallelController` before that scheduler-side skip. With `round_robin`, a generation health request currently advances the same dispatch state used by user requests. For load-aware methods, it can also participate in the user load-budget refresh/update path. This means a health request that is later discarded can still perturb user-request ownership across DP ranks. In a long-prefill DP-Attention workload, this produced a reproducible scheduling failure chain: ```text generation health request -> user LB state is mutated -> per-rank user ownership becomes uneven -> some DP ranks become idle while peers continue prefill -> PrefillDelayer sees persistent mixed states / timeout -> effective concurrency and throughput drop ``` The root-cause investigation is tracked in #35241. ## Modifications This PR isolates generation-health dispatch state from user load-balancing state in `DataParallelController`: - Detect generation health requests before normal user LB dispatch. - Use an independent round-robin counter for health requests. - Do not refresh or mutate the user `DPBudget` for health-only dispatches. - For batch generate, refresh the user load budget only when the batch contains a user request. - Preserve explicit `routed_dp_rank` behavior. - Preserve `FOLLOW_BOOTSTRAP_ROOM` semantics for PD/disaggregated serving, since that path uses request-specific routing rather than shared mutable user LB state. This PR does **not** change DP Attention, PrefillDelayer, scheduler busy-health skip behavior, or the health endpoint semantics. ## Regression Tests Added CPU unit coverage for: - independent user-RR and health-RR state; - health dispatch using only active workers; - explicit `routed_dp_rank` not advancing health RR state; - health dispatch bypassing user load-budget refresh; - health-only batch dispatch not refreshing user load state; - `FOLLOW_BOOTSTRAP_ROOM` health routing compatibility. ```text python3 -m pytest test/registered/unit/managers/test_data_parallel_controller.py -q 23 passed git diff --check clean pre-commit run --files \ python/sglang/srt/managers/data_parallel_controller.py \ test/registered/unit/managers/test_data_parallel_controller.py all passed ``` ## Runtime Validation Validated on 8x NVIDIA B300 with DeepSeek-V4-Pro, TP8/DP8, DP Attention, MegaMoE, PrefillDelayer, round-robin routing, 8k effective prefill chunk, C16/N160, 60k input / 1 output. The external watchdog continued issuing generation health checks during the patched runs. | Configuration | Input TPS | avg running | HEALTH at DPC | IDLE-while-EXTEND | Delayer timeout | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | Original + generation health ON (observed HIT) | 76,417 | 6.84 | 59 | 33 | 9 | | Original + generation health OFF | 94,720-94,974 | 8.55-8.76 | 0 | 0 | 0 | | Patched + generation health ON, 4/4 runs | 94,372-94,822 | 8.60-8.69 | 49-51 | 0 | 0 | All patched runs completed 160/160 requests with no fatal errors. Generation-health traffic remained present at DPC, while the user-ownership hole and associated concurrency collapse disappeared. This is a scoped validation for the tested failure family; it is not intended to claim that generation health is the cause of every low-throughput state. ## Scope The intended invariant is: > Generation health traffic must not mutate the load-balancing state used by user requests when it is routed through DP serving. This PR does not make round-robin load-aware and does not change the configured load-balancing policy. Related: #35241 <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32386249966](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32386249966)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32386249757](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32386249757)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32386249986](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32386249986)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [Fix][GDN] Route DFlash/DSpark commits through ReplaySSM spec fold
signals.text: ## Motivation ReplaySSM speculative-state folding already supports GDN when speculative decoding commits through `commit_mamba_states_after_verify()`. DFlash and DSpark use a different path and call `HybridLinearAttnBackend.update_mamba_state_after_mtp_verify()` directly after target verification. Before this change, the direct commit path recognized ReplaySSM only for KDA. A GDN target therefore fell back to the regular intermediate-state scatter path, even though `--enable-linear-replayssm-spec` intentionally removes `intermediate_ssm`. The KV-cache configurator prevented this invalid path by rejecting every non-KDA DFlash/DSpark target. This PR routes the built-in GDN backend through the existing ReplaySSM fold implementation from #28695. It does not change the ReplaySSM kernels, model outputs, public flags, or the generic speculative-decoding commit path. ## Modifications - Resolve the direct ReplaySSM verify-commit handler when `HybridLinearAttnBackend` is initialized. - Select the KDA handler only when speculative folding is enabled, and select the GDN handler only for a concrete `GDNAttnBackend`. - Keep the existing intermediate-state scatter fallback for every other backend and for ReplaySSM-disabled execution. - Replace the pool-local KDA-only rejection with validation scoped to DFlash/DSpark target workers before memory-pool sizing. - Fail fast for unsupported direct-verify configurations: non-GDN/KDA targets, non-CUDA/ROCm devices, unified memory, and non-static ragged verification for GDN. KDA compact-ragged verification remains supported. - Add a focused CPU regression test for GDN/KDA handler selection, constructor wiring, direct commit dispatch, and configuration guards. ## Accuracy Tests The following focused and neighboring regression tests pass: | Test | Result | |---|---:| | New GDN direct-commit regression test | 3/3 passed | | GDN ReplaySSM speculative fold parity | 4/4 passed | | GDN/KDA ReplaySSM packed-decode parity | 6/6 passed | | GDN attention backend regression suite | 9/9 passed | | Mamba2 attention backend regression suite | 9/9 passed | | Hybrid FlashInfer metadata regression suite | 2/2 passed | | NGRAM/Mamba verify-update regression suite | 14/14 passed | | ReplaySSM ring accounting | 3/3 passed | The GPU tests were run on a single NVIDIA H20. The clean end-to-end A/B test used Qwen3.8-27B as the target, Qwen3.8-27B-DFlash2 as the draft model, DFlash with one speculative step and eight draft tokens, TP=1, Triton attention backends, CUDA graphs disabled, five-shot GSM8K with 200 questions, parallelism 4, temperature 0, and top-p 1. The only server-side difference was `--enable-linear-replayssm-spec`. | Configuration | Accuracy | Invalid outputs | Exact output match | |---|---:|---:|---:| | Baseline | 194/200 (97.0%) | 0 | Reference | | ReplaySSM | 194/200 (97.0%) | 0 | 200/200 | ## Speed Tests and Profiling N/A. This PR fixes routing to the existing ReplaySSM implementation and does not change its kernels. The GSM8K run above is reported only as an accuracy test; its single-run wall-clock timing is intentionally not used as a performance claim. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). signals.title: [NPU][Bugfix] Fix OOB gather in decode KV allocation when free pool is tight
signals.text: ## Motivation NPUPagedTokenToKVPoolAllocator.alloc_decode crashes with an out-of-bounds gather when the free-page pool is exactly tight (len(self.free_pages) == num_new_pages). start_new_pages = torch.cumsum(need_new_pages, 0) - need_new_pages is a prefix index into self.free_pages. For rows that do not need a new page (need_new_pages == 0), start_new_pages == end_new_pages; for the last row this equals num_new_pages. The subsequent self.free_pages[start_new_pages] then indexes past the end (valid range is [0, len(free_pages) - 1] == [0, num_new_pages - 1]). When the pool has slack, the index still lands in-bounds, so the bug is latent; it only fires under exact exhaustion. Observed in CI (test_npu_schedule_conservativeness.py, gsm8k) — the NPU index-check kernel aborts with exactly this condition, then the server traps and dies: ``` Index out of range in dimension 0: index value 1 exceeds bounds 1! [AIV Block ...] [ASSERT] .../index_check/index_check.h:130: ... Assertion `(idx < bound)' failed. ... EZ9999 ... exception of aivec error ... "AI Core Error" ... http.client.RemoteDisconnected: Remote end closed connection without response ... ConnectionRefusedError: [Errno 111] Connection refused Ran 1 test in 251.536s FAILED (errors=1) ``` ## Modifications - In alloc_decode, clamp the gather index: start_new_pages = start_new_pages.clamp(max=num_new_pages - 1). - The clamp is safe: the clamped rows all satisfy need_new_pages == 0, and out_indices weights them by need_new_pages (via (1 - need_new_pages) and * need_new_pages), so their gathered value is masked out and never used. - The num_new_pages == 0 path returns early, so num_new_pages - 1 >= 0 holds whenever the clamp line executes (no max=-1 degeneracy). ## Accuracy Tests Verified on an Ascend NPU machine. The previously failing test_npu_schedule_conservativeness.py now passes — 2 runs, both OK: - run 1: - run 2: No Index out of range assertion and no EZ9999 ... AI Core Error trap remain. ## Speed Tests and Profiling N/A: adds one element-wise clamp per decode batch (O(batch size)), negligible versus the free_pages gather. ## Checklist - [ ] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [ ] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. signals.title: [codex] Fix persistent kernel shared memory fallback
signals.text: ## Summary - Retry deterministic persistent matmul and BMM with `num_stages=2` only when Triton reports a shared-memory `OutOfResources` error. - Cache a successful fallback by operator, normalized device, dtype, and the complete original kernel config, while logging one warning per cache key. - Add CPU tests for the exception and cache contract plus CUDA tests that exercise both real persistent kernel launch sites. ## Root cause The fixed float16 persistent-kernel config uses `num_stages=3`. On affected SM89 deployments, Triton can compile that launch to require 106496 bytes of shared memory, exceeding the 101376-byte per-block limit. Because the footprint depends on the architecture, compiler, and specialization, a static architecture gate can either miss affected builds or unnecessarily reduce stages on builds where stage 3 fits. This change preserves the existing stage-3 fast path. It retries only the exact shared-memory resource failure, caches only after a successful stage-2 launch, and leaves non-shared-memory failures untouched. Shapes and batch size are intentionally excluded from the cache key so one process does not switch launch configuration based on request batching. This addresses #29149 and is a runtime alternative to the static config selection proposed in #34486. ## Validation - `python -m unittest discover -s test/registered/unit/batch_invariant_ops -p "test_persistent_kernel_fallback*.py" -v` (`7` passed) - `python test/registered/unit/batch_invariant_ops/test_batch_invariant_ops.py -v` (`6` passed) - RTX 4090D CUDA tests verified `num_stages=3 -> 2 -> 2` for both matmul and BMM, with exact single-token versus multi-token outputs. - An offline Qwen3-0.6B deterministic-inference server run naturally reproduced `106496 > 101376`, emitted one matmul fallback warning, completed all generation requests with HTTP 200, and produced identical text and token logprobs for repeated and mixed-batch requests. - `py_compile`, `git diff --check`, and trailing-whitespace checks passed. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32393952417](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32393952417)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32393952014](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32393952014)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32393952340](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32393952340)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [Bugfix] Fix TVM FFI tuple access in CUDA IPC JIT
signals.text: ## Motivation The CUDA IPC JIT module can fail to compile with NVCC 12.8 and `apache-tvm-ffi==0.1.11`: ```text error: no matching function for call to 'get(const tvm::ffi::Tuple<...>&)' note: couldn't deduce template parameter 'I' ``` `get<I>(pair)` relies on unqualified lookup and ADL. In this toolchain combination, NVCC finds the TVM FFI overloads but does not resolve the explicit tuple index. The exception is caught during custom all-reduce setup, so the server continues after falling back to NCCL. ## Modifications Use the existing `tvm::ffi::Tuple::get<I>()` member accessor for the CUDA IPC handle and offset. This bypasses the problematic free-function lookup without changing the tuple values or custom all-reduce behavior. ## Accuracy Tests Not applicable. This only changes how two fields are accessed during CUDA IPC manager initialization; it does not change model outputs or kernel arithmetic. Focused regression validation with Python 3.12.13, PyTorch `2.13.0+cu129`, NVCC 12.8, and `apache-tvm-ffi==0.1.11`: ```python from sglang.kernels.ops.communication.all_reduce import IPCManager manager = IPCManager() manager.destroy() print("jit_ipc_ok") ``` The test used an empty `SGLANG_JIT_CACHE_DIR`, compiled the `cuda_ipc` module, instantiated `IPCManager`, and printed `jit_ipc_ok`. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Not applicable. This is a JIT compiler compatibility fix and does not modify the generated custom all-reduce kernel. ## Checklist - [x] Format the code according to the project style; `git diff --check` passes. - [x] Exercise the affected JIT compilation and registration path with an empty cache. - [x] Documentation is unchanged because there is no user-facing API change. - [x] Accuracy and speed benchmarks are not applicable to this lookup-only change. - [x] Follow the SGLang code style guidance. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32394345576](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32394345576)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32394345229](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32394345229)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32394345470](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32394345470)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->
