signals.title: [diffusion] park a layerwise component's non-layer weights between uses
signals.text: ## Motivation Layerwise offload streams a component's blocks and releases them when its use ends. Everything else the component owns — embeddings, projections, norms, heads — stays on the device for the whole request. That is right while it is the component being used, and pure cost afterwards. On a small card the stage that follows is the one that needs the room. MiniMax-H3 at 864x480 / 124 frames / 20 steps, one RTX 4090, host memory capped at 32 GiB. The VAE decode is half the request, because `decode_temporal` re-runs the whole decoder per temporal chunk — so under layerwise offload the VAE's 36 blocks are re-streamed every chunk: ``` [MiniMaxH3TextEncodingStage] finished in 0.50 s [MiniMaxH3DenoisingStage] finished in 141.20 s [MiniMaxH3DecodingStage] finished in 140.60 s <- as much as 20 denoise steps ``` Holding those blocks resident (`--layerwise-resident-layers video_vae=36`, #35688) is what makes the decode cheap — 23 s instead of 150 — and it needs 9 GB. With a hard 12 GiB allocator cap the decode then dies for want of 20 MiB: ``` CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 20.00 MiB. 12.00 GiB allowed; Of the allocated memory 11.86 GiB is allocated by PyTorch ``` Of that 11.86 GiB, the DiT is still holding 2.09 GB and the text encoder 1.40 GB that the decode never touches. `PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True` does not close the gap. ## Modifications `park_non_layer_weights()` moves the parameters no manager streams to the host and leaves a `(1,)` placeholder behind; `restore_non_layer_weights()` brings them back. `LayerwiseOffloadStrategy` calls them from `finish_use` and `prepare_for_use`, so a component gives up that memory exactly while it is not the one being used. Scope is deliberately narrow: - **Parameters only.** Buffers stay resident because layerwise offload keeps them on purpose — a shared RoPE cache is referenced by many layers. - **One host copy, made once.** Steady state is one transfer each way per use: about 0.35 s for H3's 3.5 GB, against the 130 s the resident VAE saves. - **Follows `--performance-mode memory`**, which already trades latency for footprint. Nothing changes under the other modes. - **MPS untouched.** It has its own subphase-scoped mechanism. ## Accuracy Tests Which device holds a weight; the weights themselves are unchanged. Three unit tests cover the mode gate, that streamed layer weights are never parked and buffers stay resident, and that parking is a no-op outside memory mode. `test_layerwise_offload.py` (with the checkpoint-mapping branch applied, since that is the configuration measured): 117 passed. ## Speed Tests and Profiling H3 `fl2va`, 864x480 / 124 frames / 20 steps, seed 1101, single RTX 4090, host memory capped at 32 GiB. The 12 GiB VRAM budget is **enforced** with `torch.cuda.set_per_process_memory_fraction`, not inferred from `nvidia-smi` — which reports the caching allocator's reserved pool and so overstates it. | configuration | denoise | decode | end to end | 12 GiB cap | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | default | 141 s | 150 s | 303 s | fits, but decode dominates | | `video_vae=36` | 158 s | 23 s | 192 s | OOM in decode | | `video_vae=36` + this change | 159 s | **13 s** | **177 s** | **fits** | Host memory is unchanged at 24.5 GiB. Denoise varies 141–159 s with load on this shared box; decode is the term this change is about and it is stable. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #32395791332](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32395791332)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32395814506](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32395814506)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32395791126](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32395791126)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->
signals.author: mickqian

signals.title: [kernel] Split the custom all-reduce communicator into push/pull planes
signals.text: > Generated by Claude. ## Motivation Every JIT collective in `csrc/distributed` and `csrc/kimi_k3/comm` took one flat `CommunicatorObj` that carried every buffer any of them might want: `2 * world_size` push slots, a pull workspace, per-block semaphores, a rank-local counter, and one of the three multicast addresses. Consequences: - The other two multicast addresses travelled out of band. `ws_mc_base` was an `int64_t` argument repeated at five call sites, always the same constant; `pull_sem_mc_ptr` went through a per-world-size Python dict populated by `register_comm()`, duplicated in three modules. - A push-only owner (the fused qk-norm instances in `minimax_m2`) had to allocate a placeholder 1 KB pull buffer plus one semaphore purely to satisfy the constructor. - Only `custom_all_reduce.cuh` ever read `pull_workspaces` / `pull_bytes` / `pull_mc_workspace`. The K3 pull kernels reduce in place on the caller's own symmetric input and borrow the plane just to barrier on, so half the object was dead weight for most callers. - `custom_all_reduce.cuh` defined helpers at `namespace sglang` scope and was `#include`d by three K3 files across directories, so renaming anything inside it silently broke downstream kernels. ## What changed Split the object by lifetime rather than by direction: | | contents | |---|---| | `sgl.distributed.PushPlane` | zero-filled symmetric push slots, rank-local phase counter, multicast base | | `sgl.distributed.PullPlane` | symmetric pull buffers + per-block semaphores, both multicast bases. Either half may be a 0-element tensor | | `sgl.distributed.Communicator` | the two planes (either optional) + the pull launch widths; what every kernel takes | Both *fixed* multicast addresses now live on the planes. That deletes the `ws_mc_base` parameter from five entry points and the `_PULL_SEM_MC_MAP` registry from three modules. The *per-call* multicast address — a slice of the caller's own symmetric buffer, so it changes every call — stays a plain `intptr_t`, which is what it should be. `PullPlane`'s optional halves replace the placeholder-buffer trick: `minimax_m2` now constructs `Communicator(push=..., pull=None)` and a kernel that needs a missing plane fails with a message instead of reading a dummy buffer. ### Shared vocabulary moved under `include/` - **`include/sgl_kernel/distributed/ptx.cuh`** collects the inline PTX the collectives share into `sglang::device::ptx`, which `mbarrier.cuh` and the two K3 files reopen. Removed: three identical copies of the multimem flag increment, three copies of the "multicast alias of a semaphore's flag" helper (now `Semaphore::mc_flag`), and the 16B access helpers that were defined at `namespace sglang` scope inside `custom_all_reduce.cuh`. `csrc/kimi_k3/comm/ptx_sys.cuh` is deleted. The five communication kernels now contain zero inline PTX. - **`Barrier` / `McBarrier`** (unicast fan-out and one-`multimem.red` variants of the same window protocol) and **`LamportTrait`** (the pos-zero marker) live next to the planes, so each protocol has one implementation instead of one per kernel. - The three `csrc` → `csrc` includes of `custom_all_reduce.cuh` are gone. What they actually used — `reduce_vec`, the marker traits — moved under `include/`. - `alloc_workspace_tensor` moved to `host::ffi`, so `utils.cuh` no longer depends on `ffi.h`. `tp_qknorm`'s 8B `ld.volatile` / `st.volatile` pair became `ld_relaxed_8B` / `st_relaxed_8B` at `.sys` scope (PTX defines volatile as relaxed at system scope, and the store is cross-GPU). Load scope measured identical at `.gpu`, so the `.gpu` load variant was dropped and the vocabulary has one scope. ## Verification (8×B200, SM100) **Correctness — 291 tests, all passing** | test | | |---|---| | `test_custom_all_reduce.py` (8 GPU) | 180 passed | | `test_ar_fusion.py` (8 GPU) | 58 passed | | `test_tp_qknorm.py` (8 GPU) | 42 passed | | `test_collectives.py` (8 GPU) | 5 passed | | `test_compute.py` | 6 passed | | `test_custom_all_reduce_v2_capability.py` | 4 passed | | `test_attn_residual.py` | 1 passed | All 11 affected JIT modules build; `fp8_blockwise_scaled_mm_sm120` verified with a direct SM120 nvcc compile. clangd reports zero diagnostics on every touched file except two pre-existing cutlass include-path gaps in `.clangd`. **Registers / spills** — `cuobjdump -res-usage`, this branch vs the merge base, kernels paired by hand where the refactor renamed them: - **No spills anywhere** (`STACK=0`, `LOCAL=0` for every kernel). - Unchanged or better everywhere except `1shot_push`: bf16 60→63, fp16 61→63, fp32 56→58. That kernel is 2.7–6.2 % *faster* — `LamportTrait`'s 4-byte-atom marker test replaces a per-bf16-half test, cutting its SASS from 512 to 344 instructions. - `2shot_pull` eager improves (bf16 53→51) and the multicast variants drop one register. **Performance** — kernel time only, measured by replaying a CUDA graph of 20 chained calls so host dispatch is excluded; three interleaved rounds per arm, per-arm spread under 1 %: | variant | delta vs merge base | |---|---| | `1shot_push` / eager (dispatched ≤ 768 KB) | **−2.7 % … −6.2 %** | | `2shot_pull` / multicast (dispatched > 768 KB) | −0.03 % … +0.39 % | | `1shot_pull` eager and multicast | −1.1 % … +0.6 % | | `2shot_pull` / eager | +0.5 % … +0.9 % | 33 points: median +0.32 %, worst +0.92 %. On the path the tuned SM100/world-8 config actually dispatches: median **−3.30 %**, worst +0.39 %. One note on how that number was reached. An earlier revision of this branch regressed `2shot_pull` eager by 7–18 %. Bisecting with self-contained reference kernels showed the params layout, the `Barrier` object and the `Impl` abstraction were all innocent — an exact transplant of the old body still regressed. The cause was the address form: folding the shard offset into the eight base pointers as a typed 32-bit vector index keeps the peer table on the uniform datapath (`UIMAD.WIDE` off a constant-bank base), whereas biasing `vid` per access, or using a 64-bit byte offset, makes all eight addresses thread-varying and costs ~12 registers per thread. Also, binding a params array address to a named local that stays live across the kernel breaks the same proof. Both are noted in comments at the point of use, since either one silently costs ~10 %. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32400438557](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32400438557)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #32406638953](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32406638953)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32400438446](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32400438446)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: docker: pin matplotlib>=3.8 to fix CUDA-13 Python 3.12 build
signals.text: ## Problem On the CUDA-13 image (`nvidia/cuda:13.0.3-...-ubuntu24.04`, Python 3.12) the `framework` stage fails at the "Install essential Python packages" step: ``` File "/tmp/pip-install-.../matplotlib_.../versioneer.py", line 401, in get_config_from_root parser = configparser.SafeConfigParser() AttributeError: module 'configparser' has no attribute 'SafeConfigParser' ERROR: Failed to build 'matplotlib' when getting requirements to build wheel ``` ## Root cause That step installs dev/plotting tools with `-c /sgl-workspace/constraints.txt`, where the runtime packages are pinned but `matplotlib` is not. Under the fully-pinned constraints, pip backtracks `matplotlib` through every release trying to satisfy the solve, descending past the cp312-wheel versions into **pre-3.8 releases that ship no Python 3.12 wheels**. pip then builds those from sdist, and their bundled `versioneer.py` calls `configparser.SafeConfigParser()` — removed in Python 3.12 — so the build dies. (Observed pip walking 3.11.1 → ... → 3.4.3 before failing.) ## Fix Pin `matplotlib>=3.8`. matplotlib 3.8 is the first release providing Python 3.12 (cp312) wheels, so pip stays on wheels and never falls back to the unbuildable legacy sdists. This mirrors the existing style in the same install list (e.g. `"runai-model-streamer[...]>=0.15.7"`). ## Testing Full CUDA-13 image build (`BUILD_TYPE=all CUDA_VERSION=13.0.3`) completes past the framework stage with this change. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #32404767651](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32404767651)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32404767507](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32404767507)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:heavy_minus_sign: **No AMD PR run found for this commit**.<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [multimodal] Fix NVFP4 diffusion models on sm_120 (RTX PRO 6000 / RTX 50xx)
signals.text: ## Motivation NVFP4 diffusion checkpoints cannot be served on sm_120 GPUs (RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell / RTX 50xx). Two independent defects in the shared ModelOpt FP4 path are involved; neither is model-specific. **1. The default FP4 GEMM backend does not exist on sm_120.** `CudaPlatformBase.get_modelopt_flashinfer_fp4_backend()` defaults to `"trtllm"`, and `flashinfer.mm_fp4` rejects it there: ``` ValueError: mm_fp4 does not support backend 'trtllm' with capability 120 ``` so the first quantized linear aborts and no NVFP4 model runs at all. **2. The block-scale layout is chosen by a heuristic whose negative branch is unreachable.** In `ModelOptFp4LinearMethod.process_weights_after_loading()` the `trtllm` branch fetches its own shuffled scale layout and **returns**. Everything still executing below it is therefore a TMA-layout consumer (`cutlass`, `cudnn`, `auto`) — but the layout was instead selected by a module-name test: ```python uses_flux1_scale_layout = not getattr( self.quant_config, "checkpoint_uses_packed_qkv", False ) and getattr(layer, "prefix", "").startswith( ("transformer_blocks.", "single_transformer_blocks.") ) if flashinfer_backend is None or uses_flux1_scale_layout: ``` Any model whose blocks are not named with the FLUX.1 prefixes skips the swizzle and hands the kernel block scales in the wrong layout. This does not raise — it silently produces broken output. ## Modifications - `runtime/platforms/cuda.py`: default the FP4 GEMM backend to `"auto"` on sm_120 (which resolves to flashinfer's sm_12x NVFP4 kernel) and keep `"trtllm"` elsewhere. `SGLANG_DIFFUSION_FLASHINFER_FP4_GEMM_BACKEND` still overrides. Uses the pre-existing `is_sm120()`, so no other capability changes behaviour. - `runtime/layers/quantization/modelopt_quant.py`: apply the 128x4 TMA reshape unconditionally, and delete the unreachable heuristic. This also removes two defensive `getattr()`s and the now-redundant second `_get_fp4_gemm_op()` call. - `test/unit/test_modelopt_fp4_backend.py`: new unit test pinning the default-backend resolution (sm_120 vs other, all explicit env spellings, unknown value falls back to the platform default). ## Accuracy Tests Verified on one RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition (sm_120) with an NVFP4 MiniMax-H3 checkpoint: - before: startup fails on (1); forcing a backend past it renders grey noise, which is (2). - after: output is **bit-identical** (md5 of the produced mp4) to the previously env-forced workaround, with no environment variables set. Same seed, same request, three runs. `python -m pytest python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/unit/test_modelopt_fp4_backend.py` — 4 passed. ## Speed Tests and Profiling No performance change is expected or measured: the same kernel is selected, and the scale reshape is a one-time weight-load step. Paired single-GPU runs before/after differ by 0.2%, inside this box's run-to-run floor. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). --- sm_120 also needs #35740 (MiniMax-H3 model-side quantized-scale fixes) for a working NVFP4 MiniMax-H3; the two are in different layers and independent, hence separate PRs. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32409392442](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32409392442)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32409391600](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32409391600)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32409391640](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32409391640)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [multimodal] MiniMax-H3: fix quantized qkv scales and missing-param policy
signals.text: ## Motivation Two MiniMax-H3 model-side defects that only appear on a quantized checkpoint (NVFP4 or fp8). **1. Per-output-row quantization metadata is not reordered with its rows.** MiniMax-H3 checkpoints store qkv grouped, so `_install_qkv_weight_loader()` permutes the fused qkv weight's output rows into `q|k|v` order via `_reorder_grouped_qkv_to_qkv()`. NVFP4 block scales and fp8 per-channel scales are indexed by that same output row, and they were loaded unpermuted — every scale ends up attached to the wrong row. The weights are correct; the dequantized values are not. The symptom is grey mush, with no error anywhere. **2. `_mark_missing_params_required()` overwrites each quant method's own missing-parameter policy.** A quant method declares in `create_weights()` what it can synthesize when a scale is absent from the checkpoint — weight-only NVFP4 has no `input_scale` and marks it `missing_param_init = "ones"`. H3 then blanket-stamps every parameter `"error"`, so the declaration is lost and the loader raises: ``` ValueError: Required checkpoint parameter '...input_scale' was not loaded ``` ## Modifications - New module-level helper `_install_qkv_row_reorder()` wraps a qkv parameter's weight loader (and its `rank_local_weight_transform`, needed by rank-local FSDP) with the same row permutation used for the weight. Applied to every `qkv_proj` parameter except the weight itself. The gate is the row count: a tensor whose leading dim is not the checkpoint's qkv row count is passed through untouched, which covers per-tensor scalars and swizzled block-scale layouts that are not row-indexed. It reads the **loaded checkpoint tensor**, not the local parameter, so it also holds under tensor parallelism, where the local parameter only owns its own shard of the rows. - `_mark_missing_params_required()` now only claims parameters that have no declared policy. - `test/unit/test_minimax_h3_qkv_scale_reorder.py`: new unit test covering both branches of the row-count gate (row-indexed metadata is permuted, swizzled and per-tensor metadata is not) on the wrapped loader and on `rank_local_weight_transform`. Depends on nothing else, but on sm_120 both this and #35739 are required to get a working NVFP4 MiniMax-H3 (the two fixes are in different layers, hence separate PRs). ## Accuracy Tests On one RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition (sm_120) with an NVFP4 MiniMax-H3 checkpoint: - (2) alone is a hard load failure. - With (2) fixed, (1) renders grey mush. - With both fixed, output is structurally the same as the bf16 checkpoint, and bit-identical across repeated runs at the same seed. The reorder is only reachable for a quantized checkpoint with per-row scales; a bf16 run has no parameters other than the weight on `qkv_proj`, so it is unaffected. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Weight-load-time only; no change to the forward path and none measured (paired runs within 0.2%). ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32409454008](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32409454008)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32409453473](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32409453473)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32409453790](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32409453790)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [Intel GPU] Route MXFP4 MoE to the sgl-kernel-xpu W4A16 grouped GEMM
signals.text: MXFP4 checkpoints (GPT-OSS) could not run on XPU: `mxfp4` was registered only for cpu/cuda/gfx95, and `Mxfp4MoEMethod` had no XPU branch, so it fell through to a bf16 upcast needing `triton_kernels` and ~42 GB for GPT-OSS-20B. `moe_grouped_mm_nt_xe20_w4a16` consumes the checkpoint layout as-is (packed e2m1 + N-outer ue8m0 g32 scales, interleaved gate/up rows), so add the XPU dispatch, skip the upcast, and keep the layout unpadded. signals.title: Fix Qwen3.5 mRoPE positions silently dropped by fused QK RMSNorm+RoPE kernel
signals.text: ## Motivation Fixes #35345. On CUDA, `Qwen3_5AttentionDecoderLayer.self_attention` selected `fused_qk_gemma_rmsnorm_rope_gate` whenever `attn_output_gate` was set, with no check on the shape of `positions`. That kernel indexed positions as 1D `[T]` (`pos = tl.load(positions_ptr + token)`). Multimodal Qwen3.5 checkpoints supply `[3, T]` mRoPE positions. Reading them as 1D picks up only the temporal row, so the height and width rotary dimensions were silently wrong for visual tokens — no error, no warning, just degraded multimodal quality. Affects Qwen3.6-27B, Qwen3.8-27B and Qwen3.8-27B-FP8. ## Modifications The issue suggested a conservative `positions.ndim == 1` guard. This PR instead extends the kernel to real mRoPE, so multimodal batches keep the fused path rather than falling back for every image request. **`fused_qk_rmsnorm_rope_gate.py`** - The kernel takes a positions row stride plus `mrope_section` / `mrope_interleaved` constexprs, and selects each rotary pair's angle from the temporal, height or width row. Both the interleaved (round-robin) and sectioned (contiguous) layouts are supported, using the same masked-load-and-sum idiom as `rotary_triton.py:60-73`. - Axis masks are ANDed with `rot_mask`, so padded lanes (`ROT_HALF_BLOCK > HALF_ROTARY`) never address past the end of a `cos_sin_cache` row. - `_check_positions_contract` validates shape, token count, section length and sum, and token-dim contiguity. It raises `ValueError` rather than asserting — these guard against silently computing the wrong RoPE, and `assert` vanishes under `python -O`. - GLM-interleaved mRoPE is explicitly rejected rather than silently mishandled. **`qwen3_5.py`** - `_fused_mrope_kwargs` derives the kernel metadata from the `MRotaryEmbedding` itself and returns `None` for anything the kernel does not implement. - `None` falls back to `forward_prepare_native`, which handles `attn_output_gate` in full and applies the unfused mRoPE correctly — so an unfusable configuration loses the fused RMSNorm's speed but never correctness. **Text-only path is untouched.** The `MROPE=False` specialization's PTX instruction stream is byte-identical to before; the only difference in the compiled module is one unused `.param .u32` slot. ## Accuracy Tests New `test/registered/kernels/ops/attention/test_fused_qk_rmsnorm_rope_gate.py` (12 cases). The reference is an independent `torch.gather` formulation over a permuted `[T, half, 3]` tensor, deliberately *not* a restatement of the kernel's mask arithmetic. Coverage: 1D positions; equal-axis `[3, T]` (must reproduce the 1D result); real interleaved Qwen3.5 geometry (`head_dim=256`, `rotary_dim=64`, `mrope_section=[11, 11, 10]`); a temporal-only negative control; sectioned mRoPE; non-power-of-two half-rotary (`rotary_dim=48`); positions sliced from a wider CUDA-graph buffer (`stride(0) != T`, as produced by `base_runner.py:468`); the no-gate path; the contract rejections; and the dispatch metadata against a real `MRotaryEmbedding`. The regression case was confirmed **red before the fix** (`max |q - ref| = 9.19`) and green after. Results: **12/12 pass** in a CUDA container (torch 2.13.0+cu130). 11/12 also pass on a local SM 8.6 card across a second, independent stack (torch 2.11.0+cu128 / Triton 3.7.1); the 12th needs `sglang.srt`, which does not import on Windows. ## Speed Tests and Profiling **Not measured — I do not have Hopper hardware, and would appreciate a maintainer running CI on this.** What I can state: - The text-only path cannot regress: its PTX instruction stream is unchanged. - The mRoPE path issues 4 extra masked `cos_sin_cache` loads per program versus the 1D path, matching what `rotary_triton.py` already does. - The PDL branch (`ENABLE_PDL`, sm_90+) is unreachable on my hardware, so I verified it by cross-compiling for `sm_90`: `MROPE=True` with PDL enabled compiles and emits `griddepcontrol`, and an `sm_86` + PDL control correctly fails ptxas. That is compile-time evidence only — it is not a runtime result. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). — no user-facing behavior change to document - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). — no Hopper hardware available; see above <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32416088090](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32416088090)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32416087751](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32416087751)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32416088138](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32416088138)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [multimodal] MiniMax-H3: accept target.width/height as an exact canvas
signals.text: ## Motivation `target.short_edge` names a *policy* size and lets `adapt_shape_v1` choose the canvas. A caller that already knows the geometry it wants — a fixed delivery format, a UI preset — has to work backwards to a nominal short edge plus a ratio string that round to it, and gets no error when the guess is wrong: unknown `target` keys are silently ignored, so a request carrying `width`/`height` is admitted and rendered at whatever the ratio resolved to. (`conditions[i]` and the canonical request both reject unknown keys; `target` is the one place that does not.) Naming both axes is exact, because the ratio *is* the canvas: the resolver's nominal-times-ratio step reproduces it and the nearest-32 rounding is a no-op. So this needs no resolver or stage change — validation rewrites the pair into the `short_edge` + `aspect_ratio` it denotes, and the canonical request keeps its existing three-key projection. A test asserts the resolved shape is identical to the equivalent ratio request (the resolved shape does not carry the ratio string, so nothing downstream can tell them apart). ## Modifications - `request_validation.py`: `_normalize_exact_canvas()` rewrites `target.width`+`height` into `short_edge=min(w, h)` and `aspect_ratio="W:H"`. - refuses a canvas off the 32px grid or over `MINIMAX_H3_MAX_PIXELS` rather than rounding or scaling it — silently changing the requested geometry is worse than refusing it; - refuses naming both spellings, and half a pair; - defers the inclusive 1:4..4:1 range and the grid to `minimax_h3_resolve_spatial_shape` (asks the resolver whether it reproduces the canvas) instead of restating those rules; - keeps the forced-`"auto"` task guard, since the rewrite ends in a concrete ratio; - an exact canvas is exempt from the finite-ratio allowlist: that allowlist constrains *ratio* requests to tested shapes, and a caller naming both axes has already chosen. - `configs/sample/minimax_h3.py`: add `width`/`height` to the `target` projection in `_validate()`, otherwise the offline path drops them before validation sees them. - `test/unit/test_minimax_h3_exact_target_canvas.py`: new, 16 cases (accepted canvas, plan geometry, equivalence with the ratio spelling, the pixel-budget edge, allowlist exemption, fl2va, and each rejection). ## Accuracy Tests No change for existing requests: `width`/`height` absent takes the same path as before. `pytest python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/unit/ -k minimax` → 103 passed. ## Speed Tests and Profiling N/A (request validation only). ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). --- Other MiniMax-H3 PRs from the same bring-up: #35739 (sm_120 NVFP4), #35740 (H3 qkv scale row order), #35745 (short-edge warning), and #35743 (a `--attention-backend` selector issue). <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32411483474](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32411483474)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32411483182](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32411483182)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32411483409](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32411483409)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: Fix overlap prebuilt row reuse race
signals.text: Wait for outstanding overlap forward work before prebuilt batch processing can seed a reused request-pool row. ## Motivation Bug fix for race condition in FutureMap. publish() call can happen in two cases: (1) in forward stream after draft+verify. (2) in schedule stream, when PD disagg is enabled, and prefill request is arriving. publish() modifies shared states in FutureMap, so they must be ordered correctly to avoid race. publish_ready cannot be used for synchronization because stash() after record also has FutureMap shared state modification. ## Modifications (1) schedule stream to wait for forward stream before calling publish in PD disagg (2) remove unnecessary chaining in record as (1) guarantees ordering (3) unit test ## Accuracy Tests N/A ## Speed Tests and Profiling N/A ## Checklist - [V] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [V] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [V] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process). 2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers. 3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so. - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci` 4. signals.title: [diffusion] read the next mapped layer ahead instead of faulting on it
signals.text: ## Motivation A weight left on the checkpoint mapping (#35701) is copied to the device synchronously, so when the page cache has dropped its pages the read happens on the critical path: the copy stalls in a major fault while the GPU waits. On MiniMax-H3 that is 44 GiB of DiT weights walked once per denoise step against roughly 8 GiB of page cache, so most steps fault. It shows up as load sensitivity — the denoise stage tracks how contended the host's memory bandwidth is, because the faults are competing for it. Every alternative that buys overlap buys it with host memory this budget does not have: pinning cannot be done on a mapping at all, and staging copies are the thing the mapping exists to avoid. Readahead buys it with nothing. ## Modifications `MADV_WILLNEED` over the next layer's mapped range, issued when the current layer is staged. Asynchronous readahead: free when the pages are already resident, overlapped with the current layer's compute when they are not, and it commits no memory of its own. One call per layer rather than per weight — a layer's mapped tensors are slices of the same checkpoint shard, so advising min..max covers them together and keeps this to one syscall per prefetch. `madvise` is bound through `ctypes` once and left as `None` where libc does not offer it, so the advice is skipped rather than guarded at every call site. ## Accuracy Tests Which pages are resident when a copy runs; the bytes copied are identical. `test_layerwise_offload.py` on this branch: 55 passed. ## Speed Tests and Profiling H3 `fl2va`, 864x480 / 124 frames / 20 steps, seed 1101, single RTX 4090, 12 GiB VRAM cap enforced with `torch.cuda.set_per_process_memory_fraction`, host memory capped at 32 GiB, `--layerwise-resident-layers video_vae=36`. This box is shared and its load average swings between 80 and 220, which is exactly the axis this change is about, so the samples are reported with it: | | load | denoise | decode | end to end | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | without readahead | 87 | 144.65 s | 13.08 s | 161.44 s | | without readahead | 131 | 157.05 s | 13.21 s | 175.72 s | | without readahead | 152 | 146.68 s | 12.92 s | 163.25 s | | **with readahead** | **139** | **144.89 s** | 12.88 s | **161.50 s** | | **with readahead** | **217** | **144.82 s** | 12.76 s** | **161.34 s** | Without it, end to end swings 161–176 s with load. With it, load 139 and load 217 both land at 161.3–161.5 s: the load-sensitive term is gone, which is the point. The decode stage is unchanged, as expected — its weights are held resident for the stage rather than re-read. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). Stacked on #35701, which is what puts weights on a mapping in the first place. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #32437536525](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32437536525)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32437536401](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32437536401)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #32437536515](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32437536515)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [CI] Gate `/rerun-test` on commenter trust and remove `/rerun-stage`
signals.text: ## Summary - Remove `/rerun-stage` entirely: the command handler, its workflow trigger, the `can_rerun_stage` permission key, and every doc reference. The command has only posted a deprecation notice for a while; stage-level dispatch remains available through the Actions UI on the AMD workflows. - Gate `/rerun-test` and `/rerun-group` on the commenter alone. Where the PR comes from is no longer part of the decision, and neither is PR authorship. ## Permission matrix `/rerun-test` and `/rerun-group`, by commenter and PR origin: | Commenter | Same-repo PR | Fork PR | | --- | --- | --- | | `write` / `admin` on the repo | allowed | allowed | | `cooldown_interval_minutes: 0` | allowed | allowed | | `cooldown_interval_minutes > 0` | denied | denied | | Absent from `CI_PERMISSIONS.json` | denied | denied | The two columns are identical by design. A selective rerun dispatches `rerun-test.yml` directly, which never passes through `pr-gate.yml`, so it bypasses that rate limit by construction -- anyone allowed to run one is unthrottled in practice. That is already what `cooldown_interval_minutes: 0` declares, and it is the same pair of signals `pr-gate.yml` itself uses to waive the limit (write permission, or a zero cooldown). So no new permission key is introduced; the existing cooldown value carries the trust level. Authoring a PR grants nothing here. Authors keep their automatic `/rerun-failed-ci` allowance, which is unchanged. ## Changes **Removals** - Drop the `/rerun-stage` branch in `slash_command_handler.py` and its `contains()` clause in `slash-command-handler.yml` - Drop `can_rerun_stage` from all 241 entries in `CI_PERMISSIONS.json` and from the `update_ci_permission.py` templates **Gating** - `_check_rerun_test_permissions` now checks `cooldown_interval_minutes == 0` first, then repo permission -- so trusted users cost zero extra API calls - Remove the early exit in `main()` on a missing `CI_PERMISSIONS.json` entry, so a write-holder absent from the file reaches the handler. The other commands re-check their own key and still deny silently. **Hardening** - Pass `persist-credentials: false` on the three `rerun-test.yml` checkouts that can hold a fork's code. Without it, checkout leaves the job token in `.git/config`, where the code those jobs go on to execute could read it. The steps that need the token already take it from `secrets` explicitly, and nothing in those jobs runs git. - Drop the workflow-level `actions: write` in `rerun-test.yml`. Every job declares its own `permissions`, which replaces rather than merges with the workflow-level block, so no job could ever obtain it. **Docs** - Record the permission keys and the cooldown/rerun coupling in `.github/FOLDER_README.md` - Fix a pre-existing error in the `contribution_guide.mdx` permission table, which claimed a fork PR author had an automatic grant -- the fork check ran first, so an author without write was denied - Retire `/rerun-stage` references in the ascend guide, `test/README.md`, the CI workflow guide, and the AMD workflow comments (where the `target_stage` input itself stays, since it is still dispatched from the Actions UI) ## Impact Of the 241 entries in `CI_PERMISSIONS.json` (118 accounts hold repo write): - 174 keep access -- 151 via `cooldown_interval_minutes: 0`, 23 more via write permission - 67 lose it, all of them `"reason": "custom override"` with a non-zero cooldown. No `"top contributor"` entry is affected. Setting a user's cooldown to `0` restores it. - 16 accounts with write permission but no entry in the file gain access Note for #35600, which adds four entries to the same file: under this gating, `can_rerun_stage: true` on those entries has no effect -- granting them selective rerun means setting `cooldown_interval_minutes` to `0`. The two PRs also touch every entry in `CI_PERMISSIONS.json` and will conflict. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32422201099](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32422201099)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32422200850](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32422200850)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32422201197](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32422201197)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: Support GPT-OSS MXFP4 checkpoints on Intel XPU
signals.text: ## Motivation `openai/gpt-oss-20b` and `-120b` ship MXFP4-quantized MoE weights. SGLang's MXFP4 support targets CUDA (`triton_kernels` / Marlin / FlashInfer cutlass), HIP (aiter) and CPU (AMX), so on `--device xpu` the checkpoint is rejected before any layer is built: ``` ValueError: Unknown quantization method: mxfp4. Must be one of ['fp8', 'mxfp8', ...] configs/model_config.py:1588 in _verify_quantization ``` `mxfp4.py` already contains a device-neutral fallback that upcasts MXFP4 to bf16 once at load time and serves through the ordinary unquantized MoE. This PR makes that existing path reachable and functional off-CUDA; no new kernel or backend is introduced. ## Modifications Two files, `+69/-15`. **1. Register `mxfp4` for XPU** — `layers/quantization/__init__.py` ```diff -if is_cpu() or is_cuda() or _is_gfx95_supported: +if is_cpu() or is_cuda() or is_xpu() or _is_gfx95_supported: ``` **2. Device-neutral chunked upcast** — new `_upcast_mxfp4_to_bf16()` in `mxfp4.py` The generic branch of `process_weights_after_loading` imported `triton_kernels.numerics_details.mxfp.upcast_from_mxfp`, which is CUDA/HIP-only. The helper prefers it when importable and otherwise runs a pure-torch upcast, so **CUDA behavior is unchanged**. Chunking is required, not stylistic. `MXFP4QuantizeUtil.dequantize` in `mxfp4_tensor.py` computes identical values but whole-tensor: it promotes unpacked nibbles to `int64` for the LUT gather and builds `float32` sign/magnitude temporaries, so one `w13_weight` expands to several GB and exhausts a 24 GB card. The helper writes bf16 directly into a preallocated output in row chunks, matching the strategy in transformers' `_convert_moe_packed_tensors(rows_per_chunk=...)`. **3. `torch.cuda.empty_cache()` -> `empty_device_cache()`** in the generic post-load path. The two remaining calls in this file are inside SM90-cutlass / trtllm helpers that cannot run on XPU and are left untouched. **4. Pad the MoE intermediate on this path** `models/gpt_oss.py:985` shards by whole MXFP4 blocks: ```python per_rank_intermediate_size_block = math.ceil(intermediate_size_block / moe_tp_size) per_rank_intermediate_size = per_rank_intermediate_size_block * mxfp4_block ``` For gpt-oss-20b at tp=4 that is `ceil(90/4) * 32 = 736`, while `intermediate_size_per_partition` is `2880/4 = 720`, so the rank's slice is larger than its nominal share and the loader's copy overflows: ``` RuntimeError: The size of tensor a (360) must match the size of tensor b (368) at non-singleton dimension 2 ``` Every other branch in `create_weights` absorbs this in its own alignment (64 for triton_kernels, 128 for Marlin/cutlass, 256 for aiter) — which is what the function's existing comment says the padding is for. This path had none. Padding is numerically inert: the extra `w13` rows stay zero, so gate and up are zero, and the matching `w2` columns contribute nothing. Note this is **latent for any non-padding backend**, not XPU-specific; it only appears when `intermediate_size / tp` is not a multiple of 32, which is why tp=1 and tp=2 never hit it. Scoped to `is_xpu()` to keep the diff reviewable — happy to generalize it to a default if maintainers prefer. ## Accuracy Tests The upcast is the only change that touches numerics. It is **bit-exact** (`torch.equal`, no tolerance) against transformers' `_convert_moe_packed_tensors`, the reference unpacking used for `Mxfp4Config(dequantize=True)`, on random packed data shaped like a real expert weight (`[4, 64, 2880]`, full byte range, exponents 90-160): | Case | Result | |---|---| | CPU vs transformers | bit-exact | | XPU vs transformers | bit-exact | | XPU, `rows_per_chunk=1000` (forces mid-tensor chunk boundaries) | bit-exact | End-to-end on 4x Intel Arc Pro B60, `gpt-oss-20b`, tp=4, `--attention-backend intel_xpu`. Server reaches `ready to roll`; 10.39 GB/rank. Streaming reasoning (`--reasoning-parser gpt-oss`): ``` Prompt: Solve this problem step by step: What is 15% of 240? Thinking: 15% of 240 means 0.15 * 240 ... Response: ... 5. Result: 36 Verification: 10 % of 240 = 24, 5 % of 240 = 12, sum = 36 ``` Streaming tool calling (`--tool-call-parser gpt-oss`): ``` Tool call: get_weather({"location": "Beijing", "unit": "celsius"}) Final answer: The current weather in Beijing is 22 C and sunny. ``` **Benchmark accuracy is not yet run.** Because this path serves dequantized weights, the published MXFP4 numbers should not be assumed to carry over, and GSM8K needs measuring against the reference 0.535 for 20b before this leaves draft. Flagging rather than glossing over. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Not run. This changes weight preparation at load time only; the forward path is the existing unquantized MoE. Load time is 5.3 s/rank for 20b at tp=4. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Known limitations - **gpt-oss-120b is untested.** ~235 GB of dequantized bf16 will not fit in 96 GB of XPU memory; 120b likely needs a real MXFP4 MoE kernel rather than this upcast. - Serving dequantized weights forgoes the memory saving of MXFP4. This is functional enablement, not a performance path. - Requires capping context/concurrency on 24 GB cards; with defaults, SGLang derives `context_len=131072` / `max_running_requests=3764` and warmup OOMs allocating the attention page table. ## Remaining before undraft 1. GSM8K on 20b vs the 0.535 reference. 2. Unit test pinning `_upcast_mxfp4_to_bf16` bit-exactness against a stored reference vector. 3. Maintainer call on the two scoping questions above (XPU-gated vs. general fix for items 1 and 4). <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32416346228](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32416346228)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32416345862](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32416345862)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32416346390](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32416346390)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [docs] Tell Qwen3.8-27B DFLASH2 users to build from main
signals.text: ## Motivation Follow-up to #35663 (merged), fixing two things that PR got wrong. 1. **The build requirement was undocumented.** The page pins `lmsysorg/sglang:qwen38-27b`, but DFlash2 only landed in #35371, and NVFP4's quantized `lm_head` needs #35496 on top of it — both newer than that tag and than the latest release. A reader following the page today gets a boot failure (`requires a dense FP16/BF16/FP32 target lm_head` on NVFP4) with nothing telling them why. 2. **`# DFLASH2 on this platform: final verification in progress` was a hint line inside the command.** The panel already has a verification badge with an `in-progress` state; a `#` comment glued into a copy-paste command is both uglier and easier to miss. #35663 should have used the badge. ## Modifications - `Qwen3.8-27B.mdx`: a `<Warning>` under the Deploy panel where the DFLASH2 pick is made, a `<Warning>` in the Install accordion, and commented-out `docker pull lmsysorg/sglang:dev` / from-source lines in the two install blocks, so the requirement travels with the command a reader copies. Both warnings state that None / EAGLE / DSPARK still run on the pinned tag, so this does not read as a page-wide version bump. - `qwen3.8-27b.jsx`: drop the hint line; the H200, DGX Spark and GB300 cells now report `in-progress` **for the DFLASH2 pick only**, and stay Verified for every other pick. - `_deployment.jsx`: `verificationStatus` may be a function of the selection, so a cell can report a per-pick verification state. - `.claude/skills/cookbook-add-model/`: document that field in the authoring reference (it was undocumented even before this change) and point at it from the config template. - `check_cookbook_configs.mjs`: probe `cells[].verificationStatus` when it is a function. The checker already probes every function-valued **dim/option** field over the whole selection space; cells had none until now, so this closes the gap the engine change opens — a status typo or a throwing predicate fails the check instead of reaching the rendered page. Verified by mutation: a typo'd `"in-progres"` and a crashing predicate each fail it, and the real config passes. ## On the `_deployment.jsx` change A pick-scoped badge is not expressible without it: `cellVerifyStatus` reads a static field off the cell and never sees the selection, so the only config-only option is a static `in-progress` that mislabels the other picks on those platforms as unverified. Blast radius: `verificationStatus` is read at exactly one call site (`cellVerifyStatus`, used once); `_playground.jsx` and `check_cookbook_configs.mjs` never read it. The only other config that sets it is `kimi-k3.jsx` — 49 occurrences, all static strings, which take the unchanged path. Booleans, strings, `undefined` and unknown values all behave exactly as before (unknown still falls back to `unverified`, so a typo can never read as a green Verified badge). ## Accuracy Tests N/A (docs only). ## Speed Tests and Profiling N/A (docs only). `docs/scripts/check_cookbook_configs.mjs` passes; page renders clean with the badge flipping on the DFLASH2 pick and staying Verified on the others. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #32428769870](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32428769870)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32428769632](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32428769632)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:heavy_minus_sign: **No AMD PR run found for this commit**.<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [Diffusion] Z-Image: autotune the shared transformer block at both token scales
signals.text: Z-Image reuses one transformer block for the context refiner (a few dozen caption tokens), the noise refiner (4096) and the unified stream (4128 at 1024x1024). The flash-attn call breaks the graph, so the block's attention compiles into a frame of its own that is entered with all three counts; automatic dynamic shapes make its token dim symbolic, and Inductor autotunes the fused-qkv GEMM once, against whichever count it traced first. The caption branch wins that race and the resulting BLOCK_M=32/BLOCK_N=32 config then runs the 4096- and 4128-token layers. It is the only dynamic-shape Triton template the model selects, and it accounts for the whole torch.compile regression reported in BBuf/how-to-optim-algorithm-in-cuda#21. Set inductor's multi_kernel_hints for this model, so the block is compiled once per hint and dispatched on the runtime shape and the token dim stays dynamic. The knob is a generic DiTConfig.torch_compile_inductor_config passthrough that is empty for every other model; inductor config is process-global and is read when a graph compiles, so it cannot be scoped to the torch.compile call, and `mode` rules out torch.compile(options=...). The root cause is the flash-attn graph break, which is what routes three very different token counts through one compiled frame. Removing it would fix this for any DiT with mixed sequence lengths and is worth doing separately. Test Plan: Steady-state denoise on one H100, min of requests 2..8 (request 1 carries the compile), stock preset with no extra flags: ``` export CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 CI=1 SGLANG_DIFFUSION_SYNC_STAGE_PROFILING=1 \ FLASHINFER_DISABLE_VERSION_CHECK=1 B=python/sglang/multimodal_gen/.claude/skills/sglang-diffusion-benchmark-profile/scripts/bench_diffusion_denoise.py rm -rf ~/.cache/sgl_diffusion/torch_compile_cache python3 $B --model zimage-base --iterations 8 --label compile --output-dir /tmp/zb python3 $B --model zimage-base --iterations 8 --label eager --no-torch-compile --output-dir /tmp/zb ``` | arm | denoise | vs eager | |-----------------|----------|----------| | eager | 9.567 s | -- | | compile, before | 13.575 s | 1.42x | | compile, after | 9.577 s | 1.00x | First-request e2e goes 79.6 s -> 96.2 s, the cost of autotuning the block at two sizes instead of one. signals.title: [Docker] Defer CUDA 13 NCCL override until after dependency resolution

signals.title: fix: FA4 paged-KV zero-size page-table registers on SM90
signals.text: ## Motivation Serving `Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B-FP8` with `--attention-backend fa4` on a GH200 (Hopper, SM90) crashes in the scheduler during startup warmup, before the server ever accepts a request: ``` Generate warm up request for compiling DeepGEMM... [2026-08-20 14:09:01] Scheduler hit an exception: Traceback (most recent call last): File "sglang/srt/managers/scheduler.py", line 5174, in run_scheduler_process scheduler.run_event_loop() [...] File "sglang/srt/models/qwen3_5.py", line 1212, in self_attention attn_output = self.attn(q, k, v, forward_batch) File "sglang/srt/layers/attention/hybrid_linear_attn_backend.py", line 1134, in forward_extend return self.full_attn_backend.forward_extend( File "sglang/srt/layers/attention/flashattention_backend.py", line 1496, in forward_extend result = flash_attn_with_kvcache( File "sglang/kernels/ops/attention/flash_attention_v4.py", line 276, in flash_attn_with_kvcache result = flash_attn_varlen_func( File "sglang/kernels/ops/attention/flash_attn/cute/interface.py", line 1628, in _flash_attn_fwd _flash_attn_fwd.compile_cache[compile_key] = cute.compile( [... CUTLASS DSL trace-building frames elided ...] File "sglang/kernels/ops/attention/flash_attn/cute/flash_fwd_sm90.py", line 806, in then_block_9 self.load( File "sglang/kernels/ops/attention/flash_attn/cute/flash_fwd_sm90.py", line 983, in while_after_block_2 paged_kv_manager = PagedKVManager.create( File "sglang/kernels/ops/attention/flash_attn/cute/paged_kv.py", line 119, in create tPrPage = cute.make_rmem_tensor((page_entry_per_thread,), Int32) [...] File "nvidia_cutlass_dsl/dsl_packages/cutlass/cute/core.py", line 339, in _check_shape raise ValueError( f"Expected size in shape to be strictly positive, but got {shape}" ) ValueError: Expected size in shape to be strictly positive, but got 0 ``` Environment: GH200 480GB (SM90), CUDA 13.2, `nvidia-cutlass-dsl` 4.6.2, sglang built from source at `eac91ac36` (line numbers above are from that commit). Reproduced with: ``` python -m sglang.launch_server --model-path Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B-FP8 \ --attention-backend fa4 --kv-cache-dtype auto \ --speculative-algorithm DFLASH \ --speculative-draft-model-path z-lab/Qwen3.8-27B-DFlash2 \ --speculative-num-draft-tokens 8 ``` ### Root cause `PagedKVManager.create()` sizes its per-thread page-table registers with a floor division: ```python page_entry_per_thread = n_block_size // num_threads # num_threads = 128 ``` When `tile_n < 128` this evaluates to `0`, and `cute.make_rmem_tensor((0,), Int32)` fails the shape check above. Qwen3.8-27B's full-attention layers have `head_dim=256`, and `_tile_size_fwd_sm90()` returns `tile_n = 80` for that head dim (64 with a sliding window). sglang's default `page_size=1` never equals `tile_n`, so the non-TMA cp.async path — the one that stages the page table in registers — is always the one selected. So every paged-KV FA4 run on SM90 at `head_dim=256` hits this; `head_dim=192` is affected too (`tile_n` 112 / 96). This is the same assertion seen in #32118 (merged) and #31903, but those addressed the SM100 diff-headdim split-KV case by not shrinking `tile_n` to 64 in `interface.py`; the division itself was left as-is. That doesn't cover SM90, where `tile_n = 80` is not a conditional shrink but the tile the heuristic picks unconditionally — there is no configuration that steers around it. Upstream FA4 (`Dao-AILab/flash-attention`, `flash_attn/cute/paged_kv.py`) already uses ceiling division here, with a comment about counting the final partially populated wave of rows. sglang's vendored copy diverged. ## Modifications One line in `python/sglang/kernels/ops/attention/flash_attn/cute/paged_kv.py`: use `cute.ceil_div` instead of floor division. Why `ceil` is the right size rather than merely non-zero: `load_KV()` indexes `tPrXPtr[m // gmem_threads_per_row]` for `m` in `range(n_block_size * gmem_threads_per_row / num_threads)`, so the largest index used needs exactly `ceil(n_block_size / num_threads)` entries. The entries this over-allocates when `n_block_size < num_threads` are already predicated off by the `row < n_block_size` check in `load_page_table()` (which writes `page = 0`), and are never consumed by the `shuffle_sync` in `load_KV()`. Risk is limited to configurations that cannot currently run: `ceil == floor` whenever `n_block_size % num_threads == 0`, which is true of every tile that compiles today, so those kernels are bit-identical. ## Accuracy Tests Standalone script calling `flash_attn_with_kvcache` on the paged path, checked against an fp32 SDPA reference, on GH200 (SM90). Deliberately shuffled page tables so page-index/offset mix-ups can't hide. Every case fails to compile on `main` and passes with this change: | case | page_size | causal | window | max abs err | |---|---|---|---|---| | b1, s_q=s_k=512 | 1 | yes | – | 0.0156 | | b3 ragged, s_q=[300,17,128], s_k=[300,1000,128] | 1 | yes | – | 0.0156 | | b4 spec-decode, s_q=8, s_k=[513,80,81,1024] | 1 | yes | – | 0.0039 | | b2, non-causal | 1 | no | – | 0.0039 | | b2, multi-token pages | 64 | yes | – | 0.0156 | | b2, sliding window (tile_n=64) | 1 | yes | (256, 0) | 0.0078 | (`ref_absmax` ≈ 1.3–4.1, so these are bf16 rounding.) End-to-end: `Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B-FP8` on GH200 with `--attention-backend fa4` now completes startup warmup and serves. A 7044-token prompt with a needle placed mid-context returned the needle exactly, which exercises many `n_block` iterations of the cp.async page-table path rather than just compilation. Not covered: SM100. `ceil == floor` for the tiles that arch uses, so no behavior change is expected there, but I don't have Blackwell hardware to confirm. ## Speed Tests and Profiling No impact. `page_entry_per_thread` is a compile-time constant and the generated kernel is unchanged for every configuration that compiles today. ## Follow-up (deliberately not in this PR) With the root cause fixed, the `not (page_table is not None and q_stage == 1)` guard added by #32118 could likely be relaxed to restore its SMEM-saving `tile_n = 64` for SM100 diff-headdim decode. I can't validate that without Blackwell, so I've left it alone. ## Note on test coverage `test/registered/attention/unittests/dense/test_fa4.py` runs `HEAD_DIM = 64` only, which is why this went unnoticed — no FA4 test exercises a `tile_n` that isn't a multiple of 128. Precedent: #32118 fixed the same assertion in this subsystem and validated it with a standalone repro rather than a committed test. Happy to add a regression case (here or under `test/registered/kernels/ops/attention/`) gated to SM90 if reviewers want one; `1-gpu-large` is an H100 runner, so it would genuinely guard this. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32422366336](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32422366336)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32422366126](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32422366126)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32422366252](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32422366252)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [DSA] Bound the indexer MQA-logits chunk: read free memory live, and cap the chunk absolutely
signals.text: ## Motivation `_get_topk_ragged` chunks the MQA-logits matrix to avoid OOM, and sizes each chunk as ```python bytes_per_row = k_offset * self._MQA_LOGITS_BYTES_PER_ELEM max_rows = max(1, int(logits_budget_bytes // max(bytes_per_row, 1))) ``` so **`_get_mqa_logits_budget_bytes()` is the size of every chunk allocation**. That budget comes from a single `torch.cuda.mem_get_info` reading, taken on the first non-capture prefill past `_MQA_LOGITS_STATIC_SKIP_ELEMS`, cached in a **class-level** dict shared by every `Indexer` instance in the process, and never revalidated. A reading taken while memory was plentiful therefore keeps authorizing that same multi-GiB allocation for the life of the process. Observed on a DSA + EAGLE-MTP prefill (178.35 GiB device, TP8, `--chunked-prefill-size 32768`, `--mem-fraction-static 0.92`): ``` tvm.error.InternalError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 2.63 GiB. GPU 3 has a total capacity of 178.35 GiB of which 2.20 GiB is free. ... 4.70 GiB allocated in private pools (e.g., CUDA Graphs), and 6.46 GiB is reserved by PyTorch but unallocated. [...] Received SIGQUIT. Scheduler failed/hung; shutting down. ``` with the traceback landing on the **chunked** branch: ``` dsa_indexer.py _get_topk_ragged logits_chunk = deep_gemm.fp8_mqa_logits( <-- the guard fired, and still deep_gemm/__init__.py fp8_mqa_logits asked for 6x the free memory -> torch::empty -> CUDACachingAllocator::malloc ``` `token usage: 0.06` on the same log line — this is not KV pressure. Working backwards from the log alone: a 2.63 GiB allocation implies a budget ≥ 2.63 GiB, hence ≥ 13.15 GiB free when it was measured (`frac` 0.2); free at crash was 2.20 GiB. The missing 10.95 GiB matches the log's 4.70 GiB of CUDA-graph private pools plus 6.46 GiB reserved-but-unallocated (11.16 GiB) to within 2%. **Speculative decoding makes this systematically worse.** `_draft_extend_for_prefill` builds its batch with `ForwardBatch.init_new(...)`, which keeps the prefill batch's `EXTEND` mode, so it misses the `is_draft_extend_v2() -> _get_topk_paged` path and issues the same ragged chunk the target model just issued — except now the target's prefill activations are still live and the overlap scheduler has two batches in flight. The target's identical allocation succeeding moments earlier is not evidence that the draft's will. Two secondary factors, both addressed by the cap below: the chunk size varies per request (it depends on `k_offset`), so the caching allocator accumulates large, oddly-sized segments that cannot be recycled — which is exactly what "6.46 GiB reserved but unallocated" is, enough memory in the wrong shapes for a request needing 2.63 GiB *contiguous*. ## Modifications The cache was introduced deliberately in #25299 (replacing a live per-call check) because `mem_get_info` synchronizes the host. This keeps that intent and closes both holes: | Env | Default | Effect | |---|---|---| | `SGLANG_DSA_MQA_LOGITS_BUDGET_CACHE_S` | `0` = never reuse a reading | Kills the staleness outright. `> 0` reuses a reading for that long, `< 0` reuses forever (today's behaviour). | | `SGLANG_DSA_MQA_LOGITS_MAX_CHUNK_BYTES` | 256 MiB | Caps one chunk absolutely — the part a live reading **cannot** give you. `0` disables. | **Why reading live is affordable here.** `_should_chunk_mqa_logits` returns before asking for a budget unless the logits matrix exceeds `_MQA_LOGITS_STATIC_SKIP_ELEMS` (32 MB), so the query only happens when the engine is about to spend milliseconds on a large GEMM. The gate was already there; this change just stops caching across it. **Why the cap is still needed once the reading is live.** Two things `mem_get_info` cannot tell you: 1. *Contiguity.* The 6.46 GiB "reserved by PyTorch but unallocated" above is enough free bytes in the wrong shapes — segments the allocator cannot merge for one large contiguous request. A 256 MiB chunk is servable out of those existing blocks. 2. *The opposite regime.* 20% of free memory on a nearly-empty 178 GiB device is a **35 GiB single allocation**. Correct by the budget's own logic, and a fragmentation and latency disaster. So the two bind in different regimes — the cap normally, the live reading once free memory falls below it. Capture mode is unchanged: static budget, no query, no caching. Setting the cap to `0` and the cache to `-1` restores today's behaviour exactly, so there is no separate feature-off path to maintain. **Prior art, corrected.** I initially cited the DSV4 indexer's `_QUERY_CHUNK = 1024` as precedent for a fixed cap — that was wrong, and I'd rather flag it than leave it standing: that constant is in `fp8_paged_mqa_logits_torch_sm120`, a pure-torch SM120 fallback for *paged decode* that chunks the batch dimension, not a peer of this path. `main`'s C4/DSV4 non-paged path has no budget at all. The real prior art is **#33288** (unmerged, on `origin/image/dev20260805-211ee642-swafix`), which hit this same stale-cache bug in the C4 indexer and also chose to re-read live, with the comment: > The cached budget is calculated once (typically right after CUDA-graph capture when free memory > is near its peak) and never updated. At prefill time the actual free memory can be > significantly lower due to KV-cache occupancy and prefill activations, so a chunk sized from > the stale cache can still OOM. It uses `0.5 × free` capped at `0.3 × total` and no absolute cap, and it additionally routes per-request so the `k` axis is one request's padded length rather than the concatenated batch — a bigger, orthogonal win for multi-request prefill that I have deliberately not attempted here. Happy to align the two indexers on whatever shape reviewers prefer. Deliberately out of scope to keep this reviewable, happy to follow up: - retrying with a halved chunk on `torch.OutOfMemoryError` (+ `empty_cache()`) so a transient allocator state costs latency rather than the whole server; - `_get_topk_ragged_with_cp`, which calls `fp8_mqa_logits` with **no chunking guard at all**. ## Accuracy Tests No numerical change, by construction: the chunk loop slices strictly per row — `ks[start:end]`, `seq_lens_expanded[start:end]`, `global_topk_offset[start:end]`, `token_to_batch_idx[start:end]` — and `topk_transform` is called per chunk with those slices, so results do not depend on how the query axis is partitioned. Only the number of partitions changes. The `not need_chunk` fast path is untouched for any matrix that fits the cap. ## Benchmarking and Profiling Not measured, and I would rather say so than guess: total logits work is unchanged (same matrix, same FLOPs), so only the launch count moves. For the crashing shape (`q = k = 32768`, a 4.00 GiB fp32 matrix) that is **2 chunks of 2630 MiB → 16 chunks of 256 MiB**. Raising `SGLANG_DSA_MQA_LOGITS_MAX_CHUNK_BYTES` recovers the old chunking exactly if a regression does show up on some shape. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the pre-commit config - [x] Add unit tests — `test/registered/attention/test_dsa_mqa_logits_budget.py`, 12 cases driving the real methods with the numbers from the crash log: the uncapped premise (a test that *asserts the bug*, so the regression cannot silently stop being one), the capped budget, the derived chunk-row count, the `_MQA_LOGITS_STATIC_SKIP_ELEMS` fast path, snapshot reuse inside the window vs. expiry after it, capture mode (asserts `mem_get_info` is **not** called and the cache is not seeded), both knobs off, the ≥1-row floor at a 512k context, zero free memory, and `mem_fraction_static = None`. Registered `register_cuda_ci(est_time=15, stage="base-b", runner_config="1-gpu-small")`. - [ ] Update documentation — no user-facing docs; both knobs are documented where they are declared in `srt/environ.py`. - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results — see the two sections above. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32432387561](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32432387561)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32432386894](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32432386894)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32432387461](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32432387461)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->
