signals.title: [Perf] Tune the W4AFP8 DeepEP low-latency requant launch geometry
signals.text: ## Motivation `fp8_per_token_to_per_tensor_quant_triton()` turns DeepEP low-latency's per-token-group fp8 payload into the per-tensor fp8 that the first CUTLASS W4A8 grouped GEMM consumes. It is a pure streaming pass — two bytes moved and two multiplies per element — but three properties of its launch shape cost more than the arithmetic does. **Access width.** A 1024-element tile over 8 warps is 4 B/thread, which is exactly where Triton stops vectorizing: the compiled kernel contained only `ld.global.b32` / `st.global.b32` on both H200 and B200. 4 warps put 8 B/thread in flight and restore `v2.b32` accesses (2 warps reach `v4.b32`, but measured slower than 4). **Scale addressing.** Scales were indexed on the element axis (`(k_offsets // 128) * stride2`), so each 1024-lane load resolved to 8 distinct addresses read 128 times each. The dispatcher returns the last two scale dims column-major for TMA (`[E, M, hidden // 128]` with `stride1 == 1`), so those 8 addresses are `m` elements apart — a scattered gather, replicated per row, per tile. **Grid shape.** The m-grid was pinned to 32 programs per expert regardless of how many rows were live, so at low-latency decode row counts most programs only loaded `masked_m`, compared, and exited. This is by far the largest effect, and it grows with the local expert count: at 256 local experts and one row each, the kernel spent 35 µs to move 3 µs of data. ## Modifications `python/sglang/kernels/ops/moe/ep_moe_kernels.py` - Tile the payload as `[G_BLOCK_SIZE, 128]` — whole scale groups — instead of a flat run of elements. The per-group scale becomes one scalar load, the fast axis stays contiguous, and a partial `k` masks whole groups. - Launch with 4 warps. - 8 groups per program (1024 elements), widening to 16 once there are >= 32 local experts, where the expert axis alone fills the machine. The tile is rounded down to the payload so a small hidden size never runs a mostly-masked tile. - `requant_launch_geometry()` sizes the m-grid from `expected_rows`: one program per expected row, floored at 4, never above the historical 32, and additionally capped by the expert count while fewer than 64 rows per expert are live — past that the extra programs carry real work rather than early exits, and the cap costs a few percent. It therefore only ever *shrinks* the grid, which is why no measured cell regresses. `expected_rows=None` reproduces the previous geometry exactly, so any other caller is unaffected. `cutlass_w4a8_moe.py` / `w4afp8.py` — thread the dispatcher's `expected_m` (already computed host-side in `dispatch_a`, and constant for a captured CUDA graph) down to the requant. It is a launch hint only: correctness does not depend on it, and an expert that receives more rows than expected simply loops over more of them. Tests: the GPU unit test covers the geometry combinations (row estimates, 4/40/128 experts, row-major and column-major scales, uneven per-expert row counts); a CPU test pins the heuristic's contracts; and a new `base-b-kernel-benchmark` entry benchmarks the shipped geometry against the previous one. ## Accuracy Tests Output is **bitwise identical to the merged kernel** on H200 and B200 — every shape below at 0, 1, 3, 7, 64 and all padded rows live, both scale layouts, plus a skewed `masked_m` where every expert gets a different row count: ``` == bitwise equality vs main, high expert counts == ok k7168 E64 ok k7168 E128 ok k7168 E256 ok k3584 E112 ok k3584 E256 ok k3584 E512 ALL PASS ``` Unit tests, H200 and B200 (`torch 2.11.0+cu130` / `triton 3.6.0`): 47 passed (`test_fp8_per_token_to_per_tensor_quant.py` plus the CPU `test/registered/unit/layers/moe/` suite, which includes the existing W4AFP8 dtype and post-reorder tests). ## Speed Tests and Profiling Merged `main` vs this branch, DeepEP column-major scales, timed inside a CUDA graph, variants interleaved and order-swapped (the first variant measured reads ~10% fast on sub-2 µs shapes). `rows` is live rows per expert. **8 to 56 local experts** | shape | rows | H200 | B200 | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | 7168, 8 experts | 8 / 32 / 128 | 1.08x / 1.10x / 1.13x | 0.99x / 1.18x / 1.18x | | | 512 / 1024 | 1.29x / 1.24x | 1.36x / **1.47x** | | 3584, 8 experts | 8 / 32 / 128 | 1.27x / 1.14x / 1.19x | 1.00x / 1.14x / 1.19x | | | 512 / 1024 | 1.27x / 1.07x | 1.21x / 1.23x | | 3584, 56 experts | 8 / 32 | **2.51x** / 1.93x | **2.31x** / 1.99x | | | 128 / 256 | 1.54x / 1.40x | 1.73x / 1.81x | | 1152, 8 experts | 8 / 32 / 128 | 1.10x / 1.06x / 1.13x | 1.01x / 1.05x / 1.12x | | | 512 / 1024 | 1.19x / 1.20x | 1.17x / 1.19x | **64 to 512 local experts** — where the old fixed grid hurt most (`main` µs -> branch µs, H200): | shape | rows=1 | rows=8 | rows=32 | rows=128 | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | 7168, 64 experts | 9.3 -> 1.9 (**5.0x**) | 9.6 -> 2.9 (3.3x) | 12.6 -> 6.5 (1.95x) | 45.2 -> 33.7 (1.34x) | | 7168, 128 experts | 18.1 -> 2.1 (**8.5x**) | 18.2 -> 4.3 (4.2x) | 29.8 -> 16.5 (1.81x) | 86.7 -> 62.0 (1.40x) | | 7168, 256 experts | 35.3 -> 3.4 (**10.5x**) | 35.8 -> 7.0 (5.2x) | 61.8 -> 33.8 (1.83x) | 167.0 -> 118.6 (1.41x) | | 3584, 112 experts | 9.5 -> 1.8 (5.2x) | 9.6 -> 2.7 (3.6x) | 13.2 -> 5.8 (2.27x) | 42.2 -> 29.3 (1.44x) | | 3584, 256 experts | 20.6 -> 2.2 (9.4x) | 20.8 -> 3.9 (5.3x) | 35.6 -> 16.3 (2.18x) | 90.8 -> 60.8 (1.49x) | | 3584, 512 experts | 40.3 -> 3.4 (**12.0x**) | 40.9 -> 6.7 (6.1x) | 69.8 -> 33.7 (2.07x) | — | B200 is the same shape, generally a little better at rows >= 32 (e.g. 3584/512 experts at 32 rows: 62.1 -> 21.7, **2.87x**; 7168/256 experts at 128 rows: 142.5 -> 76.1, 1.87x). The in-tree benchmark reproduces the low-expert-count end (H200, µs): ``` hidden num_experts m rows | tuned legacy 7168 8 1024 8 | 1.5698 2.2400 7168 8 1024 256 | 8.9140 11.0138 3584 56 256 8 | 2.3238 5.5467 3584 56 256 256 | 28.9774 39.4359 ``` Two things I'd flag rather than hide. The heuristic was fitted from sweeps of `m_grid ∈ {1..64}` x `g_block ∈ {8, 16, 32}` over hidden sizes 1152/3584/7168, expert counts 8 to 512 and row counts 1 to 256, on both parts; the shipped choice lands within ~0-5% of the per-cell optimum in the low-latency decode range, with a few ~10% outliers on sub-4 µs shapes at very high expert counts. And the *best* tile/warp pair is architecture-dependent at high expert counts — H200 and B200 disagree there — so the values here are the ones that win on both, and closing the remaining few percent would need autotuning rather than constants. Not covered: a multi-node end-to-end decode run. This is a kernel-level change with bitwise-equal output, so the risk is confined to performance, but the e2e number is still outstanding. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). — no user-facing behaviour or flags change. - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

signals.title: Add Cloud Agent dev environment (CPU: lint + Rust services)
signals.text:
## Summary Adds a Cursor Cloud Agent development environment for SGLang via `.cursor/environment.json` (repo-managed) + an idempotent `.cursor/install.sh`. It uses Cursor's default base image and installs everything from the install script, so merging this PR activates the environment for future Cloud Agents on `main` automatically (no dashboard Save needed). The Cloud Agent VM is CPU-only, so this environment targets the parts of SGLang that build and run without a GPU: - The contributor lint/CI toolchain (`pre-commit`), mirroring the `Lint` GitHub Actions workflow (isort, ruff, black, codespell, clang-format, nbstripout, the local lint-script unit tests, and all Rust `rustfmt`/`clippy` hooks). - The Rust workspaces: `rust/` (gRPC / multimodal / server crates) and `sgl-model-gateway/` (the router / control plane), both buildable and testable on CPU. The full CUDA serving stack (`torch==2.13.0`, flashinfer, sgl-kernel, ...) needs an NVIDIA GPU and the `lmsysorg/sglang` image, and is intentionally out of scope for this CPU environment. ## What `install.sh` does 1. Installs the system build deps the default image is missing: - `libstdc++-14-dev` — `esaxx-rs` (pulled in by the HuggingFace `tokenizers` crate) is compiled by clang, which targets the gcc-14 libstdc++ headers; the base image ships only `libstdc++-13-dev`, so `` is otherwise unresolved. - `libssl-dev` / `pkg-config` — cover any `openssl-sys` build. - `protobuf-compiler` + `libprotobuf-dev` — the gateway's `smg-grpc-client` uses `prost-build` with a system `protoc` (no vendored fallback) plus the well-known types (`google/protobuf/*.proto`). - `redis-server` — the gateway's Redis history-backend integration test spawns a local instance. 2. Installs `pre-commit` and warms all hook environments. 3. Installs a nightly `rustfmt` (used by the fmt hooks) and builds the `rust/` workspace and `sgl-model-gateway`. ## Validation Validated on the CPU VM: - `pre-commit run --all-files` — all hooks pass (Python + clang-format + Rust fmt/clippy). - `cd rust && cargo test --workspace` — 287 tests pass. - `cd sgl-model-gateway && cargo test` — 840 tests pass. - Install idempotence — re-running `install.sh` is a clean no-op (~9s). - End-to-end: launched `sgl-model-gateway`, confirmed `/liveness` returns `200 OK`, `/parse/reasoning` splits `` reasoning from the answer, and `/parse/function_call` extracts the tool call. Validated via a prebuilt environment build (fresh cold build on the default image from this branch, then verified in a fresh Cloud Agent booted from that exact build): - Build `bld-20260820-9eb4ff4e` (default image + `install.sh`, cold) — SUCCEEDED, all 5 install phases green. - Fresh Cloud Agent from that build — 6/6 checks pass: toolchains present, all gateway binaries + rust libs built, `pre-commit run --all-files` all-pass, `rust/` tests 287/0, and the gateway `/liveness` + `/parse/reasoning` e2e both return HTTP 200.

signals.title: [AMD][CI] Fix ROCm 7.0's dead apt index fail the MORI dependency install
signals.text: ## Motivation Fixes cluster **R387** from the Aug-20 AMD CI monitor report: all 27 jobs in [PR Test ROCm 7.0 (AMD) run 32399046576](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32399046576), plus the nightly-7.0 kimi-k26 job, died identically in "Install dependencies". The report filed this as pure infra needing an AMD artifactory restore. **It is also a code regression, it is specific to ROCm 7.0, and the code half is fixable here.** From the failing [job log](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32399046576/job/96522664507): ``` Err:13 http://compute-artifactory.amd.com/artifactory/list/rocm-osdb-22.04-deb compute-rocm-rel-7.0/38 amd64 Packages 404 Not Found [IP: 10.216.51.87 80] Fetched 48.0 MB in 3s (18.2 MB/s) E: Some index files failed to download. They have been ignored, or old ones used instead. ##[error]Process completed with exit code 100. ``` ### Where it came from The `apt-get update` is new. It was added on 2026-08-20 by c7478228dd (#30984, the ROCm 7.2.4 / Python 3.12 / torch 2.11 upgrade), inside a `docker exec ... bash -c` that runs under `set -euo pipefail`: ```bash git submodule update --init --recursive apt-get update apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends libgrpc++-dev 2>/dev/null || true ``` Every *other* change that PR made to this script is gated on the image flavor — the extras swap (`dev_hip` → `dev_hip_rocm724`), the AITER `torch.Stream` patch, and the AITER commit lookup all sit behind `IMAGE_STAGE_SUFFIX == "-rocm724"`. These two apt lines are the only ungated change in the PR, so a 7.2.4 fix also began running on ROCm 7.0. Before that commit the MORI reinstall did no apt work at all and was immune. ### Why only ROCm 7.0 Not because the code path is 7.0-specific — the identical path runs on 7.2.4 and passes. It is purely base-image lineage: | Flavor | Base image | `rocm-osdb` source | |---|---|---| | 7.0 | `rocm/sgl-dev:rocm7-vllm-20250904` (AMD-internal dev image) | **yes** | | 7.2.0 | `rocm/pytorch:rocm7.2_ubuntu22.04_py3.10_pytorch_release_2.9.1` | no | | 7.2.4 | `rocm/pytorch:rocm7.2.4_ubuntu24.04_py3.12_pytorch_release_2.10.0` | no | Only 7.0 builds on an AMD-internal image, which is what drags in `compute-artifactory.amd.com/.../rocm-osdb-22.04-deb`. The dead index name encodes it exactly: `compute-rocm-rel-7.0/38` is the internal ROCm 7.0 release channel, build 38. Confirmed against a real 7.2.4 job from the same day ([96420374950](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32367546070/job/96420374950)), which runs the same MORI reinstall and the same `apt-get update`, and succeeds. Its apt hosts are entirely public — `apt.llvm.org`, `archive.ubuntu.com`, `packages.broadcom.com`, `ppa.launchpadcontent.net`, `repo.radeon.com` — with no `compute-artifactory.amd.com` entry, so it fetches 40.1 MB cleanly and reaches `[MORI] Done.` ### Why it deserves a code fix rather than only an artifactory restore Three things stand out about the failure: 1. **We neither own nor install from the failing source.** Nothing in this repo references `rocm-osdb`; it is inherited from the base image. Every index we actually use fetched fine (48 MB, including Ubuntu main and universe). 2. **apt itself treated it as recoverable** — "They have been ignored, or old ones used instead" — but still exits 100, because `apt-get update` returns non-zero if *any* index fails. Under `set -e` that is fatal. 3. **The package it feeds is optional.** `rocm.Dockerfile` builds MORI without `libgrpc++-dev` on every flavor, and the install was already best-effort (`|| true`). So one dead third-party index, for a package we do not need, zeroed a whole workflow. "Rerun once the artifactory recovers" also only holds until the next ROCm 7.0 internal build rotates out. ## Modifications **`scripts/ci/amd/amd_ci_install_dependency.sh`** — make both apt steps non-fatal, and log which one degraded: ```bash apt-get update || echo '[MORI] apt-get update reported errors; continuing with the indexes it did fetch' apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends libgrpc++-dev || echo '[MORI] libgrpc++-dev unavailable; building MORI without it' ``` Dropping `2>/dev/null` in favour of an explicit message keeps the reason for a degraded install visible instead of swallowing it. No retry logic is added: the image already sets `Acquire::Retries "5"` via `/etc/apt/apt.conf.d/80-net-hardening` (visible in the log as the repeated `Ign:13` attempts), and a 404 is not retryable. This was the only unguarded `apt-get update` left in the AMD CI path; every other one under `scripts/ci/` is already `|| true` or wrapped in a retry loop, matching `scripts/ci/cuda/ci_install_dependency.sh`. The guard is deliberately applied to all flavors rather than scoped to 7.0. 7.2.0 and 7.2.4 are public images today, but the invariant we want is that no optional apt call can zero a workflow, on any image. A reviewer who prefers to also restore the pre-#30984 behaviour on 7.0/7.2.0 could additionally gate these two lines on `IMAGE_STAGE_SUFFIX == "-rocm724"`, matching the rest of #30984 — happy to add that if wanted. **`test/registered/unit/tools/test_amd_ci_install_dependency.py`** — a 45-line guard asserting that no `apt-get` call in this script can abort the run. It runs on `base-a-test-cpu` (no docker, no ROCm, no GPU) alongside the existing CI-tooling tests in `test/registered/unit/tools/`. This carries more weight than it looks, because **no pull-request-triggered workflow can catch this regression**. `pr-test-amd.yml` (ROCm 7.0) was demoted to a daily shadow in #34204 and now has only `schedule` / `workflow_dispatch` / `workflow_call` triggers — no `pull_request`. The PR gate is `pr-test-amd-rocm720.yml`, which defaults to `rocm724`. So the image that carries the dead index is never exercised pre-merge, and the static check is the only pre-merge signal on this invariant. ## Accuracy Tests Not applicable — CI dependency-install script and its test only; no runtime or model code touched. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Not applicable. ## Verification The test fails against the pre-fix script, naming the offending line, and passes against the fix: ``` # against origin/main's script AssertionError: Lists differ: ['apt-get update'] != [] # against this branch 1 passed ``` While developing the fix I also replayed the incident end to end — a stub `apt-get` reproducing the 404 and exit 100, driving the apt lines extracted from the script inside the same `set -euo pipefail` context — and confirmed the MORI build that follows is still reached, both when `libgrpc++-dev` remains resolvable and when it does not, with no regression on the healthy path. That harness is not checked in: once the line reads `... || echo`, it mostly asserts that `||` suppresses `set -e`, and it required string-parsing the `docker exec` block out of the script, which would break on unrelated edits. Also run: the full `test/registered/unit/tools/` directory (12 passed), `run_suite.py` collection with `sanity_check=True` plus `validate_all_suites` over all registered files (clean; the new test resolves into `base-a-test-cpu`), `shellcheck -S warning` on the script (no new findings — the only diff versus `main` is a line-number shift on a pre-existing `SC2034`), `bash -n`, `black`, `isort`, `ruff`, `codespell`, and the `check-registered-tests` / `check-no-bare-pytest-main` lint hooks. **Note for reviewers:** this PR's own AMD CI cannot reproduce R387, for the trigger reason above — it runs 7.2.4, whose public base has no `rocm-osdb` source. In-situ validation needs the daily `pr-test-amd.yml` cron (17:30 UTC) or a manual `workflow_dispatch` of it. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). — n/a. - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). — n/a. - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process). 2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers. 3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:no_entry_sign: [Run #32427680934](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32427680934)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32427680717](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32427680717)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32427680846](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32427680846)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: Avoid MAX_LEN padding for prefill BCG when a DP rank is idle
signals.text: Under MAX_LEN a zero-token rank fabricates a dummy EXTEND request whose tokens are counted as real (deliberately, to avoid starving the MoE all-to-all), so they bypass the dispatch mask and enter the shared EP grouped GEMMs. The changed per-expert batch sizes perturb live requests' logits nondeterministically (up to 0.21 nats measured). Fall back to SUM_LEN (eager prefill) for idle-rank steps and re-enable the determinism test that was skipped for this bug. ## Motivation & Modifications Adds a fix to avoid breakable prefill cuda graph replay with DP attention where at least one rank has zero tokens. Follows the chain of #30898, #31125, #31487, #31705. When using breakable cuda graphs + DP attention for prefill, we pad data to match the expected replay graph shape for collective ops under MAX_LEN mode. A mask will keep track of which tokens are non-padded. However, when a rank is idle, we fabricate a request set to max_len and set `num_token_non_padded` to this max_len (see comment [here](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/f3beb2c52903ad77202a1e307017996d1ada22a1/python/sglang/srt/model_executor/forward_batch_info.py#L1465-L1470) explaining why). This seems to perturb downstream MoE operations for live ranks and ultimately corrupt the resulting logits. The solution is to check for an idle rank and not enable MAX_LEN mode in this case. Under the current logic, this will hence run eagerly instead of with BCG. Also Re-enables the determinism test skipped in #31125. It seems like this failsafe already [exists](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/54c44fef73e784a1390308d7cc3732d635244a8d/python/sglang/srt/model_executor/runner/prefill_cuda_graph_runner.py#L743-L752) but doesn't function as intended because of how `global_num_tokens_cpu` is re-written after padding by `prepare_mlp_sync_batch` under MAX_LEN mode (see below): https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/f3beb2c52903ad77202a1e307017996d1ada22a1/python/sglang/srt/model_executor/forward_batch_info.py#L1373 and https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/f3beb2c52903ad77202a1e307017996d1ada22a1/python/sglang/srt/model_executor/forward_batch_info.py#L1494 ## Additional Explanation (from Claude) Two different kinds of padding result: - A rank with fewer tokens than the max appends **pad token rows**. These are masked out of MoE dispatch (`topk_ids[i >= num_token_non_padded] = -1`) and excluded from attention output. Harmless. - A rank with **zero** tokens has no request to pad, so it **fabricates a dummy EXTEND request** -- and then deliberately counts its tokens as real (`num_token_non_padded.fill_(num_tokens)`), because a rank contributing zero tokens to the MoE all-to-all starves the EP layers (see the comment at the fill site). The dummy's tokens therefore bypass the dispatch mask and enter the shared DeepEP expert buffers alongside every other rank's real tokens. ## Why unmasked dummy tokens perturb OTHER requests' logits Per-token MoE math is independent in exact arithmetic; the coupling is numerical, and it compounds: 1. **Dummy tokens change each expert's batch size.** Expert parallelism physically groups tokens from all DP ranks by expert into shared buffers and runs one grouped GEMM per expert segment. Dispatched dummy tokens occupy rows in those segments, so the per-expert token counts (the M dimensions of the grouped GEMM) differ from the no-dummy execution. 2. **GEMM outputs are not batch-size-invariant.** deep_gemm/grouped kernels pick tilings, split strategies, and accumulation orders as a function of segment sizes. A real token's output row is mathematically identical under any order, but in FP8/BF16 the floating-point sum differs at the last-bits level when the reduction order changes. (This is the ordinary reason temp-0 outputs vary with batch composition; masked padding does NOT trigger it precisely because masked rows are never dispatched.) 3. **MoE routing turns tiny noise into discrete divergence.** The router is a top-k over expert scores: a last-bits perturbation flips the expert choice of any real token near a top-k boundary. A flipped token computes through a different expert -- a macroscopically different value -- and feeds the next layer. Over ~60 MoE layers these flips compound. 4. **The dummy content itself varies run to run** (fabricated request state is not derived from any real workload), so its routing -- and hence the perturbation pattern of steps 1-3 -- differs per run: nondeterminism, not just bias. Measured effect: around 0.21 nats on live tokens' output logprobs (a ~23% probability change; reduction-order noise alone is ~1e-6), enough to flip greedy argmax mid-generation. Up to 0.459 on DSv4-Pro. The #31125 skip message reached the same conclusion ("its hidden states vary run to run and perturb real tokens' logits through the shared EP grouped GEMMs"); this PR fixes the cause instead of skipping the test. Severity depends on the attention backend only in degree: FlashMLA shows nondeterministic-but-plausible outputs; the trtllm DSV4 backend (PR #30805) showed reliably EMPTY generations under the same mechanism, which is how it resurfaced. ## Evidence Protocol: same prompt 8 times at temperature 0, one request at a time (so peer DP ranks are idle during each prefill), `/flush_cache` between runs so every run re-prefills. A correct server is bit-deterministic here. Recipe = the BCG CI class (DeepSeek-V4-Flash, tp4 dp4, DeepEP, breakable prefill graphs), default FlashMLA backend, clean sgl-project main (b956e916ae) -- no trtllm code involved. | Run | Configuration | Distinct outputs | First divergence | Max delta logprob (shared prefix) | |-----|---------------|------------------|------------------|-----------------------------------| | 1 | clean main | 2 / 8 | token 45 | 0.206 | | 2 | clean main + this gate (only change) | 1 / 8 (bit-identical) | none | 0.000000 | | 3 | clean main (gate absent), DeepSeek-V4-Pro tp8 dp2 (model generality) | 4 / 8 | token 5 | 0.459 | Run 1 proves the bug on the default backend on upstream main; run 2 proves this one-line gate eliminates it; run 3 shows it is not model-specific. Repro scripts: `idle_probe.py`, `launch_idle_repro.sh` (this directory). ## Cost, and the path to keeping BCG on idle-rank steps The gate does NOT disable BCG+DP globally: steps where every rank has real tokens keep MAX_LEN and the breakable graph. Only steps where some rank is idle fall back to SUM_LEN (eager prefill). At high load idle ranks are rare; the affected regime is low-concurrency traffic. The root enabler of the bug is that a zero-token rank cannot currently participate safely in the MoE all-to-all, which is why the fabricated tokens were unmasked in the first place. The follow-up that would restore BCG for idle-rank steps is: make zero-token (or fully-masked) ranks safe in the dispatch/combine path, then keep the dummy request but MASK its tokens like ordinary padding (`num_token_non_padded = 0`) -- restoring the invariant that batch composition seen by the experts is a pure function of the real workload. Until then, this gate trades a graph replay on rare idle-rank steps for correct and deterministic logits. ## Accuracy Tests Local validation on 4x B200 (`python -m unittest test_deepseek_v4_flash_fp4_b200.<Class>`): | Class | Result | GSM8K | Spec accept len | |---|---|---|---| | TestDSV4FlashFP4B200 (LowLatency, TP4+MTP) | OK (9 tests) | 0.98 | 2.77 | | TestDSV4FlashFP4B200Balanced (MTP+DP4) | OK (9 tests) | 0.97 | 1.95 | | TestDSV4FlashFP4NonMTPB200 (DP4) | OK (8 tests) | 0.975 | n/a | | TestDSV4FlashFP4BreakableCudaGraphB200 (DP4+BCG, the fix's target) | OK (8 tests, 1 pre-existing skip) | 0.97 | n/a | ## Speed Tests and Profiling <!-- If this pull request impacts inference speed, provide benchmarking and profiling results. --> ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process). 2. signals.title: Fix Prometheus name[] filtering for multiprocess metrics
signals.text: ## Motivation Closes #35752. Upper-layer schedulers and resource managers such as llm-d and AIBrix may request only selected SGLang metrics from `/metrics` using repeated `name[]` query parameters. In multiprocess mode, SGLang's Prometheus registry could omit `MultiProcessCollector` during restricted collection, causing filtered requests to return no SGLang samples even though unfiltered scrapes work. This PR preserves upstream `prometheus_client` name-based filtering behavior for SGLang multiprocess metrics. ## Modifications - Bump the minimum `prometheus-client` version from `0.20.0` to `0.25.0` across package variants. - Create the metrics registry with `CollectorRegistry(support_collectors_without_names=True)` so restricted registries can still include multiprocess collectors. - Add registered observability coverage for `/metrics?name[]=...` requests, verifying that only the requested SGLang metric names are returned. ## Accuracy Tests N/A. This change only affects Prometheus metrics exposition and does not affect model outputs. ## Speed Tests and Profiling N/A. signals.title: Fix buffer-mode HiCache load-back ownership races; add optional prefetch anchor lock
signals.text: # Fix buffer-mode HiCache load-back ownership races; add optional prefetch anchor lock ## Motivation In buffer-only host memory mode, `init_load_back` consumes a staged storage prefetch by allocating device slots, queueing a layer-gated H2D transfer, and then inserting the span into the radix tree. The insert is what adjudicates slot ownership — and it ran *after* the transfer was already in flight. If the tree gained an overlapping span while the fetch was held — a concurrent request publishing the same prefix between staging and consumption, or live full-KV sitting under an SWA tombstone (invisible to the unified match length but still deduped against by the insert walk) — the insert freed the very slots the in-flight copy targeted: a queued use-after-free. Reallocation of those slots produced silent KV corruption and downstream allocator faults. ## Changes 1. **Ownership pre-check (always on):** before launching the transfer, re-match against live tree state and require both the unified match length and `full_kv_hit_length` to equal the staged `matched_len`. This proves the insert can only add nodes, never dedup-free the incoming slots. Invalid holds drop with a warning and the request recomputes. 2. **Post-insert fail-stop:** if the post-insert canonical tree slice diverges from the incoming slots, raise instead of returning indices that a queued transfer no longer owns. 3. **Canonical ownership:** return the post-insert tree slice rather than the raw allocation. 4. **Optional anchor lock (env-gated, default off):** `SGLANG_ENABLE_HICACHE_BUFFER_ANCHOR_LOCK=1` pins the staged prefetch's device anchor from IO commit to consumption so eviction cannot invalidate the splice and waste the fetch. Locked tokens are capped at `SGLANG_HICACHE_BUFFER_ANCHOR_LOCK_CAP` × the device pool (default 0.5); over-cap holds launch unlocked, so queued holds can never make the pool unevictable. Locks are released idempotently at every consume/drop/abort exit, with a fail-loud accounting assert. ## Testing - Three regression tests covering the race class: sibling-published span (unified drift), full-KV overlap masked by an SWA tombstone (only `full_kv_hit_length` can see it), and the post-insert fail-stop. All three fail on the pre-fix code and pass with the fix. - Full `test_unified_radix_cache_unittest.py` passes. - Verified in an extended production-shaped soak on an internal deployment (buffer-only mode with a storage backend): the ownership checks drop conflicting holds cleanly under concurrent same-prefix traffic, the anchor lock eliminates eviction-caused prefetch waste in steady and moderate-churn regimes, and the lock accounting stayed exact across many engine restarts. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32434867464](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32434867464)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32434867293](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32434867293)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #32434867408](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32434867408)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [AMD] Optimize Kimi-K3 Triton MLA prefill on gfx950
signals.text: ## Motivation Kimi-K3 uses two attention representations during prefill at TP8 on MI355X: - Fresh/zero-prefix MHA: 12 heads with QK/V dimensions 192/128. - Cached-prefix absorbed MLA: 12 query heads, one KV head, and QK/V dimensions 576/512. Current Triton prefill leaves performance on the table for both shapes: 1. The exact K3 kernels use one pipeline stage and natural-exponential online softmax. 2. Absorbed 576/512 prefill processes one full 512-wide value accumulator, increasing register pressure. 3. FP8 cached-prefix P·V can underflow small softmax probabilities. 4. Aiter supports native FP8 zero-prefix prefill, but Triton lacks an equivalent opt-in path. ## Changes ### K3 prefill tuning - Use two pipeline stages for exact gfx950 K3 192/128 and N32 576/512 prefill kernels. - Fold `log2(e)` into the attention scale and use `exp2` for unmodified K3 logits. - Convert stored LSE back to natural-log units. - Preserve current compact ragged-grid scheduling and the generic Triton-3.7 fallback. ### 4×128 absorbed MLA kernel Add a dedicated split-dimension kernel for cached-prefix K3 MLA: ```text Q/K latent: 4 × 128 Q/K tail: 64 V/output: 4 × 128 ``` The kernel maintains one online-softmax state and four independent FP32 value accumulators before concatenating the normalized 128-wide outputs. Dispatch is restricted to: - gfx950; - 12 query heads and one KV head; - QK/V dimensions 576/512; - BF16 current Q/K/V and output; - BF16 cached prefix with unit scales, or opt-in FP8 cached prefix with supported descales; - causal attention; - page size 1; - contiguous last dimensions; - no custom mask, sliding window, logit cap, XAI temperature, sink, LSE, score modifier, auxiliary tensor, or skipped stage. Unsupported calls immediately use the existing generic kernel. ### FP8 prefill Add: ```bash SGLANG_TRITON_FP8_PREFILL_ATTN=1 ``` This is enabled by default. Set `SGLANG_TRITON_FP8_PREFILL_ATTN=0` to disable native FP8 prefill. On exact K3 gfx950 shapes: - Zero-prefix 192/128 Q/K/V are cast from BF16 to FP8 before launch, matching Aiter behavior. - Absorbed 576/512 prefill keeps current-chunk Q/K/V in BF16 while using the FP8 cached prefix. - Softmax probabilities are multiplied by `FP8_MAX` before FP8 P·V and the accumulator contribution is divided by the same factor. - Non-unit cached-prefix K/V descales are supported. The default-on path achieved 98% GSM8K accuracy in model-level validation. ## Performance MI355X measurements used a device warmup and HIP-graph replay. Against unmodified current main: | K3 prefill case | Current main | This change | Speedup | |---|---:|---:|---:| | Zero-prefix BF16, 8K | 0.726 ms | 0.415 ms | 1.75× | | Zero-prefix FP8, 8K, casts included | 0.726 ms | 0.420 ms | 1.73× | | Absorbed BF16, 8K prefix + 8K extend | 8.658 ms | 4.133 ms | 2.09× | | Absorbed FP8, 8K prefix + 8K extend | 6.770 ms | 3.687 ms | 1.84× | FP8 zero-prefix compared with the optimized BF16 path: | Length | BF16 | FP8, casts included | Result | |---:|---:|---:|---:| | 8K | 0.414 ms | 0.421 ms | No difference | | 16K | 1.500 ms | 1.400 ms | FP8 1.07× faster | | 32K | 6.255 ms | 5.145 ms | FP8 1.22× faster | The default-on policy intentionally follows Aiter and enables native FP8 at every length despite the small 8K crossover loss. ### End-to-end serving Throughput uplift is computed as the geometric mean of the per-concurrency ratios at concurrency 2, 4, 8, and 16. Kimi-K3 TP8, ISL/OSL 8192/1024: | Concurrency | Baseline tok/s | This change tok/s | Uplift | |---:|---:|---:|---:| | 2 | 874.18 | 879.54 | +0.6% | | 4 | 1529.69 | 1586.17 | +3.7% | | 8 | 2554.27 | 2586.82 | +1.3% | | 16 | 3892.75 | 3940.95 | +1.2% | | **Geomean** | — | — | **+1.70%** | Kimi-K3 TP8, ISL/OSL 68K/350: | Concurrency | Baseline tok/s | This change tok/s | Uplift | |---:|---:|---:|---:| | 2 | 6092.96 | 6910.34 | +13.4% | | 4 | 7060.28 | 8185.23 | +15.9% | | 8 | 7655.63 | 9017.19 | +17.8% | | 16 | 7973.53 | 9540.03 | +19.6% | | **Geomean** | — | — | **+16.67%** | The long-context gain is predominantly improved prefill/TTFT; median ITL is effectively unchanged in both comparisons. ## Numerics - BF16 absorbed split versus current-main generic output: relative L2 approximately `9.5e-5`. - FP8 absorbed split versus the corrected generic FP8 path: relative L2 approximately `6.6e-5`. - Zero-prefix FP8 versus BF16: relative L2 approximately 3.4-3.5%. - Kimi-K3 model-level GSM8K accuracy with FP8 prefill enabled: 98%. Additional long-context logits and workload validation remain recommended. ## Platform scope All specialized execution paths require gfx950 and exact K3 shapes. On NVIDIA and other AMD architectures: - the split-dimension dispatcher returns false; - FP8 Q/K/V casting is disabled; - FP8 probability scaling is disabled; - K3 `exp2` and two-stage specializations are disabled; - existing generic attention behavior remains active. ## Validation - Ruff 0.15.1 passed with the repository's configured rule selection. - Black 26.1.0 passed. - Isort 7.0.0 passed. - `git diff --check` passed. - Kimi-K3 GSM8K accuracy with FP8 prefill enabled: 98%. - Four focused K3 BF16/FP8 parity and dispatch tests pass on gfx950. - The focused kernel tests are registered in the per-PR `stage-b-test-1-gpu-small-amd-mi35x` suite. - Generic Triton-3.7 fallback tests passed after the final gfx950-only gate. Recommended E2E matrix: - ISL/OSL 8192/1024 and 68000/350; - concurrency 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, and 64; - BF16 and FP8 KV cache; - flag off/on with identical prompts, seeds, request counts, and cache state; - model-level accuracy and logits comparison. ## Files changed ```text python/sglang/kernels/ops/attention/extend_attention.py python/sglang/kernels/ops/attention/extend_attention_split_dim.py python/sglang/srt/environ.py test/registered/unit/layers/attention/test_triton_mla_prefill_gfx950.py ``` <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:no_entry_sign: [Run #32434478524](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32434478524)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32434478563](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32434478563)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #32434478698](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32434478698)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [GDN] remove XPU path of causal_conv1d_fn and causal_conv1d_update
signals.text: <!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. --> ## Motivation Fix https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/34720. There will be two backend for linear attention on XPU: triton and intel_xpu. Our plan: For the triton backend, we always use triton kernels. That means we need to remove the standalong SYCL conv1d kernel from SGLang. signals.title: [Kimi K3] Exclude template-rendered response_format tokens from billed prompt_tokens
signals.text: ## Problem For Kimi K3, requests with `response_format` report inflated `usage.prompt_tokens`. A vendor conformance run measured **186 vs the reference API's 119** for the same request, breaking billing alignment with the official K3 API. Root cause: `_encode_messages` (kimi_k3 branch) passes `response_format` into the checkpoint's chat template, which renders the JSON schema plus wrapper instructions into the prompt. Those tokens land in `origin_input_ids` and are counted as prompt tokens. The grammar/constraint path adds zero prompt tokens — the inflation comes solely from the template render. ## What this PR does - In the kimi_k3 encoder, when `response_format` is present, render the template once more without the `response_format` kwarg and record the token-count delta on the request (`_response_format_prompt_tokens`). Measuring the diff is robust to whatever wrapper the checkpoint template adds — no hardcoded schema-length math. - `_reported_prompt_tokens` subtracts that count alongside the existing `_KIMI_K3_GENERATION_STUB_TOKENS` adjustment, so billed/reported prompt tokens match the reference API with and without `response_format`. Cost: one extra CPU-side template render per response_format request; no behavior change for other models or for requests without `response_format`. ## Tests `test_kimi_k3_response_format_tokens_not_billed` — mocks the two renders (186 with the schema block, 119 baseline), asserts the measured delta (67) is excluded from reported prompt tokens and that requests without `response_format` keep the existing stub-only adjustment. Also updated `test_kimi_k3_encoder_receives_wire_request_fields` for the extra baseline render. ``` $ pytest test/registered/unit/entrypoints/openai/test_serving_chat.py test/registered/unit/entrypoints/openai/test_protocol.py 155 passed ``` ## Known gap (pre-existing, not made worse by this PR) `/v1/responses` (`serving_responses.py`) reads `prompt_tokens` from meta_info directly and does not go through `_reported_prompt_tokens`, so neither this adjustment nor the existing 3-token generation-stub adjustment applies there. K3 vendor conformance is chat-completions-only, so this is out of scope here; flagging for a follow-up if Responses API billing parity is ever needed. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #32439564964](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32439564964)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32439564942](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32439564942)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #32439564948](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32439564948)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: Extend dLLM volatile-block cache fix (#35270) to swa/mamba/unified/cpp radix caches
signals.text: ## Motivation #35470 fixed a KV-pool accounting bug in `RadixCache.cache_unfinished_req`: a dLLM request's in-flight denoise block is rewritten in full on every step (`dllm_incomplete_ids`), and since `_dllm_page_size` pins `page_size` to the dLLM block size, that block is a whole trailing page of the radix key. Caching it makes the next step's key diverge at the block boundary, which drives the prefix match below `cache_protected_len`, inverts the `free_segment` slice (freeing nothing), and leaves the tree owning two nodes for the same physical pages — inflating `evictable_size()` past what the pool holds and tripping the idle pool-invariant check (#35270). The fix there was `req.get_fill_ids()` → `req.get_cacheable_fill_ids()` (added via `ReqDllmMixin`), scoped to `RadixCache` only. The PR author flagged in review notes that `SWARadixCache`, `MambaRadixCache`, `UnifiedRadixCache`, and `RadixCacheCpp` all call `req.get_fill_ids()` at the identical point in their own `cache_unfinished_req`, carrying the same latent assumption, but left them out to keep that PR scoped and because dLLM doesn't exercise those caches today. This PR applies the same one-line substitution to all four, so the fix is consistent across every radix-cache implementation rather than leaving three latent instances of the same bug for whenever dLLM is combined with SWA, Mamba, the unified cache, or the experimental C++ tree. ## Change Same substitution in each `cache_unfinished_req`, same explanatory comment as #35470: - `python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/mamba_radix_cache.py` - `python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/radix_cache_cpp.py` - `python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/swa_radix_cache.py` - `python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/unified_radix_cache.py` No other call sites feed the cached radix key in any of these files. ## Tests None added here. I checked whether the same CPU-only regression-test pattern from #35470 (`test_radix_cache_dllm_volatile_block.py`, built on `MHATokenToKVPool` + `PagedTokenToKVPoolAllocator` on `device="cpu"`) could be replicated for these four, but: - `SWARadixCache`, `MambaRadixCache`, and `UnifiedRadixCache`'s own unit-test suites are all `register_cuda_ci`/`register_amd_ci` and build their pools via `get_device()` — there's no established CPU-backed fixture for them in this repo today. - `RadixCacheCpp` has no unit-test harness at all; it wraps the C++-bound tree and isn't importable without the compiled `sgl_kernel` extension. I don't have GPU access, so I didn't want to fabricate new pool fixtures for three different subsystems that I have no way to actually run. Happy to add coverage if a maintainer points me at (or already has) a CPU-safe way to construct these, or this can be left to existing CI. ## Depends on #35470 — this branch is rebased on `main` with #35470's single commit (`1f05bc6`) cherry-picked in for buildability (`get_cacheable_fill_ids` doesn't exist on `main` yet). Once #35470 merges, I'll rebase this PR and the diff will collapse to just the 4 files above. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32439851629](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32439851629)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32439851561](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32439851561)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32439851637](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32439851637)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [Router] Add abort_request fan-out support
signals.text: ## Summary Add an `/abort_request` endpoint to the SGLang router. The router does not currently track which worker owns a particular request ID. To ensure that an abort reaches the correct worker, the endpoint forwards the original request body to every registered worker. Workers that do not own the request can safely treat it as a no-op. ## Changes - Add `POST /abort_request` to the router. - Forward the original JSON request body to all registered workers. - Preserve the `application/json` content type when forwarding requests. - Limit concurrent worker requests to avoid unbounded fan-out. - Handle plain, prefill, and decode workers consistently. - Return a per-worker success and failure breakdown. - Return `502 Bad Gateway` when one or more workers cannot process the request. - Add coverage for successful fan-out, partial failures, unreachable workers, trailing-slash URLs, empty registries, mixed worker modes, and request-body forwarding. ## Testing - Verified the patch with `git diff --check`. - Rust tests could not be executed locally because the Rust toolchain is not available in the current environment. Fixes #6531 ## AI Assistance OpenAI Codex assisted with the implementation and test preparation. I reviewed the proposed behavior and code changes and take responsibility for the contribution. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #32440106002](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32440106002)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32440105893](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32440105893)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:heavy_minus_sign: **No AMD PR run found for this commit**.<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [Simulator] Add high-fidelity CPU-based inference simulator
signal.text: ## Motivation This PR introduces SGLang Simulator, a CPU-based inference simulator for evaluating SGLang scheduling, latency, throughput, and prefix-cache behavior without loading model weights or executing model kernels. It is a current-main rework of the simulator prototype in [#22250](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/22250), while retaining SGLang v0.5.16 as the tested compatibility floor. Large-scale inference configuration studies are expensive to run directly on accelerators. SGLang Simulator reuses the real SGLang scheduler, radix cache, hierarchical cache, and request lifecycle, while replacing model-forward execution with a latency predictor. It supports measured traces, synthetic workloads, and both in-process and HTTP serving workflows. ## What This PR Adds - Add `tools/sglang-simulator` as a monorepo component. - Reuse the SGLang scheduler, cache allocator, radix cache, hierarchical cache, and request lifecycle with dummy model weights and a minimal KV allocation. - Add three forward-latency predictors: - AIConfigurator; - an sklearn-compatible ML predictor; - batch-composition replay. - Support Random, ShareGPT, and timestamped Autobench workloads. - Support direct Python execution through `SGLangBenchmarkRunner`. - Support server and benchmark-client execution through the HTTP serving path. - Collect request, latency, throughput, prefix-cache, cache-tier, and predictor metrics. - Add reusable example configurations, workloads, tokenizer assets, and replay fixtures. - Add compatibility checks for SGLang launch and serving APIs. - Run the simulator regression suite from CPU PR CI when `tools/sglang-simulator` changes. ## Simulation Modes The simulator provides two execution modes: - `OFFLINE`: advances a logical clock without sleeping, intended for fast configuration and workload studies. - `BLOCKING`: sleeps for predicted forward latency and visible L2-to-L1 load latency, intended for serving-path and timing-semantics validation. Replay replaces model-forward latency only. CPU preprocessing and postprocessing overhead remain enabled by default. For `OFFLINE` runs, latency, throughput, and duration should be read from the server-side simulator metrics rather than benchmark-client wall-clock time. ## Accuracy Validation The following results compare simulator output with measured serving traces. Latency, throughput, and duration values are absolute percentage errors. Prefix reuse is reported as absolute percentage-point error. The `SGLang baseline` column identifies the version used by the real service that produced the measurement trace. | Model | SGLang baseline | Hardware | Predictor / coverage | TTFT | TPOT | ITL | Input throughput | Duration | Prefix reuse | |:---|:---:|:---:|:---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | Qwen3-8B | v0.5.9 | H20 | AIConfigurator; no-cache, L1, and L2 cases | 2.38–4.15% | 1.64–4.05% | 1.78–4.07% | 1.41–2.40% | 1.39–2.33% | 0.00–0.04 pp | | Qwen3-32B-FP8 | v0.5.9 | H20 | AIConfigurator; no-cache, L1, and L2 cases | 2.40–3.05% | 0.58–1.11% | 0.52–1.02% | 0.52–1.13% | 0.51–1.12% | 0.00–0.04 pp | | GLM-5.1-FP8 | v0.5.11 | GPU | ML; L1 and L2 cases | 5.27% | N/A | N/A | 1.11% | 1.08% | 0.028 pp | | DeepSeek-V4-Pro | v0.5.11 | GPU | ML; L1 and L2 cases | 6.12% | N/A | N/A | 0.23% | 0.22% | 0.048 pp | | DeepSeek-V4-Flash | v0.5.16 | GPU | ML; L1 case | 0.786–1.343% | N/A | N/A | 0.000212% | 0.000212% | 0.000 pp | TPOT and ITL are not applicable to the GLM-5.1-FP8, DeepSeek-V4-Pro, and DeepSeek-V4-Flash validation traces because they use one-token outputs(Prefill-Decode Disaggregation). Prefix-cache accuracy is particularly sensitive to `max_total_tokens`. This value determines simulated device KV-cache capacity and also affects hierarchical host-cache sizing and eviction behavior. signal.title: [Feature] Optimize AR and DiT overlap for GLM-Image dynamic batching
signal.text: ## Motivation This PR adds AR/DiT overlap to accelerate GLM-Image generation. This reduces the 10-prompt, concurrency-4 benchmark duration from about 223.79 to 182.39s, an **end-to-end improvement of roughly 18.4%.** By default, the overlap mode is disabled, so the existing execution behavior is unchanged: `--ar-dit-overlap-mode off` Users can explicitly enable it with: `--ar-dit-overlap-mode on`. When enabled, the scheduler can prefetch AR outputs for the next compatible request batch while the current DiT requests are being executed sequentially. This helps keep the DiT device fed in 1-AR / 1-DiT separated deployments and reduces idle time under higher concurrency. GLM-Image supports AR/DiT separation with external AR serving and native grouped requests. The original execution pattern is: ```text AR(batch N) -> DiT(req 1) -> DiT(req 2) -> ... -> DiT(req N) -> next AR(batch) ``` This batches the AR stage correctly, but the **next AR batch is only dispatched after all DiT requests in the current batch finish.** In a 1 AR + 1 DiT deployment, DiT runs sequentially on one device and becomes the throughput bottleneck. If AR is not prefetched while DiT is running, the DiT device has to wait for the next AR batch, creating pipeline bubbles. This PR changes the execution pattern to overlap external AR prefetch with sequential DiT execution: ``` AR(batch N) -> DiT(req 1), while prefetching next AR batch -> DiT(req 2) -> ... -> consume prefetched requests ``` The goal is to keep the DiT device fed with prepared AR tokens and reduce idle time in the separated AR/DiT deployment. # Modifications - Add an explicit supports_async_ar_prefetch() pipeline capability. - Enable async AR prefetch only for GLM-Image with an external SRT encoder URL. - Add a GLM-Image-specific async AR prefetch path instead of using the generic grouped pipeline executor from a background thread. - Prefetch AR tokens on CPU while sequential DiT execution is running. - Prefer already-prefetched requests before falling back to normal dynamic dispatch. - Add unit coverage for grouped and single-request GLM-Image external AR prefetch paths. # Accuracy Tests | model | LongText-Bench ZH | |---|---:| | GLM-Image (Official) | 0.9788 | | GLM-Image (AR & Dit Overlap) | **0.9803** | And run unit test: ``` PYTHONPATH=python python3 python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/unit/test_glm_image_ar.py ``` Result: ``` Passed ``` # Speed Tests and Profiling Server start command ``` export HCCL_IF_BASE_PORT=25000 export HCCL_HOST_SOCKET_PORT_RANGE="25000-25199" export HCCL_NPU_SOCKET_PORT_RANGE="25200-25399" export ASCEND_RT_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 --enable-multimodal \ --cuda-graph-max-bs 8 \ --device npu \ --attention-backend ascend \ --disable-fast-image-processor export SGLANG_CACHE_DIT_FN=2 export SGLANG_CACHE_DIT_BN=1 export SGLANG_CACHE_DIT_WARMUP=4 export SGLANG_CACHE_DIT_RDT=0.4 export SGLANG_CACHE_DIT_MC=4 export SGLANG_CACHE_DIT_TAYLORSEER=true export SGLANG_CACHE_DIT_TS_ORDER=2 export SGLANG_CACHE_DIT_ENABLED=true Instead, each layer calls `rotary_emb.get_cos_sin_with_position` to compute its own RoPE cos/sin, then runs the fused `split_qkv_rmsnorm_rope` op for QKV split + RMSNorm + RoPE. - **Fix hybrid SWA decode accuracy** (`ascend_backend.py`): Tighten the FIA v2 entry condition to `self.is_hybrid_swa and self.use_fia`, and add a `BSND`-layout path for SWA-layer decode — using the static `swa_mask` to encode the sliding window (since decode has `S1=1`, the kernel ignores `pre_tokens`), while other layers still use the `TND` path with `pre_tokens` and the fixed 2048-wide causal mask. - **Align graph-replay CPU input attribute name** (`npu_graph_runner.py`): Add a branch in `_get_update_attr_name` so that the `use_fia + hybrid SWA + MHA` combination (i.e. Mellum running with FIA on NPU) returns the v2 kernel's parameter name `actual_seq_kvlen`, keeping the graph-replay seq-len key consistent with the `npu_fused_infer_attention_score_v2` formal parameter actually consumed in the forward pass (v1 kernel uses `actual_seq_lengths_kv`; v2 uses `actual_seq_kvlen`). signal.title: [MoonEP] Kimi-K3 production integration roadmap
signal.text: ## Goal Track the work required to take MoonEP support for Kimi-K3 from the merged BF16 correctness PoC to a reproducible, tested, and performance-validated production integration. This is the dedicated MoonEP roadmap under the broader Kimi-K3 roadmap in #32607. ## Current status (2026-08-21) - The BF16 integration seam and correctness PoC were merged into the `moonep` branch in #33249. - #34874 is the production-path candidate for MXFP4 experts in symmetric memory using the DeepGEMM runner. It reports end-to-end Kimi-K3 validation on 4x GB200 with TP16/EP16, but is currently open and needs to be rebased onto the merged `moonep` branch. - The compatible generalized MoonEP prefetch/local-first API is being developed in MoonshotAI/MoonEP#32. - The original fork-side PoC map is wirybeaver/sglang#7. ## Completed: BF16 PoC and integration seam - [x] Research the SGLang DeepEP seam and MoonEP dispatch/plan/prefetch/combine contract. - [x] Add `moonep` as a distinct MoE A2A backend. - [x] Add MoonEP dispatch and combine data contracts. - [x] Add the process-wide static MoonEP buffer facade and sizing knobs. - [x] Define the initial static token-capacity policy. - [x] Add the correctness-first contiguous BF16 expert layout. - [x] Add the BF16 `cu_seqlens` segment runner. - [x] Wire eager dispatch -> prefetch -> compute -> combine. - [x] Add the distributed BF16 validation harness. - [x] Validate the synthetic BF16 path on 8x H100 SXM: all eight ranks passed with zero numerical error. - [x] Merge the BF16 PoC into upstream `moonep` via #33249. The merged work intentionally remains a PoC: eager-only, BF16-only, memory-heavy global expert storage, and a correctness-first Python expert loop. ## Milestone 0: Land the MXFP4/DeepGEMM production-path candidate - [ ] Land and version the MoonEP API needed by the SGLang integration. - [ ] Merge or supersede MoonshotAI/MoonEP#32. - [ ] Pin/document an exact compatible MoonEP revision or wheel. - [ ] Rebase #34874 onto the latest `upstream/moonep`. - [ ] Resolve conflicts so the PR contains only its MXFP4/DeepGEMM/symmetric-memory delta. - [ ] Run pre-commit and fix lint. - [ ] Trigger and pass the required SGLang CPU/GPU CI suites. ## Milestone 1: Make the supported runtime contract safe and explicit - [ ] Remove the silent rank-0 fallback from MoonEP rank resolution. - [ ] Prevent padded routes from distorting MoonEP planner expert statistics. - [ ] Explicitly reject unsupported expert-bias configurations. - [ ] Define the TBO/SBO contract. - Near-term option: fail fast or disable overlap for MoonEP. - Long-term option: give every in-flight sub-batch explicit buffer/plan ownership. - [ ] Keep CUDA graph disabled unless capture/replay is validated; do not expose an unverified opt-in as supported behavior. - [ ] Replace broad DeepEP-family capability assumptions with explicit MoonEP capability checks where necessary. ## Milestone 2: Add automated coverage for the production path - [ ] Test symmetric-pool alignment, sizing, lifecycle, and global-expert-to-row mapping across EP ranks. - [ ] Test MXFP4 checkpoint loading and post-load weight/scale residency in symmetric memory. - [ ] Test remote-prefetch source and destination slot remapping. - [ ] Test MoonEP-to-DeepGEMM pre/post-permute logic, including `m_indices`. - [ ] Test route-weight application, empty groups, padded groups, and capacity boundaries. - [ ] Test prefill/decode capacity selection and rank-uniform buffer selection. - [ ] Add a real SGLang integration test that instantiates the actual Kimi-K3 `FusedMoE`/MXFP4 path without import stubs. - [ ] Retain the synthetic BF16 harness as a separately identified component test. ## Milestone 3: Reproducible Kimi-K3 acceptance validation - [ ] Re-run end-to-end Kimi-K3 validation on the rebased, pinned stack. - [ ] Record exact SGLang, MoonEP, and DeepGEMM revisions. - [ ] Record the complete launch command, container/wheel versions, topology, GPU count, and TP/EP configuration. - [ ] Validate prefill and decode over small and large batches. - [ ] Validate token-capacity overflow and unsupported-configuration failure behavior. - [ ] Measure resident and peak memory for the symmetric expert pool. - [ ] Run long-duration/stability validation. - [ ] Validate correctness with an agreed evaluation suite and thresholds. ## Milestone 4: Demonstrate the performance value - [ ] Define acceptance thresholds before benchmarking. - [ ] Compare MoonEP with DeepEP under identical Kimi-K3 MXFP4 settings. - [ ] Measure TTFT, inter-token latency, throughput, and memory. - [ ] Cover decode/small-batch and larger-batch operating points relevant to #32607. - [ ] Break down dispatch, planning, prefetch, expert GEMM, and combine time. - [ ] Tune and document token capacity, padding, prefetch slots, and communication SM count. - [ ] Profile representative bottlenecks where profiler permissions and hardware permit. ## Milestone 5: Package and document the supported configuration - [ ] Provide a reproducible MoonEP wheel/container installation path. - [ ] Add hardware and topology prerequisite checks with actionable errors. - [ ] Add a Kimi-K3 MoonEP launch recipe. - [ ] Document supported dtype, quantization, EP topology, CUDA graph, overlap, PP, and disaggregation combinations. - [ ] Add troubleshooting guidance for capacity, VMM/fabric, multicast, and dependency-version failures. - [ ] Update #32607 when the agreed completion boundary is met. ## Follow-up capabilities These should not block the first narrowly defined Kimi-K3 production configuration unless the acceptance contract explicitly requires them. - [ ] Asynchronous dispatch/prefetch/combine event chaining and stream overlap. - [ ] CUDA graph capture/replay. - [ ] TBO/SBO support with explicit multi-in-flight ownership. - [ ] Fused shared experts. - [ ] Sharded symmetric storage for the BF16 diagnostic path, or removal of the memory-heavy BF16 production path. - [ ] Pipeline parallelism. - [ ] PD disaggregation and speculative-decoding combinations. - [ ] Additional models, quantization formats, and hardware generations. ## Decisions still required Child decision issues should settle these before this roadmap is converted into implementation tickets: 1. Is the first completion boundary Kimi-K3 MXFP4 on GB200/GB300 only, or a generic MoonEP backend contract? 2. What exact topology and GPU matrix is required for acceptance? 3. What DeepEP-relative performance threshold is required to call the integration successful? 4. Should TBO/SBO and CUDA graph be explicitly unsupported for v1, or required before completion? 5. Who owns and publishes the compatible MoonEP dependency artifact? 6. Which follow-up capabilities belong in this roadmap versus separate roadmaps? ## Completion criteria The primary roadmap is complete when: - the compatible MoonEP dependency and SGLang integration are merged and reproducibly installable; - the MXFP4 symmetric-memory + DeepGEMM path passes focused tests and SGLang CI; - the supported configuration fails early for unsupported combinations; - Kimi-K3 acceptance validation is reproducible from recorded revisions and commands; and - MoonEP's benefit relative to DeepEP is measured against a pre-agreed threshold, or the result is documented and the roadmap scope is explicitly revised.

signal.title: [Router] Add abort_request fan-out support
signal.text: ## Summary Add an `/abort_request` endpoint to the SGLang router. The router does not currently track which worker owns a particular request ID. To ensure that an abort reaches the correct worker, the endpoint forwards the original request body to every registered worker. Workers that do not own the request can safely treat it as a no-op. ## Changes - Add `POST /abort_request` to the router. - Forward the original JSON request body to all registered workers. - Preserve the `application/json` content type when forwarding requests. - Limit concurrent worker requests to avoid unbounded fan-out. - Handle plain, prefill, and decode workers consistently. - Return a per-worker success and failure breakdown. - Return `502 Bad Gateway` when one or more workers cannot process the request. - Add coverage for successful fan-out, partial failures, unreachable workers, trailing-slash URLs, empty registries, mixed worker modes, and request-body forwarding. ## Testing - Verified the patch with `git diff --check`. - Rust tests could not be executed locally because the Rust toolchain is not available in the current environment. Fixes #6531 ## AI Assistance OpenAI Codex assisted with the implementation and test preparation. I reviewed the proposed behavior and code changes and take responsibility for the contribution. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #32440106002](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32440106002)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32440105893](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32440105893)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:heavy_minus_sign: **No AMD PR run found for this commit**.<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [CPU] Fix wrongly causal-masked bidirectional attention
signal.text: <!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. --> ## Motivation <!-- Describe the purpose and goals of this pull request. --> On the Intel AMX CPU attention backend, `extend_attention_cpu` always masked the extend stage of attention as causal. This is correct for decoder-style self-attention, but wrong for bidirectional, encoder-only self-attention (e.g. BERT-family rerankers/embedders like bge-reranker). On this backend such models silently got causally-masked attention scores, producing incorrect outputs. When running `BAAI/bge-reranker-base` on CPU: For the below request: ``` { "model": "BAAI/bge-reranker-base", "query": "what is panda?", "documents": [ "hi", "The giant panda (Ailuropoda melanoleuca), sometimes called a panda bear or simply panda, is a bear species endemic to China." ], "return_documents": true } ``` Before this fix: `"hi"` and `"The giant panda ..."` both get the same score: 2.611328125, which is not reasonble. After this fix: Scores diverge correctly, matching what a real cross-encoder should produce: `"The giant panda ..."`: score is 6.1875 `"hi"`: score is -8.15625 ## Modifications <!-- Detail the changes made in this pull request. --> - `python/sglang/kernels/aot/csrc/cpu/extend.cpp`: add an `is_causal` parameter (default `true`) to `extend_attention_cpu`. The stage-2 loop now iterates over the full extend range and only applies the causal mask when `is_causal` is set, instead of unconditionally limiting keys to `[0, m + BLOCK_M)` and masking `n + n_size - 1 > m`. - `python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/intel_amx_backend.py`: compute `is_causal = not (layer.is_cross_attention or layer.attn_type == AttentionType.ENCODER_ONLY)` and pass it into `extend_attention_fwd`, mirroring the existing pattern in `triton_backend.py`: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/ee1f2e8dfdbb264727134aeac4b8dec155ec6efe/python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/triton_backend.py#L1360-L1368. ## Accuracy Tests <!-- If this pull request affects model outputs (e.g., changes to the kernel or model forward code), provide accuracy test results. --> ```sh python test/registered/cpu/test_extend.py -k test_extend_attention_bidirectional ``` ## Checklist - [ ] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [ ] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. signal.title: Support deepseek v4 and kimi k3 on ssd
signal.text: # [Feature] Add SSD-backed Expert Pack inference for DeepSeek-V4-Flash and Kimi-K3 ## Summary This PR adds an opt-in SSD-backed inference path for **DeepSeek-V4-Flash** and **Kimi-K3**. It allows these MoE models to run when their complete weights are larger than GPU VRAM and host RAM combined. Routed expert weights are stored on SSD and loaded only when selected by the router. The implementation uses: - an expert-major **Expert Pack** layout for efficient random access; - direct I/O into aligned pinned host buffers; - asynchronous host-to-device transfers; and - a byte-budgeted LFU/LRU GPU cache for frequently used experts. The runtime does not prune, merge, skip, replace, or re-quantize experts, and does not reduce Expert Top-K. The default `auto`, `safetensors`, and `gguf` loading paths remain unchanged; SSD execution is enabled only through the explicit `expert_pack` path. ## Usage Install this branch from source before running the examples: ```bash python3 -m pip install -e "python" ``` ### DeepSeek-V4-Flash Download the tested FP4/FP8 GGUF from [`frob/deepseek-v4-flash`](https://ollama.com/frob/deepseek-v4-flash). The benchmark used the immutable model blob with SHA-256 `947ac34c08c0e5c5752ac76398f934b3b6b4075cfe915ba43dd5ac754900a4cd`. ```bash python3 examples/runtime/deepseek_v4/benchmark_deepseek_5090.py \ --gguf /path/to/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-FP4-FP8-native.gguf \ --prompt "Explain why the sky appears blue." \ --max-new-tokens 200 ``` ### Kimi-K3 Download all 38 Q2_K GGUF shards from [`Blackfrost-AI/KIMI-K3-Q2_K-GGUF-ABLITERATED`](https://huggingface.co/Blackfrost-AI/KIMI-K3-Q2_K-GGUF-ABLITERATED). Also place the tokenizer/config files from [`moonshotai/Kimi-K3`](https://huggingface.co/moonshotai/Kimi-K3) in a sibling directory named `kimi-k3-tokenizer`. ```bash hf download Blackfrost-AI/KIMI-K3-Q2_K-GGUF-ABLITERATED \ --include "KIMI-K3-MXP4-DERISKED-Q2_K-*.gguf" \ --local-dir /path/to/kimi-k3 ``` ```bash python3 examples/runtime/kimi_k3/benchmark_kimi_k3_5090.py \ --gguf /path/to/kimi-k3/KIMI-K3-MXP4-DERISKED-Q2_K-00001-of-00038.gguf \ --prompt "Explain why the sky appears blue." \ --max-new-tokens 200 ``` The first shard is only the entrypoint. The launcher automatically discovers and uses all 38 shards in the same directory. Both launchers derive the remaining paths automatically. If the Expert Pack is missing, it is built on the first launch and reused afterward. | Model | First Expert Pack build | Approximate first-run readiness | | --- | ---: | ---: | | DeepSeek-V4-Flash | Estimated **5-10 minutes** on the benchmark NVMe SSD | **8-15 minutes** | | Kimi-K3 | **29 minutes 42 seconds measured** | **35-45 minutes** | The 38 Kimi-K3 source shards and generated Expert Pack occupy approximately 1.814 TiB in total, so a 4 TB SSD is recommended for practical headroom. ## Correctness - DeepSeek-V4-Flash produced semantically equivalent answers to Ollama across travel planning, science, history, programming, and mathematics prompts. - Kimi-K3 matched the 200-token SGLang reference output exactly. All 92 routed layers executed Top-16 experts with `fallback_count=0` and `io_errors=0`. ## Performance The target platform is one RTX 5090 with 32 GB VRAM, 32 GB host RAM, and NVMe SSD storage. The retained measurements were collected on RTX 5090 hosts; host RAM and SSD capacity differed between the two model runs. ### DeepSeek-V4-Flash vs Ollama Five prompts were measured with 200 generated tokens per prompt. | Metric | SGLang | Ollama | Result | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | | Prefill | 3.265 token/s | 1.457 token/s | **2.24x faster** | | Decode | 2.020 token/s | 1.354 token/s | **1.49x faster** | ### Kimi-K3 vs llama.cpp The SGLang run used a 91-token prompt and generated 200 tokens. | Metric | SGLang | llama.cpp | Result | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | | Prefill | 0.66412 token/s | 0.11289 token/s | **5.88x faster** | | Decode | 0.44830 token/s | 0.1810 token/s | **2.48x faster** | The llama.cpp decode baseline came from an earlier 50-token run, so the 2.48x decode figure is indicative rather than a strict equal-length comparison. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: **Missing `run-ci` label** -- add it to run CI tests.<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: **Blocked** -- `run-ci` is required first.<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:heavy_minus_sign: **No AMD PR run found for this commit**.<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->
signal.author: beyondHJM

signal.title: [Fix] Forward an explicit CXX to nvcc via -ccbin in JIT builds
signal.text: ## Problem The JIT build resolves the host compiler from `CXX` (`toolchain.host_compiler_path()`) and uses it for the `.cpp` translation units and the link step — but never tells nvcc. nvcc ignores `CXX` entirely: it takes `-ccbin` or falls back to `gcc` from `PATH`. So on a machine whose default gcc is newer than the CUDA toolkit's nvcc supports, every JIT kernel build fails: ``` host_config.h:132: #error -- unsupported GNU version! gcc versions later than 12 are not supported! ``` even when the user explicitly set `CXX=/usr/bin/g++-12` to fix exactly that. Repro on such a machine (CUDA 12.x nvcc + default gcc 13): ```python import os os.environ["CXX"] = "/usr/bin/g++-12" from sglang.kernels.jit.utils.compile import toolchain print(toolchain.host_compiler_path()) # /usr/bin/g++-12 (.cpp units + link) print(toolchain.base_cuda_flags()) # ['-Xcompiler', '-fPIC'] <- no -ccbin ``` The generated `build.ninja` compiles `.cpp` with `$cxx` (g++-12) while the `compile_cuda` rule lets nvcc pick `gcc` (13) for all host code inside `.cu` units. ## Fix `base_cuda_flags()` appends `-ccbin $CXX` when `CXX` is set explicitly (resolved through the `@cache_once`-cached `explicit_host_compiler()`, so both call sites see one value). When `CXX` is unset the flags are unchanged — nvcc's own default (`gcc` from PATH) is preserved, since forwarding the `"c++"` fallback would silently change the default host compiler. The HIP branch is untouched (hipcc takes no `-ccbin`). The build key follows automatically: it is taken over the generated `build.ninja` text (which now embeds the flag) and `_environment_fingerprint` already fingerprints `host_compiler_path()`, so a changed `CXX` re-keys the build instead of reusing stale binaries. Verified end to end on an RTX 3080 / CUDA 12.0 / default gcc 13 machine: with the JIT cache cleared, `CXX=/usr/bin/gcc-12 python3 -m sglang.launch_server ...` now compiles all JIT kernels and serves traffic. Before the fix the same command failed every `.cu` build with the error above, and the only workaround was to also set `NVCC_CCBIN` — a variable this code path never reads. Per review, no unit test is attached: the behavior depends on a compiler the CI machine is not guaranteed to have, so the change ships without a test. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:warning: [Run #32434634900](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32434634900)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:warning: [Run #32434634637](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32434634637)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:warning: [Run #32434634736](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32434634736)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->
