signal.title: Fix Qwen3.5 GDN multi-item scoring
signal.text: ## Motivation Qwen3.5 hybrid models use recurrent GDN layers alongside full-attention layers. Multi-item scoring already gives the full-attention layers an item-branching mask, but the GDN prefill path previously processed the packed suffix as one continuous recurrent sequence. As a result, later items could inherit convolution and SSM state from earlier items. Fixes #31969. ## Modifications - Add a read-only final-state mode to the Triton chunk gated-delta-rule path while preserving in-place updates by default. - Build GDN-specific MIS metadata once per forward for compact query and item segments. - Run GDN MIS prefill in two phases: compute each request query once, then branch every item from the query-end convolution and SSM states. - Keep item recurrence read-only against the request SSM pool and use unique cloned convolution slots per item. - Reject unsupported combinations, including non-Triton GDN prefill, page-major layout, cached prefixes, non-prefill requests, and hybrid linear backends without MIS support. - Add kernel, causal-convolution, backend, metadata, validation, and Qwen3.5 end-to-end coverage. ## Accuracy Tests Tested on one NVIDIA H20 with `Qwen/Qwen3.5-4B` in BF16, FlashInfer full attention, and Triton linear-attention prefill. - Qwen3.5 MIS end-to-end: 3 tests passed, covering empty queries, concurrent requests, varied item counts and lengths, and sibling modification/reordering. - Focused recurrent, causal-convolution, GDN backend, metadata, and validation suite: 27 tests passed with 46 subtests. - Full recurrent and causal-convolution test files: 275 tests passed. - Multi-item scores match per-item MIS scoring with `atol=2e-2, rtol=2e-2`. - Formatting, import checks, spelling, syntax compilation, CI registration validation, and whitespace checks passed. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Single H20, `Qwen/Qwen3.5-4B`, query length 120, item length 180, 10 items per request, 10 warmup requests, followed by three 60-second runs. CUDA graph, radix cache, and chunked prefill were disabled in both modes. | Mode | Items/s/GPU | P50 latency | P99 latency | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | | Independent pointwise scoring | 52.80 | 189.06 ms | 195.25 ms | | Multi-item scoring | 62.75 | 158.74 ms | 167.21 ms | This is an 18.84% throughput increase, with P50 latency reduced by 16.04% and P99 latency reduced by 14.36%. ## Checklist - [x] Format the code with the repository formatters and static checks. - [x] Add unit and end-to-end tests. - [x] Documentation is not required because this does not change the public API or Score API schema. - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results. - [x] Follow the SGLang code style guidance. ## Review and Merge Process 1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. 2. Get approvals from CODEOWNERS and other reviewers. 3. Trigger the required CI tests. 4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls to merge the PR. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #32440079933](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32440079933)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32440079714](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32440079714)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #32440079745](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32440079745)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: feat(kv-events): Add component_types field to BlockStored for per-component placement tracking
signal.text: ## Motivation KV-aware routers consume `BlockStored` / `BlockRemoved` to track which blocks live on which tier. On hybrid models the unified radix tree keeps several independent KV components on one node — full attention, sliding window, mamba state — and evicts and restores them independently. A `BlockStored` today only says "this block is on GPU". That is ambiguous once SWA has been tombstoned off an internal node while its full KV stays resident: the router still believes the block is fully reusable and routes a request that then has to recompute the window. This adds an opt-in per-component placement dimension so a consumer can tell what is actually resident at a given medium, following the same shape as #18205 which added the `medium` field. ## Modifications Gated behind `--enable-kv-events-component-types`, off by default. 1. **Schema.** A trailing `Optional[list[str]]` on `BlockStored` plus the `KV_COMPONENT_FULL/SWA/MAMBA` wire names. `BlockRemoved` stays whole-block — a removal always means the base (full) component left the tier, so there is nothing partial to express. 2. **Plumbing.** The flag flows from `ServerArgs` through `CacheInitParams` into the cache builder, and is documented in the server arguments reference. The UMBP subscriber logs the component dimension but does not forward it; its external-KV API is keyed by `(hashes, tier)` only. 3. **Emission.** `KVCacheEventMixin` gains a `_component_types_for_page` hook defaulting to `None`; `UnifiedTreeCore` overrides it and reports residency off live tree state, anchoring the single per-leaf mamba state to the leaf's last page. 4. **Tests.** 20 unit tests in `TestUnifiedRadixCacheComponentPlacementEvents`, plus wire-layout tests in `test_kv_events.py`. Three ordering constraints shaped the implementation and are worth flagging for review: - *Gains defer, losses do not.* SWA and Mamba attach device values through barrier-applied actions (`SWARebuild`, `MambaEvictExcessPathStates`), so a node's component set is not final until those apply. Inserts collect nodes in `_InsertWalkState` and emit one snapshot per node in the TAIL step; evictions are final when the component is dropped and emit immediately. - *Emission is root-first.* SWA splits the fresh leaf at commit time, so nodes are noted in neither tree nor creation order. `_record_store_event` seeds a node's lazily computed hash chain off its parent's hash, so announcing a child first would publish it as a root block under a hash no other code path reproduces. - *Partial eviction restates, never removes.* When SWA or Mamba is tombstoned while full survives the block has not left the tier, so we restate the smaller component set. Whole-block teardowns (`_demote`, host-leaf eviction) keep emitting `BlockRemoved` and never restate. `commit_load_back` also moves its emit after every component restores, unioning each component's `nodes_to_load`; emitting on full's list alone reported a promoted block as full-only. ## Subscriber compatibility `BlockStored` is a msgspec `array_like` struct, so every field is always encoded positionally — an unset `component_types` is a trailing `nil`, not an omitted slot (pinned by `test_component_types_is_the_trailing_slot`). With the flag **off** that `nil` is exactly what a positional decoder reads for an absent optional, so subscribers are unaffected; verified against both in-tree decoders, sgl-router (which drains unknown trailing fields, `experimental/sgl-router/src/policies/kv_events/wire.rs:420`) and dynamo's kv-router. With the flag **on**, the slot holds a list. sgl-router still ignores it. dynamo's kv-router, however, shares one positional layout with vLLM in which that slot is `lora_name` (a string), so it rejects the whole event batch. This is exactly why the feature is opt-in, and enabling it against a dynamo subscriber is not supported today. Aligning the two representations — dynamo already models this as one event per KV-cache group tagged with `kv_cache_spec_kind` — is a larger cross-project change and deliberately out of scope here. Only component-aware caches honour the flag; the mixin hook returns `None` elsewhere, so `radix_cache`, `hiradix_cache`, `swa_radix_cache`, `mamba_radix_cache` and `hi_mamba_radix_cache` are untouched. ## Accuracy Tests Not applicable — observability only. This touches no kernel, no model forward path, and no cache eviction or placement decision; it changes what is reported about placement, never the placement itself. Unit tests run locally across page_size 1/4/16/64/128 and the FULL, FULL+SWA, FULL+MAMBA and FULL+SWA+MAMBA configurations (`test_unified_radix_cache_unittest.py`, `test_kv_events.py`, and the radix/hiradix/swa/mamba mem_cache units): 1113 passed, 1030 skipped (config-conditional), 140 subtests passed. `test_unified_radix_cache_unittest.py` is one of the 12 files currently deferred at module level by #31812 during the ServerArgs config-namespace migration, so those cases will not run in CI until that skip is lifted upstream; the run above was done locally with the module skip removed. The wire-layout tests live in `test_kv_events.py`, which is not deferred and does run in CI. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Not applicable. With the flag off the added cost is one boolean check per store event. With it on, a per-page component scan bounded by the component count (at most 3) plus one ancestor walk per insert flush. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process). 2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers. 3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so. - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci` 4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #32440003851](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32440003851)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #32440003648](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32440003648)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #32440003706](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32440003706)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [CPU] Fix NUMA/core binding for DP ranks
signal.text: <!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. --> ## Motivation <!-- Describe the purpose and goals of this pull request. --> Before this PR, `ModelRunner.init_threads_binding` picked the NUMA node / core group for a worker using `tp_rank`. Under DP, DP rank 0 and DP rank 1 both resolve to tp_rank=0 and get bound to the same NUMA node/cores instead of being spread across the machine. This PR fixes this incorrect binding. ## Modifications <!-- Detail the changes made in this pull request. --> 1. `init_threads_binding` now takes `numa_index` (the worker's global device id) and `world_size = dp_size * tp_size * pp_size`, instead of `tp_rank` and `tp_size`, so every rank across every DP replica maps to a distinct NUMA node / core group. Removed the `world_size == len(threads_bind_list)` equality assert for the explicit `SGLANG_CPU_OMP_THREADS_BIND` path, replacing it with only the per-rank bounds check. This permits the router-mode case (local `world_size=1`, multi-group bind string) while still catching a bind list that's too short. 2. `test/registered/cpu/test_subblock_sparse_attention.py`, added in https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/34680, fails in Xeon CPU CI with `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'imageio'`: importing it pulls in `sglang.multimodal_gen`, which needs `diffusers/imageio/addict` from the diffusion extra. Install `.[diffusion]` instead of `.` in `docker/xeon.Dockerfile` — the extra is already declared in `python/pyproject_cpu.toml`. Note this grows the CI image. ## Accuracy Tests <!-- If this pull request affects model outputs (e.g., changes to the kernel or model forward code), provide accuracy test results. --> ## Speed Tests and Profiling <!-- If this pull request impacts inference speed, provide benchmarking and profiling results. --> ## Checklist - [ ] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [ ] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. signal.title: Extend dLLM volatile-block cache fix (#35270) to swa/mamba/unified/cpp radix caches
signal.text: ## Motivation #35470 fixed a KV-pool accounting bug in `RadixCache.cache_unfinished_req`: a dLLM request's in-flight denoise block is rewritten in full on every step (`dllm_incomplete_ids`), and since `_dllm_page_size` pins `page_size` to the dLLM block size, that block is a whole trailing page of the radix key. Caching it makes the next step's key diverge at the block boundary, which drives the prefix match below `cache_protected_len`, inverts the `free_segment` slice (freeing nothing), and leaves the tree owning two nodes for the same physical pages — inflating `evictable_size()` past what the pool holds and tripping the idle pool-invariant check (#35270). The fix there was `req.get_fill_ids()` → `req.get_cacheable_fill_ids()` (added via `ReqDllmMixin`), scoped to `RadixCache` only. The PR author flagged in review notes that `SWARadixCache`, `MambaRadixCache`, `UnifiedRadixCache`, and `RadixCacheCpp` all call `req.get_fill_ids()` at the identical point in their own `cache_unfinished_req`, carrying the same latent assumption, but left them out to keep that PR scoped and because dLLM doesn't exercise those caches today. This PR applies the same one-line substitution to all four, so the fix is consistent across every radix-cache implementation rather than leaving three latent instances of the same bug for whenever dLLM is combined with SWA, Mamba, the unified cache, or the experimental C++ tree. ## Change Same substitution in each `cache_unfinished_req`, same explanatory comment as #35470: - `python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/mamba_radix_cache.py` - `python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/radix_cache_cpp.py` - `python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/swa_radix_cache.py` - `python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/unified_radix_cache.py` No other call sites feed the cached radix key in any of these files. ## Tests None added here. I checked whether the same CPU-only regression-test pattern from #35470 (`test_radix_cache_dllm_volatile_block.py`, built on `MHATokenToKVPool` + `PagedTokenToKVPoolAllocator` on `device="cpu"`) could be replicated for these four, but: - `SWARadixCache`, `MambaRadixCache`, and `UnifiedRadixCache`'s own unit-test suites are all `register_cuda_ci`/`register_amd_ci` and build their pools via `get_device()` — there's no established CPU-backed fixture for them in this repo today. - `RadixCacheCpp` has no unit-test harness at all; it wraps the C++-bound tree and isn't importable without the compiled `sgl_kernel` extension. I don't have GPU access, so I didn't want to fabricate new pool fixtures for three different subsystems that I have no way to actually run. Happy to add coverage if a maintainer points me at (or already has) a CPU-safe way to construct these, or this can be left to existing CI. ## Depends on #35470 — this branch is rebased on `main` with #35470's single commit (`1f05bc6`) cherry-picked in for buildability (`get_cacheable_fill_ids` doesn't exist on `main` yet). Once #35470 merges, I'll rebase this PR and the diff will collapse to just the 4 files above. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32439851629](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32439851629)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32439851561](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32439851561)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32439851637](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32439851637)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [NPU] Use fused Triton MRoPE for Qwen3.x
signal.text: <!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. --> ## Motivation The existing NPU MRoPE path cannot correctly handle multimodal position embeddings, causing accuracy issues in image grounding tasks. This PR replaces `split_qkvgate_gemma_rmsnorm_rope` with the fused `triton_split_qkv_rmsnorm_mrope` kernel used by vLLM Ascend. The new kernel supports Q/K RMSNorm, QKV/Gate splitting, and MRoPE in a single operation. signal.title: Qwen3.8-27B NVFP4 on RTX 5090: cookbook mem-fraction OOMs at decode-graph capture (~5GB) and torch.compile + decode graph is a 6x regression
signal.text: ## Describe the bug The Qwen3.8-27B cookbook recipe for **RTX 5090 (32GB) + NVFP4 + no-spec + low-latency tier** (`hw=rtx5090&variant=default&quant=nvfp4&nodes=single&spec=none&tier=low-latency&ssmDtype=float32`) has two issues we measured on real hardware: 1. **The recommended `--mem-fraction-static` values cannot boot on an RTX 5090**: the no-spec recipe enables a *full* target decode CUDA graph capture that consumes **~5 GB of VRAM during capture** (see log below). At the recommended mem-fraction (0.90–0.94) the server enters an OOM crash-restart loop during graph capture. We had to drop to `--mem-fraction-static 0.80` **and** add `--cuda-graph-backend-prefill disabled` to boot at all. 2. **`--enable-torch-compile` combined with a captured decode CUDA graph is a ~6x performance regression** on this model/GPU: 9.8–10.2 tok/s vs 59.4 tok/s with the graph alone. The graph apparently bakes in unoptimized kernels when torch.compile is active. ## Environment - GPU: 1x RTX 5090 32GB (SM120), driver 595.80, CUDA 13.2 - SGLang: 0.5.17 (pip) + the DFlash2 overlay files from the Qwen3.8-27B cookbook (runs fine otherwise) - Model: `RadixArk/Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4` (quantized checkpoint, `kv_cache_quant_algo: FP8` honored via `--kv-cache-dtype auto`) - Container instance (compshare), pure-text serving with `--language-only` - Benchmark: single-stream chat completion, 1024 output tokens, streaming, Chinese technical prompt ## Reproduction Recipe A (as emitted by the cookbook panel for rtx5090/nvfp4/spec=none/low-latency/float32): ```bash python -m sglang.launch_server \ --model-path RadixArk/Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4 \ --attention-backend flashinfer \ --chunked-prefill-size 2048 \ --mamba-ssm-dtype float32 \ --mamba-radix-cache-strategy extra_buffer_lazy \ --mem-fraction-static 0.94 \ # also tried 0.90, 0.85, 0.88 --max-running-requests 4 \ --reasoning-parser qwen3 --tool-call-parser qwen3_coder ``` Result at 0.94 / 0.90 / 0.85 — crash loop during capture: ``` Capture target decode CUDA graph begin. backend=full, num_tokens_per_req=1, bs=[1], avail mem=1.41 GB Exception: Capture cuda graph failed: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 96.00 MiB. GPU 0 has a total capacity of 31.36 GiB of which 39.81 MiB is free. ``` Only at 0.80 + `--cuda-graph-backend-prefill disabled` does capture succeed — and it reveals the real budget: ``` Capture target decode CUDA graph begin. backend=full, num_tokens_per_req=1, bs=[1], avail mem=5.72 GB Capture target decode CUDA graph end. elapsed=215.75 s, mem usage=4.95 GB, avail mem=0.77 GB. ``` **The decode graph itself permanently consumes 4.95 GB.** With NVFP4 weights ~16.5 GB + a ~1 GB CUDA-IPC multimodal feature pool (see finding 3), there is simply no room for the cookbook's mem-fraction on 32 GB. Side finding: `SGLANG_MM_FEATURE_CACHE_MB` defaults to 1024 MiB and is reserved on the base GPU even for **text-only** serving (we use `--language-only`). Setting `SGLANG_MM_FEATURE_CACHE_MB=16` frees ~1 GB. Might be worth defaulting low when the served path is text-only. ## Measured matrix (same GPU, same checkpoint, same benchmark) | # | Spec | torch.compile | Decode graph | mem-frac | tok/s (single stream) | |---|------|---------------|--------------|----------|------------------------| | 1 | none | no | yes | 0.80 | **59.4** | | 2 | none | yes | yes | 0.80 | 10.2 | | 3 | none | yes | yes | 0.80 (bf16 ssm) | 9.8 | | 4 | DFLASH2 (DFlash2 draft, bf16 ssm, `--speculative-num-draft-tokens 8`) | yes | no (verify graph only) | 0.92 | **86–98 steady, 142–151 peak** | Notably, the DFlash2 configuration cannot capture the full decode graph either (VRAM), but it doesn't need to: with only the target-verify + draft-verify graphs plus torch.compile it is **1.5–2.5x faster than the best bootable no-spec recipe** (86–98 vs 59.4 tok/s) and ~9x faster than the torch.compile+graph combination. ## Expected behavior - The RTX 5090 cells of the cookbook should either (a) carry a mem-fraction that actually boots with the decode graph budget included (0.80 or lower + prefill graph disabled), or (b) note that the decode graph costs ~5 GB so users can make an informed trade-off. - The interaction between `--enable-torch-compile` and decode CUDA graph capture looks like a real bug worth investigating (graph should capture *post-compile* kernels), or at minimum the cookbook should warn not to combine them on this model. - Consider lowering the default multimodal IPC feature pool for text-only serving. Happy to provide full logs, the exact launch scripts, or to re-run any cell with instrumentation if that helps.

signal.author: xinguozhu-2026

signal.title: [Fix] Preserve deterministic DSpark target-verify parity
signal.text: ## Motivation Addresses #35150. With deterministic inference, ordinary Qwen3.8 decode and linear DSpark `TARGET_VERIFY` differed in two numerically relevant places: - decode rounds the GDN beta value through the activation dtype, while target verify kept it in FP32; - decode uses `decode_attention_fwd`, while target verify used `extend_attention_fwd_unified`. Either difference can perturb the persistent GDN state over repeated reject/commit rounds. A routing-only negative control still diverged from the clean packed-decode Base output at token 13 with all 95 drafts rejected, so attention routing alone is insufficient. ## Modifications - Round target-verify beta through its source activation dtype before accumulating in FP32. - Represent an unmasked linear verify block as independent decode streams with KV lengths `prefix_len + 1, ..., prefix_len + verify_len`. - Route only the deterministic CUDA DSpark target-worker path through the existing Triton decode kernel, in eager execution and CUDA Graph replay. - Preserve the existing path for non-deterministic inference, draft workers, masked/tree or ragged verification, MLA, DCP, sliding-window attention, unified memory, encoder-decoder models, and non-CUDA platforms. ## Validation Status Validation uses one NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5090 with CUDA 13.0, `RadixArk/Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4` and `RadixArk/Qwen3.8-27B-DSpark`, TP=1, Triton attention, deterministic inference, FP32 SSM state, gamma=1, and the exact 96-token reproduction from #35150. - Clean production Base packed-decode oracle: 96 tokens, SHA256 `3ca7a432820875b0dc7c1f2d2e644664e8b864947592a0e876d00400848b6e72`. - Routing-only negative control: 0/95 drafts accepted and first divergence from the clean Base output at token 13. - The combined beta and attention changes match a sequential/unpacked decode diagnostic, but fail against the clean production packed-decode Base oracle: 0/95 drafts accepted, first divergence at output token 6 (`Base=279`, `DSpark=781`), DSpark SHA256 `5fc99930b4c8f106a1267003582448c2f9bfe1f17c4db52839924cfc8e830fa1`. - This PR remains Draft while the remaining packed GDN decode difference is localized; the current commit does not yet fix #35150. - Focused GQA probe: target-verify attention is bitwise equal to sequential decode (`unequal=0`, `max_abs=0`); eager and CUDA Graph `kv_indptr`, KV indices, and split metadata are identical. - `py_compile`, Black 26.1.0, Ruff, and `git diff --check` pass. ## Speed Tests and Profiling No speed claim. The new path is selected only for explicit deterministic inference, where decode parity is the goal. Default non-deterministic serving is unchanged. ## Related Work - The beta-rounding hunk is also present in #34734 by @qq1060; credit to that PR for identifying this alignment. That broader feature PR adds ragged and checkpoint support but does not route deterministic verification through decode and explicitly leaves greedy equivalence unresolved. If #34734 lands first, the duplicate one-line hunk can be dropped during rebase. - #34597 uses the same decode-kernel routing principle for DeepSeek-V4 MTP. - #34821 changes target-verify causal convolution; it does not align Triton full attention. - #33291 adds an opt-in Decode-Verify-Rollback algorithm; this fix preserves the existing DSpark path. ## Checklist - [x] Format the code with the repository's Black version. - [x] Run focused attention metadata tests. - [ ] Verify exact clean packed-decode Base parity in eager and CUDA Graph execution. - [x] Keep documentation unchanged because no public API or option changes. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32439583932](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32439583932)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32439583890](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32439583890)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32439583924](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32439583924)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: fix: resolve CPU device compatibility issues
signal.text: ## Motivation This PR fixes two runtime failures in the LTX-2.3 two-stage serving path and one dtype failure in the LTX-2.3 vocoder path. First, LoRA offload management previously used backend-specific cache APIs that were not portable across all device backends in this call site. Second, LTX-2.3 two-stage original mode can build a stage-2 LoRA switch spec that applies both: - user-provided LoRA - built-in distilled LoRA to the same transformer target. Dynamic LoRA supports only one adapter per target, so this could trigger: ValueError: Dynamic LoRA currently supports only one adapter per target Additionally, the LTX-2.3 vocoder BWE path could hit: Input type (float) and bias type (c10::BFloat16) should be the same when input was forced to float32 but module weights/bias were bf16. ## Modifications 1. fix: portable cache-management calls in LoRA offload path - Update cache clear logic in lora_pipeline.py - Replace backend-specific torch device-module calls with platform abstraction: - `current_platform.synchronize()` - `current_platform.empty_cache()` - This keeps behavior consistent across backends and avoids unsupported direct backend API assumptions in this path. 2. fix: Dynamic LoRA one-adapter-per-target conflict in stage2 original mode - Update two-stage LoRA merge decision flow in `ltx_2_pipeline.py` - Keep original default behavior: prefer dynamic LoRA in original mode to avoid request-time merge/unmerge on a single DiT - Add narrow fallback: when stage2 needs both user LoRA and distilled LoRA on the same transformer target, force `merge_weights=true` - Refactor this fallback into `_should_merge_lora_for_phase`, with a new optional parameter `distilled_lora_strength` that has a default value, so existing callers remain compatible without explicit argument passing. 3. fix: vocoder dtype mismatch in BWE path - Update dtype handling in `ltx_2_vocoder.py` - Align vocoder input dtype to `vocoder.conv_pre` weight dtype - Align bwe_generator input dtype to `bwe_generator.conv_pre` weight dtype - Preserve output cast-back behavior ## Accuracy Tests - Verified LTX-2.3 two-stage generation runs successfully in original mode. - The previous Dynamic LoRA multi-adapter stage2 failure is no longer reproducible. - Verified vocoder decode path no longer reproduces the float vs bf16 conv dtype mismatch. - Static checks on modified files report no new errors. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32439571589](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32439571589)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32439571453](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32439571453)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #32439571562](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32439571562)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [Perf][DSV4] add ag_gemm and moe_rs overlap kernels for dsv4 prefill
signal.text: ## 1. Motivation We implement communication-computation overlap for DeepSeek V4 Prefill CP by introducing two fused Triton kernels built on `torch.symmetric_memory`: 1. Fused AllGather + FP8 Quantization + GEMM: the CP AllGather is performed on a dedicated stream via Copy Engine (CE) P2P pulls (consuming no SMs), while a fused kernel on the compute stream performs on-the-fly FP8 quantization and shared expert `gate_up_proj` GEMM. The compute kernel poll signals to consume each chunk as soon as the CE delivers it, overlapping the AllGather with computation. 2. Fused MoE TopK-Reduce + Shared Expert Add + ReduceScatter: the routed expert output reduction, shared expert addition, and ReduceScatter send are fused into a single kernel, overlapping the ReduceScatter communication with the reduction computation. - Co-auther: @zxdukki ## 2. Modifications - **Environment Variable** - Add `SGLANG_OPT_USE_TORCH_SYMM_MEM_FUSED_KERNEL` (default `False`) to enable the fused kernels. - **New Triton Kernels (`symm_mem_kernels/`)** - Add allgather_gemm_symm_mem.py: triton kernel for CE-driven AllGather + on-the-fly FP8 quantization and GEMM with signal-based coordination across two streams. - Add moe_reduce_rs_symm_mem.py: fused MoE topk-reduce + shared expert addition + ReduceScatter in a single triton kernel. - **TorchSymmMemCommunicator (torch_symm_mem.py)** - Split `disabled` / `allreduce_disabled` so fused-kernel contexts work without multicast support. - Add lazy-init helpers to cache AG-GEMM and MoE-RS contexts. - Add CP-mode activation via `set_use_cp()` / `get_active_comm()`. - **Model & Layer (parallel_state.py, fused_moe.py, deepseek_v2/v4.py)** - Initialize `TorchSymmMemCommunicator` when the fused-kernel env var is enabled. - Add `no_topk_reduce` option to skip in-kernel reduction (deferred to the fused RS kernel). - Integrate `maybe_fused_ag_shared_experts` and `maybe_fused_shared_add_rs` into the MoE forward path. - Skip the standalone CP AllGather in `DeepseekV4DecoderLayer` when the fused path is active. ## 3. Evaluation ### 3.1. Experiment Setup - 3 nodes, with 8 × H20 GPUs and 4 dual-port 200Gbps NICs per node. DSV4 Flash uses 1 node with CP8-TP8 for prefill. DSV4 Pro uses 3 nodes with PP3-CP8-TP8 for prefill. - Input length 16k/32k/64k/128k, output length 1. ### 3.2. Performance Evaluation - DSV4 Flash mean TTFT: | Input Len | Baseline (ms) | Overlap (ms) | Speedup | | ---- | ---- | ---- | ---- | | 16k | 548.89 | 521.44 | 5.00% | | 32k | 1092.81 | 1034.50 | 5.33% | | 64k | 2200.69 | 2122.33 | 3.56% | | 128k | 4664.76 | 4500.17 | 3.53% | - DSV4 Pro mean TTFT: | Input Len | Baseline (ms) | Overlap (ms) | Speedup | | ---- | ---- | ---- | ---- | | 16k | 1066.37 | 1028.04 | 3.59% | | 32k | 1641.93 | 1586.49 | 3.37% | | 64k | 2832.55 | 2731.91 | 3.55% | | 128k | 5355.57 | 5173.78 | 3.39% | - Bench Script: ``` # (random-input-len, num-prompts) BENCH_CONFIGS=( "16384 300" "32768 150" "65536 100" "131072 50" ) for cfg in "${BENCH_CONFIGS[@]}"; do read -r INPUT_LEN NUM_PROMPTS <<< "$cfg" python -m sglang.bench_serving \ --backend sglang --host localhost --port 8288 \ --dataset-name random \ --dataset-path ./ShareGPT_V3_unfiltered_cleaned_split.json \ --num-prompts $NUM_PROMPTS --max-concurrency 1 \ --random-input-len $INPUT_LEN --random-output-len 1 \ --random-range-ratio 1.0 --request-rate inf done ``` ### 3.3. Profiling Here we take DSV4 Flash as an example to show profiling before and after optimization. - AllGather + FP8 Quantization + GEMM (476μs->309μs): - Baseline: - Overlap: - MoE TopK-Reduce + Shared Expert Add + ReduceScatter (415μs->235μs): - Baseline: - Overlap: ### 3.4. signal.title: [Kimi K3] Exclude template-rendered response_format tokens from billed prompt_tokens
signal.text: ## Problem For Kimi K3, requests with `response_format` report inflated `usage.prompt_tokens`. A vendor conformance run measured **186 vs the reference API's 119** for the same request, breaking billing alignment with the official K3 API. Root cause: `_encode_messages` (kimi_k3 branch) passes `response_format` into the checkpoint's chat template, which renders the JSON schema plus wrapper instructions into the prompt. Those tokens land in `origin_input_ids` and are counted as prompt tokens. The grammar/constraint path adds zero prompt tokens — the inflation comes solely from the template render. ## What this PR does - In the kimi_k3 encoder, when `response_format` is present, render the template once more without the `response_format` kwarg and record the token-count delta on the request (`_response_format_prompt_tokens`). Measuring the diff is robust to whatever wrapper the checkpoint template adds — no hardcoded schema-length math. - `_reported_prompt_tokens` subtracts that count alongside the existing `_KIMI_K3_GENERATION_STUB_TOKENS` adjustment, so billed/reported prompt tokens match the reference API with and without `response_format`. Cost: one extra CPU-side template render per response_format request; no behavior change for other models or for requests without `response_format`. ## Tests `test_kimi_k3_response_format_tokens_not_billed` — mocks the two renders (186 with the schema block, 119 baseline), asserts the measured delta (67) is excluded from reported prompt tokens and that requests without `response_format` keep the existing stub-only adjustment. Also updated `test_kimi_k3_encoder_receives_wire_request_fields` for the extra baseline render. ``` $ pytest test/registered/unit/entrypoints/openai/test_serving_chat.py test/registered/unit/entrypoints/openai/test_protocol.py 155 passed ``` ## Known gap (pre-existing, not made worse by this PR) `/v1/responses` (`serving_responses.py`) reads `prompt_tokens` from meta_info directly and does not go through `_reported_prompt_tokens`, so neither this adjustment nor the existing 3-token generation-stub adjustment applies there. K3 vendor conformance is chat-completions-only, so this is out of scope here; flagging for a follow-up if Responses API billing parity is ever needed. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #32439564964](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32439564964)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32439564942](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32439564942)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #32439564948](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32439564948)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [NPU]Ensure tensors allocated by empty_like are contiguous

signal.title: [HiCache] Fix PP inconsistency with HiCache L3 (#22607)
signal.text: ## Motivation When deploying HiCache and PP, multiple PP ranks go diverge and eventually cause sglang crash. The detailed reason was discussed in issue #22607. ## Modifications This patch introduces two kinds of synchronization mechanisms to fix the issue. I will illustrate this idea with an example of pp_size=2 and tp_size=1. 1. **pp_sync** across scheduler threads. pp_sync is a new name introduced by this patch. PP0's scheduler thread determine the number of completion events in its local queues (ack_load_queue, ack_prefetch_queue, etc). Then, PP1 must consume the **exact** same number of events from its queues. This prevents divergence. 2. **all_reduce** across prefetch threads. Consider a case that PP0 and PP1 have different lengths on their L3 storage for a given sequence. They have to reach an agreement on the length, by perform all_reduce(MIN). This behavior is consistent with TP. This patch also changes how `check_prefetch_progress` works. Before this patch, it simply does all_reduce(MIN) to determine the final tokens prefetchted. However, this would not work on PP, as we cannot do that in the scheduler thread. This patch adds a new background thread `prefetch_sync_thread`, which does the all_reduce work instead. ## Accuracy Tests Added `test_unified_radix_cache_hicache_pp_kl.py`. I have also tested SWE-bench verified with DSv4 flash model. I ran two groups: - Group A: The baseline, commit 5747ed3b, without this PR, TP=8, L3 enabled. Resolved 356/500. - Group B: This PR, PP=4, TP=2, L3 enabled. Resolved 353/500. I analyzed the difference, and found 351 cases successful in both group, 5 are successful only in group A, and 2 are successful only in group B. The 7 cases that are successfuly in one group but failed in another, are due to container exits after a long time. Here are commands for anyone has interested in reproducing this test. Hints to make L3 are in-use: - Use large number of workers (128), leading to large number of running requests. - Limit number of tokens in L1 and L2. ```sh # Group A sglang serve \ --model=deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash \ --tp-size 8 \ --moe-runner-backend flashinfer_mxfp4 \ --disable-cuda-graph \ --mem-fraction-static 0.85 \ --reasoning-parser deepseek-v4 \ --tool-call-parser deepseekv4 \ --host 0.0.0.0 \ --port 30000 \ --max-total-tokens=500000 \ --swa-full-tokens-ratio=0.4 \ --enable-metrics \ --enable-hierarchical-cache \ --hicache-storage-backend=mooncake \ --hicache-storage-backend-extra-config '{"master_server_address": "127.0.0.1:50051", "local_hostname": "localhost", "metadata_server": "http://127.0.0.1:8080/metadata", "global_segment_size": "512gb", "protocol": "tcp"}' # Group B sglang serve \ --model=deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash \ --pp-size 4 \ --tp-size 2 \ --moe-runner-backend flashinfer_mxfp4 \ --disable-cuda-graph \ --mem-fraction-static 0.85 \ --reasoning-parser deepseek-v4 \ --tool-call-parser deepseekv4 \ --host 0.0.0.0 \ --port 30000 \ --max-total-tokens=500000 \ --swa-full-tokens-ratio=0.4 \ --enable-metrics \ --enable-hierarchical-cache \ --hicache-storage-backend=mooncake \ --hicache-storage-backend-extra-config '{"master_server_address": "127.0.0.1:50051", "local_hostname": "localhost", "metadata_server": "http://127.0.0.1:8080/metadata", "global_segment_size": "512gb", "protocol": "tcp"}' # SWE bench agent python -m minisweagent.run.benchmarks.swebench \ --subset verified \ --split test \ -c swebench.yaml -c environment.container_timeout=24h \ -o /root/swe_test/result \ -m "openai/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash" \ -w 128 # SWE evaluation python -m swebench.harness.run_evaluation \ --predictions_path /root/swe_test/result/preds.json \ --dataset_name princeton-nlp/SWE-Bench_Verified \ --split test \ --max_workers 32 \ --run_id test-mini-swe-agent \ --timeout 1200 ``` ## Speed Tests and Profiling I tested with L1 only, L1+L2 and L1+L2+L3. signal.title: [diffusion] Fuse LTX-2.5 decoder 3D RoPE
signal.text: ## Summary - cache the compact fp32 temporal/height/width RoPE tables across decoder blocks at the same grid - add a paired BF16 JIT CUDA kernel that rotates Q and K in one launch while preserving the eager fp32 operation order - guard the fast path with first-sight bit-exact verification and a permanent eager fallback - add pointer-alignment and shape guards, CUDA correctness coverage, representative benchmarks, CPU cache/fallback tests, registry entries, and kernel docs ## H200 results Checked-in paired-RoPE benchmark: | Shape | Eager | JIT | Speedup | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | | stage 0 | 0.9381 ms | 0.0950 ms | 9.87x | | stage 4 tile | 2.5454 ms | 0.2467 ms | 10.32x | | stage 5 tile | 9.3790 ms | 0.8643 ms | 10.85x | Full decoder-component benchmark used the default 960x544x121 geometry, all 24 blocks, tiled decode, and NATTEN `na3d`: - median latency: 5379.54 ms -> 4463.80 ms (17.0% faster) - output SHA256 was identical across baseline/candidate runs: `b3a693021e1251d69847903a772e67dca4046425c576c60ce87bfee6689a6a68` - peak allocated memory was effectively unchanged: 7,422,371,328 -> 7,422,650,880 bytes - ptxas on sm_90a: 30 registers, 0 spill stores, 0 spill loads, 0 barriers The LTX-2.5 Hugging Face repo is gated and the benchmark host had no accepted credential, so this draft has not yet run the published checkpoint. The component benchmark instead used deterministically initialized full-size decoder weights; it exercises the production architecture, shapes, tiling, and NATTEN path. ## Validation - `python -m pytest -q test/registered/kernels/ops/diffusion/test_ltx25_decoder_rope.py test/registered/kernels/ops/diffusion/test_import_surface.py python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/unit/test_ltx2_5_config.py` (55 passed, 5 subtests passed) - final alignment-guard rerun: `test_ltx25_decoder_rope.py` (5 passed) - `uvx ruff check` on the new wrapper, CUDA test, and benchmark - `uvx ruff format --check` on changed Python files - `git diff --check` The failed gated download used a task-owned model cache; it contained no weight files and was removed and verified absent after this model group. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32378347205](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32378347205)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32378346938](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32378346938)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #32378347143](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32378347143)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [MLX] Upgrade to Torch 2.13/MLX 0.32+ and redesign the Torch-MLX tensor bridge
signal.text: ## Motivation MLX 0.32 can import Torch MPS allocations directly, while Torch 2.13 changes the runtime and DLPack edge cases that the Apple Silicon integration must support. The existing bridge stages MPS tensors through CPU memory, obscures borrowed-versus-owned lifetimes, and pays payload-sized copies. Separately, diffusion's `SGLANG_USE_MLX` norm override is not selected by normal MPS `CustomOp` dispatch; forcing those norms through Torch-MLX crossings is slower end to end. This PR upgrades the `srt_mps` runtime, fails fast on unsupported Torch/MLX pairs, separates owned copies from scoped zero-copy borrows, and removes the unreachable diffusion-only MLX fallback. It does not replace the existing SRT MLX runner; the stacked [yeahdongcn/sglang#7](https://github.com/yeahdongcn/sglang/pull/7) consumes these bridge primitives while redesigning that backend. ## Modifications - Update `srt_mps` in `python/pyproject_other.toml` to Torch 2.13.0, MLX >= 0.32.0, TorchVision 0.28.0, TorchAudio 2.11.0, and TorchCodec 0.15.0. The versions stay directly in `srt_mps`, matching the existing extra layout; `all_mps` inherits them through `srt_mps`. MLX keeps a 0.32.0 minimum but has no upper bound; startup accepts newer stable MLX releases. TorchAudio 2.11 remains intentional and was validated with the tested Torch 2.13 MPS stack. CPU and standalone `diffusion_mps` dependency lists are unchanged. - Move the SRT MLX version/device validation to the earliest model-independent `ServerArgs` bootstrap. With `SGLANG_USE_MLX=1`, SGLang requires stable Torch 2.13.x and stable MLX >= 0.32.0. Older MLX, Torch outside 2.13.x, and rc/dev builds fail before model path resolution/downloads and before the dummy-model short circuit. With the flag unset, importing SGLang still does not import MLX. - Redesign `tensor_bridge.py` around explicit ownership and batching: - `torch_to_mlx` creates and materializes MLX-owned storage when the result must outlive its Torch source. - `MlxTensorView` and `borrow_torch_tensors` provide persistent and batched zero-copy MPS borrows while retaining every Torch storage owner. - `mlx_call` and `mlx_call_multi` validate the target before work, fence Torch producers once, keep all borrowed inputs alive through lazy evaluation, evaluate ordinary multi-output results at one shared `mx.eval` boundary, batch the additional materialization boundary required by negative-stride outputs, and export them through DLPack. - `mlx_to_torch` uses evaluated DLPack views for MPS and explicit CPU views. Positive-stride layouts, including CPU float64, remain zero-copy. Negative-stride MLX views are materialized because Torch 2.13's DLPack importer otherwise aborts the process instead of raising a Python exception; unsupported CPU dtypes fail instead of silently narrowing. This PR intentionally owns these shared Torch-MLX bridge primitives. The stacked MPS redesign in [yeahdongcn/sglang#7](https://github.com/yeahdongcn/sglang/pull/7) consumes them for Torch-owned model weights and provider outputs, while its provider-specific invalidation callbacks and phase timing stay in that PR. - Remove `mps_fallback.py`, route diffusion MPS kernels to native Torch fallbacks, and use `F.layer_norm`/`F.rms_norm` instead of the old manual decomposition. The shared fallback remains compatible with both the default Torch 2.11 and CPU-backend Torch 2.12 stacks. RMSNorm preserves the optional-bias and input-dtype contracts even with fp32 parameters. The removed rotary and scale/shift entries were already aliases to Torch implementations; only the norm entries had MLX-specific implementations. - Remove diffusion's `SGLANG_USE_MLX` runtime handling and clarify in the existing documentation that the variable applies only to SRT serving. SRT keeps its existing `SGLANG_USE_MLX=1` opt-in. - Add Torch 2.13-compatible Triton import-stub symbols used by Inductor on MPS. - Rebase the branch onto upstream `main` at `978244d67148`; update VAE and Transformer component loaders to the upstream unified residency API so MPS layerwise offload remains valid after the upstream loader refactor. The diffusion MLX norm path is intentionally dropped after tracing and measurement. `CustomOp.dispatch_forward()` routes MPS to `forward_native`, so the legacy MLX override is unreachable in the normal production graph. Sana instrumentation confirmed zero legacy entrypoint calls, and forcing all 58 norms per DiT forward through MLX was slower end to end. Isolated large fp32 LayerNorm microbenchmarks sometimes favored MLX by a few percent, but the result was not robust across the common fp16/bf16 cases and did not justify repeated framework crossings. A future fully MLX-resident diffusion path can be evaluated separately. ## Accuracy Tests - `PATH="$PWD/sglang-metal/bin:$PATH" SGLANG_USE_MLX=1 HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 ./sglang-metal/bin/python test/run_suite.py --hw mlx --suite stage-a-unit-test-mlx` - **21/21 registered test files passed locally** on Apple M1 at PR head `c1f34a81d1`, including bridge, startup runtime gate, Triton-stub, and diffusion fallback coverage. - The focused bridge/runtime/diffusion-loader bundle passed **121 tests plus 36 subtests** after the rebase. - All four new test files are registered in `stage-a-unit-test-mlx`. `test_diffusion_torch_fallback.py` is additionally registered in `base-a-test-cpu`, `base-b-test-cpu`, and `base-b-test-cpu-arm64`. - The same six fallback UTs passed **6/6** in isolated Torch 2.11.0 and 2.12.0 CPU environments, including fp16/bf16 inputs with fp32 parameters. - Runtime tests verify Torch 2.12/2.14, MLX 0.31, and Torch/MLX rc/dev builds are rejected, while stable Torch 2.13 patch releases and stable MLX releases from 0.32.0 onward (including future minor versions) are accepted. Incompatible versions abort `ServerArgs` creation even for `model_path="dummy"`; missing MLX, unavailable PyTorch MPS, and unavailable MLX Metal each produce actionable startup errors. The disabled path constructs `ServerArgs` without importing MLX. - Bridge ownership checks cover owned/scoped/persistent lifetimes, source mutation and deletion, single-fence batched borrows, shared-eval multi-output calls, bfloat16/non-contiguous views, CPU float64 and unsupported dtypes, autograd detachment, invalid-target fail-fast behavior, and negative-stride materialization in an abort-safe subprocess. - SRT serving smoke with local `Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B`: both `SGLANG_USE_MLX=1` and the no-env Torch-MPS path returned **200** from `/health` and `/generate`. For prompt `The capital of France is` with greedy 8-token decoding, both paths returned identical output token IDs `[12095, 13, 576, 6722, 315, 9625, 374, 1083]` and text `Paris. The capital of France is also`. - Sana 600M, prompt `A small red cube on a plain white background`, seed 42, 256x256, 4 steps: native Torch output and the hypothetical all-MLX norm output remained visually consistent (PSNR 41.95 dB; max pixel delta 50). The final `mlx_call` image was byte-identical to the earlier explicit- keepalive MLX image. The ordinary Sana path recorded 58 Torch norm calls per DiT forward and zero legacy norm-fallback entrypoint calls. After the rebase, a native Torch-MPS Sana smoke with the same 256x256/4-step configuration produced a valid RGB PNG in 24.87s with 6.33GB peak memory. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Environment: Apple M1, macOS 26.5.2, Torch 2.13.0, MLX 0.32.0. All timings include the required producer/consumer synchronization. The operation table reports end-to-end norm-call timings, including bridge/export and synchronization, rather than raw kernel-only timings. It is one representative median-after-warmup run; an independent rerun preserved the common-Sana ordering but flipped whether large-fp32 MLX was slightly ahead or behind. | Case | Torch native | MLX owned copy | MLX scoped borrow | |---|---:|---:|---:| | Sana RMSNorm `(1,300,1152)` fp32 | 230 us | 676 us | 259 us | | Sana LayerNorm `(1,256,1152)` bf16 | 254 us | 913 us | 324 us | | Flux LayerNorm `(1,4096,3072)` fp32 | 2508 us | 4763 us | 2441 us | Bridge A/B directly calls the final `mlx_call(lambda a: a, tensor)` API against the pre-change CPU-staging implementation at the branch merge base (Apple M1, Torch 2.13.0, MLX 0.32.0). The table reports the range of per-batch p50 values across three independent batches; each batch used 5 warmups and 20 measured samples with producer/consumer synchronization: | Logical tensor | dtype / payload | Old CPU-staging p50 range | Final `mlx_call` p50 range | Minimum paired speedup | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:| | `(4096,4096)` | fp32 / 64 MiB | 32.134-57.424 ms | 0.0410-0.0871 ms | 368.8x | | `(4096,4096)` | bf16 / 32 MiB | 10.301-34.715 ms | 0.0293-0.0418 ms | 351.2x | | `(4096,8192)` | bf16 / 64 MiB | 16.896-22.184 ms | 0.0407-0.0617 ms | 273.7x | The old MPS round-trip staged payload through CPU/NumPy in both directions. The final `mlx_call` path aliases the Metal allocation through DLPack, removing the payload-sized copies; the synchronized wrapper/barrier cost was 29-87 us across these repeats. The same-shape bf16 case is 32 MiB because each element uses two bytes; the final row adds a true 64 MiB bf16 payload. This zero-copy result applies to the scoped-borrow API, not to an MLX array that must own its storage after the call. For that ownership contract, the 64 MiB fp32 materialized copy is about 4.08 ms versus about 60 us for a scoped borrow. This is why the API separates owned and borrowed semantics instead of exposing an unchecked `copy=False` default. Final-API Sana 4-step E2E forced-MLX experiment using `mlx_call` for all 58 norms per DiT forward (clean paired repeat): | Metric | Torch native | MLX scoped borrow | MLX penalty | |---|---:|---:|---:| | Denoising step median | 720.18 ms | 1170.40 ms | +62.5% | | DiT forward median | 375.06 ms | 581.92 ms | +55.2% | | Steady DiT median (drop first 2) | 353.42 ms | 581.92 ms | +64.7% | A second same-configuration measurement had higher Torch variance and a smaller penalty (+20.6% step, +21.9% DiT), but MLX was slower in both runs. ## Checklist - [x] Formatted with repository pre-commit hooks. - [x] Added and ran registered unit tests. - [x] Registered the shared diffusion fallback in CPU CI. - [x] Updated Apple Metal and diffusion documentation. - [x] Included accuracy and speed evidence above. - [x] CPU dependency pins remain unchanged. ## Review and Merge Process This is a draft for review of the ownership contract and the diffusion path decision. Please review the Torch/MLX lifetime semantics first; CI should run the MLX, CPU, JIT-kernel, and multimodal-generation change paths before promotion. In particular, the draft-gated MLX, Xeon CPU, and ARM64 CPU jobs must complete before this PR is marked ready. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #32438848514](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32438848514)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32438848397](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32438848397)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #32438848438](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32438848438)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [P/D disagg] Decode-side radix cache for SWA hybrid models (unified radix tree)
signal.text: <!-- codex-pr-description:start --> This PR enables device-resident decode-side radix reuse for hybrid SWA models on the experimental unified radix tree. It keeps full-attention KV reusable while transferring a fresh SWA window, reducing repeated P/D KV transfer without introducing HiCache or Mamba support. ### How This Was Implemented - Caps the reused full-attention prefix at the SWA window boundary and allocates only the fresh SWA tail. - Caches an unfinished request's computed prefix, deduplicates overlapping full-attention KV, then repoints the live request to the cache-owned slots. - Carries SWA lock boundaries through rejection paths, including when the cap reduces a matched prefix to zero. - Requires the unified radix tree and rejects hierarchical cache, Mamba/SSM, DSA, and SWA-compress variants. - Adds registered device-only gpt-oss-20b P/D coverage. ### Before and After | Unfinished-request state | Before | After | |---|---|---| | Full-attention KV is device-resident but the old SWA window is tombstoned | The normal full+SWA match can return zero indices after insertion has deduplicated the request's full KV. Repointing then fails `new_prefix_len <= len(new_indices)`; continuing would leave the request referencing freed duplicate slots. | This one lifecycle path requests the full device-resident match, rewrites the request table to the cache-owned full-KV slots, and transfers its lock to the deepest full-resident node. Normal scheduler matching remains SWA-window-safe. | <details> <summary>Walkthrough</summary> #### Mental model Full-attention KV remains reusable across turns, while SWA KV is valid only for the current live window. ```mermaid flowchart LR P["Prefill delta"] --> D["Decode admission"] M["Unified-tree prefix match"] --> D D --> F["Reuse full-attention KV"] D --> W["Allocate fresh SWA tail"] F --> C["Cache unfinished request"] W --> C ``` #### Why a full-device match is required `cache_unfinished_req` is named for the request lifecycle, not for a single pointer operation: it commits the current prefix of a request that will continue running. It inserts the prefix into the shared radix tree, deduplicates request-owned full-KV slots that the tree already owns, resolves the canonical cached slots, rewrites the live request's token table, and moves the request's tree lock. For a four-token reused prefix: ```text request-owned full KV before insert: R0 R1 R2 R3 cache-owned full KV: C0 C1 C2 C3 cache-owned SWA KV: tombstoned insert result: prefix_len = 4; duplicate R0-R3 are released normal match: [] because SWA is tombstoned full-device match: [C0 C1 C2 C3] canonical slots for repointing ``` The normal match would make the safety check `4 <= 0` fail. The full-device match makes it `4 <= 4`, so the request is repointed to `C0-C3` before it continues; `return_full_match` defaults to false and is enabled only at this repoint call, so admission and reuse decisions still require an SWA-valid match. #### Request lifecycle Decode matches and locks the device prefix, caps reuse at the SWA window boundary, checks both full and SWA pool budgets, and allocates the remaining full pages plus the live SWA tail. Admission rejection releases the original matched-node lock even when capping reduces the usable prefix to zero; unfinished caching then commits the live prefix, tombstones out-of-window SWA positions, repoints full-attention slots, and transfers the request lock. #### Boundaries and limitations This change is device-only. SWA decode radix combined with hierarchical cache is rejected, and Mamba/SSM, DSA, and SWA-compress models remain unsupported. </details> ### Validation - `PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 .venv/bin/python test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_decode_radix_lock_ref.py -v` — 6 passed. - `PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 .venv/bin/python test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_unified_radix_cache_unittest.py` — 1,818 ran; 758 skipped; OK. - Mocked `build_kv_cache` smoke — device-only path succeeds; SWA + hierarchical cache raises. - `.venv/bin/pre-commit run --files ...` — passed. - Targeted `/rerun-group disaggregation` — SWA decode-radix passed on 8×H20; hybrid-attention passed on 8×H200. <!-- codex-pr-description:end --> ## Motivation Extend the decode-side radix cache (P/D disaggregation, #19746) to **sliding-window-attention (SWA) hybrid models** such as gpt-oss, which are currently rejected at startup. With this, a decode worker can **reuse a cached prefix's full-attention KV across requests/turns** and request only the delta from the prefill worker, instead of receiving the entire prefix KV every time. The feature is gated to the **experimental unified radix tree** (`SGLANG_ENABLE_UNIFIED_RADIX_TREE`). The default `SWARadixCache` and the Mamba/SSM pools remain unsupported on this path, as do DSA (DeepSeek-V4) and SWA-compress (Gemma/MiMo) variants. > Supersedes #26218, which took the same feature through the default `SWARadixCache`. We're standardizing on the unified tree for SWA decode-radix, so that path is dropped here. ## Background: why SWA needs special handling A hybrid SWA model keeps **two** KV caches with different lifetimes: - **Full-attention layers** — keep KV for every token, as long as it's cached. Large, sticky. - **Sliding-window layers** — keep KV for only the last *W* tokens; older slots recycle as the window advances. Bounded. So on the decode worker the prefix's **full-attention** KV can be reused directly, but its **sliding-window** KV cannot — by reuse time the original writer's window has slid past it. Such a node is a **tombstone** (full KV present, SWA recycled). This is normal and harmless for correctness: a reuser only needs the window for its *own* current position, which it gets fresh. ## What this PR does - **`kv_cache_builder.py`** — allow SWA + `--disaggregation-decode-enable-radix-cache` **only when the unified tree is active**; otherwise raise (DSA / SWA-compress still blocked even under unified). - **`decode.py`** — decode-side SWA mechanics: cap full-attention prefix reuse at the sliding-window start so the window lands in the fresh delta; `alloc_extend_swa_tail` on radix hits; mark the non-window prefix `swa_evicted_seqlen` (SWA tombstone); SWA-aware budget/eviction accessors; thread the SWA lock uuid through prefix lock/release. - **`unified_radix_cache.py` + `swa_component.py` + `base_prefix_cache.py`** — two `UnifiedRadixCache` fixes this path needs: 1. **SWA pool leak.** `SWAComponent.prepare_for_caching_req` only forwarded `swa_evicted_seqlen` when `is_finished=True`; on the unfinished path the out-of-window prefix tokens were inserted as *live* SWA and counted as `swa_evictable`, so at idle `available + evictable` exceeds the pool. Forward it on both paths so they become tombstones (`0` on the aggregated path → unchanged there). 2. **`cache_unfinished_req` repoint.** The dedup/repoint operates on full-attention cards but was sized by the SWA-window-safe match. On a reused, tombstoned prefix the window-safe match collapses to `0` while the cards number in the hundreds, tripping `assert new_prefix_len <= len(new_indices)`. Add `MatchPrefixParams.return_full_match`: `_match_prefix_helper` returns the deepest device-resident node, `_match_post_processor` returns the full cards + that node. The unified `inc_lock_ref` already skips tombstones, so no lock change is needed. No `swa_radix_cache.py` changes — the old path is intentionally not supported. ## Usage ``` --disaggregation-mode decode \ --disaggregation-transfer-backend {nixl|mooncake} \ --disaggregation-decode-enable-radix-cache \ --page-size 64 # with SGLANG_ENABLE_UNIFIED_RADIX_TREE=1 in the env ``` ## Test `test/manual/disaggregation/test_disaggregation_decode_radix_cache_swa.py` (gpt-oss-20b; manual because the model isn't in the CI pool) launches with the unified tree via `extra_*_env` and runs the shared decode-radix mixin (multi-turn cache-hit + 2-pass gsm8k). Validated on `openai/gpt-oss-20b`, 1P1D on 2×L40S, `--page-size 64 --attention-backend triton`, strict idle + per-iteration memory checks: | Check | Result | |---|---| | Multi-turn prefix reuse (decode cache hit) | cached tokens grow across rounds (0 → 1792 → 3584) | | gsm8k, 500 ex, 2 passes (2nd hits the cache) | 0.532 / 0.572 | | SWA-pool leak / `cache_unfinished_req` assert | **0 / 0** | ## Deep dive Writeup of the two `UnifiedRadixCache` bugs hit while enabling this path — exact errors, root causes, fix walkthrough, before/after validation: https://gist.github.com/ishandhanani/ed3cd2082381f31d848a7f6fcac977c6 <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:no_entry_sign: [Run #32277331665](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32277331665)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #32438839011](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32438839011)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32277331696](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32277331696)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: feat(kernels): generalize persistent CuTe JIT cache
signal.text: ## Motivation SGLang already has a persistent CuTe JIT cache for FlashAttention, but it lives under the FlashAttention package and only supports TVM-FFI exports. Kimi-K3 KDA also uses explicit `cute.compile` calls, but its cache is process-local. ## Modifications - Move the existing cache to `sglang.kernels.jit.cute_aot_cache`. - Generalize it over consumer source roots and CuTe ABI while keeping per-key file locking. - Include the explicit `CUTE_DSL_ARCH` target, or the detected local CUDA architecture, in the source fingerprint. GPU probing remains lazy when persistence is disabled. - Publish compiled objects through a temporary path and `os.replace`, so readers never observe a partially written final object and failed exports leave no temporary artifact. - If an object fails to load, discard it while the per-key shared lock still excludes writers, then fall back to compilation. - Keep routine cache activity at debug level so enabling persistence does not add normal INFO-level server noise. - Keep FlashAttention as the TVM-FFI consumer. A small cache adapter preserves `FLASH_ATTENTION_CUTE_DSL_CACHE_*` behavior and gives `SGLANG_CUTE_AOT_CACHE_DIR` precedence when both configurations are present. - Add `SGLANG_CUTE_AOT_CACHE_DIR` as the shared opt-in cache root and document that it must be trusted. - Make Kimi-K3 KDA MTP the second consumer using the native CuTe ABI. - Normalize CUDA device ordinals only for disk keys so same-architecture ranks can share objects; KDA includes compute capability and indexing width in its compile key. The default remains process-local. This does not introduce rank authority, compiler monkeypatching, or kernel math changes. ## Reviewability Git detects the existing cache module as a 51%-similarity rename. The aggregate patch is 394 additions and 86 deletions across six files; 184 added lines are focused tests. The large add/delete presentation from the previous revision was caused by rename detection falling below GitHub's threshold and has been removed. ## Validation ### Focused unit and static validation - Eleven focused cache cases cover new/legacy FlashAttention environment precedence, quiet routine logging, disabled behavior, lazy architecture detection, factory/source/architecture namespacing, CUDA device ordinal normalization, both native and TVM-FFI export/load paths, atomic publication, failed-export cleanup, and invalid-object eviction. - SGLang's registered-test collector resolves the pytest file to `base-a-test-cpu`. - Black, Ruff, isort (for applicable paths), codespell, Python syntax compilation, `scripts/lint/check_registered_tests.py`, and `git diff --check` pass. ### Real GPU cache validation Validated commit `e48384b39c` on one NVIDIA B300 SXM6 AC (SM103) with Python 3.12.3, PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130, NVIDIA CUTLASS DSL 4.6.2, and TVM-FFI 0.1.11. This was cache/kernel validation only; no model was loaded. - **KDA native ABI:** `TestKimiK3ComputeKernels.test_mtp_replayssm_ring` cold-compiled and exported two objects. A fresh process with `cute.compile` replaced by an exception loaded both objects, passed the same output and recurrent-state checks, and left object hashes unchanged. - **FlashAttention TVM-FFI ABI:** a BF16 `[1, 64, 4, 64]` causal forward cold-compiled and exported one object. A fresh process with `cute.compile` replaced by an exception loaded it and produced the identical output SHA-256 (`780881b74eb262e7831f1f2a710c53a5ec209f52f371ec4fe51c6b43b2ff9678`). Against an FP32 reference, relative L2 was `0.001861` and max absolute error was `0.007716`. - **Corruption recovery:** the FlashAttention object was replaced with invalid bytes. The next process detected and removed it, recompiled with the same output SHA-256, and published a repaired object. A final fresh process with `cute.compile` blocked loaded the repaired object successfully. [Validation run](https://modal.com/apps/modal-flash/main/ap-3PyR14z34YcGgsm8zGdHgO) - No object hashes changed and no `.tmp.o` artifacts remained after validation. ## Speed tests and profiling No end-to-end speed benchmark is included. A warm process can load an existing FlashAttention or KDA object instead of compiling it again. ## Checklist - [x] Format code according to the project configuration. - [x] Add focused unit tests. - [x] Document the new environment variable and trust boundary. - [x] Validate native and TVM-FFI cold-to-warm round trips on a real GPU. - [x] Validate invalid-object eviction, recompilation, and repaired warm loading. - [x] Keep the cache move visible as a rename for review. - [x] Follow the SGLang code style guidance. - [ ] Provide an end-to-end speed benchmark (out of scope for cache validation). <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32091161530](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32091161530)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32091161307](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32091161307)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->
