signal.title: [AMD][CI][Fix] Guard FP32 LM head mm(out_dtype) fast path on ROCm
signal.text: ## Motivation `test/registered/rl/test_fp32_lm_head.py` fails deterministically on the AMD `stage-b-test-1-gpu-small-amd` shard (`linux-mi300-1gpu-sglang`, partition 7): ``` RuntimeError: gemm input type at::BFloat16 and output type float is not supported for ROCm ``` The FP32 LM head fast path added in #32370 selects `torch.mm(..., out_dtype=torch.float32)` whenever `hidden_states.is_cuda`: ```python use_mm_out_dtype = ( hidden_states.is_cuda and hidden_states.dtype == lm_head.weight.dtype and hidden_states.dtype in (torch.float16, torch.bfloat16) ) ``` `is_cuda` is `True` on ROCm, but the mixed input/output GEMM is **not** available in the torch build the failing image ships. `rocm/sgl-dev:*-rocm700-*` is based on `rocm/sgl-dev:rocm7-vllm-20250904`, which pins torch `2.9.0a0+git7bcbafe` (upstream commit `7bcbafe`, 2025-08-04). In that source `at::cuda::blas::gemm<at::BFloat16, float>()` rejects unconditionally, before any backend dispatch: ```cpp template <> void gemm<at::BFloat16, float>(CUDABLAS_GEMM_ARGTYPES_AND_C_DTYPE(at::BFloat16, float)) { #ifdef USE_ROCM TORCH_CHECK(false, "gemm input type at::BFloat16 and output type float is not supported for ROCm"); #else ... #endif gemm_internal<at::BFloat16, float>(...); // unreachable on ROCm } ``` pytorch#161540 (`a8d6943d36c1`, 2025-09-02) removed these four unconditional checks — in v2.9.1 the same guard reads `#ifndef USE_ROCM` and only covers the CUDA compute-capability case. The `rocm720` images use `rocm/pytorch:rocm7.2_..._pytorch_release_2.9.1` and so include it. **The dividing line is torch source older than 2025-09-02, not the ROCm version** — `rocm700-mi35x` (gfx950) also ships the old torch, while `rocm720-mi30x` (gfx942) ships 2.9.1, so this does not track gfx942 vs gfx950 either. On newer torch there is a second, narrower raise site: the Composable Kernel branch inside `gemm_internal`. That one requires an explicit `torch.backends.cuda.preferred_blas_library("ck")` — `blasPreferredBackend()` only ever resolves to `Cublas` or `Cublaslt` from env, and SGLang never calls the setter — so it is not what CI hits. The two are distinguishable by message: the CK branch in `gemm_internal<at::BFloat16, float>` prints `at::Half` (an upstream copy-paste typo, still present in v2.9.1), whereas CI reports `at::BFloat16`, which only the unconditional check emits. The capability gate below is deliberately agnostic to *which* of these applies. It never probes with a real GEMM: an earlier revision of this PR did, and the hipBLASLt algorithm lookup cost ~700 ms on MI355X without amortizing into the first real LM head GEMM. This is pre-existing CI debt on `main`, not a regression from any in-flight PR; the same shard fails on scheduled `main` runs. ## Modifications **`python/sglang/srt/layers/logits_processor.py`** - Add `_supports_mm_fp32_out_dtype(device_type, dtype)` and make it a conjunct of `use_mm_out_dtype`, so an unsupported build falls back to the pre-existing explicit-FP32-cast `torch.matmul` path instead of raising. It decides from metadata, no GEMM: - **ROCm**: gate on `torch >= 2.9.0`, the first release containing pytorch#161540. - **CUDA**: BF16 additionally requires compute capability 8.0+, which torch enforces in the `#ifndef USE_ROCM` branch of the very same function. FP16 has no such restriction. The version comparison is prerelease-aware on purpose. The rocm700 image ships `2.9.0a0+git7bcbafe`, and `utils/common.py`'s existing `torch_release` tuple discards the alpha marker: | version string | `parse(...) >= parse("2.9.0")` | `.release >= (2,9,0)` | |---|---|---| | `2.8.0` | False ✅ | False ✅ | | `2.9.0a0+git7bcbafe` (**the failing image**) | **False ✅** | **True ❌** | | `2.9.0` | True ✅ | True ✅ | | `2.9.1+rocm7.2.0.git7e1940d4` | True ✅ | True ✅ | Using the `.release` tuple would leave the shard red. There is a regression test pinned to exactly this. Deliberately **not** a plain `is_hip()` gate. `torch.mm(out_dtype=...)` works fine on ROCm with a current torch (verified on gfx950 / ROCm 7.2), and disabling it there would give up #32370's optimization on hardware that supports it — measured at 5.3× (batch 8) to 8.6× (batch 256) for a 152064x4096 BF16 LM head, plus a 2.32 GiB transient FP32 weight copy per forward. A bare `is_hip` gate would also have missed the CUDA sm80 rule and simply relocated the crash to V100. **Coverage deliberately dropped**: the Composable Kernel BLAS backend rejects this op on *any* torch version, and the version gate does not catch it. Reaching CK requires an explicit `torch.backends.cuda.preferred_blas_library("ck")`; no env var selects it (`Context.h` maps `TORCH_BLAS_PREFER_{CU,HIP}BLASLT` to `Cublaslt` only) and SGLang never calls the setter. **`test/registered/rl/test_fp32_lm_head.py`** - Derive the expected op from the same helper rather than `torch.cuda.is_available()`, which encoded the wrong assumption. - Add `force_support` to `_run_case`, pinning the helper's answer so **both** selection branches are exercised on every runner, NVIDIA included. Without it the suite is tautological: it asserts against the same predicate production consults, so the assertion holds by construction and the fallback branch is only ever reached on a host that already lacks support. - Add `TestMMFP32OutDtypeGate` covering the version strings, the ROCm gate, the sm80 rule, and non-CUDA devices. Pure metadata, so it needs no GPU. ## Accuracy Tests No numerical change on any backend that was already working — where the gate returns `True` the emitted op is byte-identical to before. Where it returns `False` the code takes the explicit-FP32-cast path, which is the same path used before #32370 and which is strictly higher precision than the `bf16`-input GEMM it replaces (both accumulate to FP32; the fallback additionally upcasts the inputs). No accuracy run is attached because on the available hardware (MI355X, ROCm 7.2, hipBLASLt) the gate returns `True` and this PR is a no-op at runtime. ## Speed Tests and Profiling No steady-state delta, and no added device work anywhere: - The fused `mm(out_dtype=fp32)` path is preserved bit-for-bit on every build that implements it. - The gate issues **zero GEMMs**. `_TORCH_HAS_ROCM_MM_FP32_OUT` is a single `packaging.version.parse` at import. `_supports_mm_fp32_out_dtype` is `@lru_cache`d on `(device_type, dtype)`; on ROCm it only reads that bool, and `torch.cuda.get_device_capability()` is reached only on NVIDIA + BF16, once. - Per forward this is one cached-function call plus a tuple hash (sub-microsecond, host-side), and it is the **last** conjunct of a short-circuiting `and`, so it is not even evaluated unless the three cheap dtype/device checks already passed. - No CUDA-graph impact: the gate is Python, so it runs at capture time and never during replay. ### Unit tests `11 passed` (16 subtests) on MI355X / ROCm 7.2 / torch 2.9.1. The suite needs no GPU for the gate tests. Both branches of the selection are asserted on every runner via `force_support`, and the gate is asserted directly against the real-world version strings including the failing image's `2.9.0a0+git7bcbafe`. **Mutation checks** — the PR head is green. To show the new tests are not tautological, the fix was broken locally in two ways and reverted; each breakage is caught: | mutation applied locally, then reverted | caught by | |---|---| | drop `and _supports_mm_fp32_out_dtype(...)` from `use_mm_out_dtype` | `test_probe_unsupported_falls_back_to_explicit_fp32_matmul`, for both FP16 and BF16 — the fallback stops being selected and the ROCm raise comes back | | swap the prerelease-aware `parse()` for a `.release` tuple compare | `test_torch_version_compare_is_prerelease_aware`, on exactly `2.9.0a0+git7bcbafe` — the failing image's torch gets misread as `>= 2.9.0` | No pre-existing test reacts to the first mutation, which is why the original suite was blind to this regression. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process). 2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers. 3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so. 4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR. cc @ilyasher-harmonic (author of #32370) <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #31701376978](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31701376978)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #31701376794](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31701376794)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #31701376988](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31701376988)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [AMD] Add AITER HIP backend for packed GDN decode on gfx950
signal.text: ## Motivation SGLang currently uses the Triton GDN kernel for Qwen3.5 decode on ROCm. For the fixed packed BF16 contract on MI355X, the new AITER HIP kernel reduces decode latency by about 13–23% while keeping the existing one-launch packed data flow. This PR wires that kernel into SGLang as an explicit decode backend. Unsupported contracts continue to use Triton. ## Modifications - Add `--linear-attn-decode-backend hip` and `LinearAttnKernelBackend.HIP`; keep `hip` out of the shared/default and prefill backend choices, and reject it for non-GDN models during initialization. - Add `HipGDNKernel`, which calls AITER directly for the exact packed BF16 gfx950 contract. - Gate the AITER path with `is_gfx95_supported()` and fall back to Triton decode on other ROCm architectures. - Keep ReplaySSM and unsupported shapes, dtypes, strides, scales, or layouts on `TritonGDNKernel`. - Keep prefill/extend and verify paths on Triton. - Add unit tests for exact-contract dispatch, architecture and contract fallback, CLI scope, non-GDN rejection, ReplaySSM fallback, and prefill/verify dispatch. No QKV split/copy, state conversion, temporary tensor, or additional kernel launch is added to the supported decode path. The default backend is unchanged unless `hip` is selected. ## Accuracy Tests GSM8K, 5-shot, all 1319 questions, temperature 0, max new tokens 2048; Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-MXFP4, TP2, MI355X. Both servers used Triton prefill and BF16 Mamba state. | Backend | Accuracy | Correct | Invalid | |---|---:|---:|---:| | Triton | 92.6459% | 1222/1319 | 8/1319 | | AITER HIP | 92.3427% | 1218/1319 | 6/1319 | This single deterministic pair differs by four correct answers (`-0.3033` percentage points). It is reported as a draft result rather than an accuracy-parity claim; prediction-level diffing and/or repeated evaluation is required before marking the PR ready. Normalized output throughput was `+0.819%`; total latency is not compared because the two runs generated different token counts. ## Benchmarking and Profiling ### Kernel (exact AITER PR commit) AITER `test_common.perftest`: two warmup iterations followed by 101 profiled decode calls, with default input rotation and device-time averaging. The table reports the median of five fresh-process `avg us/iter` results. | BS | Triton BF16 | AITER HIP | Latency reduction | |---:|---:|---:|---:| | 32 | 18.174 us | **13.965 us** | **23.16%** | | 64 | 31.746 us | **24.764 us** | **21.99%** | | 128 | 56.940 us | **49.603 us** | **12.89%** | ### End-to-end Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-MXFP4, TP2, MI355X; random ISL/OSL 8192/1024, range ratio 0.8, request rate `inf`, prompts = concurrency x 10. Each point used a fresh server and an identical full-workload warmup. Only the decode backend changed; prefill remained Triton. | Concurrency | Triton output tok/s | AITER HIP output tok/s | Throughput | Median TPOT (Triton -> HIP) | |---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | 4 | 362.097 | 367.788 | **+1.572%** | 10.334 -> 10.181 ms | | 8 | 589.844 | 609.401 | **+3.316%** | 12.785 -> 12.541 ms | | 16 | 858.537 | 873.679 | **+1.764%** | 17.984 -> 17.663 ms | | 32 | 1140.530 | 1166.321 | **+2.261%** | 27.119 -> 26.482 ms | | 64 | 1461.569 | 1486.747 | **+1.723%** | 43.125 -> 42.335 ms | | 128 | 1823.527 | 1859.667 | **+1.982%** | 69.714 -> 68.288 ms | Across the six points, the non-weighted mean improvement was `+2.103%` output throughput and `+1.901%` median TPOT. signal.text: Reduce GDN prefill launches for benchmarked BF16/FP32 GPU shapes while preserving the original path on unsupported platforms, dtypes, layouts, and launch-bound wide shapes. <!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. --> ## Motivation The Triton GDN prefill path normalizes Q and K with two separate `l2norm_fwd` launches. Qwen3.5 GDN uses equal Q/K head layouts, so both normalizations can be computed in one Triton launch. This change reduces GDN prefill launch overhead on AMD GPUs while preserving the existing two-kernel implementation as the fallback. <!-- Describe the purpose and goals of this pull request. --> ## Modifications - Add `fused_l2norm_qk` to normalize compatible Q/K tensors in one Triton launch. - Preserve runtime token-count behavior with `do_not_specialize` to avoid recompilation by sequence length. - Enable automatic fused routing only when: - the platform is AMD; - execution is in the GDN `chunk_gated_delta_rule` path; - Q/K are GPU BF16/FP32 tensors with identical shape and contiguous layout. - Preserve two existing `l2norm_fwd` calls for: - non-AMD platforms; - asymmetric Q/K row layouts; - non-contiguous or otherwise incompatible tensors. - unbenchmarked head dimensions larger than 512; - the launch-bound `head_dim=512, rows<32` corner. - Add AMD/CUDA correctness tests, explicit fused/fallback dispatch tests, and a focused benchmark. signal.title: perf: overlap Qwen shared expert with DeepEP routed experts
signal.text: ## Motivation For Qwen MoE models using CUDA and DeepEP, the shared expert currently runs on the default stream before the routed-expert path. This serializes two independent computations and leaves an available alternate stream unused. This PR adds an opt-in path that overlaps the Qwen shared expert with routed-expert/DeepEP execution. ## Modifications - Add `SGLANG_QWEN_DEEPEP_SHARED_OVERLAP` (default: `false`). - When enabled on CUDA, enqueue the shared expert on `alt_stream`, execute the routed-expert path on the current stream, and wait on an event immediately before accumulating the shared output. - When breakable CUDA graph is active, skip this optimization and retain the existing serial shared-expert path; cross-segment overlap across the eager DeepEP break is out of scope. - Document the new environment variable. ## Accuracy Tests The accuracy evidence below was collected on predecessor `38f714d28e1fa01ae5b1ce38ce576373b8293722`, based on upstream main `0c072235f44fce4b89e594c2d3348e4f48e774b8`, with a clean source tree. Current head `76815b3766deb3a3c9aceef1cb346093f691d976` differs only by making breakable CUDA graph use the pre-existing serial fallback instead of an alternate-stream path with an immediate wait; the non-breakable overlap implementation measured below is unchanged. Configuration: `nvidia/Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-NVFP4`, 8x GB300, FP4 weights, FP8 KV cache, TP8/DP8/EP8, NEXTN draft length 6, DeepEP low-latency mode, 200 GSM8K examples, 5 shots, temperature 0.6, top-p 0.95, and top-k 20. The run used natural NEXTN acceptance. | Metric | Result | Gate | |---|---:|---:| | GSM8K score | **0.990** (200/200) | >= 0.95 | | Request-weighted mean accepted length | **4.6102** (1,379 decode-log rows; request weight 11,625) | > 3.3 | | Evaluation latency | 95.646 s | -- | | Evaluation output throughput | 5,621.1 token/s | -- | All eight ranks completed target verify CUDA graph capture, followed by draft decode and draft extend graph capture. The job completed successfully with exit code 0. Breakable CUDA graph is now intentionally excluded from this optimization, and no performance gain is claimed for that fallback. ## Speed Tests and Profiling The performance A/B exercised the same overlap mechanism on the benchmark stack before this upstream-main port. The upstream-main commit listed in the accuracy section was validated separately through CUDA graph capture and GSM8K. The end-to-end A/B comparison used the same configuration and differed only in the job name and `SGLANG_QWEN_DEEPEP_SHARED_OVERLAP=true`. Configuration: `nvidia/Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-NVFP4`, 24x GB300 disaggregated serving (four TP4/DP4/EP4 prefill replicas and one TP8/DP8/EP8 decode replica), FP4 weights, FP8 KV cache, NEXTN draft length 6, concurrency 896, fixed accepted length 4.8, and a 3,600-second AgentX replay. | AIPerf metric | Disabled | Enabled | Delta | |---|---:|---:|---:| | Total token throughput | 2,649,331.82 token/s | 2,705,912.48 token/s | **+2.14%** | | Output token throughput | 25,466.20 token/s | 26,000.99 token/s | **+2.10%** | | Request throughput | 27.980 request/s | 28.516 request/s | **+1.91%** | | Mean inter-token latency | 18.220 ms | 17.623 ms | **-3.28%** | | Theoretical prefix-cache hit | 95.433% | 95.452% | +0.020 pp | These are end-to-end AIPerf results without profiler instrumentation. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). signal.title: [Fix] Transformers-fallback (GPT-NeoX) + KV pool config (DeepSeek-VL2)
signal.text: ## Summary Three small fixes surfaced by consecutive downstream accuracy runs. All three are one-liners (plus comments); the first two live in the Transformers-fallback layer, the third in `ModelConfig`. ### 1. `hf_to_sglang_mapper` — map `gpt_neox.` and `embed_out.` `GPTNeoXForCausalLM` has no native SGLang impl → falls back to `TransformersForCausalLM`. The fallback calls `AutoModel.from_config(config)`, which returns the bare `GPTNeoXModel` backbone (`embed_in`, `layers`, `final_layer_norm`) as `self.model`; `self.lm_head` is materialized separately by `CausalMixin`. Pythia / NeoX checkpoints were saved from `GPTNeoXForCausalLM.state_dict()`, so keys carry a `gpt_neox.` wrapper prefix for the backbone and a top-level `embed_out.` for the LM head. The base mapper has no rule for either, so the catch-all `""` → `"model."` fires and produces `model.gpt_neox.embed_in.weight` — which the loader can't find (`ValueError: No module or parameter named 'model.gpt_neox' ...`). **Fix:** add two prefix rules alongside the existing `"transformer.": "model."` (GPT-2 analogue): - `"gpt_neox.": "model."` — strip the wrapper prefix so backbone keys land under `self.model.*`. - `"embed_out.": "lm_head."` — route the LM head to SGLang's `self.lm_head` slot. ### 2. `skip_substrs` — skip GPT-NeoX-style `.attention.bias` causal-mask buffer Older GPT-NeoX checkpoints include a persistent causal-mask buffer named `gpt_neox.layers.N.attention.bias`. Newer transformers versions register the same buffer with `persistent=False`, so it is absent from the constructed model's tree. `self.skip_substrs` already skips GPT-2-style `.attn.bias` / `.attn.masked_bias` (attention module named `attn`), but not GPT-NeoX-style `.attention.bias` (attention module named `attention`). Result: `ValueError: No module or parameter named 'model.layers.0.attention.bias' ...`. **Fix:** add `.attention.bias` to the skip list. The already-present `.masked_bias` catches the fill-value counterpart regardless of attention module name. ### 3. `ModelConfig.v_head_dim` — treat `0` as unset (fixes DeepSeek-VL2 non-MLA V-cache) `deepseek-ai/deepseek-vl2-tiny`'s `language_config` sets `use_mla=False` **and** `v_head_dim=0` — the `0` is an MLA-disabled sentinel from the checkpoint's DeepseekV2-flavored config, not a real head dimension. `ModelConfig.__init__` currently substitutes `head_dim` for `v_head_dim` only when the attribute is `None`, so a `getattr` that returns `0` slips through into `self.v_head_dim`. `pool_configurator.py` then reads `model_config.v_head_dim` directly in the non-MLA branch, and per-slot V-buffers get allocated with last dim = 0. The first extend prefill fails: ``` File ".../mem_cache/memory_pool.py", line 192, in _set_kv_buffer_impl v_cache[indices] = v RuntimeError: shape mismatch: value tensor of shape [432, 10, 128] cannot be broadcast to indexing result of shape [432, 10, 0] ``` DeepSeek-VL2 explicitly selects the standard (non-MLA) `DeepseekForCausalLM` language model when `use_mla=False` (`sglang/srt/models/deepseek_vl2.py`), which produces real V with the usual `num_kv_heads * head_dim` layout — the attention layer is correct; the pool is what's mis-sized. **Fix:** swap the guard to `if not self.v_head_dim:` so both `None` and `0` fall back to `self.head_dim`. MLA architectures are unaffected — their architecture-specific `elif` branches later in the same block overwrite `self.v_head_dim` with the real value from the text config. ## Test plan - [x] `pre-commit run --files <changed>` — passes locally for all three files. - [x] `EleutherAI/pythia-12b` (TP=2, triton) — reproduces the missing-mapper failure on `main`; loads through with fix 1. - [x] `EleutherAI/gpt-neox-20b` (TP=2, triton) — with fix 1 applied, reproduces the missing-skip failure on `main`; loads through with fix 2, warmup succeeds, first `POST /generate` returns 200. - [x] `deepseek-ai/deepseek-vl2-tiny` (TP=1, triton, `--disable-radix-cache`, mem-fraction 0.55) — reproduces the `_set_kv_buffer_impl` shape-mismatch on `main`; with fix 3, KV cache allocates `K size = V size = 3.38 GB` (previously `V size = 0.00 GB`), text `POST /generate` returns 200 with valid tokens. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:no_entry_sign: [Run #32404965067](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32404965067)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32404964663](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32404964663)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #32404964731](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32404964731)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: Fix overlap prebuilt row reuse race
signal.text: Wait for outstanding overlap forward work before prebuilt batch processing can seed a reused request-pool row. ## Motivation Bug fix for race condition in FutureMap. publish() call can happen in two cases: (1) in forward stream after draft+verify. signal.text: <!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. --> ## Motivation Fix https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/34720. There will be two backend for linear attention on XPU: triton and intel_xpu. Our plan: For the triton backend, we always use triton kernels. That means we need to remove the standalong SYCL conv1d kernel from SGLang. signal.title: [AMD] Perf Kimi-K3 low concurrency optimizations
signal.text: ## Summary - Vendor selected Kimi-K3 gfx950 FlyDSL kernels in SGLang with a fail-closed source selector. - Add MLA output-gate, KDA group64/B2, 12-head AITER MLA decode-side padding, and optional latent-tail integrations. - Use one cooperative preactivated MoE producer for exact M2/M4 while larger batches retain the existing fallback. - Add the Kimi-K3 M16384 GEMM tuning profile. - Use the AITER revision already pinned by SGLang; no AITER update is required. ## Runtime configuration Base Kimi-K3 AITER configuration: ```bash export SGLANG_USE_AITER=1 export SGLANG_AITER_K3_OPT=1 export AITER_FLYDSL_FORCE=1 export AITER_SITUV2_A8W4=1 export AITER_SITUV2_A4W4=0 export SGLANG_K3_FLYDSL_SOURCE=sglang ``` Enable the PR features: ```bash # MLA output-gate fusion export SGLANG_K3_AITER_MLA_GATE=1 # KDA input projection; B2_FUSIONS adds its exact-M2 specialization export SGLANG_K3_AITER_KDA_GROUP64=1 export SGLANG_K3_AITER_B2_FUSIONS=1 # Unified exact-M2/M4 cooperative MoE preroute export SGLANG_K3_AITER_MOE_PREROUTE_FP8=1 export SGLANG_K3_PREROUTE_PREACTIVATED_SHARED=1 # M=16384 GEMM tuning rows export SGLANG_K3_AITER_M16384_PROFILE=1 ``` The latent-tail profile is independent and remains off by default because it reduces token capacity. Enable it only when explicitly evaluating that trade-off: ```bash export SGLANG_K3_AITER_LATENT_TAIL_FP8=1 ``` The 12-head padding path has no feature flag. It is selected automatically for the covered Kimi-K3 shape when using AITER MLA decode, for example: ```bash sglang serve \ --model-path /path/to/Kimi-K3 \ --tp-size 8 \ --attention-backend aiter \ --decode-attention-backend aiter ``` All integrations are shape/architecture guarded and fail closed to the existing implementation when the runtime contract is not covered. ## Performance - Unified M2 cooperative preroute: `+1.08%` throughput, `-1.11%` TPOT over the prior M2 design. - Unified M4 cooperative preroute: `+3.08%` throughput, `-3.33%` TPOT over the matched M4 baseline. - M16384 profile: approximately `+0.7%` throughput at C8/C16/C32 and `-2.34%` C32 TTFT. ## Accuracy - GSM8K 1319: `0.953` - Invalid responses: `0.001` ## Test plan - [x] Selected FlyDSL tests against pinned AITER `d9e5ef7`: 35 passed - [x] C2 8192/256 smoke: 8/8 requests succeeded - [x] C4 8192/256 smoke: 8/8 requests succeeded - [x] GSM8K 50: 1.000 - [x] GSM8K 1319: 0.953 - [x] Forbidden listed-PR path audit and `git diff --check` The current container installs a newer FlyDSL than the old AITER pin expects for full-model MoE startup. The vendored focused kernels were tested directly against the exact pin; full-model smoke used the current compatible AITER checkout. signal.title: [AMD] Perf Kimi-K3 fuse MLA Q and cache preparation
signal.text: ## Summary - Fuse Kimi-K3 identity-RoPE Q materialization, Q concat, and latent KV-cache write through AITER's per-head MLA cache operator. - Support BF16-Q/BF16-KV, FP8-Q/FP8-KV, and BF16-Q/FP8-KV mixed output for Triton decode. - Dispatch only on gfx950 decode/idle batches with contiguous covered inputs; DCP and unsupported contracts fail closed to the existing split/cat/cache path. ## Runtime configuration ```bash export SGLANG_K3_AITER_MLA_Q_CACHE_FUSION=1 ``` Validated FP8-KV configuration: ```bash sglang serve \ --model-path /path/to/Kimi-K3 \ --tp-size 8 \ --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 \ --attention-backend triton \ --prefill-attention-backend triton \ --decode-attention-backend triton ``` BF16 KV is also covered. The larger measured gain is with BF16-Q + FP8-KV. ## AITER dependency This SGLang integration requires AITER #4342 / commit `770790cd` or newer `fused_qk_rope_concat_and_cache_mla` semantics, including the `compute_all_q_rope` behavior used for correct batch-64 execution. The AITER revision currently pinned by main (`d9e5ef7`) is insufficient: its old schema rejects the new argument, and a 14-argument compatibility call produces incorrect token-64 output. This PR intentionally documents rather than changes the AITER pin. ## Accuracy Tests - Focused operator tests: `9 passed` - GSM8K 1319: `0.955` - Invalid responses: `0.001` ## Speed Tests and Profiling Historical matched results for the same integration: - BF16 KV: C32 `+0.63%`, C64 `+0.53%` - FP8 KV: C32 `+3.26%`, C64 `+3.57%` - FP8-KV median TPOT: approximately `-4%` ## Test plan - [x] BF16/BF16, FP8/FP8, and BF16-Q/FP8-KV operator tests at token counts 1 and 64 - [x] Negative slot handling - [x] CUDA Graph replay with changed inputs - [x] Narrow support/fallback predicates - [x] Full GSM8K 1319 with Triton prefill/decode and FP8 KV - [ ] Re-run after the target branch updates its AITER pin AITER prefill was not used in the full-model test because 12-head AITER attention-backend enablement is maintained separately; this fusion acts on the decode path. signal.author: alphabetc1

signal.title: feat(hicache): support Ascend Mamba states with FIA and async IO
signal.text: ## Motivation Qwen3.6 hybrid models require both Full KV and the matching Mamba state when a HiCache prefix is reused on Ascend. PR #32275 introduced the correct Torch-based Ascend host-transfer fallback for these Mamba state sidecars. This PR preserves that fallback and extends the integration in two areas found during Qwen3.6 NPU validation: 1. FIA exposes KV cache buffers as per-layer views, while Ascend HiCache's all-layer exchange path requires the original contiguous allocation. HiCache write-through can otherwise fail or hang when FIA is enabled. 2. The Torch Mamba transfer path materializes the layout before D2H/H2D. A native asynchronous transfer operator can avoid that overhead when the matching `sgl-kernel-npu` capability is installed. This PR therefore supersedes #32275 while preserving its commits and default behavior. ## Modifications ### Ascend Mamba State HiCache IO - Keep the synchronous Torch implementation as the default. - Add an optional runtime mode: ```bash SGLANG_NPU_HICACHE_MAMBA_IO=sync|async ``` - `sync`: existing Torch fallback (default); - `async`: require the native operator and fail fast at startup when it is unavailable. - Support conv and temporal state components, including conv-only models. - Accept physically dense transposed/NEXTN state payloads without requiring a logical contiguous layout. - Check native operator availability in SGLang before selecting the async path. - Keep tensor layout, dtype, pinned-memory, pitch, layer-range, and index validation in the native operator as the single transfer-safety boundary. - Dispatch the native path from the same component-level copy helpers used by the CUDA/ROCm implementation: per-layer PF->LF for Host-to-Device loads and all-layer LF->PF for Device-to-Host backups. Temporal and conv components retain their existing outer-loop structure instead of bypassing it through a monolithic Ascend-only fast path. - Preserve the helpers as `@staticmethod` functions with their original signatures. The H2D native entry consumes the current-layer Device view already passed as `dst`; no full `device_layers` argument or additional IO backend name is introduced. `kernel_ascend` remains the sole Ascend backend, with `sync|async` selecting its implementation. - Keep CUDA/ROCm HiCache paths unchanged. ### FIA + HiCache Compatibility - Retain contiguous all-layer Ascend K/V backing tensors. - Continue exposing per-layer views to FIA so graph capture does not retain the full tensor. - Let HiCache explicitly retrieve the contiguous backing tensors for `kernel_ascend` transfers. - Allocate the backing tensors inside the existing KV-cache memory-saver region so the allocation lifecycle remains unchanged. ### Tests - Add unit coverage for explicit sync/async selection, operator fail-fast, and conv-only states. - Cover component-level async dispatch and preservation of the synchronous Torch fallback. - Cover transposed dense layouts and invalid payload rejection in the native operator tests. - Extend staged write-back dispatch coverage for the Ascend Mamba path. ## Dependency The optional native path uses: - https://github.com/sgl-project/sgl-kernel-npu/pull/626 SGLang remains functional without that PR because `sync` is the default. Explicit `async` mode requires the matching native operator. ## Validation Latest component-level integration update (2026-08-12): - `python -m py_compile` passed for the modified SGLang files. - `git diff --check` passed. - The matching component-level native entries were loaded and exercised by the NPU microbenchmark reported in the kernel PR. - The current Codex environment does not expose an NPU, so the device-dependent unit file was not re-run here; the failure occurs during NPU availability detection before test collection. Earlier NPU unit and end-to-end results are retained below. The subsequent interface cleanup that preserves the static helper signatures passed Python compilation and `git diff --check`. Its current-layer Device-view entry still requires a fresh NPU build/unit/end-to-end run; the performance numbers below were collected before this interface-only cleanup and are not relabelled as a new measurement. - `test_npu_mamba_async_layout.py`: 4/4 passed. - `test_hicache_staged_write_back_dispatch.py`: 13 passed, 1 expected skip. - Native kernel tests: 9/9 passed on NPU. - Python compilation and `git diff --check` passed. Qwen3.6 AIME26 deterministic concurrent HiCache validation: - Round 1: cold build, 10 requests. - Round 2: 10/10 Device/L1 hits. - Round 3 after L1 pressure: all 10 requests hit cache (5 Device + 5 Host in the concurrent run). - Round 2 and Round 3 scores were both 1.0. Prewarmed 20-request, one-token-completion transfer A/B: - Torch fallback mean request latency: 641.15 ms. - Native async mean request latency: 505.01 ms. - Observed request-level speedup: 1.27x. Both variants recorded 20/20 Host/L2 hits. This transfer-heavy workload keeps generation to one token so that the host reload path is a material part of request latency. Repeated full end-to-end serving benchmark: - Five repeats per variant with rotated execution order. - Identical full-workload prewarming before measurement. - 16 prompts, 16K input tokens, 512 output tokens, concurrency 4. - `temperature=0`, fixed L1 capacity 486208, HiCache write-through with ratio 2. Mean results over five repeats: | Variant | Wall time | Mean TTFT | Mean TPOT | Mean E2E | Total TPS | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | | PR baseline | 70.930 s | 5243 ms | 10.948 ms | 10838 ms | 171.52 | | Adapted sync, FIA off | 70.878 s | 5111 ms | 11.144 ms | 10806 ms | 173.51 | | Adapted async, FIA off | 69.722 s | 5042 ms | 10.902 ms | 10612 ms | 175.75 | | FIA on, sync | 71.183 s | 5209 ms | 11.244 ms | 10955 ms | 171.20 | | FIA on, async | 71.836 s | 5384 ms | 10.802 ms | 10905 ms | 169.46 | Paired five-repeat comparisons: - The adapted synchronous path with FIA disabled is effectively neutral versus the clean PR baseline: wall-time difference +0.06%. - With FIA disabled, native async versus sync improves wall time by 1.60%, mean E2E by 1.77%, TTFT by 1.14%, TPOT by 2.14%, and throughput by 1.34%. - FIA is a compatibility path rather than a general performance optimization for this workload. The full FIA+async stack is 1.28% slower in wall time than the clean PR baseline, while TPOT improves by 1.33%. The isolated native operator benchmark is reported in the kernel PR. The gap between the isolated transfer and full serving gains is expected: Mamba state reload is only one part of long-context prefill and decode. ### Follow-up forced Host/L2 validation The five-variant comparison above is retained for completeness. A subsequent FIA-off A/B used stricter Host/L2 controls: - five repeats with alternating `sync -> async` / `async -> sync` order; - 16 prompts, 16K input tokens, 512 output tokens, concurrency 4; - PrefillDelayer disabled; - every measured variant/repeat recorded 16/16 pure Host hits, 261120 cached Host tokens, and zero Device hits. Mean Round-2 Host/L2 results: | Metric | Sync | Native async | Paired async improvement | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | | Wall time | 29.868 s | 28.884 s | 3.30% (3.14% median) | | Mean TTFT | 669.44 ms | 589.07 ms | 11.95% (12.94% median) | | Mean TPOT | 12.796 ms | 12.342 ms | 3.56% (3.40% median) | | Mean E2E | 7208.36 ms | 6895.76 ms | 4.34% (3.65% median) | | Output throughput | 274.32 tok/s | 283.72 tok/s | 3.42% (3.24% median) | All five paired wall-time samples favored the native path, with improvements from 2.06% to 5.21%. Because this follow-up removes the PrefillDelayer scheduling confounder and validates every Host/L2 hit, it is the more reliable result for the FIA-off forced-Host-reload path. It does not replace the FIA-on compatibility comparison above. ### Ascend Profile analysis (diagnostic only) A separate single-run Ascend Profile compared the Torch fallback and native path with FIA enabled. It used 16 prompts, 16K input tokens, 512 output tokens, concurrency 4, and verified 16/16 pure Host/L2 hits in the measured round. This run is used for attribution only; profiler overhead and the single sample make it unsuitable as a replacement for the repeated serving results above. - The identifiable Torch fallback materialization path accounted for about 1.884 s of Host API self time (`index_select`, `copy_`, `index_copy_`, and `_to_copy`). - Its state-specific device gather/scatter work was about 598.8 ms, but 93.2% of it overlapped those Host API intervals, so it must not be added again to the 1.884 s. - The native `transfer_state_dim_exchange` path used about 42.9 ms of Host API time. Its H2D and D2H DMA tasks totaled about 18.84 ms. - The timeline observed no overlap between those DMA tasks and model compute (including FIA) in this workload. The Profile therefore attributes the gain primarily to the layout-aware direct copy, which removes the fallback gather, temporary materialization, H2D Tensor creation, and device scatter. `aclrtMemcpy2dAsync` provides stream-ordered nonblocking submission, but this measurement does not claim a compute-overlap gain. Even perfect overlap of all currently visible native DMA would save at most about 18.84 ms, or 0.06% of the 31.64 s profiled async wall time. ## Checklist - [x] Synchronous fallback remains the default. - [x] Existing CUDA/ROCm paths are unchanged. - [x] SGLang checks native operator availability before enabling `async`. - [x] Native operator owns all transfer layout and bounds validation. - [x] Explicit `async` mode fails fast instead of silently changing behavior. - [x] Unit and NPU kernel validation pass. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:no_entry_sign: [Run #32341171117](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32341171117)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32341170613](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32341170613)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #32341171177](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32341171177)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [BugFix][Qwen3.8] Support Qwen3.8-MXFP4 DCP by registing Qwen3_5 text-only archs in mamba radix cache whitelists
signal.text: ## Motivation Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B ships as `Qwen3_5MoeForCausalLM`, a text-only Qwen3.5 arch missing from both mamba-radix-cache whitelists in `arg_groups/overrides.py`. `mamba_extra_buffer` therefore stays disabled, while DCP widens the allocator page size to `page_size * dcp_size = 2`, so startup fails: ``` AssertionError: MambaComponent requires page_size=1 when mamba_extra_buffer is disabled, got 2 ``` - `--dcp-size 2` cannot start on this model; without DCP the cache is silently lost instead. - **Platform-agnostic — nothing on this path is is_hip()-gated.** ## Modifications Register `Qwen3_5MoeForCausalLM` and `Qwen3_5ForCausalLM` in `_MAMBA_RADIX_CACHE_ARCHS` and `_MAMBA_EXTRA_BUFFER_ARCHS`. They wrap the same hybrid GDN body as the VL variants, and `is_qwen3_5()` already lists all four. ## Accuracy Tests GSM8K Passed. root@smci355-ccs-aus-n12-13:/sgl-workspace/sglang# python3 /sgl-workspace/sglang/benchmark/gsm8k/bench_sglang.py --port 8000 --num-questions 1319 100%|███████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████| 1319/1319 [04:58<00:00, 4.42it/s] Accuracy: 0.931 Invalid: 0.000 Latency: 298.404 s Output throughput: 769.999 token/s ## Speed Tests and Profiling ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. signal.title: [AMD] ci: cache the CI image on mi30x runners instead of re-pulling it every job
signal.text:
## Motivation AMD CI jobs spend ~49 GPU-machine-hours per night in container setup before a single test runs — 23.1 h on [Nightly Test (AMD)](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31415730698) and 25.6 h on [ROCm 7.2](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31415528605) (Aug 10, 90 jobs). Two costs, in roughly equal share: | Phase | Nightly (AMD) | Nightly ROCm 7.2 | |---|---|---| | `git fetch --tags origin` | 13.7 h (p50 4.6 min, p90 54 min) | 12.9 h (p50 0.6 min, p90 57 min) | | image pull | 9.2 h (p50 3.7 min, p90 26 min) | 12.5 h (p50 4.2 min, p90 59 min) | The p50/p90 spread is contention: ~90 jobs hitting github.com and one registry for the same objects at once. The runners are docker-in-docker with **ephemeral** storage and each job starts the container once, so an image pulled by one job is gone before the next begins — all 89 sampled jobs pulled the full image, and no in-daemon cache can help. The volume at `/home/runner/sglang-data` is the only thing that survives between jobs, and it is genuinely shared: an 8-GPU mi30x DeepSeek-V3.2 job resolves its weights from `/sgl-data/hf-cache/...` and downloads nothing. ## Result From [run 32309085572](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32309085572) (ROCm 7.2 AMD, 28 jobs, head `1f155a0c35`). Both rows are the same run, so same window and contention: | Image source | n | median | mean | range | |---|---|---|---|---| | **cache hit** (`local-tarball`) | 15 | **530s** | 556s | 334–738s | | registry pull (`registry-mirror`) | 7 | 8998s | 7130s | 197–10757s | Two caveats on that ~17x. A registry pull measured **617s** in isolation the day before, so the gap is a concurrency effect — one registry host serving ~20 jobs at once — not a property of the registry. And most hits were on the `20260819` tag while most pulls were the fresh `20260820` one, so the ratio is approximate. Seeding costs 299s and one 60 GB tarball per tag per volume, so it pays back on the first hit. Tarballs are uncompressed because the runners have neither `zstd` nor `pigz`. Also confirmed in that run: `version_resolve=0s` on every job (against a 136s median on [run 31636206736](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31636206736) A/B'd against 22 runs without the change); the seed lock holding under concurrency (`Another job is seeding ...; skipping`); and `container-start failures: none` across all 28 jobs. The new unit test passes in CI — 10/10 `base-a-test-cpu` shards on [run 32309085608](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32309085608). ## Not yet verified - The three most recent commits are locally verified only: prune now runs on every job rather than only before a seed, tarballs age out by last use rather than write time, and the volume's capacity is logged. [Run 32424637702](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32424637702) is in flight to exercise them. - The volume's actual capacity. Nothing logged it until that last commit; the only bound is `avail ≥ 165 GB`, inferred from the guard admitting a seed. - Whether compression helps. Shrinking the write to ~25 GB should speed seeds if the volume is the bottleneck (60 GB in 299s ≈ 200 MB/s), but `docker load` still writes the full 60 GB into the local store either way, so the load-side gain is unclear. - Whether that run's four `Run test` failures are pre-existing on main: `perf/test_bench_one_batch_2gpu.py`, `moe/test_torch_compile_moe.py` (same Triton `USE_PDL` failure this workflow hit on Aug 12, file identical to main), `moe/test_fused_moe.py`, and `amd/disaggregation/test_disaggregation_basic.py` — the last on the disaggregation path this PR does not touch. All in `Run test`, none in setup. ## Scope **mi30x only.** Both the cache and the registry probe are on for mi30x and off elsewhere; `AMD_CI_IMAGE_TARBALL_CACHE=1` opts another pool in, `=0` opts mi30x out. Touched files are `scripts/ci/amd/` plus one CPU unit test. Deliberately untouched: the nightly release workflows (the image still publishes to Docker Hub as today), `amd_ci_start_container_disagg.sh` (mi35x-fabric only), and `scripts/release/get_version_tag.py` (setuptools-scm runs it for every pyproject and the PyPI release workflows shell out to it, so no non-AMD wheel version can move). ## Modifications **Tarball cache on the persistent volume** — new `scripts/ci/amd/amd_ci_image_cache.sh`. First job to miss seeds `/home/runner/sglang-data/docker-images`; later jobs `docker load` and report `source=local-tarball`. That volume also holds the HF weight cache, and storage pressure on it is what shelved the previous seeding attempt and forced the path move in [#26642](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/26642), so it is bounded and best-effort — full, slow, locked or corrupt all fall back to pulling and never fail a job: - seeds under an `mkdir` lock, so concurrent jobs cannot all stream tens of GB; - writes to a temp path and renames, so no reader sees a partial tarball; - sizes the free-space requirement from `docker image inspect` (uncompressed layers, so on-disk size *is* tarball size) and keeps a reserve (`AMD_CI_IMAGE_CACHE_RESERVE_GB`, default 100); - prunes on every job by last use (`AMD_CI_IMAGE_CACHE_MAX_AGE_DAYS`, default 1). `find_latest_image` walks back up to a week when a nightly is missing, so a tarball past the window can still be the wanted tag — ageing on write time would delete it and force a fresh 60 GB seed each day the tag does not advance; - logs the volume's capacity and the cache's footprint, so thresholds are auditable from a job log; - prefers `zstd`, then `pigz`; verifies the image is in the store after a load and falls through to a pull if not. **`ls-remote` instead of a full tag fetch** — new `scripts/ci/amd/amd_ci_latest_release_tag.py` reads tag names with `git ls-remote --tags --refs` (refs only, no objects) and falls back to local tags when the remote is unreachable. It imports `parse_version_tuple` from the shared helper rather than reimplementing the ordering, so it picks the same tag the release workflow published under, stable/post above rc ([#23644](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/23644)). **Registry probe only on mi30x** — it lives in that fleet's network; elsewhere the attempt just adds a 15s connect timeout before the pull that has to happen anyway. `AMD_CI_DOCKER_REGISTRY_MIRROR` retargets or disables it without a code change; the address has already moved twice ([#23607](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/23607), [#29765](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/29765)). **One log line per job** — the step previously reported a single duration mixing both costs, which is why finding the split took log scraping: ``` [amd-ci-setup] image=rocm/sgl-dev:v0.5.17-rocm720-mi30x-20260820 source=local-tarball version_resolve=0s image_acquire=471s ``` `source` is one of `local-tarball`, `registry-mirror`, `docker-hub`, `custom-image`, `dockerfile-build`. The table above is these lines aggregated. **Unit test** — `test/registered/unit/tools/test_amd_ci_latest_release_tag.py` (`base-a-test-cpu`, no GPU) pins what the image tag depends on: `ls-remote` avoiding object transfer, `--refs` dropping peeled `^{}` entries, ordering matching the shared helper, fallback to local tags, and a failed `git` call being non-fatal. ## Accuracy Tests N/A — CI plumbing only, no model or kernel changes. ## Speed Tests and Profiling See **Result**. Also verified locally with stubbed `docker`, `hostname` and `df`: cold mi30x seeds and the next job loads with no pull at all; non-mi30x skips both probe and cache, with both env overrides working; a held lock skips seeding; a 60 GB image is refused at 150 GB free and admitted at 200 GB; two 5-day-old tarballs are reclaimed while today's is kept with no seed attempted; a 3-day-old tarball that is still the wanted tag is refreshed on hit and survives, and is reclaimed when unused. 16/16 unit tests, `pre-commit` and `bash -n` clean. Checked rather than assumed: dropping `git fetch --tags origin` does not change the editable install's version. It is already `0.0.0.dev1+g955aab8db` **with** the fetch, because a depth-1 `actions/checkout` HEAD cannot `git describe` from a tag even with tags present. ## Follow-ups - Install `zstd` or `pigz` on the mi30x runners: cuts a tarball from 60 GB to ~25 GB, no code change needed. `zstd` first, since gzip streams cannot be decompressed in parallel. - Confirm the four `Run test` failures above are pre-existing on main. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). — `--help` and the cache helper's header document the new env vars; no user-facing docs affected. - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process). 2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers. 3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so. - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci` 4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR.

signal.title: [diffusion] let offloaded weights stay on the checkpoint mapping
signal.text: ## Motivation Layerwise offload copies every layer into host memory at startup, so host memory has to be at least as large as the component. MiniMax-H3's DiT is 61.73 GiB, which rules out a 12 GiB + 32 GiB budget outright -- not by a slow margin, but at initialization. Most of those bytes are already in host memory once, as a mapping. Measured on one H3 load: ``` PRE-OFFLOAD text_encoder: host pageable: 48.09 GB PRE-OFFLOAD transformer: host mmap: 50.53 GB, host pageable: 11.20 GB ``` 50.53 GiB of the DiT's 61.73 GiB reach the offload manager as views into the checkpoint: the loader builds the model on meta and `_can_assign_cpu_tensor_without_copy` hands the parameter the loaded tensor rather than copying into it. That holds because H3 stores the DiT in BF16 and runs it in BF16 -- checked against the safetensors headers, 61.66 GiB of the 61.73 GiB is BF16. Copying them a second time is what does not fit. ## Modifications A third host store sits beside the consolidated and stride-preserving ones, holding weights that are still views into the file. The page cache then decides what stays resident. The choice is not free. Pinning is what lets the copy stream run ahead of compute -- 1.03 s against 1.90 s per step on a measured Wan2.1 run -- and a mapping cannot be pinned, so those copies run on the compute stream instead. It is taken only when the copies do not fit, so nothing changes on a host with room. Three places had to agree that a mapping is the checkpoint, not a buffer: - `sync_layer_to_cpu` skips mapped weights. Inference does not mutate them, and writing would copy-on-write the mapping into the anonymous memory this exists to avoid. - `prefetch_layer` copies straight from the mapping, and no longer treats the consolidated store as the gate for whether a layer has weights at all. - `iter_cpu_weights` yields them, so checksums still see every weight. `MappedRegions` answers "is this tensor in a file mapping", built once because reading /proc/self/maps per tensor would be quadratic over H3's weight count. It replaces the closure #35618 had inlined for the same question. The encoder needed the same thing and mostly already had it. `_mps_zero_copy_weight_loading` let compatible CPU safetensors stay mapped instead of being copied, and the H3 encoder already honoured it -- it was gated on `current_platform.is_mps()`, on the reasoning that unified memory makes the copy pointless. "The copy does not fit" is the stronger form of that same argument and is not platform-specific, so the gate becomes "MPS, or the copies would not fit", measured from the checkpoint's on-disk size because the decision is made before a weight is read. Both callers now ask one predicate, `host_copies_would_not_fit` in host_memory_budget.py, which already owns the question of what this process may commit. The DiT path and the encoder path had each grown their own copy of the 4 GiB reserve and the comparison. Renamed with the gate, since both are now read on non-MPS paths: `_mps_zero_copy_weight_loading` -> `_keep_checkpoint_mapping`, `mps_zero_copy_unsafe` -> `checkpoint_mapping_unsafe`. `mps_layerwise_cpu_staging` keeps its name -- it is still set only under `is_mps()`. ## Accuracy Tests Which memory holds a weight; the weights themselves are untouched. Four new unit tests cover a file-backed weight staying mapped, an affordable one still being copied, the writeback leaving a mapping alone, and checksums still seeing mapped weights. Full `test/unit` suite: 1846 passed, with the same four pre-existing failures (`realtime/`, `sana_wm/`) that fail with this change reverted. Verified end to end on H3 `fl2va`, single GPU, host memory reported as 32 GiB: ``` Layerwise offload: leaving 49.36 GiB of weights on the checkpoint mapping -- copying them into host memory needs more than the 32.00 GiB available [m32] READY after 125s text_encoder (vram: 1.40 GB, host pinned: 0.77 GB, host mmap: 1.45 GB) transformer (vram: 2.09 GB, host pinned: 12.20 GB) video_vae (vram: 0.95 GB, host pinned: 9.00 GB) ``` The DiT's share of host memory goes from 61.73 GiB to 12.20 GiB and the encoder's from 46.18 GiB to 2.22 GiB. Load-time peak is 5176 MiB of VRAM and 23.42 GB of host memory, against the 12 GiB + 32 GiB the model is being asked to fit; before this the load failed outright. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Not measured on H3 yet, and the PR does not claim a speed result. What is known: a page-cache-resident mapping copies at 12.38 GB/s against 13.39 for pinned on one RTX 4090, so the bandwidth gap is small; what is given up is the overlap, which on Wan2.1 was worth 1.03 s against 1.90 s per step. On a host where the copies fit, this path is not taken and nothing changes. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## What this does not do This is a load-time result. It gets H3 into the budget at initialization; it does not claim a runtime one, and runtime activations are measured separately. Nothing here changes a host that has room -- both gates are "the copies do not fit", so a serving box takes the pinned path exactly as before. Building the encoder on meta was tried first and does not work: custom weight loaders such as `VocabParallelEmbedding`'s write into `param.data` slices, which a meta parameter has none of. Reusing the flag the MPS path already had avoids that entirely. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #32437583407](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32437583407)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32437583392](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32437583392)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #32437583361](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32437583361)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [diffusion] read the next mapped layer ahead instead of faulting on it
signal.text: ## Motivation A weight left on the checkpoint mapping (#35701) is copied to the device synchronously, so when the page cache has dropped its pages the read happens on the critical path: the copy stalls in a major fault while the GPU waits. On MiniMax-H3 that is 44 GiB of DiT weights walked once per denoise step against roughly 8 GiB of page cache, so most steps fault. It shows up as load sensitivity — the denoise stage tracks how contended the host's memory bandwidth is, because the faults are competing for it. Every alternative that buys overlap buys it with host memory this budget does not have: pinning cannot be done on a mapping at all, and staging copies are the thing the mapping exists to avoid. Readahead buys it with nothing. ## Modifications `MADV_WILLNEED` over the next layer's mapped range, issued when the current layer is staged. Asynchronous readahead: free when the pages are already resident, overlapped with the current layer's compute when they are not, and it commits no memory of its own. One call per layer rather than per weight — a layer's mapped tensors are slices of the same checkpoint shard, so advising min..max covers them together and keeps this to one syscall per prefetch. `madvise` is bound through `ctypes` once and left as `None` where libc does not offer it, so the advice is skipped rather than guarded at every call site. ## Accuracy Tests Which pages are resident when a copy runs; the bytes copied are identical. `test_layerwise_offload.py` on this branch: 55 passed. ## Speed Tests and Profiling H3 `fl2va`, 864x480 / 124 frames / 20 steps, seed 1101, single RTX 4090, 12 GiB VRAM cap enforced with `torch.cuda.set_per_process_memory_fraction`, host memory capped at 32 GiB, `--layerwise-resident-layers video_vae=36`. This box is shared and its load average swings between 80 and 220, which is exactly the axis this change is about, so the samples are reported with it: | | load | denoise | decode | end to end | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | without readahead | 87 | 144.65 s | 13.08 s | 161.44 s | | without readahead | 131 | 157.05 s | 13.21 s | 175.72 s | | without readahead | 152 | 146.68 s | 12.92 s | 163.25 s | | **with readahead** | **139** | **144.89 s** | 12.88 s | **161.50 s** | | **with readahead** | **217** | **144.82 s** | 12.76 s** | **161.34 s** | Without it, end to end swings 161–176 s with load. With it, load 139 and load 217 both land at 161.3–161.5 s: the load-sensitive term is gone, which is the point. The decode stage is unchanged, as expected — its weights are held resident for the stage rather than re-read. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). signal.title: [AMD] Perf Kimi-K3 fuse ROCm KDA decode boundary
signal.text: Defer the `f_b` projection into the gfx950 FlyDSL kernel so decode fuses convolution, recurrent state update, and gated RMSNorm while preserving the existing fail-closed fallback. ## Summary - Vendor the Kimi-K3 KDA-only FlyDSL wrapper and gfx950 decode kernels in SGLang. - Prefer the local implementation through the source selector while retaining the AITER module as a fail-closed fallback. - Remove the dependency on the unreleased `aiter.ops.flydsl.kimi_k3_kda_decode` module; stock pinned AITER supplies only FlyDSL tensor/vector/JIT shims. - Automatically select the validated cooperative `f_a`, wave-specialized front, fused norm reduction, BF16 `fdot2`, WPE3 schedule only for exact C2. - Keep every other batch on the original kernel schedule. ## Modifications - Add a trimmed KDA-only vendored FlyDSL package and source selector. - Route the existing HIP fused KDA adapter through the SGLang module first. - Make the exact-C2 winner an internal batch specialization with no per-knob environment configuration. - Add focused recurrent/graph tests and an allocation-free graph benchmark. ## Runtime gate and fallback The fused ROCm KDA boundary is opt-in: ```bash export SGLANG_K3_KDA_FUSED_BACKEND=aiter ``` This flag controls the entire PR path, not only the C2 tuning. During model initialization, Kimi-K3 prepares the deferred `f_b` weights and fused decode arguments only when the value is exactly `aiter` and the gfx950 FlyDSL implementation is available. During decode, `covered()` revalidates runtime shapes, dtypes, strides, state indices, and output buffers before dispatch. Behavior by configuration: - Flag unset or any value other than `aiter`: preserve the existing unfused KDA path. - Flag set to `aiter`, supported gfx950 inputs: use the fused `f_b + convolution + recurrence + gated RMSNorm` boundary. - Flag set but unsupported runtime inputs: fail closed to the existing KDA implementation. - Exact C2: automatically select the validated WPE3/cooperative/front-specialized/fused-reduction/`fdot2` schedule. - C1 and C4+: use the original fused-kernel build options; the C2 specialization does not apply. `SGLANG_K3_FLYDSL_SOURCE` defaults to `auto`, which prefers the vendored SGLang kernel and falls back to the AITER module if needed. `SGLANG_K3_AITER_KDA_GROUP64` is a separate, optional input-preparation optimization and is not required by this PR. ## Accuracy Tests - GSM8K 1319: `0.950` - Invalid responses: `0.001` ## Speed Tests and Profiling Automatic-profile micro A/B on the integration branch: ```text batch baseline us auto-profile us delta 1 12.2758 12.3008 +0.20% 2 12.7725 11.9959 -6.08% 4 12.8509 12.8770 +0.20% 8 13.4043 13.3785 -0.19% 16 14.0342 14.0324 -0.01% ``` Non-C2 changes are within the measurement noise floor; only C2 changes build options. Prior production-like results: - 69-layer graph: `9.20 -> 8.38 us/layer` (`-8.9%`). - Matched C2 endpoint: `+0.19%` throughput, `-0.20%` TPOT. ## Validation - [x] KDA FlyDSL focused tests on PR branch: 15 passed - [x] KDA FlyDSL focused tests on integration branch: 15 passed - [x] C1/C2/C4/C8/C16 graph micro A/B - [x] GSM8K 1319 - [x] Fail-closed non-C2 fallback ## Checklist - [ ] Run repository pre-commit hooks - [x] Add focused unit tests - [x] Provide accuracy and speed results - [x] Preserve fail-closed fallback <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:no_entry_sign: [Run #32343549943](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32343549943)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32343549985](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32343549985)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32343550227](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32343550227)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [RL, Spec] DFlash: top-p mask capture
signal.text: ## Relationship to existing work https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/27408 introduced the machinery needed to return masks from nucleus sampling via `/generate`. https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/33593 expands that functionality with top-p only masks and laces it through `/v1/chat/completions` via `return_meta_info=true`. https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/34037 bounds the effects of such requests on concurrent requests. As of #33459, the DFlash SpecV2 path is capable of returning logprobs. This PR extends this line of work to allow for top-p masking when DFlash SpecV2 is enabled. ## Motivation Top-p sampling masks are useful in RL to reduce trainer-inference mismatch. Speculative decoding can [accelerate RL training](https://www.lmsys.org/blog/2025-11-19-miles/#speculative-decoding-with-online-draft-model-training) and reduce rollout generation bottleneck. Top-p sampling masks are useful for reduce training-inference mismatch, which is often necessary for stable async RL. ## Modifications - Enable return_sampling_mask for DFlash speculative decoding. - Return one sampling support and selected-token logprob for every accepted output token. - Preserve support after top-k/top-p/min-p filtering and renormalization. - Align metadata with DFlash accepted-token lengths and finished/EOS truncation. - Support mixed batches and greedy decoding; greedy masks are singleton token sets. - Reject requests whose realized support exceeds --sampling-mask-max-tokens. - Require exact DFlash acceptance thresholds (1.0) when masks are requested. - Defer Python-list materialization until result processing, keeping outputs tensor-backed and using asynchronous device-to-host copying. ## Accuracy Tests Targeted final implementation: - 4/4 DFlash sampling-mask unit tests passed in Modal: - tensor-backed deferred materialization; - filtered target probabilities and selected-token logprobs; - greedy singleton masks; - whole-request rejection on support overflow. - Added registered DFlash server coverage asserting: - seven generated tokens produce seven masks and seven logprobs; - every sampled token belongs to its corresponding support. - Full Qwen3.6 NVFP4+DFlash B200 run: - 98,304 measured output tokens; - 49,152 requested masks returned, with no missing masks; - maximum observed top-p support was 5,306; a repeat reached 7,476; - completed without generation or mask-alignment errors. This feature only returns metadata and is not intended to change sampling decisions, so no downstream task-accuracy benchmark was run. ## Speed Tests and Profiling One B200 with: - nvidia/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-NVFP4; - modal-labs/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-DFlash; - DFlash block size 8, FA4 draft attention; - 32 concurrent requests, 512 generated tokens each; - warmup followed by six alternating mask/no-mask rounds. Results: - Without masks: 4,163.78 tok/s median - With masks: 4,160.45 tok/s median - Ratio: 0.9992, or approximately −0.08% The difference was within run-to-run noise. A complete repeat also showed no slowdown. ## Checklist - [ ] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [ ] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process). 2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers. 3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so. - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci` 4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32434359994](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32434359994)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32434359971](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32434359971)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32434359985](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32434359985)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [NPU] Adapt DFlash2 speculative decoding to Ascend NPUs
signal.text: ## Motivation DFlash2 (#35371) landed on main as the successor to DFlash: a block-diffusion drafter with local grouped convolutions and a candidate selector, currently CUDA-only. First-generation DFlash drafts already run on Ascend NPUs (#23122, #31739), but the DFlash2 checkpoints cannot serve on NPU yet, and I found no existing issue/PR tracking this. This PR adapts the DFlash2 verify path so it can serve on Ascend NPUs (and any Triton-free environment), while keeping the CUDA path byte-for-byte identical. ## Changes - **Triton import guards** (`triton_compat.py`, new): kernel modules in `kernels/ops/speculative/` imported triton unconditionally, which broke module import on Triton-free Ascend images. The new compat shim degrades `@triton.jit` to a stub that raises only on *launch*, so non-CUDA devices can import the DFlash/DSpark modules and dispatch to torch fallbacks. This is generic: any environment without triton benefits, CUDA is untouched. - **Torch chain speculative-sampling fallback** (`chain_speculative_sampling_torch` in `reject_sampling.py`): buffer-for- buffer mirror of `speculative_sampling_classic_kernel` (same `coin * q < p` accept rule, same residual `max(p - q, 0)` final sampling, NaN draft entries treated as 0, same `predicts`/`accept_index`/`accept_token_num` layouts). Used by DSpark on NPU and covered by unit tests on CPU. - **Device dispatch** (`dspark_accept.py`): `_accept_sampling_core` now routes through `inputs_on_cuda(candidates)` — triton kernel on CUDA (unchanged), torch fallback elsewhere (NPU/CPU). Also routed the `@triton.jit` helper kernels in this module through the compat shim. - **NPU verify fix** (`dflash_worker_v2.py`): `skip_attn_backend_init` is now `None if _is_npu else True`. The CUDA `prepare_for_verify` pre-plans (load_batch / init_forward_metadata); the NPU branch deliberately leaves planning to the forward path, so marking metadata ready here crashed the NPU graph runner (`raw_num_token` never initialized). - **NPU greedy verify alignment** (`dflash_worker_v2.py`): on NPU, skip the selector full-vocab sampling verify (`_selector_sampling_accept` and the chain-sampling branch) and take the argmax greedy verify instead, matching what EAGLE/first-gen DFLASH already do unconditionally on NPU. The full-vocab path scatters a dense [bs, gamma, vocab] buffer whose cost does not shrink with the verify window; on the 200K-vocab Qwen3.8 it dominates the step. CUDA behavior unchanged. - **Docs**: Qwen3.8-27B cookbook — DFlash2 drafter recipe and NPU support status. ## Tests - New unit tests (`test/registered/unit/spec/test_chain_speculative_sampling.py`, registered in `base-a-test-cpu`): analytic accept/reject/bonus cases, NaN handling, batch independence, statistical losslessness (20k samples, TV < 0.02), triton-compat helpers, and a CUDA parity check that runs the torch and triton kernels on identical buffers (`@skipIf` no CUDA). - Verified end-to-end on Ascend 910C (target `Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B`, draft `z-lab/Qwen3.8-27B-DFlash2`, tp=2): server starts, DFlash2 selector draft loads, both NPU graph captures succeed (incl. the in-graph sampler RNG), and requests pass, before and after the greedy-verify change. ## Plan status - [x] P0: pure-torch chain speculative-sampling verify + device dispatch + CPU unit tests against the Triton reference - [x] P0.5: guard the triton imports so Triton-free environments import the DFlash modules - [x] P1: validate NPU (aclgraph) capture of the DFlash2 selector draft sampler (done on 910C; `SGLANG_DFLASH_EAGER_DRAFT_SAMPLER=1` remains the escape hatch) - [x] P1: e2e greedy + sampling correctness on Ascend (server starts, requests pass) - [x] P2: performance investigation — moved to a follow-up PR. Profiling (phase timing + torch-profiler traces, gated by the new `SGLANG_DFLASH_DEBUG_TIMING` flag) showed the original suspects (vocab-wide `torch.topk` in the selector, dense chain sampling) are not the bottleneck: the selector top-k costs ~0.04 ms/step and DFLASH matches NEXTN kernel-for-kernel. The decode step is bounded by a shared TP2 per-layer allreduce floor (~43 collectives/step) of the target model verify. Optimization directions (accept-length tuning, verify-prep host-path reduction) will be pursued separately. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: **Missing `run-ci` label** -- add it to run CI tests.<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: **Blocked** -- `run-ci` is required first.<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:heavy_minus_sign: **No AMD PR run found for this commit**.<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->
