signal.title: Support mxfp8 KV cache in PD transfer
signal.text: ## Motivation MXFP8 KV refused PD disaggregation outright: `get_contiguous_buf_infos` raised `KV transfer / disaggregation is unsupported for MXFP8 KV cache (scale buffers are not exposed)`. This exposes them, so a hybrid attention + linear-attention model serves PD with `--kv-cache-dtype mxfp8`. The scales do not go on the KV lists. Four call sites derive geometry from their length -- `len(kv_data_ptrs) // layer_num` in `setup_state_kv_args`, `len(kv_item_lens) // 2` in the staging handler, the layer range in `prefill.py`, and per-token bytes in `common/conn.py` -- so appending buffers there would silently skew all of them. They ride the multi-component state channel instead, which already carries KV-adjacent buffers for `SWA_RING`, `C128_STATE` and `MINIMAX_INDEX_K`. Two components rather than one, because a SWA pool nests two MXFP8 pools and their scales need different index payloads: the full-attention scales follow the whole sequence, the sliding-window scales follow the window through `translate_loc_from_full_to_swa`. One component cannot carry both. `item_lens` splits on the layout: the interleaved buffer (the `page_size == 128` path) puts pages on the leading axis so one row is one page, while the flat buffer is per slot and a page spans `page_size` rows. Removing the refusal surfaced a second gap: this pool overrides `_create_buffers` wholesale, and the base class only builds `_kv_buffer_descs` at the end of the method it replaced, so the inherited accessor hit an `AttributeError`. The descriptors are now built there too. `set_kv_buffer_prefix_valid` still refuses -- its callers are the DSpark and DFlash speculative paths, which PD does not reach. A hybrid model also needs #35689, now on main: without it the empty mamba temporal buffer fails the batch registration before any of this runs. ## Accuracy Single-node PD, one prefill and one decode role, TP=2 each, mooncake over IB, hierarchical cache on the prefill role, `--kv-cache-dtype mxfp8`. `sgl-eval` aime26, thinking on, `max_tokens=131072`: ``` score = 0.9333 error_rate = 0.00% stop_rate = 0.9667 truncated_rate = 0.0333 total_completion_tokens = 822323 ``` One of the two misses is `finish_reason=length` with no answer extracted, so 28/29 of the samples that finished are correct -- level with the 0.9667 the same setup reads on bf16 KV, where nothing truncated. MXFP8 spends about 7% more completion tokens (822k against 768k), which is what pushes one problem into the cap. A prompt whose prefix is well past the sliding window answers correctly and repeatably. Pointing the window component at the whole-sequence payload instead degenerates it to empty or truncated completions, which is what confirms the window scales are read rather than incidentally correct. The flat layout has no hardware coverage here -- fa4 pins `page_size` to 128, so only the interleaved branch runs -- and is covered by the unit test. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #32437324281](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32437324281)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #32437324240](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32437324240)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #32437324245](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32437324245)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [AMD] CI: cut two setup cycles from the AMD multimodal-gen lanes
signal.text: ## Motivation AMD multimodal-gen jobs spend most of their runner time not testing. Measured on mi300 in [run 31443692177](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31443692177), every job pays a container pull of 27–97 min plus a dependency install of 23–98 min, so 100–155 min of fixed cost before a single test executes. Across the eight multimodal jobs in that run that is ~15.8 runner-hours of setup against ~5.6 hours of tests — roughly 74% overhead, and because both matrices are `max-parallel: 1` it is serialized into wall-clock. CUDA for comparison: `Install dependencies` takes 27 seconds and total fixed overhead is under a minute. The two clearest wins are removing whole setup cycles. ## Modifications **Fold the `unit` suite into a warm shard.** `multimodal-gen-unit-test-amd` paid ~110 min of setup to run ~5 min of portable CPU-style tests. It now runs as a step of `multimodal-gen-test-1-gpu-amd` part 0 (and the ROCm 7.2 counterpart), on the container that job already warmed. The step runs after the diffusion tests and on failure as well, so a diffusion regression cannot mask a unit regression, and it carries its own `timeout-minutes` so it cannot eat the diffusion step's budget. Trigger conditions are unchanged — on both lanes the 1-GPU job already gates on exactly the inputs the unit job did (`multimodal_gen` on `pr-test-amd`, `main_package || sgl_kernel` on ROCm 7.2). The standalone job, its `target_stage_select` entry, and its `needs` entry are removed; the `ci_coverage_report.py` comment naming it is updated (the `"unit": ("CUDA", "AMD")` mapping itself still holds). **2-GPU: 3 shards → 2.** Per-case timings from the same run were 14, 26 and 21 min of healthy work across the three shards; the third shard's other 96 min was `flux_image_t2i_2_gpus` (77.7 min) and `flux2_modelopt_fp8_tp2_t2i` (18.1 min) retrying, which is the known ROCm flux bug (#34351 / #34352), not real work. Two shards therefore land near 30 min of case time each — and even if one shard inherited both flux cases while they stay broken, ~126 min is still inside the 180 min step timeout. Net effect: 8 AMD multimodal jobs → 5 per lane, i.e. ~4 fewer setup cycles across the two AMD workflows, on the order of 8 runner-hours per full PR run. ## What this deliberately does not do **1-GPU stays at 4 shards.** It has no headroom today: shard 0 already ends with `The action 'Run diffusion server tests (1-GPU)' has timed out after 90 minutes`, spent retrying the broken `flux_image_t2i`. Merging 1-GPU shards should wait until that case is fixed or skipped, and would likely want the step timeout raised to 150 min to match the 2-GPU lane. **The retry amplification and the image pull are untouched.** Retrying a deterministically broken case seven times is what turns a 20-minute shard into a 127-minute one, and the ROCm image pull is the single largest line item in the whole lane — caching or pre-pulling it on the mi300 runners would beat any amount of matrix tuning. Both are worth separate work. ## Validation Dispatched on this branch against the ROCm 7.2 lane (the PR gate since #34204): [run 31638833841](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31638833841). **The unit fold works, including the case it had to get right.** On 1-GPU part 0 the diffusion step failed (7 passed, 1 setup error) and the folded `Run diffusion unit tests` step still ran and passed — 1360 passed, 10 skipped in 102 s. `if: matrix.part == 0 && (success() || failure())` fires after a failed predecessor, and the step is correctly skipped on parts 1-3. **The 2 two-GPU shards cover the suite and fit the timeout, but with less margin than I estimated.** They split into 13 cases + 3 standalone and 13 cases + 4 standalone. Shard 1 spent 45 min on cases plus 9 min on standalone. Shard 0 reached **149 min** against the 180 min step cap — not because two shards is too coarse, but because `flux_image_t2i_2_gpus` fails and the harness retries it: 64 min for the case block, then repeated ~13 min retry passes. Both shards' remaining failures are the pre-existing ROCm set (flux #34351 / #34352, and `test_ar_models` failing warmup with `Inference tensors do not track version counter`). So the split is safe today and drops to ~45-65 min per shard once the flux retries stop, but if a reviewer wants insurance while flux is broken, the options are to hold this until flux lands or to raise the 2-GPU step timeout. I have deliberately not raised it here: a larger cap means a wedged job holds a scarce mi300 runner longer. ## Accuracy Tests N/A — CI orchestration only. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Covered above: the change is motivated entirely by measured CI wall-clock, and the numbers come from the per-step and per-case timings of run 31443692177. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. signal.title: [HCU] Add Qwen3.5 and GLM-5 support
signal.text: <!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. --> ## Motivation <!-- Describe the purpose and goals of this pull request. --> ## Motivation This PR adds initial HCU support to SGLang for `gfx928`, `gfx936`, and `gfx938`, enabling Qwen3.5 and GLM-5 model serving on HCU. The changes address HCU-specific kernel compilation, unsupported runtime fast paths, EAGLE CUDA Graph buffer allocation, and GLM-5 inference accuracy. All platform-specific behavior is isolated behind `is_hcu()` or `USE_HCU` to preserve the existing CUDA and ROCm paths. This PR contains the following commits: - `[HCU] Adapt Qwen3.5-27B` - `[HCU] Fix EAGLE CUDA Graph custom mask buffer allocation` - `[HCU] Fix GLM-5 inference accuracy` - `[HCU] Unify MoE align kernel implementation` ## Modifications ### HCU platform detection and runtime fallbacks - Add `is_hcu()` detection for `gfx928`, `gfx936`, and `gfx938`. - Disable the unsupported multimem symmetric-memory all-gather path on HCU. - Disable the unavailable vLLM RMSNorm fast path on HCU. - Reject Quark W4A4 MXFP4 explicitly on HCU because its required AITER kernels are unavailable. - Keep these fallbacks HCU-only without changing the existing CUDA and ROCm behavior. ### sgl-kernel build support - Add and refine `setup_hcu.py`. - Support `gfx928`, `gfx936`, and `gfx938`. - Add `HCU_TARGET` for explicitly selecting the compilation target. - Use HCU-specific names for target detection and configuration. - Compile with `USE_HCU` and the HCU FP8 configuration. - Reuse the common `csrc/moe/moe_align_kernel.cu`. - Select the HCU Blelloch scan through `USE_HCU`. - Preserve the original CUDA warp scan and ROCm Blelloch scan paths. - Remove the duplicated `moe_align_kernel_hcu.cu`. ### EAGLE CUDA Graph support - Increase the HCU CUDA Graph custom-mask buffer capacity for EAGLE verification. - Account for the per-request draft-token square in addition to the context mask. - Keep the additional allocation isolated to HCU. ### GLM-5 inference accuracy - Bypass the unavailable Hadamard transform on HCU while keeping query and key tensors in the same unrotated space. - Preserve the existing CUDA and standard ROCm indexer paths. - Prevent the routed scaling factor from being applied twice when the HCU Triton MoE runner already applies it. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32437222023](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32437222023)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32437221867](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32437221867)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32437222146](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32437222146)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [AMD] [GLM5] Fuse the ROCm DSA indexer q/k prep into aiter's single kernel
signal.text:
## Summary On ROCm the DSA indexer spends 11 kernels per decode layer on q/k prep. This PR collapses most of that into one aiter kernel. * `indexer_qk_rope_quant_and_cache` does k LayerNorm + RoPE + fp8 quant + paged index-k store, q RoPE + fp8 quant, and the head-gate scale in a single launch — six kernels become one. Like the CUDA fused path it drops the Hadamard rotation, which is logit-preserving and only shifts fp8 quantisation error. Prefill drops it too, since prefill writes the index-K cache decode reads back and the two must agree on basis. * `wk` and `weights_proj` are folded into one `wk_weights_proj` GEMM. This needs only the concatenated weight, no fused kernel, but was gated on CUDA; it now runs on CUDA or HIP and is numerically identical to the split projections. * The aiter kernel is tuned for decode's one-token-per-sequence shape and costs about twice what it replaces at prefill widths, so it is gated to decode. It also requires gfx95x, `SGLANG_USE_AITER`, and an aiter build exporting the symbol — a capability probe, not a preference: anything outside the envelope falls back to the existing path. CUDA and NPU are unchanged. Decode indexer on GLM-5.2 / MI355X: **11 kernels / 70.8 us per layer → 5 kernels / 41.4 us (−41.5%)**, which closes the MI355X-vs-B200 indexer gap from 2.55x to 1.49x. Drive-by fix: define the module-level `_use_dsa_indexer_fusion` that `lora_manager.py` already imports but nothing defined, so an indexer-targeted LoRA adapter raised `ImportError` instead of the intended `ValueError`. ## Test plan MI355X TP4, GLM-5.2-MXFP4, fp8 KV, `chunked_prefill=16384`, DSA backend triton, i8192 / o1024, one run per point. Baseline is the same AMD GLM-5.2 stack without this PR (#30519, #30575, #30715, #30808, #31323, #31324, #32888, plus ROCm/aiter#4453). | conc | Output tok/s | Median ITL (ms) | Median TTFT (ms) | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | 4 | 323.3 → 335.9 (+3.9%) | 10.61 → 10.16 (−4.2%) | 366.7 → 367.6 (+0.2%) | | 8 | 465.3 → 482.3 (+3.6%) | 14.02 → 13.43 (−4.2%) | 379.1 → 379.8 (+0.2%) | | 16 | 731.5 → 762.9 (+4.3%) | 15.73 → 14.86 (−5.5%) | 378.0 → 383.3 (+1.4%) | | 32 | 1044.3 → 1081.1 (+3.5%) | 19.39 → 18.37 (−5.3%) | 393.7 → 389.5 (−1.1%) | | 64 | 1342.4 → 1382.2 (+3.0%) | 25.33 → 24.03 (−5.1%) | 631.6 → 615.6 (−2.5%) | ITL improves −4.2% to −5.5% at every concurrency, matching the 29.4 us/layer the kernel table predicts over the 21 layers that run the indexer (0.62 ms per decode forward). TTFT is flat, which is the check that matters given the kernel is decode-only. GSM8K (1200 questions): 0.928 baseline, 0.934 this PR. The index-K cache is bit-exact against the unfused path across both `preshuffle` and `scale_fmt`; the q fp8 payload differs by 1 ULP on 0.10% of elements, because aiter multiplies by the reciprocal rather than dividing.
Per-layer decode indexer kernels, and why the aiter kernel is decode-only | baseline | us | this PR | us | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `hgemm_16x64x128x3` (wk) | 6.59 | `hgemm_16x64x128x3` (merged wk_weights_proj) | 6.50 | | `hgemm_16x64x64x6` (weights_proj) | 5.30 | — | — | | `Layernorm2dFwd` | 4.19 | `indexer_qk_rope_quant_and_cache` | 5.60 | | `kn_entry_2c_sbhd_cached_indirect` (RoPE) | 8.78 | | | | `fast_hadamard_transform_kernel` | 4.43 | | | | `_hadamard_quant_kernel` | 4.55 | | | | `indexer_k_quant_and_cache_kernel` | 4.19 | | | | `triton_poi_fused_mul_unsqueeze_0` | 4.18 | | | | `wv_splitk_small` (q proj) | 5.70 | `wv_splitk_small` | 5.95 | | `fp8_paged_mqa_logits_preshuffle` | 4.34 | `fp8_paged_mqa_logits_preshuffle` | 4.46 | | `topk_transform_decode_kernel` | 18.60 | `topk_transform_decode_kernel` | 18.93 | | **total** | **70.8** | **total** | **41.4** | Of the 29.4 us/layer saved, 5.4 is the merged projection and 21.3 is six kernels becoming one; downstream topk and logits move by 0.1–0.3 us, which is noise. With the aiter kernel enabled for prefill too, the prefill indexer went from 1614.5 up to 1780.5 us/layer: the fused kernel alone costs 300.4 us/layer against the 162.8 of the six it replaces, and drags downstream topk and logits ~8% each. Gating it to decode gives prefill 1519.6 us/layer (−5.9%), since prefill still benefits from the merged projection and from dropping the Hadamard.

signal.title: [AMD] Fix gfx950 Triton compiler crash on fp8 KV-cache attention
signal.text: ## Motivation `test/registered/attention/test_verify_shared_kv.py::test_qwen3_5_fp8_kv_cache` has never passed on `stage-b-1-gpu-small-amd-mi35x` since it was added (#34517); it fails inside the Triton AMD backend, not in sglang code ([latest instance](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32166850277/job/95808413702)): ``` python3: llvm/ADT/SmallVector.h:292: Assertion `idx < size()' failed. extend_attention.py:305:0: error: Failures have been detected while processing an MLIR pass pipeline extend_attention.py:305:0: note: Pipeline failed while executing [`ConvertTritonAMDGPUToLLVM` ...] RuntimeError: PassManager::run failed ``` Only the fp8 variant fails; the bf16 variants of the same test pass. The crash is not test-specific — it is in the shared prefill kernel, so a model served on MI35x with `--kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3` **through the Triton attention backend** hits it, in decode as well as prefill. (Backends that do not route through these kernels, and the two ROCm Triton kernels that cannot take an fp8 pool at all, are out of scope; see Modifications.) **Scope: the ROCm 7.0 image only — 7.2 was never affected.** The dividing line is the Triton wheel, not ROCm. On the pre-fix ROCm 7.2 MI35x lane ([job 95705686213](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32135460766/job/95705686213), Aug 18, before any commit here) `test_verify_shared_kv.py` reported `"passed": true` with no `PassManager::run failed` or `idx < size()` in the log; that lane's only red was the unrelated `test_quark_mxfp4.py` near-miss. The 7.0 log carries aiter's `require triton>=3.6.0, found 3.4.0`, while 7.2 emits no such warning, so its Triton clears 3.6.0 (`docker/rocm.Dockerfile` installs aiter's pin over the base ROCm Torch `triton==3.5.1` when `BUILD_TRITON=1`). ### Root cause Every Triton attention kernel that reads a KV pool casts the wide operand *down* to the pool dtype before the dot (`tl.dot(q.to(k.dtype), k)`, `tl.dot(p.to(v.dtype), v)`), so an fp8 pool also feeds the fp8 matrix core. On gfx950 `AccelerateAMDMatmul` promotes an fp8 x fp8 `tl.dot` to the scaled `V_MFMA_*_F8F6F4` family, which is **16x16x128** under the `matrix_instr_nonkdim=16` launch hint all of these kernels pass. A dot whose reduction is narrower than 128 does not tile that instruction: `AMDMfmaEncodingAttr::getRepForOperand` clamps the resulting zero K-repetitions up to one, and `ScaledDotOpMFMAConversionHelper` then reads `kBase = 32` elements per lane from a register range that only holds `K / 4`. That is the out-of-bounds `SmallVector` access. `P @ V` reduces `BLOCK_N`, which is 64 (extend, verify) or 32 (decode, split-KV verify) — never 128 — so the fp8 path never compiles on gfx950. `Q @ Kpe` reduces `BLOCK_DPE` (32/64) and `Q @ K` reduces `BLOCK_DMODEL`, which is also below 128 at head_dim <= 64. Triton rejects the intrinsic instead of miscompiling it as of [triton-lang/triton#8278](https://github.com/triton-lang/triton/pull/8278), which dropped the `enforcedNonKDim == 0 &&` escape hatch that had let an explicit `matrix_instr_nonkdim` skip Triton's own "K is not a multiple of the intrinsic's kDim" check. That fix missed 3.5 and landed in 3.6: | Triton branch | guard in `chooseMfmaInstruction` | narrow fp8 dot | |---|---|---| | `release/3.4.x`, `release/3.5.x` | `enforcedNonKDim == 0 && inputKSize % kDim != 0` | promoted, then aborts | | `release/3.6.x` and later | `if (inputKSize % kDim != 0)` | rejected, falls back to non-scaled fp8 MFMA | So anything on 3.4 or 3.5 with `matrix_instr_nonkdim` set — which is every kernel here — crashes, and the ROCm 7.0 image ships 3.4.0. This is why the patch is deliberately independent of the Triton version rather than gated on a version check: 7.0 needs it today, and on 7.2 every flag resolves to the same fallback a fixed Triton picks anyway, at identical throughput. An image bump makes the workaround redundant rather than wrong. ## Modifications - New `python/sglang/kernels/ops/attention/fp8_dot_support.py` with `dot_in_kv_dtype(kv_dtype, reduction_width)`: `True` for every non-fp8 pool and every arch other than gfx950, and on gfx950 only for reduction widths that tile the scaled MFMA instruction. - Each dot that casts an operand down to the tile it reads gets its own constexpr verdict (`QK_DOT_IN_KV_DTYPE`, `QK_PE_DOT_IN_KV_DTYPE`, `PV_DOT_IN_KV_DTYPE`, `PV_EXTEND_DOT_IN_V_DTYPE`). When it is `False` the KV tile is upcast to the query dtype instead of the query tile being cast down. This covers `_fwd_kernel` and `_fwd_kernel_unified` (extend), `_fwd_grouped_kernel_stage1` (decode), `_verify_mla_prefix_stage1`, and `_verify_prefix_stage1` — including `_fwd_kernel`'s extend-stage `P @ V`, whose V is the caller's current-chunk tensor rather than the pool. Every flag is `True` on non-gfx950 hardware and for bf16/fp16 pools, so those paths generate the same code as before. `matrix_instr_nonkdim`, tile sizes, warp counts, and the `#mma` layout are all untouched. **Non-AMD impact: none, verified rather than argued.** `is_gfx95_supported()` returns `False` for every non-HIP build without touching the device, so `dot_in_kv_dtype` short-circuits to `True` on NVIDIA and the guards select the pre-existing expression. To confirm that costs nothing, I compiled the original kernel body and the guarded one (flags `True`) for five targets with Triton 3.4.0 and diffed the emitted TTGIR and LLIR modulo debug locations: **identical on sm90 (bf16 and fp8), sm100 (fp8), gfx942 (fp8) and gfx950 (bf16)**. That check is what caught the one real difference — writing the guard as `tl.dot(p.to(v.dtype), v)` reorders the P cast against the `acc * re_scale` multiply, which on Hopper with an fp8 pool moved the async `warp_group_dot` relative to the accumulator scaling. Keeping `p = p.to(v.dtype)` as its own statement inside the guard restores exact equivalence, which is why it is written that way. NVIDIA fp8 KV keeps casting down to fp8 and keeps its fp8 tensor-core path. The residual cost off gfx950 is one extra Triton compile (the new constexpr parameters change the cache key) and three or four integer / `frozenset` comparisons per launch. Two other ROCm Triton kernels dot against a tile that could in principle be fp8, and deliberately get no verdict: - `prefill_attention.py` never reads a KV pool, its `Q @ K` is uncast (so its operands already share a dtype), and its gfx950 `BLOCK_N` is 128 — which tiles the scaled instruction even if `P @ V` ran in fp8. - `rocm_mla_decode_rope.py` does read the pool, but its `Q @ K` is uncast too, so a bf16 query against an fp8 pool fails Triton's frontend with `Unsupported rhs dtype fp8e4nv` well before the AMD backend. That is a separate pre-existing gap in that kernel, not this crash, and a per-dot verdict would not make it work. The verify combine kernels compute their draft-draft block with `tl.sum(q[:, None, :] * ke[None, :, :], 2)`, not `tl.dot`, so no matrix-core promotion applies there. **On unit tests:** I wrote and then dropped a CPU test for the predicate. Asserting `dot_in_kv_dtype(fp8, 64) is False` against a body of `width % 128 == 0` only restates the expression, and the one assertion with real coupling — that the gfx950 head_dim-256 config yields a `BLOCK_N` the guard rejects — would fail if someone legitimately retuned `BLOCK_N` to 128, which is the documented fallback here. Pinning that would block an improvement rather than catch a bug. The failure mode worth guarding is "a new narrow fp8 dot appears on gfx950", and what catches that is compiling the real kernel on real gfx950, i.e. the MI35x lane. Alternatives considered and rejected: dropping or raising `matrix_instr_nonkdim` for the fp8 path (Triton's own guard then rejects the intrinsic, but the 16x16 tile becomes 32x32, which changes `warpsPerTile` for the chain-dot tail from `[8, 1]` to `[4, 2]` and inserts a layout conversion between the two dots), and forcing `BLOCK_N = 128` (fixes only head_dim 256 and re-tunes the bf16 path with it). ## Accuracy Tests `stage-b-test-1-gpu-small-amd-mi35x` now passes on MI35x hardware. [Run 32217006660](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32217006660) is a targeted dispatch of just that stage against this PR's head (ROCm 7.0, since that lane is schedule-only and a PR event never runs it): **9/9 passed**, `test_verify_shared_kv.py` reports `"passed": true` with `test_qwen3_5_fp8_kv_cache` executing, and the log contains no `PassManager::run failed` or `idx < size()`. ([Run 32212523645](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32212523645) is the same result on the first commit.) The change only affects gfx950 with an fp8 KV pool, where nothing compiled before, so there is no prior behaviour to regress. Within that path `P` reaches the dot as bf16 rather than quantized to e4m3, which is strictly more accurate; `extend_attention_fwd` and `verify_shared_kv_fwd` widen the same dots, so `test_qwen3_5_fp8_kv_cache`'s parity check compares like with like. ## Speed Tests and Profiling No throughput measurement yet — the run above establishes correctness, not perf. The reasoning for expecting no loss: the wide `Q @ K` dot keeps `tt.dot_scaled` (verified in the emitted TTGIR below), and for the narrow dots CDNA4's non-scaled `V_MFMA_F32_16X16X32_FP8_FP8` — what a Triton carrying #8278 would fall back to — reduces the same 32 elements per instruction as `V_MFMA_F32_16X16X32_BF16`, so bf16 operands run at the same rate. The extra cost is the fp8 -> bf16 converts on the V tile and a larger LDS footprint for it (80 KB total at head_dim 256 versus 128 KB for a bf16 pool, so still well inside the 160 KB budget). ## Verification Triton 3.4.0's AMD backend compiles for `hip:gfx950` without a GPU, so the fix was checked by driving the ttir/ttgir/llir stages directly on the same tile shape and launch hints as `extend_attention` at head_dim 256 (`BLOCK_M=128`, `num_warps=8`, `matrix_instr_nonkdim=16`): | KV dtype | `PV_DOT_IN_KV_DTYPE` | `BLOCK_N` | Result | |---|---|---|---| | fp8_e4m3 | True (today) | 64 | **`RuntimeError: PassManager::run failed`** | | fp8_e4m3 | False (this PR) | 64 | compiles | | fp8_e4m3 | True | 32 | **`Assertion 'idx < size()' failed`** | | fp8_e4m3 | False | 32 | compiles | | fp8_e4m3 | True | 128 | compiles (128 tiles the instruction) | | bf16 | True | 64 | compiles (unchanged path) | The fixed variant's TTGIR keeps the fp8 fast path where it is legal and drops to bf16 only for `P @ V`, both under the same `#mma` layout as before: ``` %50 = tt.dot_scaled %28, %49, %cst_2 lhs = e4m3 rhs = e4m3 : tensor<128x256xf8E4M3FN, dot_op<{opIdx = 0, parent = #mma, kWidth = 16}>> * tensor<256x64xf8E4M3FN, ...> %77 = tt.dot %76, %75, %73 : tensor<128x64xbf16, dot_op<{opIdx = 0, parent = #mma, kWidth = 4}>> * tensor<64x256xbf16, dot_op<{opIdx = 1, parent = #mma, kWidth = 4}>> ``` The K3 MLA tile (`BLOCK_DMODEL=512`, `BLOCK_DPE=64`, `BLOCK_N=64`), where two of the three dots widen, behaves the same way: crashes today, compiles with the per-dot verdicts. Narrowing `BLOCK_DMODEL` to 64 crashes the `Q @ K` dot too, which is why the verdict is computed per dot rather than assuming `Q @ K` is always wide enough. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). The regression test is the existing `test_verify_shared_kv.py::test_qwen3_5_fp8_kv_cache` on `stage-b-test-1-gpu-small-amd-mi35x`, which this PR turns green; no new test file is added (see below). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

signal.title: [Kimi K3] Rework skipped-think fix as opt-in force_nonempty_content with streaming coverage
signal.text: Stacked on top of #33995. Keeps @yhyang201's original commit `d11868d7d9` in history and supersedes it with a rework. ## Problem K3 sometimes closes its think channel before producing any answer (EOS inside think), so responses come back with `reasoning_content` but empty `content`. #33995 fixed the non-stream path by treating marker-less output as content, which has two leaks: - **Truncated reasoning becomes content**: a `max_tokens` cut also produces zero think markers, so truncated thinking gets misclassified as the answer. - **Streaming stays broken**: the branch only exists in `detect_and_parse`; `parse_streaming_increment` starts in `force_reasoning=True` and streams the raw payload as `reasoning_text`, so `stream=True` still returns `content=""`. ## What this PR does Reworks the fix as an opt-in, K3-native `force_nonempty_content`: - `KimiK3Detector.__init__` accepts `force_nonempty_content` so the existing `chat_template_kwargs` plumbing in `ReasoningParser` works (previously `TypeError`). - `detect_and_parse` reclassifies only on positive evidence: `RESPONSE_CLOSE` or `MESSAGE_CLOSE` present and zero think markers (full or partial). Bare marker-free text (truncated reasoning) stays reasoning. - Streaming **never holds chunks back**. A hold-back would starve SSE during long thinking runs (no delta until the channel decision) and trip client idle timeouts (observed: ~300 s client-side `terminated` while the server is still decoding). Instead, undecided prethink text streams as `reasoning_content` in real time, and `finish()` re-emits the cleaned payload as `content` once the response/message close proves skipped-think — mirroring the base class's `finish()` re-emit of accumulated reasoning. - The `finish()` re-emit is gated on `_in_reasoning`, i.e. it only fires when no channel decision ever happened mid-stream. Without the gate, answers that already streamed as `content` (`RESPONSE_OPEN` expressible, or `force_reasoning=False`) would be emitted a second time. - Under `stream_reasoning=False`, reasoning buffered past a mid-stream cut (e.g. `max_tokens`) still flushes: the non-fnc path delegates to the base `finish()`, and the fnc path flushes the buffer as `reasoning_text` itself, because the base implementation would reclassify it as `content` under fnc — the leak this flag exists to prevent. Clients therefore see: live `reasoning_content` while the model thinks → final `content` delta carrying the actual answer for skipped-think runs; long thinking runs stream uninterrupted end to end. No behavior change for `force_nonempty_content=False`; all existing K3 parser tests unchanged. ## Tests - `test_fnc_non_stream_skipped_think_vs_truncated_reasoning` — non-stream skipped-think vs truncated reasoning under `force_nonempty_content=True`. - `test_fnc_streaming_skipped_think_answer` — real-time reasoning deltas + finish() content re-emit, across chunk sizes 1/5/13. - `test_fnc_streaming_truncated_reasoning_stays_reasoning` — no close evidence → stays reasoning. - `test_fnc_streaming_long_think_streams_without_close` — 20k chars of marker-free thinking streams every chunk live; no hold-back. - `test_fnc_streaming_response_open_not_reemitted` / `test_fnc_streaming_force_reasoning_off_not_reemitted` — answer streams exactly once; the finish() re-emit never duplicates it. - `test_stream_reasoning_off_truncation_flushes_reasoning` — truncated reasoning flushes as reasoning, fnc on and off. - `test_fnc_stream_reasoning_off_skipped_think_reemits_content` — skipped-think re-emit still works when nothing streamed live. The duplication and flush-regression tests fail on the pre-gate code (verified by stashing the fix); everything passes after it. ``` $ pytest test/registered/unit/parser/test_kimik3_reasoning_parser.py test/registered/unit/parser/test_reasoning_parser.py 138 passed ``` <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:no_entry_sign: [Run #32400319883](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32400319883)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32400319481](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32400319481)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #32400319720](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32400319720)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [DSv4] Integrate TRT-LLM DSv4 Attention for SM100/103
signal.text: ## Motivation Integrates TRT-LLM attention kernel for DSv4 style attention (CSA, HCA). ## Modifications ## Accuracy Tests ``` SGLANG_DSV4_ATTN_DECODE_BACKEND=flashmla/trtllm_gen \ python -m sglang.launch_server --model-path deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro \ --trust-remote-code --tp 8 --moe-runner-backend flashinfer_mxfp4 \ --chunked-prefill-size 4096 --disable-flashinfer-autotune \ --mem-fraction-static 0.88 --max-running-requests 32 ``` ### GSM8K Accuracy GSM8K V4-Pro flashmla: 0.965 GSM8K V4-Pro trtllm_gen: 0.985 ### GPQA (add --chat-template to above server command) ``` python3 -m sglang.test.run_eval --port 21000 --eval-name gpqa \ --num-examples 198 --max-tokens 120000 --repeat 8 \ --thinking-mode deepseek-v3 ``` FlashMLA: Repeat: 8, mean: 0.885 Scores: ['0.889', '0.879', '0.889', '0.879', '0.869', '0.899', '0.904', '0.874'] TRTLLM: Repeat: 8, mean: 0.907 Scores: ['0.919', '0.904', '0.894', '0.904', '0.909', '0.919', '0.904', '0.904'] ## Speed Tests and Profiling ### Unit Kernel Benchmarking (ran with private benchmarking repo): ``` # prefill (varlen), long contexts python benchmark.py --backends flashmla_dsv4,trtllm_gen_dsv4 --model deepseek-v4 \ --hw b200 --dtype fp8 --mode prefill --tp 1 \ --batch-sizes 1,2 --seq-lens 4096,16384,65536 --graph # decode, low/mid concurrency x long contexts python benchmark.py --backends flashmla_dsv4,trtllm_gen_dsv4 --model deepseek-v4 \ --hw b200 --dtype fp8 --mode decode --tp 1 \ --batch-sizes 1,4,16,64 --seq-lens 1024,4096,16384,65536,131072 --graph # decode, high concurrency python benchmark.py --backends flashmla_dsv4,trtllm_gen_dsv4 --model deepseek-v4 \ --hw b200 --dtype fp8 --mode decode --tp 1 \ --batch-sizes 128,256,512,1024 --seq-lens 256,1024,4096,16384 --graph ``` Prefill: ~1.2x faster Decode: ~1.45x faster The performance for TP > 1 scales better on trtllm-gen, since it seems the flashmla variant requires padding the head_dim to 64 or 128. I've attached some sample graphs showing the kernel perf comparison. ### E2E bench-serving ```bash python -m sglang.bench_serving --backend sglang --host 127.0.0.1 --port 21000 \ --dataset-name random --random-input-len 131072 --random-output-len 128 \ --random-range-ratio 1 --num-prompts 8 --max-concurrency 4 ``` flashmla: ``` Benchmark duration (s): 59.92 Total input tokens: 1048576 Input token throughput (tok/s): 17500.55 Mean E2E Latency (ms): 29950.67 Mean TTFT (ms): 19009.87 (median 19636.34) Mean TPOT (ms): 86.15 Median ITL (ms): 12.12 ``` trtllm_gen: ``` Benchmark duration (s): 60.09 Total input tokens: 1048576 Input token throughput (tok/s): 17448.78 Mean E2E Latency (ms): 30039.27 Mean TTFT (ms): 16808.71 (median 15734.66) Mean TPOT (ms): 104.18 Median ITL (ms): 13.11 ``` ## Checklist - [ ] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [ ] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. signal.title: [Diffusion] Enable vectorized JointThreshold decoding on CUDA
signal.text: ## Motivation JointThreshold decoding already has a batched tensor implementation, but CUDA defaults to the per-row Python path. At higher concurrency, that path serializes argmax, confidence, edit, and completion work across requests and repeatedly synchronizes the host with the device. This PR enables the existing vectorized JointThreshold path by default on CUDA. The change targets JointThreshold specifically: LowConfidence is already vectorized, and DiffusionGemma uses the separate Gemma4Renoise sampler. ## Modifications - Default `vectorized_decoding` to true on CUDA, matching the existing NPU policy. - Preserve `vectorized_decoding: false` as a compatibility/debug escape hatch. - Document the default and its applicability to `LLaDA2MoeModelLM`, `SDARForCausalLM`, and `SDARMoeForCausalLM`. ## Accuracy Tests SGLang already has a registered CUDA E2E test for this exact path: `test/registered/dllm/test_dllm_fdfo_joint_threshold.py`. It launches `inclusionAI/LLaDA2.1-mini` with JointThreshold and requires byte-identical outputs between FDFO and synchronous execution. Since this PR changes the CUDA default, both arms exercise the vectorized implementation. I also ran an external real-model E2E A/B matrix by launching two SGLang HTTP servers with `sglang.launch_server` and driving them with `sglang.benchmark.serving`. All 3,968/3,968 measured LLaDA2.1-mini requests completed with the requested output token count and no request errors. This validates the real serving path and output completion, not downstream task accuracy. No locally available SDAR checkpoint was available, so this PR does not claim real-model SDAR coverage. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Configuration: - H200, TP1, BF16, FDFO; - FlashInfer attention; - radix cache disabled; - maximum 128 running requests; - 8,192-token context; - exact token-ID inputs; - baseline and vectorized arms used identical server and benchmark settings; - each result below contains 32, 64, 128, 256, or 512 requests at concurrency 1, 8, 32, 64, or 128 respectively. **Metric definitions:** request throughput is the achieved end-to-end client throughput (`completed requests / benchmark duration`). TPOT is time per output token excluding the first token: `(request E2E latency - TTFT) / (output tokens - 1)`. The latency columns below are TPOT, not full end-to-end request latency. ### Decode-heavy: 512 input / 2,048 output tokens | Concurrency | E2E request throughput | Delta | Mean TPOT | Delta | p95 TPOT | Delta | |---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | 1 | 0.172 -> 0.168 req/s | -2.7% | 2.72 -> 2.79 ms | +2.8% | 5.07 -> 5.20 ms | +2.5% | | 8 | 0.532 -> 0.685 req/s | +28.7% | 6.89 -> 5.03 ms | -27.0% | 12.87 -> 10.66 ms | -17.2% | | 32 | 0.774 -> 1.079 req/s | +39.4% | 17.60 -> 12.40 ms | -29.6% | 31.66 -> 22.11 ms | -30.2% | | 64 | 1.001 -> 1.493 req/s | +49.2% | 27.67 -> 18.32 ms | -33.8% | 54.96 -> 37.30 ms | -32.1% | | 128 | 1.158 -> 1.842 req/s | +59.0% | 48.08 -> 29.78 ms | -38.1% | 100.22 -> 64.81 ms | -35.3% | ### Long-prefill: 4,096 input / 1,536 output tokens | Concurrency | E2E request throughput | Delta | Mean TPOT | Delta | p95 TPOT | Delta | |---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | 1 | 0.269 -> 0.258 req/s | -4.0% | 1.84 -> 1.91 ms | +3.7% | 5.06 -> 5.20 ms | +2.8% | | 8 | 0.641 -> 0.674 req/s | +5.2% | 6.61 -> 6.44 ms | -2.6% | 25.42 -> 24.67 ms | -3.0% | | 32 | 0.878 -> 0.924 req/s | +5.2% | 20.29 -> 19.36 ms | -4.6% | 70.97 -> 62.97 ms | -11.3% | | 64 | 0.984 -> 1.119 req/s | +13.8% | 36.76 -> 32.41 ms | -11.9% | 138.68 -> 122.23 ms | -11.9% | | 128 | 1.173 -> 1.308 req/s | +11.5% | 61.80 -> 56.39 ms | -8.8% | 237.48 -> 219.20 ms | -7.7% | A GPU-swapped control reproduced the concurrency-64 gains: - decode-heavy: +49.0% request throughput and -33.4% mean TPOT; - long-prefill: +12.5% request throughput and -10.2% mean TPOT. The batch-1 regression is an intentional tradeoff for one consistent CUDA execution path; the benefit grows with batch size because it removes per-request Python work and host synchronization. Benchmark runtime used PyTorch `2.11.0+cu130` and FlashInfer `0.6.14`. Current SGLang pins FlashInfer `0.6.15.post1`. ## Checklist - [x] Format code according to the pre-commit configuration. - [x] Add unit tests. - [x] Update documentation. - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results. - [x] Follow the SGLang code style guidance. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #31730664744](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31730664744)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #31730664268](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31730664268)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

This provides cleaner code, better type handling, and comprehensive validation. ## Motivation Fix #16256 Previously, the server argument parsing logic handled configuration files by manually reconstructing a list of command-line arguments (e.g., converting config values back to strings and appending them to sys.argv). This approach had several drawbacks: - **Complexity & Fragility**: Manually reconstructing argv strings is error-prone, especially when dealing with different data types (booleans, lists) and edge cases. - **Redundancy**: The old approach manually converted config values to CLI argument strings (handling booleans, lists, type-to-string conversion), then had argparse re-parse them. This duplicated logic that `parser.set_defaults()` handles natively without string conversion. - **Maintenance**: It makes the codebase harder to read and maintain. ## Modifications ### Core Changes | Before | After | |--------|-------| | Manually reconstructed CLI arguments from config | Use `parser.set_defaults(**config)` directly | | Type validation by argparse (after string conversion) | Explicit type validation in ConfigArgumentMerger (no string round-trip) | | Boolean handling required manual `--flag` construction | Direct boolean value support with strict validation | | Only YAML support | YAML and JSON support | | Silent failures for invalid options | Explicit errors for invalid choices, types, and rejected options | ### Key Implementation Details 1. **ConfigArgumentMerger class** (server_args_config_parser.py) - parse_config(): Parses config file and returns validated dict - remove_config_from_argv(): Removes `--config` from argv for argparse - _parse_config_file(): Supports both YAML and JSON formats - _convert_value(): Smart type conversion with special handling for: - `None` values (YAML null) - pass through - Already matched types - skip redundant conversion - `json.loads`/`json_list_type` - skip for pre-parsed dict/list - nullable_str - convert numeric values to string first 2. **Validation Features** - **Rejected options**: `config`, `help`, `h`, and custom actions (e.g., `DeprecatedAction`, `LoRAPathAction`) cannot be specified in config files - **Choices validation**: Validates both single values and nargs lists - **store_true validation**: Rejects non-boolean values (int, string) - **Unknown options**: Logs warning and ignores 3. **Dynamic Required Argument Handling** When a required argument is provided in the config file, we dynamically set `action.required = False`: ```python for action in parser._actions: if action.dest in config_values and action.required: action.required = False ``` Why this is needed: - parser.set_defaults() only sets default values, it doesn't affect the required flag - Without this, argparse would still raise "required argument missing" error even when the value is in config - This allows config file to satisfy required arguments without CLI specification 4. **Argument Precedence** CLI Args > Config File > Default Values ### Files Changed | File | Change | |------|--------| | python/sglang/srt/server_args.py | Added config merging logic in `prepare_server_args()` | | python/sglang/srt/server_args_config_parser.py | Refactored ConfigArgumentMerger class with enhanced validation| | test/manual/test_config_integration.py | Updated test suite with comprehensive coverage | ## Tests Added comprehensive test suite in test/manual/test_config_integration.py ### Test Coverage | Test Class | Coverage | |------------|----------| | TestConfigArgumentMerger | Basic parsing, key normalization, choices validation | | TestPrepareServerArgs | End-to-end config loading, JSON support, CLI override | | TestErrorHandling | File not found, multiple configs, unsupported extension, rejected options | | TestTypeValidation | store_true, type conversion, null passthrough, dict/JSON skip | | TestEdgeCases | Empty config, .yml extension, unknown options, non-dict root, nullable_str | ### Practical scenario validation ```bash root@localhost:/workspace/sglang/python# cat /workspace/config.yaml enable-metrics: true disable_cuda_graph: true host: 127.0.0.1 port: 3009 model-path: /root/.cache/Qwen3-4B-GGUF/Qwen3-4B-Q8_0.gguf device: npu attention-backend: ascend tokenizer_mode: auto log-requests-target: ["/workspace/mock1","/workspace/mock2"] log-requests: true mem-fraction-static: 0.8 quantization_param_path: null zzzzzzzzz: 11111111111111 root@localhost:/workspace/sglang/python# python3 -m sglang.launch_server --config /workspace/config.yaml [2026-01-16 02:43:45] WARNING server_args_config_parser.py:54: Unknown config option 'zzzzzzzzz' will be ignored. Check if the option name is correct. /workspace/sglang/python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/awq.py:76: UserWarning: Only CUDA, HIP and XPU support AWQ currently. warnings.warn(f"Only CUDA, HIP and XPU support AWQ currently.") signal.title: fix: avoid aliased tensor in fused add+norm for EXAONE4 post-LN in forward_split_prefill
signal.text: ## Summary - EXAONE4 uses **post-LN** architecture where each decoder layer returns `hidden_states` and `residual` pointing to the **same tensor object** (`residual = hidden_states`) - The `forward_split_prefill` path called `self.model.norm(hidden_states, residual)` with two args, passing both aliased tensors to `fused_add_rmsnorm` - This is inconsistent with the regular `forward` path (line 386) which correctly calls `self.norm(hidden_states)` with a single argument - Fix: match the regular forward path's single-arg norm call ## Root cause In EXAONE4's post-LN decoder layer, the final lines are: ```python hidden_states = self.post_feedforward_layernorm(hidden_states) hidden_states = hidden_states + residual residual = hidden_states # same object return hidden_states, residual ``` When `forward_split_prefill` passes both to `fused_add_rmsnorm`, it computes `residual += hidden_states` in-place on aliased memory. ## Test plan - Run EXAONE4 inference with chunked prefill / pipeline parallelism - Compare logits between `forward` and `forward_split_prefill` paths
signal.author: Bias92

signal.title: Fix conv_states dtype mismatch when using --dtype half with Mamba models
signal.text: ## Motivation Fix https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/19773 I reproduce this bug using ``` # For simplicity I use 9B model python -m sglang.launch_server --model-path Qwen/Qwen3.5-9B --dtype half # And send a request curl -s http://localhost:30000/v1/completions \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"model": "default", "prompt": "Write a long story about", "max_tokens": 256}' ``` ``` RuntimeError: Expected conv_states_.scalar_type() == input_type to be true, but got false. ``` **Root cause:** The Mamba `conv_states` cache is allocated using the dtype from [`mamba2_state_dtype()`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/python/sglang/srt/configs/mamba_utils.py#L68), which defaults to `bfloat16` (hardcoded via [`SGLANG_MAMBA_CONV_DTYPE`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/python/sglang/srt/environ.py#L443) env var default). When the user passes `--dtype half`, model activations are `float16`, but conv_states remain `bfloat16`. The `causal_conv1d` kernel rejects this mismatch. The existing workaround in [`test_generation_models.py`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/test/registered/models/test_generation_models.py#L151-L152) explicitly sets `SGLANG_MAMBA_CONV_DTYPE` to match the inference dtype, confirming this is a known gap. ## Modifications **[`python/sglang/srt/configs/model_config.py`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/python/sglang/srt/configs/model_config.py#L200)** - After `_get_and_verify_dtype()` resolves the final dtype, sync it back to `hf_text_config.torch_dtype` so downstream consumers can read the actual running dtype. **[`python/sglang/srt/configs/mamba_utils.py`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/python/sglang/srt/configs/mamba_utils.py#L68)** - In `mamba2_state_dtype()`, use `envs.SGLANG_MAMBA_CONV_DTYPE.is_set()` to distinguish between a user-explicit env var and the default. - When the user has **not** explicitly set the env var, read `config.torch_dtype` (now reflecting the resolved `--dtype` value) instead of hardcoding `bfloat16`. - When the user **has** explicitly set the env var, honor it as before. - Fall back to `bfloat16` if neither source provides a valid dtype. ## Result Before modification [2026-03-03 13:52:30] Mamba2 state dtype: conv_dtype=torch.bfloat16, ssm_dtype=torch.float32 and it crash like in the issue After modification [2026-03-03 13:51:03] Mamba2 state dtype: conv_dtype=torch.float16, ssm_dtype=torch.float32 And it can work properly ## Accuracy Tests No changes to model forward code or kernels — this only affects the dtype used for conv_states cache allocation, ensuring it matches the model's actual running dtype. Existing Mamba model tests (which explicitly set `SGLANG_MAMBA_CONV_DTYPE`) are unaffected since `is_set()` returns `True` for those. ## Benchmarking and Profiling No impact on inference speed — this change only affects cache allocation dtype selection at startup. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review Process 1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the PR flow. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process). 2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers. 3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so. - `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci`, `/tag-and-rerun-ci` 4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls to merge.
signal.author: ShanningZhuang

signal.title: [EPLB] Add topology-aware expert placement algorithm
signal.text: ## Summary Implements a topology-aware Expert Parallel Load Balancing (EPLB) algorithm that reduces cross-node RDMA traffic by **25.2%** while maintaining comparable decode performance for DeepSeek-R1 inference, fix #19487 ## Problem The default DeepSeek hierarchical EPLB algorithm places redundant experts without considering network topology, resulting in high cross-node traffic during expert dispatch. In multi-node deployments with Expert Parallelism (EP) spanning across nodes, this causes: - Increased RDMA communication overhead - Higher latency for expert token routing - Suboptimal network bandwidth utilization ## Solution The topology-aware EPLB algorithm: 1. **Prioritizes node locality** - Places redundant experts on the same node as their primary experts 2. **Minimizes cross-node dispatches** - Reduces inter-node communication while maintaining load balance 3. **Greedy allocation strategy** - Optimizes expert placement based on network topology ## Benchmark Results **Configuration:** - Model: DeepSeek-R1-0528 (256 experts + 64 redundant) - Hardware: 8xH20, Decode: EP=16 across 2 nodes (DP=16) - Workload: 200 prompts, max concurrency 200 ### Cross-Node Traffic Reduction | Algorithm | Cross-Node Ratio | Improvement | |-----------|------------------|-------------| | DeepSeek r64 | 0.5038 | baseline | | Topology-Aware r64 | 0.3770 | **-25.2%** | ### Decode Performance | Metric | DeepSeek r64 | Topology-Aware r64 | Change | |--------|--------------|-------------------|--------| | Mean ITL (ms) | 49.84 | 49.29 | -1.1% | | Mean TPOT (ms) | 36.72 | 36.15 | -1.6% | | Output Throughput (tok/s) | 4154 | 4223 | +1.7% | ## Key Findings | Metric | Result | |--------|--------| | Cross-Node Traffic | **-25.2%** reduction (0.50 → 0.38) | | Output Throughput | **+1.7%** improvement | | ITL/TPOT | Comparable or slightly better | ## Recommendation Use **Topology-Aware EPLB with 64 redundant experts** for: - Significant reduction in cross-node RDMA traffic - Slight improvement in decode throughput - Better network efficiency in multi-node deployments This is especially beneficial for: - Multi-node inference clusters with RDMA networking - High-concurrency production workloads - Cost-sensitive deployments where network bandwidth is a constraint ## Usage The benchmark results use **static dispatch** with a pre-generated expert location file. ### Step 1: Generate Expert Location File ```bash python eplb/generate_expert_location.py \ --algorithm topology_aware \ --output expert-location-topology-aware-r64.json \ --num-logical-experts 256 \ --num-redundant-experts 64 \ --num-gpus 16 \ --num-nodes 2 \ --num-groups 128 ``` ### Step 2: Deploy with Static Dispatch ```bash python -m sglang.launch_server \ --model-path /models/DeepSeek-R1-0528/ \ --tp 16 --dp 16 \ --ep-num-redundant-experts 64 \ --init-expert-location expert-location-topology-aware-r64.json \ --ep-dispatch-algorithm static ``` ### Step 3: Monitor Cross-Node Traffic (Optional) ```bash python -m sglang.launch_server \ --model-path /models/DeepSeek-R1-0528/ \ --tp 16 --dp 16 \ --ep-num-redundant-experts 64 \ --init-expert-location expert-location-topology-aware-r64.json \ --ep-dispatch-algorithm static \ --expert-distribution-recorder-mode per_pass \ --enable-expert-distribution-metrics ``` ### Monitoring Logs Example When `--enable-expert-distribution-metrics` is enabled, cross-node traffic is logged per forward pass: ``` [Expert Balancedness] forward_pass_id=100 balancedness=0.603 avg10=0.590 avg100=0.585 avg1000=0.548 cross_node_ratio=0.377 tokens=92800 [Expert Balancedness] forward_pass_id=101 balancedness=0.595 avg10=0.591 avg100=0.584 avg1000=0.549 cross_node_ratio=0.381 tokens=92800 [Expert Balancedness] forward_pass_id=102 balancedness=0.603 avg10=0.592 avg100=0.585 avg1000=0.550 cross_node_ratio=0.373 tokens=92800 ``` - **balancedness**: Expert utilization rate (higher = better load balance) - **cross_node_ratio**: Fraction of expert accesses crossing node boundaries (lower = less RDMA traffic) - **tokens**: Total tokens processed in this forward pass ## Testing - [x] Benchmarked with 200 prompts on 4-node cluster - [x] Verified 25.2% cross-node traffic reduction - [x] Confirmed decode performance parity - [x] Generated step-by-step visualization
signal.author: Yancey0623

signal.title: Enhance Kimi K2.5 support with improved reasoning parser and function call detector
signal.text: ## Motivation Kimi K2.5 models exhibit special behaviors that required dedicated handling: - Reasoning Mode Issue: When deciding to invoke a tool while in reasoning mode (`<think>...</think>`), the model may output tool call markers directly without first outputting the `</think>` closing tag. - UUID Format Support: Support UUID-style call IDs (e.g., `call_6b0e7c24f0c44f0d996b59e5`). This ensures compatibility for scenarios that mix models (e.g., using Model A in the first round and Model Kimi-K2.5 in the second round). - Streaming Robustness: The original streaming parser had issues with special token leakage and incomplete state management. Related Issues: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/18086 ## Modifications ### Reasoning Parser 1. New KimiK2Detector Class (inherits from Qwen3Detector) Force exit reasoning mode, return content before marker as reasoning_text, content from marker onwards as normal_text ### Function Call Detector 1. UUID Format Support Extended regex patterns to support both standard and UUID formats 3. Function Name Inference New `_infer_function_name_from_args()` method for UUID format 4. Robust State Management Added proper state tracking and reset methods 5. Special Token Leakage Prevention Comprehensive token filtering to prevent special tokens from leaking to normal_text 6. Improved Streaming State Machine Refactored `parse_streaming_increment()` with clearer state transitions 7. Hyphenated Function Name Support Updated regex to support hyphenated function names (common in MCP tools) Example: `mcp__portal__search-documents` ## Accuracy Tests <!-- If this pull request affects model outputs (e.g., changes to the kernel or model forward code), provide accuracy test results. --> ## Benchmarking and Profiling <!-- If this pull request impacts inference speed, provide benchmarking and profiling results. --> ## Checklist - [ ] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [ ] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review Process 1. signal.title: [Diffusion] [Wan]: Fuse the element-wise operations cross transformer blocks
signal.text: <!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. --> ## Motivation <!-- Describe the purpose and goals of this pull request. --> 1. Fuse the element-wise operations at the end of block i (`MulAdd`) and the beginning of block i+1 (`LayerNormScaleShift`) into a single `ScaleResidualLayerNormScaleShift` kernel to reduce kernel launches and improve efficiency. 2. Store null_gate, null_shift, and null_scale as attributes instead of recreating them in each block during the forward pass, reducing repeated tensor allocations and runtime overhead. 3. Modified block inputs and outputs to propagate residual, ff_output, and c_gate_msa between blocks, improving data flow. ## Modifications <!-- Detail the changes made in this pull request. --> ## Accuracy Tests <!-- If this pull request affects model outputs (e.g., changes to the kernel or model forward code), provide accuracy test results. --> ## Wan2.2 benchmark: Test input image: ![ikun](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5ea81548-b369-404a-81da-a149cde3a67c) ### command ```bash CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES="0,1,2,3,4,5,6,7" sglang generate \ --model-path "Wan-AI/Wan2.2-I2V-A14B-Diffusers" \ --attention-backend fa \ --trust-remote-code \ --num-gpus 8 \ --ulysses-degree 8 \ --use-fsdp-inference false \ --dit-cpu-offload false \ --dit-layerwise-offload false \ --text-encoder-cpu-offload false \ --image-encoder-cpu-offload false \ --vae-cpu-offload false \ --pin-cpu-memory false \ --backend sglang \ --num-frames 81 \ --fps 16 \ --height 720 \ --width 1280 \ --num-inference-steps 40 \ --prompt "一位名叫蔡徐坤的中国男明星站在室外篮球场中央，夕阳的金色光线洒在球场上。他手持篮球，深情而自信地凝望镜头。镜头缓慢推进，他开始运球，在球场上做出流畅的篮球动作。随着节奏感强烈的音乐，他一边打篮球一边跳舞，将篮球动作与舞蹈动作自然结合。他的身材修长而结实，动作充满节奏感和魅力，舞步干净利落，充满舞台表现力。篮球在地面弹跳，他转身、运球、投篮，同时加入优雅又富有力量感的舞蹈动作。整体氛围充满运动活力与男性魅力，画面具有电影质感，慢动作镜头、动态跟拍、光影细节丰富，4K，high detail，cinematic lighting。" \ --image-path "ikun.jpeg" \ --warmup \ --save-output ``` ### log: - main: ```text [02-27 07:26:49] Running pipeline stages: ['input_validation_stage', 'text_encoding_stage', 'image_v_a_e_encoding_stage', 'latent_preparation_stage', 'timestep_preparation_stage', 'denoising_stage', 'decoding_stage'] [02-27 07:26:49] [InputValidationStage] started... signal.title: [Feature] Implement image number limitation for image processors
signal.text: ## Motivation Fixes #8540 Currently, there is no default limitation on the number of images during multimodal data processing. The only existing check (`_validate_mm_limits` in TokenizerManager) only runs if the admin explicitly sets `--limit-mm-data-per-request`, which defaults to `None`. Without this, a user could send an excessive number of images, each consuming ~1GB GPU memory via the fast image processor, potentially causing OOM. This PR adds a per-processor default image limit as a safety net. ## Modifications **`python/sglang/srt/multimodal/processors/base_processor.py`:** - Added `IMAGE_NUM_LIMITATION = 5` class constant to `BaseMultimodalProcessor` - Added `_get_image_limit()` helper method that returns the effective limit (CLI override takes priority over processor default) - Added image count validation in `load_mm_data()` before any images are downloaded **`python/sglang/srt/multimodal/processors/internvl.py`:** - Added `IMAGE_NUM_LIMITATION = 12` override (InternVL supports more images) **`test/unit/test_image_num_limitation.py`:** - Unit tests covering: default limit, subclass override, CLI override priority, within-limit pass-through, exceeds-limit rejection ## Priority Order `--limit-mm-data-per-request` CLI flag > processor `IMAGE_NUM_LIMITATION` constant > no protection ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). - [ ] Work with maintainers to merge your PR. signal.title: feat(disagg): KV return — reverse RDMA transfer from decode to prefill
signal.text: ## Summary Adds **KV return**: when a disaggregated decode worker finishes generating tokens, it transfers the generated KV cache back to the originating prefill worker via NIXL RDMA and inserts it into the prefill's RadixCache. This enables multi-turn cache hits without re-computing prefill for prior conversation turns. **Key design choices:** - **On-demand page allocation**: Decode requests destination pages from prefill via ZMQ round-trip (no pre-reserved pools). Prefill can decline under memory pressure. - **Async post-and-poll**: `_try_kv_return()` posts the alloc request non-blocking; `_poll_kv_return_replies()` handles alloc replies and RDMA completions from the scheduler event loop. Decode scheduler never blocks on KV return. - **Page-aligned insertion**: Returned KV is truncated to `floor(N/page_size) * page_size` tokens to match RadixCache page boundaries. ## Changes **9 commits, 1,744 lines across 13 files:** | File | Purpose | |------|---------| | `server_args.py` | `--enable-kv-return` flag | | `disaggregation/nixl/conn.py` | NIXL reverse RDMA transport, ZMQ metadata/alloc channels, prefill-side insertion receiver | | `managers/scheduler.py` | `_process_kv_return_alloc_requests()`, `_process_kv_return_insertions()`, memory accounting, poll integration | | `managers/scheduler_output_processor_mixin.py` | `_try_kv_return()` (async post), `_poll_kv_return_replies()` (non-blocking poll), `_start_kv_return_rdma()` (RDMA helper), `PendingKvReturn` state machine | | `managers/scheduler_runtime_checker_mixin.py` | Idle-path poll + alloc processing, queue size accounting for pending KV returns | | `disaggregation/decode.py` | Decode-side integration hook | | `disaggregation/fake/conn.py` | Stub for non-NIXL backends | | `test_kv_return_insertion_unit.py` | 261-line CPU-only unit test (insertion, dedup, memory accounting) | | `test_kv_return_2worker.sh` | Single-GPU integration test | | `test_kv_return_multiturn.sh` | 3-request multi-turn flow (cold → cache hit → partial prefix) | ## Bugs Found & Fixed | ID | Bug | Discovery | Fix | Commit | |----|-----|-----------|-----|--------| | B1 | `_process_kv_return_alloc_requests()` missing from scheduler idle path → 0% cache hits | Same-GPU test | Added to `self_check_during_idle()` | `534fddfc` | | C1 | Page leak on RDMA failure — prefill allocated pages but decode never sent cancel | Code review | Cancel message with `dst_page_indices` on failure | `85b7faeb` | | C4 | Reply ordering under concurrent requests — ZMQ PULL delivers replies out of order | Code review | `request_id` matching with buffered reply dict | `85b7faeb` | | I6 | Page truncation leak — non-aligned generated tokens left partial pages unreleased | Code review | Free `gen_indices[num_pages * page_size:]` after alignment | `85b7faeb` | | I2 | Dead `kv_return_pending` dict from earlier implementation | Code review | Removed | `5e17e661` | | B2 | Alloc serialization under 5x concurrent — sync ZMQ round-trip caused 52.8ms blocking | Cross-node test | Refactored to async post-and-poll (`PendingKvReturn` state machine) | `5f09b75c` | | R2 | Duplicated RDMA-start logic in 2 code paths | Code review (C2) | Extracted `_start_kv_return_rdma()` helper | `0a4aacff` | | R8 | Missing exception safety in poll loop → permanent page leak on unexpected error | Code review (C2) | Top-level `try/except` with emergency drain | `0a4aacff` | ## Validation Results ### Hardware | Test | Hardware | Model | Nodes | |------|----------|-------|-------| | Same-GPU | 1x H100-80GB | Qwen3-0.6B | 1 (both workers) | | Cross-node (0.6B) | 2x H100-PCIe (81GB) | Qwen3-0.6B | 2 | | Cross-node (8B) | 2x H100-PCIe (81GB) | Qwen3-8B | 2 | ### Same-GPU Validation (Qwen3-0.6B, 1x H100-80GB) - 48/49 cached tokens (98%), alloc 6-18ms, 0.0ms RDMA (local memcpy) - Confirmed end-to-end pipeline: decode → alloc → RDMA → metadata → RadixCache insertion → cache hit ### Cross-Node Validation (Qwen3-0.6B, 2x H100-PCIe) | Test | Requests | KV Returns | Failures | Key Result | progressive cache hits | | Rapid-fire (7x same prompt) | 7 | 7 | 0 | Confirms async insertion timing | | **Subtotal** | **49+** | **49+** | **0** | | ### Cross-Node C2 Async Validation (Qwen3-0.6B, 2x H100-PCIe) | Test | KV Returns | Failures | Notes | |------|-----------|----------|-------| | Sanity | 1 | 0 | Cache hit verified (32/34 = 94%) | | 5x concurrent | 5 | 0 | Scheduler no longer blocks | | 20x concurrent | 20 | 0 | All completed | | Cache hit | 6 | 0 | Working | | **Subtotal** | **32** | **0** | | ### Cross-Node Validation (Qwen3-8B, 2x H100-PCIe) | Test | Requests | KV Returns | Failures | Key Result | |------|----------|-----------|----------|------------| | 10x concurrent burst | 10 | 10 | 0 | ~2.14s batched, 4 pages/req | | Photosynthesis (3 turns) | 3 | 3 | 0 | 67% → 9% → 50% cache hits | | Neural networks (3 turns) | 3 | 3 | 0 | 0% → 9% → 51% cache hits | | Climate (4 turns) | 4 | 4 | 0 | 0% → 10% → 51% → 66% cache hits | | **Subtotal** | **22** | **22** | **0** | Progressive multi-turn caching confirmed | ### Sustained Load (bench_serving, Qwen3-8B, 2x H100-PCIe) `bench_serving --dataset-name random --num-prompts 500 --random-input-len 256 --random-output-len 128 --request-rate 4 --max-concurrency 16` | Metric | Value | |--------|-------| | **Successful requests** | 500/500 (100%) | | **Duration** | 118.4s | | **Request throughput** | 4.22 req/s | | **Total throughput** | 842 tok/s | | **Mean E2E latency** | 1088ms | | **P99 E2E latency** | 2603ms | | **Mean TTFT** | 255ms | | **Median TPOT** | 12.5ms | | **P99 ITL** | 72.3ms | | **KV return attempts** | 497 | | **KV return RDMA succeeded** | 445 | | **KV return declined (pool full)** | 0 | | **NIXL RDMA failures** | **0** | | **Crashes / deadlocks** | 0 | | **Page leaks** | 0 | **Bug fix (838135b)**: Earlier runs showed permanent `NIXL_ERR_NOT_FOUND` failures. Root cause was a page-index bug in the reverse RDMA path — source KV indices were not divided by `page_size`, causing RDMA source addresses to be `page_size`× too large and exceeding the registered memory region. The forward path (prefill→decode) correctly used `kv_to_page_indices()` but the reverse path (decode→prefill) did not. Fixed in `838135b`. ### Memory Pressure (60K token pool) Prefill deployed with `--mem-fraction-static 0.30` → 60,048 token pool (3,753 pages). 200 requests at 4 req/s with 256-token prompts and 512-token outputs: | Outcome | Count | |---------|-------| | Allocs granted | 412 | | Allocs declined (pool full) | 33 | | NIXL RDMA failures | **0** | | Requests completed | **500/500 (100%)** | When the pool reaches `avail=0`, the prefill declines subsequent alloc requests with empty replies. Decode detects the empty reply, logs `"prefill declined alloc"`, calls `release_kv_cache()`, and skips RDMA — no crash, no data corruption, no impact to user requests. KV return declines are entirely transparent to end users. ### Aggregate | Metric | Value | |--------|-------| | **Total KV returns** | **445+** | | **RDMA failures** | **0** | | **Page leaks** | **0** | | **Models tested** | Qwen3-0.6B, Qwen3-8B | | **Concurrency tested** | 1x, 5x, 10x, 20x | | **Multi-turn sessions** | 7 (3-4 turns each, two model sizes) | | **Sustained load** | 500 requests at 4 req/s, 0 RDMA failures, 445 KV returns | | **Memory pressure** | 500 requests against 60K-token pool, 33 graceful declines, 0 RDMA failures | ### Multi-Turn Cache Hit Pattern Each conversation shows progressive cache accumulation: ``` Turn 1: 0% hit (cold start) Turn 2: ~9-10% hit (only original prompt prefix matches) Turn 3: ~50% hit (Turn 1+2 KV now in cache) Turn 4: ~66% hit (Turn 1+2+3 KV accumulated) ``` Cache alignment: `floor(N/page_size) * page_size` — e.g., 128 generated tokens with page_size=16 → 8 pages returned. ## Configuration ```bash # Prefill worker python3 -m sglang.launch_server \ --disaggregation-mode prefill \ --disaggregation-transfer-backend nixl \ --enable-kv-return \ --page-size 16 # Decode worker python3 -m sglang.launch_server \ --disaggregation-mode decode \ --disaggregation-transfer-backend nixl \ --enable-kv-return \ --page-size 16 ``` `--enable-kv-return` is opt-in and has no effect when disaggregation is not enabled. ## Test plan - [x] Unit tests: `test_kv_return_insertion_unit.py` (CPU-only, page alignment, dedup, memory accounting) - [x] Same-GPU integration: `test_kv_return_2worker.sh` (single H100, basic P↔D transfer) - [x] Multi-turn integration: `test_kv_return_multiturn.sh` (3-request flow: cold → cache hit → partial prefix) - [x] Cross-node RDMA: 2x H100-PCIe, Qwen3-0.6B (5x/10x/20x concurrent, multi-turn chain) - [x] 8B model: 2x H100-PCIe, Qwen3-8B (10x concurrent, 3 multi-turn sessions with 3-4 turns) - [x] Async KV return (C2): scheduler non-blocking under concurrent load - [x] Sustained load: `bench_serving` 500 requests at 4 req/s — 100% success, 0 RDMA failures, 445 KV returns succeeded - [x] Memory pressure: `--mem-fraction-static 0.30` (60K pool) — 500 requests, 33 graceful declines under pressure, 0 RDMA failures

signal.title: [Quantization] Fix per-tensor FP8 MoE parameter identity for EPLB hot-reload
signal.text: ## Motivation When using per-tensor FP8 quantized MoE models (e.g., `RedHatAI/DeepSeek-Coder-V2-Lite-Instruct-FP8`) with Elastic EP Load Balancing (EPLB), the failover weight hot-reload crashes with: ``` AttributeError: 'Parameter' object has no attribute 'weight_loader' ``` followed by (after working around the above): ``` RuntimeError: mat1 and mat2 shapes cannot be multiplied (2x2048 and 1536x2048) ``` This was also mentioned in https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/18191. **Issue 1 — Parameter identity loss in per-tensor FP8 MoE** `Fp8MoEMethod.process_weights_after_loading()` creates new `Parameter` objects via `torch.nn.Parameter(...)` for `w13_input_scale`, `w2_input_scale`, and `w13_weight_scale`. This destroys custom attributes (`weight_loader`, `quant_method`) that `deepseek_weight_loader.py` relies on during EPLB hot-reload. The block-quant path was already fixed in #17449 via `_copy_or_rebind()`, but the per-tensor path was never updated. **Issue 2 — Double `process_weights_after_loading` on partial reload** `update_weights_from_disk()` calls `load_weights_and_postprocess()`, which runs `process_weights_after_loading()` on **all** quantized modules unconditionally — even when only expert weights were reloaded. For FP8 linear attention layers (e.g., `q_proj`), this means the weight gets transposed twice (once during initial load, once during reload), corrupting the shape from `[K, N]` back to `[N, K]`. ## Modifications ### `python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/fp8.py` **Dynamic-quant path** (non-checkpoint FP8): - Use `.data =` for weight rebinding and `.data[expert].fill_()` for scale updates instead of `Parameter` replacement. **Checkpoint-FP8 path — `input_scale` merging:** - Replace `torch.nn.Parameter(max_val)` with `layer.w13_input_scale.data.fill_(max_val)` to preserve the original `Parameter` object in-place. **Checkpoint-FP8 path — `w13_weight_scale` merging:** - Instead of replacing the `[E, 2]` Parameter with a new `[E]` one, fill both columns with the same per-expert max in-place. The `[E, 2]` shape is preserved so `weight_loader` can still index `param.data[expert_id][shard_idx]` during reload. **`apply()` — DeepGEMM path:** - Add `ndim == 2` guard to collapse `w13_weight_scale` from `[E, 2]` to `[E]` via `[:, 0]` before expanding to block shape. ### `python/sglang/srt/model_executor/model_runner.py` **Partial reload isolation:** - When `weight_name_filter` is set (EPLB expert rebalancing), split `load_weights` and `process_weights_after_loading` into two steps, only calling the latter on modules whose names match the filter. This prevents double-processing of attention layers and other non-expert modules. ## Accuracy Tests Validated with `test_mooncake_ep_small.py` (use DeepSeek-Coder-V2-Lite-Instruct-FP8): 7/7 tests passed. ![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7ed0ab46-5794-4cd1-a930-32e93a7ef841) ## Benchmarking and Profiling <!-- If this pull request impacts inference speed, provide benchmarking and profiling results. --> ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [ ] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review Process 1. signal.text: ## Motivation FlashInfer's `fused_topk_deepseek` only supports compute capability 89, 90, 100, 103, 120, 121, and does not support lower archs like sm_86.
