signal.title: [Scheduler] Add early finish check for overlap mode to prevent redundant decode
signal.text: ## Motivation Based on [#18165](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/18165), we find redundant decode in overlap mode, not only for requests with attribute max_tokens=1, but all requests due to overlap mechanism, which would not check results after forward immediately. Problem: In event_loop_overlap scheduling mode, when a request reaches its max_tokens limit, it cannot terminate early before the next batch starts. This causes redundant decode iterations because: 1. Batch N completes forward pass 2. Batch N+1 is prepared and started before batch N's results are processed 3. Requests that reached max_tokens in batch N are incorrectly included in batch N+1, wasting GPU compute ## Modifications Add environment variable SGLANG_ENABLE_OVERLAP_EARLY_FINISH_CHECK (default: false) to enable early termination check in get_next_batch_to_run(). When enabled: - Checks current output_ids length against max_new_tokens before batch preparation - Marks requests with to_finish flag if they've reached the limit - Filters them out to prevent inclusion in the next batch ## Accuracy Tests <!-- If this pull request affects model outputs (e.g., changes to the kernel or model forward code), provide accuracy test results. --> ## Benchmarking and Profiling <!-- If this pull request impacts inference speed, provide benchmarking and profiling results. --> ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review Process 1. signal.title: [Perf] O(1) expert weight matching in DeepSeek weight loader
signal.text: ## Motivation Large MoE models like GLM-5 with 256 routed experts generate hundreds of thousands of weight tensors. The original weight loading code used an O(N*M) algorithm (linear scan of 771+ mapping entries for each tensor), causing weight loading to take 25-40+ minutes on Blackwell GPUs. ## Modifications Replaced the O(N*M) linear scan with an O(1) dict lookup: 1. Pre-build a dict mapping projection names → (param_name, shard_id) from expert_params_mapping 2. Use regex to extract expert_id and projection name from weight names 3. Perform single dict lookup instead of scanning all 771 entries per tensor 4. Added comprehensive unit tests validating against real HuggingFace model weight maps ## Benchmarking and Profiling Measured on nvidia/DeepSeek-R1-NVFP4 (256 experts, 180,364 weight tensors): | Metric | Before | After | Speedup | |--------|--------|-------|---------| | **Total matching time** | 6.67s | 0.13s | **50x** | | **Per-tensor latency** | 36.9 μs | 0.7 μs | **50x** | | **String comparisons** | ~179M | 0 | — | ## Accuracy Tests All 10 unit tests pass, verifying bit-for-bit identical matching results on all three test models (DeepSeek-V3.2, DeepSeek-V3, DeepSeek-R1-NVFP4). No changes to model behavior—pure optimization. ## Checklist - [x] Code follows SGLang style guidelines - [x] Unit tests added and passing (3 correctness tests + 7 threshold tests) - [x] Performance benchmarked against real model weight maps

signal.title: [dLLM] Cut per-step host overhead in the dLLM extend path
signal.text: ## Motivation dLLM inference disables the overlap scheduler (each denoise step has a hard input dependency on the previous step's result), so every bit of host time between steps is exposed directly as device idle. Profiling LLaDA2 at bs=128 on Ascend 910B3 showed three host-side costs on the per-step path, none of which needed to be there: 1. `AscendAttnBackend.init_forward_metadata` took two D2H syncs to obtain values the scheduler already holds on the host (`seq_lens_max`, `extend_seq_lens_cpu_int`). 2. `NPUGraphRunner` re-read `forward_batch.seq_lens.cpu()` before every replay, a blocking D2H behind whatever is queued on the stream, while the same host mirror was already available. 3. `_alloc_extend_loc_with_kv_reuse` (the dLLM FDFO retained-KV path) re-read each reuse row's retained block with its own slice + cast kernel, and pulled every scheduling scalar out of CPU tensors one element at a time. Both costs grow linearly with batch size. ## Modifications **`hardware_backend/npu/attention/ascend_backend.py`** — take `seq_lens_max` from `seq_lens_cpu` and build `extend_seq_lens_cpu_int` from `extend_seq_lens_cpu`. Gated on `forward_mode.is_dllm_extend()`, so the decode/prefill path is byte-identical. **`hardware_backend/npu/graph_runner/npu_graph_runner.py`** — use `forward_batch.seq_lens_cpu` when present, falling back to `.cpu()` when it is not. This one is **not** dLLM-gated and affects every non-DeepSeek-DSA/V4 model on this path, so it is worth stating why it is equivalent: `seq_lens_cpu` is already the authoritative host mirror here — the Ascend attention backend derives its own `seq_lens_cpu_int` from it for every forward mode, and likewise adds the draft width on target-verify. Reading the device tensor in the graph runner made the two components disagree on their source for the same forward; this aligns them. The `is_target_verify()` adjustment is unchanged, and the two former branches collapse into one because they now differ only by that addition. **`mem_cache/allocation.py`** — three changes inside `_alloc_extend_loc_with_kv_reuse`, which is reached only via `if batch.is_dllm()` in `alloc_for_extend`, so non-dLLM requests never enter it: - Add `_gather_reused_block_locs`: the retained blocks all share one length, so fetch them with a single flat index op instead of one slice + cast kernel per row. It replaces one kernel launch per row with a fixed index build + H2D, so it wins on wide batches and loses on narrow ones. The gate is the reuse-row count, re-evaluated every round, so a batch that shrinks falls back on its own — a small-batch latency deployment keeps the per-row path without configuring anything. The threshold defaults to the backend's measured break-even (8 on Ascend, where break-even is ~6) and is unset on backends where it has not been measured, so those keep today's behavior. `SGLANG_DLLM_BATCHED_GATHER_MIN_ROWS` overrides it: a row count to retune, or `-1` to disable the batched path outright for A/B and rollback. Rows of non-uniform block length keep the per-row path regardless. The resolved default is logged once at INFO. - Replace the per-element `int(cpu_tensor[i])` reads with one `.tolist()` per tensor. Unconditional: strictly less work at any batch size. At bs=128 the old code did roughly 770 of these, each allocating a temporary 0-dim tensor. - Hoist the `torch.tensor([-1], device=...)` filler out of the `last_loc` comprehension. Unconditional for the same reason. Every empty-prefix row was allocating its own identical device tensor; the list is consumed by `torch.cat`, which copies, so one shared tensor is equivalent. ### Configuration One new environment variable, `SGLANG_DLLM_BATCHED_GATHER_MIN_ROWS` (`EnvInt(None)` in `environ.py`), the minimum number of dLLM FDFO reuse rows at which the retained blocks are gathered in one flat index op. Nothing needs to be set for the intended behavior on either an Ascend or a non-Ascend deployment: | Value | Behavior | When to use | | --- | --- | --- | | unset (default) | Ascend: batch at 8+ reuse rows. Other backends: always per-row. | Normal serving, both latency and throughput. | | `N` (>= 0) | Batch at `N`+ reuse rows. | Enabling it on a backend after measuring its break-even, or retuning Ascend. | | `-1` | Never batch. | Production A/B and quick rollback. | ```bash # enable on a non-Ascend backend after measuring its break-even SGLANG_DLLM_BATCHED_GATHER_MIN_ROWS=8 python3 -m sglang.launch_server ... # roll back to the per-row path without redeploying SGLANG_DLLM_BATCHED_GATHER_MIN_ROWS=-1 python3 -m sglang.launch_server ... ``` The resolved default is logged once at INFO: ``` dLLM retained-block gather: batching enabled above 8 reuse rows (Ascend default). Override with SGLANG_DLLM_BATCHED_GATHER_MIN_ROWS. ``` ## Accuracy Tests No effect on model outputs — all three changes are host-side bookkeeping that produce the same values (the same slot indices, the same metadata) by different means. Verified with LLaDA2-mini on gsm8k (zero-shot, full 1319 samples): accuracy unchanged. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Measured on Ascend 910B3 at bs=128 (LLaDA2-mini, 32-token dLLM blocks), microbenchmarking each site against the code it replaces: | Site | Before | After | Saved | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | | Retained-block gather (128 reuse rows x 32) | 5671 us | 309 us | **5.4 ms** | | ~770 scheduling scalar reads | 3849 us | 54 us | **3.3 ms** | | `init_forward_metadata` (idle stream) | 251 us | 83 us | 168 us | | Graph replay `seq_lens` (idle stream) | 44 us | 6 us | 38 us | The gather is the dominant one and the only part that changes complexity: the per-row path costs about 44 us per reuse row (one kernel launch each) and scales linearly, while the batched path is roughly constant at about 270 us. That constant is why it is row-gated rather than unconditional — below the break-even the per-row path is genuinely faster: | reuse rows | per-row | batched | | | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- | | 1 | 120 us | 305 us | per-row path taken | | 4 | 196 us | 269 us | per-row path taken | | 6 | 279 us | 271 us | break-even | | 8 | 362 us | 268 us | Ascend default threshold | | 32 | 1449 us | 277 us | | | 64 | 2762 us | 268 us | | | 128 | 5671 us | 309 us | | | 256 | 11466 us | 353 us | | The `last_loc` hoist is not in the table because its benefit depends on how many requests have an empty prefix: each such row was allocating a device tensor at about 70 us, so it saves that times the number of empty-prefix rows in the batch (up to 8.9 ms at bs=128 when every row is fresh, and nothing when every row has a cached prefix). On Ascend at bs=128 this removes about 8.7 ms per step out of the box, against a step time of about 98 ms. On a backend where the gather threshold is unset it removes about 3.5 ms (the scalar reads plus the two D2H syncs); the gather itself is one env var away once its break-even has been measured there. ## Unit Tests `test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_dllm_reused_block_gather.py` (CPU-only, no server) pins the flat index arithmetic in `_gather_reused_block_locs` against per-row slicing. Each case covers a way the gather can be heterogeneous across rows, which is where a "looks equivalent" rewrite goes wrong: distinct per-row start offsets, unsorted pool indices, and a block ending exactly at the row boundary. Changing `row * width` to `row * block_len` in the implementation fails all three. These are deliberately not a re-test of the happy path. `test_dllm_fdfo_kv_reuse.py` covers that already in principle, but its reuse rows all share one prefix length and ascending pool indices, so an implementation that broadcast row 0's offset across every row would still pass it. (It is also module-level skipped today, and its fixtures no longer match `alloc_for_extend` — un-skipping it raises `SimpleNamespace has no attribute out_cache_loc_dsv4` — so it is not currently guarding anything either way.) The two D2H changes have no new tests: they need an NPU, and their equivalence is structural (`seq_lens_cpu` is the mirror of `seq_lens`, which the same backend already relies on). ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. signal.title: fix: avoid shutdown hang on warmup thread
signal.text: <!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. --> ## Motivation When `uvicorn` fails to bind (e.g., the port is already in use), the HTTP server process hangs for around 120 seconds before exiting. The reason is: 1. The warmup thread keeps polling `/model_info` and may run for up to 120s. 2. In the FastAPI lifespan handler, the `finally` block calls `warmup_thread.join()`, which blocks indefinitely while waiting for the thread. 3. After `uvicorn.run()` returns, Python’s internal `threading._shutdown()` also waits for non-daemon threads, causing another blocking point. As a result, the process appears stuck instead of exiting promptly. ## Modifications - Set `daemon=True` when creating the warmup thread so interpreter shutdown does not wait for it. - Change the explicit join in lifespan to use a timeout: `warmup_thread.join(timeout=5.0)` This prevents indefinite blocking during shutdown and allows the process to exit quickly if startup fails. ## Notes - `grpc_server.py` already contains similar explicit cleanup logic. - This change only affects shutdown behavior when the server fails to start. - Normal warmup and serving flow are unchanged. ## Checklist - [ ] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [ ] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review Process 1. signal.title: feat: Add proportion-based scheduler for router selection
signal.text: <!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. --> ## Motivation In real-world production environments, LLM inference workloads are rarely uniform. They typically consist of a mix of requests with varying prompt lengths. Sgl-router offers two highly effective yet specialized router, each with distinct performance characteristics: * Regular router: It can achieve very high QPS for chat-like workloads. * PD router: The prefill and decode stages are handled by separate, specialized workers. This architecture is exceptionally efficient for long-prompt requests. This hybrid scheduling approach delivers significant performance and efficiency gains, primarily by: * Maximizing QPS: By routing short-prompt requests to regular router and long-prompt requests to PD router, the system prevents either workload type from creating a bottleneck. This specialization allows each part of the cluster to operate at its peak efficiency, dramatically increasing the total QPS the system can handle for mixed workloads. * Reducing TTFT and Preventing Head-of-Line Blocking: Long-prompt requests are a primary cause of high latency, not just for themselves, but for all other requests due to head-of-line blocking in a standard worker queue. * Isolate Heavyweight Tasks: We prevent long prefill computations from blocking the processing of short, interactive queries. * Accelerate Long Prompts: We leverage the PD cluster's specialized design to reduce the TTFT for these complex requests. ## Modifications ### Proportion Scheduler #### Crossover Point Adjustment Goal: Find a single crossover point T_c (a token count) that splits the total token load of recent requests proportionally between Regular and PD worker pools, based on their respective capacities. Algorithm Steps (runs every adjust_interval) 1. Calculate Ideal Share: Determine the ideal load share S_ideal for the Regular pool using the current worker counts and weights. * S_ideal = (N_reg * W_reg) / ( (N_reg * W_reg) + N_pd ) * N_reg: Number of active Regular workers. * N_pd: Number of active PD workers. * W_reg: The configured regular_worker_weight. 2. Analyze Recent Load: Collect all token counts T_i from the current request history queue. Calculate the total load in this window, L_total = Σ T_i. 3. Determine Crossover T_c: * Sort the collected token counts in ascending order to get T_sorted. * Linearly scan T_sorted, accumulating load: L_accum += T_i. * When the running sum L_accum first meets or exceeds the target proportional load (L_accum / L_total ≥ S_ideal), set T_c to the current token count T_i and stop. Complexity: O(M log M) due to sorting the M requests in the time window. #### Routing Scheduler (per request) 1. Load-Imbalance Guard: First, check if the normalized load on one router type significantly exceeds the other (beyond configured balance_abs_threshold and balance_rel_threshold). If so, immediately route the request to the less-loaded pool, bypassing the crossover logic. 2. Crossover Logic: If the system is balanced, compare the incoming request's token count T with the current crossover point T_c. * If T ≤ T_c, route to the Regular pool. * If T > T_c, route to the PD pool. Complexity: O(1). ### Modify Bucket Policy The existing BucketPolicy was designed exclusively for Prefill/Decode (PD) disaggregated deployments. This PR extends its functionality to support Regular (non-disaggregated) workers, enabling bucket-based routing in a wider range of deployment scenarios. Step | Description -- | -- 1.1 Worker Detection | A new step is added during the server's initialization phase to detect if the default routing policy is bucket. 1.2 Grouping | If the bucket policy is active, the system now retrieves all active Regular workers from the WorkerRegistry. These workers are then grouped by their model_id. 1.3 Initialization | For each model group, the BucketPolicy now calls a new method, init_regular_worker_urls. This method initializes or updates the corresponding model's bucket with the URLs of the Regular workers, just as it previously did for Prefill workers. 2. Unified Bucket Logic The internal logic of the Bucket struct (including threshold adjustment and worker selection) is reused for both Regular and PD worker pools. The key change is in the initialization path: the policy can now be populated with worker URLs from either Prefill workers (in a PD setup) or Regular workers (in a regular setup). 3. Routing Decision (Impact) When a request arrives and the bucket policy is active for a Regular router, it now correctly locates the appropriate bucket for the request's model. It then uses the established bucket thresholds to select a Regular worker from that bucket's pool, applying the same load-balancing and imbalance-guarding logic that was previously only available for Prefill workers. ## Benchmarking and Profiling ### Test Command: 1. regular & pd worker ``` python -m sglang.launch_server \ --model-path /workspace/model \ --served-model-name Qwen3 \ --tp 1 \ --trust-remote-code \ --host 0.0.0.0 \ --port 9001 \ --mem-fraction-static 0.70 \ --attention-backend fa3 \ --page-size 64 \ --max-running-requests 48 \ --cuda-graph-max-bs 16 \ --chunked-prefill-size 2048 \ --disable-radix-cache \ --dtype auto \ --kv-cache-dtype auto \ --context-length 32768 \ --log-level info \ --disable-cuda-graph \ --enable-metrics python -m sglang.launch_server \ --model-path /workspace/model \ --served-model-name Qwen3/32B \ --tp 1 \ --trust-remote-code \ --disaggregation-mode prefill \ --disaggregation-bootstrap-port 30001 \ --host 0.0.0.0 \ --port 9002 \ --mem-fraction-static 0.70 \ --attention-backend fa3 \ --page-size 64 \ --max-running-requests 48 \ --cuda-graph-max-bs 48 \ --chunked-prefill-size 2048 \ --disable-radix-cache \ --dtype auto \ --kv-cache-dtype auto \ --context-length 32768 \ --log-level debug \ --enable-cache-report \ --enable-metrics python -m sglang.launch_server \ --model-path /workspace/model \ --served-model-name Qwen3/32B \ --trust-remote-code \ --disaggregation-mode decode \ --host 0.0.0.0 \ --port 9003 \ --mem-fraction-static 0.70 \ --tp 1 \ --max-running-requests 48 \ --chunked-prefill-size 2048 \ --attention-backend fa3 \ --page-size 64 \ --cuda-graph-max-bs 48 \ --disable-radix-cache \ --dtype auto \ --kv-cache-dtype auto \ --context-length 32768 \ --log-level debug \ --enable-cache-report \ --enable-metrics ``` 2. 2p4d(pd-disaggregation) ``` python3 -m sglang_router.launch_router \ --pd-disaggregation \ --prefill http://33.181.225.19:9001 30001 \ --prefill http://33.181.225.19:9002 30002 \ --decode http://33.184.122.82:9001 \ --decode http://33.184.122.82:9002 \ --decode http://33.184.122.82:9003 \ --decode http://33.184.122.82:9004 \ --policy random ``` 3. 1r2p3d(enable-igw) ``` python3 -m sglang_router.launch_router \ --enable-igw \ --scheduler-strategy proportion \ --scheduler-balance-abs-threshold 2000 \ --scheduler-balance-rel-threshold 1.0001 \ --scheduler-regular-worker-weight 0.4 \ --scheduler-adjust-interval-secs 1 \ --scheduler-adjust-window-sec 5 \ --policy bucket \ --balance-rel-threshold 1.0001 \ --balance-abs-threshold 3200 \ --bucket-adjust-interval-secs 1 ``` 3. benchmark ``` export HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 python3 -m sglang.bench_serving \ --backend sglang-oai \ --base-url "http://127.0.0.1:30000" \ --model "Qwen3/32B" \ --tokenizer "/workspace/Qwen3-32B" \ --max-concurrency 150 \ --request-rate inf \ --dataset-name random-ids \ --random-input-len 4096 \ --random-output-len 1536 \ --num-prompts 500 \ --random-range-ratio 0.1 \ --output-file "test_dynamoic.json" ``` ### conclusion To better evaluate the performance of the PDR hybrid strategy, I conducted two sets of experiments using 12 H20 GPUs. The control group had a PD ratio of 2:4, which is the best PD separation ratio given a constant total number of GPUs. The experimental group had a PDR ratio of 2:3:1, which is also the best configuration. Here we set a service level SLO, with P50 TTFT at 3000ms and TTOT P99 at 100ms. Then we continuously increase the concurrency to obtain the maximum performance of the two sets of experiments. Metric Category | Metric | Scenario A (150 Concurrency) | Scenario B (180 Concurrency) | Change -- | -- | -- | -- | -- QPS & Throughput | Request Throughput (QPS) | 3.43 req/s | 3.70 req/s | +7.87% | Output Token Throughput | 2869.49 tok/s | 3098.12 tok/s | +7.97% | Total Token Throughput | 10646.16 tok/s | 11497.41 tok/s | +7.80% Time to First Token | Mean TTFT | 6536.12 ms | 6021.32 ms | -7.88% | Median (P50) TTFT | 2723.44 ms | 2221.30 ms | -18.44% | P99 TTFT (Tail Latency) | 30204.30 ms | 28186.24 ms | -6.68% 1. Throughput and QPS: Request Throughput (QPS) saw a substantial 7.87% increase, rising from 3.43 to 3.70 req/s. Output Token Throughput grew by 7.97%, from 2869 tok/s to 3098.12 tok/s. This indicates a clear enhancement in the system's overall processing capacity and efficiency. 2. Time to First Token (TTFT): The user-perceived initial response time improved, with Mean TTFT decreasing by 7.88%. Median TTFT decreasing by 18.44% and P99 TTFT decreasing by 6.68%, optimize overall long-tail latency. In summary, the changes successfully boosted the system's throughput while simultaneously improving the average and tail-end latencies for Time to First Token, showcasing a more robust and higher-capacity serving performance. ## Checklist - [ ] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [ ] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review Process 1. signal.title: docker: pin matplotlib>=3.8 to fix CUDA-13 Python 3.12 build
signal.text: ## Problem On the CUDA-13 image (`nvidia/cuda:13.0.3-...-ubuntu24.04`, Python 3.12) the `framework` stage fails at the "Install essential Python packages" step: ``` File "/tmp/pip-install-.../matplotlib_.../versioneer.py", line 401, in get_config_from_root parser = configparser.SafeConfigParser() AttributeError: module 'configparser' has no attribute 'SafeConfigParser' ERROR: Failed to build 'matplotlib' when getting requirements to build wheel ``` ## Root cause That step installs dev/plotting tools with `-c /sgl-workspace/constraints.txt`, where the runtime packages are pinned but `matplotlib` is not. Under the fully-pinned constraints, pip backtracks `matplotlib` through every release trying to satisfy the solve, descending past the cp312-wheel versions into **pre-3.8 releases that ship no Python 3.12 wheels**. pip then builds those from sdist, and their bundled `versioneer.py` calls `configparser.SafeConfigParser()` — removed in Python 3.12 — so the build dies. (Observed pip walking 3.11.1 → ... → 3.4.3 before failing.) ## Fix Pin `matplotlib>=3.8`. matplotlib 3.8 is the first release providing Python 3.12 (cp312) wheels, so pip stays on wheels and never falls back to the unbuildable legacy sdists. This mirrors the existing style in the same install list (e.g. `"runai-model-streamer[...]>=0.15.7"`). ## Testing Full CUDA-13 image build (`BUILD_TYPE=all CUDA_VERSION=13.0.3`) completes past the framework stage with this change. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #32404767651](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32404767651)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32404767507](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32404767507)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:heavy_minus_sign: **No AMD PR run found for this commit**.<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [NPU] Fix ModelSlim NEXTN startup: unquantized MoE fallback and UB-aware mamba scatter
signal.text: close Issue #34211 ## Motivation Fixes startup failure when serving ModelSlim-quantized Qwen3.5 NEXTN checkpoints on NPU, where the MTP (draft) module is stored unquantized (all `mtp.*` entries in `quant_model_description.json` are `FLOAT`) while the main model is `W8A8_DYNAMIC`. Additionally fixes a runtime crash on the first inference request due to Ascend UB overflow in the mamba state scatter kernel. ## Modifications **1. ModelSlim MoE unquantized fallback (`modelslim.py`)** - `get_quant_method`: Use `is_layer_skipped` before `get_moe_scheme` and return `None` only when every expert projection is explicitly marked `FLOAT` - Preserve `get_moe_scheme` validation and `ValueError` handling for missing, mixed, or unsupported schemes **2. MTP whole-model unquant detection (`qwen3_5_mtp.py`)** - Add ModelSlim branch to `_mtp_quant_config` helper that detects when all `mtp.*` entries are `FLOAT` and drops `quant_config` entirely - This ensures the bf16 MoE dispatch overrides in `forward()` (`SGLANG_DEEPEP_BF16_DISPATCH`, `DEEP_NORMAL_MODE_USE_INT8_QUANT`) are triggered **3. UB-aware mamba scatter (`ascend_hybrid_linear_attn_backend.py`)** - Compute `h_block_size` dynamically from Ascend UB budget (192KB) instead of hardcoding `h_block_size=2` - For this model (V=128, K=128, fp32), the tile is 128KB single-buffered but Bisheng multi-buffer pass doubles it to 256KB, exceeding 192KB UB - The computed `h_block_size=1` brings the tile to 64KB single / 128KB double, fitting within budget - Add warning when a single (V,K) plane already overflows UB ## Accuracy Tests **Before:** - Startup fails with `ValueError: Unsupported ModelSlim MoE schemes for layer mtp.layers.0.mlp.experts: W13='FLOAT', W2='FLOAT'` - After workaround with `--speculative-draft-model-quantization unquant`, first request crashes with `error: ub overflow, requires 2097152 bits while 1572864 bits available!` **After:** - Startup succeeds with original command line (no extra flags needed) - MTP loads in bf16 (3.90 GB as expected) - First request completes successfully - Unit-tested `move_intermediate_cache` with `h_block_size=1`: numerically exact vs reference (max abs diff = 0.0) **Known limitation:** Speculative decoding output quality degrades (garbled/repeated text) compared to no-spec baseline on this checkpoint. This is a separate pre-existing issue in the NPU verify/state-commit path, not caused by these fixes. The corruption persists across graph/radix toggles and draft depths, pointing to the SSM state scatter indexing or conv-state management. Baseline (no spec) output is correct. ## Speed Tests and Profiling ```bash python3 -m sglang.benchmark.serving \ --backend sglang \ --base-url http://127.0.0.1:8898 \ --model /workspace/user_data/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-w8a8 \ --served-model-name Qwen3.6-35B-A3B \ --dataset-name random-ids \ --num-prompts 100 \ --random-input-len 1024 \ --random-output-len 100 \ --random-range-ratio 1.0 \ --request-rate inf \ --max-concurrency <1|5|10> \ --tokenize-prompt \ --output-file /tmp/bench_conc_<N>.jsonl \ --disable-tqdm ``` ### Metrics | Metric | Concurrency 1 | Concurrency 5 | Concurrency 10 | |---|---|---|---| | Benchmark Duration (s) | 181.1 | 87.2 | 56.0 | | Successful Requests | 100 | 100 | 100 | | Request Throughput (req/s) | 0.55 | 1.15 | 1.78 | | Input Throughput (tok/s) | 565.4 | 1174.5 | 1827.2 | | **Output Throughput (tok/s)** | **55.2** | **114.7** | **178.4** | | Total Throughput (tok/s) | 620.6 | 1289.2 | 2005.7 | | Mean E2E Latency (ms) | 1810 | 4339 | 5419 | | Mean TTFT (ms) | 324 | 1634 | 1288 | | Mean TPOT (ms/tok) | 15.0 | 27.3 | 41.7 | ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the Format code with pre-commit - [x] Add unit tests - [x] Update documentation - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results - [x] Follow the SGLang code style guidance <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32436301371](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32436301371)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32436301021](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32436301021)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32436301332](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32436301332)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. --> ## Motivation As per the title. Add INT4 dense linear support for AWQ/GPTQ quantized models on Intel XPU, enabling INT4 inference on this backend. ## Modifications - New `python/sglang/srt/hardware_backend/xpu/quantization/: int4pack_utils.py, awq_kernels.py, gptq_kernels.py` — INT4 checkpoint conversion and native XPU packed-MM helpers. - Wire up scheme routing in `awq/awq.py, awq/schemes/awq_linear.py, gptq/gptq.py, gptq/schemes/gptq_linear.py, and layers/quantization/__init__.py` to dispatch dense INT4 linear to the XPU kernels. - Add unit tests: `test/registered/xpu/test_xpu_int4_dense.py`. ## Accuracy Tests Model: `hugging-quants/Meta-Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct-AWQ-INT4` / `hugging-quants/Meta-Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct-GPTQ-INT4` GSM8K: AWQ `~0.78`; GPTQ `~0.785`. ## Limitations GPTQ + TP>1 is only rejected when a row-parallel shard actually splits a quantization group — i.e. when `act_order` (`desc_act=true`) has permuted `g_idx` so the local channels no longer sort into whole `group_size` blocks. signal.title: [Feature] Coordinate FullCG prefill across DP-attention ranks
signal.text: ## Motivation DP-attention ranks share communication collectives during prefill, so they must agree on both CUDA-graph admission and the captured shape. signal.title: [NPU] Enable LLaDA2.2 block routing and graph-captured JTI on Ascend
signal.text: ## Summary This PR adds self-contained LLaDA2.2-flash support for block-routing MoE and JointThresholdInDel (JTI) on Ascend NPU. Model-forward graph capture continues to use SGLang's existing NPU dLLM graph path; this PR adds graph capture only for the fixed-width JTI token-update step. It incorporates only the block-routing contract needed from #31768 and the JTI semantics needed from #31773. Those PRs are implementation references, not merge dependencies; this branch remains buildable on `main`. ## Scope and boundaries Model- and algorithm-specific code stays under LLaDA2/JTI: - `python/sglang/kernels/ops/llada2/block_topk_npu.py`: Ascend block routing. - `python/sglang/kernels/ops/llada2/indel_npu.py`: edit-token reductions. - `python/sglang/srt/dllm/algorithm/joint_threshold_indel.py`: fixed-shape eager and NPU-graph JTI. - `python/sglang/srt/models/llada2.py`: selects block routing only for checkpoints that declare `expert_capacity`; the LLaDA2.1 path is unchanged. There are no changes to shared model-executor, prefill-runner, NPU attention, or NPU graph-backend code. Both dLLM prefill and iterative decode already use `ForwardMode.DLLM_EXTEND`, which is captured by the existing `NPUGraphRunner`. ## Block-routing behavior The NPU block-routing path follows this contract: 1. select `expert_capacity` experts from the maximum corrected score in each token block; 2. select each token's ordered top-k within that compact capacity; 3. use unbiased sigmoid scores for the returned weights; 4. resolve exact ties by lower expert ID without perturbing close but unequal scores; 5. normalize in FP32 when `top_k > 1`; preserve the raw sigmoid score for `top_k == 1`. The implementation keeps the CANN top-k fast path and folds `routed_scaling_factor` into `topk_weights`, matching the existing NPU MoE contract. ## JointThresholdInDel The JTI implementation preserves the required termination and accuracy semantics: - the prompt is the immutable contiguous prefix before the first MASK; - an original MASK predicted as MASK uses the best non-MASK fallback; - DELETE/SPLIT move original-mask tracking through compaction; - regular and post-edit budgets force a final scrub that excludes MASK, DELETE, and SPLIT; - a cleanup that changes token IDs gets one final forward to persist KV state; - graph and non-graph paths use fixed-shape state and are covered for parity. `enable_graph` applies only to the fixed-width JTI token-update step and is NPU-only. Model-forward graph capture remains on the existing `NPUGraphRunner`. FDFO keeps the non-graph fixed-shape path because its batch composition changes between rounds. ## Hardware results Ascend 910B3 (4 dies), BF16, TP4, `max_running_requests=1`, block size 32, native top-8 routing, NPU-graph JTI update auto-enabled, `HCCL_DETERMINISTIC=true`. Serving: ```bash python3 -m sglang.launch_server \ --model-path inclusionAI/LLaDA2.2-flash --trust-remote-code \ --device npu --dtype bfloat16 --tp-size 4 --mem-fraction-static 0.92 \ --attention-backend ascend --sampling-backend ascend \ --disable-radix-cache --max-running-requests 1 --random-seed 1234 \ --dllm-algorithm JointThresholdInDel --dllm-algorithm-config jti.yaml --no-dllm-fdfo \ --host 127.0.0.1 --port 31119 ``` Accuracy, full GSM8K: ```bash python3 -m sglang.test.few_shot_gsm8k --num-questions 1319 --num-shots 5 \ --max-new-tokens 512 --parallel 128 --host http://127.0.0.1 --port 31119 ``` | Split | Requests | Accuracy | Invalid | Output throughput | Wall time | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | | Smoke (20) | 20 | 100.0% (20/20) | 0.000 | 41.802 tok/s | 80.26 s | | Full GSM8K (1319) | 1319 | 91.2% (1203/1319) | 0.001 (1/1319) | 43.516 tok/s | 71 min 54 s | This is the same invocation shape as the registered NPU CI test (`test/registered/npu/basic_function/runtime_opts/test_npu_tp4_bf16.py`): 5-shot, `--max-new-tokens 512 --parallel 128`. Server logs confirm the fused InDel reductions stayed active for the whole run (zero fallback-to-Torch events) and NPU-graph decode capture completed on all 4 ranks. Serving throughput: ```bash python3 -m sglang.bench_serving --backend sglang --host 127.0.0.1 --port 31119 \ --dataset-name random --random-input-len 1024 --random-output-len 512 \ --random-range-ratio 1.0 --num-prompts 64 --max-concurrency 1 ``` | Metric | Value | | --- | ---: | | Successful requests | 64 / 64 | | Benchmark duration | 397.33 s | | Output token throughput | 82.47 tok/s | | Peak output token throughput | 324.00 tok/s | | Mean TTFT | 1863.91 ms | | Median E2E latency | 4485.79 ms | | P99 E2E latency | 19756.74 ms | | Mean ITL | 8.97 ms | ## Configuration ```yaml threshold: 0.5 edit_threshold: 0 max_post_edit_steps: 8 ``` ```text --dllm-algorithm JointThresholdInDel --dllm-algorithm-config /path/to/jti.yaml ``` The NPU-graph JTI update turns itself on wherever its constraints hold (NPU device, fixed batch x block width, non-FDFO); `enable_graph: false` forces the eager path. The fused `argmax_softmax_prob` op from `sgl-kernel-npu` and the in-tree Triton scrub reduction are each imported behind a guard and used only when both are available, so an older kernel wheel degrades to the Torch path. No environment variable selects any of this. `delete_token_id` and `split_token_id` come from the checkpoint config when it declares them. The published LLaDA2.2-flash config does not, so SGLang falls back to the ids declared by that checkpoint's own `modeling_llada2_moe.py` (156930 / 156931) — the same table that already carries `mask_id` and `block_size` per architecture. `--json-model-override-args` is no longer required. ## Current-head validation - JTI graph/non-graph parity, termination, configuration, and LLaDA2 routing tests: **11 passed** on CPU. - Python compilation and `git diff --check`: passed; GitHub Lint is pending on this head. - Rebased cleanly on current `upstream/main`. - NPU kernel regression tests cover tail blocks, exact ties, close unequal scores, ordered top-k, `top_k == 1`, and final scrub behavior. Device CI awaits the protected `run-ci` / `run-ci-extra` labels. ## Known limitations - DeepEP block routing is rejected until its capacity-routing semantics are implemented. - JTI can require more forwards per output token than JointThreshold because DELETE/SPLIT may introduce masks and post-edit rounds. - Current NPU graph mode does not support FDFO state packing. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32435390748](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32435390748)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32435390628](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32435390628)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32435390708](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32435390708)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [EAGLE] Prune draft-extend logits to selected rows
signal.text: ## Motivation During EAGLE draft extension under CUDA graph execution, the model computes full-vocabulary logits for every draft row even though the speculative worker only consumes selected per-request rows. The unnecessary LM-head rows increase graph time and temporary memory usage on the decode critical path. ## Modifications - Select the rows consumed by the speculative verifier before applying the LM head during draft-extend CUDA graph execution. - Keep the full six-row draft forward unchanged so hidden-state and speculative-state evolution remain identical. - Preserve the eager path and existing output contract while sizing the graph logits buffer for the selected rows. ## Accuracy Tests | Natural-acceptance metric | Baseline | Candidate | | --- | ---: | ---: | | Completed requests | 112 / 112 | 112 / 112 | | Output length | 860 | 860 | | Mean acceptance length | 3.684250 | 3.652805 | | Acceptance rate | 0.536375 | 0.530488 | | CUDA graph enabled | Yes | Yes | | Queue / retractions / errors | 0 / 0 / 0 | 0 / 0 / 0 | ## Speed Tests and Profiling - Setup: Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-NVFP4 on one node with 4 GB300 GPUs, TP4/DP4/EP4 with DP attention, FP8 KV cache, TRTLLM-MHA, FlashInfer CuTeDSL MoE plus FlashInfer A2A for target and draft, NEXTN with 5 speculative steps and 6 draft tokens, online-NVFP4 draft weights, ReplaySSM circular history, Mamba `extra_buffer`, and CUDA graph tiers through batch 32. - Workload: one frozen 88,786-token input repeated as a 112-request cohort, 112 warmup requests with OSL 64, 112 measurement requests with exact OSL 860, temperature 0, fixed AL 4.8, and no request replenishment during the measured pure-generation interval. - Measurement gate: all four ranks must simultaneously report achieved batch 28, CUDA graph enabled, queue depth 0, and no completion/drain row inside the selected interval. | Serving metric | Baseline | Candidate | Delta | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | | Stable rank intervals | 17 / 17 / 17 / 17 | 17 / 17 / 17 / 16 | — | | Mean context tokens/rank | 103,367.5 | 102,725.7 | -0.6209% | | Target-step host time | 29.688688 ms | 28.996720 ms | -0.691968 ms / -2.3307% | | Fixed-AL4.8 output tokens/s/GPU | 4,526.977 | 4,635.007 | +2.3864% | - To remove the small context difference, an independent exact-context match paired 40 windows at the same mean context of 102,342.4 tokens/rank and measured 4,542.499 to 4,653.987 output tokens/s/GPU (+2.4543%). - The final zero-resident-context drain row is excluded from both arms. | Nsight metric for draft-extend graph `10658` | Baseline | Candidate | Delta | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | | Graph time/GPU-step | 1.113471 ms | 0.974980 ms | -0.138491 ms / -12.44% | | Selected-row projection | 0.371574 ms | 0.296726 ms | -0.074848 ms | | Large output copy | 0.098430 ms | 0.017771 ms | -0.080659 ms | | Graph capture memory | 0.15 GB | 0.07 GB | -0.08 GB / -53.3% | - The Nsight capture contains 40 actual-B28 steps on every rank with CUDA graph enabled and queue depth 0. - Draft-decode graph `10637` still performs four full-vocabulary projections per target step by design; this optimization only owns draft-extend graph `10658`. - `Output tokens/s/GPU` is an engine-side pure-generation metric derived from the fixed-B28 target-step window, not a service-level AIPerf total-throughput metric. - As a cross-engine diagnostic only, applying the measured within-SGL gain to the fixed-work authority gives 4,608.074 output tokens/s/GPU versus TRT-LLM at 4,791.788, or 96.166% with a 3.834% remaining gap; this does not replace a direct final integration comparison. ## Checklist - signal.title: [Bug] Qwen3-VL vision features diverge from Transformers/vLLM in v0.5.17 on fine-grained grounding
signal.text: ### Checklist - [x] I searched related issues but found no solution. - [x] The bug persists in the latest version. - [x] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback. - [x] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed. - [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed. ### Describe the bug ### Summary On the latest release, SGLang v0.5.17 (commit `29481685462732237d80d86076d6563e1f658102`), we observe a large accuracy discrepancy for fine-grained visual grounding with two Qwen3-VL-family checkpoints: `Tencent/UI-Mate-27B` and `Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B`. We replayed the same captured prompt contents and image bytes through SGLang, Hugging Face Transformers, and vLLM under greedy decoding (`temperature=0.0`, `top_p=1.0`). Only the engine changed. Transformers and vLLM agree closely, while SGLang produces systematically incorrect click coordinates. | Model | Engine | Dtype | Half-row hits | Median absolute y error / row pitch | |---|---|---:|---:|---:| | UI-Mate-27B | SGLang 0.5.17 | BF16 | 0/20 | 0.9748 | | UI-Mate-27B | Transformers | BF16 | 20/20 | 0.0636 | | UI-Mate-27B | vLLM (official-style TP2) | BF16 | 20/20 | 0.0649 | | Qwen3.8-27B | SGLang 0.5.17 | BF16 | 1/20 | 4.5964 | | Qwen3.8-27B | Transformers | BF16 | 20/20 | 0.0481 | | Qwen3.8-27B | vLLM | BF16 | 20/20 | 0.0559 | The criterion is whether the first click falls within half of one rendered row pitch. All arms use the same 20 fixed first-step inputs. This is intentionally a narrow fine-grained grounding test; we are not claiming that all Qwen3-VL tasks fail in SGLang. ### Evidence localizing the discrepancy For an aligned Qwen3.8 seed: - `input_ids` are identical between the Transformers replay and SGLang (same shape and hash). - `image_grid_thw` is identical: `[[1, 62, 100]]`. - The processor output shape is identical: `pixel_values=[6200, 1536]`, float32. - The default SGLang GPU processor differs slightly from the CPU processor (max absolute pixel delta `2/255`, mean absolute delta `1.56e-6`). Disabling the fast image processor remains 1/20, so this small preprocessing delta is not sufficient to explain the failure. - Text token embeddings before multimodal replacement are exactly equal elementwise in our probe. - Immediately after the vision merge, image-token relative L2 difference is approximately `0.0401`. - After the first GDN layer and the first full-attention layer, the relative L2 difference remains approximately `0.036`. This suggests the discrepancy is already present in the vision output and is then propagated by the language model. With an exact Transformers-generated prefix forced into both engines, both choose the same first action token and, after a prefix ending in `"y":`, the same leading coordinate digit with probability effectively 1. This argues against an action parser problem or a fixed coordinate-output-head bias. ### Controlled SGLang ablations (Qwen3.8 BF16, same 20 inputs) | Change from baseline | Half-row hits | Median error / row pitch | |---|---:|---:| | Baseline | 1/20 | 4.5964 | | Disable fast image processor | 1/20 | 4.5068 | | Disable prefill CUDA graph | 1/20 | 4.5516 | | Multimodal attention FA3 -> SDPA | 1/20 | 3.5061 | | Enable precise embedding interpolation | 1/20 | 4.5964 | | Compatibility-adapted v0.5.6.post2 `qwen3_vl.py` vision path | 0/20 | 4.5964 | ### Related issue This may be related to #19513, which reported incorrect Qwen3-VL vision output in older SGLang releases. However, we do not assume the same root cause: unlike that report, a compatibility-adapted v0.5.6.post2 vision-file rollback did **not** recover accuracy on our current v0.5.17 / Transformers 5.12 stack. We would appreciate guidance on the best supported way to compare the vision-encoder output against the Transformers reference, or on any known correctness flags/patches for this model family. ### Reproduction ### Minimal replay (Qwen3.8-27B, seed 8001) The attachment `qwen_seed8001_greedy_payload.json.txt` is a self-contained OpenAI chat-completions payload. It contains the exact prompt and the screenshot as a data URL. Compared with the captured benchmark request, only three fields were normalized: model ID → `Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B`, `temperature` → `0.0`, and `top_p` → `1.0`. The message contents and image bytes are unchanged. Start SGLang: ```bash python3 -m sglang.launch_server \ --model-path Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B \ --host 0.0.0.0 --port 30000 \ --tp-size 1 \ --dtype bfloat16 \ --trust-remote-code \ --context-length 131072 \ --chunked-prefill-size 4096 \ --reasoning-parser qwen3 ``` Download the attachment and replay it: ```python import json import requests payload = json.load(open("qwen_seed8001_greedy_payload.json.txt")) response = requests.post( "http://127.0.0.1:30000/v1/chat/completions", json=payload, timeout=600, ) response.raise_for_status() message = response.json()["choices"][0]["message"] print(message.get("reasoning_content")) print(message.get("content")) ``` Oracle row center for this screenshot: `y=277.1328125` in the declared 1000x1000 output space. Half-row acceptance interval: `[260.39453125, 293.87109375]`. Observed final actions under greedy decoding: ```text SGLang 0.5.17 BF16: {"type":"click","x":150,"y":125,"button":"left"} Transformers BF16: {"type":"click","x":150,"y":276,"button":"left"} vLLM BF16: {"type":"click","x":144,"y":275,"button":"left"} ``` Prompt-token counts are identical for this Qwen replay (2639). signal.title: [Fix] Pass Anthropic thinking history as reasoning_content for custom chat encoders
signal.text: ## Motivation Run Kimi-K3 with `--reasoning-parser kimi_k3 --tool-call-parser kimi_k3` and talk to it on `/v1/messages` with `thinking` on. Any agentic client sends assistant `thinking` blocks back in history — the Messages API requires it for tool-use turns — and a few turns in, raw XTML channel markers show up in visible assistant text: ``` turn 3 [text] '<|open|>think<|sep|<|sep|>Something is very strange. […]' turn 4 [text] '<|open|>think<|sep|' ``` Turns 1-2 are fine, then every turn after that is corrupted — it never recovers. Drop the `thinking` blocks from the replayed history and it never happens at all, so the problem is how prior reasoning gets fed back, not the reasoning parser. **Root cause.** K3 ships no Jinja chat template, so SGLang renders it through the checkpoint's own XTML encoder. That encoder frames the `think` / `response` / `tools` channels itself and wants prior reasoning in an assistant `reasoning_content` field. The Anthropic adapter never used it — instead it wrapped prior thinking in the reasoning detector's markers and spliced that into assistant **content**. Here is what the two forms actually render to, straight from the K3 tokenizer: ``` # before — think channel empty, reasoning nested inside the response channel <|open|>think<|sep|><|close|>think<|sep|><|open|>response<|sep|><|open|>think<|sep|>PRIOR <|close|>think<|sep|>Here is my answer.<|close|>response<|sep|> # after <|open|>think<|sep|>PRIOR<|close|>think<|sep|><|open|>response<|sep|>Here is my answer.<|close|>response<|sep|> ``` Every replayed turn taught the model the same lesson: think channel empty, think block sitting inside the response channel. Two turns of that and it starts writing `<|open|>think<|sep|>` as ordinary response text. None of this is K3-specific. All four Python chat encoders that bypass `apply_chat_template` frame their own reasoning channel and read `reasoning_content`, so the splice was wrong for every one of them. ## Modifications - **`entrypoints/openai/chat_encoding.py`** — adds `spec_owns_reasoning_history(spec)`, right under `resolve_chat_encoding_spec` so the contract sits with the specs it describes. It covers the whole custom-encoder family (`spec is not None`) rather than listing specs, so whoever adds the fifth one gets the safe default for free. An encoder that ignores the field drops history — what the splice path already does for models with no reasoning detector — instead of leaking. - **`entrypoints/openai/serving_chat.py`** — `supports_native_reasoning_history()`, a one-line delegate. - **`entrypoints/anthropic/serving.py`** — `_convert_assistant_thinking_blocks` now returns `(reasoning_content, text)`. Custom encoders get the history in the field, everyone else keeps the splice untouched. `redacted_thinking` still raises before the branch, and the best-effort drop for detector-less models survives. Nothing needed a schema change: `ChatCompletionMessageGenericParam` already declared `reasoning_content`, and messages are dumped without `exclude_none`, so it flows straight through. `wrap_reasoning_history` has exactly one production caller, so that is the whole mechanism. `dsv4`/`dsv32` also land on their official multi-turn contract now instead of bypassing it. Jinja-path models stay on the splice on purpose — their markers (`<think>`, `[THINK]`, `◁think▷`) really do live in the content stream, so it reproduces what the model emitted anyway. ## Test Plan ### Live server Same deployment before and after — `moonshotai/Kimi-K3` on 2x4 GB300, TP8, DSPARK spec-decode — same scripts, `temperature=0`: | run | main | with the fix | | --- | --- | --- | | 12-turn tool loop, streaming `/v1/messages` | leaks turns 3-12, all ten of them | clean, and the loop converges at turn 9 | | 8-turn tool loop, non-streaming | leaks turns 3-8 | clean | | 6 concurrent sessions x 5 turns | all six leak, every one first at turn 3 | none leak | | thinking dropped from replayed history | clean | clean | | `thinking: {"type": "disabled"}` | clean | clean | | reasoning passed as `reasoning_content` on `/v1/chat/completions` | clean | clean | | thinking-only history turn, and a turn with two thinking blocks | clean | clean | | `redacted_thinking` history | 400 | 400 | On main the onset is turn 3 every single time, and it never recovers — the `thinking` block stops appearing at all from there on and the markers move into `text`. That is also why the loop never converges: each turn re-reads its own corrupted history and re-diagnoses the same phantom problem. With the fix, `thinking` comes back on essentially every turn and the model finishes the task. Asked what it had just been thinking, the model quoted the injected reasoning back — the history really does land in the think channel rather than being quietly dropped. Prompt rendering was also diffed against the real K3 tokenizer for a thinking + text + tool_use turn. ### Unit tests `anthropic/test_serving.py` — 61/61. Two new cases: history reaches a channel-framing encoder as `reasoning_content` and never through the wrap path, and a thinking-only turn keeps its reasoning across the empty-content placeholder branch. Both go red against pre-fix code, and the existing wrap-path test still covers the default encoder. `openai/test_serving_chat.py` — 111/111. Two more: the real `OpenAIServingChat` predicate across all four specs plus `None`, and a guard that parses the literals `resolve_chat_encoding_spec` can return and checks them against the tuple the capability test iterates. Add an encoder without classifying it and CI fails. Mutation-checked, so it is not passing vacuously. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #32435140730](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32435140730)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32435140644](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32435140644)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #32435140704](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32435140704)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: fix: Allow remote-loaded instances to serve as TransferEngine weight seeds
signal.text: ## Motivation **Fix:** After syncing weights from another instance via the transfer engine, it cannot serve as a seed to provide weights for other instances. When an instance loads model weights from another SGLang instance through TransferEngine, its destination memory regions are registered before the transfer and `weight_info` is already populated. Previously, `RemoteInstanceWeightTransporter` registered and published weight metadata only when `weight_info` was `None`. As a result, a destination instance could receive weights successfully but would not publish its existing TransferEngine session and weight metadata, preventing it from serving as a seed for downstream instances. ## Modifications - Decouple TransferEngine memory registration from seed metadata publication. - Reuse existing `weight_info` when the destination buffers were registered by the remote-instance loader. - Register model memory only when `weight_info` is missing. - Publish registered weight metadata when the instance is configured to start a TransferEngine seed service. ## Accuracy Tests Not applicable. This change only affects weight-transfer metadata registration and publication. It does not modify model weights, kernels, or model forward logic. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Not applicable. This change does not affect the inference execution path.It also avoids unnecessary duplicate memory registration. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. signal.title: [VLM] Default to two multimodal preprocessing workers
signal.text: Stacked on #35342 (which routes every processor through the worker pool's call site). Review that one first; this PR is the one line that actually turns the pool on. ## Motivation Preprocessing an image costs real CPU time on the tokenizer's event loop, so with a single worker a model's request throughput is capped at `1 / preprocess_time` no matter how much GPU is idle. That cap is why PaddleOCR-VL saturated at 6.7 req/s on an H200 with GPU headroom to spare — and only four processors in tree had opted out of it. ## The benefit generalizes, because the mechanism does Image preprocessing is numpy / torch / PIL underneath, so it releases the GIL. Wall-clock speedup of 4 threads over 1 on the same work, 1080p input, `torch.set_num_threads(1)` so intraop parallelism cannot be mistaken for thread scaling: | image processor | 1 thread | 4 threads | speedup | `deepcopy` | |---|---|---|---|---| | Qwen2VL (fast / slow) | 24.3 / 24.1 ms | 7.1 / 7.0 ms | 3.41x / 3.45x | ok | | Idefics3 | 46.1 ms | 12.7 ms | 3.64x | ok | | Pixtral | 19.0 ms | 5.2 ms | 3.64x | ok | | Llama4 | 27.0 ms | 7.7 ms | 3.52x | ok | | GLM4V | 31.8 ms | 9.0 ms | 3.51x | ok | | PaddleOCR-VL | 28.4 ms | 8.7 ms | 3.27x | ok | | CLIP | 9.1 ms | 2.8 ms | 3.28x | ok | | Gemma3 | 5.7 ms | 1.9 ms | 2.94x | ok | | SigLIP | 5.5 ms | 2.1 ms | 2.69x | ok | | *pure-Python control* | *81.0 ms* | *80.5 ms* | *1.01x* | — | The control validates the probe. `copy.deepcopy` succeeded on all nine, and the executor already falls back to synchronous processing with a warning if cloning ever fails. ## Two workers, and not more Past two, spreading request arrivals fragments the GPU prefill batches faster than the extra overlap pays for itself — the tradeoff `qwen_vl`'s processor already documents. Swept at 32-way concurrency on an H200: | workload | 1 worker | 2 workers | 4 workers | |---|---|---|---| | PaddleOCR-VL 1080p pages, 128-token outputs | 6.72 | **9.55** | 8.92 req/s | | PaddleOCR-VL 360p pages, 512-token outputs | 22.38 | **25.20** | 25.06 req/s | | Qwen2.5-VL 360p images, 512-token outputs | 12.54 | **12.60** | 12.25 req/s | The middle row is the shape that was supposed to break this: light preprocessing, where overlap has little to win, and long outputs, where batch fragmentation has the most to cost. Two workers gained 13% there instead of regressing. Four workers is where the documented regression actually appears (bottom row, −2.3%). Greedy output is unaffected: two workers against one is byte-identical across five page geometries × two task prompts on PaddleOCR-VL. ## Limitation reviewers should weigh All of this is **Hopper**. The regression `qwen_vl` documents was observed on Blackwell, and no B200 was available to me (GB300 is arm64). A Blackwell check on the light-preprocessing / long-output shape would be worth having before this rides a release — that is the one measurement that could still overturn the default. ## Checklist - [x] Format the code and run lint locally - [x] Add a test pinning the default (`test_default_worker_count_stays_at_the_measured_optimum`), so raising it requires a fresh sweep - [x] Benchmark on real hardware, including the shape most likely to regress - [x] Verify greedy output is unchanged 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:no_entry_sign: [Run #32224837223](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32224837223)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32224837024](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32224837024)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32224837269](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32224837269)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [AMD] perf: fuse Kimi-K2.5 MLA projection, RoPE, and KV-cache write
signal.text: <!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. --> ## Motivation During Kimi-K2.5 MXFP4 graph decode on ROCm gfx95, the absorbed MLA key projection, rotary embedding, and KV-cache write are launched separately on the latency-critical path even though they share operands. Fusing these operations reduces decode launch overhead and improves long-context serving performance. ## Modifications - Fuse the absorbed MXFP4 `w_kc` projection, RoPE, and KV-cache write into one AITER grid using `fused_fp4_bmm_rope_cat_and_cache_mla`. - Add `SGLANG_ROCM_FUSE_MLA_PROJECTION_ROPE_CACHE`, enabled by default. - Restrict the fast path to ROCm gfx95/AITER graph decode with MXFP4 `w_kc`. - Validate the fused kernel's shape requirements before dispatch: - `kv_lora_rank` must be a power of two. - `qk_rope_head_dim` must be a power of two and at least 2. - `qk_nope_head_dim` must be a power of two between 32 and 256. - Retain the existing split path for unsupported configurations, including DSA, DCP, optimized LoRA execution, and active `kv_b_proj` LoRAs. - Carry the fusion decision from `forward_absorb_prepare` to `forward_absorb_core` through `RocmMlaProjectionFusionPlan`. - Add CPU unit coverage for backend, graph-decode, and kernel-shape gating. - Document the new environment variable. ## Accuracy Tests Hardware and model: - 4× AMD Instinct MI355X (`gfx950`) - Model: `Kimi-K2.5-MXFP4` - TP=4 - AITER prefill and decode attention - AITER MoE and all-reduce fusion - FP8 E4M3 KV cache - Full GSM8K test set: 1,319 questions, 8-shot, maximum 512 new tokens - Project accuracy threshold: 0.92 | Configuration | Accuracy | Invalid responses | Status | | --- | ---: | ---: | --- | | Fusion disabled | 0.925 | 0.000 | PASS | | Fusion enabled | 0.930 | 0.000 | PASS | The fused path preserved accuracy and remained above the existing 0.92 threshold. Focused unit tests: ```text 2 passed, 5 subtests passed ``` The tests cover the AITER graph-decode gate and reject unsupported non-power-of-two or out-of-range shapes. ## Speed Tests and Profiling The A/B benchmark follows the Kimi-K2.5 ROCm recipe. Configuration: - 4× AMD Instinct MI355X (`gfx950`) - Kimi-K2.5 MXFP4, TP=4 - AITER prefill/decode attention and MoE - AITER all-reduce fusion - FP8 E4M3 KV cache, page size 16 - Breakable prefill graph and full decode graph - Maximum concurrency: 4 - ISL: 8,192 - OSL: 1,024 - 20 measured requests after warmup - Identical seed and generated workload for both arms - The only A/B feature change was `SGLANG_ROCM_FUSE_MLA_PROJECTION_ROPE_CACHE=0/1` | Metric | Fusion disabled | Fusion enabled | Change | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | | Output throughput | 428.77 tok/s | 433.33 tok/s | +1.06% | | Total token throughput | 3,861.04 tok/s | 3,902.11 tok/s | +1.06% | | Median TPOT | 8.81 ms | 8.68 ms | -1.48% | | Median end-to-end latency | 8,455.36 ms | 8,328.59 ms | -1.50% | | Median TTFT | 246.43 ms | 247.99 ms | +0.63% | The fusion improves decode-sensitive throughput, TPOT, and end-to-end latency for the 8k/1k workload. The small TTFT variation is expected because this optimization targets graph decode rather than prefill. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. signal.title: [RFC] Sglang non-GPU process rust migration
signal.text: ### Checklist - [x] If this is not a feature request but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed. - [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed. **PR** - https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/29799 Refer Roadmap https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/22949 Release Roadmap https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/1Y71GY3DOzZwuAp2ytehW0rJ4uzOx276PMtgTORgD49c/edit?slide=id.g3e59bc0132c_0_0#slide=id.g3e59bc0132c_0_0 ### Motivation **Status**: Draft **Author**: @rainj-me **Created**: Apr 20 2026 **Version**: 0.1 # Rust Server Migration Plan **Status:** Draft · **Last updated:** 2026-06-18 · **Owner:** Rain Jiang Migration of the SGLang request front-half (everything from network ingress up to the point a tokenized request is handed to the GPU scheduler) from Python to a multi-threaded Rust implementation. --- ## 1. Goals & scope **Goal.** Replace the Python tokenizer/detokenizer managers and HTTP server with a single-process, thread-per-core Rust implementation that owns the request lifecycle up to scheduler submission. **In scope:** HTTP(S)/gRPC/WS/h2/h3 server, request FSM, tokenizer & detokenizer managers, multimodal encoder dispatch, control API (abort/flush/weight update etc.), large tensor zero-copy handoff to the scheduler, cross-dp-group dispatch. **Out of scope (this plan):** model kernels, attention backends, KV-cache internals, quantization. The Rust server keeps the existing Python scheduler and GPU worker framework; it does not reimplement them. **Non-goals:** behavioral changes to the public API. The Rust server must be a drop-in for the Python one — same endpoints, same request/response schemas, same streaming semantics — so it can ship behind a flag and be A/B'd against Python. --- ## 2. Architecture summary The design this phase implement (decided separately; recorded here for context): - **Two FSMs, one process.** An **ingress FSM** (per request, multi-threaded, thread-per-core) carrying a request from `Received` through validation and optional encode/tokenize to `Queued`; and an **egress FSM** handling streaming (`Streaming` self-loop → `Finalizing` → `Completed`). They are the two halves of one request's lifecycle, owned by the same core and meeting at the ring-buffer / scheduler boundary — no shared locks. - **Six thread groups:** (1) **api-server** on an async runtime — accepts connections, terminates protocols; (2) **tokenizer-manager** running the ingress/egress request FSMs, CPU-core-bound; (3) **encoder** (core-bound); (4) **tokenizer** (core-bound); (5) **detokenizer** (core-bound); and (6) the python **scheduler** group within main thread. Groups talk only via channels — no shared locks across group boundaries. - **Channels:** bounded **MPSC** TokenizerManager→Scheduler (`try_send` = backpressure), per-core **SPSC** returns; userspace rings carry the payload, no ZMQ involved. Crossing the Rust→Python boundary, request objects are serialized with **msgpack** so only immutable bytes transfer — keeping the GIL out of the hot path. Tensor data bypasses msgpack entirely and is shared through **pinned memory**, handed across as a handle rather than copied or serialized. - **Zero-copy:** for encoded multimodal data, Python pre-allocates the pinned buffer pool at startup and Rust writes into slots by index during the encode/tokenize phase. Channels move slot handles (plus small msgpack metadata), never tensor bytes; lifetime is the pool's slot-reuse policy — a slot returns to the free list only after both Python's read and any GPU DMA complete, not Rust's `Drop`. - **Cross-rank:** For DP attention, the first rank of each DP group runs the Rust server *without* the api-server; a single api-server then fans **control** messages to every DP group (duplicated, since control must reach all), while **generation** requests are **round-robined** across DP groups for load balancing. - **Streaming:** a single `Streaming` macro state self-loops per chunk; non-streaming is just a stream whose frames are accumulated and emitted in `Finalizing`. See the request-FSM and topology diagrams in the Appendix for detail. --- ## 3. Phase 1 — Rust server (tok/detok manager + HTTP server) **Target: 2026-07-17** Phase 1 delivers the Rust front-half running in front of the **existing Python scheduler + GPU worker**, inside one process via multi-threaded Rust ⇄ Python. ### 3.1 Work breakdown | | Item | Status | Depends on | Notes | | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | | 1 | Rust frontend \+ scheduler PoC | ✅ Done | — | PR [\#23360](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/23360) \[Closed\] | | 2 | Architecture design | ✅ Done | — | Pending final approval | | 3 | Pickle → msgpack migration | ✅ Done | — | PR [\#28688](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/28688) \[Merged\] Followup issue [\#29465](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/29465) | | 4 | Single-process framework: multi-threaded Rust \+ Python scheduler/GPU worker | ✅ Done | 3 | | | 5 | Tokenizer & detokenizer manager | ✅ Done | 4 | | | 6 | HTTP server: /generate \+ streaming | ✅ Done | 4, 5 | | | 7 | Encoder support | 🟡 WIP | 4, 5 | Work with dynamo team check whether this can export to dynamo crate. | | 8 | PD disaggregation | ✅Done | 4 | Large. Prefill/decode split — see risk note. | | 9 | DP attention \+ cross-node DP controller | ✅ Done | 4 | Large, cross-node. See risk note. | | 10 | Metrics / logging | 🟡 WIP | 4 | Logging Done, Metrics WIP | | 11 | Port existing HTTP APIs other than the listed APIs below | ⏳ Pending | 6 | Full endpoint parity for drop-in replacement. | | 12 | Unified multi-protocol lib (server \+ gateway) | ⏳ Pending | 6 | Shared http(s)/h2/h3/gRPC/WS layer reused by sglang-gateway. | | 13 | Code Refactor | 🟡 WIP | | | | 14 | AuthZ support | | | | | 15 | Parallel Sampling | | | | | 16 | Benchmark\_serving perf optimization | 🟡 WIP | | | | 17 | Embedding request | | | | | 18 | offline Engine API support | | | | | 19 | Other flags in the TokenizedGenerateReqInput | | | | | 20 | cache\_tokens | | | | | 21 | custom\_logit\_processor | | | | | 22 | preferred\_sampling\_params | | | | | 23 | Standalone API-Server for DP Attn | 🟡 WIP | | | | 24 | Anthorpic API support | | | | | 25 | SageMaker API support | | | | | 26 | Vertex AI API support | | | | | 27 | Ollama compatible API support | | | | | 28 | Weight update APIs | | | | | 29 | HiCache APIs | | | | ### 3.2 Sequencing & critical path Items are **not** independent. The dependency spine is: ``` #3 pickle→msgpack ──► #4 single-process framework ──► #5 tok/detok ──► #6 /generate+stream ──► #11 API parity └─► #10 metrics (parallel) └─► #7 encoder (parallel, after #5) ``` **Critical path to a usable July 17 milestone:** 3 → 4 → 5 → 6, with 10 landing in parallel and 11 close behind. That subset is what makes the Rust server a working, A/B-testable drop-in for text LLM traffic. **Recommend deferring out of the July 17 milestone** (track as Phase 1.5 / stretch): items **8 (PD disaggregation)** and **9 (DP attention + cross-node DP controller)**. Both are large, both can land after the core path is proven, and bundling them into the July date puts the whole milestone at risk. Item **12 (unified protocol lib)** is valuable but is a refactor that can follow once #6 stabilizes the protocol surface. > **Date reality check.** July 17 is ~4 weeks out and #4 (the foundation) is still > pending-start. The 3→4→5→6+7 path is achievable in that window if #4 starts > immediately and 8/9/12 are explicitly descoped. Carrying all 12 to July 17 is not > realistic; pick the milestone definition deliberately. ### 3.3 Phase 1 exit criteria - Rust server handles `/generate` (streaming + non-streaming) at parity with Python. - Tok/detok managers run in-process; detok is incremental and order-correct. - Encoder path works for at least one multimodal input type. - Metrics + logs at parity; runs behind a flag, A/B-able against Python. - Endpoint parity sufficient to route production text traffic. --- ## 4. Cross-cutting concerns **Rollout / fallback.** Every phase ships behind a flag with the Python path as the live fallback. Migrate by traffic slice (shadow → small % → ramp), not big-bang. keep the Python path runnable as the live fallback until the Rust path reaches parity. **Testing.** Differential testing against Python (same inputs → same tokens/frames) is the primary correctness gate. Add: FSM property tests (every state has a terminal exit; post-terminal events are no-ops/idempotent); streaming order + UTF-8-boundary tests for detok. **Observability.** Metrics/logging (P1 #10) should land *with* the core path, not after — debugging the channel/FSM/threading layers without it is painful. Per-state request counts, queue depths (ring-buffer occupancy = backpressure signal), per-core load, and control-op latencies. **Kernel / environment.** io_uring features used (`MSG_RING` 5.18+, `SEND_ZC` 6.0+, `DEFER_TASKRUN` 6.1+) set a minimum kernel; some hardened/container environments disable io_uring — keep an epoll+eventfd fallback behind the same loop abstraction. --- ## 5.
