signal.title: Fix buffer-mode HiCache load-back ownership races; add optional prefetch anchor lock
signal.text: # Fix buffer-mode HiCache load-back ownership races; add optional prefetch anchor lock ## Motivation In buffer-only host memory mode, `init_load_back` consumes a staged storage prefetch by allocating device slots, queueing a layer-gated H2D transfer, and then inserting the span into the radix tree. The insert is what adjudicates slot ownership — and it ran *after* the transfer was already in flight. If the tree gained an overlapping span while the fetch was held — a concurrent request publishing the same prefix between staging and consumption, or live full-KV sitting under an SWA tombstone (invisible to the unified match length but still deduped against by the insert walk) — the insert freed the very slots the in-flight copy targeted: a queued use-after-free. Reallocation of those slots produced silent KV corruption and downstream allocator faults. ## Changes 1. **Ownership pre-check (always on):** before launching the transfer, re-match against live tree state and require both the unified match length and `full_kv_hit_length` to equal the staged `matched_len`. This proves the insert can only add nodes, never dedup-free the incoming slots. Invalid holds drop with a warning and the request recomputes. 2. **Post-insert fail-stop:** if the post-insert canonical tree slice diverges from the incoming slots, raise instead of returning indices that a queued transfer no longer owns. 3. **Canonical ownership:** return the post-insert tree slice rather than the raw allocation. 4. **Optional anchor lock (env-gated, default off):** `SGLANG_ENABLE_HICACHE_BUFFER_ANCHOR_LOCK=1` pins the staged prefetch's device anchor from IO commit to consumption so eviction cannot invalidate the splice and waste the fetch. Locked tokens are capped at `SGLANG_HICACHE_BUFFER_ANCHOR_LOCK_CAP` × the device pool (default 0.5); over-cap holds launch unlocked, so queued holds can never make the pool unevictable. Locks are released idempotently at every consume/drop/abort exit, with a fail-loud accounting assert. ## Testing - Three regression tests covering the race class: sibling-published span (unified drift), full-KV overlap masked by an SWA tombstone (only `full_kv_hit_length` can see it), and the post-insert fail-stop. All three fail on the pre-fix code and pass with the fix. - Full `test_unified_radix_cache_unittest.py` passes. - Verified in an extended production-shaped soak on an internal deployment (buffer-only mode with a storage backend): the ownership checks drop conflicting holds cleanly under concurrent same-prefix traffic, the anchor lock eliminates eviction-caused prefetch waste in steady and moderate-churn regimes, and the lock accounting stayed exact across many engine restarts. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32434867464](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32434867464)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32434867293](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32434867293)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #32434867408](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32434867408)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: Publish per-scheduler load on a dedicated socket for load-aware routers
signal.text: ## Motivation The cache-aware-zmq router infers a worker's load from a router-side in-flight counter. That counter measures what *this router* dispatched — it misses traffic from other routers and direct clients, and for streaming responses it stays held for the whole response rather than the time the request occupies the scheduler. The engine already builds the right number: `SchedulerLoadInquirer.get_loads()` produces a `LoadSnapshot` every publish cycle (feeding `/v1/loads` and DP-attention dispatch). This exposes that snapshot to out-of-process consumers so a router can price workers on real queue depth / KV occupancy. Ported to `main` from a production branch; the router-side consumer lands separately. ## Modifications **A dedicated per-scheduler load PUB socket.** `SchedulerLoadPublisher` publishes a compact `LoadStat` gauge (`num_running_reqs`, `num_waiting_reqs`, `num_tokens`, `max_total_num_tokens`) on its own ZMQ PUB socket, independent of KV-cache events. The payload is a tagged subset of `LoadSnapshot` so the router-facing wire contract stays fixed as the internal snapshot grows. Framing matches the KV-event socket (`[b"load", big-endian i64 seq, msgpack LoadStat]`) so one subscriber loop handles both. Transport is a plain synchronous PUB socket — a send just enqueues to ZMQ's IO thread — so there is no background thread or replay buffer, which a gauge does not need. **One resolver for the port, shared by the bind and the advertisement.** `resolve_load_pub_range` decides where the load range lives and returns `((host, base), reason)`. Both `SchedulerLoadPublisher` (which binds `base + rank`) and `/server_info`'s `describe_kv_events_publisher` (which advertises `base` under the `kv_events` block, plus `load_topic`) route through it, so the engine cannot advertise a range it will not bind. With auto, the range packs immediately after the KV-event range, bumping past the replay ROUTER range when the two overlap (with the conventional `replay = kv + 1`, always). **Opt-in via `--load-publish-endpoint` (observability namespace).** **Off by default** — unset (or `off`) reserves no port, so an upgrade of an existing `--kv-events-config` deployment can't collide with a co-hosted neighbor's KV bind. `auto` packs the range after the KV-event range; an explicit wildcard-host `tcp://` address places it outright (a concrete host would be *connected to*, not bound). Also requires `--kv-events-config`, since routers discover the base through `/server_info`. **Cadence.** When enabled, publishing is throttled by call count, and an unchanged gauge is deduped to a ~1s heartbeat while a changed one goes out immediately (transitions are never delayed). When the DP-balancing sink also published this cycle, the scheduler hands its already-computed snapshot to the load publisher rather than walking the queues again. When disabled (the default), the publisher holds no socket or thread and each call is a bound method plus a `None` check. **Load also publishes on stalled no-batch iterations.** `on_idle` now publishes before its fully-idle gate — a stall (queues parked under KV pressure / disagg transfer) has no `process_batch_result` to publish the growing gauge. That path spins without sleeping, so a ~50ms wall-clock floor bounds the `get_loads()` refresh for both the DP-balancing writer and the load socket; the fully-idle publish stays at its original post-flush position so the idle gauge reflects compacted KV. **Failure handling is best-effort.** A publish failure never crashes the loop (routers fall back to their own counter) and is logged once per failure episode (the publish path runs every scheduler loop, so it must not flood). **Startup validation.** `--load-publish-endpoint` set without a `--kv-events-config` publisher, not bindable, or overlapping the KV range fails at the entrypoint (`check_load_publish_args`) rather than only warning from a scheduler subprocess. ## Notes for reviewers - **Breaking change to an override point** (per `large-class-init-style` rule 28): `Scheduler.publish_load_snapshot` now returns the `LoadSnapshot` it published (previously nothing); both call sites feed it to the router-facing publisher to avoid a second queue walk. A downstream override returning `None` stays functionally correct — the publisher falls back to `load_inquirer.get_loads` at its own throttled cadence — but silently loses the shared-snapshot optimization. Return the snapshot you wrote to keep it. - **Intentional user-visible change:** endpoint parsing is now strict (`NetworkAddress.parse`), so a bare unbracketed IPv6 kv endpoint (`tcp://::1:5557`) drops the whole `kv_events` block from `/server_info`, where the old `rfind(":")` split advertised it unusably. - **Port footprint (opt-in only):** with `--load-publish-endpoint auto`, a worker reserves `2 * dp_size` ports from its KV base (`2 * dp_size + 1` with the conventional adjacent replay). Co-hosted workers must space their KV bases at least that far apart, or place the range with an explicit address. This is why it's opt-in rather than default-on — see the server-arguments table. - **Inherited limit:** with DP-attention across `nnodes > 1`, the single advertised base is paired with one worker-URL host, so ranks on other nodes aren't reachable at that host — same constraint as the existing KV-event discovery, noted in the resolver docstring. ## Accuracy Tests Not applicable — no change to model execution or output. ## Speed Tests and Profiling No benchmark run. The disabled path (default) is a bound-method call plus a `None` check per batch — no socket, no thread. When enabled, the load socket reuses the DP-balancing snapshot whenever that sink also published this cycle (otherwise it collects its own on the same call throttle), and a stalled no-batch loop is bounded to one `get_loads()` per ~50ms for both sinks. ## Checklist - [ ] Format your code according to the [Format Code](https://docs.sglang.ai/references/contribution_guide.html) guide. - [ ] Add unit tests as outlined in the [Test Guide](https://docs.sglang.ai/references/contribution_guide.html). - [ ] Update documentation as needed. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:no_entry_sign: [Run #32274220697](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32274220697)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32274220217](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32274220217)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32274220246](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32274220246)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [AMD] Perf Kimi-K3 MoE optimization
signal.text: ## Motivation Kimi-K3 SiTUv2 MXFP4 MoE requires different preshuffled weight layouts for different activation quantization modes: - A16W4 and A8W4 use AITER's GU-interleaved `shuffle_weight_a16w4` layout. - A4W4 uses the generic separated layout. - When both A8W4 and A4W4 flags are set, AITER gives A8W4 precedence. Using the wrong layout causes catastrophic real-checkpoint output corruption. In a layer-1 A4W4/A8W4 comparison before the fix, cosine similarity was `0.0057` and relative L2 error was `1.148`; GSM8K dropped to `0.005`. The Kimi-K3 AITER path also repeated two per-layer materializations on every decode step: casting the routing correction bias and propagating a distinct FFI result tensor instead of the already-published MoE output buffer. ### AITER dependency This PR requires [ROCm/aiter#4534](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/4534) (`6dc26b7a817bba2ae92ff22a7a63c0c024f4c7e5`) or a newer AITER revision. That PR provides the optimized Kimi-K3 Opus/FlyDSL A8W4 SiTUv2 MoE dispatch used by the benchmarks below and depends on FlyDSL 0.3.0. The A4W4 SiTUv2 mode was introduced by [ROCm/aiter#4463](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/4463), which is already included in the required #4534 revision. ## Modifications - Make Kimi-K3 SiTU weight preprocessing follow AITER's activation-mode precedence. - Keep A16W4/A8W4 on the GU-interleaved preshuffle path. - Route A4W4 through the generic separated shuffle path. - Preserve A8W4 precedence when both AITER mode flags are enabled. - Cache the AITER routing correction-bias dtype conversion and invalidate it when the loaded parameter changes. - Return the explicit published SiTU MoE output buffer instead of a distinct FFI wrapper/allocation. - Add registered AMD/CPU/CUDA tests for layout precedence, correction-bias caching, reload invalidation, and the zero-copy output contract. ## Accuracy Tests Environment: 8x MI35x/gfx950, TP8, public Kimi-K3 checkpoint. - Focused layout/copy/cache unit tests: `11 passed`. - AITER strict K3 A4W4 oracle with SiTU beta `4.0` / linear beta `25.0`: all 17 K3 cases passed. - A4W4 GSM8K 50: `1.000`. - A4W4 GSM8K 200 after the fix: `0.980` (before fix: `0.005`). - A8W4 GSM8K 200: `0.980`. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Required AITER revision: `6dc26b7a8` from [ROCm/aiter#4534](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/4534). Server command: ```bash SGLANG_USE_AITER=1 \ SGLANG_AITER_K3_OPT=1 \ AITER_FLYDSL_FORCE=1 \ AITER_SITUV2_A8W4=1 \ AITER_SITUV2_A4W4=0 \ SGLANG_K3_FLYDSL_AR_NORM=1 \ sglang serve \ --model-path /data/models/Kimi-K3 \ --trust-remote-code \ --tp 8 \ --attention-backend triton \ --dtype bfloat16 \ --mem-fraction-static 0.85 \ --cuda-graph-max-bs-decode 256 \ --host 127.0.0.1 \ --port 8000 \ --disable-radix-cache \ --reasoning-parser kimi_k3 \ --tool-call-parser kimi_k3 ``` Client workload: - Random dataset, `random-range-ratio=1.0`. - Fixed input/output lengths: `8192 / 1024`. - `num-prompts = 8 * concurrency`. - `warmup-requests = 2 * concurrency`. Final results with the MoE copy optimization, compared with the original MI35x reference: | Concurrency | Total throughput (tok/s) | Delta | Per GPU (tok/s/GPU) | Median E2EL (ms) | Median TTFT (ms) | Median TPOT (ms) | Median ITL (ms) | |---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | 2 | 882.44 | +2.95% | 110.31 | 20887.60 | 852.91 | 19.58 | 19.39 | | 4 | 1594.32 | +4.75% | 199.29 | 23121.70 | 1609.19 | 21.04 | 20.67 | | 8 | 2527.54 | +1.18% | 315.94 | 29152.66 | 2552.72 | 25.97 | 24.53 | | 16 | 3893.59 | +2.06% | 486.70 | 37909.76 | 4785.77 | 32.39 | 28.88 | | 32 | 5381.41 | +2.68% | 672.68 | 54853.02 | 8985.35 | 44.81 | 37.19 | At concurrency 32 versus the original reference, total token throughput improves by `2.68%`, median E2EL by `2.55%`, TTFT by `3.57%`, TPOT by `2.54%`, and ITL by `2.29%`. The MoE copy change was also measured against the immediately preceding sweep with identical server/client settings: | Concurrency | Throughput delta | E2EL delta | TTFT delta | TPOT delta | ITL delta | |---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | 2 | +0.86% | -0.84% | -10.61% | -0.15% | -1.12% | | 4 | +1.57% | -1.17% | -0.46% | -1.17% | -1.15% | | 8 | +0.93% | -0.87% | -0.34% | -0.99% | -1.01% | | 16 | +0.64% | -0.65% | -0.10% | -0.74% | -0.79% | | 32 | +0.42% | -0.39% | -0.57% | -0.33% | -0.53% | Throughput improves by `0.42%–1.57%` and TPOT/ITL improve at every tested concurrency after adding the copy optimization. The C2 TTFT delta is based on a small 16-request sample and should be treated as higher variance. A4W4 is now numerically correct but is not the performance default for this workload: its median output throughput was `530.84 tok/s`, versus `537.33 tok/s` for post-fix A8W4. ## Checklist - [x] Format code with pre-commit (`pre-commit run --all-files` passes). - [x] Add registered unit tests. - [x] Documentation is not required; this does not add a user-facing interface. - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results. - [x] Follow the SGLang code style guidance. ## Review and Merge Process 1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process). 2. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so. - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci`. 4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:no_entry_sign: [Run #32319934749](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32319934749)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32319934659](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32319934659)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32319934688](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32319934688)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [PD] Fix reasoning token accounting for the handoff token
signal.text: ## Motivation Fixes #32897. In PD disaggregation, the prefill worker samples the first output token and the decode worker commits it to the request. The colocated prefill path updates reasoning-token accounting at the same point, but the PD handoff path previously only appended the token to `output_ids`. This undercounts reasoning usage by one for a normal handoff. If the handoff token is the think-end token, it can also leave the accounting state in the reasoning phase and count later answer tokens incorrectly. ## Modifications - Update reasoning-token accounting when decode commits a newly sampled PD handoff token. - Skip the update when true-retraction rebootstrap replays an already emitted boundary token, because its accounting state is retained and must not be counted twice. ## Accuracy Tests This change does not alter model outputs, sampling, or KV transfer behavior. It only updates usage metadata for the handoff token. Live PD validation passed: with the change applied, reasoning-token usage was correct for a response stopped by `max_tokens` during the reasoning phase. Validation performed: - `black --check python/sglang/srt/disaggregation/decode.py` - `ruff check --no-cache python/sglang/srt/disaggregation/decode.py` - Python syntax compilation of `decode.py` - `git diff --check` The existing decode-queue CPU test file could not be collected locally because Triton is unavailable in the CPU-only environment. No new test file is included in this minimal patch. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Not applicable. signal.title: Inference Support Mamba 2 and 1
signal.text: <!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. --> ## Motivation Add SGLang support for the **Mamba family of pure state-space models**, none of which could be served before — they crashed at startup or fell through to attention code paths they don't fit. This PR covers both generations: - **Mamba2 (SSD):** `mistralai/Mamba-Codestral-7B-v0.1` - **Mamba-1 (selective-scan):** `tiiuae/falcon-mamba-7b` / `-instruct`, `state-spaces/mamba-130m-hf`, and the raw `state-spaces/mamba-{130m,790m,2.8b}` checkpoints Root causes addressed: these configs have no `num_attention_heads`/`head_dim`, so shape derivation tripped before any weights loaded; the pure-SSM path routed through the paged decoder KV cache (an SSM keeps none); Mamba2 checkpoints use `backbone.*` names with no `max_position_embeddings`; and the raw state-spaces configs carry no `model_type`/`architectures`, so `AutoConfig` rejected them outright. ## Modifications - **New models:** `Mamba2ForCausalLM` (`models/mamba2.py`), `FalconMambaForCausalLM` (`models/falcon_mamba.py`), `MambaForCausalLM` (`models/mamba.py`) — pre-norm mixer decoder layers, no MLP; weight loaders remap `backbone.* → model.*`, `embeddings/embedding. → embed_tokens`, `norm_f → norm` (Mamba2 also `A_log → A`; Mamba-1 keeps `A_log`). - **New Mamba-1 mixer** (`layers/attention/mamba/mamba1.py`, `MambaMixer1`): causal conv over intermediate channels, `x_proj`/`dt_proj` selection, optional Falcon weightless RMSNorm on `B`/`C`/`dt`. Decode reuses `selective_state_update`; prefill uses a portable per-timestep selective scan (works off-CUDA, e.g. XPU). - **Reuse of the Mamba2 backend for Mamba-1:** express the full-rank Mamba-1 state on the Mamba2 head layout (`num_heads = intermediate_size`, `head_dim = 1`) via `Mamba2StateShape.create_mamba1`, so it rides the existing attention backend and memory pool unchanged. - **Config/wiring (gated, additive):** `AttentionArch.SSM`; `PURE_SSM_ARCHITECTURES` / `PURE_MAMBA1_ARCHITECTURES` with `_is_pure_mamba2` / `_is_pure_mamba1` flags; KV-less handling (`head_dim = 0`) in `model_config.py`; cache-param build in `hybrid_arch.py`; SSM backend selection in `attention_backend_setup.py`; forward-metadata guard in `eager_runner.py`. - **Raw-checkpoint support:** `_try_load_raw_mamba_config` pre-`AutoConfig` hook in `utils/hf_transformers/config.py` builds a `MambaConfig` from the minimal `d_model`/`n_layer`/`ssm_cfg` config. - **Conv dtype fix** for fp32 checkpoints (`SGLANG_MAMBA_CONV_DTYPE` mismatch); CPU unit test for Mamba2 weight remapping; docs entry. All changes are gated behind the SSM arch/flag; existing MLA/MHA models keep their original code paths. ## Accuracy Tests | Model | Task | Metric | SGLang (Intel XPU) | |---|---|---|---| | Mamba-Codestral-7B-v0.1 | gsm8k (1319, 5-shot, greedy) | flexible / strict | 0.4579 / 0.4488 | | falcon-mamba-7b | gsm8k (1319, 5-shot) | flexible / strict | 0.5140 / 0.5095 | | falcon-mamba-7b-instruct | gsm8k (1319, 5-shot, chat) | flexible / strict | 0.5883 / 0.5534 | | state-spaces/mamba-130m-hf | piqa (1000, 5-shot) | acc / acc_norm | 0.649 / 0.637 (≈ published 0.64) | | state-spaces/mamba-130m (raw) | hellaswag (limit-50, 5-shot) | acc / acc_norm | 0.34 / 0.48 | | state-spaces/mamba-790m, 2.8b (raw) | — | greedy generation | coherent | All models load with 0 real skipped params. Stock server commands run unchanged (raw checkpoints need `--tokenizer-path EleutherAI/gpt-neox-20b`, a deployment flag). ## Speed Tests and Profiling Adds new models with no change to existing code paths or their speed. Serving on Intel XPU (2× Arc Pro B60): Mamba-Codestral ~36 concurrent sequences / ~220 tok/s decode (tp-size 2); Falcon-Mamba ~42 / ~200 tok/s (tp-size 1). Pure SSM models report a zero-byte KV cache, so concurrency is bounded by `--max-total-tokens` / Mamba state-cache slots rather than KV memory. Mamba-1 prefill uses a per-token selective scan (no in-tree chunked-scan kernel yet), so prefill throughput is low — a Triton Mamba-1 scan kernel is the natural follow-up. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. signal.title: [Feature] PP Support PD + DSpark
signal.text: <!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. --> ## Motivation Fixes #32750. The existing PD + DSpark path works without Pipeline Parallelism because the prefill worker captures all required target hidden states, injects draft KV locally, and transfers target KV + draft KV to the decode worker. With PP enabled, the captured target hidden states are distributed across PP stages. Each stage only owns a subset of the features required by the DSpark context projection. Injecting draft KV independently on each stage is not equivalent to the non-PP computation because RMSNorm must be applied after the full context projection is accumulated. ## Design This PR keeps the existing PD data plane unchanged: ```text Prefill -> target KV + draft KV -> Decode ``` Hidden states are not transferred across the PD boundary. Each prefill PP stage computes its local pre-norm context contribution: ```text ctx_i = h_i @ W_i.T ``` The accumulated context is carried through PP proxy tensors: ```text ctx_acc = recv_ctx_acc + ctx_i ``` The last PP stage performs: ```text ctx_norm = RMSNorm(ctx_acc) K, V = KVProj(ctx_norm) ``` and writes draft KV into the prefill-side draft KV pool. This preserves the original non-PP computation: ```text concat(h1, ..., hk) @ W_fc.T == sum_i(h_i @ W_i.T) ``` while keeping the additional PP payload fixed at `[num_tokens, hidden_size]`. ## Changes ### PP-aware target capture - Capture only target layers owned by the current PP rank. - Carry local captures through `dspark_aux_hidden_states`. - See [`deepseek_v4.py`](https://github.com/bytedance-iaas/sglang/blob/fix/dspark-lifecycle-draft-kv-pool/python/sglang/srt/models/deepseek_v4.py#L2455-L2467) and [`kimi_k3.py`](https://github.com/bytedance-iaas/sglang/blob/fix/dspark-lifecycle-draft-kv-pool/python/sglang/srt/models/kimi_k3.py#L2483-L2525). ### Fixed-size PP context accumulation - Each rank computes its local projection contribution. - `dspark_ctx_acc` remains `[num_tokens, hidden_size]` across PP hops. - Raw `dspark_aux_hidden_states` is removed after local projection. - RMSNorm is applied once on the final PP rank. - See [`dspark_worker_v2.py`](https://github.com/bytedance-iaas/sglang/blob/fix/dspark-lifecycle-draft-kv-pool/python/sglang/srt/speculative/dspark_components/dspark_worker_v2.py#L693-L726). ### DSV4 block-FP8 column slicing - Slice matching FP8 weight columns and scale blocks. - Support canonical FP8 scales and DeepGEMM packed UE8M0 scales. - Avoid repeated zero-padded full-K GEMMs for cross-rank target features. - See [`deepseek_v4_dspark.py`](https://github.com/bytedance-iaas/sglang/blob/fix/dspark-lifecycle-draft-kv-pool/python/sglang/srt/models/deepseek_v4_dspark.py#L70-L147). Unsupported quantization backends retain the full-K fallback in [`project_target_hidden_partial()`](https://github.com/bytedance-iaas/sglang/blob/fix/dspark-lifecycle-draft-kv-pool/python/sglang/srt/models/deepseek_v4_dspark.py#L803-L846). ### Single-owner fast path When all target layers belong to the final PP rank, that rank uses the existing full projection directly. Non-owner DSV4 ranks use lifecycle-only skeleton models: - No draft stages or heads. - No checkpoint weight loading. - No draft KV pool. - No planner, proposer, or injector. - Distributed lifecycle remains aligned across ranks. See [`dspark_config.py`](https://github.com/bytedance-iaas/sglang/blob/fix/dspark-lifecycle-draft-kv-pool/python/sglang/srt/speculative/dspark_components/dspark_config.py#L41-L73) and [`deepseek_v4_dspark.py`](https://github.com/bytedance-iaas/sglang/blob/fix/dspark-lifecycle-draft-kv-pool/python/sglang/srt/models/deepseek_v4_dspark.py#L678-L708). ### Draft KV injection and transfer - Add projected-context KV injection on the final PP rank. - Apply normalization, WKV projection, KV normalization, and RoPE before writing draft SWA KV. - Assign target KV global layer IDs. - Use the `1_000_000+` namespace for draft KV entries. - Only the final PP rank transfers draft KV; every PP rank transfers its local target KV. See [`dspark_kv_inject.py`](https://github.com/bytedance-iaas/sglang/blob/fix/dspark-lifecycle-draft-kv-pool/python/sglang/srt/speculative/dspark_components/dspark_kv_inject.py#L77-L159), [`utils.py`](https://github.com/bytedance-iaas/sglang/blob/fix/dspark-lifecycle-draft-kv-pool/python/sglang/srt/disaggregation/utils.py#L965-L1001), and [`prefill.py`](https://github.com/bytedance-iaas/sglang/blob/fix/dspark-lifecycle-draft-kv-pool/python/sglang/srt/disaggregation/prefill.py#L197-L257). ### PP bootstrap and transfer consensus - Ordered intersection for successful bootstrap/transfer requests. - Ordered union for failures. - Any PP-rank failure becomes a global failure. - KV is not released until the local transfer reaches a terminal state. See [`scheduler_pp_mixin.py`](https://github.com/bytedance-iaas/sglang/blob/fix/dspark-lifecycle-draft-kv-pool/python/sglang/srt/managers/scheduler_pp_mixin.py#L861-L914) and [`prefill.py`](https://github.com/bytedance-iaas/sglang/blob/fix/dspark-lifecycle-draft-kv-pool/python/sglang/srt/disaggregation/prefill.py#L857-L938). ## Supported Scope - Supported: `PP + DSPARK + PD prefill` - Unsupported: `PP + DSPARK decode` - Unsupported: `PP + DSPARK unified serving` - Unsupported: `DSPARK + context parallelism` ## Why `scheduler_pp_mixin.py` Is Modified The last PP stage performs additional work because it injects and transfers draft KV, while the other PP stages only transfer their local target KV. This creates asymmetric transfer completion times. The previous PP scheduler logic treated successful and failed transfers as one unordered set. It could also admit requests based only on `KVPoll.WaitingForInput`, before confirming that every PP stage had sufficient local metadata credits. Under sustained load, these behaviors could cause: - different PP stages to admit requests in different orders; - early KV release on stages that completed before the last PP stage; - inflight queue divergence after a transfer failure; - PP send/receive or proxy-tensor scheduling desynchronization. The scheduler changes make the control plane deterministic: - bootstrap readiness is probed without reserving resources; - request order is preserved during PP intersection and union; - transfer success requires intersection across all PP stages; - transfer failure is propagated as a union across all PP stages; - release occurs only after the last PP stage has completed both target KV and draft KV transfer; - DSpark draft input is reconstructed after PP output processing; - PP output tokens are moved to the batch device before creating the next draft state. The scheduler does not transfer hidden states or draft KV itself. Its role is to keep admission, completion, and release decisions consistent across PP stages despite the extra work performed by the last stage. ## fixes state-component matching This patch fixes state-component matching for PD transfer when PP ranks expose different state component layouts. Previously, state components were matched positionally: ```text prefill state[i] -> decode state[i] ``` That is not always valid for DSV4 under PP. Some state components are optional per PP stage. For example, `C128_STATE` only exists on PP ranks that own C128 layers. When the final PP rank sends draft SWA but does not own any C128 layer, the source and destination layouts can diverge: ```text Prefill final PP rank: state[0] = target SWA state[1] = draft SWA Decode rank: state[0] = target SWA state[1] = target C128_STATE state[2] = draft SWA ``` With positional matching, `prefill state[1]` would incorrectly map to `decode state[1]`, so draft SWA could be written into the target C128 state buffer. The fix is to include `state_types` in the decode registration metadata and match state components by `(StateType, occurrence)` instead of list index: ```text prefill SWA #1 -> decode SWA #1 prefill SWA #2 -> decode SWA #2 ``` This keeps the existing behavior when layouts are already aligned, while correctly handling missing optional components such as `C128_STATE`. The change is applied to both Mooncake and NIXL transfer paths. For mixed-version compatibility, if the peer does not provide `state_types`, the code falls back to the old positional mapping. This does not change the actual KV/state data layout or copy logic. It only changes how the destination state component is selected. ## Accuracy Tests ``` SGLANG_PP_LAYER_PARTITION="6,5,6,5,6,5,5,5" SGLANG_DISAGGREGATION_BOOTSTRAP_TIMEOUT=600 NCCL_SOCKET_IFNAME=eth0 NCCL_IB_DISABLE=0 SGLANG_DSV4_FP4_EXPERTS=1 GLOO_SOCKET_IFNAME=eth0 python3 -m sglang.launch_server --model-path /data02/models/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 --host 0.0.0.0 --port 30000 --trust-remote-code --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 --mem-fraction-static 0.9 --max-running-requests 64 --chunked-prefill-size 8192 --max-prefill-tokens 16384 --pp-size 8 --attention-backend dsv4 --reasoning-parser deepseek-v4 --tool-call-parser deepseekv4 --disable-overlap-schedule --disable-piecewise-cuda-graph --disaggregation-transfer-backend mooncake --enable-metrics --moe-runner-backend flashinfer_mxfp4 --speculative-algo DSPARK --disaggregation-mode prefill --disaggregation-ib-device "mlx5_1,mlx5_2,mlx5_3,mlx5_4" --disable-flashinfer-autotune --disable-shared-experts-fusion SGLANG_DSV4_FP4_EXPERTS=1 SGLANG_JIT_DEEPGEMM_PRECOMPILE=1 SGLANG_OPT_DEEPGEMM_HC_PRENORM=1 SGLANG_OPT_USE_TILELANG_MHC_PRE=1 GLOO_SOCKET_IFNAME=eth0 NCCL_MIN_NCHANNELS=24 NCCL_IB_QPS_PER_CONNECTION=8 sglang serve --trust-remote-code --model-path /data02/models/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 --tp 8 --dp-size 8 --enable-dp-attention --cuda-graph-max-bs 32 --max-running-requests 256 --enable-metrics --host 0.0.0.0 --port 30000 --mem-fraction-static 0.85 --tool-call-parser deepseekv4 --reasoning-parser deepseek-v4 --moe-runner-backend flashinfer_mxfp4 --disaggregation-mode decode --disaggregation-ib-device "mlx5_1,mlx5_2,mlx5_3,mlx5_4" --speculative-algo DSPARK --tokenizer-worker-num 8 --enable-dp-lm-head --load-balance-method round_robin --swa-full-tokens-ratio 0.8 --disable-shared-experts-fusion ``` signal.title: [AMD][CI] Fix ROCm 7.0's dead apt index fail the MORI dependency install
signal.text: ## Motivation Fixes cluster **R387** from the Aug-20 AMD CI monitor report: all 27 jobs in [PR Test ROCm 7.0 (AMD) run 32399046576](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32399046576), plus the nightly-7.0 kimi-k26 job, died identically in "Install dependencies". The report filed this as pure infra needing an AMD artifactory restore. **It is also a code regression, it is specific to ROCm 7.0, and the code half is fixable here.** From the failing [job log](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32399046576/job/96522664507): ``` Err:13 http://compute-artifactory.amd.com/artifactory/list/rocm-osdb-22.04-deb compute-rocm-rel-7.0/38 amd64 Packages 404 Not Found [IP: 10.216.51.87 80] Fetched 48.0 MB in 3s (18.2 MB/s) E: Some index files failed to download. They have been ignored, or old ones used instead. ##[error]Process completed with exit code 100. ``` ### Where it came from The `apt-get update` is new. It was added on 2026-08-20 by c7478228dd (#30984, the ROCm 7.2.4 / Python 3.12 / torch 2.11 upgrade), inside a `docker exec ... bash -c` that runs under `set -euo pipefail`: ```bash git submodule update --init --recursive apt-get update apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends libgrpc++-dev 2>/dev/null || true ``` Every *other* change that PR made to this script is gated on the image flavor — the extras swap (`dev_hip` → `dev_hip_rocm724`), the AITER `torch.Stream` patch, and the AITER commit lookup all sit behind `IMAGE_STAGE_SUFFIX == "-rocm724"`. These two apt lines are the only ungated change in the PR, so a 7.2.4 fix also began running on ROCm 7.0. Before that commit the MORI reinstall did no apt work at all and was immune. ### Why only ROCm 7.0 Not because the code path is 7.0-specific — the identical path runs on 7.2.4 and passes. It is purely base-image lineage: | Flavor | Base image | `rocm-osdb` source | |---|---|---| | 7.0 | `rocm/sgl-dev:rocm7-vllm-20250904` (AMD-internal dev image) | **yes** | | 7.2.0 | `rocm/pytorch:rocm7.2_ubuntu22.04_py3.10_pytorch_release_2.9.1` | no | | 7.2.4 | `rocm/pytorch:rocm7.2.4_ubuntu24.04_py3.12_pytorch_release_2.10.0` | no | Only 7.0 builds on an AMD-internal image, which is what drags in `compute-artifactory.amd.com/.../rocm-osdb-22.04-deb`. The dead index name encodes it exactly: `compute-rocm-rel-7.0/38` is the internal ROCm 7.0 release channel, build 38. Confirmed against a real 7.2.4 job from the same day ([96420374950](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32367546070/job/96420374950)), which runs the same MORI reinstall and the same `apt-get update`, and succeeds. Its apt hosts are entirely public — `apt.llvm.org`, `archive.ubuntu.com`, `packages.broadcom.com`, `ppa.launchpadcontent.net`, `repo.radeon.com` — with no `compute-artifactory.amd.com` entry, so it fetches 40.1 MB cleanly and reaches `[MORI] Done.` ### Why it deserves a code fix rather than only an artifactory restore Three things stand out about the failure: 1. **We neither own nor install from the failing source.** Nothing in this repo references `rocm-osdb`; it is inherited from the base image. Every index we actually use fetched fine (48 MB, including Ubuntu main and universe). 2. **apt itself treated it as recoverable** — "They have been ignored, or old ones used instead" — but still exits 100, because `apt-get update` returns non-zero if *any* index fails. Under `set -e` that is fatal. 3. **The package it feeds is optional.** `rocm.Dockerfile` builds MORI without `libgrpc++-dev` on every flavor, and the install was already best-effort (`|| true`). So one dead third-party index, for a package we do not need, zeroed a whole workflow. "Rerun once the artifactory recovers" also only holds until the next ROCm 7.0 internal build rotates out. ## Modifications **`scripts/ci/amd/amd_ci_install_dependency.sh`** — make both apt steps non-fatal, and log which one degraded: ```bash apt-get update || echo '[MORI] apt-get update reported errors; continuing with the indexes it did fetch' apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends libgrpc++-dev || echo '[MORI] libgrpc++-dev unavailable; building MORI without it' ``` Dropping `2>/dev/null` in favour of an explicit message keeps the reason for a degraded install visible instead of swallowing it. No retry logic is added: the image already sets `Acquire::Retries "5"` via `/etc/apt/apt.conf.d/80-net-hardening` (visible in the log as the repeated `Ign:13` attempts), and a 404 is not retryable. This was the only unguarded `apt-get update` left in the AMD CI path; every other one under `scripts/ci/` is already `|| true` or wrapped in a retry loop, matching `scripts/ci/cuda/ci_install_dependency.sh`. The guard is deliberately applied to all flavors rather than scoped to 7.0. 7.2.0 and 7.2.4 are public images today, but the invariant we want is that no optional apt call can zero a workflow, on any image. A reviewer who prefers to also restore the pre-#30984 behaviour on 7.0/7.2.0 could additionally gate these two lines on `IMAGE_STAGE_SUFFIX == "-rocm724"`, matching the rest of #30984 — happy to add that if wanted. **`test/registered/unit/tools/test_amd_ci_install_dependency.py`** — a 45-line guard asserting that no `apt-get` call in this script can abort the run. It runs on `base-a-test-cpu` (no docker, no ROCm, no GPU) alongside the existing CI-tooling tests in `test/registered/unit/tools/`. This carries more weight than it looks, because **no pull-request-triggered workflow can catch this regression**. `pr-test-amd.yml` (ROCm 7.0) was demoted to a daily shadow in #34204 and now has only `schedule` / `workflow_dispatch` / `workflow_call` triggers — no `pull_request`. The PR gate is `pr-test-amd-rocm720.yml`, which defaults to `rocm724`. So the image that carries the dead index is never exercised pre-merge, and the static check is the only pre-merge signal on this invariant. ## Accuracy Tests Not applicable — CI dependency-install script and its test only; no runtime or model code touched. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Not applicable. ## Verification The test fails against the pre-fix script, naming the offending line, and passes against the fix: ``` # against origin/main's script AssertionError: Lists differ: ['apt-get update'] != [] # against this branch 1 passed ``` While developing the fix I also replayed the incident end to end — a stub `apt-get` reproducing the 404 and exit 100, driving the apt lines extracted from the script inside the same `set -euo pipefail` context — and confirmed the MORI build that follows is still reached, both when `libgrpc++-dev` remains resolvable and when it does not, with no regression on the healthy path. That harness is not checked in: once the line reads `... || echo`, it mostly asserts that `||` suppresses `set -e`, and it required string-parsing the `docker exec` block out of the script, which would break on unrelated edits. Also run: the full `test/registered/unit/tools/` directory (12 passed), `run_suite.py` collection with `sanity_check=True` plus `validate_all_suites` over all registered files (clean; the new test resolves into `base-a-test-cpu`), `shellcheck -S warning` on the script (no new findings — the only diff versus `main` is a line-number shift on a pre-existing `SC2034`), `bash -n`, `black`, `isort`, `ruff`, `codespell`, and the `check-registered-tests` / `check-no-bare-pytest-main` lint hooks. **Note for reviewers:** this PR's own AMD CI cannot reproduce R387, for the trigger reason above — it runs 7.2.4, whose public base has no `rocm-osdb` source. In-situ validation needs the daily `pr-test-amd.yml` cron (17:30 UTC) or a manual `workflow_dispatch` of it. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). — n/a. - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). — n/a. - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process). 2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers. 3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:no_entry_sign: [Run #32427680934](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32427680934)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32427680717](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32427680717)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32427680846](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32427680846)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [AMD] Add Radix-4 MoE top-k router kernel for Kimi-K3 routing
signal.text: <!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. --> co-author: @kkHuang-amd ## Motivation <!-- Describe the purpose and goals of this pull request. --> Kimi-K3 routes 16 of 896 experts, ungrouped. That lands on aiter's generic `biased_grouped_topk`, which spends one round per selected expert — cost tracks `topk`, ~10.4us per layer on MI355X. aiter's faster pivot-based path is gated on DeepSeek's exact shape (256 experts, 8 groups, top-8), so K3 never reaches it. Set `SGLANG_K3_RADIX4_TOPK=1` to enable the radix4 topk path. ## Modifications <!-- Detail the changes made in this pull request. --> Radix-4 select for this shape: the pivot is resolved four key bits at a time, so the round count follows the key width rather than `topk`. Tuned to CDNA — a 16-bin histogram packed as nibbles into one 64-bit register, experts spread over several waves, and a 4-step DPP prefix sum plus a ballot in place of the 16-step walk over the bins. - `kernels/jit/csrc/moe/route_radix4_hip.cuh` — kernel (CDNA-only; uses amdgcn DPP and wave64 ballots) - `kernels/ops/moe/moe_route_radix4.py` — JIT wrapper - `srt/layers/moe/topk.py` — dispatch for covered inputs - `test/registered/kernels/ops/moe/test_moe_route_radix4.py` — pinned against real aiter (oracle match, tie order, NaN/extremes/saturated rows, reproducibility, graph replay, coverage gating) `covered()` is narrow: `[M, 896]` row-contiguous scores, top-16, ungrouped, and `M <= 1024`. Everything else stays on aiter. The token cap is a performance gate rather than a correctness one — the kernel runs one block per token, so past ~1.5k tokens the grid saturates the machine and spreading a token over four waves costs more than it buys. Decode batches sit well under the cap; prefill chunks are far above it and stay on aiter. ### tie contract When scores tie exactly, the common approach (the CUDA router in route_radix.cuh) breaks the tie by expert id -- whichever id is smaller wins. aiter's biased_grouped_topk instead resolves ties via an order implicit in its internal wave64 max reduction (warp reduction), which depends on how it pairwise-compares threads at the hardware level and has no direct relation to expert id. We currently dispatch by M (batch size): large-M prefill goes to aiter's topk implementation, small-M decode goes to this radix4 topk implementation we wrote ourselves. If the two implementations pick different experts on a tie, the same token would get routed to different experts purely because it showed up during prefill versus decode -- prefill and decode routing would disagree. So our current approach is to have our own kernel replicate aiter's tie-break order. kAiterTieLaneRank (in route_radix4_hip.cuh) is that order, read off directly by comparison against aiter, and it's pinned against real aiter calls in test_route_radix4_tie_order_is_aiters / test_route_radix4_tie_straddling_the_cutoff_matches_aiter, so a change on aiter's side surfaces as a test failure rather than a silent divergence. ## Accuracy Tests gsm8k 1319 0.952 <!-- If this pull request affects model outputs (e.g., changes to the kernel or model forward code), provide accuracy test results. --> ## Speed Tests and Profiling e2e 1-3% improvement in TTT. Kernel time on MI355X, 896 experts top-16, graph-captured: | M | aiter | radix4 | speedup | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | 1 | 10.24us | 5.99us | 1.71x | | 8 | 10.56us | 5.75us | 1.84x | | 16 | 10.64us | 5.51us | 1.93x | | 64 | 10.45us | 5.77us | 1.81x | | 256 | 10.48us | 6.38us | 1.64x | | 512 | 10.97us | 7.05us | 1.56x | | 1024 | 11.09us | 9.44us | 1.17x | | 1536 | 12.08us | 11.95us | 1.01x | <!-- If this pull request impacts inference speed, provide benchmarking and profiling results. --> ## Checklist - [ ] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [ ] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. signal.title: [AMD] Add a probe that verifies torch.profiler captures HIP-graph kernels
signal.text: ## Motivation AMD/Silo report that on every `lmsysorg/sglang*` ROCm 7.2 image (v0.5.12 through v0.5.17, `*-rocm720-*`), `torch.profiler` traces contain no GPU kernels for work launched through hipGraph, and they have been swapping `libamdhip64.so.7.2.70200` / `libroctracer64.so.4.1.70200` for the 7.2.4 versions to work around it. The cause is upstream and already fixed: - ROCTracer can fail to report kernel operations: [ROCm/ROCm#6102](https://github.com/ROCm/ROCm/issues/6102), closed with "Resolved in ROCm 7.2.2". - ROCm 7.2.0's HIP runtime also has a wrong doorbell index in `dispatchGenericAqlPacketBatch` (the graph batch-dispatch path) plus an InterceptQueue ring-buffer heap corruption, both fixed in 7.2.1 ([pytorch/pytorch#177873](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/pull/177873)). That matches the `CUDAGraph::replay` deadlock inside `libamdhip64.so.7.2.70200` seen in our own CI (#34452) — the same bug class surfacing as a hang instead of a gap. - The 7.2.4 bases carry the fixed libraries: `rocm/pytorch:rocm7.2.4_*` ships `libamdhip64.so.7.2.70204` and `libroctracer64.so.4.1.70204` (`hip-runtime-amd` 7.2.26015.70200 -> 7.2.53211.70204, `roctracer` 4.1.70200 -> 4.1.70204). #30984 has since landed the `rocm724` flavors, so images with the fixed ROCm are being published — and the measurement in [this comment](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/35390#issuecomment-5350686772) shows why that is not the end of it: the torch wheel vendors its own HIP and roctracer under `torch/lib` and `libtorch_hip.so` carries `RPATH $ORIGIN`, so a 7.2.4 image still profiles through 7.2.0 libraries unless they are preloaded, and `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` cannot override an `RPATH`. Reading the ROCm version in the image tells you nothing about what `torch.profiler` is using. What is missing is a way to tell those states apart, for these images and for any future base or torch bump. Nothing in CI can currently tell a working profiler from a broken one: `test/registered/profiling/test_start_profile.py` only asserts that the trace directory is non-empty, so an image whose traces contain no GPU kernels passes it, and since #34452 the profiling suite runs without CUDA graphs on ROCm, so it never exercises the replay path at all. ## Modifications ### `scripts/ci/amd/check_hip_graph_profiling.py` Captures a graph, replays it under `torch.profiler`, and counts the device events that reach the exported trace against the number of dispatches it asked for. Counting matters: the reported loss is partial (448 of 512 kernels on 7.2.0), and a 4-node graph is traced correctly there, so both a "non-empty trace" threshold and a small graph would call the broken runtime healthy. The default workload is therefore 64 nodes replayed 8 times, and any shortfall fails with the count. An eager control run separates "this runtime cannot trace graph replay" from "this runtime cannot trace anything", and each phase runs in its own process under a timeout because ROCm 7.2.0 can wedge inside `hipGraphLaunch` rather than merely lose events. It also reports the **paths** of the HIP and tracing libraries torch mapped, not their sonames, flags any that did not come from the ROCm install, and prints the `LD_PRELOAD` that switches them — otherwise this failure reads as an unfixable image rather than a load-order problem. `--print-ld-preload` exposes that value for callers that must set it before the process starts. It also warns when the device reports no marketing name, the symptom of an image without libdrm-amdgpu. It depends on nothing but torch and the HIP runtime, so it qualifies any image or base image: A rocm724 image as shipped, which is the case the comment measured: ``` torch 2.11.0+rocm7.2 (hip 7.2.41134), rocm 7.2.4 device: 'AMD Instinct MI355X' (gfx950) hip/tracing libs: /opt/venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages/torch/lib/libamdhip64.so, .../libroctracer64.so eager launch: 512/512 kernel events, 9000 us device time, 12000 trace events graph replay: 448/512 kernel events, 7800 us device time, 12000 trace events note: torch is using its own HIP/roctracer, not the ROCm install's: .../torch/lib/libamdhip64.so, .../torch/lib/libroctracer64.so export LD_PRELOAD="/opt/rocm/lib/libamdhip64.so.7.2.70204:/opt/rocm/lib/libroctracer64.so.4.1.70204..." must be set before the process starts; LD_LIBRARY_PATH cannot override the RPATH the wheel's libtorch_hip.so carries VERDICT: FAIL -- eager launches are traced in full but 64 of 512 graph-replay kernels never reached the trace. ... ``` With that preload it reaches `512/512` and `VERDICT: PASS`. Not registered in the AMD suites here: on a rocm720 image it is expected to fail and, per #34452, can take the process down with it. #35398 runs it against the published rocm724 images instead. ### `test/registered/unit/ci/test_hip_graph_profiling_probe.py` The probe's value is that a red run says *which* failure happened: nothing traceable at all, a wedged `hipGraphLaunch`, or kernels lost under graph replay. A GPU job can only ever exercise whichever case its image is in, so the mapping is driven on CPU with canned phase results instead — every verdict, the exit codes, the ROCm/ROCm#6102 citation appearing only for the untraced-graph case, the marketing-name warning, and the trace parser, where counting a host-only trace as device work would turn the whole check into a false pass. Registered as `base-a-test-cpu`, 9 tests, no GPU. ### `docs/docs/developer_guide/benchmark_and_profiling.mdx` Document the gap, how to check an image, that the `rocm724` tags install the fix but need the `LD_PRELOAD` to actually use it, and the `--disable-cuda-graph` fallback where preloading is not an option, with the caveat that decode numbers collected that way exclude the replay path. ## Accuracy Tests No model or kernel code changes. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Not applicable to the change itself; it measures whether profiling works rather than changing performance. ## Test plan Verified locally without a GPU: - The new unit test passes (16 tests): every verdict path and exit code, the partial-loss shortfall, vendored-runtime detection, the preload value (real files, not the symlinks), and the trace parser. - Trace parsing additionally checked against a real `export_chrome_trace` output, including a capitalized `Kernel` category. - The timeout path's process-group kill verified against a wedged child. - On a host with no GPU the probe reports `environment: unusable -- no GPU visible to torch` and exits 1. - `scripts/lint/check_registered_tests.py`, `check_no_bare_pytest_main.py`, black, isort and codespell all pass. Needs a GPU host — the decisive measurement, and it needs no SGLang build: ```bash GPU="--device=/dev/kfd --device=/dev/dri --group-add video --security-opt seccomp=unconfined" # ROCm 7.2.0 runtime: expected FAIL (reproduces the report) docker run --rm $GPU -v "$PWD:/w" -w /w \ rocm/pytorch:rocm7.2_ubuntu22.04_py3.10_pytorch_release_2.9.1 \ python3 scripts/ci/amd/check_hip_graph_profiling.py # ROCm 7.2.4 runtime: expected PASS docker run --rm $GPU -v "$PWD:/w" -w /w \ rocm/pytorch:rocm7.2.4_ubuntu22.04_py3.10_pytorch_release_2.9.1 \ python3 scripts/ci/amd/check_hip_graph_profiling.py ``` Same torch 2.9.1, same probe, only the ROCm patch level differs. Then run it in a published `*-rocm724-*` image (expected PASS) and a `*-rocm720-*` image (expected FAIL). ## Measured on hardware Run against today's published image (`rocm/sgl-dev:v0.5.17-rocm724-mi35x-20260820`) on an MI355X, via a dispatch of the nightly workflow with this branch's probe and #35398's job ([run](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32337394284)): | run | mapped HIP/roctracer | eager | graph replay | verdict | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | image default | `torch/lib/libamdhip64.so`, `torch/lib/libroctracer64.so` | 512/512 | **448/512** | FAIL | | `LD_PRELOAD` of the image's 7.2.4 | `/opt/rocm-7.2.4/lib/…70204` | 512/512 | **512/512** | PASS | That reproduces the numbers in [the review comment](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/35390#issuecomment-5350686772) exactly, on the artifact users pull. Also confirmed there: `torch.cuda.get_device_name(0)` is `'AMD Instinct MI355X'` (libdrm is fine), torch reports `hip 7.2.26015` — the 7.2.0 build — inside a ROCm 7.2.4 image, and `--print-ld-preload` resolved to the same value by hand-checking `/opt/rocm/lib`. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). <!-- The probe is the test; registering it in the AMD suites requires images on a ROCm 7.2.2 or newer runtime. --> - [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). <!-- N/A --> - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. signal.title: [Feature] Support PP in full prefill CUDA graphs
signal.text: ## Motivation Full prefill CUDA graphs currently cannot replay pipeline-parallel stages. The runner has no graph-stable storage for pipeline inputs, does not pass those inputs to non-first stages, and rejects pipeline proxy outputs. ## Modifications - Add token-major pipeline proxy buffers for full-prefill graph capture and replay. - Register pipeline inputs with the prefill graph buffer registry so live inputs are copied and padded safely. - Preserve global attention-layer indexing on partitioned pipeline stages. - Pass graph-stable pipeline inputs to non-first stages and trim pipeline outputs to the live token count. - Add unit coverage for layer alignment, buffer allocation, registry filling, and output trimming. - Add a dedicated two-GPU FullCG test under `test/registered/cuda_graph/full_prefill/` while retaining the existing generic PP canary test. - Replay a 47-token PP prompt through the 64-token prefill bucket with the normal FullCG decode path enabled, and assert that the request actually uses the prefill graph. ## Accuracy Tests No numerical kernels or model math are changed. The two-GPU end-to-end test passes with KV canary checks enabled and observes `cuda graph: True` for the 47-token prefill batch. - 46 focused CPU tests passed. - Two-GPU mock-model FullCG prefill and decode test passed on GB300. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Not applicable. This enables a previously unsupported configuration without changing the non-PP or eager execution paths. ## Checklist - [x] Format code with the repository pre-commit configuration. - [x] Add unit and end-to-end tests. - [x] No documentation update is required for this runner capability. - [x] No benchmark is required because no existing execution path is modified. - [x] Follow the SGLang code style guidance. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:no_entry_sign: [Run #32416467775](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32416467775)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32416467627](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32416467627)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #32416467679](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32416467679)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [Fix] Harden FlashAttention CUDA graph metadata bounds
signal.text: ## Motivation Full-prefill CUDA graph buckets are sized by aggregate batch tokens, which can exceed the maximum context length of any single request. The FlashAttention sliding-window write-location buffer is currently allocated from max_context_len, so a valid aggregate-token bucket can exceed its capacity. Separately, idle graph batches may expose an empty CPU sequence-length tensor, for which max() is invalid. ## Modifications - Size the full-prefill sliding-window write-location buffer from the captured token capacity. - Validate replay token counts before copying into the graph-stable buffer. - Use the static context bound when CPU sequence lengths are absent or empty. - Add CPU regression tests for aggregate-token capacity, replay overflow detection, and empty idle batches. ## Accuracy Tests No attention math is changed. The tests validate metadata sizing and fallback behavior. - 2 focused unit tests passed. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Not applicable. These changes affect metadata allocation and boundary checks, not attention kernels. ## Checklist - [x] Format code with the repository pre-commit configuration. - [x] Add unit tests. - [x] No documentation update is required. - [x] No speed benchmark is required for this metadata correctness fix. - [x] Follow the SGLang code style guidance. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:no_entry_sign: [Run #32416500122](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32416500122)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #32416499661](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32416499661)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #32416499821](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32416499821)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [Fix] Honor `--config=path.yaml` when merging the YAML config
signal.text: ## Problem `--config path.yaml` and `--config=path.yaml` are both accepted by argparse, but only the first one actually works. The YAML merge in `prepare_server_args` is gated on the exact token `"--config"`: ```python if "--config" in argv: ... argv = config_merger.merge_config_with_args(argv) ``` `"--config=path.yaml"` is not that token, so the gate is skipped and `parse_args` receives the raw argv: the file path is stored in `--config` but **every setting inside the file is silently dropped** — no warning, no error. A config-driven deployment quietly runs with defaults for everything that was supposed to come from the YAML. Repro (on current main): ```python from sglang.srt.server_args import prepare_server_args # config.yaml contains: mem-fraction-static: 0.42 # max-running-requests: 128 a = prepare_server_args(["--model-path", "dummy", "--config", "config.yaml"]) b = prepare_server_args(["--model-path", "dummy", "--config=config.yaml"]) print(a.mem_fraction_static, b.mem_fraction_static) # 0.42 None ``` ## Fix Normalize the equals form to the space form in `prepare_server_args` before the gate (`_normalize_config_flag`), so the existing exact-token matching in `server_args_config_parser.py` sees a uniform spelling. Only the `--config=` prefix is split; nothing else in argv is rewritten and the space-form path is byte-identical to before. ## Test `test_config_equals_form_is_merged` in `test/registered/unit/server_args/test_server_args.py` (next to the existing config-merge tests): both spellings must resolve the YAML settings identically. Verified the case fails on main and passes with the fix. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:warning: [Run #32434713762](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32434713762)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:warning: [Run #32434713626](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32434713626)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:warning: [Run #32434713858](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32434713858)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: CI Maintenance Mode
signal.text: This post introduces a maintenance mode for our CI infrastructure. When the CI is unhealthy (due to too many flaky tests or unstable machines), we will open this issue, and the project will enter CI Maintenance mode. While maintenance mode is active, normal PRs' CI runs will be paused. Instead, we will allocate all resources to PRs that attempt to fix the CI. Once the CI is healthy and `pr-test.yml` is all green, we will close this issue to declare the end of maintenance mode. Typically, we will enter the maintenance mode when the scheduled pr-test on main is broken for some consecutive runs https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/workflows/pr-test.yml?query=event%3Aschedule Rebase required past #33384 (build the Rust extension modules once per run): without it every CUDA job recompiles the `rust/` cargo workspace during its editable install, and jobs sharing a host serialize on uv's editable sdist lock until the queue's tail hits its timeout. signal.title: [AMD] Optimize Kimi-K3 Triton MLA prefill on gfx950
signal.text: ## Motivation Kimi-K3 uses two attention representations during prefill at TP8 on MI355X: - Fresh/zero-prefix MHA: 12 heads with QK/V dimensions 192/128. - Cached-prefix absorbed MLA: 12 query heads, one KV head, and QK/V dimensions 576/512. Current Triton prefill leaves performance on the table for both shapes: 1. The exact K3 kernels use one pipeline stage and natural-exponential online softmax. 2. Absorbed 576/512 prefill processes one full 512-wide value accumulator, increasing register pressure. 3. FP8 cached-prefix P·V can underflow small softmax probabilities. 4. Aiter supports native FP8 zero-prefix prefill, but Triton lacks an equivalent opt-in path. ## Changes ### K3 prefill tuning - Use two pipeline stages for exact gfx950 K3 192/128 and N32 576/512 prefill kernels. - Fold `log2(e)` into the attention scale and use `exp2` for unmodified K3 logits. - Convert stored LSE back to natural-log units. - Preserve current compact ragged-grid scheduling and the generic Triton-3.7 fallback. ### 4×128 absorbed MLA kernel Add a dedicated split-dimension kernel for cached-prefix K3 MLA: ```text Q/K latent: 4 × 128 Q/K tail: 64 V/output: 4 × 128 ``` The kernel maintains one online-softmax state and four independent FP32 value accumulators before concatenating the normalized 128-wide outputs. Dispatch is restricted to: - gfx950; - 12 query heads and one KV head; - QK/V dimensions 576/512; - BF16 current Q/K/V and output; - BF16 cached prefix with unit scales, or opt-in FP8 cached prefix with supported descales; - causal attention; - page size 1; - contiguous last dimensions; - no custom mask, sliding window, logit cap, XAI temperature, sink, LSE, score modifier, auxiliary tensor, or skipped stage. Unsupported calls immediately use the existing generic kernel. ### FP8 prefill Add: ```bash SGLANG_TRITON_FP8_PREFILL_ATTN=1 ``` This is enabled by default. Set `SGLANG_TRITON_FP8_PREFILL_ATTN=0` to disable native FP8 prefill. On exact K3 gfx950 shapes: - Zero-prefix 192/128 Q/K/V are cast from BF16 to FP8 before launch, matching Aiter behavior. - Absorbed 576/512 prefill keeps current-chunk Q/K/V in BF16 while using the FP8 cached prefix. - Softmax probabilities are multiplied by `FP8_MAX` before FP8 P·V and the accumulator contribution is divided by the same factor. - Non-unit cached-prefix K/V descales are supported. The default-on path achieved 98% GSM8K accuracy in model-level validation. ## Performance MI355X measurements used a device warmup and HIP-graph replay. Against unmodified current main: | K3 prefill case | Current main | This change | Speedup | |---|---:|---:|---:| | Zero-prefix BF16, 8K | 0.726 ms | 0.415 ms | 1.75× | | Zero-prefix FP8, 8K, casts included | 0.726 ms | 0.420 ms | 1.73× | | Absorbed BF16, 8K prefix + 8K extend | 8.658 ms | 4.133 ms | 2.09× | | Absorbed FP8, 8K prefix + 8K extend | 6.770 ms | 3.687 ms | 1.84× | FP8 zero-prefix compared with the optimized BF16 path: | Length | BF16 | FP8, casts included | Result | |---:|---:|---:|---:| | 8K | 0.414 ms | 0.421 ms | No difference | | 16K | 1.500 ms | 1.400 ms | FP8 1.07× faster | | 32K | 6.255 ms | 5.145 ms | FP8 1.22× faster | The default-on policy intentionally follows Aiter and enables native FP8 at every length despite the small 8K crossover loss. ### End-to-end serving Throughput uplift is computed as the geometric mean of the per-concurrency ratios at concurrency 2, 4, 8, and 16. Kimi-K3 TP8, ISL/OSL 8192/1024: | Concurrency | Baseline tok/s | This change tok/s | Uplift | |---:|---:|---:|---:| | 2 | 874.18 | 879.54 | +0.6% | | 4 | 1529.69 | 1586.17 | +3.7% | | 8 | 2554.27 | 2586.82 | +1.3% | | 16 | 3892.75 | 3940.95 | +1.2% | | **Geomean** | — | — | **+1.70%** | Kimi-K3 TP8, ISL/OSL 68K/350: | Concurrency | Baseline tok/s | This change tok/s | Uplift | |---:|---:|---:|---:| | 2 | 6092.96 | 6910.34 | +13.4% | | 4 | 7060.28 | 8185.23 | +15.9% | | 8 | 7655.63 | 9017.19 | +17.8% | | 16 | 7973.53 | 9540.03 | +19.6% | | **Geomean** | — | — | **+16.67%** | The long-context gain is predominantly improved prefill/TTFT; median ITL is effectively unchanged in both comparisons. ## Numerics - BF16 absorbed split versus current-main generic output: relative L2 approximately `9.5e-5`. - FP8 absorbed split versus the corrected generic FP8 path: relative L2 approximately `6.6e-5`. - Zero-prefix FP8 versus BF16: relative L2 approximately 3.4-3.5%. - Kimi-K3 model-level GSM8K accuracy with FP8 prefill enabled: 98%. Additional long-context logits and workload validation remain recommended. ## Platform scope All specialized execution paths require gfx950 and exact K3 shapes. On NVIDIA and other AMD architectures: - the split-dimension dispatcher returns false; - FP8 Q/K/V casting is disabled; - FP8 probability scaling is disabled; - K3 `exp2` and two-stage specializations are disabled; - existing generic attention behavior remains active. ## Validation - Ruff 0.15.1 passed with the repository's configured rule selection. - Black 26.1.0 passed. - Isort 7.0.0 passed. - `git diff --check` passed. - Kimi-K3 GSM8K accuracy with FP8 prefill enabled: 98%. - Four focused K3 BF16/FP8 parity and dispatch tests pass on gfx950. - The focused kernel tests are registered in the per-PR `stage-b-test-1-gpu-small-amd-mi35x` suite. - Generic Triton-3.7 fallback tests passed after the final gfx950-only gate. Recommended E2E matrix: - ISL/OSL 8192/1024 and 68000/350; - concurrency 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, and 64; - BF16 and FP8 KV cache; - flag off/on with identical prompts, seeds, request counts, and cache state; - model-level accuracy and logits comparison. ## Files changed ```text python/sglang/kernels/ops/attention/extend_attention.py python/sglang/kernels/ops/attention/extend_attention_split_dim.py python/sglang/srt/environ.py test/registered/unit/layers/attention/test_triton_mla_prefill_gfx950.py ``` <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:no_entry_sign: [Run #32434478524](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32434478524)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32434478563](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32434478563)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #32434478698](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32434478698)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [3/N] elastic-ep: Recapture decode CUDA graphs after scale-up
signal.text: ## Summary This PR follows [PR #30553](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/30553) and adds FULL decode CUDA graph recapture after runtime Elastic EP scale-up. Primary and joiner ranks rebuild their graphs for the expanded topology before the new EP size is committed. The existing scale-up API and EPLB lifecycle are unchanged. ## Changes - Defer initial decode graph capture on joining ranks until they enter the expanded world. - Finish the current sampling step, release the old graph state, and rebuild decode graphs with the expanded Mooncake WORLD and NIXL rank mask. - Require primary and joiner ranks to resolve the same graph mode and capture configuration before recapture. - Reuse SGLang's existing FULL decode graph initializer and synchronize all ranks before committing the scale operation. - Add graph-stable FA3 MLA metadata for the validated DeepSeek path. - Reject execution modes that do not use the supported decode finalization path. ## Configuration Launch primary and joiner groups with the same resolved graph settings: ```text --cuda-graph-backend-decode full --cuda-graph-backend-prefill disabled --cuda-graph-bs-decode 1 2 4 8 16 ``` The scale request and status API are inherited from the base scale-up PR. ## Known Limitations - Only FULL decode graph recapture is supported. Prefill and piecewise graph recapture are outside this PR. - Primary and joiner groups must use the same resolved CUDA graph configuration and effective capture sizes. - Recapture is synchronous. Configuring more decode batch sizes increases the scale-finalization pause. - The validated DeepSeek MLA path requires FlashAttention 3. - Speculative decoding, embedding, diffusion, encoder-only execution, forward hooks, and PDMux split-prefill are not supported with Elastic EP recapture. - The topology, scale-direction, and post-scale recovery limitations of the base scale-up PR still apply. ## Test Plan The manual Elastic EP tests cover direct, single-rank, mixed-cohort, and repeated scale-up: - `TestElasticScaleUp4To5CudaGraph` - `TestElasticScaleUp4To6CudaGraph` - `TestElasticScaleUp4To8CudaGraph` - `TestElasticScaleUp4To5To6CudaGraph` Each test captures decode batch sizes `1 2 4 8 16` and checks post-scale generation, routed joiner traffic, input logprobs, and GSM8K correctness. ```bash CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1,2,3,4,5,6,7 \ python -m pytest -v -s \ test/manual/ep/test_elastic_scale.py::TestElasticScaleUp4To5To6CudaGraph::test_scale_up_on_demand ``` The repeated 4-to-5-to-6 and direct 4-to-6 validations passed with all five decode graph sizes captured on every participating rank. ## References - [PR #30553](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/30553) - EPLB after scale-up - [PR #30164](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/30164) - runtime EP scale-up - [[RFC] Elastic EP Scale](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/22788) <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32138752782](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32138752782)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32138752466](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32138752466)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32138752639](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32138752639)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->
