signal.title: [Kernel] Add H200 Nemotron MoE configs and cache selection
signal.text: > [!NOTE] > **Draft: default-H200 CUDA-graph A/B/A is serving-positive.** The earlier > inconclusive A/B/A accidentally capped decode graphs at batch 16, forcing the > parallel-64 workload onto the eager path. With SGLang's default H200 graph > configuration, tuned v2 improves median GSM8K latency by 6.12% and median > output-token throughput by 3.15% against the average of stable bracketing > baselines, with zero invalid outputs. ## Summary Add NVIDIA H200 Triton 3.6 fused-MoE configs for `nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Lightning-30B-A3B-BF16`: - TP1: `E=128,N=1856`, with 26 measured serving token counts from M=1 to 8192 - TP2 per rank: `E=128,N=928` Both shapes previously used the generic fallback config. The change also caches nearest-config selection by shape and token count so a dense JSON table does not rescan every key for all 23 MoE layers on every forward step. ## Forced-Triton real-model validation Tested official revision `d468880b6ad3c6e0d21377ce7242adaea4cc884d` with SGLang v0.5.17 (`29481685462732237d80d86076d6563e1f658102`), Torch 2.11.0, Triton 3.6.0, and `--moe-runner-backend triton` on one H200. Each comparison used ten 200-question GSM8K runs, five shots, parallelism 64, and zero-temperature sampling. | TP1 candidate | Median latency | Median output throughput | Quality | |---|---:|---:|---:| | Original up only vs baseline | +0.79% | -1.70% | up to 0.5% invalid in three runs | | Original up + tuned down vs baseline | +5.78% | -4.68% | zero invalid | | Decode-aware up + down vs fresh baseline | -2.23% | -1.69% | zero invalid | | Decode-aware up only vs fresh baseline | -0.22% | -1.68% | zero invalid | | Alignment-aware up only vs reverse-order baseline | +3.95% | -2.86% | zero invalid | | Full-path v1 vs baseline | +4.86% | -2.91% | 0.5% invalid in one run | | Corrected dense full-path v2 vs baseline | +10.04% | -6.64% | zero invalid; 3-run rejection screen | | Dense full-path v2 + config-selection cache vs fresh baseline | -4.50% | +5.30% | zero invalid; initial non-bracketed 3-run screen | | Dense v2 + cache, graph capped at 16 | +6.94% | -2.37% | inconclusive: parallel-64 ran eager and baselines drifted | | Dense v2 + cache, default H200 graphs | **-6.12%** | **+3.15%** | zero invalid; fresh A/B/A acceptance | The decode-aware searches added M=1,4,16,32,64,128 entries, used 100 real routed-expert tensors covering all 128 experts, and matched up/down `BLOCK_SIZE_M`. A conservative follow-up fixed decode `BLOCK_SIZE_M=16` to reduce expert padding and route-alignment overhead. Neither approach produced a serving-positive table. A reverse-order baseline recovered its original performance, ruling out simple node drift. The first full-path search included route alignment, padding, both projections, `relu2`, and combine, but its synthetic benchmark modeled the non-gated Nemotron up projection at twice its real width. The corrected search used the exact serving shapes (`w1=[128,1856,2688]`, `w2=[128,2688,1856]`), added the previously omitted baseline dimensions, and tuned 26 observed serving token sizes from M=1 through M=8192. It evaluated 6,674 valid candidates, produced exact output matches at every size, and measured isolated reductions from 1.48% to 35.77%. Its three-run serving screen nevertheless regressed median latency by 10.04% and normalized output throughput by 6.64%. An actual SGLang trace exposed the missing cost and the limited end-to-end headroom. Across the complete 12-step trace, v2 reduced total `fused_moe_kernel` GPU time by 17.77%, but that number includes non-steady work. In steady decode, fused-MoE time fell only from 7.867 ms to 7.468 ms (-5.08%). Fused MoE was 62.8% of steady GPU-active time, so Amdahl's law predicts about a 3.19% reduction in GPU-active time; the trace measured 3.10%. Meanwhile, uncached CPU decode-step time increased by 0.66%. `try_get_optimal_moe_config` CPU time increased from 2.64 ms to 13.99 ms because each of the 23 MoE layers scanned all 26 keys for both projections. Caching the nearest config removes that repeated Python work: | Controlled 64-request test | Baseline median | v2 median | v2 delta | |---|---:|---:|---:| | Before lookup cache | 1,784.8 tok/s | 1,757.2 tok/s | -1.54% | | With lookup cache | 1,816.3 tok/s | 1,817.8 tok/s | +0.08% | The initial cache-aware three-run GSM8K screen measured: - Median latency: 17.186 s baseline, 16.413 s v2 (**-4.50%**) - Median output throughput: 1,074.6 tok/s baseline, 1,131.6 tok/s v2 (**+5.30%**) - Mean output throughput: **+2.46%** - Invalid outputs: **0%** An initial fresh A/B/A on a new two-H200 iDev appeared inconclusive: | Phase | Median latency | Median output throughput | Invalid | |---|---:|---:|---:| | Baseline A | 16.657 s | 1,097.7 tok/s | up to 0.5% in one run | | Tuned v2 + cache | 17.101 s | 1,098.3 tok/s | 0% | | Baseline A2 | 15.326 s | 1,152.3 tok/s | 0% | The post baseline was 7.99% faster in median latency and 4.97% higher in median throughput than the pre baseline, confirming substantial run-order drift. Tuned was effectively tied with baseline A on throughput (+0.06%) and 2.67% slower on latency. The arithmetic comparison against the average of the two baselines is +6.94% latency and -2.37% throughput, but that is not a valid causal estimate when the baseline itself moves this much. One tuned run also stalled at 26.025 seconds and 717.4 tokens/s; excluding that outlier, the other two tuned runs still show no meaningful throughput gain over baseline A. That experiment had `--cuda-graph-max-bs-decode 16` hard-coded while serving 64 concurrent requests, so its high-concurrency decode path ran eagerly. Removing the manual cap resolves the H200 TP1 default to max batch 256, clamped by this model's request pool to 241. SGLang captured `[1,2,4,8,12,16,24,...,240,241]`; all measured decode batches used CUDA graphs. Capture consumed 0.61 GB and left 19.64 GB available. The corrected default-graph A/B/A measured: | Phase | Median latency | Median output throughput | Invalid | |---|---:|---:|---:| | Baseline A | 11.318 s | 1,648.9 tok/s | 0% | | Tuned v2 + cache | 10.602 s | 1,703.4 tok/s | 0% | | Baseline A2 | 11.269 s | 1,653.8 tok/s | 0% | Relative to the average of the two bracketing baselines, tuned v2 reduced median latency by 6.12% and increased median output throughput by 3.15%. Baseline A2 differed from baseline A by only -0.43% latency and +0.30% throughput, so the prior order-drift problem did not recur. Fixed 128-token decode sweeps show where the table helps: | Client concurrency | Tuned vs bracket-average baseline | |---:|---:| | 64 | -0.55% throughput | | 128 | -0.19% throughput | | 256 | **+17.64% throughput** | The 256-client run used the server's maximum 241 active requests with 15 queued. This agrees with the isolated full-path result: the dense table is roughly neutral at fixed 64/128-request decode but substantially faster near the M=192–256 configurations, while the variable-length GSM8K workload gains 3.15% overall. The model is not corrupted: all 14 user-NFS weight shards and the tokenizer, config, index, generation config, and chat template are byte-identical to the canonical ELR publication at `/shared/public/elr-models/nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Lightning-30B-A3B-BF16/ce38b6ab8b252b4b8ee7165b4605e93191cafd73`. **Decision:** retain the corrected 26-point table and bounded nearest-config cache in the draft PR. Under SGLang's actual default H200 decode-graph path, the combined change provides a stable end-to-end GSM8K gain and a large high-batch fixed-decode gain. Keep the PR in draft for reviewer assessment of the config-cache runtime change and the model-specific table. ## Environment - GPU: NVIDIA H200 - GPUs available: 2 - Torch: `2.11.0+cu130` - CUDA runtime: 13.0 - Triton: 3.6.0 - SGLang tuning commit: `c2c1c4d3ebc42402264002f6ec57f90fee58c30c` - Token counts: 256, 512, 1024 - Validation repetitions: 3 baseline and 3 tuned per shape ## Results | TP | Tokens | Baseline (us) | Tuned (us) | Speedup | Latency reduction | |---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | 1 | 256 | 1435.44 | 930.48 | 1.543x | 35.18% | | 1 | 512 | 1550.47 | 967.20 | 1.603x | 37.62% | | 1 | 1024 | 1694.77 | 1023.66 | 1.656x | 39.60% | | 2 | 256 | 734.74 | 493.07 | 1.490x | 32.89% | | 2 | 512 | 780.75 | 529.32 | 1.475x | 32.20% | | 2 | 1024 | 845.91 | 548.78 | 1.541x | 35.13% | The TP2 per-rank config was also run concurrently on both H200s. Both ranks selected the same configs; their measured means were within 0.6% to 1.0%. ## Reproduction commands The upstream tuner imports Ray only for scheduling. Ray was not available in the test environment, so the same worker was executed directly by `tuning_fused_moe_triton_no_ray.py`, one process per GPU. ```bash ROOT=/shared/user/vjhaveri/sglang-h200-tuning VENV=/shared/user/qwen35-9ms-sla/venvs/sglang-v0.5.16-cu130 MODEL=/shared/user/vjhaveri/sglang-h200-model-configs/nemotron35-lightning RESULTS=/shared/user/vjhaveri/sglang-h200-tuning-results export PATH="$VENV/bin:$PATH" export PYTHONPATH="$ROOT/python:$ROOT/benchmark/kernels/fused_moe_triton" export CPATH="/shared/user/qwen35-9ms-sla/system-deps/python3-devel/root/usr/include/python3.12${CPATH:+:$CPATH}" ``` Full TP1 and TP2 searches: ```bash mkdir -p "$RESULTS/nemotron-tp1" "$RESULTS/nemotron-tp2" ( cd "$RESULTS/nemotron-tp1" CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 \ TRITON_CACHE_DIR="$RESULTS/cache-nemotron-tp1/triton" \ TORCHINDUCTOR_CACHE_DIR="$RESULTS/cache-nemotron-tp1/torch" \ "$VENV/bin/python" /shared/user/vjhaveri/tuning_fused_moe_triton_no_ray.py \ --model "$MODEL" \ --tp-size 1 \ --batch-sizes 256 512 1024 \ --tune \ 2>&1 | tee tune.log ) & ( cd "$RESULTS/nemotron-tp2" CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=1 \ TRITON_CACHE_DIR="$RESULTS/cache-nemotron-tp2/triton" \ TORCHINDUCTOR_CACHE_DIR="$RESULTS/cache-nemotron-tp2/torch" \ "$VENV/bin/python" /shared/user/vjhaveri/tuning_fused_moe_triton_no_ray.py \ --model "$MODEL" \ --tp-size 2 \ --batch-sizes 256 512 1024 \ --tune \ 2>&1 | tee tune.log ) & wait ``` Baseline and tuned validation, repeated three times for each TP size: ```bash for repeat in 1 2 3; do CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 "$VENV/bin/python" \ /shared/user/vjhaveri/tuning_fused_moe_triton_no_ray.py \ --model "$MODEL" --tp-size 1 --batch-sizes 256 512 1024 \ 2>&1 | tee "$RESULTS/nemotron-tp1/baseline-repeat-$repeat.log" CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=1 "$VENV/bin/python" \ /shared/user/vjhaveri/tuning_fused_moe_triton_no_ray.py \ --model "$MODEL" --tp-size 2 --batch-sizes 256 512 1024 \ 2>&1 | tee "$RESULTS/nemotron-tp2/baseline-repeat-$repeat.log" done CONFIG_DIR="$ROOT/python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/moe_runner/triton_utils/configs/triton_3_6_0" cp "$RESULTS/nemotron-tp1/E=128,N=1856,device_name=NVIDIA_H200.json" "$CONFIG_DIR/" cp "$RESULTS/nemotron-tp2/E=128,N=928,device_name=NVIDIA_H200.json" "$CONFIG_DIR/" for repeat in 1 2 3; do CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 "$VENV/bin/python" \ /shared/user/vjhaveri/tuning_fused_moe_triton_no_ray.py \ --model "$MODEL" --tp-size 1 --batch-sizes 256 512 1024 \ 2>&1 | tee "$RESULTS/nemotron-tp1/tuned-repeat-$repeat.log" CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=1 "$VENV/bin/python" \ /shared/user/vjhaveri/tuning_fused_moe_triton_no_ray.py \ --model "$MODEL" --tp-size 2 --batch-sizes 256 512 1024 \ 2>&1 | tee "$RESULTS/nemotron-tp2/tuned-repeat-$repeat.log" done ``` Concurrent dual-H200 TP2 per-rank validation: ```bash for gpu in 0 1; do ( CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES="$gpu" "$VENV/bin/python" \ /shared/user/vjhaveri/tuning_fused_moe_triton_no_ray.py \ --model "$MODEL" --tp-size 2 --batch-sizes 256 512 1024 \ >"$RESULTS/nemotron-tp2-dual-rank-gpu$gpu.log" 2>&1 ) & done wait ``` Patch checks: ```bash git diff --check git apply --check --reverse \ /shared/user/vjhaveri/sglang-h200-tuning-results/nemotron35-lightning-h200-configs.patch ```

signal.title: [Sampling] Add explicit bounded sampling-mask mode
signal.text: ## Why #27408 added SGLang's native sampling-mask response, but reconstructed support after sampling and used finite `top_k` as its safety bound. #33593, now merged in `main`, made top-p-only requests valid and exposed sampling masks through the OpenAI chat extension. The remaining contract must therefore be general: top-p/min-p support is data-dependent, and SGLang's threshold primitives retain every token tied at the cutoff, so even finite top-k does not bound realized support. This PR makes the response describe the distribution that actually sampled the token, then bounds only its transport. This is a general serving contract, not an RL-only path. ## Contract For the post-filter weights `w` used to sample token `y`, let `S = {i | w[i] > 0}` and `C = --sampling-mask-max-tokens`: - sampling itself is unchanged; - if `|S| <= C`, the returned token IDs are the complete support `S`; - exact mode is the default, so `|S| > C` aborts before `y` is committed; - `sampling_mask_mode="bounded"` opts into at most `C` IDs and reports `output_token_sampling_mask_truncated=true`; - bounded mode keeps the highest-weight prefix and retains `y` by replacing its final entry when necessary; - the selected-token logprob is always `log(w[y] / sum(w))` over the full realized support, never over the truncated return; - missing or internally inconsistent producer output is an internal error, not truncation. The cap changes metadata only. It never changes the sampling distribution. ## Design - Capture the producer's representation. PyTorch reuses its filtered weights and token permutation; FlashInfer uses SGLang's existing top-k/top-p renormalization primitives and min-p predicate; deterministic logprob sampling and greedy sampling use their native representations. - Keep internal results tensor-backed. `SamplingMaskOutput` is a dataclass following the existing result-holder `map_device_tensors`/async-D2H path; `_SamplingMaskCapture` is a sampler-private `NamedTuple`. - Maintain opted-in device row indices in `SamplingBatchInfo`, including filter/merge, so mixed batches restrict dense work and transfer to requested rows. - Emit factual `OK`, `TRUNCATED`, or `INVALID` status in the sampler, reach TP/CP consensus through the existing process groups, and apply exact/bounded policy in the scheduler. - Propagate the per-token truncation bit through streaming, multi-tokenizer output, sessions, PP, and PD disaggregation. PD reuses its existing 64-byte padded metadata row; the first two slots carry returned length and truncation. - Reuse the OpenAI chat sampling-mask path merged in #33593 and forward its `sampling_mask_mode` into the existing native request field. - Abort exact overflow before committing the sampled token and release every request-owned KV slot, including overlap-allocated slots without a committed token ID. ## Internal API changes - Private `Sampler._sample_from_probs` now returns sampled IDs plus optional producer capture data. - `top_k_top_p_min_p_sampling_from_probs_torch` keeps its existing token-only behavior by default; a keyword-only opt-in returns already-computed filtered data for capture. - Private `_attach_*` helpers became `_build_*` because they now return a tensor holder. The post-hoc `_compute_sampling_mask_from_probs` reconstruction was removed because it was not the producer's source of truth. - Request fields are placed so existing positional constructors and the tokenized Rust wire layout do not shift. - The PD field changed from `output_token_sampling_mask_len` to `output_token_sampling_mask_metadata` because the same padded row now carries length and truncation. No layout class, one-use global size constant, or additional RDMA buffer is introduced. - Existing PP `get_logprob_*` helper names remain unchanged; only their logits-output payload is widened. - Existing optional backend KV-release hooks are used at the release site; no new base-worker lifecycle interface is added. No public sampling function is removed or renamed. ## Performance - Feature-off requests add Python flag/tuple plumbing only: no new tensor operation, dense allocation, D2H copy, PP tensor, or TP/CP collective. - Opted-in rows require dense `O(R * V)` support work because current sampling primitives produce dense weights. Packing transfers `4 * R * C + 12 * R` bytes. A fixed cap avoids a GPU-to-CPU synchronization to discover a data-dependent width; finite top-k is not a valid bound because cutoff ties are retained. - On one H200 at `V=128256`, `C=4096`, measured opt-in operator overhead was approximately 0.28-0.72 ms across FlashInfer joint, min-p, and PyTorch paths. - Dense temporary storage scaled with opted-in rows: approximately 1.7 MB at `R=1`, 54 MB at `R=32`, and 107 MB at `R=64`. Bounded D2H payload p50 was approximately 53-55 us from `R=1` through `R=64` (16 KB to 1.05 MB). - Same-node TP2/4/8 status consensus measured approximately 20-42 us across 1-1024 rows. ## Validation - 295 focused tests passed, 2 skipped, with 75 subtests on one H200 using `lmsysorg/sglang:nightly-dev-cu13-20260817-d91c3682` and the rebased PR source. - Seven end-to-end H200 serving contracts passed on the rebased tree: finite support/logprob consistency, exact overflow abort, bounded truncation signal, top-p-only policy, OpenAI chat bounded-mode propagation, invalid-mode rejection, and deterministic sampling preservation. - A 4,927-check H200 operator matrix passed against independent support and selected-logprob oracles, including uniform cutoff ties and min-p input isolation. - One-node H200 TP2/4/8 collective probes passed. - Repository-native `pre-commit run --all-files` passed on current `main`, including registered-test validation, lint-checker tests, Rust formatting, and workspace clippy. `git diff --check` passed. The existing CUDA/AMD end-to-end sampling-mask test remains registered in its current CI suites. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32076643369](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32076643369)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32076642814](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32076642814)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [Scheduler] Release all request-owned KV on no-insert cleanup
signal.text: ## Why `RadixCache.cache_finished_req(..., is_insert=False)` discards a request without inserting its KV into the radix cache. The old implementation derived the release range from committed token IDs rather than from `kv_len_to_handle`. Under overlap scheduling, a forward pass can commit a KV slot before its sampled output token is accepted, leaving the token-ID list one element shorter and leaking the final request-owned slot. ## Ownership contract - `[0, cache_protected_len)` is cache-owned and must be preserved. - `[cache_protected_len, kv_len_to_handle)` is request-owned committed KV and must be released on no-insert cleanup. - Overallocated KV after `kv_len_to_handle` is released by `release_kv_cache`. ## Change - Release the request-owned committed range directly from the request-to-token mapping with the existing `free_segment` allocator primitive. - Release the request's radix-node lock as before. - Leave the normal cache-insertion path unchanged. - Extend the existing matched-prefix failure test to cover a committed KV slot with no corresponding output token. ## Validation - Focused registered unit test: 6 passed on one H200 using `lmsysorg/sglang:nightly-dev-cu13-20260817-d91c3682`. - Repository pre-commit checks passed for both changed files, including the registered-test validator. - `git diff --check` passed. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32076641901](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32076641901)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32076641658](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32076641658)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: Support sampling masks without finite top-k
signal.text: ## Context #27408 introduced sampling-mask responses with finite `top_k` as the bound on reconstruction and returned metadata. #33593 admitted top-p-only mask requests and exposed the feature through the OpenAI chat extension. However, `top_p < 1` does not bound realized support: depending on the distribution, a mask can still approach the full vocabulary. #35205 restores the finite-`top_k` requirement while this general case is designed. #34037 contains an initial implementation exploring faithful support capture, fixed transport capacity, and explicit bounded output. ## Goal Support `return_sampling_mask` without finite `top_k` while preserving the requested sampling distribution, bounding serving work and transport, and giving clients an unambiguous response contract. ## Requirements - Define support from the post-filter distribution used to sample the token, including backend cutoff-tie semantics. - Restrict support computation and transfer to requests that opt in. - Bound transport independently of `top_k`, `top_p`, and `min_p`. - Never silently present partial support as exact. - Define exact overflow behavior and, if bounded output is supported, expose truncation explicitly per token. - Keep the selected-token logprob normalized over the complete sampling distribution rather than a truncated response. - Preserve the contract through batching, TP/CP, pipeline parallelism, streaming, sessions, and prefill/decode disaggregation. - Add correctness coverage across supported sampling backends and measure feature-on and feature-off overhead.
signal.author: nanjiangwill

signal.title: Support GPT-OSS MXFP4 checkpoints on Intel XPU
signal.text: ## Motivation `openai/gpt-oss-20b` and `-120b` ship MXFP4-quantized MoE weights. SGLang's MXFP4 support targets CUDA (`triton_kernels` / Marlin / FlashInfer cutlass), HIP (aiter) and CPU (AMX), so on `--device xpu` the checkpoint is rejected before any layer is built: ``` ValueError: Unknown quantization method: mxfp4. Must be one of ['fp8', 'mxfp8', ...] configs/model_config.py:1588 in _verify_quantization ``` `mxfp4.py` already contains a device-neutral fallback that upcasts MXFP4 to bf16 once at load time and serves through the ordinary unquantized MoE. This PR makes that existing path reachable and functional off-CUDA; no new kernel or backend is introduced. ## Modifications Two files, `+69/-15`. **1. Register `mxfp4` for XPU** — `layers/quantization/__init__.py` ```diff -if is_cpu() or is_cuda() or _is_gfx95_supported: +if is_cpu() or is_cuda() or is_xpu() or _is_gfx95_supported: ``` **2. Device-neutral chunked upcast** — new `_upcast_mxfp4_to_bf16()` in `mxfp4.py` The generic branch of `process_weights_after_loading` imported `triton_kernels.numerics_details.mxfp.upcast_from_mxfp`, which is CUDA/HIP-only. The helper prefers it when importable and otherwise runs a pure-torch upcast, so **CUDA behavior is unchanged**. Chunking is required, not stylistic. `MXFP4QuantizeUtil.dequantize` in `mxfp4_tensor.py` computes identical values but whole-tensor: it promotes unpacked nibbles to `int64` for the LUT gather and builds `float32` sign/magnitude temporaries, so one `w13_weight` expands to several GB and exhausts a 24 GB card. The helper writes bf16 directly into a preallocated output in row chunks, matching the strategy in transformers' `_convert_moe_packed_tensors(rows_per_chunk=...)`. **3. `torch.cuda.empty_cache()` -> `empty_device_cache()`** in the generic post-load path. The two remaining calls in this file are inside SM90-cutlass / trtllm helpers that cannot run on XPU and are left untouched. **4. Pad the MoE intermediate on this path** `models/gpt_oss.py:985` shards by whole MXFP4 blocks: ```python per_rank_intermediate_size_block = math.ceil(intermediate_size_block / moe_tp_size) per_rank_intermediate_size = per_rank_intermediate_size_block * mxfp4_block ``` For gpt-oss-20b at tp=4 that is `ceil(90/4) * 32 = 736`, while `intermediate_size_per_partition` is `2880/4 = 720`, so the rank's slice is larger than its nominal share and the loader's copy overflows: ``` RuntimeError: The size of tensor a (360) must match the size of tensor b (368) at non-singleton dimension 2 ``` Every other branch in `create_weights` absorbs this in its own alignment (64 for triton_kernels, 128 for Marlin/cutlass, 256 for aiter) — which is what the function's existing comment says the padding is for. This path had none. Padding is numerically inert: the extra `w13` rows stay zero, so gate and up are zero, and the matching `w2` columns contribute nothing. Note this is **latent for any non-padding backend**, not XPU-specific; it only appears when `intermediate_size / tp` is not a multiple of 32, which is why tp=1 and tp=2 never hit it. Scoped to `is_xpu()` to keep the diff reviewable — happy to generalize it to a default if maintainers prefer. ## Accuracy Tests The upcast is the only change that touches numerics. It is **bit-exact** (`torch.equal`, no tolerance) against transformers' `_convert_moe_packed_tensors`, the reference unpacking used for `Mxfp4Config(dequantize=True)`, on random packed data shaped like a real expert weight (`[4, 64, 2880]`, full byte range, exponents 90-160): | Case | Result | |---|---| | CPU vs transformers | bit-exact | | XPU vs transformers | bit-exact | | XPU, `rows_per_chunk=1000` (forces mid-tensor chunk boundaries) | bit-exact | End-to-end on 4x Intel Arc Pro B60, `gpt-oss-20b`, tp=4, `--attention-backend intel_xpu`. Server reaches `ready to roll`; 10.39 GB/rank. Streaming reasoning (`--reasoning-parser gpt-oss`): ``` Prompt: Solve this problem step by step: What is 15% of 240? Thinking: 15% of 240 means 0.15 * 240 ... Response: ... 5. Result: 36 Verification: 10 % of 240 = 24, 5 % of 240 = 12, sum = 36 ``` Streaming tool calling (`--tool-call-parser gpt-oss`): ``` Tool call: get_weather({"location": "Beijing", "unit": "celsius"}) Final answer: The current weather in Beijing is 22 C and sunny. ``` **Benchmark accuracy is not yet run.** Because this path serves dequantized weights, the published MXFP4 numbers should not be assumed to carry over, and GSM8K needs measuring against the reference 0.535 for 20b before this leaves draft. Flagging rather than glossing over. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Not run. This changes weight preparation at load time only; the forward path is the existing unquantized MoE. Load time is 5.3 s/rank for 20b at tp=4. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Known limitations - **gpt-oss-120b is untested.** ~235 GB of dequantized bf16 will not fit in 96 GB of XPU memory; 120b likely needs a real MXFP4 MoE kernel rather than this upcast. - Serving dequantized weights forgoes the memory saving of MXFP4. This is functional enablement, not a performance path. - Requires capping context/concurrency on 24 GB cards; with defaults, SGLang derives `context_len=131072` / `max_running_requests=3764` and warmup OOMs allocating the attention page table. ## Remaining before undraft 1. GSM8K on 20b vs the 0.535 reference. 2. Unit test pinning `_upcast_mxfp4_to_bf16` bit-exactness against a stored reference vector. 3. Maintainer call on the two scoping questions above (XPU-gated vs. general fix for items 1 and 4). <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32416346228](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32416346228)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32416345862](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32416345862)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32416346390](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32416346390)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [AMD] Fix Load and Inference of MLA models with Quark PTPC FP8 attention on ROCm
signal.text: ## Motivation Loading and running MLA models (like `GlmMoeDsaForCausalLM`) with quark-quantized MXFP4 weights + per-token-per-channel FP8 attention on ROCm/gfx95 fails with multiple errors. The root cause is that the aiter gfx95 `_gfx95_quant_format="fp8"` path fuses RMSNorm + FP8 quantization into a single kernel (`fused_rms_fp8_group_quant`), passing pre-quantized **tuples** instead of plain bf16 tensors downstream. This pattern was already handled for compressed_tensors attention quantization across three prior PRs: - **#12181** added the `apply_fp8_ptpc_linear` routing in `compressed_tensors_w8a8_fp8.py` for pre-quantized tuple inputs - **#21403** added the `isinstance(input, tuple)` branch in `apply_fp8_ptpc_linear` itself - **#22258** added the 3-tuple `(fp8, scale, bf16)` passthrough from `fused_rms_fp8_group_quant` in `communicator.py`, and the corresponding unwrap in `dsa_indexer._project_and_scale_head_gates` None of these extended to **quark** attention quantization, and this PR closes that gap. ## Modifications **`fp8_utils.py`: `channel_quant_to_tensor_quant`** Reshape 1D per-channel scale `[N]` -> `[N, 1]` before multiplying against the 2D weight. Quark's `kv_b_proj` has a per-channel FP8 weight with a 1D scale vector that failed to broadcast correctly against the `[N, K]` weight. **`fp8_utils.py`: `apply_fp8_ptpc_linear`** Unpack pre-quantized input tuple as `input[0], input[1]` instead of destructuring, to tolerate both 2-tuples and 3-tuples (the 3-tuple was introduced in #22258 but the unpack assumed exactly 2 elements). **`quark_w8a8_fp8.py`: `apply_weights`** Mirror the handling that #12181 added to `compressed_tensors_w8a8_fp8.apply_weights`, extended for quark's weight layout and both tuple formats Note: unlike compressed_tensors which stores `shuffle(w)`, quark stores `shuffle(w).t()`, making the weight layout incompatible with `apply_fp8_ptpc_linear`/`gemm_a8w8_bpreshuffle`; So we dequantize to bf16 and use the existing `apply_fp8_linear` path without requiring weight storage changes. **`dsa_indexer.py`: `_get_q_k_bf16` and `_get_k_bf16`** Mirror the unwrap added in #22258 for `_project_and_scale_head_gates`, applied to the two remaining methods that also receive `x` and call `self.wk`. ## Validation Accuracy is evaluated using [lm_eval](https://github.com/EleutherAI/lm-evaluation-harness) on MI355X. Model: GLM-5.2 (`GlmMoeDsaForCausalLM`) with routed and shared experts quantized to MXFP4 and self-attention projections quantized to PTPC FP8. | Task | flexible-extract | strict-match | |---|---|---| | GSM8K | 93.93% ± 0.66% | 93.71% ± 0.67% | ## Reproduction ### Launch server ```bash SGLANG_USE_AITER=1 sglang serve \ --model-path amd/GLM-5.2-MXFP4-AttnFP8 \ --trust-remote-code --tp 8 \ --json-model-override-args '{"qk_rope_head_dim": 64}' \ --speculative-algorithm EAGLE \ --speculative-num-steps 5 \ --speculative-eagle-topk 1 \ --speculative-num-draft-tokens 6 \ --mem-fraction-static 0.8 \ --chunked-prefill-size 16384 \ --watchdog-timeout 1200 \ --model-loader-extra-config '{"enable_multithread_load": true, "num_threads": 8}' \ --host 127.0.0.1 --port 30000 ``` ### Accuracy ```bash lm_eval --model local-completions \ --model_args model=amd/GLM-5.2-MXFP4-AttnFP8,base_url=http://localhost:30000/v1/completions,num_concurrent=128,max_retries =10,max_gen_toks=2048,timeout=60000 \ --batch_size auto --tasks gsm8k --num_fewshot 8 ``` <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:no_entry_sign: [Run #32428200148](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32428200148)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32428199997](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32428199997)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #32428200125](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32428200125)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: Add Cloud Agent dev environment (CPU: lint + Rust services)
signal.text:
## Summary Adds a Cursor Cloud Agent development environment for SGLang via `.cursor/environment.json` (repo-managed) + an idempotent `.cursor/install.sh`. It uses Cursor's default base image and installs everything from the install script, so merging this PR activates the environment for future Cloud Agents on `main` automatically (no dashboard Save needed). The Cloud Agent VM is CPU-only, so this environment targets the parts of SGLang that build and run without a GPU: - The contributor lint/CI toolchain (`pre-commit`), mirroring the `Lint` GitHub Actions workflow (isort, ruff, black, codespell, clang-format, nbstripout, the local lint-script unit tests, and all Rust `rustfmt`/`clippy` hooks). - The Rust workspaces: `rust/` (gRPC / multimodal / server crates) and `sgl-model-gateway/` (the router / control plane), both buildable and testable on CPU. The full CUDA serving stack (`torch==2.13.0`, flashinfer, sgl-kernel, ...) needs an NVIDIA GPU and the `lmsysorg/sglang` image, and is intentionally out of scope for this CPU environment. ## What `install.sh` does 1. Installs the system build deps the default image is missing: - `libstdc++-14-dev` — `esaxx-rs` (pulled in by the HuggingFace `tokenizers` crate) is compiled by clang, which targets the gcc-14 libstdc++ headers; the base image ships only `libstdc++-13-dev`, so `` is otherwise unresolved. - `libssl-dev` / `pkg-config` — cover any `openssl-sys` build. - `protobuf-compiler` + `libprotobuf-dev` — the gateway's `smg-grpc-client` uses `prost-build` with a system `protoc` (no vendored fallback) plus the well-known types (`google/protobuf/*.proto`). - `redis-server` — the gateway's Redis history-backend integration test spawns a local instance. 2. Installs `pre-commit` and warms all hook environments. 3. Installs a nightly `rustfmt` (used by the fmt hooks) and builds the `rust/` workspace and `sgl-model-gateway`. ## Validation Validated on the CPU VM: - `pre-commit run --all-files` — all hooks pass (Python + clang-format + Rust fmt/clippy). - `cd rust && cargo test --workspace` — 287 tests pass. - `cd sgl-model-gateway && cargo test` — 840 tests pass. - Install idempotence — re-running `install.sh` is a clean no-op (~9s). - End-to-end: launched `sgl-model-gateway`, confirmed `/liveness` returns `200 OK`, `/parse/reasoning` splits `` reasoning from the answer, and `/parse/function_call` extracts the tool call. Validated via a prebuilt environment build (fresh cold build on the default image from this branch, then verified in a fresh Cloud Agent booted from that exact build): - Build `bld-20260820-9eb4ff4e` (default image + `install.sh`, cold) — SUCCEEDED, all 5 install phases green. - Fresh Cloud Agent from that build — 6/6 checks pass: toolchains present, all gateway binaries + rust libs built, `pre-commit run --all-files` all-pass, `rust/` tests 287/0, and the gateway `/liveness` + `/parse/reasoning` e2e both return HTTP 200.

signal.title: [fmha_v2] perf: use non-interleaved paged KV input for trtllm sm90/120 prefill
signal.text: <!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. --> ## Motivation Dependent on https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/23112 and https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/4124. Improves TRT-LLM SM90/120 prefill performance to beat FA3 by removing an expensive copy-operation that was previously needed to pass interleaved KV to the kernel API. ## Modifications Allocate KV together (no functional change to any other backend), allowing us to use the new indexing mode to read data efficiently for fmha_v2. > the below accuracy/perf data was collected and summarized by Claude ## Accuracy Tests PQA Diamond, 198 questions x 8 repeats (1,584 rollouts per config), temperature 0.6, top-k 20, max-tokens 81920. **Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B-Thinking-FP8:** | Config | KV dtype | Score | Repeat range | |---|---|---|---| | FA3 | bf16 | 0.725 | 0.712-0.742 | | fmha_v2 (trtllm_mha) | bf16 | 0.723 | 0.702-0.753 | | FA3 + MTP | bf16 | 0.734 | 0.712-0.758 | | fmha_v2 prefill + MTP (fa3 verify) | bf16 | 0.721 | 0.707-0.732 | | FA3 | fp8_e4m3 | 0.727 | 0.707-0.747 | | **fmha_v2 (trtllm_mha)** | **fp8_e4m3** | **0.724** | 0.682-0.753 | Per-repeat std is ~0.015, so every row is a tie. The fp8 fmha_v2 row ran the **zero-copy path in this PR**, making it a 1,584-rollout validation of the new KV addressing against the e4m3 kernel. **Qwen3-32B-FP8, fp8 KV:** | Config | Score | Range | |---|---|---| | FA3 | 0.630 | 0.606-0.677 | | fmha_v2 | **0.630** | 0.606-0.657 | Exact tie. **MTP acceptance** (draft/target property -- matching rates show fmha_v2 prefill does not perturb the target distribution): | Config | Accept len | Accept rate | |---|---|---| | FA3 + MTP (bf16) | 2.37 | 0.46 | | fmha_v2 prefill + MTP (bf16) | 2.45 | 0.48 | <details> <summary>Repro</summary> ```bash python3 -m sglang.test.run_eval --port 30000 --eval-name gpqa \ --num-examples 198 --repeat 8 --num-threads 16 \ --max-tokens 81920 --thinking-mode qwen-3 --temperature 0.6 --top-k 20 ``` </details> ## Speed Tests and Profiling **Before/after on identical config** (Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B-Thinking-FP8, bf16 KV, `--chunked-prefill-size 2048`). "Before" is the original `torch.stack([k_cache, v_cache], dim=1)` full-pool copy; "after" is this PR's non-interleaved zero-copy path. | ISL | metric | before (stack) | after (zero-copy) | FA3 | |---|---|---|---|---| | 1k | total tok/s | 11017 | **14940** | 14833 | | 1k | median TTFT (ms) | 1696 | **719** | 841 | | 8k | input tok/s | 13853 | **22266** | 22982 | | 8k | median TTFT (ms) | 6566 | **2952** | 2713 | | 128k | input tok/s | 14859 | **25506** | 29363 | | 128k | median TTFT (ms) | 11215 | **5706** | 4764 | **Root cause of the "before" column** (torch profiler, 2.7k-token request, 24 prefill / 384 decode layer-calls): | | fmha_v2 (stack) | FA3 | |---|---|---| | prefill attention | 1.59 ms | 0.98 ms | | decode attention | 15.4 ms (bf16 XQA) | 6.8 ms | | KV-pool stack copy | **120.5 ms** (`direct_copy_kernel`, 1008 calls) | -- | The stack copied the entire per-layer KV pool (~4 GB, ~5 ms) per prefill layer call, per chunk, regardless of batch size. Causality check -- only the pool size varies: | mem-fraction-static | KV pool per side | input tok/s @8k | median TTFT (ms) | |---|---|---|---| | 0.8 | 24.0 GB | 13853 | 6566 | | 0.55 | 15.0 GB | 19292 | 3809 | **At the default chunk size** (fp8 KV, `--chunked-prefill-size 8192`; code pinned via git worktrees, sglang@3c02143bb7 + flashinfer fmha_v2_test = perf_qtile@2a14301a + cherry-picked 49b01545). signal.title: Fix _GenerationStreamAccumulator logprob_end off-by-one under retract
signal.text: ## Summary Fix an output-logprob cursor off-by-one when overlap scheduling retracts an in-flight request before its prefill result is processed. The fix is deliberately retraction-specific. Non-retracted prefill-only requests with `max_new_tokens=0` retain the existing behavior of returning their first logprob. ## Root cause Under overlap scheduling and retraction: 1. A prefill forward pass is launched. 2. The request is retracted while that pass is in flight, setting `req.is_retracted = True`. 3. `process_batch_result_prefill` skips appending the sampled token for that request, but still passes the full batch to the output streamer. 4. For a non-streaming request with no output IDs, the forced-stream condition is true because `0 % DEFAULT_FORCE_STREAM_INTERVAL == 0`. 5. `max(len(output_ids_), 1)` advances `send_output_token_logprobs_offset` to 1 while `send_token_offset` remains 0. Every later output is therefore shifted by one logprob, and the final response has one fewer output logprob than output token. ## Fix ```python logprob_end = ( len(output_ids_) if req.is_retracted else max(len(output_ids_), 1) ) ``` For a retracted request with no output IDs, both cursors stay at zero. For a legitimate non-retracted prefill-only request, the existing first-logprob behavior remains intact. ## Tests - Added CPU unit coverage that verifies a retracted empty-output request does not advance its logprob cursor. - Added CPU unit coverage that verifies a non-retracted `max_new_tokens=0` request still returns its first logprob. - Kept the end-to-end forced-retraction regression and registered it in CUDA `base-b` and AMD `stage-b-test-1-gpu-small-amd` CI. - Ran all pre-commit hooks on the changed files successfully. - Ran Python syntax compilation successfully. - The focused runtime unit test was not run locally because this bare checkout lacks SGLang runtime dependencies; it is registered with CPU CI. The original end-to-end reproduction produced 2/32 mismatched responses in five consecutive pre-fix trials and 0/32 in eight consecutive post-fix trials. ## Checklist - [x] Format code with pre-commit. - [x] Add regression coverage. - [x] Preserve prefill-only logprob behavior raised in review. - [x] Rebase onto current upstream `main`. cc @Qiaolin-Yu <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:no_entry_sign: [Run #32424716944](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32424716944)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32424716741](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32424716741)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:no_entry_sign: [Run #32424716660](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32424716660)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [WIP][Feature] Beam search dev branch
signal.text: Beam search as a per-request feature: `sampling_params.beam_width = k` returns the top-`n` sequences. No server flag; beam and ordinary requests share the same batches and memory pools. ## Results `Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B-Base`, 1x H200, `beam_width = 5000`. End-to-end latency (ms): | output tokens | sync mean / p50 / p90 | overlap mean / p50 / p90 | |---|---|---| | 3 | 244.6 / 158.0 / 469.0 | 259.1 / 176.6 / 470.4 | | 16 | 927.7 / 1028.8 / 1120.6 | 903.9 / 957.6 / 1361.7 | | 32 | 1690.7 / 1788.6 / 1827.3 | 1650.9 / 1716.8 / 2003.0 | | 64 | 3511.0 / 3554.1 / 3697.7 | 3303.3 / 3277.3 / 3506.5 | | 128 | 8087.3 / 8267.2 / 8655.6 | 7067.0 / 7164.5 / 7201.3 | Forward-pass occupancy under saturated load, `sglang:fwd_occupancy` median / whole-device utilization: 43.7% / 67% (16 tokens, sync), 46.9% / 87% (64, sync), 46.5% / 83% (16, overlap), 50.1% (64, overlap). ## Repro ```bash python -m sglang.launch_server \ --model-path Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B-Base \ --host 127.0.0.1 --port 30000 \ --dtype bfloat16 --attention-backend flashinfer \ --mem-fraction-static 0.4 --max-running-requests 20004 \ --context-length 4096 --random-seed 0 --enable-metrics \ --disable-radix-cache --disable-chunked-prefix-cache # add --disable-overlap-schedule for the sync column ``` ```python # beam_len_sweep.py -- latency vs output length at fixed beam width import argparse, asyncio, statistics, time, aiohttp PROMPTS = [ "Required Requirements: software engineer with Java and distributed systems experience.", "Senior data scientist with machine learning, Python, and large-scale experimentation expertise.", "Product manager with B2B SaaS and go-to-market experience.", "Staff backend engineer specializing in Kafka, gRPC, and high-throughput services.", ] async def main(a): sem = asyncio.Semaphore(a.concurrency) t0 = time.perf_counter() async def one(session, i): await asyncio.sleep(max(0.0, t0 + i / a.qps - time.perf_counter())) async with sem: start = time.perf_counter() async with session.post( f"{a.url}/generate", json={ "text": PROMPTS[i % len(PROMPTS)], "sampling_params": { "max_new_tokens": a.max_new_tokens, "n": a.beam_width, "beam_width": a.beam_width, }, }, ) as r: body = await r.json(content_type=None) beams = body.get("meta_info", {}).get("beam_results") or [] assert r.status == 200 and len(beams) == a.beam_width, (r.status, len(beams)) return (time.perf_counter() - start) * 1000 async with aiohttp.ClientSession(timeout=aiohttp.ClientTimeout(total=1800)) as s: lat = sorted(await asyncio.gather(*[one(s, i) for i in range(a.num_requests)])) print( f"len={a.max_new_tokens} n={len(lat)} mean={statistics.mean(lat):.1f} " f"p50={lat[len(lat) // 2]:.1f} p90={lat[int(len(lat) * 0.9)]:.1f}" ) p = argparse.ArgumentParser() p.add_argument("--url", default="http://127.0.0.1:30000") p.add_argument("--beam-width", type=int, default=5000) p.add_argument("--max-new-tokens", type=int, default=16) p.add_argument("--num-requests", type=int, default=10) p.add_argument("--qps", type=float, default=0.3) p.add_argument("--concurrency", type=int, default=2) asyncio.run(main(p.parse_args())) ``` Per-row `(max_new_tokens, num_requests, qps, concurrency)`: `(3, 23, 0.8, 4)`, `(16, 10, 0.3, 2)`, `(32, 8, 0.25, 2)`, `(64, 6, 0.2, 2)`, `(128, 4, 0.15, 2)`. For the occupancy row, relaunch with `SGLANG_ENABLE_METRICS_DEVICE_TIMER=1` and `--decode-log-interval 2`, drive `--qps 100`, and take the median of `sglang:fwd_occupancy` from `/metrics`. `--decode-log-interval 1` reports `NaN` there: the window resets every batch and never reaches the branch that computes the ratio, so 2 is the smallest usable value. ## Verification - Unit tests (`beam_search`, managers, mem_cache): 2062 passed, 0 failed. - HF parity (`test/manual/beam_search/test_beam_parity.py`): sequence-set overlap 8/10 at `k = 10`. - Load (`test/manual/beam_search/test_beam_search_load.py`): mixed widths 2-100, 100 requests at 10 QPS, p50/p90/p99 = 53/58/175 ms; 3200-wide fan-out passes. - Beam mixed with ordinary penalized requests in the same batches: 36/36. - `SGLANG_ENABLE_STRICT_MEM_CHECK_DURING_BUSY=1` silent throughout, sync and overlap. - Sync and overlap agree digest-for-digest. - Ordinary-path regression: `few_shot_gsm8k` 200q greedy scores 0.470 unchanged. ## Not supported yet Rejected at admission with an explicit error: speculative decoding, PD disaggregation, `page_size > 1`, pipeline parallelism, hierarchical cache, SWA/mamba hybrid caches, encoder-decoder, LoRA, diffusion LLM, sessions, constrained decoding, stop strings/regex, `min_new_tokens`, `return_logprob`, `return_hidden_states`; also excluded from mixed-chunk prefill batches. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32426521577](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32426521577)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32426521400](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32426521400)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32426521540](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32426521540)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [AMD] Add ROCm 7.14 (gfx942 / gfx950) release
signal.text: ## Motivation ROCm 7.14 is published only as pip wheels and docker images — `repo.radeon.com` has no apt repo for it — so its stack has to be assembled from AMD's ROCm pip channels on top of `ubuntu:24.04`. That places the SDK in `site-packages` instead of `/opt/rocm`, which the existing stages of `docker/rocm.Dockerfile` assume throughout. This PR adds gfx942 and gfx950 ROCm 7.14 stages built that way, plus the adjustments the pip-SDK layout forces on the existing build and CI steps. The index is `https://repo.amd.com/rocm/whl-multi-arch/`, AMD's release channel. Deliberately not the nightly or devrelease channels: those get pruned. An earlier revision of this PR pinned a 7.15 nightly (`7.15.0a20260712`) because 7.15 never had a stable release — the line ran from `7.15.0a20260626` to `7.15.0a20260728` and was then renumbered 10.0 — which would have left this Dockerfile unbuildable, and the image unreproducible, once that nightly aged out of the index. 7.14 is a released SDK, so the pin is stable. torch is 2.11, the same as the `rocm724` flavors already on `main`, so the 7.14 stages reuse the existing `*_rocm724` extras for the `compressed-tensors` 0.16.0 pin rather than adding a third hand-synced copy of the same dependency list. `python/pyproject_other.toml` is unchanged by this PR. The `rocm7_15` / gfx1250 stage and its workflow are untouched. ## Modifications ### `docker/rocm.Dockerfile` - Added a shared `rocm714-base` stage: `ubuntu:24.04` + Python 3.12 in a venv + the ROCm 7.14 pip stack — `rocm-sdk-{core,libraries,devel,device-gfx942,device-gfx950}==7.14.0`, `torch`/`torchaudio` `2.11.0+rocm7.14.0`, `torchvision 0.26.0+rocm7.14.0`, `triton 3.7.1+git0263a6a6.rocm7.14.0`. - Added two thin per-arch stages, `gfx942-rocm714` and `gfx950-rocm714`, which set build flags and `PIP_CONSTRAINT`. Both arches' torch device wheels go into the shared base; `GPU_ARCH_LIST` still narrows what AITER and sgl-kernel actually compile for. - `BASE_IMAGE_942_ROCM714` / `BASE_IMAGE_950_ROCM714` default to the `rocm714-base` stage rather than a published image. Naming them keeps these stages shaped like every other stage in this file, which matters because `scripts/ci/amd/amd_ci_install_dependency.sh` locates a stage's `AITER_COMMIT_DEFAULT` by grepping for `FROM $BASE_IMAGE_<arch><suffix> AS <arch><suffix>`. They can also be pointed at a prebuilt image to skip building the base. - Single `--index-url`; the release index mirrors the PyPI packages torch pulls in, so no `--extra-index-url` and no `--pre` are needed. - torch and torchvision device wheels are named as separate specs rather than combined device extras. Several device extras in one spec (`torch[device-gfx942,device-gfx950]`) silently installs only the first, and the missing arch then fails at runtime with `hipErrorInvalidImage`. - Python 3.12 (the Ubuntu 24.04 default) rather than 3.13/3.14: `st_attn==0.0.7`, `vsa==0.0.4`, `petit_kernel==0.0.2` and `wave-lang==3.8.2` publish wheels only up to cp313 and no sdist, so on 3.14 pip has no candidate at all for `srt_hip`. - Path fixups for the non-`/opt/rocm` SDK: `ROCM_HOME` / `ROCM_PATH` / `CPATH` / `LIBRARY_PATH` / `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` point at the site-packages `_rocm_sdk_devel` tree; a `/opt/rocm` symlink because AITER shells out to `/opt/rocm/llvm/bin/amdgpu-arch` to pick `DEFAULT_GPU_ARCH` and the rest of this Dockerfile refers to `/opt/rocm`; and a `/usr/lib64/libc.so` symlink because the SDK's `hsakmtTargets.cmake` hardcodes that path from its own build host. - libdrm: skipped for `*rocm714*`. The pip SDK's `libdrm_amdgpu.so` links the device-ID table in rather than reading `share/libdrm/amdgpu.ids` — the `.so` carries the MI300X / MI325X / MI355X names and never opens that file — so the apt step the 7.2.4 flavor needs is unnecessary here. - amdsmi: installed for `*rocm714*` (same branch as the 7.2 flavors), since the pip SDK does not pre-install it. - `PIP_CONSTRAINT`: the 7.14 stages define and populate it the same way the `rocm724` stages do, so resolving AITER and SGLang dependencies cannot swap the image's ROCm torch for a PyPI CUDA build. - MORI: point the build at the SDK's vendored `lib/rocm_sysdeps` tree via `CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH` / `CPATH` / `LIBRARY_PATH` plus an `ldconfig` entry, for NUMA (`hsakmt-config.cmake` calls `find_dependency(NUMA)`) and libdrm (`rocm_smi.h` includes `<libdrm/drm.h>`, `mori_application` links `-ldrm`/`-ldrm_amdgpu`). Guarded on the directory existing, so the apt-based ROCm images keep their current behaviour. - nixl: the existing `libabsl-dev` removal is extended to `*-rocm714`, which is on the same Ubuntu 24.04 base as `rocm724` and hits the same meson/abseil conflict. - The SGLang install and the post-install validation step both treat `rocm714` like `rocm724`. ### `scripts/ci/amd/amd_ci_install_dependency.sh` - Recognise `-rocm714` in the image `GPU_ARCH` stamp and map it to `_ROCM714` / `-rocm714` so the AITER pin lookup finds the right Dockerfile stage. - Select the `dev_hip_rocm724` extras for `-rocm714` as well, matching what the Dockerfile does at build time. Without this a 7.14 image would get `compressed-tensors` 0.15.0, which requires `torch<2.11`, and the resolve would fail. - Apply the same `rocm_sysdeps` handling to the in-image MORI rebuild, kept scoped to that build instead of exported image-wide because `rocm_sysdeps/include` also carries `zlib.h` / `expat.h` / `elf.h`, which would shadow the system headers for every other component. ### `.github/workflows/release-docker-amd-rocm714-nightly.yml` - New workflow, following this repo's one-file-per-ROCm-version convention (`rocm700` / `rocm720` / `rocm7_15`), with a `gfx942-rocm714` / `gfx950-rocm714` matrix and `rocm714-mi30x` / `rocm714-mi35x` tags. The `rocm7_15` workflow is not modified. - The schedule is commented out for now; the workflow is dispatch-only until the gfx950 leg has had a green run. ## Accuracy Tests All of the following was run on an MI300X host (gfx942). **1. Image build.** `GPU_ARCH=gfx942-rocm714` builds end to end, all 34 steps, 45.8 GB image. The in-image validation step reports: ``` Validated ROCm stack: {'torch': '2.11.0+rocm7.14.0', 'torchaudio': '2.11.0+rocm7.14.0', 'torchvision': '0.26.0+rocm7.14.0', 'triton': '3.7.1'} HIP 7.14.60850 ``` with `pip check` clean and no `nvidia-*-cu*` packages pulled in. **2. In-image smoke test on real hardware.** 8 devices visible, `get_device_name(0)` is `AMD Instinct MI300X` (correct marketing name with no `amdgpu.ids` file present, confirming the ids table is linked into the SDK's libdrm), `gcnArchName` is `gfx942:sramecc+:xnack-`, a bf16 matmul on device returns finite values, and `triton`, `torchvision`, `torchaudio`, `aiter`, `mori`, `tilelang`, `nixl`, `amdsmi`, `sglang` and `compressed_tensors` (0.16.0, i.e. the right extras were selected) all import. **3. CI dependency install.** `scripts/ci/amd/amd_ci_install_dependency.sh` exits 0 against a `ci_sglang` container started from the image. The parts this PR touches behave as intended: ``` [CI-IMAGE] Image GPU_ARCH=gfx942-rocm714 Image torch 2.11.0+rocm7.14.0, HIP 7.14.60850; installing python extras: [dev_hip_rocm724,tracing] [CI-AITER-CHECK] Using FROM $BASE_IMAGE_942_ROCM714 AS gfx942-rocm714 from Dockerfile... [CI-AITER-CHECK] Dockerfile expects AITER_COMMIT=d9e5ef7ce08ee7045d583aed768cff41aa9210fe [CI-AITER-CHECK] AITER version inside CI image: v0.1.20.dev12+gd9e5ef7ce [MORI] Reinstalling MORI 12d1bc32d0c93dcd5062e74f4e0f772e36e1aac4 (MORI_GPU_ARCHS=gfx942) [MORI] Done. ``` **4. CI test suite.** `run_suite.py --hw amd --suite stage-a-test-1-gpu-small-amd` reports **8/8 passed**, exit code 0: | Test | Result | Elapsed | | --- | --- | --- | | `attention/test_wave_attention_kernels.py` | pass | 73s | | `quant/test_fused_rms_fp8_group_quant.py` | pass | 20s | | `quant/test_awq_dequant.py` | pass | 22s | | `amd/test_fp8_per_channel_detection.py` | pass | 14s | | `core/test_basic_sanity.py` | pass | 396s | | `core/test_basic_sanity_eagle3.py` | pass | 220s | | `unit/mem_cache/test_umbp_store.py` | pass | 14s | | `unit/models/test_vit_pos_embed_interpolate.py` | pass | 16s | `test_umbp_store.py` passing is the relevant check for the MORI changes above: it exercises `mori.umbp`, which needs the gRPC symbols the rebuilt MORI must carry. **Both arches build.** `gfx950-rocm714` had never been built when the local verification above was done; it has since built successfully on CI, first try, in the same run as gfx942. See the upstream validation note below. What is still unverified for gfx950 is *runtime* behaviour — the only host available here is MI300X, so nothing has executed on MI355X hardware yet. **Upstream CI validation.** The workflow added here cannot be `workflow_dispatch`-ed until it exists on the default branch, so it is being exercised from a throwaway branch, `bingxche/rocm714-ci-test`, which carries this PR head plus a branch-scoped `push` trigger. That branch also redirects the images to a scratch repository (`bingxche/sgl-test`) so nothing unvalidated lands in `rocm/sgl-dev` or `lmsysorg/sglang-rocm`. Neither the trigger nor the scratch registry is part of this PR. [Run #32380153563](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32380153563) built and pushed both arches successfully: | Image | Size | | --- | --- | | `bingxche/sgl-test:v0.5.17-rocm714-mi30x-20260820` | 16.3 GB | | `bingxche/sgl-test:v0.5.17-rocm714-mi35x-20260820` | 16.5 GB | **Follow-up, not in this PR.** Wiring the AMD test workflows to pick a 7.14 image automatically needs two small changes elsewhere: `find_latest_image` in `scripts/ci/amd/amd_ci_start_container.sh` hardcodes `rocm/sgl-dev`, so the repository has to become configurable before images in any other namespace can be discovered; and `rocm714` needs to be an accepted `rocm_version` in `pr-test-amd-rocm720.yml` (plus a fallback entry in the same script). The arch selection itself already works by convention: the script maps the runner hostname to `mi30x` / `mi35x` and looks for `v<version>-<rocm_version>-<arch>-<date>`, which is exactly the tag shape the workflow here produces. **Note on reproducing the local build above:** `arrayref` 0.3.5-0.3.9 were briefly yanked on crates.io on 2026-08-20, which broke `blake3`'s `arrayref = "^0.3.5"` and with it the `sgl-model-gateway` step for every ROCm image build on `main`, not just this branch. They have since been un-yanked. The local verification above was done during that window with a `[patch.crates-io]` pointing `arrayref` at the authentic 0.3.9 artifact from `static.crates.io`; that patch was never part of this PR and nothing in the diff depends on it. ## Speed Tests and Profiling <!-- If this pull request impacts inference speed, provide benchmarking and profiling results. --> ## Checklist - [ ] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [ ] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. signal.title: [AMD] [sgl-kernel] Bypass caches for peer traffic in ROCm custom all-reduce
signal.text: <!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. --> ## Motivation Bypass caches for peer traffic in ROCm custom all-reduce ## Modifications The custom all-reduce reads every peer's buffer over xGMI and writes results peers consume once, so caching that traffic in L2 only pollutes the cache with single-use data. Route the packed 128-bit peer loads and result stores through cache-bypassing accessors modeled on RCCL's op128.h load128/store128. The bypass path is enabled via ROCM_HAVE_GLOBAL_DWORDX4_BUILTINS, derived from __has_builtin(__builtin_amdgcn_global_load_b128) && __has_builtin(__builtin_amdgcn_global_store_b128): when present, the b128 builtins with a system syncscope lower to global_{load,store}_dwordx4 with the sc0/sc1 cache-bypass bits set; otherwise it falls back to nontemporal (SLC) 64-bit accesses. All paths are guarded by USE_ROCM so CUDA builds are unchanged. ## Accuracy Tests Verified on gfx950 (MI35x): ISA confirms sc0/sc1 on the reduce kernel, and correctness passes for TP=2/4/8 (bitwise deterministic). ## Speed Tests and Profiling Deterministic all-reduce benchmark (TP=8, hidden=16384, bf16, 10 trials, deterministic-kernel latency in ms), baseline (ce1f2c6f4a) vs this change: batch tensor baseline bypass delta 1 32 KB 0.094 0.043 -54% 2 64 KB 0.034 0.029 -15% 4 128 KB 0.035 0.030 -14% 8 256 KB 0.038 0.032 -16% 16 512 KB 0.045 0.037 -18% 32 1 MB 0.059 0.046 -22% 64 2 MB 0.086 0.064 -26% 128 4 MB 0.146 0.100 -32% 256 8 MB 0.256 0.172 -33% 384 12 MB 0.365 0.250 -32% 512 16 MB 2.804 2.763 -1% 768 24 MB 3.054 2.940 -4% 1024 32 MB 3.276 3.052 -7% Within the custom-AR operating range (<=~8 MB) bypass consistently cuts latency ~14-33%, growing with size as L2 pollution matters more. Beyond that the 1-stage kernel is out of its intended regime (per-rank O(N) reads); bypass still never regresses. All sizes remain bitwise deterministic on both builds. ## Checklist - [ ] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [ ] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. signal.title: Fix graceful shutdown: drain survives group-delivered stop signals
signal.text: ## Motivation The tokenizer manager's graceful-drain path (`gracefully_exit` → `/health` 503 → wait for in-flight requests → `ShutdownReq` → kill) is bypassed when stop signals reach the **whole process group** rather than only the main process: - Scheduler and detokenizer subprocesses receive SIGINT and can exit through the default handler during a forward pass, severing in-flight streaming responses before the drain completes. - In the main process, SIGINT reaches uvicorn's default handler and begins shutting down the HTTP server instead of entering SGLang's drain path. Group delivery occurs with terminal Ctrl-C and with entrypoints or supervisors that forward signals to a process group, such as `tini -g`, `kill -- -PID` wrappers, or `killpg`-based supervisors. In our Modal canaries, SIGINT and SIGTERM both reached the SGLang process group within the same second, with their order varying between stops. Plain Kubernetes and `docker stop` normally send SIGTERM to the main process only. Those setups do not expose workers to group delivery, but this change still gives SIGINT the same drain behavior as SIGTERM and adds explicit escalation and timeout semantics. This was traced in production after a healthy container received a stop signal and returned 502s for its in-flight requests, including a 14-minute stream. With this patch, a canary on the same platform completed a rolling redeploy: workers survived the observed SIGINT/SIGTERM delivery, the drain armed, and the in-flight stream completed before shutdown with zero requests remaining. ## Modifications 1. **Worker subprocesses ignore SIGINT and SIGTERM.** `ignore_external_stop_signals()` is installed at worker process startup in `run_scheduler_process`, `run_detokenizer_process`, `run_multi_detokenizer_router_process`, and `run_data_parallel_controller_process`, and as the initializer for the multimodal preprocessing `ProcessPoolExecutor`. Worker lifecycle remains owned by the shutdown coordinator: drain, then `ShutdownReq`, then cleanup through `kill_process_tree`. 2. **SIGINT uses the graceful-drain handler.** The tokenizer manager handles SIGINT through the same path as SIGTERM, so Ctrl-C or group-delivered SIGINT drains instead of invoking uvicorn's default shutdown behavior. 3. **Distinct signals join the active drain; repetition escalates.** During a drain, the first occurrence of another signal kind is treated as part of the same stop event. Repeating an already-seen signal kind is treated as an explicit escalation and force-exits, abandoning in-flight requests. Deduplication is identity-based rather than time-window-based so closely delivered distinct signals are not mistaken for escalation. 4. **`SGLANG_GRACEFUL_SHUTDOWN_TIMEOUT` bounds the drain when configured.** The new float-valued environment variable is registered in `sglang/srt/environ.py`. Unset or `<= 0` preserves the existing unbounded wait, leaving the orchestrator's SIGKILL as the backstop. An invalid value logs a warning and falls back to no timeout. SIGQUIT crash cleanup and SIGKILL behavior are unchanged. ## Tests `test/registered/core/test_graceful_drain_signals.py` is registered in CPU CI (`base-a-test-cpu`) and covers: - workers ignoring group-delivered stop signals through a real process group (`killpg` with SIGTERM and SIGINT); - the first stop signal arming the drain, a distinct signal joining it, and a repeated signal forcing exit; - parsing valid `SGLANG_GRACEFUL_SHUTDOWN_TIMEOUT` values and tolerating invalid values. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32086531607](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32086531607)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32086531508](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32086531508)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: fix(openai): avoid duplicate routed expert in response when `return_meta_info = True`
signal.text: ## Summary Avoid duplicate routed-expert payloads in non-streaming chat completion responses. ## Symptom & Reproduction - **Symptom:** The base64 `routed_experts` payload appeared in both `choices[*].meta_info` and response-level `sglext` when both return flags were enabled. - **Reproduction:** Build and serialize a non-streaming `/v1/chat/completions` response with both flags enabled. - **Expected:** Each choice contains its routed experts once in `meta_info`. - **Observed before the fix:** `sglext.routed_experts` repeated the first choice's routed experts. ## Root Cause 1. `_build_chat_response` projected first-choice `routed_experts` into `SglExt`. 2. `choice_meta_info` serialized the same routed payload for every choice. ## Fix When `return_meta_info` is enabled, omit only response-level `sglext.routed_experts` and keep each choice's `meta_info` authoritative for routed experts. Independently requested `cached_tokens_details` and `spec_tokens_details` remain in `sglext`; `return_meta_info=false`, streaming chat, and `/v1/completions` behavior remain unchanged. ## Verification - `env PYTHONPATH=/tmp/sglang-dedupe-chat-meta-sglext/python python3 -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider test/registered/unit/entrypoints/openai/test_serving_chat.py test/registered/unit/entrypoints/openai/test_serving_completions.py`: 130 passed and 55 subtests passed. - `ruff check --ignore E402 python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/openai/serving_chat.py test/registered/unit/entrypoints/openai/test_serving_chat.py`: passed. - `ruff format --check python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/openai/serving_chat.py test/registered/unit/entrypoints/openai/test_serving_chat.py`: both files already formatted. - `git merge-tree --write-tree 1f87d8f512e09a6fe230da1e6d4ab228f6bbb91c 584a0880b29cbb5fa0db5a67e08ec8b8c8e0ffaf`: merged cleanly against `main@1f87d8f512e09a6fe230da1e6d4ab228f6bbb91c`. ## Review Focus - `_build_chat_response`: dual-flag requests must omit only response-level routed experts. - `SglExt`: cache/spec projections and their `n > 1` ordering must remain intact. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:no_entry_sign: [Run #32402094935](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32402094935)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32402094501](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32402094501)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:no_entry_sign: [Run #32402094636](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32402094636)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [RFC] Rust Tree Core Full Component
signal.text: ## Motivation UnifiedTreeCoreInterface support in Rust (focus on FULL component-only in this PR for early review feedbacks) ## Motivation The Unified Radix Cache was split so the tree state machine lives behind `UnifiedTreeCoreInterface`, selected by `SGLANG_UNIFIED_RADIX_TREE_CORE_BACKEND` (default `python`). This PR adds a Rust implementation of that interface as an in-tree backend registered under `rust`, covering the Full attention component. The tree core does the per-request radix walks, lock bookkeeping, and eviction scans on the scheduler's critical path; moving it to Rust takes that work off the GIL and smooths tail latency, while cache orchestration (pools, controller, action application) stays in Python. **Review guide**: the PR is two commits. The first seeds the three main Rust files with their python counterparts commented out; the second replaces them with the Rust implementation, so its diff reads as the python-to-rust translation side by side. Files without a direct python counterpart arrive as new files in the second commit. ## Modifications ### `rust/mem-cache/` — the tree core crate **Tree state machine** - `src/unified_tree_core.rs` — match/insert walks (resumable inserts with action barriers), lock APIs, device/host eviction walks, tombstone-chain deletion, HiCache backup/load-back/prefetch specs, and the sanity checker. - `src/node.rs` — the tree node: per-(component × tier) value slots and child edges keyed `(namespace, page key)`, mirroring `RadixKey.child_key`. - `src/node_arena.rs` — node storage: freelist-recycled slots behind monotonic never-recycled `NodeId` handles, with a single root serving every namespace. - `src/value.rs` — the `NodeId`/`NodeIdx_` handle types and per-slot value state. **Keys and hashing** - `src/key.rs` — the child-key trait over unigram (`Vec<i64>`) and bigram/EAGLE (`(i64, i64)`) page keys. - `src/hash.rs` — per-page SHA-256 hash chains, bit-identical to the python/native hasher. **Eviction machinery** - `src/unified_lru_list.rs` — intrusive per-slot LRU lists with lock-aware walkers. - `src/evictable_node_set.rs` — O(1) evictable-leaf sets (swap-remove vector plus a slot lookup table). - `src/eviction_strategy.rs` — LRU/FIFO/FILO priority keys for the eviction heap. **Components** - `src/components/mod.rs` — the `TreeComponent` trait the per-attention components implement, plus shared dispatch helpers. - `src/components/full.rs` — the Full attention component: lock walks, eviction, and transfer commits. Only the `[Full]` set is enabled; SWA and Mamba follow later. - `src/component_type.rs` — the `ComponentType` boundary enum (`FULL`/`SWA`/`MAMBA` values shared with python). **Boundary** - `src/python_bindings.rs` — the PyO3 binding exposing unigram and bigram tree cores; component sets other than `[Full]` are rejected with a clear error. - `src/events.rs` — KV cache events (`BlockStored`/`BlockRemoved`/`AllBlocksCleared`) for cache-aware routing. - `src/error.rs` — typed tree-core errors. **Crate scaffolding** - `Cargo.toml` / `README.md` / `src/lib.rs` — standalone crate (links libtorch via `tch`; PyO3 behind a default feature, so `cargo test` runs `--no-default-features`), docs, and module wiring. - `src/tests/` — the unit suite mirroring `src/` one file per module (566 tests, including a randomized multi-namespace op-sequence fuzz with per-step sanity checks). ### `python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/rust_tree_core/` — the backend package - `__init__.py` — registers the `rust` backend factory; the extension import stays inside the factory so unselected installs pay nothing. - `adapter.py` — `RustUnifiedTreeCore`, satisfying `UnifiedTreeCoreInterface` over the binding (tagged-tuple action/transfer marshaling at the boundary). - `extension.py` — build-and-load shim: compiles the crate with cargo on first use, deriving libtorch and the Python headers from the running interpreter's torch install, and rpaths torch/lib into the cdylib. ### Wiring and tests - `python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/unified_cache/tree_core_registry.py` — `SGLANG_UNIFIED_RADIX_TREE_CORE_BACKEND=rust` lazy-registers the in-tree backend on first lookup (no import-order dependence). - `test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_rust_tree_core.py` — end-to-end smoke through the compiled extension: registry resolution, insert/match round trip, lock accounting, and namespace isolation; module-skips when cargo is absent. ## Verification - `cargo test --no-default-features`: 566 passed. - Smoke suite: 4 passed end-to-end, including the first-use cargo build path. ## Perf Measurement & Accuracy TBD ## Review and Merge Process 1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process). 2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers. 3. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:no_entry_sign: [Run #32414095165](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32414095165)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32414095034](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32414095034)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #32414095095](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32414095095)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->
