signal.title: [Scheduler] Fix final chunked-prefill abort commit race
signal.text: ## Motivation Fixes #34149. Related prior report: #34112. While testing chunked-prefill cancellation on latest `main`, we independently reproduced the same user-visible symptom reported in #34112: a cancelled request can expose one token and then finish with `abort`. The #34112 attachment used SGLang v0.5.9. Its negative batch-level output IDs were old FutureMap relay handles and are not the failure criterion or target of this PR. Current `main` no longer uses that `ScheduleBatch.output_ids` representation. Our deterministic current-main reproduction isolates a final-prefill overlap race. An abort can arrive after the final chunked-prefill `EXTEND` is launched but before its delayed result is committed. At that point `scheduler.chunked_req` is already clear, `Req.output_ids` is empty, and the result is pending in `result_queue`. ## Root cause There were two commit boundaries to protect: 1. `abort_request()` records `req.to_finish = FINISH_ABORT()`, but the prefill result processor previously appended the sampled token and token-derived metadata before `update_finish_state()` consumed the pending finish. 2. In the CUDA/HIP overlap loop, scheduling the next batch happens before processing the delayed final-prefill result. Without an admission guard, the pending-finish prefill request can enter optimistic decode, increment `decode_batch_idx` / the KV committed watermark, and perform an optimistic decode step and its associated allocation before the result is dropped (which may reserve multiple slots or pages under speculative decoding). Filtering only in the output streamer is too late: request output, reasoning state, logprobs, hidden states, sampling metadata, grammar state, and KV accounting may already be mutated. ## Modifications - When a delayed result is actually pending, exclude pending-finish prefill requests from the prefill-to-decode merge before optimistic decode preparation. - Keep decode requests in mixed batches on their existing partial-output path. - In the final-prefill result processor, promote the pending finish with `new_accepted_len=0` and reuse normal finished-request cleanup. - Do not commit the dropped token's output ID, reasoning state, hidden state, customized info, sampling mask, returned logprob values, or grammar state. - Still advance packed hidden-state and logprob cursors so later live requests in the same batch read their own slices. - Preserve synchronous, MLX, and PP scheduling semantics by applying the merge guard only while `result_queue` contains a delayed result. - Leave PD-prefill transfer lifecycle unchanged; it uses a separate scheduler/result path. ## Regression coverage The scripted test deterministically waits for this window: - the request has passed through chunked prefill; - the final `EXTEND` is launched; - `scheduler.chunked_req is None`; - no middle chunks remain in flight; - `Req.output_ids` is empty; - the final result is pending. It then aborts and verifies: - finish reason is `FINISH_ABORT`; - no token is appended; - no optimistic decode step occurs; - the request-pool row and KV object are released; - reclaimable KV capacity returns to its baseline after the scheduler drains. Additional CPU tests cover both sides of the scheduler gate (pending queue vs. already-processed result), mixed prefill/decode membership, and a two-request packed-logprob case where the aborted segment advances the cursor without attaching metadata to the aborted request. ## Accuracy Tests Cancellation control flow only; normal token generation is unchanged. Validated on top of `main` commit `7605529bdf98ded2815e48c7054b1bc4533256c9`: ```text PYTHONPATH=python .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q \ test/registered/unit/managers/test_scheduler_chunked_req_gate.py \ test/registered/unit/managers/test_batch_result_processor_hidden_states.py \ test/registered/unit/managers/test_batch_result_processor_spec_grammar.py 11 passed, 2 subtests passed ``` ```text SGLANG_USE_MLX=1 PYTHONPATH=python .venv/bin/python \ test/registered/scripted_runtime/test_scripted_runtime_core.py \ TestScriptedRuntimeCore.test_abort_at_last_chunk_does_not_append_output Ran 1 test in 129.234s OK ``` Also passed: - direct CI-style execution of the two modified CPU test files; - Python compile checks for all touched files; - registered-test and package-registration repository checks; - Black 26.1.0, Ruff 0.15.1, isort 7.0.0, codespell 2.4.1, and `git diff --check`. The packed-logprob test was mutation-checked: it fails both if the aborted request attaches returned logprobs and if its packed cursor contribution is skipped. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Not applicable. The new checks are scheduler control-flow predicates; the result-drop branch runs only for a request that is already finishing. ## Topology notes The race is not caused by TP, DP, or PP. TP/DP use the same per-request result state. PP and MLX process their pending result before the relevant `last_batch` is reused, so the queue-gated admission change is a no-op there while the result-drop protection remains valid. PD-prefill is intentionally out of scope because it has a separate transfer and result lifecycle. The registered end-to-end regression is TP=1 / DP=1 / PP=1. Multi-rank topology behavior was source-reviewed but not claimed as a multi-GPU runtime validation. ## Checklist - [x] Rebased onto current `main`. - [x] Added deterministic registered regression coverage. - [x] Added focused scheduler and packed-metadata unit coverage. - [x] Ran relevant unit and scripted-runtime tests. - [x] Ran formatting, compile, and test-registration checks. - [x] Documentation and performance benchmarks are not applicable to this abort-only correctness fix. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32135933113](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32135933113)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32135932799](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32135932799)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [diffusion] Warmup-calibrated auto residency promotion in performance-mode auto
signal.text: ## Motivation Under `--performance-mode auto`, component placement is decided **before load** from static per-model thresholds (`keep_resident_min_available_gb`). On GPUs with ample free VRAM this leaves components needlessly offloaded — e.g. a layerwise-offloaded text encoder on an 80–140 GB card pays a full H2D reload every request for VRAM nobody else uses — and fixing it by hand requires per-model, per-GPU flag tuning. This PR makes `auto` mode **calibrate residency from the server warmup it already runs**: measure real memory behavior, then promote implicitly offloaded components to GPU-resident when the default workload provably fits, before the server turns ready. Frozen after `/health`; no changes after startup. ## Modifications **Measurement** - Server warmup forwards record `peak_reserved` + a pre-forward baseline on **every rank** (previously output-rank only). - Video warmup (which caps frames to bound startup) adds one extra small-frame **calibration forward**; a two-point affine fit in workload units (`batch × W × H × frames`) separates constant (weights/buffers) from linear (activation) memory and extrapolates the default-workload peak with a 1.2× margin on the linear part only. Image warmup already runs the default shape, so it is a direct measurement, no extrapolation. - The loader now records real weight/buffer sizes alongside the GPU-load delta (`memory_usages` is ≈0 for exactly the offloaded components residency decisions are about). **Decision + promotion (between last warmup req and ready)** - All ranks all-gather `{estimated peak, budget, candidates}` and compute one deterministic plan: candidates are implicitly offloaded, known-size, native CUDA components only; ranked by per-request H2D savings (layerwise DiT counts default denoise steps); promoted greedily while `estimated_peak + promoted_bytes + reserve ≤ budget`, with `reserve = max(10 % budget, 4 GiB)` and `budget = free + torch-reserved` (min across ranks; excludes other processes on shared GPUs). - Promotion reuses existing primitives: component-offload → resident via `require_component_resident`, layerwise via `disable_offload()`; the strategy cache is invalidated explicitly. - A **re-warm forward** after promotion re-establishes compile/kernel caches and proves the promoted layout actually serves; any failure rolls every rank back to the original strategy (only a rollback failure aborts startup). - Excluded paths: explicit placement / `manual` mode, FSDP, diffusers backend, quantized DiT (ModelOpt FP8/NVFP4, SVDQuant), Cache-DiT, breakable CUDA graph, realtime/disagg, `batching_max_size > 1`, any warmup failure. Kill switch: `SGLANG_DIFFUSION_DISABLE_AUTO_RESIDENCY=1`. **Fixes and unification along the way** - Warmup frame caps now run the pipeline's `adjust_num_frames`: LongLive2's server warmup was silently a no-op (17 capped frames → 5 latent frames, not divisible by `num_frames_per_block=8`, error swallowed by fail-open). - The post-request residency hint (`get_can_stay_resident_components`) now shares the promotion's candidate collection and H2D ranking — it previously read the ≈0 `memory_usages`, making the recommendation meaningless, and could recommend FSDP/custom-strategy components. - Logs narrate the adjustment: decision summary (`target/measured/estimated_peak/reserve/budget/promoted`), per-component `mode -> resident` with the **equivalent `--component-residency` flags** users can pin, and the kill switch. ``` Server warmup complete; adjusting component residency for the default workload (--performance-mode auto). Auto residency: target=1024x1024x1f steps=9, measured=[1024x1024x1f=17.4GiB], estimated_peak=17.4 GiB, reserve=13.3 GiB, budget=133.5 GiB, promoted=[text_encoder(layerwise-offload, 6.8 GiB)] Auto residency: adjusted text_encoder: layerwise-offload -> resident. Equivalent server args: --component-residency text_encoder=resident. ... ``` The optimization target is the model-default workload (default resolution/frames, batch 1). Larger or batched workloads should pin residency explicitly; the reserve bounds the blast radius. Static model deployment configs remain as the fallback when calibration is skipped. No numerics change for non-promoted paths; promoted components run identical code at a different placement. ## Test - `test/unit/test_auto_residency.py`: estimation (same-shape, single-point, two-point fit, negative-slope fallback, covering measurement), plan (skip propagation, reserve, cumulative fit, ranking), multi-rank worst-casing, promotion/rollback on stub modules, eligibility gates, LongLive2 frame alignment, applied-changes log, hint/promotion ranking consistency. - H200, Z-Image-Turbo serve: text encoder (layerwise, 6.8 GiB) promoted; warmup 9.15 s, decision <1 s, post-promotion re-warm 0.15 s; `/health` stays 503 until after promotion. - 2×H100, Wan2.1-T2V-14B: VAE promoted; text encoder correctly refused (estimated 65.6 GiB + 6.5 GiB TE > 70.2 GiB budget). Single-GPU 14B correctly refuses all promotions (72.6 vs 72.8 GiB). - Steady-state E2E improved on promoted image cases; no OOM observed in any validated case, including the refusal boundaries. ## Post-submission hardening (adversarial review pass) A 10-angle review over the diff surfaced and fixed, in `harden auto residency against review findings`: - **Measurement**: per-forward `empty_cache` + peak reset (allocator-pool carryover flattened the calibration slope → under-estimate → post-ready OOM); calibration forward moved after the main warmup so one-time allocations can only steepen the slope (safe direction); only `is_warmup` requests are measured (compile prewarm ran a different layout); failed warmups are recorded on every exit path; **`--enable-torch-compile` is excluded** — its warmup deliberately runs a stripped memory layout (layerwise DiT + evicted aux components) whose peaks are not serving peaks; unknown default workloads skip instead of trusting the capped peak. - **Distributed/rollback**: everything before the first all-gather is fenced into a skip report (a raise there parked peer ranks in the collective); error gathers filter on `is not None` with never-empty error strings; a failed in-apply rollback now surfaces as `rollback_failed` (aborts startup) instead of masquerading as rolled back; `disable_offload` re-arms hooks when `load_all_layers` fails; mechanism/mode mismatches from the `offload_during_compile` window are excluded and guarded; `_required_resident_components` tracks an owner feature so rollback cannot release loader hard-requirements. - **Startup contract**: apply-RPC failures honor the warmup fail-open contract; the post-rollback restore warmup keeps `--warmup-resolutions`' fail-closed contract; the calibration request shares `auto_residency_skip_reason` (the kill switch and excluded configs no longer pay for a measurement they never consume); warmup records are consumed exactly once (one-shot handler); re-warm passes no longer double-advance the warmup progress bar. - The warmup/target frame contract (cap → `adjust_num_frames` → `num_gpus` latent alignment) is now one shared helper extracted from `SamplingParams._adjust_visual_fields`, used by real requests, warmup requests, and the workload resolver. Known accepted conservatisms (documented in code): the budget check double-counts bytes of a component already partially on GPU at the measured peak (safe direction), and the reserve stays at `max(10 %, 4 GiB)`. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #32410205639](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32410205639)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32410205044](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32410205044)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #32410205559](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32410205559)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [Bug] Qwen3.6/Qwen3.8 multimodal mRoPE positions are passed to a 1D fused QK RMSNorm+RoPE CUDA kernel
signal.text: ### Checklist - [x] I searched related issues but found no solution. - [x] The bug persists in the latest version. - [x] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback. - [x] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed. - [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed. ### Describe the bug ## Summary On NVIDIA CUDA, the Qwen3.5-family full-attention implementation unconditionally selects `fused_qk_gemma_rmsnorm_rope_gate` when `attn_output_gate=True`. The fused kernel accepts only one-dimensional token positions (`positions: [T]`) and loads one scalar with: ```python pos = tl.load(positions_ptr + token).to(tl.int64) ``` However, Qwen3.6-27B and Qwen3.8-27B are multimodal Qwen3.5-family checkpoints. Their image/video prefill path supplies contiguous mRoPE positions with shape `(3, T)`, representing temporal, height, and width positions. Passing contiguous `(3, T)` positions to the current kernel makes it read only the first (temporal) row. Height and width positions are not applied to their assigned rotary dimensions. This silently changes Q/K for visual tokens and can degrade image understanding and GUI coordinate grounding. The same defect is present in SGLang v0.5.16, v0.5.17, and current `main`. ## Affected checkpoints | Checkpoint | Immutable revision | Architecture/config | Affected by this bug | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `Qwen/Qwen3.6-27B` | [`6a9e13bd6fc8f0983b9b99948120bc37f49c13e9`](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3.6-27B/blob/6a9e13bd6fc8f0983b9b99948120bc37f49c13e9/config.json) | Multimodal `Qwen3_5ForConditionalGeneration`, interleaved mRoPE | Yes | | `Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B` | [`1d4bf0f2ff6012fd82039f2fa52739d0dd7c60c0`](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B/blob/1d4bf0f2ff6012fd82039f2fa52739d0dd7c60c0/config.json) | Multimodal `Qwen3_5ForConditionalGeneration`, interleaved mRoPE | Yes | | `Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B-FP8` | [`017b9c7af6b5689d5dd426a76e0bc077eb5ca20a`](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B-FP8/blob/017b9c7af6b5689d5dd426a76e0bc077eb5ca20a/config.json) | Same multimodal architecture and mRoPE config | Yes | | `Qwen/Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B` | [`207bd685a7e3696cfaff12ded7c6a7ea0f88c996`](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B/blob/207bd685a7e3696cfaff12ded7c6a7ea0f88c996/config.json) | Text-only `Qwen3_5MoeForCausalLM`, no `mrope_section` | No, not this specific bug | The affected 27B configs contain: ```json { "architectures": ["Qwen3_5ForConditionalGeneration"], "language_model_only": false, "text_config": { "attn_output_gate": true, "head_dim": 256, "partial_rotary_factor": 0.25, "rope_parameters": { "mrope_interleaved": true, "mrope_section": [11, 11, 10], "rope_theta": 10000000, "rope_type": "default" } } } ``` SGLang registers `Qwen3_5ForConditionalGeneration` through the same `qwen3_5.py` implementation that contains the fused CUDA dispatch: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/63d783bbe0955237ec41f9ddabf7235ddf04673c/python/sglang/srt/models/qwen3_5.py#L2354-L2366 ## SGLang versions reviewed | Version | Commit | | --- | --- | | v0.5.11 reference path | [`612785ffdcaf35552f1ed433a981d596ca9fe900`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/commit/612785ffdcaf35552f1ed433a981d596ca9fe900) | | v0.5.16 | [`fdebc938f7f4d16fe6b9f55dcd9a767cf0899ea1`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/commit/fdebc938f7f4d16fe6b9f55dcd9a767cf0899ea1) | | v0.5.17 | [`29481685462732237d80d86076d6563e1f658102`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/commit/29481685462732237d80d86076d6563e1f658102) | | latest `main` reviewed on 2026-08-18 | [`63d783bbe0955237ec41f9ddabf7235ddf04673c`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/commit/63d783bbe0955237ec41f9ddabf7235ddf04673c) | The kernel file has the same Git blob ID in v0.5.16, v0.5.17, and the reviewed `main`: ```text 56d442098c02fa289414fecf0958638dd7906d5b ``` ## Source-level reproduction ### 1. The multimodal processor constructs three-axis positions `QwenVLImageProcessor.compute_mrope_positions()` calls `MRotaryEmbedding.get_rope_index()`: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/63d783bbe0955237ec41f9ddabf7235ddf04673c/python/sglang/srt/multimodal/processors/qwen_vl.py#L451-L471 `ForwardBatch` documents the result as `[3, total_seq_len]` and concatenates it along dimension 1 before moving it to the model device: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/63d783bbe0955237ec41f9ddabf7235ddf04673c/python/sglang/srt/model_executor/forward_batch_info.py#L1128-L1132 https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/63d783bbe0955237ec41f9ddabf7235ddf04673c/python/sglang/srt/model_executor/forward_batch_info.py#L1212-L1253 For image/video tokens, the temporal, height, and width rows are different. For ordinary text prefill/decode they are normally equal, which is why text-only accuracy tests may not expose the bug. ### 2. The VLM passes `(3, T)` positions into the language model The Qwen3-VL wrapper replaces normal positions with `forward_batch.mrope_positions` and asserts `(3, seq_len)` for multimodal prefill: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/63d783bbe0955237ec41f9ddabf7235ddf04673c/python/sglang/srt/models/qwen3_vl.py#L1423-L1453 ### 3. CUDA dispatch has no shape or mRoPE guard Current `main` uses the fused path whenever CUDA and the attention output gate are enabled: ```python if _is_cuda and self.attn_output_gate: q, k, v, gate = self.forward_prepare_cuda_fused( positions=positions, hidden_states=hidden_states, ) ``` https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/63d783bbe0955237ec41f9ddabf7235ddf04673c/python/sglang/srt/models/qwen3_5.py#L1147-L1163 There is no check for `positions.ndim`, `MRotaryEmbedding`, `mrope_section`, or `mrope_interleaved`. ### 4. The selected kernel is strictly one-dimensional The wrapper documents `positions: [T]`, and the Triton kernel loads only `positions_ptr + token`: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/63d783bbe0955237ec41f9ddabf7235ddf04673c/python/sglang/kernels/ops/attention/fused_qk_rmsnorm_rope_gate.py#L107-L114 https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/63d783bbe0955237ec41f9ddabf7235ddf04673c/python/sglang/kernels/ops/attention/fused_qk_rmsnorm_rope_gate.py#L131-L153 The kernel receives no positions row stride, mRoPE section sizes, or interleaving metadata. For a contiguous `(3, T)` tensor, `positions_ptr + token` addresses only row 0. ## Minimal runtime assertion On an NVIDIA CUDA machine, add this temporary assertion at the beginning of `forward_prepare_cuda_fused`: ```diff def forward_prepare_cuda_fused(self, positions, hidden_states): + assert positions.ndim == 1, ( + f"1D fused RoPE received shape={tuple(positions.shape)}, " + f"stride={positions.stride()}, rotary={type(self.rotary_emb).__name__}" + ) ``` Then launch either multimodal checkpoint and send one image request: ```bash python -m sglang.launch_server \ --model-path Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B \ --host 0.0.0.0 \ --port 30000 ``` Expected result with current code: image prefill reaches the assertion with a shape equivalent to `(3, T)`. Removing the assertion silently feeds that tensor to the one-dimensional kernel. The same assertion can be reproduced with `Qwen/Qwen3.6-27B`. ## Why existing validation missed it The fused CUDA path was introduced by PR #28320: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/28320 That PR changed two production files and did not add a fused-vs-native tensor correctness test. Its reported accuracy validation used a text Qwen3.5 checkpoint and AIME26. Text positions have equal T/H/W rows, so reading only the first row is accidentally equivalent for that control case. ## Expected behavior For two-dimensional mRoPE positions, Q/K must use the configured temporal, height, and width positions according to `mrope_section` and `mrope_interleaved`, matching `MRotaryEmbedding`. The one-dimensional fused kernel must not be called with a two-dimensional tensor unless it is explicitly extended to implement the same mRoPE semantics. ## Actual behavior On NVIDIA CUDA with `attn_output_gate=True`, `(3, T)` positions are passed to a `[T]` kernel. Only temporal positions are read, so H/W rotary dimensions are incorrect during image/video prefill. ## Suggested minimal correctness fix Use the fused path only for its documented one-dimensional input contract: ```diff -if _is_cuda and self.attn_output_gate: +if _is_cuda and self.attn_output_gate and positions.ndim == 1: q, k, v, gate = self.forward_prepare_cuda_fused(...) else: q, k, v, gate = self.forward_prepare_native(...) ``` Also fail fast in the fused wrapper: ```python if positions.ndim != 1: raise ValueError( f"fused_qk_gemma_rmsnorm_rope_gate only supports [T] positions, " f"got {tuple(positions.shape)}" ) ``` This is a conservative fix. In the current mRoPE scheduler, Qwen3.6/Qwen3.8 text and decode positions may also be represented as `(3, T)` with equal rows, so this guard can reduce fusion coverage for those models. Correctness should take priority; a follow-up optimization can safely pass `positions[0]` in paths where equal rows are guaranteed without performing a synchronizing GPU comparison. The complete performance fix is to extend the fused kernel to accept `(3, T)` positions plus the row stride, `mrope_section`, and interleaving mode. ## Tests requested Please add a CUDA fused-vs-native test using identical Q/K, norm weights, and RoPE cache: | Case | Positions | Expected result | | --- | --- | --- | | Text control | `[T]` | Fused and native close within dtype tolerance | | Equal-axis control | `(3, T)`, all rows equal | Either safely reduce to row 0 or use the native path | | Real mRoPE | `(3, T)`, T/H/W differ | Must bypass the 1D kernel or match `MRotaryEmbedding` numerically | An end-to-end image grounding regression test would also be useful, but the tensor-level contract test should be sufficient to prevent this silent correctness bug from recurring. ## Scope and current evidence The source-level shape/semantic mismatch is deterministic and independently reproducible. It confirms a correctness defect in the CUDA path and confirms that Qwen3.8-27B shares the affected configuration and implementation path. I do not include a controlled end-to-end CUDA grounding A/B in this report yet. Therefore, this issue does not claim that this kernel explains every observed visual benchmark regression; it claims the narrower, directly provable bug that genuine three-axis mRoPE positions are silently processed as one-dimensional positions. ### Reproduction ``` python -m sglang.launch_server \ --model-path Qwen/Qwen3.6-27B \ --port 8000 \ --tp-size 8 \ --mem-fraction-static 0.8 \ --reasoning-parser qwen3 ``` ### Environment I use the 0.5.16+cu129 docker. ``` Python: 3.12.3 (main, Jun 19 2026, 12:46:00) [GCC 13.3.0] CUDA available: True GPU 0,1,2,3,4,5,6,7: NVIDIA H100 80GB signal.title: [docs] Add DFlash2 speculative cells to the Qwen3.8-27B cookbook
signal.text: ## Motivation #35496 (quantized target `lm_head` in the DFlash2 selector) is merged, so the NVFP4 checkpoint can run DFlash2. This adds a DFLASH2 option to the Qwen3.8-27B cookbook's Speculative Decoding row, on every platform with a cell. Validation is graded: NVFP4 measured end-to-end on RTX PRO 6000 / RTX 5090, the RTX PRO 6000 BF16/FP8 cells validated to boot and serve, and the remaining platforms (H200, DGX Spark, GB300) offered with a **Final Verification In Progress** badge while the DFLASH2 pick is selected. ## Modifications - `qwen3.8-27b.jsx`: DFLASH2 Deploy-panel overlay option (draft `incoai/Qwen3.8-27B-DFlash2`, `--speculative-num-draft-tokens 8`) and the matching Playground card entry. On the RTX 5090 the option re-pins `--mem-fraction-static` (0.90 bf16 / 0.945 fp32), and for fp32 also re-pins `--mamba-full-memory-ratio 10` in place of the calculator's balanced value — the L=9216 ratio leaves the fp32 state pool one slot short at every serviceable mem-fraction. - `Qwen3.8-27B.mdx`: DFlash2 bullet in Configuration Tips (including the 5090 fp32 caveats), DFLASH added to the ratio accordion's `D` term, validation Note updated. - `_deployment.jsx`: `verificationStatus` may now be a function of the selection (overlay picks included), so a cell can report "Final Verification In Progress" for one speculative option while staying Verified for the rest. Backward compatible — string/boolean forms unchanged. ## Accuracy Tests N/A (docs only). Serving correctness of the quantized-head path was validated in #35496 (GSM8K 95.5% spec vs 98.0% base, 200q). ## Speed Tests and Profiling All 8 cells validated at ISL 8192 / OSL 1024, concurrency 1 (bench_serving random, 1 warmup + 4 prompts, exact-shape checks, real acceptance): | Card | Tier | SSM dtype | mem-frac | ratio | TPOT | tok/s/user | accept | |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---| | RTX PRO 6000 | Low-Latency | float32 | 0.85 | 6.63 | 7.56 ms | 132.3 | 3.41 | | RTX PRO 6000 | Low-Latency | bfloat16 | 0.85 | 3.38 | 7.64 ms | 130.9 | 3.09 | | RTX PRO 6000 | High-Throughput | float32 | 0.85 | 6.12 | 7.58 ms | 131.9 | 3.41 | | RTX PRO 6000 | High-Throughput | bfloat16 | 0.85 | 3.12 | 7.84 ms | 127.6 | 3.20 | | RTX 5090 | Low-Latency | bfloat16 | 0.90 | 3.38 | 6.11 ms | 143 | 3.30 | | RTX 5090 | High-Throughput | bfloat16 | 0.90 | 3.12 | 6.12 ms | 143 | 3.30 | | RTX 5090 | Low-Latency | float32 | 0.945 | 10 | 8.30 ms | 120.3 | 3.09 | | RTX 5090 | High-Throughput | float32 | 0.945 | 10 | 8.32 ms | 120.1 | 3.09 | 5090 fp32 boundaries, all measured: mf 0.94 → state pool one slot short; mf 0.95 → runtime OOM on the first request; balanced ratios 6.63/6.12 → `max_mamba_cache_size` below the required slots at every mem-fraction. Low-Latency fp32's KV pool is a single-request envelope (9,454 tokens), documented in the Tips bullet. RTX PRO 6000 BF16/FP8 boot grid (same cell command + DFLASH swap, calculator ratios; each arm booted, answered a greedy completion, and logged the selector folded into the draft CUDA graph): | Checkpoint | LL+fp32 (6.63) | LL+bf16 (3.38) | HT+fp32 (6.12) | HT+bf16 (3.12) | |---|---|---|---|---| | BF16 | OK | OK | OK | OK | | FP8 | OK | OK | OK | OK | (Both checkpoints keep a dense `lm_head` — no weight scales in their indexes — so these ride the classic dense path; NVFP4 is the only checkpoint exercising the quantized-head gate.) <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #32352483457](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32352483457)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32352483142](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32352483142)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:heavy_minus_sign: **No AMD PR run found for this commit**.<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [AMD] Fix weight checking for AITER-shuffled block FP8 weights
signal.text: ## Motivation This ports #34016 from `sglang-miles` to `main` following maintainer feedback. AITER pre-shuffles block-FP8 weights on ROCm for optimized inference kernels. The weight checker was treating the shuffled physical layout as the original logical layout during dequantization, causing false weight-update mismatches even though inference was correct. AITER rotary `cos_cache` and `sin_cache` buffers were also missing from the checker's existing derived-buffer skip patterns. ## Modifications - Mark dense and MoE block-FP8 parameters after AITER layout shuffling. - Propagate the layout metadata into the weight checker. - Restore the logical FP8 layout before checker dequantization, checksum, and ULP comparison. - Skip AITER rotary `cos_cache` and `sin_cache` buffers during weight checking. - Add unit tests for layout restoration, metadata propagation, and rotary-cache handling. - Register the weight-checker unit tests for AMD CI. The layout conversion is only applied to weights explicitly marked as AITER-shuffled. NVIDIA and other unshuffled paths retain the existing behavior. ## Accuracy Tests Validated on AMD MI355 with the Miles [DeepSeek V4 four-layer E2E test](https://github.com/radixark/miles/blob/main/tests/e2e/megatron/model_scripts/test_deepseek_v4_flash_4layer_ci.py). Both rollout runs passed, and all checked FP8 weights reported `num_exceed=0`. Weight-checker unit tests: - New focused tests: 6 passed - Full unit suite: 64 passed, 1 skipped because NVIDIA DeepGEMM is unavailable on ROCm This PR does not modify model forward computation or inference kernels. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Not applicable. The only inference-path change is setting metadata during weight loading. Layout restoration runs exclusively when the weight checker is enabled and does not affect normal inference performance. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #32053738759](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32053738759)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32053738308](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32053738308)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [NPU] [Diffusion] Fix npu diffusion regressions & restore 2-NPU CI testcase
signal.text: ## Motivation Ring Attention on Ascend NPU currently breaks when execution reaches the packed variable-length FlashAttention fallback (added for Minimax-H3 support). The shared Ring Attention path uses `flash_attn_varlen_func` for variable-length packed sequences, but that entry point did not have an NPU implementation. As a result, Ring Attention regressed on NPU in the current `main` branch. This PR implement the NPU path by adding Ascend support for packed variable-length attention and wiring it into both the generic FlashAttention compatibility API and the diffusion Ascend attention backend. The implementation is based on the Ascend varlen attention work from [#33569](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/33569), extracted here as a focused Ring Attention compatibility fix. ### Before ### After This PR fix this behavior by implementing this fallback: ## Modifications ### Ascend packed variable-length attention - Add `ascend_fused_infer_attention_varlen`, backed by `torch.ops.npu.npu_fused_infer_attention_score`. - Use the Ascend `TND` layout with packed sequence boundaries supplied through `actual_seq_lengths` and `actual_seq_lengths_kv`. - Validate Q/K/V layout, device placement, dtype, head dimensions, and cumulative sequence lengths. - Support optional host-side cumulative sequence lengths to avoid unnecessary device-to-host synchronization when they are already available. - Handle empty packed segments and non-contiguous Q/K/V views. - Support returning softmax LSE when requested. ### `flash_attn_varlen_func` NPU dispatch - Route NPU tensors from the generic `flash_attn_varlen_func` compatibility API to the Ascend packed-attention implementation. - Explicitly reject FlashAttention options that are not supported by the Ascend implementation instead of silently producing incorrect behavior. - Leave the existing CUDA/FlashAttention v3 path unchanged. ### Diffusion Ascend attention backend - Implement `AscendFlashAttnImpl.forward_varlen`. - Use the shared fused `TND` implementation for non-causal packed attention. - Preserve sequence boundaries for causal attention by processing each packed segment independently through the existing Ascend attention path. ## Accuracy Tests - **Before this PR:** the packed variable-length fallback used by Ring Attention does not have a working NPU implementation. - **After this PR:** the same Ring Attention path successfully dispatches through the Ascend varlen implementation. ## Speed Tests and Profiling This PR is primarily a correctness and dispatch fix; no standalone end-to-end performance benchmark was collected. ## Checklist - [ ] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [ ] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process). 2. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so. - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci` 4. signal.title: [AMD] Fix Qwen3.5 MTP dropping fused shared-expert weights
signal.text: ## Motivation Since #33889, Qwen3.5 MXFP4 with MTP speculative decoding on MI355X lost about 12% throughput. The cause is that the MTP draft model is loaded without its shared-expert weights. **What fusion does to the weight layout.** When a Qwen3.5 MoE layer fuses its shared expert, it deliberately does not build a separate `shared_expert` module — the shared expert becomes one more routed expert, living in slot `num_experts`. Any loader for such a layer therefore has to route `mlp.shared_expert.*` into that slot. `qwen3_5.py` does exactly that; `qwen3_5_mtp.py` never learned to. **Why the target model is unaffected.** In this checkpoint the target's routed experts are MXFP4 while its shared expert stays bf16. Fusing them would push a higher-precision tensor through the quantized routed-expert path, so `can_fuse_shared_expert()` refuses. The target therefore always takes the unfused path, keeps its `shared_expert` module, and loads normally — the gap in the MTP loader is invisible from here. **Why the draft model is affected, and only recently.** The MTP module is excluded from quantization in full: all 1536 `mtp.*` routed-expert tensors and its shared expert alike. The draft is thus uniformly bf16, nothing is mixed-precision, and fusing it is perfectly valid — the gate correctly says yes. It simply never had the chance before. Until #33889, the target's Quark config installed a single process-wide `disable_shared_experts_fusion` override, which switched fusion off for every runner, draft included. #33889 made that decision per-runner, so the draft started fusing for the first time and immediately ran into the loader gap. **Why nobody noticed.** With fusion on there is no `shared_expert` module to load into, and the expert mapping only covers slots `0 .. num_experts-1`, so each `mlp.shared_expert.{gate,up,down}_proj.weight` matches nothing and ends at `logger.warning_once("Parameter ... not found in params_dict, skip loading")` — three tensors per TP rank, one suppressed log line, no error. The draft then runs with an uninitialized shared expert. Since a speculative draft cannot corrupt verified output, accuracy is unaffected; the damage appears only as a fall in accept rate, from 0.65 to 0.51, and hence in throughput. This PR teaches the MTP loader to place those weights into the fused slot, so the draft that #33889 legitimately enabled actually receives them. ## Modifications `python/sglang/srt/models/qwen3_5_mtp.py`, mirroring `qwen3_5.py`: - Size the expert mapping as `num_experts + num_fused_shared_experts` so slot `num_experts` has an entry. The fusion count is read from the constructed modules, because `num_fused_shared_experts` is set on `Qwen3_5MoeForConditionalGeneration` and the MTP wraps a `Qwen3_5ForCausalLM`, which does not carry it. - Rewrite `mlp.shared_expert.` to `mlp.experts.{num_experts}.` before the mapping loops. Both are keyed on the model's actual fusion state rather than on a platform check. When nothing fuses, `num_fused_shared_experts` is `0`, the mapping size is unchanged and the rewrite never fires, so this is a no-op for every non-fusing configuration. Not covered: the fused-checkpoint variant (a single `experts.gate_up_proj` tensor). `qwen3_5.py` handles that with a dedicated branch that chunks the tensor into `w1`/`w3`; the MTP loader's `load_fused_expert_weights` indexes per expert id and cannot serve a single shared-expert tensor. Adding that path untested seemed worse than leaving it, since no checkpoint on hand exercises it. ## Accuracy Tests No accuracy change is expected: only the draft model changes, and a speculative draft cannot alter verified output. The visible effect is the accept rate. Measured over ~100 decode-batch samples per point. | conc | accept_len before | after | accept_rate before | after | |---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | 4 | 2.5278 | 2.9533 | 0.5097 | 0.6509 | | 8 | 2.5507 | 2.9374 | 0.5168 | 0.6457 | | 16 | 2.5144 | 2.9508 | 0.5054 | 0.6501 | Skipped weights during load go from 3 per TP rank to 0. ## Speed Tests and Profiling ### Summary at conc=4 | Config | Total Throughput | Median E2E (ms) | Median TTFT (ms) | Median TPOT (ms) | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:| | `eda0ddc260d4` (last good) | 5365.74 | 5992.71 | 326.84 | 6.25 | | `b61a06921e` (#33889) | 4716.15 | 6662.60 | 322.72 | 7.05 | | `b61a06921e` + PR #35719 | 5429.77 | 5912.64 | 326.93 | 6.11 | The third row was obtained by switching shared-expert fusion off on `b61a06921e`, which removes the unloaded-shared-expert condition from the draft; this PR removes the same condition by loading the fused weights instead of dropping them. ### Full sweep MI355X, `amd/Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-MXFP4`, TP=2, EAGLE MTP (3 steps / topk 1 / 4 draft tokens), page-size 16, `fp8_e4m3` KV, `--attention-backend aiter`, ISL=8192 / OSL=1024, `num_prompts = 10 x conc`, server relaunched per concurrency with `--max-running-requests = conc`. Server flags follow `benchmarks/single_node/fixed_seq_len/qwen3.5_fp4_mi355x_mtp.sh`. Before and after were run back to back on the same GPU pair, both at `7f8f030000`. | conc | Total Throughput before | after | Delta | Median E2E (ms) before | after | Median TTFT (ms) before | after | Median TPOT (ms) before | after | |---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | 4 | 4746.11 | 5417.31 | **+14.14%** | 6726.7 | 5969.1 | 333.3 | 336.7 | 7.07 | 6.22 | | 8 | 6835.64 | 7626.54 | **+11.57%** | 9243.7 | 8370.3 | 336.4 | 335.9 | 9.67 | 8.82 | | 16 | 9011.82 | 10141.08 | **+12.53%** | 13997.8 | 12840.5 | 346.1 | 361.6 | 14.86 | 13.48 | The gain is decode-side, as expected from an accept-rate change: TTFT is flat, TPOT improves by 9–12%. This restores the configuration to its previously published InferenceX level. The last sweep on image `lmsysorg/sglang-rocm:v0.5.16-rocm720-mi35x-20260730` recorded 582.84 / 852.30 / 1130.14 output tok/s at conc 4 / 8 / 16; with this patch the same setup measures 602.47 / 857.12 / 1123.38. Bisecting `accept len` over the 759 commits between that image's sglang and `63d783bbe0` lands on #33889, with a clean split (2.84–2.92 before, 2.50–2.57 after, no intermediate values). ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:no_entry_sign: [Run #32389114863](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32389114863)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32389114508](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32389114508)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32389114842](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32389114842)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [mem_cache][12/N] refactor: stop allocators round-tripping through the KV pool
signal.text: ## Motivation Part of #25371. Rebased onto current `main` and renumbered -- the branch had been sitting since June and `[6/N]` had meanwhile been taken by #30249. Allocators reach through the KV pool for two things they do not need it for: 1. **`get_cpu_copy` / `load_cpu_copy` pass-throughs.** `TokenToKVPoolAllocator` and `SWATokenToKVPoolAllocator` each define these purely to forward to `self._kvcache`, and `BaseTokenToKVPoolAllocator` declares them only to raise `NotImplementedError`. Retraction backup is a pool operation; routing it through the allocator adds a layer that carries no decision. 2. **Round-trips through the pool to read a tensor the allocator itself owns.** The allocator allocates `full_to_swa_index_mapping` / `full_to_hisparse_device_index_mapping` in `__init__`, hands the *same object* to the pool via `register_mapping`, and writes it on every alloc and free. `self._kvcache.translate_loc_from_full_to_swa(x)` is then literally `self.full_to_swa_index_mapping[x]` with an extra call frame. ## Modifications - Drop `get_cpu_copy` / `load_cpu_copy` from `allocator/base.py`, `allocator/token.py`, `allocator/paged.py`, `allocator/swa.py`. The two call sites in `Req.save_kv_cache` / `Req.load_kv_cache` go through `token_to_kv_pool_allocator.get_kvcache()` instead. - `SWATokenToKVPoolAllocator.translate_loc_from_full_to_swa` and the HiSparse allocators' `get_last_loc_hisparse_device` / `free_hisparse` / `free_compressed` index the allocator-owned mapping directly. - `full -> compressed` is deliberately **left** as a pool call: it is genuine C4-layout arithmetic (`(i + 1) % compress_ratio`), a pool responsibility, not a mapping lookup. Comments at both sites say so, to keep the next reader from "simplifying" it too. No behavior change: every removed indirection resolved to the same tensor index or the same pool method. ## Accuracy Test Rebase resolution, verified on an H200 devbox against a pristine `main` baseline on the same box: ``` rebased branch: 1746 passed, 1074 skipped, 201 subtests passed pristine main: 1746 passed, 1074 skipped, 201 subtests passed ``` (`test/registered/unit/mem_cache/` plus `spec/test_resolve_swa_kv_pool.py`; `--ignore` on `test_umbp_store.py`, which needs the `mori` package that is absent from the image.) Zero delta, so the 1074 skips are pre-existing. The rebase kept the original diff shape exactly (+32/-45 across 7 files). Three of the four conflicts were context drift around the deleted methods -- `main` had added `translate_kv_indices_for_transfer` to `allocator/base.py`, `_copy_for_free_group` to `allocator/token.py`, and `PureSWATokenToKVPoolAllocator` plus `swa_free_group` to `allocator/swa.py`. All are preserved; `PureSWATokenToKVPoolAllocator` is byte-identical to `main`, and it overrides `translate_loc_from_full_to_swa` with an identity, so it is unaffected by the change here. The fourth conflict was real: `main` had reworked retraction backup onto `RetractionBackup(cpu_tensors=...)`, so the resolution keeps that structure and only reroutes the call through `get_kvcache()`. The ownership assumption was re-checked against current `main` rather than trusting the June-era diff: `allocator/swa.py` builds the tensor, `register_mapping` hands the same object to the pool, and the pool's `translate_loc_from_full_to_swa` indexes that very tensor -- so the direct index is identical, including the `-1` sentinel row. A repo-wide grep confirms no allocator-level `get_cpu_copy` / `load_cpu_copy` caller or override survives; every remaining one is on a pool. ## Benchmark and Profiling Results Not applicable -- removes call frames, changes no kernel or memory layout. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Code Formatting with Pre-Commit](https://docs.sglang.ai/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-formatting-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests as outlined in the [Running Unit Tests](https://docs.sglang.ai/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#running-unit-tests-adding-to-ci). - [x] Update documentation / docstrings / example tutorials as needed, according to [Writing Documentation](https://docs.sglang.ai/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#writing-documentation-running-docs-ci). - [x] Provide throughput / latency benchmark results and accuracy evaluation results as needed, according to [Benchmark and Profiling](https://docs.sglang.ai/developer_guide/benchmark_and_profiling.html). - [x] For reviewers: If you haven't made any contributions to this PR and are only assisting with merging the main branch, please remove yourself as a co-author when merging the PR. - [x] Please feel free to join our Slack channel at https://slack.sglang.ai to discuss your PR. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:no_entry_sign: [Run #32388833079](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32388833079)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32388832657](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32388832657)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32388832963](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32388832963)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [multimodal] MiniMax-H3: accept target.width/height as an exact canvas
signal.text: ## Motivation `target.short_edge` names a *policy* size and lets `adapt_shape_v1` choose the canvas. A caller that already knows the geometry it wants — a fixed delivery format, a UI preset — has to work backwards to a nominal short edge plus a ratio string that round to it, and gets no error when the guess is wrong: unknown `target` keys are silently ignored, so a request carrying `width`/`height` is admitted and rendered at whatever the ratio resolved to. (`conditions[i]` and the canonical request both reject unknown keys; `target` is the one place that does not.) Naming both axes is exact, because the ratio *is* the canvas: the resolver's nominal-times-ratio step reproduces it and the nearest-32 rounding is a no-op. So this needs no resolver or stage change — validation rewrites the pair into the `short_edge` + `aspect_ratio` it denotes, and the canonical request keeps its existing three-key projection. A test asserts the resolved shape is identical to the equivalent ratio request (the resolved shape does not carry the ratio string, so nothing downstream can tell them apart). ## Modifications - `request_validation.py`: `_normalize_exact_canvas()` rewrites `target.width`+`height` into `short_edge=min(w, h)` and `aspect_ratio="W:H"`. - refuses a canvas off the 32px grid or over `MINIMAX_H3_MAX_PIXELS` rather than rounding or scaling it — silently changing the requested geometry is worse than refusing it; - refuses naming both spellings, and half a pair; - defers the inclusive 1:4..4:1 range and the grid to `minimax_h3_resolve_spatial_shape` (asks the resolver whether it reproduces the canvas) instead of restating those rules; - keeps the forced-`"auto"` task guard, since the rewrite ends in a concrete ratio; - an exact canvas is exempt from the finite-ratio allowlist: that allowlist constrains *ratio* requests to tested shapes, and a caller naming both axes has already chosen. - `configs/sample/minimax_h3.py`: add `width`/`height` to the `target` projection in `_validate()`, otherwise the offline path drops them before validation sees them. - `test/unit/test_minimax_h3_exact_target_canvas.py`: new, 16 cases (accepted canvas, plan geometry, equivalence with the ratio spelling, the pixel-budget edge, allowlist exemption, fl2va, and each rejection). ## Accuracy Tests No change for existing requests: `width`/`height` absent takes the same path as before. `pytest python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/unit/ -k minimax` → 103 passed. ## Speed Tests and Profiling N/A (request validation only). ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). --- Other MiniMax-H3 PRs from the same bring-up: #35739 (sm_120 NVFP4), #35740 (H3 qkv scale row order), #35745 (short-edge warning), and #35743 (a `--attention-backend` selector issue). <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32411483474](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32411483474)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32411483182](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32411483182)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32411483409](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32411483409)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [multimodal] MiniMax-H3: do not warn that the recommended short edge is unverified
signal.text: ## Motivation `request_validation._validate_target` calls `warn_unverified_short_edge(short_edge)` unconditionally, so a stock request at the recommended short edge logs a warning that names the requested value as the verified one: ``` WARNING ... target.short_edge=768 is outside the verified configuration: 768 is the only short edge MiniMax publishes recipes and reference outputs for ... ``` `resolved_plan._validate_base_short_edge` already guards the same call with `if short_edge != MINIMAX_H3_BASE_SHORT_EDGE`. This applies that guard at the request boundary too, so the warning only fires for the case it is about. ## Modifications - `request_validation.py`: warn only when `short_edge != MINIMAX_H3_RECOMMENDED_SHORT_EDGE`. - `test/unit/test_minimax_h3_short_edge.py`: two tests through `minimax_h3_validate_canonical_request` — the recommended edge does not warn, an unverified edge does. signal.title: [MoE Refactor] Migrate SM100 trtllm-gen mxfp4 MoE onto MoeRunner
signal.text: ## Motivation Part of the MoE refactor tracked in #8715. cc @ch-wan `Mxfp4MoEMethod` was the last quant method with a partially migrated path: the SM90 CUTLASS branch went through `MoeRunner` (#26489), but the SM100 trtllm-gen branch still called the kernel inline from `apply`, with `create_moe_runner` falling through to `pass` and a `TODO`. This migrates it, so both FlashInfer MXFP4 GPU paths in `Mxfp4MoEMethod` now use the shared runner pipeline. ## Modifications - Add `FlashInferTrtllmGenMxfp4MoeQuantInfo` and `_fused_experts_flashinfer_mxfp4_sm100_trtllm_gen`, holding the relocated kernel call. - `fused_experts_none_to_flashinfer_mxfp4` becomes a dispatcher: both mxfp4 paths register under the single `("none", "flashinfer_mxfp4")` key quant_info type selects the kernel. - `create_moe_runner` accepts `trtllm_sm100` alongside `cutlass_sm90` and now raises `NotImplementedError` for unhandled combinations instead of silently leaving `self.runner` unset. New tests - `test_mxfp4_trtllm_gen.py` (`base-b`, `4-gpu-b200`): asserts that `apply` and a direct `trtllm_fp4_block_scale_moe` call produce equal output. Both reach the same kernel, so what this actually checks is that `apply` assembles the kernel arguments correctly. ## Accuracy Tests Validated on a single B200 (driver 580.159.04, CUDA 13.0, flashinfer 0.6.15.post1, torch 2.11.0+cu130) with `openai/gpt-oss-20b` (mxfp4), `--moe-runner-backend flashinfer_mxfp4`, at ep_size=1 tp_size=1. Bitwise logprob comparison, base `8727d105d` against this branch, 6 fixed prompts, greedy, 192 scored output tokens per cell: | precision | text identical | token ids equal | logprobs bitwise equal | |---|---|---|---| | default | yes | yes | yes, max delta 0.000e+00 | | bf16 | yes | yes | yes, max delta 0.000e+00 | GSM8K was also run with `few_shot_gsm8k --num-questions 200`. The accuracy column is the fraction of the 200 questions whose parsed answer was correct, so 0.520 means 104 of 200: | commit | precision | accuracy | invalid | |---|---|---|---| | `8727d105d` base | default | 0.525 | 0.155 | | this branch | default | 0.520 | 0.165 | | `8727d105d` base | bf16 | 0.540 | 0.155 | | this branch | bf16 | 0.520 | 0.140 | | `8727d105d` base, rerun of the same commit | bf16 | 0.570 | 0.145 | The last row is the important one. Identical code scored 0.540 and then 0.570, a 0.030 swing larger than any gap between base and branch, so GSM8K at 200 questions cannot resolve this comparison in either direction. The bitwise comparison above is the meaningful result. ## Speed Tests and Profiling N/A ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [ ] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. signal.title: [multimodal] MiniMax-H3: fix quantized qkv scales and missing-param policy
signal.text: ## Motivation Two MiniMax-H3 model-side defects that only appear on a quantized checkpoint (NVFP4 or fp8). **1. Per-output-row quantization metadata is not reordered with its rows.** MiniMax-H3 checkpoints store qkv grouped, so `_install_qkv_weight_loader()` permutes the fused qkv weight's output rows into `q|k|v` order via `_reorder_grouped_qkv_to_qkv()`. NVFP4 block scales and fp8 per-channel scales are indexed by that same output row, and they were loaded unpermuted — every scale ends up attached to the wrong row. The weights are correct; the dequantized values are not. The symptom is grey mush, with no error anywhere. **2. `_mark_missing_params_required()` overwrites each quant method's own missing-parameter policy.** A quant method declares in `create_weights()` what it can synthesize when a scale is absent from the checkpoint — weight-only NVFP4 has no `input_scale` and marks it `missing_param_init = "ones"`. H3 then blanket-stamps every parameter `"error"`, so the declaration is lost and the loader raises: ``` ValueError: Required checkpoint parameter '...input_scale' was not loaded ``` ## Modifications - New module-level helper `_install_qkv_row_reorder()` wraps a qkv parameter's weight loader (and its `rank_local_weight_transform`, needed by rank-local FSDP) with the same row permutation used for the weight. Applied to every `qkv_proj` parameter except the weight itself. The gate is the row count: a tensor whose leading dim is not the checkpoint's qkv row count is passed through untouched, which covers per-tensor scalars and swizzled block-scale layouts that are not row-indexed. It reads the **loaded checkpoint tensor**, not the local parameter, so it also holds under tensor parallelism, where the local parameter only owns its own shard of the rows. - `_mark_missing_params_required()` now only claims parameters that have no declared policy. - `test/unit/test_minimax_h3_qkv_scale_reorder.py`: new unit test covering both branches of the row-count gate (row-indexed metadata is permuted, swizzled and per-tensor metadata is not) on the wrapped loader and on `rank_local_weight_transform`. Depends on nothing else, but on sm_120 both this and #35739 are required to get a working NVFP4 MiniMax-H3 (the two fixes are in different layers, hence separate PRs). ## Accuracy Tests On one RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition (sm_120) with an NVFP4 MiniMax-H3 checkpoint: - (2) alone is a hard load failure. - With (2) fixed, (1) renders grey mush. - With both fixed, output is structurally the same as the bf16 checkpoint, and bit-identical across repeated runs at the same seed. The reorder is only reachable for a quantized checkpoint with per-row scales; a bf16 run has no parameters other than the weight on `qkv_proj`, so it is unaffected. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Weight-load-time only; no change to the forward path and none measured (paired runs within 0.2%). ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32409454008](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32409454008)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32409453473](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32409453473)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32409453790](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32409453790)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [multimodal] Fix NVFP4 diffusion models on sm_120 (RTX PRO 6000 / RTX 50xx)
signal.text: ## Motivation NVFP4 diffusion checkpoints cannot be served on sm_120 GPUs (RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell / RTX 50xx). Two independent defects in the shared ModelOpt FP4 path are involved; neither is model-specific. **1. The default FP4 GEMM backend does not exist on sm_120.** `CudaPlatformBase.get_modelopt_flashinfer_fp4_backend()` defaults to `"trtllm"`, and `flashinfer.mm_fp4` rejects it there: ``` ValueError: mm_fp4 does not support backend 'trtllm' with capability 120 ``` so the first quantized linear aborts and no NVFP4 model runs at all. **2. The block-scale layout is chosen by a heuristic whose negative branch is unreachable.** In `ModelOptFp4LinearMethod.process_weights_after_loading()` the `trtllm` branch fetches its own shuffled scale layout and **returns**. Everything still executing below it is therefore a TMA-layout consumer (`cutlass`, `cudnn`, `auto`) — but the layout was instead selected by a module-name test: ```python uses_flux1_scale_layout = not getattr( self.quant_config, "checkpoint_uses_packed_qkv", False ) and getattr(layer, "prefix", "").startswith( ("transformer_blocks.", "single_transformer_blocks.") ) if flashinfer_backend is None or uses_flux1_scale_layout: ``` Any model whose blocks are not named with the FLUX.1 prefixes skips the swizzle and hands the kernel block scales in the wrong layout. This does not raise — it silently produces broken output. ## Modifications - `runtime/platforms/cuda.py`: default the FP4 GEMM backend to `"auto"` on sm_120 (which resolves to flashinfer's sm_12x NVFP4 kernel) and keep `"trtllm"` elsewhere. `SGLANG_DIFFUSION_FLASHINFER_FP4_GEMM_BACKEND` still overrides. Uses the pre-existing `is_sm120()`, so no other capability changes behaviour. - `runtime/layers/quantization/modelopt_quant.py`: apply the 128x4 TMA reshape unconditionally, and delete the unreachable heuristic. This also removes two defensive `getattr()`s and the now-redundant second `_get_fp4_gemm_op()` call. - `test/unit/test_modelopt_fp4_backend.py`: new unit test pinning the default-backend resolution (sm_120 vs other, all explicit env spellings, unknown value falls back to the platform default). ## Accuracy Tests Verified on one RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition (sm_120) with an NVFP4 MiniMax-H3 checkpoint: - before: startup fails on (1); forcing a backend past it renders grey noise, which is (2). - after: output is **bit-identical** (md5 of the produced mp4) to the previously env-forced workaround, with no environment variables set. Same seed, same request, three runs. `python -m pytest python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/unit/test_modelopt_fp4_backend.py` — 4 passed. ## Speed Tests and Profiling No performance change is expected or measured: the same kernel is selected, and the scale reshape is a one-time weight-load step. Paired single-GPU runs before/after differ by 0.2%, inside this box's run-to-run floor. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). --- sm_120 also needs #35740 (MiniMax-H3 model-side quantized-scale fixes) for a working NVFP4 MiniMax-H3; the two are in different layers and independent, hence separate PRs. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32409392442](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32409392442)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32409391600](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32409391600)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32409391640](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32409391640)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [Spec][LoRA] Support multi-adapter LoRA with EAGLE/NEXTN/DFLASH/DSPARK speculative decoding
signal.text: ## Motivation #12903 enabled LoRA with NGRAM speculative decoding. This extends it to **EAGLE / NEXTN / EAGLE3, DFLASH and DSPARK with multiple adapters co-batched**, one of the LoRA items in #11762. Adapters apply to the target model only; one shared draft runs unadapted. Speculation stays lossless per adapter (verify samples from the adapted target), so only the accept rate is affected. Supersedes #28395, which strips LoRA from a per-draft `ServerArgs` copy — a mechanism that no longer exists now that per-runner values are constructor arguments. Thanks to @tengxiaoliu for the original approach and the MoE target-verify fix this builds on. ## Modifications **Draft runner is unadapted.** Every worker gets the same published `ServerArgs`, so `enable_lora` is `True` for the draft too; the exclusion is keyed on `is_draft_worker` in `maybe_init_lora_manager`. Otherwise the draft loads the target's adapters into a model with a different layer count and startup fails. `ModelRunner.lora_manager` is now always present (`None` when unset) and every LoRA path keys off it rather than the config, so a draft runner skips them by construction. **`TARGET_VERIFY` token counts.** It reports `is_extend()` but leaves `extend_seq_lens(_cpu)` as `None`, breaking three call sites: | Path | Failure | |---|---| | triton eager segments | `max(None)` (hit whenever `bs > max_bs_in_cuda_graph`) | | MoE `_add_moe_lora_info` | `sum(None)` | | csgmv `_determine_chunk_size` | `None` comparison, with `--max-lora-chunk-size > 16` | New `get_batch_token_counts` holds the forward-mode dispatch in one place; all three route through it. The triton graph path now asserts the verify width matches the captured `seg_lens` width instead of silently mis-segmenting adapters — that backend bakes `seg_lens` at capture time and never refreshes it, so a differing width would map adapters onto the wrong token rows. **MoE LoRA cuda-graph buffers** were sized in requests while verify capture feeds `bs * draft_token_num` tokens; the per-token buffers are now sized by verify width. This was also undersized for NGRAM + MoE LoRA. **Shared lm_head.** An MTP draft implementing `set_lm_head_from_target` shares the target's lm_head *module*; if LoRA-wrapped, draft forwards apply the target's deltas against batch metadata of a different shape. The draft now gets the unwrapped base layer, so lm_head adapters cost accept rate rather than correctness. Adapters carrying embedding weights warn as they load; rejecting them would rule out every MTP-capable base, whose public adapters all ship `unembed_tokens` under an `all-linear` config. **Validation.** The NGRAM-only rejection becomes `_check_lora_speculative_compatibility`: multi-adapter EAGLE/NEXTN/EAGLE3, DFLASH and DSPARK allowed on either kernel backend, rejecting `--speculative-adaptive` (the draft reads a static speculative config), the `experimental_sgl_trtllm` MoE runner (its TopK reads the LoRA config per forward), and `SGLANG_ENABLE_OVERLAP_PLAN_STREAM` (LoRA batch prep would run on the plan stream, unordered against in-flight forwards). ## Accuracy Tests Unit tests cover the argument matrix, the draft-runner gate, the `TARGET_VERIFY` segment math, and the embedding warning (`base-a-test-cpu`, plus one `1-gpu-small` file). The e2e test (`base-b-test-1-gpu-large`) asserts serving properties rather than output text, since greedy decoding is not bitwise reproducible across batch shapes here. Losslessness is verified out of band by `test/manual/lora/run_spec_lora_matrix.py`, comparing spec-on vs spec-off **per adapter** across solo, mixed-adapter, and wider-than-cuda-graph batches, after measuring the reproducibility floor so model nondeterminism is not read as failure. | Config | Result | |---|---| | NEXTN Qwen3.5-35B-A3B, `triton` | **PASS** — every reproducible pair matched | | NEXTN Qwen3.5-35B-A3B, `csgmv` | **PASS** — every reproducible pair matched | | DFLASH Llama-3.1-8B, `triton` | **PASS** — 0 comparisons skipped | | DFLASH Llama-3.1-8B, `csgmv` | **PASS** — 0 comparisons skipped | | DSPARK Inkling-Small (TP8) | **PASS** — 9 of 36 comparisons made | DFLASH is the strongest signal: Llama-3.1-8B is fully reproducible, so every comparison was made and matched on both kernel backends, with two adapters differing in rank (64 / 8) and module set. DSPARK is the weakest — Inkling-Small is nondeterministic on 9 of 12 (route, prompt) pairs — but it is the only leg exercising an adapter that wraps the target's lm_head. Adapter identity inside one verify batch was also checked directly, which text equality cannot do on a nondeterministic model: with three adapters whose trained behavior is to prefix every output word with their own name, one batch carrying base plus all three returned **16/16 requests wearing their own prefix and no foreign one**. Crossed verify segments would be plainly visible. Accept length is unchanged by that co-batching (≤0.6 SE against the same routes measured alone). Two bugs these runs caught that no unit test reached: a config-vs-manager gate crashing the spec server on every TP rank once `enable_lora` reads True on the draft, and drafts taking the target's lm_head / embed_tokens *module* then dereferencing base-layer attributes the LoRA wrapper does not forward. The second is why unwrapping happens at every acquisition point. Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct-2507 + EAGLE3 was also run; its one divergent prompt diverges identically with **zero adapters loaded**, so it belongs to that model's topk>1 tree-verify path. `test/manual/lora/check_spec_baseline_divergence.py` is the control. ## Accept length Every route measured at the same decode depth (20-token cap, a shared prompt set, natural sampling), so no arm is averaged over a different number of verify steps. Each row is self-contained — the spec config differs per algorithm, so only base vs adapters within a row is comparable. With the public adapters each config already uses, 96 prompts per route (mean ± standard error; per-prompt spread is 0.23-1.09, so 16 prompts could not separate these): | Config | base | adapters | vs base | |---|---|---|---| | NEXTN Qwen3.5-35B-A3B (TP4) | 3.097 ± 0.034 | 3.208 ± 0.024 | +3.6%, t=2.7 | | DFLASH Llama-3.1-8B | 2.793 ± 0.061 | 2.708 ± 0.067, 2.669 ± 0.069 | −3.1% / −4.5%, t≤1.4 | | DSPARK Inkling-Small (TP8) | 2.919 ± 0.123 | 2.878 ± 0.119, 2.663 ± 0.097 | −1.4% / −8.8%, t≤1.6 | Only NEXTN separates from base at all, and it goes slightly *up*. DFLASH and DSPARK show nothing distinguishable, including between their two adapters (t=0.4 and t=1.4). So serving these adapters costs no meaningful accept length — none of them moves the output distribution much. That is the whole reason, and it does not generalize. Repeating it on Qwen3.5-35B-A3B (TP4, 4 draft tokens) with three private adapters that force a heavy shift — each prefixes every output word — at mixed rank, one carrying per-expert MoE and lm_head weights (n=16; every gap below is ≥3.9 SE): | route | NEXTN | DFLASH | EAGLE3 | |---|---|---|---| | base | **3.085** | 2.479 | 2.166 | | A (r16) | 2.468 (−20.0%) | 1.635 (−34.0%) | 1.231 (−43.2%) | | B (r32) | 2.507 (−18.7%) | 1.628 (−34.3%) | 1.289 (−40.5%) | | C (r32, +lm_head, MoE) | 2.132 (−30.9%) | 1.636 (−34.0%) | 1.285 (−40.7%) | First-draft-token acceptance, measured exactly by running a one-token draft chain so accept length minus 1 is the probability: | route | NEXTN | DFLASH | EAGLE3 | |---|---|---|---| | base | **0.921** | 0.705 | 0.611 | | A | 0.760 | 0.487 | 0.219 | | B | 0.826 | 0.473 | 0.257 | | C | 0.732 | 0.488 | 0.227 | So the shared-draft design costs accept rate in proportion to how far an adapter moves the output distribution, and self-drafting tolerates it best: NEXTN's own MTP layers lose 19-31%, while separately trained heads lose ~34% (DFLASH) and ~41% (EAGLE3) and give up most of it at the first proposal. Correctness is unaffected in every case — verify still samples from the adapted target. EAGLE3 numbers here are indicative only: they need a local fix to `set_eagle3_layers_to_capture` on this model (unrelated to LoRA, to be filed separately) and were run at `topk=1` for comparability rather than EAGLE3's usual tree verify. ## Benchmarking and Profiling 256 requests x 512 in / 128 out, adapters round-robin, Qwen3.5-35B-A3B + NEXTN, TP4 on 4xGB300. Output tok/s: | concurrency | base, no spec | base + spec | LoRA, no spec | **LoRA + spec** | |---|---|---|---|---| | 1 | 290.8 | 552.2 | 154.4 | **327.3** | | 8 | 1865.4 | 1985.9 | 942.5 | **758.0** | | 32 | 5788.8 | 4011.7 | 2975.4 | **1419.7** | Speculation with adapters gives 2.12x at c=1, falling below 1x by c=32 where speculation loses with or without LoRA. Serving adapters costs ~2-3x throughput independently of speculation. Two follow-ups found while testing, both **general LoRA issues rather than speculative-decoding ones**, so deliberately not gated here: LoRA + `--enable-two-batch-overlap` (TBO children are built by `filter_batch`, which slices `lora_ids` but never rebuilds the LoRA batch info) and LoRA + `--enable-lora-overlap-loading` (an adapter was observed silently not applied while a sibling applied correctly; reproduces with speculation off). ## Checklist - [x] Format code with pre-commit - [x] Add unit tests - [x] Provide accuracy and speed results <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:no_entry_sign: [Run #32329478822](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32329478822)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32329478643](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32329478643)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32329478825](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32329478825)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->
