signal.title: [Fix] Land the decode mamba checkpoint depth on the tree page under DCP
signal.text: ## Motivation A donated mamba checkpoint is only reusable at a depth the radix tree can name. `cache_finished_req` / `cache_unfinished_req` floor the insert key with `page_aligned(tree_page)`, so a checkpoint taken off that grid is attached to the *preceding* node while its state already covers tokens past it — a later request matching that node resumes the linear-attention recurrence mid-stream and then re-consumes those tokens. Silent, no assert, wrong output. #34808 fixed this for the **extend** path with `mamba_checkpoint_grid(tree_page)`, and scoped itself explicitly: > Only the prefill donation depth changes here. Decode tracking keeps its own `--mamba-track-interval` grid. That decode grid does not land on the tree page. `--mamba-track-interval` has one guard, `assert mamba_track_interval % view.page_size == 0` (`server_args.py`), against the **configured** page — and is never resolved anywhere (`grep` over `arg_groups/` and `configs/` is empty). Under DCP the tree allocates on `page_size * dcp_size` (`kv_cache_builder.py`: `page_size=... else token_to_kv_pool_allocator.page_size`), so that guard stops implying the invariant. The insert-time guard that would have caught this was deferred to #34760 and #34780 — **both closed, never merged** — and there is no mamba depth check on the insert in `main` today, so the misalignment stays silent. **Break condition:** `mamba_track_interval % (page_size * dcp_size) != 0`. | page | dcp | tree page | interval | | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | 64 | 4 | 256 | 256 | ok | | 64 | 8 | **512** | 256 | **broken** | | 128 | 4 | 512 | 256 | broken | | 256 | 2 | 512 | 256 | broken | Two shipped recipes are on the broken row today, both in `test_kimi_k3_b300.py`: `TestKimiK3B300Balanced` (`--tp-size 8 --dcp-size 8 --enable-hierarchical-cache`) and `TestKimiK3B300MegaMoE` (`--dcp-size 8` + DSPARK — spec is only rejected under DCP *with* HiCache, so the mamba grid is live there too). Kimi-K3 DCP forces `cutedsl_mla`, which pins `page_size` to 64, and `KimiK3Config.text_config` is a `KimiLinearConfig` so the tree carries a `MAMBA` component. The tree pages at 512 while decode checkpoints every 256, so every odd multiple of 256 names a depth no node carries. Every other DCP hybrid config in tree is page 64 × dcp 4, where `64 * 4 == 256` — the default interval — and the two grids line up by coincidence. That is also why the DCP HiCache KL case (#35380) cannot catch this. ## Modifications `mamba_track_grid(tree_page)` beside `mamba_checkpoint_grid` — the same `lcm`, carrying the requested interval as well: ```python def mamba_track_grid(tree_page: int) -> int: return math.lcm( mamba_checkpoint_grid(tree_page), get_exec().mamba.mamba_track_interval ) ``` Read where a checkpoint depth is picked: `schedule_batch.prepare_for_decode`, the three `batch_result_processor` boundary sites, and the spec verify/prepare paths in `spec_utils`, `dspark_worker_v2`, `dflash_worker_v2`. Pure derivation — nothing is mutated, and `server_args.mamba_track_interval` keeps the value the operator typed. The tree page is a process constant, so each site only needs a live handle to the tree. `prepare_for_decode` and the spec paths take it off the batch, as the extend path already does. The batch-result processor takes it off **its own** `tree_cache`: the batch it is handed is the result-queue `copy()`, whose field list is scoped to what `process_batch_result` needs and does not carry one. Going through `mamba_checkpoint_grid` rather than just rounding onto the page keeps the decode depth chunk-aligned too, which the extend path relies on: a decode-donated depth becomes the prefix of a later extend, and `_force_track_h` asserts `i % mamba_cache_chunk_size == 0` there. Two readers stay on the raw arg because they are flush/write cadence rather than checkpoint depth: `hybrid_linear_attn_backend`'s ReplaySSM force-flush mask and Inkling's `sconv` (which holds only a `ForwardBatch`). `lcm` makes the derived grid a multiple of the raw interval, so every snapshot step is still a flush step and the flush mask's invariant survives. Note the comment at `hybrid_linear_attn_backend.py:403` says the two "fire on the same steps"; after this change they fire on nested sets of steps. `test_batch_result_processor_mamba_boundary.py` is a pre-existing test (#33477) whose hand-built `ScheduleBatch` and processor double now need a `tree_cache`, since `prepare_for_decode` did not read one before this change. Same edit #34808 made to its own double. Page and chunk are set to the interval already under test, so the derived grid stays 4 and every existing boundary expectation is unchanged. ## Accuracy Tests **Not yet measured — this is why the PR is a draft.** #34808 shipped a cold-vs-warm teacher-forced logprob comparison on a live Kimi-Linear dcp8 server for the prefill half; the decode half deserves the same evidence, and this PR currently argues from page alignment alone. An 8×B300 run on the `TestKimiK3B300Balanced` recipe, before and after, is the next step. What is verified statically: - **Cache reuse is unchanged.** The insert floors the donated depth to the tree page, so the node it lands on is `floor(min(N, floor(N/grid)·grid) / 512) · 512` — which collapses to the same `512q` under both grids (checked for every request length in [0, 4096): zero differ). Same number of cached checkpoints, same node depths, same KV prefix. What changes is *which state* is attached: previously a state that had already consumed 256 more tokens than the node it hung on. Snapshot writes into the ping-pong buffer halve on the affected recipes — less decode work, not fewer cache entries. - **Grid unchanged everywhere else:** page 64 × dcp 4, page 32 × dcp 4 (tree 128), and every non-DCP config. signal.title: [Spec] Read the draft checkpoint config with the target's resolution inputs
signal.text: ## Motivation Five call sites read the **draft** checkpoint's HF config while `ServerArgs.__post_init__` resolves arguments, and each one hand-rolls its own subset of `get_config()` arguments. They disagree with each other and with the target's loader: | call site | `revision` | `model_override_args` | `model_config_parser` | decrypted config | |---|---|---|---|---| | target: `ModelConfig.__init__` | yes | yes | yes | yes | | `_resolve_speculative_algorithm_alias` (Gemma4 alias probe) | no | no | **no** | yes | | `_handle_dflash` (block-size inference) | yes | yes | **no** | no | | `_resolve_dflash_draft_attention_backend` | yes | yes | **no** | no | | `read_draft_checkpoint_gamma` (DSpark) | yes | yes | **no** | no | | `draft_is_deepseek_v4` | yes | yes | yes | no | The alias probe is the worst case: with `model_config_parser` dropped, `get_config` re-resolves `"auto"` → the `hf` parser → `transformers` → the HF Hub. A checkpoint whose target config resolves through a parser registered via `@register_model_config_parser` therefore dies at CLI-parse time: ``` File "python/sglang/srt/arg_groups/speculative_hook.py", line 36, in _resolve_speculative_algorithm_alias cfg = get_config( File "python/sglang/srt/utils/hf_transformers/config.py", line 63, in _try_load_longcat_config config_dict, _ = PretrainedConfig.get_config_dict( huggingface_hub.errors.HFValidationError: Repo id must be in the form 'repo_name' or 'namespace/repo_name': '/.../models--Org--Model/snapshots/<sha>/'. Use `repo_type` argument if needed. ``` The traceback names neither the draft nor the flag that supplied the path, because these reads happen before any model config exists. ## Modifications - **`ModelConfig.get_draft_hf_config(server_args)`** — one loader for the draft checkpoint's HF config, whose inputs mirror the ones `from_server_args(..., is_draft_model=True)` feeds `ModelConfig`: `trust_remote_code`, the draft revision (falling back to `--revision`, as `from_server_args` does), parsed `--json-model-override-args`, `--model-config-parser`, and `--decrypted-draft-config-file` as `_configuration_file`. - **All five reads go through it**, so argument resolution and the draft worker's own load (`tp_worker._init_model_config`, already on `from_server_args`) now resolve the same config. Side effect: the five reads collapse onto one `get_config` lru entry instead of up to four distinct ones. - A read failure is re-raised naming `--speculative-draft-model-path`, the revision and the parser, with the cause both chained and in the message text — the two callers that swallow it log with `"Error: %s"`, which never formats `__cause__`. - `--json-model-override-args` is parsed *before* the read, so a quoting error in that flag is not reported as an unreadable draft checkpoint. ### Tests - `test/registered/unit/configs/test_draft_hf_config_resolution.py` — the read inputs (including the `model_override_args`-as-dict conversion and the `_configuration_file` whitespace handling), the error message and cause, and an `ast` parity check comparing the keyword sets of *both* `get_config` call sites in `ModelConfig`, so a new input on the target read that never reaches the draft read fails the suite. Plus the bug as behavior: a draft served by a registered plugin parser at a path the `hf` parser cannot read, covering the `FROZEN_KV_MTP` promotion, the `EAGLE3` rejection and the plain `NEXTN` alias — none of which had coverage before. - `test/registered/unit/test_draft_config_read_ratchet.py` — asserts no raw `get_config(` call remains under `srt/arg_groups/` or `srt/speculative/`, matched by `ast` (a comment naming `get_config()` must not fail CI) and self-checking that it actually scanned files. A full draft `ModelConfig` cannot be built during argument resolution: `_config_draft_model` rewrites `hf_config.architectures[0]` for drafts, and its DeepseekV4 branch is gated on the `speculative_algorithm` that the alias probe is still resolving. Only the config read is shared; the docstring records that invariant. ## Deliberately out of scope Unifying the read *inputs* leaves the read's *failure policy* split across the five sites: fatal at the alias probe and at `_resolve_dflash_draft_attention_backend`, swallowed-and-defaulted at `_handle_dflash` (`speculative_num_draft_tokens = 16`) and at the DSpark gamma read. Those two swallows are now weaker than they look: before this change the arg-resolution read used a *narrower* argument set than the draft `ModelConfig` load, so a failure there could be a false alarm the load would survive; now the two reads are identical and hit the same `get_config` cache entry, so a failed read recurs verbatim at load time. The fallback mostly relocates the crash into the scheduler subprocess, and in the transient-failure case DFLASH boots with a guessed block size that `dflash_worker_v2` only warns about. Changing that is a behavior change for DFLASH users and belongs in its own PR; this one keeps the policy as-is and makes the swallowed warning carry the root cause. ## Accuracy Tests Not applicable — argument resolution only; no kernel or model forward code is touched. The resolved `hf_config` is unchanged for any launch that already passed the same inputs at both layers. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Not applicable. Startup-only path; strictly fewer config reads than before. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32403698111](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32403698111)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32403697915](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32403697915)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32403698251](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32403698251)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [AMD] perf: fuse MLA value projection with MXFP4 output quantization
signal.text: <!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. --> ## Motivation This PR complements #32935, which separately fuses the absorbed MLA key projection, RoPE, and KV-cache write. The two optimizations are independent; this branch is based directly on `main` and contains only the value-projection fusion. During Kimi-K2.5 MXFP4 decode on ROCm gfx95, the absorbed value projection still runs as a batched A16W4 GEMM that materializes a BF16 tensor. `o_proj` immediately reads that tensor and quantizes it back to MXFP4. Folding the quantization into the GEMM epilogue avoids this intermediate HBM round trip and removes one launch from the decode path. ## Modifications - Add `batched_gemm_a16wfp4_flatten_mxfp4_quant`, a Triton kernel that fuses the absorbed value-projection GEMM with flattened MXFP4 output quantization. - Preserve the split path's BF16 rounding boundary so the fused output and scales match bit-for-bit. - Route eligible AITER decode calls through the fused kernel when `w_vc` and `o_proj` use MXFP4. - Add `SGLANG_ROCM_FUSE_MLA_VALUE_MXFP4_QUANT`, enabled by default. - Probe shape, dtype, and AITER configuration support before dispatch; unsupported configurations fall back to the split GEMM plus `fused_flatten_mxfp4_quant`. - Keep DSA, optimized LoRA execution, and active `kv_b_proj` LoRAs on the existing split path. - Support eager execution, `torch.compile`, and HIP graph capture. - Add AMD parity coverage, CPU gate coverage, a focused microbenchmark, and environment-variable documentation. ## Accuracy Tests Hardware and model: - 4x AMD Instinct MI355X (`gfx950`), TP=4 - Model: `Kimi-K2.5-MXFP4` - AITER prefill/decode attention, MoE - AITER all-reduce fusion - FP8 E4M3 KV cache - Full GSM8K test set: 1,319 questions, 8-shot, maximum 512 new tokens - Project pass threshold: 0.92 | Configuration | Accuracy | Invalid responses | Status | | --- | ---: | ---: | --- | | Value fusion enabled | 0.936 | 0.000 | PASS | Focused correctness tests: ```text test_rocm_mla_value_fusion.py: 1 passed test_rocm_mla_value_mxfp4.py: 1 passed, 3 subtests passed ``` The GPU parity test compares fused output values and scales bit-for-bit (`rtol=0`, `atol=0`) against the split BF16 GEMM plus MXFP4 quantization path for 1, 17, and 64 tokens. It also covers `torch.compile`, HIP graph capture, and the unsupported-configuration fallback. ## Speed Tests and Profiling End-to-end incremental A/B configuration (following the Kimi-K2.5 ROCm recipe): - 4x AMD Instinct MI355X (`gfx950`), TP=4 - Kimi-K2.5 MXFP4 - AITER prefill/decode attention and MoE - AITER all-reduce fusion - FP8 E4M3 KV cache, page size 16 - Breakable prefill graph and full decode graph - ISL=8,192, OSL=1,024, concurrency=4 - 20 measured requests after 8 warmup requests - Identical seed (`42`) and generated workload in both arms - The #32935 projection/RoPE/cache fusion was enabled in both arms - The only A/B change was `SGLANG_ROCM_FUSE_MLA_VALUE_MXFP4_QUANT=0/1` | Metric | Value fusion disabled | Value fusion enabled | Change | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | | Output throughput | 434.01 tok/s | 434.58 tok/s | +0.13% | | Total token throughput | 3,908.17 tok/s | 3,913.37 tok/s | +0.13% | | Median TPOT | 8.717 ms | 8.696 ms | -0.25% | | Median inter-token latency | 8.185 ms | 8.175 ms | -0.12% | | Median end-to-end latency | 8,349.80 ms | 8,337.28 ms | -0.15% | | Median TTFT | 246.32 ms | 245.57 ms | -0.31% | Focused kernel benchmark on one MI355X: | Decode tokens | Split | Fused | Speedup | | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | | 1 | 40.627 us | 20.779 us | 1.955x | | 2 | 41.338 us | 19.958 us | 2.071x | | 4 | 41.004 us | 20.329 us | 2.017x | | 8 | 40.912 us | 19.904 us | 2.056x | | 16 | 41.888 us | 20.935 us | 2.001x | | 32 | 41.646 us | 20.097 us | 2.072x | | 64 | 42.064 us | 20.146 us | 2.088x | ## Checklist - signal.title: [Bug] A global --attention-backend kills the server when a non-DiT component does not declare it (MiniMax-H3 audio_vae)
signal.text: ### Checklist - [x] I searched related issues but found no solution. - [x] The bug persists in the latest version. - [x] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback. - [x] Please use English. ### Describe the bug Passing a global `--attention-backend` that the *DiT* supports takes the whole server down if any **non-DiT** component's attention layer does not declare that backend — even when the layer declares a `default_attention_backend` for exactly this case. With MiniMax-H3 and `--attention-backend sage_attn`: ``` ValueError: Attention backend 'sage_attn' is not supported by this attention layer; supported backends: ['fa', 'torch_sdpa'] ... Failed to load customized audio_vae ... Rank 0 scheduler is dead ``` The audio VAE's attention layer is constructed with both a supported set and a default: `python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/models/vaes/minimax_h3_audio_vae/audio_vae.py:60-70` ```python supported_attention_backends={AttentionBackendEnum.FA, AttentionBackendEnum.TORCH_SDPA}, default_attention_backend=AttentionBackendEnum.TORCH_SDPA, ``` `get_attn_backend()` does have a fallback path, but it is gated on the selection not being explicit (`selector.py:188-201`): ```python selection_is_explicit = isinstance(server_args, ServerArgs) and server_args.is_arg_explicitly_set("attention_backend") ... elif not selection_is_explicit: allowed_fallback_reason = "platform default fallback" ``` A `--attention-backend` on the command line is explicit, so `allowed_fallback_reason` stays `None`, `candidate_backends` holds only the requested backend, and `selector.py:233-241` turns it into the hard `ValueError` above. Not honouring an explicit request silently is reasonable; the problem is that a *global* flag is treated as an explicit request **for every component**, including ones that cannot possibly satisfy it and that ship a declared default for that situation. Practical consequence: any global sparse/fp8 attention backend requires the operator to know the full component list up front and repeat it, and getting it wrong is a dead server rather than a warning. On MiniMax-H3 all three non-DiT components (`text_encoder`, `audio_vae`, `video_vae`) have to be exempted, and the set has grown between nightlies, so a config that worked on an earlier image fails on a later one with an error that points at the VAE rather than at the flag. ### Reproduction ```bash sglang serve --model-path <MiniMax-H3> --model-variant fl2va \ --num-gpus 1 --attention-backend sage_attn ``` Startup fails as above. Works with the components enumerated: ```bash --attention-backend sage_attn \ --component-attention-backends text_encoder=torch_sdpa,audio_vae=torch_sdpa,video_vae=torch_sdpa ``` ### Environment One RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition (sm_120), CUDA 13, `lmsysorg/sglang` nightly. The code path is unchanged on current `main` (read at `a49560ce50`), so this is not specific to that GPU or image — any global backend a non-DiT component doesn't declare reproduces it. ### Suggested direction Any of these would work; the first is the smallest: 1. Treat `--attention-backend` as explicit only for components that declare support, and fall back to the layer's `default_attention_backend` elsewhere with a `logger.warning` naming the component. This keeps "don't silently downgrade what the user asked for" for the DiT, where the request is meaningful. 2. Keep failing closed, but make the message actionable: name the component being loaded and print the `--component-attention-backends component=torch_sdpa` line that fixes it. Happy to send a PR for either once maintainers pick one.

signal.title: fix(cache): retain shared SWA slots until final free
signal.text: ## Problem Different full-cache indices can reference the same physical sliding-window-attention slot. Freeing one mapping previously returned that slot to the allocator even while another mapping still referenced it, allowing the live slot to be reallocated and later freed again. This PR targets `sglang-miles`; [Miles #2666](https://github.com/radixark/miles/pull/2666) exercises the affected path. ## Change Track a reference count for each physical SWA slot whenever full-to-SWA mappings are written, replaced, or cleared. `free_swa` now clears the requested mappings and returns token slots, or whole pages, only when their remaining counts are zero. Reset counts on allocator clear while preserving PureSWA's direct identity mapping.
signal.author: Arist12

signal.title: fix(lora): build the MoE LoRA align JIT kernel on ROCm
signal.text: ## Problem The MoE-LoRA alignment kernel is JIT-compiled without hipify on ROCm. Its CUDA-only CUB include and CUDA runtime names therefore fail under `hipcc`, and HIP's function-attribute API requires a `const void *` kernel pointer. This PR targets `sglang-miles`; [Miles #2666](https://github.com/radixark/miles/pull/2666) is a downstream consumer. ## Change Select hipCUB for ROCm and alias its namespace to the kernel's existing `cub` use. Add ROCm mappings for the shared-memory device and function attributes, pass the kernel through `std::bit_cast<const void *>`, and register the existing kernel test for AMD CI.

signal.title: [kernel] Split the custom all-reduce communicator into push/pull planes
signal.text: > Generated by Claude. ## Motivation Every JIT collective in `csrc/distributed` and `csrc/kimi_k3/comm` took one flat `CommunicatorObj` that carried every buffer any of them might want: `2 * world_size` push slots, a pull workspace, per-block semaphores, a rank-local counter, and one of the three multicast addresses. Consequences: - The other two multicast addresses travelled out of band. `ws_mc_base` was an `int64_t` argument repeated at five call sites, always the same constant; `pull_sem_mc_ptr` went through a per-world-size Python dict populated by `register_comm()`, duplicated in three modules. - A push-only owner (the fused qk-norm instances in `minimax_m2`) had to allocate a placeholder 1 KB pull buffer plus one semaphore purely to satisfy the constructor. - Only `custom_all_reduce.cuh` ever read `pull_workspaces` / `pull_bytes` / `pull_mc_workspace`. The K3 pull kernels reduce in place on the caller's own symmetric input and borrow the plane just to barrier on, so half the object was dead weight for most callers. - `custom_all_reduce.cuh` defined helpers at `namespace sglang` scope and was `#include`d by three K3 files across directories, so renaming anything inside it silently broke downstream kernels. ## What changed Split the object by lifetime rather than by direction: | | contents | |---|---| | `sgl.distributed.PushPlane` | zero-filled symmetric push slots, rank-local phase counter, multicast base | | `sgl.distributed.PullPlane` | symmetric pull buffers + per-block semaphores, both multicast bases. Either half may be a 0-element tensor | | `sgl.distributed.Communicator` | the two planes (either optional) + the pull launch widths; what every kernel takes | Both *fixed* multicast addresses now live on the planes. That deletes the `ws_mc_base` parameter from five entry points and the `_PULL_SEM_MC_MAP` registry from three modules. The *per-call* multicast address — a slice of the caller's own symmetric buffer, so it changes every call — stays a plain `intptr_t`, which is what it should be. `PullPlane`'s optional halves replace the placeholder-buffer trick: `minimax_m2` now constructs `Communicator(push=..., pull=None)` and a kernel that needs a missing plane fails with a message instead of reading a dummy buffer. ### Shared vocabulary moved under `include/` - **`include/sgl_kernel/distributed/ptx.cuh`** collects the inline PTX the collectives share into `sglang::device::ptx`, which `mbarrier.cuh` and the two K3 files reopen. Removed: three identical copies of the multimem flag increment, three copies of the "multicast alias of a semaphore's flag" helper (now `Semaphore::mc_flag`), and the 16B access helpers that were defined at `namespace sglang` scope inside `custom_all_reduce.cuh`. `csrc/kimi_k3/comm/ptx_sys.cuh` is deleted. The five communication kernels now contain zero inline PTX. - **`Barrier` / `McBarrier`** (unicast fan-out and one-`multimem.red` variants of the same window protocol) and **`LamportTrait`** (the pos-zero marker) live next to the planes, so each protocol has one implementation instead of one per kernel. - The three `csrc` → `csrc` includes of `custom_all_reduce.cuh` are gone. What they actually used — `reduce_vec`, the marker traits — moved under `include/`. - `alloc_workspace_tensor` moved to `host::ffi`, so `utils.cuh` no longer depends on `ffi.h`. `tp_qknorm`'s 8B `ld.volatile` / `st.volatile` pair became `ld_relaxed_8B` / `st_relaxed_8B` at `.sys` scope (PTX defines volatile as relaxed at system scope, and the store is cross-GPU). Load scope measured identical at `.gpu`, so the `.gpu` load variant was dropped and the vocabulary has one scope. ## Verification (8×B200, SM100) **Correctness — 291 tests, all passing** | test | | |---|---| | `test_custom_all_reduce.py` (8 GPU) | 180 passed | | `test_ar_fusion.py` (8 GPU) | 58 passed | | `test_tp_qknorm.py` (8 GPU) | 42 passed | | `test_collectives.py` (8 GPU) | 5 passed | | `test_compute.py` | 6 passed | | `test_custom_all_reduce_v2_capability.py` | 4 passed | | `test_attn_residual.py` | 1 passed | All 11 affected JIT modules build; `fp8_blockwise_scaled_mm_sm120` verified with a direct SM120 nvcc compile. clangd reports zero diagnostics on every touched file except two pre-existing cutlass include-path gaps in `.clangd`. **Registers / spills** — `cuobjdump -res-usage`, this branch vs the merge base, kernels paired by hand where the refactor renamed them: - **No spills anywhere** (`STACK=0`, `LOCAL=0` for every kernel). - Unchanged or better everywhere except `1shot_push`: bf16 60→63, fp16 61→63, fp32 56→58. That kernel is 2.7–6.2 % *faster* — `LamportTrait`'s 4-byte-atom marker test replaces a per-bf16-half test, cutting its SASS from 512 to 344 instructions. - `2shot_pull` eager improves (bf16 53→51) and the multicast variants drop one register. **Performance** — kernel time only, measured by replaying a CUDA graph of 20 chained calls so host dispatch is excluded; three interleaved rounds per arm, per-arm spread under 1 %: | variant | delta vs merge base | |---|---| | `1shot_push` / eager (dispatched ≤ 768 KB) | **−2.7 % … −6.2 %** | | `2shot_pull` / multicast (dispatched > 768 KB) | −0.03 % … +0.39 % | | `1shot_pull` eager and multicast | −1.1 % … +0.6 % | | `2shot_pull` / eager | +0.5 % … +0.9 % | 33 points: median +0.32 %, worst +0.92 %. On the path the tuned SM100/world-8 config actually dispatches: median **−3.30 %**, worst +0.39 %. One note on how that number was reached. An earlier revision of this branch regressed `2shot_pull` eager by 7–18 %. Bisecting with self-contained reference kernels showed the params layout, the `Barrier` object and the `Impl` abstraction were all innocent — an exact transplant of the old body still regressed. The cause was the address form: folding the shard offset into the eight base pointers as a typed 32-bit vector index keeps the peer table on the uniform datapath (`UIMAD.WIDE` off a constant-bank base), whereas biasing `vid` per access, or using a 64-bit byte offset, makes all eight addresses thread-varying and costs ~12 registers per thread. Also, binding a params array address to a named local that stays live across the kernel breaks the same proof. Both are noted in comments at the point of use, since either one silently costs ~10 %. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32400438557](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32400438557)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #32406638953](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32406638953)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32400438446](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32400438446)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.author: TallMessiWu

signal.title: [AMD] DSv4: fuse the qk-norm-rope pair on the MTP target-verify path
signal.text: ## Summary On the DeepSeek-V4 unified-KV path, the fused qk-norm-rope kernel is wired to decode only. MTP **target-verify** falls back to running the same work as two separate launches per layer — `sglang::fused_q_norm_rope` for q and `sglang::fused_norm_rope` for kv — which is 122 launches per verify step across the 61 target layers. This PR routes target-verify through the same fused kernel, **with the cache store left off**. The store half deliberately does not move. Decode is a 1-source consumer: the ring holds everything, so writing it before attention is required. Target-verify is **2-source** — attention reads history from the ring and takes the current chunk as `k`/`v` so the draft tokens stay causally masked against one another. Writing the current chunk into the ring ahead of attention makes those tokens indistinguishable from history, and every draft position then attends to all of them regardless of order. Fusing the store as well drops GSM8K from 0.950 to 0.027 while looking like a ~7% throughput win, because it skips exactly the work correctness depends on. Only the norm+RoPE half is sound, and that is what this PR fuses. ## Modifications - **`python/sglang/srt/models/deepseek_v4.py`** (`MQALayer._forward_prepare`) - `do_fused_store` now also admits `is_target_verify()` when the new gate is on. The kernel is token-indexed (`q`, `kv` and `positions` are all length M), so a verify batch carrying several draft tokens per request is a shape it already handles. - On that path the kernel is called with `swa_cache`/`swa_loc` left as `None`, so it performs q-norm+RoPE and kv-norm+RoPE and stores nothing. `get_unified_swa_loc` is not called at all — it exists solely to address a store this path no longer performs. - `kv` is returned instead of being set to `None`, so the caller's existing contract drives the rest unchanged: `attn_k = kv` gives attention the real current-chunk source, and `save_kv_cache = kv is not None` makes the backend write the ring after attention, exactly as the unfused path did. - `kv` is materialised with `.contiguous()` first: it is a strided slice of `qkv_a`, and the ring store requires a contiguous buffer. The unfused path pays the identical copy inside `_compute_kv_bf16`, so this is parity, not added overhead. - **`python/sglang/srt/environ.py`** — new `SGLANG_OPT_FUSED_QK_NORM_ROPE_VERIFY` (default on). Set to 0 to fall back to the unfused chain on the verify path. Decode, prefill and the non-unified paths are untouched. ### Kernel-level evidence Per target-verify forward, from graphs-off traces segmented by the 61 `DeepseekV4DecoderLayer` frames (TP8, 8k/1k, conc 16, rank 0). `fused_q_norm_rope` and `fused_norm_rope` both go to zero and one `_fused_qk_norm_rope_store_kernel` replaces them; no other kernel is added. | layer type | launches/fwd (base → patched) | GPU us/fwd excl. collective | |---|---|---| | CSA (30 layers) | 1920.0 → 1800.0 | 15779 → 15488 (−1.8%) | | HCA (31 layers) | 1526.8 → 1410.5 | 12385 → 12014 (−3.0%) | "excl. collective" is the number to read: `cross_device_reduce` blocks until the slowest rank arrives, so its duration tracks inter-rank skew rather than work this change moves. ## Accuracy Model `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro`, MI355X (gfx950), TP8. GSM8K, full 1319 questions, 5-shot, greedy. | run | accuracy | invalid | |---|---|---| | baseline (gate 0) | 0.950 | 0.000 | | patched (gate 1) | 0.949 | 0.000 | | patched (gate 1, repeat) | 0.945 | 0.000 | Note this is measured **without** `SGLANG_SIMULATE_ACC_LEN`. The throughput harness pins acceptance to the golden AL, which fabricates which draft tokens are accepted — fine for speed, but it would bypass the accept/reject path this change touches. Acceptance here is whatever the draft model earns. ```bash export SGLANG_HACK_FLASHMLA_BACKEND=unified_kv_triton export SGLANG_ENABLE_UNIFIED_RADIX_TREE=1 export SGLANG_OPT_UNIFIED_CACHE_FREE_OUT_OF_WINDOW_SLOTS=1 export AITER_BF16_FP8_MOE_BOUND=0 export SGLANG_DEFAULT_THINKING=1 SGLANG_DSV4_REASONING_EFFORT=high # flip this between 0 (baseline) and 1 (patched) export SGLANG_OPT_FUSED_QK_NORM_ROPE_VERIFY=1 python3 -m sglang.launch_server \ --model-path deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro \ --served-model-name deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro \ --host 0.0.0.0 --port 31710 --trust-remote-code \ --tensor-parallel-size 8 \ --attention-backend dsv4 \ --page-size 256 --swa-full-tokens-ratio 0.10 \ --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 \ --disable-shared-experts-fusion \ --tool-call-parser deepseekv4 --reasoning-parser deepseek-v4 \ --chunked-prefill-size 8192 --mem-fraction-static 0.85 \ --max-running-requests 32 --cuda-graph-max-bs 32 \ --speculative-algorithm EAGLE --speculative-num-steps 3 \ --speculative-eagle-topk 1 --speculative-num-draft-tokens 4 python3 benchmark/gsm8k/bench_sglang.py \ --backend srt --host http://127.0.0.1 --port 31710 \ --num-questions 1319 --num-shots 5 \ --max-new-tokens 1024 --temperature 0.0 --parallel 32 ``` ## Performance Same model and hardware. 8k input / 1k output, TP8, steady state (10 waves through a `--max-concurrency` gate). Each cell is the mean of 2 repeats run in `off, on, on, off` order per concurrency, so a monotonic drift over the block shifts both arms equally instead of being credited to the patch. Repeated all-gates-off runs on this node put the noise floor at 0.25% (1σ). | concurrency | output tok/s (base → patched) | uplift | mean TPOT ms | accept len | |---|---|---|---|---| | 4 | 332.43 → 341.07 | **+2.60%** | 11.37 → 11.06 | 2.499 → 2.498 | | 8 | 543.73 → 555.57 | **+2.18%** | 13.75 → 13.46 | 2.499 → 2.469 | | 16 | 839.00 → 857.32 | **+2.18%** | 17.98 → 17.57 | 2.499 → 2.507 | | 32 | 1167.14 → 1186.66 | **+1.67%** | 25.79 → 25.34 | 2.482 → 2.508 | Acceptance length is flat across arms, so the uplift is kernel time and not a shift in speculation behaviour. ```bash # same server launch as above, with SGLANG_OPT_FUSED_QK_NORM_ROPE_VERIFY # flipped 0/1 between arms, plus the throughput harness env: export SGLANG_SIMULATE_ACC_LEN=2.49 export SGLANG_SIMULATE_ACC_METHOD=match-expected export SGLANG_SIMULATE_ACC_TOKEN_MODE=real-draft-token # CONC in {4, 8, 16, 32}; --max-running-requests/--cuda-graph-max-bs = 2*CONC # capped at 32 on both arms (this image cannot capture a decode graph at bs 48). CONC=16 python3 -m sglang.bench_serving --backend sglang \ --host 127.0.0.1 --port 31710 --model deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro \ --dataset-name random --random-input-len 8192 --random-output-len 1024 \ --random-range-ratio 0.8 --num-prompts $((CONC * 10)) \ --max-concurrency $CONC ``` `bench_serving` ignores EOS by default here (it only offers `--disable-ignore-eos`), so every request runs to exactly 1024 output tokens and neither arm can win by generating less. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:no_entry_sign: [Run #32377716380](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32377716380)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32377716823](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32377716823)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32377716407](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32377716407)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [MoE] Add FlashInfer SM90 MXFP4 W4A8 CUTLASS MoE
signal.text: ## Motivation SGLang currently supports FlashInfer's SM90 MXFP4 W4A16 CUTLASS MoE path, which was introduced in SGLang #24816 on top of FlashInfer [#3084](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/3084). FlashInfer [#3738](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/3738) adds a different Hopper path that dynamically quantizes activations to FP8 and runs MXFP4-weight x FP8-activation MoE GEMMs using Humming-style pre-MMA E8M0 scale fusion. This PR wires that path into SGLang as an explicit opt-in: ```bash --moe-runner-backend flashinfer_mxfp4 \ --flashinfer-mxfp4-moe-precision fp8 ``` The existing `default` and `bf16` behavior is unchanged. Related work: - SGLang https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/24816 - FlashInfer https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/3738 ### FlashInfer version requirement This integration intentionally targets the corrected API from FlashInfer #4431, where the FC1 and FC2 residual scales are FP32 tensors in local-expert order with shape `[num_local_experts]`. FlashInfer reuses its internal expert permutation to map those scales to routed rows, including global-to-local expert mapping under EP. The original #3738 ABI briefly shipped before being reverted from FlashInfer 0.6.17 by #4411. It required downstream runtimes to construct routed-row residual tensors during every forward. SGLang does not support that older ABI. The new option therefore requires both: - `flashinfer-python >= 0.6.18` - `preprocess_moe_weights_for_sm90_mixed_gemm_humming` SGLang currently pins FlashInfer 0.6.17. This PR does not change that global pin. With 0.6.17, selecting `fp8` fails immediately with an actionable error, while all existing FlashInfer paths remain compatible. The dependency, cubin, and JIT-cache pins should be upgraded together in a follow-up change. GPU validation for this PR used FlashInfer 0.6.18 built from commit `8044d94bf9acc5369857baf88d28906bb32bf264`, which contains the corrected API from FlashInfer #4431. ## Modifications ### Runtime selection and compatibility - Add `fp8` to `--flashinfer-mxfp4-moe-precision`. - Select the new path only for `flashinfer_mxfp4` on SM90. - Keep W4A16 as the default SM90 behavior. - Reject the SM90-specific `fp8` option on SM100 and SM120 to avoid confusing it with their existing MXFP8 activation paths. - Require the corrected FlashInfer 0.6.18+ API instead of accepting the older routed-row residual ABI. - Pass `use_wfp4afp8_humming=True` only when the new path is selected. The keyword is omitted completely for FlashInfer 0.6.17 compatibility. ### Weight preprocessing - Use `preprocess_moe_weights_for_sm90_mixed_gemm_humming` for both FC1 and FC2 during post-load processing. - Store the folded interleaved weight scales produced by FlashInfer. - Store `residual * 64` as one FP32 value per local expert for FC1 and FC2. - Preserve GPT-OSS gate/up layout conversion and its existing padding rules. - Fill synthetic E8M0 scale padding from an existing scale in the same expert, preventing padding from changing that expert's min/max exponent range. - Support both the GPT-OSS MXFP4 quantization path and the DeepSeek-V4 MXFP4 expert path. ### Kernel invocation Construct the five Humming quant-scale slots expected by the corrected FlashInfer API: 1. FC1 folded weight block scales 2. FC1 per-local-expert residual scale, including the fixed `2^6` compensation 3. Reserved scalar FC2 activation scale 4. FC2 folded weight block scales 5. FC2 per-local-expert residual scale, including the fixed `2^6` compensation The existing TP/EP topology is forwarded to FlashInfer so it can map global expert IDs to the corresponding local residual scale. ### Tests and benchmark - Extend the registered SM90 MXFP4 test suite with: - GPT-OSS preprocessing checks against the FlashInfer helper - five-scale kernel invocation and direct FlashInfer comparison - aligned and non-aligned hidden/intermediate dimensions - padding invariance for per-expert residual scales - EP rank with global expert IDs - DeepSeek-V4 preprocessing - fail-fast behavior on FlashInfer versions before 0.6.18 - Extend the manual SM90 benchmark to compare: - SGLang Marlin W4A16 - FlashInfer CUTLASS W4A16 - FlashInfer CUTLASS W4A8 - Update the server-argument documentation. ## Accuracy Tests The registered SM90 MXFP4 suite passed: ```bash python -m pytest \ test/registered/unit/layers/quantization/test_mxfp4_sm90_cutlass.py -v ``` ```text 18 passed, 1 skipped ``` The DeepSeek-V4 MXFP4 checkpoint was launched with: ```bash python -m sglang.launch_server \ --model-path /home/models/DeepSeek-V4-Flash \ --trust-remote-code \ --tp 4 \ --moe-runner-backend flashinfer_mxfp4 \ --flashinfer-mxfp4-moe-precision fp8 \ --enforce-disable-flashinfer-allreduce-fusion \ --host 0.0.0.0 \ --port 30000 ``` DeepSeek-V4 accuracy was evaluated using the same 200-example GSM8K setup as SGLang #24816. Both runs used the same TP=4 configuration, dataset, sampling parameters, and server options; only `--flashinfer-mxfp4-moe-precision` changed between `bf16` and `fp8`. ```bash PYTHONPATH=/sgl-workspace/sglang_dev/python \ python -m sglang.test.run_eval \ --port 30000 \ --eval-name gsm8k \ --num-examples 200 \ --api chat \ --max-tokens 1024 \ --num-threads 32 \ --temperature 0 \ --gsm8k-data-path /tmp/gsm8k-test.jsonl ``` | MoE precision | GSM8K score | Total latency | Output throughput | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | | W4A16 (`bf16`) | 0.985 | 37.301 s | 611.809 token/s | | W4A8 (`fp8`) | 0.985 | 32.952 s | 683.574 token/s | W4A8 preserved the W4A16 GSM8K score while reducing evaluation latency by 11.7% and increasing output throughput by 11.7%. The score also matches the 0.985 W4A16 result reported in SGLang #24816. ## Speed Tests and Profiling The downstream benchmark uses the GPT-OSS-like shape from SGLang #24816: hidden size 4096, intermediate size 2048, 256 experts, and top-k 6. Each FlashInfer path was fully autotuned, followed by 5 warmup iterations and 30 timed iterations. The remaining token shapes were run in parallel with one independent shape per H20 GPU; each W4A16/W4A8 pair ran on the same GPU. The benchmark can be reproduced with FlashInfer 0.6.18+: ```bash PYTHONPATH=python:/path/to/flashinfer \ FLASHINFER_DISABLE_VERSION_CHECK=1 \ python test/manual/layers/moe/bench_mxfp4_sm90_kernels.py ``` Results on NVIDIA H20-3e: | Tokens | CUTLASS W4A16 median (min) | CUTLASS W4A8 median (min) | Speedup | | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | | 4 | 0.275 ms (0.272 ms) | 0.164 ms (0.162 ms) | 1.68x | | 16 | 0.842 ms (0.840 ms) | 0.463 ms (0.460 ms) | 1.82x | | 64 | 1.894 ms (1.892 ms) | 1.037 ms (1.019 ms) | 1.83x | | 256 | 2.410 ms (2.403 ms) | 1.478 ms (1.383 ms) | 1.63x | | 1024 | 3.912 ms (3.906 ms) | 2.093 ms (1.999 ms) | 1.87x | | 2048 | 6.973 ms (6.954 ms) | 3.394 ms (3.384 ms) | 2.05x | | 4096 | 13.013 ms (12.971 ms) | 6.295 ms (6.210 ms) | 2.07x | | 8192 | 25.624 ms (25.546 ms) | 12.308 ms (12.293 ms) | 2.08x | FlashInfer CUTLASS W4A8 was faster at every measured token count, with speedups ranging from 1.63x to 2.08x. The gain reaches approximately 2.0x for token counts of 2048 and above. The GSM8K latency and throughput numbers above provide an end-to-end serving sanity check, but the kernel benchmark is the more controlled performance comparison because generated output lengths are not fixed. ## Scope and Limitations - The implementation is SM90-only. - It is opt-in and does not change the default W4A16 path. - A coordinated FlashInfer 0.6.18 dependency update is required before production enablement. ## Checklist - [x] Format the code with pre-commit. - [x] Add unit tests according to the repository test conventions. - [x] Update server-argument documentation. - [x] Run the registered tests on an SM90 GPU with FlashInfer 0.6.18. - [x] Add a DeepSeek-V4 end-to-end smoke-test result. - [ ] Upgrade the FlashInfer Python, cubin, and JIT-cache pins together in a coordinated follow-up change. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32393619327](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32393619327)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32393619734](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32393619734)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #32393619293](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32393619293)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: fix(openai): omit DSV tools when tool choice is none
signal.text: ## Motivation DeepSeek-V4 and DeepSeek-V3.2 still encode tool schemas when a Chat Completions request sets `tool_choice="none"`. Output parsing is disabled for this choice, so a model-generated native tool call can leak into `message.content` as raw DSML. Fixes #35736 ## Modifications - Remove request-level and message-level tools from the copied DSV4/DSV32 messages when tools are disabled. - Preserve the existing tool encoding behavior for `tool_choice="auto"`. - Add regression coverage for DSV4 and DSV32, including system and developer message tools. ## Accuracy Tests Added prompt-encoding unit tests for `tool_choice="none"` and `tool_choice="auto"`. This change does not modify model execution. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Not applicable. signal.title: [Bugfix] Fix full prefill CUDA graph padding and EAGLE capture
signal.text: ## Motivation Full prefill CUDA graphs replay fixed token buckets that may be larger than the live batch. Models that mask padded hidden states need the live `num_token_non_padded` boundary even when attention tensors are not gathered. Without it, padded rows can propagate through the captured graph. EAGLE target prefill also consumes the full target hidden-state sequence. FullCG previously captured the configured return-hidden-state mode, which could be insufficient and force target prefill back to eager execution. ## Modifications - Register and populate `num_token_non_padded` for FullCG, including non-gathered execution. - Capture `FULL` hidden states for EAGLE target prefill under FullCG while retaining `LAST` for breakable draft workers. - Keep the EAGLE eager fallback specific to `tc_piecewise`, whose fixed capture ceiling can remain below `FULL`. - Add focused regression tests for the non-gathered token boundary and FullCG EAGLE admission. ## Accuracy Tests No model math or kernels are changed. - 42 focused unit tests passed, including 2 parameterized subtests. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Not applicable. The changes update CUDA graph metadata and capture mode; they do not add work to attention or model kernels. ## Checklist - [x] Format code with the repository pre-commit configuration. - [x] Add focused regression tests. - [x] No documentation update is required. - [x] No speed benchmark is required for this graph-correctness fix. - [x] Follow the SGLang code style guidance. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:no_entry_sign: [Run #32325612785](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32325612785)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32325612649](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32325612649)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32325612768](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32325612768)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.text: ## Motivation Dynamo's native SGLang sidecar needs a validated description of SGLang's ZMQ KV-event publisher to subscribe each registered data-parallel rank for event-driven KV routing. SGLang already exposes this structured `kv_events` descriptor through HTTP `/server_info`, but native gRPC `GetServerInfo` currently returns only the raw `ServerArgs` fields. Consumers would otherwise need to duplicate SGLang's endpoint validation and DCP-aware block-size calculation. ## Modifications - Add the existing `ServerArgs.describe_kv_events_publisher()` result to native gRPC `GetServerInfo.json_info` under `kv_events`. - Preserve all existing flat server-information fields. - Keep the protobuf contract unchanged; this is an additive field inside the existing JSON payload. - Keep the high-volume KV-event stream on SGLang's existing ZMQ publisher rather than proxying it through request/response gRPC. ## Accuracy Tests Not applicable. signal.title: [Bug] DeepSeek-V4 leaks raw DSML when tool_choice="none"
signal.text: ### Checklist - [x] I searched related issues but found no solution. - [x] The bug persists in the latest version. - [x] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback. - [x] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed. - [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed. ### Describe the bug DeepSeek-V4 leaks its raw DSML tool-call markup into `message.content` when a Chat Completions request contains a non-empty `tools` array and sets `tool_choice: "none"`. The response is HTTP 200 with `finish_reason: "stop"` and no structured `tool_calls`, but `message.content` contains output such as: ```text <｜DSML｜tool_calls> <｜DSML｜invoke name="Bash"> <｜DSML｜parameter name="command" string="true">pwd</｜DSML｜parameter> </｜DSML｜invoke> </｜DSML｜tool_calls> ``` This reproduced 7/7 times across streaming and non-streaming requests, with and without `reasoning_effort`. The official DeepSeek API does not reproduce the leak. With an equivalent user prompt and the same tool schema, `tool_choice: "none"` used 94 prompt tokens and returned no DSML or tool call. The `auto` request used 359 prompt tokens and returned a structured tool call. The `none` response's reasoning also explicitly stated that no tool was available. This indicates that the official implementation removes the tool definition from the model input when tools are disabled. The causal path in SGLang is: 1. `serving_chat.py` correctly skips the tool constraint and output parser when `request.tool_choice == "none"`. 2. The DSV4 encoding path still unconditionally copies `request.tools` into the first system message: ```python if request.tools: messages[0]["tools"] = [tool.model_dump() for tool in request.tools] ``` 3. `encoding_dsv4.py` renders those tools into `TOOLS_TEMPLATE`, which instructs the model to emit DSML. 4. Because output parsing is disabled for `none`, generated DSML is returned as normal content. The deployed source files match the official `v0.5.17` tag byte-for-byte. The same unconditional DSV4 tool injection remains on current `origin/main` at `a4ffb996db3e823708a53637f851e2677d4455a8`. Related issue #30925 reported a similar symptom for GLM, but it was closed after the reporter could not reproduce it on v0.5.15. This report is specific to the DSV4 encoder and is deterministic on v0.5.17. Expected behavior: `tool_choice: "none"` must not expose the tool schema or native tool-call instructions to the model. The response must contain neither structured tool calls nor raw DSML markup. ### Reproduction Model: `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash` Start SGLang: ```bash python3 -m sglang.launch_server \ --model-path deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash \ --served-model-name DeepSeek-V4-Flash \ --tp-size 2 \ --tool-call-parser deepseekv4 \ --reasoning-parser deepseek-v4 \ --port 30000 ``` Send the minimal non-streaming request: ```bash curl -sS http://127.0.0.1:30000/v1/chat/completions \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d '{ "model": "DeepSeek-V4-Flash", "messages": [ {"role": "user", "content": "Call Bash to run pwd. Return no prose."} ], "tools": [{ "type": "function", "function": { "name": "Bash", "description": "Run a command", "parameters": { "type": "object", "properties": { "command": {"type": "string"} }, "required": ["command"] } } }], "tool_choice": "none", "temperature": 0, "max_tokens": 384 }' | jq '.choices[0]' ``` Observed response shape: ```json { "message": { "role": "assistant", "content": "<｜DSML｜tool_calls>...<｜DSML｜invoke name=\"Bash\">...", "tool_calls": null }, "finish_reason": "stop" } ``` A minimal fix is to avoid attaching `request.tools` to DSV4 messages when `request.tool_choice == "none"`. A regression test should assert that the encoded DSV4 prompt does not contain `## Tools`, the tool name, or `<｜DSML｜tool_calls>` for this request shape. ### Environment Output of `python3 -m sglang.check_env` from the reproducing server: ```text Python: 3.12.3 (main, Jun 19 2026, 12:46:00) [GCC 13.3.0] CUDA available: True GPU 0,1: NVIDIA B300 SXM6 AC GPU 0,1 Compute Capability: 10.3 signal.title: [rotary] Fix the fused Qwen3.5 RoPE kernel discarding mrope height and width
signal.text: ## Motivation `fused_qk_gemma_rmsnorm_rope_gate` loads one position per token, `tl.load(positions_ptr + token)`. Multimodal Qwen3.5 passes mrope positions shaped `[3, T]`, one row per axis, so that offset only ever lands in row 0: height and width were discarded, and every image token rotated as if it sat at its temporal position on all three axes. Text tokens hold the same position on all three rows, so they were already correct and no text benchmark could catch this. The path is not behind a flag — `Qwen3_5AttentionDecoderLayer.self_attention` takes it whenever `_is_cuda and self.attn_output_gate` (default `True`) — so `Qwen3_5ForConditionalGeneration` and `Qwen3_5MoeForConditionalGeneration` on CUDA were affected for every request carrying an image. `forward_native`, the HIP/XPU/CPU/NPU branches, and text-only users of the same layer (`qwen3_5_mtp`, `minicpmv`, `interns2preview`) are unaffected. ## Modifications - `fused_qk_rmsnorm_rope_gate.py`: the kernel takes `mrope_axis_map` and an `MROPE: tl.constexpr`; each rotary lane loads the axis that owns it and indexes `positions` by that row. The row stride comes from the tensor rather than `T`, since CUDA-graph decode replays `mrope_positions[:, :num_tokens]` out of a `[3, max_num_token]` buffer. - `MRotaryEmbedding._build_axis_map`: generalized from GLM-interleaved only to all three layouts, which differ only in which axis owns which lane. - `_legacy_axis_map`: `triton_mrope_fused` and the out-of-tree `sgl_kernel.multimodal_rotary_embedding` keep receiving `None` outside GLM. This PR changes no input to either. - `Ernie4_5_VLRotaryEmbedding._build_axis_map` returns `None`: it reads `mrope_section` as h, w, t while the shared builder assumes t, h, w. - `qwen3_5.py`: passes the map when positions are 2-D. ## Accuracy Tests Both kernels against `MRotaryEmbedding.forward_native`, at Qwen3.6-35B-A3B's shape (16 q heads, 2 kv heads, `head_dim` 256, `rotary_dim` 64) and its shipped interleaved `mrope_section [11, 11, 10]`, bf16, with error grouped by the axis owning each lane: | positions | kernel | max abs error | t-lanes | h-lanes | w-lanes | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | distinct t, h, w | stock | 19.875 | 0.0625 | 5.891 | 19.875 | | distinct t, h, w | this PR | 0.0625 | 0.0625 | 0.031 | 0.0625 | | t == h == w | stock | 0.0625 | 0.0625 | 0.031 | 0.0625 | 0.0625 is the bf16 floor here. Stock sits on it for temporal lanes and up to 300x above it for height and width, which is one row applied and two ignored; this PR brings every lane to the floor. The last row is why it shipped. New `test_fused_qk_rmsnorm_rope_gate.py` compares the kernel with `forward_native` over interleaved and contiguous `[11, 11, 10]` and `[24, 20, 20]` (no pass-through tail), with positions sliced out of a wider buffer to reproduce the CUDA-graph stride, plus 1-D parity and rejection of both illegal position/map pairings. New `test_mrope_axis_map.py` checks each layout against the function that consumes it, and pins GLM's order (its consumer is out of tree) and Ernie's opt-out. End to end, which is what shows the model is wired to the map: `Qwen/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B` at `995ad96`, 1xB200, greedy, three words asked for separately on a generated page. The reference column disables the fused branch, dropping CUDA to the plain path that ropes through `MRotaryEmbedding` — same weights and hardware, only the rope kernel differs. | word | reference (unfused) | this PR | before | |---|---|---|---| | AURORA | 680, 509, 781, 522 | 680, 509, 781, 523 | 800, 480, 900, 492 | | BASALT | 640, 508, 717, 524 | 640, 509, 719, 528 | 800, 480, 900, 494 | | CINDER | 760, 508, 810, 520 | 752, 508, 810, 520 | 800, 487, 882, 501 | Before, all three share `x1 = 800`: the word being asked about does not move the box. After, each tracks the unfused path within 8 px. This is parity between the two paths, not a grounding score. ## Speed Tests and Profiling `MROPE` is a `tl.constexpr`, so the 1-D path keeps its own specialization. Same shape, `triton.testing.do_bench`, median per launch on 1xB200: | tokens | 1-D before | 1-D after | mrope | 1-D delta | |---|---|---|---|---| | 3072 (one page of prefill) | 65.4 us | 65.4 us | 65.5 us | -0.08% | | 32 (decode graph batch) | 8.2 us | 8.2 us | 8.3 us | +0.11% | The mrope specialization costs one `int64` load per lane, with no extra launches, synchronization or allocations. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32403620430](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32403620430)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32403620235](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32403620235)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32403620252](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32403620252)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [diffusion] park a layerwise component's non-layer weights between uses
signal.text: ## Motivation Layerwise offload streams a component's blocks and releases them when its use ends. Everything else the component owns — embeddings, projections, norms, heads — stays on the device for the whole request. That is right while it is the component being used, and pure cost afterwards. On a small card the stage that follows is the one that needs the room. MiniMax-H3 at 864x480 / 124 frames / 20 steps, one RTX 4090, host memory capped at 32 GiB. The VAE decode is half the request, because `decode_temporal` re-runs the whole decoder per temporal chunk — so under layerwise offload the VAE's 36 blocks are re-streamed every chunk: ``` [MiniMaxH3TextEncodingStage] finished in 0.50 s [MiniMaxH3DenoisingStage] finished in 141.20 s [MiniMaxH3DecodingStage] finished in 140.60 s <- as much as 20 denoise steps ``` Holding those blocks resident (`--layerwise-resident-layers video_vae=36`, #35688) is what makes the decode cheap — 23 s instead of 150 — and it needs 9 GB. With a hard 12 GiB allocator cap the decode then dies for want of 20 MiB: ``` CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 20.00 MiB. 12.00 GiB allowed; Of the allocated memory 11.86 GiB is allocated by PyTorch ``` Of that 11.86 GiB, the DiT is still holding 2.09 GB and the text encoder 1.40 GB that the decode never touches. `PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True` does not close the gap. ## Modifications `park_non_layer_weights()` moves the parameters no manager streams to the host and leaves a `(1,)` placeholder behind; `restore_non_layer_weights()` brings them back. `LayerwiseOffloadStrategy` calls them from `finish_use` and `prepare_for_use`, so a component gives up that memory exactly while it is not the one being used. Scope is deliberately narrow: - **Parameters only.** Buffers stay resident because layerwise offload keeps them on purpose — a shared RoPE cache is referenced by many layers. - **One host copy, made once.** Steady state is one transfer each way per use: about 0.35 s for H3's 3.5 GB, against the 130 s the resident VAE saves. - **Follows `--performance-mode memory`**, which already trades latency for footprint. Nothing changes under the other modes. - **MPS untouched.** It has its own subphase-scoped mechanism. ## Accuracy Tests Which device holds a weight; the weights themselves are unchanged. Three unit tests cover the mode gate, that streamed layer weights are never parked and buffers stay resident, and that parking is a no-op outside memory mode. `test_layerwise_offload.py` (with the checkpoint-mapping branch applied, since that is the configuration measured): 117 passed. ## Speed Tests and Profiling H3 `fl2va`, 864x480 / 124 frames / 20 steps, seed 1101, single RTX 4090, host memory capped at 32 GiB. The 12 GiB VRAM budget is **enforced** with `torch.cuda.set_per_process_memory_fraction`, not inferred from `nvidia-smi` — which reports the caching allocator's reserved pool and so overstates it. | configuration | denoise | decode | end to end | 12 GiB cap | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | default | 141 s | 150 s | 303 s | fits, but decode dominates | | `video_vae=36` | 158 s | 23 s | 192 s | OOM in decode | | `video_vae=36` + this change | 159 s | **13 s** | **177 s** | **fits** | Host memory is unchanged at 24.5 GiB. Denoise varies 141–159 s with load on this shared box; decode is the term this change is about and it is stable. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #32395791332](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32395791332)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32395814506](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32395814506)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32395791126](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32395791126)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [Bug] deepseekv32/deepseekv4 tool-call parsers drop calls when the streamed output has two chunks
signal.text:
### Checklist - [x] I searched related issues but found no solution. - [x] The bug persists in the latest version. - [x] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback. - [x] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed. - [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed. ### Describe the bug Use the `deepseekv32` or `deepseekv4` parser with streaming on. ``` deepseekv32 non-streaming: 3 calls {0: search {}, 1: run_query {}, 2: get_weather {"city": -7}} deepseekv32 2-chunk stream: 1 call {2: ['', '{"city": -7}']} # 2 calls and the names are gone deepseekv4 non-streaming: 2 calls {0: get_weather {"city": 42}, 1: get_weather {"city": -7}} deepseekv4 2-chunk stream: 1 call {1: ['', '{"city": -7}']} # 1 call and the name are gone ``` The non-streaming `detect_and_parse` on the same text is correct. Thus streaming clients and non-streaming clients get different tool calls. **Expected:** each division of the same text must give the calls that `detect_and_parse` gives. ### Reproduction
reproduce_deepseek_dsml_two_chunk.py ```python #!/usr/bin/env python3 """deepseekv32 / deepseekv4 detectors: splitting the model output into just TWO streaming chunks makes earlier tool calls disappear from the stream. The split point is inside the number "-7" ("-" | "7") — a perfectly normal token boundary — so any real streamed generation can hit it. pip install "sglang[all]==0.5.17" (CPU is enough) python reproduce_deepseek_dsml_two_chunk.py # exit 1 = bug present """ import json import warnings warnings.filterwarnings("ignore") from sglang.srt.entrypoints.openai.protocol import Function, Tool from sglang.srt.function_call.function_call_parser import FunctionCallParser def tool(name): return Tool(type="function", function=Function( name=name, parameters={"type": "object", "properties": {}})) TOOLS = [tool("get_weather"), tool("search"), tool("run_query")] CASES = { # three calls; the last one has an argument whose value "-7" straddles # the chunk boundary "deepseekv32": ( '<｜DSML｜function_calls>' '<｜DSML｜invoke name="search">' '<｜DSML｜invoke name="run_query">' '<｜DSML｜invoke name="get_weather">' '<｜DSML｜parameter name="city" string="false">-7' '', 189, ), # two calls; same "-7" straddle in the second one "deepseekv4": ( '<｜DSML｜tool_calls>' '<｜DSML｜invoke name="get_weather">' '<｜DSML｜parameter name="city" string="false">42' '' '<｜DSML｜invoke name="get_weather">' '<｜DSML｜parameter name="city" string="false">-7' '', 208, ), } def stream(name, chunks): d = FunctionCallParser.ToolCallParserEnum[name]() calls = {} for chunk in list(chunks) + ["", ""]: # trailing flushes, as serving does r = d.parse_streaming_increment(chunk, TOOLS) for c in r.calls: e = calls.setdefault(c.tool_index, ["", ""]) if c.name: e[0] = c.name if c.parameters: e[1] += c.parameters return calls bad = 0 for name, (text, cut) in CASES.items(): d = FunctionCallParser.ToolCallParserEnum[name]() final = {i: [c.name, c.parameters] for i, c in enumerate(d.detect_and_parse(text, TOOLS).calls)} streamed = stream(name, [text[:cut], text[cut:]]) print(f"{name}: split {text[cut-2:cut]!r} | {text[cut:cut+2]!r}") print(f" non-streaming: {len(final)} calls {final}") print(f" 2-chunk stream: {len(streamed)} calls {streamed}") same = len(streamed) == len(final) and all( streamed.get(i, ["", ""])[0] == final[i][0] and json.loads(streamed.get(i, ["", "null"])[1] or "null") == json.loads(final[i][1] or "null") for i in final) if not same: bad += 1 print(" BUG: streaming lost tool calls vs non-streaming\n") raise SystemExit(1 if bad else 0) ```
### Environment ``` Python: 3.12.13 (main, Jun 23 2026, 15:18:55) [Clang 22.1.3 ] CUDA available: True GPU 0: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4090 GPU 0 Compute Capability: 8.9 CUDA_HOME: /usr/local/cuda NVCC: Cuda compilation tools, release 12.9, V12.9.86 CUDA Driver Version: 580.173.02 PyTorch: 2.11.0+cu130 sglang: 0.5.17 sglang-kernel: 0.4.5 flashinfer_python: 0.6.15.post1 flashinfer_cubin: Module Not Found flashinfer_jit_cache: Module Not Found triton: 3.6.0 transformers: 5.12.1 torchao: 0.17.0 numpy: 2.3.5 aiohttp: 3.14.3 fastapi: 0.141.1 huggingface_hub: 1.28.0 interegular: 0.3.3 modelscope: 1.39.1 orjson: 3.12.0 outlines: 0.1.11 packaging: 26.3 psutil: 7.2.2 pydantic: 2.14.0b1 python-multipart: 0.0.32 pyzmq: 27.1.0 uvicorn: 0.52.4 uvloop: 0.22.1 vllm: Module Not Found xgrammar: 0.2.1 openai: 2.6.1 tiktoken: 0.14.0 anthropic: 0.124.0 ```

signal.title: [Responses] Fix multimodal Kimi-K3 /v1/responses returning 400 "texts cannot be empty"
signal.text: …mpty' <!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. --> ## Motivation A `/v1/responses` request against a **multimodal Kimi-K3** deployment fails immediately: ```json {"error":{"message":"texts cannot be empty and tokenizer must be initialized","type":"invalid_request_error","param":null,"code":400}} ``` The equivalent /v1/chat/completions request with the same messages and tools works, so the bug is specific to the /v1/responses path for multimodal Kimi-K3. ## Why The kimi_k3 custom encoder produces a usable prompt_ids (via apply_chat_template(tokenize=True, ...)) but leaves prompt == "" — the only prompt = decode(prompt_ids) assignment lives in the prompt_ids is None branch, which kimi_k3 never enters. OpenAIServingResponses._make_request forwarded that empty prompt as text on the multimodal branch, producing GenerateReqInput(text=""). In TokenizerManager.generate_request, input_ids is None and input_text is empty, so control reaches _tokenize_texts(""), which raises the error above. serving_chat._convert_to_internal_request already special-cases this (elif is_multimodal and self.chat_encoding_spec == "kimi_k3": prompt_kwargs = {"input_ids": ...}); the responses path was missing the same guard. A text-only Kimi-K3 deployment (is_multimodal == False) takes the else branch and uses prompt_ids, so it is unaffected — which is why the bug only surfaces for multimodal Kimi-K3. Fixes #35460 ## Modifications - python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/openai/serving_responses.py: - test/registered/unit/entrypoints/openai/test_serving_responses.py: add ## Accuracy Tests N/A — no kernel or model-forward change; this only fixes which prompt field the responses path hands to the engine. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [ ] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32231404454](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32231404454)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32231403957](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32231403957)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: TP/PP Consensus checker
signal.text: ## Motivation We have spent a lot of time in investigation into PP/TP divergence issues. The most difficult problems is that, when PP/TP divergence happens (e.g. the server hangs), you will have the stacktrace, but it is not the real time-point which divergence happens. Think of a case. A PP/TP divergence may happen silently, forr example, the kv cache available memory size differs because of a software bug. The server continue to process requests. When a single request is accepted in TP0 but rejected in TP1, the batch size diverges, and then the server hangs. However, the request is just a victim, not the trigger. We have to find the trigger request to figure out why this happens. This PR introduces a **consensus checker**, which checks for early divergence. There are two ways to use the consensus checker. 1. (Prefered) Using `@rank_consensus_checker` decorator. This decorator checks that `check_prefetch_progress` is called at **every rank** with **identical parameters and results**. If this assertion breaks, the server will abort. ```py @rank_consensus(same_params=True, same_results=True) def check_prefetch_progress(self, req_id: str) -> bool: ... ``` You can also check consensus of one of the parameters or one field of a parameter, like `rank_consensus(same_params=["len(foo)", "operation.req_id"])`. it internally calls `assert_same`. 2. Call `rank_consensus_checker.assert_same`. You can alternatively call `rank_consensus_checker.assert_same` programmatically in a function. The function takes a string, which must be same over all ranks. Both `@rank_consensus` and `assert_same` must be called in the scheduler thread. Here is an example that divergence is detected. The results of `check_prefetch_progress` differ in PP0 and PP1. ## Modifications 1. Add a environment variable `SGLANG_ENABLE_RANK_CONSENSUS_CHECKER`, which enables the consensus checker. **Default to false**. 2. Add `rank_consensus_checker.py`. It simply creates a background thread. When `assert_same` is called, it pushes a message to a queue. The background thread consumes the queue of events, and compares events with other ranks. Unless divergence, all ranks must have the same sequence of events. 3. Add `@rank_consenus` to a few functions in hicache code. This work is in progress. Feel free to talk to me if you have better idea, e.g. more convenient decorator, better naming, which code to add the decorator, etc. ## Test ### Effectiveness With rank consensus checker enabled, we could detect PP divergence with L3 in a few minutes. The problem is fixed after patching #27010. Use the following command to reproduce this. ```sh nohup env HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 SGLANG_ENABLE_RANK_CONSENSUS_CHECKER=1 \ sglang serve --model-path Qwen/Qwen3.5-27B \ --reasoning-parser qwen3 \ --tool-call-parser qwen3_coder \ --mamba-radix-cache-strategy extra_buffer \ --mem-fraction-static 0.8 \ --tp-size=1 \ --pp-size=2 \ --host 0.0.0.0 \ --port 30000 \ --max-total-tokens=$((64*1024)) \ --hicache-ratio=2 \ --enable-metrics \ --enable-hierarchical-cache \ --hicache-storage-backend=mooncake \ --hicache-storage-backend-extra-config '{"master_server_address": "127.0.0.1:50051", "local_hostname": "localhost", "metadata_server": "http://127.0.0.1:8080/metadata", "global_segment_size": "128gb", "protocol": "tcp"}' \ > sglang.log 2>&1 & python benchmark/hicache/bench_multiturn.py \ --num-clients=32 \ --num-rounds=10 \ --disable-auto-run \ --model=Qwen/Qwen3.5-27B \ --enable-round-barrier \ --request-rate 1 ``` ### Performance Tested 3 groups: - A: Baseline (4a5d7d3c). - B: This PR, with consensus checker **disabled** - C: This PR, with consensus checker **enabled** Conconlusion: There is no overhead when then checker is disabled compared the baseline. Testing commands: ```sh nohup env HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 SGLANG_ENABLE_RANK_CONSENSUS_CHECKER=1 \ sglang serve --model-path Qwen/Qwen3.5-27B \ --reasoning-parser qwen3 \ --tool-call-parser qwen3_coder \ --mamba-radix-cache-strategy extra_buffer \ --mem-fraction-static 0.8 \ --tp-size=2 \ --pp-size=1 \ --host 0.0.0.0 \ --port 30000 \ --max-total-tokens=$((64*1024)) \ --hicache-ratio=2 \ --enable-metrics \ --enable-hierarchical-cache \ --hicache-storage-backend=mooncake \ --hicache-storage-backend-extra-config '{"master_server_address": "127.0.0.1:50051", "local_hostname": "localhost", "metadata_server": "http://127.0.0.1:8080/metadata", "global_segment_size": "128gb", "protocol": "tcp"}' \ > sglang.log 2>&1 & python benchmark/hicache/bench_multiturn.py \ --num-clients=32 \ --num-rounds=10 \ --disable-auto-run \ --model=Qwen/Qwen3.5-27B \ --enable-round-barrier \ --request-rate 1 ``` ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [ ] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1.
