signal.title: fix: keep speculative overshoot out of the radix cache key
signal.text: ## Motivation A speculative verify step commits a whole accepted chunk, so a request's `output_ids` can run past the point where it actually stopped — measured 0–7 tokens for DSPARK `block_size=7` at `max_new_tokens=1024`. The client is served `output_ids_through_stop`; the radix cache is keyed on raw `output_ids`: ```python # mem_cache/unified_radix_cache.py, cache_finished_req token_ids = (req.origin_input_ids + req.output_ids)[:kv_len_to_handle] ``` So the tree stores a suffix no continuation can reproduce. A follow-up turn is built from what the client received and therefore diverges from the cached sequence at `prompt + returned`. On a full-KV model that is wasted pages. On a hybrid model it costs the whole decode region. Under `--mamba-radix-cache-strategy extra_buffer` the insert carries exactly one mamba checkpoint, at `floor(committed / interval) * interval`, and `MambaComponent.create_match_validator` is a hard gate — a node without a mamba value cannot extend the mamba boundary. When the checkpoint lands past the divergence point, the matched prefix has no checkpoint at all and reuse falls back to the prefill-time insert: ``` prompt=3964 committed=1029 insert_len=4992 reachable=4988 Decode cache miss for prompt 1 | cached=3840 prompt_len=3964 ``` `3840 == floor(3964 / 128) * 128` — the second turn matched a page-aligned prefix of the prompt and none of the 1024 generated tokens. Predicate: `floor((prompt + committed) / interval) * interval > prompt + returned`. Over a measured 4x B200 sample of 36 first-turn prompts it fires exactly once, on the one prompt that missed, 10/10 reps. The window is at most `chain_len - 1` positions out of `interval`, so it reads as intermittent — roughly one prompt in 32 — but it is deterministic given the prompt. Without speculation `committed == returned` and the gap is empty. ## Modifications `Req.effective_kv_committed_len()` is the single point where the finish-time KV length is decided: `release_kv_cache` hands it to every cache implementation as `kv_len_to_handle`, and everything past it is released as overallocated. Capping it at what the client received keeps the overshoot out of the key and frees it in the same step, for all eight cache implementations at once rather than patching each `(origin_input_ids + output_ids)` site. The method already had precedent for this shape: `strip_thinking_cache` caps at the prompt for the same reason (#22373), "so thinking + answer fall into the overallocated range and are reclaimed by release_kv_cache". `StreamingSession.try_cache_finished_req` is stronger precedent still — the session path already calls `_trim_overshoot(req, finished_len)` and sets `slot.kv_committed_len = min(len(origin_input_ids) + finished_len, ...)`. The overshoot was already understood to be untrustworthy for reuse there; the plain `release_kv_cache` path never learned it. One companion change: `_release_overallocated_kv_indices` asserts a non-speculative request has nothing overallocated, and a stop landing before the last committed token now legitimately breaks that, so the assert learns about it the same way it already knows about `strip_thinking_cache`. No leak. The tail moves from "inserted" to "freed", and `ceil_align(start_p, page_size)` still lands on the page `cache_finished_req` just released, so the two frees meet without a gap and without double-freeing. ## Accuracy Test `test/registered/unit/managers/test_spec_overshoot_cache_len.py`, CPU, 4 cases — length overshoot, EOS landing mid-chunk, an exact stop, and an unfinished request. The last two are the guard against over-capping. ``` 4 passed ``` Reverted against the fix, the two overshoot cases go red and the two no-overshoot cases stay green: ``` 2 failed, 2 passed ``` ### End to end, 4x B200 Two arms of the same tree, differing only in this method, same server config, same prompts, same seed. Prompts constructed so `(prompt + max_new_tokens) % 128 == 127`, which is where the predicate can fire, plus a `% 128 == 0` control group that it can never reach: | prompt | before | after | |---|---|---| | 2431 (`%128 == 127`) | `cached=2304` **MISS** | `cached=3328` **HIT** | | 7 other `%128 == 127` | HIT | HIT | | 8 control `%128 == 0` | HIT | HIT | `2304 == floor(2431 / 128) * 128` is the prefill-time insert — the second turn reused none of the 1024 generated tokens. `3328 == floor((2431 + 1024) / 128) * 128` is exactly the length the cap produces, so the fix does not merely stop the miss, it lands the reuse where the arithmetic says it should. Deterministic: identical across both reps of both arms. The control group is byte-identical between arms, so nothing is over-capped. Model `thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small-NVFP4` + draft `RadixArk/Inkling-Small-DSpark`, `--tp 4 --speculative-algorithm DSPARK --mamba-radix-cache-strategy extra_buffer --mamba-track-interval 128 --page-size 128 --enable-deterministic-inference`, `SGLANG_ENABLE_UNIFIED_RADIX_TREE=1`. #35293 loosened `min_cache_hit_ratio` from 0.99 to 0.90 on the DSPARK class precisely because of this, so this PR puts it back to 0.99 — that class is then the e2e regression guard for this fix on `4-gpu-b200`, at every prompt rather than 90% of them. ### CI, 4x B200 `/rerun-test` on this branch's head, with the bar back at every prompt: ``` [CI Test Method] TestInklingSmallNvfp4DsparkDeterministic.test_input_output_logprobs_match avg_kl_div=0.0 [CI Test Method] TestInklingSmallNvfp4DsparkDeterministic.test_input_output_logprobs_match_decode_cache_hit avg_kl_div=0.0 [CI Test Method] TestInklingSmallNvfp4DsparkDeterministic.test_input_output_logprobs_match_prefill_cache_hit avg_kl_div=0.0 Ran 5 tests in 875.658s All 1 test(s) passed in 893s ``` No `Decode cache miss` lines and no `Too few decode cache hits` — the assertion that read 31/32 twice on this runner now passes at 32/32, and all three KL cases stay at exactly 0. ## Benchmark and Profiling Results Not applicable — one `min()` on the request-finish path, once per request. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Code Formatting with Pre-Commit](https://docs.sglang.ai/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-formatting-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests as outlined in the [Running Unit Tests](https://docs.sglang.ai/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#running-unit-tests-adding-to-ci). - [x] Update documentation / docstrings / example tutorials as needed, according to [Writing Documentation](https://docs.sglang.ai/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#writing-documentation-running-docs-ci). - [x] Provide throughput / latency benchmark results and accuracy evaluation results as needed, according to [Benchmark and Profiling](https://docs.sglang.ai/developer_guide/benchmark_and_profiling.html). - [x] For reviewers: If you haven't made any contributions to this PR and are only assisting with merging the main branch, please remove yourself as a co-author when merging the PR. - [x] Please feel free to join our Slack channel at https://slack.sglang.ai to discuss your PR. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32389777707](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32389777707)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32398380663](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32398380663)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32389777556](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32389777556)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [AMD] Add dense-FP8 for MXFP4 checkpoints with fused silu, mul, activation quant
signal.text: <!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. --> ## Motivation Quark MXFP4 checkpoints leave a handful of large dense projections unquantized in bf16 — most notably the Qwen3.5 `shared_expert.down_proj`. On the AMD ROCm/aiter path these leftover bf16 GEMMs are comparatively heavy, and the cost shows up most in prefill-bound regimes where the dense projection is on the critical path. Today there is no way to promote just these excluded layers without re-quantizing the whole checkpoint. This PR adds an opt-in `--enable-dense-fp8` path that promotes only the eligible large bf16 dense layers (which the checkpoint left unquantized) to **online w8a8 FP8**, and fuses the preceding `SiluAndMul` + per-token activation quantization into a single aiter kernel. Instead of running `SiluAndMul`, then a separate activation quant, then the GEMM, the fused kernel emits a pre-quantized `(fp8, scale)` tuple that feeds straight into `down_proj`. The path is numerically a dynamic per-token FP8 quant of an otherwise bf16 layer, is ROCm/aiter-only, and is fully opt-in, so default behavior is unchanged. ## Modifications - **`server_args.py`**: Add the `--enable-dense-fp8` server arg (AMD/aiter, default **off**). Requires `SGLANG_USE_AITER` and `SGLANG_USE_AITER_FP8_PER_TOKEN`. - **`quark/quark.py`**: Give `QuarkConfig` a model-registered dense-FP8 policy. `register_dense_fp8_modules(include, exclude, min_output_size)` lets a model declare which excluded (bf16) layers may be promoted — quark itself owns no module names or thresholds. In `get_quant_method`, a layer that would normally fall back to `UnquantizedLinearMethod` is instead routed to an online dynamic `Fp8LinearMethod` (`Fp8Config(is_checkpoint_fp8_serialized=False, activation_scheme="dynamic")`) when `--enable-dense-fp8` is set and the layer matches the policy (include substring, not excluded, output size ≥ min). - **`models/qwen3_5.py`**: Register the Qwen3.5 policy — include only `.shared_expert.down_proj`, exclude tiny/routing/embedding layers (`conv1d`, `shared_expert_gate`, `mlp.gate`, `in_proj_*`, `lm_head`, `embed`), and require `N ≥ 2048`. Aiter-only, so the tuned policy lives with the model. - **`models/qwen2_moe.py`**: In the MoE block forward, when `down_proj` is running as online w8a8 FP8 per-token on aiter, fuse `SiluAndMul` + per-token quant into a single `aiter.silu_and_mul_quant` call that produces the `(fp8, scale)` tuple consumed directly by `down_proj`, skipping a separate activation + quant pass. Gated on `use_aiter_fp8_per_token`; default off. - **`layers/quantization/fp8.py`**: Teach `Fp8LinearMethod.apply` to accept a pre-quantized `(fp8, scale)` tuple input (from the fused kernel) and route it to the aiter PTPC helper `apply_fp8_ptpc_linear`, since `apply_fp8_linear` has no tuple path. Weight is transposed `(K, N) → (N, K)` to match the helper's expectation. ## Usage Opt-in via `--enable-dense-fp8`. It is AMD/aiter-only and requires aiter FP8 per-token, so set the two aiter env flags. The same command applies to both Qwen3.5 checkpoints (add `--kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3` for the MXFP4-AttnFP8 checkpoint): ```bash SGLANG_USE_AITER=1 SGLANG_USE_AITER_FP8_PER_TOKEN=1 \ python3 -m sglang.launch_server \ --model-path /path/to/Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-MXFP4 \ --trust-remote-code \ --tensor-parallel-size 2 \ --attention-backend aiter \ --enable-dense-fp8 ``` The `SiluAndMul`+per-token-quant fusion is on by default whenever `--enable-dense-fp8` is active on the aiter per-token path; it can be disabled for debugging with `SGLANG_DISABLE_DENSE_FP8_SILU_FUSE=1` (not recommended — fusion is neutral-to-faster and saves the bf16 intermediate round-trip). ## Accuracy Tests The same `--enable-dense-fp8` config (online PTPC FP8 + fused `SiluAndMul`+quant) is applied to **both** Qwen3.5-397B-A17B checkpoints, TP=2, aiter backend. GSM8K 5-shot, 1319 questions. **MXFP4-AttnFP8** (fp8_e4m3 KV cache): | config | accuracy (flexible / strict) | |------------------------------------------|------------------------------| | `dense_off` (baseline, down_proj bf16) | 0.9363 / 0.9409 | | `dense_on` (this PR, down_proj FP8) | 0.9393 / 0.9454 | **Plain MXFP4** (3-seed mean ± per-seed stderr ≈ 0.007): | config | flexible (3 seeds) | strict (3 seeds) | |------------------------------------------|-------------------------------|-------------------------------| | `dense_off` (baseline, down_proj bf16) | 0.9340 / 0.9356 / 0.9295 | 0.9401 / 0.9409 / 0.9371 | | `dense_on` (this PR, down_proj FP8) | 0.9340 / 0.9257 / 0.9325 | 0.9401 / 0.9409 / 0.9416 | Accuracy is unchanged within noise on both checkpoints — the per-seed spread (±0.007) exceeds the dense_off↔dense_on difference, so promoting `down_proj` to FP8 is accuracy-neutral. ## Speed Tests and Profiling TP=2, `--attention-backend aiter`, `--page-size 16`, `--chunked-prefill-size 8192`, `--mem-fraction-static 0.8`, allreduce-fusion on, tuned bf16 GEMM present. A = `dense_off` (baseline), B = `dense_on` (this PR); all other knobs identical. **Throughput below is total token throughput (input+output) across the TP=2 group**, i.e. `tok/s = (tok/s/gpu) × 2`. TPOT is the median per-output-token latency. ### MXFP4-AttnFP8 (`--kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3`) **ISL/OSL = 1024/1024** (decode-bound): | concurrency | total tok/s OFF→ON | Δ throughput | median TPOT OFF→ON (ms) | Δ TPOT | |-------------|--------------------|--------------|-------------------------|--------| | 4 | 776 → 774 | −0.3% | 9.96 → 9.97 | +0.1% | | 8 | 1362 → 1372 | +0.7% | 11.39 → 11.31 | −0.7% | | 16 | 2238 → 2240 | +0.1% | 14.10 → 14.09 | −0.1% | | 32 | 3124* → 3140 | +0.5% | 20.06* → 20.00 | −0.3% | | 64 | 4378 → 4360 | −0.4% | 28.97 → 29.11 | +0.5% | \* The captured `dense_off` cc=32 point was a noisy outlier; a repeat baseline run is used here. At 1k/1k the dense projection is too compute-light to move the needle — results are **at parity (no regression)** on both throughput and TPOT. **ISL/OSL = 8192/1024** (prefill-heavy): | concurrency | total tok/s OFF→ON | Δ throughput | median TPOT OFF→ON (ms) | Δ TPOT | |-------------|--------------------|--------------|-------------------------|--------| | 4 | 3170 → 3182 | +0.4% | 10.76 → 10.68 | −0.7% | | 8 | 5216 → 5338 | +2.3% | 13.05 → 12.74 | −2.4% | | 16 | 7874 → 8008 | +1.7% | 17.46 → 17.14 | −1.8% | | 32 | 10260 → 10462 | +2.0% | 27.07 → 26.34 | −2.7% | | 64 | 12840 → 13120 | +2.2% | 44.06 → 42.88 | −2.7% | In the prefill-heavy 8k/1k regime — where the bf16 `down_proj` GEMM actually matters — the fused FP8-dense path gives a **consistent ~2% total-throughput gain** and a **~2–3% lower TPOT** at every concurrency. Net: neutral at 1k/1k, a clear win for prefill-bound workloads, with no TPOT regression anywhere. ### Plain MXFP4 Node-pinned (single NUMA node, fixed GPU pair) to suppress host/neighbor contention. **ISL/OSL = 8192/1024** (prefill-heavy): | concurrency | total tok/s OFF→ON | Δ throughput | median TPOT OFF→ON (ms) | Δ TPOT | |-------------|--------------------|--------------|-------------------------|--------| | 4 | 3258 → 3348 | +2.8% | 10.22 → 10.18 | −0.4% | | 8 | 5140 → 5174 | +0.7% | 13.25 → 13.15 | −0.8% | | 16 | 7798 → 7804 | +0.1% | 17.62 → 17.58 | −0.2% | | 32 | 10184 → 10198 | +0.1% | 27.06 → 27.01 | −0.2% | | 64 | 12878 → 12884 | +0.05% | 43.68 → 43.64 | −0.1% | **ISL/OSL = 1024/1024** (decode-bound) — mean of 3 warm sweeps per arm, with a flat `dense_off` control measured in the same window (control spread ≤0.6%, confirming an uncontended measurement): | concurrency | total tok/s OFF→ON | Δ throughput | median TPOT OFF→ON (ms) | Δ TPOT | |-------------|--------------------|--------------|-------------------------|--------| | 4 | 819 → 819 | 0.0% | 9.43 → 9.42 | −0.1% | | 8 | 1331 → 1341 | +0.8% | 11.68 → 11.58 | −0.9% | | 16 | 2203 → 2199 | −0.2% | 14.30 → 14.32 | +0.1% | | 32 | 3089 → 3091 | +0.1% | 20.28 → 20.34 | +0.3% | | 64 | 4352 → 4323 | −0.7% | 29.08 → 29.32 | +0.8% | On the plain MXFP4 checkpoint the dense-FP8 path is **at parity (no regression)** on this host — both throughput and TPOT are unchanged within run-to-run noise across all concurrencies, verified at **8k/1k** and **1k/1k** (the latter across 3 warm sweeps against a flat control). The PTPC+fusion config is therefore **safe to enable uniformly on both checkpoints**: a clear prefill-bound win on MXFP4-AttnFP8, and neutral on plain MXFP4. ## Checklist - [ ] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [ ] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process). 2. signal.title: Add NIXL as a backend for weight transfer
signal.text: Adds NIXL as a passive weight-transfer target backend alongside the existing Mooncake path, so an external training engine (Miles) can RDMA-write updated weights directly into SGLang's GPU memory. The transfer-engine metadata that SGLang publishes is extended to support both backends. Using NIXL yields a 1.5x-5x reduction in weight refit time, depending on model and configuration. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32377150149](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32377150149)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32377150174](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32377150174)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:heavy_minus_sign: **No AMD PR run found for this commit**.<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [Model] Support Ling-3.0-flash (BailingMoeV3)
signal.text: ## Motivation Day-0 support for [inclusionAI/Ling-3.0-flash](https://huggingface.co/inclusionAI/Ling-3.0-flash) (`BailingMoeV3ForCausalLM`, `model_type=bailing_hybrid`): a hybrid MoE architecture interleaving KDA linear attention (with a safe-gate lower bound) and MLA, with MTP (NEXTN) and DSPARK speculative decoding support. ## Modifications - `BailingMoeV3ForCausalLM` model (`bailing_hybrid` config): KDA + MLA hybrid layers, 512-expert MoE, and MTP (NEXTN). - DSPARK support for the KDA hybrid path: graph-folded draft proposal, fused KDA chain-verify kernel, and DSA token-to-KV pool sizing. - KDA safe gate propagation through the Triton decode/target-verify kernels and their call sites, matching fused verification. - `ling3` reasoning and tool-call parsers. - BF16, FP8, compressed-tensors INT4, and native MXFP4 checkpoint support on Hopper and Blackwell. - Exactness, fusion-gate, quantization, and parser tests. ## Validation All serving runs kept decode CUDA Graph enabled and used the default graph sizing. No run used `--disable-cuda-graph` or `--cuda-graph-max-bs-decode`. ### Quantized checkpoints Full GSM8K uses 1,319 questions. Performance uses 80 exact-length random requests at ISL/OSL 8192/1024 with concurrency 1 and 16; throughput includes input and output tokens per second per GPU. | GPU | format | GSM8K | stop rate | throughput/GPU (c1 / c16) | P50 TTFT ms (c1 / c16) | P50 TPOT ms (c1 / c16) | default graph range | |---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | H200 | INT4 | 95.30% | 100% | 1,159 / 7,184 | 205.96 / 1,891.74 | 3.68 / 8.16 | through batch 218 | | H200 | MXFP4 | 96.29% | 100% | 709 / 5,215 | 305.23 / 2,725.52 | 6.05 / 11.17 | through batch 227 | | B200 | INT4 | 96.74% | 99.70% | 482 / 1,344 | 641.41 / 6,202.62 | 8.72 / 48.01 | through batch 305 | | B200 | MXFP4 | 96.29% | 99.62% | 785 / 7,933 | 127.97 / 1,117.16 | 5.60 / 7.98 | through batch 314 | INT4 selects Marlin on H200 and the graph-compatible Triton WNA16 path on B200. MXFP4 routed experts use the native FlashInfer runner on both GPUs. The B200 MXFP4 checkpoint also contains block-FP8 dense/shared projections, which use the Triton FP8 GEMM backend to avoid an unsupported FlashInfer FP8 tactic without converting the routed experts. BF16 and FP8 were rerun on H200 and B200 after the quantization changes. All four combinations served with CUDA Graph enabled, completed generation, and passed the 20-example GSM8K regression gate with 100% stop rate. ### Speculative decoding Ling-3.0-flash BF16, 4x B200 TP4, `temperature=1.0 / top_p=0.95`, thinking on, full GSM8K, `max_tokens=8192`: | spec decoding | score | stop rate | error rate | |---|---:|---:|---:| | DSPARK | 96.66% | 99.77% | 0.00% | | MTP (NEXTN) | 96.44% | 99.62% | 0.00% | Non-stop finishes are long reasoning outputs reaching `max_tokens`, not repetition loops. ## Checklist - [x] Format code with pre-commit. - [x] Add unit tests and register them in CI. - [x] Validate serving correctness, stop rate, and accuracy on H200 and B200. - [x] Publish deployment recipes and benchmark results in #34363. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:no_entry_sign: [Run #32359477855](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32359477855)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #32359477828](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32359477828)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32359477784](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32359477784)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: fix(multimodal): keep LLaVA image fetch off the CPU-preprocess timeout budget (flaky test_mixed_batch)
signal.text: ## Summary Fixes the flaky `test/registered/vlm/test_vision_openai_server_a.py::TestLlavaServer::test_mixed_batch` (and removes a real robustness gap that affects all LLaVA‑family models in production). `LlavaImageProcessor._process_single_image` ran the **entire** image pipeline — network fetch **+** decode **+** CPU preprocessing — inside a single `cpu_executor` (ProcessPool) task, wrapped in: ```python timeout = int(os.environ.get("REQUEST_TIMEOUT", "10")) return await asyncio.wait_for(fut, timeout=timeout) ``` So the **network fetch was inside the CPU‑preprocessing timeout budget**. When the image host is transiently slow (e.g. `raw.githubusercontent.com` under CI network contention), the fetch pushes the task past the budget → `asyncio.TimeoutError` → **HTTP 500**. Two things make it worse: 1. **A `ProcessPoolExecutor` future can't be cancelled once it's running.** On timeout `wait_for` abandons the asyncio wrapper, but the worker keeps grinding the slow fetch. With a small pool and a burst of requests (`test_mixed_batch` fires 12 via a 4‑thread client), stuck workers saturate the pool and **cascade 500s** across otherwise‑fast requests — defeating both the OpenAI client's auto‑retries and the CI test‑level `retry()`. 2. Only LLaVA‑family models hit this: every other VLM uses the base `load_mm_data` path, which already separates cancellable io loading from CPU work. That's why this one test is the flaky one. ## Fix Split the two phases, matching `BaseMultimodalProcessor`'s existing io/cpu design: - **fetch + decode** in the shared **io thread pool** (`self.io_executor`), with a couple of retries for transient network blips; - **CPU‑only preprocessing** in the ProcessPool, so `asyncio.wait_for` now bounds **CPU work only**, never the network. No new config is required; `SGLANG_MM_LOAD_MAX_RETRIES` (default `2`) tunes the load retries. ## Evidence — flake probability before/after Controlled fault injection on 1×H200 with `lmms-lab/llava-onevision-qwen2-0.5b-ov`. Each image fetch is made "slow enough to cross the budget" with probability **p = 0.12** (`REQUEST_TIMEOUT=3`, `SGLANG_CPU_WORKERS=4`), reproducing transient network slowness at exactly the point the real code fetches the image. Images served locally (`file://`) so there is **zero real‑network variance** — the only variable between runs is the fix. signal.title: [model-gateway] Add opt-in `fips` feature using the AWS-LC FIPS module
signal.text: ## Motivation Some deployments (government and other regulated environments) require all cryptography to come from a FIPS 140-3 validated module. This PR adds an opt-in `fips` cargo feature to sgl-model-gateway so those users can build a compliant gateway. Default builds are not affected. ## Modifications Behind the new `fips` feature (off by default): - rustls uses the AWS-LC FIPS provider instead of ring for all TLS (HTTPS server and the reqwest/kube outbound clients; tonic is built without TLS features and does no TLS itself). - JWT verification uses the jsonwebtoken AWS-LC backend. - The wasm module SHA-256 hash uses AWS-LC. - `aws-lc-fips-sys` uses a normal caret requirement (`0.14`) so builds pick up the latest AWS-LC FIPS release (currently 0.14.1, bundling AWS-LC FIPS 4.1.0). AWS-LC FIPS is a CMVP-validated module lineage (see [certificate #5314](https://csrc.nist.gov/projects/cryptographic-module-validation-program/certificate/5314) for the 3.x static module). The exact module version in any given build can be read from the binary with `strings <binary> | grep "AWS-LC FIPS"`. Deployments that need a version literally listed on an issued certificate can pin, for example `=0.13.11` (AWS-LC FIPS 3.1.0, the exact version on #5314). - At startup the gateway asserts the installed rustls provider is FIPS and that the AWS-LC JWT provider was installed. If not, it fails to start. - The Python and Go bindings expose the same `fips` feature. Changes that apply to all builds: - New `src/crypto.rs` with `ensure_crypto_provider_installed()`, which replaces the two previous ad-hoc `ring::default_provider().install_default()` call sites, and a `Sha256Hasher` wrapper used for wasm module hashing. Default builds keep ring and RustCrypto sha2. - `jsonwebtoken` upgraded 9.3 to 10.4 and `smg-auth` 1.0.0 to 1.2.2. jsonwebtoken 9 was hardwired to ring; version 10 has pluggable backends. Default builds use its `rust_crypto` backend. Not changed: blake3/xxhash (used for cache-aware routing and consistent hashing, not security relevant) and the openssl dependency (test cert generation and the optional `vendored-openssl` feature only). Build note: `--features fips` (and therefore `--all-features`, used by `make lint` and the rust CI lint job) needs cmake and Go to compile AWS-LC. The CI lint job passes since GitHub runners include both. <details> <summary>FIPS verification evidence</summary> - The fips binary embeds the AWS-LC FIPS module version string (checked with `strings`, currently `AWS-LC FIPS 4.1.0`); the default binary does not. - The fips binary starts cleanly and serves `/liveness` and `/health`. - TLS handshake against the fips build negotiates TLS 1.3 `TLS_AES_256_GCM_SHA384`. Forcing `TLS_CHACHA20_POLY1305_SHA256` (not FIPS approved) fails against the fips build and succeeds against the default build, showing the provider swap is active. - Known residual: ring and the jsonwebtoken RustCrypto backend remain linked (cargo features are additive) but are never selected at runtime, which the startup assertions enforce. smg-auth internally uses RustCrypto sha2 for API key fingerprinting; that code only runs when control plane API keys are configured. </details> ## Accuracy Tests N/A, no model or inference code touched. ## Speed Tests and Profiling N/A, default builds keep the same crypto stack. The fips path only affects opt-in builds. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). (`cargo test --test security_tests` passes 48/48 with and without `--features fips`, covering JWT auth, API keys, and mTLS. `cargo clippy --all-targets` is clean in both modes.) - [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). (N/A, no model or inference code touched.) - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. signal.title: [Bugfix] Fix TVM FFI tuple access in CUDA IPC JIT
signal.text: ## Motivation The CUDA IPC JIT module can fail to compile with NVCC 12.8 and `apache-tvm-ffi==0.1.11`: ```text error: no matching function for call to 'get(const tvm::ffi::Tuple<...>&)' note: couldn't deduce template parameter 'I' ``` `get<I>(pair)` relies on unqualified lookup and ADL. In this toolchain combination, NVCC finds the TVM FFI overloads but does not resolve the explicit tuple index. The exception is caught during custom all-reduce setup, so the server continues after falling back to NCCL. ## Modifications Use the existing `tvm::ffi::Tuple::get<I>()` member accessor for the CUDA IPC handle and offset. This bypasses the problematic free-function lookup without changing the tuple values or custom all-reduce behavior. ## Accuracy Tests Not applicable. This only changes how two fields are accessed during CUDA IPC manager initialization; it does not change model outputs or kernel arithmetic. Focused regression validation with Python 3.12.13, PyTorch `2.13.0+cu129`, NVCC 12.8, and `apache-tvm-ffi==0.1.11`: ```python from sglang.kernels.ops.communication.all_reduce import IPCManager manager = IPCManager() manager.destroy() print("jit_ipc_ok") ``` The test used an empty `SGLANG_JIT_CACHE_DIR`, compiled the `cuda_ipc` module, instantiated `IPCManager`, and printed `jit_ipc_ok`. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Not applicable. This is a JIT compiler compatibility fix and does not modify the generated custom all-reduce kernel. ## Checklist - [x] Format the code according to the project style; `git diff --check` passes. - [x] Exercise the affected JIT compilation and registration path with an empty cache. - [x] Documentation is unchanged because there is no user-facing API change. - [x] Accuracy and speed benchmarks are not applicable to this lookup-only change. - [x] Follow the SGLang code style guidance. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32394345576](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32394345576)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32394345229](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32394345229)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32394345470](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32394345470)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [DCP][Spec] EAGLE/EAGLE3 support for decode context parallelism — stacked on #21637
signal.text: Makes **EAGLE / EAGLE3** work with decode context parallelism (`--dcp-size > 1`). Stacked on #21637. DFlash × DCP already worked (see #33912, `_dflash_draft_cell_size`); it gets one shared fix here, not new support. **Root cause:** the target KV pool is sharded across DCP ranks, but the draft pool is **replicated**. Draft-side code that reads the DCP topology therefore builds rank-local metadata against a full pool. Every change below follows from that. ## Results 8×B200, K2.5-NVFP4 + EAGLE3 (ns2/topk1/ndt3), `--dcp-comm-backend a2a --dcp-replicate-q-proj`, jobs 1496709–1496996. Accept length is the correctness gate: the DCP arm must match the off arm, since a draft chain fed rank-local metadata degenerates after the first token. | config | off (ms) | DCP=8 (ms) | ratio | AL off → DCP | |---|---|---|---|---| | 50K / cc4 | 4.96 | 5.93 | 0.84× | 2.239 → 2.234 | | 128K / cc16 | 19.58 | 20.44 | 0.96× | 2.160 → 2.150 | | 128K / cc24 | 37.66 | **26.78** | **1.41×** | 2.172 → 2.163 | | 256K / cc8 | 20.63 | 22.19 | 0.93× | 1.756 → 1.781 | | 256K / cc16 | 59.51 | **38.14** | **1.56×** | 1.748 → 1.745 | GSM8K 0.940–0.960 on every arm. Below the KV-pool edge DCP pays the verify addon for no benefit; past it the off arm loses admission first and DCP wins. Attention FLOPs are conserved under context sharding, so there is no headroom to beat the off arm at shallow overcommit — the ~16% cost at 50K/cc4 is the design point, not a regression. ## Tests `test_dcp_draft_guard.py`, `test_dcp_draft_pool_bounds.py`, `test_dcp_spec_topk_guard.py` — all three cover failures that are otherwise **silent**: a guard that stops unsharding draft forwards corrupts the chain with no error, an under-budgeted draft pool OOMs at the first large prefill far from its cause, and a mis-scoped topk validator returns wrong tokens rather than raising. The topk tests pin that DSPARK is *not* gated (`is_dflash_family()` would pull it in and reject the shipping Kimi-Linear + DSPARK + DCP path). Registered DCP/spec suites pass on 8×B200, including main's `test_kimi_linear_dcp4.py`. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32373996467](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32373996467)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32373996066](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32373996066)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32373996469](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32373996469)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->
signal.author: thanhhao98

signal.title: Skip empty linear-attention state buffers in PD transfer
signal.text: ## Motivation PD disaggregation cannot transfer state for Inkling: every request fails with `Failed to send kv chunk`, and once one send fails the session is blacklisted, so every later request reports `remote mooncake session ... is not alive`. The blacklisting hides the first error. With mooncake logging turned up the real order shows: ``` E transfer_engine_impl.cpp:777] Transfer Engine does not support zero length memory region E rdma_transport.cpp:656] Memory region not registered by any active device(s): 0x7960b8040000 ``` Registration comes first, and it fails on an empty buffer. `MambaPool._iter_transfer_state_tensors` walks the state fields and skips the ones that are `None` or explicitly non-transferable, but a field can also be present and empty: a ShortConv layer has no recurrent temporal state, so its `temporal` shape is declared degenerate and the pool allocates a zero-byte tensor per layer. Those get advertised as transferable state, the engine rejects a zero-length region, and the failed batch registration leaves the real buffers unregistered too, so the transfer then fails on a live buffer with a message that points somewhere else. Measured on Inkling-Small, per role: the mamba component reports 42 empty entries out of 294, one per layer and all from `temporal`, while `conv` reports 0 out of 252 and the attention and aux buffers report none. A model whose linear layers do carry temporal state never hits this. The skip goes in the iterator rather than in a transfer backend: five call sites build parallel per-tensor lists from it (pointers, lengths, item lengths, sliceable dims, field names), so filtering there keeps them aligned with each other, and both the mooncake and NIXL registration paths get it. Prefill and decode run the same code, so they skip the same entries and stay in step. Not a regression: the degenerate `temporal` shape has been there since the initial Inkling support (#31681), the pre-refactor version of this code advertised `temporal` the same way, and the mooncake version is unchanged. ## Accuracy Single-node PD, one prefill and one decode role, TP=2 each, mooncake transfer over IB, hierarchical cache on the prefill role. Before this change no request completes at all. `sgl-eval` aime26, thinking on, `max_tokens=131072`: ``` score = 0.9667 error_rate = 0.00% stop_rate = 1.00 truncated_rate = 0.00% total_completion_tokens = 768226 ``` Long generations are the load-bearing part here: ~25k completion tokens per problem means the decode role advances the convolution state for tens of thousands of steps off what was transferred, so a lossy or misaligned transfer would not survive it. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:no_entry_sign: [Run #32370515187](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32370515187)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #32370515110](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32370515110)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #32370515225](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32370515225)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [Fix][GDN] Route DFlash/DSpark commits through ReplaySSM spec fold
signal.text: ## Motivation ReplaySSM speculative-state folding already supports GDN when speculative decoding commits through `commit_mamba_states_after_verify()`. DFlash and DSpark use a different path and call `HybridLinearAttnBackend.update_mamba_state_after_mtp_verify()` directly after target verification. Before this change, the direct commit path recognized ReplaySSM only for KDA. A GDN target therefore fell back to the regular intermediate-state scatter path, even though `--enable-linear-replayssm-spec` intentionally removes `intermediate_ssm`. The KV-cache configurator prevented this invalid path by rejecting every non-KDA DFlash/DSpark target. This PR routes the built-in GDN backend through the existing ReplaySSM fold implementation from #28695. It does not change the ReplaySSM kernels, model outputs, public flags, or the generic speculative-decoding commit path. ## Modifications - Resolve the direct ReplaySSM verify-commit handler when `HybridLinearAttnBackend` is initialized. - Select the KDA handler only when speculative folding is enabled, and select the GDN handler only for a concrete `GDNAttnBackend`. - Keep the existing intermediate-state scatter fallback for every other backend and for ReplaySSM-disabled execution. - Replace the pool-local KDA-only rejection with validation scoped to DFlash/DSpark target workers before memory-pool sizing. - Fail fast for unsupported direct-verify configurations: non-GDN/KDA targets, non-CUDA/ROCm devices, unified memory, and non-static ragged verification for GDN. KDA compact-ragged verification remains supported. - Add a focused CPU regression test for GDN/KDA handler selection, constructor wiring, direct commit dispatch, and configuration guards. ## Accuracy Tests The following focused and neighboring regression tests pass: | Test | Result | |---|---:| | New GDN direct-commit regression test | 3/3 passed | | GDN ReplaySSM speculative fold parity | 4/4 passed | | GDN/KDA ReplaySSM packed-decode parity | 6/6 passed | | GDN attention backend regression suite | 9/9 passed | | Mamba2 attention backend regression suite | 9/9 passed | | Hybrid FlashInfer metadata regression suite | 2/2 passed | | NGRAM/Mamba verify-update regression suite | 14/14 passed | | ReplaySSM ring accounting | 3/3 passed | The GPU tests were run on a single NVIDIA H20. The clean end-to-end A/B test used Qwen3.8-27B as the target, Qwen3.8-27B-DFlash2 as the draft model, DFlash with one speculative step and eight draft tokens, TP=1, Triton attention backends, CUDA graphs disabled, five-shot GSM8K with 200 questions, parallelism 4, temperature 0, and top-p 1. The only server-side difference was `--enable-linear-replayssm-spec`. | Configuration | Accuracy | Invalid outputs | Exact output match | |---|---:|---:|---:| | Baseline | 194/200 (97.0%) | 0 | Reference | | ReplaySSM | 194/200 (97.0%) | 0 | 200/200 | ## Speed Tests and Profiling N/A. This PR fixes routing to the existing ReplaySSM implementation and does not change its kernels. The GSM8K run above is reported only as an accuracy test; its single-run wall-clock timing is intentionally not used as a performance claim. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). signal.title: [Feature] Support for same GPU native DP replicas with optional CUDA MPS
signal.text: ## Motivation Phase 1 for <https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/35648>. But It will work great for one shot models that don't need to save KV cache, like prefill embedding only models. This change adds `--same-gpu-replicas N` for running `N` native SGLang data-parallel replicas on one physical GPU through one public server endpoint. For example: ```bash --same-gpu-replicas 2 ``` resolves to: ```bash --dp-size 2 --gpu-id-step 0 ``` CUDA MPS is optional and remains externally managed. SGLang runs with normal CUDA scheduling when MPS is unavailable and logs a CUDA startup warning when `nvidia-cuda-mps-control` is not installed. ## Modifications - Add `--same-gpu-replicas N` for guarded same-GPU native DP. - Validate the supported topology: TP=1, PP=1, single node, no DP attention, disaggregation, elastic scaling, or Ray, and explicit `--max-total-tokens`. - Launch same-GPU replicas sequentially to reduce startup memory contention. - Keep one public SGLang endpoint; the native DP controller routes requests across private scheduler/model replicas. - Log whether the NVIDIA MPS control utility is available when same-GPU replicas run on CUDA. - Add unit coverage for flag resolution, the legacy alias, conflicts, and topology validation. - Tested using custom `bench_same_gpu_mps.py` for endpoint throughput and latency benchmarking. ## Accuracy tests N/A. This change modifies replica placement and request routing; it does not change model-forward or kernel numerics. ## Speed tests and profiling Hardware: RTX 4070 Ti 12 GB Model: `Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B` Workload: 100 requests, concurrency 6, four warmup requests, and 128 output tokens per request. CUDA MPS was unavailable in this WSL environment, so these results compare normal CUDA scheduling with one versus two same-GPU replicas. | Configuration | Completion throughput | p50 latency | p90 latency | p99 latency | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:| | 1 replica | 279.7 tok/s | 2.093 s | 3.949 s | 4.157 s | | 2 same-GPU replicas | 538.9 tok/s | 1.176 s | 1.228 s | 4.930 s | Two same-GPU replicas improved aggregate completion throughput by **92.7%** and reduced p50 latency by **43.8%**. The p99 result should be validated with repeated runs. ### CUDA MPS validation CUDA MPS is optional and must be started outside SGLang. ```bash export CUDA_MPS_PIPE_DIRECTORY=/tmp/sglang-mps-pipe export CUDA_MPS_LOG_DIRECTORY=/tmp/sglang-mps-log mkdir -p "$CUDA_MPS_PIPE_DIRECTORY" "$CUDA_MPS_LOG_DIRECTORY" nvidia-cuda-mps-control -d ``` Launch SGLang with two same-GPU replicas: ```bash python -m sglang.launch_server \ --model-path Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B \ --same-gpu-replicas 2 \ --mem-fraction-static 0.35 \ --max-total-tokens 1024 \ --max-running-requests 4 \ --disable-cuda-graph ``` Verify that both scheduler processes attached to the MPS server: ```bash MPS_SERVER_PID=$( printf 'get_server_list\n' | nvidia-cuda-mps-control | awk 'NF {print $1; exit}' ) printf 'get_client_list %s\n' "$MPS_SERVER_PID" | nvidia-cuda-mps-control ps -eo pid,ppid,args | grep '[s]glang::scheduler' ``` The two scheduler PIDs must appear in the MPS client list. ## Checklist - [x] Add unit tests. - [x] Add a manual benchmark utility. - [ ] Run NVIDIA CUDA MPS attachment and benchmark validation on native Linux. - [ ] Run formatting and full relevant CI. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32378164132](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32378164132)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32378164193](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32378164193)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32378164100](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32378164100)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [codex] Fix persistent kernel shared memory fallback
signal.text: ## Summary - Retry deterministic persistent matmul and BMM with `num_stages=2` only when Triton reports a shared-memory `OutOfResources` error. - Cache a successful fallback by operator, normalized device, dtype, and the complete original kernel config, while logging one warning per cache key. - Add CPU tests for the exception and cache contract plus CUDA tests that exercise both real persistent kernel launch sites. ## Root cause The fixed float16 persistent-kernel config uses `num_stages=3`. On affected SM89 deployments, Triton can compile that launch to require 106496 bytes of shared memory, exceeding the 101376-byte per-block limit. Because the footprint depends on the architecture, compiler, and specialization, a static architecture gate can either miss affected builds or unnecessarily reduce stages on builds where stage 3 fits. This change preserves the existing stage-3 fast path. It retries only the exact shared-memory resource failure, caches only after a successful stage-2 launch, and leaves non-shared-memory failures untouched. Shapes and batch size are intentionally excluded from the cache key so one process does not switch launch configuration based on request batching. This addresses #29149 and is a runtime alternative to the static config selection proposed in #34486. ## Validation - `python -m unittest discover -s test/registered/unit/batch_invariant_ops -p "test_persistent_kernel_fallback*.py" -v` (`7` passed) - `python test/registered/unit/batch_invariant_ops/test_batch_invariant_ops.py -v` (`6` passed) - RTX 4090D CUDA tests verified `num_stages=3 -> 2 -> 2` for both matmul and BMM, with exact single-token versus multi-token outputs. - An offline Qwen3-0.6B deterministic-inference server run naturally reproduced `106496 > 101376`, emitted one matmul fallback warning, completed all generation requests with HTTP 200, and produced identical text and token logprobs for repeated and mixed-batch requests. - `py_compile`, `git diff --check`, and trailing-whitespace checks passed. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32393952417](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32393952417)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32393952014](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32393952014)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32393952340](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32393952340)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [MUSA] Harden CI dependencies and diffusion warmup
signal.text: ## Summary Harden the SGLang MUSA CI Python environment and restore steady-state timing for the Wan diffusion smoke. ## Changes - Isolate each GitHub Actions MUSA job with a task-local `PYTHONUSERBASE`, while retaining pip's shared wheel cache so independent jobs do not repeatedly cold-download the same artifacts. - Install and verify the MUSA Triton and `torchada` wheels by version, SHA256, MUSA metadata, and `mtgpu` backend. - Install vendor wheels without dependency resolution, then generate constraints from the installed MUSA stack. Fail closed on mismatched Torch/Torch-MUSA lines, an unexpected Triton target, missing MUSA runtime/device, or an incompatible `compressed-tensors` version. - Add unit coverage for stack constraint generation and validation, and make all `scripts/ci/musa/**` changes select the relevant MUSA CI lanes. - Extend MUSA dependency-install timeouts from 15 to 30 minutes to accommodate cold cache/bootstrap jobs. - Remove the stale per-token FP8 AOT test command from the PR and nightly MUSA workflows. The upstream test was removed during the CUDA JIT migration; MUSA production continues to use its AOT path, so this PR does not substitute a CUDA-only registered test. - For the MUSA Wan 2.1 1-GPU benchmark, use request-based warmup. The first parsed request is `832x480x24f`, while the generic server warmup is capped at 17 frames; warming the exact request shape keeps first-shape initialization out of measured denoising metrics. ## Root cause The original MUSA CI failure was not a generally slow Wan model. Every fresh server paid a large first `Denoise Step 0` cost because the synthetic server warmup used 17 frames and the benchmark request used 24 frames. Steps 1–49 remained near the normal steady-state latency. In parallel, reused runner user-sites allowed public dependency resolution to replace the MUSA Triton stack with generic Torch/Triton packages. The Wan change is benchmark warmup hygiene: it does not claim to eliminate cold-start wall time for a first production request. ## Validation - `python3 -m unittest scripts/ci/musa/test_musa_python_stack.py` — 5 passed. - `bash -n scripts/ci/musa/musa_install_dependency.sh` and ShellCheck passed. - Targeted/full pre-commit checks passed for the changed files. - [Exact squashed-head MUSA run](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32361329056) passed all MUSA jobs after rerunning network-only checkout/clone failures: Qwen-Image, Wan 2.1, 2-GPU diffusion, `sgl-kernel`, multimodal layer tests, and the MUSA finish gate. - On that exact head, the Wan request warmup was logged as `832x480x24f, 1/50 steps`; the measured request then passed 50 denoising steps with step 0 `184.75 ms`, average `356.25 ms`, median `354.41 ms`, and `1 passed`. - Qwen-Image may log a non-fatal synthetic-warmup compiler/`.mubin` warning; its real request completed successfully, so that warning is intentionally out of scope here. ## Scope This PR is limited to MUSA CI dependency isolation/validation, stale MUSA workflow cleanup, and the Wan benchmark warmup mismatch. It does not change the global diffusion warmup policy or attempt to fix the non-blocking Qwen-Image compiler warning. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #32361329332](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32361329332)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32361329006](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32361329006)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #32361329046](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32361329046)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->
signal.author: yeahdongcn

signal.title: [Feature] Token-aware admission cap (--max-inflight-prefill-tokens)
signal.text: The admission knobs we have today (`--max-running-requests`, `--max-queued-requests`) are count-based. They can't tell a 4k prompt from a 500k one. So when a burst of long-context requests lands, the server admits them by count, over-commits prefill memory, and OOM-crashes instead of shedding. On a GLM-5.2-FP8 tp8/dp8 run, 8 concurrent 500k-token prompts take the whole server down (every request net-fails). This adds a token-aware bound: `--max-inflight-prefill-tokens N`. The tokenizer manager sits in front of the workers (one per server, before requests are dispatched to the DP ranks), so it's the right place to bound total work before anything is scheduled. A new request is rejected up front when the prompt tokens already in flight plus this request would exceed `N`. The one subtle part is the accounting. The charge is recorded on the request's `ReqState` inside `_validate_one_request`, which runs synchronously (no `await`), so the read of the in-flight total and the charge are atomic against other in-flight requests. That matters under a concurrent burst: if you compute the in-flight total lazily, 8 requests that arrive together all read an empty total and all get admitted (I hit exactly this and watched it still OOM). Charging synchronously fixes it. The charge is released for free when the request finishes and leaves `rid_to_state`, so there's no separate counter to leak on aborts or disconnects. Default is unset, which is a no-op: the `is not None` guard short-circuits, zero overhead. When set, the only added cost is an int sum over in-flight requests at admission time. Validation (GLM-5.2-FP8, tp8/dp8, dp-attention, `--mem-fraction-static 0.55`): - Without the cap: 8x500k over-admits and OOM-crashes the server, 24/24 requests net-fail. - With `--max-inflight-prefill-tokens 500000`: 4x500k and 8x500k come back as clean 503 rejects, 0 net-fail, server stays healthy (health 200 and no OOM in the log across the whole sequence). - Safe load unaffected: 50 concurrent 4k prompts (206k tokens, under budget) all served, 0 rejects, ttft p50 ~21 ms. I logged the per-request admission decision to confirm the accounting: the first 500k request is admitted at inflight=0 and charged ~507k, and every following one sees inflight=~507k and is rejected, so there's no over-admission and no double count. The budget is sized to what the server can actually serve at once. Set it to the total prefill tokens your memory headroom allows in flight; unset leaves behavior exactly as before. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32392793328](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32392793328)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32392792879](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32392792879)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32392793144](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32392793144)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [Perf] Fuse prefill norm/act quantization for NVFP4 W4A4 hybrid models (Qwen3.5 family)
signal.text: > Rebased onto `main` after #34859 merged: the SiLU+FP4-quant base fusion landed with the model support, so this PR's net diff contains the three remaining changes (attention-layer SiLU coverage, post-LN+FP4-quant, and gated-norm+FP8-quant). ## Motivation For Qwen3.5-family hybrid (GDN + attention) models served with a mixed ModelOpt NVFP4(W4A4)+FP8 checkpoint, prefill spends a measurable share of GPU time in standalone norm / activation / quantization glue kernels: every projection input is normalized, written to HBM in bf16, then re-read and quantized by a separate kernel. Kernel-level tracing against vLLM 0.27.1 on the same model showed the GEMM/attention/GDN families at parity while SGLang lost time in this glue (vLLM fuses norm+quant and act+quant via torch.compile). This PR removes the extra round-trips with three targeted fusions (all bit-equivalent up to FP4/FP8 rounding ties, each with a kill switch): 1. **SiLU+mul + NVFP4 quant** for dense MLPs: replaces `act_and_mul` + the standalone per-block FP4 quantize with FlashInfer's `silu_and_mul_scaled_nvfp4_experts_quantize` (single-group form), handing `down_proj` a prequantized `(fp4, swizzled_scale)` tuple through the existing `_accepts_prequantized_fp4` path. Enabled for both GDN-layer and attention-layer MLPs. 2. **Post-attention GemmaRMSNorm + NVFP4 quant**: FlashInfer `add_rmsnorm_fp4quant` fuses the residual-add, the norm, and the `gate_up` input quant into one kernel. Gemma's `(1 + w)` scaling is folded into a precomputed weight; the swizzled block-scale is exposed as the 2D `(m_padded, K/16)` view so the cuDNN mm_fp4 backend's shape validation also passes. 3. **GDN gated RMSNorm + static-FP8 quant**: adds an fp8-store epilogue to the `fla` `layernorm_gated` Triton kernel (skips the bf16 intermediate write entirely) and teaches `ModelOptFp8LinearMethod` to accept a prequantized `(fp8, scale)` tuple for `out_proj` (explicit opt-in attribute, mirroring the fp4 path). Kill switches: `SGLANG_DISABLE_SILU_FP4_QUANT_FUSION=1`, `SGLANG_DISABLE_POST_LN_FP4_QUANT_FUSION=1`, `SGLANG_DISABLE_GATED_NORM_FP8_QUANT_FUSION=1`. The fusions auto-enable only when the touched projections use the matching ModelOpt linear method (NVFP4 W4A4 for 1-2, per-tensor static FP8 for 3), so other checkpoints and quant modes keep their current control flow. ## Benchmark Re-benchmarked on 2026-08-20 against the current PR base and head. Both lanes ran back-to-back on the same otherwise-idle physical GPU with the same container, model snapshot, server flags, prompt seed, and client command. ### Environment and revisions | Item | Value | |---|---| | GPU | NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition (SM120), physical GPU 2 | | Driver | 580.159.03 | | Container | `lmsysorg/sglang:qwen38` | | PyTorch / CUDA | `2.13.0+cu130` / CUDA 13.0 | | FlashInfer | 0.6.18 | | Model | `RadixArk/Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4` | | Model snapshot | `554ebba9b5f1b79dc11246341960360e6ef05ef4` | | main/base | `a4ffb996db3e823708a53637f851e2677d4455a8` | | PR head | `a3facf77a9bf07464d87299d21dede0837df8e9d` | | merge base | `a4ffb996db3e823708a53637f851e2677d4455a8` | Because the merge base equals the tested main revision, this comparison isolates the PR's net diff. ### Commands The commands below were run inside the existing `sglang_bbuf` container. For the main lane, `SGLANG_TREE=/work/pr34934-rebench-main`; for the PR lane, `SGLANG_TREE=/work/pr34934-rebench-head`. Server: ```bash SGLANG_TREE=/work/pr34934-rebench-head CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=2 \ PYTHONPATH="${SGLANG_TREE}/python" \ python -m sglang.launch_server \ --model-path RadixArk/Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4 \ --host 0.0.0.0 \ --port 31002 \ --tp-size 1 \ --chunked-prefill-size 8192 \ --max-prefill-tokens 8192 \ --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 \ --mamba-ssm-dtype bfloat16 \ --disable-radix-cache ``` Benchmark client: ```bash SGLANG_TREE=/work/pr34934-rebench-head LANE=pr ROUND=1 CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES= \ PYTHONPATH="${SGLANG_TREE}/python" \ python -m sglang.bench_serving \ --backend sglang \ --host 127.0.0.1 \ --port 31002 \ --dataset-name random \ --model RadixArk/Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4 \ --random-input-len 8192 \ --random-output-len 1024 \ --random-range-ratio 1 \ --num-prompts 5 \ --request-rate inf \ --max-concurrency 1 \ --seed 1234 \ --warmup-requests 1 \ --disable-tqdm \ --output-details \ --output-file "/work/pr34934-rebench-artifacts/${LANE}-round-${ROUND}.jsonl" ``` For each revision, one complete five-request run was discarded as a pre-run, then the recorded command was run three times (five requests per round, 15 measured requests per revision). Every invocation also ran the client's one built-in warmup request. GPU 2 had 0 MiB allocated before the first server was started and after the final server was stopped. ### Per-round results | Revision | Round | Mean TTFT (ms) | Median TTFT (ms) | Output tok/s | Median ITL (ms) | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | main | 1 | 655.48 | 642.42 | 64.66 | 14.94 | | main | 2 | 655.66 | 649.62 | 64.22 | 14.96 | | main | 3 | 653.87 | 638.01 | 64.41 | 14.96 | | PR | 1 | 638.52 | 626.78 | 64.32 | 14.95 | | PR | 2 | 640.99 | 627.77 | 64.42 | 14.95 | | PR | 3 | 640.33 | 628.54 | 64.53 | 14.95 | ### Aggregate result TTFT aggregates all 15 per-request observations. Output throughput is total generated tokens divided by total benchmark duration across the three recorded rounds. | Metric | main | main + this PR | Delta | |---|---:|---:|---:| | Mean TTFT | 655.00 ms | **639.95 ms** | **-15.06 ms (-2.30%)** | | Median TTFT | 642.42 ms | **627.77 ms** | **-14.65 ms (-2.28%)** | | Output throughput | 64.43 tok/s | 64.42 tok/s | -0.02% | | Median ITL | 14.957 ms | 14.949 ms | -0.008 ms | For the paired TTFT observations, the mean gain was 15.06 ms and the approximate 95% confidence interval was 10.79-19.32 ms. The current result supports a stable ~2.3% prefill TTFT improvement; decode throughput and ITL are unchanged within run-to-run noise. Startup logs confirmed that the optimized paths were active for the expected layers: - post-LN + FP4 quant: 64 layers - SiLU + FP4 quant: 64 layers - gated RMSNorm + FP8 quant: 48 GDN layers Both server logs were checked for traceback, CUDA error, OOM, and exception signatures; none were found. ### Correctness validation Correctness was not rerun as part of the 2026-08-20 performance pass. The earlier full GSM8K validation (1319 examples) reported: | Configuration | Score | |---|---:| | fusions off | 0.9635 | | fusions on | 0.9658 | The fused kernels were also previously checked for identical residual propagation relative to `fused_add_rmsnorm`. ### Data provenance The performance tables above come from the current PR head and its exact merge base, using three saved `bench_serving --output-details` JSONL results per lane. They replace the older 5-request/FlashInfer-0.6.17 table, which was measured against an earlier base and was not reproducible as a current-main/current-PR comparison. The previous H200 FP8-dynamic table was removed because these W4A4-specific fusions are inactive for that checkpoint and therefore it did not measure this PR's performance effect. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Code Formatting with Pre-Commit](https://docs.sglang.ai/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-formatting-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests as outlined in the [Running Unit Tests](https://docs.sglang.ai/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#running-unit-tests). - [x] Update documentation / docstrings / example tutorials as needed, according to [Writing Documentation](https://docs.sglang.ai/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#writing-documentation). - [x] Provide throughput / latency benchmark results and accuracy evaluation results as needed, according to [Benchmark and Profiling](https://docs.sglang.ai/developer_guide/benchmark_and_profiling.html) and [Accuracy Results](https://docs.sglang.ai/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#accuracy-results). - [x] For reviewers: If you haven't made any contributions to this PR and are only assisting with merging the main branch, please remove yourself as a co-author when merging. - [x] Please feel free to join our Slack channel at https://slack.sglang.ai to discuss your PR. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32368351888](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32368351888)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32368351907](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32368351907)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32368351823](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32368351823)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [Feature] Add DeepEPv2 (ElasticBuffer) MoE A2A backend
signal.text: > Reland of #29525, which was reverted in #35568. > > The revert was caused by one line in the new e2e test: it registered itself to > `runner_config="deepep-8-gpu-h200"`, a runner config that does not exist. > `run_suite.py` validates every registered test's suite before collecting any > of them, so that single bad name aborted unrelated lanes as well -- the ARM CPU > and NPU suites both failed with `Tests registered to invalid suites`. It is > fixed here in a separate commit on top of a clean revert-of-the-revert, so the > restored change can be diffed against the original merge. Running the tests as > single files never goes through `run_suite.py`, which is why local runs stayed > green; `python3 test/run_suite.py --hw cpu --suite base-b-test-cpu-arm64` > reproduces it in one command and now passes. ## Motivation DeepEP v2's `ElasticBuffer` is an NCCL-symmetric-memory all-to-all engine with a fixed per-rank capacity. Fixed capacity means static communication shapes, which makes the MoE decode path CUDA-graph capturable under any topology — including multi-node, where legacy `low_latency` is not available as a graphable path. This PR adds it as a standalone backend `deepep_v2` alongside `deepep`; only expert-parallel dispatch/combine is replaced. Validated on Hopper (H20, H200) and Blackwell (B200 `sm_100`, B300 `sm_103`). ## Modifications - **`layers/moe/token_dispatcher/deepep_v2.py`** (new): the dispatcher. `--deepep-v2-mode direct|hybrid` selects the ElasticBuffer topology — **not** the legacy `normal/low_latency` split. Layout is chosen per batch by inference phase, not by comm mode: decode uses the expanded layout + masked GEMM (static shapes, graph-capturable, available under `hybrid` too), extend/prefill uses the contiguous layout. Single-shot `dispatch()/combine()` with a strict handle lifecycle; the guards run before the DeepEP import check so the module imports cleanly without DeepEP installed. - **`kernels/ops/moe/ep_moe_kernels.py`**: masked-slab repack kernels. A fixed per-expert worker pool keeps the grid static (graph-safe); top-k weights are folded in-kernel; the scale copy takes the source pack-dim stride, which is what makes Blackwell's packed-UE8M0 (column-major) layout correct alongside Hopper's row-major fp32. - **`layers/moe/moe_runner/deep_gemm.py`**: the FP8 adapter (masked decode / contiguous prefill, consuming DeepEP's 128-aligned psum directly as group offsets). `deep_gemm` is the only supported runner: deepep_v2 dispatches FP8 activations plus scales, and no other a2a backend targets a different runner family either. `--moe-runner-backend` is checked at startup, but the runner is chosen per layer by the quant method and several hard-select Triton regardless, so `MoeRunner` rejects the mismatch too — otherwise such a model would reach the permute registry and die on a bare assert after the weights are loaded. - **`layers/moe/ep_moe/layer.py`**: `get_moe_impl_class` resolves `deepep_v2` to `DeepEPMoE` like every other a2a backend — this is what makes the UE8M0 load-time weight requant apply on Blackwell. - **`server_args.py`, `arg_groups/overrides.py`**: the new flags; `ep_size` and `disable_shared_experts_fusion` are declared through the a2a passes, and the runner is validated against `resolved_view(...)` so a model declaration that restores an unsupported runner fails fast. Boot-time capacity check for the chunked-prefill budget. TBO/SBO and enforced shared-expert fusion are rejected at startup. - **`state_capturer/routed_experts.py`**: classify deepep_v2 as a scattered-a2a backend; otherwise `dp_rank > 0` reads unwritten buffer rows under `--enable-return-routed-experts`. - **No CI/Docker changes**: `sgl-deep-ep==0.1.1` already provides `ElasticBuffer`, so CI can exercise this backend as-is; it stays inert for every other configuration, fails fast when DeepEP is missing, and its unit tests need only Triton. - **Tests**: `test_deepep_v2_masked_slab.py` covers the masked-slab repack round-trip -- bf16/fp8, empty experts, the `max_m` boundary, overflow fail-fast, a production packed-UE8M0 scale, and CUDA-graph capture/replay -- and needs only Triton. `test_routed_experts_scattered_a2a.py` pins the capturer's backend classification. `test_routed_experts_dp_readback.py` is the only multi-GPU one: it runs DP>1 with dummy weights over a single 24-expert layer, because `dp_rank 0` sits at buffer offset 0 and looks correct even when the classification is wrong, so nothing below DP>1 can catch that regression; it also covers legacy `deepep` on the same path. Happy to drop or move any of these if they are not worth the coverage. ## Usage DeepEP v2 needs NCCL symmetric memory, which SGLang turns off by default (`NCCL_CUMEM_ENABLE` is set to `int(enable_symm_mem)` when the variable is unset), so an otherwise correct launch fails with `nccl.cu:104: Communicator does not support symmetric memory!`. Pass `NCCL_CUMEM_ENABLE=1` (used for every benchmark here) or `--enable-symm-mem`, which also works but additionally enables NVLS and a 4 GB symmetric-memory prealloc. `SGLANG_DEEPEP_V2_NUM_MAX_DISPATCH_TOKENS_PER_RANK` is the fixed per-rank buffer capacity. It must cover the per-rank chunk (`--chunked-prefill-size / dp_size` under DP attention), and that chunk must be a multiple of `page_size` — with `page_size=256, dp_size=8` the smallest usable pair is capacity 256 with `--chunked-prefill-size 2048`. Smaller capacity is better for decode; prefill servers size it to their chunk budget and add `--disable-cuda-graph`. No extra install step: the pinned `sgl-deep-ep==0.1.1` ships `ElasticBuffer` (`deep_ep 2.1.0`), so this backend runs on a stock environment. Re-validated on H20 x8 against that wheel with no source build and no code change -- `direct` GSM8K 0.970 / MMLU 0.890, `hybrid` 0.970 / 0.886, three-question gate passing in both modes. Earlier development used a DeepEP source build at `d4f41e4`; the packaged API is a superset of what the dispatcher calls. Multi-node: add `--deepep-v2-mode hybrid --enable-dp-lm-head --nnodes 2 --node-rank {0,1}`. Blackwell with a BF16 `wo_a` checkpoint: `SGLANG_OPT_FP8_WO_A_GEMM=0`. ## Accuracy Tests DeepSeek-V4-Flash-FP8, `--tp 8 --dp 8 --ep 8 --enable-dp-attention`, `deep_gemm`, kv fp8. | | deepep_v2 `direct` | deepep_v2 `hybrid` | deepep | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | H20 x8 — MMLU (500) | 0.888 | 0.890 | 0.888 | | H20 x8 — GSM8K (100) | 0.980 | 0.980 | 0.970 | | B200 x8 — MMLU (500) | 0.886 | 0.884 | — | | B200 x8 — GSM8K (100) | 0.950 | 0.970 | — | MMLU at 500 examples has a ~1.4pp standard error at this accuracy, which is wider than every gap in the table; repeat runs of one configuration spanned 0.884-0.896. These numbers show the absence of a systematic shift against the same-node `deepep` baseline, not a ranking. The three-question gate passes on every configuration above. Unit tests (CI, no DeepEP required): masked-slab repack including a production packed-UE8M0 scale and CUDA-graph capture/replay, handle-lifecycle guards, server-args resolution, capturer classification, plus a DP>1 routed-experts readback e2e. The three-question gate also passes on the multi-node configuration below. Earlier validation on the same dispatch path: needle retrieval across chunk boundaries and 8-way concurrent requests 24/24; prefill/decode disaggregation functional. ## Speed Tests | | deepep_v2 | deepep | delta | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | H20 x8 decode | 4,339 tok/s | 4,379 | -0.9% | | H20 x8 prefill | 22,353 in_tok/s | 21,651 | +3.2% | | B200 x8 decode | 8,429 tok/s | 8,675 | -2.8% | | B200 x8 prefill | 32,447 in_tok/s | 31,533 | +2.9% | Each backend pair was measured back-to-back on the same node, on torch 2.13 / sglang-kernel 0.4.6.post1, with the prefill cells interleaved so drift cannot bias one side. H20 prefill averages 4 samples per cell (sd 95 and 72), B200 prefill 2 per cell (sd 132 and 57); decode is one cell per side. Decode reproduces well across nodes -- deepep_v2 measured 8,385 / 8,403 / 8,429 tok/s on three different B200 nodes -- but the `deepep` side moved more, so the decode delta has landed between -0.9% and -2.8% across runs; read it as "a low single-digit percentage behind" rather than a precise figure. Prefill has been consistently ahead by roughly 3%. Multi-node (2x H20x8, TP16/EP16/DP16, `hybrid`, same protocol): **4,610 tok/s** decode with the masked-GEMM + CUDA-graph path over RDMA — a graphable cross-node decode path legacy `low_latency` does not provide — and **20,688 in_tok/s** prefill (two samples: 20,322 / 21,054). There is no same-fabric deepep baseline for this pair: DeepEP's NVSHMEM data plane does not complete across nodes on this RoCE setup, reproduced with DeepEP's own `test_internode.py` outside SGLang. Reproduction (5 rounds per boot, mean of the last 3; prefill flushes the radix cache before each round): ```bash # common: NCCL_CUMEM_ENABLE=1, SGLANG_DEEPEP_V2_NUM_SMS=20, capacity 1024 # deepep_v2: --moe-a2a-backend deepep_v2 --deepep-v2-mode direct # deepep : --moe-a2a-backend deepep --deepep-mode low_latency|normal --deepep-dispatcher-output-dtype fp8 # (with SGLANG_DEEPEP_NUM_MAX_DISPATCH_TOKENS_PER_RANK=1024) NCCL_CUMEM_ENABLE=1 SGLANG_DEEPEP_V2_NUM_SMS=20 \ SGLANG_DEEPEP_V2_NUM_MAX_DISPATCH_TOKENS_PER_RANK=1024 \ python3 -m sglang.launch_server --model-path $MODEL --trust-remote-code \ --tp-size 8 --dp-size 8 --ep-size 8 --enable-dp-attention --context-length 4096 \ --chunked-prefill-size 8192 --moe-runner-backend deep_gemm --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 \ --host 127.0.0.1 --port 30000 $BACKEND_FLAGS \ --mem-fraction-static 0.70 --cuda-graph-max-bs 128 # decode # --mem-fraction-static 0.80 --disable-cuda-graph --disable-piecewise-cuda-graph # prefill # decode python3 -m sglang.bench_serving --backend sglang --port 30000 --dataset-name random \ --num-prompts 128 --random-input-len 1 --random-output-len 1024 --random-range-ratio 1 --max-concurrency 128 # prefill (curl -s localhost:30000/flush_cache before each round) python3 -m sglang.bench_serving --backend sglang --port 30000 --dataset-name random \ --num-prompts 64 --random-input-len 1024 --random-output-len 1 --random-range-ratio 1 --max-concurrency 16 ``` ## Checklist - [x] Format code with pre-commit. - [x] Add unit tests. - [ ] Update documentation (separate follow-up PR). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmarks (above). - [x] Code style. ### Notes for reviewers - Prerequisites: none beyond the current pins -- `sgl-deep-ep==0.1.1` provides `ElasticBuffer`. NCCL symmetric memory must be on (see Usage). - Follow-ups: TBO/SBO comm-compute overlap (a PoC showed the naive two-phase split cannot overlap because `ElasticBuffer.dispatch` is host-blocking; it needs a `return_recv_hook`-style split in DeepEP), adapters for other MoE runners, documentation. Co-authored-by: jianxiongzhang <40026647+jianxiongzhang@users.noreply.github.com> <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:no_entry_sign: [Run #32391082659](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32391082659)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32391082519](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32391082519)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32391082794](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32391082794)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->
