signal.title: [Feature] [RFC] Same-GPU model replicas with managed CUDA MPS and a shared KV pool
signal.text: ## Summary This issue proposes an experimental SGLang mode for running multiple homogeneous replicas of a small or medium language model on one NVIDIA GPU. The initial target is two replicas of `Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B`. The mode combines: 1. native data-parallel request routing; 2. optional SGLang-managed CUDA Multi-Process Service (MPS); 3. one daemon-owned CUDA allocation for model weights, when weight-cache mode is enabled; and 4. one global HBM KV pool shared by every colocated scheduler. `DataParallelController` is the authority for shared KV metadata. A minimal CUDA helper process owns the physical KV slab and exports CUDA-IPC handles. Schedulers map the slab and write only pages leased to them. This is an RFC and performance hypothesis, not a claim that MPS always improves throughput. ## Motivation Small models can leave GPU execution resources underutilized because serving also contains CPU tokenization, scheduling, serialization, launch gaps, and small or irregular batches. Multiple scheduler processes may fill some of those gaps under CUDA MPS. Today, however, colocating independent replicas duplicates the resources that matter most: - model weights; - KV pools; - prefix-cache contents; - CUDA graphs and workspaces; and - unused capacity stranded inside each process-local allocator. MPS alone only multiplexes execution. It does not combine CUDA allocations, allocator state, or prefix metadata. A prefix computed by replica 0 is still a miss on replica 1. For a memory-constrained GPU, process-local KV pools also create a packing problem. One replica can retract or reject work while another replica has free pages that it cannot lend. ## Potential benefits The proposal is intended to test the following benefits. ### 1. Eliminate duplicate prefix KV across replicas Identical prefixes would resolve to the same physical KV pages regardless of which DP rank receives the next request. System prompts, shared document contexts, few-shot examples, and repeated conversation prefixes would consume one set of pages instead of one copy per replica. ### 2. Pool capacity globally All schedulers allocate from one global page budget. Bursty traffic can use currently free pages without pre-partitioning HBM equally between replicas. This should reduce stranded capacity and avoid cases where one rank retracts requests while another rank's private pool is idle. ### 3. Increase effective context or concurrency on GPUs The approximate private-replica memory shape is: ```text replicas * weights + replicas * KV reservation + replicas * graph/workspace memory ``` With shared immutable weights and a shared KV pool, it becomes: ```text one weight allocation + one global KV reservation + replicas * graph/workspace memory + shared-control metadata ``` This does not remove per-process graph and activation overhead, but it can leave substantially more of VRAM available for useful KV. ### 4. Preserve prefix locality without sticky routing Round-robin or load-aware routing would no longer destroy prefix reuse merely because related requests reach different ranks. Sticky routing may still be valuable for active sessions and CPU locality, but it would not be required to reuse published KV pages. ### 5. Improve utilization for underfilled workloads CUDA MPS may overlap otherwise-idle execution from multiple small-model schedulers. This is most plausible for CPU-gapped, bursty, prefill-heavy, or small-batch workloads. ### 6. Reduce retraction and improve burst absorption A global allocator can admit a request using any free page in the pool. Compared with fixed per-rank pools, this can reduce decode retraction caused by temporary imbalance. ### 7. Keep one endpoint and native request ownership The existing DP controller remains the frontend. A request is dispatched once and stays with one scheduler through prefill, decode, streaming, abort, and completion. Operators do not need to run and route between separate HTTP servers. ### 8. Create a foundation for broader replica packing If the ownership and recovery protocol proves reliable, later work could support larger Qwen models, more replicas, multiple GPUs with per-GPU pools, and cache-aware admission policies. ## Why these benefits are hypotheses There are meaningful costs: - allocator and radix-directory RPCs enter the scheduling path; - multiple decode processes can contend for the same SMs and memory bandwidth; - per-process CUDA graphs and activations remain duplicated; - global metadata can become a controller bottleneck; - cross-process synchronization adds latency; and - long concurrent decodes may worsen inter-token latency even if aggregate throughput improves. The feature should not be promoted based only on reduced HBM. It needs measured throughput, TTFT, ITL, tail latency, hit rate, and failure behavior. ## Current SGLang behavior The checked-in implementation currently has these boundaries: - `DataParallelController.launch_dp_schedulers()` advances each replica by `tp_size * pp_size * gpu_id_step`. - `ServerArgs.check_server_args()` requires `gpu_id_step >= 1`. - `build_kv_cache()` constructs a request pool, token-to-KV allocator, device KV pool, and radix tree inside each scheduler process. - `PagedTokenToKVPoolAllocator` owns a process-local free-page tensor. - `RadixCache` owns process-local tree nodes, lock references, LRU state, and physical KV indices. - CUDA MPS is not started, stopped, or verified by SGLang. - Existing CUDA-IPC weight-cache support can map one immutable daemon-owned model allocation into multiple engine processes. - Existing multimodal CUDA-IPC transport demonstrates pooled allocation, process mapping, generations, and stream-ordered ready/ack words, but it is a transport pool rather than a serving KV allocator. Therefore, making a tensor visible through CUDA IPC is not the main missing piece. The missing subsystem is authoritative cross-process allocation, publication, reference counting, eviction, synchronization, and recovery. ## Proposed user experience The initial experimental command would be: ```bash python -m sglang.launch_server \ --model-path Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B \ --same-gpu-replicas 2 \ --enable-shared-kv-pool \ --shared-kv-max-total-tokens 4096 \ --cuda-mps-mode managed \ --max-running-requests 8 ``` Proposed arguments ( Just a suggestion) : | Argument | Meaning | |---|---| | `--enable-shared-kv-pool` | Enable the experimental controller-owned shared allocator and prefix directory. | | `--shared-kv-max-total-tokens` | Global capacity across all colocated replicas, after page alignment. | | `--cuda-mps-mode off` | Do not use or manage MPS; ordinary CUDA time-slicing remains valid. | | `--cuda-mps-mode external` | Require and verify an operator-managed MPS daemon. | | `--cuda-mps-mode managed` | Start a private MPS daemon before any SGLang CUDA process and stop only that daemon at shutdown. | `--max-total-tokens` retains its existing per-scheduler meaning when shared KV is disabled. Shared mode uses a separate global argument to avoid silently changing an existing option's semantics. ## Initial support boundary The first draft PR intentionally supports only: - NVIDIA CUDA on native Linux; - one physical GPU; - `Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B`; - two homogeneous native-DP replicas; - TP1 and PP1; - standard dense Qwen3 MHA/GQA KV layout; - page size 1; - one tokenizer/model configuration; - greedy and ordinary sampling generation; - streaming and non-streaming requests; and - optional existing CUDA-IPC shared weights. It does not support: - heterogeneous models or revisions; - more than one GPU; - tensor or pipeline parallelism; - DP attention; - speculative decoding; - sliding-window attention; - Mamba or other recurrent state caches; - multimodal models; - HiCache or LMCache integration; - disaggregation; - elastic scaling; - online weight mutation; - memory release/resume; or - controller recovery without restarting the endpoint. Unsupported combinations must fail before a CUDA process launches. ##MPS test plan 1. one Qwen3-0.6B replica; 2. two same-GPU replicas with private KV and no MPS; 3. two replicas with private KV and managed MPS; 4. two replicas with shared KV and managed MPS; ## Acceptance criteria The experiment is successful when: 1. both schedulers map one physical KV allocation; 2. page ownership prevents concurrent writes; 3. rank 1 reuses a prefix written by rank 0 without recomputation; 4. active decode uses globally allocated pages; 5. no stale generation can be read after page reuse; 6. global eviction never frees reserved or referenced pages; 7. scheduler death reclaims only unsafe/uncommitted state; 8. controller, memory-server, and MPS failures stop the endpoint safely; 9. single-replica output parity holds; 10. the 12 GB host completes sustained concurrent generation without corruption or OOM; and 11. measured results identify whether HBM savings and MPS concurrency justify the controller-RPC overhead. ## Requested maintainer feedback 1. Is `DataParallelController` the right authority for global KV metadata, or should the CUDA memory server own metadata too? 2. Should managed MPS be part of SGLang, or should the first version support only external verification? 3. Is a separate `--shared-kv-max-total-tokens` clearer than changing `--max-total-tokens` semantics? 4. Is page-size-1 Qwen3-0.6B narrow enough for an initial experimental draft? 5. Should the first mergeable version be reduced to immutable published prefixes while retaining the full mutable-pool work in a follow-up?

signal.title: [NPU][Bugfix] Fix OOB gather in decode KV allocation when free pool is tight
signal.text: ## Motivation NPUPagedTokenToKVPoolAllocator.alloc_decode crashes with an out-of-bounds gather when the free-page pool is exactly tight (len(self.free_pages) == num_new_pages). start_new_pages = torch.cumsum(need_new_pages, 0) - need_new_pages is a prefix index into self.free_pages. For rows that do not need a new page (need_new_pages == 0), start_new_pages == end_new_pages; for the last row this equals num_new_pages. The subsequent self.free_pages[start_new_pages] then indexes past the end (valid range is [0, len(free_pages) - 1] == [0, num_new_pages - 1]). When the pool has slack, the index still lands in-bounds, so the bug is latent; it only fires under exact exhaustion. Observed in CI (test_npu_schedule_conservativeness.py, gsm8k) — the NPU index-check kernel aborts with exactly this condition, then the server traps and dies: ``` Index out of range in dimension 0: index value 1 exceeds bounds 1! [AIV Block ...] [ASSERT] .../index_check/index_check.h:130: ... Assertion `(idx < bound)' failed. ... EZ9999 ... exception of aivec error ... "AI Core Error" ... http.client.RemoteDisconnected: Remote end closed connection without response ... ConnectionRefusedError: [Errno 111] Connection refused Ran 1 test in 251.536s FAILED (errors=1) ``` ## Modifications - In alloc_decode, clamp the gather index: start_new_pages = start_new_pages.clamp(max=num_new_pages - 1). - The clamp is safe: the clamped rows all satisfy need_new_pages == 0, and out_indices weights them by need_new_pages (via (1 - need_new_pages) and * need_new_pages), so their gathered value is masked out and never used. - The num_new_pages == 0 path returns early, so num_new_pages - 1 >= 0 holds whenever the clamp line executes (no max=-1 degeneracy). ## Accuracy Tests Verified on an Ascend NPU machine. The previously failing test_npu_schedule_conservativeness.py now passes — 2 runs, both OK: - run 1: - run 2: No Index out of range assertion and no EZ9999 ... AI Core Error trap remain. ## Speed Tests and Profiling N/A: adds one element-wise clamp per decode batch (O(batch size)), negligible versus the free_pages gather. ## Checklist - [ ] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [ ] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. signal.title: [AMD] Drop redundant FP8 bpreshuffle scale transpose via fused AR kernel
signal.text: Dependent on https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/4478, merged but need aiter update. ## Motivation On gfx95 (MI35x, ROCm >= 7.2) the gfx95 bpreshuffle FP8 block-scale GEMM consumes the per-group activation scale in a **column-major** layout, whereas the fused all-reduce + RMSNorm + per-group-FP8-quant kernel emits it **row-major**. To bridge the two, the fused-quant path in `layernorm.py` currently runs an explicit post-kernel transpose (`materialize_bpreshuffle_fp8_scale`, i.e. `scale.t().contiguous().t()`) on every eligible layer. That `.contiguous()` launches an extra copy kernel per fused-quant call — pure overhead in the decode-latency-bound regime where the model is dominated by many small kernel launches. aiter's fused kernel already has a compile-time `TRANSPOSE_SCALE` template (ROCm/aiter#3652) that can write the scale directly in the column-major layout the bpreshuffle GEMM wants, at zero extra cost (it only changes the store-index math). This PR plumbs that flag through so the fused kernel emits the transposed scale itself, and drops the redundant post-kernel transpose on the fused-success paths. The emitted layout is byte-for-byte identical to what `materialize_bpreshuffle_fp8_scale` produced (column-major storage `(num_groups, M)` viewed as `(M, num_groups)`, stride `(1, M)`), so this is a numerics-preserving change. This is FP8-only. The MXFP4 path uses a different kernel (`custom_fused_ar_rms_mxfp4_quant`) and is untouched. **Dependency:** requires the paired aiter change that forwards `transpose_scale` through `custom_fused_ar_rms_per_group_quant` / `fused_ar_rms_per_group_quant` / the ops stub to the (already capable) C++ op, plus a bundled-aiter pin bump. Without it, the fused-kernel call falls back (the flag is ignored / raises and is caught), so this PR should land together with / after the aiter bump. ## Modifications - `python/sglang/srt/distributed/communication_op.py`: add a `transpose_scale` kwarg to `tensor_model_parallel_fused_allreduce_rmsnorm_quant_per_group` and forward it to the group coordinator. - `python/sglang/srt/distributed/parallel_state.py`: add `transpose_scale` to `GroupCoordinator.fused_allreduce_rmsnorm_quant_per_group` and forward it into the `ca_comm.custom_fused_ar_rms_per_group_quant` call. - `python/sglang/srt/layers/layernorm.py`: pass `transpose_scale=use_bpreshuffle` to both fused per-group-quant calls (the `keep_bf16=False` attention path and the `keep_bf16=True` GDN emit_bf16 path), and remove the now-redundant `materialize_bpreshuffle_fp8_scale` on the two fused-success return paths. - The two separate-per-group-quant **fallback** paths intentionally keep `materialize_bpreshuffle_fp8_scale`: `per_1x128_quant`'s own `transpose_scale` byte-shuffles the scale into a different physical arrangement, not the column-major layout this GEMM consumes. - The FP8 linear consumer (`aiter_w8a8_block_fp8_linear`) is unchanged: the scale layout reaching it is identical, and its own `materialize` call becomes an idempotent no-op (`.contiguous()` short-circuits on an already-column-major tensor). ## Accuracy Tests Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-FP8, TP4 (MI35x), `--enable-aiter-allreduce-fusion`, gsm8k (1319 questions): | Metric | Reference (with transpose) | This PR (fused transpose_scale) | |---|---|---| | Accuracy | 0.947 | **0.955** | | Invalid | 0.008 | 0.008 | Within run-to-run noise (marginally higher) — the change is numerics-preserving. ## Benchmarking and Profiling **Kernel-level confirmation (conc4 profile, IL8192/OL1024, 8 steps):** the fused kernel template flipped `TRANSPOSE_SCALE` false→true (`allreduce_fusion_kernel_1stage_per_group<…Lb0ELb0E>` → `<…Lb0ELb1E>`, 354 calls; `local_device_load_rmsnorm_quant_per_group_naive` Lb0→Lb1, 59 calls). The removed transpose copy (`elementwise_kernel_manual_unroll<…nocast>`) dropped from **960 → 547 = −413**, exactly `354 + 59` (one `.contiguous()` per fused-quant call). Total GPU kernel launches: 11555 → 11142. **End-to-end (Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-FP8, TP4, IL8192/OL1024, num_prompts = concurrency × 10):** | Concurrency | Output tok/s (before → after) | Δ throughput | Median TPOT ms (before → after) | Δ TPOT | |---|---|---|---|---| | 4 | 438.8 → 443.1 | +0.98% | 8.44 → 8.41 | −0.37% | | 8 | 744.7 → 754.0 | +1.25% | 9.67 → 9.54 | −1.30% | | 16 | 1058.3 → 1071.4 | +1.24% | 13.53 → 13.30 | −1.67% | | 32 | 1525.8 → 1536.3 | +0.69% | 18.05 → 17.97 | −0.42% | | 64 | 1960.7 → 1973.7 | +0.66% | 27.27 → 27.09 | −0.65% | | 128 | 2615.1 → 2621.7 | +0.25% | 38.42 → 38.38 | −0.09% | Output-throughput geomean **+0.84%**; decode TPOT consistently lower across the sweep. A small but clean, zero-risk reduction — the benefit is the removal of ~per-layer kernel launches in the decode path. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review Process 1. signal.title: [AMD] [Spec] Enable stochastic tree verification on ROCm
signal.text: ## Motivation ROCm EAGLE verification currently routes every HIP request through greedy `argmax`, even when `temperature`, `top_p`, or `top_k` request stochastic sampling. ROCm also lacks the CUDA target-only tree-sampling kernel and its top-k/top-p renormalization operators. While validating a portable tree verifier with GLM-5.2-FP8, EAGLE top-k > 1 exposed a second blocker: DSA’s page-64 index cache received physical token-slot IDs but indexed them as page rows: ```python index_k[tgt_loc_flat] = index_k[src_loc_flat] ``` On MI355X this failed during draft cache preparation, before target verification: ```text HSA_STATUS_ERROR_EXCEPTION: An HSAIL operation resulted in a hardware exception (0x1016) torch.AcceleratorError: HIP error: unspecified launch failure ``` Both the stochastic verifier and page-aware DSA relocation are required for a complete ROCm top-k > 1 tree path. ## Modifications ### Target-only tree verification - `python/sglang/kernels/ops/speculative/tree_sampling.py` - Add the Triton target-only stochastic tree verifier and residual bonus-token sampling. - `python/sglang/kernels/ops/speculative/__init__.py` - Register the Triton tree-sampling operator for CUDA and HIP. - `python/sglang/srt/speculative/eagle_utils.py` - Route non-greedy HIP EAGLE requests to the Triton tree verifier; preserve chain rejection sampling and greedy dispatch. - `python/sglang/srt/speculative/dflash_utils.py` - Enable the same target-only Triton verifier for DFLASH on HIP. - `python/sglang/srt/speculative/spec_utils.py` - Advertise tree-kernel availability on HIP. ### Portable probability renormalization - `python/sglang/kernels/ops/sampling/renorm.py` - Add exact threshold-based top-k/top-p pivots, tie handling, and full-sort overflow fallback. - `python/sglang/kernels/ops/sampling/renorm_triton.py` - Fuse pivot application, masked reduction, and normalization for HIP. - `python/sglang/kernels/ops/sampling/__init__.py` - Select CUDA AOT, HIP Triton, or portable Torch implementations through the kernel registry. - `python/sglang/srt/layers/sampler.py` - Reuse the portable top-p semantics in the Torch sampler path. ### Page-aware DSA tree relocation - `python/sglang/kernels/ops/attention/dsa/index_buf_accessor.py` - Add overlap-safe gather/scatter kernels that move each token’s 128-byte FP8 index key and 4-byte FP32 scale by `(page, offset)`. - Preserve AITer’s 16x16 preshuffled K layout and CUDA’s row-major layout. - `python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/index_key_cache.py` - Replace token-slot-as-page-row indexing with logical K/scale relocation. - `python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/dsa_cache_layer_split.py` - Remove the duplicated broken override so layer-sharded caches inherit the corrected implementation. ### Tests - `test/registered/kernels/ops/speculative/test_tree_speculative_sampling_triton.py` - `test/registered/kernels/ops/speculative/test_spec_verify_distribution.py` - `test/registered/kernels/ops/attention/test_dsa_index_cache_move.py` ## Accuracy Tests ### MI355X unit tests on final PR commit ```text TestTreeSpeculativeSamplingTriton.test_matches_torch_oracle TestTreeSpeculativeSamplingTriton.test_seeded_inputs_are_repeatable TestTreeSpeculativeSamplingTriton.test_dflash_sampling_integration_matches_oracle TestTreeSpeculativeSamplingTriton.test_branched_tree_preserves_target_distribution TestTreeSpeculativeSamplingTriton.test_matches_cuda_aot_oracle [skipped on ROCm] TestSpecSamplingDispatch.test_hip_target_only_uses_triton_tree TestSpecSamplingDispatch.test_rejection_sampling_uses_triton_chain TestSpecVerifyDistribution.test_chain_sampler_preserves_target_distribution TestSpecVerifyDistribution.test_greedy_verify_collapses_to_argmax TestPortableSpecRenorm.test_top_k_scalar_and_per_row TestPortableSpecRenorm.test_top_p_per_row_and_zero_mass TestDSAIndexCacheMove.test_cross_page_overlap_and_identity TestDSAIndexCacheMove.test_empty_move TestDSAIndexCacheMove.test_layer_split_skips_non_owned_buffers TestDSAIndexCacheMove.test_page64_tree_prefix_tail_duplication ``` | Test file | Result | |---|---:| | `test_tree_speculative_sampling_triton.py` | 4 passed, 1 CUDA-only skip | | `test_spec_verify_distribution.py` | 5 passed, 1 sgl-kernel-only skip | | `test_dsa_index_cache_move.py` | 4 passed | | Pre-commit, all 15 changed files | Passed | CUDA-only registered renormalization oracles: ```text TestSpecRenormFallbacks.test_top_k_fallback_matches_kernel TestSpecRenormFallbacks.test_top_p_fallback_matches_kernel ``` ### GLM-5.2-FP8 customer workload Apex Shortlist problem 4, gold answer `2618`, `n=8`, `temperature=1.0`, `top_p=0.95`, `max_tokens=131072`, EAGLE top-k 2 / 5 steps / 6 draft tokens. | Platform | Correct | Stop | Length | Completion tokens | Server exceptions | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | MI355X, TP8 | 7/8 | 8 | 0 | 317,649 | 0 | | GB300, TP4 | 7/8 | 8 | 0 | 357,376 | 0 | MI355X top-k 3 stress: 27,681 completion tokens, 0 server exceptions. ## Speed Tests and Profiling No valid end-to-end before/after comparison exists: the previous HIP path silently executed greedy verification instead of the requested stochastic algorithm, and DSA top-k > 1 page-64 serving crashed before completion. Kernel optimization will follow separately. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). signal.title: [Fix][Profiler] Count target verify as decode stage
signal.text: ## Motivation Partially addresses #34943 and complements #35115, which handles asynchronous trace export. During speculative decoding, scheduler batches use `ForwardMode.TARGET_VERIFY`. That mode is intentionally extend-shaped and therefore satisfies `is_prefill()`, so the legacy by-stage profiler counted verify iterations as prefill and never advanced or completed its decode-stage window. The unfinished profile could then stop during a later request. ## Modifications - Treat both `DECODE` and `TARGET_VERIFY` as decode-stage work in the legacy by-stage profiler. - Give that lifecycle classification precedence over the extend-shaped `is_prefill()` classification. - Add a CPU regression test covering the `EXTEND -> TARGET_VERIFY -> TARGET_VERIFY` transition and its stage start/stop calls. ## Accuracy Tests No model computation or output values are changed. - `pytest -q test/registered/unit/managers/scheduler_components/test_profiler_manager.py` (`1 passed`) - Black, isort, and focused Ruff checks pass for both changed files. - `python scripts/lint/check_registered_tests.py` ## Speed Tests and Profiling No benchmark was run. signal.title: [Unified Cache][Draft POC]: Add optional external-cache linker mode to Unified Radix Cache
signal.text: ## Motivation Unified Radix Cache manages heterogeneous model states, including full-attention KV, SWA KV, and model-specific sidecars. On GB platforms, **deployments may need to aggregate larger memory regions into a shared Global Memory pool**. This requires an efficient way for Unified Radix Cache to access remote memory directly without overhead on the inference critical path. This PR adds an optional external-cache linker mode. It allows the tree to access a Global Memory pool through backends such as Mooncake or UMBP .. while retaining ownership of allocation, insertion, component consistency, and cache-node lifetime. The existing hierarchical cache path remains unchanged. The linker is an opt-in alternative for deployments that need a larger shared memory pool while preserving inference performance. ## Modifications This PR is currently at the proof-of-concept stage and will be split into several smaller, focused PRs: - [ ] Introduce the external linker interface and common linker wrapper - [ ] Integrate external linker support into `UnifiedRadixCache` - [ ] Add direct linker implementations for Mooncake、UMBP - [ ] Expand correctness, compatibility, and performance testing - [ ] Support prefetch - [ ] Support other implementations ## Speed Tests and Profiling The optional Mooncake linker was benchmarked against the existing L3 Mooncake path on 8 * H200 GPUs. Lower TTFT is better. A positive percentage means that the linker is faster. signal.title: [AMD][CI] Name the ROCm Image That Actually Ran in AMD Job Names
signal.text: Follow-up to #35602 and #35603. After #35602 the ROCm 7.2 PR gate pulls the **7.2.4** image, but every job in it is still named `...-rocm720`. After #35603 a single nightly run covers both images, and since no nightly job declares a `name:`, GitHub auto-appends the matrix value and prints `nightly-test-1-gpu-unit-rocm720 (rocm724)` — one name carrying both version numbers. This stops the name stem from hardcoding a ROCm version. The stem becomes just the job's own name, and the ROCm flavor is shown after it. ## Naming The flavor moves out of the stem into the paren coordinates, ahead of the runner and shard: | before | after | | --- | --- | | `stage-c-test-large-8-gpu-amd-rocm720 (linux-mi300-8gpu-sglang, 3)` | `stage-c-test-large-8-gpu-amd (rocm724, linux-mi300-8gpu-sglang, 3)` | | `stage-c-test-large-8-gpu-amd (linux-mi300-8gpu-sglang, 3)` | `stage-c-test-large-8-gpu-amd (rocm700, linux-mi300-8gpu-sglang, 3)` | | `nightly-test-1-gpu-unit-rocm720 (rocm724)` | `nightly-test-1-gpu-unit (rocm724)` | Three things this buys: - **The flavor is printed unconditionally.** `pr-test-amd-extra.yml` suppressed the suffix for whatever was currently the default, so #35602 silently changed what the bare name `extra-a-test-1-gpu-small-amd` referred to — 7.2.0 before, 7.2.4 after — with no visible diff in the Actions UI. - **The stem stops moving when the pinned image is bumped.** A future 7.2.5 renames nothing. - **The stem is now exactly the `run_suite.py` suite name**, which is what you pass to reproduce a failure locally. The paren value is the ROCm lane the run is configured for, i.e. `inputs.rocm_version` (or the ROCm 7.0 lane's fixed default). It is not a claim about the image digest: `amd_ci_image` / `AMD_CI_IMAGE` still takes priority inside `amd_ci_start_container.sh`, so a dispatch that pins a custom image will show its configured lane rather than that image. That escape hatch is deliberately out of scope here. **Job ids are unchanged.** `needs:` lists, the `target_stage_select` options and the `job_filter` conditions all key off ids, so they are untouched. ## The two consumers that match on display names Neither of these reads job ids, so both have to follow the rename. **`wait-for-jobs`** gates stage B on stage A and stage C on stage B by polling `job.name` with `name === prefix || name.startsWith(prefix + ' ')`. Its four prefixes in the 7.2 gate carried the `-rocm720` suffix and would have matched nothing, spinning stage A for its full 240-minute budget and stage B for 480 after that. They now use the bare stems, which match on the trailing space and still exclude the `-nondeterministic` and `-mi35x` variants (next character is a dash). The 7.0 gate already used bare stems and was unaffected. **`amd-ci-job-monitor.yml`** builds its report targets from job ids and hands them to `query_job_status.py`, which prefix-matches them against display names: - The 7.2 lanes strip the `-rocm720` id suffix to recover the stem. - The nightly asks for each flavor by full name. A stem-only prefix matches both `(rocm724)` and `(rocm720)` — `_job_name_matches_filter` accepts a following space — so it would merge the two images into a single row and show a 7.2.4-only regression as a ~50% flake rate on a row labelled `rocm720`. - The extra call and the two stage waits drop out of the 7.2 gate list: they run on `ubuntu-latest`, so the self-hosted-only snapshot never had data for them. ## Verification Rendered every job name in all four workflows, expanding each `strategy.matrix` the way GitHub does, then replayed both consumers against those names — the monitor filters through the real `_job_name_matches_filter`, and every `wait-for-jobs` prefix through the action's own rule, asserting each resolves to exactly its declared `expected_count`. | workflow | names | monitor filters | wait prefixes | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `pr-test-amd-rocm720.yml` | 45 | 19 | 4 | | `nightly-test-amd-rocm720.yml` | 94 | 94 | 0 | | `pr-test-amd.yml` | 46 | 20 | 4 | | `nightly-test-amd.yml` | 43 | 43 | 0 | Every name is unique, every monitor filter resolves to exactly one job, every job is covered, and every wait prefix hits its expected count. The uniqueness assertion caught a draft in which the explicit `name:` added to the mi35x jobs dropped their `matrix.runner` / `matrix.part` and collapsed three shards onto one name. Per-job history in `query_job_status.py` splits at this commit, since the names change. Nothing gates on the old strings: `GET /repos/sgl-project/sglang/rules/branches/main` returns only `deletion`, `non_fast_forward`, `pull_request` and `required_linear_history`, with no `required_status_checks`. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests <!-- N/A: CI configuration change --> - [ ] Update documentation <!-- N/A --> - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:no_entry_sign: [Run #32388017995](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32388017995)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:no_entry_sign: [Run #32388017547](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32388017547)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:no_entry_sign: [Run #32388018196](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32388018196)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [AMD][DCP] Skip unused QuickAllReduce allocation for DCP groups
signal.text: ## Motivation On ROCm, `GroupCoordinator` currently initializes QuickAllReduce whenever custom all-reduce is enabled. That is useful for TP, but current DCP communication paths do not dispatch to QuickAllReduce: - `ag_rs`: all-gather plus reduce-scatter for MLA, or an FP32 all-reduce for MHA. - `a2a` / `fi_a2a`: all-to-all. In a Kimi-K3 TP8/DCP8 profile on MI350X, constructing the DCP QuickAllReduce communicator reserved 4.002 GiB per GPU. Across 1,152 recorded rank-0 DCP collective dispatches, QuickAllReduce was selected zero times. TP QuickAllReduce remains useful and must stay enabled. Related to #29736. ## Modifications - Add an optional `use_quick_allreduce` control to `GroupCoordinator` and `init_model_parallel_group`. - Preserve the existing behavior by default: the new option inherits `use_custom_allreduce` when unspecified. - Disable QuickAllReduce only for the DCP group. - Keep the AITER custom-all-reduce and PyNccl setup unchanged. - Add a unit test that verifies DCP opts out while TP retains the default behavior. ## Accuracy Tests This does not change model math or the collective selected by current DCP paths. The targeted construction test passes: ``` 1 passed, 5 deselected ``` ## Speed Tests and Profiling This PR targets static memory rather than latency. Measured DCP communicator initialization on MI350X: | Component | Reserved per GPU | | --- | ---: | | PyNccl | 1.883 GiB | | AITER custom all-reduce | 3.002 GiB | | QuickAllReduce | 4.002 GiB | QuickAllReduce had zero selections in the recorded DCP dispatches, so this change reclaims the 4.002 GiB DCP allocation without removing TP QuickAllReduce. ## Checklist - [x] Ran pre-commit on the changed files. - [x] Added a focused unit test. - [x] No documentation change is required; the default API behavior is preserved. - [x] No model kernel or output math is changed. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #31354533291](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31354533291)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #31354533157](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31354533157)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:heavy_minus_sign: **No AMD PR run found for this commit**.<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [Bug] 0.5.17: generation degenerates into token loops on Qwen3.5-arch model (works on 0.5.6.dev, with/without DFLASH)
signal.text: ### Bug report **Model**: orcarouter/Qwen3.8-27B-Uncensored-NVFP4 (arch `Qwen3_5ForConditionalGeneration`, NVFP4 quantized) + z-lab/Qwen3.8-27B-DFlash2 draft, single 80GB GPU. **Version broken**: 0.5.17 (PyPI wheel). **Version working**: 0.5.6.post3.dev9196+ga4ffb996d (git @a4ffb996d). Same model, same flags, same venv. **Symptom**: after upgrading to 0.5.17, generation degenerates into single-token repetition loops (e.g. `What What What What …` in content, or `"Let's verify." "Let's verify." …` inside reasoning_content), and never exits thinking / never reaches tool calls. `finish_reason: length`, empty content. **Isolation already done** (all still reproduce on 0.5.17): 1. With DFLASH (8 draft tokens) → loops 2. Without DFLASH (no spec) → loops 3. Without `--reasoning-parser qwen3` → loops (no reasoning_content now, content loops) 4. Plain chat request, no tools → loops 5. Same requests on 0.5.6.dev9196, identical flags → clean output, tool call returned normally **Repro** (plain chat, no tools): ```bash python -m sglang.launch_server \ --model-path <main-model> --served-model-name qwen3.8-27b \ --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 --attention-backend flashinfer \ --reasoning-parser qwen3 --max-running-requests 8 \ --mem-fraction-static 0.90 --max-total-tokens 1500000 curl -s localhost:8000/v1/chat/completions -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{ "model":"qwen3.8-27b","max_tokens":160,"temperature":0.6, "messages":[{"role":"user","content":"What is the capital of France? Answer in one short sentence."}]}' ``` Expected: clean answer. Actual (0.5.17): `content: "The user asks for the answer one short sentence.The question asks What What What What What What What What …"`, `finish_reason: length`. Looks like a generation-level regression in 0.5.17 for this Qwen3.5-based arch (sampling/logits/pipe), independent of speculative decoding. Happy to provide full logs or bisect help.

signal.title: [BugFix][DP] Prevent health checks from perturbing user request routing
signal.text: ## Motivation Generation health checks (`HEALTH_CHECK_*`) are intentionally skipped by the scheduler while normal inference is already making progress. Under DP serving, however, the request passes through `DataParallelController` before that scheduler-side skip. With `round_robin`, a generation health request currently advances the same dispatch state used by user requests. For load-aware methods, it can also participate in the user load-budget refresh/update path. This means a health request that is later discarded can still perturb user-request ownership across DP ranks. In a long-prefill DP-Attention workload, this produced a reproducible scheduling failure chain: ```text generation health request -> user LB state is mutated -> per-rank user ownership becomes uneven -> some DP ranks become idle while peers continue prefill -> PrefillDelayer sees persistent mixed states / timeout -> effective concurrency and throughput drop ``` The root-cause investigation is tracked in #35241. ## Modifications This PR isolates generation-health dispatch state from user load-balancing state in `DataParallelController`: - Detect generation health requests before normal user LB dispatch. - Use an independent round-robin counter for health requests. - Do not refresh or mutate the user `DPBudget` for health-only dispatches. - For batch generate, refresh the user load budget only when the batch contains a user request. - Preserve explicit `routed_dp_rank` behavior. - Preserve `FOLLOW_BOOTSTRAP_ROOM` semantics for PD/disaggregated serving, since that path uses request-specific routing rather than shared mutable user LB state. This PR does **not** change DP Attention, PrefillDelayer, scheduler busy-health skip behavior, or the health endpoint semantics. ## Regression Tests Added CPU unit coverage for: - independent user-RR and health-RR state; - health dispatch using only active workers; - explicit `routed_dp_rank` not advancing health RR state; - health dispatch bypassing user load-budget refresh; - health-only batch dispatch not refreshing user load state; - `FOLLOW_BOOTSTRAP_ROOM` health routing compatibility. ```text python3 -m pytest test/registered/unit/managers/test_data_parallel_controller.py -q 23 passed git diff --check clean pre-commit run --files \ python/sglang/srt/managers/data_parallel_controller.py \ test/registered/unit/managers/test_data_parallel_controller.py all passed ``` ## Runtime Validation Validated on 8x NVIDIA B300 with DeepSeek-V4-Pro, TP8/DP8, DP Attention, MegaMoE, PrefillDelayer, round-robin routing, 8k effective prefill chunk, C16/N160, 60k input / 1 output. The external watchdog continued issuing generation health checks during the patched runs. | Configuration | Input TPS | avg running | HEALTH at DPC | IDLE-while-EXTEND | Delayer timeout | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | Original + generation health ON (observed HIT) | 76,417 | 6.84 | 59 | 33 | 9 | | Original + generation health OFF | 94,720-94,974 | 8.55-8.76 | 0 | 0 | 0 | | Patched + generation health ON, 4/4 runs | 94,372-94,822 | 8.60-8.69 | 49-51 | 0 | 0 | All patched runs completed 160/160 requests with no fatal errors. Generation-health traffic remained present at DPC, while the user-ownership hole and associated concurrency collapse disappeared. This is a scoped validation for the tested failure family; it is not intended to claim that generation health is the cause of every low-throughput state. ## Scope The intended invariant is: > Generation health traffic must not mutate the load-balancing state used by user requests when it is routed through DP serving. This PR does not make round-robin load-aware and does not change the configured load-balancing policy. Related: #35241 <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32386249966](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32386249966)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32386249757](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32386249757)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32386249986](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32386249986)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [CI/NPU] Isolate multi-node tests by run_id to prevent concurrent-run…
signal.text: <!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. --> ## Motivation Apply run-scoped isolation across the NPU multi-node test pipeline so that concurrent runs sharing the same k8s namespace and PVC no longer overwrite each other's source code, pollute each other's ConfigMap, or accidentally delete each other's pods during cleanup. <!-- Describe the purpose and goals of this pull request. --> ## Modifications - Source code path on the shared PVC is suffixed with github.run_id to avoid concurrent runs overwriting /root/.cache/tests/sglang/. - Pre-test Clear resources: bounded retry (max 60 x 30s = 30min) with fail-fast exit 1 when stale pods refuse to die. signal.title: fix(constrained): reject NUL bytes in grammar specs to stop an xgrammar segfault
signal.text: ## Motivations A `regex` beginning with a NUL byte kills the server. xgrammar's regex converter appends its own NUL terminator and indexes past it, raising **SIGSEGV** — an OS signal, so the `except RuntimeError` in `dispatch_regex` cannot catch it. The scheduler dies with `exit code -11` and all later requests are refused. ```python python3 -c 'import xgrammar; xgrammar.Grammar.from_regex(chr(0))' # SIGSEGV ``` Two measured details: - Trigger is a **leading** NUL, not control characters generally — `\x01`, `\x02`, `\x1f` and non-leading NUL all compile fine. Rejecting all control characters would break valid patterns like `[\t\n]+`. - A **JSON schema reaches the same converter via `pattern`**, where the NUL may be an escape (`\u0000`) — no NUL byte in the request body at all. Guarding only `regex` leaves that path open. No release fixes it: 0.2.0-0.2.4 and 0.2.6rc1 all crash on the `regex` path (`regex_converter.cc` is unchanged v0.2.5 through HEAD). ## Modifications - `base_grammar_backend.py`: `_grammar_key_contains_nul()`, called at the top of `_init_value_dispatch` — the choke point for all four grammar types and every backend. Returns `InvalidGrammarObject`, which flows through the existing failure path to the same clean error an invalid pattern already gets. For `json`/`structural_tag` the spec is decoded and walked, so an escaped `\u0000` in a nested `pattern` is caught; malformed JSON falls through to the backend's own error. Placed at the dispatcher, not `xgrammar_backend.py`, because the JSON path reaches the same native code and a segfault cannot be caught after the fact. - `test_base_grammar_backend.py`: `TestNulByteGrammarRejection` — NUL specs rejected without the backend being called (`regex` and JSON `pattern`, raw and escaped, plus a non-leading NUL so the guard can't be narrowed to `startswith()`); valid patterns, non-NUL control characters and malformed JSON still dispatch normally. A NUL has no meaning in a regex, schema or grammar, so no legitimate request is affected. Verified on aarch64/GB200: the file passes **33 tests / 17 subtests** with no regressions; the new cases fail 8/8 without the guard; on a live server the two crashing payloads go from killing the process to **HTTP 400**, `/health` 200, no segfault markers. ## Accuracy Tests N/A — no change to kernels or the model forward path. ## Speed Tests and Profiling N/A — one substring check per uncached grammar compilation (for JSON, a parse the backend already performs). ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). — N/A, no user-facing API change. - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). — N/A, see above. - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #32308365762](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32308365762)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32308365506](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32308365506)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [Runtime] Don't override CUDA_MODULE_LOADING
signal.text: ## Motivation `_set_envs_and_config()` currently assigns `CUDA_MODULE_LOADING=AUTO` before spawning scheduler processes. This silently replaces an explicit `DEFAULT`, `EAGER`, or `LAZY` deployment choice, even though SGLang has no corresponding CLI option that would justify overriding this CUDA control plane. This matters when a deployment intentionally uses eager loading to move first-use module initialization out of the request path, accepting additional startup time and memory for more predictable request latency. Today that setting is lost before the model-loading scheduler processes are spawned. ## NVIDIA CUDA contract The NVIDIA CUDA Programming Guide documents [`CUDA_MODULE_LOADING`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cuda-programming-guide/05-appendices/environment-variables.html#cuda-module-loading) with these possible values: > `DEFAULT`: Default behavior, equivalent to `LAZY`. > `LAZY`: The loading of specific kernels is delayed until a CUDA function handle ... is extracted. > `EAGER`: Fully loads CUDA modules and kernels at program initialization. `AUTO` is not a documented value. NVIDIA's [Lazy Loading guide](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cuda-programming-guide/04-special-topics/lazy-loading.html) also states: > As of CUDA 12.3 lazy loading is enabled by default on all platforms, but can be controlled via the `CUDA_MODULE_LOADING` environment variable. and: > Lazy loading can be disabled by setting the `CUDA_MODULE_LOADING` environment variable to `EAGER`. ## Change Stop assigning `CUDA_MODULE_LOADING` in `_set_envs_and_config()`. - Explicit CUDA values now reach spawned scheduler processes unchanged. - When the variable is absent, supported CUDA versions retain their native default lazy-loading behavior. - This PR does not add an SGLang CLI flag or change `CUDA_DEVICE_MAX_CONNECTIONS`. ## Validation - `pre-commit run --files python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/engine.py` - `git diff --check` <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32383857645](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32383857645)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32383857195](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32383857195)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32383857473](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32383857473)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [PP&Sepc] enable dspark under pipeline parallelism (deepseek-v4 & kimi-k3)
signal.text: ## Motivation roadmap: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/11857, https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/30344, https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/32607 Our previous PR (https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/31139) enabled PP + EAGLE support. Testing showed DSpark speculation performs far better than EAGLE, so this PR builds on it to add DSpark + PP compatibility. This PR depends on the previous one and should be merged afterwards. DSpark's verify path is structurally different from EAGLE's (per-layer aux hidden capture, linear block verify, confidence-driven budget), so it could not reuse the EAGLE PP machinery verbatim. This PR lifts that ban and makes DSpark run under PP, targeting DeepSeek-V4-Flash + the bundled DSpark draft checkpoint. ## Modifications The core idea mirrors the EAGLE PP design — the draft model lives only on the last PP rank, every rank runs its own target verify forward, and the draft proposal is relayed across stages so each rank rebuilds an identical verify context. The DSpark-specific work is making the per-layer aux-hidden capture and the linear block verify cross the PP boundary correctly. 1. **Per-rank draft proposal carrier (`DSparkPPVerifyInputRaw`).** A new spec input type carries the last rank's draft / confidence / accounting fields (bonus tokens, draft tokens, new seq lens, confidence, accept/cap-trim/verify lens) across the PP ring. Every rank rebuilds an identical verify layout from the same source each iteration, so all PP ranks produce byte-identical verify windows. It mixes in the shared `DFlashDecodePrepareMixin` so the non-last rank's verify forward (which reads `verify_cache_loc` from `req_to_token`) pre-allocates KV headroom exactly like the last rank. Linear verify reuses the formal `req_to_token` slots, so `accept_index` is always `None` and the token-move step in `batch_result_processor` is skipped automatically. 2. **Per-layer aux hidden capture across PP stages (`deepseek_v4.py`).** DSpark's draft needs per-layer aux hidden states (`dspark_aux_hidden_states`), but each PP rank only executes layers in its own `[start_layer, end_layer)` range. The aux list is now stacked as `[L, num_tokens, hidden]`, relayed downstream under the `"dspark_aux"` key in `PPProxyTensors`, and rebuilt in global layer order on the last rank (upstream layers first, then local captures). `set_dspark_layers_to_capture` no longer early-returns on non-last ranks, so every rank registers its own capture range. 3. **PP-aware verify forward.** `pp_proxy_tensors` is threaded through `TargetVerifyExecutor.run` / `run_non_compact` so the target verify forward relay hidden states along the PP ring on every rank. `TargetVerifyResult` carries `pp_hidden_states_proxy_tensors` back to the scheduler. Logits adjustments (penalizer / vocab mask / logit bias) are now gated on `result.logits_output is not None`, since non-last ranks never sample and their logits output is `None`. 4. **Embed / weight loading split (`deepseek_v4_dspark.py`).** The DSpark draft used to borrow `embed_tokens` from the target. Under PP the last rank builds its own `VocabParallelEmbedding` and only `lm_head` is shared from the target; `attach_shared_modules` now takes `embed_tokens: Optional` so the PP path passes `None` and the draft keeps its locally-built embedding. Weight-name remapping keeps `embed_tokens.weight` on the last PP rank. 5. **PP proxy buffer sizing (`base_runner.py`).** The static `pp_proxy_tensors` buffers are allocated by max token count, not batch size, so the dummy / capture buffer fits the verify-token-expanded shape `[num_tokens, *hidden]` produced under speculative decoding. 6. **Planner / draft fixes for the relayed layout.** `alloc_verify_window` and `DraftBlockProposer` derive `prefix_lens` from the verify window's anchor position instead of `batch.seq_lens`, because the last rank's re-propose pass builds the next window from post-iter seq lens while `batch.seq_lens` is still the pre-iter value. The planner forces `RAGGED_VERIFY_MODE=STATIC` and non-compact (eager) verify under PP, since the confidence-driven ragged scheduler and the cuda-graph compact path only run on the last rank and cannot keep cross-rank layout identity. Supporting changes: `draft_worker_common.build_draft_tp_worker` accepts a `pp_global_random_seed` so the draft sampler on the last rank is seeded consistently with the target; `speculative_hook` replaces the blanket `pp_size != 1` ban with a narrower "PP + DP-attention unsupported" check (DP-attention partitions the batch, which conflicts with the PP requirement that every rank see an identical batch). ### Limitations asserted now - **PP + DP-attention** is rejected. Only `--dp-size 1` is permitted under PP. - **PP forces static verify and eager (non-cuda-graph) verify** ## Accuracy Tests Model: DeepSeek-V4-Flash-FP8 GSM8K accuracy (200 examples, 5-shot, temperature=0): | Configuration | GSM8K Accuracy (%) | |---|---| | PP2-TP4 (no spec) | 98.00 | | PP2-TP4 + DSpark (this PR) | 98.50 | ## Speed Tests Setup: DeepSeek-V4-Flash-FP8, single 8*H20 node; three PP2+TP4 configs: - **PP2-TP4** — PP2+TP4, no spec (baseline) - **PP2-TP4-MTP314** — PP2+TP4 + EAGLE (`speculative-num-steps=3`, `speculative-eagle-topk=1`, `speculative-num-draft-tokens=4`) - **PP2-TP4-DSpark** — PP2+TP4 + DSpark (this PR) bench_serving: `--dataset-name random` with local ShareGPT path (`--dataset-path /datasets/ShareGPT_V3_unfiltered_cleaned_split.json`), `--random-range-ratio 1.0`, `--num-prompts 5`, `--max-concurrency 1`, `--random-output-len 1024`, `--seed 42`; 3 rounds per point, reporting the min. **TPOT (ms)** | Configuration | 16k | 32k | 64k | |---|---|---|---| | PP2-TP4 (no spec) | 11.11 | 11.14 | 11.13 | | PP2-TP4 + MTP314 | 5.39 | 5.43 | 5.65 | | PP2-TP4 + DSpark (this PR) | 2.30 | 2.34 | 2.38 | **Average accepted length (tokens / iter)** | Configuration | 16k | 32k | 64k | |---|---|---|---| | PP2-TP4 + MTP314 | 2.75 | 2.90 | 2.83 | | PP2-TP4 + DSpark (this PR) | 4.91 | 4.85 | 4.87 | ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to the [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to the [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [ ] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process). 2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers. 3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so. - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci` 4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: **Missing `run-ci` label** -- add it to run CI tests.<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: **Blocked** -- `run-ci` is required first.<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:heavy_minus_sign: **No AMD PR run found for this commit**.<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [GDN] Route Qwen TP4 decode and verify rows through Cake
signal.text: ## Summary - lazily load the optional public FlashInfer Cake GDN decode package on SM100/SM103 - fail closed on unsupported dtype, layout, shape, stride, state-pool, or graph-capture combinations - preserve caller-stream and CUDA graph semantics with preallocated workspace/state and cached FP32 dt bias - route the actual Qwen3-Next TP4 BF16 decode and verify rows through the promoted tile16 full-warp kernels ## Qualification - rebased onto current SGLang main b814a7e812fb9367d994af307085bd30de329f96 - B200/SM100, job 3752127 on umbriel-b200-037: 9 tests passed and 26 subtests passed, including actual TP4 eager and CUDA Graph paths - GB300/SM103, job 510532 on nvl72d093-T03: 9 tests passed and 26 subtests passed, including the same paths - exact route IDs: cake.gdn_decode.indexed_bf16_t1.tile16_fullwarp and cake.gdn_decode.indexed_bf16_verify_t4.tile16_fullwarp - exact TP4 shapes: B=4,T=1,H=4,HV=8 and B=2/3/5/8,T=4,H=4,HV=8; adjacent B=4,T=4 and every unmeasured layout fail closed - same-environment cold-L2 CUPTI kernel A/B versus live FlashInfer 8044d94bf9: - B200 T1 0.003296 vs 0.003472 ms (1.053x), T4 0.006400 vs 0.006944 ms (1.085x), geometric mean 1.069x - GB300 T1 0.003040 vs 0.003296 ms (1.084x), T4 0.006304 vs 0.006736 ms (1.069x), geometric mean 1.076x - correctness uses fixed BF16 atol=rtol=1e-2; dual-arch public ABI/stream/graph and sanitizer gates pass - exact Qwen3-Next 80B FP8 TP4/MTP model replay, four GB300s, job 3137824: 4/4 tests pass; cache-hit KL 0.0007701/0.0017106 versus the fixed 0.0035 ceiling; all four TP ranks record the Cake T4 route during CUDA Graph capture - attributed serving ABBA, four GB300s, job 3137849: all eight measured 128-request rounds complete; four-round median output/total throughput 1.000280x, mean/median TPOT 1.003214x/1.005037x, and mean TTFT 0.987693x versus FlashInfer (the ~1.25% TTFT regression is retained explicitly) Current-head real-model evidence is recorded below. Review and merge are intentionally deferred in this evidence-only phase. ## Current-head decision evidence This replay uses FlashInfer #4581 head `4215a24cb` and supersedes the earlier `45b60f98` jobs/comment. Review and merge are intentionally deferred. ### Environment and attribution - real Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B-Instruct-FP8 weights, revision `c5f5f263bdd5cc134092897864e8905d8fe7b928` - four NVIDIA GB300 CC 10.3 GPUs on healthy replacement nodes; SGLang `ee8378ad4`, Torch `2.13.0a0+nv26.07`, CUDA 13.3 - `sglang-kernel 0.4.6.post1+cu130`, `sgl-deep-gemm 0.1.5.post3`, `apache-tvm-ffi 0.1.11` - source-matched FlashInfer JIT in both arms; the released image AOT package is removed equally. Candidate phases route all four TP ranks through Cake; baseline phases route none ### Accuracy and model behavior Both arm orders run the full 1,319-row GSM8K file with five fixed exemplars, so 1,314 answers are scored, plus decode/prefill cache-hit KL and prefix-cache branching: | Job / order | FlashInfer | Cake | Paired delta | FlashInfer KL | Cake KL | |---|---:|---:|---:|---|---| | `516222`, baseline → Cake | 1256/1314 (0.955860) | 1248/1314 (0.949772) | -8 / -0.608828 pp | 0.00136385 / 0.00157485 | 0.00134804 / 0.00159145 | | `516345`, Cake → baseline | 1249/1314 (0.950533) | 1248/1314 (0.949772) | -1 / -0.076104 pp | 0.00078810 / 0.00255420 | 0.00073162 / 0.00252816 | All four tests pass in every arm, all scores exceed the fixed `0.93` gate, and every KL value is below `0.0035`. Cake's exact score reproduces across node and order, but exact no-drop is false. The baseline itself varies by seven answers, so the first paired eight-answer delta cannot be assigned wholly to Cake. ### Uninstrumented E2E A/B Job `516223` uses baseline/Cake/Cake/baseline order, counterbalanced workload order, eight rounds per arm/workload, and 20,000 deterministic round-bootstrap resamples. Every request completes. | Workload | Metric | FlashInfer | Cake | Speedup (95% CI) | Decision | |---|---|---:|---:|---:|---| | 128 prompts, 512 in / 256 out, c=8 | output throughput | 1231.754012 tok/s | 1237.596662 tok/s | 1.004743x [0.998292, 1.020776] | indistinguishable | | | mean E2E latency | 839.608126 ms | 832.389779 ms | 1.008672x [0.999705, 1.020929] | indistinguishable | | | mean TPOT | 6.216159 ms | 6.113625 ms | 1.016771x [1.001588, 1.026764] | speedup | | 64 prompts, 128 in / 1024 out, c=8 | output throughput | 1403.321505 tok/s | 1412.172752 tok/s | 1.006307x [0.994657, 1.042125] | indistinguishable | | | mean E2E latency | 2834.498442 ms | 2840.753832 ms | 0.997798x [0.986704, 1.034864] | indistinguishable | | | mean TPOT | 5.561249 ms | 5.532944 ms | 1.005116x [0.993362, 1.016897] | indistinguishable | Dynamic B2/B3/B5 coverage removes the former statistically resolved decode-heavy throughput regression. Balanced mean TPOT has a resolved gain, and both aggregate-throughput point estimates are positive, but both throughput confidence intervals cross 1.0. Therefore this head passes the fixed model correctness gates but does not establish exact GSM8K no-drop or a general statistically resolved E2E throughput speedup. ## Dependencies - FlashInfer: https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/4581 Supersedes #35328 because repository rules prohibit force-pushing its protected head branch after rebase. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32381879935](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32381879935)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32381879713](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32381879713)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32381880059](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32381880059)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->
