signal.title: test: switch the Inkling-Small NVFP4 deterministic suite to DSPARK
signal.text: ## Motivation Roadmap item under #34899 — bit-exact correctness coverage for the unified radix cache, speculative-decoding row (DSpark / DFlash). `TestUnifiedHybridMTPBitExact` in `test_unified_radix_cache_kl_hybrid_bitexact.py` was added to cover the spec side of the sconv/mamba checkpoint save. It cannot reach it: `_is_mamba_track_enabled()` is a method of `PrefillCudaGraphRunner`, and EAGLE targets disable the prefill CUDA graph outright (`cuda_graph_setup.py`, #28386), so the runner is never constructed. Measured — reverting #34043 leaves that class green: ``` TestUnifiedHybridMTPBitExact, #34043 reverted → 2 passed, avg_kl_div=0.0 log: "Disable prefill CUDA graph for EAGLE target on tc_piecewise (#28386)" ``` DSPARK and DFlash are not `is_eagle()`, keep the prefill graph, and are the algorithms #34043 actually fixed (that PR measured a DFlash SWEBench subset going 55% → 35% from zeroed sconv state). ## Modifications `TestInklingSmallNvfp4Deterministic` now runs with DSPARK driving decode, and is renamed `TestInklingSmallNvfp4DsparkDeterministic`. The helpers, the 1e-9 floor, the `extra_buffer` / SWA / mamba-ratio / `KL_MAX_NEW_TOKENS` setup and the dedicated server are all unchanged. Three knobs move: `--mem-fraction-static` 0.85 → 0.80 for this class only (see below), the file's `est_time` 1700 → 2000 for the draft load and graph capture, and `min_cache_hit_ratio` 0.99 → 0.90 on the decode case (see *Why the hit-ratio bar moves*). This replaces rather than adds: the DSPARK config exercises the same NVFP4 weights and the same `flashinfer_trtllm` fp4 GEMM/MoE path, so the FP4-regression coverage the class was written for is retained, and the non-spec cache-restore logic is covered on the shrunken checkpoint in `test_unified_radix_cache_kl_hybrid_bitexact.py`. A second no-spec arm here would cost another server launch on a `4-gpu-b200` slot for coverage that is not unique. The trade that buys: a reading here is no longer self-attributing. Inkling-Small is a 256-expert MoE where dropping `--enable-deterministic-inference` alone reads 5.0e-02 — the same order as the bug signal below — so a red case needs a manual re-run without the speculative flags to separate a state-reuse bug from batch variance. That is written into the class docstring. ## Accuracy Tests Revert-then-red against #34043. First measured on the **bf16** `Inkling-Small` checkpoint at tp=4 on GB300 (same server args plus `--speculative-algorithm DSPARK`, minus the fp4 flags): | | fix in place | #34043 reverted | |---|---|---| | `..._logprobs_match` | 0.0 | 0.0 | | **`..._prefill_cache_hit`** | 0.0 | **8.05e-02** | | `..._decode_cache_hit` | 0.0 | 0.0 | | no-spec arm (all three) | 0.0 | 0.0 | Eight orders of magnitude above the floor, and the failure lands where the mechanism predicts — the corruption reaches a request that *restores* a prefix, so the flush-both comparison and the decode-side reuse stay clean. The no-spec arm staying green under the same revert is what identified the reading as speculative-state-specific. Sanity of that run: `speculative_algorithm='DSPARK'`, accept len 1.7–3.5, `cuda graph: True`, and `cuda_graph_config.prefill.backend` resolves to `full`, so the class reaches the line #34043 changed. Probe sensitivity with `--enable-deterministic-inference` dropped: 5.0e-02 / 4.3e-02 / 5.9e-03. Since re-measured on this file's own config — NVFP4 `Inkling-Small` at tp=4 on 4x GB300 (SM100, same `modelopt_fp4` / `flashinfer_trtllm` path the class already used; there is precedent for that pairing in `test/registered/gb300/test_glm52_nvfp4.py`): | | fix in place | #34043 reverted | |---|---|---| | `..._logprobs_match` | 0.0 | 0.0 | | **`..._prefill_cache_hit`** | 0.0 | **1.10e-01** | | **`..._decode_cache_hit`** | 0.0 | **`Too few decode cache hits: 31/32`** | ``` fix in place : 3 passed (650.79s) #34043 revert: 2 failed, 1 passed ``` So both open questions are closed: the bf16 DSPARK draft does pair with the `modelopt_fp4` target, and the exact-0 baseline holds on NVFP4. The signal is stronger here than on bf16 — the revert also drops one prompt out of the decode-cache reuse. Note that at the 0.90 bar this PR ships, that second symptom no longer trips the assertion; the 1.10e-01 on `prefill_cache_hit` is what detects the revert. Whole file on 4x GB300: 5 passed in 1093 s. **`--mem-fraction-static` is 0.80 for this class, not the 0.85 the others use.** The first CI run OOMed mid-test on B200: the draft weights and the speculative CUDA graphs (`974.89 MiB allocated in private pools`) left `avail mem=0.40 GB` at 0.85 on a 178 GB card. The GB300 verification could not have caught this — 284 GB per GPU is 60% more headroom. At 0.80 the KV pool still reports ~6.2M tokens against the ~130k this file uses, so the slack costs nothing. ## Why the hit-ratio bar moves The class inherited `min_cache_hit_ratio=0.99` from the non-speculative version, where every prompt reuses its decode region unconditionally. Under DSPARK it fails on B200 for roughly one prompt in 32 (`Too few decode cache hits: 31/32`), reproducibly, and passes 32/32 on GB300. That is not a test artifact. The last verify step commits a whole accepted chunk, so a request overshoots `max_new_tokens` by up to `chain_len - 1` — measured 0–7 for DSPARK `block_size=7`. Those tokens are in the KV pool and in the radix insert but truncated from the `output_ids` the client receives, so a follow-up turn diverges from the cached sequence at `prompt + returned`. With `extra_buffer`, the insert carries exactly one mamba checkpoint, at `floor(committed / interval) * interval`. When that lands past the divergence point the matched prefix has no checkpoint at all and the whole decode region is unreusable: ``` prompt=3964 committed=1029 insert_len=4992 reachable=4988 -> miss, 10/10 reps Decode cache miss for prompt 1 | cached=3840 prompt_len=3964 ``` `3840 == floor(3964 / 128) * 128` — the second turn matched a page-aligned prefix of the prompt and none of the 1024 generated tokens. The two misses seen in earlier CI runs on this PR fit the same arithmetic (2302 → 3328 > 3326; 3071 → 4096 > 4095). Without speculation `committed == returned`, the gap is empty, and 260 sampled requests showed no deficit. So it is a reuse-efficiency defect in the product, not a correctness one — KL over the prompts that do hit reads exactly 0 in every run measured, including the ones that miss. Loosening the bar keeps the exactness check running; the bar goes back to 0.99 when the insert stops storing tokens the client never received. Filed separately rather than fixed here, so this PR stays test-only. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Test-only. On 4x GB300 the class runs 650.79 s and the whole file 1093 s; spec roughly doubles this class against the no-spec arm it replaces (360 s → 685 s on the bf16 checkpoint at the same tp). `est_time` 2000 is an estimate for B200 pending a real CI number, which `scripts/ci/update_est_time.py` will correct. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32355177021](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32355177021)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32355176714](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32355176714)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32355176809](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32355176809)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [diffusion] Guard unsupported quantized component checkpoints
signal.text: ## Summary - add one fail-closed admission boundary for native auxiliary component loaders that only materialize plain state dicts - reject detected top-level, nested text-config, and compressed-tensors quantization metadata before model construction or large weight reads - apply the boundary to connectors/duration heads, bridges, diffusion decoders, sound tokenizers, spatial upsamplers, and vocoders - keep the local PE model on its Transformers `from_pretrained` path, where compatible quantization formats remain model-specific - use one documentation contract across the overview, CLI, compatibility matrix, and quantization guide ## Motivation #35184 makes independent component repository routing generic and safely routes supported quantized VAEs. The remaining raw-state native loaders still had no common quantization admission rule, so a quantized component repo could be interpreted as a dense module or fail only after allocating/loading weights. Path routing and quantized materialization are separate capabilities. This PR does not add a generic per-component quantization knob: such a knob would overstate support until each loader has a matching backend. Existing transformer, native encoder, VAE, PE/Transformers, and upstream AutoModel quantization paths remain unchanged. ## Validation - all pre-commit hooks pass - focused unit coverage added for metadata layouts and early rejection order - runtime tests left to CI <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #32365499195](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32365499195)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32365498737](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32365498737)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #32365498954](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32365498954)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [Feature] Bit-exact correctness coverage for Unified Radix Cache
signal.text: ## Motivation Cache correctness is difficult to verify from model output alone. A corrupted KV block or recurrent-state checkpoint can still produce fluent text, and the resulting numerical drift can remain far below the tolerance used by accuracy and KL tests. These failures have shipped because the existing signals are approximate. Bit-exact logprob consistency turns one of these approximate signals into a correctness oracle. `kl_test_utils` evaluates the same token through prefill and decode. If both paths are batch-invariant and compute the same function, they must produce identical logprobs. Once that baseline is established, the contract for every cache-reuse path becomes: > **Any nonzero KL is a KV/state reuse bug.** This is stronger than threshold-based testing. It does not ask whether the error is large enough to matter to a benchmark. It asks whether restoring cached state is exactly equivalent to recomputing it. Bugs that previously sat below a model-specific noise floor become unambiguous regressions. Examples: - Incorrect reused state: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/34043, https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/34184, https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/29792 ## Foundation Bit-exactness depends on the model and execution path. Deterministic inference can remove batch-dependent kernel and communication behavior, but it cannot make two mathematically different algorithms identical. For example, Qwen3-Next uses different GDN kernels for prefill and decode, and retains a nonzero numerical floor. Inkling provides the combination needed for continuous gating. Its prefill and decode paths compute the same function, so under deterministic inference its prefill-versus-decode KL is exactly `0`. A shrunken checkpoint runs on one GPU. The model also contains `FULL`, `SWA`, and `MAMBA` cache components, so one test process exercises full KV, sliding-window, and recurrent-state reuse together. The resulting foundation has four layers: 1. deterministic execution makes repeated computation batch-invariant; 2. logprob consistency establishes an exact prefill/decode baseline; 3. cache tests apply that baseline to each state restoration path; 4. revert-then-red validation proves that each regression guard can detect the defect it claims to cover. Supporting work: - Inkling deterministic execution: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/33417, https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/34159 - Workflow tools: [KL consistency test skill](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/tree/main/.claude/skills/kl-consistency-test), https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/34169 - Real-weight consistency coverage: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/34168, https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/34356 - Per-commit guards: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/34607 - Calibration and follow-up validation: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/34405, https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/34653 ## Roadmap The remaining work is coverage, not a new testing method. Every feature that can save, move, or restore model state introduces a distinct correctness boundary and needs its own exact-KL test class. - [x] Base cache path - [x] Mamba `extra_buffer` - [x] Mamba `extra_buffer_lazy` - [x] HiCache multi-turn - [x] Speculative decoding - [x] MTP https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/35161 - [x] DSpark / DFlash @alphabetc1 - Support return_logprob https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/35058 - https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/35293 - [ ] Unified memory

signal.title: [NPU][Tracking] Ascend A5 MXFP8/MXFP4 Capability and Model Coverage
signal.text: ## Background The community-wide Quantization 2026 H2 Roadmap (#31783) already covers the common quantization framework, weight lifecycle, capability validation, and related infrastructure. The Ascend cross-generation adaptation architecture is defined separately in #35709: > **Standalone kernel/provider differences belong to `sgl-kernel-npu`; runtime-visible dtype/layout/metadata differences belong to SGLang `DeviceOperator`.** Therefore, this issue does not introduce another quantization or device-abstraction framework. It focuses on: > **Ascend A5 MXFP8/MXFP4 model/operator coverage and applying the cross-generation adaptation model from #35709 to MXFP-specific differences.** --- ## 1. Scope This issue mainly tracks the following A5 MXFP schemes: | Scheme | Target | | ---------- | ----------- | | MXFP8 W8A8 | Dense / MoE | | MXFP4 W4A8 | Dense / MoE | | MXFP4 W4A4 | Dense / MoE | Primary model coverage: * Qwen3 Dense / MoE * Qwen3.5 Dense / MoE * Future models should preferably reuse existing Scheme / Kernel implementations instead of introducing model-specific MXFP paths. --- ## 2. A5 MXFP Capability Matrix | Model / Layer | MXFP8 W8A8 | MXFP4 W4A8 | MXFP4 W4A4 | | ----------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------ | | **Qwen3 Dense** | ✅ Merged [#22352](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/22352) | ✅ Merged [#23650](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/23650) | ✅ Merged [#23795](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/23795) | | **Qwen3 MoE** | ✅ Merged [#30768](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/30768) | ✅ Merged [#30318](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/30318) | ✅ Merged [#30319](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/30319) | | **Qwen3.5 Dense** | 🚧 Validation [#32150](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/32150) / Offline fix [#32266](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/32266) | 🚧 Validation [#32150](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/32150) | 🚧 Validation [#32150](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/32150) | | **Qwen3.5 MoE** | 🚧 Online supported / Offline WIP [#30768](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/30768) [#32266](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/32266) | 🚧 WIP [#32601](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/32601) | 🚧 WIP [#32602](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/32602) | The Qwen3.5 dense validation PR remains open, while the offline W8A8 fix and MoE W4A8/W4A4 work are still draft/WIP. Suggested status labels: * Production * Experimental * WIP * Planned * Unsupported A merged implementation does not automatically imply production readiness. Final status should consider correctness, accuracy, performance, representative TP/EP scenarios, CI coverage, and known limitations. ### Supporting PRs | Area | PR | | --------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | MXFP8 Dense online/offline kernel reuse | [#28505](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/28505) | | ModelSlim MXFP4 packed-weight loading | [#32013](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/32013) | | Qwen3.5 A5 GemmaRMSNorm support | [#32745](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/32745) | | Portable GemmaRMSNorm API | [sgl-kernel-npu #638](https://github.com/sgl-project/sgl-kernel-npu/pull/638) | | Generic target-provider staging | [sgl-kernel-npu #734](https://github.com/sgl-project/sgl-kernel-npu/pull/734) | | Cross-generation adaptation RFC | [#35709](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/35709) | --- ## 3. MXFP Integration with Cross-Generation Device Adaptation The common quantization architecture continues to follow #31783: ```text Config → Method → Scheme → Kernel ``` #35709 defines an orthogonal device-adaptation boundary. It does **not** add another mandatory layer to every quantization path. For MXFP, generation-specific differences should be classified as follows: ```text MXFP generation difference │ ▼ Can it be hidden behind a stable standalone operator contract? │ ┌────┴────┐ │ Yes │ No ▼ ▼ sgl-kernel-npu Runtime-visible dtype/layout/ Stable Operator metadata/state difference? │ ▼ SGLang DeviceOperator ``` ### 3.1 Kernel-local differences Differences that are local to one operator should preferably be hidden by `sgl-kernel-npu`, including: * provider differences across Ascend targets; * operator-local scale/layout normalization; * local reshape/cast/preprocessing; * equivalent operator implementations with the same logical I/O contract. `sgl-kernel-npu #638` provides the first reference implementation, while #734 generalizes it into target-specific provider staging: ```text Stable Operator API │ ┌────┴─────┐ ▼ ▼ Ascend910 Ascend950 provider provider ``` The build system selects the provider; SGLang does not perform runtime provider dispatch. ### 3.2 Runtime-visible differences If an MXFP representation is visible across multiple runtime components, it should follow SGLang `DeviceOperator` from #35709. Examples may include: * scale/layout shared across multiple MoE stages; * generation-specific metadata consumed by multiple operators; * tensor representation that affects runtime buffer preparation; * operator contracts that cannot be normalized inside one standalone kernel. In these cases: ```text Quant Scheme │ ▼ SGLang DeviceOperator runtime contract │ ▼ Stable Operator API │ ▼ sgl-kernel-npu ``` `DeviceOperator` remains optional and should only appear where a runtime-visible generation contract actually exists. ### 3.3 Quantization policy remains in the quantization layer The following decisions remain in Config / Method / Scheme rather than `DeviceOperator`: * whether MXFP8/MXFP4 is enabled; * W8A8 / W4A8 / W4A4 scheme selection; * online vs offline quantization; * supported layer/model validation. `DeviceOperator` adapts **how** an already-selected quantization feature runs on the current generation; it does not decide **whether** to enable that feature. --- ## 4. H2 Work Items ### P0 — Capability Closure * [ ] Complete validation of major Qwen3 MXFP Dense / MoE paths * [ ] Complete Qwen3.5 Dense / MoE MXFP coverage * [ ] Validate major Online / ModelSlim paths * [ ] Resolve packed-weight, scale, and layout compatibility issues * [ ] Add necessary accuracy, performance, and CI coverage ### P0 — Cross-Generation Adaptation Following #35709: * [ ] Classify existing A2/A3/A5 MXFP differences by ownership * [ ] Move standalone provider/operator differences behind stable `sgl-kernel-npu` APIs * [ ] Reuse the target-provider mechanism from `sgl-kernel-npu #734` where applicable * [ ] Move only runtime-visible dtype/layout/metadata differences into SGLang `DeviceOperator` * [ ] Avoid new generation branches in Model / QuantMethod / QuantScheme code ### P1 — Follow-up Based on actual requirements and profiling results: * MXFP Attention * MXFP / INT8 Communication * Additional model coverage --- ## 5. Out of Scope This issue does not redesign: * Common Quant Framework / Weight Lifecycle → #31783 * Ascend cross-generation adaptation architecture → #35709 * Global Capability Registry → #31774 * INT8 / FP8 / FP4 KV Cache → corresponding roadmaps/issues * Unified Communication Quantization → #31783 * Future formats such as HiF4 * A new `AscendQuantOps` framework * A second quantization-specific `DeviceOperator` --- ## Success Criteria 1. Close the major A5 MXFP8/MXFP4 Dense and MoE capability gaps. 2. Allow Qwen3.5 and future models to primarily reuse existing Scheme / Kernel implementations. 3. Avoid further propagation of A2/A3/A5 differences into Model / QuantMethod / QuantScheme code. 4. Follow #35709 for all cross-generation ownership decisions. 5. Prefer `sgl-kernel-npu` stable operators for kernel-local differences. 6. Use SGLang `DeviceOperator` only for runtime-visible representation/contract differences. 7. Keep this issue as the source of truth for A5 MXFP model/format capability coverage. --- ## Related * #31783 — Quantization 2026 H2 Roadmap * **#35709 — Ascend Cross-Generation Device Adaptation** * #31774 — Capability / Compatibility Validation * #29762 — Ascend A5 MoE MXFP * #24695 — Ascend INT8 KV Cache * #29641 — Ascend FP8 KV Cache * #29913 — FP4 KV Roadmap * #20520 — Ascend TP Communication Compression * [sgl-kernel-npu #638](https://github.com/sgl-project/sgl-kernel-npu/pull/638) — Portable GemmaRMSNorm API * **[sgl-kernel-npu #734](https://github.com/sgl-project/sgl-kernel-npu/pull/734) — Generic target-specific provider staging**

signal.title: perf: cut device syncs and redundant launches from decode scheduling
signal.text: On a PD-disaggregated decode node there is a ~4ms GPU bubble between two forwards. nsys shows the scheduler thread blocked in cudaStreamSynchronize, 8-12ms each. All of those syncs sit on schedule_stream, and _apply_war_barrier fences that stream behind the in-flight forward, so anything that needs a value back on the host waits out a whole forward; the remaining host work (MLP-sync all_gather plus launch prep) then lands in the window before the next forward. Each sync point is removed in turn: 1. Preallocation (DecodePreallocQueue.pop_preallocated) - torch.tensor([...], device=...) becomes a pinned staging buffer plus a non_blocking copy. A pageable H2D goes through memcpy_and_sync in aten, i.e. cudaMemcpyAsync + cudaStreamSynchronize; the pinned copy is still ordered before the allocator kernel that reads it, so semantics are unchanged. Shared helper: pinned_int64_pair() in allocator/base.py. - Same three blocking H2D in SWATokenToKVPoolAllocator.alloc_extend_swa_tail (swa_seq_lens / swa_last_loc / mapping[...] = 0); the last one now writes a cached device scalar. - The page/state indices sent to the prefill node were read back with .cpu() at admission time. They are now registered as device tensors and read back by flush_pending_metadata() after the next forward has been launched, on a separate stream (gated on an event, pinned async D2H, record_stream). The writes stay on schedule_stream so WAR ordering is unchanged. 2. KV release on request completion free() dedups page ids with torch.unique, and free_swa() additionally reads the mapping back (unique plus a > 0 mask) to discover which pages carry SWA state. Both shapes are data-dependent, hence the sync. The caller can name the range instead: - PagedTokenToKVPoolAllocator.free_page_reps(): release by one representative token per page. - SWATokenToKVPoolAllocator.free_full_segment() / free_swa_segment() / free_swa_page_reps(): the mapping preserves a token's offset within its page (both pools advance on the same seq_lens), so one token every page_size positions from a page-aligned start hits each SWA page exactly once. - SWAChunkCache.cache_finished_req releases the two pools separately: the full pool from cache_protected_len, the SWA pool only from swa_evicted_seqlen, since window eviction already released what came before. _release_overallocated_kv_indices and the window eviction in free_swa_out_of_window_slots go through the same segment API. Composite allocators keep falling back to free(): radix cache nodes are not guaranteed to still be SWA-mapped, so the positional derivation does not hold for them. The aliased-pool allocator (PureSWATokenToKVPoolAllocator, where full_attn_allocator IS swa_attn_allocator) also falls back, otherwise the split release would free the same slots twice. 3. Batched window eviction (maybe_evict_swa) Calling the release per request put O(batch_size) calls on the scheduler thread right before the launch, ~90us each. The whole batch's out-of-window ranges are now gathered in one indexed read. That single call is then made sync-free by gathering one token per page (step=page_size) and releasing through free_swa_page_reps(), so eviction costs one op and no sync. 4. NVTX NVTX ranges for the scheduler's hot regions, and real NVTX step spans for ModelRunner.forward and the multi-layer draft-extend replay path (previously only torch record_function, invisible in nsys). 5. C128 state reset on admission (clear_c128_req_state) With the syncs gone, this region was still bimodal: 0.05ms without an admission, 5-8ms with one. The cost had become launch count -- one fill_ plus one zero_ per C128 pool, ~40 launches per admitted request, and a kernel launch on this ARM host is ~17us. The written constants are fixed, so the first call bakes a template and every later call issues a single _foreach_copy_ over contiguous slices: 40 kernels collapse to 1. The template is built with the same ops as the old path, so the bytes written are bitwise identical even where -inf saturates in the pool dtype. Both C128 layouts are covered; mismatched pool shape/dtype/ring_size falls back to the per-pool loop. Measured on a 4-rank decode node (per-rank per-iteration means): - cudaStreamSynchronize in pop_preallocated: 263 calls / 2518ms -> 0 - prebuilt batch assembly: 1.16 -> 0.22 ms/iter, p90 6.68 -> 1.64ms - get_next_batch_to_run: 10.74 -> 8.31 ms/iter - iteration rate: 35.1 -> 39.3 iter/s per rank (+13%) - clear_c128_req_state microbenchmark: 40 -> 1 kernels, 0.721 -> 0.078 ms - batched sync-free eviction removed 901 syncs / 2761ms per 14.2s window, 85% of the time spent in the eviction region Page conservation for the positional release was validated with SGLANG_DEBUG_MEMORY_POOL=1 over ~10k decode steps (its assertions are host-visible syncs, so that flag must not be mixed into a perf run), plus equivalence tests against the unique-based path for the strided gather and for free_swa_page_reps. The batched out-of-window free in maybe_evict_swa originates from an internal patch by a teammate; a Co-authored-by trailer will be added before merge. <!-- Thank you for your contribution! signal.title: Enable num_splits > 1 for FA3 deterministic inference
signal.text: ## Summary SGLang's deterministic inference mode currently forces `num_splits=1` for FA3, which limits prefill throughput. With the `batch_invariant` scheduling fix in flash-attention (sgl-project/sgl-flash-attn#43), we can safely use `num_splits > 1` while maintaining bit-exact determinism. This PR sets `num_splits=4` for FA3 deterministic mode, improving prefill throughput by up to **2.1x** on prefill-bound workloads. ## Benchmark Results (Qwen3-8B, H200, `--attention-backend fa3 --decode-attention-backend flashinfer --enable-deterministic-inference`) | Workload | num_splits=1 | num_splits=4 | Speedup | |----------|-------------|-------------|---------| | **Short prefill** (512 in, 128 out) | | | | | Total throughput (tok/s) | 8,614 | 18,101 | **2.10x** | | Mean TTFT (ms) | 482 | 1,432 | 0.34x | | Mean E2E (ms) | 8,970 | 3,986 | **2.25x** | | Mean ITL (ms) | 131 | 40 | **3.3x** | | P99 ITL (ms) | 5,875 | 704 | **8.3x** | | **Medium prefill** (2048 in, 256 out) | | | | | Total throughput (tok/s) | 18,533 | 23,371 | **1.26x** | | Mean TTFT (ms) | 2,628 | 2,688 | 0.98x | | Mean E2E (ms) | 10,409 | 8,073 | **1.29x** | | Mean ITL (ms) | 62 | 34 | **1.8x** | | P99 ITL (ms) | 4,397 | 2,068 | **2.1x** | | **Long prefill** (4096 in, 512 out) | | | | | Total throughput (tok/s) | 16,601 | 18,073 | **1.09x** | | Mean TTFT (ms) | 2,850 | 1,887 | **1.51x** | | Mean E2E (ms) | 9,233 | 8,910 | **1.04x** | > **TTFT vs ITL tradeoff on short prefill:** With `num_splits=1` at `request-rate=inf`, prefills run serially — early requests get fast TTFT (482ms) but cause massive decode stalls (P99 ITL 5.9s). With `num_splits=4`, prefills complete faster in aggregate, so decode runs smoothly (P99 ITL 704ms, 8x better), but individual TTFT is higher because more prefills are batched concurrently. E2E latency and throughput are the meaningful comparisons. At realistic request rates this TTFT difference disappears. ## Changes - **`flashattention_backend.py`**: Set `num_splits=4` for FA3 deterministic mode, pass `batch_invariant=True` - **`flash_attention.py`**, **`flash_attention_v3.py`**: Thread `batch_invariant` param through FA3 call chain - **sgl-kernel**: Add `batch_invariant` to fwd op schema, Python wrapper, C++ header - **sgl-kernel/tests**: Add `test_flash_attn_deterministic_num_splits` (128 test cases, all passing) ## Deterministic validation All three sglang deterministic test modes pass with `num_splits=4`: - `test_deterministic --test-mode single` (15 trials, batch 1-15): **PASS** (1 unique output) - `test_deterministic --test-mode prefix` (4 prefix lengths, logprobs): **PASS** (all identical) - `test_deterministic --test-mode radix_cache`: **PASS** (cached == uncached) ## Reproduce benchmark results **1. Launch server (num_splits=4, this PR):** ```bash python3 -m sglang.launch_server \ --model Qwen/Qwen3-8B \ --trust-remote-code \ --attention-backend fa3 \ --decode-attention-backend flashinfer \ --enable-deterministic-inference \ --cuda-graph-max-bs 32 \ --port 30000 ``` **2. Run benchmarks (in a separate terminal):** ```bash # Short prefill (512 input, 128 output) python3 -m sglang.bench_serving \ --backend sglang --port 30000 \ --dataset-name random \ --random-input-len 512 --random-output-len 128 \ --num-prompts 300 --request-rate inf # Medium prefill (2048 input, 256 output) python3 -m sglang.bench_serving \ --backend sglang --port 30000 \ --dataset-name random \ --random-input-len 2048 --random-output-len 256 \ --num-prompts 200 --request-rate inf # Long prefill (4096 input, 512 output) python3 -m sglang.bench_serving \ --backend sglang --port 30000 \ --dataset-name random \ --random-input-len 4096 --random-output-len 512 \ --num-prompts 100 --request-rate inf ``` **3. For num_splits=1 baseline**, temporarily change `flashattention_backend.py` line 210 from `self.num_splits = 4` to `self.num_splits = 1`, restart server, and re-run the same benchmarks. ## Reproduce deterministic tests ```bash python3 -m sglang.launch_server \ --model Qwen/Qwen3-8B \ --trust-remote-code \ --attention-backend fa3 \ --decode-attention-backend flashinfer \ --enable-deterministic-inference \ --cuda-graph-max-bs 32 \ --port 30000 # In a separate terminal: python3 -m sglang.test.test_deterministic \ --host 0.0.0.0 --port 30000 --test-mode single --n-start 10 --n-trials 15 python3 -m sglang.test.test_deterministic \ --host 0.0.0.0 --port 30000 --test-mode prefix --n-start 10 --n-trials 10 --return-logprob python3 -m sglang.test.test_deterministic \ --host 0.0.0.0 --port 30000 --test-mode radix_cache ``` ## Dependencies Requires: sgl-project/sgl-flash-attn#43 (`batch_invariant` flag) ## Test plan - [x] 128/128 kernel-level batch invariance tests pass (sgl-kernel) - [x] All 3 sglang deterministic test modes pass - [ ] CI passes <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #28138299519](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/28138299519)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #28138299333](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/28138299333)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [Model] Boogu-Image: reference-image edit (TI2I / I2I) pipeline
signal.text:
> **Stacked on #33182** (its base branch), so the diff below still contains #33182's > commits. Reviewable delta = `git diff feat/boogu-image...` → 9 files, +784/−15. > Will rebase and drop the duplicates once #33182 lands. ## Motivation #33182 added the text-to-image `BooguImagePipeline`. The same Boogu-Image checkpoint also serves **reference-image editing** (TI2I / I2I). This PR extends that one pipeline to serve both: a single pipeline + config (`task_type=TI2I`) handles text-only and reference-conditioned requests, matching the one-pipeline house pattern (`GlmImage`, `Flux2`). With no reference image it degrades to the existing T2I behavior, so base T2I output is unchanged. ## Modifications The edit path reuses the DiT, VAE, Qwen3-VL encoder, and scheduler unchanged. A reference image is routed to **both** the Qwen3-VL encoder (image-aware instruction embeddings) and the VAE (reference latents threaded through the DiT via `ref_image_hidden_states`). With no reference image the pipeline degrades to T2I. - `configs/pipeline_configs/boogu_image.py` — `BooguImagePipelineConfig` gains `task_type=TI2I` and `BooguImageCFGPolicy`: dual text+image CFG (1/2/3 branches), collapsing to standard CFG `c + (s-1)(c-u)` when there is no reference. - `configs/sample/boogu_image.py` — adds `guidance_scale_2` (image guidance, default `1.0` = off, so a text-only request runs exactly two CFG branches). - `runtime/pipelines/boogu_image_pipeline.py` — builds the reference-aware `BooguImageEncodingStage`, so the single pipeline serves both paths; no `--pipeline-class-name` and no separate edit pipeline. - `.../stages/model_specific_stages/boogu_image.py` — dual-resolution reference preprocessing (384 px VLM copy, 2048 px VAE copy), VAE-encode `(sample - shift) * scale`, TI2I system prompt with image-before-text ordering; falls back to the plain T2I encode when no reference is present. - `.../stages/model_specific_stages/boogu_image_processor.py` — native port of the reference downscale-only, alignment-aware preprocessing (drops the external `boogu` dep). - `runtime/warmup_request_builder.py` — opts out of the synthetic warmup image so the server warms at the real 1024×1024, following the `GlmImagePipelineConfig` precedent. - `runtime/pipelines_core/schedule_batch.py` — additive `ref_image_hidden_states` field. Boogu's `head_dim` is 120, which is not an FA-supported size, so q/k/v are zero-padded to 128 and the output sliced back. The softmax scale stays `head_dim**-0.5` = 1/sqrt(120): zero columns leave `q·k` unchanged, so the padded dim must not enter the temperature. It is passed explicitly because `Attention.__init__` defaults to `head_size**-0.5`, and `head_size` there is the padded 128. (This lives in the base T2I DiT from #33182; it is not part of this PR's diff.) ## Accuracy Tests CPU-only unit tests: `test_boogu_image.py` **14 passed**. They pin the dual-CFG branch construction and combine formula, the T2I-unchanged path (reference-free build → 2 branches, combine → `c + (s-1)(c-u)`), `task_type=TI2I`, VAE-encode shift-then-scale order, `guidance_scale_2` defaulting off, and image-before-text message building. Same weights and conditioning across all three stacks: 1024×1024, 50 steps, seed 42, text guidance 4.0, image guidance 1.0, empty negative prompt, bf16. Reference input for the edit row (`input_image_examples/03.jpg`): | | diffusers (reference) | vllm-omni | sglang (this PR) | |---|---|---|---| | **TI2I** edit
`把背景替换到沙滩.` | | | | | **T2I** base
*(decoupling check)* | | | | sglang's edit output reproduces the reference sample at **36.8 dB** vs diffusers; the residual is bf16 / kernel drift, and `torch.compile` does not change it. Base T2I is unaffected — **34.7 dB** vs diffusers, and folding the edit path into the shared pipeline left the T2I output identical to the pre-merge run (**42.3 dB** pairwise, within bf16 run-to-run noise). vllm-omni's edit is a *different valid sample* rather than a degraded one — lower horizon, brighter ocean — while its T2I matches, so that difference is specific to its reference-image conditioning path. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Full-pipeline wall time per image (text encode + 50 steps + VAE decode), 1024×1024, concurrency 1, warmup excluded, H20. All four sglang arms are from the single merged build. | | diffusers | vllm-omni
eager | vllm-omni
compile | sglang
eager | sglang
compile | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | **TI2I** edit | 159.84 s | 136.76 s | 130.71 s | 143.97 s | **124.81 s (1.28×)** | | **T2I** base | 68.21 s | 61.03 s | 58.10 s | 64.67 s | **54.77 s (1.25×)** | sglang compile is fastest on both paths; eager-vs-eager it trails vllm-omni by ~5 %, because compile buys sglang −13.3 %/−15.3 % vs vllm-omni's −4.4 %/−4.8 % (vllm-omni's `_repeated_blocks` excludes its double-stream and refiner layers). Head-dim padding is what makes FA usable here, and it is worth **−12.6 %** on TI2I (SDPA 164.76 s → padded FA 144.02 s) and **−7.4 %** on T2I (69.84 s → 64.67 s), eager. Nearly all the time is the denoise loop — TI2I e2e 143.97 s against a 143.39 s denoise sum, so the edit path's extra VAE encode + image-fused VLM forward is ~0.6 s. **Caveats:** every GPU on this host carries a foreign tenant at ~79–81 % utilization, so absolute seconds are contended. diffusers and sglang ran on the same card (ratios are apples-to-apples); vllm-omni ran on a second card, so its column is cross-card. The T2I image cell and the T2I latency come from different runs, because vllm-omni's timed T2I arm uses `dataset: random`, which substitutes its own prompt and injects a synthetic negative prompt. ## Checklist - [x] Format code with pre-commit - [x] Add unit tests - [ ] Update documentation (compatibility matrix — add the edit pipeline row) - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results - [x] Follow the SGLang code style guidance AI assistance (Claude Code) was used for implementation and benchmarking; every line reviewed, and all numbers above are from real runs on the hardware described. --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): :x: **Missing `run-ci` label** -- add it to run CI tests. signal.title: [RFC][NPU] Ascend Cross-Generation Device Adaptation
signal.text: ## Summary As Ascend A5 support is being added to SGLang, generation differences are no longer limited to kernel availability. They increasingly affect operator providers, signatures, tensor dtypes/layouts, KV representations, and quantization metadata. If these differences continue to be handled directly in Attention, MoE, Quantization, Model, and Memory components: ```python if is_a5(): ... else: ... ``` generation-specific logic will keep leaking into feature code. This RFC proposes a two-layer adaptation model: ```text Model / Attention / MoE / Quant / Memory │ ▼ SGLang DeviceOperator runtime-visible device contract │ ▼ sgl-kernel-npu Stable Operator │ ▼ target-specific provider Ascend910 / Ascend950 │ ▼ torch_npu / ACLNN / AscendC / Triton ``` The core rule is: > Hardware differences that can be fully hidden behind a stable standalone operator contract should be handled in `sgl-kernel-npu`. Differences that change SGLang runtime-visible dtype, layout, metadata, or cross-operator state should be handled by SGLang `DeviceOperator`. --- ## Motivation Current A5 support already exposes two fundamentally different kinds of generation differences. ### Kernel-local differences For example, Gemma RMSNorm uses different implementations across generations: ```text A2/A3: torch_npu.npu_gemma_rms_norm A5: torch_npu.npu_rms_norm(input, 1 + weight) ``` However, both can expose the same semantic API: ```python npu_gemma_rms_norm(input, weight, eps) ``` `sgl-kernel-npu`[#638](https://github.com/sgl-project/sgl-kernel-npu/pull/638) demonstrates this model: provider selection happens while building a target-specific wheel, while SGLang only consumes a stable operator API and does not select providers at runtime. ### Runtime-visible differences Other generation differences cannot be hidden inside a standalone operator. For example, an A5 KV/attention path may change: ```text INT8 KV -> FP8 KV scale format -> different metadata representation KV layout -> packed representation attention API -> different operator contract ``` These differences affect Memory Pool, Attention, and possibly other runtime components before a kernel is invoked. Therefore, we need an explicit ownership boundary between kernel implementation differences and runtime device contract differences. --- ## Goals This RFC aims to: * reduce scattered Ascend generation checks in SGLang; * keep kernel/provider differences inside `sgl-kernel-npu` whenever possible; * centralize runtime-visible generation contracts in SGLang `DeviceOperator`; * preserve existing ownership of Attention, MoE, Memory, and Quantization components; * provide a consistent extension model for future Ascend generations; * avoid introducing a large device abstraction that wraps every NPU operator. --- ## Ownership Model The default decision rule is: ```text Generation difference │ ▼ Can it be hidden behind one stable standalone operator API? │ ┌────┴────┐ │ Yes │ No ▼ ▼ sgl-kernel Does runtime require different -npu dtype/layout/metadata/state? │ ┌────┴────┐ │ Yes │ No ▼ ▼ SGLang Feature / DeviceOp capability ``` Typical ownership: | Difference | Owner | | ------------------------------------------------------------ | ----------------------- | | torch_npu / ACLNN / AscendC / Triton provider difference | `sgl-kernel-npu` | | Same semantic operator with different kernel implementations | `sgl-kernel-npu` | | Operator-local reshape/cast | `sgl-kernel-npu` | | Runtime KV dtype/layout | SGLang `DeviceOperator` | | Runtime metadata contract | SGLang `DeviceOperator` | | Representation shared across multiple operators | SGLang `DeviceOperator` | | Enable MXFP4 / FP8 KV | Feature / Config | | KV allocation and lifetime | Memory Pool | | DSA/MLA or TP/EP policy | Feature | An operator signature difference alone does **not** require SGLang `DeviceOperator`. If the difference can be cleanly normalized behind a stable standalone API, it should remain in `sgl-kernel-npu`. --- ## sgl-kernel-npu: Stable Operator + Target Provider We do not propose another large abstraction such as: ```python class BaseDeviceOps: ... class A5DeviceOps(BaseDeviceOps): ... ``` inside `sgl-kernel-npu`. Instead, the kernel layer follows: > **Stable Operator Contract + Target-specific Provider** For example: ```text npu_gemma_rms_norm() │ ┌────────┴────────┐ ▼ ▼ Ascend910 provider Ascend950 provider native ACLNN ``` SGLang only depends on: ```python npu_gemma_rms_norm(...) ``` and does not need to know which provider is used. A stable operator should remain standalone: ```text Tensor / scalar / attributes │ ▼ Stable Operator │ ▼ Tensor / outputs ``` It should not depend on SGLang runtime objects such as: ```text ForwardBatch MemoryPool Scheduler ModelRunner AttentionBackend ``` --- ## Target-specific Provider Staging `sgl-kernel-npu` [#734](https://github.com/sgl-project/sgl-kernel-npu/pull/734) generalizes the Gemma-specific mechanism introduced in[#638](https://github.com/sgl-project/sgl-kernel-npu/pull/638) into generic target-provider staging. Its core principle is: > **The build system knows targets, but does not know operators.** Providers are organized by target and stable module path: ```text target_providers/ ├── Ascend910/ │ └── norm/ │ └── gemma_rmsnorm.py │ └── Ascend950/ └── norm/ └── gemma_rmsnorm.py ``` During wheel build: ```text target_providers/Ascend950/norm/gemma_rmsnorm.py │ ▼ sgl_kernel_npu/ norm/ gemma_rmsnorm.py ``` The installed public API therefore remains: ```python sgl_kernel_npu.norm.gemma_rmsnorm ``` regardless of the target implementation. ### Directory as Registry There is intentionally no global operator registry such as: ```python PROVIDERS = { "norm.gemma_rmsnorm": ..., "quant.dynamic_mx": ..., } ``` Instead, the directory layout itself acts as the registration mechanism. Adding another portable operator only requires matching module paths: ```text target_providers/ ├── Ascend910/ │ └── quant/dynamic_mx.py └── Ascend950/ └── quant/dynamic_mx.py ``` The generic build framework does not need to know whether the module implements Gemma RMSNorm, MXFP, MoE, or Attention. [#734](https://github.com/sgl-project/sgl-kernel-npu/pull/734) reduces provider staging to: ```text validate target ↓ scan provider tree ↓ stage provider modules ``` No operator-specific build logic is required. --- ## Build-time, Not Runtime Dispatch Provider selection should happen while building the target-specific wheel: ```text Concrete SoC │ ▼ normalize provider target │ ├── Ascend910 └── Ascend950 │ ▼ stage provider tree │ ▼ target-specific wheel ``` The runtime does not contain: ```python if is_a5(): ... ``` or: ```python provider = registry[current_device] ``` There is also no silent runtime fallback. Unknown targets, missing provider directories, and conflicts with common modules should fail during the build. This keeps provider compatibility out of the inference hot path and makes target mismatches explicit. --- ## Provider Contract A target-specific provider is appropriate when all of the following are true: ```text same semantic operation + different target implementation + same logical input/output contract ``` For example: ```text Ascend910: npu_gemma_rms_norm(input, weight, eps) Ascend950: npu_rms_norm(input, 1 + weight, eps) ``` Both expose: ```python npu_gemma_rms_norm(input, weight, eps) -> (output, rstd) ``` [#734](https://github.com/sgl-project/sgl-kernel-npu/pull/734) also enforces that target provider trees expose the same module set, keeping target differences at the implementation layer rather than the public API layer. --- ## SGLang DeviceOperator When generation differences cross the standalone operator boundary, they should be handled in SGLang. For example: ```text A3: INT8 KV FP16 scale legacy sparse-attention contract A5: FP8 packed KV different scale metadata different sparse-attention contract ``` In this case, the Memory Pool must allocate a different representation before the kernel executes. A kernel provider alone cannot hide the difference. The proposed responsibility is: ```text SGLang DeviceOperator │ ├── runtime dtype contract ├── layout contract ├── metadata contract └── semantic operator adaptation │ ▼ sgl-kernel-npu stable ops ``` `DeviceOperator` should **not** own: ```text kernel provider selection feature enable/disable KV lifetime algorithm selection ``` In short: > `DeviceOperator` defines how an already-selected feature runs on the current device generation. It does not decide whether the feature should be enabled. --- ## Representative Cases ### Gemma RMSNorm ```text different implementation same standalone semantic contract ``` → `sgl-kernel-npu` target provider [#638](https://github.com/sgl-project/sgl-kernel-npu/pull/638) + [#734](https://github.com/sgl-project/sgl-kernel-npu/pull/734)provide the reference implementation. ### MXFP scale layout If normalization is operator-local: ```text kernel output ↓ local reshape / normalization ↓ stable public representation ``` → `sgl-kernel-npu` If the representation is stored and consumed across multiple runtime components: ```text producer ↓ runtime state ↓ multiple consumers ``` → SGLang `DeviceOperator` ### KV / Sparse Attention If generation differences affect: ```text KV dtype physical KV layout scale metadata memory allocation contract ``` → SGLang `DeviceOperator` The concrete standalone kernels used by that path remain in: ```text sgl-kernel-npu ``` --- ## Rollout The two repositories can evolve independently under the same ownership model. ### sgl-kernel-npu ```text #638(https://github.com/sgl-project/sgl-kernel-npu/pull/638) Gemma stable operator ↓ #734(https://github.com/sgl-project/sgl-kernel-npu/pull/734) generic target-provider staging ↓ additional portable operators ``` After [#734](https://github.com/sgl-project/sgl-kernel-npu/pull/734), adding a new cross-generation operator only requires: 1. confirm that it has the same semantic and logical I/O contract; 2. add the same module path under the required `target_providers/<target>/` directories; 3. add contract tests. No generic build-system changes should be required. ### SGLang Introduce a minimal `DeviceOperator` and migrate only existing runtime-visible differences, such as: ```text KV representation Sparse Attention contract Indexer dtype/layout cross-operator quantization metadata ``` This RFC does not propose wrapping every NPU operator. --- ## Acceptance Criteria The intended long-term rules are: 1. SGLang feature code does not directly select kernel providers. 2. Standalone generation differences are handled in `sgl-kernel-npu` whenever possible. 3. `sgl-kernel-npu` exposes stable semantic/module contracts. 4. Target-specific providers are selected during wheel build. 5. The build framework knows targets, not individual operators. 6. Provider dispatch is kept out of the inference hot path. 7. SGLang `DeviceOperator` only handles runtime-visible device contracts. 8. Feature, Memory, and Scheduler ownership remains unchanged. 9. Neither repository introduces a God Object covering all NPU operators. --- ## Open Questions 1. Do we agree on the following default ownership rule? ```text standalone kernel/provider difference → sgl-kernel-npu runtime-visible representation/contract difference → SGLang DeviceOperator ``` 2. Which existing runtime-visible A5 difference should be the first minimal SGLang `DeviceOperator` migration to validate the abstraction? --- ## References * [sgl-kernel-npu #638 — Add portable Gemma RMSNorm API](https://github.com/sgl-project/sgl-kernel-npu/pull/638) * [sgl-kernel-npu #734 — Generalize target-specific operator provider staging](https://github.com/sgl-project/sgl-kernel-npu/pull/734) * [SGLang #32745 — Fix Qwen3.5 GemmaRMSNorm on Ascend 950](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/32745) * [SGLang #33030 — Add Ascend 950 backend paths for DeepSeek-V4](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/33030) * vLLM-Ascend `device_op.py` — prior art for runtime device adaptation

signal.title: [DSA] Route the ragged prefill top-k to the v2 kernel
signal.text: > Generated by Claude. **Stacked on #35041.** GitHub cannot use that PR's branch as a base here (its head lives in the fork, and a cross-fork PR's base must be a branch of the base repo), so this targets `main` and carries #35041's commit underneath. **Review only the second commit** (`[DSA] Route the ragged prefill top-k to the v2 kernel`); the diff collapses to it once #35041 merges and this is rebased. ## Motivation The extend-shaped `RAGGED` transform is the last DSA top-k path still served by the legacy sgl-kernel kernel (`topk_transform_prefill_ragged_kernel`), even though it is the cheapest one to serve. The DeepGEMM contiguous-KV indexer emits columns that are already absolute positions in the batch's flattened KV, so unlike the paged path there is no page table to gather through -- the entire transform is a per-row add. That is exactly v2's raw-index mode (added in #35041) plus a bias. ## What this does - **`TopKProblem` gains a `bias` field (default 0)** that `emit` adds to every selected index. Every pre-existing construction site omits it, so the compiler constant-folds the add away — see the SASS check below. - **`topk_ragged_kernel`** selects inside `[row_starts[b], row_starts[b] + seq_lens[b])` and emits `position + out_offsets[b]`. One block per row, and **no cluster path**: the cluster split exists to spread one very long row across blocks, which only pays off for the few-row decode shapes; prefill has thousands of rows. - **Unaligned window starts.** The window start is an arbitrary token offset, so the read base is rounded down to a 4-float boundary and the ≤ 3 columns that pulls in are masked to `-FLT_MAX` in place. They are a preceding request's columns *of the same row* — real finite scores that would otherwise win the selection. The row belongs to this block alone and the score buffer is dead after the top-k, so the write races with nothing. It lands after the PDL wait (the indexer rounds its own KV base down to 4 as well and would otherwise overwrite the mask) and is published by the `__syncthreads()` that every `forward()` already runs before it reads any score. - Rows with `seq_len <= topk` keep a trivial path that never reads the scores, so alignment never arises there. It cannot reuse `trivial_transform`, whose `-1` padding would pick up the bias. - `dsa_topk_backend` routes the RAGGED branch to it; prefill-CP (`batch_idx_list is not None`) stays on the legacy kernel, since its `topk_indices_offset` is built from `cu_seqlens_q` rather than the KV bases. ## The existing kernels are untouched Built the JIT module before and after and diffed the SASS per function (`cuobjdump -sass`, 12 kernels / 56648 instructions): | kernel | result | |---|---| | `topk_main_kernel` × {level 0..3} × {INDICES, PAGE_TABLE} | byte-identical | | `topk_small_batch_kernel` × {INDICES, PAGE_TABLE} | byte-identical | | `topk_plan` | byte-identical | | `topk_persistent_cluster_kernel` | same instruction count (2808); `+1 IMAD.MOV.U32 / -1 NOP` | `cuobjdump -res-usage` is identical field for field on all 12 (`REG:32 STACK LOCAL:0 SHARED CONSTANT`). The new kernel itself is `REG:32 STACK:0 SHARED:20224 LOCAL:0`, no spill. To keep it that way, the ragged bias must be set through its own construction path — assigning a runtime bias in `TopKPagedParams::problem()` would put a real `IADD` in every mode's `emit`. ## Tests `test/registered/kernels/ops/attention/test_topk_v2.py`: **278 passed** (234 existing + 44 new). The new cases cover every `row_start % 4` residue against each template band (trivial / Register2 / Register4 / Streaming), mixed lengths in one launch, the selection boundaries (`seq == k`, `k+1`, 8192/8193, 16385), long context, `row_starts=None`, and an offset distinct from `row_starts`. Everything outside a window is filled with a score that beats every in-window value, so a leak shows up as a wrong selection; each case also asserts that nothing outside the masked head was written. Also checked, unchanged from the base branch: `test_dsa_indexer.py` (same pass/fail set) and `test/registered/attention/unittests/dsa/test_dsa.py` (3 pre-existing `impl='trtllm'` hardware-gate failures, per `KNOWN_FAILURES.md §B`). And the v2 output matches the legacy kernel exactly when driven through `DSATopKBackend`, across aligned/unaligned starts and both the trivial and radix paths. ## Benchmark `bench_topk.py` gains a ragged benchmark alongside the paged one (this also un-shadows `benchmark_paged`, which a duplicate function name had replaced with a body-less stub). B200, k=2048, µs: | seq_len | batch | jit_v1 | **jit_v2** | flashinfer | torch | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | 4096 | 1 | 4.10 | **4.03** | 6.37 | 34.27 | | 4096 | 128 | 7.35 | **4.34** | 7.07 | 45.34 | | 4096 | 1024 | 24.61 | **16.52** | 28.20 | 147.51 | | 65536 | 1 | 37.52 | 20.35 | **13.15** | 71.30 | | 65536 | 128 | 39.40 | **21.52** | 37.48 | 157.22 | | 65536 | 1024 | 175.84 | **103.70** | 195.88 | 923.18 | 1.3–1.8× over the legacy kernel, except the single-row 64K shape where the cluster split flashinfer/the paged path use still wins — not a prefill shape (prefill's row count is the extend-token count). <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:no_entry_sign: [Run #32349896322](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32349896322)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #32364175881](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32364175881)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #32349896357](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32349896357)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [Scheduler] Reuse per-step cuda events uniformly (WAR read_done + copy_done)
signal.text: ## Motivation Follow-up to #31468, several paths construct a fresh cuda `Event()` every decode step: the WAR `read_done` in `DecodeCudaGraphRunner.execute()` (twice per DFlash step: draft + verify runners), the same in `EagleDraftExtendCudaGraphRunner`, and the scheduler's `copy_done` (both the overlap and non-overlap spec paths). Each costs a `cudaEventCreate` + Python object churn (~µs/step) — not a host sync, purely allocation/GC hygiene, so no throughput change is expected; a no-regression A/B is attached below. ## Modifications - New `ReusableEventRing` (`sglang/srt/utils/cuda_event_ring.py`): lazy fixed ring of re-recordable events; a slot is re-recorded only after every consumer of its previous record has waited/synchronized, so depth = max records in flight (+ margin). - `read_done` sites (decode graph runner, eagle draft-extend runner): depth **2** per runner — the WAR barrier `wait_event`s and clears `war_fastpath_read_done_event` right after `run_batch`, so at most one record is outstanding. - Scheduler `copy_done` (overlap + non-overlap spec): depth **3** — `result_queue` momentarily holds the previous result plus the just-appended one (≤2 in flight); every consumer (`batch_result_processor`, disaggregation prefill) synchronizes exactly once before a slot recurs. - **Intentionally out of scope:** the unified-memory `forward_done` event — `MultiEndedAllocator` retains and `query()`s old references, so re-recording would silently change what a retained handle reports; it needs its own lifecycle. Likewise the PP microbatch `d2h_event`s, whose lifetime is the PP async depth, not the decode pipeline. ## Test `test/registered/unit/spec/test_cuda_event_ring.py` (CI-registered): lazy fixed allocation + round-robin ordering, distinct-objects-within-depth, depth validation, and a CUDA record/wait/synchronize cycle across ring wrap-around mimicking both lifecycles. ## Benchmarks No-regression e2e posted in the comments: per-cc deltas within the harness noise band (mean +0.6%), GSM8K 0.955/0.965, AL parity. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Code Formatting with Pre-Commit](https://docs.sglang.ai/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-formatting-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests as outlined in the [Running Unit Tests](https://docs.sglang.ai/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#running-unit-tests-writing-documentation). - signal.title: [PD] Introduce runtime role switching between prefill and decode
signal.text: ## [PD] Introduce runtime prefill<->decode role switching (mori backend) ### Motivation SGLang's PD disaggregation currently **pins each instance's role (`prefill` / `decode`) at startup** with no way to change it at runtime — to re-balance the P:D ratio you must tear down and relaunch servers. This PR introduces **runtime P<->D role switching**: an operator/router can convert a prefill instance into a decode instance (or vice versa) live, without restarting the server or reloading weights. It lands as a first PoC on the **mori** transfer backend; the control plane is backend-agnostic. ### Design: in-place role flip Key enabler: **the token KV pool is role-independent** — prefill and decode allocate the same KV memory structure. Only the *role-specific* disaggregation structures differ (prefill: bootstrap queue + KV sender; decode: receiver/poll threads, bootstrap registration, role-specific queues/metadata buffers). A flip therefore does **not** reallocate the KV pool or touch model weights. It only tears down and rebuilds the small role-specific structures, then re-dispatches the scheduler event loop to the new role. Draining to idle before teardown is a correctness requirement (an in-flight decode request's KV is owned by an upstream prefill). ### API ``` POST /pd_role_switch {"new_role": "prefill" | "decode", "decode_cuda_graph_bs": [..]?} ``` Gated by `--enable-pd-role-switch` (default **off**, zero impact on existing PD). ### What's in this PR - **Control plane**: `--enable-pd-role-switch`; `PdRoleSwitchReqInput/Output`; `POST /pd_role_switch`; `handle_pd_role_switch` + teardown/rebuild in a dedicated `disaggregation/role_switch.py`; event-loop re-dispatch on flip. Hardened with an in-progress re-entrancy guard, a fail-fast "unhealthy" state on rebuild failure, and table-driven precondition checks. - **Decode CUDA graph on flip**: enable and capture the decode graph on the flip to decode; the captured batch sizes are queryable via `/get_server_info` and can be passed as `decode_cuda_graph_bs` for a size-matched capture; idempotent. - **Backend opt-in interface**: `BaseKVManager.supports_role_switch` + `teardown()`, so other transfer backends can support role switching (checked up-front in the reject path). - **mori & mooncake backends**: teardown/rebuild hooks for KV-transfer managers (worker threads poll-based so they observe the stop flag; sockets, zmq context, RDMA registrations and the IOEngine / transfer engine released). mooncake: @LLLL114 (Mooncake team). - **Radix / hicache compatibility**: release the prefix cache on flip; removes the previous `--disable-radix-cache` requirement (works with `--disaggregation-decode-enable-radix-cache`). - **Plumbing / invariants**: `disagg_service.py` (bootstrap started on role-switch instances), `tokenizer_control_mixin.py`, `model_runner_kv_cache_mixin.py` (role-agnostic pre-alloc), `invariant_checker.py` (leak check keyed on the pool, not the role). - **Unit tests** (CPU-only, mocked): `test/registered/unit/disaggregation/test_pd_role_switch.py`. ### Validation **Unit tests** — `test/registered/unit/disaggregation/test_pd_role_switch.py`: **17 passed** (control-plane contract, all reject branches, same-role no-op, successful-flip orchestration, serialization, teardown thread-leak, radix-on prefix-cache release). **E2E accuracy (original)** — DeepSeek-R1-0528-MXFP4, 1P1D on 2×MI355X, mori KV transfer, TP8 (pure-TP MoE), concurrency 128, GSM8K (1319, lm_eval flexible/strict): | stage | flexible-extract | strict-match | |-------|------------------|--------------| | baseline (P=node A, D=node B) | 0.9469 | 0.9462 | | after flip (roles swapped via /pd_role_switch) | 0.9462 | 0.9454 | | after flip back (reverted) | 0.9416 | 0.9447 | **Accuracy + performance with radix cache ON (new)** — Qwen3-32B (dense, TP=8, pure-TP), mori, 1P1D on 2×MI300X; 8k1k = random 8192/1024, 320 prompts, concurrency 32, warmup 64: | state | gsm8k | out tok/s | total tok/s | TTFT med | TPOT med | |-------|-------|-----------|-------------|----------|----------| | ① baseline | 0.840 | 2680 | 24119 | 649 ms | 10.62 ms | | ② flip | 0.850 | 2655 | 23895 | 633 ms | 10.77 ms | | ③ flip-back | 0.840 | 2641 | 23772 | 679 ms | 10.69 ms | **Leak stress (new)** — 25 round-trip cycles = **100 role switches**, run once with the radix cache OFF and once ON, metrics recorded per cycle. `flip_fails=0`; weight / kvcache / graph / GPU-free / thread-count stay flat across cycles 2–25 in both configs ⇒ no resource leak. | metric (radix OFF) | baseline | cycles 1–25 | |--------------------|----------|-------------| | kvcache / graph (GB) | 115.05 / 1.09 | constant | | gpu_free (MB) | P=53567 D=53488 | constant | | threads (lwp) | P=2127 D=2047 | constant | | metric (radix ON) | baseline | cycles 1–25 | |-------------------|----------|-------------| | kvcache / graph (GB) | 115.05 / 1.07 | constant | | gpu_free (MB) | P=50908 D=50748 | bit-for-bit constant | | threads (lwp) | P=2519 D=2224 | ±16, non-monotonic | ### Limitations / follow-ups - Only the **mori** backend's teardown/rebuild hooks are implemented; other backends opt in via `supports_role_switch` + `teardown()`. - Validated with pure-TP MoE (`--tp-size 8`, no EP / DP-attention / MoE a2a). With `--moe-a2a-backend mori`, the a2a dispatch buffer is sized per-role at startup and is not yet rebuilt on flip — a follow-up. - Flip is driven externally (operator/router); an automatic load-based flip policy is out of scope here. ### How to use ```bash # launch both instances with the flag (add --disaggregation-decode-enable-radix-cache to run with radix on) python3 -m sglang.launch_server ... --disaggregation-mode prefill --enable-pd-role-switch python3 -m sglang.launch_server ... --disaggregation-mode decode --enable-pd-role-switch # (optional) query a decode server's captured decode-graph batch sizes curl http://<decode>:8000/get_server_info # -> internal_states[].decode_cuda_graph_bs # after draining, flip (optionally pass decode_cuda_graph_bs for a size-matched capture) curl http://<inst>:8000/pd_role_switch -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{"new_role":"decode"}' ``` Co-authored-by: huanglong <huanglong@linux.alibaba.com> <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:no_entry_sign: [Run #32347885045](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32347885045)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32347884906](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32347884906)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #32347884960](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32347884960)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: feat(load-reporter): add push-based engine load reporting
signal.text:
## Motivation Load-aware routing needs one authoritative view of scheduler load across data-parallel ranks. Polling every Worker from every Router adds fan-out, creates inconsistent views, and churns connections. This PR adds the Worker-side reporter: a push channel built on the scheduler's existing snapshot publication. One shared pull per fire is broadcast to every registered Router over long-lived bidirectional gRPC streams. Router-side ingestion, discovery, retries, and the Prefill throughput extension are intentionally split into follow-up PRs so each layer can be reviewed independently. > The push channel controls *delivery*, not *snapshot age*. End-to-end > freshness stays bounded by the scheduler's snapshot publication interval; > see [Freshness](#freshness). ## Modifications ### Architecture ```mermaid flowchart LR Scheduler["Scheduler
published per-DP-rank load snapshots"] Source["Per-mode snapshot source
manager get_loads / Router SHM reader"] Fire["Single fire loop
one pull per fire + rank-set validation"] Builder["LoadReport builder
HEALTHY / STALE / UNREACHABLE"] Service["Worker gRPC service
--load-reporter-port"] Router["Routers dial in
drive Monitor streams"] Scheduler --> Source --> Fire --> Builder --> Service --> Router ``` ### Protocol and configuration - The Worker hosts `sglang.router.loadmonitor.v1.LoadMonitorService.Monitor(stream RouterFrame) returns (stream WorkerFrame)` on a fixed, opt-in `--load-reporter-port`; each external Router dials in and drives its own stream (`register` → ack → bounded first fire → periodic reports). Stable field numbers and enum values are preserved. - `RouterFrame` = `register | update_config | keep_alive | stop`, with `register` required first; `WorkerFrame` = `registered | report | error`. Re-registering the same `router_id` replaces its old session; different `router_id`s coexist. - Package `grpcio` and `protobuf` through the optional `load-reporter` extra across all supported Python wheel variants. - Reporting stays opt-in so normal SGLang installations gain no mandatory runtime dependencies. ### Reporter runtime — one timer, one pull, broadcast - A single fire-loop task owns the only timer; sessions are passive bookkeeping (deadline, lease, capacity-1 queue) and own no task or timer. - Each fire performs exactly one bounded snapshot pull (`get_loads()`, 1 s budget). The same budget covers one retry when the expected DP-rank set changes mid-pull. - One report per pull, validated and built from that attempt only: `HEALTHY`, `STALE`, or `UNREACHABLE` (empty ranks + `last_error`). There is no persistent store and no cross-report merge, so a slow or stale rank is never replaced with historical data. - The fire broadcasts the same report to every session whose deadline fired; sessions registered before the next fire share its pull for their initial report. - Each session has a capacity-1 latest-wins queue, lease TTL with keep-alive renewal, mid-stream config updates, registration-anchored deadlines, and idempotent shutdown. - Pull, transport, and shutdown failures never propagate into the inference request path. ### Freshness End-to-end snapshot freshness is bounded by the scheduler's snapshot publication path (`load_snapshot_publish_interval`), not by the gRPC delivery cadence. The report interval controls how often a report is sent, not how old the snapshot inside it is — a poll at the same cadence observes data of the same age. What the push stream adds over polling is delivery, not freshness: a negotiated per-Router cadence, connection reuse, one-pull multi-Router fan-out, leases, and bounded backpressure. ### Tokenizer integration - Single-tokenizer HTTP and native gRPC start one reporter runtime in the FastAPI lifespan (native gRPC reuses the same process and listener). - Multi-tokenizer mode: `MultiTokenizerRouter` is the sole runtime owner; HTTP workers open no streams, and elastic scale changes update the expected DP-rank set (observed by the next fire). - Standalone SMG gRPC starts the reporter at request-manager readiness; older servicers without the readiness hook fail loudly when the reporter is enabled. - The embedded offline Engine API does not own the reporter; cleanup runs in the HTTP-server lifespan, the SMG gRPC-server finally path, and `MultiTokenizerRouter.close()`. ### Tests and documentation - Unit/integration coverage (CPU, real in-process `grpc.aio`): proto contract, fire loop (shared pull deadlines, broadcast to due sessions, per-session lease gating, rank-set-change retry sharing one budget, registration-anchored cadence, stale/error reports, re-registration, shutdown), snapshot validation and report-builder contracts, snapshot sources, service handshake and error frames, composition-root lifecycle, and standalone SMG wiring. - Negative invariants: request dispatch/completion/abort never trigger a pull; topology updates never pull immediately. - Registered GPU E2E tests with a real `grpc.aio` fake Router cover single-owner, multi-owner, and standalone SMG reporting. - Documentation covers the wire contract, serving-mode matrix, fire-loop schedule, freshness model, network/deployment assumptions, and shutdown behavior. ### Design advantages - **Zero request-path coupling:** dispatch, completion, and abort have no edge into the reporting graph; there is no per-request overhead. - **Efficient fan-out:** one pull per fire shared by all due sessions, persistent bidi streams, no Router-side polling fan-out or connection churn. - **Topology-safe:** reports preserve per-DP-rank detail; rank-set changes are validated and retried within the same fire budget. - **Resilient:** per-attempt status semantics, session replacement, leases, latest-wins backpressure, and bounded shutdown prevent stale tasks from accumulating. - **Extensible:** a stable protocol and a single validation entry point provide a clean foundation for the separately reviewed Router monitor and future metrics. ## Accuracy Tests N/A for model accuracy. This PR does not change model forward code, kernels, sampling, or generated outputs. Functional validation: - Registered CPU tests cover the protocol contract, fire-loop scheduling/broadcast, snapshot validation, report builder, service behavior, lifecycle, and standalone SMG wiring. - Registered GPU E2E tests drive a real `grpc.aio` fake Router against single-owner, multi-owner, and standalone SMG modes. - Generated protobuf/gRPC bindings import successfully and expose the expected `sglang.router.loadmonitor.v1` service. ## Speed Tests and Profiling N/A for inference throughput benchmarking. This is an opt-in control-plane feature and does not modify model execution. The reporter adds no request-path overhead: there are no hooks on the dispatch/completion paths, and sampling/network I/O runs in the single background fire task. No inference-speed improvement is claimed. Reporter cadence and freshness are exercised functionally by the registered tests; no new micro-benchmarks are claimed in this revision. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. signal.title: [XPU][model]: Intel XPU support for encoder embeddings (bge/NomicBERT/ModernBERT) + InternVL3_5
signal.text: Intel XPU support for four embedding / vision models, combined for review: `BAAI/bge-base-en-v1.5`, `nomic-ai/nomic-embed-text-v1.5`, `ibm-granite/granite-embedding-english-r2`, and `OpenGVLab/InternVL3_5-30B-A3B`. ## Motivation - **bge-base-en-v1.5** (`BertModel`) loads on XPU but returns wrong embeddings — SciFact 0, cosine vs HF 0.26-0.47. Two XPU-specific bugs in shared code affect every BERT/RoBERTa encoder on `intel_xpu`. - **nomic-embed-text-v1.5** (`NomicBertModel`) had no SGLang model, so the Transformers fallback raised `NotImplementedError: get_input_embeddings ...`. - **granite-embedding-english-r2** (`ModernBertModel`) fell back and crashed in the forward pass (`RuntimeError` in `set_kv_buffer`) — a bidirectional encoder routed through the paged decoder KV cache. - **InternVL3_5-30B-A3B** crashed at load (`AttributeError: 'InternVLChatConfig' object has no attribute 'num_experts'`) and, once loading, hung/crashed the vision encoder under concurrent multimodal at tp>1 (Level Zero USM-memcpy deadlock on a per-block device->host `.item()`; DEVICE_LOST batching ViT tiles). ## Modifications Encoder embeddings: - `layers/attention/xpu_backend.py`: honor `AttentionType.ENCODER_ONLY` / `DECODER_BIDIRECTIONAL` (was `causal = not is_cross_attention`). - `managers/{scheduler,tokenizer_manager,utils}.py`: preserve the trailing separator token when truncating over-length embedding inputs (gated on `not is_generation`). - `models/nomic_bert.py` (new): `NomicBertModel` — RoPE, SwiGLU, post-norm; SDPA. - `models/modernbert.py` (new): `ModernBertModel` — RoPE, local/global attn, GeGLU; SDPA. InternVL: - `models/internvl.py`: read `num_experts` from `config.llm_config`; pass the host-side `max_seqlen` into `prepare_vision_attention_metadata`; chunk the ViT forward to `SGLANG_VIT_MAX_TILES` tiles on XPU. - `layers/attention/vision.py`: `VisionIntelXPUAttention` uses the metadata's host `max_seqlen` instead of re-deriving it from GPU `cu_seqlens` per block. - `environ.py`: add `SGLANG_VIT_MAX_TILES` (default 12). All XPU paths are guarded by `is_xpu()`; the encoder truncation change is embedding-only; decoder generation is unchanged. ## Accuracy Test Intel XPU (Arc Pro B60), vs the HuggingFace reference. Encoder — MTEB SciFact NDCG@10 (300 queries / 5183 corpus), tp-1: | Model | cosine vs HF | SciFact NDCG@10 | HF ref | |---|---|---|---| | bge-base-en-v1.5 | 0.99997 | 0.6981 | 0.7387 | | nomic-embed-text-v1.5 | 1.00000 | 0.6803 | (prefix-sensitive) | | granite-r2 (ModernBERT) | 1.000000 fp32 / >=0.9999 bf16 | 0.6720 | 0.6815 | InternVL3_5-30B-A3B — tp-4 (61.7 GB bf16, ~14.43 GB/rank): loads with 0 skipped params, MoE initialized, multimodal smoke (red image -> "Red"); P1 lmms-eval: **mathvision_testmini 38.2, mmmu_val 27.4**. All four load with 0 skipped params. ## Speed Test and Profiling No change to existing code paths. Encoder fixes flip a boolean / run once per over-length request; the two new encoders are small SDPA models (no KV cache). InternVL removes a per-block device->host sync on XPU and bounds the ViT forward; non-XPU paths are unchanged. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32368977663](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32368977663)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32368977011](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32368977011)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #32368977328](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32368977328)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->
