signal.title: [Bug] Anthropic endpoint: tool_reference parts in tool_result break chat templates without deferred-reference support (HTTP 500)
signal.text: ## Describe the bug The Anthropic-compatible endpoint (`/v1/messages`) converts `tool_reference` blocks found inside `tool_result` content into structured parts `{"type": "tool_reference", "name": ...}` (deferred tool loading, #22702). That part type is only understood by chat templates that implement deferred-reference expansion (GLM family). For any other model, the template hits the unknown item type and the whole request fails with HTTP 500: ``` jinja2.exceptions.TemplateError: Unexpected item type in content. ... [ts] Anthropic error response api_error (exception=ValueError): Internal server error ``` With Claude Code this is especially disruptive: once a session uses deferred tool loading (ToolSearch) and a `tool_reference` block enters the conversation history, **every subsequent request in that session fails** — the history carries the block forward, so retries cannot recover and only clearing/compacting the context fixes it. We observed ~26 consecutive 500s on a single session until it was abandoned. ## Reproduction Server: SGLang 0.5.17 (same code on `main`), any model whose chat template does not handle `tool_reference` (reproduced with the stock Qwen3.8-27B template): ```bash curl -s http://127.0.0.1:30000/v1/messages \ -H 'content-type: application/json' -H 'x-api-key: dummy' -d '{ "model": "qwen3.8-27b", "max_tokens": 16, "stream": false, "tools": [{"name": "DemoTool", "description": "demo", "input_schema": {"type": "object", "properties": {}}}], "messages": [ {"role": "user", "content": "list the deferred tools"}, {"role": "assistant", "content": [ {"type": "tool_use", "id": "toolu_1", "name": "ToolSearch", "input": {"query": "select:Foo"}} ]}, {"role": "user", "content": [ {"type": "tool_result", "tool_use_id": "toolu_1", "content": [ {"type": "text", "text": "Found 1 tool:"}, {"type": "tool_reference", "tool_name": "DemoTool"} ]} ]}, {"role": "user", "content": "now use it"} ] }' ``` Actual: `HTTP 500 {"type":"error","error":{"type":"api_error","message":"Internal server error"}}` with `TemplateError: Unexpected item type in content` in the server log. Same request with the `tool_reference` item removed: `HTTP 200`. (A `thinking` block in assistant history does not trigger this; the minimal trigger is the `tool_reference` item in a `tool_result` content list.) ## Root cause `python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/anthropic/serving.py`, `_convert_to_chat_completion_request` → `_convert_tool_result_content`: ```python elif item_type == "tool_reference": ref_name = item.get("tool_name") or item.get("name") if ref_name: tool_content_parts.append( {"type": "tool_reference", "name": ref_name} ) ``` The structured part is emitted unconditionally. Templates without deferred-reference expansion (e.g. Qwen's `render_content` macro, which only accepts `text`/`image`/`video` items) raise `TemplateError`, which is surfaced as a 500. Suggested fix: detect whether the loaded chat template handles `tool_reference` (e.g. substring check on the template source, mirroring how the unit tests fake `tokenizer_manager.tokenizer.chat_template`) and, when it does not, degrade the reference to a text part such as `[tool reference: <name>]` so history echoes keep working for all models while GLM behavior is preserved. A PR implementing this is coming. ## Environment ``` Python: 3.12.12 | packaged by conda-forge CUDA available: True GPU: 8x NVIDIA H100 80GB HBM3 (CC 9.0), Driver 580.95.05, CUDA 12.9 PyTorch: 2.11.0+cu130 sglang: 0.5.17 sglang-kernel: 0.4.5 flashinfer_python: 0.6.15.post1 triton: 3.6.0 transformers: 5.12.1 numpy: 2.3.5 fastapi: 0.141.1 pydantic: 2.14.0b1 anthropic: 0.125.0 ``` Full `python3 -m sglang.check_env` output: ``` Python: 3.12.12 | packaged by conda-forge | (main, Oct 22 2025, 23:25:55) [GCC 14.3.0] CUDA available: True GPU 0,1,2,3,4,5,6,7: NVIDIA H100 80GB HBM3 GPU signal.title: [Feature] Support Custom OTLP Trace Service Name
signal.text: ### Checklist - [x] If this is not a feature request but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed. - [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed. ### Motivation ## Summary Currently, SGLang hardcodes the OpenTelemetry trace service name as `"sglang"` in all components. This makes it difficult to distinguish between multiple SGLang instances in distributed tracing systems (Jaeger, Tempo, etc.) when running multiple servers for different purposes (staging, production, different models, etc.). Request: Add support for customizing the OTLP trace service name via CLI parameter and/or environment variable. ## Current Behavior When `--enable-trace` is set, all traces report with `service.name = "sglang"`: ```bash python -m sglang.launch_server \ --model-path Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B-FP8 \ --enable-trace \ --otlp-traces-endpoint localhost:4317 ``` **Result in OTLP collector:** - All spans show `service.name: "sglang"` - Cannot distinguish between multiple SGLang instances - Environment variable `OTEL_SERVICE_NAME` is ignored ### Related resources ## Proposed Changes ### 1. Add CLI parameter in `server_args.py` ```python otlp_service_name: A[ str, "Service name for OTLP traces (displayed as 'service.name' in trace backends). Defaults to 'sglang'.", NS("observability"), ] = "sglang" ``` ### 2. Update all `process_tracing_init` calls Replace `"sglang"` with `server_args.otlp_service_name` in: - `http_server.py` - `scheduler.py` - `engine.py` - `encode_server.py` - `data_parallel_controller.py` ### 3. (Optional) Support `OTEL_SERVICE_NAME` fallback In `trace.py`, only set `SERVICE_NAME` if `server_name` is provided: ```python attributes = {} if server_name: attributes[SERVICE_NAME] = server_name # If not provided, OTEL_SERVICE_NAME env var will be used by OpenTelemetry SDK resource = Resource.create(attributes=attributes) ``` Or read the env var explicitly: ```python import os service_name = server_name or os.getenv("OTEL_SERVICE_NAME", "sglang") resource = Resource.create(attributes={SERVICE_NAME: service_name}) ```

signal.title: [XPU] Use SYCL kernels for DeepSeek V4 MHC on XPU
signal.text: ## Motivation Enable XPU-specific optimized kernels for the DeepSeek V4 MHC (Multi-Head Compression) path on Intel XPU hardware. The existing CUDA-path kernels (deep_gemm, CUDA-first device selection) are either unavailable or suboptimal on XPU, causing incorrect device dispatch or missing performance opportunities. ## Modifications deepseek_v4.py: On XPU, dispatch hc_head to sgl_kernel.mhc.fused_hc_head (SYCL kernel) instead of the Triton implementation; dispatch mhc_fused_post_pre to the XPU-specific kernel; fix device selection to avoid falling back to CUDA when XPU is available. ## Accuracy Tests Verified the accuracy of MHC kernels in sgl-kernel-xpu: hc_head: https://github.com/sgl-project/sgl-kernel-xpu/pull/345 mhc_fused_post_pre: https://github.com/sgl-project/sgl-kernel-xpu/pull/302 All configurations pass accuracy tests. ## Speed Tests and Profiling signal.title: [diffusion] feat: add weight source reader
signal.text: ## Motivation Reading a checkpoint was a boolean. `safetensors_weights_iterator` took `use_runai_model_streamer: bool | None`, branched on it inline, and carried one rule hardcoded around it: ```python if key_filter is not None: # streamer filters after materializing all tensors, so it cannot skip # a checkpoint partition at load time use_runai_model_streamer = False ``` That comment is describing a property of the Run:ai streamer, but it lives at the call site, so every future caller has to rediscover it. And the two paths differ in more than speed: `safe_open` maps the file, so the CPU tensors it yields are views into the checkpoint, while the streamer copies into anonymous memory. Nothing named that difference, which makes it invisible to anyone reasoning about host memory. ## Modifications Move both readers into `runtime/loader/weight_readers/` behind a protocol that states what separates them: ``` weight_readers/ ├── __init__.py select_weight_reader() -- the whole decision ├── base.py WeightReader protocol ├── runai_streamer.py RunaiStreamerReader └── safetensors_mmap.py SafetensorsMmapReader ``` Two capabilities: - `supports_key_filter` -- can it skip keys while reading? The streamer cannot, so the rule that used to sit at the call site now sits on the reader that owns it. - `retains_file_mapping` -- are the yielded tensors views into the checkpoint file? `select_weight_reader()` honours an explicit request, falls back when a reader is not installed, and passes over one that cannot filter when the caller needs filtering. The old boolean still works and maps onto a reader name, so no call site changes behaviour. `safetensors_mmap.py` is named for the mapping rather than for `safe_open`, because the mapping is the reason the file exists. ## Accuracy Tests Behaviour-preserving refactor; no numerics touched. Full `test/unit` suite goes from 1720 to 1730 passed, the ten new ones being reader-selection tests, with the same four pre-existing failures (`realtime/`, `sana_wm/`) that fail with this change reverted -- checked by reverting it and re-running those four. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Not applicable: the same reader runs, chosen the same way, for every existing caller. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Notes `retains_file_mapping` is the property a follow-up needs. File-backed pages are droppable under memory pressure without swap; anonymous pages are not, and on a swapless host -- which container runtimes commonly are -- that is the difference between the kernel having something to reclaim and having nothing. Measured on one RTX 4090, host-to-device bandwidth for a 2 GiB transfer: 13.09 GB/s from pinned anonymous memory, 8.84 GB/s from pageable anonymous, and 8.5 GB/s from a cache-resident file mapping. Giving up the consolidated per-layer buffer costs nothing measurable -- 66 per-tensor copies matching a real DiT layer's size distribution move 542 MiB at 13.41 GB/s against 13.39 GB/s for one consolidated copy -- so a mapped host copy is a viable source. This PR only names the property; it does not change which reader anything uses. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #32347298556](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32347298556)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32347298271](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32347298271)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #32347298505](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32347298505)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [diffusion] Forward multimodal token type IDs in image encoding
signal.text: ## Motivation Transformers 5.12 Qwen3-VL requires `mm_token_type_ids` when multimodal grid inputs are present. The JoyAI image-edit processor already returns this tensor, but `ImageEncodingStage` selected only the older processor outputs before calling the text encoder. As a result, JoyAI image editing failed before inference with the error reported in #34366. ## Modifications - Centralize the text-encoder input assembly for image encoding. - Forward `mm_token_type_ids` when the processor returns it, in both the positive and classifier-free-guidance negative paths. - Preserve the previous call shape when processors omit the optional field. - Add CPU unit coverage with a real `transformers.BatchFeature`, distinct positive/negative token-type IDs, dtype/device assertions, and a strict legacy encoder signature without `**kwargs`. The change is intentionally limited to stage plumbing; it does not alter model-side position-ID computation. ## Accuracy Tests - `TORCHDYNAMO_DISABLE=1 PYTHONPATH=python python -m pytest -q python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/unit/test_image_encoding_stage.py` — 3 passed. - The existing `joyai_image_edit_ti2i` 1-GPU case is the focused end-to-end regression smoke test. It was not run locally because a compatible GPU and model weights were unavailable, so it is requested in CI. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Not applicable. This only forwards an existing integer tensor and adds no model computation or tensor copy. ## Checklist - [x] Format the Python changes with the repository pre-commit hooks. All affected-file hooks passed; the repository-wide non-Rust hooks also passed (Rust-only hooks were skipped because this PR does not touch Rust). - [x] Add unit tests according to the contribution guide. - [x] Document the behavior and compatibility scope in this PR; no user-facing API documentation changes are needed. - [x] Provide the relevant accuracy/speed rationale above; the GPU smoke test is delegated to CI. - [x] Follow the SGLang code-style guidance. Fixes #34366 <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #32337649348](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32337649348)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32337648995](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32337648995)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #32337649598](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32337649598)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [Model Loader] Harden startup weight-load overlap and expand model coverage
signal.text: ## Summary This is the hardening and coverage follow-up to #32017. It keeps startup weight-load overlap opt-in, makes admission/fallback deterministic, and extends the path to hybrid, MoE/EP, and one narrowly validated FP8 model profile. - Replace implicit support checks with a structured admission plan and deterministic rejection report. - Add `--startup-weight-load-mode=auto`: admitted configurations use overlap; rejected configurations preserve serial startup. - Check resolved checkpoint capabilities before capture-safe mutation, so `auto` can fall back for PT or secondary weights without allocating the model twice. - Freeze graph-visible parameter, buffer, and explicitly registered derived-tensor storage across the real-weight commit, then reject stale capture sentinels or storage rebinding. - After graph capture, cooperatively cancel and drain checkpoint prefetch before the real commit. If the bounded drain times out, continue with the conservative commit-reader policy while the cancelled daemon worker exits, without waiting a second time. - Preserve serial post-load semantics for optional parameters that intentionally skip dummy-weight validation. - Report complete overlap phase timings and assign `ModelRunner.weight_load_time` only after the real commit. - Add exact profiles for Qwen hybrid/MoE models and GLM-5.2 FP8. The default remains `serial`. Explicit `overlap` fails during preflight with actionable reasons when unsupported; `auto` logs the same reasons and follows the serial path. ## Supported profiles | Profile | Admitted configuration | | --- | --- | | Native dense | Native `LlamaForCausalLM`, `Qwen2ForCausalLM`, or `Qwen3ForCausalLM`; FP16/BF16; TP1/TP2 | | Qwen3.5-family hybrid VLM | Native `Qwen3_5ForConditionalGeneration` (including Qwen3.6 dense checkpoints); BF16; TP2/TP4; Triton linear attention; breakable or disabled prefill CUDA graphs | | Qwen3.5 MoE hybrid VLM | Native `Qwen3_5MoeForConditionalGeneration`; BF16; TP2+EP2; Triton MoE and linear attention; standard EP path; breakable or disabled prefill CUDA graphs | | Qwen3 MoE EP | Native `Qwen3MoeForCausalLM`; BF16; TP2+EP2; Triton MoE runner; standard EP path (`moe_a2a_backend=none`) | | GLM-5.2 FP8 | Native `GlmMoeDsaForCausalLM` with the GLM-5.2 fingerprint; serialized dynamic E4M3 FP8 with 128x128 blocks; BF16 execution/KV cache; Hopper SM90; TP8/TP16 with EP1; DSA with FA3 prefill/decode; Triton FP8 GEMM and MoE; prefill graphs disabled; shared-expert fusion off | The GLM profile is keyed to the native GLM-5.2 IndexShare fingerprint (default `cli_factor`, no custom `index_topk_pattern`, `index_topk_freq=4`, and `index_skip_topk_offset=3`), not merely the architecture name. Other quantized/repacked-weight paths, speculative decoding, LoRA/offload, and parallel/backend combinations outside the rows above remain rejected. `auto` sends them through serial startup. ## Design details `StartupWeightLoadAdmission` separates side-effect-free config preflight from native model-class resolution. Cheap rules run first; implementation resolution/import only happens for a viable candidate. Checkpoint format and secondary weights are checked after source resolution but before sentinel initialization, which gives `auto` a final safe serial-fallback boundary. `ModelStorageManifest` records tensor identity, pointer, shape, stride, dtype, device, and storage offset after dummy post-load preparation. Finalization proves that real loading refreshed the same graph-visible storage. Models can enumerate derived tensors through a per-module hook without a recursive attribute scan; the GLM/DeepSeek path uses this for MLA-derived weights and scales. Checkpoint staging remains best-effort. After graph capture, the manager cooperatively stops and joins the worker before starting normal multithreaded commit. If the bounded stop times out, the handle remains active and the loader preserves its conservative concurrency policy. Worker failure, intentional cancellation, and full-file completion remain distinguishable, and no filesystem/path-specific policy is used. Real-weight commit failures after capture-safe preparation are terminal startup failures. `auto` intentionally does not retry serial loading after model mutation or graph capture. ## H100 validation ### Controlled Qwen3.6 startup benchmark `Qwen/Qwen3.6-27B@6a9e13bd6fc8f0983b9b99948120bc37f49c13e9`, BF16, TP2, FA3, Triton GDN/linear attention, prefill CUDA graph disabled, decode FullCG, local NVMe. Three interleaved trials per mode were run after separate JIT warmup. Before every trial, checkpoint pages were evicted with `POSIX_FADV_DONTNEED` and verified with `mincore` to have zero resident bytes. | Metric (median) | Serial | Overlap | Change | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | | Process ready | 50.193 s | 46.122 s | **-8.11% / 1.088x** | | Scheduler startup | 30.03 s | 26.30 s | -12.4% | | `load_weight` | 11.66 s | 7.50 s | -35.7% | Every overlap trial exercised the active handoff rather than an already-complete prefetch: capture ended with only 8-9 of 15 shards fully staged, the worker stopped in about 3.8 s, and multithreaded commit then resumed. There were no fallback, timeout, manifest, or sentinel errors. The server requested decode graph BS 256, but the hybrid Mamba-state capacity resolved the maximum running/captured BS to 39. The actual capture shapes were `[1, 2, 4, 8, 12, 16, 24, 32, 39]`; this resolved limit was identical in both modes. Across all six startups, two fixed prompts produced bit-identical text, token IDs, input/output logprobs, and top-logprobs. The timing is an end-to-end `serial` versus `overlap` mode comparison; coordinated checkpoint staging and its handoff are part of the overlap path, not a claim about graph capture in isolation. ### Coverage and correctness probes - `zai-org/GLM-5.2-FP8@ba978f7d347eaf65d22f1a86833408afdb953541`, BF16, TP16 on H100, DSA+FA3, Triton FP8/MoE, BF16 KV: `serial`, `overlap`, and `auto` passed storage validation and produced matching token IDs/logprobs. - `Qwen/Qwen3.5-35B-A3B`, BF16, TP2+EP2, FA3, Triton MoE/linear attention: text, image, batched, and prefix-branching requests matched across `serial`, `overlap`, and `auto`. - `Qwen/Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct-2507`, BF16, TP2+EP2, FA3, Triton MoE: multi-route batched and prefix-branching requests matched exactly across startup modes. These additional probes establish model/topology correctness coverage; the controlled Qwen3.6 experiment above is the performance result. ## Tests - Final focused startup/prefetch suite on the GPU development image: `84 passed, 98 subtests passed`. - Unit coverage includes deterministic admission/rejection, `auto` fallback boundaries, timing ownership, storage/sentinel validation, derived-tensor refresh, optional single/both-scale post-load behavior, prefetch EOF/cancel/crash races, bounded drain/timeout, and loader dispatch after handoff. - The registered one-GPU parity test compares both `overlap` and `auto` with default serial startup. - `black --check`, `isort --check-only`, `ruff check --select F401,F821,UP037`, `codespell`, `py_compile`, and `git diff --check` pass on the changed files. ## Follow-up This PR intentionally leaves `serial` as the default. Follow-up work can add separately validated DeepSeek V4 Flash and Kimi Linear/K3 profiles; define a two-phase, capture-stable contract for quantization methods that repack or replace weight storage; broaden backend/topology and storage evidence; isolate graph overlap with a serial-plus-coordinated-prefetch benchmark arm; and then consider making automatic overlap selection the default. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32357825842](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32357825842)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32357825733](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32357825733)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32357825862](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32357825862)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [AMD] Pass USE_PDL explicitly to Triton kernel launches
signal.text: ## Motivation Fixes #35348. On ROCm with torch 2.11 and Triton 3.7, torch.compile can generate an Inductor launcher whose signature does not match the call when a Triton kernel constexpr USE_PDL is omitted on non-PDL architectures. ## Modifications - Pass USE_PDL explicitly for the fused MoE gate, static FP8 quantization, top-k packing, and Inkling SiLU-and-mul Triton launches. - Keep launch_pdl enabled only when the architecture supports PDL. - Add a CPU-only source contract test covering all four PDL-aware launch sites. ## Accuracy Tests - CPU-only PDL launcher contract: passed. - Python compile checks: passed. - Registered-test lint check: passed. - ROCm 7.2.4 torch.compile integration: not run locally; requires AMD CI hardware and the unpublished ROCm 7.2.4 environment. ## Checklist - [x] Add focused regression tests. - [x] Keep the change limited to the PDL launcher argument handling. - [ ] Run the ROCm 7.2.4 integration test in CI. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32357311812](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32357311812)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32357311631](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32357311631)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32357311886](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32357311886)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: Auto-detect aiter decode attention backend for MLA models on ROCm
signal.text: > **Draft migration of #22638 to the correct Miles dependency branch.** Changing the old PR's base from `main` to `sglang-miles` caused GitHub to auto-close it because its historical `amdpilot-org/sglang` source repository is outside the current fork network and could not be reopened. This draft preserves the same two commits on the normal `Arist12/sglang` fork. ## Motivation On MI355X, the AITER MLA decode backend materially reduced GLM-5.1 FP8 decode latency compared with the then-default backend. Automatically selecting it when the user has not chosen either attention backend could remove a manual tuning step for supported ROCm MLA models. ## Current blockers - `sglang-miles` moved DeepSeek-family defaults into `python/sglang/srt/arg_groups/overrides.py`; mechanically resolving the old `server_args.py` hunk would restore code in the wrong layer. - The original condition does not establish whether DSA models such as GLM-5.x should receive a raw `decode_attention_backend="aiter"` override after the newer `attention_backend="dsa"` resolution. - `importlib.util.find_spec("aiter")` proves only that the package exists, not that the installed build, GPU, model shape, and decode mode are supported. - The branch has no regression tests for default selection, explicit user overrides, or unavailable/unsupported AITER. - The 42.6% result was measured on one MI355X GLM configuration and must not be generalized to every listed model or ROCm GPU without evidence. ## Required refresh before marking ready - [x] Target `sglang-miles`, which is the branch Miles images consume. - [ ] Re-implement the default in `_deepseek_family_overrides` or the appropriate current resolution pass. - [ ] Add focused tests for default selection, both user override flags, missing AITER, DSA/non-DSA behavior, and unsupported capability. - [ ] Rerun the GLM-5.1 MI355X benchmark against current `sglang-miles` and record exact commands. - [ ] Smoke-test at least one additional supported MLA architecture or narrow the documented model scope. - [ ] Run current lint and AMD CI. This PR intentionally remains draft and conflicting until the behavior is redesigned and independently validated. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #24352912710](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/24352912710)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: **Blocked** -- `run-ci` is required first.<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [SM120] DeepSeek-V4: DeepGEMM paged-MQA indexer +FP4 MoE+ page-split
signal.text: **Motivation:** a 4x RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell (SM120) box can hold DeepSeek-V4-Flash, but on current main the only configuration that starts there is the slow torch fallback — this PR makes the DeepGEMM and FlashInfer paths work on SM120, cutting decode latency up to 3.4x. It routes the sparse-MLA indexer to DeepGEMM's paged-MQA-logits kernel, enables batched sparse-MLA prefill through FlashInfer, and unblocks the DeepGEMM FP4 MoE backend. ## Split out of this PR Following @Fridge003's review, the changes here that were not SM120 enablement now have their own PRs: - #35116 — allocate the page-split buffer outside inference mode (correctness fix) - #35118 — fuse the hc-prenorm combine into a Triton kernel (arch-independent) **This PR now depends on #35116**: without it the page-split buffer is allocated under inference mode during autotune and CUDA graph capture cannot write to it. Will rebase once it lands. The E2E tables below were measured with #35118 still in this tree. Measured separately on the same box with only that kernel toggled (ISL 8K, BS1, TP4, deep_gemm MoE), it accounts for **3.2% of the TPOT gain** (12.81 -> 12.40 ms, two repeats each, run-to-run spread 0.01 ms) and roughly 2% of TTFT. Discount the tables by that much, or land #35118 first to reproduce them as written. ## What is in it 1. **Sparse-MLA indexer on DeepGEMM** — route the indexer to DeepGEMM's paged-MQA-logits kernel instead of the eager-torch fallback that scales with batch x context and dominates decode. Opt in with `SGLANG_FP8_PAGED_MQA_LOGITS_TORCH=0 SGLANG_OPT_USE_TILELANG_INDEXER=0`. 2. **Batched sparse-MLA prefill** — prefill (q_len > 64) goes through FlashInfer's `_sparse_mla_sm120_paged_attention`; indexer metadata is chunked at M=4096 (the DeepGEMM row cap is SKU-dependent) and built once per batch instead of per layer. 3. **Page-split dirty mask** — `_split_kv_pages_to_64` re-laid out the whole SWA KV pool (~105 MB/layer) every decode step; now only the pages this step's top-k references are split (CUDA-graph safe, bit-identical). 4. **DeepGEMM FP4 MoE on SM120** — probe the block-scale entry point (DeepGEMM#324) instead of hard-disabling DeepGEMM at `sm==120`, plus the contiguous grouped-GEMM prefill path, the UE8M0 pow2-scale quant fix, and the swiglu-clamp fallback for TP>=2 shapes. 5. **SM120 kernel fixes** — u64 page-split copy, sparse-prefill head pad removal, TileLang `mhc_pre` compile fix, and the paged-MQA metadata kernel now sizes its shared-memory request from the device budget instead of a fixed 128 KB. Non-SM120 architectures are unchanged: every behavioural change is either gated on `is_sm120_supported()` or is a fix that only engages where the previous code was wrong (the UE8M0 pow2-scale quant and the shared-memory cap). ## E2E benefit "main" is marlin MoE + the torch paged-MQA fallback, because that is the only SM120 path on `14bd315d` that starts: the default (`flashinfer_mxfp4` + TileLang indexer) dies in the TileLang JIT for `sm_120a` (TileLang ships nvcc 13.3, `lmsysorg/sglang:dev-cu13` has CUDA 13.0 headers), and `--moe-runner-backend deep_gemm` raises `AttributeError: module 'sglang.srt.layers.deep_gemm_wrapper' has no attribute 'get_mn_major_tma_aligned_tensor'` (SM120 disables `ENABLE_JIT_DEEPGEMM` while the runner stays selectable). Both sides then run identical server args, only the tree differs: TP4, marlin MoE, CUTLASS FP8, chunked prefill 8192, `--disable-radix-cache`, and no speculative decoding except where the tables say otherwise. 4x RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell (SM120, 96 GB, PCIe), DeepSeek-V4-Flash, OSL 256, `--warmup-requests 0` so every measured request is a real prefill. TTFT is a median. **Single request (BS=1)** — 3 sequential requests, median. TTFT: | ISL | main | this PR | | |---|---|---|---| | 8K | 1124 ms | 899 ms | −20% | | 32K | 4540 ms | 3585 ms | −21% | | 128K | 20107 ms | 15481 ms | −23% | TPOT, without and with MTP-2 (EAGLE, 2 steps / 3 draft tokens) on both sides: | ISL | main | this PR | | main + MTP-2 | this PR + MTP-2 | | |---|---|---|---|---|---|---| | 8K | 36.1 ms | 10.5 ms | **3.4x** | 13.6 ms | 6.0 ms | 2.3x | | 32K | 35.8 ms | 10.7 ms | **3.3x** | 12.6 ms | 5.7 ms | 2.2x | | 128K | 36.1 ms | 11.9 ms | **3.0x** | 13.4 ms | 6.8 ms | 2.0x | Accepted length is within 0.2 of each other on the two sides at every context length, so the MTP gain comes from the decode path itself, not from better speculation. **Concurrent (ISL 8K)** — `--num-prompts BS --max-concurrency BS`: | BS | TTFT main | TTFT this PR | | TPOT main | TPOT this PR | | output tok/s main | output tok/s this PR | |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---| | 4 | 3574 ms | 2826 ms | −21% | 42.9 ms | 16.8 ms | 2.6x | 71 | 147 | | 8 | 5660 ms | 4530 ms | −20% | 51.9 ms | 24.3 ms | 2.1x | 108 | 191 | | 16 | 10482 ms | 8365 ms | −20% | 71.6 ms | 40.9 ms | 1.8x | 143 | 219 | TTFT holds at −20% across batch sizes; the decode multiple decays with batch (3.4x at BS1, 1.8x at BS16) because what this PR removes is per-step fixed cost, which amortises as the batch grows. Speculative decoding amortises it the same way. GSM8K (50 questions) is 0.980 on main and 0.960 on this PR at 8K — one question apart. All tables are without prefill context parallelism, which is upstream code this PR does not touch. <details> <summary>Recipes</summary> Common to both: `--fp8-gemm-backend cutlass --chunked-prefill-size 8192 --max-prefill-tokens 8192 --swa-full-tokens-ratio 0.15 --cuda-graph-max-bs 32`, plus `SGLANG_SM120_FLASHMLA_BACKEND=flashinfer SGLANG_FP8_PAGED_MQA_LOGITS_TORCH=0 SGLANG_OPT_USE_TILELANG_INDEXER=0`. **Prefill-optimised** — `--moe-runner-backend deep_gemm --mem-fraction-static 0.85`, `SGLANG_OPT_FIX_MEGA_MOE_MEMORY=1 SGLANG_OPT_DEEPGEMM_HC_PRENORM=1`. **Decode-optimised** — `--moe-runner-backend marlin --mem-fraction-static 0.90 --speculative-algorithm EAGLE --speculative-eagle-topk 1 --speculative-num-steps 2 --speculative-num-draft-tokens 3`, `SGLANG_OPT_USE_TILELANG_MHC_PRE=1`. </details> ## Dependencies - FlashInfer 0.6.15.post1 (SM120 sparse-MLA kernels) and sglang-kernel 0.4.5 — both are what `lmsysorg/sglang:dev-cu13` currently ships. - DeepGEMM at or after deepseek-ai/DeepGEMM#324 for the FP4 MoE backend. The `fp8_paged_mqa_logits` indexer path additionally needs DeepGEMM's attention host-gates to accept SM120 (a 3-line arch gate, not yet upstream in sgl-project/DeepGEMM); without it, keep the TileLang indexer default. ## Tests `test/registered/kernels/ops/attention/test_silu_and_mul_contig_post_quant.py` (9 cases, registered for CI) covers the fused swiglu-clamp + silu_mul + fp8-quant kernel against a reference. GSM8K numbers are from `sglang.test.few_shot_gsm8k`. Reviewed and validated with @ormandj (conflict resolution) and @moxcat (inference-mode buffer fix, now #35116) on 2x and 4x RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell. Re-validated after the split on 4x RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell, FlashInfer 0.6.15.post1 (the pinned version), this tree plus #35116: GSM8K-50 1.000 with `--moe-runner-backend deep_gemm`, 0.960 with MTP-2; ISL 8K BS1 TTFT 116/88 ms, TPOT 12.8/7.3 ms. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32351543120](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32351543120)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32351542983](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32351542983)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32351543356](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32351543356)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [Roadmap]Fast Engine Recovery: Weight Cache Daemon
signal.text: # [Roadmap] Fast Engine Recovery: Weight Cache Daemon @liusy58 @QiuMike @alexnails Phase 1 landed in #27139 — a per-rank daemon holds post-quantized weights and serves them over CUDA IPC; weight load drops from ~306–327s to <1s on Qwen3-235B FP8 ([blog](https://github.com/QiuMike/lm-sys.github.io/blob/sglang_fast_recovery/blog/2026-07-28-sglang-fast-recovery.md)). This issue tracks the next steps. Contributions and feedback are welcome. Related: #27052 (Fast Recovery framework), #27310 (GPU Memory Service / VMM) Goals: <10s cold restart and <1s warm standby switch; broaden model & quant coverage; make the cache outlive the daemon; make resident weights usable beyond the one GPU they sit on. Where Phase 1 stands: TP + PP, single-node and multi-node launch (each node spawns its share of ranks and joins one dist group), zero-copy IPC per GPU, unquantized + block-wise FP8. Not yet: cross-node daemon coordination / failover, DP & EP shard keying, spec-decoding draft models, weight update / sleep-wake, cache surviving daemon death. ## Model & quantization coverage - [ ] parity harness — disk-load vs daemon-load `state_dict` diff (names / shape / dtype / stride / byte hash) + short GSM8K gate; required evidence for every new allowlist entry - [ ] carry post-processing metadata in the manifest (final shape/stride, layout tag, whitelisted module attrs) instead of reproducing `process_weights_after_loading` on a meta-init model — this is what blocks most quant methods today - [ ] quant methods: per-tensor fp8 / w8a8 int8 / mxfp8 / nvfp4 / compressed-tensors / awq / gptq-marlin #32398 - [ ] archs: MoE (DeepSeek V3/V4, Ling, Kimi K3) / hybrid linear attention / multimodal (vision tower + projector) / LoRA base weights - [ ] MTP & EAGLE draft models (per-rank draft daemon), removing the `--speculative-algorithm` rejection in `server_args.py` #32744 - [ ] generic post-map rebuild hook to replace the hardcoded `_rebuild_stale_views`; make tied storages, param→buffer flips and non-persistent buffers explicit in the manifest - [ ] publish the support matrix in docs; unsupported combinations keep hard-erroring (no silent wrong numerics) ## Transport: CUDA VMM shareable handles (#27310 §4.2) - [ ] `vmm_fd` backend (skeleton already in `weight_cache/transport.py`): `cuMemCreate` + FD handles over `SCM_RIGHTS`, VA reservation on import, `torch_ipc` stays the fallback, `--weight-cache-transport {auto,torch_ipc,vmm_fd}` #33279 ## Weight update without reload - [ ] epoch handoff on stable VAs: readers unmap → writer commits → readers remap at the same VAs, so captured CUDA graphs stay valid - [ ] daemon as the weight delivery agent for trainer pushes (NCCL/RDMA); un-gate the `update_weights_*` rejections in `weight_updater.py` - [ ] colocated RL: engine itself takes the writer role, same protocol, no daemon in the loop ## Multi-instance & cross-GPU sharing - [ ] key the cache by physical GPU UUID + config fingerprint (plus optional `--weight-cache-namespace`) under a configurable runtime dir. Today the socket is `/tmp/sglang_weight_cache_rank{global_rank}.sock`, so 2× tp=4 on one 8-GPU node collide and rank 0 of the second instance attaches to the GPU 0 daemon - [ ] discovery: replace static socket paths with a lightweight registry (file-based dir, optionally etcd) so an engine rank selects a daemon by `CacheConfig` match rather than by process rank, and locates daemons across nodes without a manual `--weight-cache-socket` - [ ] `--weight-cache-peer-copy` — when no daemon holds the shard on the local GPU, `cudaMemcpyPeerAsync` it from a peer-GPU daemon (NVLink-domain check, chunked on a low-priority stream, bandwidth cap so a serving neighbour is not disturbed). 1× memory per instance, sub-second over NVLink vs ~300s from disk - [ ] preference order local zero-copy > peer copy > disk, reported per rank - [ ] fleet fill: a daemon fills itself from a peer daemon instead of disk (P2P on-node, NCCL/RDMA cross-node), so a fleet cold start pays one disk read per shard group — the real bottleneck for 1T+ models on shared FS; align with the checkpoint-engine broadcast path - [ ] out of scope for now: resharding across TP/EP topologies (tp=4 daemon → tp=8 engine) ## Multi-node, DP & EP - [ ] primary–secondary daemon coordination for multi-node TP (e.g. TP=16 = 2 nodes × 8 GPUs): primary orchestrates daemon startup, cross-node NCCL process-group formation and readiness signalling; secondaries load their local shards in parallel and serve IPC handles to engines on their own node. Basic multi-node launch already works via `--nnodes/--node-rank/--dist-init-method`; what is missing is the cluster state machine - [ ] cross-node daemon lifecycle: primary tracks which secondaries are alive, triggers coordinated restarts, signals engines on a dead secondary's node to fall back to disk; promote a secondary when the primary dies - [ ] DP support: every DP rank on a GPU maps the same daemon's handles, so a model is read from disk and quantized exactly once per GPU regardless of DP degree (today each DP rank disk-loads independently). This is about supporting SGLang's DP deployment model, not cross-GPU sharing - [ ] EP support: expert shards differ per EP rank, so cache and key them by `ep_rank`; handle partial expert loading when a rank owns a subset of experts - [ ] `CacheConfig`: add `ep_rank`, `dp_rank` and `node_rank` for correct shard identification under EP and multi-node (`dp_size`/`ep_size` are already there) ## Ops & reliability - [ ] `daemon status` command + Prometheus metrics (resident bytes, attached clients, load time, hit / mismatch / fallback), and an engine endpoint reporting how each rank got its weights - [ ] runtime dir with owner-only permissions + `SO_PEERCRED` check before handing out handles (no world-writable `/tmp` sockets) - [ ] `protocol_version` in the handshake with a documented skew policy (the env stamp already covers torch / arch skew) - [ ] `--weight-cache-max-bytes`, refcount-aware eviction, admission check against `gpu_memory_utilization` - [ ] systemd unit + k8s DaemonSet recipes; document container requirements for cross-container IPC - [ ] CI: CPU unit tests, 1-GPU daemon→client restart e2e with accuracy, 2-GPU TP e2e, nightly multi-node, restart-latency regression gate - [ ] docs page: three modes, support matrix, ops runbook, failure semantics - [ ] reclaim on daemon restart (Phase 6): the daemon holds no heavy logic and is robust by construction, but if it exits for an external reason its clients still hold the GPU memory alive through IPC refcounts — a restarted daemon should re-adopt that memory from a live client's references instead of reloading from disk ## Rest of the startup path - [ ] Phase 2 — CUDA graph serialization: persist captured graphs to shared memory or disk and replay instead of recapturing; needs pool-offset translation for address relocation, which is why it depends on the stable VAs above. ~34.9s (~9% of startup) → <3s - [ ] Phase 3 — kernel warmup: persist DeepGEMM JIT-compiled kernels across restarts, parallelize warmup across batch sizes. ~23.1s → <2s - [ ] Phase 4 — server & distributed init: lazy tokenizer init, config caching, NCCL session reuse. ~22s → <5s - [ ] KV cache alloc + warmup ~3.9s → <1.5s (KV reuse, skip warmup requests on restart) - [ ] standby orchestration: health / promotion, request draining and KV handoff, scheduler-level pause/resume for priority co-serving ## Open questions - [ ] manifest schema + versioning: SGLang-owned, stored by the memory owner as an opaque blob — what compatibility window across SGLang versions? - [ ] backend selection UX: server arg, TMS-side registration, or both? - [ ] peer copy: automatic whenever a peer daemon exists, or always explicit opt-in? default bandwidth cap next to a serving instance? ## KV Restore?

signal.title: [Bug][Spec] fix startup crash and reduce CUDA graph memory usage for speculative adaptive
signal.text: ## Motivation Three separate problems show up when `--speculative-adaptive` is enabled: 1. **Startup crash.** `ModelRunner.max_decode_logits_rows()` sizes the shared logits buffer from the *static* `decode_num_tokens_per_req()`, but adaptive speculative decoding replays runners built for larger draft-token widths. The buffer is too small and the server fails to start. (mentioned in #30549) 2. **IMA on the first replay.** `DecodeCudaGraphRunner.capture_one_shape` looked up `on_after_cuda_graph_warmup` on `self.model_runner.attn_backend` instead of on the backend this capture actually ran against (`attn_backend` from `capture_prepare`). For the runner the `ModelRunner` owns these are the same object, but adaptive speculative decoding builds extra runners bound to their own freshly created backend while `model_runner.attn_backend` still points at the active one. Hooking the wrong backend leaves this capture's warmup-upgraded metadata (raw→full, FlashMLA scheduler meta) frozen into the graph, which produces an illegal memory access on the first replay. 3. **Redundant CUDA graph memory.** Each capture pass opened `graph_capture()` without a stream, so every pass captured on a fresh stream. The caching allocator partitions the graph pool's segments **by stream**, so each pass re-reserved the pool's MoE / DeepEP scratch instead of reusing what an earlier pass left inactive. With adaptive speculative decoding that is one pass per candidate step × three runners — tens of GB of segments that all read back `inactive`. ## Modifications 1. `max_decode_logits_rows()` now derives `num_tokens_per_req` from `max_speculative_num_draft_tokens`, so the shared logits buffer is sized for the widest adaptive graph. (Same fix as #30554.) 2. `decode_cuda_graph_runner.py:1226-1237` — resolve `post_warmup_hook` from the capture-local `attn_backend` rather than `model_runner.attn_backend`, with a comment recording why. 3. Added `get_or_create_global_graph_capture_stream()` in `runner_utils/pool.py` (a named stream lease in the `Resources` tier, alongside the existing process-wide graph memory pool) and used it as the `graph_capture(stream=...)` argument in both `DecodeCudaGraphRunner.capture` and `PrefillCudaGraphRunner.capture`. All capture passes therefore share one stream and reserve that scratch exactly once. Captures are strictly serial (`Scheduler.init_all_cuda_graphs` runs target and draft workers in turn; the adaptive controller builds one runtime state at a time), so a single shared stream is safe. Also added a CPU unit test `test/registered/unit/model_executor/test_graph_capture_resources.py` covering both the pool and the new capture-stream lease. ## Accuracy Tests Server launched following the cookbook: ```bash sglang serve \ --trust-remote-code \ --model-path deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash \ --tp 4 \ --moe-runner-backend flashinfer_mxfp4 \ --speculative-algorithm EAGLE \ --speculative-num-steps 3 \ --speculative-eagle-topk 1 \ --speculative-num-draft-tokens 4 \ --speculative-adaptive \ --disable-flashinfer-autotune \ --swa-full-tokens-ratio 0.1 \ --host 0.0.0.0 \ --port 30000 ``` Evaluated on the three datasets shown in the cookbook: | | GPQA Diamond | AIME25 | GSM8k | | -------- | ------------ | ------ | ----- | | cookbook | 88.1 | 95 | 96.13 | | before | 88.13 | 98.33 | 96.89 | | after | 88.04 | 97.29 | 96.97 | ## Speed Tests and Profiling No throughput change is expected; the win is memory. With the launch command above and the default adaptive speculative decoding parameters, CUDA graph memory drops from **14.4 GB → 10.13 GB**. With my own serving config and adaptive speculative decoding parameters, it drops from **44.3 GB → 16 GB**, which frees the corresponding capacity for the KV cache. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process). 2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers. 3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so. - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci` 4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32356219911](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32356219911)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32356219685](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32356219685)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32356219965](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32356219965)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: Add FlashBoot load format integration
signal.text: ## Motivation Current model loading and cloning paths operate primarily at tensor granularity. The Hugging Face auto loading path loads and copies tensors individually. For large MoE models such as DSV4 Pro, the large number of expert tensors introduces substantial per-tensor overhead and makes large, contiguous I/O difficult. Existing clone implementations have a similar limitation: many small tensor transfers cannot fully utilize NVLink or RDMA bandwidth. NCCL-based cloning also incurs significant communicator setup overhead. In our DSV4 Pro experiments on GB300, NCCL communicator initialization takes more than 10 seconds, while the actual clone transfer takes only about 0.3 seconds. FlashBoot instead treats each rank-local checkpoint as a contiguous storage arena. It copies checkpoint data in large file-level blocks and rebinds model parameters to tensor views within the loaded arena. The same arena can then be cloned as large contiguous ranges over NVLink or RDMA, avoiding per-tensor loading and transfer overhead while making better use of the available link bandwidth. ## Summary - add `flashload` and `flashclone` load formats - dispatch FlashBoot loading to the external `flashboot` package from https://github.com/scitix/flashboot-release - add optional sharded-state export hooks and documentation - add `docker/Dockerfile_flashboot` for images that include FlashBoot, without changing the default `docker/Dockerfile` ## Validation - `python -m py_compile python/sglang/srt/configs/load_config.py python/sglang/srt/server_args.py python/sglang/srt/model_loader/loader.py python/sglang/srt/model_executor/model_runner.py` - `python -m json.tool docs/docs.json` - parsed `python/pyproject.toml` with `tomllib` - installed FlashBoot from `git+https://github.com/scitix/flashboot-release.git` in a local CUDA 13 / H100 environment with `FLASHBOOT_CUDA_ARCH=9.0 FB_BUILD_RDMA=auto` - imported `flashboot._C` after importing `torch` and verified the RDMA `Endpoint` binding exists - verified `get_model_loader` dispatches both `flashload` and `flashclone` to the external FlashBoot loader - checked that `docker/Dockerfile` does not contain FlashBoot install logic The PR intentionally does not vendor the FlashBoot implementation.

signal.title: [AMD] GDN linear out-proj fusion
signal.text: ## Motivation Each GatedDeltaNet (GDN) layer ends a token step with an **output gated-RMSNorm** followed by the `out_proj` linear. On AttnFP8-style Qwen3.5 checkpoints `out_proj` runs as an **a8w8 GEMM** (per-token activation × per-channel weight FP8), so the bf16 gated-RMSNorm output has to be quantized to FP8 per-token *before* the GEMM. Today that is three passes over the GDN output on the decode-adjacent critical path: gated RMSNorm → write bf16 → separate per-token activation quant → write fp8 → GEMM. The intermediate bf16 round-trip is pure overhead. This PR fuses the **gated-RMSNorm + FP8 per-token activation quant** into a single AITER kernel (`gated_rmsnorm_fp8_per_token_quant`) that emits the `(fp8, scale)` pair directly, which is fed straight into the same `out_proj` a8w8 GEMM the non-fused path uses. The numerics are identical (same weight layout, same scales) — it only removes the bf16 intermediate and the redundant standalone quant. The path is ROCm/aiter-only, auto-enabled where applicable, and a clean no-op fallback everywhere the per-layer capability check doesn't match, so default behavior is unchanged on non-AttnFP8 checkpoints. **Please be noted that this PR works along with Aiter#3844 to take effect.** ## Modifications - **`layers/quantization/fp8_utils.py`**: Add `apply_fp8_linear_aiter_prequant`, a dedicated helper for an activation that a fused producer has **already FP8-quantized**. Given `(qinput_fp8, x_scale)` it routes straight to `gemm_a8w8_bpreshuffle` using `weight.T` and per-channel `weight_scale`, mirroring the AITER per-token branch of `apply_fp8_linear` exactly (same layout/scales) but skipping the activation quant. Keeping this in its own function avoids overloading `apply_fp8_linear`'s input contract with a tuple fast-path. - **`models/qwen3_5.py`**: - Add module-level gate `_fuse_gdn_oproj` (auto-on under AITER; force off with `SGLANG_DISABLE_GDN_OUT_PROJ_FUSION=1`). - `_can_fuse_oproj` (`cached_property`): the real per-layer capability check, evaluated once on first `forward()` (weights/scales are loaded by then) and cached on the instance. It fuses only when `out_proj` is a genuine FP8 a8w8 **per-token** GEMM — detected via `Fp8LinearMethod.use_per_token_if_dynamic` **or** Quark `QuarkW8A8Fp8` `scheme.per_token` (either guarantees the pre-shuffled `bpreshuffle` weight layout) — and the weight dtype is **`torch.float8_e4m3fn`**, `head_v_dim == 128`, v-heads-per-rank ≤ 128, and the output gate is SiLU/none. The dtype is restricted to OCP `e4m3fn` (AttnFP8 weights are always `e4m3fn`; the fused kernel does not handle `fnuz`). Anything else falls back to the original path (fusing without the pre-shuffled weight would corrupt the GEMM output). - `_fused_norm_quant_out_proj`: calls the AITER `gated_rmsnorm_fp8_per_token_quant` kernel to produce `(q_fp8, q_scale)` from `core_attn_out`, `z`, `norm.weight`, and `eps`, then feeds them into `apply_fp8_linear_aiter_prequant` with `out_proj.weight` / `out_proj.weight_scale`. - `forward`: when `_can_fuse_oproj` is true, take the fused path; otherwise the original `norm` → reshape → `out_proj` path is unchanged. > Default behavior is preserved: on any checkpoint where `out_proj` is not FP8 per-token a8w8 (or shapes/gate/dtype don't match), `_can_fuse_oproj` is `False` and the original code runs. ## Usage The fusion is **on by default** on the AITER/HIP path and engages automatically for AttnFP8 checkpoints whose `out_proj` is FP8 per-token a8w8. No new flag is needed to enable it; disable it for debugging/A-B with `SGLANG_DISABLE_GDN_OUT_PROJ_FUSION=1`. ```bash SGLANG_USE_AITER=1 SGLANG_USE_AITER_FP8_PER_TOKEN=1 \ python3 -m sglang.launch_server \ --model-path /path/to/Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-MXFP4-AttnFP8 \ --trust-remote-code \ --tensor-parallel-size 2 \ --attention-backend aiter \ --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 ``` ## Accuracy Tests `lm_eval` GSM8K 5-shot, full 1319 questions, Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-**MXFP4-AttnFP8**, TP=2, aiter backend, `fp8_e4m3` KV cache, `--enable-dense-fp8 --enable-mixed-chunk`. Fusion is the only variable (`OFF` = `SGLANG_DISABLE_GDN_OUT_PROJ_FUSION=1`). To rule out single-seed sampling noise, the A/B was repeated over **3 seeds** (seed changes the 5-shot exemplar sampling): | config | strict-match (mean ± std) | flexible-extract (mean ± std) | per-seed strict | |----------------|---------------------------|-------------------------------|---------------------| | fusion **OFF** | 0.9388 ± 0.0056 | 0.9335 ± 0.0068 | 0.9378 / 0.9462 / 0.9325 | | fusion **ON** | 0.9378 ± 0.0108 | 0.9295 ± 0.0082 | 0.9409 / 0.9234 / 0.9492 | The strict-match mean gap is **+0.0010 (off − on)** — essentially zero and far below the per-seed spread (± ~0.01). ON is in fact *higher* than OFF in 2 of the 3 seeds. The fused kernel feeds the identical weight/scales into the identical GEMM, so the path is numerically equivalent — accuracy is unaffected. `lm_eval` GPQA-Diamond CoT (`gpqa_diamond_cot_zeroshot`, all 198 questions, generative chain-of-thought via the chat template, 32k generation budget so the reasoning trace completes), same checkpoint and serving config (Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-**MXFP4-AttnFP8**, TP=2, aiter backend, `fp8_e4m3` KV cache, `--enable-dense-fp8 --enable-mixed-chunk`), fusion the only variable. Metric is `exact_match` (flexible-extract). To control for sampling noise the A/B was repeated over **2 seeds** with the recommended Qwen sampling (`temperature=0.6, top_p=0.95, top_k=20`): | config | GPQA-Diamond (CoT), mean ± std | per-seed | |----------------|--------------------------------|-----------------| | fusion **OFF** | 0.8687 ± 0.0000 | 0.8687 / 0.8687 | | fusion **ON** | 0.8712 ± 0.0178 | 0.8838 / 0.8586 | The mean gap is **+0.0025 (on − off)**, far inside the ±0.018 seed-to-seed spread — statistically indistinguishable. Both arms match the official BF16 model card (GPQA **88.4**) to within ~1 point, i.e. the MXFP4-AttnFP8 quantization is effectively lossless here and the out_proj fusion does not perturb it. ## Speed Tests and Profiling TP=2, `--attention-backend aiter`, `--page-size 16`, `--chunked-prefill-size 8192`, `--mem-fraction-static 0.8`, allreduce-fusion on, tuned bf16 GEMM present, measured on our tuned serving config for this checkpoint (fused-AR-quant and `--enable-dense-fp8` both on). **Out-proj fusion is the only knob toggled** (A = OFF via `SGLANG_DISABLE_GDN_OUT_PROJ_FUSION=1`, B = ON). **Throughput is total token throughput (input+output) across the TP=2 group** (`tok/s/gpu × 2`); TPOT is median per-output-token latency. ### MXFP4-AttnFP8 — ISL/OSL = 1024/1024 (decode-bound) | concurrency | total tok/s OFF→ON | Δ throughput | median TPOT OFF→ON (ms) | Δ TPOT | |-------------|--------------------|--------------|-------------------------|--------| | 4 | 840 → 842 | +0.24% | 9.15 → 9.07 | −0.87% | | 8 | 1366 → 1376 | +0.73% | 11.36 → 11.23 | −1.14% | | 16 | 2226 → 2236 | +0.45% | 14.18 → 14.07 | −0.78% | | 32 | 3122 → 3146 | +0.77% | 20.15 → 19.98 | −0.84% | | 64 | 4306 → 4352 | +1.07% | 29.44 → 29.17 | −0.92% | ### MXFP4-AttnFP8 — ISL/OSL = 8192/1024 (prefill-heavy) | concurrency | total tok/s OFF→ON | Δ throughput | median TPOT OFF→ON (ms) | Δ TPOT | |-------------|--------------------|--------------|-------------------------|--------| | 4 | 3448 → 3482 | +0.99% | 9.87 → 9.77 | −1.01% | | 8 | 5330 → 5370 | +0.75% | 12.75 → 12.66 | −0.71% | | 16 | 7992 → 8048 | +0.70% | 17.18 → 17.02 | −0.93% | | 32 | 10426 → 10480 | +0.52% | 26.44 → 26.31 | −0.49% | | 64 | 13062 → 13138 | +0.58% | 43.03 → 42.85 | −0.42% | The fusion is a **small, consistent, no-downside win** at every concurrency on both shapes: TPOT −0.4% to −1.1% (always faster) and total throughput +0.2% to +1.1%. TTFT additionally improves **−3% to −5%** at 1k/1k (short-prompt, decode-adjacent path) and is **neutral at 8k/1k** (TTFT there is prefill-dominated, which this GDN-output fusion doesn't touch — expected). No TPOT regression anywhere. ## Checklist - [ ] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [ ] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process). 2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers. 3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so. - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci` 4. signal.title: [Fix] Spawn, don't fork, the benchmark server process
signal.text: `sglang.benchmark.*` launched the server with the platform-default start method (fork on Linux), but the parent already initializes the accelerator in ServerArgs.__post_init__ -- get_xpu_memory_capacity() calls torch.xpu.mem_get_info(), get_device_sm() calls torch.cuda.get_device_capability(). The forked child inherits a dead context and dies on its first device op: RuntimeError: Cannot re-initialize XPU in forked subprocess. launch_server() does force spawn, but only via _set_envs_and_config() once it is already running inside the child, which is too late. Use an explicit spawn context for the process itself. Latent on text-only CUDA runs, where the forked child touches the device only after handing off to spawned scheduler workers; reproducible on XPU and on any backend once the child does device work during warmup (e.g. a VLM processor's image.to(device)). Fixes #34709 <!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. --> ## Motivation sglang.benchmark.* launches the server with the default start method (fork on Linux), but the parent already initialized the accelerator in ServerArgs.__post_init__ (XPU: torch.xpu.mem_get_info(); CUDA: torch.cuda.get_device_capability()). The forked child inherits a dead context and fails on its first device op: RuntimeError: Cannot re-initialize XPU in forked subprocess. launch_server() forces spawn, but only from inside the already-forked child (entrypoints/engine.py:1703) — too late. Latent on text-only CUDA (the child does no device work before spawning scheduler workers); fatal on XPU, and on any backend once the child touches the device during warmup (e.g. a VLM processor's image.to(device)). ## Modifications endpoint.py: launch_or_reuse_server() — create the server process with an explicit spawn context: proc = multiprocessing.get_context("spawn").Process(...) Payload is picklable; the child already expects spawn semantics. ## Accuracy Tests N/A — no kernel/model-forward change; outputs bit-identical. Verified on Nvidia GPU and Intel XPU backend environment. ## Speed Tests and Profiling No inference-path impact. Spawn adds a few seconds of one-time startup cost, outside every measurement window (benchmarks start only after server_is_up()). ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:no_entry_sign: [Run #32327811322](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32327811322)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32327811154](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32327811154)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32327811318](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32327811318)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [diffusion] MiniMax-H3 Spectrum skip-step + fused RMSNorm/AdaLN
signal.text: ## Summary Wires training-free Spectrum skip-step into MiniMax-H3 and fuses RMSNorm + indexed AdaLN. On one 24GB GPU, 50-step BF16+FA (**1008.6 s**) drops to **285.3 s (3.53×)** with exact attention, up to **219.0 s (4.61×)** with Sage→Sol hybrid + Spectrum. 1344×768 · 107 frames · 50 NFE · same process: warmup (seed 0) → timed (seed 42), timed only. PSNR is per-frame vs the **same-tree** INT8+FA video (Spectrum off). | Config | timed e2e | vs BF16+FA | PSNR mean / min | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | | BF16 + FlashAttention (baseline) | 1008.6 s | 1.00× | — | | `kitchen_int8` + FA (Spectrum off) | 718.5 s | 1.40× | — | | **`kitchen_int8` + FA + Spectrum `11/5/1.0`** — recommend | **285.3 s** | **3.53×** | **27.37 / 25.28** | | `kitchen_int8` + FA + Spectrum `15/5/0` | 387.4 s | 2.60× | 30.82 / 28.69 | | `kitchen_int8` + `sage_attn` + Spectrum `15/5/0` | 245.3 s | 4.11× | 23.56 / 21.01 | | `kitchen_int8` + Sage→Sol hybrid + Spectrum `15/5/0.5` | **219.0 s** | **4.61×** | 20.57 / 17.75 | | *(external reference)* ComfyUI INT8 workflow | 752.6 s | 1.34× |- | ComfyUI is a 24GB yardstick only. Same-INT8 gap is 752.6 vs 718.5 s (**1.05×**). ## Motivation [#34581](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/34581) already moved the 24GB path onto `kitchen_int8` + FlashAttention (~14 s/step). H3's default is **50 steps**, so the remaining cost is running the 50-layer stack every step (~12 min). Cache-DiT (`quality="high"`) is the in-tree skip-compute for multi-GPU H3, but it cannot combine with `--dit-layerwise-offload`, so a 24GB card that must stream the DiT cannot use it. On the audited 4×H200 recipe it is also only 1.40× and still walks the first blocks. Spectrum ([arxiv:2603.01623](https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.01623)) is already wired for FLUX.1 / Wan / HunyuanVideo / SD3: it forecasts DiT features and **skips the whole stack**, and it works with layerwise offload. H3 could not use it because the packed sequence is not a uniform video stream. ## Modifications ### 1. Spectrum on MiniMax-H3 Opt-in via `--enable-spectrum`. Off path does not enter the mixin — bit-exact vs today's H3. - Forecast only the packed **target** suffix: contiguous target audio immediately before `infer_out_pos` video. Earlier reference-audio rows are dropped (Wan2GP `hidden[audio_start:]`). - Comfy blends: **audio hold** (0), **video lerp 0.5**. - History on CPU, default `history_size` 100 → **8** (24GB). - `layer_names = ["blocks", "token_refiner.blocks"]` so a skip is the 50-layer stack, not a Cache-DiT wrap. Works with DiT layerwise offload. - Fail-closed with `quality="high"` / `enable_cache_dit`, and with sequence-parallel `sp_ws > 1`. Generic Spectrum defaults (`warmup=5, window=2, flex=0.75`) are the 20 NFE row. H3's model default is 50 steps; **`warmup=5` is a quality cliff there**. The recommended 50-step schedule is `11 / 5 / 1.0` (all frames >25 dB vs FA). Sage / Sol + Spectrum is faster but the PSNR ceiling is the attention backend (~23.6 dB vs FA at 50 NFE). If the bar is "looks like FA", keep `fa`. ### 2. Fused RMSNorm + indexed AdaLN `fused_indexed_rmsnorm_scale_shift` writes `RMSNorm(x) * (1+scale[idx]) + shift[idx]` without materializing the normalized tensor. Gate: BF16, not `torch.compile`; otherwise the existing eager modulate. Lossless (1 ULP; `mean|Δ|≈2e-8`). Exclusive 20 NFE INT8+FA: 290.8 → **289.7 s** (−1.06 s, ~0.3%). Same kernel every step, so ~−2.3 s at 50 NFE. On whenever the Triton path matches; no flag. ## Accuracy Tests Same prompt and seed (42). First pair is 50 NFE, exact attention; the Spectrum row is the recommend schedule. Second pair is 20 NFE library defaults. **`kitchen_int8` + FA, 50 NFE — 718.5 s** **`kitchen_int8` + FA + Spectrum `11/5/1.0`, 50 NFE — 285.3 s (27.4 dB)** **`kitchen_int8` + FA + Spectrum `5/2/0.75`, 20 NFE — 189.5 s (25.6 dB)** ## Example Exact-attention recommend (**3.53×** vs BF16) — INT8 Linear, FlashAttention, Spectrum `11/5/1.0`: ```bash pip install comfy-kitchen # required only for --quantization kitchen_int8 sglang generate \ --model-path MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3 \ --model-variant fl2va \ --quantization kitchen_int8 \ --attention-backend fa \ --enable-spectrum \ --spectrum-warmup-steps 11 \ --spectrum-window-size 5 \ --spectrum-flex-window 1.0 \ --performance-mode memory \ --layerwise-offload-components dit,text_encoder \ --dit-offload-prefetch-size 1 \ --dit-layerwise-resident-layers 0 \ --enable-torch-compile false \ --prompt "A cat walking on a sunny beach, gentle waves." \ --save-output ``` Speed ceiling (**4.61×** vs BF16) — same offload, Sage→Sol hybrid on the DiT and Spectrum `15/5/0.5`. Approximate attention; PSNR 20.6 / 17.8 dB vs FA. ```bash sglang generate \ --model-path MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3 \ --model-variant fl2va \ --quantization kitchen_int8 \ --attention-backend sol_attn \ --attention-backend-config dense_backend=sage_attn,dense_steps=10 \ --component-attention-backends text_encoder=torch_sdpa,transformer=sol_attn \ --enable-spectrum \ --spectrum-warmup-steps 15 \ --spectrum-window-size 5 \ --spectrum-flex-window 0.5 \ --performance-mode memory \ --layerwise-offload-components dit,text_encoder \ --dit-offload-prefetch-size 1 \ --dit-layerwise-resident-layers 0 \ --enable-torch-compile false \ --prompt "A cat walking on a sunny beach, gentle waves." \ --save-output ``` `--layerwise-offload-components` omits `vae` (same as #34581). Omit `--enable-spectrum` and the three `--spectrum-*` flags for the 718 s INT8+FA path. At 20 NFE, `--enable-spectrum` alone is enough (library defaults). Drop `--quantization` for BF16. ## Benchmarking and Profiling RTX 4090 D 24GB · CUDA 13.0 · 1344×768 / 107 frames / euler · `torch.compile` and Cache-DiT **disabled** · load → warmup (seed 0) → timed (seed 42), **timed pass only**. Cross-framework PSNR vs Comfy (~16 dB) is TE NVFP4 vs BF16 — not a quality column. The `kitchen_int8` SwiGLU fuse (`int8_linear(input_act=swiglu)`) is **not** on in these numbers. Released `comfy-kitchen==0.2.26` leaves `silu*up` in fp32 and rewrites INT8 rows (50 NFE vs unfused: **22.0 / 19.8 dB** — a different sample). [comfy-kitchen#124](https://github.com/Comfy-Org/comfy-kitchen/pull/124) rounds to the storage dtype first; fc2 is then bit-exact and the fuse is about **−4.4 s / 20 NFE** (~−10 s at 50). Leave it off until that lands. Results are in the table at the top. Text encoding and VAE decode are unchanged; Spectrum only skips selected DiT stacks. ## Checklist - [ ] Format code with pre-commit hooks - [ ] Unit tests: `test_minimax_h3_spectrum.py` - [ ] Default (`--enable-spectrum` omitted) unchanged - [ ] Cookbook + `spectrum.mdx` list MiniMax-H3 and the 50-step schedule - [ ] Benchmark and PSNR vs same-tree FA included above <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32355274217](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32355274217)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32355273961](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32355273961)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32355274147](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32355274147)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: fix(npu): split packed MTP HiCache transfers by pool
signal.text: > [!IMPORTANT] > For standalone Ascend HiCache validation, this PR branch bundles the complete > commit history of #32500 through `#32500@9acc6b733`. Users can fork this branch > and run it directly without fetching another PR. For upstream review and > merge, #32500 should still land first; GitHub will then remove the shared > commits from this PR's diff. #34560 is already merged into `main`. End-to-end > Qwen3.6 validation also uses the checkpoint semantic fix in #35086, but that > PR is not included in this branch. Recommended merge order: #32500, #35086, > then this PR. ## Motivation After #34560, the HiCache host K/V layer dimension includes both the target model layers and the NEXTN/MTP draft layers. #32500 adds the Ascend fused `transfer_kv_dim_exchange` path for `page_first_direct`, but that path invokes the operator once with the target device pool and the full packed host buffer. On Ascend, the target and draft K/V layers are separate device pools. A single invocation therefore pairs a target-only device buffer with a `target + draft` host-layer range, so the draft K/V layers are not transferred through the matching device pool. CUDA does not have this mismatch. Its existing path packs target and draft per-layer pointers into one pointer array, and the per-layer transfer kernels map each host layer to the corresponding device pointer. The Ascend fused operator accepts one contiguous device pool per invocation, so each pool must be transferred separately. ## Minimal reproduction Apply #32500 on top of a revision that contains #34560, then launch Qwen3.6-27B on Ascend with the following relevant options: ```text --tp-size 2 --attention-backend ascend --device npu --page-size 128 --enable-hierarchical-cache --hicache-write-policy write_through --hicache-storage-backend mooncake --hicache-storage-prefetch-policy wait_complete --speculative-algorithm NEXTN --speculative-num-steps 3 --speculative-eagle-topk 1 --speculative-num-draft-tokens 4 ``` 1. Generate from a 3000-token prompt to populate HiCache. 2. For L2, generate a separate 6000-token filler to evict the original prefix from L1, then replay the original prompt. 3. For L3, wait for write-through completion, call `/flush_cache`, then replay the original prompt. 4. Request `return_cached_tokens_details` and inspect the target/draft transfer at the first `kernel_ascend` H2D or D2H operation. Without this change, the fused operation receives the full packed host layer range with only the target device pool. The draft pool is not transferred by a matching invocation. ## Changes - Skip CUDA-style packed device pointer arrays for the Ascend MTP path. - Iterate over the target pool and every draft pool on Ascend. - Slice the packed host K/V buffer to the layer range that belongs to each device pool. - Invoke `transfer_kv_dim_exchange` once per pool for both H2D and D2H. - Add focused tests for Ascend initialization and target/draft host-layer slicing. - Bundle all #32500 commits through `9acc6b733` so this fork branch is directly runnable for Ascend HiCache validation. Focused validation: - latest `upstream/main`: `2 passed` - exact branch head with `#32500@9acc6b733`: `3 passed, 17 deselected` - complete stacked focused tests with #35086: `8 passed` - pre-commit on both changed files: passed ## L2/L3 replay validation Validation stack: latest `main` with #34560, `#32500@9acc6b733`, #35086, and this fix. The first mismatch positions were `[217, 322, 293, 58]` for both L2 and L3. Since the L2 and L3 replays match each other exactly, Mooncake L3 does not introduce an additional divergence. #35086 fixes the packed Mamba checkpoint index; the remaining cold/replay divergence is the separate cold-prefill persistence-boundary issue described in #33515. ## Accuracy validation Ran the repository's `benchmark/gsm8k/bench_sglang.py` against the same NEXTN + Mooncake service using the first 200 examples from the official GSM8K test set: ```text num_questions=200 num_shots=5 parallel=4 temperature=0 max_new_tokens=512 chat_template_kwargs={"enable_thinking": false} ``` Result on the complete stack: `194/200` correct (`97.0%` accuracy), `0%` invalid responses, no request failures, and `218.519 s` latency.
