signal.title: [Diffusion][Refactor] Refactor and unify RoPE execution for DiT models using RotaryEmbedding based on CustomOp
signal.text:
## Motivation Currently, DiT models across SGLang call various ad-hoc functions to apply Rotary Position Embeddings. The choice of function depends on the target hardware device, argument types, and model-specific configurations. Furthermore, internal branches within these functions often perform device type checks again, leading to code fragmentation and duplication. To clean up and unify this behavior, this PR leverages SGLang's existing `CustomOp` mechanism to enhance the core `RotaryEmbedding` class located in `sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/layers/rotary_embedding/base.py`. This abstraction allows models to invoke RoPE through a single, unified interface without writing device-specific handling inside model code, significantly simplifying codebase maintainability and cross-platform execution. ## Modifications This PR is a continuation of [PR #31453](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/31453). Modified 5 key files to implement unified RoPE dispatch and propagate complex frequencies: ### 1. `python/sglang/multimodal_gen/configs/pipeline_configs/qwen_image.py` - Updated `get_freqs_cis()` to return both standard `cos_sin_cache` tuples (`freqs_cis`) and pre-calculated complex frequency tuples (`freqs_complex`). - Propagated `freqs_complex` through `_prepare_cond_kwargs` and pipeline stages. - Added Sequence Parallelism sharding for `img_complex` via `shard_rotary_emb_for_sp()`, enabling pre-computed complex frequencies to be passed directly to the Qwen Image DiT model. ### 2. `python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/layers/rotary_embedding/base.py` - Implemented `forward_npu`, `forward_cuda`, and `forward_native` backend methods inside the `RotaryEmbedding`. - Extended signatures to flexibly accept any RoPE inputs: `complex_freqs`, `cos`/`sin`, or 2D `cos_sin_cache`. - Integrated unified dispatching across lower-level implementations: - `_apply_rotary_emb_complex` (for complex multiplication). - `_apply_rotary_emb` (for standard PyTorch RoPE). - `apply_flashinfer_rope_qk_inplace` (for optimized CUDA execution). - Standardized tensor dimension expectations: `query` and `key` as 4D `[batch, seq_len, num_heads, head_size]`, `complex_freqs` as 3D `[num_tokens, 1, head_size // 2]`, and `cos`/`sin` as 2D `[num_tokens, head_size // 2]`. ### 3. `python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/layers/layernorm.py` - Added optional `freqs_complex` parameter to `apply_qk_norm_rope` and `apply_qk_norm_with_optional_rope`. - Replaced FlashInfer calls in the fallback path with the unified `RotaryEmbedding`. - Preserved the existing CUDA fused QK-Norm + RoPE kernel (`fused_inplace_qknorm_rope`) to ensure zero performance regression on CUDA. ### 4. `python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/models/dits/mova_video_dit.py` - Refactored `SelfAttention.forward` to implement the usage of `RotaryEmbedding`. ### 5. `python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/models/dits/qwen_image.py` - Updated `QwenImageCrossAttention` to extract `freqs_complex` from `cross_attention_kwargs`. - Passed `img_complex` and `txt_complex` into `apply_qk_norm_with_optional_rope`, enabling Qwen Image DiT cross-attention layers to leverage complex RoPE. ### 6. `python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/models/dits/glm_image.py` - Updated `GlmImageAttention` with `RotaryEmbedding` class usage. - Replaced the `_apply_rotary_emb` and `apply_flashinfer_rope_qk_inplace` functions with `self.rotary_emb()` call . ### 7. `python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/models/dits/flux.py` - Updated `FluxAttention` with `complex_freqs` computing and forwarding them into `apply_qk_norm_with_optional_rope`. ### 8. `python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/models/dits/flux_2.py` - Updated `Flux2Attention` with `complex_freqs` computing and forwarding them into `apply_qk_norm_with_optional_rope`. ### 9. `python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/models/dits/joy_image.py` - Updated `MMDoubleStreamBlock` with `complex_freqs` computing and forwarding them into `apply_qk_norm_with_optional_rope`. ## Tests The changes were tested on openmoss/MOVA-360p, GLM-Image, black-forest-labs/FLUX.1-dev, unsloth/FLUX.2-dev, jd-opensource/JoyAI-Image-Edit-Diffusers, nv-community/Cosmos3-Super-Text2Image and MusePublic/Qwen-image models.
Accuracy test, speed tests and profiling for Mova ### Mova video generation (the same as before changes): https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/396ce85d-df45-432a-a7bf-6d87b1fdb6ee ### 1. SGLang Server Launch Command ```bash sglang serve --model-path $(pwd)/mova_video_360p --pipeline-class-name MOVAPipeline --num-gpus 4 --ring-degree 1 --ulysses-degree 4 --performance-mode memory --dit-layerwise-offload --dit-offload-prefetch-size 0.1 --text-encoder-cpu-offload true --vae-cpu-offload true --enable-torch-compile --warmup-mode server --vae-tiling --vae-sp ``` ### 2. Video Generation Request ```bash curl -X POST "http://localhost:30000/v1/videos" -F "prompt=A curious raccoon" -F "input_reference=@/.../images/raccoon.png" -F "size=640x352" -F "num_frames=49" -F "fps=24" -F "num_inference_steps=25" -F "guidance_scale=5.0" -o create_video.json ``` ### 3. Offline Profiling Command ```bash SGLANG_DIFFUSION_TORCH_PROFILER_DIR="" sglang generate --model-path --pipeline-class-name MOVAPipeline --prompt "A curious raccoon" --image-path --width 640 --height 352 --num-frames 49 --fps 24 --num-inference-steps 25 --guidance-scale 5.0 --profile --num-profiled-timesteps 10 --num-gpus 4 --ulysses-degree 4 --enable-torch-compile --warmup-mode request --dit-layerwise-offload --dit-offload-prefetch-size 0.1 ``` ### 4. Profiler Latency Results (Ascend NPU) The table below compares the detailed execution times of the rope functions on NPU before and after modifications: | Implementation | func_name | time(%) | total_time(us) | num_calls | Avg(us) | Min(us) | Max(us) | | :--- | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | | **Baseline** | rope_apply_head_dim | 100 | 8546089.76 | 3080 | 2774.7045 | 2358.73 | 5281.49 | | **Modified** | _apply_rotary_emb_complex | 100 | 8414414.11 | 3080 | 2731.9526 | 2097.39 | 7318.95 |
Accuracy test, speed tests and profiling for QwenImage ### QwenImage image generation (the same as before changes): ### 1. Image Generation Command ```bash SGLANG_CACHE_DIT_ENABLED=true sglang generate --model-path $(pwd)/qwen_image --model-id qwen-image --num-gpus 4 --tp-size 4 --text-encoder-cpu-offload true --vae-cpu-offload true --prompt "A coffee shop entrance features a chalkboard sign reading Qwen." --warmup-mode request --save-output ``` ### 2. Offline Profiling Command ```bash SGLANG_DIFFUSION_TORCH_PROFILER_DIR="" SGLANG_CACHE_DIT_ENABLED=true sglang generate --model-path $(pwd)/qwen_image --model-id qwen-image --num-gpus 4 --tp-size 4 --text-encoder-cpu-offload true --vae-cpu-offload true --prompt "A coffee shop entrance features a chalkboard sign reading Qwen." --width 1024 --height 1024 --profile --num-profiled-timesteps 10 --warmup-mode request ``` ### 3. Bench Serving Commands #### Server: ```bash SGLANG_CACHE_DIT_ENABLED=true sglang serve --model-path $(pwd)/qwen_image --model-id qwen-image --num-gpus 4 --tp-size 4 --text-encoder-cpu-offload true --vae-cpu-offload true --port 30000 ``` #### Request: ```bash python3 -m sglang.multimodal_gen.benchmarks.bench_serving --backend sglang-image --dataset vbench --task text-to-image --num-prompts 10 --max-concurrency 1 --port 30000 ``` ### 4. Profiler Latency Results (Ascend NPU) The table below compares the detailed execution times of the rope functions on NPU before and after modifications: | Implementation | func_name | time(%) | total_time(us) | num_calls | Avg(us) | Min(us) | Max(us) | | :--- | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | | **Baseline** | apply_rotary_embedding_native | 100 | 13628501.78 | 2448 | 5567.1984 | 4108.45 | 12372.26 | | **Modified** | _apply_rotary_emb_complex | 100 | 9655076.15 | 2448 | 3944.0671 | 2750.82 | 8124 | | **Baseline** | apply_qk_norm_with_optional_rope | 100 | 23891794.86 | 1224 | 19519.4402 | 15016.6 | 39062.05 | | **Modified** | apply_qk_norm_with_optional_rope | 100 | 14707268.69 | 1224 | 12015.7424 | 8519.32 | 20765.84 | There the `apply_rotary_embedding_native` and `_apply_rotary_emb_complex` functions are imlementing the RoPE logic and the `apply_qk_norm_with_optional_rope` is the common place where they're being called. ### 5. signal.title: [AMD] DeepSeek-V4 MI355X: eliminate bpreshuffle fp8-scale copies at producer sites (MoE down, MLA o_proj bmm)
signal.text: ## Summary Follow-up to the dense-linear bpreshuffle scale no-copy. Several DeepSeek-V4 sites **pre-quantize** an activation and hand a `(fp8, scale)` tuple to a downstream Linear; those scales are emitted row-major and then relaid out with `materialize_bpreshuffle_fp8_scale` — a relayout **copy per site, per layer** on MI355X (gfx950). This PR eliminates those copies for the producer quant kernels that honor `transpose_scale`, via a zero-copy `torch.as_strided` reinterpret. ## What changed - **`python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/fp8_utils.py`** — one producer-neutral `view_aiter_fused_rms_transposed_fp8_scale` (+ `_tuple`) helper: the zero-copy stride reinterpret of a scale a quant kernel already emitted with `transpose_scale=True`. This **consolidates** the identical `view_aiter_fused_rms_transposed_fp8_scale` that landed on main in #31727 with this PR's producer helper (both were `as_strided(scale, scale.shape, (1, scale.shape[0]))`) into a single operation, keeping the established #31727 name for consistency. Also adds `emit_transposed_bpreshuffle_scale(m, on_bpreshuffle_gfx95=...)`, centralizing the shared `M >= 2` emit gate. - **`python/sglang/srt/models/deepseek_v4.py`** — fused-RMS producer repointed to the consolidated helper. - **`python/sglang/srt/models/deepseek_v2.py`** — MLP down-proj input producer (`fused_clamp_act_mul`): request `transpose_scale=True` and reinterpret instead of copy (gated `M>=2`). - **`python/sglang/srt/models/deepseek_common/attention_forward_methods/forward_mla_rocm.py`** — o_proj bmm producers ×2 in `rocm_absorb_v_bmm` (`fused_flatten_fp8_group_quant`): same treatment. (ROCm MLA now dispatches here after the recent `forward_mla_rocm.py` split; the optimization was moved off `forward_mla.py`, which is back to matching upstream, so it lands on the actual MI355X call path.) Sites fed by `fused_rms_fp8_group_quant` follow the same helper now (the #31727 fix made that kernel honor `transpose_scale`). ## Tests - **CPU** (`test_fp8_bpreshuffle_scale.py`) — helper-level stride/no-copy contract, and the centralized `emit_transposed_bpreshuffle_scale` gate incl. the `M == 1` materialize fallback. - **MI35X GPU** (`test_fp8_bpreshuffle_producer_mi35x.py`, `stage-b-test-1-gpu-small-amd-mi35x`) — invokes **both real producers** (`fused_clamp_act_mul`, `fused_flatten_fp8_group_quant`) with `transpose_scale=True` + no-copy vs `transpose_scale=False` + materialize, asserting bit-identical quantized output, equal scale values, the `(1, M)` column-major stride, and zero-copy storage sharing (M ∈ {1, 2, 8, 16}; M==1 exercises the materialize fallback). This is the direct producer-level equivalence evidence — the invariant the optimization relies on, checked on the real kernels rather than a fabricated layout. ## Validation Model: `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro`. Hardware: MI355X (gfx950), TP8. Image: `rocm/sgl-dev:v0.5.16-rocm720-mi35x-20260731`. Env: `SGLANG_USE_AITER=1 AITER_BF16_FP8_MOE_BOUND=0 SGLANG_HACK_FLASHMLA_BACKEND=unified_kv_triton`. ### Accuracy (GSM8K, 1319 questions × 2 runs) | run | baseline | patched | |----:|:--------:|:-------:| | 1 | 0.942 | 0.933 | | 2 | 0.939 | 0.931 | The patched runs sit ~0.8–0.9 pt below baseline. With only two runs per arm this is consistent with, but does not by itself establish, DeepSeek-V4 fp4-MoE run-to-run noise. The correctness guarantee for this PR comes instead from the **producer-level bit-exact test** above: the converted kernels emit identical quantized output and scale values on both paths, so the reroute cannot change the model result. (Happy to add more GSM8K reps if useful.) ### Perf (random 8k/1k, `--random-range-ratio 1.0`, seed 42) — preliminary **Single-shot, one run per arm — treat as preliminary, not an established speedup.** The Δ below (≈ ±0.4–0.8%) is within DeepSeek-V4 decode run-to-run noise at these concurrencies and is not backed by repeated A/B runs, so I'm not claiming it as a confirmed win. The correctness/no-regression guarantee for this PR is the **producer-level bit-exact test** above (identical quantized output + scale values on both paths); the value here is eliminating a per-site/per-layer relayout copy, which these numbers are consistent with but do not by themselves prove. signal.title: [RFC] Integrating Ascend MemCache as an HiCache L3 Backend
signal.text: ## 1. Summary This RFC proposes an Ascend MemCache-backed L3 storage backend for SGLang HiCache. SGLang preserves its existing hierarchy: L1 resides in NPU HBM, L2 resides in local host DRAM, and L3 is a distributed memory pool provided by MemCache. Radix Cache and HiCache Controller continue to own prefix matching, page lifetime, and tier migration. MemCache owns object metadata, cross-process addressing, and host/device data transfer. The backend implements the existing `HiCacheStorage` interface and uses `batch_exists`, `batch_get`, and `batch_set` for batched page lookup, read, and write. Its data plane uses MemFabric transport protocols and reuses pages already allocated in the HiCache host KV pool, avoiding serialization of KV tensors into Python bytes. We have validated the initial MHA/MLA path on Ascend NPU and evaluated Qwen3-32B-W8A8 for accuracy and performance. The same architecture will be extended to the cache layouts required by DeepSeek V4, hybrid Qwen3.x models, GLM-5.x, and Kimi K3. --- ## 2. Motivation Long-context and high-concurrency inference produce large KV caches. NPU HBM provides the lowest latency but limited capacity. L2 expands capacity with local host DRAM, but remains local to one instance. Once a page is evicted from L2, or when a request with the same prefix is routed to another instance, the service must recompute the prefix. This cost is particularly visible with long system prompts, multi-turn conversations, shared document prefixes, and multi-replica or Prefill/Decode deployments. Repeated prefill directly increases TTFT and consumes compute capacity that could otherwise process new tokens. HiCache already defines L1, L2, and L3 semantics, but Ascend requires an L3 backend that understands NPU/host memory, supports batched object operations, and uses Ascend transfer primitives. Ascend MemCache, built on MemFabric, provides a distributed memory pool, MetaService, object APIs, and data paths such as `device_sdma` and `host_shm`, making it suitable for HiCache L3. The integration changes only where cache pages are stored and how they are restored. It does not change the attention algorithm, Radix Cache matching, or model computation. If restored cache values are identical, it introduces no additional numerical approximation. --- ## 3. Goals - Provide an Ascend HiCache L3 backend enabled by `--hicache-storage-backend ascend_memcache`. - Reuse `HiCacheStorage` and HiCache Controller instead of creating a MemCache-specific prefix cache or scheduler. - Use batched lookup and transfer to reduce per-page RPC, Python scheduling, and unnecessary copies. - Support MHA/MLA layouts used by the current Ascend host KV pool, including `page_first_kv_split`. - Isolate TP-rank objects correctly and define a clear key extension path for DCP, PP, and cross-instance sharing. - Treat temporary MemCache or MetaService unavailability as an L3 miss so L1/L2 and normal inference continue. - Define verifiable tests for real L3 hits, accuracy, and performance. --- ## 4. Non-Goals - Replacing Mooncake, file, HF3FS, or other existing HiCache L3 backends. - Changing prefix matching or eviction semantics in Radix Cache and Unified Radix Cache. - Claiming automatic compatibility with every model architecture. A model is supported only after all required cache states can be exported and restored correctly. --- ## 5. Design ### 5.1. Architecture Overview ```text ┌──────────────────────────────── SGLang Worker ────────────────────────────────┐ │ │ │ Radix / Unified Radix Cache │ │ │ │ │ HiCache Controller │ │ │ │ │ ┌───────┴────────┐ │ │ │ │ │ │ L1 NPU HBM L2 Host KV Pool │ │ │ │ │ AscendMemcacheStore │ └───────────────────────┼───────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ │ object metadata + memory descriptors ▼ ┌───────────────────────┐ │ MemCache MetaService │ └───────────┬───────────┘ │ ┌───────────▼───────────┐ │ MemFabric Data Plane │ │ host_shm/device_sdma │ └───────────┬───────────┘ ▼ Distributed L3 Pool ``` HiCache Controller decides when to back up L2 pages to L3 and when to prefetch L3 pages for a matching prefix. `AscendMemcacheStore` translates these operations into MemCache object operations. MetaService manages object placement and node information, while MemFabric moves the data. Each TP rank creates an independent MemCache client and processes its local cache shard. Ranks share prefix semantics, but keys contain rank and parallel-configuration information so different shards cannot overwrite each other. ### 5.2. Memory Registration and Buffer Metadata HiCache L2 pages reside in the host KV pool. For memory directly accessible by the selected MemFabric protocol, `AscendMemcacheStore` submits page addresses, lengths, and buffer metadata without serializing data into Python bytes. `page_first_direct` locates a logical page in one contiguous buffer. With `page_first_kv_split`, K/V or MLA data for one logical page may live in multiple physical buffers. The backend registers every relevant buffer and describes each page with correct offsets and lengths. Registration lifetime covers asynchronous `batch_set` and `batch_get`; a page cannot be released or reused before I/O completes. Zero-copy is valid only for registered address ranges understood by MemFabric. If an address type, alignment, or object size violates protocol constraints, the backend must not pass the invalid pointer to a native API. Unsupported combinations return a clear error during initialization or initial layout validation. ### 5.3. Storage Interface `AscendMemcacheStore` implements the following HiCache L3 operations: ```text batch_exists(keys) -> test whether cache pages exist batch_set(keys, pages) -> write L2 pages into L3 batch_get(keys, pages) -> restore L3 pages into target L2 buffers ``` Control messages carry keys, object information, and memory descriptors. KV tensors travel through the MemFabric data plane. Batched operations inspect and restore multiple consecutive pages without a per-page call bottleneck. `batch_set` runs asynchronously in the HiCache backup worker. Pages remain pinned until transfer completes. `batch_get` runs in the prefetch path, and HiCache exposes tokens as hits only after complete pages have been restored successfully. ### 5.4. Cache Key and Parallelism L3 keys must distinguish models, cache formats, and parallel shards. The current key covers at least a model identifier, page or prefix hash, TP rank, and page ordinal. To prevent incompatible services from sharing objects, the schema should additionally include cache-layout version, dtype, quantization mode, TP size, DCP size/rank, and PP rank. Process-local information such as virtual addresses and PIDs cannot be part of persistent keys. Two instances may share L3 objects only when model weights, cache layout, and parallel sharding match. Until DCP-aware keys are implemented, combining L3 with `dcp_size > 1` should fail explicitly rather than silently collide. ### 5.5. Write and Restore Flow The write flow is: 1. Radix Cache identifies complete cacheable pages. 2. HiCache Controller pins the pages and enqueues backup work. 3. `AscendMemcacheStore` builds keys and memory descriptors and invokes `batch_set`. 4. MemCache stores the objects and updates metadata. 5. Page pins are released after I/O; write failure does not invalidate existing L1/L2 data. The restore flow is: 1. Radix Cache completes local L1/L2 prefix matching. 2. HiCache invokes `batch_exists` for remaining candidate pages and finds the longest continuous L3 prefix. 3. HiCache reserves destination L2 pages and invokes `batch_get`. 4. Fully restored pages return to NPU HBM through the existing L2-to-L1 path. 5. The scheduler skips only successfully restored prefix tokens; failed pages are recomputed. ### 5.6. Configuration and Deployment The backend uses existing HiCache arguments: ```bash python3 -m sglang.launch_server \ --model-path /path/to/model \ --device npu \ --attention-backend ascend \ --enable-hierarchical-cache \ --hicache-storage-backend ascend_memcache \ --hicache-ratio 2.0 \ --hicache-storage-prefetch-policy timeout \ --hicache-storage-backend-extra-config \ '{"meta_service_url":"tcp://127.0.0.1:5000", "config_store_url":"tcp://127.0.0.1:6000", "protocol":"device_sdma", "prefetch_threshold":128, "dram_size":"50GB"}' ``` MetaService starts before SGLang workers connect. The protocol is selected according to memory placement and topology, not performance expectations alone. For example, `device_sdma` requires device mappings and target memory compatible with MemFabric. A configuration-file environment variable and trace/debug controls support deployment and diagnosis. --- ## 6. Evaluation We evaluate Qwen3-32B-W8A8 with TP2 and `page_first_kv_split` on Ascend NPU. ### 6.1. Accuracy The accuracy experiment uses 200 GSM8K samples: | Configuration | Accuracy | Invalid rate | Total time | Output throughput | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | | HiCache disabled | 0.835 | 0.000 | 606.545 s | 98.032 token/s | | MemCache L3 enabled | 0.825 | 0.000 | 582.603 s | 101.762 token/s | Both runs have an invalid rate of zero, and we observe no systematic output error caused by L3 data movement. The dataset-score difference requires more samples and token-by-token equality tests; one GSM8K run alone does not establish complete equivalence. ### 6.2. Prefix-Reuse Performance The performance experiment uses an average input length of approximately 3.5K tokens and a fixed output length of 100 tokens: | Configuration | Average E2EL | Average TTFT | Average TPOT | Average per-request output rate | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | | HiCache disabled | 18011.7 ms | 6120.7 ms | 120.1 ms | 5.734 token/s | | MemCache L3 enabled | 12826.0 ms | 3601.4 ms | 93.2 ms | 8.179 token/s | | Change | -28.8% | -41.2% | -22.4% | +42.6% | For requests reusing a sufficiently long cached prefix, restore can cost less than recomputing prefill. Actual gains depend on a real L3 hit, hit length, transfer bandwidth, concurrency, and background-backup overhead. --- ## 7. Future Work ### 7.1. Model Support We will extend support to the following model families: - **DeepSeek V4 family:** support its MLA/DSA cache layouts, including L3 persistence and restore of sparse-attention metadata and speculative-decoding auxiliary states. - **Qwen3.x family:** cover regular MHA/GQA models and hybrid models containing Mamba/SSM or linear-attention states. - **GLM-5.x family:** support MLA/DSA, `page_first_kv_split`, and auxiliary states produced by NEXTN and other speculative-decoding methods. - **Kimi K3:** add L3 write and restore for the cache states required by its actual attention and cache layout in SGLang. Each model family must pass baseline-output validation, a real L3 hit after L1/L2 eviction, and token-by-token greedy-decoding equality. A model is marked supported only when every cache state required for inference can be stored and restored correctly. ### 7.2. PP and DCP Parallelism Support The current cache key and page management primarily target TP. Future work will support Pipeline Parallelism (PP) and Decode Context Parallelism (DCP). PP support will add the pipeline rank or equivalent layer-ownership information to L3 keys. Each stage will write and restore only its locally owned cache layers, and objects belonging to the same prefix but different PP stages will remain isolated. DCP support will add `dcp_size` and `dcp_rank` to keys and persist pages by DCP shard. Lookup and restore must preserve shard consistency. Until this support is complete, combining L3 with `dcp_size > 1` should fail explicitly at startup to prevent different DCP ranks from reading or writing the same object. PP and DCP qualification will cover each strategy independently and in combination with TP. Tests will verify consistent L3 hit-page counts across ranks, correct restored cache content, and model output equal to the HiCache-disabled baseline.

signal.title: [Bug] NIXL/UCX prefill segfault (nixlUcxSharedThread -> cuEventQuery) is not fixed — reproduces on v0.5.17 / CUDA 13.0 / B200; #23489 and #23499 were closed without a root cause
signal.text: ## Summary The NIXL/UCX prefill segfault reported in #23489 and #23499 is **not fixed**. Both issues were closed without a root cause — #23489 same-day as "Resolved via rebase", #23499 with no linked PR or commit — and #23499 already has an unanswered 2026-07-07 comment from someone hitting it again on a different GPU/CUDA/SGLang combination. We reproduce it today on **v0.5.17 / CUDA 13.0 / B200 x86**, and we have traced it to a missing CUDA context in NIXL's UCX progress thread. Filing separately here because SGLang's `num_threads = 8` choice for prefill is what exposes every NIXL PD user to it, while decode's `0` makes decode immune. Upstream issue: https://github.com/ai-dynamo/nixl/issues/2102 ## Reproduction Production 8×B200 host, both roles co-located: - prefill: TP4/DP4 on GPUs 0-3, decode: TP4/DP4 on GPUs 4-7 - `--disaggregation-transfer-backend nixl`, `--moe-a2a-backend megamoe`, `--kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3` - `nixl` / `nixl-cu13` 1.3.2, `UCX_TLS=cuda_copy,cuda_ipc,tcp`, `UCX_MEMTYPE_CACHE=n` - image `lmsysorg/sglang:v0.5.17-cu130` **9 prefill crashes in 43 hours** of steady traffic, ~one every 4.8h, evenly spread across the clock — not tied to load, deploys, or any request shape. The decode role, on the same host with the same image, UCX env and traffic, has **never** crashed. ## Stack — identical every time ``` Fatal Python error: Segmentation fault File "<unknown>", line 0, in cuEventQuery File "<unknown>", line 0, in uct_cuda_base_iface_event_fd_arm File "<unknown>", line 0, in ucp_worker_arm File "<unknown>", line 0, in nixlUcxWorker::arm() const File "<unknown>", line 0, in nixlUcxSharedThread::run() File "<unknown>", line 0, in __clone ``` ## A debugging note that cost us time `faulthandler` dumps **every** thread, and the Python main-thread frame is different on every crash — we saw `deepseek_v4_backend.init_compression_metadata`, `mem_cache/allocator/swa.free_swa`, `forward_batch_info.init_new`, `scheduler_components/dp_attn.all_gather`, and `utils/common.broadcast_pyobj` across nine dumps of the same bug. All of those are innocent bystanders. Only the C++ frames matter, and they never change. Likewise the `Scheduler hit an exception: ... RuntimeError: [gloo] ... Connection reset by peer` tracebacks that follow are the surviving DP ranks reacting to a dead peer, not the fault. #23499's original report made the same observation. Anyone triaging a report like this should grep the dump for `nixlUcxSharedThread`, not for the scheduler frames. ## Root cause `nixlUcxSharedThread::run()` (nixl `src/plugins/ucx/ucx_backend.cpp:339`) calls `worker->arm()` without ever establishing a CUDA context on that thread. `arm()` reaches UCX's `cuda_copy` transport, which calls `cuEventQuery` and segfaults. NIXL's UCX plugin contains **no** CUDA context management at all — a repo-wide grep for `vramApplyCtx|pthrCudaCtx|cuCtxSetCurrent` hits only `src/plugins/libfabric/`, which received exactly this fix in ai-dynamo/nixl#1157. ## Why prefill only `python/sglang/srt/disaggregation/nixl/conn.py`: ```python num_threads = 8 if disaggregation_mode == DisaggregationMode.PREFILL else 0 ``` and in nixl `ucx_backend.cpp:763`, the shared progress thread is only constructed when the UCX backend receives `num_threads > 0`. So prefill gets `nixlUcxSharedThread` and decode does not, which matches our 9-vs-0 crash split exactly. ## Workaround (confirmed at the source level, running it now) ```bash export SGLANG_DISAGGREGATION_NIXL_BACKEND_PARAMS='{"num_threads":"0"}' ``` The `setdefault` in `conn.py` means an explicit value wins, and `num_threads=0` makes NIXL skip `nixlUcxThreadPoolEngine` entirely, so the crashing thread never exists. ## Asks 1. **Reopen #23499.** It was closed without a fix and its 2026-07-07 follow-up is still unanswered. 2. **Document `SGLANG_DISAGGREGATION_NIXL_BACKEND_PARAMS`** in `docs/advanced_features/pd_disaggregation.md`. It was added in #24169 but the PD docs only mention `SGLANG_DISAGGREGATION_NIXL_BACKEND`, so the only workaround for this crash is currently undiscoverable without reading `environ.py`. 3. **Reconsider the hardcoded `num_threads = 8` for prefill**, or at minimum make it a documented, overridable knob with a note about this failure mode, until the NIXL fix lands.

signal.title: [AMD] Strict bit-exact SWA HiCache for DeepSeek-V4 with unified_kv: SWA-window + c4/indexer state riding across L1/L2/L3
signal.text: <!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. --> ## Motivation <!-- Describe the purpose and goals of this pull request. --> DeepSeek-V4's `unified_kv` backend on ROCm packs three KV families in one pool: the content-addressed compressed KV (C4/C128), the per-request **SWA ring** (addressed by `req_pool_idx * window + pos % window`), and the compressor's **c4 / indexer overlap state**. Only the compressed KV is content-stable; the SWA ring and the c4/indexer overlap state are not, and are never written into the radix tree. Two prior PRs made reuse of such prefixes *safe* but only **approximately correct**: - **#29417** enabled unified_kv HiCache, but it offloads **only** the compressed KV (C4/C128). The SWA ring is not preserved, so on a hierarchical hit the trailing sliding window is **re-prefilled** (`swa_reprefill_tail_tokens()`) rather than restored. - **#30339** applied the same **re-prefill** idea to the radix-only path: cap the match by the trailing window and recompute it into the request's own ring, so decode never reads a stale ring. Re-prefill recomputes the trailing window (and, implicitly, the c4/indexer overlap state for that region) instead of reproducing the exact values the original prefill wrote. That is enough to prevent gross stale-ring errors and to keep GSM8K-level accuracy within noise — but it is **not bit-exact**: a partial re-prefill cannot reconstruct the original SWA window and c4/indexer overlap state byte-for-byte, so the reused output can differ from a full fresh compute at the bit level. This PR closes that gap. Instead of re-prefilling an approximation, it **captures and offloads the true values** of the SWA window and the c4/indexer overlap state across L1→L2→L3, and **restores them exactly** on a hierarchical hit — making unified_kv SWA prefix reuse **strict and bit-exact**. A hard reuse gate re-prefills only when the truth is unavailable (never a stale/approximate read). This is an **opt-in** gated by `SGLANG_UNIFIED_KV_BIT_EXACT_HICACHE` (default **off**), and it engages only when **all** of the following hold at once: - running **DeepSeek-V4** on **ROCm/HIP**; - the **`unified_kv_triton`** attention backend is chosen (`SGLANG_HACK_FLASHMLA_BACKEND=unified_kv_triton`); - **HiCache is enabled** (`--enable-hierarchical-cache`). In every other case, the feature is a strict no-op, no pool is allocated, no capture, no restore; behavior is byte-identical to `main`. ## Modifications <!-- Detail the changes made in this pull request. --> Organized as three layers: **1. Substrate (Commit 1–5):** - `SGLANG_UNIFIED_KV_BIT_EXACT_HICACHE` flag + `--hicache-swa-offload-page-stride` arg (`environ.py`, `server_args.py`). - Dedicated pinned-host SWA-window offload pool with capture-done handshake + upstream deferred release (`memory_pool_host.py`). - Two independent, tile-start-addressed L3 pools for c4 state and indexer state, packing (`deepseek_v4_memory_pool.py`, `hybrid_cache/hybrid_pool_assembler.py`). - Version-namespaced L3 keys (`hicache_storage.py`, `storage/nixl/hicache_nixl.py`). - Startup fail-fast guard (`hybrid_pool_assembler.py`): with the strict flag on, raise a clear `ValueError` unless `--hicache-write-policy write_through`, before any host pool is pinned. **2. Capture (Commit 6–8):** - Capture the SWA ring window at each completed prefill/decode page with EAGLE-safe geometry (`deepseek_v4_backend_hip_radix.py`, `model_runner.py`, `deepseek_v4.py`). - Snapshot c4/indexer overlap state for the same window into the independent state pools (`compress_hip.py`, `compressor_v2.py`). **3. Reuse/restore + strict gate (Commit 9–10):** - Ride the captured window + state back to device at the correct `buf_lo` offset on a hierarchical hit; **strict reuse gate** caps the match and re-prefills any tail that isn't provably bit-exact, never a stale read; commit-coupling guard keeps window+state+full-KV committed atomically (`swa_component.py`, `unified_radix_cache.py`, `base_prefix_cache.py`, `schedule_batch.py`, `schedule_policy.py`). ## Note to reviewers This PR can be split into three cumulative sub-PRs on request — substrate / capture / reuse (boundaries C1–5 / C6–8 / C9–10) — each gated by the same flag and a strict no-op by default. ## Accuracy Tests <!-- If this pull request affects model outputs (e.g., changes to the kernel or model forward code), provide accuracy test results. --> Two detectors (like #30339): a byte-exact harness is the real detector; GSM8K is only a no-regression guard. ### 1. Unit Tests (5 test files, 163 UTs total) **How:** `cd test && python3 -m pytest -q srt/mem_cache/test_swa_*.py` **Expected:** `163 passed` — byte-exact swa+c4_state/c4_indexer_state capture/restore across L1→L2→L3, strict-gate reject, commit-coupling guard, dirty-read protection, L3-only restore. ### 2. E2E (DeepSeek-V4 unified_kv on ROCm, HiCache + strict flag) **How:** launch with the gates on and `SGLANG_SWA_DBG_CHECKSUM=1` (emits a per-window checksum vs a fresh device re-read), trigger prefix reuse, grep the log. ```bash export SGLANG_HACK_FLASHMLA_BACKEND=unified_kv_triton export SGLANG_UNIFIED_KV_BIT_EXACT_HICACHE=1 # dev; set 0 for the "off" baseline export SGLANG_SWA_DBG_CHECKSUM=1 # + standard dsv4 env as in #30339 python3 -m sglang.launch_server --model-path /data/models/DeepSeek-V4-Pro --attention-backend dsv4 \ --page-size 256 --swa-full-tokens-ratio 0.1 --enable-cache-report --port 30001 \ --enable-hierarchical-cache --hicache-write-policy write_through \ --hicache-io-backend direct --hicache-mem-layout layer_first \ --tp 4 --dp 4 --enable-dp-attention 2>&1 | tee server.log # decode + EAGLE spec path (tp8/dp8): add --speculative-algorithm EAGLE --speculative-num-steps 3 --speculative-num-draft-tokens 4 --speculative-eagle-topk 1 # L3-only variant: add --hicache-storage-backend file --hicache-storage-prefetch-policy wait_complete # + SGLANG_HICACHE_FILE_BACKEND_STORAGE_DIR=/ssd/dir, populate, kill, restart same dir, resend prefix ``` **Trigger reuse** — send the same long prompt N rounds; `cached_tokens` climbs 0 → large: ```bash python3 - <<'PY' import json, urllib.request P = "This is a long shared prefix sentence. " * 4000 # >> page_size (256) tokens for r in range(6): # 6 for prefill; 20 for decode dp8 (every rank must hit) b = json.dumps({"model": "x", "prompt": P, "max_tokens": 8, "temperature": 0}).encode() u = json.loads(urllib.request.urlopen(urllib.request.Request( "http://127.0.0.1:30001/v1/completions", data=b, headers={"Content-Type": "application/json"})).read())["usage"] print("round", r, "cached_tokens", (u.get("prompt_tokens_details") or {}).get("cached_tokens", 0)) PY ``` **Expected** (grep `server.log`): | check | grep | expect | | --- | --- | --- | | byte-exact SWA + c4/indexer | `[C4-STATE-DBG]` state ride bit-exact / `[LB-DEV]` device landing byte-exact / `[SWA-DBG]` restore verified | **L1/L2 same-process reuse**: all three **> 0**. **L3-only cross-restart**: `[LB-DEV]` + `[C4-STATE-DBG]` **> 0** (`[SWA-DBG]` is **0** on this path — the prefill checksum is not persisted across a process restart, so the window's byte-exact verification is carried by `[LB-DEV]` device-landing). | | no failure / no dirty read | `MISMATCH\|reuse_reject\|BIND-MISS\|AssertionError\|Traceback` | **0** | | L3-only source | `prefetch .*matched=[0-9]+ loaded=[0-9]+` | `matched=0 loaded>0` | **L3-only restore validated** (cold restart, empty L1/L2): `prefetch matched=0 loaded=2304`, the first request immediately reports `cached_tokens=2304`, `[LB-DEV]` + `[C4-STATE-DBG]` byte-exact all pass, zero `MISMATCH`. **gsm8k eval**: Two arms, each run once per server profile — off (SGLANG_UNIFIED_KV_BIT_EXACT_HICACHE=0) and dev (=1) — with the cache flushed (/flush_cache) before each pass and temperature=0, so the only variable is the strict flag. GSM8K is a no-regression guard (the byte-exact harness above is the real correctness detector); the acceptance criterion is that dev is not below off and invalid ≈ 0. - non-thinking ``` python3 benchmark/gsm8k/bench_sglang.py \ --host 127.0.0.1 --port 30001 --num-shots 8 --num-questions 1319 --parallel 256 ``` For off (SGLANG_UNIFIED_KV_BIT_EXACT_HICACHE=0) and dev (=1) , all above tests we got acc ~0.94(invalid ≈ 0). - thinking ``` python3 -m sglang.test.run_eval \ --eval-name gsm8k --host 127.0.0.1 --port 30001 \ --num-threads 256 --temperature 0.0 --repeat 1 --num-shots 8 --max-tokens 8192 ``` For off, we got 0.933, and for dev, we got 0.942(invalid 0). ## Speed Tests and Profiling <!-- If this pull request impacts inference speed, provide benchmarking and profiling results. --> Both arms HiCache on, `DBG=0`, `--hicache-ratio 1.0` (single variable = strict flag); customer clients. signal.title: [sgl-router] Worker Snapshot Support for Recoverable KV Placement State in sgl-router
signal.text: ## Motivation KV-aware routing depends on an accurate view of the KV blocks available on each worker replica. Previously, sgl-router built this view only from live `BlockStored` and `BlockRemoved` events. If the Router started after the Worker cache had already been populated, or if the Router restarted and lost its in-memory index, the existing KV placement state could not be reconstructed. Missing or stale placement metadata does not affect inference correctness, but it reduces cache-aware routing quality and may lower the KV cache hit rate. This PR implements the snapshot bootstrap and full-recovery portion of #33394. Short-gap recovery through the replay endpoint remains separate follow-up work related to #32729. ## Modifications ### Worker-side snapshot provider - Add an optional `snapshot_endpoint` to the built-in ZMQ KV-event publisher. The endpoint is exposed independently for each routable DP or attention-DP replica using `base_port + dp_rank`. - Maintain an in-memory KV placement mirror inside the publisher thread. Sequence assignment, event application, and snapshot capture are serialized by the same thread, so the snapshot and its live-event barrier represent one consistent placement cut. - Include the replica lifecycle `epoch`, `replica_rank`, `barrier_seq`, `resume_seq`, `barrier_id`, and the active block records required to reconstruct parent relationships. - Stream large snapshots in chunks of up to 4096 records. The chunk size limits each ZMQ message, not the total snapshot size. - Scope the publisher epoch to one DP replica lifecycle, so restarting one DP rank does not invalidate the other ranks. - Keep the replay buffer complete after a sequence number is assigned even if live PUB delivery fails, and index the snapshot mirror by `block_hash` for direct removal. ### Discovery and compatibility - Advertise the optional snapshot host, base port, and protocol version through `/server_info`. An invalid or absent snapshot configuration does not hide an otherwise valid live KV-event publisher. - Append NUL-delimited epoch and snapshot-barrier metadata to the ZMQ topic frame only for snapshot-capable publishers. The sequence frame and event payload remain unchanged. - Preserve compatibility with existing ZMQ consumers because SUB filters are prefix-based. - Keep workers without a snapshot endpoint in the existing `LegacyBestEffort` live-only mode. ### Router-side recovery For each `(worker_url, dp_rank)` replica, sgl-router now: 1. subscribes to the live event stream; 2. fetches the replica snapshot while buffering live events; 3. waits for and validates the matching snapshot barrier; 4. verifies contiguous sequence numbers and applies post-snapshot updates; 5. replaces the replica placement state in the HashTree; and 6. marks the replica `READY`. One snapshot is fetched per independently routable DP or attention-DP replica, rather than per TP rank. Snapshot-capable replicas remain absent from the cache-aware placement tree until synchronization completes. Normal routing fallback remains available while a replica is synchronizing. A sequence gap, epoch change, publisher reset, decode failure, or invalid snapshot clears only the affected replica placement state and triggers a fresh synchronization. Snapshot retries use bounded buffering, cancellation-aware tasks, and exponential backoff. ### Code organization - Add `snapshot.rs` for the chunked snapshot wire protocol and validation. - Add `sync.rs` for bootstrap, barrier catch-up, replica state transitions, gap detection, and resynchronization. - Keep `index.rs` as the lifecycle facade for worker discovery, subscriber management, and snapshot task ownership. ## Accuracy Tests This PR does not change model execution, kernels, or generated outputs. The following tests passed: ```bash PYTHONPATH=python python3 -m pytest -q \ test/registered/unit/disaggregation/test_kv_events.py # 10 passed PYTHONPATH=python python3 -m pytest -q \ test/registered/unit/entrypoints/test_server_info.py # 17 passed cd experimental/sgl-router cargo test --lib policies::kv_events # 102 passed cargo test --test component # 41 passed ``` The snapshot recovery E2E test also passed with two Workers and one Router: - KV blocks populated before Router startup were recovered from snapshots. - Live KV events produced after the Router became ready were applied incrementally. - After restarting the Router, the placement view was rebuilt and the same cached prefixes continued to route to the expected Workers. The legacy compatibility E2E test also passed: Workers without a snapshot endpoint continued to use live-only indexing, and two Router instances converged to the expected prefix routing results. ## Speed Tests and Profiling No model throughput benchmark was run because this PR does not modify the inference or request-forwarding path. Snapshot capture uses the publisher in-memory placement mirror, and snapshot network transfer runs on a separate thread using bounded chunks. Normal live-event processing remains incremental. ## Checklist - [x] Format the code according to the repository pre-commit configuration. - [x] Add unit tests for snapshot capture, chunking, epoch isolation, protocol validation, recovery, failure handling, and legacy compatibility. - [x] Document the snapshot protocol and synchronization lifecycle in the implementation. - [x] Provide accuracy and speed-test applicability and E2E validation results. - [x] Follow the existing SGLang Python and Rust code organization and style. Related RFC: #33394 Related replay work: #32729 <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32347033732](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32347033732)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32347033624](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32347033624)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32347033721](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32347033721)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [mem_cache] docs: add a layer map and placement rules
signal.text: ## Motivation Part of #25371. `mem_cache/` has 40 top-level modules plus 10 subpackages and no index. Answering "is this class an allocator or a pool?" or "may `pool_host/` import `allocator/`?" currently means reading the RFC or grepping. ## Modifications Adds `python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/README.md`: - **Layers** -- the stack from `allocation.py` down through `allocator/`, `pool/`, `pool_host/`, `storage/`, with each layer's in/out contract. Names prefix-cache trees and the construction layer (`kv_cache_configurator.py`, `kv_cache_builder.py`, `cache_init_params.py`, `allocation_sizing.py`, `kv_cache_dtype.py`, `kv_vmm_backing.py`, `hybrid_cache/hybrid_pool_assembler.py`) as sitting outside that stack rather than in it. - **Where does my class go?** -- home by base class, not by name, plus the `Allocator`-means-two-things distinction (`BaseTokenToKVPoolAllocator` hands out KV slots and lives in `allocator/`; `HostTensorAllocator` hands out pinned host memory and does not). - **Conventions** -- the naming rule, family-as-package, and the dependency-direction invariants. Documentation only; no code changes. **Deliberately coarse.** An earlier draft carried a per-family x per-layer matrix naming the module that holds each class today. That inventory would need updating by every one of the ~20 remaining moves under #25371, and it already has a home that cannot rot: the shrink-only pins in the layout ratchet (#35638), which fail the build when a pinned class moves. Duplicating it here would just give the same fact a second home to drift from. The README documents the rules, which are stable; for "where does class X live today", `git grep` is the answer, and the README says so. ## Accuracy Test Not applicable -- documentation only. ## Benchmark and Profiling Results Not applicable -- documentation only. ## Checklist - signal.title: [BugFix] Fix symmetric memory allocation during CUDA graph capture
signal.text: ## Motivation With symmetric memory, speculative decoding, TP > 1, and CUDA graph capture enabled together, collective buffers could be captured at different NCCL registration windows across ranks. This violates the `NCCL_WIN_COLL_SYMMETRIC` contract and can silently produce incorrect model outputs without a CUDA or NCCL error. The divergence came from using the eager NCCL memory pool during graph capture. Rank-local JIT and warmup history changed that pool's free-list state before multiple speculative-decoding graphs were captured. ## Modifications - Keep the existing eager NCCL memory pool and add a dedicated pool for symmetric-memory CUDA graph allocations. - Before retaining each breakable or full CUDA graph, run the same shape once in a disposable capture. Defer NCCL registration during that capture, then register any newly created segments outside capture. - Recapture the retained graph from the same pool so its collective buffers reuse registered graph-pool blocks with rank-consistent window/offset pairs. - Preserve the existing eager and `tc_piecewise` behavior. - Add a 2-GPU regression that creates rank-divergent eager-pool state and captures and replays three successive graphs. Priming is intentionally done per retained graph. Later shapes can be the first to require another symmetric-memory segment, so a session-wide one-time prime does not establish the invariant for every graph. ## Reproduction The minimal regression requires two CUDA GPUs and recreates rank-divergent eager-pool state without loading a model: ```bash python3 test/registered/cuda_graph/test_pynccl_symmetric_memory_pool.py ``` The model-level reproduction used Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-FP8 with 1P1D, TP4 on prefill and decode, PP1 prefill, NEXTN with 3 speculative steps / top-k 1 / 4 draft tokens, breakable prefill CUDA graphs, full decode CUDA graphs, and symmetric memory enabled. After starting the server, run the accuracy evaluation with: ```bash python3 -m sglang.test.run_eval --base-url http://<router-host>:<port> --model qwen35-397b --eval-name gsm8k --num-examples 200 --num-shots 8 --max-tokens 16384 --num-threads 16 --temperature 0 ``` Run the serving benchmark once for each of the following three arms while keeping every other server setting unchanged: parent commit with symmetric memory enabled, this PR with symmetric memory disabled, and this PR with symmetric memory enabled. ```bash for concurrency in 16 64 256; do python3 -m sglang.benchmark.serving --backend sglang --base-url http://<router-host>:<port> --model qwen35-397b --tokenizer <tokenizer-path> --dataset-name random --num-prompts $((concurrency * 5)) --random-input-len 8192 --random-output-len 64 --random-range-ratio 1.0 --request-rate inf --max-concurrency "$concurrency" --warmup-requests $((concurrency * 2)) --output-file "result_c${concurrency}.jsonl"; done ``` ## Accuracy Tests GSM8K used 200 questions, 8-shot prompts, temperature 0, and reports accuracy as a score in `[0, 1]`. | Configuration | GSM8K score | Accuracy | | --- | ---: | ---: | | Before fix, symmetric memory enabled | 0.940 | 94.0% | | After fix, symmetric memory enabled | 0.990 / 0.990 / 0.990 | 99.0% / 99.0% / 99.0% | | After fix, symmetric memory disabled control | 0.990 | 99.0% | The before-fix result reproduces the previously observed approximately `0.95` accuracy. The fix restores the expected `0.99` accuracy without disabling symmetric memory, speculative decoding, or CUDA graphs. The 2-GPU/TP2 regression fails during capture on the parent implementation. The fixed implementation captures and replays three successive graphs and verifies rank-consistent offsets and outputs. An instrumented model-level capture recorded 94,328 symmetric-memory allocations across target prefill/verify and draft extend/decode with zero cross-rank window/offset mismatches. The GPU results above were collected on the same core implementation before a final non-functional cleanup that removed unused state and test compatibility scaffolding. The exact public commit passes targeted pre-commit hooks, `py_compile`, `git diff --check`, and `git show --check`; public CI on the exact commit is pending. ## Speed Tests and Profiling The metric is `total_token_throughput` in `tokens/s`. All three arms were run in the same batch with random fixed-length ISL 8192 / OSL 64, request rate `inf`, and three repetitions per concurrency. | Concurrency | Before fix, symm ON (tokens/s) | After fix, symm OFF (tokens/s) | After fix, symm ON (tokens/s) | | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | | 16 | 52,229.25 / 51,756.62 / 52,104.05 (mean 52,029.97) | 50,252.12 / 49,789.34 / 50,190.87 (mean 50,077.44) | 52,033.24 / 52,304.27 / 52,258.73 (mean 52,198.75) | | 64 | 53,474.89 / 53,194.81 / 53,184.14 (mean 53,284.61) | 50,592.58 / 50,734.43 / 50,860.22 (mean 50,729.08) | 53,276.41 / 53,006.39 / 53,212.94 (mean 53,165.25) | | 256 | 52,544.23 / 52,435.58 / 52,499.45 (mean 52,493.09) | 50,290.20 / 49,808.08 / 50,323.21 (mean 50,140.50) | 52,340.47 / 52,666.02 / 52,603.16 (mean 52,536.55) | | Concurrency | After fix symm ON / before fix symm ON | After fix symm ON / after fix symm OFF | | ---: | ---: | ---: | | 16 | 1.0032 | 1.0424 | | 64 | 0.9978 | 1.0480 | | 256 | 1.0008 | 1.0478 | The fix preserves the before-fix symmetric-memory throughput and retains its approximately 4-5% advantage over disabling symmetric memory. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). (N/A: no user-facing API or configuration change.) - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. signal.title: [RFC][Refactor] `mem_cache` pool / allocator restructure
signal.text: > **Roadmap v2.** Rewritten against `sglang/main` @ 2026-08-20; the original body is > in this issue's edit history. Hardware backends (`hardware_backend/npu/`, > `hardware_backend/mlx/`) are **out of scope** and are not covered by any item or > guard below. --- ## 1. TL;DR Reorganize `mem_cache/` from "a few catch-all files plus cross-feature pollution" into per-family one-module-per-family packages: - `allocator.py` → `allocator/` package — **done**, keep it closed - `memory_pool_host.py` → `pool_host/` package — **in progress**, 3 items left - `memory_pool.py` + 6 sibling files → `pool/` package — **not started**, and it is the only part of `mem_cache/` still actively getting worse - Untangle DSv4 ↔ HiSparse class misplacement - Naming rule: **remove role affixes that don't differentiate** - Add `mem_cache/README.md` (type × scope) index - Land a CI guard so the layout cannot regress once a target directory exists --- ## 2. Why v2: what changed since the RFC was opened The RFC was opened 2026-05-15. Three months of data: | File | 2026-05-15 | 2026-08-20 | Δ | |---|---|---|---| | `memory_pool.py` | 2257 lines / 11 classes | **5042 lines / 17 classes** | **+123%** | | `memory_pool_host.py` | 2105 lines / 8 classes | **1517 lines / 6 classes** | −28% | The layer that got a target directory shrank. The layer that did not got 2.8k lines and 6 new classes dumped into it: `PageMajorMHATokenToKVPool`, `MHATokenToKVPoolMXFP8`, `MHATokenToKOnlyPool`, `MiniMaxSparseKVPool`, `DSATokenToKVPool`, plus `KVWriteLoc` / `KvBufferDesc`. Two consequences drive v2: 1. **`pool/` moves from last to first.** It is the only remaining catch-all and the only one still growing. 2. **A directory alone is not a rule.** #29678 (2026-07-01) added `multi_ended_allocator.py` (2559 lines, 3 allocator classes) at top level *two months after* `allocator/` existed. Section 8 adds the guard. Additional drift the original body does not reflect: - `unified_cache_components/` was moved to `unified_cache/components/` in 60d6914f1 (2026-07-28), but the `_component` suffix was kept. The naming rule was silently dropped; the tree in the old §3.2 is contradicted by a landed PR. - `NSATokenToKVPool` → `DSATokenToKVPool`; `NSAIndexerPoolHost` → `DSAIndexerPoolHost`. All `nsa` names in the old tree are stale. - `allocator/mamba.py` holds `MambaSlotAllocator`, not `MambaTokenToKVPoolAllocator`. - `allocator/swa.py` gained `PureSWATokenToKVPoolAllocator` — filed correctly, which is the evidence that the rule works once the directory exists. - New, entirely uncovered by the old roadmap: `unified_memory_pool.py` (1691), `multi_ended_allocator.py` (2559), `kv_cache_configurator.py` (2190), `mamba_checkpoint_pool.py`, `index_key_cache.py`, `dsa_cache_layer_split.py`, `mamba_slot_fused.py`, `kv_vmm_backing.py`, `layout/`, `buffer_mode/`, `allocation.py`, `allocation_sizing.py`, `embedding_store.py`. --- ## 3. Rules for every PR under this issue 1. Title must carry the `[mem_cache][N/N]` prefix and state whether it is a **Mechanical Move**. 2. Mechanical Moves must satisfy the `mechanical-refactor-verify` skill. 3. Preserve git blame as far as possible; `git blame -C -C` is the accepted fallback. 4. **No compatibility shims.** Each move updates all importers in the same PR. This is the established precedent — `allocator.py` was deleted outright, not left as a re-export. `memory_pool.py` currently has 98 importers; they get updated, not forwarded. 5. Every PR must shrink the guard allowlist (§8) by exactly the classes it moved. 6. Adequate test coverage, and detailed review — no exceptions for "trivial" moves. --- ## 4. Naming rules 1. **Drop role affixes that do not differentiate.** If every file in a directory shares the role the directory already names, the affix carries no information: `pool_host/mha.py`, not `pool_host/mha_pool_host.py`. Keep `_backend` / `_controller` style only where same-directory siblings have *different* roles. 2. **A family is a module, and a module may be a file or a package.** One file per family is the default; a family over ~1500 lines becomes a package (`pool/deepseek_v4/` already does this, and `pool/mha/` must — see §5). 3. `Allocator` is overloaded and the two meanings must not be merged: - **slot allocator** — a `BaseTokenToKVPoolAllocator` subclass, answers "which slots are free". These belong in `allocator/`. - **host tensor allocator** — `HostTensorAllocator` and its subclasses (`ShmHostTensorAllocator`, `MooncakeHostTensorAllocator`, `UMBPHostTensorAllocator`), answers "give me pinned host memory". These stay in `pool_host/common.py` and `storage/`, and are **not** in scope for `allocator/`. --- ## 5. Target tree ``` mem_cache/ ├── README.md # (type × scope) index │ ├── allocator/ # slot indexing — CLOSED except for the two items in §6.1 │ ├── __init__.py │ ├── base.py # BaseTokenToKVPoolAllocator (abc only) │ ├── token.py # TokenToKVPoolAllocator (page_size=1) │ ├── paged.py # PagedTokenToKVPoolAllocator │ ├── mamba.py # MambaSlotAllocator │ ├── swa.py # SWATokenToKVPoolAllocator │ │ # PureSWATokenToKVPoolAllocator │ ├── hisparse.py # HiSparseTokenToKVPoolAllocator │ │ # DeepSeekV4HiSparseTokenToKVPoolAllocator │ └── multi_ended.py # MultiEndedAllocator │ # UnifiedMambaTokenToKVPoolAllocator │ # UnifiedSWATokenToKVPoolAllocator │ ├── pool/ # device physical storage │ ├── __init__.py │ ├── base.py # KVCache + BaseSWAKVPool + KVWriteLoc + KvBufferDesc │ ├── req_to_token.py # ReqToTokenPool + HybridReqToTokenPool │ ├── mha/ # 6 classes / ~1900 lines → package │ │ ├── __init__.py │ │ ├── base.py # MHATokenToKVPool │ │ ├── noop.py # NoOpMHATokenToKVPool │ │ ├── fp4.py # MHATokenToKVPoolFP4 │ │ ├── mxfp8.py # MHATokenToKVPoolMXFP8 │ │ ├── page_major.py # PageMajorMHATokenToKVPool │ │ └── k_only.py # MHATokenToKOnlyPool │ ├── mla.py # MLATokenToKVPool + MLATokenToKVPoolFP4 │ ├── dsa.py # DSATokenToKVPool + HiSparseDSATokenToKVPool │ │ # + LayerSplitDSATokenToKVPool │ │ # + IndexKeyCache + LayerSplitIndexKeyCache │ ├── mamba.py # MambaPool + MambaCheckpointPool + Int8CheckpointStore │ ├── hybrid.py # HybridLinearKVPool │ ├── swa.py # SWAKVPool │ ├── hisparse.py # HiSparseC4DevicePool │ ├── minimax.py # MiniMaxSparseKVPool │ ├── unified/ # shared-arena variants (see §9 D1) │ │ ├── __init__.py │ │ ├── arena.py # UnifiedKVPool + SubPoolSpec + MHA/MLA/Mamba specs │ │ ├── mha.py # UnifiedMHATokenToKVPool │ │ ├── mla.py # UnifiedMLATokenToKVPool │ │ ├── mamba.py # UnifiedMambaPool + UnifiedMambaSlotAllocator │ │ ├── swa.py # UnifiedSWAKVPool │ │ └── hybrid.py # UnifiedHybridReqToTokenPool + UnifiedHybridLinearKVPool │ └── deepseek_v4/ │ ├── __init__.py │ ├── composite.py # DeepSeekV4TokenToKVPool + DeepSeekV4UnifiedKVPool │ ├── single.py # DeepSeekV4SingleKVPool │ ├── indexer.py # DeepSeekV4IndexerPool │ └── compress_state.py # KVAndScore + CompressStatePool │ ├── pool_host/ # host-side mirrors for supported device pools │ ├── __init__.py │ ├── base.py # HostKVCache (abc) + synchronized decorator │ ├── common.py # HostTensorAllocator + ShmHostTensorAllocator + helpers │ ├── mha.py # MHATokenToKVPoolHost + MHATokenToKOnlyPoolHost │ │ # + AsymmetricMHATokenToKVPoolHost │ ├── mla.py # MLATokenToKVPoolHost │ ├── dsa.py # DSAIndexerPoolHost │ ├── mamba.py # MambaPoolHost │ ├── hisparse.py # HiSparseHostPoolMixin │ ├── group.py # PoolEntry + HostPoolGroup + LogicalHostPool │ └── deepseek_v4.py # DeepSeekV4PagedHostPool + DeepSeekV4StateHostPool │ ├── hybrid_cache/ # multi-pool orchestrator │ ├── controller.py # HybridCacheController │ └── pool_assembler.py # HybridPoolAssembler │ ├── unified_cache/components/ │ ├── __init__.py │ ├── base.py # TreeComponent (abc) + shared enums │ ├── full.py # FullComponent │ ├── mamba.py # MambaComponent │ └── swa.py # SWAComponent │ ├── allocation.py # scheduler-facing allocation policy (unchanged) ├── layout/ # cross-cutting memory layout helpers (unchanged) ├── buffer_mode/, storage/, sparsity/ # (unchanged) └── ... tree-layer files # (unchanged, #20415 territory) ``` Deleted when their last class moves out: `memory_pool.py`, `memory_pool_host.py`, `deepseek_v4_memory_pool.py`, `deepseek_v4_compress_state.py`, `swa_memory_pool.py`, `base_swa_memory_pool.py`, `hisparse_memory_pool.py`, `unified_memory_pool.py`, `multi_ended_allocator.py`, `mamba_checkpoint_pool.py`, `dsa_cache_layer_split.py`, `index_key_cache.py`. --- ## 6. Roadmap ### 6.1 `mem_cache/allocator/` — nearly done - [x] [Mechanical Move] split `allocator.py` into `allocator/` subpackage — #26675 - [x] [Mechanical Move] `SWATokenToKVPoolAllocator` — #26676 - [x] [Mechanical Move] HiSparse allocators — #26678 - [x] [Modify] Mamba allocator — #27256 - [ ] [Mechanical Move] `MultiEndedAllocator` → `allocator/multi_ended.py` (2559 lines / 3 classes — split into 3 PRs: `MultiEndedAllocator`, `UnifiedMambaTokenToKVPoolAllocator`, `UnifiedSWATokenToKVPoolAllocator`) - [ ] [Guard] land §8 with `allocator/` at zero allowlist entries ### 6.2 `mem_cache/pool_host/` — 3 items left - [x] [Mechanical Move] base subpackage (`__init__` + `base` + `hisparse` + `common`) — #27273 - [x] [Mechanical Move] `MHATokenToKVPoolHost` — #30249 - [x] [Mechanical Move] `MLATokenToKVPoolHost` — #30616 - [x] [Mechanical Move] `MambaPoolHost` — #31180 - [ ] [Mechanical Move] `DSAIndexerPoolHost` → `pool_host/dsa.py` — #35306 *(in review)* - [ ] [Mechanical Move] `DeepSeekV4PagedHostPool` + `DeepSeekV4StateHostPool` → `pool_host/deepseek_v4.py` - [ ] [Mechanical Move] `PoolEntry` + `HostPoolGroup` + `LogicalHostPool` → `pool_host/group.py`, delete `memory_pool_host.py` - [ ] [Guard] extend §8 to `pool_host/` at zero allowlist entries ### 6.3 `mem_cache/pool/` — **promoted to top priority, not started** Order matters: `base.py` first so every later PR has a target for its base class, then leaves before composites. - [x] [Mechanical Move] create `pool/` + `base.py` — `KVCache`, `BaseSWAKVPool` (from `base_swa_memory_pool.py`), `KVWriteLoc`, `KvBufferDesc`, `unwrap_write_loc` — #35647. The `_set_kv_buffer_*` helpers stay put: the moved region references none of them, so moving them would only widen the diff. - [ ] [Mechanical Move] `ReqToTokenPool` + `HybridReqToTokenPool` → `pool/req_to_token.py` - [ ] [Mechanical Move] `pool/mha/` package — one PR for `base.py` (`MHATokenToKVPool`, 1112 lines), then one PR per variant group: `noop` + `k_only`, `fp4` + `mxfp8`, `page_major` - [ ] [Mechanical Move] `MLATokenToKVPool` + `MLATokenToKVPoolFP4` → `pool/mla.py` - [ ] [Mechanical Move] `DSATokenToKVPool` + `HiSparseDSATokenToKVPool` → `pool/dsa.py`, delete `hisparse_memory_pool.py` - [ ] [Mechanical Move] `IndexKeyCache` → `pool/dsa.py`, delete `index_key_cache.py` *(same module as its sole owner `DSATokenToKVPool`, which removes the `TYPE_CHECKING` import cycle between the two)* - [ ] [Mechanical Move] `LayerSplitDSATokenToKVPool` + `LayerSplitIndexKeyCache` → `pool/dsa.py`, delete `dsa_cache_layer_split.py` - [ ] [Mechanical Move] `MambaPool` → `pool/mamba.py`; fold in `MambaCheckpointPool` + `Int8CheckpointStore`, delete `mamba_checkpoint_pool.py` - [ ] [Mechanical Move] `SWAKVPool` → `pool/swa.py`, delete `swa_memory_pool.py` - [ ] [Modify] `HybridLinearKVPool` → `pool/hybrid.py` (rename to `HybridKVPool` — the only non-mechanical item here, needs its own discussion) - [ ] [Mechanical Move] `MiniMaxSparseKVPool` → `pool/minimax.py` - [ ] [Mechanical Move] `HiSparseC4DevicePool` → `pool/hisparse.py` *(untangles the DSv4 ↔ HiSparse misplacement in `deepseek_v4_memory_pool.py`)* - [ ] [Mechanical Move] `pool/deepseek_v4/` — `single.py`, `indexer.py`, `composite.py`, `compress_state.py`; delete `deepseek_v4_memory_pool.py` and `deepseek_v4_compress_state.py` - [ ] [Mechanical Move] `pool/unified/` (see §9 D1); delete `unified_memory_pool.py` - [ ] Delete `memory_pool.py` - [ ] [Guard] extend §8 to `pool/` at zero allowlist entries ### 6.4 Naming cleanups - [ ] [Mechanical Move] `hybrid_cache/hybrid_cache_controller.py` → `controller.py` - [ ] [Mechanical Move] `hybrid_cache/hybrid_pool_assembler.py` → `pool_assembler.py` - [x] [Mechanical Move] `unified_cache/components/{full,mamba,swa}_component.py` → `{full,mamba,swa}.py`; `tree_component.py` → `base.py` — #35644 *(this was missed by #32484, which moved the directory but kept the suffixes)* ### 6.5 Documentation and guard - [x] `mem_cache/README.md` — layer map, placement-by-base-class, §4 naming rules, §7 dependency invariants — #35643. Deliberately coarse: a per-class inventory would need updating by every remaining move, and it already has a rot-proof home in §8's shrink-only pins. - [x] `test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_mem_cache_layout_ratchet.py` (§8) — R1 (allocator + pool_host), R2, R3, R4 — #35638 (draft, stacked on #35306) - [x] `.claude/skills/mem-cache-layout/SKILL.md` + trigger line in `.claude/rules/modify-component-must-read.md` - [ ] enable R1 for the `pool` role once `mem_cache/pool/` exists (first item of §6.3) --- ## 7. Layering and dependency invariants ``` scheduler / model_runner / attention backend │ ▼ ┌──────────────────────────────────────────┐ │ allocation.py │ per-batch allocation policy └──────────────────────────────────────────┘ │ ▼ ┌──────────────────────────────────────────┐ │ hybrid_cache/ │ multi-pool router └──────────────────────────────────────────┘ │ ▼ ┌──────────────────────────────────────────┐ │ allocator/ │ "give me N slots" └──────────────────────────────────────────┘ │ holds a reference to ↓ ▼ ┌────────────────────────┐ ┌──────────────────────────┐ │ pool/ (device, L1) │ ─ hicache ►│ pool_host/ (host, L2) │ └────────────────────────┘ offload └──────────────────────────┘ │ ▼ ┌──────────────────────────┐ │ storage/ (L3) │ └──────────────────────────┘ construction layer (cuts across all of the above, not a tier): kv_cache_configurator.py, kv_cache_builder.py, cache_init_params.py, allocation_sizing.py, kv_cache_dtype.py, kv_vmm_backing.py, hybrid_cache/pool_assembler.py ``` | Module | Cares about | In → Out | |---|---|---| | `allocation.py` | per-batch allocation policy | `batch` → `out_cache_loc` | | `hybrid_cache/` | per-layer routing across pools | `layer_id` → pool | | `allocator/` | which slots are free | `need_size` → `indices` | | `pool/` | physical KV / SSM state layout | `(layer_id, indices) ↔ tensor` | | `pool_host/` | host mirror + H2D/D2H | `device_indices ↔ host_indices` | **Dependency invariants** (machine-checkable, enforced by §8): - `pool/` must not import `allocator/`, `hybrid_cache/`, or `allocation.py`. - `pool_host/` must not import `allocator/` or `hybrid_cache/`. - `allocator/` may import `pool/` (it holds the pool it allocates into); the reverse is forbidden. - Nothing under `pool/`, `pool_host/`, or `allocator/` may import the construction layer. Construction depends on them, never the other way round. The original RFC declared per-layer responsibilities but no dependency direction. Without an enforced direction, the split only relocates files — the layers stop being layers the first time a pool reaches back up into an allocator. --- ## 8. Guard: `test_mem_cache_layout_ratchet.py` A directory is not a rule (see §2). The guard is a ratchet test in `test/registered/unit/mem_cache/`, modelled on the existing `test/registered/unit/test_module_state_ratchet.py` and registered into `base-a-test-cpu`. Four pins, each shrink-only, each covering one way the layout regressed after the restructure was agreed. ### R1 — a class lives where its base class says **Role is decided by base class, never by class name** — `HostTensorAllocator` is named `Allocator` but hands out pinned host memory, not KV slots (§4.3). Because inheritance crosses modules, the test builds a class graph over `mem_cache/` and takes its transitive closure. Class names do collide (three modules define `TreeNode`), so ancestry is unioned across same-named definitions: over-approximating turns a collision into a review conversation, where dropping all but one definition would turn it into a silent miss. | Transitive base | Required home | |---|---| | `BaseTokenToKVPoolAllocator` | `mem_cache/allocator/` | | `HostKVCache` | `mem_cache/pool_host/` | | `KVCache`, `BaseSWAKVPool`, `ReqToTokenPool`, `MambaPool` | `mem_cache/pool/` *(deferred)* | `_LEGACY_HOMES` pins the five classes still misfiled today (3 allocators in `multi_ended_allocator.py`, 2 host pools in `memory_pool_host.py`). **The pool role is enforced only once `mem_cache/pool/` exists.** An error telling someone to file a class into a package nobody has created is a trap, not a rule. R3 covers the device pools in the meantime; when the first `pool/` PR lands, `pool` joins the enforced roles and its 29 classes move from R3's pin into `_LEGACY_HOMES`. ### R2 — no new top-level modules `_TOP_LEVEL_MODULES` freezes the 40 `mem_cache/*.py` files that exist today. A new top-level module must go into a package, or grow the pin in the same PR — which forces the "why is this not in a package?" conversation into review instead of leaving it to be noticed three months later. ### R3 — modules slated for deletion only shrink R1 and R2 both miss the most damaging case: a class appended to a module that already exists. That is exactly how `memory_pool.py` gained `PageMajorMHATokenToKVPool`, `MHATokenToKVPoolMXFP8`, `MHATokenToKOnlyPool`, `MiniMaxSparseKVPool` and `DSATokenToKVPool` after the split was agreed. `_SHRINKING_MODULES` pins the class list of every module §5 marks for deletion. It needs no target package to exist, so it is what stands in for the pool role until R1 takes over. ### R4 — layers don't import upwards Asserts the §7 dependency invariants over the import graph. It passes on `main` today, so it locks in a property the code already has rather than demanding new work. ### Mechanics - Pins hold today's state, so the test is green on landing and never blocks unrelated work. - A violation that is not pinned → fail, with an error naming the correct target file and linking this roadmap. - **Every pin also fails when it rots**: a class that has moved, a module that is gone, a file that no longer exists. This makes every move PR shrink a pin (Rule 5 in §3) and turns the pins into the migration's progress ledger. - Scope is `python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/` only. `hardware_backend/` is explicitly excluded — its NPU/MLX pools and allocators are a separate device axis and are not governed by this issue. Each of the six failure paths (four violations, two rot cases) was verified to fire by injecting the violation into a scratch copy of the tree; a guard nobody has seen go red is not a guard. A skill (`.claude/skills/mem-cache-layout/SKILL.md`) covers the same rules for coding agents, but is *not* the guard: human PRs never read `.claude/skills/`. The ratchet blocks; the skill only teaches. --- ## 9. Resolved design decisions **D1 — `Unified*` shared-arena classes stay cohesive.** `unified_memory_pool.py` and `multi_ended_allocator.py` (both from #29678) are `Unified*` variants of every family, but they are coupled to a shared `UnifiedKVPool` arena rather than to their own families. Folding each into its family file would spread one concern across six files. They keep their cohesion in `pool/unified/` and `allocator/multi_ended.py`, as §5 shows. `pool/unified/` is the one place where the one-module-per-family rule (§4.2) is deliberately overridden by a one-module-per-arena split. **D2 — the construction layer is a follow-up issue, not part of this one.** `kv_cache_configurator.py` (2190) + `kv_cache_builder.py` + `cache_init_params.py` + `allocation_sizing.py` + `kv_cache_dtype.py` + `kv_vmm_backing.py` + `hybrid_cache/pool_assembler.py` (1960) is ~5.5k lines with no home in the tier diagram. §7 recognizes it as a cross-cutting layer; §5 deliberately leaves the files where they are. `mem_cache/build/` gets planned as its own issue **after §6.3 lands** — moving construction and storage in the same window would churn the same importers twice and make every Mechanical Move proof harder to review. **D3 — `IndexKeyCache` goes into `pool/dsa.py`, with no new base class.** Its only two importers are `DSATokenToKVPool` and `LayerSplitIndexKeyCache`, both of which land in `pool/dsa.py`; it holds a `self.pool` back-reference and reads ten pool attributes, so today the two sides only avoid an import cycle via `TYPE_CHECKING` and a string annotation. Same module removes the cycle. Its whole API (`move`, `get_buffer`, `store_quantized`, `cpu_copy`, `load_cpu_copy`, `state_buf_infos`) is the storage contract, and `DSATokenToKVPool` forwards to it one line at a time — it is simply DSA's second device buffer. It is **not** given a `KVCache` base just so the guard can classify it: inventing an abstraction to satisfy a linter is the wrong direction. Rule 2 of §8 covers it instead, by pinning the top-level module list.

signal.title: [diffusion] feat: load GGUF transformer checkpoints (MiniMax-H3)
signal.text: ## Motivation MiniMax-H3's transformer is 61.7 GiB in BF16, and the FL2VA partition is 135 GiB in total. Layerwise offload already lets the model run on a consumer GPU, so the remaining barriers are the checkpoint download, host memory, and bytes streamed per layer. This adds a pre-quantized GGUF transformer path. The validated Q4_K_M DiT is 17.5 GiB instead of 61.7 GiB. It complements online `kitchen_int8`: GGUF avoids first downloading and pinning the complete BF16 DiT, while `kitchen_int8` remains the faster compute-oriented path. ## Interface `--model-path` continues to provide the pipeline components and `--transformer-weights-path` selects the GGUF DiT. The loader accepts a local file, `owner/repo/path/file.gguf`, or `owner/repo:QUANT_TYPE` when that suffix matches exactly one file. Repositories containing multiple variants require the full file path. ```bash sglang serve \ --model-path MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3 \ --model-variant fl2va \ --transformer-weights-path \ leejet/MiniMax-H3-GGUF/minimax_h3_fl2va-Q4_K_M.gguf \ --attention-backend fa \ --performance-mode memory \ --layerwise-offload-components dit,text_encoder \ --dit-offload-prefetch-size 1 \ --dit-layerwise-resident-layers 0 \ --enable-torch-compile false \ --port 30010 ``` `--quantization gguf` is intentionally rejected: quantization is encoded in the checkpoint and the file path is the selector. ## Implementation - Reuses SRT's GGUF file detection, Hub resolver, quantization type sets, and CUDA dequantization helper. Diffusion no longer carries duplicate download resolution, GGML support tables, or dequantization shape logic. - Keeps a small diffusion-specific header reader because model construction needs each tensor's exact logical and packed shape before parameters exist. Packed tensors stay mmap-backed until the generic loader copies their TP shard, which avoids cloning the complete 17.5 GiB checkpoint during load. - Uses dequantization followed by native GEMM for DiT linears. SRT's fused MMVQ/MMQ path is optimized for low-token LLM inference and regresses normal diffusion sequence lengths. - Supports block-aligned tensor parallel row/column/merged linear slicing. Incompatible TP degrees fail during model construction. - Supports both the original MiniMax-H3 timestep MLP and pruned community checkpoints containing an unquantized `adaln_t_table` curve. - Fails before download for conflicting or unsupported configurations: non-CUDA, FSDP for the GGUF component, LoRA, another `--quantization`, SVDQuant, and the separate MiniMax-H3 AdaLN cache/online paths. - Keeps `quality=high` fail-closed when replacement transformer weights are supplied. F32/F16/BF16 tensors use the ordinary linear path. Quantized tensors must be 2D `.weight` matrices and have valid GGML block alignment; malformed, corrupt, opposite-endian, or unsupported files fail at load. ## Validation ### Automated - Changed-files pre-commit: passed. - Focused remote NVIDIA suite: **163 passed, 2 subtests passed**. - Coverage includes header corruption/endianness/BF16 handling, Hub resolution and ambiguity, type selection, CPU-offload loading, pre-download guards, quality admission, pruned curve interpolation, and TP row/column/merged slicing. ### Kernel selection On H200 with the real H3 Q4_K QKV matrix `(21504, 5376)`, fused MMVQ is useful only at one or two tokens. At 256 and 2048 tokens, SRT MMQ took 2.60 ms and 20.61 ms versus 0.37 ms and 0.91 ms for dequantize + GEMM. The final diffusion adapter therefore keeps the native-GEMM path. ### End to end 1x H200, FL2VA Q4_K_M, layerwise-offloaded DiT/text encoder, fixed seed, 1344x768, 107 frames, 2 inference steps: | Revision | Warmup | Generation | Peak GPU | Output | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- | | Original PR dense-dequant path | 12.67 s | 10.11 s | 17,174 MB | H.264 + AAC | | Refactored SRT-reuse path | 12.64 s | 10.13 s | 17,174 MB | H.264 + AAC | The two MP4 files are byte-identical (same SHA-256; PSNR infinite, SSIM 1.0). The refactored loader constructed the 17.49 GiB DiT in about 1 second versus about 19 seconds in the original PR run because packed values are no longer cloned wholesale during iteration. The pruned `unsloth/MiniMax-H3-GGUF` FL2VA Q4_K checkpoint also completed server warmup and a real 1344x768, 107-frame video + AAC request on H200; its loaded DiT size was 10.72 GiB. The original RTX 5090 measurements remain valid: 39.0 s denoise and 26.3 GiB peak with `dit,text_encoder` offload; adding VAE offload lowered peak to 19.6 GiB and increased VAE decode from 9.5 s to 57.2 s. Not yet validated end to end: `ref2va`, quantization types other than the listed Q4 variants, and multi-GPU GGUF. TP packed slicing is unit-tested, but a requested 2x H100 validation box remained in infrastructure provisioning and is not reported as a successful run. ## Checklist - [x] Format code with pre-commit. - [x] Add unit tests. - [x] Update CLI, quantization, compatibility, and MiniMax-H3 documentation. - [x] Run real checkpoint and end-to-end NVIDIA validation. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32256244219](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32256244219)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #32256243954](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32256243954)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->
